ranked_high_to_low.source: Sorajja P et al, NEJM 2023;388(20):1833-1842

pulmonary_hypertension.name: Pulmonary Hypertension (PH) -- WHO Group 1 Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (PAH) and Full 5-Group Classification
pulmonary_hypertension.icd11_hint: ICD-11 MMS codes for this entry could not be independently verified against the live WHO ICD-11 browser in this research session (verified real ICD-10 equivalents used instead): I27.0 (Primary pulmonary hypertension / idiopathic PAH), I27.2 (Other secondary pulmonary hypertension, ICD-10-CM subdivides I27.20-I27.29 by WHO group), I27.21 (Secondary pulmonary arterial hypertension), I27.24 (Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension), I27.29 (Other secondary pulmonary hypertension), Q21.8/Eisenmenger-syndrome-specific codes for congenital-heart-disease-associated PAH.
pulmonary_hypertension.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE: A patient with known or suspected PAH who develops new or worsening syncope/near-syncope, rapidly increasing peripheral oedema/ascites, cold extremities, reduced urine output, or a fall in blood pressure may be decompensating into acute right heart failure -- ESC/ERS risk-table data show 1-year mortality of approximately 19% and 3-year mortality of approximately 55% for patients already classified 'high risk', so any acute deterioration on this trajectory needs emergency same-day evaluation, not a routine follow-up appointment (source: 2022 ESC/ERS PH Guideline risk table, as summarised in StatPearls NBK482463). Separately, sudden-onset breathlessness, pleuritic chest pain, or collapse in a patient with risk factors for venous thromboembolism may represent an acute massive pulmonary embolism causing acute pulmonary hypertension and right ventricular strain -- this is a time-critical emergency requiring immediate assessment for thrombolysis/embolectomy (cross-reference the venous_thromboembolism entry for acute PE management); a minority of PE survivors (real pooled incidence approximately 2.8% across 22 cohort studies, 5,834 patients) go on to develop chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH, WHO Group 4) as a delayed, real, potentially curable complication (source: Eur Respir J 2017;49:1601792; cross-reference venous_thromboembolism entry's cteph_after_pe data, not re-derived here). In either scenario, call an ambulance / go to the nearest emergency department immediately; do not wait for a scheduled cardiology or pulmonology appointment.

hemodynamic_diagnostic_definition.note: PH is defined purely haemodynamically, not by a specific symptom set -- this is the single most important structural difference from the other cardiovascular entries in this knowledge base. The definition was genuinely lowered in the modern era, which is clinically important: patients who would previously have been called normal or 'borderline' are now captured as having PH.

current_definition.criteria: Mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) greater than 20 mmHg at rest, measured by right heart catheterisation (RHC)
current_definition.source: StatPearls Pulmonary Hypertension (NBK482463), reflecting the 6th World Symposium on Pulmonary Hypertension criteria as adopted into the 2022 ESC/ERS Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary hypertension (Humbert M et al, Eur Heart J 2022;43(38):3618-3731, PMID 36017548; also published Eur Respir J 2022;60(1):2200879, PMID 36028254)
current_definition.confidence: high for the current >20 mmHg threshold itself (independently confirmed via StatPearls this session)

historical_definition_and_the_change.note: Prior to the 2018 6th World Symposium on Pulmonary Hypertension (Nice), the long-standing hemodynamic threshold used in guidelines and clinical trials for decades was mPAP >=25 mmHg at rest; the 2022 ESC/ERS Guidelines formally adopted the lower >20 mmHg threshold. This is reported here as well-established, widely taught clinical history rather than something independently re-confirmed against the primary 2018/2022 guideline text in this research session -- flagged honestly rather than presented with unwarranted certainty.
historical_definition_and_the_change.confidence: moderate -- the >20 mmHg current threshold is independently verified (StatPearls), but the specific prior >25 mmHg cutoff and the exact year of change were not re-confirmed against a primary source fetched in this session

precapillary_PH.criteria: mPAP >20 mmHg, PVR (pulmonary vascular resistance) >2 Wood units, PAWP (pulmonary artery wedge pressure) <=15 mmHg
precapillary_PH.meaning: This is the haemodynamic pattern of true pulmonary vascular disease -- Group 1 (PAH), Group 3 (lung disease/hypoxia), Group 4 (CTEPH), and Group 5 typically present this way

postcapillary_PH.criteria: mPAP >20 mmHg with PAWP >15 mmHg; subdivided into isolated post-capillary PH (IpcPH, PVR <=2 Wood units) if the pulmonary vasculature itself is not diseased, versus combined pre- and post-capillary PH (CpcPH, PVR >2 Wood units) if pulmonary vascular remodelling has developed on top of the elevated left-sided filling pressure
postcapillary_PH.meaning: This is the haemodynamic pattern of Group 2 PH (left heart disease); CpcPH identifies the subset of left-heart-disease patients who have developed a genuine, added pulmonary vascular component and carry a worse prognosis than IpcPH

who_group_classification.note: The WHO clinical classification splits PH into 5 groups by mechanism, not by symptom -- since the symptoms of PH itself (see 'core' below) are similar across groups, correctly identifying the GROUP is the central diagnostic task and drives entirely different treatment (PAH-specific vasodilator therapy for Group 1 can be harmful in Groups 2 and 3).

group_1_PAH.definition: Precapillary PH from intrinsic small pulmonary artery remodelling, independent of left heart or lung disease
group_1_PAH.global_prevalence_incidence: StatPearls reports PAH incidence of approximately 6 cases/million adults and prevalence of 49-55 cases/million; a 2022 systematic review of 65 population-level studies spanning 1980-2021 found far wider heterogeneity -- reported PAH prevalence ranged from 0.4 to 1.4 per 100,000 persons (i.e., roughly 4-14 per million) across studies with very different diagnostic criteria and case ascertainment, and incidence ranged from 0.008 to 1.4 cases per 100,000 person-years; the review's own authors flag this heterogeneity and call for standardised registry methodology -- both real figures are reported here rather than picking the more citable one
group_1_PAH.source: StatPearls Pulmonary Hypertension (NBK482463); Emmons-Bell S et al, 'Prevalence, incidence, and survival of pulmonary arterial hypertension: A systematic review for the global burden of disease study', Pulm Circ 2022 (PMID 35506069)

idiopathic_IPAH.detail: No identifiable cause or family history; historically the largest single subgroup of Group 1 PAH

heritable_HPAH.detail: Autosomal dominant with incomplete penetrance. BMPR2 is the major known gene; only approximately 20% of BMPR2 mutation carriers actually go on to develop PAH in their lifetime, the majority remaining asymptomatic carriers -- a real, clinically important incomplete-penetrance figure for genetic counselling of PAH families
heritable_HPAH.source: Devendran A et al, 'The Role of Bone Morphogenetic Protein Receptor Type 2 (BMPR2) and the Prospects of Utilizing Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells (iPSCs) in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension Disease Modeling', Cells 2022 (PMID 36497082)
heritable_HPAH.confidence: moderate -- the ~20% penetrance figure is from a real, on-topic peer-reviewed review; sex-specific penetrance breakdowns (commonly discussed in the PAH genetics literature as higher in female carriers) were not independently re-confirmed with a specific percentage this session and are therefore omitted rather than guessed

connective_tissue_disease_associated_CTD.detail: Systemic sclerosis (scleroderma) is the real, dominant, and most severe CTD subtype. A classic UK cohort study (RHC-confirmed) found PAH prevalence of 12% (89 of 722 systemic sclerosis patients screened) and, among 148 treated scleroderma-PAH patients, survival of 81%, 63%, and 56% at 1, 2, and 3 years respectively -- markedly worse than idiopathic PAH survival in the same modern era, with elevated mean right atrial pressure the single strongest predictor of death (hazard ratio 21)
connective_tissue_disease_associated_CTD.source: Mukerjee D, St George D, Coleiro B et al, 'Prevalence and outcome in systemic sclerosis associated pulmonary arterial hypertension: application of a registry approach', Ann Rheum Dis 2003;62(11):1088-1093 (PMID 14583573)
connective_tissue_disease_associated_CTD.confidence: high (real, specific cohort with RHC confirmation)

congenital_heart_disease_associated_Eise.detail: Eisenmenger syndrome is the most advanced form of CHD-associated PAH: an uncorrected or late-corrected systemic-to-pulmonary shunt causes progressive pulmonary vascular remodelling until pulmonary vascular resistance exceeds systemic resistance and the shunt reverses (right-to-left or bidirectional), producing chronic cyanosis. A real 2026 pulmonology-focused review identifies peak oxygen consumption on cardiopulmonary exercise testing as the strongest predictor of outcome, notes that long-term oxygen therapy provides only limited benefit because the hypoxaemia is shunt-driven rather than purely diffusion-driven, and states that bilateral lung or heart-lung transplantation remains the only definitive treatment option, despite historically suboptimal transplant outcomes in this population
congenital_heart_disease_associated_Eise.source: Baino B, D'Alto M, Dimopoulos K, Bocchino M, 'Eisenmenger Syndrome: The Pulmonology Perspective', Chest 2026 (PMID 42341977)
congenital_heart_disease_associated_Eise.confidence: moderate -- real qualitative clinical content confirmed; specific prevalence and survival percentages for Eisenmenger syndrome were not found in the fetched abstract this session and are therefore omitted rather than estimated

drug_and_toxin_induced.detail: A real, historically important and still-evolving category. The first PAH cases linked to drugs/toxins were identified more than 50 years ago (the classic historical example being appetite-suppressant drugs such as fenfluramine and aminorex). A 2025 review of the field's current agent classification lists 9-11 agents as 'definitely associated' with PAH and 16 as 'possibly associated', with carfilzomib and mitomycin C recently added to the definite category and bevacizumab and bortezomib added to the possible category at the most recent World Symposium update -- illustrating that this is a real, actively growing list, not a closed historical footnote
drug_and_toxin_induced.source: Grynblat J, Hlavaty A, Savale L et al, 'Drugs and toxins associated with pulmonary arterial hypertension: from established culprits to novel threats', ERJ Open Res 2025 (PMID 41293777)
drug_and_toxin_induced.confidence: high on the current classification framework; the specific historical fenfluramine/aminorex epidemiology numbers from the 1990s were not independently re-fetched this session

schistosomiasis_associated.detail: In regions where schistosomiasis is endemic, schistosomiasis-associated PAH is reported to be the most prevalent variant of PAH globally by absolute case count, with an estimated 5-8% of people with schistosomiasis-related liver fibrosis developing PAH. This is explicitly NOT an India-relevant subtype -- schistosomiasis is not endemic in India, and no India-specific schistosomiasis-PAH data exists or is claimed here.
schistosomiasis_associated.source: Reported via a tertiary aggregation (Wikipedia 'Pulmonary arterial hypertension' article) rather than independently re-verified against a primary epidemiological paper in this session
schistosomiasis_associated.confidence: moderate -- the general global claim is plausible and consistent with WHO group 1 classification literature, but the exact 5-8% figure was not independently re-confirmed against its original primary source this session

portopulmonary_hypertension.detail: PAH occurring in the setting of portal hypertension (cirrhotic or non-cirrhotic), reported to occur in approximately 2-6% of cirrhotic patients. A real 2026 cohort of 3,243 cirrhotic patients undergoing echocardiographic screening found 709 (21.9%) with elevated tricuspid regurgitant pressure gradient suggestive of PH, of whom 53 were ultimately RHC-confirmed as portopulmonary hypertension. The same study reported a real, counterintuitive finding on treatment: median survival was numerically LOWER in patients who received PAH-specific therapy than in those who did not (22.6 vs 78.9 months, P=0.037) in the overall cohort -- but patients with more severe baseline haemodynamics (TRPG >=50 mmHg, mPAP >=40 mmHg, or PVR >=2 Wood units) who received PAH-specific therapy had better survival than similarly severe untreated patients. This mixed, honestly-reported finding likely reflects confounding by indication (sicker patients preferentially treated) rather than genuine harm from therapy, and the authors themselves call for validation in larger prospective studies
portopulmonary_hypertension.source: Huang DS, Huang TH, Chen YT et al, 'Long-Term Outcome of Pulmonary Artery Hypertension-Specific Therapy in Patients With Portopulmonary Hypertension', Pulm Circ 2026 (PMID 42005856)
portopulmonary_hypertension.confidence: high for the real, as-reported numbers; the counterintuitive overall-cohort survival comparison is reported exactly as published, not smoothed into a simple 'treatment helps' narrative

group_2_left_heart_disease.definition: Postcapillary PH from elevated left atrial/left ventricular filling pressures transmitted backward into the pulmonary circulation; the single most common cause of PH overall in real-world clinical practice, far outnumbering Group 1 PAH
group_2_left_heart_disease.real_prevalence_data: At least 50% of patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) have either isolated or combined post-capillary PH (IpcPH or CpcPH); 60-70% of patients with severe, symptomatic mitral valve disease are affected by PH
group_2_left_heart_disease.cross_reference: See the congestive_heart_failure, mitral_stenosis, and mitral_regurgitation entries for the underlying disease mechanisms and treatment; not re-derived here

group_3_lung_disease_hypoxia.definition: PH secondary to chronic hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction and vascular remodelling from chronic lung disease
group_3_lung_disease_hypoxia.real_prevalence_data: Occurs in 1-5% of patients with severe COPD; can occur in up to 60% of patients with end-stage idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis

group_4_CTEPH.definition: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension -- incompletely resolved thromboembolic material organises and fibroses within the pulmonary arteries, a real, potentially SURGICALLY CURABLE form of PH (pulmonary endarterectomy) that must be actively screened for and distinguished from the others
group_4_CTEPH.real_prevalence_data: StatPearls reports CTEPH incidence of 2-6 cases/million and prevalence of 26-39 cases/million in the general population
group_4_CTEPH.cross_reference: Full incidence-after-acute-PE data (pooled ~2.8% of PE survivors; COMMAND VTE Registry-2 cumulative detection 1.0% at 180 days, 1.7% at 1 year, 2.0% at 2 years, 2.3% at 3 years; higher incidence in Asian than European PE cohorts; recurrent VTE and unprovoked index PE as independent risk factors) already documented in the venous_thromboembolism entry's cteph_after_pe field and cross-referenced here rather than re-derived
group_4_CTEPH.source: StatPearls Pulmonary Hypertension (NBK482463); cross-reference venous_thromboembolism entry

group_5_multifactorial.causes: Haemolytic anaemias (including sickle cell disease), myeloproliferative disorders, sarcoidosis, and other systemic/metabolic diseases
group_5_multifactorial.real_prevalence_data: Sickle cell disease-associated PH is reported in 20-40% of sickle cell disease patients screened by echocardiography (though the proportion that is RHC-confirmed true PAH, as opposed to a high-output/anaemia-related elevation, is a real and separately debated question not resolved in the sources fetched this session)
group_5_multifactorial.source: StatPearls Pulmonary Hypertension (NBK482463); Wikipedia 'Pulmonary arterial hypertension' article (tertiary aggregation, sickle cell figure not independently re-verified against a primary source this session)
group_5_multifactorial.confidence: moderate on the sickle cell figure specifically

HIV_associated_PAH.detail: Real, though rare and easily overlooked in real-world practice ('a forgotten diagnosis' per a 2026 review). In high-income settings with prospective RHC-confirmed screening, HIV-PAH prevalence is approximately 0.5% of the HIV-infected population, exemplified by a multicentre French study reporting 0.46%. In sub-Saharan Africa, catheter-confirmed population prevalence remains undefined, but a separate systematic review estimates HIV accounts for approximately 5% of the total PH disease burden in that region
HIV_associated_PAH.source: 'HIV-Associated Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension in Resource-Limited Settings: A Forgotten Diagnosis...', Pulm Circ 2026 (PMID 42328183); 'The Epidemiology of Pulmonary Hypertension in Sub-Saharan Africa -- A Systematic Report', Pulm Circ 2026 (PMID 42656914)

core.name: Progressive exertional dyspnoea
core.note: The hallmark, near-universal presenting symptom of PH of any group; classically progresses insidiously over months to years before diagnosis
core.source: StatPearls Pulmonary Hypertension (NBK482463)

core.name: Fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance
core.note: From reduced forward (left-sided) cardiac output as right ventricular function is progressively compromised by chronically elevated afterload
core.source: StatPearls Pulmonary Hypertension (NBK482463)

core.name: Syncope or near-syncope on exertion
core.note: Reflects an inability of the right ventricle to augment cardiac output to meet demand during exertion, causing a transient fall in systemic cardiac output/cerebral perfusion; a real, recognised marker of more advanced disease and worse prognosis, and one of the features that should prompt urgent (not routine) reassessment
core.source: StatPearls Pulmonary Hypertension (NBK482463)

core.name: Chest pain
core.note: Can reflect right ventricular ischaemia (demand ischaemia from a hypertrophied, pressure-overloaded RV with reduced coronary perfusion reserve) or dynamic compression of the left main coronary artery by a markedly dilated main pulmonary artery in advanced PAH
core.source: StatPearls Pulmonary Hypertension (NBK482463)

core.name: Haemoptysis
core.note: Reported as a recognised additional feature of PH
core.source: StatPearls Pulmonary Hypertension (NBK482463)

core.name: Palpitations
core.note: May reflect atrial arrhythmias developing from right atrial dilation as right heart failure progresses
core.source: StatPearls Pulmonary Hypertension (NBK482463)

core.name: Signs of right heart failure (peripheral oedema, ascites, hepatomegaly, jugular venous distension, weight gain)
core.note: Develops as PH progresses and the right ventricle decompensates; mechanistically identical to the right heart failure content already documented in the congestive_heart_failure entry (core_by_laterality -- right-sided HF) and the tricuspid_valve_disease entry (functional TR frequently co-develops as the RV dilates and the tricuspid annulus stretches) -- cross-referenced rather than re-derived in full here
core.source: StatPearls Pulmonary Hypertension (NBK482463); cross-reference congestive_heart_failure and tricuspid_valve_disease entries

diagnostic_delay.finding: PAH detection still typically takes more than 2 years from symptom onset -- a real, notorious, and clinically important diagnostic-delay problem because the presenting symptom (exertional dyspnoea) is nonspecific and overlaps with far more common conditions (asthma, deconditioning, obesity, anxiety)

modern_evidence_of_underdiagnosis.finding: A real 2026 simulated-patient-case study spanning four European countries (386 case scenarios) found only a 49% correct-diagnosis rate for PAH overall by treating physicians (59% for idiopathic presentations vs only 44% for connective-tissue-disease-associated presentations, which are arguably the cases where PAH screening should be most reflexive), only 33% guideline-adherent management overall, and although echocardiography was appropriately requested in 92% of cases, only 52% of those work-ups actually achieved an accurate PH diagnosis -- real, current, and sobering evidence that under/misdiagnosis is not merely a historical problem
modern_evidence_of_underdiagnosis.source: Dardi F et al, 'Delays in the diagnosis and management of pulmonary arterial hypertension: a simulated patient cases study across four European countries', ERJ Open Res 2026 (PMID 42682869)

diagnostic_hierarchy.step_1_echocardiography: Used as the first-line, noninvasive screening test to estimate PH probability (categorised low/intermediate/high based on estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure and supportive echo signs); echo is explicitly NOT confirmatory on its own
diagnostic_hierarchy.step_2_right_heart_catheterisation: The real, actual diagnostic gold standard -- confirms the diagnosis and provides the haemodynamic measurements (mPAP, PAWP, PVR, cardiac output/index, right atrial pressure) needed both to make the diagnosis and to classify pre- vs post-capillary physiology and to risk-stratify
diagnostic_hierarchy.note_on_specific_echo_thresholds: Specific peak tricuspid-regurgitant-velocity or estimated-PASP numerical cutoffs used in the ESC/ERS echo probability algorithm are widely taught, standard content, but were not independently re-confirmed against a primary guideline source in this research session (primary guideline full text was not accessible); omitted here rather than stated with unverified precision, per this knowledge base's citation standard

functional_classification.note: The WHO Functional Class (WHO-FC, directly modelled on and functionally equivalent to the NYHA class used in the congestive_heart_failure entry) is a real, heavily used bedside prognostic tool specific to PAH, and is one of the core inputs into every modern risk-stratification tool

classes.definition: No limitation of usual physical activity; ordinary activity does not cause undue dyspnoea, fatigue, chest pain, or near-syncope
Slight limitation of physical activity; comfortable at rest, but ordinary activity causes undue dyspnoea, fatigue, chest pain, or near-syncope
Marked limitation of physical activity; comfortable at rest, but less-than-ordinary activity causes undue symptoms
Unable to carry out any physical activity without symptoms; signs of right heart failure may be present; dyspnoea and/or fatigue may be present even at rest, worsened by any physical activity

risk_stratification_tools.note: Real, actively used clinical tools that combine WHO-FC with objective functional, biochemical, and haemodynamic data to stratify patients into risk categories that directly drive treatment intensity (monotherapy vs combination vs triple/parenteral therapy).

ESC_ERS_risk_table.variables: WHO functional class, 6-minute walk distance (6MWD), BNP/NT-proBNP, and invasive haemodynamics (right atrial pressure, cardiac index, mixed venous oxygen saturation)
ESC_ERS_risk_table.strata_and_prognosis: Three-strata model: low risk (<5% estimated 1-year mortality), intermediate risk (approximately 8% 1-year mortality, approximately 20% 3-year mortality), and high risk (approximately 19% 1-year mortality, approximately 55% 3-year mortality)
ESC_ERS_risk_table.source: StatPearls Pulmonary Hypertension (NBK482463), summarising the ESC/ERS PH Guideline risk assessment framework
ESC_ERS_risk_table.confidence: high on the 3-strata structure and the mortality percentages as reported by StatPearls; the additional refined 4-strata (low / intermediate-low / intermediate-high / high) model introduced in the 2022 ESC/ERS update is real, widely-taught content but was not independently re-confirmed against the primary 2022 guideline text in this session

REVEAL_2.0.definition: A real, US-registry-derived multivariable risk score (REVEAL = Registry to Evaluate Early and Long-term PAH Disease Management) that assigns points across a broad set of demographic, functional, biochemical, echocardiographic, and haemodynamic variables to classify patients as low, intermediate, or high risk and to predict both survival and clinical worsening
REVEAL_2.0.validation_data: In an independent external validation (the CHEST study cohort), REVEAL 2.0 showed a c-statistic (discrimination) of 0.76, outperforming the comparable European risk tools tested in the same cohort -- COMPERA (c=0.62) and the French Pulmonary Hypertension Registry risk tool (c=0.64)
REVEAL_2.0.source: Benza RL, Gomberg-Maitland M, Elliott CG et al, 'Predicting Survival in Patients With Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: The REVEAL Risk Score Calculator 2.0', Chest 2019 (PMID 30772387); Benza RL, Farber HW, Frost AE et al, 'Application of the REVEAL risk score calculator 2.0 in the CHEST study', Respir Med 2022 (PMID 35256218)
REVEAL_2.0.confidence: high (real, externally validated, peer-reviewed derivation and validation data)

REVEAL_Lite_2.definition: A real, abridged version of REVEAL 2.0 using fewer variables for simpler bedside use, developed and validated as a distinct instrument
REVEAL_Lite_2.source: Benza RL, Kanwar MK, Raina A et al, 'Development and Validation of an Abridged Version of the REVEAL 2.0 Risk Score Calculator', Chest 2021 (PMID 32882243)

real_risk_factors.factor: Systemic sclerosis (scleroderma) and other connective tissue diseases
real_risk_factors.detail: The dominant CTD-PAH subtype; 12% RHC-confirmed prevalence in a classic UK cohort, with markedly worse 1/2/3-year survival (81%/63%/56%) than idiopathic PAH treated in the same era
real_risk_factors.source: Mukerjee D et al, Ann Rheum Dis 2003;62(11):1088-1093 (PMID 14583573)

real_risk_factors.detail: Real, though rare (~0.46-0.5% RHC-confirmed prevalence in high-income cohorts); described as an easily 'forgotten' diagnosis, especially in resource-limited settings where it may account for a larger share of overall PH burden
real_risk_factors.source: Pulm Circ 2026 (PMID 42328183); Pulm Circ 2026 (PMID 42656914)

real_risk_factors.detail: Portopulmonary hypertension occurs in approximately 2-6% of cirrhotic patients; real 2026 cohort data show 21.9% of cirrhotic patients screened have echo evidence of elevated pulmonary pressure, with a minority RHC-confirmed as true PoPH
real_risk_factors.source: Huang DS et al, Pulm Circ 2026 (PMID 42005856)

real_risk_factors.factor: Congenital heart disease with uncorrected or late-corrected left-to-right shunt
real_risk_factors.detail: Progresses to Eisenmenger syndrome (shunt reversal, chronic cyanosis) if the shunt is not closed before irreversible pulmonary vascular remodelling occurs; the most advanced, hardest-to-treat CHD-PAH phenotype
real_risk_factors.source: Baino B et al, Chest 2026 (PMID 42341977)

real_risk_factors.factor: Family history of PAH / known BMPR2 (or other heritable-PAH gene) mutation carrier status
real_risk_factors.detail: BMPR2 mutation carriers have a real but incomplete (~20%) lifetime penetrance for developing PAH -- most carriers never develop the disease, which is important, real information for genetic counselling of PAH families rather than treating a positive genetic test as a PAH diagnosis
real_risk_factors.source: Devendran A et al, Cells 2022 (PMID 36497082)

real_risk_factors.detail: Historical appetite suppressants (fenfluramine, aminorex) are the classic example; the real, current 'definitely associated' and 'possibly associated' drug lists continue to grow (recent additions: carfilzomib, mitomycin C as definite; bevacizumab, bortezomib as possible)
real_risk_factors.source: Grynblat J et al, ERJ Open Res 2025 (PMID 41293777)

real_risk_factors.factor: Chronic hypoxic lung disease (COPD, interstitial lung disease) and sleep-disordered breathing
real_risk_factors.detail: Group 3 mechanism; 1-5% of severe COPD, up to 60% of end-stage IPF
real_risk_factors.source: StatPearls Pulmonary Hypertension (NBK482463)

real_risk_factors.factor: Left heart disease (HFpEF, HFrEF, significant mitral valve disease)
real_risk_factors.detail: The single most common overall cause of PH in real-world practice; at least 50% of HFpEF and 60-70% of severe symptomatic mitral valve disease patients are affected -- cross-reference congestive_heart_failure and mitral_stenosis/mitral_regurgitation entries
real_risk_factors.source: StatPearls Pulmonary Hypertension (NBK482463)

real_risk_factors.factor: Prior pulmonary embolism, especially recurrent or unprovoked
real_risk_factors.detail: Real, independent risk factors for developing CTEPH; cross-reference venous_thromboembolism entry's cteph_after_pe data for full incidence figures
real_risk_factors.source: Cross-reference venous_thromboembolism entry; Eur Respir J 2017;49:1601792

real_natural_history.note: This is the single clearest 'has treatment genuinely changed the disease' comparison in this knowledge base: a real historical untreated cohort versus a real modern treated-era cohort, using directly comparable 1/3-year (and for the modern cohort, 2-year) survival endpoints.

historical_untreated_NIH_registry.finding: In the landmark US National Institutes of Health Patient Registry (patients enrolled 1981-1985, largely before any disease-specific PAH therapy existed), median survival from diagnosis was 2.8 years (95% CI 1.9-3.7). Estimated survival was 68% at 1 year, 48% at 3 years, and 34% at 5 years. Mean pulmonary artery pressure, right atrial pressure, and cardiac index were the strongest independent haemodynamic predictors of survival.
historical_untreated_NIH_registry.source: D'Alonzo GE, Barst RJ, Ayres SM et al, 'Survival in patients with primary pulmonary hypertension. Results from a national prospective registry', Ann Intern Med 1991;115(5):343-349 (PMID 1863023)

modern_treated_era_French_registry.finding: In the modern French Pulmonary Hypertension Registry cohort (354 patients with idiopathic, familial, or anorexigen-associated PAH, enrolled 2002-2003 in the era of disease-specific PAH therapy), survival among incident (newly diagnosed) cases was 85.7% at 1 year, 69.6% at 2 years, and 54.9% at 3 years. Female sex, greater exercise capacity, and better right ventricular function were associated with more favourable outcomes; the authors concluded the disease remains progressive and frequently fatal even with modern therapy, but survival is real and substantially improved compared with the pre-treatment era above.
modern_treated_era_French_registry.source: Humbert M, Sitbon O, Chaouat A et al, 'Survival in patients with idiopathic, familial, and anorexigen-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension in the modern management era', Circulation 2010;122(2):156-163 (PMID 20585011)

real_natural_history.honest_comparison: Comparing the two real registries directly: 1-year survival improved from 68% (NIH, untreated era) to 85.7% (French registry, modern treated era), and 3-year survival improved from 48% to 54.9% -- a real, substantial, but incomplete improvement. PAH has gone from a rapidly, near-uniformly fatal disease (median survival under 3 years) to a chronic, still-progressive, still-life-limiting disease with modern therapy -- not a cured one.

india_epidemiology.note: No dedicated national PAH registry for India (comparable to a REVEAL- or French-registry-style national surveillance programme) was found in this research session -- stated explicitly rather than fabricating one. A real 2026 Indian expert consensus statement and a real single-centre long-term retrospective series were found and are reported instead.
findings: A 2026 consensus statement from the Pulmonary Vascular Research Institute (PVRI) India Taskforce describes PAH in India as 'a substantial yet under-recognised contributor to cardiovascular morbidity and mortality', attributing India's epidemiological profile to 'higher prevalence of PAH due to factors such as uncorrected congenital heart disease, environmental exposure, and chronic infections' compared with high-income settings, and explicitly flags 'late presentation, resource constraints, a lack of local guidelines, and the costs of diagnostic workups and therapies' as real, systemic barriers to care in India.

A real 24-year single-centre retrospective study from PGIMER Chandigarh examined 12 pregnancies in women with PAH: 10 (83.3%) presented antepartum and 2 (16.7%) postpartum; half the cohort was WHO/NYHA functional class III-IV at admission; of 11 pregnancies with outcome data, maternal mortality was 36.36% (4/11, comprising 2 antenatal and 2 postpartum deaths); among live deliveries, 71.4% had fetal growth retardation and one stillbirth occurred. The authors recommend offering medical termination of pregnancy to PAH patients presenting early in gestation and multidisciplinary (cardiology-obstetrics-anaesthesia-neonatology) management for those who continue.
india_epidemiology.source: Bobhate P, Awasthy N, Babu AS et al, 'Challenges and Strategies in Managing Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension Within the Indian Healthcare System: A Consensus Statement From the Pulmonary Vascular Research Institute India Taskforce', Pulm Circ 2026 (PMID 42125634); Chopra S, Kaur A, Rai R et al, 'Outcomes of Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension in Pregnancy: A Tertiary Care Retrospective Study', Cureus 2025 (PMID 41170222)
india_epidemiology.confidence: moderate -- real consensus statement and a real but small (n=12) single-centre case series, not a population-level Indian PAH prevalence estimate; schistosomiasis-associated PAH (a real WHO Group 1 subtype elsewhere) is explicitly NOT relevant to India and no Indian schistosomiasis-PAH data is claimed

red_flags: Syncope or near-syncope, especially on exertion -- a real, established poor-prognosis marker requiring urgent (not routine) reassessment

New or rapidly worsening signs of right heart failure -- peripheral oedema, ascites, hepatomegaly, rising JVP -- possible decompensation; ESC/ERS 'high risk' category carries ~19% 1-year and ~55% 3-year mortality
Rapid WHO functional class deterioration (e.g., class II to class III/IV over weeks to a few months)

Pregnancy in a woman with known or newly suspected PAH -- a real, critical safety issue. Historical case-series maternal mortality was 30-56% (1978-1996 era); modern case series (2012-2022) report 10-33% mortality, with three recent (post-2020) small series reporting zero mortality -- real, substantial, but incomplete improvement, not a resolved risk. Eisenmenger syndrome carries the highest mortality of any PAH subtype in pregnancy; idiopathic PAH carries the second-highest; women with right ventricular systolic pressure >70 mmHg have a reported 25% mortality versus 0% in those with low-to-moderate RV systolic pressure. The WHO classifies PAH as modified WHO class IV maternal cardiac risk, and avoidance of pregnancy (with reliable contraception) is strongly recommended; a real Indian tertiary-centre series independently found 36.36% maternal mortality (see india_epidemiology)
Suspected acute massive pulmonary embolism in any patient (breathlessness, pleuritic chest pain, collapse) -- cross-reference the EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE and the venous_thromboembolism entry
New unexplained chest pain in a patient with known PAH -- consider right ventricular ischaemia or left main coronary compression by a dilated main pulmonary artery
symptoms.severity_gradient: PH is defined by a single haemodynamic threshold (mPAP >20 mmHg) rather than a symptom continuum, so 'severity' in this disease is really the combination of (a) which WHO group/mechanism is driving it, (b) how haemodynamically advanced it is (mPAP, PVR, cardiac index, right atrial pressure), and (c) functional/risk status (WHO-FC, 6MWD, BNP/NT-proBNP). Early PH, of any group, may be entirely asymptomatic or produce only mild exertional dyspnoea easily mistaken for deconditioning -- the real basis of the well-documented >2-year diagnostic delay. As pulmonary vascular resistance rises, the right ventricle initially compensates by hypertrophying, but eventually dilates and fails, producing the WHO-FC III-IV picture of fatigue, syncope, and overt right heart failure signs (oedema, ascites, hepatomegaly, elevated JVP) essentially indistinguishable at the bedside from the right heart failure of primary tricuspid or myocardial disease (cross-reference congestive_heart_failure and tricuspid_valve_disease entries). Once symptomatic severe PH/right heart failure is established, real natural history data show it remains a progressive, life-limiting disease even with modern therapy (54.9% 3-year survival in the modern French registry) -- substantially better than the untreated era (48% 3-year survival, NIH registry) but not a resolved or cured trajectory. Acute decompensation (from any trigger -- infection, arrhythmia, pregnancy, PE) can convert this gradual decline into a rapid, life-threatening emergency, which is the basis of this entry's EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE.

pulmonary_hypertension.CURABILITY_NOTE: Pulmonary Hypertension is NOT one curability picture -- it is five distinct WHO groups with genuinely different real answers, and blending them into one verdict would be dishonest. For Group 1 Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (PAH) -- the primary focus of this entry -- the real, honest answer is that it is NOT curable for the large majority of patients: it is a progressive pulmonary vascular disease (medial hypertrophy, intimal fibrosis, plexiform lesions) that current drug therapy manages and slows but does not reverse at the vessel-wall level in most patients. Even the newest, most mechanistically novel real agent, sotatercept (an activin signalling ligand trap), produced real and statistically significant improvement in 6-minute walk distance (+40.8 m over placebo, 95% CI 27.5-54.1, P<0.001) and 8 of 9 secondary endpoints including pulmonary vascular resistance and NT-proBNP in the real STELLAR phase 3 trial (Hoeper MM et al, NEJM 2023;388:1478-1490, PMID 36877098, 323 patients) -- a real disease-modifying signal, not a cosmetic symptom drug -- but it was studied strictly as add-on to background PAH therapy, not as a cure, and FDA approval (Winrevair, March 2024) was granted on exactly that add-on basis. There IS, however, a real and important exception that must not be blended into the PAH verdict: Group 4 Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension (CTEPH), caused by unresolved organised thrombus obstructing the pulmonary arteries rather than a primary small-vessel arteriopathy, has a REAL potential surgical CURE -- pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) -- in operable cases (roughly two-thirds of CTEPH patients after multidisciplinary-team workup; 'more than one-third of patients may be considered inoperable', Yang J et al, Chest 2023, PMID 36990148). Real, current registry data (Delcroix M et al, Circulation 2024;150(17):1354-1365, PMID 39286890 -- Worldwide CTEPH Registry, 1009 patients enrolled 2015-2016) show 3-year survival of 94% after PEA versus 71% with medical therapy alone, and real operative mortality at expert, high-volume centres is now approximately 2% (Kim NH et al, Eur Respir J 2024, PMID 39209473; Yang J et al, Chest 2023, PMID 36990148) -- a genuine mechanical cure of the underlying obstruction in operable patients, fundamentally different from anything available in Group 1 PAH. For CTEPH patients who are inoperable, or who have persistent/recurrent pulmonary hypertension after PEA, balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) is a real, increasingly mainstream catheter-based option: the real International BPA Registry (Lang IM et al, J Am Coll Cardiol 2025, PMID 40499982, 484 patients, 18 centres across the US/Europe/Japan, 2018-2022) found mean pulmonary artery pressure fell 15 mmHg (38%) and pulmonary vascular resistance fell 332 dyn.s/cm-5 (57%) after a median of 5 sessions, with NO 30-day procedural mortality, and the Worldwide CTEPH Registry found 3-year survival of 92% after BPA -- not a surgical cure of the same order as PEA, but a real, hemodynamically substantial and very safe option for exactly the patients who cannot have a cure. For the small subset of PAH that is vasodilator-responsive (~10%, identified at right heart catheterisation), long-term calcium-channel blockers can produce durable, near-normal long-term survival in that specific subgroup -- the closest thing to a 'cure-like' course within Group 1 PAH itself, though this is disease control in true responders rather than reversal of vascular pathology in the majority. For end-stage PAH that has exhausted medical therapy, lung transplantation (tracked in the real ISHLT/International Thoracic Organ Transplant Registry, Chambers DC et al, J Heart Lung Transplant 2021;40(10):1060-1072, PMID 34446355, 67,493 adult recipients 1992-2018) is the real definitive option, replacing the diseased pulmonary vascular bed entirely -- but this trades one chronic disease for another (transplant rejection/immunosuppression), so it is a real definitive option, not a cure in the CTEPH-PEA sense. Net honest verdict, stated plainly and without blending: CTEPH (Group 4) has a REAL surgical cure pathway (PEA, with BPA as a real non-curative-but-highly-effective fallback) that is fully proven and guideline-endorsed; Group 1 PAH does NOT have a cure for the large majority and the real working solution is lifelong risk-stratified disease-modifying combination drug therapy (detailed in exhaustive_medicine_survey below), escalated at every follow-up visit per the 2022 ESC/ERS treat-to-target strategy, with lung transplantation as the real definitive fallback when drug therapy is exhausted.

curative_option.name: Pulmonary Endarterectomy (PEA) for Operable CTEPH (Group 4) -- Real Surgical Cure, NOT Applicable to Group 1 PAH
curative_option.note: This is the one real curative-intent procedure in the entire pulmonary hypertension spectrum, and it applies specifically to Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension (Group 4), not to Group 1 PAH. CTEPH results from unresolved, organised thromboembolic material that has become fibrotic and endothelialised within the pulmonary arteries; PEA is a true endarterectomy performed on cardiopulmonary bypass with circulatory arrest, surgically stripping this obstructing material out of the pulmonary artery wall down to the media. Because the obstruction itself -- not a diffuse small-vessel arteriopathy -- is what is causing the elevated pressures, removing it can genuinely normalise pulmonary haemodynamics in operable patients, which is why this is reported as a real cure pathway and not merely disease control. Operability requires multidisciplinary CTEPH-team assessment (surgically accessible proximal/segmental thrombus on CT pulmonary angiography/ventilation-perfusion scan/conventional pulmonary angiography plus adequate cardiopulmonary reserve); real data indicate more than one-third of CTEPH patients are found inoperable at expert-centre workup, for whom BPA (below) is the real fallback.
curative_option.source: Delcroix M et al, Circulation 2024;150(17):1354-1365 (PMID 39286890); Kim NH et al, Eur Respir J 2024 (PMID 39209473); Yang J et al, Chest 2023 (PMID 36990148)
curative_option.confidence: high (real, current international multicentre registry and expert-centre operative data)

alternative.name: Balloon Pulmonary Angioplasty (BPA) for Inoperable or Persistent/Recurrent CTEPH -- Real, Highly Effective Non-Curative Fallback
alternative.note: For CTEPH patients found inoperable, or who have persistent/recurrent pulmonary hypertension after PEA, BPA is a real, catheter-based, staged sequential dilation of the more distal, surgically inaccessible obstructed pulmonary artery segments. It is not curative in the PEA sense (it does not remove disease from a single operation and haemodynamic normalisation is less complete), but real, current international registry data show it is highly effective and very safe when performed at experienced centres.
alternative.source: Lang IM et al, J Am Coll Cardiol 2025 (PMID 40499982) -- International BPA Registry, 484 patients, 18 centres, US/Europe/Japan; Delcroix M et al, Circulation 2024;150(17):1354-1365 (PMID 39286890)
alternative.confidence: high (real, current, multinational registry data including Japan, the country that pioneered BPA)

real_survival_data.mean_PAP_reduction: 15 mmHg (38% reduction) after a median of 5 BPA sessions over 4.9 months
real_survival_data.procedural_30_day_mortality: 0% (no patient died within 30 days of BPA)
real_survival_data.three_year_survival_BPA: 92% (Worldwide CTEPH Registry, 185/1009 patients underwent BPA; Delcroix M et al, Circulation 2024)

curative_option.riociguat_dual_indication_note: Riociguat is the real drug bridging both worlds -- it is FDA/EMA-approved for BOTH inoperable/persistent/recurrent CTEPH (real CHEST-1 trial: Ghofrani HA et al, NEJM 2013;369(4):319-329, PMID 23883377 -- 6-minute walk distance increased a mean 39 m by week 16 vs a decrease with placebo) AND Group 1 PAH (real PATENT-1 trial: Ghofrani HA et al, NEJM 2013;369(4):330-340, PMID 23883378 -- 6-minute walk distance increased a mean 30 m by week 12 in the 2.5mg-maximum titration group), making it the real drug-therapy option for CTEPH patients who are not surgical/BPA candidates or who have residual pulmonary hypertension after intervention -- but it is medical therapy, not a cure.

real_survival_data.operability_rate: Roughly two-thirds operable after multidisciplinary-team workup; 'more than one-third of patients may be considered inoperable' (Yang J et al, Chest 2023, PMID 36990148)
real_survival_data.operative_mortality_expert_centres: Approximately 2% at expert centres (Kim NH et al, Eur Respir J 2024, PMID 39209473; Yang J et al, Chest 2023, PMID 36990148)
real_survival_data.three_year_survival_PEA: 94% (Worldwide CTEPH Registry, 605/1009 patients underwent PEA; Delcroix M et al, Circulation 2024;150(17):1354-1365, PMID 39286890)
real_survival_data.three_year_survival_medical_therapy_alon: 71% (same registry, patients managed with medical therapy alone -- i.e. no PEA/BPA)

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Covers, in order: the real CTEPH (Group 4) cure pathway (PEA, BPA, riociguat) which is fundamentally distinct from Group 1 PAH disease-modifying therapy; the full real Group 1 PAH drug-class landscape with pivotal trial data (endothelin receptor antagonists, PDE5 inhibitors, soluble guanylate cyclase stimulators, prostacyclin pathway agents including the activin signalling inhibitor sotatercept); real upfront combination-therapy evidence; the real 2022 ESC/ERS risk-stratified treat-to-target strategy; real supportive therapy including the evolving anticoagulation evidence; real surgical/device options for end-stage disease (atrial septostomy, lung transplantation); and a real, explicit caution that PAH-specific drugs are not indicated and can be harmful in Group 2/3 PH, where treating the underlying left-heart or lung disease is the real primary approach. Every entry below states the real working solution/recommended action, not just the finding.

medicines.name: Pulmonary Endarterectomy (PEA) -- Real Surgical Cure for Operable CTEPH
medicines.type: Surgical procedure (cardiopulmonary bypass, circulatory arrest, true endarterectomy)
medicines.effectiveness: 3-year survival 94% post-PEA vs 71% with medical therapy alone; operative mortality ~2% at expert centres
medicines.reason_why: CTEPH is caused by organised, endothelialised thromboembolic material physically obstructing proximal/segmental pulmonary arteries, not a diffuse small-vessel arteriopathy; surgically stripping this material out removes the actual cause of the elevated pulmonary pressures, which is why outcomes can approach normalisation rather than just symptom control.
medicines.real_working_solution: Every CTEPH patient must be referred to a high-volume, multidisciplinary CTEPH-team expert centre for operability assessment; if operable, PEA is the real, guideline-endorsed, potentially curative first-line treatment -- not lifelong drug therapy.
medicines.source: Delcroix M et al, Circulation 2024;150(17):1354-1365 (PMID 39286890); Kim NH et al, Eur Respir J 2024 (PMID 39209473); Yang J et al, Chest 2023 (PMID 36990148)
medicines.confidence: high

medicines.name: Balloon Pulmonary Angioplasty (BPA) -- Real Fallback for Inoperable/Persistent/Recurrent CTEPH
medicines.type: Catheter-based procedure (staged sequential balloon dilation of distal pulmonary artery segments)
medicines.effectiveness: mPAP reduced 38%, PVR reduced 57% after median 5 sessions; 0% 30-day procedural mortality; 3-year survival 92%
medicines.reason_why: Distal, surgically inaccessible chronic thromboembolic obstructions can still be mechanically opened with staged balloon dilation performed over multiple sessions to limit reperfusion pulmonary oedema risk per session.
medicines.real_working_solution: For the >1/3 of CTEPH patients found inoperable at expert-centre workup, or those with residual PH after PEA, refer for BPA at an experienced BPA centre rather than defaulting to drug therapy alone.
medicines.source: Lang IM et al, J Am Coll Cardiol 2025 (PMID 40499982); Delcroix M et al, Circulation 2024;150(17):1354-1365 (PMID 39286890)
medicines.confidence: high

medicines.name: Riociguat for CTEPH (Inoperable/Persistent/Recurrent) -- Soluble Guanylate Cyclase Stimulator
medicines.effectiveness: 6-minute walk distance increased mean 39 m by week 16 vs a decrease with placebo (CHEST-1)
medicines.reason_why: Riociguat directly stimulates soluble guanylate cyclase independent of endogenous nitric oxide and also sensitises the enzyme to residual NO, increasing intracellular cGMP and producing pulmonary vasodilation plus antiproliferative effects on vascular smooth muscle.
medicines.real_working_solution: Start riociguat in CTEPH patients who are inoperable, or who have persistent/recurrent PH after PEA/BPA, as the real guideline-approved medical option in this group.
medicines.source: Ghofrani HA et al, NEJM 2013;369(4):319-329 (CHEST-1, PMID 23883377)
medicines.confidence: high

medicines.name: Sotatercept -- Activin Signalling Inhibitor (Add-On, Group 1 PAH)
medicines.type: Subcutaneous biologic (fusion protein ligand trap), add-on to background PAH therapy
medicines.effectiveness: 6-minute walk distance +40.8 m over placebo (95% CI 27.5-54.1, P<0.001); 8 of 9 secondary endpoints significantly favoured sotatercept including PVR and NT-proBNP
medicines.reason_why: Sotatercept traps activin and GDF ligands that signal through the activin receptor type IIA, rebalancing pro- versus anti-proliferative BMPR2/activin signalling that drives the pulmonary vascular smooth-muscle/endothelial proliferation underlying PAH -- a genuinely new, disease-modifying mechanism distinct from all prior PAH drug classes, which only vasodilate.
medicines.real_working_solution: Add sotatercept (Winrevair, FDA-approved March 2024) to background PAH therapy (ERA/PDE5i/prostacyclin-pathway agent) in intermediate-to-high-risk patients per current real-world eligibility criteria, as the newest real disease-modifying option -- not as monotherapy and not as a cure.
medicines.source: Hoeper MM et al, NEJM 2023;388:1478-1490 (STELLAR, PMID 36877098)
medicines.confidence: high

medicines.name: Upfront Combination Therapy -- Endothelin Receptor Antagonist + PDE5 Inhibitor (Ambrisentan + Tadalafil)
medicines.effectiveness: Hazard ratio 0.50 for the primary composite clinical-failure endpoint vs monotherapy (ambrisentan or tadalafil alone)
medicines.reason_why: Combining two distinct disease-specific pathways (endothelin blockade + nitric oxide-cGMP pathway augmentation) from the moment of diagnosis produces additive/synergistic pulmonary vasodilation and antiremodelling effect, rather than waiting for monotherapy to fail before adding a second drug.
medicines.real_working_solution: Start newly diagnosed, treatment-naive Group 1 PAH patients on upfront combination ERA+PDE5i therapy rather than sequential monotherapy, per this real, practice-changing trial -- this is now standard of care for most low/intermediate-risk newly diagnosed patients.
medicines.source: Galiè N et al, NEJM 2015;373(9):834-844 (AMBITION, PMID 26308684)
medicines.confidence: high

medicines.name: Endothelin Receptor Antagonists -- Bosentan, Ambrisentan, Macitentan
medicines.effectiveness: Macitentan 10mg: composite morbidity/mortality event in 31.4% vs 46.4% placebo (HR 0.55, 97.5% CI 0.39-0.76, P<0.001)
medicines.reason_why: Endothelin-1 is a potent pulmonary vasoconstrictor and smooth-muscle mitogen that is upregulated in PAH; blocking ETA (and ETB, for bosentan) receptors reduces vasoconstriction and vascular smooth-muscle proliferation.
medicines.real_working_solution: Macitentan (the ERA with the strongest real morbidity/mortality trial data) or ambrisentan/bosentan as part of upfront or sequential combination therapy, with routine liver-function monitoring for bosentan specifically.
medicines.source: Pulido T et al, NEJM 2013;369:809-818 (SERAPHIN, PMID 23984728)
medicines.confidence: high

medicines.name: PDE5 Inhibitors -- Sildenafil, Tadalafil
medicines.effectiveness: Real, guideline-standard first-line vasodilator class; component of the real AMBITION upfront-combination survival/clinical-failure benefit above (tadalafil arm)
medicines.reason_why: PDE5 inhibitors block breakdown of cGMP generated by the nitric oxide pathway, prolonging pulmonary vascular smooth-muscle relaxation and exerting antiproliferative effects.
medicines.real_working_solution: Use tadalafil (once-daily, real AMBITION combination-trial partner) or sildenafil as the PDE5i backbone of upfront or sequential combination therapy in Group 1 PAH.
medicines.source: Galiè N et al, NEJM 2015;373(9):834-844 (AMBITION, PMID 26308684)
medicines.confidence: high

medicines.name: Riociguat for Group 1 PAH -- Soluble Guanylate Cyclase Stimulator
medicines.effectiveness: 6-minute walk distance increased mean 30 m by week 12 (2.5mg-maximum titration group) vs placebo (PATENT-1)
medicines.reason_why: Same mechanism as in CTEPH -- direct, NO-independent stimulation of soluble guanylate cyclase raising intracellular cGMP -- but here applied to Group 1 PAH's small-vessel arteriopathy.
medicines.real_working_solution: Riociguat is an alternative to PDE5 inhibitors in the nitric oxide-cGMP pathway class for Group 1 PAH (never combine with a PDE5 inhibitor -- real, guideline-flagged hypotension risk from combining two drugs in the same pathway).
medicines.source: Ghofrani HA et al, NEJM 2013;369(4):330-340 (PATENT-1, PMID 23883378)
medicines.confidence: high

medicines.name: Prostacyclin Pathway -- Intravenous Epoprostenol
medicines.type: Continuous IV infusion drug (original/most potent real prostacyclin-pathway agent)
medicines.effectiveness: All 8 deaths in the 12-week trial occurred in the conventional-therapy control group vs 0 in the epoprostenol group (P=0.003); 6-minute walk distance 362 m vs 315 m at baseline; PVR change -21% (epoprostenol) vs +9% (control)
medicines.reason_why: Epoprostenol is a synthetic prostacyclin (PGI2) analogue restoring the vasodilator/antiproliferative/antiplatelet prostacyclin pathway that is deficient relative to thromboxane in PAH; it remains the only PAH drug with a real, classic RCT-level all-cause mortality signal this strong.
medicines.real_working_solution: For high-risk/WHO functional class IV Group 1 PAH patients, IV epoprostenol (via a permanent indwelling catheter and ambulatory infusion pump, requiring careful patient training because abrupt interruption can be fatal from rebound pulmonary hypertension) remains the real most potent first-line option with the strongest real mortality-benefit evidence in the entire PAH drug landscape.
medicines.source: Barst RJ et al, NEJM 1996;334:296-301 (PMID 8532025)
medicines.confidence: high (real, classic landmark RCT, though small by modern standards -- 81 patients)

medicines.name: Prostacyclin Pathway -- Treprostinil (Subcutaneous / IV / Inhaled / Oral)
medicines.type: Drug class, multiple real approved delivery routes of the same prostacyclin analogue molecule
medicines.effectiveness: Median 6-minute walk distance improved with a 16 m between-group difference over placebo (P=0.006) in the pivotal subcutaneous-infusion trial; effect was dose-dependent and greater in more severely ill patients
medicines.reason_why: Treprostinil is a more chemically stable prostacyclin analogue than epoprostenol (longer half-life, room-temperature stable), which real drug development exploited to create SC, IV, inhaled, and oral formulations of the same validated molecule, letting route be matched to disease severity and patient tolerance of continuous infusion/site pain.
medicines.real_working_solution: Use SC treprostinil as a non-central-line alternative to IV epoprostenol in moderate-to-severe PAH (accepting real, common infusion-site pain as the main tolerability tradeoff), or inhaled/oral treprostinil as an add-on in lower-risk patients not requiring continuous parenteral therapy.
medicines.source: Simonneau G et al, Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2002;165(6):800-804 (PMID 11897647)
medicines.confidence: high on the pivotal SC formulation; moderate on inhaled/oral route-specific effect sizes (real approved formulations of the same molecule, but this survey did not independently re-verify a separate pivotal trial citation for each route in this session)

medicines.name: Prostacyclin Pathway -- Selexipag (Oral, Non-Prostanoid IP Receptor Agonist)
medicines.effectiveness: Real, significant reduction in risk of the composite primary endpoint (death or a PAH-related complication) vs placebo in 1,156 patients (GRIPHON)
medicines.reason_why: Selexipag is chemically distinct from prostacyclin itself but selectively agonises the same IP prostacyclin receptor, giving prostacyclin-pathway vasodilation/antiproliferative benefit via a convenient twice-daily oral tablet rather than continuous infusion or inhalation.
medicines.real_working_solution: Add oral selexipag as the prostacyclin-pathway component of combination therapy in patients for whom continuous parenteral/inhaled prostanoid delivery is not desired or not yet indicated by risk status.
medicines.source: Sitbon O et al, NEJM 2015;373(26):2522-2533 (GRIPHON, PMID 26699168)
medicines.confidence: high

medicines.name: Risk-Stratified Treat-to-Target Strategy (2022 ESC/ERS Guidelines)
medicines.type: Guideline-based clinical strategy, not a single drug
medicines.effectiveness: Real, current European Society of Cardiology/European Respiratory Society guideline strategy mapping validated risk-stratification tools (e.g. REVEAL 2.0/ESC-ERS 4-strata model) to treatment intensity at every follow-up visit
medicines.reason_why: PAH risk (1-year mortality risk) is determined by a combination of WHO functional class, 6-minute walk distance, NT-proBNP/BNP, and haemodynamics; matching drug-therapy intensity (monotherapy vs dual vs triple, oral vs parenteral prostacyclin) to real measured risk at diagnosis AND at every reassessment, rather than treating to a fixed regimen, is the real current standard of care.
medicines.real_working_solution: Formally risk-stratify every PAH patient at diagnosis and at each follow-up visit; low-risk patients are treated with (typically) upfront oral combination therapy, while intermediate/high-risk patients are escalated to triple therapy including a parenteral/inhaled prostacyclin-pathway agent (or now sotatercept) without delay -- treating to a target of low-risk status, not just symptom improvement.
medicines.source: Humbert M et al, Eur Heart J 2022;43(38):3618-3731 (2022 ESC/ERS PH Guidelines, PMID 36017548)
medicines.confidence: high

medicines.name: Supportive Therapy -- Oxygen, Diuretics, and the Evolving Anticoagulation Question
medicines.effectiveness: Not a disease-modifying effectiveness percentage -- real, standard supportive care for hypoxaemia and right heart failure congestion; anticoagulation's role has genuinely narrowed over time
medicines.reason_why: Supplemental oxygen corrects hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction; loop diuretics relieve right heart failure-driven systemic venous congestion (ascites, leg oedema, hepatic congestion) that is a major real source of PAH morbidity independent of pulmonary pressure itself; anticoagulation was historically extrapolated from small, mostly non-randomised, older idiopathic-PAH cohorts suggesting a survival benefit, but real contemporary evidence (including outcomes in the SERAPHIN, GRIPHON and other modern PAH-drug RCT cohorts and subsequent observational analyses) has not consistently reproduced that benefit and has raised real bleeding-risk concerns, particularly in non-idiopathic (e.g. connective-tissue-disease-associated, portopulmonary) PAH.
medicines.real_working_solution: Give supplemental oxygen to keep SpO2 >=90-92% and loop diuretics titrated to euvolaemia in all symptomatic PAH patients as real, low-risk supportive measures; do NOT anticoagulate routinely across all PAH aetiologies as older practice did -- reserve anticoagulation for idiopathic/heritable PAH on an individualised bleeding-risk basis per current guideline stance, and avoid it in non-idiopathic PAH subtypes where the risk-benefit is real and unfavourable.
medicines.source: Humbert M et al, Eur Heart J 2022;43(38):3618-3731 (2022 ESC/ERS PH Guidelines, PMID 36017548)
medicines.confidence: moderate on the anticoagulation-narrowing evidence specifically (real guideline-level shift in stance, cited to the guideline itself rather than to one dedicated anticoagulation RCT, because no adequately powered RCT of anticoagulation in PAH exists)

medicines.name: Atrial Septostomy / Atrial Flow Regulator -- Palliative Bridge for End-Stage PAH
medicines.type: Catheter-based procedure (creates or regulates a right-to-left atrial shunt)
medicines.effectiveness: Real but honestly poor-prognosis population: in a real prospective device study of a novel atrial flow regulator, 9 of 25 severe PAH patients died and 3 underwent lung transplantation within 1-year follow-up (36% mortality), alongside improved RV function/cardiac performance in survivors
medicines.reason_why: Creating a controlled right-to-left interatrial shunt decompresses a failing right ventricle at the cost of some arterial desaturation, improving systemic cardiac output in patients whose right heart failure (not hypoxaemia) is the dominant threat to life -- a real haemodynamic tradeoff, not free improvement.
medicines.real_working_solution: Reserve atrial septostomy/atrial flow regulator placement as a real palliative bridge to lung transplantation, or for recurrent syncope/refractory right heart failure despite maximal drug therapy, at a centre experienced in the procedure -- understanding real mortality in this population remains high regardless, because it reflects end-stage disease rather than a fixable complication.
medicines.source: Bartunek J et al, J Soc Cardiovasc Angiogr Interv 2026 (AFR-Prophet study, PMID 42183131); Dong M et al, Eur J Med Res 2025 (PMID 40604947)
medicines.confidence: moderate (real but small device study, n=25; classic balloon/blade atrial septostomy has a longer real track record described qualitatively in the cited review but without an independently re-verified pooled mortality figure in this session)

medicines.name: Lung Transplantation -- Real Definitive Option for End-Stage PAH
medicines.type: Surgical procedure (bilateral, or heart-lung for selected complex congenital PAH)
medicines.effectiveness: Real, internationally tracked outcome in a dedicated registry of 67,493 adult lung transplant recipients (1992-2018); this survey could not independently re-verify a specific PAH-stratified 1-year/5-year survival percentage from the registry abstract text in this research session
medicines.reason_why: Transplantation replaces the entire diseased pulmonary vascular bed, removing the anatomical substrate of PAH entirely -- the only intervention in Group 1 PAH that is curative of the pulmonary vascular disease itself, at the real cost of trading it for chronic transplant-related disease (rejection, infection, immunosuppression, chronic lung allograft dysfunction).
medicines.real_working_solution: Refer patients for lung transplant evaluation once they remain high-risk despite maximal combination drug therapy (including parenteral prostacyclin-pathway therapy/sotatercept) -- do not wait until they are too sick to be listed; this is real, guideline-endorsed practice, and pulmonary vascular disease is now reported as a leading indication for heart-lung transplantation specifically.
medicines.source: Chambers DC et al, J Heart Lung Transplant 2021;40(10):1060-1072 (ISHLT/ITOTR 38th Adult Lung Transplantation Report, PMID 34446355); Gottlieb J et al, JHLT Open 2025 (PMID 41216317)
medicines.confidence: moderate (real registry and its real cohort size confirmed; a precise PAH-specific survival percentage was not extracted from an accessible abstract in this session, so none is stated here to avoid fabrication)

medicines.name: CAUTION: PAH-Specific Drugs Are Generally NOT Indicated and Can Be Harmful in Group 2/3 PH
medicines.type: Guideline-level safety caution, not a treatment
medicines.effectiveness: Real, documented HARM signal when a PAH-class drug (ambrisentan, an ERA) was trialled in a lung-disease population with pulmonary hypertension: disease progression in 27.4% vs 17.2% placebo (P=0.010) and respiratory hospitalisation in 13.4% vs 5.5% placebo (P=0.007), leading to early trial termination
medicines.reason_why: In Group 2 PH (left heart disease) and Group 3 PH (chronic lung disease/hypoxia), pulmonary hypertension is usually a downstream consequence of impaired ventilation-perfusion matching or elevated left-sided filling pressures rather than a primary pulmonary vascular arteriopathy; PAH-specific vasodilators can worsen ventilation-perfusion mismatch (redirecting blood flow to poorly ventilated lung units) or precipitate pulmonary oedema/systemic hypotension by increasing pulmonary blood flow into an already congested left heart.
medicines.real_working_solution: In Group 2/3 PH, the real primary approach is treating the underlying left heart disease (see congestive_heart_failure, mitral_regurgitation, aortic_stenosis entries) or lung disease (COPD/ILD management) -- do NOT reach for ERAs/PDE5i/prostacyclin-pathway drugs/sotatercept as first-line therapy in these groups outside of specialist, case-by-case exceptions, because real trial evidence in an analogous lung-disease population showed harm, not benefit.
medicines.source: Raghu G et al, Ann Intern Med 2013;158(9):641-649 (ARTEMIS-IPF, PMID 23648946); Humbert M et al, Eur Heart J 2022;43(38):3618-3731 (2022 ESC/ERS PH Guidelines, PMID 36017548)
medicines.confidence: high on the ARTEMIS-IPF harm signal itself (real RCT, stopped early); high on the guideline-level caution being real and current

medicines.name: Medical Equipment/Devices -- Prostacyclin Delivery Pump Systems and BPA Catheter Systems
medicines.type: Medical device category (drug-delivery hardware and interventional catheter systems)
medicines.effectiveness: Not a drug-effectiveness percentage -- real, clinically essential enabling technology without which IV/SC prostanoid therapy and BPA could not be delivered at all
medicines.reason_why: IV epoprostenol requires a dedicated ambulatory infusion pump connected to a permanent tunnelled central venous catheter, with cold-chain/ice-pack handling because epoprostenol is unstable at room temperature and interruption risks fatal rebound pulmonary hypertension; SC treprostinil uses a smaller ambulatory microinfusion pump with a subcutaneous cannula; BPA requires dedicated small-diameter coronary-style balloon catheters, guidewires, and fluoroscopic/optical coherence tomography or intravascular ultrasound guidance systems adapted for the pulmonary arterial tree to avoid reperfusion pulmonary injury.
medicines.real_working_solution: Ensure any PAH patient started on IV/SC prostanoid therapy is trained by a specialist PH centre on pump/catheter care and has a clear rescue protocol for pump/line failure before discharge; ensure BPA is performed only at centres with the specific catheter/imaging equipment and staged-session protocols shown safe in the real International BPA Registry data above, not as an ad hoc extension of routine coronary angioplasty skillsets.
medicines.source: Barst RJ et al, NEJM 1996;334:296-301 (PMID 8532025); Simonneau G et al, Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2002;165(6):800-804 (PMID 11897647); Lang IM et al, J Am Coll Cardiol 2025 (PMID 40499982)
medicines.confidence: high on the real necessity/nature of the equipment; this is a device-category description drawn from the same pivotal trials/registry above rather than a separate device trial

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These are real, differently-defined outcome metrics (real-world/expert-centre operative survival, registry 3-year survival, procedural safety/haemodynamic change, classic RCT mortality signal, RCT hazard ratios, 6-minute-walk-distance trial deltas, and a real documented harm signal) placed on one comparative scale -- not equivalent statistics, and NOT a claim that any single number captures 'how good' each option is. CTEPH's PEA/BPA cure-and-near-cure pathway is ranked at the top and is explicitly a DIFFERENT disease process (Group 4, thromboembolic obstruction) from Group 1 PAH's disease-modifying-but-not-curative drug therapies ranked below it -- do not read this table as saying PAH drugs are 'worse than' PEA for PAH patients; PEA is not an option for Group 1 PAH at all. The Group 2/3 caution entry is ranked at the bottom with a HARM percentage, not an efficacy percentage, and is included specifically as a warning, not a treatment option.
