ventricular_arrhythmia_scd.name: Ventricular Arrhythmias and Sudden Cardiac Death (VT/VF and the Inherited Channelopathies: Long QT Syndrome, Brugada Syndrome, CPVT)
ventricular_arrhythmia_scd.icd11_hint: ICD-11 MMS codes for this entry could not be independently verified against the live WHO ICD-11 browser in this research session (verified real ICD-10-CM equivalents used instead): I47.2 (Ventricular tachycardia), I49.0 (Ventricular fibrillation and flutter; I49.01 VF, I49.02 VFlutter), I46.2/I46.8/I46.9 (Cardiac arrest due to underlying cardiac condition / other underlying condition / unspecified), I45.81 (Long QT syndrome), I42.8 (Other cardiomyopathies - the code conventionally used for Brugada syndrome in the absence of a dedicated ICD-10-CM code). CPVT has no dedicated ICD-10-CM code and is typically captured under I47.2 or R94.31 (abnormal ECG) plus the causative RYR2/CASQ2 genetic finding - stated directly rather than inventing a code.
ventricular_arrhythmia_scd.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE: Sudden cardiac arrest from pulseless ventricular tachycardia or ventricular fibrillation is the ultimate real cardiac emergency and MUST trigger immediate emergency response (call emergency services, start CPR, use an AED the moment one is available) - there is no doctor-approval gate that applies here, this is a call-emergency-services-now pattern, not a consult-first pattern. Real, sobering survival data: overall survival to hospital discharge after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) is only approximately 10% globally (Yan et al., Critical Care 2020;24:61, systematic review/meta-analysis), and bystander CPR is performed in fewer than 30% of OHCA cases despite being one of the few interventions proven to improve survival - dispatcher-assisted bystander CPR has been shown in meta-analysis to improve survival compared with undirected bystander CPR (2019 meta-analysis, cited in AHA-aligned resuscitation literature). In-hospital cardiac arrest survival to discharge is meaningfully higher, approximately 22% (Kronick et al., Circulation 2015;132(18 Suppl 2):S397, 2015 AHA Guidelines Update Part 4: Systems of Care). This entry additionally covers new unexplained syncope during exercise/swimming, syncope with fever, or a family history of unexplained sudden death under 40 years of age as real red-flag patterns requiring urgent cardiology/electrophysiology referral even without a witnessed arrest - these patterns identify people who may have LQTS, Brugada syndrome, or CPVT before their first, potentially fatal, arrhythmic event.

symptoms.core_note: This entry covers ventricular tachycardia (VT), ventricular fibrillation (VF), and sudden cardiac death (SCD) as a primary ELECTRICAL/ARRHYTHMIC disease process, plus the major real inherited channelopathies that cause SCD in structurally normal hearts (Long QT Syndrome, Brugada Syndrome, CPVT). It deliberately does NOT duplicate the SCD risk-stratification content already documented for structural diseases elsewhere in this knowledge base - see hypertrophic_cardiomyopathy for the HCM Risk-SCD model and dilated_cardiomyopathy for the LMNA-risk VTA calculator; those entries cover SCD risk specific to their structural substrate. This entry covers VT/VF as a general arrhythmic syndrome across all substrates, plus the channelopathies as a distinct primary-electrical category.

real_classification.note: Real definitions used clinically and in the governing US guideline for this disease group.

by_duration.sustained_VT: VT lasting >30 seconds, OR requiring termination sooner because of haemodynamic compromise (hypotension, syncope, near-syncope).
by_duration.nonsustained_VT_NSVT: 3 or more consecutive ventricular beats at a rate >100/min, self-terminating within 30 seconds, without haemodynamic compromise.
by_duration.source: 2017 AHA/ACC/HRS Guideline for Management of Patients With Ventricular Arrhythmias and the Prevention of Sudden Cardiac Death (Circulation 2018;138(13):e272-e391)

by_morphology.monomorphic_VT: Every QRS complex has the same shape on a given ECG lead, reflecting a single, stable reentry circuit or focus - usually arising from a fixed anatomical substrate such as post-myocardial-infarction scar.
by_morphology.polymorphic_VT: Beat-to-beat variation in QRS morphology/axis, reflecting a less stable or multifocal electrical substrate - more often linked to acute ischaemia, electrolyte derangement, or a channelopathy (e.g. torsades de pointes in LQTS is a specific polymorphic VT with a twisting-around-the-baseline pattern).
by_morphology.ventricular_fibrillation_VF: Chaotic, disorganised ventricular electrical activity with no discernible QRS complexes and no effective mechanical contraction - haemodynamically equivalent to cardiac arrest and fatal within minutes without defibrillation.
by_morphology.source: 2017 AHA/ACC/HRS VA/SCD Guideline (Circulation 2018;138(13):e272-e391); standard cardiac electrophysiology classification

structural_substrate_categories.note: The majority of sustained monomorphic VT in adults arises on a structural scar substrate, not a primary channelopathy - this entry cross-references rather than re-documents the structural diseases themselves.

post_MI_scar_VT.data: Scarring from prior myocardial infarction alters normal ventricular conduction pathways and creates the fixed reentry substrate that is the most common cause of monomorphic VT in adults with structural heart disease. See ischaemic_heart_disease in this knowledge base for the acute coronary event itself; this entry covers the chronic post-infarct scar as an arrhythmic substrate, a distinct downstream consequence.
post_MI_scar_VT.confidence: moderate - qualitative mechanism is well established; a single precise pooled percentage of 'all VT' attributable to post-MI scar could not be verified with a real citation in this research session and is therefore not stated as a number
post_MI_scar_VT.source: Standard MI complications literature (see Wikipedia Myocardial infarction, 'Complications' section, for the qualitative mechanism); mechanism corroborated by 2017 AHA/ACC/HRS VA/SCD Guideline

nonischemic_cardiomyopathy_VT.data: Nonischemic dilated cardiomyopathy is also a real, distinct arrhythmic substrate, with genotype-specific malignant-arrhythmia risk (notably LMNA- and RBM20-related DCM) that can occur even at only mildly reduced ejection fraction. See dilated_cardiomyopathy in this knowledge base for the full LMNA-risk VTA calculator and genotype-specific detail - not duplicated here.
nonischemic_cardiomyopathy_VT.source: Cross-reference to dilated_cardiomyopathy entry in this knowledge base; JACC 2022;80(6):543 (LMNA risk model)

arvc.name: Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy/Dysplasia (ARVC/D)
arvc.data: A real, distinct structural arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (fibrofatty replacement of ventricular myocardium, classically right ventricular) that merits its own diagnostic-criteria mention because it is a leading cause of SCD in young people and athletes in some populations. Diagnosis uses the 2010 revised Task Force Criteria across five domains - right ventricular structural/functional abnormality, tissue characterisation (fibrofatty replacement on biopsy), ECG repolarisation abnormalities, ECG depolarisation/conduction abnormalities, ventricular arrhythmia pattern, and family history/genetics - with a definite diagnosis requiring 2 major criteria, or 1 major + 2 minor criteria, or 4 minor criteria.
arvc.epidemiology: Estimated general-population prevalence approximately 1 in 1,000 to 1 in 10,000 depending on population studied; reported to account for up to 17% of sudden cardiac deaths in the young in some US series, and is reported as the leading cause of SCD in the young in parts of Italy (prevalence estimates as high as 40 per 10,000 in some Italian series) and in Newfoundland (Canada), reflecting real geographic/founder-mutation clustering rather than a uniform global rate. Predominantly affects males; 30-50% of cases are familial.
arvc.confidence: high for the diagnostic framework and directionality of the epidemiology; the specific prevalence figures vary meaningfully by population/country and are cited as reported, not as one universal global rate
arvc.source: Marcus FI, McKenna WJ, Sherrill D, et al. 'Diagnosis of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy/dysplasia: proposed modification of the task force criteria.' Circulation. 2010;121(13):1533-1541 (the real 2010 Task Force Criteria)

primary_electrical_disease_channelopathi.note: These are real, genetically-determined arrhythmia syndromes that occur in structurally NORMAL hearts - the defect is in cardiac ion-channel or calcium-handling proteins, not in the heart's anatomy. They are the dominant real explanation for SCD in children/young adults without structural heart disease and are the reason cascade family screening matters.

genotype_specific_triggers.LQT1_KCNQ1: Most common subtype, accounting for roughly 30-35% of all genotyped LQTS cases; classic trigger is exercise, especially SWIMMING.
genotype_specific_triggers.LQT2_KCNH2_hERG: Second most common subtype, roughly 25-30% of cases; classic trigger is a sudden loud noise/auditory stimulus (e.g. an alarm clock or phone ringing) or acute emotional stress.
genotype_specific_triggers.LQT3_SCN5A: Classic trigger is SLEEP or rest, with events occurring at low heart rates rather than during exertion - a real, clinically important genotype-phenotype distinction because these patients are relatively LESS protected by exercise restriction alone.
genotype_specific_triggers.source: Bohnen MS et al., Physiological Reviews 2017 (LQT1/LQT2 percentages); Tester DJ, Ackerman MJ, in 'Electrical Diseases of the Heart' 2013 (LQT3 sleep/rest trigger pattern)

qtc_diagnostic_cutoffs.data: A QTc <450 ms covers 95% of normal males and <460 ms covers 95% of normal females; more stringent 99th-percentile cutoffs of approximately 470 ms (men) and 480 ms (women) are also used. A markedly prolonged QTc (>=480ms) is itself a major Schwartz-score criterion (see below).
qtc_diagnostic_cutoffs.source: Giudicessi JR, Ackerman MJ, Current Problems in Cardiology 2013 (QTc normal-range cutoffs)

schwartz_lqts_diagnostic_score.data: A validated composite score combining ECG findings, clinical history, and family history. Representative point values include: QTc >=480 ms = 3 points; QTc 460-470 ms = 2 points; documented torsades de pointes = 2 points; syncope occurring WITH stress/exercise = 2 points; T-wave alternans = 1 point (the full score also incorporates additional ECG findings such as notched T-waves and low resting heart rate for age, syncope without stress, congenital deafness, and family history of LQTS or unexplained sudden death under 30 in an immediate family member, which were not independently re-verified with exact point values in this research session and are therefore described qualitatively rather than numerically here). A total score of >=4 points indicates a high probability of LQTS.
schwartz_lqts_diagnostic_score.confidence: high for the cited point values and threshold; the additional qualitative criteria are real but their exact point weightings were not independently re-verified this session
schwartz_lqts_diagnostic_score.source: Schwartz PJ, Moss AJ, Vincent GM, Crampton RS. 'Diagnostic criteria for the long QT syndrome. An update.' Circulation. 1993;88(2):782-784

epidemiology.data: Estimated prevalence approximately 1 in 2,500 to 1 in 7,000 people, causing an estimated ~3,500 deaths per year in the US when unrecognised/untreated.
epidemiology.confidence: moderate - range reflects genuine variation across cited sources rather than a single precise figure
epidemiology.source: NIH/NHLBI 2017 fact sheet; Levine E et al., Cleveland Clinic Journal of Medicine 2008

ecg_diagnostic_criteria.data: The diagnostic Type 1 Brugada ECG pattern is a coved-type ST-segment elevation of >=2 mm in at least one of leads V1-V2 (placed in a standard or superior intercostal position), followed by a gradually descending ST segment and a negative T-wave. This Type 1 pattern, when present spontaneously or unmasked by a sodium-channel blocker challenge (e.g. ajmaline/flecainide) together with clinical criteria (documented VF/polymorphic VT, family history of SCD <45y, coved-type ECGs in family members, syncope, or nocturnal agonal respiration), establishes the diagnosis.
ecg_diagnostic_criteria.source: Bayes de Luna A et al., 'Current electrocardiographic criteria for diagnosis of Brugada pattern: a consensus report,' Journal of Electrocardiology 2012;45(5):433-442

epidemiology.data: Estimated prevalence approximately 2-5 per 10,000 people overall, but real, well-documented geographic and ethnic clustering: substantially more prevalent in individuals of Southeast Asian descent, and it is reported as the most common cause of sudden death in young males without known structural heart disease in Thailand and Laos. It is 8-10 times more common in clinically diagnosed men than women (this male excess is NOT present in pediatric cases, and is attributed to post-pubertal testosterone/sex-specific ionic-current differences). Average age at diagnosis is approximately 41 years. Brugada syndrome is estimated to account for 4-12% of all sudden cardiac deaths and up to 20% of sudden deaths in patients without structural heart disease.
epidemiology.source: Shukla K, Basile EJ, Van Name JP, Ahmed I. 'Brugada Syndrome.' StatPearls, StatPearls Publishing, updated 2025; Polovina MM et al., European Journal of Internal Medicine 2017;44:19-27

genetics.data: SCN5A (cardiac sodium channel gene) mutations are identified in only an estimated 15-30% of clinically diagnosed Brugada syndrome cases, despite it being the most extensively studied and most definitively-linked gene; roughly 19 genes have been implicated overall, meaning the majority of clinically diagnosed cases remain genotype-negative on current panels.
genetics.source: Shukla K et al., 'Brugada Syndrome,' StatPearls, updated 2025; Kapplinger JD et al., Heart Rhythm 2010;7(1):33-46

fever_as_trigger.data: Fever is a real, clinically important unmasking/precipitating trigger for the Brugada ECG pattern and for arrhythmic events in Brugada syndrome - elevated core body temperature can unmask a previously concealed Type 1 pattern and precipitate VF, which is why an otherwise unexplained febrile-illness-associated syncope or cardiac arrest should prompt Brugada workup.
fever_as_trigger.source: Shukla K et al., 'Brugada Syndrome,' StatPearls, updated 2025; Sarquella-Brugada G et al., Genetics in Medicine 2016;18(1):3-12

genetics.data: The majority of identified CPVT cases (CPVT1) are caused by mutations in RYR2, encoding the cardiac ryanodine receptor, which causes abnormal/leaky sarcoplasmic-reticulum calcium release under catecholamine stimulation. A minority (CASQ2 mutations, CPVT2) account for only an estimated 3-5% of cases and follow autosomal recessive inheritance. A precise overall percentage for RYR2-positive cases specifically (as opposed to 'most common') could not be independently verified with a real citation in this research session and is therefore not stated as an exact number; genetic testing in patients presenting later in life frequently fails to identify a causative gene.
genetics.confidence: high for the qualitative genotype hierarchy and CASQ2 percentage; RYR2 exact percentage omitted as unverified
genetics.source: Priori SG et al., Circulation Research 2011 (RYR2 mechanism); real prevalence/genetics summary corroborated in standard channelopathy literature

clinical_pattern.data: Classic presentation is exercise- or acute-emotion-triggered syncope or cardiac arrest in a child or young adult with a structurally and electrically NORMAL resting ECG (normal QTc). The pathognomonic (though not always seen) arrhythmia is bidirectional ventricular tachycardia - a polymorphic VT with a beat-to-beat alternating QRS axis. Estimated prevalence is approximately 1 in 10,000 people, and CPVT is estimated to underlie approximately 15% of unexplained sudden cardiac deaths in young people. More than 60% of affected individuals experience their first syncope or cardiac arrest episode by age 20, and untreated patients have a reported 13-20% risk of a life-threatening arrhythmic event over 7-8 years of follow-up.
clinical_pattern.source: Standard CPVT clinical literature; Priori SG et al. and related channelopathy reviews (RYR2/CASQ2 CPVT characterisation)

idiopathic_vf.name: Idiopathic Ventricular Fibrillation
idiopathic_vf.data: A real diagnosis of exclusion applied when VF/cardiac arrest occurs with no identifiable structural heart disease, no diagnostic channelopathy pattern, and no reversible precipitant found after a complete real workup (echocardiography, coronary assessment, provocative drug-challenge ECG testing, and genetic testing). Historically estimated to account for approximately 1% of all out-of-hospital cardiac arrests, 3-9% of VF cases unrelated to myocardial infarction, and up to 14% of VF resuscitations in patients under age 40 - i.e. a real, disproportionately young-skewed entity, though modern more complete channelopathy/genetic workups reclassify some of these cases over time.
idiopathic_vf.confidence: high for the historical proportions cited; note this is an older foundational dataset and modern reclassification rates with contemporary genetic testing were not independently re-verified in this session
idiopathic_vf.source: Viskin S, Belhassen B, American Heart Journal 1990 (foundational idiopathic VF epidemiology, as cited in standard VF literature)

clinical_presentation.palpitations: A common but nonspecific presenting symptom of both benign and life-threatening ventricular arrhythmia; palpitations immediately preceding a syncopal episode is itself a real red flag for an arrhythmic (rather than vasovagal) cause.

presyncope_syncope_red_flags.data: Real clinical features that should raise suspicion for arrhythmic/cardiac syncope rather than benign vasovagal (reflex) syncope include: syncope during exertion or while supine (vasovagal syncope is typically upright/positional and provoked by prolonged standing, heat, pain, or emotional triggers), absence of a typical vasovagal prodrome (light-headedness, nausea, pallor, sweating, blurred vision building gradually), syncope preceded by palpitations, an abnormal resting ECG (long QTc, Brugada pattern, bundle branch block, etc.), age over 35 at first episode, and a personal history of structural heart disease or atrial fibrillation. Family history of unexplained sudden death is an additional, separate real red flag for an inherited arrhythmia syndrome specifically.
presyncope_syncope_red_flags.confidence: moderate-high - directionally well-established clinical teaching corroborated across sources, though the specific consolidated red-flag list here is drawn from general syncope risk-stratification literature rather than one single quoted guideline table verified line-by-line this session
presyncope_syncope_red_flags.source: Peeples SY et al., Emergency Medicine Practice 2014 (cardiac syncope risk stratification); corroborated by standard syncope literature referencing ECG findings (long QT, Brugada pattern) as the specific arrhythmic red flags relevant to this entry

sudden_cardiac_arrest_as_first_presentat.data: A real, sobering fact central to this disease group: cardiac arrest is NOT preceded by any warning symptoms in approximately 50% of people - i.e. sudden cardiac death is the first clinical manifestation of underlying heart disease in about half of cases, which is precisely why population/family screening (rather than waiting for symptoms) matters for known channelopathy families and why any of the specific red flags in this entry (exertional syncope, febrile syncope, family history) must be taken seriously even in an otherwise asymptomatic person.
sudden_cardiac_arrest_as_first_presentat.source: Standard sudden cardiac death epidemiology literature (cardiac arrest asymptomatic-first-presentation proportion, ~50%)

overall_incidence.data: Approximately 535,000 cardiac arrests occur annually in the US (roughly 13 per 10,000 people per year) per the 2015 AHA Guidelines Update; of these, about 61% (326,000) occur out-of-hospital and about 39% (209,000) occur in-hospital.
overall_incidence.source: Kronick SL et al., 'Part 4: Systems of Care and Continuous Quality Improvement,' 2015 AHA Guidelines Update for CPR and ECC, Circulation 2015;132(18 Suppl 2):S397

attribution_by_cause_and_age.data: Coronary artery disease underlies an estimated 68% of sudden cardiac deaths in the US overall, but this proportion is real and age-dependent: CAD is a substantially LESS common cause of SCD in people under 40. In people under 30, structural heart disease other than CAD (cardiomyopathies, congenital coronary anomalies) accounts for over 30% of sudden cardiac arrests, non-atherosclerotic coronary abnormalities account for an estimated 10-15% of cardiac arrest/SCD, and inherited primary electrical disease/channelopathies (LQTS, Brugada, CPVT) account for an estimated 5-10% of sudden cardiac arrests overall - a proportion that is real and CONCENTRATED disproportionately among younger victims, consistent with US young-athlete/young-sudden-death autopsy series in which hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (~26%), coronary anomalies (~14%), and ARVC (~3%) predominate structurally, while roughly 20% of cases remain 'autopsy-negative' after full pathological workup - a subgroup in which an underlying channelopathy (undetectable at autopsy because there is no structural abnormality) is the leading suspected explanation.
attribution_by_cause_and_age.confidence: high for the directional age-pattern (channelopathies proportionally more important in the young); the specific percentages are drawn from a US-population evidence base and should not be read as precise global figures
attribution_by_cause_and_age.source: Standard SCD epidemiology literature citing CAD/structural/electrical attribution by age; young-athlete/young-sudden-death autopsy series (387 US deaths under 35) cited in standard sports-cardiology sudden death literature

chain_of_survival_and_ohca_outcomes.data: Overall survival to hospital discharge after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) is only approximately 10% globally, with meaningful geographic variation - relatively lower survival in some Asian-country series and higher survival in parts of Europe/North America, and survival at home alone (unwitnessed, no immediate responder) is as low as roughly 6%. Survival is substantially and consistently HIGHER when the arrest is witnessed and bystander CPR is initiated. Bystander CPR is nonetheless performed in fewer than 30% of OHCA cases, representing a real, large, and actionable survival gap - dispatcher-assisted ('telephone') CPR has been shown in meta-analysis to further improve outcomes compared with undirected bystander CPR, and early AED use for a shockable rhythm (VF/pulseless VT) is one of the few interventions proven to improve OHCA survival. In-hospital cardiac arrest survival to discharge is meaningfully higher, at approximately 22%, reflecting the effect of immediate witnessed response and monitoring.
chain_of_survival_and_ohca_outcomes.source: Yan S et al., 'The global survival rate among adult out-of-hospital cardiac arrest patients who received cardiopulmonary resuscitation: a systematic review and meta-analysis,' Critical Care 2020;24:61; Kronick SL et al., 2015 AHA Guidelines Update Part 4, Circulation 2015;132(18 Suppl 2):S397

real_risk_factors.name: Family history of SCD or a known channelopathy
real_risk_factors.note: A real, guideline-important risk factor specifically because inherited channelopathies (LQTS, Brugada, CPVT) are autosomal-dominant in the majority of cases - a first-degree relative of a person with a diagnosed channelopathy or of a young (<40-45y) unexplained sudden death has a real, actionable indication for CASCADE genetic/clinical screening (ECG +/- genetic testing) even if currently asymptomatic, because up to half of eventual sudden deaths in these families are first presentations.
real_risk_factors.confidence: high
real_risk_factors.source: HRS/EHRA/APHRS-aligned cascade-screening principle for inherited arrhythmia syndromes; corroborated across channelopathy literature cited elsewhere in this entry

real_risk_factors.name: Structural heart disease with reduced ejection fraction
real_risk_factors.note: The single largest population-level risk factor for SCD via scar-related monomorphic VT/VF, chiefly from prior MI - see ischaemic_heart_disease and congestive_heart_failure in this knowledge base for the EF-based risk detail (this entry does not duplicate that content).

real_risk_factors.name: Drug-induced QT prolongation
real_risk_factors.note: A real, common, and often overlooked ACQUIRED cause of torsades de pointes/polymorphic VT, especially when combined with a subclinical genetic QT-prolongation predisposition, bradycardia, or hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia. Clinically, risk is assessed using a maintained public list-based approach (e.g. the CredibleMeds database, www.crediblemeds.org, maintained by AZCERT) which categorises drugs by real, evidence-graded risk of Torsades de Pointes (Known Risk, Possible Risk, Conditional Risk, Special Risk categories) and is the real reference tool clinicians and LQTS patients are advised to consult before starting a new QT-prolonging medication.
real_risk_factors.confidence: high
real_risk_factors.source: CredibleMeds (AZCERT) QT-drug risk categorisation, referenced in standard LQTS management literature

real_risk_factors.name: Electrolyte abnormalities (hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia)
real_risk_factors.note: Both lower the arrhythmic threshold and are common, correctable precipitants of polymorphic VT/torsades, particularly in combination with QT-prolonging drugs or an underlying channelopathy.

real_risk_factors.name: Illicit drug use
real_risk_factors.note: Sympathomimetic drugs (cocaine, methamphetamine) and certain other illicit substances are real, recognised precipitants of both acute coronary ischaemia and direct pro-arrhythmic effects (some also prolong QT), contributing to SCD risk independent of pre-existing structural or electrical disease.

real_risk_factors.name: Competitive athletics in an undiagnosed channelopathy or cardiomyopathy carrier
real_risk_factors.note: Real, well-documented risk pattern: exercise is a direct trigger for LQT1 and CPVT events specifically, and vigorous exertion is a recognised precipitant of SCD in undiagnosed HCM/ARVC. Pre-participation screening (history, examination, ECG in some protocols) aims to catch these carriers before a first, potentially fatal, event, though real pilot data (e.g. a Texas youth-athlete screening pilot of ~2,500 athletes) show meaningful false-positive rates alongside genuine case detection, and exertional syncope/near-syncope is flagged as the single most important symptom warranting detailed cardiac evaluation before return to sport.
real_risk_factors.confidence: moderate-high
real_risk_factors.source: Sports-cardiology sudden-death-in-athletes literature; corroborated by LQTS/CPVT genotype-specific exercise-trigger data cited above

diagnostic_tools.resting_12_lead_ecg: First-line, essential test - measures QTc (LQTS), looks for a spontaneous Type 1 Brugada pattern, and can show conduction abnormalities or prior-MI Q-waves relevant to structural VT risk. A completely normal resting ECG does NOT exclude CPVT (diagnosed on exercise/catecholamine challenge) or a concealed Brugada pattern (may need a sodium-channel-blocker drug challenge to unmask).
diagnostic_tools.exercise_stress_testing: Can unmask CPVT (bidirectional/polymorphic VT emerging with exercise-driven catecholamine surge) and can unmask or worsen QT-related abnormalities in LQT1 specifically, making it a real, targeted diagnostic tool for these two genotype/syndrome patterns rather than a generic screening test for all channelopathies.
diagnostic_tools.signal_averaged_ecg: Detects late potentials (low-amplitude signals at the end of the QRS reflecting delayed, fragmented ventricular conduction through diseased/scarred myocardium) and is used as an ancillary tool in the structural arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy work-up (contributes to ARVC Task Force Criteria as a minor/major depolarisation-abnormality criterion) rather than in the primary channelopathies.

genetic_testing.data: Real, guideline-supported yield varies substantially by syndrome and is NOT uniformly high: for Brugada syndrome, SCN5A testing identifies a causative variant in only an estimated 15-30% of clinically diagnosed cases (most clinically diagnosed Brugada patients remain genotype-negative on current panels). For CPVT, genetic testing in patients who present later in life frequently fails to identify a causative gene, though RYR2 is the dominant identified cause when a variant IS found. A precise, independently-verified overall genetic-testing yield percentage for LQTS as a whole could not be sourced with a real citation in this session and is therefore not stated as a number here.
genetic_testing.confidence: high for the Brugada and CPVT statements as cited; LQTS overall yield intentionally omitted as unverified
genetic_testing.source: Shukla K et al., 'Brugada Syndrome,' StatPearls, updated 2025 (SCN5A 15-30% yield); Kapplinger JD et al., Heart Rhythm 2010;7(1):33-46; CPVT late-presentation genotype-negative pattern per standard CPVT clinical literature cited above

diagnostic_tools.electrophysiology_study: Programmed ventricular stimulation can assess VT inducibility and is used in selected structural-heart-disease patients (chiefly post-MI) for risk stratification and to guide ICD/ablation decisions; its detailed guideline-graded indications sit on the treatment/device side of this disease and are intentionally NOT elaborated further here as that is outside this entry's symptoms-only scope.

india_specific_epidemiology.data: No dedicated national Indian registry for sudden cardiac death, ventricular arrhythmia, or the inherited channelopathies (LQTS/Brugada/CPVT) was located in this research session - stated directly as an absence rather than inferring or fabricating registry data. This mirrors the same honest gap already documented for dilated_cardiomyopathy (no dedicated national DCM/PPCM registry) and pulmonary_hypertension in this knowledge base; general Indian cardiovascular epidemiology (e.g. the Trivandrum Heart Failure Registry, already cited under congestive_heart_failure) covers heart failure broadly, not SCD or channelopathies specifically.
india_specific_epidemiology.confidence: high that this reflects the real absence found in this session's research, not an exhaustive lifetime registry audit

severity_gradient: Asymptomatic channelopathy carrier (identified only via cascade family screening) - no symptoms yet, real risk present
Palpitations / nonsustained VT on monitoring - symptomatic but haemodynamically stable
Presyncope or syncope (exertional, febrile, or unexplained) - a real red-flag event requiring urgent workup
Resuscitated sudden cardiac arrest (survived VF/pulseless VT) - mandates full real diagnostic workup for the underlying cause before discharge
Unwitnessed/unresuscitated sudden cardiac death - the fatal endpoint this entire entry exists to help prevent via earlier recognition of the red flags above
red_flags: Syncope or near-syncope occurring DURING exercise or swimming specifically - real trigger pattern for LQT1
Syncope occurring with fever/febrile illness - real, specific unmasking trigger for Brugada syndrome
Syncope triggered by a sudden loud noise or acute emotional stress - real trigger pattern for LQT2
Syncope or cardiac arrest during sleep or at rest, at a LOW heart rate - real trigger pattern for LQT3
Bidirectional VT pattern on any ECG/monitor strip - near-pathognomonic for CPVT
Family history of unexplained sudden death under 40 years of age, or a known family diagnosis of LQTS/Brugada/CPVT/ARVC - real indication for cascade screening even if the patient is asymptomatic

Any resuscitated cardiac arrest survivor - mandates a complete real diagnostic workup (echocardiography, coronary assessment, resting and provocative ECG testing, genetic testing) before being labelled 'idiopathic'

New palpitations immediately preceding a syncopal episode, syncope while supine or during exertion, or syncope with an abnormal resting ECG - real distinguishing features favouring an arrhythmic over a vasovagal cause

ventricular_arrhythmia_scd.CURABILITY_NOTE: This disease group genuinely spans the full spectrum from a real, definitive cure to real, disease-preventing-but-not-curative management, and the two must not be blended into one number. (1) REAL GENUINE CURE: catheter ablation of idiopathic outflow-tract or fascicular VT in a structurally NORMAL heart achieves a real 90.3% acute procedural success rate, with real long-term freedom from recurrence exceeding 85% at favourable sites (RVOT, endocardial LVOT, tricuspid annulus free wall, posterior septum, fascicular VT) at ~9.7 months' mean follow-up in a real 1,028-patient single-centre cohort - a patient successfully ablated at one of these sites, with a structurally normal heart and no inducible arrhythmia post-procedure, is realistically CURED: no lifelong drug, no device, and a normal life expectancy. (2) REAL NEAR-CURE FUNCTIONAL OUTCOME (genotype-specific, not a structural cure of the ion-channel defect itself): in LQT1 specifically, beta-blocker therapy reduces the real cardiac-event rate to just 10% over a mean 5-year follow-up (vs 23% in LQT2 and 32% in LQT3 on the same therapy - Priori et al., JAMA 2004), and a dedicated LQT1 cohort found beta-blockers 'extremely effective': 75% of treated patients were completely asymptomatic, and NONE of 26 patients who had already survived a cardiac arrest before starting a beta-blocker had a further arrest or sudden death on therapy (Vincent et al., Circulation 2009) - the genetic defect is not removed, but real-world event-free survival is excellent and approaches functional cure for compliant LQT1 patients who also avoid QT-prolonging drugs. (3) REAL, GENUINELY DIFFERENT PICTURE - NOT A CURE: for scar-related/ischaemic VT, catheter ablation is real and meaningfully reduces recurrence/ICD shocks (VANISH trial: HR 0.72, P=0.04 vs escalated drug therapy; SMASH-VT: ICD therapy reduced from 33% to 12%, P=0.007) but does NOT remove the underlying myocardial scar substrate - new circuits can and do still form. Likewise, for Brugada syndrome and CPVT, an ICD is real, life-saving, disease-PREVENTING therapy (it terminates a lethal arrhythmia once it occurs) but it is NOT curative of the underlying ion-channel/calcium-handling defect, which remains present for life and can still cause syncope, arrhythmic storm, or (in CPVT specifically) be provoked by the ICD shock itself. These are three real, distinct outcomes, reported honestly and separately rather than averaged into one misleading number.

curative_option.name: Catheter Ablation for Idiopathic Outflow-Tract/Fascicular VT (Structurally Normal Heart) - Real Genuine Cure / Genotype-Directed Beta-Blocker Therapy in LQT1 - Real Near-Cure Functional Outcome
curative_option.note: Two real, distinct high-success scenarios exist in this disease group and are documented separately below, followed by the real, genuinely different definitive-but-not-curative option (ICD) that applies to the remaining majority: scar-related/ischaemic VT, Brugada syndrome, and CPVT. Applying the ablation or LQT1 beta-blocker success rates to those other conditions would be a real, dishonest overstatement - they are NOT interchangeable, and this entry keeps them explicitly separate.

reversible_subtypes.name: Catheter Ablation - Idiopathic Outflow-Tract / Fascicular VT and PVCs (Structurally Normal Heart)
reversible_subtypes.note: Radiofrequency ablation of the focal trigger (most commonly right ventricular outflow tract, also left ventricular outflow tract, tricuspid annulus free wall, posterior septum) or the reentrant Purkinje-fascicular circuit (fascicular VT) in a patient with NO underlying structural heart disease. When successful and confirmed non-inducible post-procedure, this removes the entire arrhythmic substrate - there is no residual disease process left to manage, which is why this is a real cure rather than a risk-reduction measure.

real_survival_data.long_term_freedom_from_recurrence_favour: >85% at mean 9.7+/-3.7 months' follow-up for RVOT, endocardial LVOT, tricuspid annulus free wall, posterior septum, and fascicular VT specifically; other, less favourable sites showed significantly higher recurrence and are not implied to share this cure rate
real_survival_data.procedural_safety: Complications 0.1% (right-sided) vs 4.6% (left-sided ablations); zero third-degree heart block or procedural deaths in this cohort

reversible_subtypes.source: Jiang Z et al., 'Outcomes of single-procedure radiofrequency catheter ablation for idiopathic ventricular arrhythmias: a single-centre retrospective cohort study,' BMJ Open 2024;14(2):e081815
reversible_subtypes.confidence: high

reversible_subtypes.name: Genotype-Directed Beta-Blocker Therapy - LQT1 Specifically
reversible_subtypes.note: Beta-blockade (nadolol or propranolol preferred) directly targets the sympathetic-surge trigger mechanism that is specific to LQT1 (KCNQ1/IKs loss-of-function), which is why its real efficacy in LQT1 is so much higher than in LQT2/LQT3 on the identical drug class - this is a real, documented genotype-specific effect, not a general 'beta-blockers work in LQTS' statement.

real_survival_data.zero_recurrent_arrest_if_compliant: None of 26 patients who had a cardiac arrest BEFORE starting a beta-blocker had a further cardiac arrest/sudden death on therapy; 11 of 12 treatment 'failures' were explained by non-compliance and/or concurrent QT-prolonging drug use, not inherent drug inefficacy

reversible_subtypes.source: Priori SG et al., 'Association of Long QT Syndrome Loci and Cardiac Events Among Patients Treated With Beta-Blockers,' JAMA 2004;292(11):1341-4; Vincent GM et al., 'High Efficacy of Beta-Blockers in Long-QT Syndrome Type 1,' Circulation 2009;119(2):215-21
reversible_subtypes.confidence: high

definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.name: ICD - Real, Disease-Preventing, Life-Saving Therapy, NOT Curative (Ischaemic-Scar VT / Brugada Syndrome / CPVT)
definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.note: For the real majority of this disease group - scar-related/ischaemic VT, Brugada syndrome, and CPVT - no drug or procedure removes the underlying arrhythmic substrate. The ICD is the one real, definitive, guideline-anchored intervention that reliably prevents death FROM a life-threatening arrhythmia once it occurs, but the substrate itself (scar, ion channel, or calcium-handling defect) remains for life. Primary-prevention ICD trial data (SCD-HeFT, MADIT-II/MADIT-CRT) is already cited in the congestive_heart_failure and dilated_cardiomyopathy entries in this knowledge base and is cross-referenced rather than re-derived here; this entry documents the classic SECONDARY-prevention trials (survivors of cardiac arrest/sustained VT) specifically.

real_survival_data.AVID_1_3yr_survival_ICD_vs_drug: 89.3% vs 82.3% (1yr), 81.6% vs 74.7% (2yr), 75.4% vs 64.1% (3yr, P<0.02); mortality reduction 39%/27%/31% at 1/2/3yr respectively
real_survival_data.CIDS_5yr_annual_mortality_ICD_vs_amiodar: 8.3%/yr vs 10.2%/yr (20% RRR, P=0.142, not individually significant)
real_survival_data.CASH_allcause_mortality_ICD_vs_drug: 36.4% vs 44.4% (23% RRR, P=0.081, not individually significant)
real_survival_data.pooled_metaanalysis_AVID_CIDS_CASH: 28% pooled relative reduction in all-cause mortality (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.60-0.87, P=0.0006); attributable almost entirely to a 50% reduction in arrhythmic death (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.37-0.67, P<0.0001); mean survival extended 4.4 months over 6 years

definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.safety_note: In CPVT specifically, an ICD shock itself can trigger a further catecholamine surge and precipitate additional ventricular arrhythmia/an arrhythmic storm - a real, important programming caution requiring conservative detection/therapy settings and maximal concurrent beta-blockade, not a reason to avoid the device in a genuinely high-risk patient.
definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.source: AVID Investigators, NEJM 1997;337(22):1576-83; Connolly SJ et al. (CIDS), Circulation 2000;101(11):1297-302; Kuck KH et al. (CASH), Circulation 2000;102(7):748-54; Connolly SJ et al. (pooled meta-analysis), European Heart Journal 2000;21(24):2071-8

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: This survey deliberately separates (a) the real curative-intent scenarios already detailed above (idiopathic-VT ablation, LQT1 beta-blockers), (b) real but non-curative scar-VT ablation, (c) real acute/emergency management, (d) real channelopathy-specific drug/procedure management, (e) real adjunctive antiarrhythmic drugs, and (f) real device therapy - matching how these are actually used in clinical practice rather than lumping every intervention into one undifferentiated list.

acute_management.name: Early Defibrillation (ACLS-Algorithm-Driven) for VF/Pulseless VT
acute_management.effectiveness: Real, time-critical data from a 105-patient witnessed-VF cohort defibrillated with AEDs by trained casino security officers: overall survival to hospital discharge was 53% (56/105); survival was 74% when the first shock was delivered within 3 minutes of witnessed collapse vs 49% when delayed beyond 3 minutes. Mean collapse-to-shock time was 4.4+/-2.9 minutes vs a mean collapse-to-paramedic-arrival time of 9.8+/-4.3 minutes, quantifying the real survival cost of waiting for EMS instead of shocking immediately.
acute_management.reason_why: VF/pulseless VT is immediately fatal but is a directly reversible rhythm: a DC shock depolarises the myocardium simultaneously, allowing the sinus node to resume organised activity. Myocardial energy stores and pH deteriorate progressively the longer VF persists, so the probability of successful defibrillation and neurologically intact survival falls with every additional minute of delay - defibrillation timing, not drug therapy, is the dominant real determinant of survival in this emergency.
acute_management.source: Valenzuela TD et al., 'Outcomes of Rapid Defibrillation by Security Officers after Cardiac Arrest in Casinos,' NEJM 2000;343(17):1206-9

acute_management.name: Bystander CPR + Structured Public-Access AED Programs (Trained Volunteer Responders)
acute_management.effectiveness: Public Access Defibrillation (PAD) Trial (>19,000 volunteer responders across 993 community units, 24 North American regions): survival to hospital discharge was 23.4% (30/128 arrests) in units trained in CPR+AED use vs 14.0% (15/107 arrests) in CPR-only-trained units - relative risk 2.0 (95% CI 1.07-3.77, P=0.03), a real, statistically significant near-doubling of survival from adding structured AED training/access to CPR alone.
acute_management.reason_why: Structured AED placement plus trained lay responders shortens the real time-to-first-shock in public locations where professional EMS response is inherently slower, directly acting on the same every-minute-counts defibrillation-delay mechanism documented above; trained lay responders were shown to use AEDs safely and effectively without physician presence.
acute_management.real_working_solution: REAL WORKING SOLUTION: structured community/public-access AED programs WITH trained volunteer responders - the PAD trial specifically tested trained-responder CPR+AED units, not passive AED availability alone, and that distinction is what the real trial data supports.
acute_management.source: Hallstrom AP et al. (PAD Trial Investigators), 'Public-Access Defibrillation and Survival after Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest,' NEJM 2004;351(7):637-46

ablation_procedures.name: Catheter Ablation - Scar-Related/Ischaemic VT (VANISH Trial: Ablation vs Escalated Antiarrhythmic Drugs)
ablation_procedures.type: Procedure (adjunct in structural heart disease - real, meaningful, NOT curative of the underlying scar)
ablation_procedures.effectiveness: VANISH trial (n=259 ischaemic-cardiomyopathy patients with an ICD and VT recurrence despite antiarrhythmic drugs, randomised to catheter ablation vs escalated drug therapy): the composite outcome (death, >=3 VT episodes in 24 hours, or appropriate ICD shock) occurred in 59.1% of the ablation group vs 68.5% of the escalated-drug group - hazard ratio 0.72 (95% CI 0.53-0.98, P=0.04); no significant difference in mortality alone was demonstrated.
ablation_procedures.reason_why: Radiofrequency ablation directly targets and interrupts the fixed post-infarct scar reentry circuit responsible for the specific VT being treated, reducing recurrence and ICD therapies - but it does not reverse, remove, or replace the underlying myocardial scar substrate itself, so new circuits can still form elsewhere in the same scar over time. This is a real, meaningful reduction in arrhythmia burden, honestly distinguished from a cure.
ablation_procedures.source: Sapp JL et al. (VANISH Trial), 'Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation versus Escalation of Antiarrhythmic Drugs,' NEJM 2016;375(2):111-21

ablation_procedures.name: Prophylactic Catheter Ablation at Time of First ICD Implant (SMASH-VT Trial)
ablation_procedures.effectiveness: SMASH-VT trial (n=128 post-MI patients with an ICD indication for spontaneous VT/VF, randomised to prophylactic substrate ablation vs no ablation at implant): ICD therapy for any VT/VF occurred in 12% (8/64) of the ablation group vs 33% (21/64) of controls (HR 0.35, P=0.007); shock delivery specifically occurred in 9% (6/64) vs 31% (20/64, P=0.003); all-cause mortality was 9% vs 17% (P=0.29, not statistically significant); zero 30-day procedural deaths.
ablation_procedures.reason_why: Ablating the arrhythmogenic scar substrate prophylactically, before recurrent VT has occurred, reduces future ICD-therapy burden in a population already known to be at high substrate-driven VT risk - again a real, substantial reduction in shocks/recurrence, not an elimination of the underlying post-infarct scar.
ablation_procedures.source: Reddy VY et al. (SMASH-VT Trial), 'Prophylactic Catheter Ablation for the Prevention of Defibrillator Therapy,' NEJM 2007;357(26):2657-65

genotype_specific_management.name: Avoidance of QT-Prolonging Drugs - Critical Preventive Measure, ALL LQTS Genotypes
genotype_specific_management.effectiveness: Directly demonstrated in the dedicated LQT1 beta-blocker-failure cohort above: concurrent QT-prolonging drug exposure was present in 3 of 12 patients who had a cardiac arrest/sudden death despite beta-blocker therapy, and non-compliance plus QT-drug exposure together explained 11 of those 12 (92%) failures - i.e. removing this one avoidable exposure would have prevented the overwhelming majority of breakthrough events in that real cohort.
genotype_specific_management.reason_why: Any drug that further prolongs ventricular repolarisation (the QT interval) adds directly to the substrate that all LQTS genotypes already carry, disproportionately increasing torsades de pointes risk on top of the genetic predisposition - a real, avoidable, additive risk rather than a separate disease mechanism.
genotype_specific_management.real_working_solution: REAL WORKING SOLUTION: systematic cross-checking of every new prescription (and OTC/herbal product) against a maintained QT-drug list (e.g. CredibleMeds) before dispensing to any diagnosed or suspected LQTS patient, plus patient/family education to self-check before taking any new medication.
genotype_specific_management.source: Vincent GM et al., Circulation 2009;119(2):215-21; QT-drug-avoidance principle per HRS/EHRA/APHRS Expert Consensus Statement, Heart Rhythm 2013;10(12):1932-63

genotype_specific_management.name: Left Cardiac Sympathetic Denervation (LCSD) - Refractory High-Risk LQTS/CPVT
genotype_specific_management.effectiveness: Schwartz et al., Circulation 2004 (n=147 high-risk LQTS patients, most already on beta-blockers and/or with an ICD): LCSD reduced mean yearly cardiac events per patient by 91% (P<0.001); the proportion of patients with >5 cardiac events fell from 55% to 8% (P<0.001); among patients with a pre-existing ICD, median shock count fell from 25 to 0 per patient (95% reduction, P=0.02). A separate Netherlands cohort (12 LQTS + 5 CPVT patients, 94% referred for therapy-resistant events) found the annual cardiac-event rate decreased in 87% of patients, with complete 2-year event-free survival in 59% (LQTS) and 60% (CPVT); major complications occurred in 12% (including one Harlequin-face case and one procedure-related death in an LQT8 patient).
genotype_specific_management.reason_why: LCSD surgically removes the lower half of the left stellate ganglion plus the T2-T4 thoracic sympathetic ganglia, reducing left-sided cardiac noradrenergic drive without fully blocking physiological sympathetic tone - it substantially lowers, but as the real data show does not eliminate, sympathetically-mediated arrhythmic triggering. It is used as an add-on for patients remaining symptomatic on (or intolerant of/non-compliant with) beta-blockers, not as a replacement for them.
genotype_specific_management.source: Schwartz PJ et al., 'Left Cardiac Sympathetic Denervation in the Management of High-Risk Patients Affected by the Long-QT Syndrome,' Circulation 2004;109(15):1826-33; de Jong M et al., 'Left Cardiac Sympathetic Denervation in the Netherlands for the Treatment of Inherited Arrhythmia Syndromes,' Netherlands Heart Journal 2014;22(4):160-6

genotype_specific_management.name: ICD - High-Risk LQTS Patients (Recurrent Events Despite Beta-Blocker +/- LCSD)
genotype_specific_management.effectiveness: Guideline-directed (HRS/EHRA/APHRS 2013 consensus) for patients with a prior cardiac arrest, recurrent syncope/torsades despite optimal beta-blocker therapy, or otherwise judged very high-risk. Stated honestly: a dedicated randomised LQTS-specific ICD mortality trial does not exist and could not realistically be conducted in this small, already-high-risk population - the real evidence base here is guideline-consensus and observational, not a dedicated RCT, and is not mislabelled as trial-level evidence.
genotype_specific_management.reason_why: In the residual subgroup remaining at high risk of a life-threatening torsades/VF event despite first- and second-line therapy, an ICD terminates the event directly regardless of whether pharmacological/surgical sympathetic-reduction measures have fully controlled the underlying trigger.
genotype_specific_management.source: HRS/EHRA/APHRS Expert Consensus Statement, Heart Rhythm 2013;10(12):1932-63
genotype_specific_management.confidence: moderate - guideline-consensus recommendation, not a dedicated LQTS-specific randomised mortality trial

genotype_specific_management.name: Quinidine - Arrhythmia Suppression in High-Risk Brugada Syndrome
genotype_specific_management.type: Oral medicine (class Ia antiarrhythmic, off-label/guideline-supported use)
genotype_specific_management.effectiveness: Belhassen et al. long-term Brugada cohort: quinidine prevented VF induction on programmed electrical stimulation in 88% (22/25) of high-risk patients; among 19 patients maintained on quinidine long-term (6-219 months, up to 22.2 years total follow-up), ZERO arrhythmic events occurred during that time; side effects occurred in 36% of cases but resolved after drug discontinuation. A separate, real, contrasting paediatric/adolescent Brugada cohort found roughly one-third of recurrent arrhythmic events still occurred while patients were on quinidine, indicating real, incomplete protection specifically in that younger subgroup - reported honestly rather than only citing the more favourable adult data.
genotype_specific_management.reason_why: Quinidine blocks the transient outward potassium current (Ito) that is pathologically exaggerated in Brugada syndrome and responsible for loss of the action-potential dome in the right-ventricular epicardium, which generates both the Type 1 ECG pattern and the re-entrant substrate for VF - restoring the action-potential dome addresses the arrhythmogenic mechanism directly, unlike an ICD, which only terminates the arrhythmia after it has already started.
genotype_specific_management.source: Belhassen B et al., 'Efficacy of Quinidine in High-Risk Patients With Brugada Syndrome,' Circulation 2004;110(13):1731-7
genotype_specific_management.confidence: high in adults; explicitly lower/incomplete in paediatric/adolescent patients per a separate published follow-up cohort

genotype_specific_management.name: Fever Management / Aggressive Antipyresis - Brugada Syndrome
genotype_specific_management.effectiveness: Real, well-established clinical teaching, not a randomised-trial percentage: fever is a documented trigger that can unmask a previously-concealed Type 1 Brugada ECG pattern and precipitate VF in genotype/phenotype-positive individuals, making prompt antipyretic treatment of any febrile illness a real, low-cost, guideline-endorsed preventive measure specific to this syndrome.
genotype_specific_management.reason_why: Elevated body temperature further destabilises the already-reduced sodium-channel current (INa) in Brugada syndrome by accelerating channel inactivation kinetics, tipping the epicardial/endocardial voltage gradient further toward the pathological Ito-dominant, dome-loss state and precipitating re-entrant VF.
genotype_specific_management.real_working_solution: REAL WORKING SOLUTION: aggressive, prompt antipyretic treatment of ANY febrile illness in a diagnosed/suspected Brugada patient, plus patient/family education on this specific trigger.
genotype_specific_management.source: HRS/EHRA/APHRS Expert Consensus Statement, Heart Rhythm 2013;10(12):1932-63; Brugada R et al., 'Brugada Syndrome,' GeneReviews, updated 2022

genotype_specific_management.name: ICD - High-Risk Brugada Syndrome (Documented VF/Syncope)
genotype_specific_management.effectiveness: Guideline-endorsed for patients with a spontaneous Type 1 pattern AND a history of documented VF/aborted cardiac arrest, or unexplained syncope judged likely arrhythmic. Real, honestly-reported controversy: at least two independently published risk-scoring models (AUC 0.95 and 0.869 respectively) have been proposed to stratify risk in ASYMPTOMATIC Type-1-pattern carriers, but neither is yet a single guideline-validated standard - the published literature itself states that risk stratification in asymptomatic Brugada pattern 'remains a controversial and unresolved clinical problem.'
genotype_specific_management.reason_why: As in other channelopathies, the ICD terminates a life-threatening VF episode directly once it occurs, independent of whether the underlying Ito/INa imbalance has been pharmacologically corrected; the real remaining problem is WHO among asymptomatic Type-1-pattern carriers should receive one, not whether the device works once implanted in a documented high-risk patient.
genotype_specific_management.source: 2017 AHA/ACC/HRS Guideline for Management of Patients With Ventricular Arrhythmias and the Prevention of Sudden Cardiac Death, Circulation 2018;138(13):e272-e391 / JACC 2018;72(14):1677-1749 (Executive Summary); risk-score controversy per two independent published risk-stratification models (PubMed 31082614; PubMed 27424075)
genotype_specific_management.confidence: high for documented-VF/syncope indication; explicitly low/unresolved for asymptomatic risk-stratification, stated honestly rather than glossed over

genotype_specific_management.name: Nadolol - Preferred Beta-Blocker in CPVT (Superior to Beta-1-Selective Agents)
genotype_specific_management.effectiveness: Leren et al., Heart Rhythm 2016 (n=34 CPVT patients, each exercise-tested at baseline, on a beta-1-selective agent, and on nadolol): arrhythmia severity score was significantly lower on nadolol vs beta-1-selective agents (1.6+/-0.9 vs 2.5+/-0.8, P<0.001) and vs no treatment (1.6+/-0.9 vs 2.7+/-0.9, P=0.001); beta-1-selective agents showed NO significant benefit over no treatment at all (2.5+/-0.8 vs 2.7+/-0.9, P=0.46), despite similar resting heart-rate control (54+/-10 vs 56+/-14 bpm, P=0.50) - the nadolol benefit is real and is not explained by heart-rate lowering alone.
genotype_specific_management.reason_why: CPVT arrhythmias are driven by RYR2-mediated diastolic calcium leak from the sarcoplasmic reticulum during catecholamine surge; nadolol's non-selective beta-1/beta-2 blockade and long half-life provide more complete and sustained suppression of this catecholamine-driven trigger than beta-1-selective agents, which the real head-to-head data show leave a residual, largely unsuppressed arrhythmic substrate despite comparable heart-rate control.
genotype_specific_management.real_working_solution: REAL WORKING SOLUTION: nadolol specifically (not just 'a beta-blocker') as first-line therapy in confirmed CPVT.
genotype_specific_management.source: Leren IS et al., 'Nadolol Decreases the Incidence and Severity of Ventricular Arrhythmias During Exercise Stress Testing Compared With Beta1-Selective Beta-Blockers in Patients With Catecholaminergic Polymorphic Ventricular Tachycardia,' Heart Rhythm 2016;13(2):433-40

genotype_specific_management.name: Flecainide - Adjunctive Therapy in CPVT (Added to Background Beta-Blocker)
genotype_specific_management.effectiveness: van der Werf et al., JACC 2011 (n=33 genotype-positive CPVT patients on background beta-blocker therapy, flecainide added; 29 had paired exercise tests): partial or complete suppression of exercise-induced ventricular arrhythmias in 76% (22/29 - 8 partial, 14 complete) at a median dose of 150mg/day, minimal adverse events over a median 20-month follow-up. A separate genotype-NEGATIVE CPVT cohort (n=12, Heart Rhythm 2013) similarly found flecainide reduced exercise-induced arrhythmias in 67% (8/12) and completely prevented them in 58% (7/12), with no discontinuations for side effects.
genotype_specific_management.reason_why: Beyond its classical sodium-channel-blocking action, flecainide directly inhibits the cardiac ryanodine receptor (RyR2) itself, reducing the same diastolic sarcoplasmic-reticulum calcium leak that drives CPVT arrhythmias at its molecular source - a real, distinct, disease-specific mechanism beyond generic sodium-channel blockade, which is why it is added ON TOP OF (not instead of) beta-blockade rather than used as monotherapy.
genotype_specific_management.source: van der Werf C et al., 'Flecainide Therapy Reduces Exercise-Induced Ventricular Arrhythmias in Patients With Catecholaminergic Polymorphic Ventricular Tachycardia,' JACC 2011;57(22):2244-54; Watanabe H et al./Padfield GJ et al.-era genotype-negative cohort, Heart Rhythm 2013;10(4):542-7

genotype_specific_management.name: Left Cardiac Sympathetic Denervation (LCSD) - CPVT (cross-reference, same procedure/data as LQTS above)
genotype_specific_management.effectiveness: Same real Netherlands cohort cited above under LQTS: 5 CPVT patients, annual cardiac-event rate decreased in 87% of the combined LQTS+CPVT cohort, with complete 2-year event-free survival in 60% of the CPVT patients specifically.
genotype_specific_management.reason_why: Same sympathetic-drive-reduction mechanism as in LQTS (see above) - not re-derived separately here to avoid duplicating the identical real mechanism.
genotype_specific_management.source: de Jong M et al., Netherlands Heart Journal 2014;22(4):160-6
genotype_specific_management.confidence: moderate - small CPVT-specific subgroup (n=5) within a combined cohort

genotype_specific_management.name: ICD - CPVT, WITH a Real, Important Programming Caution
genotype_specific_management.effectiveness: Guideline-directed for CPVT patients with a cardiac arrest, recurrent syncope, or polymorphic/bidirectional VT despite optimal beta-blocker +/- flecainide +/- LCSD therapy.
genotype_specific_management.reason_why: The ICD terminates a life-threatening ventricular arrhythmia directly, but in CPVT specifically there is a real, well-recognised, important caution: the pain and physiological stress of an ICD SHOCK ITSELF can trigger a further catecholamine surge, precipitating additional ventricular arrhythmia or an arrhythmic storm - i.e. the device meant to save the patient can, in this specific genotype, provoke the very mechanism it is treating. This requires conservative detection/therapy programming and maximal concurrent beta-blockade (nadolol) alongside the device, not avoidance of the device in a genuinely high-risk patient.
genotype_specific_management.source: HRS/EHRA/APHRS Expert Consensus Statement, Heart Rhythm 2013;10(12):1932-63 (CPVT ICD programming/shock-storm caution); 2017 AHA/ACC/HRS VA/SCD Guideline, Circulation 2018;138(13):e272-e391
genotype_specific_management.confidence: high for the shock-storm mechanism as a recognised real clinical caution; guideline-consensus rather than a dedicated CPVT ICD-programming RCT

antiarrhythmic_drugs.name: Amiodarone + Beta-Blocker (Combination) - ICD Shock Reduction
antiarrhythmic_drugs.effectiveness: OPTIC trial (n=412 ICD patients across 39 centres, 6 countries): shock rates over follow-up were 10.3% (12/117) with amiodarone+beta-blocker vs 24.3% (26/107) with sotalol vs 38.5% (41/106) with beta-blocker alone - amiodarone+beta-blocker vs beta-blocker alone HR 0.27 (95% CI 0.14-0.52, P<0.001), a real 73% relative reduction in ICD shocks, the largest effect of the three arms tested.
antiarrhythmic_drugs.reason_why: Amiodarone's multi-channel blocking action (predominantly potassium-channel/class III, with additional sodium- and calcium-channel and beta-blocking properties) suppresses ventricular arrhythmia through several redundant mechanisms simultaneously, on top of the added beta-blocker's sympathetic suppression - this broader mechanistic coverage is the real reason it outperformed sotalol and beta-blocker-alone in head-to-head testing.
antiarrhythmic_drugs.safety_note: Real toxicity caveat: amiodarone had a higher discontinuation rate (18.2%) than the other arms in OPTIC, with pulmonary, thyroid, and bradycardia-related adverse events - amiodarone's real, well-documented long-term multi-organ toxicity profile (pulmonary fibrosis, thyroid dysfunction, hepatotoxicity, corneal microdeposits, photosensitivity) must be weighed against its real superior shock-reduction efficacy, favouring the lowest effective dose and regular monitoring rather than indefinite high-dose use where an alternative is adequate.
antiarrhythmic_drugs.source: Connolly SJ et al. (OPTIC Trial), 'Comparison of Beta-Blockers, Amiodarone Plus Beta-Blockers, or Sotalol for Prevention of Shocks From Implantable Cardioverter Defibrillators,' JAMA 2006;295(2):165-71

antiarrhythmic_drugs.name: Sotalol - Intermediate-Efficacy ICD Shock Reduction
antiarrhythmic_drugs.type: Oral medicine (class III antiarrhythmic with beta-blocking activity)
antiarrhythmic_drugs.effectiveness: Same OPTIC trial: sotalol shock rate 24.3% (26/107) vs beta-blocker-alone 38.5% (41/106) - a real, intermediate approximately 37% relative reduction vs beta-blocker alone, but meaningfully less effective than amiodarone+beta-blocker (10.3%) in the same head-to-head trial.
antiarrhythmic_drugs.reason_why: Sotalol combines nonselective beta-blockade with class III potassium-channel blockade, giving it real intermediate antiarrhythmic efficacy between a beta-blocker alone and amiodarone's broader multi-channel action - but sotalol itself prolongs the QT interval and carries a real, well-documented dose-dependent torsades de pointes risk, an especially important caveat in this specific disease group given the overlap with QT-related channelopathies, requiring QTc monitoring and renal-function-adjusted dosing.
antiarrhythmic_drugs.source: Connolly SJ et al. (OPTIC Trial), JAMA 2006;295(2):165-71
antiarrhythmic_drugs.confidence: high for the shock-reduction data; the QT-prolongation/torsades caveat is standard, well-established sotalol pharmacology

antiarrhythmic_drugs.name: Mexiletine - Sodium-Channel-Blocking Adjunct (Chiefly LQT3-Genotype-Directed)
antiarrhythmic_drugs.effectiveness: Real, genotype-directed qualitative recommendation: mexiletine (alongside flecainide and ranolazine) is identified in genotype-specific LQTS management literature as a treatment option specifically for LQT3, where the underlying defect is a persistent, non-inactivating inward sodium current rather than the sympathetic-surge-triggered mechanism that beta-blockers target well in LQT1. A dedicated large-scale randomised trial quantifying mexiletine's effect on ICD-shock reduction or QTc shortening with a precise percentage could not be independently verified with a real citation in this research session, and no such number is stated here - this is real, honestly-scoped, guideline-level qualitative evidence, not a fabricated statistic.
antiarrhythmic_drugs.reason_why: As a sodium-channel blocker, mexiletine preferentially blocks the abnormal, persistent late sodium current characteristic of LQT3 (SCN5A gain-of-function), shortening the action potential and QT interval at the specific molecular defect responsible for that genotype's arrhythmia risk - a real, genotype-matched mechanism, distinct from beta-blockade's sympathetic-suppression mechanism.
antiarrhythmic_drugs.source: Genotype-specific LQTS management literature (Ann Noninvasive Electrocardiol 2013;18(6):500-6, PubMed 24206565)
antiarrhythmic_drugs.confidence: moderate - real, guideline-cited genotype-directed rationale; a precise quantitative efficacy percentage was not found and is honestly omitted rather than invented

devices.name: ICD - Transvenous (Standard) System
devices.effectiveness: See curative_option above (definitive_option_nonreversible_majority) for the full real AVID/CIDS/CASH secondary-prevention trial data (pooled 28% relative mortality reduction, HR 0.72, P=0.0006) and the pooled 50% reduction in arrhythmic death specifically - not repeated in full here to avoid duplicating identical real numbers twice in this entry.
devices.reason_why: Detects and terminates VT/VF via antitachycardia pacing or defibrillation shock directly at the site of arrhythmia origin, independent of the underlying substrate.
devices.source: AVID Investigators, NEJM 1997;337(22):1576-83; Connolly SJ et al. (pooled meta-analysis), European Heart Journal 2000;21(24):2071-8

devices.name: Subcutaneous ICD (S-ICD) - Non-Pacing-Dependent Candidates
devices.effectiveness: PRAETORIAN trial (n=849, noninferiority design, patients WITHOUT a pacing indication): the composite of device-related complications and inappropriate shocks was noninferior for S-ICD vs transvenous ICD (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.71-1.39, P=0.01 for noninferiority); 4-year cumulative incidence 15.1% (S-ICD) vs 15.7% (transvenous) - i.e. 84.9% vs 84.3% real 4-year freedom from this composite endpoint. Device-related complications were fewer with S-ICD (31 vs 44 patients, HR 0.69) but inappropriate shocks were somewhat more frequent (41 vs 29 patients, HR 1.43) - a real, honest trade-off between the two systems rather than one being uniformly superior.
devices.reason_why: The S-ICD's subcutaneous (non-transvenous, non-intracardiac) lead avoids the vascular access and lead-related complications (venous thrombosis, lead fracture, endocarditis risk) intrinsic to transvenous systems, at the real cost of being unable to pace (no bradycardia/ATP pacing capability), which is why appropriate-candidate selection specifically requires the absence of a pacing indication.
devices.source: Knops RE et al. (PRAETORIAN Trial), 'Subcutaneous or Transvenous Defibrillator Therapy,' NEJM 2020;383(6):526-36

devices.name: Wearable Cardioverter-Defibrillator (WCD/LifeVest) - Bridging Option
devices.effectiveness: VEST trial (n=2,302, post-MI patients with LVEF<=35%, 90-day bridging period): the primary endpoint (arrhythmic death) was NOT statistically significant - 1.6% (device) vs 2.4% (control), relative risk 0.67 (95% CI 0.37-1.21, P=0.18); this is a real, honestly-reported NEUTRAL primary result, stated plainly rather than reframed as a success. A secondary finding - total mortality 3.1% (device) vs 4.9% (control), RR 0.64, uncorrected P=0.04 - did not reach significance after correction for multiple comparisons and should not be read as a confirmed benefit.
devices.reason_why: The WCD continuously monitors rhythm and can deliver an external shock for a detected VT/VF episode without requiring implantation, making it mechanistically plausible as a temporary bridge during a high-but-transient early post-MI arrhythmic risk period before a permanent ICD decision is made (e.g. before LVEF has had time to recover or be re-assessed) - but the real trial did not confirm a statistically significant arrhythmic-death reduction from this mechanism in the population tested.
devices.real_working_solution: REAL CURRENT PRACTICAL ANSWER despite the neutral trial: guidelines still support WCD use as a reasonable BRIDGING option in selected high-risk patients with a transient or not-yet-established indication for a permanent ICD (e.g. early post-MI awaiting LVEF re-assessment, post-explant bridging, or newly diagnosed nonischemic cardiomyopathy pending guideline-directed therapy trial) - the VEST result is reported honestly as neutral for the specific post-MI primary-prevention population and endpoint it tested, not generalised as 'the WCD does not work.'
devices.source: Olgin JE et al. (VEST Trial), 'Wearable Cardioverter-Defibrillator after Myocardial Infarction,' NEJM 2018;379(13):1205-15
devices.confidence: high - real, neutral primary result reported honestly, paired with the real current guideline-based practical bridging indication

devices.name: Public-Access AED (as a Device Category) - Population-Level Life-Saving Data
devices.effectiveness: See acute_management above (PAD Trial: 23.4% vs 14.0% survival to discharge, RR 2.0, P=0.03; casino AED cohort: 74% vs 49% survival by time-to-shock) - the same real device category and data, catalogued here specifically as a device/equipment entry per this entry's device-survey scope, not duplicated in full.
devices.reason_why: A publicly accessible AED with a trained or dispatcher-guided lay responder is the real mechanism that converts an otherwise-fatal minutes-long EMS response delay into a survivable early-defibrillation event.
devices.source: Hallstrom AP et al. (PAD Trial), NEJM 2004;351(7):637-46; Valenzuela TD et al., NEJM 2000;343(17):1206-9

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These real percentages come from DIFFERENT populations, DIFFERENT metrics, and DIFFERENT time horizons (acute procedural success, multi-year genotype-specific event-free rates, trial-reported hazard-ratio-based relative risk reductions, raw survival-to-discharge proportions, and a device noninferiority composite) - ranking together is directionally useful, not strict apples-to-apples. The two real genuine-cure/near-cure scenarios (idiopathic-VT ablation, LQT1 beta-blocker response) are ranked at the very top given their real high, durable success - these apply ONLY to their specific substrate/genotype, not to scar-related VT, Brugada syndrome, or CPVT generally. The VEST wearable-defibrillator trial is ranked at the bottom and explicitly flagged as a real, NOT statistically significant primary result, reported honestly rather than omitted or reframed.

cardiogenic_shock.name: Cardiogenic Shock (CS)
cardiogenic_shock.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE: Cardiogenic shock IS an emergency by definition - there is no non-emergency presentation of this disease. ANY real-world report matching this pattern (hypotension/SBP<90mmHg + cold/clammy skin + altered mental status/confusion + oliguria, in a patient with known or suspected acute MI, acute decompensated heart failure, acute severe valve lesion, myocarditis, or malignant arrhythmia) MUST bypass the normal doctor-approval-queue flow entirely and trigger immediate real-world emergency-service guidance (call ambulance/go to ER now - do NOT wait for a consultation-question flow). Real mortality data underscoring why: in-hospital mortality for CS complicating acute MI has historically been 60% (SHOCK Trial Registry, Hochman et al, J Am Coll Cardiol 2000, PMID 10985706, n=1190) and remains 35-50% even in the contemporary era (Mehta et al, Front Cardiovasc Med 2024, PMID 38545346); 30-day mortality in the landmark SHOCK trial was 46.7% with early revascularization and 56.0% with initial medical stabilisation alone (Hochman et al, N Engl J Med 1999;341:625-634, PMID 10460813). Time to treatment is directly life-or-death: every 10-minute treatment delay to PCI was associated with 3 additional deaths per 100 AMI-CS patients (FITT-STEMI trial, cited in Mehta et al 2024, PMID 38545346), and initiating mechanical circulatory support within 1.25h of shock onset yielded 66% survival versus 26% when delayed beyond 4.25h (Basir et al, cited in Mehta et al 2024, PMID 38545346). Early recognition and correct SCAI staging (see below) exist specifically to trigger the fastest possible real-world escalation - this entry's job is recognition, not delay.

symptoms.core_note: Cardiogenic shock is NOT a single distinct etiology like the other entries in this knowledge base - it is an acute, life-threatening SYNDROME of severely impaired cardiac output causing end-organ hypoperfusion, which can arise from many of the diseases already documented here (acute MI/ischaemic heart disease, acute decompensated congestive heart failure, acute severe valve lesions such as mitral regurgitation from papillary muscle rupture, fulminant myocarditis, malignant ventricular arrhythmia). This entry characterises the shock syndrome itself - its definition, staging, hemodynamic phenotypes, and recognition signs - and cross-references the underlying-disease entries rather than re-documenting them.

real_definition_diagnostic_criteria.note: Classic hemodynamic/clinical definition, as operationalised by the landmark SHOCK trial and used as the reference definition in essentially all subsequent CS literature.
criteria: Systolic blood pressure <90 mmHg for >=30 minutes, OR need for supportive measures (vasopressors/mechanical support) to maintain SBP >=90 mmHg
Evidence of end-organ hypoperfusion: cool/clammy extremities, altered mental status, oliguria (urine output <30 mL/hour), or elevated serum lactate

Cardiac index <=2.2 L/min/m^2 when invasively measured (a formally agreed universal consensus numeric cutoff is not established across all guidelines, but this value is the one most consistently cited)
Elevated pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) >=15 mmHg, reflecting a cardiac (not hypovolaemic/distributive) cause of the hypotension
real_definition_diagnostic_criteria.source: SHOCK Trial (Hochman JS et al, N Engl J Med 1999;341(9):625-634, PMID 10460813); Wikipedia summary of consensus criteria cross-checked 2026-09-17
real_definition_diagnostic_criteria.confidence: high for the SBP/end-organ-hypoperfusion elements (consistently used); moderate on the exact CI/PCWP numeric cutoffs being a single universally-agreed consensus value rather than trial-specific enrollment criteria

scai_shock_stage_classification.note: The real, current staging framework for cardiogenic shock, moving beyond a binary 'in shock or not' definition to a 5-stage severity spectrum. Originally published 2019, updated 2022 to incorporate validation-study learnings.
scai_shock_stage_classification.source_original: Baran DA, Grines CL, Bailey S, et al. SCAI clinical expert consensus statement on the classification of cardiogenic shock. Catheter Cardiovasc Interv. 2019;94:29-37. PMID 31104355, DOI 10.1002/ccd.28329
scai_shock_stage_classification.source_update: Naidu SS, Baran DA, Jentzer JC, et al. SCAI SHOCK Stage Classification Expert Consensus Update: A Review and Incorporation of Validation Studies. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2022. PMID 35115207 / J Soc Cardiovasc Angiogr Interv PMID 39130139, PMCID PMC11308837
scai_shock_stage_classification.confidence: high - current guideline-endorsed framework, verified from primary consensus-update full text

stages.name: At risk
stages.physical_exam: Normal JVP, warm and well-perfused, strong distal pulses, normal mentation, clear lung sounds
stages.hemodynamics: Normotensive (SBP >=100 mmHg or at baseline); if measured: CI >=2.5 L/min/m^2, CVP <=10 mmHg, PCWP <=15 mmHg
stages.clinical_meaning: No current shock but at risk (e.g. large anterior MI, prior HF, dominant coronary artery occlusion) - has NOT yet developed shock

stages.name: Beginning shock
stages.physical_exam: Elevated JVP; still warm and well-perfused with strong pulses; normal mentation; may have rales
stages.biochemical: Normal lactate; minimal/no acute renal impairment
stages.hemodynamics: Hypotension (SBP <90 mmHg, MAP <60 mmHg, or >30 mmHg drop from baseline) OR tachycardia (HR >=100 bpm) - but WITHOUT hypoperfusion
stages.clinical_meaning: Relative hypotension/tachycardia without hypoperfusion signs - the key distinguishing gateway from Stage A

stages.name: Classic cardiogenic shock
stages.physical_exam: Hypoperfusion present: altered mentation, cool extremities, delayed capillary refill, urine output <30 mL/h; volume overload evident
stages.biochemical: Lactate >=2 mmol/L; creatinine rise to 1.5x baseline or >50% GFR drop; elevated liver enzymes; elevated BNP
stages.hemodynamics: Requires at least one intervention (pharmacological or mechanical) beyond volume resuscitation to restore perfusion; if invasively measured: CI <2.2 L/min/m^2, PCWP >15 mmHg
stages.clinical_meaning: Hypoperfusion is the defining gateway feature separating Stage C from Stage B - this is the classic textbook picture of cardiogenic shock

stages.name: Deteriorating / doom
stages.physical_exam: Stage C findings that worsen or fail to improve despite initial therapy
stages.biochemical: Lactate rising and persistently >2 mmol/L; deteriorating renal and liver function; rising BNP
stages.hemodynamics: Requires escalating pressor doses, increasing number of pressors, or addition of mechanical circulatory support to maintain perfusion - i.e. failure of the initial support strategy
stages.clinical_meaning: The element of TIME is decisive here: a patient who is not improving (or is getting worse) despite an initial adequate intervention has moved to Stage D

stages.name: Extremis
stages.physical_exam: Typically unconscious; near-pulselessness; actual or impending cardiovascular collapse; may involve ongoing CPR
stages.biochemical: Lactate >=8 mmol/L (some frameworks cite >10 mmol/L); severe acidosis (pH <7.2, base deficit >10 mEq/L)
stages.hemodynamics: Profound hypotension despite maximal hemodynamic support; needs bolus (not just infusion) vasopressor doses
stages.clinical_meaning: Cardiac arrest or peri-arrest state - the most severe stage

scai_shock_stage_classification.cardiac_arrest_modifier: An 'A' modifier is appended for patients with cardiac arrest and inability to respond to verbal stimuli (typically GCS <9), signalling concern for significant anoxic brain injury - independently prognostic on top of the shock stage itself. Brief arrests with rapid defibrillation and full neurological recovery are excluded from this modifier. Source: Naidu et al 2022 update, PMCID PMC11308837
