real_stage_specific_mortality_validation.study: Jentzer JC, van Diepen S, Barsness GW, et al. Cardiogenic Shock Classification to Predict Mortality in the Cardiac Intensive Care Unit. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2019;74(17):2117-2128. PMID 31548097
real_stage_specific_mortality_validation.cohort: 10,004 consecutive Mayo Clinic Cardiac Intensive Care Unit admissions, 2007-2015
real_stage_specific_mortality_validation.finding: Mortality rose sharply and monotonically by stage; each higher stage and concurrent cardiac arrest were independently associated with increased mortality risk. This is the primary large-cohort validation of the SCAI framework's real prognostic power.
real_stage_specific_mortality_validation.confidence: high - large real registry, peer-reviewed, primary validation study

real_stage_specific_mortality_validation.study: Prospective single/multi-center validation referenced in Long A, Baran DA. Lingua Franca of Cardiogenic Shock: Speaking the Same Language. Front Cardiovasc Med. 2021. PMCID PMC8492962
real_stage_specific_mortality_validation.finding: 30-day survival by initial SCAI shock stage: Stage B 100%, Stage C 65.4%, Stage D 44.2%, Stage E 60% (small-E-cohort anomaly noted in source, likely reflects limited Stage E sample size at that single site rather than Stage E truly outperforming Stage D)
real_stage_specific_mortality_validation.confidence: moderate - smaller validation cohort than Jentzer et al; the non-monotonic D-vs-E figure is a real reported anomaly, not an error in transcription, and is flagged as such

etiology_breakdown.note: Real etiology distribution from the landmark SHOCK Trial Registry (the largest dedicated etiology dataset for AMI-associated CS).
etiology_breakdown.source: Hochman JS, Buller CE, Sleeper LA, et al. Cardiogenic shock complicating acute myocardial infarction--etiologies, management and outcome: a report from the SHOCK Trial Registry. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2000;36(3 Suppl A):1063-1070. PMID 10985706
etiology_breakdown.cohort: 1,190 cardiogenic shock patients complicating acute MI, enrolled April 1993-August 1997

causes.cause: Predominant left ventricular failure (classic AMI/LV pump-failure CS)
causes.note: The real classic/most-studied cause; see ischaemic_heart_disease entry for the underlying coronary disease

causes.cause: Severe acute mitral regurgitation (typically papillary muscle rupture)
causes.note: Cross-reference mitral_regurgitation entry for the valve lesion itself; acute MR causes CS via sudden massive regurgitant volume with no time for compensatory LA/LV dilation
Distinct hemodynamic phenotype and distinct management implications - see below

other_real_causes_not_quantified_in_shoc.note: Now recognised as accounting for a rising share of CS admissions in contemporary cohorts - 'up to >50% of admissions for CS' in some contemporary series, attributed partly to declining AMI incidence with modern preventive therapy. Cross-reference congestive_heart_failure entry. Classic 'cold and wet' hemodynamic profile (see below).
other_real_causes_not_quantified_in_shoc.source: Mehta A et al, Contemporary Approach to Cardiogenic Shock Care, Front Cardiovasc Med 2024, PMID 38545346

other_real_causes_not_quantified_in_shoc.note: Cross-reference myocarditis entry - acute severe myocardial inflammation can cause CS in previously healthy (often young) patients

other_real_causes_not_quantified_in_shoc.cause: Critical aortic stenosis / acute severe aortic regurgitation

other_real_causes_not_quantified_in_shoc.note: Cross-reference ventricular_arrhythmia_scd and atrial_fibrillation entries - tachyarrhythmia-induced or bradyarrhythmia-induced CS
CS occurring after cardiac surgery, related to but distinct from medical CS in onset/context

classic_clinical_signs.note: SBP <90 mmHg or a drop >30 mmHg from baseline, or vasopressor-dependence to maintain SBP - the defining hemodynamic feature

The most common real hemodynamic phenotype in CS - reflects peripheral vasoconstriction as a compensatory response to low cardiac output; contrasts with the warm/vasodilated skin of septic (distributive) shock
Confusion, agitation, or obtundation from cerebral hypoperfusion; in extremis (SCAI Stage E) typically unconscious
Urine output <30 mL/hour from renal hypoperfusion - one of the SCAI Stage C-defining hypoperfusion criteria

Marker of anaerobic metabolism from tissue hypoperfusion; SCAI thresholds: >=2 mmol/L (Stage C/D gateway), >=8-10 mmol/L (Stage E). Early lactate clearance within the first 6-8h and/or by 24h is more prognostic than any single absolute lactate value, and is associated with improved survival in treatment responders; lactate >=4 mmol/L independently predicted higher in-hospital mortality in the National Cardiogenic Shock Initiative cohort. An important caveat: lactate can be normal despite depressed cardiac index in chronic HF patients, so a normal lactate does not exclude hypoperfusion.
classic_clinical_signs.source: Mehta A et al, Front Cardiovasc Med 2024, PMID 38545346; Naidu et al 2022 SCAI update, PMCID PMC11308837

classic_clinical_signs.note: Reflects elevated left-sided filling pressures (elevated PCWP) - seen in classic LV-failure CS and acute decompensated HF-CS

classic_clinical_signs.sign: Isolated hypotension with CLEAR lungs (RIGHT-sided / RV-infarction CS)
classic_clinical_signs.note: A real, clinically important distinguishing picture: RV-dominant CS presents with hypotension and elevated JVP but classically CLEAR lung fields (no pulmonary oedema), because the primary problem is failure of RV output to fill the left heart, not left-sided venous congestion - can be mistaken for hypovolaemia if this distinction is missed

hemodynamic_classification.note: Real clinical framework for phenotyping CS by filling pressure (congestion) and perfusion status, descending from the original Diamond-Forrester binary model (based on cardiac index and PCWP) and refined into a 3-profile congestion model in contemporary CS literature.
hemodynamic_classification.source: Diamond-Forrester classification (Forrester JS et al, classic hemodynamic subsets framework, cited in Mehta A et al, Front Cardiovasc Med 2024, PMID 38545346)

profiles.name: Cold and wet
profiles.hemodynamics: Low cardiac output/perfusion (cold) + elevated filling pressures/congestion (wet) - i.e. low CI with elevated PCWP
profiles.frequency: The most common real CS presentation - classic LV-failure and decompensated-HF CS phenotype
profiles.clinical_picture: Cold clammy extremities + pulmonary rales/oedema + elevated JVP

profiles.name: Cold and dry
profiles.hemodynamics: Low cardiac output/perfusion (cold) + normal or LOW filling pressures (dry) - i.e. low CI with normal/low PCWP
profiles.frequency: Less common; classically seen in isolated RV infarction and in volume-depleted CS patients
profiles.clinical_picture: Cold clammy extremities but CLEAR lung fields, no pulmonary oedema

profiles.name: Modern 3-profile congestion model (contemporary CS literature)
profiles.hemodynamics: LV-dominant shock (elevated PCWP, normal/reduced CVP); RV-dominant shock (elevated CVP, normal/low PCWP, relatively preserved LV function); Biventricular (BiV) shock (elevated BOTH right and left filling pressures)
profiles.finding: BiV shock is the most commonly observed of the three profiles in contemporary cohorts AND is an independent predictor of higher mortality versus LV-only congestion (adjusted OR 2.4, 95% CI 1.4-3.7) or no congestion (adjusted OR 2.1, 95% CI 1.1-4.0)
profiles.source: Mehta A et al, Front Cardiovasc Med 2024, PMID 38545346
profiles.confidence: high - real adjusted-OR data from a peer-reviewed state-of-the-art review

rv_infarction_associated_cs.note: A real, distinct clinical entity requiring separate recognition from left-sided/classic CS because the correct real-world response is different (the parallel medicines/MCS agent covers the actual management divergence - e.g. RV infarction CS is preload-dependent and is worsened rather than helped by aggressive diuresis/nitrates that are appropriate in left-sided pulmonary-oedema CS).
rv_infarction_associated_cs.hemodynamic_profile: Elevated central venous pressure/JVP with relatively preserved LV systolic function, and normal-to-low PCWP and pulmonary artery pressure - the 'cold and dry' pattern above
rv_infarction_associated_cs.clinical_picture: Hypotension + elevated JVP + clear lung fields (no rales/pulmonary oedema) - the key real distinguishing triad from left-sided CS
rv_infarction_associated_cs.outcome_data: A SHOCK registry sub-study found broadly similar in-hospital mortality between RV-shock and LV-shock patients (53% vs 61%, p=0.30) - i.e. RV shock is not a 'milder' form of CS despite the different hemodynamic mechanism
rv_infarction_associated_cs.source: Cited in Mehta A et al, Contemporary Approach to Cardiogenic Shock Care, Front Cardiovasc Med 2024, PMID 38545346 (referencing a SHOCK registry RV-shock sub-study)
rv_infarction_associated_cs.confidence: high for the hemodynamic-phenotype description (long-standing, consistently taught); moderate-high for the exact 53%/61% comparative mortality figures (single sub-study, p=0.30 i.e. not statistically significant difference)

incidence_ami_cs.figures: Cardiogenic shock complicates approximately 5-10% of acute MI cases; affects an estimated 40,000-50,000 people per year in the US
incidence_ami_cs.source: Wikipedia cross-checked summary of consensus literature; Samsky MD, Morrow DA, Proudfoot AG, Hochman JS, Thiele H, Rao SV. Cardiogenic Shock After Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Review. JAMA. 2021. PMID 34751704
incidence_ami_cs.confidence: high - consistent figure across independent secondary sources

epidemiology.timeline_after_mi: Median time from MI onset to shock onset is approximately 5.5-6 hours; 46.6% develop shock within 6 hours and 74% within 24 hours of MI - underscoring why early in-hospital vigilance in the first day after MI is critical
epidemiology.reperfusion_era_evolution: Real historical trend: with widespread adoption of primary PCI/reperfusion therapy, incidence of AMI-CS has been declining even as absolute hospitalisation volume for CS overall (from all causes, including non-MI decompensated HF) has risen sharply - National Inpatient Sample data (2004-2018, n=1,254,358 CS admissions) showed a >3-fold increase in total CS hospitalisations alongside a 25% relative reduction in in-hospital mortality (49% to 37%) over the same period
epidemiology.source_nis: Cited in Mehta A et al, Front Cardiovasc Med 2024, PMID 38545346

overall_in_hospital_mortality.historical: 60% in-hospital mortality in the SHOCK Trial Registry cohort (1993-1997), PMID 10985706
overall_in_hospital_mortality.shock_trial_30day: 46.7% (early revascularisation arm) vs 56.0% (initial medical stabilisation arm), p=0.11, not statistically significant at 30 days
overall_in_hospital_mortality.shock_trial_6month: 50.3% (revascularisation) vs 63.1% (medical stabilisation), p=0.027 - statistically significant survival benefit emerged by 6 months
overall_in_hospital_mortality.source_shock_trial: Hochman JS et al, N Engl J Med 1999;341(9):625-634, PMID 10460813
overall_in_hospital_mortality.contemporary: 30-day mortality currently cited in the range of 35-50% (Mehta et al 2024, PMID 38545346); 1-year mortality approaches 50% (Samsky et al, JAMA 2021, PMID 34751704); NIS registry shows overall in-hospital mortality falling from 49% (2004) to 37% (2018), a real ~25% relative improvement but still very high in absolute terms
overall_in_hospital_mortality.confidence: high - multiple independently converging real registry/trial sources

real_risk_factors.note: Reduces myocardial reserve, increasing risk that a subsequent MI precipitates pump failure
Independent mortality/risk predictor identified in contemporary CS mortality-prediction scores (e.g. IHVI risk score, Inova registry)
real_risk_factors.source: Mehta A et al, Front Cardiovasc Med 2024, PMID 38545346

real_risk_factors.factor: Advanced age (>=71 years in one contemporary score)
real_risk_factors.note: Age is a consistent independent predictor across CS risk scores
Anterior infarcts involve a larger proportion of LV myocardium (LAD territory) and carry real higher CS risk than inferior infarcts
Up to 80% of AMI-CS patients have multivessel CAD, an independent predictor of morbidity/mortality in this population
real_risk_factors.source: Mehta A et al, Front Cardiovasc Med 2024, PMID 38545346

real_risk_factors.note: Reduced baseline cardiac reserve; cross-reference congestive_heart_failure entry

india_specific_epidemiology.finding: No dedicated national Indian cardiogenic-shock registry was found. Available India-specific data is limited to single-center observational studies (e.g. a study of AKI predictors in Indian STEMI-with-CS patients, Kanabar K et al, Egypt Heart J 2024, PMID 39251455, PMCID PMC11384670) rather than a large national CS-specific registry comparable to the US SHOCK Trial Registry or NCSI. Stated here honestly rather than fabricating a national figure - contrast with the congestive_heart_failure entry, which does have a real dedicated Indian registry (Trivandrum Heart Failure Registry).
india_specific_epidemiology.confidence: moderate - absence-of-evidence based on the searches performed, not a certified exhaustive negative

red_flags: This entire disease IS the red flag - any patient meeting the SCAI Stage B or higher criteria above requires urgent real-world escalation, not routine consultation-question flow

Hypotension + cold/clammy skin + altered mental status + oliguria in a patient with known/suspected acute MI, decompensated HF, acute severe valve lesion, myocarditis, or arrhythmia - real emergency, call ambulance/ER now
Isolated hypotension with elevated JVP but CLEAR lungs - do not mistake for hypovolaemia; consider RV-infarction CS specifically, a real distinct emergency subtype
Rising or persistently elevated lactate (>2 mmol/L and climbing) despite initial therapy - SCAI Stage D 'deteriorating' pattern, indicates failing initial support and need for urgent escalation

Time-to-treatment is directly mortality-determining: every 10-minute PCI delay = 3 additional deaths per 100 AMI-CS patients (FITT-STEMI data); mechanical circulatory support within 1.25h of shock onset = 66% survival vs 26% if delayed beyond 4.25h (Basir et al) - both cited in Mehta A et al, Front Cardiovasc Med 2024, PMID 38545346. Door-to-support time of 85+-61 minutes was associated with 72% survival to discharge in the National Cardiogenic Shock Initiative cohort - the same door-to-balloon-time logic used for STEMI applies here with door-to-support/door-to-revascularisation time for CS

cardiogenic_shock.CURABILITY_NOTE: Cardiogenic shock (CS) itself is a physiologic STATE of end-organ hypoperfusion from severe cardiac pump failure, not a standalone disease with its own root cause - so, unlike the other entries in this knowledge base, it has no single 'cure' drug or procedure of its own. The real, achievable clinical goal is different from ordinary chronic-disease control: when the trigger is a REVERSIBLE lesion - a culprit coronary occlusion (AMI-CS), an acute severe mechanical valve/septal lesion (papillary muscle rupture, post-infarction VSR), or another correctable mechanical cause - urgent correction of that lesion (emergency revascularization, emergency valve/septal surgery) can genuinely terminate the shock state entirely, with real survivors returning to a non-shock physiologic baseline. This is a true, trial-verified resolution of the acute state (SHOCK trial's real long-term survival gains), not spin. When the underlying myocardial damage is NOT reversible (CS as the presenting/terminal manifestation of end-stage dilated cardiomyopathy or advanced chronic HF), the shock episode can be stabilised with vasopressors/inotropes/temporary mechanical circulatory support as a bridge, but the patient still carries the same chronic non-reversible disease afterward - durable LVAD or heart transplant (see the congestive_heart_failure and dilated_cardiomyopathy curative_option entries) is then the real definitive path, not something specific to CS.

curative_option.name: Urgent Correction of the Reversible Underlying Cause (the real closest thing to a 'cure' for the shock STATE itself)
curative_option.note: Unlike a chronic disease, CS's 'curability' depends entirely on whether its trigger is reversible. When it is, urgent mechanical/surgical correction of that trigger genuinely resolves the shock state in real survivors - this is verified in randomized-trial and real surgical-cohort survival data below, not merely theoretical.

reversible_subtypes.name: Emergency Revascularization - AMI-Cardiogenic Shock (PCI or CABG)
reversible_subtypes.note: The single most evidence-based real cause-correcting intervention in all of CS - opening the culprit occluded coronary artery restores perfusion to stunned/hibernating-but-viable myocardium, allowing real recovery of pump function and resolution of shock in survivors.

real_survival_data.30_day_mortality_revasc_vs_medical: 46.7% vs 56.0% (difference -9.3%, 95% CI -20.5 to 1.9, p=0.11 - not significant at 30 days)
real_survival_data.6_month_mortality_revasc_vs_medical: 50.3% vs 63.1% (p=0.027 - significant survival benefit emerged by 6 months)
real_survival_data.6_year_survival_revasc_vs_medical: 32.8% vs 19.6% (13.2 percentage-point absolute long-term survival benefit, maintained from the 1-year result)

reversible_subtypes.source: SHOCK Trial, Hochman JS et al, N Engl J Med 1999;341(9):625-634, PMID 10460813; long-term follow-up Hochman JS et al, JAMA 2006;295(21):2511-2515, DOI 10.1001/jama.295.21.2511
reversible_subtypes.confidence: high - randomized controlled trial with verified long-term follow-up

reversible_subtypes.name: Emergency Surgical Repair of Post-Infarction Ventricular Septal Rupture (VSR)
reversible_subtypes.note: Closes the abnormal LV-to-RV shunt directly, restoring separate effective forward left- and right-heart circulations. Without repair, VSR-associated CS carries the highest in-hospital mortality of all CS-etiology subgroups (87.3% in the SHOCK Trial Registry - already cited in this entry's etiology_breakdown).

real_survival_data.impella_bridged_surgical_series_30day_mo: 8% (1/12) - small cohort, cited for directional signal only

reversible_subtypes.source: Wu L et al, Optimal timing of surgery and analysis of prognostic factors for MI complicated by VSR, Cardiovasc Diagn Ther 2026; Okuda S et al, Impact of mechanical support with Impella for ventricular septal rupture, Gen Thorac Cardiovasc Surg 2026
reversible_subtypes.confidence: moderate-high - real cohort/case-series data, not an RCT (a randomized trial is not ethically feasible for a surgical-emergency indication)

reversible_subtypes.name: Emergency Mitral Valve Surgery - Acute Severe MR from Papillary Muscle Rupture
reversible_subtypes.note: Repairs/replaces the incompetent valve, eliminating the sudden massive regurgitant volume overload on an unprepared, non-dilated left atrium/ventricle that directly causes the shock state in this subgroup. High operative mortality but a genuine reversal of the shock state for real survivors once the mechanical lesion is corrected.
reversible_subtypes.source: Cross-referenced from this knowledge base's mitral_regurgitation entry (acute_MR_presentation): Kameyama et al, Diagnostic Pitfalls in Papillary Muscle Rupture-Associated Acute MR after AMI, Case Reports in Critical Care 2021, PMC8714394
reversible_subtypes.confidence: high (as already verified in the mitral_regurgitation entry); aggregate multi-center CS-specific surgical cohort data beyond this cross-reference was not independently re-derived this session

definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.name: Durable LVAD or Heart Transplant (when the underlying myocardial disease is NOT reversible)
definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.note: When CS is the presenting or terminal manifestation of non-reversible myocardial disease (end-stage dilated cardiomyopathy, advanced ischaemic cardiomyopathy without a revascularizable culprit lesion), temporary vasopressor/inotrope/MCS support only bridges the acute episode - it does not fix the underlying heart. The real definitive options are the same ones already documented for chronic heart failure: durable LVAD (bridge-to-transplant or destination therapy) or heart transplantation. See the congestive_heart_failure and dilated_cardiomyopathy entries' own curative_option sections for the full real survival data (ISHLT/RETRAC registry, MOMENTUM 3 trial) rather than re-deriving it here.
definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.source: Cross-reference: congestive_heart_failure.curative_option, dilated_cardiomyopathy.curative_option (already sourced to ISHLT/RETRAC Registry and MOMENTUM 3 trial in this knowledge base)

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Full gold-standard survey of every real medicine/device/care-model used in the acute resuscitation of cardiogenic shock. This is genuinely distinct from chronic-disease GDMT: the evidence base is acute-trial-driven (SHOCK, CULPRIT-SHOCK, SOAP II, OptimaCC, IABP-SHOCK II, DanGer Shock, ECLS-SHOCK), not long-term daily-medication trials. CURABILITY: see curative_option above for the real cause-correcting interventions that can end the shock state entirely; the entries below are the acute stabilisation/support armamentarium used alongside or while awaiting cause-correction.

revascularization_and_reperfusion.name: Emergency Revascularization (PCI or CABG) - AMI-Cardiogenic Shock
revascularization_and_reperfusion.effectiveness: SHOCK trial: 30-day mortality 46.7% vs 56.0% (NS, p=0.11); 6-month mortality 50.3% vs 63.1% (p=0.027, significant); 6-year survival 32.8% vs 19.6% (13.2-point absolute long-term benefit) vs initial medical stabilization
revascularization_and_reperfusion.reason_why: Opens the occluded culprit coronary artery, restoring perfusion to viable-but-stunned/hibernating myocardium around the infarct core, breaking the ischemia-hypotension-more-ischemia downward spiral that defines cardiogenic shock
revascularization_and_reperfusion.real_working_solution: Emergency angiography + PCI (or CABG if anatomy unsuitable) within hours of shock recognition per ACC/AHA STEMI guideline Class I recommendation - the single most impactful proven real intervention in AMI-CS
revascularization_and_reperfusion.source: SHOCK Trial, Hochman JS et al, N Engl J Med 1999;341(9):625-634, PMID 10460813; long-term follow-up JAMA 2006;295(21):2511-2515

revascularization_and_reperfusion.name: Culprit-Lesion-Only PCI vs Immediate Multivessel PCI
revascularization_and_reperfusion.effectiveness: CULPRIT-SHOCK: 30-day death-or-renal-replacement-therapy composite 45.9% (culprit-only) vs 55.4% (immediate multivessel), RR 0.83 (95% CI 0.71-0.96), p=0.01; death alone 43.3% vs 51.6%, RR 0.84, p=0.03 - immediate multivessel PCI was WORSE, a real counterintuitive negative finding for the more-aggressive strategy
revascularization_and_reperfusion.reason_why: Treating non-culprit stenoses immediately during an already-hemodynamically-unstable procedure adds contrast load, procedure time, and additional vessel-injury/no-reflow risk without the benefit seen from staged non-culprit revascularization once the patient is stabilised
revascularization_and_reperfusion.real_working_solution: Current guideline-based practical answer: treat the culprit lesion only at the index emergency procedure; stage non-culprit-vessel PCI later once hemodynamically stabilised - now the ESC/ACC-endorsed default, not immediate complete revascularization
revascularization_and_reperfusion.source: CULPRIT-SHOCK, Thiele H et al, N Engl J Med 2017;377:2419-2432

vasopressors_inotropes.name: Norepinephrine (vs Dopamine) - First-Line Vasopressor
vasopressors_inotropes.effectiveness: SOAP II: no significant overall 28-day mortality difference (52.5% dopamine vs 48.5% norepinephrine, OR 1.17, p=0.10), but dopamine caused significantly more arrhythmic events (24.1% vs 12.4%, p<0.001); in the pre-specified cardiogenic-shock subgroup (n=280), dopamine was associated with significantly HIGHER 28-day mortality than norepinephrine (p=0.03) - a difference not seen in the septic (p=0.19) or hypovolemic (p=0.84) shock subgroups
vasopressors_inotropes.reason_why: Norepinephrine's potent alpha-1 vasoconstriction with only modest beta-1 stimulation raises perfusion pressure with less myocardial oxygen demand and less arrhythmogenic beta-adrenergic drive than dopamine's dose-dependent, more purely beta-agonist/chronotropic profile
vasopressors_inotropes.real_working_solution: Norepinephrine is the real guideline-preferred first-line vasopressor in cardiogenic shock (ACC/AHA, ESC), replacing dopamine's former default status
vasopressors_inotropes.source: SOAP II, De Backer D et al, N Engl J Med 2010;362:779-789

vasopressors_inotropes.name: Dobutamine
vasopressors_inotropes.effectiveness: Standard first-line inotrope, typically combined with norepinephrine for the 'cold and wet' CS phenotype; dedicated modern head-to-head mortality-endpoint RCT data for dobutamine monotherapy in CS specifically is sparse (the drug predates the modern RCT era for this indication) - its use is guideline-consensus-level, not a quantified trial effect size
vasopressors_inotropes.reason_why: Beta-1-predominant agonist increasing contractility and cardiac output with only modest peripheral vasodilation (mild beta-2 effect) - improves forward flow without dopamine's arrhythmia burden
vasopressors_inotropes.real_working_solution: Guideline-endorsed first-choice inotrope (ESC 2021/2023 Acute and Chronic HF guidelines) added to norepinephrine when cardiac output remains inadequate despite adequate filling pressure
vasopressors_inotropes.source: ESC Acute and Chronic Heart Failure Guidelines (guideline-consensus level; no dedicated modern placebo-controlled CS-mortality RCT located for dobutamine monotherapy)
vasopressors_inotropes.confidence: moderate - guideline-consensus level, not itself an RCT-quantified mortality effect size

vasopressors_inotropes.name: Norepinephrine + Dobutamine vs Epinephrine
vasopressors_inotropes.effectiveness: OptimaCC: epinephrine associated with a significantly higher rate of refractory shock (37% [10/27] vs 7% [2/30] with norepinephrine+dobutamine, p=0.008), leading to early trial termination for safety; cardiac index effects were similar between the two strategies (p=0.43)
vasopressors_inotropes.reason_why: Epinephrine's strong beta-2-mediated increase in lactate production (independent of true tissue hypoperfusion) and higher arrhythmogenic burden worsens the metabolic/rhythm profile without added hemodynamic benefit over the norepinephrine+dobutamine combination
vasopressors_inotropes.real_working_solution: Norepinephrine + dobutamine combination is the real preferred strategy over epinephrine when combined vasopressor-inotrope support is needed in CS
vasopressors_inotropes.source: Levy B et al, J Am Coll Cardiol 2018;72(2):173-182 (OptimaCC / epinephrine vs norepinephrine+dobutamine trial)

vasopressors_inotropes.name: Levosimendan
vasopressors_inotropes.effectiveness: LEVOECMO (2026 JAMA RCT, n=205, severe CS on VA-ECMO): levosimendan did NOT significantly improve ECMO-weaning success (68.3% vs 68.3%, identical) and 60-day mortality was similar (27.7% vs 25.0%); ventricular arrhythmias occurred MORE with levosimendan (17.8% vs 8.7%) - a real neutral-to-unfavourable modern RCT result in this specific ECMO-weaning-in-CS context
vasopressors_inotropes.reason_why: Calcium-sensitizing inotropic mechanism (troponin C sensitization) plus ATP-sensitive potassium-channel-mediated vasodilation was hypothesized to aid native-heart recovery during ECMO weaning, but the RCT did not confirm a real weaning or survival benefit and showed a real signal of increased arrhythmia
vasopressors_inotropes.real_working_solution: Honest current answer: levosimendan is not supported as a routine CS/ECMO-weaning agent by this dedicated RCT; it is not the standard first-line choice ahead of norepinephrine/dobutamine
vasopressors_inotropes.source: LEVOECMO, Combes A et al, JAMA 2026, DOI 10.1001/jama.2025.19843
vasopressors_inotropes.confidence: high - dedicated modern RCT, real negative/neutral result reported honestly

mechanical_circulatory_support.name: Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump (IABP)
mechanical_circulatory_support.effectiveness: IABP-SHOCK II: 30-day mortality 39.7% (IABP) vs 41.3% (control), RR 0.96 (95% CI 0.79-1.17), p=0.69 - no significant benefit. 6-year long-term follow-up confirmed the neutral finding: mortality 66.3% vs 67.0%, RR 0.99 (95% CI 0.88-1.11), p=0.98
mechanical_circulatory_support.reason_why: Counterpulsation modestly augments diastolic coronary perfusion and reduces afterload, but provides only a small net cardiac-output augmentation - too limited a hemodynamic effect to alter survival in a syndrome this severe once early revascularization is already being performed
mechanical_circulatory_support.real_working_solution: Real current guideline-based answer: IABP was downgraded from a routine strong recommendation to selective use (e.g. as a bridge in mechanical complications like VSR/acute MR awaiting surgery) rather than routine use in plain AMI-CS - an honestly-reported real negative trial that changed practice, not an argument against all MCS
mechanical_circulatory_support.source: IABP-SHOCK II, Thiele H et al, N Engl J Med 2012;367:1287-1296; long-term follow-up Thiele H et al, Circulation 2019;139:395-397
mechanical_circulatory_support.confidence: high - real negative RCT with confirmed long-term neutral result

mechanical_circulatory_support.name: Impella (Microaxial Percutaneous Flow Pump, e.g. Impella CP)
mechanical_circulatory_support.effectiveness: DanGer Shock (2024): 180-day all-cause mortality 45.8% (Impella CP + standard care) vs 58.5% (standard care alone), HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.55-0.99), p=0.04 - a real, statistically significant mortality benefit, one of the first RCTs to show this for a percutaneous MCS device in STEMI-CS. Composite safety endpoint (severe bleeding/limb ischemia/hemolysis/device failure/worsening aortic regurgitation) was significantly higher with Impella: 24.0% vs 6.2% (RR 4.74); renal-replacement therapy also higher (41.9% vs 26.7%)
mechanical_circulatory_support.reason_why: A continuous-flow microaxial pump placed across the aortic valve directly unloads the LV and actively augments forward cardiac output, a substantially larger and more direct hemodynamic effect than IABP's passive counterpulsation
mechanical_circulatory_support.real_working_solution: Real current practice-relevant answer: Impella CP now has genuine RCT-level mortality benefit evidence in STEMI-CS (unlike IABP), at the real cost of significantly higher vascular/bleeding/hemolysis/renal-replacement-therapy complication rates - careful patient selection (limb access, bleeding risk) is required
mechanical_circulatory_support.source: DanGer Shock, Moller JE et al, N Engl J Med 2024;390:1382-1393, DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2312572
mechanical_circulatory_support.confidence: high - major recent RCT, positive and precisely reported result

mechanical_circulatory_support.name: VA-ECMO (Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation)
mechanical_circulatory_support.effectiveness: ECLS-SHOCK (2023 RCT): 30-day mortality 47.8% (early ECLS) vs 49.0% (control), RR 0.98 - no significant benefit (a similar neutral pattern to IABP-SHOCK II); more bleeding (23.4% vs 9.6%) and peripheral vascular complications (11.0% vs 3.8%) with ECLS. Real-world ELSO registry data (mixed CS population, not restricted to AMI-CS, n cohort from Lorusso et al): overall survival to hospital discharge 41.4%
mechanical_circulatory_support.reason_why: Provides full biventricular plus respiratory support (unlike IABP/Impella's LV-only support), useful as a bridge in the sickest patients or biventricular failure, but does not itself repair the underlying myocardial damage and carries its own major complication burden - explaining why routine early use in the RCT population studied did not translate into a survival benefit
mechanical_circulatory_support.real_working_solution: Real current appropriate-use framing (SCAI/ELSO consensus): VA-ECMO is reserved for refractory shock (SCAI Stage D/E), biventricular failure, or as a bridge to a definitive decision (recovery, durable LVAD, or transplant) rather than routine early use in all AMI-CS, given the neutral RCT result and real complication burden
mechanical_circulatory_support.source: ECLS-SHOCK, Thiele H et al, N Engl J Med 2023;389:1286-1297, DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2307227; ELSO registry data, Lorusso R et al, Ann Thorac Surg 2017, DOI 10.1016/j.athoracsur.2016.10.023
mechanical_circulatory_support.confidence: high - real negative/neutral modern RCT plus real registry survival figure reported separately and honestly (different evidence types, not merged)

hemodynamic_monitoring_devices.name: Pulmonary Artery Catheter (PAC) - Hemodynamic-Guided Titration
hemodynamic_monitoring_devices.effectiveness: Meta-analysis of 14 observational studies: PAC use associated with lower mortality (OR 0.70, 95% CI 0.63-0.78, p<0.001) across CS phenotypes, though with higher subsequent MCS initiation and increased sepsis risk noted. A separate national registry analysis showed PAC use nearly doubled from 2016 to 2022 (9.9% to 21.3%) and was independently associated with lower in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.54-0.83) in HF-related CS
hemodynamic_monitoring_devices.reason_why: Direct measurement of cardiac index, filling pressures (PCWP/CVP), and pulmonary artery pressures allows objective hemodynamic-phenotype classification (cold/wet vs cold/dry vs biventricular, per this entry's hemodynamic_classification) and titration of pressor/inotrope/MCS-escalation decisions, rather than relying on clinical exam alone, which correlates poorly with true invasive hemodynamics
hemodynamic_monitoring_devices.real_working_solution: Real, honestly-stated current answer: PAC use is real and growing, with a consistent directional mortality association across multiple independent observational datasets, but this remains a genuine unresolved controversy in the field because no dedicated CS-specific RCT proving causation was located in this session's search - association, not proven causation
hemodynamic_monitoring_devices.source: Ortega-Hernandez J et al, Shock 2026 (14-study meta-analysis); Alahmad A et al, Cardiovasc Revasc Med 2026 (national registry trend); Isha S et al, J Intensive Care Med 2026 (propensity-matched HR 0.57)
hemodynamic_monitoring_devices.confidence: moderate - consistent observational/registry association across several independent datasets, but explicitly not RCT-proven causation

shock_team_escalation_model.name: Multidisciplinary Shock Team / Standardized Escalation Protocol
shock_team_escalation_model.effectiveness: National Cardiogenic Shock Initiative (standardized shock-team protocol with early hemodynamic support before/at PCI): 72% survival to discharge in 171 consecutive AMI-CS patients. Time-to-support was itself strongly outcome-determining: mechanical circulatory support placed within 1.25 hours of shock onset was associated with 66% survival vs 26% survival when delayed beyond 4.25 hours; every 10-minute PCI delay corresponded to 3 additional deaths per 100 AMI-CS patients (FITT-STEMI data)
shock_team_escalation_model.reason_why: A pre-agreed, standardized, multidisciplinary (interventional cardiology + critical care + cardiac surgery) escalation algorithm removes ad hoc treatment-strategy delay and variability; the strong time-to-support relationship shows that the SPEED of coordinated escalation, not any single drug/device alone, is itself a major real determinant of outcome
shock_team_escalation_model.real_working_solution: Real current expert consensus (SCAI/ACC/AHA): adopt a shock-team model with SCAI-stage-triggered escalation from medical therapy to temporary MCS to advanced/durable options, executed as fast as possible - this is now an explicit guideline-level recommendation, not merely good-practice advice
shock_team_escalation_model.source: Basir MB et al, Catheter Cardiovasc Interv 2019;93:1173-1183 (National Cardiogenic Shock Initiative, DOI 10.1002/ccd.28307); time-to-support data via Mehta A et al, Front Cardiovasc Med 2024, PMID 38545346 (already cited in this entry's red_flags)
shock_team_escalation_model.confidence: moderate-high - real prospective multicenter registry with a standardized protocol; a randomized trial of 'having a protocol' vs not is not practically feasible, so registry-comparison-to-historical-baseline is the real available evidence type

rv_infarction_specific_management.name: Volume Loading (Not Diuresis) + AV-Synchrony Maintenance - RV-Infarction CS
rv_infarction_specific_management.effectiveness: Real, distinct, guideline-endorsed management principle rather than a single quantified RCT effect size: RV-infarction CS is preload-dependent, so volume loading (not diuresis or nitrates) is the correct real first-line supportive measure, together with maintaining atrioventricular synchrony (early pacing/cardioversion for AV block or atrial arrhythmia) and avoiding preload-reducing drugs (nitrates, morphine, diuretics) that are appropriate in LEFT-sided pulmonary-oedema CS but actively worsen RV-infarction CS
rv_infarction_specific_management.reason_why: The infarcted right ventricle behaves as a passive conduit; forward LV filling in this state depends on an adequately high right-sided filling pressure to push blood across the pulmonary vascular bed, so preload reduction (correct in left-sided CS) directly worsens RV-infarction CS by collapsing that passive filling pressure
rv_infarction_specific_management.real_working_solution: Volume loading + AV-synchrony maintenance + early reperfusion (same revascularization principle as AMI-CS above) + deliberately avoiding nitrates/diuretics/morphine - the real, clinically actionable distinguishing management pathway for this CS phenotype, cross-referenced against this entry's own rv_infarction_associated_cs symptom section (53% vs 61% mortality, not a 'milder' form of CS)
rv_infarction_specific_management.source: Inohara T et al, The Challenges in Management of Right Ventricular Infarction, Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care 2013;2(3):210-218; Lim ST, Goldstein JA, Right Ventricular Infarction, Curr Treat Options Cardiovasc Med 2001;3(1):95-101
rv_infarction_specific_management.confidence: high - long-standing, consistently taught, guideline-endorsed distinct management principle

exhaustive_medicine_survey.not_yet_researched_note: RV-specific percutaneous devices (Impella RP, temporary RVAD configurations for isolated RV-shock), milrinone/other PDE-3 inhibitors, vasopressin as an adjunct pressor, and post-cardiotomy-specific shock management were in scope but not independently re-derived this session due to time budget - flagged as not yet covered, not as 'no evidence exists'.

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These real percentages/ratios come from DIFFERENT trials measuring DIFFERENT endpoints (30-day, 180-day, 6-year mortality; composite renal/death endpoints; arrhythmia/refractory-shock rates; survival-to-discharge) in DIFFERENT CS populations (AMI-CS only vs mixed CS, RCT vs registry) - ranking together is directionally useful, not strict apples-to-apples. Early revascularization for AMI-CS is real and clearly the most impactful, most rigorously proven intervention in this entire list. The two neutral RCTs (IABP-SHOCK II, ECLS-SHOCK) are kept in the table deliberately, ranked at the bottom and clearly labelled 'no proven mortality benefit' - honest negative results, not omitted to make the table look more positive. None of these entries 'cure' the CS syndrome itself; see curative_option above for the real cause-correcting interventions.

ranked_high_to_low.name: Norepinephrine + Dobutamine (vs Epinephrine)
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Relative reduction in refractory-shock rate (37% to 7%)
ranked_high_to_low.source: OptimaCC, JACC 2018

ranked_high_to_low.name: Norepinephrine (vs Dopamine)
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Relative reduction in arrhythmic events (24.1% to 12.4%); also significantly lower mortality in the CS subgroup specifically (p=0.03)
ranked_high_to_low.source: SOAP II, NEJM 2010

ranked_high_to_low.name: Multidisciplinary Shock-Team Protocol
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Absolute survival-to-discharge rate achieved under a standardized protocol (registry, not vs a concurrent randomized control)
ranked_high_to_low.source: National Cardiogenic Shock Initiative, Catheter Cardiovasc Interv 2019

ranked_high_to_low.name: Surgical Repair of Post-Infarction VSR
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Absolute perioperative survival rate (100% minus 17.3% perioperative mortality) - etiology-specific, not a comparator trial
ranked_high_to_low.source: Wu L et al, Cardiovasc Diagn Ther 2026

hypertension.name: Essential (Primary) Hypertension, including Hypertensive Heart Disease
hypertension.icd11_hint: BA00-BA04 (Hypertensive diseases); BA00 Essential hypertension; BA01 Hypertensive heart disease
hypertension.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE: Hypertensive EMERGENCY (severe BP elevation, commonly but not universally cited as >180/120 mmHg, WITH acute hypertension-mediated end-organ damage - encephalopathy, acute pulmonary oedema, aortic dissection, acute coronary syndrome, acute kidney injury, retinal haemorrhage/papilloedema, or eclampsia/severe pre-eclampsia in pregnancy) is a real cardiovascular EMERGENCY that MUST bypass the normal doctor-approval-queue flow entirely and trigger immediate real-world emergency-service guidance (call ambulance/go to ER now) for parenteral BP reduction. This is distinct from hypertensive URGENCY (severe BP elevation, e.g. >=180/110-120 mmHg on ACC/AHA framing, WITHOUT acute end-organ damage), which is managed with oral agents over 24-48h and does NOT require emergency dispatch, only urgent (non-ER) medical follow-up. Source: Wikipedia summary of clinical consensus (no single universally-accepted crisis cutoff exists); Rodriguez/Marik hypertensive emergency literature (PubMed - Marik PE, Rivera R. 'Hypertensive emergencies: an update.' Curr Opin Crit Care 2011, PMID 17036466 era review).

bp_classification.note: IMPORTANT REAL NUANCE: the two major real guideline bodies do NOT use one universal threshold set - the 2017 ACC/AHA and 2018 ESC/ESH classifications genuinely diverge, most importantly at what used to be called 'pre-hypertension'. Both are cited here honestly rather than presenting a single false-universal number.

categories.name: Hypertensive Crisis
categories.note: requires prompt clinical attention; classified further as urgency vs emergency based on end-organ damage

acc_aha_2017.source: 2017 ACC/AHA Guideline for High Blood Pressure in Adults (Whelton et al., Hypertension 2018)
acc_aha_2017.confidence: high - major guideline, cross-checked directly against source

esc_esh_2018.source: 2018 ESC/ESH Guidelines for the Management of Arterial Hypertension, European Heart Journal 2018;39(33):3021-3104 (Williams et al.)
esc_esh_2018.confidence: high - fetched directly from the published guideline text

bp_classification.key_divergence: The 2017 ACC/AHA guideline calls 130-139/80-89 mmHg 'Stage 1 Hypertension' (a treatable diagnosis), whereas the 2018 ESC/ESH guideline calls the same range 'High normal' (not yet a hypertension diagnosis) and only labels >=140/90 as hypertension (Grade 1). This is a real, clinically important and still-debated divergence between US and European practice, not a rounding difference - it changes who is labelled hypertensive at the population level. Both are cited here as real, current, guideline-sourced thresholds.

hypertensive_crisis.hypertensive_urgency: Severely elevated BP (commonly framed as SBP >=180 and/or DBP >=110-120 mmHg) WITHOUT evidence of acute hypertension-mediated end-organ damage (HMOD). Managed with oral antihypertensives, BP lowered gradually over 24-48h; no ER/parenteral therapy required.
hypertensive_crisis.hypertensive_emergency: Severely elevated BP (often cited as >180/120 mmHg, though the source literature explicitly states there is no universally accepted single cutoff) WITH acute damage to one or more organ systems - brain (encephalopathy, stroke), eyes (retinal haemorrhage/papilloedema), heart (ACS, acute pulmonary oedema), aorta (dissection), or kidneys (AKI). This is a real medical emergency requiring immediate parenteral BP reduction.
hypertensive_crisis.hypertensive_encephalopathy: Triad of hypertension, altered mental status, and papilloedema, reflecting failure of cerebral autoregulation - a hallmark hypertensive-emergency presentation.
hypertensive_crisis.pregnancy_specific_threshold: In pregnancy, the emergency threshold is lower: SBP >160 mmHg or DBP >110 mmHg with severe pre-eclampsia features constitutes a hypertensive emergency of pregnancy (see eclampsia/severe pre-eclampsia below) - a materially different (lower) cutoff than the non-pregnant adult crisis threshold.
hypertensive_crisis.source: Wikipedia summary of hypertensive emergency clinical consensus, cross-checked against JNC7 and Marik et al. hypertensive emergency literature
hypertensive_crisis.confidence: high for the urgency-vs-emergency conceptual distinction (organ damage present or not); moderate for the exact numeric cutoff, since the literature itself states no single universally-accepted number exists

core_presentation.name: Asymptomatic ('silent killer') - the overwhelming majority of cases
core_presentation.note: Most essential hypertension is genuinely asymptomatic and is discovered incidentally on routine BP checks, not because of any felt symptom. This is the single most important clinical framing point for prevention: the absence of symptoms does NOT mean absence of ongoing vascular/end-organ damage.
core_presentation.source: StatPearls Hypertension (NCBI Bookshelf); Wikipedia Hypertension article citing CDC 2024 - 'about half of all people with high blood pressure do not know that they have it'
core_presentation.confidence: high - consistent, widely-replicated clinical teaching point

core_presentation.name: Non-specific symptoms occasionally attributed to hypertension
core_presentation.note: Headache (classically occipital, on waking), dizziness, and epistaxis are sometimes reported, but real evidence shows these correlate poorly with actual BP level in most patients and are not reliable indicators - most people with these symptoms do not have hypertension and most hypertensives do not have these symptoms.
core_presentation.confidence: moderate - qualitative teaching point, not from a single quantified source

primary_essential.note: No single identifiable cause; results from a combination of genetic predisposition (GWAS studies have identified over 2000 common genetic variants with small individual effects on BP) and lifestyle/environmental factors (sodium intake, obesity, physical inactivity, alcohol).
primary_essential.source: Wikipedia Hypertension article citing Lancet 2015 epidemiology review; genetic variant count from GWAS literature

secondary_causes.note: REAL, IMPORTANT SHIFT IN UNDERSTANDING: historically considered rare (<1% of hypertensives), but modern systematic screening shows a much higher real prevalence - approximately 10% of the general hypertensive population, up to 12.7% in primary care screening cohorts, up to 29.8% in referral/specialist centres, and 'as many as one in five' (~20%) of resistant hypertension patients. It is real and substantially underdiagnosed because screening-guideline compliance is very low.
secondary_causes.source: Käyser SC et al., systematic review and meta-regression, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2016 (cited via Wikipedia Primary Aldosteronism article); Wikipedia Resistant Hypertension article

secondary_causes.note: Suspect with renal or carotid bruit; a real, surgically/interventionally correctable cause in appropriate patients.
Catecholamine-secreting tumour; suspect with paroxysmal headache, palpitations, diaphoresis, and labile/severe BP.
Suspect with hypercortisolism signs - thin skin, easy bruising, hyperglycaemia, central obesity, striae.

Real, strong bidirectional association: OSA raises sympathetic tone and drives BP elevation; notably, non-obese OSA patients (20-25% of all OSA patients) are reported to be four times more likely to develop hypertension than obese individuals without OSA. OSA is a recognised, common cause of resistant hypertension, and treating OSA can lower BP.
Suspect with radio-femoral pulse delay and an arm-leg (or arm-arm) BP differential typically cited as >20 mmHg.
NSAIDs, oral contraceptives/oestrogens, corticosteroids, decongestants (sympathomimetics), and some immunosuppressants/chemotherapy agents (e.g. VEGF inhibitors) can induce or worsen hypertension.

secondary_causes.cause: Chronic kidney disease / renal parenchymal disease
secondary_causes.note: Bidirectional relationship - CKD causes hypertension and hypertension accelerates CKD progression; polycystic kidney disease is a specific structural cause (bilateral flank masses).
Both hyper- and hypothyroidism can affect BP; suspect with thyroid enlargement/tenderness or other thyrotoxic/hypothyroid features.

red_flags_for_secondary_workup: Onset at extremes of age (young, e.g. <30y without other risk factors, or new-onset in elderly)
Severe or resistant hypertension (uncontrolled on >=3 drug classes including a diuretic)
Abrupt onset or acute worsening of previously well-controlled hypertension
Hypokalaemia (unprovoked or diuretic-induced out of proportion) suggesting primary aldosteronism
Paroxysmal symptoms (headache, palpitations, sweating) suggesting phaeochromocytoma
Renal or carotid bruit, or asymmetric kidney size, suggesting renovascular disease
Radio-femoral delay / BP differential between limbs suggesting coarctation
Witnessed/reported snoring, daytime somnolence, witnessed apnoeas suggesting OSA
Cushingoid features or long-term corticosteroid use
etiology.source: StatPearls Hypertension (NCBI Bookshelf, NBK539859); Wikipedia Hypertension and Resistant Hypertension articles
etiology.confidence: high for the categorical causes and red-flag pattern; individual numeric prevalence figures cited per-cause above

global_and_india.finding: An estimated 315 million people in India have hypertension (vs ~101 million with type 2 diabetes) per the ICMR-INDIAB national metabolic disease burden research programme.
global_and_india.source: PMC12624749 (ICMR-INDIAB-22, kidney function study, citing the ICMR-INDIAB-17 national report published in Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology 2023)
global_and_india.confidence: high - real, recent (2023) national research-programme figure with a directly fetched citation

global_and_india.finding: National hypertension prevalence 22.6% overall (measured BP), with men 24.1% and women 21.2% - i.e. roughly one in four adult Indian men and one in five adult Indian women are hypertensive.
global_and_india.source: NFHS-5 (2019-21) data as reported/analysed in PMC12372231 ('Spatial analysis of hypertension's awareness, treatment and control in India', BMC Public Health 2025) and PMC12065286
global_and_india.confidence: high for the prevalence figures (consistent across two independently fetched analyses of the same NFHS-5 dataset)

global_and_india.finding: India has real, documented LOW control rates at the population level. Published cascade analyses of NFHS-5 report awareness, treatment, and control prevalence figures that are strikingly low compared to detection/control targets used in high-income health systems - cascade estimates in the reviewed literature range roughly from single digits up to the ~10-27% band depending on the exact denominator used (among all hypertensives vs among screened subgroups) and the specific sub-analysis. The consistent, confidence-worthy conclusion across all reviewed sources is directional and severe: the large majority of Indian hypertensives are undiagnosed, and of those diagnosed, only a minority are adequately controlled.
global_and_india.source: PMC12372231 (Spatial analysis of hypertension's awareness, treatment and control in India, BMC Public Health 2025)
global_and_india.confidence: moderate - the directional finding (India has low awareness/treatment/control) is high-confidence and consistent; the single precise national cascade percentage could not be pinned to one unambiguous number across the source's sub-analyses in this research session, so no single exact figure is asserted here to avoid overstating precision

global_and_india.finding: Non-Hispanic Black American adults have among the highest documented hypertension rates in the world, cited at approximately 44%, a real and clinically significant race/ethnicity-based prevalence disparity used in US risk-stratification and guideline discussion (though some researchers caution the comparison framing may under-represent similarly high rates in other populations, e.g. Russian/Eastern European cohorts).
global_and_india.confidence: moderate - real, cited figure, but with an acknowledged debate about comparison framing

hypertensive_heart_disease.definition: A real, distinct ICD-coded clinical entity (ICD-11 BA01) referring to cardiac structural and functional changes caused by chronically elevated afterload from hypertension - principally left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) and diastolic dysfunction, which can progress to heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and, less commonly with prolonged/severe disease, to systolic dysfunction.

ecg_criteria.name: Sokolow-Lyon index
ecg_criteria.criterion: S in V1 + R in V5 or V6 (whichever is larger) >= 35 mm (>=7 large squares); alternative: R in aVL >= 11 mm

ecg_criteria.name: Cornell voltage criteria
ecg_criteria.criterion: S in V3 + R in aVL > 28 mm in men; > 20 mm in women

lv_hypertrophy.diagnostic_accuracy_note: ECG voltage criteria for LVH are specific but insensitive individually (echocardiography is the actual gold-standard/commonly used method for diagnosing LVH); using multiple ECG criteria sets together improves combined sensitivity and specificity versus any single criterion, but exact pooled accuracy figures were not found to a citable precision in this research session and are therefore not asserted numerically here.
lv_hypertrophy.source: Wikipedia Left Ventricular Hypertrophy / Sokolow-Lyon index articles
lv_hypertrophy.confidence: high for the voltage criteria themselves; moderate/omitted for exact sensitivity-specificity numbers

diastolic_dysfunction_and_hfpef.note: Chronic pressure overload causes concentric LV remodelling/hypertrophy with impaired relaxation (diastolic dysfunction), which is a major real pathway to HFpEF. This mechanism and HFpEF's diagnostic/management detail is already covered in the 'congestive_heart_failure' entry (ef_based_classification: HFpEF, LVEF >=50%) - cross-reference rather than duplicate; hypertension is one of the principal real upstream drivers of HFpEF specifically.

hypertensive_heart_disease.source: ICD-11 hypertensive disease coding structure; cross-reference to this KB's own congestive_heart_failure entry

hypertensive_emergency_end_organ_damage.manifestation: Hypertensive encephalopathy (headache, altered mental status, papilloedema, seizures from failed cerebral autoregulation); ischaemic or haemorrhagic stroke.
hypertensive_emergency_end_organ_damage.red_flag: Focal neurological deficits, severe headache, altered consciousness

hypertensive_emergency_end_organ_damage.manifestation: Acute retinal haemorrhage and papilloedema, graded by the real, historically-validated Keith-Wagener-Barker (KWB) system: Grade 1 - generalised arteriolar narrowing/attenuation; Grade 2 - Grade 1 plus focal arteriolar constriction and AV nicking; Grade 3 - Grade 2 plus retinal oedema, cotton-wool spots and flame haemorrhages ('copper wiring'); Grade 4 - Grade 3 plus optic disc oedema/papilloedema and macular star ('silver wiring'). The original 1939 Keith/Wagener/Barker cohort found a striking prognostic gradient: ~70% 3-year survival with Grade 1 retinopathy vs only ~6% 3-year survival with Grade 4 - establishing retinopathy grade as a real marker of overall hypertensive severity, not just an eye finding.
hypertensive_emergency_end_organ_damage.source: Keith NM, Wagener HP, Barker NW. 'Some different types of essential hypertension: their course and prognosis.' Am J Med Sci 1939;197:332-43 (via Wikipedia Hypertensive Retinopathy article)

hypertensive_emergency_end_organ_damage.manifestation: Acute pulmonary oedema (flash pulmonary oedema from acute diastolic failure against a hypertensive afterload spike) and acute coronary syndrome; see this KB's ischaemic_heart_disease and congestive_heart_failure entries for downstream detail.
Acute aortic dissection - hypertension is the single most important real risk factor; see this KB's aortic_aneurysm_dissection entry for full detail (not duplicated here).
Acute kidney injury from malignant nephrosclerosis/fibrinoid necrosis of renal arterioles.

Severe pre-eclampsia (SBP >=160 and/or DBP >=110 mmHg with proteinuria >5g/24h or other severe features) and eclampsia (seizures in this setting) are a real, pregnancy-specific hypertensive emergency. Real global data: pre-eclampsia affects approximately 2-8% of all pregnancies worldwide; eclampsia affects about 0.56 per 1,000 pregnancies in developed countries and 10-30x that rate in low-income countries. Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy caused an estimated 46,900 deaths globally in 2015, and account for nearly one-tenth of maternal deaths in Africa/Asia and roughly one-quarter in Latin America.

real_risk_factors.note: Well-established major modifiable risk factor, real and consistently replicated across populations.
real_risk_factors.source: Wikipedia Hypertension article citing Lancet 2015

real_risk_factors.note: Real dose-response signal exists, but with an important nuance: large pooled analyses show estimated sodium intake >=6 g/day and especially >3 g/day above/below reference are associated with higher risk of death or major cardiovascular disease, but this adverse association is mainly observed in people WHO ALREADY HAVE hypertension - the mortality/CV-outcome benefit of population-wide sodium reduction in normotensive people remains less certain in the literature.
real_risk_factors.source: Wikipedia Hypertension article (citing pooled sodium-outcome cohort analyses)
real_risk_factors.confidence: moderate - real finding but with the stated outcome-uncertainty caveat, not omitted since the nuance itself is real and important

real_risk_factors.note: Established major modifiable risk factor.

Real polygenic contribution - GWAS have identified over 2000 common genetic variants each with small individual effects on BP; a specific twin-study heritability percentage could not be pinned to a single citable figure in this research session and is therefore not asserted numerically.
Prevalence rises steeply with age, reported as high as ~60% of the population above age 60.
real_risk_factors.source: StatPearls Hypertension (NBK539859)

real_risk_factors.note: Real documented disparity - non-Hispanic Black Americans cited at ~44% prevalence, among the highest reported rates globally (see epidemiology section above for the comparison-framing caveat).
Real bidirectional relationship - CKD is both a cause and a consequence of poorly controlled hypertension.
Real, strong association (see secondary-causes section) - also operates as a general risk factor even when not the sole/primary cause.

natural_history.continuous_risk_relationship: Cardiovascular risk rises as a continuous function of BP, without a safe lower threshold down to at least ~115/75 mmHg - it is not a simple binary 'hypertensive vs not' risk model. The Lewington et al. Prospective Studies Collaboration meta-analysis (Lancet 2002; individual data from ~1 million adults across 61 prospective studies) is the classic, widely-cited source establishing that vascular mortality risk approximately doubles with each ~20 mmHg rise in systolic BP or ~10 mmHg rise in diastolic BP, across the studied range.
natural_history.confidence: moderate - this specific '~20/10 mmHg doubling' figure is one of the most widely taught and cited findings in cardiovascular epidemiology and is attributed consistently to this meta-analysis across secondary/tertiary sources, but this research session's live source-verification tools could not retrieve the primary Lancet 2002 text itself (PubMed/Lancet access was blocked in-session), so this number is flagged moderate rather than high-confidence pending direct primary-source re-verification.
natural_history.source: Lewington S, Clarke R, Qizilbash N, Collins R, Peto R. 'Age-specific relevance of usual blood pressure to vascular mortality: a meta-analysis of individual data for one million adults in 61 prospective studies.' Lancet 2002;360(9349):1903-13. PMID 12493255.
natural_history.target_organ_damage_progression: Uncontrolled hypertension drives progressive target-organ damage over years: vascular remodelling and atherosclerosis acceleration (feeding into this KB's ischaemic_heart_disease, peripheral_artery_disease, aortic_aneurysm_dissection, and ventricular_arrhythmia_scd entries), LVH and diastolic dysfunction progressing toward HFpEF/CHF, hypertensive nephrosclerosis progressing toward CKD, retinal vascular damage (see KWB grading above), and cerebrovascular disease/stroke risk. Adequate BP control delays but does not reverse advanced structural damage; this is a real disease-modifying rationale for early detection given how commonly the disease is silent (see 'core_presentation' above).

red_flags: Hypertensive encephalopathy signs (altered mental status, severe headache, papilloedema, seizures) - real emergency
Acute chest/back pain radiating pattern suggesting aortic dissection in a severely hypertensive patient - real emergency, see aortic_aneurysm_dissection entry
Acute dyspnoea suggesting flash pulmonary oedema in a hypertensive crisis - real emergency
Focal neurological deficits suggesting acute stroke in the setting of severe BP elevation - real emergency
Severe pre-eclampsia features (SBP>=160 or DBP>=110 with proteinuria/severe features) or eclamptic seizure in pregnancy - real, pregnancy-specific hypertensive emergency

New severe/resistant hypertension with hypokalaemia, paroxysmal symptoms, or renal/carotid bruit - real red flags for a secondary, potentially correctable cause requiring workup (not itself an ER emergency, but a diagnostic priority)

hypertension.CURABILITY_NOTE: Essential (primary) hypertension - roughly 90-95% of all hypertension cases - has no single identifiable reversible cause and is NOT cured by any drug, diet, or device; it is a lifelong condition CONTROLLED by combining lifestyle modification with antihypertensive drug therapy, with the real, hard-outcome-trial-proven goal of reducing stroke/MI/heart-failure/death, not reversing the underlying vascular pathophysiology. Secondary hypertension (the remaining 5-10%) is genuinely different: when a single identifiable root cause is found and treated, hypertension itself can be REAL-CURED (not just controlled) in a meaningful fraction of patients - see curative_option below for the real, evidence-based curative-intent pathways (adrenalectomy for a unilateral aldosterone-producing adenoma; renal-artery revascularization for fibromuscular-dysplasia-driven stenosis, which responds far better than atherosclerotic renal artery stenosis; and CPAP for OSA-driven hypertension, which is real but only modestly effective and rarely fully curative alone).

curative_option.name: Root-Cause Treatment of Secondary Hypertension (subtype-specific; NOT applicable to essential/primary hypertension)
curative_option.note: These are the real curative-intent pathways that exist ONLY when a specific, identifiable secondary cause of hypertension is found on workup. They do not apply to essential hypertension, which has no curative option - see definitive_option_nonreversible_majority below and exhaustive_medicine_survey for essential-hypertension control.

reversible_subtypes.name: Adrenalectomy for unilateral Primary Aldosteronism (aldosterone-producing adenoma / unilateral hyperplasia)
reversible_subtypes.note: Real, important honest nuance: the adenoma itself is cured (biochemical cure) in almost all cases, but complete cure of the HYPERTENSION is real yet lower - a meaningful fraction of patients still need at least one antihypertensive drug after surgery because of irreversible vascular/renal remodeling from years of aldosterone excess. Predictors of lower clinical-cure probability: higher BMI, longer pre-operative hypertension duration.

real_recovery_data.cohort: SOPRANO meta-analysis: 32 studies, 4861 unilateral PA patients from 132 referral centres worldwide

reversible_subtypes.source: Marzano & Ronco, SOPRANO study, Hypertens Res 2024 (PMID 38182902)
reversible_subtypes.confidence: high - large modern systematic review/meta-analysis

reversible_subtypes.name: Renal artery revascularization (percutaneous angioplasty or surgery) for Fibromuscular-Dysplasia-driven renal artery stenosis
reversible_subtypes.note: Real, honest contrast with atherosclerotic renal artery stenosis (ARAS): in FMD, the stenosis itself is usually the direct cause of the hypertension, so removing it can genuinely cure it. In ARAS, the hypertension is usually driven by diffuse systemic atherosclerosis/nephrosclerosis rather than the stenosis alone, which is why the real, large, sham/control-free but randomized ASTRAL (n=806) and CORAL (n=947) trials both found NO cardiovascular or renal benefit from stenting ARAS over medical therapy alone (ASTRAL: no significant difference in renal-function decline or BP; CORAL: 35.1% vs 35.8% primary composite event rate, HR 0.94, P=0.58, only a trivial -2.3 mmHg BP difference).

real_recovery_data.cohort: 47 angioplasty studies (1616 patients) + 23 surgery studies (1014 patients)
real_recovery_data.modifier: cure probability falls with older patient age and longer disease duration - earlier intervention in younger FMD patients gives the best real chance of cure

reversible_subtypes.source: Trinquart et al., systematic review and meta-analysis, Hypertension 2010 (PMID 20625080); contrast source: ASTRAL Investigators, NEJM 2009 (PMID 19907042) and CORAL, Cooper et al., NEJM 2014 (PMID 24245566)
reversible_subtypes.confidence: high - dedicated meta-analysis of FMD-specific outcomes, with real neutral-trial contrast for ARAS

reversible_subtypes.name: CPAP for OSA-driven hypertension
reversible_subtypes.note: Real, but the honest caveat is that this is modest symptomatic-driver treatment, not a true 'cure' of the hypertension in most patients - most OSA-hypertension patients still need antihypertensive drugs after starting CPAP. Included here because treating the real underlying driver (OSA) is conceptually distinct from essential-hypertension drug control, even though its BP effect size is much smaller than adrenalectomy or FMD revascularization.

real_recovery_data.dose_response: each additional 1 hour/night of CPAP use gives a further -1.5 mmHg systolic / -0.9 mmHg diastolic

reversible_subtypes.source: Bratton et al., JAMA 2015 (PMID 26624827)
reversible_subtypes.confidence: high - large network meta-analysis; effect size itself is real but modest

definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.name: Essential (Primary) Hypertension - No Curative Option Exists
definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.note: For the ~90-95% of hypertensive patients with no identifiable secondary cause, no medicine, diet, or device cures the underlying arteriolar/vascular pathophysiology. The real, achievable goal is durable BP control below evidence-based thresholds via combination pharmacotherapy plus lifestyle modification (see exhaustive_medicine_survey below), which real, large hard-outcome trials (SPRINT, HOPE, ALLHAT, ACCOMPLISH) show meaningfully reduces stroke/MI/death - but this is genuinely lifelong control, not cure.
definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.source: 2017 ACC/AHA Hypertension Guideline; 2018 ESC/ESH Hypertension Guidelines

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Full gold-standard survey of every real lifestyle intervention, drug class, device, and acute management option used for hypertension, each ending in a stated real working solution per the standing rule. CURABILITY: none of these cure essential hypertension - see curative_option above for the real curative-intent pathways that exist only for specific secondary causes. Resistant hypertension (referenced below) is defined per the 2017 ACC/AHA guideline as BP above goal despite concurrent use of 3 antihypertensive agents of different classes (typically including a diuretic) at maximally tolerated doses, or BP controlled but requiring 4 or more agents.

lifestyle_modifications.name: DASH Diet (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension)
lifestyle_modifications.effectiveness: Combination DASH diet reduced BP by 11.4/5.5 mmHg more than a control diet in the hypertensive subgroup (baseline BP >=140/90; n=133), and by 5.5/3.0 mmHg more than control across the whole 8-week feeding trial (n=459); sodium intake was held fixed across diets, isolating the diet-pattern effect.
lifestyle_modifications.reason_why: High potassium/calcium/magnesium, low-saturated-fat, high-fibre diet lowers peripheral vascular resistance and improves endothelial/natriuretic function - a genuine dietary effect independent of sodium or weight change.
lifestyle_modifications.source: DASH trial, Appel et al., NEJM 1997 (PMID 9099655)
lifestyle_modifications.real_working_solution: Adopting a DASH-pattern diet is a real, actionable, drug-free first step for every hypertensive patient, with an effect size in hypertensives (~11 mmHg systolic) comparable to a single antihypertensive drug.

lifestyle_modifications.name: Dietary Sodium Restriction
lifestyle_modifications.effectiveness: Dose-response relationship: each 50 mmol (~1.15 g sodium / ~2.9 g salt) reduction in 24-hour urinary sodium excretion produces a 1.10 mmHg reduction in systolic BP (0.33 mmHg diastolic); across 133 pooled RCTs (n=12,197) the average sodium reduction achieved produced a 4.26/2.07 mmHg fall; effect is larger in trials lasting >15 days and in older, non-white, or higher-baseline-BP populations.
lifestyle_modifications.reason_why: Reduced sodium load lowers plasma volume and vascular smooth-muscle sodium/calcium-exchange-driven vasoconstriction - a genuine, dose-dependent physiological mechanism.
lifestyle_modifications.source: Huang et al., systematic review and meta-analysis of 133 RCTs, BMJ 2020 (PMID 32094151)
lifestyle_modifications.real_working_solution: A real, quantifiable, dose-dependent lever - roughly 1 mmHg systolic per 1 g/day sodium cut - achievable via reduced processed-food intake; a genuinely working non-drug option for every hypertensive patient.

lifestyle_modifications.name: Weight Loss
lifestyle_modifications.effectiveness: -1.05 mmHg systolic and -0.92 mmHg diastolic per kilogram of weight lost; a net 5.1 kg weight loss reduced SBP by 4.44 mmHg and DBP by 3.57 mmHg (25 RCTs, n=4874); effect significantly larger (-6.63/-5.12 mmHg) when weight loss exceeds 5 kg, and larger still in patients already on antihypertensive drugs (-5.31 vs -2.91 mmHg diastolic).
lifestyle_modifications.reason_why: Adiposity drives sympathetic-nervous-system overactivity, insulin resistance/hyperinsulinaemia, and renal sodium retention - reversing these mechanisms with weight loss genuinely lowers BP.
lifestyle_modifications.source: Neter et al., meta-analysis of 25 RCTs, Hypertension 2003 (PMID 12975389)
lifestyle_modifications.real_working_solution: A real, linear, dose-known lever (~1 mmHg per kg lost) achievable via caloric restriction and/or physical activity, with amplified benefit in patients already on drug therapy.

lifestyle_modifications.name: Aerobic Exercise
lifestyle_modifications.effectiveness: -3.84 mmHg systolic, -2.58 mmHg diastolic across 54 RCTs (n=2419); benefit seen in both hypertensive and normotensive participants, and in both overweight and normal-weight participants.
lifestyle_modifications.reason_why: Regular aerobic training improves endothelial nitric-oxide-mediated vasodilation, reduces sympathetic tone, and improves arterial compliance.
lifestyle_modifications.source: Whelton et al., meta-analysis of 54 RCTs, Ann Intern Med 2002 (PMID 11926784)
lifestyle_modifications.real_working_solution: A real, guideline-endorsed non-drug BP-lowering effect comparable to a low-dose single antihypertensive - >=150 min/week moderate aerobic activity is a directly evidence-backed prescription, not generic advice.

lifestyle_modifications.name: Alcohol Reduction
lifestyle_modifications.effectiveness: -3.31 mmHg systolic, -2.04 mmHg diastolic across 15 RCTs (n=2234); real dose-response relationship - larger percentage alcohol reduction produces larger BP reduction; effect enhanced in patients with higher baseline BP.
lifestyle_modifications.reason_why: Alcohol acutely and chronically raises sympathetic activity and impairs baroreflex/vascular tone; reducing intake reverses this real, dose-dependent effect.
lifestyle_modifications.source: Xin et al., meta-analysis of 15 RCTs, Hypertension 2001 (PMID 11711507)
lifestyle_modifications.real_working_solution: A real, dose-dependent lever, most impactful in heavy drinkers with hypertension - reducing alcohol intake is a directly evidence-based recommendation.

first_line_drug_classes.name: Chlorthalidone (thiazide-like diuretic)
first_line_drug_classes.effectiveness: ALLHAT (n=33,357): no significant difference in the primary CHD outcome vs amlodipine (RR 0.98) or lisinopril (RR 0.99); but chlorthalidone had significantly LOWER heart-failure incidence than amlodipine (7.7% vs 10.2%, RR 1.38 for amlodipine, 95% CI 1.25-1.52) and lower combined CVD (30.9% vs 33.3%, RR 1.10), stroke (5.6% vs 6.3%, RR 1.15), and heart failure (7.7% vs 8.7%, RR 1.19) than lisinopril.
first_line_drug_classes.reason_why: Blocks the Na-Cl cotransporter in the distal convoluted tubule, producing natriuresis/plasma-volume reduction and, with chronic use, direct vasodilation - validated at the scale of the largest antihypertensive outcome trial ever conducted.
first_line_drug_classes.confidence: high - largest real antihypertensive outcome trial (n=33,357)
first_line_drug_classes.real_working_solution: ALLHAT's real, hard-outcome conclusion: thiazide-type diuretics should be preferred first-step therapy - cheaper and at least as effective, with a real edge in preventing heart failure.

first_line_drug_classes.name: Ramipril (ACE inhibitor)
first_line_drug_classes.effectiveness: HOPE trial (n=9297 high-risk patients): 22% RRR in the composite of MI/stroke/CV death (14.0% vs 17.8%, RR 0.78, P<0.001); 26% RRR CV death (6.1% vs 8.1%); 20% RRR MI (9.9% vs 12.3%); 32% RRR stroke (3.4% vs 4.9%); 16% RRR all-cause mortality (10.4% vs 12.2%).
first_line_drug_classes.reason_why: ACE inhibition blocks angiotensin-II-driven vasoconstriction, aldosterone secretion, and vascular/cardiac remodelling - HOPE showed this benefit even in patients without severe hypertension or LV dysfunction, implying a real vasculoprotective effect beyond BP-lowering alone.
first_line_drug_classes.source: HOPE trial, Yusuf et al., NEJM 2000 (PMID 10639539)
first_line_drug_classes.real_working_solution: Real, large, hard-outcome cardiovascular risk reduction (~22% composite) independent of baseline BP severity - genuine first-line justification for the ACEi/ARB class in high-risk hypertensive patients.

first_line_drug_classes.name: Amlodipine (dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker)
first_line_drug_classes.effectiveness: ALLHAT: no significant difference vs chlorthalidone in the primary CHD outcome (RR 0.98) or all-cause mortality; but a real, significantly higher heart-failure risk than chlorthalidone (10.2% vs 7.7%, RR 1.38, 95% CI 1.25-1.52).
first_line_drug_classes.reason_why: Blocks L-type calcium channels in vascular smooth muscle, producing direct arterial vasodilation - effective BP-lowering, but the lack of a natriuretic/anti-remodelling effect explains its real, trial-proven higher heart-failure signal relative to a diuretic.
first_line_drug_classes.real_working_solution: Real first-line option - but the honest trial-proven heart-failure signal means it should be combined with, not blindly substituted for, a diuretic/ACEi in patients at risk of heart failure.

combination_therapy.name: ACEi + CCB (benazepril + amlodipine) vs ACEi + thiazide (benazepril + hydrochlorothiazide)
combination_therapy.effectiveness: ACCOMPLISH (n=11,506 high-risk hypertensives): benazepril+amlodipine reduced the composite CV-death/MI/stroke/angina-hospitalisation/resuscitated-cardiac-arrest outcome by a 19.6% RRR vs benazepril+HCTZ (9.6% vs 11.8% events, HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.72-0.90, P<0.001); trial stopped early for benefit at mean 36 months, despite near-identical achieved BP (131.6/73.3 vs 132.5/74.4 mmHg).
combination_therapy.reason_why: The ACEi+CCB combination's benefit over ACEi+diuretic was NOT explained by lower BP (BP was essentially identical between arms) - implying a genuine non-BP-dependent vascular-protective synergy from combining RAAS blockade with direct vasodilation rather than volume depletion.
combination_therapy.source: ACCOMPLISH trial, Jamerson et al., NEJM 2008 (PMID 19052124)
combination_therapy.real_working_solution: Real, guideline-shaping result: when initial combination therapy is needed, ACEi/ARB + CCB is the evidence-preferred pairing over ACEi/ARB + thiazide for reducing hard cardiovascular events, at equivalent BP control.

bp_treatment_target_strategy.name: Intensive (<120 mmHg systolic) vs Standard (<140 mmHg) BP Target
bp_treatment_target_strategy.effectiveness: SPRINT (n=9361, non-diabetic high-CV-risk patients): intensive target achieved mean SBP 121.4 mmHg vs 136.2 mmHg standard; 25% RRR in the primary composite CV outcome (1.65%/yr vs 2.19%/yr, HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.64-0.89, P<0.001); 27% RRR all-cause mortality (HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.60-0.90, P=0.003); trial stopped early for benefit at median 3.26 years. Real, significantly HIGHER rates of serious hypotension, syncope, electrolyte abnormalities, and acute kidney injury/failure occurred in the intensive arm; injurious falls were not significantly increased.
bp_treatment_target_strategy.reason_why: Lower achieved BP directly reduces the haemodynamic stress driving hypertensive vascular and renal injury - but the same aggressive lowering mechanically increases real risk of orthostatic hypotension-related events and pre-renal AKI, an honest, trial-documented tradeoff, not a theoretical caveat.
bp_treatment_target_strategy.source: SPRINT trial, SPRINT Research Group, NEJM 2015 (PMID 26551272)
bp_treatment_target_strategy.confidence: high - landmark NIH-funded trial, stopped early for benefit
bp_treatment_target_strategy.real_working_solution: Real, guideline-adopted working answer (the 2017 ACC/AHA <130/80 target reflects SPRINT): target intensive BP control in appropriate high-CV-risk, non-diabetic patients able to tolerate it, with active monitoring for the real adverse-event tradeoff - not an unconditional target for all patients.

resistant_hypertension_management.name: Spironolactone as 4th-line add-on for resistant hypertension
