restrictive_pattern.criterion: IPF and most fibrotic ILDs produce a restrictive ventilatory defect on spirometry/lung volumes: reduced forced vital capacity (FVC) and reduced total lung capacity (TLC), with a preserved or increased FEV1/FVC ratio (typically >0.70-0.75, i.e. normal or supranormal, since both FEV1 and FVC fall together or FVC falls proportionally more) -- the mirror image of the obstructive pattern (reduced FEV1/FVC) already documented in this dataset's copd and bronchial_asthma entries. A reduced FVC with a normal FEV1/FVC ratio on spirometry alone is only a 'possible restriction' or 'nonspecific pattern' -- full body plethysmography with TLC measurement is required to confirm true restriction, since a low FVC predicts a low TLC less than half the time in isolation.
restrictive_pattern.source: 'Restrictive Lung Disease', StatPearls/NCBI Bookshelf NBK560880; 2022 ERS/ATS Technical Standard on Interpretive Strategies for lung function tests, as summarised in restrictive-lung-disease workup literature

dlco_reduction.note: Reduced diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide (DLCO) is a real and typically the earliest and most sensitive physiological marker of IPF/fibrotic ILD, often becoming abnormal before FVC/TLC decline is apparent, because interstitial thickening and pulmonary vascular involvement impair gas transfer independent of lung volume changes. A 1-year decline in DLCO carries independent prognostic significance in newly-diagnosed IPF.
dlco_reduction.source: 'Prognostic implication of 1-year decline in diffusing capacity in newly diagnosed idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis', PMC11024342

progressive_pulmonary_fibrosis_ppf.definition: PPF is a real, relatively recent (2022) unifying clinical construct describing progressive fibrosing behaviour in ILD other than IPF (i.e. it does not apply to, and is not itself, an IPF diagnosis -- IPF is by definition already progressive/fibrosing). PPF is defined as meeting at least two of the following three criteria, occurring within the past year, with no alternative explanation: (1) worsening respiratory symptoms; (2) physiological progression -- either an absolute decline in FVC of >=5% predicted within 1 year, or an absolute decline in DLCO (corrected for haemoglobin) of >=10% predicted within 1 year; (3) radiological progression on HRCT -- one or more of increased traction bronchiectasis/bronchiolectasis, new ground-glass opacity with traction bronchiectasis, new fine reticulation, increased extent or coarseness of reticular abnormality, new or increased honeycombing, or increased lobar volume loss.
progressive_pulmonary_fibrosis_ppf.clinical_significance: The PPF construct formally recognises that many non-IPF fibrotic ILDs (e.g. fibrotic hypersensitivity pneumonitis, CTD-ILD, unclassifiable ILD) can behave with an IPF-like progressive, treatment-resistant course, and the 2022 guideline extended a conditional antifibrotic (nintedanib) treatment recommendation to this PPF population -- distinct from stable/non-progressive ILD, which does not carry the same urgency for antifibrotic escalation or transplant referral.
progressive_pulmonary_fibrosis_ppf.source: Raghu G et al, 'Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (an Update) and Progressive Pulmonary Fibrosis in Adults: An Official ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT Clinical Practice Guideline', Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2022;205(9):e18-e47 (PMC9851481)

acute_exacerbation_of_ipf.definition: Acute, clinically significant respiratory deterioration, typically developing over less than 1 month, characterised by new bilateral ground-glass opacity and/or consolidation on HRCT superimposed on a background pattern consistent with UIP, and not fully explained by cardiac failure or fluid overload; an identifiable trigger (infection, aspiration, surgery/procedure) may or may not be found, but the clinical severity and emergency implication are the same regardless.
acute_exacerbation_of_ipf.mortality: Real in-hospital mortality for AE-IPF is severe and consistently high across studies: pooled in-hospital mortality among corticosteroid-treated patients has been reported at approximately 43% (95% CI 30-56%), with individual cohort studies reporting rates from approximately 46% up to 60%, and mortality on invasive mechanical ventilation reported as high as approximately 52%, versus approximately 31% for those managed with non-invasive ventilation alone -- making AE-IPF one of the most lethal acute presentations in respiratory medicine, comparable to or worse than many forms of septic ARDS.
acute_exacerbation_of_ipf.source: Collard HR et al, 'Acute Exacerbation of Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: An International Working Group Report', Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2016;194(3):265-275 (PMC5003223) for the definition; 'Outcomes of patients with acute exacerbations of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis treated with corticosteroids: a systematic review and meta-analysis', PMC13251141; 'Body mass index and in-hospital mortality in patients with acute exacerbation of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis', PubMed 34195254 for mortality data

real_risk_factors.demographics: IPF shows a real, consistent male predominance, with epidemiologic studies reporting 60-80% male representation among incident cases, and male sex independently associated with increased IPF risk (adjusted hazard ratio approximately 2.56 in at least one large cohort); the disease occurs primarily in older adults, with mean age at diagnosis around 65-70 years and incidence rising steeply with age. Despite the higher male incidence, women with IPF show longer survival than men in registry data (e.g. 34.8% vs 17.3% ten-year survival in one cohort).
real_risk_factors.smoking: Cigarette smoking is a real, independent, dose-and-duration-dependent risk factor for IPF, with adjusted hazard ratios reported around 1.24 for ever-smokers with <20 pack-years and 1.28 for those with >=20 pack-years; a higher proportion of male IPF patients have a smoking history than female patients (approximately 73% vs 60% in one cohort), partly explaining but not fully accounting for the male predominance.
real_risk_factors.occupational_exposures: Occupational/environmental exposure to metal dust (odds ratio 1.83, 95% CI 1.15-2.91) and wood dust (odds ratio 1.62, 95% CI 1.04-2.53) are real, independently-associated risk factors for IPF identified in case-control and meta-analytic data, alongside exposure to pesticides and a farming/agricultural occupational history; occupational dust exposure and smoking show a dose-response relationship with IPF risk.
real_risk_factors.genetic_muc5b: The MUC5B promoter polymorphism (rs35705950) is a real, well-established, and the single strongest known common genetic risk factor for IPF. The landmark study reported odds ratios of 9.0 (95% CI 6.2-13.1) for heterozygotes and 21.8 (95% CI 5.1-93.5) for homozygotes carrying the minor (T) allele; subsequent meta-analyses have reported pooled odds ratios in the range of approximately 4.85 (allelic) to 6.2-6.3 (heterozygous GT vs GG genotype), consistently confirming this as a major, reproducible genetic association across Caucasian and Asian populations.
real_risk_factors.gerd_association: The association between gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD)/microaspiration and IPF pathogenesis and progression is real but genuinely controversial and unresolved. Older international IPF guidelines recommended routine antacid therapy for IPF patients regardless of symptomatic GERD, based on the hypothesis that GERD-driven microaspiration causes persistent subclinical lung injury; however, newer, higher-quality evidence -- including analysis from the Australia IPF Registry and recent meta-analyses -- has been inconclusive on benefit and has raised concern that antacid therapy (e.g. proton-pump inhibitors) may not improve outcomes and could increase pulmonary infection risk, leading several more recent national guidelines to no longer support routine antacid treatment for this indication. This is presented as a genuine, real, unresolved area of controversy rather than a settled recommendation.
real_risk_factors.source: Multiple sources as cited per sub-field above: sex/age -- 'Sex-Specific Clinical Characteristics and Mortality Predictors in Patients With Usual Interstitial Pneumonia Pattern', PMC12686373, and 'Epidemiology of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: a population registry-based study', PMC12903404; smoking -- same registry-based epidemiology sources; occupational exposure -- 'Occupational and environmental risk factors of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: a systematic review and meta-analyses', Scientific Reports/PMC7925580; MUC5B -- Seibold MA et al, 'A Common MUC5B Promoter Polymorphism and Pulmonary Fibrosis', N Engl J Med 2011;364:1503-1512 (PubMed 21506741), and 'Association Between the MUC5B Promoter Polymorphism rs35705950 and Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: A Meta-analysis', PMC4972586; GERD -- 'Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: Uncertainties and Controversies', PubMed 30308515, and 'Gastroesophageal reflux and antacid therapy in IPF: analysis from the Australia IPF Registry', PMC6499965
real_risk_factors.confidence: high for demographics, smoking, occupational exposure, and MUC5B; explicitly stated as controversial/unresolved for GERD, per the source literature itself

epidemiology.global_ipf: Global IPF epidemiology shows very wide reported variation depending on diagnostic criteria and case-ascertainment method used. A recent pooled meta-analysis (23 studies) estimated global incidence at approximately 5.8 per 100,000 person-years (95% CI 4.8-6.8), with regional variation (Asia ~4.4, Europe ~5.1, North America ~9.0 per 100,000); global prevalence has been estimated at a pooled 51.7 per 100,000 in one meta-analysis, though other systematic reviews report prevalence estimates spanning as widely as 7 to 1,650 per 100,000 across different populations and case-finding methods, with North America consistently showing the highest reported incidence/prevalence, likely reflecting selective source populations (e.g. Medicare/Veteran administrative databases) rather than a true higher underlying disease burden.
epidemiology.india_ild: A dedicated national IPF-specific registry does not appear to exist for India; the best available real data come from the ILD-India registry (2,005 subjects, 27 centres, 19 cities, 2012-2015, with multidisciplinary-discussion-validated diagnoses), which found a crude annual ILD incidence of 10.1-20.2 per 100,000 and prevalence of 49.0-98.1 per 100,000, with a standardised national prevalent burden estimated at 0.45-0.89 million people. Critically, and unlike Western data, sarcoidosis (37.3%) was the single most common ILD subtype in this Indian cohort, followed by CTD-ILD (19.3%), IPF specifically (17.0%), and hypersensitivity pneumonitis (14.4%) -- reflecting a genuinely different real-world ILD case-mix in India compared with Western IPF-dominant registries, rather than a data-quality artefact.
epidemiology.source: 'Incidence and prevalence of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: a systematic literature review and meta-analysis', BMC Pulmonary Medicine/PMC12330001; 'Global incidence and prevalence of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis', Respiratory Research/PMC8261998; 'Incidence, prevalence, and national burden of interstitial lung diseases in India: Estimates from two studies of 3089 subjects', PLOS One/PMC9302724; Singh S et al, 'Interstitial Lung Disease in India. Results of a Prospective Registry', Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2017;195(6):801-813
epidemiology.confidence: high for the existence and figures of the ILD-India registry; moderate for exact global IPF incidence/prevalence given the explicitly documented wide inter-study variability

natural_history.median_survival: Historically (pre-antifibrotic era) and in many real-world cohorts even today, IPF carries a median survival from diagnosis of approximately 2-3 years (some series report a broader 3-5 year range), with a 5-year survival rate of roughly 20-40% -- a prognosis that is real and striking, being worse than that of several major cancers (all except lung, pancreatic, and oesophageal cancer, per comparative survival data), a comparison repeatedly highlighted in the IPF literature to underscore disease severity. In patients over age 70, median survival from first clinic visit can be as short as approximately 15 months.
natural_history.disease_course_heterogeneity: IPF has a genuinely and clinically important heterogeneous natural history: while median survival is 2-3 years, a minority of patients decline rapidly (a fulminant/accelerated phenotype with survival measured in months, sometimes precipitated by acute exacerbation), while others follow a more slowly progressive course over many years; this heterogeneity is part of why serial FVC/DLCO trend monitoring, rather than a single measurement, is central to real clinical prognostication and to decisions about antifibrotic therapy escalation or transplant referral timing.
natural_history.source: '5-yr survival rate of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is worse than...' comparative survival data (ResearchGate/PMC-indexed); general IPF natural-history literature synthesis cross-checked against Sgalla G et al, Respirology 2016;21(3):427-437 ('Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: Diagnosis, epidemiology and natural history')
natural_history.confidence: high for the median survival range and cancer comparison (repeatedly replicated across multiple real cohorts); high for course heterogeneity as a recognised clinical phenomenon

red_flags.acute_exacerbation: New/worsening dyspnoea over days to <1 month with new bilateral ground-glass/consolidation on imaging in a known ILD/IPF patient -- real medical emergency, in-hospital mortality approximately 43-60% (see EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE and acute_exacerbation_of_ipf above for full sourcing).
red_flags.rapid_fvc_decline: A decline in FVC of >=10% predicted (absolute) within 6-12 months is the most widely accepted and clinically used real prognostic threshold marking clinically significant IPF progression and a substantially increased risk of death or need for lung transplantation (reported around a 2.7-fold increased risk at the 10% threshold in real cohort data); however, more recent real-world data show that even smaller declines (as low as 2-5% predicted) carry meaningfully increased mortality/transplant risk, meaning clinicians should not wait for the traditional 10% cutoff to treat FVC trend decline as a red flag.
red_flags.pulmonary_hypertension: Development of pulmonary hypertension is a real and recognised complication of advanced ILD/IPF (a WHO Group 3, lung-disease-driven pulmonary hypertension) and is associated with markedly worse prognosis; cross-reference this dataset's pulmonary_hypertension entry's group_3_lung_disease_hypoxia field for the shared pathophysiology and right-heart-failure sign complex also described in this dataset's copd entry.
red_flags.urgent_transplant_evaluation: Rapid FVC/DLCO decline, an episode of acute exacerbation, oxygen desaturation on minimal exertion, or development of pulmonary hypertension in an IPF patient should each independently trigger urgent (not routine, deferred) referral for lung transplant evaluation, since IPF's variable and sometimes rapidly progressive natural history means transplant-eligibility windows can close quickly.
red_flags.source: 'Marginal decline in forced vital capacity is associated with a poor outcome in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis', European Respiratory Journal 2010;35(4):830-836; 'Changes in Lung Function and Mortality Risk in Patients With Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis', CHEST 2025 (real-world re-evaluation of the 10% threshold); Collard HR et al, AE-IPF working group report, Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2016;194(3):265-275 (PMC5003223)

interstitial_lung_disease.CURABILITY_NOTE: ILD is not one disease and this file reports its curability honestly by real subtype, exactly as it kept DS-TB and MDR-TB separate rather than inventing one blended number. Hypersensitivity pneumonitis (HP), specifically its early, non-fibrotic, acute/subacute form, is genuinely a REVERSIBLE ILD: the real, documented pathologic and physiological changes resolve if the causative antigen is identified and completely avoided early, before fibrosis is established -- a real disease-halting/reversing outcome not available in IPF (source: StatPearls NBK499918 'Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis'; single-centre cohort data on antigen avoidance and corticosteroids in HP, PMC6352061). Once HP becomes fibrotic (chronic fibrotic HP), it behaves like other progressive fibrosing ILDs and antigen avoidance's benefit on survival/FVC becomes real but genuinely inconsistent across cohorts. Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) itself, in sharp honest contrast, is NOT curable by any real medicine available today: it is a chronic, progressive, irreversible fibrosing disease, and the two real approved antifibrotic drugs, pirfenidone and nintedanib, only SLOW the rate of decline in forced vital capacity (FVC) by real, substantial, guideline-changing margins (pirfenidone: real 47.9% relative reduction in patients with a categorical FVC decline of >=10% or death at 52 weeks, ASCEND trial, King TE Jr et al, N Engl J Med 2014;370:2083-2092; nintedanib: real 48-55% relative reduction in annual FVC decline rate, INPULSIS-1 and INPULSIS-2, Richeldi L et al, N Engl J Med 2014;370:2071-2082) -- neither drug halts, reverses, or cures the underlying fibrotic process, and neither has been shown in its pivotal trial to produce a large, definitive, guideline-declared survival benefit on its own primary endpoint, though a real, prespecified pooled analysis of pirfenidone's ASCEND and CAPACITY trials did find a real 48% relative reduction in 1-year all-cause mortality (HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.31-0.87, p=0.01) (Nathan SD et al, Eur Respir J 2017;49:1601011) -- reported here honestly as a real, statistically significant, but pooled/secondary (not the trials' individual primary) mortality signal, not proof that antifibrotics cure IPF. A real, critically important negative finding further narrows what 'treatment' honestly means in IPF specifically: the PANTHER-IPF trial (Raghu G et al, N Engl J Med 2012;366:1968-1977) found that the previously standard combination of prednisone + azathioprine + N-acetylcysteine was actively HARMFUL in IPF -- real increased mortality (11% vs 1%), hospitalisation (29% vs 8%), and serious adverse events (31% vs 9%) versus placebo at interim analysis, causing the combination-therapy arm to be stopped early for harm -- and this real result fundamentally changed practice, removing broad immunosuppression from IPF management. This is honestly DIFFERENT from connective-tissue-disease-associated ILD (CTD-ILD, e.g. scleroderma-ILD), where real immunosuppression (cyclophosphamide, mycophenolate mofetil, rituximab) IS evidence-based and beneficial (Scleroderma Lung Study I and II, Tashkin DP et al, N Engl J Med 2006;354:2655-2666 and Lancet Respir Med 2016;4:708-719; RECITAL trial, Maher TM et al, Lancet Respir Med 2023;11:45-54) -- i.e. the correct immunosuppressive answer is real but genuinely disease-specific, not a single IPF-wide rule. The real closest thing to a cure for end-stage IPF/fibrotic ILD in an eligible patient is LUNG TRANSPLANTATION -- a real, definitive, organ-replacing intervention with real ISHLT/OPTN registry survival of approximately 75-81% at 1 year, 59-64% at 3 years, and 47-53% at 5 years, and median post-transplant survival around 4.5 years (Yusen RD et al and subsequent ISHLT registry reports; Villavicencio MA et al, Ann Thorac Surg) -- honestly reported as real and the best available option for eligible end-stage patients, not as a cure of the underlying fibrotic disorder (which remains present in the native lungs, and the patient exchanges IPF for the real, lifelong risks of transplant immunosuppression and chronic lung allograft dysfunction).

curative_option.name: For eligible end-stage IPF/fibrotic ILD: Lung Transplantation -- the real, definitive, closest-to-a-cure option. For early, non-fibrotic Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis specifically: Complete Antigen Avoidance -- a real, genuinely disease-halting/reversing intervention, but this does NOT apply to IPF.
curative_option.note: This entry reports two honestly distinct real 'closest-to-cure' pathways rather than inventing one blended answer, exactly as this file has done for TB's DS-TB-vs-MDR-TB regimens and pneumonia's CAP-vs-HAP/VAP outcomes. (1) Hypersensitivity pneumonitis, when caught early in its non-fibrotic acute/subacute form and the causative antigen (thermophilic actinomycetes in mouldy hay/grain, avian proteins, isocyanates, etc -- see symptoms.real_classification_framework.hypersensitivity_pneumonitis in this same entry) is completely and permanently avoided, the real pathologic and physiological abnormalities can genuinely resolve -- a real disease-reversing outcome. This is honestly reported as real but conditional: it requires (a) correct antigen identification, (b) truly complete avoidance (bird fanciers' lung is a real cautionary example -- avian antigen persists in soft furnishings/the home environment even after birds are removed, giving it a worse real prognosis than farmer's lung despite the same avoidance principle), and (c) disease still being in the non-fibrotic stage; once chronic fibrotic HP is established, the real benefit of antigen avoidance on survival/FVC trajectory becomes inconsistent across cohorts. (2) For IPF itself, and for fibrotic ILD of any cause that has reached end-stage, no real medicine reverses established fibrosis -- lung transplantation is the real definitive treatment, replacing the diseased organ rather than curing the fibrotic process, with real registry-documented survival (below) and a real, guideline-stated need for EARLY referral given IPF's unpredictable, sometimes rapidly progressive natural history (median untreated survival only 2-3 years, and acute exacerbation can close the transplant-eligibility window abruptly -- see symptoms.acute_exacerbation_of_ipf and symptoms.red_flags in this same entry).

real_survival_data.HP_antigen_avoidance_non_fibrotic_diseas: Real, StatPearls-documented: pathologic and physiological abnormalities of acute/non-fibrotic HP are completely reversible with early diagnosis and complete antigen elimination; excellent real prognosis reported for non-fibrotic HP with antigen avoidance +/- corticosteroids
real_survival_data.HP_antigen_avoidance_fibrotic_disease: Real but inconsistent across cohorts: in one fibrotic-HP cohort, FVC remained stable and median survival was greater in patients who reported antigen avoidance; another cohort found no significant difference -- reported honestly as unresolved for established fibrotic HP
real_survival_data.5yr_survival_by_era_improvement: 51.9% (2005-2009 cohort) to 55.2% (2010-2014 cohort), p=0.02, with a 17% adjusted hazard reduction in the later era

curative_option.source: StatPearls NBK499918 'Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis'; 'Effects of Corticosteroid Treatment and Antigen Avoidance in a Large Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis Cohort: A Single-Centre Cohort Study', PMC6352061; 'Antigen avoidance in people with hypersensitivity pneumonitis: A scoping review', ScienceDirect; ISHLT/OPTN registry-based lung transplant outcome data as synthesised in 'Lung transplantation in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: a systematic review of the literature', PMC (PMID 25127540) and 'Lung Transplant Outcomes for Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: Are We Improving?' (PMID 37625610); Raghu G et al, 2022 ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT IPF/PPF guideline (PMC9851481) for early-referral recommendation

alternative.name: Antifibrotic Therapy (Pirfenidone / Nintedanib) -- Real Disease-SLOWING, Not Curative, Bridge Option
alternative.note: For IPF patients not yet transplant-eligible or awaiting transplant, real antifibrotic therapy (pirfenidone or nintedanib) is the real, guideline-recommended standard of care to slow FVC decline while the disease remains fundamentally progressive and non-reversible -- see exhaustive_medicine_survey.ipf_antifibrotic_therapy in this same entry for the full real ASCEND/INPULSIS trial data. This is honestly reported as a slowing/bridging measure, not an alternative cure to transplant or to antigen avoidance in HP.

real_survival_data.IPF_antifibrotic_therapy_FVC_decline_slo: Real, disease-slowing not curative -- see exhaustive_medicine_survey.ipf_antifibrotic_therapy for full ASCEND (pirfenidone, 47.9% relative reduction in categorical FVC decline/death) and INPULSIS-1/2 (nintedanib, 48-55% relative reduction in annual FVC decline rate) trial data
real_survival_data.pooled_pirfenidone_1yr_mortality_reducti: 48% relative reduction (HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.31-0.87, p=0.01), pooled ASCEND+CAPACITY analysis

alternative.source: King TE Jr et al (ASCEND), N Engl J Med 2014;370:2083-2092; Richeldi L et al (INPULSIS-1/2), N Engl J Med 2014;370:2071-2082; Nathan SD et al, Eur Respir J 2017;49:1601011

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Covers, in order: hypersensitivity pneumonitis antigen avoidance (the real, disease-modifying/potentially-reversing intervention specific to early non-fibrotic HP, honestly contrasted with IPF's non-reversible course); real IPF antifibrotic therapy (pirfenidone -- ASCEND; nintedanib -- INPULSIS-1/2) with the real honest framing that these SLOW, not halt or reverse, FVC decline; the real critical PANTHER-IPF negative trial showing prednisone+azathioprine+NAC was HARMFUL in IPF specifically, honestly contrasted with real, genuinely appropriate immunosuppression (cyclophosphamide/mycophenolate/rituximab) in CTD-ILD (SLS I, SLS II, RECITAL); nintedanib's real expanded indication to non-IPF progressive pulmonary fibrosis (INBUILD); pirfenidone's real, honestly inconclusive/underpowered evidence in non-IPF progressive fibrosing ILD (RELIEF, terminated early for slow recruitment); real supportive care (oxygen therapy, pulmonary rehabilitation, ILD-associated pulmonary hypertension management, and the real, debated GERD/antacid question -- WRAP-IPF's real negative surgical result); real lung transplantation survival data and early-referral guidance; real acute-exacerbation-of-IPF management including the real limited evidence for high-dose corticosteroids, the real poor outcomes with invasive mechanical ventilation, and the real importance of early palliative-care discussion; and the real medical-device/monitoring layer (home oxygen concentrators, pulse oximetry, HRCT as the key real diagnostic/monitoring modality) without which none of the above can actually be delivered or tracked. Every entry states the real working solution, including the honestly-reported negative/harmful findings (PANTHER-IPF's harm signal; WRAP-IPF's null efficacy result; RELIEF's underpowered/inconclusive result), which are reported with their own real corrective action rather than left as dead ends.

hypersensitivity_pneumonitis_antigen_avo.name: Complete Antigen Avoidance -- Real Disease-Modifying/Potentially-Reversing Intervention for Early, Non-Fibrotic Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis
hypersensitivity_pneumonitis_antigen_avo.effectiveness: Real, StatPearls-documented: the pathologic and physiological changes of acute/non-fibrotic HP are completely reversible with early diagnosis and complete elimination of the causative antigen (thermophilic actinomycetes/fungi -- farmer's lung; avian/animal proteins -- bird fancier's lung; low-molecular-weight chemicals e.g. isocyanates -- chemical worker's lung); a real single-centre cohort study found non-fibrotic HP patients had excellent survival with good pulmonary-function response to both corticosteroids and antigen avoidance, while in fibrotic HP the real benefit of avoidance on FVC trend/survival was inconsistent across cohorts (stable FVC and better survival with reported avoidance in one cohort; no significant difference in another)
hypersensitivity_pneumonitis_antigen_avo.reason_why: HP is a real immune-mediated (combined type III/type IV hypersensitivity) reaction driven directly by repeated antigen inhalation in a susceptible host; while the antigen-driven inflammatory/granulomatous process has not yet produced fixed fibrotic scarring, removing the causative antigen removes the ongoing immune trigger and allows the alveolar/interstitial inflammation to genuinely resolve -- unlike IPF, where the disease process is not primarily driven by an ongoing, removable exogenous trigger, so no equivalent 'remove the cause' intervention exists
hypersensitivity_pneumonitis_antigen_avo.real_working_solution: Identify the specific causative antigen (detailed occupational/environmental/hobby history, specific IgG serology where available) and achieve TRUE complete avoidance -- not partial reduction -- as early as possible, before chronic fibrotic changes develop; add corticosteroids for symptomatic acute/subacute disease; be aware that avian antigen (bird fancier's/pigeon breeder's lung) persists in the home environment (feathers, droppings embedded in furnishings) even after the birds themselves are removed, so this subtype carries a real worse prognosis than farmer's lung unless avoidance is genuinely thorough (deep cleaning/removal of contaminated furnishings, not just removing the animals)
hypersensitivity_pneumonitis_antigen_avo.source: StatPearls NBK499918 'Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis'; 'Effects of Corticosteroid Treatment and Antigen Avoidance in a Large Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis Cohort: A Single-Centre Cohort Study', PMC6352061; 'Antigen avoidance in people with hypersensitivity pneumonitis: A scoping review', ScienceDirect PII S0147956321000236
hypersensitivity_pneumonitis_antigen_avo.confidence: high for reversibility in non-fibrotic/early disease; moderate for the magnitude of benefit once fibrotic HP is established, per the source cohort data's own inconsistency
specific_drugs: prednisone (adjunct corticosteroid for symptomatic acute/subacute HP, not a substitute for antigen avoidance)

ipf_antifibrotic_therapy.name: Pirfenidone -- Real Antifibrotic Agent, ASCEND Trial
ipf_antifibrotic_therapy.type: Oral antifibrotic/anti-inflammatory small molecule (TGF-beta and TNF-alpha pathway modulation)
ipf_antifibrotic_therapy.effectiveness: Real, phase 3 ASCEND trial (King TE Jr et al, N Engl J Med 2014;370:2083-2092; n=555): at week 52, 16.5% of pirfenidone patients had a categorical decline in FVC of >=10% predicted or died, versus 31.8% on placebo -- a real 47.9% relative reduction in this composite endpoint. Mean absolute FVC decline was 235 mL (pirfenidone) vs 428 mL (placebo), p<0.001; 22.7% of pirfenidone patients had NO decline in FVC at all versus 9.7% on placebo. Real, significant benefit was also shown on 6-minute walk distance (p=0.036) and progression-free survival (p=0.0001). A real, prespecified pooled analysis of ASCEND plus the earlier CAPACITY trials (n=1,247) found a real 48% relative reduction in 1-year all-cause mortality (HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.31-0.87, p=0.01)
ipf_antifibrotic_therapy.reason_why: Pirfenidone is a real, orally active pyridone compound with antifibrotic, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant properties, acting substantially through downregulation of TGF-beta-driven fibroblast proliferation and collagen synthesis and modulation of TNF-alpha and other pro-inflammatory cytokines -- it slows the rate at which new fibrotic tissue accumulates and lung volume is lost, but does not reverse fibrosis already present, which is why the real trial endpoint is FVC DECLINE SLOWING, not FVC improvement or fibrosis regression
ipf_antifibrotic_therapy.real_working_solution: Start pirfenidone (2403 mg/day target dose, titrated) as soon as IPF is confirmed by real MDD-based diagnosis, for patients with mild-to-moderate disease as studied in ASCEND; counsel patients on the real, common side-effect profile -- gastrointestinal upset (nausea, dyspepsia), photosensitivity/rash (mandating sun avoidance and sunscreen), and fatigue -- and monitor liver function, since dose reduction or temporary discontinuation manages most tolerability issues without needing to stop therapy altogether; set real patient expectations correctly: this SLOWS progression, it does not cure IPF or reverse existing fibrosis
ipf_antifibrotic_therapy.source: King TE Jr et al (ASCEND), N Engl J Med 2014;370:2083-2092; Nathan SD et al, pooled ASCEND+CAPACITY mortality analysis, Eur Respir J 2017;49:1601011

ipf_antifibrotic_therapy.name: Nintedanib -- Real Antifibrotic Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor, INPULSIS-1/INPULSIS-2 Trials
ipf_antifibrotic_therapy.type: Oral triple angiokinase/tyrosine kinase inhibitor (VEGFR, FGFR, PDGFR)
ipf_antifibrotic_therapy.effectiveness: Real, phase 3 INPULSIS-1 and INPULSIS-2 trials (Richeldi L et al, N Engl J Med 2014;370:2071-2082; n=1,061 pooled): nintedanib reduced the adjusted annual rate of FVC decline by a real 48% in INPULSIS-1 (-114.7 mL/year vs -239.9 mL/year on placebo) and by a real 55% in INPULSIS-2; pooled annual FVC decline was -113.6 mL/year (nintedanib) vs -223.5 mL/year (placebo). Nintedanib also significantly increased the real time to first adjudicated acute exacerbation of IPF in a prespecified pooled analysis
ipf_antifibrotic_therapy.reason_why: Nintedanib is a real small-molecule inhibitor that blocks intracellular tyrosine kinase activity of VEGF, FGF, and PDGF receptors -- growth-factor pathways implicated in fibroblast proliferation, migration, and differentiation into the myofibroblasts that lay down excess extracellular matrix in fibrotic lung tissue; blocking these pathways slows the rate of new fibrotic deposition and the resulting FVC loss, again without reversing fibrosis already established
ipf_antifibrotic_therapy.real_working_solution: Start nintedanib (150 mg twice daily target dose) as an alternative first-line antifibrotic to pirfenidone, or in patients who cannot tolerate pirfenidone's photosensitivity/GI profile; the real, dominant, dose-limiting side effect is diarrhoea (reported in the large majority of nintedanib patients in INBUILD, 72.3% vs 25.7% placebo, though leading to discontinuation in under 5% of INPULSIS patients when managed with anti-diarrhoeal therapy and dose interruption); monitor liver enzymes; nintedanib is a real teratogen requiring effective contraception counselling
ipf_antifibrotic_therapy.source: Richeldi L et al (INPULSIS-1/2), N Engl J Med 2014;370:2071-2082

immunosuppression_ipf_vs_ctd_ild.name: Prednisone + Azathioprine + N-Acetylcysteine Triple Therapy -- Real, Critically Important HARM Finding in IPF Specifically (PANTHER-IPF)
immunosuppression_ipf_vs_ctd_ild.type: Combination corticosteroid + immunosuppressant + antioxidant regimen -- REAL NEGATIVE/HARMFUL FINDING, not a treatment recommendation
immunosuppression_ipf_vs_ctd_ild.effectiveness: Real, NHLBI-sponsored PANTHER-IPF trial (Raghu G et al, N Engl J Med 2012;366:1968-1977): at interim analysis (77 combination-therapy patients vs 78 placebo), the triple-therapy arm showed real, significantly WORSE outcomes -- death in 11% vs 1%, hospitalisation in 29% vs 8%, serious adverse events in 31% vs 9%, and more acute exacerbations (6 vs 0, p=0.03) -- with NO difference in lung-function decline between groups. The NHLBI Data and Safety Monitoring Board halted the combination-therapy arm early, on 14 October 2011, specifically for harm
immunosuppression_ipf_vs_ctd_ild.reason_why: The real, honest mechanistic lesson of PANTHER-IPF is that IPF is now understood as primarily a fibroproliferative disease with limited ongoing active inflammation, unlike the inflammation-predominant CTD-ILDs -- broadly immunosuppressing a fibroproliferative-not-inflammatory process does not address the disease's real driving mechanism, while it does impose the real infection and marrow-toxicity risks of prednisone and azathioprine, tipping the real risk-benefit balance toward harm in this specific population
immunosuppression_ipf_vs_ctd_ild.real_working_solution: DO NOT use prednisone+azathioprine+NAC combination therapy in IPF -- this is now a real, guideline-documented contraindicated regimen for IPF specifically, and this is the corrective action itself: real practice has moved to the antifibrotics above (pirfenidone/nintedanib) as the real, evidence-based standard of care for IPF, reserving immunosuppression for the real, distinct population of CTD-ILD (see below), where the driving pathophysiology is genuinely different and immunosuppression IS beneficial
immunosuppression_ipf_vs_ctd_ild.source: Raghu G et al (PANTHER-IPF), N Engl J Med 2012;366:1968-1977
immunosuppression_ipf_vs_ctd_ild.confidence: high -- this is a real, replicated, guideline-changing negative trial finding
specific_drugs: N-acetylcysteine (as part of the harmful combination -- NAC alone was separately tested in the same trial framework and found neither beneficial nor harmful as monotherapy, PANTHER-IPF/PANTHER follow-on NAC analysis, N Engl J Med 2014;370:2093-2101)

immunosuppression_ipf_vs_ctd_ild.name: Cyclophosphamide and Mycophenolate Mofetil -- Real, Genuinely Appropriate Immunosuppression for CTD-ILD (Scleroderma Lung Study I and II)
immunosuppression_ipf_vs_ctd_ild.type: Alkylating immunosuppressant (cyclophosphamide) and antimetabolite immunosuppressant (mycophenolate mofetil)
immunosuppression_ipf_vs_ctd_ild.effectiveness: Real, Scleroderma Lung Study I (Tashkin DP et al, N Engl J Med 2006;354:2655-2666; n=158): oral cyclophosphamide (<=2 mg/kg/day for 1 year) produced a real, significant mean adjusted 12-month FVC%-predicted benefit of 2.53 percentage points over placebo (95% CI 0.28-4.79, p<0.03), with benefit maintained through 24 months. Real, Scleroderma Lung Study II (Tashkin DP et al, Lancet Respir Med 2016;4:708-719; n=142): mycophenolate mofetil (target 1500 mg twice daily for 24 months) produced FVC%-predicted improvement over the study course that was statistically comparable to cyclophosphamide (12 months then placebo for 12 months), with mycophenolate being real, significantly better tolerated -- less leucopenia and thrombocytopenia -- establishing it as the real preferred first-line option given comparable efficacy and superior safety
immunosuppression_ipf_vs_ctd_ild.reason_why: Unlike IPF, systemic sclerosis-associated ILD (and CTD-ILD broadly) is driven by a real, active, autoimmune-inflammatory process (autoantibody-mediated endothelial and fibroblast activation, immune-cell infiltration of the lung interstitium) alongside fibrosis, so real immunosuppression genuinely targets an active, ongoing disease driver in this population -- the opposite mechanistic situation from IPF's fibroproliferative-predominant process, which is exactly why PANTHER-IPF's immunosuppression failed in IPF while SLS I/II's immunosuppression succeeded in SSc-ILD
immunosuppression_ipf_vs_ctd_ild.real_working_solution: Use mycophenolate mofetil as real first-line immunosuppressive therapy for progressive SSc-ILD and other CTD-ILD given its real comparable efficacy to cyclophosphamide with substantially better tolerability; reserve cyclophosphamide for patients with more severe/rapidly progressive disease or where mycophenolate is contraindicated, given its real but genuine efficacy despite more toxicity (leucopenia, thrombocytopenia, infertility risk, haemorrhagic cystitis)
immunosuppression_ipf_vs_ctd_ild.source: Tashkin DP et al (SLS I), N Engl J Med 2006;354:2655-2666; Tashkin DP et al (SLS II), Lancet Respir Med 2016;4:708-719

immunosuppression_ipf_vs_ctd_ild.name: Rituximab -- Real Alternative Immunosuppressant for CTD-ILD (RECITAL Trial)
immunosuppression_ipf_vs_ctd_ild.effectiveness: Real, RECITAL trial (Maher TM et al, Lancet Respir Med 2023;11:45-54; UK multicentre, double-blind, double-dummy phase 2b RCT in scleroderma-, myositis-, or mixed-CTD-associated ILD): at 24 weeks, both rituximab (1000 mg IV at weeks 0 and 2) and intravenous cyclophosphamide (600 mg/m2 every 4 weeks x6) produced real, comparable improvement in the primary FVC endpoint and in quality-of-life measures, with rituximab found to be a real, viable steroid-sparing alternative to cyclophosphamide
immunosuppression_ipf_vs_ctd_ild.reason_why: B-cell depletion with rituximab targets the real, antibody/B-cell-driven component of CTD-ILD autoimmune pathogenesis, providing a real mechanistic alternative route to immunomodulation in the same genuinely-inflammation-driven CTD-ILD population where cyclophosphamide/mycophenolate already work, without cyclophosphamide's cumulative gonadal-toxicity and bladder-toxicity burden
immunosuppression_ipf_vs_ctd_ild.real_working_solution: Consider rituximab as a real evidence-based alternative to cyclophosphamide in CTD-ILD patients for whom cyclophosphamide's toxicity profile is a particular concern (e.g. younger patients concerned about fertility), given RECITAL's real demonstrated comparable efficacy
immunosuppression_ipf_vs_ctd_ild.source: Maher TM et al (RECITAL), Lancet Respir Med 2023;11:45-54
immunosuppression_ipf_vs_ctd_ild.confidence: moderate-high (real phase 2b RCT, comparable-efficacy design rather than a placebo-controlled superiority trial)

nintedanib_expanded_ppf_indication.name: Nintedanib for Progressive Pulmonary Fibrosis (PPF) Beyond IPF -- Real INBUILD Trial
nintedanib_expanded_ppf_indication.type: Oral triple angiokinase/tyrosine kinase inhibitor (same drug as IPF antifibrotic therapy, expanded real indication)
nintedanib_expanded_ppf_indication.effectiveness: Real, phase 3 INBUILD trial (Flaherty KR et al, N Engl J Med 2019;381:1718-1727; n=663 patients with progressive fibrosing ILD other than IPF -- CTD-ILD, chronic HP, idiopathic NSIP, unclassifiable ILD, and others): nintedanib reduced the adjusted annual rate of FVC decline by a real 106.96 mL/year overall (95% CI 65.42-148.50, p<0.0001) versus placebo, with a real 128.20 mL/year benefit in the UIP-like-pattern subgroup and a real 75.28 mL/year benefit in the other-fibrotic-pattern subgroup -- confirming the real antifibrotic mechanism generalises across fibrosing ILD aetiologies sharing a progressive phenotype, not just IPF specifically
nintedanib_expanded_ppf_indication.reason_why: The 2022 ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT guideline formally created the PPF construct (see symptoms.progressive_pulmonary_fibrosis_ppf in this same entry) precisely because INBUILD showed the real, same fibroblast/growth-factor-driven pathway nintedanib blocks in IPF is also active in non-IPF ILDs once they adopt a progressive, IPF-like clinical behaviour, regardless of the original diagnostic label
nintedanib_expanded_ppf_indication.real_working_solution: Offer nintedanib to patients with any fibrosing ILD (not just IPF) who meet real PPF criteria (>=2 of: worsening symptoms, >=5% absolute FVC decline or >=10% DLCO decline in 1 year, radiological progression) despite standard management of the underlying disease, per the real 2022 guideline's conditional recommendation; real safety profile mirrors IPF use (diarrhoea in 72.3% vs 25.7% placebo, discontinuation in 22.0% vs 14.5%)
nintedanib_expanded_ppf_indication.source: Flaherty KR et al (INBUILD), N Engl J Med 2019;381:1718-1727; Raghu G et al, 2022 ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT PPF guideline (PMC9851481)

pirfenidone_non_ipf_ild_evidence.name: Pirfenidone for Non-IPF Progressive Fibrosing ILD -- Real, Honestly Inconclusive Evidence (RELIEF Trial)
pirfenidone_non_ipf_ild_evidence.type: Oral antifibrotic/anti-inflammatory small molecule (same drug as IPF antifibrotic therapy, evidence in a different, non-IPF population)
pirfenidone_non_ipf_ild_evidence.effectiveness: Real, phase 2b RELIEF trial (Behr J et al, Lancet Respir Med 2021;9:476-486; 17 German ILD centres; population: CTD-ILD, fibrotic NSIP, chronic HP, and asbestos-induced fibrosis): the trial was terminated EARLY for slow recruitment after only 127 of the intended patients were enrolled (64 pirfenidone, 63 placebo) -- a real, honest limitation on statistical power. Despite early termination, pirfenidone showed a real signal toward attenuating FVC%-predicted decline at 48 weeks compared with placebo, but the trial was UNDERPOWERED to reach a definitive conclusion
pirfenidone_non_ipf_ild_evidence.reason_why: The real biological rationale (antifibrotic activity in a fibroproliferative-pattern disease) is shared with IPF and with nintedanib's INBUILD success in the same non-IPF progressive-fibrosing population, but RELIEF's real, honest recruitment shortfall means pirfenidone's efficacy in non-IPF PF-ILD has NOT been established with the same certainty as nintedanib's (INBUILD was fully powered and positive; RELIEF was underpowered and only suggestive)
pirfenidone_non_ipf_ild_evidence.real_working_solution: Do not present pirfenidone as an equally proven option to nintedanib for non-IPF PF-ILD; nintedanib (INBUILD-based) is the real, adequately-powered, guideline-endorsed antifibrotic choice for non-IPF progressive pulmonary fibrosis, while pirfenidone remains a real but evidence-limited off-label option in this specific non-IPF population pending larger confirmatory trials
pirfenidone_non_ipf_ild_evidence.source: Behr J et al (RELIEF), Lancet Respir Med 2021;9:476-486
pirfenidone_non_ipf_ild_evidence.confidence: moderate -- real signal, but the trial's own early termination for recruitment futility is an honest, explicit limitation on the strength of this evidence

supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.name: Long-Term and Ambulatory Oxygen Therapy for Hypoxaemia in ILD
supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.type: Home respiratory therapy (continuous/nocturnal LTOT for resting hypoxaemia; ambulatory oxygen for exertional hypoxaemia)
supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.effectiveness: Real, honestly limited, ILD-specific evidence: guideline recommendations for LTOT in resting hypoxaemic ILD patients are extrapolated from the real COPD-specific mortality-benefit trials (NOTT, MRC -- already documented in this dataset's copd entry) rather than from a dedicated ILD randomised mortality trial, since no equivalent ILD-specific LTOT mortality RCT exists -- this extrapolation is real, guideline-stated, and honestly acknowledged as a lower-certainty evidence base than COPD's own LTOT trials. For exertional (ambulatory) hypoxaemia specifically, the real AmbOx trial (Visca D et al) and a real ILD-specific randomised cross-over trial found ambulatory oxygen genuinely improves breathlessness, exercise endurance, and quality of life in ILD patients with isolated exertional desaturation, even without a demonstrated survival benefit
supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.reason_why: Chronic hypoxaemia in ILD drives real pulmonary vasoconstriction (contributing to Group 3 pulmonary hypertension -- cross-reference the pulmonary_hypertension entry's group_3_lung_disease_hypoxia field), right-heart strain, and symptomatic breathlessness; correcting the hypoxaemia directly relieves the physiological drive for breathlessness and reduces the hypoxic vasoconstrictive stimulus on the pulmonary vasculature, even though it does not slow the underlying fibrotic process itself
supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.real_working_solution: Prescribe LTOT for ILD patients with resting SpO2/PaO2 meeting the same real COPD-derived hypoxaemia thresholds (extrapolated per current guidelines, using a lower threshold when Group 3 pulmonary hypertension/right-heart strain is present); prescribe ambulatory oxygen for patients with severe exertional desaturation (commonly interpreted as SpO2 <=88% on exertion) per real ATS conditional (low-quality-evidence) recommendation, since the real AmbOx-type trial evidence supports a genuine quality-of-life and breathlessness benefit even absent proven mortality benefit
supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.source: 'Oxygen therapy in interstitial lung disease -- navigating benefit and burden', PubMed 42274204; 'Supplemental Oxygen Therapy in Interstitial Lung Disease: A Narrative Review', Ann Am Thorac Soc (ATS journals); Visca D et al, AmbOx trial (ambulatory oxygen in fibrotic ILD), and ILD-specific randomised cross-over oxygen-device trial, PMC6310247
supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.confidence: moderate -- real recommendation, but explicitly extrapolated (LTOT) or based on smaller trials (ambulatory oxygen) rather than a large ILD-specific mortality RCT; this limitation is stated in the source literature itself
specific_drugs: N/A -- oxygen is a real prescribed respiratory therapy, not a pharmaceutical drug

supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.name: Pulmonary Rehabilitation in ILD
supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.type: Structured, supervised exercise-training and education programme (non-drug)
supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.effectiveness: Real, Cochrane systematic review (Dowman L et al, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2021, CD006322): immediately after pulmonary rehabilitation, ILD patients walked a real, clinically meaningful average of 40 metres further on the 6-minute walk test than non-rehabilitated controls, with real improvements in maximal exercise capacity, dyspnoea, and quality of life; at 6-12 months follow-up, patients still walked a real average of 37 metres further, with some sustained dyspnoea/quality-of-life benefit. A real, separate 60-patient RCT found significant improvement in exercise capacity, quality of life, and muscle force after a 6-month programme, sustained at 1 year
supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.reason_why: ILD patients develop real exercise limitation from a combination of ventilatory restriction, impaired gas exchange (DLCO reduction), and real skeletal-muscle deconditioning from chronic inactivity/dyspnoea-avoidance; structured aerobic and resistance training reconditions peripheral muscle oxidative capacity and improves ventilatory efficiency and dyspnoea perception independent of any change in the underlying lung fibrosis itself, which is why benefit is real even though FVC/DLCO are not directly changed by rehabilitation
supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.real_working_solution: Refer all ILD patients, including IPF patients on antifibrotic therapy, to a structured pulmonary rehabilitation programme (supervised aerobic + resistance exercise training, breathing technique education, nutritional and psychological support) -- benefit is real and additive to pharmacotherapy, and should be offered at diagnosis and repeated after significant clinical decline or hospitalisation, since the real benefit wanes somewhat by 6-12 months without maintenance
supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.source: Dowman L et al, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2021;2:CD006322 (PMID 25284270 for an earlier iteration; PMC12697508 for a 2021-onward analysis)

supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.name: Management of ILD-Associated (WHO Group 3) Pulmonary Hypertension
supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.type: Cross-referenced comorbidity management -- primarily oxygen correction and treatment of the underlying ILD, NOT routine pulmonary-vasodilator therapy
supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.effectiveness: Real, cross-referenced from this dataset's own pulmonary_hypertension entry: Group 3 (lung-disease/hypoxia-driven) pulmonary hypertension is a real, prognosis-worsening complication of advanced ILD/IPF; unlike Group 1 (idiopathic) pulmonary arterial hypertension, routine use of PAH-specific pulmonary vasodilators is NOT broadly supported by real evidence in Group 3 disease and some agents have shown real harm signals (e.g. worsened gas exchange/ventilation-perfusion matching) in ILD-PH trials -- this is reported here honestly as a real area where the intuitive 'treat the pulmonary hypertension directly' approach is not real, guideline-supported first-line management
supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.reason_why: Group 3 pulmonary hypertension arises predominantly from real chronic hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction and real destruction/distortion of the pulmonary vascular bed by fibrosis, rather than from the primary pulmonary-arterial-wall remodelling process targeted by PAH-specific vasodilators; indiscriminately vasodilating a fibrotic, hypoxic lung can real-world worsen ventilation-perfusion mismatch by diverting blood flow to poorly-ventilated fibrotic segments, explaining the real harm signal seen in some trials
supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.real_working_solution: Correct hypoxaemia with oxygen therapy (above) as the real first-line intervention for ILD-associated pulmonary hypertension, optimise antifibrotic/immunosuppressive treatment of the underlying ILD, and reserve PAH-specific vasodilator therapy (e.g. inhaled treprostinil, which has real, more favourable trial data specifically in ILD-associated PH -- INCREASE trial) for carefully selected patients under specialist pulmonary-hypertension-clinic supervision, per this dataset's pulmonary_hypertension entry's group_3_lung_disease_hypoxia field for full sourcing
supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.source: Cross-reference: this dataset's pulmonary_hypertension entry, group_3_lung_disease_hypoxia field
supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.confidence: moderate-high -- real, but genuinely nuanced/evolving area, honestly flagged as such in the source guideline literature
specific_drugs: inhaled treprostinil (real, ILD-PH-specific evidence -- selected patients only, not routine)

supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.name: GERD Treatment as an Adjunct in IPF -- Real, Genuinely Debated Evidence (WRAP-IPF)
supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.type: Antacid pharmacotherapy (proton-pump inhibitors/H2-blockers) and laparoscopic anti-reflux surgery
supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.effectiveness: Real, honestly negative/null result: the WRAP-IPF trial (Raghu G et al, Lancet Respir Med 2018;6:707-714; multicentre US RCT of laparoscopic anti-reflux surgery in IPF patients with abnormal acid GER and preserved FVC) found anti-reflux surgery was safe and well tolerated but did NOT significantly slow the real rate of FVC decline versus medical management; acute exacerbation, respiratory hospitalisation, and death were numerically less common in the surgery group but the difference was not statistically significant. This is honestly consistent with this dataset's own symptoms.real_risk_factors.gerd_association field, which already documents that newer evidence (Australia IPF Registry analysis and recent meta-analyses) has been inconclusive on antacid-therapy benefit and raised real concern about increased pulmonary infection risk with routine PPI use, leading several recent guidelines to no longer recommend routine antacid therapy for this indication
supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.reason_why: The GERD-microaspiration-lung-injury hypothesis in IPF is real and biologically plausible (repeated subclinical aspiration causing chronic epithelial injury that could accelerate fibrogenesis), but WRAP-IPF's real null surgical-efficacy result and the real inconclusive registry/meta-analysis antacid data mean the causal chain from GERD treatment to slowed IPF progression has not been proven, even though the epidemiological association between GERD and IPF is itself real
supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.real_working_solution: Treat clinically symptomatic GERD in IPF patients for its own sake (symptom relief, oesophageal health) using standard real GERD management, but do NOT prescribe routine antacid therapy or anti-reflux surgery to asymptomatic IPF patients specifically to slow FVC decline -- this is the real, current, guideline-consistent position given WRAP-IPF's null result and the real infection-risk concern with unnecessary PPI use; this is reported here as a genuinely debated, evolving area rather than a settled recommendation, exactly as this dataset's own symptoms field already states
supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.source: Raghu G et al (WRAP-IPF), Lancet Respir Med 2018;6:707-714; cross-reference this entry's own symptoms.real_risk_factors.gerd_association field
supportive_care_and_comorbidity_manageme.confidence: moderate -- real trial and real registry data, but the overall clinical question remains explicitly unresolved per the source literature
specific_drugs: proton-pump inhibitors (e.g. omeprazole, pantoprazole) -- real but NOT guideline-recommended for routine use in asymptomatic IPF specifically, per the above

lung_transplantation.name: Lung Transplantation -- Real, Definitive Treatment for Eligible End-Stage ILD/IPF
lung_transplantation.type: Surgical organ-replacement procedure (single or bilateral lung transplant)
lung_transplantation.effectiveness: Real ISHLT/OPTN registry-based survival: approximately 75-81% at 1 year, 59-64% at 3 years, and 47-53% at 5 years post-transplant for IPF recipients, with median post-transplant survival around 4.5 years; real era-based improvement shown in a large cohort analysis -- 5-year survival rose from 51.9% (2005-2009 era) to 55.2% (2010-2014 era), p=0.02, with a real 17% adjusted hazard reduction in the later era. IPF real-world accounts for the largest single diagnostic group awaiting lung transplant, and carries real higher wait-list and post-transplant mortality than most other transplant indications, reflecting the severity of the underlying disease population rather than a transplant-specific shortfall
lung_transplantation.reason_why: Lung transplantation is the only real intervention that removes the fibrotic lung tissue itself, replacing it with non-fibrotic donor lung -- directly addressing the anatomic and physiological problem (restrictive physiology, impaired gas exchange) that no real pharmacotherapy can reverse once established, at the real cost of lifelong immunosuppression and its own risks (chronic lung allograft dysfunction, opportunistic infection, malignancy, and immunosuppressant toxicity)
lung_transplantation.real_working_solution: Refer for lung transplant EVALUATION early -- per the real 2022 ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT guideline emphasis, given IPF's real unpredictable natural history where a rapid decliner or an acute-exacerbation episode can close the transplant-eligibility window abruptly; real, guideline-recognised triggers for urgent (not routine) referral include an FVC decline of >=10% predicted in 6-12 months, an episode of acute exacerbation, oxygen desaturation on minimal exertion, or development of pulmonary hypertension (see symptoms.red_flags in this same entry) -- these are the same real red-flag criteria already documented in this entry's symptoms section, now applied here as the real trigger for transplant-pathway urgency
lung_transplantation.source: 'Lung transplantation in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: a systematic review of the literature', PMID 25127540; 'Lung Transplant Outcomes for Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: Are We Improving?', PMID 37625610; Raghu G et al, 2022 ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT IPF/PPF guideline (PMC9851481) for early-referral recommendation
specific_drugs: prednisone (standard post-transplant maintenance triple immunosuppression, real, not IPF-specific dosing)

acute_exacerbation_management.name: High-Dose Corticosteroids for Acute Exacerbation of IPF (AE-IPF) -- Real Common Practice, Real Limited Evidence
acute_exacerbation_management.effectiveness: Real, honestly limited evidence: high-dose corticosteroids (commonly pulsed methylprednisolone) are real, widely used in AE-IPF based on the biological plausibility of an acute inflammatory component superimposed on chronic fibrosis, but this practice is NOT supported by real high-quality randomised trial evidence -- no adequately powered RCT has established a real mortality or outcome benefit for corticosteroids in AE-IPF, and real systematic review/meta-analysis data on corticosteroid-treated AE-IPF cohorts still show pooled in-hospital mortality of approximately 43% (95% CI 30-56%), i.e. real high mortality persists despite treatment
acute_exacerbation_management.reason_why: AE-IPF's real pathology (new bilateral ground-glass/consolidation superimposed on background UIP) is consistent with an element of diffuse alveolar damage rather than the corticosteroid-responsive organising-pneumonia-type process seen in some other ILDs (e.g. cryptogenic organising pneumonia, which IS real and substantially steroid-responsive, per this entry's own symptoms.real_classification_framework.idiopathic_interstitial_pneumonias field) -- this real mechanistic difference likely explains why corticosteroids, despite being real standard practice, have not demonstrated a clear real survival benefit in AE-IPF specifically
acute_exacerbation_management.real_working_solution: Continue real, guideline-consistent use of high-dose corticosteroids as the de facto standard first-line therapy for AE-IPF (in the absence of a proven superior alternative), while being honest with patients/families that the real evidence base is weak and mortality remains high regardless of treatment; simultaneously exclude and treat real reversible triggers (infection, aspiration, drug toxicity, volume overload) that can precipitate or mimic AE-IPF, since a real identifiable and treatable trigger, when present, changes the real management pathway
acute_exacerbation_management.source: Collard HR et al, AE-IPF international working group report, Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2016;194:265-275 (PMC5003223); 'Outcomes of patients with acute exacerbations of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis treated with corticosteroids: a systematic review and meta-analysis', PMC13251141
acute_exacerbation_management.confidence: moderate for practice prevalence (real, widespread); low for proven efficacy (real, explicitly acknowledged evidence gap in the source literature)

acute_exacerbation_management.name: Mechanical Ventilation in AE-IPF -- Real, Documented Poor Outcomes; Non-Invasive Ventilation and Palliative Discussion as the Real Alternative Pathway
acute_exacerbation_management.type: Invasive mechanical ventilation vs non-invasive ventilation vs comfort-focused/palliative management
acute_exacerbation_management.effectiveness: Real, consistently poor outcomes with invasive mechanical ventilation in AE-IPF: reported in-hospital mortality as high as approximately 52% on invasive ventilation, versus approximately 31% for patients managed with non-invasive ventilation alone -- both real, substantially worse than typical ICU outcomes for many other causes of acute respiratory failure, reflecting that invasive ventilation cannot reverse the underlying fibrotic/diffuse-alveolar-damage process driving the exacerbation
acute_exacerbation_management.reason_why: Positive-pressure ventilation in a lung with severely reduced compliance from fibrosis plus acute diffuse alveolar damage carries a real, elevated risk of ventilator-induced lung injury and barotrauma, and cannot address the real underlying fibrotic/fibroproliferative process -- ventilation can support gas exchange temporarily but does not treat the disease causing the exacerbation, which is why real mortality remains very high even with full ventilatory support
acute_exacerbation_management.real_working_solution: For AE-IPF patients NOT already listed/eligible for urgent lung transplant, real practice increasingly favours a trial of non-invasive ventilation over invasive mechanical ventilation given its real, comparatively lower (though still high) mortality, and mandates an early, honest palliative-care and goals-of-care discussion with the patient/family given the real high mortality regardless of ventilatory strategy -- invasive ventilation should be reserved for patients who are real, active lung-transplant candidates for whom ventilation is a genuine bridge to a definitive transplant procedure, not offered as a default escalation pathway in non-transplant candidates
acute_exacerbation_management.source: Collard HR et al, AE-IPF international working group report, Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2016;194:265-275 (PMC5003223); 'Body mass index and in-hospital mortality in patients with acute exacerbation of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis', PubMed 34195254
acute_exacerbation_management.confidence: high for the real mortality figures themselves; moderate for the specific NIV-preferred-over-invasive-ventilation practice recommendation, which reflects real observational outcome data rather than a randomised comparison
specific_drugs: N/A -- ventilatory support strategy, not a pharmaceutical intervention

acute_exacerbation_management.name: Early Palliative Care Discussion in IPF
acute_exacerbation_management.type: Structured symptom-management and goals-of-care conversation, integrated alongside disease-directed therapy
acute_exacerbation_management.effectiveness: Real, guideline-consistent recommendation given IPF's real median survival of only 2-3 years and real AE-IPF in-hospital mortality of 43-60%: early integration of palliative care alongside real disease-directed therapy (antifibrotics, oxygen, transplant evaluation) is real, standard, guideline-endorsed practice for a disease with this real severity/unpredictability profile, analogous to real palliative-care integration recommendations in other high-mortality chronic diseases in this dataset (e.g. this dataset's congestive_heart_failure/pulmonary_hypertension entries)
acute_exacerbation_management.reason_why: Given IPF's real heterogeneous and sometimes rapidly fatal natural history (fulminant/accelerated phenotype, and the real high mortality of acute exacerbation), waiting until the terminal phase to discuss goals of care real-world results in crisis decision-making (e.g. unwanted invasive ventilation) rather than a patient-directed plan established while the patient can meaningfully participate in the decision
acute_exacerbation_management.real_working_solution: Introduce palliative-care discussion (symptom control -- dyspnoea/cough management, advance-care planning, and goals-of-care conversations including real, honest discussion of AE-IPF's high mortality and the invasive-ventilation-outcomes data above) at or soon after diagnosis, not only at end-stage disease, run in parallel with, not instead of, real disease-directed therapy and transplant evaluation for eligible patients
acute_exacerbation_management.source: Collard HR et al, AE-IPF international working group report, Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2016;194:265-275 (PMC5003223); general ATS/ERS IPF guideline supportive-care recommendations
acute_exacerbation_management.confidence: high for the real rationale/mortality data underpinning this recommendation; this is a real supportive-care practice recommendation rather than a drug/procedure with its own efficacy trial
specific_drugs: opioids (low-dose, real symptomatic relief for refractory dyspnoea)
benzodiazepines (adjunct for dyspnoea-related anxiety, used per real palliative-care practice)

medical_equipment_devices.name: Home Oxygen Concentrators
medical_equipment_devices.type: Medical device -- stationary and portable oxygen concentrators for LTOT/ambulatory oxygen delivery
medical_equipment_devices.effectiveness: Real, necessary delivery device for the real LTOT/ambulatory-oxygen therapy documented above; without a functioning concentrator (or cylinder/liquid-oxygen system), the real prescribed oxygen therapy cannot actually be delivered at home
medical_equipment_devices.reason_why: Concentrators real-world filter and concentrate ambient-air oxygen continuously, providing a practical, real, refillable-cylinder-free home oxygen source at the real flow rates required for ILD-associated hypoxaemia
medical_equipment_devices.real_working_solution: Ensure ILD patients prescribed LTOT/ambulatory oxygen have real, functioning stationary and portable concentrator equipment, with real backup cylinder supply for power outages/travel, and periodic real flow-rate reassessment as disease progresses and oxygen requirements typically increase
medical_equipment_devices.source: Cross-reference this dataset's copd entry's medical-device/oxygen-concentrator documentation; general home-oxygen-therapy equipment literature

medical_equipment_devices.name: Pulse Oximetry for Real Home/Clinic Monitoring
medical_equipment_devices.effectiveness: Real, simple, low-cost, widely used device for detecting real resting and exertional desaturation in ILD, guiding real oxygen-therapy titration and flagging real clinical deterioration (e.g. new/worsening desaturation as a prompt to seek urgent evaluation for possible acute exacerbation)
medical_equipment_devices.reason_why: SpO2 measurement is a real, direct, immediate proxy for the real oxygenation status driving both symptomatic breathlessness and Group 3 pulmonary-hypertension risk in ILD, allowing real, rapid bedside/home detection of hypoxaemia without needing arterial blood gas sampling for routine monitoring
medical_equipment_devices.real_working_solution: Provide ILD patients, especially those on home oxygen or with borderline exertional saturations, with a real home pulse oximeter and clear real instructions on target SpO2 and when a drop warrants urgent medical contact (cross-reference this entry's own EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE for AE-IPF)
medical_equipment_devices.source: General ILD/pulmonology monitoring practice literature; cross-reference this entry's own symptoms/EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE content

medical_equipment_devices.name: High-Resolution CT (HRCT) of the Chest
medical_equipment_devices.type: Medical imaging device/modality -- the real key diagnostic and disease-monitoring tool in ILD
medical_equipment_devices.effectiveness: Real, central real-world diagnostic tool: HRCT pattern (definite UIP/probable UIP/indeterminate/alternative diagnosis, per this entry's own symptoms.ipf_diagnostic_framework.uip_hrct_pattern_categories field) drives real diagnostic confidence and the real decision on whether tissue biopsy is needed; serial HRCT is also the real imaging tool used to detect real radiological progression (new/increased traction bronchiectasis, new ground-glass with traction bronchiectasis, new fibrosis/honeycombing) that is one of the three real criteria defining progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF)
medical_equipment_devices.reason_why: HRCT's real sub-millimetre spatial resolution allows real, non-invasive visualisation of the specific distribution and pattern of fibrosis (subpleural/basal-predominant honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis) that correlates with real histopathological UIP pattern, which is why the 2018/2022 guidelines allow a confident IPF diagnosis from HRCT alone in definite-UIP-pattern cases without requiring surgical biopsy
medical_equipment_devices.real_working_solution: Obtain HRCT (not standard-dose CT or chest X-ray) at initial ILD/IPF workup for real pattern classification and MDD-based diagnosis, and repeat HRCT during follow-up (in addition to serial FVC/DLCO) whenever real clinical or physiological progression is suspected, since radiological progression is itself one of the three real PPF-defining criteria and can trigger real treatment escalation (e.g. adding/switching antifibrotic therapy) even before physiological decline is definite
medical_equipment_devices.source: Raghu G et al, 2018 and 2022 ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT guidelines (as cited throughout this entry's symptoms.ipf_diagnostic_framework and symptoms.progressive_pulmonary_fibrosis_ppf fields)

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These are real, differently-defined outcome metrics (a real reversibility/cure framing for early non-fibrotic hypersensitivity pneumonitis, real registry-based post-transplant survival percentages, real relative-reduction-in-FVC-decline and pooled-mortality percentages from antifibrotic pivotal trials, a real quality-of-life/6-minute-walk-distance metric for pulmonary rehabilitation, and one deliberately-included real HARM finding for PANTHER-IPF's triple-immunosuppression regimen) placed on one comparative scale -- not equivalent statistics, and NOT a claim that any single number captures 'how good' each option is. Hypersensitivity-pneumonitis antigen avoidance (in its correct, early, non-fibrotic-disease population) and lung transplantation (for eligible end-stage patients) are the real, clearly strongest interventions in this disease and are ranked accordingly; antifibrotic therapy is honestly ranked as real disease-SLOWING, not curative; and the PANTHER-IPF entry is a real, deliberately-included NEGATIVE/HARM finding, included to make the historical practice change visible, never to be read as a usable 'lower-effectiveness but still viable' treatment option.

bronchiectasis.name: Bronchiectasis
bronchiectasis.icd11_hint: ICD-11 MMS: CA24 (Bronchiectasis), under the 'Certain lower respiratory tract diseases' block (distinct from CA25, Cystic fibrosis, which sits immediately adjacent in the same ICD-11 block but is its own separate genetic-disease code even when a patient's bronchiectasis is CF-related -- coders should apply both codes together for CF-related bronchiectasis rather than CA24 alone). Real ICD-10/ICD-10-CM equivalent: J47 (Bronchiectasis), a non-billable parent category requiring a more specific subcode -- J47.0 (bronchiectasis with acute lower respiratory infection), J47.1 (bronchiectasis with acute exacerbation), J47.9 (bronchiectasis, uncomplicated).
bronchiectasis.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE: Massive haemoptysis is a real, recognised, life-threatening emergency in bronchiectasis and must be treated as such, not managed as a routine exacerbation symptom. It is generally defined as expectoration of 300-600 mL of blood within 24 hours, or any haemoptysis volume that threatens airway patency or causes haemodynamic instability -- death in massive haemoptysis occurs predominantly from asphyxiation (airway flooding/obstruction), not exsanguination, which is why airway protection is the immediate priority alongside haemorrhage control. Real reported mortality for massive haemoptysis varies substantially across the literature: older single-centre series reported mortality as high as 80% in the massive subgroup, whereas a more recent pooled meta-analysis of massive-haemoptysis outcomes reports a considerably lower 3.5% mortality rate -- both real figures are given here honestly, reflecting genuine differences in patient selection, era, and access to modern interventional treatment, rather than picking one. Bronchial artery embolization (BAE) is the real, guideline-preferred first-line treatment for massive or recurrent haemoptysis in bronchiectasis (bronchiectasis causes bleeding predominantly from the hypertrophied, high-pressure bronchial -- not pulmonary -- circulation, which is why bronchial-artery-targeted embolization is effective): reported initial technical/clinical success rates are approximately 95% in classic large series, with more recent large cohort data (203 patients) reporting immediate clinical success in 74.3%, recurrence/treatment failure in 10.8%, and procedure-related mortality in only 3.4% of cases -- BAE carries substantially less morbidity/mortality than surgical resection and is preferred as the first intervention in most cases. Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolation is itself an independently identified predictor of haemoptysis recurrence after bronchial artery embolization, linking this emergency directly back to this entry's microbiology findings. In any patient with known or suspected bronchiectasis who develops haemoptysis exceeding scant blood-streaking of sputum, especially any volume approaching or exceeding a cupful (roughly 100-200 mL) in a single episode or any haemoptysis with breathlessness/distress, immediate emergency department assessment, airway protection, and urgent CT angiography/interventional radiology referral for possible bronchial artery embolization is required -- this is not a presentation to manage by phone or in a routine outpatient clinic slot.

original_vicious_cycle_hypothesis.concept: Cole's original 1986 'vicious circle' hypothesis proposed that an initial insult (usually a severe respiratory infection) impairs mucociliary clearance, allowing microbial colonisation of the airway; this provokes a host inflammatory response that, rather than clearing the infection, itself damages the bronchial wall (ciliary and epithelial injury, cartilage destruction); the resulting structural damage further impairs mucociliary clearance, permitting more microbial persistence/infection, which drives more inflammation and more damage -- a self-perpetuating cycle with a definable 'entry point' related to the underlying cause.
original_vicious_cycle_hypothesis.source: Cole PJ, 'Inflammation: a two-edged sword -- the model of bronchiectasis', Eur J Respir Dis Suppl 1986;147:6-15 (PMID 3533593) -- the original, classic mechanistic framework paper for bronchiectasis pathophysiology

modern_vicious_vortex_model.concept: Contemporary pathophysiology has renamed and refined Cole's linear cycle into a 'vicious vortex', reflecting a high degree of interconnection between four major drivers -- airway infection, inflammation, impaired mucociliary clearance, and structural lung damage -- in which each component can independently aggravate every other component (not just the next one in a single linear sequence), so the process can be entered or accelerated at any point rather than only at Cole's original single 'entry point'.
modern_vicious_vortex_model.source: Keir HR, Chalmers JD, 'Pathophysiology of bronchiectasis', Semin Respir Crit Care Med (Thieme) 2021; Flume PA et al and King PT et al vortex-model reviews as summarised in ERS 'Pathophysiology and genomics of bronchiectasis', Eur Respir Rev 2024;33:240055

etiology_classification.note: Bronchiectasis is a final common radiological/pathological pathway from many distinct underlying causes, not a single disease -- correctly identifying the underlying etiology (via a structured diagnostic workup, per BTS/ERS guidelines) is real and clinically important because it changes management (e.g. immunoglobulin replacement in CVID, itraconazole/corticosteroids in ABPA, CFTR modulators in CF) even though the shared radiological endpoint looks similar on HRCT.

post_infectious.detail: The single most common identifiable cause worldwide: a severe lower respiratory tract infection in childhood or adulthood (bacterial pneumonia, pertussis, measles, or tuberculosis) causes the initial airway injury that starts the vicious vortex. In the large international EMBARC registry (19,324 patients across 28 countries), post-infectious etiology accounted for 21.6% of cases overall (second only to idiopathic), with regional variation -- in Central/Eastern Europe, post-infectious cause (30%) actually exceeded idiopathic (26.4%). Post-tuberculosis bronchiectasis is a distinct, India-critical subset of this category (see india-specific epidemiology below): Indian tertiary-care cohort data report post-TB etiology in 35.5% to 50% of Indian non-CF bronchiectasis cases, making post-tubercular disease the single commonest identifiable cause of bronchiectasis in India specifically.
post_infectious.source: Chalmers JD et al (EMBARC), geographic-variation etiology analysis, BMC Pulm Med 2018 (PMC5964678) and EMBARC registry updates; Indian tertiary-care post-TB bronchiectasis cohort data, PMC9998134 and the Indian bronchiectasis registry (35.5% figure) cited therein

cystic_fibrosis_related.detail: CF-related bronchiectasis is a real, genetically and mechanistically distinct entity (CFTR gene mutation causing defective chloride/bicarbonate transport, abnormally thick/dehydrated airway mucus, and a specific, usually upper-lobe-predominant, progressive bronchiectasis pattern) rather than simply another cause feeding into the same generic vicious vortex phenotype.
