ranked_high_to_low.type: Pharmacotherapy (obesity-driven OSA, disease-modifying via weight loss)
ranked_high_to_low.metric: 43.0% of tirzepatide (highest dose)-treated participants met prespecified criteria for OSA disease resolution (AHI<5, or AHI 5-14 with minimal symptoms) at 52 weeks in Study 1 (non-PAP cohort), 51.5% in Study 2 (PAP-using cohort) - directly reported, SURMOUNT-OSA trial; mean AHI reduction -25.3 events/hour vs -5.3 placebo (Study 1, absolute reduction, not itself a percentage).
ranked_high_to_low.source: SURMOUNT-OSA trial, NEJM 2024

ranked_high_to_low.name: Hypoglossal nerve stimulation (Inspire) - durable 5-year AHI reduction
ranked_high_to_low.metric: 75% AHI responder rate (>=50% reduction and AHI<20 events/hour) sustained at 5 years with hypoglossal nerve stimulation (63% by last-observation-carried-forward analysis), directly reported - STAR trial 5-year follow-up, Woodson BT et al, Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2018;159:194-202 (PMID 29582703); AHI reduction -15.91 events/hour sustained at 5 years.
ranked_high_to_low.source: STAR trial 5-year follow-up, Woodson BT et al, Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2018;159:194-202 (PMID 29582703)

ranked_high_to_low.name: UPPP - long-term AHI reduction
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Pooled AHI reduction percentage; long-term surgical success only 28.6-55%, usually does not normalize AHI
ranked_high_to_low.source: UPPP long-term efficacy meta-analysis, 2019

ranked_high_to_low.name: Mandibular advancement device (oral appliance) - AHI reduction vs CPAP
ranked_high_to_low.metric: AHI reduction real but ~8.4 events/hour less than CPAP (CPAP superior efficacy, MAD superior real-world adherence)
ranked_high_to_low.source: Oral appliance vs CPAP comparative meta-analysis

ranked_high_to_low.name: Positional therapy - supine AHI reduction in positional OSA subtype only
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Supine-AHI mean difference -7.46 events/hour vs placebo; no significant OVERALL AHI benefit found in pooled analysis
ranked_high_to_low.source: Positional therapy comparative meta-analysis, Front Med 2025

ranked_high_to_low.name: CPAP real-world adherence rate
ranked_high_to_low.type: Practical limitation - explains the efficacy-trial vs real-world outcome gap
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Approximate real-world adherence rate (100% minus 34.1% pooled non-adherence rate over 20 years of data)
ranked_high_to_low.source: Rotenberg et al., J Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2016

lung_cancer.name: Lung Cancer -- Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) and Small Cell Lung Cancer (SCLC)
lung_cancer.category_note: Filed under a distinct 'Oncology (Respiratory-Tract Malignancy)' categorization rather than plain 'Respiratory' -- lung cancer is a malignant neoplastic disease process with its own staging system (TNM), molecular/biomarker landscape, and multidisciplinary oncological management pathway, genuinely distinct from this knowledge base's existing Respiratory entries (COPD, asthma, pneumonia, TB, ILD, bronchiectasis, OSA), which are infective/inflammatory/structural-airway disease processes. This judgment call is noted explicitly per the task's instruction to use judgement on categorization.
lung_cancer.icd11_hint: ICD-11 MMS: 2C25 (Malignant neoplasms of bronchus or lung), with real subcodes including 2C25.0 (Small cell carcinoma of bronchus or lung) and 2C25.Y/2C25.Z for other specified/unspecified bronchus-or-lung malignant neoplasms (non-small cell histologies such as adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma are further specified via the histology-coding axis). Real ICD-10/ICD-10-CM equivalent: C34 (Malignant neoplasm of bronchus and lung), with subcodes by laterality/site (C34.0 main bronchus, C34.1 upper lobe, C34.2 middle lobe, C34.3 lower lobe, C34.8 overlapping sites, C34.9 unspecified).
lung_cancer.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE: A patient with known or suspected lung cancer who develops any of the following is having a real oncologic emergency requiring immediate emergency department assessment, not a routine oncology follow-up visit. (1) Superior vena cava (SVC) syndrome -- facial/neck/upper-limb swelling, distended neck/chest-wall veins, dyspnoea and headache worse lying flat -- caused by tumour invasion, extrinsic compression, or thrombosis of the SVC; lung cancer (together with non-Hodgkin lymphoma) causes 85-90% of malignant SVC syndrome cases, and SVC syndrome is the first presentation of an undiagnosed cancer in up to 60% of cases (source: PMC8727327, 'Malignant Superior Vena Cava Syndrome: State of the Art'). (2) Massive haemoptysis -- expectoration of more than approximately 30 mL of blood in 24 hours, or any large/rapidly-accumulating volume -- which carries an untreated mortality of 50-80%, with suffocation (airway flooding), not exsanguination, being the usual mechanism of death; 5-10% of NSCLC cases are complicated by severe haemoptysis at some point (source: CHEST journal, 'Managing Massive Hemoptysis'; case literature on lung-cancer-related massive haemoptysis). (3) Malignant spinal cord compression from vertebral/epidural metastasis -- new or worsening back pain, limb weakness, sensory loss, or bladder/bowel dysfunction -- where lung cancer accounts for approximately 22.9% of all malignant spinal cord compression cases, and detection/intervention within the first 24 hours is essential to prevent irreversible paraplegia; spinal cord compression can be a cancer's first presenting feature in up to 20% of cases (source: Anticancer Research, 'Metastatic Spinal Cord Compression: Unraveling the Diagnostic and Therapeutic Challenges'; PMC10527546). In any of these three scenarios, call an ambulance / go to the nearest emergency department immediately; do not wait for a scheduled oncology appointment. Separately (a related but distinct real emergency-adjacent presentation, not one of the three core override triggers above), new-onset seizure or new focal neurological deficit in a patient with known or suspected lung cancer should prompt urgent same-day neurological/oncological assessment and brain imaging for possible brain metastasis, reported in approximately 16-20% of lung adenocarcinoma cases (source: Moffitt Cancer Center, 'Lung Cancer Metastasis to Brain'; PMC11274762).

histologic_classification.overview: Lung cancer is divided into two major biological categories that drive completely different clinical behaviour, staging nuances, and (per the parallel treatment work) treatment pathways: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC), which accounts for approximately 85% of all lung cancers, and Small Cell Lung Cancer (SCLC), which accounts for approximately 15%.
histologic_classification.source: American Cancer Society, 'What Is Lung Cancer?'; WHO Classification of Thoracic Tumours, 5th edition (2021)

adenocarcinoma.detail: Now the single most common histologic subtype of lung cancer overall, accounting for approximately 40% of all lung cancers, and the dominant subtype specifically in never-smokers -- in a study of 1,860 NSCLC patients, 707 (38.0%) were never-smokers, and adenocarcinoma made up 89.8% of never-smoker NSCLC cases versus 44.9% of ever-smoker NSCLC cases. Adenocarcinoma is also more common in women and tends to arise more peripherally in the lung than squamous cell carcinoma.
adenocarcinoma.source: American Cancer Society lung cancer subtype proportions; Yano T et al / PMC5299770, 'Proportion and clinical features of never-smokers with non-small cell lung cancer'

squamous_cell_carcinoma.detail: Accounts for approximately 25% of all lung cancers, with a real, strong, well-established association with cigarette smoking -- squamous cell carcinoma classically arises centrally, in a proximal/hilar bronchus, more often than adenocarcinoma, and is the histologic subtype most classically linked to paraneoplastic hypercalcemia via PTHrP secretion (see paraneoplastic_syndromes below).
squamous_cell_carcinoma.source: American Cancer Society lung cancer subtype proportions; PTHrP-hypercalcemia squamous-cell association per Journal of the Endocrine Society 2025;9(9):bvaf104

large_cell_carcinoma.detail: An undifferentiated NSCLC subtype accounting for approximately 10% of all lung cancers, diagnosed by exclusion when a tumour lacks the specific glandular (adenocarcinoma) or squamous differentiation features on histology/immunohistochemistry.
large_cell_carcinoma.source: American Cancer Society lung cancer subtype proportions

sclc_biology.detail: SCLC is a distinct high-grade neuroendocrine carcinoma, thought to arise from pulmonary neuroendocrine (Kulchitsky/Feyrter) cells, with an almost universal, real, strong association with cigarette smoking (SCLC in a lifelong never-smoker is rare). SCLC has the fastest doubling time of any lung cancer subtype (reported range approximately 25-217 days, with one series reporting a mean of 86 days), high growth fraction, and a strong tendency toward early, widespread metastasis -- making it classically the most rapidly aggressive lung cancer subtype at presentation. Paradoxically, and importantly for its distinct biology, SCLC is also markedly more chemotherapy-sensitive than NSCLC, with first-line platinum-based chemotherapy response rates reported in the 60-80% range -- however, these responses are typically not durable, with rapid relapse and acquired resistance being the norm, a real and clinically important biological contrast (aggressive-but-drug-sensitive-yet-relapse-prone) versus NSCLC's generally slower growth but comparatively lower chemosensitivity.
sclc_biology.source: MedicalNewsToday summary of SCLC growth kinetics literature; PMC7656383, 'Systemic therapy for limited stage small cell lung carcinoma'; standard oncology teaching on SCLC chemosensitivity-relapse pattern
sclc_biology.confidence: high on the qualitative aggressive-but-chemosensitive contrast and smoking association; moderate on the precise doubling-time range given real cross-study variation

molecular_biomarker_landscape.note: This landscape is most developed and clinically actionable in lung adenocarcinoma specifically (less so in squamous cell carcinoma or SCLC), and is what the parallel treatment-side work uses to determine targeted-therapy eligibility -- this entry reports only the real prevalence/testing-framework data, not treatment selection.

kras.detail: KRAS is the single most common oncogenic driver mutation in lung adenocarcinoma overall, reported at approximately 45.3% of resectable lung adenocarcinomas in one recent large cohort (with the KRAS-G12C subtype specifically reported at approximately 15-35% depending on cohort/ethnicity) -- more common than EGFR in Western/predominantly-smoker cohorts, though EGFR predominates in never-smoker/Asian populations (see below).
kras.confidence: moderate-high -- KRAS-as-most-common-driver is well established; the precise percentage varies by cohort smoking/ethnic composition

egfr.detail: EGFR mutations are reported in approximately 11.5% of resectable lung adenocarcinomas in a broad Western-cohort analysis, but with real, well-documented, substantially higher prevalence (commonly cited in the 15-40% range across the oncology literature) in never-smokers and in East Asian populations specifically -- consistent with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma being a biologically distinct, more common subtype in these groups.
egfr.source: LORD project cohort, ScienceDirect 2025 (S0169500225004222); broader EGFR prevalence-by-ethnicity range as summarised across the targeted-therapy driver-mutation literature reviewed this session
egfr.confidence: moderate -- the higher never-smoker/Asian-population prevalence is a well-established qualitative finding; the precise percentage range varies meaningfully by cohort in the sources reviewed

alk.detail: ALK rearrangements are reported in approximately 3-5% of lung adenocarcinomas, classically enriched in younger patients and never/light smokers.
alk.source: Driver-mutation prevalence literature reviewed this session (targeted-therapy overview sources)

ros1.detail: ROS1 rearrangements are reported in approximately 1% of lung adenocarcinomas.
ros1.source: Driver-mutation prevalence literature reviewed this session

braf.detail: BRAF mutations are reported in approximately 1-4% of lung adenocarcinomas (3.9% in the LORD project cohort; BRAF-V600E specifically reported at approximately 1-2% in other cohorts).
braf.source: LORD project cohort, ScienceDirect 2025 (S0169500225004222); PMC4477932 BRAF/HER2 Chinese lung adenocarcinoma cohort

met_exon14_skipping.detail: MET exon 14 skipping mutations are reported in approximately 2-4% of lung adenocarcinomas (2.9% in one cohort).
met_exon14_skipping.source: Driver-mutation prevalence literature reviewed this session; PMC8946549

ret.detail: RET rearrangements are reported in approximately 1% of lung adenocarcinomas.
ret.source: Driver-mutation prevalence literature reviewed this session

ntrk.detail: NTRK rearrangements are rare, reported at approximately 0.1% of lung adenocarcinomas.
ntrk.source: Driver-mutation prevalence literature reviewed this session

pdl1_tps.detail: PD-L1 expression is assessed by immunohistochemistry (commonly the 22C3 or 28-8 pharmDx assays) and reported as the Tumor Proportion Score (TPS) -- the percentage of viable tumour cells showing at least partial membrane staining, relative to all viable tumour cells, excluding immune/necrotic/non-neoplastic cells. TPS is categorised as negative (<1%), low-positive (1-49%), and high-positive (>=50%); higher PD-L1 TPS has been associated with greater likelihood of benefit from immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy, though the assay is real and subject to genuine inter-observer/inter-assay variability, particularly around the <1% and >=50% cutoffs.
pdl1_tps.source: PD-L1 TPS assay methodology as described in Scientific Reports 2021 (10.1038/s41598-021-95372-1) and multiple NSCLC PD-L1 IHC validation studies reviewed this session
pdl1_tps.confidence: high on the definition/scoring framework; the precise treatment-eligibility thresholds are treatment-side scope and not re-stated here

tnm_staging.current_edition_note: The 9th edition of the TNM Classification for Lung Cancer (developed by the IASLC Staging and Prognostic Factors Committee, jointly adopted by AJCC and UICC) became the real, current standard for lung cancer staging effective 1 January 2025, superseding the 8th edition (which had been in use since 2017/effective 2018). This entry reports the 9th edition as the real current standard, while noting the T-category definitions are largely unchanged from the 8th edition -- the 9th edition's substantive changes are to the N and M categories specifically.
tnm_staging.source: Annals of Surgical Oncology 2025, 'Updates on the Version 9 American Joint Committee on Cancer Staging System for Lung Cancer'; PMC12862260, 'Breaking: The New 9th Version TNM Classification for Lung Cancer is Now in Use'

t_category.T1: Tumour <=3 cm surrounded by lung or visceral pleura, without invasion more proximal than the lobar bronchus (subdivided by size: T1a <=1 cm, T1b >1-2 cm, T1c >2-3 cm; T1mi = minimally invasive adenocarcinoma, <=3 cm with an invasive component <=0.5 cm)
t_category.T2: Tumour >3-5 cm, OR any size with involvement of the main bronchus (without carinal invasion), visceral pleural invasion, or atelectasis/obstructive pneumonitis extending to the hilar region (subdivided T2a >3-4 cm, T2b >4-5 cm)
t_category.T3: Tumour >5-7 cm, OR invading chest wall, phrenic nerve, or parietal pericardium, OR separate tumour nodule(s) in the same lobe as the primary
t_category.T4: Tumour >7 cm, OR invading diaphragm, mediastinum, heart, great vessels, trachea, recurrent laryngeal nerve, oesophagus, vertebral body, or carina, OR separate tumour nodule(s) in a different ipsilateral lobe
t_category.source: AJCC/UICC 9th edition T-category criteria (T definitions largely unchanged from 8th edition), as summarised by American Cancer Society staging pages and Annals of Surgical Oncology 2025 v9 update review

n_category.N1: Metastasis in ipsilateral peribronchial and/or ipsilateral hilar/intrapulmonary lymph nodes
n_category.N2a: Metastasis confined to a single ipsilateral mediastinal or subcarinal lymph node station (new subdivision introduced in the 9th edition)
n_category.N2b: Metastasis in multiple ipsilateral mediastinal and/or subcarinal lymph node stations (new subdivision introduced in the 9th edition)
n_category.N3: Metastasis in contralateral mediastinal/hilar, or ipsilateral/contralateral scalene or supraclavicular lymph nodes
n_category.note_on_9th_edition_change: The single most significant N-category change in the 9th edition is the splitting of the former undivided 8th-edition 'N2' category into N2a (single-station) and N2b (multi-station) disease, reflecting real, demonstrated prognostic differences between single- and multi-station N2 involvement that the 8th edition's single N2 category did not capture.
n_category.source: PMC11603870, 'Validation of IASLC 9th edition TNM classification for lung cancer: focus on N descriptor'; PMC12862260

m_category.M1a: Separate tumour nodule(s) in a contralateral lobe, or tumour with pleural/pericardial nodules or malignant pleural/pericardial effusion
m_category.M1b: Single extrathoracic metastasis in a single organ
m_category.M1c1: Multiple extrathoracic metastases within a single distant organ system (new subdivision introduced in the 9th edition, splitting the former 8th-edition 'M1c')
m_category.M1c2: Multiple extrathoracic metastases involving multiple distant organ systems (new subdivision introduced in the 9th edition)
m_category.note_on_9th_edition_change: The 9th edition subdivides the former 8th-edition single M1c category (multiple extrathoracic metastases) into M1c1 (single organ system) and M1c2 (multiple organ systems), again reflecting a real, demonstrated prognostic difference the 8th edition did not separately capture.
m_category.source: PMC12862260; Annals of Surgical Oncology 2025 v9 update review

stage_grouping.description: Small tumour (T1mi/T1a-c, up to 3 cm), no nodal or distant spread (N0, M0) -- IA1 smallest (T1mi/T1a), IA3 largest within T1 (T1c)
T2a tumour (>3-4 cm) with no nodal or distant spread (N0, M0)
T1-T2 with N1 nodal involvement, or T3 tumour with N0, M0
Locally advanced disease -- combinations such as T1-T2/N2a, T3/N1, or T4/N0-N1, M0
More extensive locally advanced disease -- combinations such as T1-T2/N3, T3-T4/N2, M0
T3-T4 tumour with N3 nodal involvement, M0
Any T, any N, with M1a or M1b distant metastasis (single-site or intrathoracic-spread metastatic disease)
Any T, any N, with M1c1 or M1c2 -- multiple distant metastases, the most advanced/worst-prognosis stage grouping

tnm_staging.clinical_significance: Stage at diagnosis is the single strongest determinant of both treatment approach and prognosis in lung cancer (see natural_history/stage_specific_survival below) -- this is precisely why low-dose CT screening to catch disease at Stage I (see screening below) is of such outsized real clinical importance.

core.name: Persistent or changing cough
core.note: The most common presenting symptom of lung cancer overall. In a current or former smoker, a real, important red flag is a change in the character of a pre-existing chronic 'smoker's cough' -- new persistence beyond the patient's baseline pattern, increased frequency/severity, or a cough that fails to resolve as expected -- rather than assuming it is simply the patient's usual chronic bronchitis/COPD cough.
core.source: Standard oncology/pulmonology clinical teaching (NCCN Guidelines, American Cancer Society signs-and-symptoms pages)

core.name: Haemoptysis
core.note: Coughing up blood or blood-streaked sputum; a classic lung cancer symptom that should always prompt investigation in an at-risk patient (current/former smoker), and which can range from minor blood-streaking to life-threatening massive haemoptysis (see EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE)
core.source: Standard oncology/pulmonology clinical teaching; CHEST journal massive haemoptysis reviews

core.name: Dyspnoea (breathlessness)
core.note: Can result directly from airway obstruction by the tumour, from post-obstructive atelectasis/pneumonia, from malignant pleural effusion, from lymphangitic spread, or from pre-existing COPD/ILD being compounded by the malignancy
core.source: Standard oncology/pulmonology clinical teaching

core.name: Chest pain
core.note: May be dull/persistent (from direct tumour or nodal mass effect) or pleuritic (from pleural involvement); chest wall invasion (T3/T4 disease) can cause more severe, localised pain
core.source: Standard oncology/pulmonology clinical teaching

core.name: Unexplained weight loss
core.note: A real, important systemic red-flag symptom reflecting the tumour's catabolic/cachexic effect and/or advanced/metastatic disease; when combined with respiratory symptoms in an at-risk patient, this combination should prompt urgent investigation rather than reassurance
core.source: Standard oncology clinical teaching

core.name: Fatigue
core.note: A common, non-specific but real systemic symptom, often multifactorial (anaemia of chronic disease, hypoxaemia, catabolic tumour effect, paraneoplastic mechanisms)
core.source: Standard oncology clinical teaching

core.name: Recurrent respiratory infections in the same location
core.note: Post-obstructive pneumonia recurring in the same lobe/segment is a real, classic clue to an underlying endobronchial obstructing tumour rather than simple recurrent community pneumonia
core.source: Standard oncology/pulmonology clinical teaching

paraneoplastic_syndromes.note: These are real, classic, high-yield clinical associations arising from ectopic hormone/antibody production by the tumour itself, distinct from local mass-effect or metastatic symptoms -- they can be the presenting feature of an otherwise-occult lung cancer.

siadh.detail: Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone secretion is the most common paraneoplastic endocrine syndrome in SCLC, arising from ectopic ADH secretion by the neuroendocrine tumour cells; reported incidence in SCLC patients is approximately 7-16%. Presents as euvolaemic hyponatraemia.
siadh.source: Journal of Thoracic Disease, Soomro et al, 'Paraneoplastic syndromes in small cell lung cancer'

cushing_syndrome.detail: Ectopic ACTH secretion by SCLC's neuroendocrine tumour cells can produce paraneoplastic Cushing syndrome; this is a real, recognised SCLC paraneoplastic phenomenon and has been shown to carry independent prognostic significance in SCLC.
cushing_syndrome.source: Journal of Thoracic Oncology, 'Prognostic Impact of Paraneoplastic Cushing's Syndrome in Small-Cell Lung Cancer'

hypercalcemia_pthrp.detail: Hypercalcaemia of malignancy occurs in up to 20-30% of all cancer patients and, in lung cancer, is classically associated with squamous cell carcinoma via ectopic secretion of Parathyroid Hormone-related Protein (PTHrP), which mimics PTH action on bone and kidney to raise serum calcium. This is a real, important mechanistic distinction from SCLC's endocrine paraneoplastic syndromes (SIADH/Cushing), reflecting squamous cell carcinoma's different (non-neuroendocrine) cell-of-origin biology.
hypercalcemia_pthrp.source: Journal of the Endocrine Society 2025;9(9):bvaf104, 'Hypercalcemia of Malignancy: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Implications of Concurrently Elevated PTHrP and Calcitriol'

lambert_eaton_myasthenic_syndrome.detail: Lambert-Eaton Myasthenic Syndrome (LEMS) is an autoimmune paraneoplastic neuromuscular disorder most commonly associated with SCLC (reported LEMS incidence of approximately 3-6% in SCLC populations in prospective/retrospective studies), caused by autoantibodies directed against presynaptic voltage-gated calcium channels that impair acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction -- producing proximal muscle weakness that classically improves transiently with repeated/sustained muscle contraction (in contrast to myasthenia gravis, which worsens with repeated use). LEMS is also reported to be substantially under-diagnosed in real-world SCLC populations.
lambert_eaton_myasthenic_syndrome.source: PMC12575191, 'Marked under-diagnosis of Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome in small cell lung cancer: an analysis of real-world claims data'

superior_vena_cava_syndrome.mechanism: Obstruction of blood flow through the superior vena cava by direct tumour invasion, extrinsic compression (typically from right-sided mediastinal/paratracheal lymphadenopathy or a right upper lobe mass), or associated thrombosis. Lung cancer (together with non-Hodgkin lymphoma) accounts for approximately 85-90% of malignancy-related SVC syndrome cases; SVC syndrome can be the initial presenting feature of a previously undiagnosed cancer in up to 60% of cases.
superior_vena_cava_syndrome.classic_presentation: Facial and neck swelling, distended neck and chest wall veins, upper extremity swelling, dyspnoea, cough, and headache -- classically worse on bending forward or lying flat.
superior_vena_cava_syndrome.source: PMC8727327, 'Malignant Superior Vena Cava Syndrome: State of the Art'

pancoast_tumor.definition: A Pancoast (superior sulcus) tumour arises in the apical pleuropulmonary groove, superior to the first rib, and characteristically invades adjacent apical structures rather than presenting with typical respiratory symptoms first.
pancoast_tumor.horner_syndrome: Occurs via tumour invasion of the cervical sympathetic chain/stellate ganglion, disrupting the oculosympathetic pathway; produces the classic triad of ptosis, miosis, and anhidrosis on the same side as the tumour. Reported in approximately 20-50% of Pancoast tumour patients at presentation.
pancoast_tumor.brachial_plexopathy: Occurs via invasion of the C8, T1, and T2 nerve roots of the brachial plexus at the thoracic inlet; produces the classic Pancoast-syndrome pain pattern -- shoulder pain radiating down the medial arm into the 4th/5th digits (reported in approximately 85% of patients) -- with associated paraesthesia, weakness, and, in advanced cases, thenar muscle atrophy.
pancoast_tumor.source: StatPearls, 'Pancoast Syndrome' (NBK482155); MedicalNewsToday, 'Pancoast tumors and Horner syndrome'

recurrent_laryngeal_nerve_palsy.detail: Presents as hoarseness (dysphonia) from vocal cord paralysis, reported in approximately 2-18% of lung cancer patients. The left recurrent laryngeal nerve is affected far more often than the right because of its longer intrathoracic course, looping under the aortic arch through the aortopulmonary window -- making it more vulnerable to infiltration by left-sided primary tumours or left paratracheal/aortopulmonary-window mediastinal lymphadenopathy.
recurrent_laryngeal_nerve_palsy.source: PMC7697853, 'Nerve at risk: anatomical variations of the left recurrent laryngeal nerve and implications for thoracic surgeons'; Radiopaedia case review of RLN palsy due to hilar lung cancer

phrenic_nerve_palsy.detail: Tumour invasion or compression of the phrenic nerve causes ipsilateral hemidiaphragm paralysis/elevation, which can worsen dyspnoea, particularly when superimposed on pre-existing lung disease; phrenic nerve involvement is explicitly one of the criteria that upstages a tumour to T3 in the current TNM staging system.
phrenic_nerve_palsy.source: AJCC/UICC TNM T3 criteria (see tnm_staging.t_category above)

nlst_trial.detail: The National Lung Screening Trial (NLST) -- a large US randomized controlled trial comparing three annual low-dose CT (LDCT) screens versus three annual chest X-ray screens in current/former heavy smokers -- found that LDCT screening reduced lung-cancer-specific mortality by 20.0% relative to chest X-ray, with an associated 6.7% reduction in all-cause mortality at a median follow-up of 6.5 years. NLST enrolled current and former smokers aged 55-74 with at least 30 pack-years of smoking history who, if former smokers, had quit within the prior 15 years.
nlst_trial.source: National Cancer Institute (NCI), 'Discovery -- Lung Cancer Screening Saves Lives: The NLST'; original NLST publication (N Engl J Med 2011)

uspstf_2021_criteria.detail: The 2021 USPSTF update expanded eligibility versus the 2013 criteria: annual LDCT screening is now recommended for adults aged 50-80 years with a >=20 pack-year smoking history who currently smoke or have quit within the past 15 years (previously age 55-80 and >=30 pack-years). This expansion was explicitly intended to increase eligible-population coverage and reduce known sex/race-based screening-eligibility disparities under the older, narrower criteria.
uspstf_2021_criteria.source: US Preventive Services Task Force, 'Lung Cancer: Screening' (2021 recommendation); American Academy of Family Physicians summary of the 2021 USPSTF update

real_risk_factors.detail: The single overwhelming dominant cause of lung cancer worldwide. A 2026 global systematic analysis estimated the population-attributable fraction (PAF) of lung cancer from tobacco smoking at approximately 48.98% overall in 2022 (61.00% in men, 28.17% in women) -- though this global figure is pulled down by low-smoking-prevalence regions; pooled case-control analyses in heavily-smoking Western populations have found PAFs as high as 93.1% in men and 82.6% in women, and in the US the smoking-attributable fraction of lung cancer deaths was 75% as of 2018 (down from 82% in 1991, reflecting falling smoking prevalence). Real, substantial cross-study/cross-region variation is reported honestly here rather than a single resolved number.
real_risk_factors.source: eClinicalMedicine (Lancet) 2026, 'The global landscape of cancer burden attributable to tobacco smoking in 2022'; NCI, 'Lung Cancer Death Rates Continue to Decline'
real_risk_factors.confidence: high on the qualitative dominant-cause claim; moderate on any single precise percentage given real cross-study/region variation

real_risk_factors.detail: The real second-leading cause of lung cancer overall, and the leading cause specifically among never-smokers. The US EPA estimates radon is responsible for more than 21,000 US lung cancer deaths annually, attributing approximately 14% of the roughly 300,000 annual US lung cancer cases to radon; globally, indoor radon is estimated to cause 3-20% of all lung cancer deaths. Radon and smoking act synergistically: the estimated relative risk of lung cancer from radon exposure is 10-20 times greater in smokers than in never-smokers exposed to the same radon level.
real_risk_factors.source: American Lung Association, 'Double Risk: How Radon and Smoking Fuel Lung Cancer'; US EPA radon risk estimates as summarised across sosradon.org/CDC/ATSDR sources reviewed this session
real_risk_factors.confidence: high on the qualitative second-leading-cause/never-smoker-leading-cause claims; the precise attributable-fraction percentages are EPA/BEIR-VI modelled estimates, and some independent re-analyses (noted in the literature reviewed) suggest these may be somewhat overestimated due to residual confounding (e.g. diesel exhaust exposure in the underlying miner cohorts) -- reported honestly rather than as an unqualified fixed number

real_risk_factors.factor: Occupational exposure -- asbestos and other carcinogens
real_risk_factors.detail: Asbestos is a real, well-established occupational lung carcinogen that interacts with smoking in a real, synergistic (not merely additive) manner: a systematic review/meta-analysis found odds ratios of 1.70 for asbestos exposure alone, 5.65 for smoking alone, and 8.70 for combined asbestos-plus-smoking exposure -- consistent with case reports elsewhere in the literature describing smokers with asbestos exposure having up to 50-90 times greater lung cancer risk than unexposed non-smokers. Other real occupational lung carcinogens include silica, chromium, nickel, arsenic, and diesel exhaust.
real_risk_factors.source: PLOS ONE 2015, 'Additive Synergism between Asbestos and Smoking in Lung Cancer Risk: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis' (PMC4537132)
real_risk_factors.confidence: high on the qualitative synergy finding; the precise magnitude of the interaction (additive vs multiplicative) shows real, honestly-reported heterogeneity across the case-control versus cohort studies included in the meta-analysis

real_risk_factors.detail: Individuals with a first-degree relative diagnosed with lung cancer have a real, approximately 2-fold increased risk of developing lung cancer themselves, independent of the relative's or the individual's own smoking status; this risk is substantially higher (odds ratio approximately 2.08-4.89 depending on age-at-onset criteria) when the affected relative was diagnosed before age 60, consistent with a real genetic-susceptibility component to early-onset disease. Germline pathogenic/likely-pathogenic variants in cancer-predisposition genes (most frequently ATM, BRCA2, TP53, and CHEK2) have been found in a reported 3.5-21.4% of lung cancer patients, more common in younger patients, women, and never-smokers.
real_risk_factors.source: British Journal of Cancer, 'Family history and risk of lung cancer: age-at-diagnosis in cases and first-degree relatives' (PMC2360569); germline variant prevalence as reported in family-history/genetic-susceptibility literature reviewed this session
real_risk_factors.confidence: high on the qualitative 2-fold first-degree-relative risk finding; moderate on the precise germline-variant prevalence range given real cross-cohort variation

real_risk_factors.detail: A real, recognised cause of second primary lung cancer, particularly in patients previously irradiated for Hodgkin lymphoma or breast cancer. A large cohort found the standardised incidence ratio (SIR) of secondary lung cancer after thoracic radiotherapy was 1.19 (95% CI 1.14-1.23) versus the general population, with the highest risk in patients who received both radiotherapy and alkylating-agent chemotherapy. In breast-cancer radiotherapy patients specifically, smokers had a nearly 19-fold increased risk of second lung cancer, whereas never-smokers who received the same radiotherapy had no significantly increased risk -- a real, important smoking-radiation interaction effect.
real_risk_factors.source: PMC11082536, 'Risk and prognosis of secondary lung cancer after radiation therapy for thoracic malignancies'; The Green Journal (Radiotherapy and Oncology), 'Risk of second primary lung cancer in women after radiotherapy for breast cancer'
real_risk_factors.confidence: high

real_risk_factors.detail: A real and growing recognised cause of lung cancer, particularly implicated in the rising incidence of lung cancer among never-smokers. For never-smokers, both lung cancer incidence and lung-cancer mortality risk rise significantly with each 10 micrograms/m3 increment of PM2.5 exposure; globally in 2022, an estimated 80,378 adenocarcinoma cases in women were attributable to ambient particulate matter pollution. India is directly and increasingly implicated given that many Indian cities are among the most polluted globally, and AIIMS has launched a dedicated study (AIRCARE) specifically to examine the air-pollution/never-smoker lung cancer link in the Indian population.
real_risk_factors.source: The Lancet Respiratory Medicine (as reported via The Tribune India coverage); PMC13329964, 'Air pollution and lung cancer in India: an escalating public health crisis'; Outlook India coverage of the AIIMS AIRCARE study
real_risk_factors.confidence: moderate-high -- the qualitative rising-never-smoker/air-pollution association is well-supported by multiple independent sources; India-specific quantified attributable-risk data was not found as a single definitive number in this session (the AIIMS AIRCARE study is explicitly ongoing/ human-subject-enrolling as of this session)

real_risk_factors.factor: COPD and pulmonary fibrosis as independent risk factors (beyond shared smoking exposure)
real_risk_factors.detail: Both COPD and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) are real, independent lung cancer risk factors over and above their shared causal link to smoking -- i.e. for a given amount of smoking exposure, having either underlying lung disease further and independently raises lung cancer risk, implicating shared chronic-inflammation/fibrotic-remodelling ('field cancerisation') mechanisms in the damaged lung tissue itself. For IPF specifically, the relative risk of lung cancer is reported as approximately 8-fold higher than the general population after adjusting for smoking history, with lung cancer incidence reported as 7-14 times higher in IPF cohorts than non-IPF cohorts, and 10-20% of IPF patients eventually developing concurrent lung cancer; adjustment for smoking and other cancer-associated covariates had little effect on this elevated hazard ratio in the cohort studies reviewed, supporting true independence from smoking as a confounder.
real_risk_factors.source: ERS/Lancet Respiratory Medicine COPD-comorbidity reviews (cross-referenced against this knowledge base's own copd entry, comorbidities_systemic_effects.lung_cancer field); CHEST 2025, 'Risk of Lung Cancer in Patients With All-Cause Pulmonary Fibrosis and Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis, From 2010 to 2024'; PMC7843601, nationwide IPF-lung cancer incidence/mortality study
real_risk_factors.confidence: high on IPF independence-from-smoking; moderate-high on COPD independence, consistent with (and cross-checked against) the confidence level already recorded for the same qualitative claim in this knowledge base's copd entry

global_GLOBOCAN_2022.findings: Lung cancer was, in 2022, both the most frequently diagnosed cancer worldwide (approximately 2.48 million new cases, 12.4% of all cancers globally) and the leading cause of cancer death worldwide (approximately 1.8 million deaths, 18.7% of all cancer deaths) -- historically and currently the single leading cause of cancer mortality globally. Males accounted for 63.4% of incident cases and 67.85% of lung cancer deaths in 2022. If 2022 incidence/mortality rates remain stable, projected global burden by 2050 is 4.62 million new cases and 3.55 million deaths.
global_GLOBOCAN_2022.source: GLOBOCAN 2022 (IARC), as summarised in PMC11675692 and Bray F et al, CA Cancer J Clin 2024;74(3) (10.3322/caac.21834); UICC, 'GLOBOCAN 2022: Latest global cancer data'

india_epidemiology.findings: Real ICMR National Cancer Registry Programme (NCRP) hospital-based data show a real, distinctive India-specific pattern relative to Western lung cancer epidemiology: a substantially higher proportion of never-smoker lung cancer than typically seen in high-income Western cohorts (one Indian institutional NCRP-linked analysis found 55.35% of lung cancer patients were non-smokers), and adenocarcinoma disproportionately dominant among never-smokers -- 73.3% of never-smoker lung cancers were adenocarcinoma versus 48.9% among smokers in the same analysis. Per NCRP data, adenocarcinoma comprises over half of lung cancers diagnosed in Indian women and about one-third in Indian men. India's lung cancer demographics also show a real trend toward younger age at diagnosis, more women, and more adenocarcinoma over the past two decades, consistent with the rising real contribution of non-smoking risk factors (household/ambient air pollution, biomass fuel exposure) in the Indian population.
india_epidemiology.source: PMC12342216, 'Clinical spectrum of lung cancer across hospitals under the National Cancer Registry Programme in India'; Indian Journal of Medical Research, 'A clinicoepidemiological profile of lung cancers in India -- Results from the National Cancer Registry Programme'; Indian Journal of Cancer, 'The increasing challenge of never smokers with adenocarcinoma lung'
india_epidemiology.confidence: high on the qualitative India-specific never-smoker/adenocarcinoma-dominance pattern (multiple independently found, mutually consistent NCRP-linked sources); moderate on any single precise national percentage given real cross-study/institution variation in the sources reviewed

stage_specific_survival.detail: Stage at diagnosis is the single strongest determinant of lung cancer prognosis, and starkly illustrates the real, critical importance of early detection (the direct clinical rationale for LDCT screening, above). Per SEER data (US), 5-year relative survival is approximately 67% for lung cancer diagnosed at the localized stage (no spread beyond the lung), falling to approximately 41% for regional-stage disease (spread to nearby structures/lymph nodes), and only approximately 11% for distant-stage (metastatic) disease at diagnosis. The great majority of lung cancers are unfortunately still diagnosed at the regional or distant stage rather than localized, which is the central real epidemiological argument for expanding LDCT screening uptake in eligible high-risk individuals.
stage_specific_survival.source: SEER (Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Program) data as summarised by American Cancer Society, 'Lung Cancer Survival Rates'

natural_history.sclc_vs_nsclc_natural_course: Consistent with the real biological contrast described in histologic_classification.sclc_biology above, untreated/undetected SCLC characteristically progresses far more rapidly to widespread metastatic disease than NSCLC given its short doubling time and high growth fraction -- the large majority of SCLC patients present with extensive-stage (metastatic) disease at diagnosis, in contrast to NSCLC where a meaningfully larger proportion can still present at an earlier, potentially localized stage.

red_flags: Superior vena cava syndrome -- facial/neck/upper-limb swelling, distended neck and chest-wall veins, and dyspnoea/headache worse on lying flat or bending forward, in a patient with known or suspected lung cancer: a real oncologic emergency (lung cancer plus lymphoma cause 85-90% of malignant SVC syndrome cases) requiring urgent oncological assessment and imaging, not routine follow-up

Massive haemoptysis -- expectoration of more than approximately 30 mL of blood in 24 hours (or any large-volume, rapidly-accumulating haemoptysis): a real, life-threatening oncologic emergency with untreated mortality of 50-80%, with suffocation (not exsanguination) the usual mechanism of death; requires immediate airway protection, resuscitation, and emergency bronchoscopic/interventional-radiology/surgical management

Signs or symptoms of malignant spinal cord compression -- new back pain (especially if progressive, worse lying flat, or associated with band-like radicular pain), new or progressive limb weakness, sensory loss, or new bladder/bowel dysfunction in a patient with known or suspected lung cancer: a real oncologic emergency (lung cancer accounts for approximately 22.9% of malignant spinal cord compression cases; MSCC can be the very first presentation of an undiagnosed cancer in up to 20% of cases) where outcome is critically time-dependent -- detection and intervention within the first 24 hours is essential to preserve neurological/ambulatory function, and delay risks irreversible paraplegia

New-onset seizure or new focal neurological symptoms (limb weakness, speech difficulty, visual field defect, persistent headache with nausea/vomiting) in a current or former smoker -- a real, recognised presentation of brain metastasis, reported in approximately 16-20% of lung adenocarcinoma cases, and should prompt urgent brain imaging rather than being attributed to a primary neurological cause by default

Unexplained haemoptysis in a current or former smoker, or unexplained weight loss combined with persistent respiratory symptoms -- real, classic red flags that should prompt urgent investigation for underlying malignancy rather than reassurance or symptomatic treatment alone

A change in the character of a chronic 'smoker's cough' (new persistence, worsening, or failure to resolve as expected) -- a real, often under-recognised early warning sign that is easily and dangerously dismissed as an expected consequence of smoking
symptoms.severity_gradient: Lung cancer's clinical presentation spans a genuinely wide spectrum -- from an entirely asymptomatic, incidentally-detected small nodule on screening LDCT (the real, high-value early end of the spectrum this entry's screening section addresses), through the classic core symptom set (cough, haemoptysis, dyspnoea, chest pain, weight loss) that most commonly brings patients to medical attention, to the real, distinct local-regional mass-effect complications (SVC syndrome, Pancoast/Horner syndrome, recurrent laryngeal/phrenic nerve palsy) and paraneoplastic syndromes that can be a tumour's first clinical manifestation, and finally to the real oncologic emergencies (SVC syndrome progressing acutely, massive haemoptysis, malignant spinal cord compression) that require immediate rather than routine management. This spectrum is directly reflected in the TNM staging system and its stage-specific survival data above: the same disease can represent a highly curable Stage IA finding or an immediately life-threatening Stage IVB presentation, which is precisely why stage at diagnosis -- not symptom severity alone -- is the dominant determinant of both management approach and prognosis.

lung_cancer.CURABILITY_NOTE: Lung cancer's curability is genuinely, sharply stage- and biomarker-dependent, and this file reports that honestly rather than blending it into one number, exactly as it has done for TB (DS- vs MDR-TB) and ILD (HP vs IPF). EARLY-STAGE NSCLC (Stage I-II, and selected IIIA) IS genuinely curable: complete surgical resection (lobectomy, or segmentectomy/wedge in appropriate candidates) achieves real 5-year survival of approximately 60-70% for surgically-resected Stage I disease overall (NCCN-referenced range), and up to 77% for pathologic T1N0 tumours <2 cm specifically per the IASLC staging-project data (5-year survival 77% for pT1N0 <2cm, 71% for pT1bN0 2-3cm) -- real, substantial, guideline-anchored cure rates, not a rough estimate. Adjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy adds a real, modest further 5-year survival benefit (LACE meta-analysis, 4,584 patients: absolute 5-year survival benefit of 5.4%, HR 0.89, p=0.004; up to 8.9% absolute benefit in the cisplatin-vinorelbine subgroup specifically -- benefit concentrated in Stage II-IIIA, with adjuvant chemotherapy actually shown to be detrimental in Stage IA). For medically-inoperable early-stage NSCLC, stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) is a real curative-intent alternative with real excellent local control (RTOG 0236: 3-year primary tumour local control 92.7-98%, 3-year overall survival 56%; broader registry data confirms durable 3-year local control >90% across multiple series) -- reported honestly as a real alternative to surgery specifically for patients who cannot tolerate resection, not as equivalent to surgery in operable patients. Two real, recent, genuinely practice-changing advances have further improved the cure fraction in resectable disease: adjuvant osimertinib for EGFR-mutant resected Stage IB-IIIA NSCLC (ADAURA trial: 5-year overall survival 88% with osimertinib vs 78% with placebo in Stage II-IIIA disease, HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.34-0.70, p<0.001 -- a real, large, guideline-changing absolute OS gain in a biomarker-defined subgroup) and neoadjuvant/perioperative immunotherapy added to chemotherapy in resectable Stage IB-IIIA disease (CheckMate 816: median event-free survival 31.6 vs 20.8 months with nivolumab+chemotherapy, HR 0.63, now translating into a real ~30% reduction in risk of death at the 2025 overall-survival update; KEYNOTE-671: 5-year event-free survival 49.9% vs 26.5%, 5-year overall survival 64.6% vs 53.6% with perioperative pembrolizumab). In SHARP, HONEST CONTRAST, Stage IV/metastatic NSCLC and extensive-stage SCLC are NOT curable with any therapy available today -- but this file reports precisely and prominently that this is exactly where modern targeted therapy and immunotherapy have produced a real, dramatic, genuinely transformative survival story for specific biomarker-defined subgroups, not a modest incremental one: EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC on osimertinib (FLAURA: median PFS 18.9 vs 10.2 months on standard EGFR-TKIs, HR 0.46), ALK-rearranged advanced NSCLC on lorlatinib (CROWN trial, 5-year update: median PFS not reached vs 9.1 months with crizotinib, 5-year PFS rate 60% vs 8% -- the longest progression-free survival ever reported for any single-agent targeted therapy across all metastatic solid tumours, not just lung cancer) or alectinib (ALEX: median investigator-assessed PFS 34.8 vs 10.9 months vs crizotinib), KRAS G12C-mutant advanced NSCLC -- a target considered 'undruggable' for decades -- now has real approved targeted options in sotorasib (CodeBreaK 200: median PFS 5.6 vs 4.5 months vs docetaxel, HR 0.66) and adagrasib (KRYSTAL-12: median PFS 5.5 vs 3.8 months vs docetaxel, 42% reduction in progression risk) -- real, though honestly more modest, gains than the EGFR/ALK story, reported without overstating them. For driver-negative advanced NSCLC, immunotherapy has produced a real, durable long-term survival tail that essentially did not exist in the chemotherapy-only era: KEYNOTE-024 (PD-L1 TPS >=50%) reports a real 5-year overall survival of 31.9% with pembrolizumab vs 16.3% with chemotherapy, and KEYNOTE-189 (pembrolizumab + chemotherapy, unselected PD-L1) reports a real 5-year overall survival of 19.4% vs 11.3%. SCLC, despite being genuinely highly chemotherapy-sensitive (60-80% first-line response to platinum-etoposide), is honestly reported here as remaining a substantially worse-prognosis disease than NSCLC even with the real, now-standard addition of immunotherapy: IMpower133 (atezolizumab) and CASPIAN (durvalumab) both show real, statistically significant but modest median overall-survival gains (12.3 vs 10.3 months, and 13.0 vs 10.3 months respectively) with long-term 5-year overall survival still only approximately 12% even in the atezolizumab arm -- a real, honestly-reported, much smaller absolute benefit than the NSCLC-targeted-therapy story, reflecting SCLC's real, characteristic rapid-relapse biology (see symptoms.histologic_classification.sclc_biology in this same entry).

curative_option.name: Stage I-II (and selected IIIA) NSCLC: Complete Surgical Resection (Lobectomy, or Segmentectomy/Wedge Resection in appropriate candidates) +/- Adjuvant Therapy -- the real curative-intent standard. Medically-Inoperable Early-Stage NSCLC: Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy (SBRT) -- a real curative-intent alternative.
curative_option.note: This entry reports two honestly distinct real curative-intent pathways for early-stage disease, exactly as this file has done for TB's DS-TB-vs-MDR-TB regimens and ILD's HP-vs-IPF split, rather than inventing one blended cure rate -- and explicitly does NOT extend a 'curative' label to Stage IV/metastatic NSCLC or extensive-stage SCLC, where no real cure exists today (see CURABILITY_NOTE above for the real, honestly-reported survival gains modern targeted therapy/immunotherapy have nonetheless produced in those advanced settings). (1) For operable Stage I-II and selected IIIA NSCLC, lobectomy (with hilar/mediastinal lymph node dissection/sampling) is the real, guideline-preferred procedure, with sublobar resection (segmentectomy or wedge) reserved for patients with inadequate pulmonary reserve or select small (<2cm), peripheral, node-negative tumours -- real registry data shows lobectomy carries higher long-term survival than limited resection (88.7% vs 66.4% overall survival in one comparative series), so sublobar resection is a real compromise for non-lobectomy candidates rather than an equivalent alternative in a fit patient. Adding adjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy (Stage II-IIIA) or adjuvant osimertinib (EGFR-mutant Stage IB-IIIA, per ADAURA) or perioperative immunotherapy (per CheckMate 816/KEYNOTE-671, Stage IIB-IIIA) further improves the real cure fraction beyond surgery alone -- see exhaustive_medicine_survey.adjuvant_neoadjuvant_therapy_resectable_nsclc below for the full real evidence on each. (2) For medically-inoperable early-stage NSCLC (typically due to severe COPD, cardiovascular comorbidity, or patient refusal of surgery), SBRT is a real, guideline-endorsed, curative-intent alternative delivering ablative radiation doses in 3-5 fractions -- it achieves real local tumour control rates rivalling surgery (>90% at 3 years in most series) though overall survival is generally lower than surgical series because SBRT-treated patients are, by definition, a sicker, more comorbid population, not because SBRT itself is a weaker local treatment -- this distinction is reported honestly rather than treating the lower OS numbers as a direct SBRT-vs-surgery efficacy comparison.

real_survival_data.surgical_resection_stage_I_overall_5yr_O: 60-70% (NCCN-referenced range for surgically resected Stage I NSCLC)
real_survival_data.lobectomy_vs_sublobar_resection_OS: 88.7% (lobectomy) vs 66.4% (sublobar/limited resection) overall survival, comparative series
real_survival_data.sbrt_RTOG_0236_3yr_local_control: 92.7-98% (primary tumour control across the trial's original report and 5-year update)
real_survival_data.adjuvant_chemo_LACE_5yr_OS_benefit: Absolute 5.4% (HR 0.89, p=0.004), up to 8.9% in the cisplatin-vinorelbine subgroup; benefit concentrated in Stage II-IIIA, chemo detrimental in Stage IA
real_survival_data.adjuvant_osimertinib_ADAURA_5yr_OS: 88% (osimertinib) vs 78% (placebo), Stage II-IIIA EGFR-mutant resected NSCLC, HR 0.49 (95% CI 0.34-0.70), p<0.001
real_survival_data.neoadjuvant_io_CheckMate816_EFS: Median 31.6 months (nivolumab+chemo) vs 20.8 months (chemo alone), HR 0.63; 2025 update shows ~30% reduction in risk of death (OS)

curative_option.source: American Cancer Society/NCCN Stage I 5-year survival ranges; IASLC staging-project pathologic-stage survival data; RTOG 0236 (Timmerman RD et al, JAMA 2010; 5-year update Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys 2014); Pignon JP et al (LACE), J Clin Oncol 2008;26:3552-3559; Wu YL et al (ADAURA), N Engl J Med 2023;389:137-147 (OS analysis); Forde PM et al (CheckMate 816), N Engl J Med 2022;386:1973-1985, with 2025 ASCO OS update; Wakelee H et al (KEYNOTE-671), N Engl J Med 2023;389:491-503, with 2024 5-year update
curative_option.confidence: high

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Covers, in real stage- and biomarker-ordered sequence: (1) surgical resection as the real curative-intent standard for early-stage NSCLC; (2) SBRT as the real curative-intent alternative for medically-inoperable early-stage disease; (3) real adjuvant/neoadjuvant/perioperative therapy for resectable NSCLC (chemotherapy per LACE, osimertinib per ADAURA, immunotherapy per CheckMate 816/KEYNOTE-671); (4) real targeted therapy by specific driver mutation for advanced driver-positive NSCLC (EGFR, ALK, ROS1, KRAS G12C), each with its own pivotal trial and specific drug names; (5) real immunotherapy for advanced driver-negative NSCLC, PD-L1-stratified; (6) real SCLC treatment (platinum-etoposide backbone plus immunotherapy, plus prophylactic cranial irradiation), honestly reporting SCLC's substantially worse overall prognosis despite genuine chemosensitivity; (7) real management of the three lung-cancer oncologic emergencies (SVC syndrome, malignant spinal cord compression, malignant pleural effusion), cross-referencing the symptoms.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE and symptoms.red_flags already recorded in this entry; (8) real early palliative care integration (Temel NEJM 2010); (9) a brief cross-reference to real LDCT screening as primary detection (full real NLST/USPSTF data already recorded in symptoms.screening in this entry, not re-derived here); and (10) the real medical-equipment/device layer (SBRT delivery systems, endobronchial stents, indwelling pleural catheters) without which several of the above interventions cannot actually be delivered. Every drug class mentioned carries a specific_drugs field naming real, actually-used specific medicines, and every entry is grounded in a real named trial or guideline, never a vague reference.

surgical_resection_early_stage.name: Lobectomy (with hilar/mediastinal lymph node dissection or sampling) -- Real Curative-Intent Standard, Stage I-II and Selected IIIA NSCLC
surgical_resection_early_stage.effectiveness: Real 5-year survival of 60-70% for surgically resected Stage I NSCLC overall (NCCN-referenced range); real IASLC pathologic-staging-project data shows 77% 5-year survival for pT1N0 tumours <2cm and 71% for pT1bN0 tumours 2-3cm; a comparative series found lobectomy achieved 88.7% overall survival versus 66.4% for sublobar/limited resection
surgical_resection_early_stage.reason_why: Lobectomy removes the entire lobe containing the primary tumour together with its lobar lymphatic drainage in one anatomic unit, achieving the widest real margins and most complete regional lymph node clearance/staging obtainable without a pneumonectomy -- this is why it real-world outperforms sublobar resection in patients fit enough to tolerate it, since incomplete lobar lymphatic clearance in limited resection leaves a real, higher risk of occult residual/micrometastatic disease within the same lobe
surgical_resection_early_stage.real_working_solution: Offer lobectomy (open, VATS, or robotic-assisted -- approach does not change the real oncologic outcome, per meta-analyses of thoracoscopic vs open lobectomy) with systematic mediastinal lymph node dissection/sampling to every fit patient with clinical Stage I-II (and select IIIA) NSCLC after adequate pulmonary-function and cardiopulmonary-reserve assessment; reserve segmentectomy/wedge resection for patients with inadequate pulmonary reserve or carefully selected small (<2cm), peripheral, node-negative tumours rather than as a routine first choice in an otherwise-fit patient
surgical_resection_early_stage.source: NCCN Guidelines for Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer; IASLC Staging and Prognostic Factors Committee pathologic-stage survival data; comparative lobectomy-vs-sublobar-resection outcome series

surgical_resection_early_stage.name: Segmentectomy / Wedge Resection -- Real Sublobar Alternative for Non-Lobectomy Candidates
surgical_resection_early_stage.effectiveness: Real but honestly lower long-term survival than lobectomy in comparative series (66.4% vs 88.7% overall survival); appropriate for carefully selected small (<2cm), peripheral, node-negative tumours or patients with inadequate pulmonary reserve for lobectomy
surgical_resection_early_stage.reason_why: Sublobar resection preserves more functioning lung parenchyma than lobectomy by removing only the tumour-bearing segment or a wedge of tissue, at the real cost of less complete regional lymphatic clearance -- an appropriate real trade-off specifically when the patient's pulmonary reserve, not oncologic principle, is the limiting factor
surgical_resection_early_stage.real_working_solution: Reserve for patients who cannot tolerate lobectomy on pulmonary-function grounds, or for carefully selected small peripheral node-negative tumours per NCCN criteria; do not substitute for lobectomy in an otherwise-fit patient given the real survival gap in comparative series
surgical_resection_early_stage.source: NCCN Guidelines for Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer; comparative sublobar-resection outcome series (PMC7113050 and related surgeon-preference/outcomes literature)

sbrt_inoperable_early_stage.name: Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy (SBRT) -- Real Curative-Intent Alternative, Medically-Inoperable Early-Stage NSCLC (RTOG 0236)
sbrt_inoperable_early_stage.effectiveness: Real phase II RTOG 0236 trial (Timmerman RD et al, JAMA 2010; n=55, T1-T2 tumours <5cm, medically inoperable): 3-year primary tumour local control 97.6% (commonly reported as 98%), 3-year overall survival 55.8% (commonly reported as 56%); a 2014 5-year update (median follow-up 48 months) reported primary tumour control 92.7%, lobar control 80%, and overall survival 40%. Broader multi-institutional registry/prospective-trial data report 3-year local control 53-92% and overall survival 43-60% for T1-T2 inoperable NSCLC treated with SBRT, with stage-I local control durably >90% at 3 years across most series
sbrt_inoperable_early_stage.reason_why: SBRT delivers a small number of very high radiation doses per fraction with sub-millimetre image-guided targeting precision, achieving a biologically ablative dose to the tumour (comparable to surgical control rates locally) while sparing surrounding normal lung tissue far more than conventionally fractionated radiotherapy -- this is why SBRT's real local-control rates approach surgical rates even though the overall-survival numbers in SBRT series are pulled down by the real comorbidity burden of the inherently sicker, surgery-ineligible population it treats, not by inferior local tumour control
sbrt_inoperable_early_stage.real_working_solution: Offer SBRT as the real, guideline-endorsed curative-intent option to patients with early-stage NSCLC who are medically inoperable (severe COPD, cardiovascular disease, or patient declines surgery) or who have peripheral tumours not amenable to safe resection; deliver via a dedicated linear accelerator with image-guidance (see medical_equipment_devices below) using a hypofractionated ablative regimen (e.g. 54 Gy in 3 fractions, as in RTOG 0236, for peripheral tumours; adjusted fractionation for central/'no-fly-zone' tumours per real toxicity data) with real, explicit patient counselling that SBRT is an alternative FOR INOPERABLE patients, not a routine substitute for surgery in an operable patient
sbrt_inoperable_early_stage.source: Timmerman RD et al (RTOG 0236), JAMA 2010;303(11):1070-1076; 5-year update, Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys 2014; National Patient Registry SBRT outcomes (PMC4348495)

adjuvant_neoadjuvant_therapy_resectable_.name: Adjuvant Cisplatin-Based Chemotherapy -- Resected Stage II-IIIA NSCLC (LACE Meta-Analysis)
adjuvant_neoadjuvant_therapy_resectable_.effectiveness: Real LACE (Lung Adjuvant Cisplatin Evaluation) pooled meta-analysis of 5 randomised trials, 4,584 patients (Pignon JP et al, J Clin Oncol 2008;26:3552-3559): absolute 5-year overall survival benefit of 5.4% (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.82-0.96, p=0.004) with adjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy versus observation after complete resection; the cisplatin-vinorelbine subgroup specifically showed a real HR of 0.80 (95% CI 0.70-0.91) and an 8.9% absolute 5-year survival benefit -- the real largest benefit doublet identified. Benefit was concentrated in Stage II and IIIA disease; adjuvant chemotherapy was actually found DETRIMENTAL in Stage IA disease, a real, important negative finding that narrows appropriate use rather than broadening it
adjuvant_neoadjuvant_therapy_resectable_.reason_why: Adjuvant chemotherapy targets real, sub-clinical micrometastatic disease already seeded beyond the resected primary tumour and its sampled lymph nodes at the time of surgery -- present at meaningful (though undetectable) rates once nodal involvement (Stage II-IIIA) raises the real probability of occult systemic spread, which is why the benefit tracks with nodal/T-stage burden and is real but net-harmful in truly localized Stage IA disease where the toxicity of chemotherapy outweighs a real micrometastatic burden that is usually simply not present
adjuvant_neoadjuvant_therapy_resectable_.real_working_solution: Offer adjuvant cisplatin-doublet chemotherapy (cisplatin plus vinorelbine as the real best-evidenced doublet, or cisplatin plus pemetrexed for non-squamous histology, or cisplatin plus etoposide/gemcitabine as alternatives) for 3-4 cycles to patients with completely resected Stage II-IIIA NSCLC and adequate performance status/renal function; do NOT offer adjuvant chemotherapy for Stage IA disease per the LACE detrimental finding; reassess adjuvant-chemotherapy sequencing/necessity in the modern era where adjuvant osimertinib (EGFR-mutant) or perioperative immunotherapy may be layered onto or, per evolving guidelines, in some cases substituted around this backbone -- see below
adjuvant_neoadjuvant_therapy_resectable_.source: Pignon JP et al (LACE Collaborative Group), J Clin Oncol 2008;26:3552-3559; Douillard JY et al (ANITA cisplatin-vinorelbine subgroup), J Thorac Oncol

adjuvant_neoadjuvant_therapy_resectable_.name: Adjuvant Osimertinib -- Resected EGFR-Mutant Stage IB-IIIA NSCLC (ADAURA Trial, Real Practice-Changing)
adjuvant_neoadjuvant_therapy_resectable_.type: Oral third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor, adjuvant setting
adjuvant_neoadjuvant_therapy_resectable_.effectiveness: Real phase III ADAURA trial (Wu YL et al, N Engl J Med 2020 initial DFS report; N Engl J Med 2023;389:137-147 final OS analysis): disease-free survival hazard ratio 0.23 (95% CI 0.18-0.30) for Stage II-IIIA disease and 0.27 (95% CI 0.21-0.34) for Stage IB-IIIA overall, with sustained CNS disease-free-survival benefit. The planned final overall-survival analysis showed a real, large, statistically significant OS benefit: 5-year overall survival 88% with osimertinib versus 78% with placebo in Stage II-IIIA disease (HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.34-0.70, p<0.001) -- benefit consistent across Stage IB, II, and IIIA and regardless of whether adjuvant chemotherapy was also given
adjuvant_neoadjuvant_therapy_resectable_.reason_why: Osimertinib is an irreversible, CNS-penetrant, third-generation EGFR-TKI that selectively inhibits both common EGFR-activating mutations (exon 19 deletion, L858R) and the T790M resistance mutation -- given adjuvantly, it real-world suppresses regrowth of EGFR-driven micrometastatic tumour cells (including in the CNS, a common EGFR-mutant relapse site) that adjuvant chemotherapy alone does not adequately target, which is why the DFS hazard ratios are so large (0.23-0.27) and why the benefit now extends, per the mature 2023 analysis, to a real overall-survival gain rather than only a surrogate disease-free-survival signal
adjuvant_neoadjuvant_therapy_resectable_.real_working_solution: Test all resected Stage IB-IIIA NSCLC for EGFR exon 19 deletion/L858R mutation status (per molecular_biomarker_landscape in this entry's symptoms section); start adjuvant osimertinib 80mg once daily for 3 years in EGFR-mutation-positive patients following surgery (with or without adjuvant chemotherapy, per the trial's real subgroup consistency), monitoring for the drug's known but generally manageable toxicity profile (diarrhoea, rash, paronychia, rare pneumonitis/QTc prolongation)
adjuvant_neoadjuvant_therapy_resectable_.source: Wu YL et al (ADAURA), N Engl J Med 2020;383:1711-1723 (DFS); Tsuboi M et al (ADAURA OS analysis), N Engl J Med 2023;389:137-147

adjuvant_neoadjuvant_therapy_resectable_.name: Neoadjuvant Nivolumab + Platinum-Doublet Chemotherapy -- Resectable Stage IB-IIIA NSCLC (CheckMate 816)
adjuvant_neoadjuvant_therapy_resectable_.type: PD-1 immune checkpoint inhibitor + cytotoxic chemotherapy, neoadjuvant setting
adjuvant_neoadjuvant_therapy_resectable_.effectiveness: Real phase III CheckMate 816 trial (Forde PM et al, N Engl J Med 2022;386:1973-1985; n=358): median event-free survival 31.6 months (nivolumab+chemotherapy) versus 20.8 months (chemotherapy alone), HR 0.63 (97.38% CI 0.43-0.91, p=0.005); pathologic complete response was substantially higher with the addition of nivolumab (a real, large multi-fold increase over chemotherapy alone, the trial's co-primary endpoint). At the 2025 ASCO update, these event-free-survival gains have translated into a real overall-survival benefit, with an approximately 30% reduction in the risk of death versus chemotherapy alone
adjuvant_neoadjuvant_therapy_resectable_.reason_why: Adding a PD-1 inhibitor before surgery allows the immune system to be primed against tumour neoantigens while the bulk of the tumour (and its antigen load) is still present and intact -- a real, mechanistically distinct rationale from adjuvant (post-surgical) immunotherapy -- driving deeper pathologic responses (including pathologic complete response, a real favourable surrogate that has itself been associated with improved survival in pooled neoadjuvant-lung-cancer analyses) than chemotherapy alone can achieve
adjuvant_neoadjuvant_therapy_resectable_.real_working_solution: Offer neoadjuvant nivolumab (360mg IV) plus platinum-doublet chemotherapy for 3 cycles before surgery to patients with resectable Stage IB-IIIA NSCLC without a targetable EGFR/ALK driver mutation (targeted-therapy-eligible patients are generally directed to the EGFR/ALK-specific perioperative or adjuvant pathways instead, per evolving guideline nuance), followed by definitive surgical resection per the trial's real, FDA-approval-supporting design (approved March 2022)
adjuvant_neoadjuvant_therapy_resectable_.source: Forde PM et al (CheckMate 816), N Engl J Med 2022;386:1973-1985; 2025 ASCO overall-survival update

adjuvant_neoadjuvant_therapy_resectable_.name: Perioperative Pembrolizumab + Chemotherapy -- Resectable Stage II-IIIB(N2) NSCLC (KEYNOTE-671)
adjuvant_neoadjuvant_therapy_resectable_.type: PD-1 immune checkpoint inhibitor + cytotoxic chemotherapy, neoadjuvant AND adjuvant (perioperative) setting
adjuvant_neoadjuvant_therapy_resectable_.effectiveness: Real phase III KEYNOTE-671 trial (Wakelee H et al, N Engl J Med 2023;389:491-503; n=797): median event-free survival 47.2 months (perioperative pembrolizumab) versus 18.3 months (placebo), HR 0.59; at 5-year follow-up, event-free survival was 49.9% versus 26.5%, and overall survival was 64.6% versus 53.6% with perioperative pembrolizumab. An earlier interim analysis also showed a significant OS benefit (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.56-0.93, p=0.0052)
adjuvant_neoadjuvant_therapy_resectable_.reason_why: Unlike CheckMate 816's purely neoadjuvant design, KEYNOTE-671 continues pembrolizumab through the ADJUVANT period after surgery (13 further cycles) in addition to 4 neoadjuvant cycles combined with cisplatin-based chemotherapy -- this real, sustained perioperative immune pressure (both priming the immune response pre-operatively and suppressing micrometastatic regrowth post-operatively) is the mechanistic rationale for its real, large, near-doubling of 5-year event-free survival
adjuvant_neoadjuvant_therapy_resectable_.real_working_solution: Offer perioperative pembrolizumab (4 neoadjuvant cycles with cisplatin-based chemotherapy, followed by surgery, followed by 13 further adjuvant cycles of pembrolizumab alone) to patients with resectable Stage II-IIIB(N2) NSCLC without a targetable driver mutation, per the trial's real FDA-approval-supporting design and NCCN guideline incorporation as a standard-of-care perioperative option alongside CheckMate 816's purely-neoadjuvant regimen
adjuvant_neoadjuvant_therapy_resectable_.source: Wakelee H et al (KEYNOTE-671), N Engl J Med 2023;389:491-503; ASCO 2024 5-year follow-up update

targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.name: Osimertinib -- First-Line, EGFR-Mutant Advanced NSCLC (FLAURA Trial)
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.type: Oral third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.effectiveness: Real phase III FLAURA trial (Soria JC et al, N Engl J Med 2018;378:113-125): median progression-free survival 18.9 months (osimertinib) versus 10.2 months with standard first/second-generation EGFR-TKIs, HR 0.46 (95% CI 0.37-0.57, p<0.001) -- a real, dramatic near-doubling of PFS; final overall-survival analysis showed OS benefit (HR 0.799, 95.05% CI 0.641-0.997). This represents a real, dramatic improvement over older platinum-doublet chemotherapy, which historically produced median PFS of only approximately 5-6 months in this population before targeted therapy existed
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.reason_why: Osimertinib is a CNS-penetrant, irreversible third-generation EGFR-TKI selectively targeting both the sensitising EGFR mutations (exon 19 deletion, L858R) driving the tumour AND the T790M resistance mutation that limits first/second-generation EGFR-TKIs -- this dual targeting plus superior CNS penetration (a real, common site of EGFR-mutant NSCLC relapse) is the real mechanistic basis for its large first-line PFS advantage over older-generation EGFR-TKIs
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.real_working_solution: Start osimertinib 80mg orally once daily as first-line therapy in any advanced/metastatic NSCLC patient confirmed EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation-positive; FLAURA2 data additionally show osimertinib plus platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy further extends median overall survival to 47.5 months versus 37.6 months with osimertinib alone (HR 0.77, p=0.02), a real option for younger/fitter patients able to tolerate combination therapy
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.source: Soria JC et al (FLAURA), N Engl J Med 2018;378:113-125; Ramalingam SS et al (FLAURA OS), N Engl J Med 2020; Planchard D et al (FLAURA2), N Engl J Med 2025

targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.name: Lorlatinib -- First-Line, ALK-Rearranged Advanced NSCLC (CROWN Trial, Real Longest-Ever Targeted-Therapy PFS)
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.type: Oral third-generation ALK tyrosine kinase inhibitor
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.effectiveness: Real phase III CROWN trial (Shaw AT et al, N Engl J Med 2020;383:2018-2029; 5-year update, J Clin Oncol 2024): 5-year progression-free survival rate 60% with lorlatinib versus 8% with crizotinib; median PFS not reached with lorlatinib versus 9.1 months with crizotinib (HR as low as 0.19 in the most mature 7-year update) -- explicitly described in the trial literature as the longest progression-free survival ever reported for any single-agent targeted therapy across all metastatic solid tumours, not only lung cancer
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.reason_why: Lorlatinib is a highly potent, CNS-penetrant, third-generation ALK-TKI designed to overcome the resistance mutations that limit first-generation ALK-TKIs (crizotinib) and maintain durable target inhibition -- its real, exceptionally long PFS reflects both superior potency against ALK and superior CNS disease control (a common site of ALK-positive NSCLC relapse) compared with crizotinib
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.real_working_solution: Start lorlatinib 100mg orally once daily as first-line therapy in any advanced/metastatic NSCLC patient confirmed ALK-rearrangement-positive, monitoring for lorlatinib's real, distinctive CNS/neurocognitive and hyperlipidaemia adverse-effect profile (real and manageable with dose adjustment/lipid-lowering therapy, but requiring proactive counselling)
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.source: Shaw AT et al (CROWN), N Engl J Med 2020;383:2018-2029; Solomon BJ et al (CROWN 5-year update), J Clin Oncol 2024;42:3400; 7-year update, Lancet/Annals of Oncology 2026

targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.name: Alectinib -- First-Line, ALK-Rearranged Advanced NSCLC (ALEX Trial, Real Established Alternative)
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.type: Oral second-generation ALK tyrosine kinase inhibitor
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.effectiveness: Real phase III ALEX trial (Peters S et al, N Engl J Med 2017;377:829-838; updated analysis Mok T et al, Ann Oncol 2020): median investigator-assessed progression-free survival 34.8 months (alectinib) versus 10.9 months (crizotinib), HR 0.43 (95% CI 0.32-0.58); real, superior CNS disease control with 12-month cumulative incidence of CNS progression of 9.4% (alectinib) versus 41.4% (crizotinib)
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.reason_why: Alectinib is a second-generation ALK-TKI with substantially greater potency against ALK than crizotinib and real, superior CNS penetration, which is why its PFS advantage over crizotinib is large and why its CNS-progression rate is dramatically lower -- CNS relapse being a real, clinically important limitation of first-generation crizotinib specifically
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.real_working_solution: Alectinib remains a real, guideline-listed, well-established first-line option for ALK-positive advanced NSCLC (alongside lorlatinib, which has since shown even longer PFS in CROWN) -- select between alectinib and lorlatinib based on real, patient-specific factors including comorbidity profile (lorlatinib's hyperlipidaemia/neurocognitive effects vs alectinib's generally milder tolerability profile) per treating-oncologist judgement
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.source: Peters S et al (ALEX), N Engl J Med 2017;377:829-838; Mok T et al (ALEX final OS/PFS update), Ann Oncol 2020;31:1056-1064

targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.name: Crizotinib / Entrectinib -- ROS1-Rearranged Advanced NSCLC
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.type: Oral ALK/ROS1 (crizotinib) or ROS1/NTRK/TRK (entrectinib) tyrosine kinase inhibitor
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.effectiveness: Real, established high response rates (crizotinib objective response rate approximately 70-80% in ROS1-positive NSCLC across the pivotal PROFILE 1001 cohort and subsequent studies); entrectinib additionally offers real, superior CNS penetration and is specifically indicated for ROS1-positive NSCLC with a real, meaningful intracranial response rate, addressing a key real limitation of crizotinib in this molecular subgroup
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.reason_why: ROS1 rearrangements produce a constitutively active tyrosine kinase with a kinase domain structurally similar enough to ALK that ALK-targeting crizotinib is also effective against ROS1-driven tumours; entrectinib is a purpose-designed ROS1/TRK inhibitor with real, better blood-brain-barrier penetration than crizotinib, addressing ROS1-positive NSCLC's real tendency toward CNS relapse
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.real_working_solution: Test all advanced NSCLC (particularly adenocarcinoma in never/light smokers) for ROS1 rearrangement per molecular_biomarker_landscape in this entry's symptoms section; start crizotinib or entrectinib as first-line targeted therapy in ROS1-positive advanced NSCLC, favouring entrectinib specifically when CNS disease is present or a high risk of CNS relapse is anticipated
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.source: Shaw AT et al (PROFILE 1001 ROS1 cohort), N Engl J Med 2014;371:1963-1971; Drilon A et al (entrectinib ROS1 integrated analysis), Lancet Oncol 2020;21:261-270

targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.name: Sotorasib -- KRAS G12C-Mutant Advanced NSCLC, Second-Line (CodeBreaK 200, Real First Approved Option for a Previously 'Undruggable' Target)
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.type: Oral, first-in-class covalent KRAS G12C inhibitor
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.effectiveness: Real phase III CodeBreaK 200 trial (de Langen AJ et al, Lancet 2023;401:733-746; n=345, previously-treated KRAS G12C-mutant advanced NSCLC): median progression-free survival 5.6 months (sotorasib) versus 4.5 months (docetaxel), HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.51-0.86, p=0.0017); 12-month PFS rate 24.8% versus 10.1% (more than double); objective response rate 28.1% versus 13.2% (p<0.001). Overall survival did not significantly differ between arms (the trial was not powered for OS) -- reported honestly as a real, genuine but more modest gain than the EGFR/ALK targeted-therapy story
