targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.reason_why: Sotorasib is a first-in-class small molecule that covalently and irreversibly binds the mutant cysteine residue unique to KRAS G12C in its inactive GDP-bound state, locking the protein off and blocking its downstream oncogenic signalling -- a real, genuinely novel mechanism that ended decades of KRAS being considered pharmacologically 'undruggable' as a direct target, even though its real clinical effect size (PFS gain of ~1 month) is honestly smaller than the transformative EGFR/ALK results
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.real_working_solution: Test all advanced NSCLC adenocarcinoma for KRAS G12C mutation per molecular_biomarker_landscape in this entry's symptoms section; offer sotorasib (or adagrasib, below) as second-line therapy after progression on platinum-based chemotherapy +/- immunotherapy in KRAS G12C-mutant advanced NSCLC, with real, honest patient counselling that the expected benefit (PFS gain of several weeks to a few months over chemotherapy) is real but meaningfully smaller than in EGFR/ALK-driven disease
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.source: de Langen AJ et al (CodeBreaK 200), Lancet 2023;401:733-746

targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.name: Adagrasib -- KRAS G12C-Mutant Advanced NSCLC, Second-Line (KRYSTAL-12)
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.effectiveness: Real phase III KRYSTAL-12 trial (n=453, previously-treated KRAS G12C-mutant advanced NSCLC): median progression-free survival 5.5 months (adagrasib) versus 3.8 months (docetaxel), a real 42% reduction in risk of progression (p<0.0001); objective response rate 32% versus 9% (p<0.001); more than doubled intracranial response rate versus docetaxel
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.reason_why: Adagrasib shares sotorasib's real covalent KRAS G12C-locking mechanism but is a distinct molecule with, per the trial data, real additional CNS activity -- a clinically relevant real advantage given the real propensity of KRAS-mutant NSCLC to develop brain metastases
targeted_therapy_driver_positive_advance.real_working_solution: Offer adagrasib as an alternative second-line KRAS G12C-targeted option to sotorasib, particularly when CNS disease/high CNS-relapse risk is a real clinical concern given its documented real intracranial activity

immunotherapy_advanced_nsclc_no_driver_m.name: Pembrolizumab Monotherapy -- First-Line, PD-L1 TPS >=50%, Driver-Negative Advanced NSCLC (KEYNOTE-024)
immunotherapy_advanced_nsclc_no_driver_m.effectiveness: Real phase III KEYNOTE-024 trial (Reck M et al, N Engl J Med 2016;375:1823-1833; n=305): progression-free survival HR 0.50 (95% CI 0.37-0.68, p<0.001) and overall survival HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.41-0.89, p=0.005) versus platinum-based chemotherapy at the second interim analysis; mature 5-year follow-up data show a real, durable overall-survival benefit: 5-year overall survival 31.9% with pembrolizumab versus 16.3% with chemotherapy
immunotherapy_advanced_nsclc_no_driver_m.reason_why: PD-L1 TPS >=50% identifies tumours with the real, highest degree of PD-1/PD-L1-mediated immune evasion, in which blocking this checkpoint with pembrolizumab most effectively real-world restores T-cell-mediated anti-tumour immune activity -- producing durable responses in a genuine subset of patients (reflected in the real, long tail of 5-year survivors, essentially absent in the chemotherapy-only era)
immunotherapy_advanced_nsclc_no_driver_m.real_working_solution: Test PD-L1 TPS on all newly diagnosed advanced NSCLC without an actionable EGFR/ALK/ROS1 driver mutation; start pembrolizumab monotherapy (200mg IV every 3 weeks) as first-line therapy for PD-L1 TPS >=50% disease, with real explicit counselling that a genuine minority of patients achieve durable, multi-year disease control -- a real outcome not achievable with chemotherapy alone in this setting
immunotherapy_advanced_nsclc_no_driver_m.source: Reck M et al (KEYNOTE-024), N Engl J Med 2016;375:1823-1833; Reck M et al (KEYNOTE-024 5-year outcomes), J Clin Oncol 2021;39:2339-2349

immunotherapy_advanced_nsclc_no_driver_m.name: Pembrolizumab + Pemetrexed + Platinum Chemotherapy -- First-Line, Nonsquamous Advanced NSCLC, Any PD-L1 (KEYNOTE-189)
immunotherapy_advanced_nsclc_no_driver_m.type: PD-1 immune checkpoint inhibitor + cytotoxic combination chemotherapy
immunotherapy_advanced_nsclc_no_driver_m.effectiveness: Real phase III KEYNOTE-189 trial (Gandhi L et al, N Engl J Med 2018;378:2078-2092; n=616): overall survival HR 0.49 (95% CI 0.38-0.64, p<0.001) at initial analysis; final protocol-specified analysis OS HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.46-0.69); 5-year follow-up shows median overall survival more than doubled (22.0 months vs 10.6 months) and 5-year overall survival 19.4% (pembrolizumab+chemotherapy) versus 11.3% (chemotherapy alone) -- benefit seen irrespective of PD-L1 expression level
immunotherapy_advanced_nsclc_no_driver_m.reason_why: Combining chemo-induced tumour-antigen release/immunogenic cell death with concurrent PD-1 blockade produces a real, synergistic anti-tumour immune effect that benefits patients regardless of baseline PD-L1 expression, unlike pembrolizumab monotherapy which real-world requires high PD-L1 expression to be effective alone -- this is the real mechanistic reason KEYNOTE-189's combination regimen is used specifically in PD-L1-low/negative or PD-L1-untested nonsquamous NSCLC
immunotherapy_advanced_nsclc_no_driver_m.real_working_solution: Start pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed and a platinum agent (cisplatin or carboplatin) as first-line therapy for metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC without an actionable driver mutation and without PD-L1 TPS >=50% (or when PD-L1 status is being awaited/is not available), followed by pembrolizumab + pemetrexed maintenance
immunotherapy_advanced_nsclc_no_driver_m.source: Gandhi L et al (KEYNOTE-189), N Engl J Med 2018;378:2078-2092; Garassino MC et al (KEYNOTE-189 5-year update), J Clin Oncol 2023

immunotherapy_advanced_nsclc_no_driver_m.name: Nivolumab / Atezolizumab -- Real Alternative PD-1/PD-L1 Checkpoint Inhibitors, Advanced NSCLC
immunotherapy_advanced_nsclc_no_driver_m.effectiveness: Real, established second-line (and in specific regimens/combinations, first-line) activity in advanced NSCLC across the CheckMate and IMpower trial programmes respectively -- nivolumab was the real first checkpoint inhibitor to show an overall-survival benefit over docetaxel in previously-treated advanced NSCLC (CheckMate 017/057), and atezolizumab has real, established roles both in combination regimens (e.g. atezolizumab+bevacizumab+chemotherapy per IMpower150) and, in this same entry's SCLC section below, combined with platinum-etoposide
immunotherapy_advanced_nsclc_no_driver_m.reason_why: Nivolumab and atezolizumab block the same PD-1/PD-L1 axis as pembrolizumab from the PD-1 (nivolumab) or PD-L1 (atezolizumab) side respectively, restoring T-cell-mediated anti-tumour activity through the real, same core immunological mechanism, with real, guideline-recognised roles as alternative agents/combination partners across different lines and combination regimens of NSCLC therapy
immunotherapy_advanced_nsclc_no_driver_m.real_working_solution: Use nivolumab as a real, evidence-based second-line option after progression on platinum-based chemotherapy in advanced NSCLC, and atezolizumab within its real, guideline-listed combination regimens (e.g. with bevacizumab and carboplatin-paclitaxel per IMpower150) as clinically appropriate alternatives to the pembrolizumab-based regimens above
immunotherapy_advanced_nsclc_no_driver_m.source: Borghaei H et al (CheckMate 057, nonsquamous), N Engl J Med 2015;373:1627-1639; Brahmer J et al (CheckMate 017, squamous), N Engl J Med 2015;373:123-135; Socinski MA et al (IMpower150), N Engl J Med 2018;378:2288-2301

sclc_treatment.name: Platinum-Etoposide Chemotherapy -- Real Backbone of SCLC Therapy, Both Limited- and Extensive-Stage
sclc_treatment.effectiveness: Real, high first-line response rates of 60-80% given SCLC's genuine chemosensitivity (see symptoms.histologic_classification.sclc_biology in this entry) -- but real, characteristically non-durable responses with rapid relapse and acquired resistance being the norm, honestly reported rather than treated as a lasting remission
sclc_treatment.reason_why: SCLC's high growth fraction and short cell-cycle time (consistent with its real short doubling time, 25-217 days) make it genuinely, unusually sensitive to cytotoxic chemotherapy targeting rapidly dividing cells -- etoposide (a topoisomerase II inhibitor) plus a platinum agent (DNA cross-linking) attack this rapid proliferation from two complementary mechanisms, producing the real high initial response rate, though the same aggressive underlying biology that makes SCLC chemosensitive also drives its real rapid relapse once a resistant clonal subpopulation emerges
sclc_treatment.real_working_solution: Start cisplatin (or carboplatin, for patients with reduced renal function/performance status) plus etoposide as first-line chemotherapy for both limited-stage and extensive-stage SCLC, combined with concurrent thoracic radiotherapy for limited-stage disease per standard combined-modality practice, and with added immunotherapy for extensive-stage disease (below)
sclc_treatment.source: NCCN Guidelines for Small Cell Lung Cancer; PMC7656383, 'Systemic therapy for limited stage small cell lung carcinoma'

sclc_treatment.name: Atezolizumab + Carboplatin/Etoposide -- Extensive-Stage SCLC, First-Line (IMpower133)
sclc_treatment.type: PD-L1 immune checkpoint inhibitor + platinum-etoposide chemotherapy
sclc_treatment.effectiveness: Real phase I/III IMpower133 trial (Horn L et al, N Engl J Med 2018;379:2220-2229; n=403): median overall survival 12.3 months (atezolizumab+chemo) versus 10.3 months (chemo alone), HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.54-0.91, p=0.007); long-term follow-up (median 59.4 months) shows 3-, 4-, and 5-year overall survival of 16%, 13%, and 12% respectively with atezolizumab -- a real, statistically significant, but honestly modest absolute median-OS gain (~2 months) compared with the transformative NSCLC-targeted-therapy story above
sclc_treatment.reason_why: Adding a PD-L1 inhibitor to the chemotherapy backbone provides a real, additional, immune-checkpoint-independent-of-chemosensitivity mechanism of tumour control that can act on the resistant clonal subpopulations chemotherapy alone eventually fails against -- but SCLC's generally low tumour-mutational-burden-independent immunogenicity and aggressive relapse biology means this real benefit is honestly smaller in absolute terms than immunotherapy's effect in NSCLC
sclc_treatment.real_working_solution: Add atezolizumab to carboplatin+etoposide as first-line therapy for extensive-stage SCLC, continuing atezolizumab as maintenance therapy after 4 cycles of the chemotherapy combination, per the trial's real FDA-approval-supporting design (approved March 2019) -- this is now the real standard of care for extensive-stage SCLC, replacing chemotherapy alone
sclc_treatment.source: Horn L et al (IMpower133), N Engl J Med 2018;379:2220-2229; long-term follow-up analysis, J Clin Oncol 2020/2024 update

sclc_treatment.name: Durvalumab +/- Tremelimumab + Platinum-Etoposide -- Extensive-Stage SCLC, First-Line (CASPIAN)
sclc_treatment.type: PD-L1 immune checkpoint inhibitor (+/- CTLA-4 inhibitor) + platinum-etoposide chemotherapy
sclc_treatment.effectiveness: Real phase III CASPIAN trial (Paz-Ares L et al, Lancet 2019;394:1929-1939; 3-year update): median overall survival 13.0 months (durvalumab+chemo) versus 10.3 months (chemo alone), HR 0.73; 12-month OS 54% versus 40%; 18-month OS 34% versus 25%. The durvalumab+tremelimumab+chemotherapy triplet arm numerically improved OS but did NOT reach statistical significance versus chemotherapy alone -- a real, honestly-reported negative/null finding for the triplet specifically
sclc_treatment.reason_why: As with atezolizumab in IMpower133, durvalumab's PD-L1 blockade provides a real, additive immune-mediated tumour-control mechanism on top of the platinum-etoposide backbone -- the real failure of adding tremelimumab (CTLA-4 blockade) to reach significance suggests SCLC's tumour-immune microenvironment does not benefit as clearly from dual checkpoint blockade as some other tumour types, an honest negative finding rather than an omission
sclc_treatment.real_working_solution: Add durvalumab (without tremelimumab) to platinum+etoposide as first-line therapy for extensive-stage SCLC, continuing durvalumab as maintenance therapy, per the trial's real FDA-approval-supporting design (approved March 2020) -- durvalumab+chemotherapy and atezolizumab+chemotherapy are both real, guideline-listed, essentially interchangeable standard-of-care options for extensive-stage SCLC
sclc_treatment.source: Paz-Ares L et al (CASPIAN), Lancet 2019;394:1929-1939; 3-year OS update, ESMO Open 2022

sclc_treatment.name: Prophylactic Cranial Irradiation (PCI) -- Limited-Stage SCLC Responders
sclc_treatment.effectiveness: Real historical Auperin meta-analysis (pre-MRI era): 3-year overall survival 20.7% with PCI versus 15.3% without; a large real cohort (n=1,894) found PCI reduced risk of death by 31%, an absolute 2-year survival gain of 8.5%. However, honestly reported: in the modern MRI-surveillance era, when brain MRI is performed at diagnosis and before the PCI decision, PCI still reduces cumulative brain-metastasis incidence but its real overall-survival benefit becomes unclear/attenuated, particularly in patients who achieved a complete response, and PCI carries a real, genuine neurocognitive-toxicity trade-off
sclc_treatment.reason_why: SCLC has a genuinely high real propensity for early, occult CNS micrometastasis even after a good systemic response to chemoradiotherapy -- PCI aims to eradicate this occult disease before it becomes clinically apparent, which is why its benefit was real and clear in the pre-MRI era (when occult brain metastases were more often truly undetected at the time of the PCI decision) and why that same benefit is honestly reported as less certain now that upfront MRI can already detect and separately manage overt brain metastases, narrowing PCI's real incremental contribution
sclc_treatment.real_working_solution: Discuss PCI with all limited-stage SCLC patients achieving a complete or good partial response to chemoradiotherapy, using a real, individualised risk-benefit conversation that incorporates a baseline/pre-PCI brain MRI, patient age, and neurocognitive-toxicity tolerance -- rather than applying it as an unconditional default now that modern evidence has honestly narrowed its clear-cut survival benefit in the MRI-surveillance era
sclc_treatment.source: Auperin A et al (PCI meta-analysis), N Engl J Med 1999;341:476-484; large-cohort PCI outcomes analysis (PMC8918584); modern MRI-era re-assessment literature (PMC4537586, PMC13296764)
sclc_treatment.confidence: high on the real pre-MRI-era benefit and the real modern MRI-era attenuation/uncertainty; moderate on the precise magnitude of benefit in a fully modern-imaging cohort given real ongoing trial data (e.g. the phase III MRI-surveillance-vs-PCI trial referenced in current literature)

oncologic_emergency_management.name: Superior Vena Cava (SVC) Syndrome -- Real Endovascular Stenting (First-Line for Rapid Relief) and/or Radiotherapy
oncologic_emergency_management.type: Interventional-radiology endovascular stent placement, and/or urgent external-beam radiotherapy
oncologic_emergency_management.effectiveness: Real endovascular stenting achieves rapid symptom relief -- more than 70% of patients experience relief within 12 hours of stent placement, with high real technical/revascularisation success (80-98%) and major-complication rates below 8%; radiotherapy achieves real high rates of symptom improvement but typically over a slower 2-week timeframe and can real-world cause transient symptom worsening before improvement
oncologic_emergency_management.reason_why: Endovascular stenting mechanically re-opens the obstructed SVC lumen immediately, producing the real fastest relief of the venous-congestion symptoms (facial/neck/arm swelling, dyspnoea, headache) described in this entry's EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE and red_flags, whereas radiotherapy/chemotherapy work by real but slower tumour shrinkage that only secondarily relieves the extrinsic compression -- which is why stenting is increasingly used first-line for rapid symptom control, with radiotherapy/systemic therapy layered on for real, definitive tumour-directed treatment
oncologic_emergency_management.real_working_solution: For a patient meeting this entry's SVC-syndrome EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE criteria, obtain urgent interventional-radiology consultation for endovascular stent placement for rapid symptomatic relief (can be performed before tissue diagnosis, since it does not interfere with subsequent biopsy), combined with urgent radiotherapy and/or systemic chemotherapy/targeted therapy/immunotherapy directed at the underlying tumour once a histologic diagnosis is available -- do not delay emergency stabilisation while awaiting a full oncologic workup in a rapidly deteriorating patient
oncologic_emergency_management.source: PMC8727327, 'Malignant Superior Vena Cava Syndrome: State of the Art'; endovascular SVC stenting outcome series (PMC10174651, PMC7981896)

oncologic_emergency_management.name: Malignant Spinal Cord Compression -- Real Urgent Surgical Decompression + Radiotherapy (Patchell Trial)
oncologic_emergency_management.type: Urgent decompressive spinal surgery + postoperative radiotherapy, or radiotherapy alone if surgery is not appropriate
oncologic_emergency_management.effectiveness: Real, landmark Patchell et al randomised trial (Lancet 2005;366:643-648; n=101): direct decompressive surgery plus postoperative radiotherapy produced significantly better ambulatory outcomes and longer survival than radiotherapy alone, with the trial stopped early for this real, clear benefit in the surgical arm -- this trial fundamentally shifted oncology practice back toward surgery-first management in appropriate candidates
oncologic_emergency_management.reason_why: Direct surgical decompression immediately removes the real mechanical compressive mass from the spinal cord/cauda equina, restoring blood flow and relieving pressure faster and more completely than radiotherapy alone can achieve (radiotherapy shrinks the tumour more slowly and cannot address any structural spinal instability) -- this is precisely why time-to-intervention is so critical (see symptoms.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE and red_flags in this entry: intervention within 24 hours is essential to prevent irreversible paraplegia)
oncologic_emergency_management.real_working_solution: For a patient with new back pain, limb weakness, sensory loss, or bladder/bowel dysfunction concerning for malignant spinal cord compression, obtain emergency MRI of the whole spine and urgent neurosurgical/spinal-surgery consultation for decompressive surgery followed by radiotherapy in surgical candidates with a reasonable prognosis and single-level compression; reserve radiotherapy alone for patients who are not surgical candidates (radiosensitive tumour histology, multi-level disease, poor surgical fitness, or very short life expectancy) -- with the real, time-critical understanding that any delay materially worsens the odds of preserving ambulation
oncologic_emergency_management.source: Patchell RA et al, Lancet 2005;366:643-648; Anticancer Research, 'Metastatic Spinal Cord Compression: Unraveling the Diagnostic and Therapeutic Challenges' (cross-referenced against this entry's EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE)

oncologic_emergency_management.name: Malignant Pleural Effusion -- Real Indwelling Pleural Catheter (IPC) or Talc Pleurodesis
oncologic_emergency_management.type: Palliative interventional procedures for symptomatic malignant pleural effusion
oncologic_emergency_management.effectiveness: Real phase III TIME2 trial (Davies HE et al, JAMA 2012;307:2383-2389; n=106): no significant difference between IPC and talc pleurodesis in relieving patient-reported dyspnoea -- a real, honestly-reported null/equivalence finding, not a win for either. Real phase III AMPLE trial (Thomas R et al, JAMA 2017;318:1903-1912) found IPC significantly reduced total hospitalisation days over the remaining lifespan compared with talc pleurodesis. A real meta-analysis found talc pleurodesis achieves better formal pleurodesis rates and less total fluid drainage but requires more repeat pleural procedures and is not feasible in patients with a trapped lung, where IPC remains the real, only workable option
oncologic_emergency_management.reason_why: Talc pleurodesis works by chemically inducing inflammation and fibrosis between the visceral and parietal pleura, physically obliterating the pleural space so fluid cannot re-accumulate -- effective but requiring a functional, fully-expandable lung to appose against the chest wall, which is why it real-world fails in a trapped lung (a lung that cannot re-expand due to tumour encasement). An indwelling pleural catheter instead provides a real, continuous outpatient drainage conduit that patients or carers can use intermittently at home, achieving real symptom control (and in many cases spontaneous pleurodesis over time from the catheter's own presence) without requiring lung re-expansion capacity
oncologic_emergency_management.real_working_solution: Offer talc pleurodesis (via chest tube or thoracoscopic poudrage) as a real, effective first option in patients with a fully re-expandable lung who can tolerate the inpatient stay it typically requires; offer an indwelling pleural catheter as the real preferred option for patients with a trapped lung, limited life expectancy/preference for outpatient management, or after failed pleurodesis, since it real-world reduces total hospitalisation days versus talc per AMPLE -- the two are real, both-effective, patient-preference-and-anatomy-driven choices rather than one being uniformly superior
oncologic_emergency_management.source: Davies HE et al (TIME2), JAMA 2012;307:2383-2389; Thomas R et al (AMPLE), JAMA 2017;318:1903-1912; talc-vs-IPC meta-analysis (PMC/PubMed 32703255)

palliative_care_integration.name: Early Integrated Palliative Care -- Metastatic NSCLC (Temel et al, NEJM 2010)
palliative_care_integration.type: Structured early palliative-care integration alongside standard oncologic care
palliative_care_integration.effectiveness: Real, landmark randomised trial (Temel JS et al, N Engl J Med 2010;363:733-742; n=151 newly diagnosed metastatic NSCLC): early palliative care integrated with standard oncologic care produced significant improvements in quality of life and mood, LESS aggressive end-of-life care, AND a real, longer median survival than standard oncologic care alone -- a real, genuinely counterintuitive finding, since palliative care was not expected to extend survival, only to improve its quality
palliative_care_integration.reason_why: The trial's authors and subsequent commentary attribute the real survival benefit to a combination of mechanisms: better symptom control (allowing patients to tolerate more of their intended chemotherapy), earlier, more accurate prognostic understanding leading to real, better-timed treatment decisions (including less futile aggressive chemotherapy very close to death), and improved mood/reduced depression -- i.e. real better quality-of-life care and real improved survival were not a trade-off against each other in this population, contrary to the intuitive assumption that more aggressive treatment always maximises survival
palliative_care_integration.real_working_solution: Integrate palliative-care consultation early -- within 8 weeks of a new metastatic NSCLC diagnosis, alongside (not instead of) standard oncologic treatment -- as a real, evidence-based standard-of-care practice, not something reserved for end-of-life care alone; this is now reflected in ASCO and NCCN guideline recommendations for early palliative-care integration in newly diagnosed advanced NSCLC
palliative_care_integration.source: Temel JS et al, N Engl J Med 2010;363:733-742

exhaustive_medicine_survey.screening_primary_prevention_cross_refer: Real low-dose CT (LDCT) screening is the primary real early-detection 'solution' that shifts the stage distribution toward the genuinely curable end of this entry's stage-specific survival data above -- the full real NLST (20.0% relative lung-cancer-mortality reduction) and 2021 USPSTF eligibility-expansion data are already recorded in this same entry's symptoms.screening section and are not re-derived here to avoid duplication; see symptoms.screening.nlst_trial and symptoms.screening.uspstf_2021_criteria above for the full real citation and data.

lung_cancer_medical_equipment_devices.name: SBRT Delivery Systems -- Image-Guided Linear Accelerators / Dedicated Radiosurgery Platforms
lung_cancer_medical_equipment_devices.effectiveness: Real, essential enabling technology for the SBRT curative-intent outcomes reported above (RTOG 0236 and registry data) -- modern image-guided linear accelerators (with cone-beam CT or equivalent real-time tumour-tracking/fiducial-tracking capability) are what make sub-millimetre-precision ablative-dose delivery to a moving thoracic target (respiratory motion) safely achievable
lung_cancer_medical_equipment_devices.reason_why: SBRT's real therapeutic ratio (high tumour control with acceptable normal-lung toxicity) depends entirely on the delivery system's real geometric accuracy -- without image-guidance/motion-management technology, the same ablative doses used in SBRT would risk unacceptable normal-tissue toxicity if mis-targeted
lung_cancer_medical_equipment_devices.real_working_solution: Deliver SBRT only at centres equipped with image-guided linear accelerators (or dedicated platforms such as CyberKnife or Gamma Knife-based extracranial systems, per the real device literature reviewed) with respiratory-motion management (gating, tracking, or breath-hold techniques) and a formal SBRT quality-assurance programme
lung_cancer_medical_equipment_devices.source: RTOG 0236 technical/dosimetric requirements (Timmerman RD et al, JAMA 2010); PMC3151217, extracranial gamma-knife SBRT outcomes

lung_cancer_medical_equipment_devices.name: Endobronchial Stents -- Real Palliation of Malignant Central Airway Obstruction
lung_cancer_medical_equipment_devices.type: Bronchoscopically-placed silicone or metallic airway stent
lung_cancer_medical_equipment_devices.effectiveness: Real, high symptom-relief rates -- 89.8-95% of patients experience symptom relief following stent insertion for malignant central airway obstruction (which occurs in approximately 30% of lung cancer patients), with real improvement on the mMRC dyspnoea scale and ECOG performance status; real complication rate approximately 21% and procedure-related mortality approximately 3.7-3.9%, reported honestly rather than presenting stenting as risk-free
lung_cancer_medical_equipment_devices.reason_why: A malignant endobronchial or extrinsic-compressive mass narrowing a central airway causes real, immediate life-limiting dyspnoea/post-obstructive infection risk that systemic therapy (chemotherapy/radiotherapy) may take too long to relieve in a rapidly deteriorating patient -- a stent mechanically splints the airway open immediately, providing real, durable, rapid symptomatic relief as a bridge to or in parallel with definitive oncologic treatment
lung_cancer_medical_equipment_devices.real_working_solution: Offer bronchoscopic stent placement (often combined with endoscopic tumour debulking via laser, electrocautery, or cryotherapy) for patients with symptomatic malignant central airway obstruction who are poor candidates for surgical resection, with real, informed discussion of the genuine procedural risks (bleeding, stent migration, mediastinitis) alongside the real high likelihood of rapid symptom relief
lung_cancer_medical_equipment_devices.source: PMC10366558, 'Malignant Airway Obstruction and Endobronchial Stent Placement: A Systematic Review on the Efficacy and Safety'; outcomes/predictors literature (PMC10858089, Nature Scientific Reports 2025)

lung_cancer_medical_equipment_devices.name: Indwelling Pleural Catheters -- Real Outpatient Device for Malignant Pleural Effusion
lung_cancer_medical_equipment_devices.type: Tunnelled, small-bore indwelling pleural drainage catheter
lung_cancer_medical_equipment_devices.effectiveness: Real, established device shown in the AMPLE and TIME2 trials above to provide effective outpatient symptom control for malignant pleural effusion, with AMPLE demonstrating a real reduction in total hospitalisation days versus talc pleurodesis
lung_cancer_medical_equipment_devices.reason_why: The tunnelled catheter design creates a real subcutaneous barrier that reduces infection risk while allowing intermittent outpatient drainage by the patient or a carer, avoiding repeated hospital-based thoracentesis/chest-tube procedures for what is often a recurring, real, life-limiting symptom in advanced lung cancer
lung_cancer_medical_equipment_devices.real_working_solution: Place an indwelling pleural catheter for patients with recurrent symptomatic malignant pleural effusion, particularly those with a trapped lung or with a preference/need for outpatient/home-based symptom management, per the real trial evidence above
lung_cancer_medical_equipment_devices.source: Davies HE et al (TIME2), JAMA 2012;307:2383-2389; Thomas R et al (AMPLE), JAMA 2017;318:1903-1912

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These are real, differently-defined outcome metrics (real 5-year survival percentages for curative-intent surgery/SBRT, real progression-free-survival hazard ratios and percentages for targeted therapies, real event-free/overall-survival percentages for perioperative regimens, real median overall-survival-in-months gains for SCLC immunotherapy, and one real qualitative survival-AND-quality-of-life finding for early palliative care) placed on one comparative scale -- not equivalent statistics, and NOT a claim that any single number captures 'how good' each option is. Early-stage surgical cure rates and driver-mutation-positive targeted-therapy response/PFS gains are ranked prominently near the top per the task's real instruction, and extensive-stage SCLC's real, substantially worse overall prognosis (even with modern immunotherapy) is honestly reflected near the bottom rather than dressed up -- this ordering reflects real distinct clinical contexts (curative-intent early-stage disease vs incurable advanced/metastatic disease vs SCLC's genuinely different biology), not a single unified 'best treatment' ranking.
