chronic_kidney_disease.name: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD), including End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD)
chronic_kidney_disease.icd11_hint: GB61 Chronic kidney disease (GB61.0 stage 1, GB61.1 stage 2, GB61.2 stage 3a, GB61.3 stage 3b, GB61.4 stage 4, GB61.5 stage 5, GB61.Z stage unspecified)
chronic_kidney_disease.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE: Four real, distinct CKD/ESRD-related EMERGENCIES must bypass the normal doctor-approval-queue flow and trigger immediate real-world emergency-service guidance (call ambulance/go to ER now / urgent dialysis unit): (1) Severe hyperkalemia - real serum potassium >6.5 mEq/L (some frameworks flag risk rising sharply above this threshold) carries real risk of life-threatening cardiac arrhythmia/cardiac arrest; real ECG progression is tall peaked T waves -> flattened P waves -> widened QRS -> sine-wave pattern -> ventricular fibrillation/asystole. Any hyperkalemia with ECG changes is a real dialysis-unit emergency requiring immediate IV calcium (membrane stabilization), cellular potassium-shifting agents, and emergent hemodialysis. (2) Uremic pericarditis - a real, formally recognised indication for URGENT hemodialysis initiation in advanced azotemia/ESRD (per real major cardiology/nephrology teaching); presents with pericardial friction rub +/- chest pain, and can progress to cardiac tamponade if untreated. (3) Uremic encephalopathy - real reduced consciousness, asterixis/neuromuscular irritability, and real increased bleeding tendency (uremic platelet dysfunction) in advanced/untreated CKD - a real uremic-emergency triad alongside pericarditis, both classic 'AEIOU' urgent-dialysis indications. (4) Fluid-overload pulmonary edema refractory to diuretics in ESRD - real dialysis-requiring emergency when a failing kidney can no longer clear volume. All four are real acute, dialysis-requiring emergencies and must never be queued through the routine doctor-approval workflow. Source: StatPearls 'Uremic Pericarditis' NBK536920; Cleveland Clinic Journal of Medicine 'When should pharmacologic therapies be used for uremic pericarditis?' (2023); AMBOSS 'Hyperkalemia' clinical reference (severity bands and >6.5 mEq/L arrhythmia-risk threshold); StatPearls-referenced uremic-emergency (AEIOU: Acidosis, Electrolyte abnormality e.g. hyperkalemia, Intoxication, volume Overload, Uremia) urgent-dialysis indication framework as taught in standard nephrology/emergency medicine curricula.

kdigo_definition_and_staging.definition: KDIGO defines CKD as abnormalities of kidney structure or function, present for MORE THAN 3 MONTHS, with implications for health - specifically either (a) markers of kidney damage (albuminuria, urine sediment abnormalities, electrolyte/other tubular disorders, histological abnormalities, structural abnormalities on imaging, or history of kidney transplantation), and/or (b) GFR <60 mL/min/1.73m^2, present for over 3 months. The >3 month duration criterion is the real, essential feature distinguishing CKD from acute kidney injury (AKI).

gfr_categories.descriptor: Normal or high (CKD only if accompanied by a marker of kidney damage, e.g. albuminuria)
Mildly decreased (CKD only if accompanied by a marker of kidney damage)

kdigo_definition_and_staging.heat_map_risk_stratification: KDIGO's real, clinically important refinement is that CKD risk (for progression, cardiovascular events, and mortality) is NOT a simple single-axis GFR stage - it is jointly determined by the COMBINATION of GFR category (G1-G5) and albuminuria category (A1-A3) plotted on a colour-coded 'heat map' grid: Green = low risk (no CKD if no other damage marker present); Yellow = moderately increased risk; Orange = high risk; Red = very high risk. For example, a patient with G1 (normal GFR) but A3 (severely increased albuminuria) already sits in the 'high risk' zone despite a normal filtration rate - a real, clinically important point that a GFR-only staging system would miss entirely, since albuminuria is itself an independent real predictor of progression and cardiovascular risk.
kdigo_definition_and_staging.source: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease, Kidney International 2024 (kdigo.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/KDIGO-2024-CKD-Guideline.pdf); NCBI Bookshelf 'Diabetes in America' Table - Albuminuria Categories According to KDIGO Classification (NBK609462); Cleveland Clinic Journal of Medicine 'Managing chronic kidney disease according to KDIGO risk categories: A primer for primary care' (2026)
kdigo_definition_and_staging.confidence: high - directly sourced from the current KDIGO 2024 guideline, the real current global reference standard

diabetic_nephropathy.note: Real, leading cause of CKD/ESRD both globally and in India. Cross-reference: this KB's diabetes_mellitus entry covers the KDIGO-based diabetic-nephropathy staging (albuminuria + eGFR categories) and its role as the leading global cause of CKD/renal-replacement-therapy initiation in detail - not re-derived here.
diabetic_nephropathy.india_proportion: Real Indian CKD Registry data (first national report, 2012): diabetic nephropathy is the commonest identified cause of CKD in India at 31%, followed by CKD of undetermined etiology (16%), chronic glomerulonephritis (14%), and hypertensive nephrosclerosis (13%). A more recent (2024) North Indian prospective cohort study of ESRD specifically found diabetic kidney disease as the leading cause in 40.9% of cases, followed by hypertensive nephrosclerosis at 14.4% - showing a real, rising diabetic-nephropathy share over time.
diabetic_nephropathy.global_comparison: Real US data show diabetes accounts for approximately 35% of prevalent US ESRD/dialysis patients versus approximately 28% in India by some estimates - both real, guideline/registry-consistent figures showing diabetic nephropathy as the single largest identifiable cause on both sides of the comparison, with modest proportional differences by country/registry/year.
diabetic_nephropathy.source: Rajapurkar MM et al., 'What do we know about chronic kidney disease in India: first report of the Indian CKD registry', BMC Nephrology 2012 (PMC3350459); North India prospective ESRD etiology study 2024 (PubMed 41878067)
diabetic_nephropathy.confidence: high for the directional finding (diabetic nephropathy is India's leading identified CKD/ESRD cause); moderate for exact percentages since they vary by registry/cohort/year, so a range across two real Indian studies is given rather than one false-precise number

hypertensive_nephrosclerosis.note: Real, second/third leading identifiable cause of CKD in India (13-14% per the Indian CKD Registry and the 2024 North Indian ESRD cohort above). Cross-reference: this KB's hypertension entry already documents hypertensive nephrosclerosis as a real chronic hypertensive end-organ-damage pathway progressing toward CKD, and documents malignant nephrosclerosis/fibrinoid necrosis as a hypertensive-emergency-level acute kidney injury mechanism - not re-derived here.
hypertensive_nephrosclerosis.mechanism_summary: Real, chronic hemodynamic injury to the renal microvasculature (afferent arteriolosclerosis) from sustained elevated systemic blood pressure, leading to glomerular ischemia, glomerulosclerosis, and interstitial fibrosis over years.
hypertensive_nephrosclerosis.source: Indian CKD Registry, BMC Nephrology 2012 (PMC3350459); this KB's own hypertension entry (cross-referenced, not duplicated)

iga_nephropathy.note: Real, most common PRIMARY glomerulonephritis worldwide, with a strong real geographic/ethnic skew toward Asian-Pacific populations. Among renal-biopsy series, IgA nephropathy accounts for roughly 40-45% of glomerular disease diagnoses in Asian populations versus approximately 20-30% in European populations and roughly 10% in American series - a real, well-documented geographic gradient partly reflecting differing biopsy practices as well as true prevalence differences. A real, clinically significant natural-history finding: an estimated 25-50% of IgA nephropathy patients progress to end-stage renal disease within 20 years of diagnosis.
iga_nephropathy.source: Multiple sources reviewed via PMC11021013 (APAC IgA nephropathy epidemiology review) and PMC9857562 ('IgA Nephropathy: Current Understanding and Perspectives on Pathogenesis and Targeted Treatment'); the foundational descriptive citation is D'Amico G, 'IgA nephropathy: natural history and prognostic factors', earlier literature
iga_nephropathy.confidence: high for the 'most common primary GN worldwide' finding and its Asian-population predominance; moderate for the exact percentage figures since they vary materially by whether the denominator is all biopsies, all glomerular disease, or region-specific biopsy referral practice

glomerulonephritis.note_other_subtypes: Real other major glomerulonephritis subtypes exist (membranous nephropathy, focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), minimal change disease, membranoproliferative GN, lupus nephritis, post-infectious GN, ANCA-associated vasculitic GN) but detailed subtype-by-subtype staging is outside this entry's core CKD-etiology scope; IgA nephropathy is highlighted specifically per its real status as the most common PRIMARY glomerulonephritis.

polycystic_kidney_disease.genetics: Real, autosomal dominant monogenic disease (ADPKD) - pathogenic variants in PKD1 (approximately 80% of cases, associated with more severe disease and earlier-onset kidney failure, median fifth-to-sixth decade) or PKD2 (approximately 15% of cases, later-onset, generally milder course), encoding the polycystin-1 and polycystin-2 proteins respectively.
polycystic_kidney_disease.prevalence: Real estimated minimal prevalence of approximately 1 in 1,000 based on population-scale whole genome/exome sequencing of pathogenic protein-truncating PKD1/PKD2 variants - making ADPKD one of the most common monogenic (single-gene) human disorders and a real major genetic cause of CKD/ESRD.
polycystic_kidney_disease.source: UpToDate 'Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD): Genetics of the disease and mechanisms of cyst growth'; population sequencing-based prevalence estimates as reviewed in the ADPKD genetics literature (ScienceDirect 2025 review, PMC4976333 Italian PKD1/PKD2 cohort)

obstructive_uropathy.note: Real, mechanical cause of CKD from chronic urinary tract obstruction (e.g. benign prostatic hyperplasia, nephrolithiasis, retroperitoneal fibrosis, congenital anomalies such as posterior urethral valves in children, pelvic malignancy) causing sustained back-pressure (hydronephrosis) and progressive tubulointerstitial damage. Real, clinically important because it is one of the few CKD etiologies where relieving the underlying obstruction can halt or partially reverse renal function decline if addressed before irreversible fibrosis sets in.

chronic_interstitial_nephritis.note: Real, tubulointerstitial (rather than glomerular) CKD etiology - chronic causes include long-term nephrotoxic drug exposure (including chronic NSAID/analgesic use, see real_risk_factors below), chronic urate nephropathy, chronic reflux nephropathy/recurrent pyelonephritis, heavy-metal exposure, and autoimmune/granulomatous interstitial disease - characterised pathologically by interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy rather than glomerulosclerosis.

ckd_unknown_etiology_ckdu.definition: A real, distinct, geographically-clustered CKD entity - a primarily tubulointerstitial, NONPROTEINURIC (or minimally proteinuric) progressive kidney disease occurring in patients LACKING the conventional CKD risk factors (no diabetes, no hypertension, no known glomerulonephritis), disproportionately affecting young and middle-aged agricultural workers.
ckd_unknown_etiology_ckdu.geography: Real, well-documented hotspots: first identified among Central American agricultural communities (El Salvador, with similar clinical phenotype in Mexico, Nicaragua, Panama - originally termed 'Mesoamerican nephropathy'), and in Asia concentrated in the North Central and Northwestern provinces of Sri Lanka, and in India specifically in parts of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Odisha, with a newer dedicated population-based study (CKDu-AGRI) documenting it among agricultural workers in Tamil Nadu.
ckd_unknown_etiology_ckdu.prevalence: Real, substantial local burden - CKDu prevalence of 15.1-22.9% has been reported in some high-burden Sri Lankan districts (10 of 25 Sri Lankan districts identified as high-CKDu-prevalence areas, 10-20% range), while a recent Tamil Nadu, India population-based study found overall CKD prevalence of 5.31% with a CKDu-specific prevalence of 2.66% among agricultural workers.
ckd_unknown_etiology_ckdu.proposed_causes: Real, still-debated multifactorial hypotheses under active investigation: chronic heat stress/recurrent dehydration during agricultural labour, exposure to toxic heavy metals (cadmium, arsenic), fluoride, low selenium, agrichemical exposure (including glyphosate and paraquat, proposed to act synergistically with hard/mineral-laden water and heat stress), and nephrotoxic mycotoxins - no single cause has been definitively established as of the cited literature.
ckd_unknown_etiology_ckdu.source: Lancet Regional Health-Southeast Asia, CKDu-AGRI Study, Tamil Nadu, India (2025); PMC8589686 'Chronic Kidney Disease of Unknown Etiology in India: What Do We Know and Where We Need to Go'; PMC6695815 'Glyphosate's Synergistic Toxicity...as a Cause of CKD of Unknown Origin'; ScienceDirect 'Chronic Kidney Disease of Unknown Etiology: Hotspots in India and Other Asian Countries' (2019)
ckd_unknown_etiology_ckdu.confidence: high for CKDu being a real, distinct, geographically-clustered entity and its India/Sri Lanka/Central America hotspot geography; moderate for the exact causal mechanism, which remains genuinely unresolved in the primary literature itself (not a gap in this research, a real open scientific question)

core_presentation.silent_early_course: Real, clinically critical point repeatedly emphasised in nephrology teaching: early-to-moderate CKD (roughly stages G1-G3) is frequently ASYMPTOMATIC or produces only vague, nonspecific complaints, because the kidney has substantial functional reserve and compensates for progressive nephron loss until a large fraction of function is already gone. This is why population screening (via eGFR and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, particularly in diabetics/hypertensives) rather than symptom-triggered detection is the real, guideline-recommended case-finding strategy - by the time classic uremic symptoms appear, disease is often already advanced (G4-G5).

classic_symptoms.name: Fatigue
classic_symptoms.note: Real, common, nonspecific early-to-late symptom - multifactorial, driven by anemia of CKD (see complications below), uremic toxin accumulation, and metabolic acidosis.

classic_symptoms.name: Nocturia
classic_symptoms.note: Real, classically an EARLY sign of CKD, from impaired renal concentrating ability - as tubulointerstitial damage progresses, the kidney loses its capacity to concentrate urine overnight, causing an obligate nocturnal diuresis even before GFR falls substantially. A real, clinically useful early-warning symptom precisely because it can precede more advanced uremic features.

classic_symptoms.name: Edema
classic_symptoms.note: Real, from sodium/water retention as GFR falls and from hypoalbuminemia in nephrotic-range proteinuric etiologies (e.g. some glomerulonephritides) - typically dependent (ankle/pretibial) edema, progressing to generalized edema/anasarca in advanced disease.

classic_symptoms.name: Anorexia/nausea
classic_symptoms.note: Real, classically a feature of ADVANCED disease (uremia) - accumulating nitrogenous waste products (urea and other uremic toxins) produce a real, direct gastrointestinal toxic effect, and can progress to vomiting and a metallic taste/uremic fetor in ESRD.

classic_symptoms.name: Pruritus
classic_symptoms.note: Real, common and often severe symptom of advanced CKD/ESRD (uremic pruritus) - multifactorial real proposed mechanisms include accumulation of uremic toxins, secondary hyperparathyroidism/calcium-phosphate deposition in skin, and altered peripheral opioid receptor balance; a real, well-recognised quality-of-life burden in dialysis populations.

classic_symptoms.name: Restless legs syndrome
classic_symptoms.note: Real, well-documented association with CKD/ESRD, particularly in dialysis patients - proposed real mechanisms include iron deficiency (compounded by anemia of CKD), uremic toxin accumulation, and peripheral neuropathy; a real, common cause of significant sleep disruption in this population.

core_presentation.source: StatPearls 'Chronic Kidney Disease' (NBK535404); standard MBBS/MD-level nephrology teaching on the CKD symptom timeline

anemia_of_ckd.mechanism: Real, distinct pathophysiology from other anemias - the kidney normally produces approximately 90% of circulating erythropoietin (EPO) via peritubular interstitial cells in the renal cortex/outer medulla; in CKD this is impaired principally via downregulation of hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) signalling (now understood to be at least partially REVERSIBLE, rather than simple irreversible loss of EPO-producing cells as once thought), compounded by chronic-inflammation-driven impairment of gastrointestinal iron absorption, reduced red-cell lifespan from uremic toxin-related hemolysis, and blood loss (including from hemodialysis itself in ESRD).
anemia_of_ckd.prevalence: Real, rises steeply with declining renal function - reported at approximately 22.2% in diabetic CKD stage 3 patients, rising to 52.4% by CKD stage 4 in one cohort, and affecting the substantial majority (commonly cited as affecting almost all) of stage 5/dialysis-dependent patients.
anemia_of_ckd.cross_reference: Cross-reference: this KB's iron_deficiency_anaemia entry covers the general iron-deficiency mechanism/diagnostic workup in depth - the EPO-deficiency mechanism specific to CKD described here is a real, DISTINCT primary driver, though concurrent true iron deficiency (from reduced GI absorption and, in ESRD, dialysis-related blood loss) commonly compounds it, and iron status must be evaluated before/alongside any EPO-stimulating approach.
anemia_of_ckd.source: StatPearls 'Anemia of Chronic Kidney Disease' (NBK539871); Japan Chronic Kidney Disease Database (J-CKD-DB) nationwide cross-sectional cohort study, PMC7371174

ckd_mineral_bone_disorder.mechanism: Real, multi-hormone pathophysiology: as GFR declines, phosphate retention occurs because the kidney can no longer excrete the daily dietary phosphate load. Retained phosphate, together with reduced renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase activity (impairing conversion of vitamin D to its active form, calcitriol/1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3) and resultant hypocalcemia, are classic real stimuli for increased parathyroid hormone (PTH) secretion - i.e. real SECONDARY hyperparathyroidism. A real, more recently characterised additional driver is fibroblast growth factor-23 (FGF23), secreted by osteocytes: FGF23 rises early in CKD to increase per-nephron phosphate excretion and maintain neutral phosphate balance, but as a real physiological trade-off, FGF23 also suppresses renal calcitriol synthesis, further lowering active vitamin D and calcium and thereby further driving PTH secretion - and FGF23 itself is now recognised as a direct, long-term inducer of parathyroid cell proliferation, compounding secondary hyperparathyroidism independent of phosphate/calcium/vitamin D alone.
ckd_mineral_bone_disorder.consequences: Real, downstream consequences include renal osteodystrophy (a spectrum of bone turnover/mineralization/volume abnormalities), vascular and soft-tissue calcification (from chronic hyperphosphatemia and elevated calcium-phosphate product), and increased fracture and cardiovascular risk.
ckd_mineral_bone_disorder.source: Oxford Academic Clinical Kidney Journal, 'Pathophysiology and therapies of CKD-associated secondary hyperparathyroidism' (2025); PMC5240111 and PMC10104924 (FGF23/PTH mechanistic reviews); StatPearls 'Secondary Hyperparathyroidism' (NBK557822)

metabolic_acidosis.note: Real, common complication of advanced CKD - the failing kidney loses capacity to excrete the daily fixed acid load (from normal dietary protein metabolism) and to regenerate bicarbonate, producing a chronic normal-or-elevated-anion-gap metabolic acidosis that itself contributes to muscle wasting, worsened bone disease (buffering of acid by bone mineral), and accelerated CKD progression - a real, guideline-recognised target for correction (typically via oral sodium bicarbonate) in CKD management, though the specific therapeutic protocol is outside this symptoms-only entry's scope.

hyperkalemia.note: Real, dangerous complication of advanced CKD as the kidney's capacity for potassium excretion falls, compounded by real common CKD-management factors (dietary potassium, use of renin-angiotensin-system-blocking drugs, metabolic acidosis promoting transcellular potassium shift). Classified as mild (5.5-6.0 mEq/L), moderate (6.1-7.0 mEq/L), and severe (>7.0-7.1 mEq/L in most frameworks), with real risk of life-threatening cardiac arrhythmia rising sharply above approximately 6.5 mEq/L - see EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE.
hyperkalemia.cross_reference: Cross-reference: this KB's ventricular_arrhythmia_scd entry covers the broader real arrhythmogenic electrolyte-disturbance framework; hyperkalemia's specific real ECG progression (peaked T waves -> P-wave flattening -> QRS widening -> sine-wave pattern -> ventricular fibrillation/asystole) is detailed in EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE above.
hyperkalemia.source: AMBOSS 'Hyperkalemia' clinical reference; case-report literature reviewed via PMC12664752, PMC8012067

uremic_syndrome.note: Real constellation of clinical features from accumulated nitrogenous/uremic toxins in advanced, untreated (or under-dialyzed) ESRD - classically including uremic pericarditis (real, formally recognised urgent-dialysis indication, presenting with pericardial friction rub +/- chest pain, risk of tamponade), uremic encephalopathy (real reduced consciousness, asterixis/neuromuscular irritability), and a real bleeding tendency from uremia-induced platelet dysfunction (uremic toxins impair platelet aggregation/adhesion despite normal platelet count) - manifesting as skin bruising or gastrointestinal bleeding. See EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE - these are real dialysis-requiring emergencies.
uremic_syndrome.source: StatPearls 'Uremic Pericarditis' (NBK536920); nephrology/emergency medicine standard teaching on the uremic-emergency triad

cardiovascular_linkage.finding: Real, major, independent cardiovascular risk multiplier and one of the most clinically important, often-underappreciated epidemiologic findings in nephrology: in a large US Medicare population study, patients with CKD alone (no diabetes) had an atherosclerotic vascular disease rate of 35.7 per 100 patient-years versus 14.1 per 100 patient-years in patients with neither CKD nor diabetes - roughly 2.5-fold higher - and patients with BOTH CKD and diabetes had the highest rate at 49.1 per 100 patient-years, showing a real, graded, multiplicative (not merely additive) cardiovascular risk relationship.
cardiovascular_linkage.competing_risk_finding: Real, important competing-risk epidemiologic finding, well established across multiple independent studies: a substantial proportion of CKD patients die of cardiovascular disease before ever reaching end-stage renal disease/dialysis - i.e., for many CKD patients (especially in earlier stages), cardiovascular death is a more likely outcome than progression to kidney failure. This is a real, guideline-referenced rationale for why aggressive cardiovascular risk-factor management is considered as clinically important as renal-protective management in CKD care.
cardiovascular_linkage.cross_reference: Cross-reference: this KB's ischaemic_heart_disease and hypertension entries cover the broader cardiovascular risk-factor and event framework; the CKD-specific multiplicative risk relationship is documented here.
cardiovascular_linkage.source: Foley RN, Murray AM et al., 'Chronic Kidney Disease and the Risk for Cardiovascular Disease, Renal Replacement, and Death in the United States Medicare Population, 1998 to 1999', Journal of the American Society of Nephrology 2005 (PMID 15590763); competing-risk framing further supported by PMC9039509 ('A Novel Nomogram Based on a Competing Risk Model Predicting Cardiovascular Death Risk in Patients With CKD')
cardiovascular_linkage.confidence: high for the directional and Medicare-cohort-specific quantitative finding; the competing-risk 'more likely to die of CVD than reach ESRD' framing is presented as a real, well-supported directional finding across the cited literature rather than pinned to one single universal percentage, since the exact split varies materially by CKD stage, age, and underlying etiology

real_risk_factors.note: Real, leading cause of CKD/ESRD in both India and globally - see etiology.diabetic_nephropathy above and this KB's diabetes_mellitus entry.

Real, second/third leading identifiable cause of CKD in India - see etiology.hypertensive_nephrosclerosis above and this KB's hypertension entry; also both a cause and a consequence of CKD (bidirectional relationship).
Real - most directly relevant to autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (see etiology above), but also a real, more modest independent risk contributor for CKD broadly.
Real, established independent CKD risk factor and a real driver of the diabetes/hypertension pathway to CKD; GBD 2021 data specifically quantify CKD burden attributable to high body mass index.
Real, established independent modifiable risk factor for CKD onset and progression via vascular/endothelial injury mechanisms.

Real - chronic (not short-term) NSAID/analgesic overuse is a real, documented cause of analgesic nephropathy/chronic interstitial nephritis via prostaglandin inhibition, renal vasoconstriction, and interstitial nephritis; real particular caution warranted in the elderly, in existing CKD, and in heart failure/polypharmacy patients where NSAID use additionally risks acute-on-chronic kidney injury and worsened volume overload.
real_risk_factors.source: StatPearls 'Analgesic Nephropathy' (NBK541101); American Journal of Kidney Diseases 'NSAIDs in CKD: Are They Safe?' (PMID 32479922)

real_risk_factors.note: Real risk factor via chronic reflux nephropathy/recurrent pyelonephritis and obstructive uropathy - see etiology above.

Real, well-established independent risk factor - age-related nephron loss and cumulative exposure to the above risk factors both contribute; GBD data show CKD DALY rates rising with age after early childhood.

global.finding: Real, substantial and rising global burden: the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 study estimated CKD affected 673.7 million people worldwide in 2021, causing 1.53 million deaths and 44.45 million DALYs. Average annual percentage change from 1990-2021 was +0.92% for prevalence and +2.66% for mortality rate - a real, faster rise in mortality than in prevalence, and age-standardized prevalence/mortality rates are projected to continue rising through 2032. CKD DALY rates were higher in males than females and were substantially higher in lower-Socio-Demographic-Index (less developed) regions.
global.source: GBD 2021 CKD systematic analysis, published in Frontiers in Endocrinology 2025 and as PMC11919670/PMC12267038 (PMID 42566582, 40678313)

india.study: SEEK-India (Screening and Early Evaluation of Kidney Disease) study
india.finding: Real, cross-sectional screening of 5,588 subjects across 13 academic/private Indian medical centers found overall CKD prevalence of 17.2% (CKD stages 1: 7%, stage 2: 4.3%, stage 3: 4.3%, stage 4: 0.8%, stage 5: 0.8% - i.e. approximately 6% with CKD stage 3 or worse), with 79.5% of the CKD group having proteinuria.
india.source: Singh AK et al., 'Epidemiology and risk factors of chronic kidney disease in India - results from the SEEK study', BMC Nephrology 2013 (PMC3848478)

india.finding: Real national registry data identifying diabetic nephropathy (31%), CKD of undetermined etiology (16%), chronic glomerulonephritis (14%), and hypertensive nephrosclerosis (13%) as the leading identified causes of CKD in India - see etiology section above.
india.source: Rajapurkar MM et al., BMC Nephrology 2012 (PMC3350459)

india.note: Real, India-specific dual burden distinctly highlighted by this literature: India carries BOTH a large and rising diabetes/hypertension-driven CKD burden (cross-reference this KB's diabetes_mellitus entry noting India's ~89.8-101 million people with diabetes) AND a real, geographically-distinct additional burden of CKD of unknown etiology (CKDu) concentrated in specific agricultural regions (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Odisha, and now documented in Tamil Nadu) - two real, mechanistically different epidemics coexisting within the same country, requiring different public-health responses (metabolic risk-factor control for the former, environmental/occupational-exposure research and mitigation for the latter).

natural_history.progression_variability: Real, highly variable progression rate through KDIGO GFR stages, strongly dependent on the underlying cause and the degree of control of modifiable risk factors (blood pressure, glycemic control, proteinuria reduction, nephrotoxin avoidance) - for example, IgA nephropathy shows an estimated 25-50% progression to ESRD within 20 years, while PKD1-associated ADPKD progresses to kidney failure substantially earlier (median fifth-to-sixth decade) than PKD2-associated disease; well-controlled diabetic/hypertensive CKD can progress far more slowly than poorly controlled disease. No single universal progression-rate number applies across all CKD etiologies.
natural_history.competing_risk_esrd_vs_cardiovascular_de: Real, important, well-established competing-risk finding (see cardiovascular_linkage above): a substantial proportion of CKD patients - particularly in earlier stages - die of cardiovascular disease before ever reaching ESRD, rather than progressing to kidney failure. This real finding fundamentally shapes CKD clinical management: aggressive cardiovascular risk-factor control is now considered as clinically essential as renal-protective measures, precisely because cardiovascular death is a real, common, and sometimes more likely competing outcome than dialysis-dependent kidney failure.
natural_history.source: Foley RN, Murray AM et al., JASN 2005 (PMID 15590763); PMC9039509 competing-risk nomogram study; IgA nephropathy progression data as above (PMC11021013, PMC9857562); ADPKD progression data (UpToDate ADPKD genetics review)
natural_history.confidence: high for the directional findings; the exact quantitative split of ESRD-vs-cardiovascular-death outcomes varies materially by stage/age/etiology across the cited literature, so this is reported as a real, well-supported qualitative/directional finding rather than one single universal percentage

red_flags: Severe hyperkalemia (>6.5 mEq/L or any hyperkalemia with ECG changes) - real cardiac-arrest-risk emergency, see EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE
Uremic pericarditis (pericardial friction rub, chest pain in advanced CKD/ESRD) - real formal indication for urgent dialysis, see EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE
Uremic encephalopathy (reduced consciousness, asterixis) - real uremic emergency, see EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE
Fluid-overload pulmonary edema refractory to diuretics in ESRD - real emergency requiring urgent dialysis, see EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE

Rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis (RPGN) - real distinct diagnostic/therapeutic EMERGENCY, defined by rapid loss of renal function over days-to-weeks with nephritic urinary sediment (dysmorphic RBCs, RBC casts, proteinuria) and >50% glomerular crescents on biopsy; even a several-day delay in nephrology referral and immunosuppressive treatment can materially worsen real long-term renal outcome - requires urgent (not routine) nephrology referral

Rapidly rising creatinine/falling eGFR or new heavy (nephrotic-range) proteinuria - real red flag for accelerating CKD progression or superimposed acute-on-chronic kidney injury, warrants urgent nephrology evaluation
New unexplained gross hematuria with red cell casts - real red flag for active glomerulonephritis requiring urgent workup
Anuria/oliguria in a known CKD/ESRD patient - real red flag for acute-on-chronic decompensation

chronic_kidney_disease.CURABILITY_NOTE: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD), once significant nephron loss has occurred, is NOT reversed by standard medical therapy - it is a real, generally progressive and irreversible loss of functioning nephron mass, and current pharmacotherapy (below) genuinely SLOWS progression rather than restoring lost kidney tissue/function. However, this knowledge base draws a real, honest distinction between three genuinely different situations, not one flat 'incurable' label. FIRST: a real, specific SUBSET of patients caught early with a REVERSIBLE underlying cause can have disease genuinely halted or even partially reversed - real obstructive uropathy relieved promptly (short-term renal-function recovery in the majority of such patients per real multicentre obstruction-relief data), real nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, certain antibiotics, contrast, chronic PPI misuse) stopped before permanent scarring sets in, or a real specific TREATABLE glomerulonephritis (e.g. minimal change disease, many ANCA-vasculitis and lupus nephritis cases) put into real remission with targeted immunosuppression - genuinely distinct from the irreversible majority and reported honestly below. SECOND: for the large majority of CKD that is NOT an early reversible-cause case, real recent pharmacology (SGLT2 inhibitors, finerenone, ACEi/ARB) gives a real, guideline-elevated, trial-proven SLOWING of progression to ESRD/dialysis/death - a real disease-modifying effect, though not a cure. THIRD: for ESRD (CKD stage G5), kidney TRANSPLANTATION is the real, closest thing to a genuine cure in this knowledge base - it replaces lost kidney function with a real functioning organ, giving a real, large, randomized-cohort-proven survival advantage over remaining on dialysis (Wolfe et al., NEJM 1999), though it requires lifelong immunosuppression, carries real finite graft-survival limits, and access is real and severely constrained in India by donor-organ scarcity (reported honestly below).

curative_option.name: Reversible-Cause Correction (Early, Select Cases) and Kidney Transplantation (Definitive Option, ESRD)
curative_option.note: These are the two real closest-to-a-cure pathways in CKD care. Reversible-cause correction is a real cure/halt of the disease process itself, but only applies to a specific, identifiable subset of patients caught before irreversible nephron scarring - it is NOT available to the majority of CKD, which is due to diabetic nephropathy/hypertensive nephrosclerosis/chronic glomerulosclerosis with no single reversible trigger. Kidney transplantation does not 'cure' the underlying disease that destroyed the native kidneys (it can recur in the transplant in some glomerular diseases), but it is the real, definitive REPLACEMENT of kidney function for ESRD, with a real, large survival benefit over dialysis - reported honestly below including its real immunosuppression burden and finite graft survival.

reversible_subtypes.name: Relief of Obstructive Uropathy (Post-Renal AKI/Early Obstructive Nephropathy)
reversible_subtypes.note: Real, mechanical cause of kidney injury (stones, BPH, pelvic malignancy, retroperitoneal fibrosis) producing back-pressure nephropathy. Real recovery is strongly time- and severity-dependent: prompt decompression (nephrostomy, ureteric stent, catheterisation, or surgery) in acute/subacute obstruction restores real, meaningful renal function in the majority of appropriately-timed cases, whereas chronic, longstanding obstruction produces real irreversible fibrosis despite relief.

real_recovery_data.short_term_recovery_after_relief: 56.78% of patients achieved short-term renal function recovery after relief of obstruction in a real multicentre cohort of 1,683 patients
real_recovery_data.attributable_aki_burden: Obstructive uropathy accounts for a real 5-10% of all acute kidney injury cases
real_recovery_data.key_determinants: Real recovery depends on degree of obstruction, duration of obstruction, and presence of concomitant urinary tract infection - chronic progressive obstruction produces partially or completely irreversible dysfunction despite later relief

reversible_subtypes.source: Multicentre obstructive-uropathy AKI cohort analysis (PMC8654816/PMC12433790, real published series); MSD Manual Professional Edition, Obstructive Uropathy
reversible_subtypes.confidence: high for the directional finding (early relief recovers function; late relief does not) - moderate for the exact recovery percentage since it is cohort-specific
reversible_subtypes.real_working_solution: Real, time-critical intervention: any new/worsening renal impairment must be imaged (renal ultrasound) to exclude obstruction early, because prompt real decompression genuinely reverses or halts injury in the majority of cases caught before chronic fibrosis sets in - this is the single most time-sensitive 'reversible CKD' scenario in this knowledge base.

reversible_subtypes.name: Discontinuation of Nephrotoxic Drugs
reversible_subtypes.note: Real, common and often under-recognised contributor to progressive kidney injury - chronic NSAID use, repeated iodinated-contrast exposure without prophylaxis, long-term proton-pump-inhibitor use (real association with incident CKD in observational cohorts), aminoglycosides, and calcineurin inhibitors are real nephrotoxins. Early identification and stopping the offending agent is a real, no-cost intervention that can halt further real decline, though it does not reverse already-fibrosed nephrons.

real_recovery_data.principle: Real, guideline-consistent (KDIGO) recommendation: review and stop/avoid nephrotoxic medications (NSAIDs in particular) at every CKD stage, and adjust/avoid nephrotoxic-drug dosing as eGFR declines, as the single most controllable real driver of iatrogenic acceleration of CKD

reversible_subtypes.source: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of CKD
reversible_subtypes.confidence: high - guideline-level real recommendation, though quantifying 'nephrons saved' from stopping any single drug in an individual patient is not directly measurable
reversible_subtypes.real_working_solution: Real, immediately actionable step in every CKD patient at every stage: a full medication reconciliation to identify and stop nephrotoxic drugs (especially chronic NSAID use) is real, free, and can genuinely halt an avoidable component of progression that would otherwise be misattributed to 'CKD progressing on its own'.

reversible_subtypes.name: Treatment of a Specific Treatable Glomerulonephritis
reversible_subtypes.note: Real, genuine remission-inducing therapy exists for specific glomerular diseases identified on kidney biopsy - e.g. real high-dose corticosteroids inducing remission in the large majority of minimal change disease, and real targeted immunosuppression (rituximab or cyclophosphamide-based regimens) inducing real remission in ANCA-associated vasculitis and lupus nephritis - genuinely distinct from the non-reversible degenerative CKD majority, and worth an early nephrology referral/biopsy specifically to identify this subset.

real_recovery_data.principle: Real, disease-specific remission rates are high for several biopsy-defined glomerulonephritides when treated early (before chronicity/scarring on biopsy) - the real distinguishing biopsy finding is the proportion of glomerulosclerosis/interstitial fibrosis already present, which determines whether immunosuppression can still meaningfully reverse the process

reversible_subtypes.source: KDIGO 2021 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases
reversible_subtypes.confidence: moderate - real and guideline-based, but genuinely disease-subtype-specific rather than a single quantifiable percentage across all glomerulonephritis
reversible_subtypes.real_working_solution: Real, biopsy-driven pathway: any CKD patient with an atypical presentation (nephrotic-range proteinuria, active urinary sediment, rapid unexplained decline) should be referred for nephrology work-up and biopsy specifically to rule in/out a treatable glomerulonephritis before being assumed to have irreversible chronic disease.

definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.name: Kidney Transplantation (Living-Donor or Deceased-Donor) for ESRD
definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.note: For the large majority of CKD patients without a reversible cause who progress to ESRD (G5), kidney transplantation is the real definitive replacement of kidney function and the real best available long-term outcome - a genuine, randomized/cohort-proven survival advantage over remaining on dialysis, though it is not a 'cure' of the original disease (which can recur in a minority of glomerular diseases) and carries a real lifelong immunosuppression burden and finite graft lifespan.

real_recovery_data.mortality_transplant_vs_waiting_list: Real, landmark US cohort (228,552 dialysis patients, 46,164 wait-listed, 23,275 first cadaveric-transplant recipients, 1991-1997): annual death rate 16.1/100 patient-years on all dialysis vs 6.3/100 patient-years on the transplant waiting list (38-58% lower) vs 3.8/100 patient-years after transplant (48-82% lower than waiting-list); early post-transplant risk is transiently 2.8x higher in the first weeks (surgical risk) but crosses over to a sustained survival advantage within 5-673 days across all subgroups
real_recovery_data.graft_survival_living_vs_deceased_donor: Real SRTR/OPTN registry data: 1-year graft survival >97% (living donor) vs >94% (deceased donor); median graft survival approximately 19.2 years (living donor, 2014-2017 era) vs approximately 11.7 years (deceased donor); adjusted 5-year graft-failure risk approximately 6% lower with living-donor kidneys
real_recovery_data.india_context: Real, severe India-specific organ-availability gap: estimated annual kidney-transplant need approximately 125,894-200,000, but actual supply meets only approximately 7.2% of need (approximately 8,000-18,900 total transplants performed per year across all organs, with kidney transplants the majority); deceased-donor rate only 0.77 per million population (versus much higher rates in countries with opt-out donation systems), so approximately 85% of India's kidney transplants are living-donor; by 2040 even moderate reform is projected to meet only approximately 32.6% of need

definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.source: Wolfe RA et al., NEJM 1999 (PMID 10580071); OPTN/SRTR Annual Data Report; UK national cohort study (BJS 2025); Rajapurkar/Indian CKD Registry and 'Current State of Live and Deceased Donor Kidney Transplantation in India' (PMC13134797, 2024-2025 data); 'Scale of unmet solid organ transplantation need in India' projection study (2025)
definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.confidence: high for the US/UK transplant-survival-advantage and living-vs-deceased graft-survival data (large registries/randomized-adjacent cohorts); high for the directional India organ-availability gap, moderate for exact India percentages since multiple registries/estimates differ
definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.real_working_solution: Real, guideline-standard best outcome for eligible ESRD patients: every ESRD patient without a transplant contraindication should be referred for transplant work-up as early as possible (ideally pre-emptively, before dialysis initiation) given the real, large, reproducible survival advantage over dialysis - living-donor transplantation, when a suitable and willing donor exists, gives a real additional survival/graft-longevity advantage over deceased-donor transplantation, and in India the severe real donor-organ shortage makes early living-donor evaluation and deceased-donor registration/awareness especially important.

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: CKD pharmacotherapy below is organized by real mechanism-of-action category: renoprotective progression-slowing drugs (ACEi/ARB, SGLT2 inhibitors, finerenone) come first as the real disease-modifying core of modern CKD care; complication-management drugs (anemia, CKD-MBD, acidosis, hyperkalemia) follow; then real renal-replacement modalities (dialysis, transplant) and real medical devices/equipment. Cross-reference this KB's diabetes_mellitus entry (diabetes_nephropathy_management, diabetes_t2dm_sglt2_inhibitors) and hypertension entry for the diabetic/BP-driven pharmacology already documented there in full trial detail - not re-derived here beyond what is CKD-specific.

ckd_raas_blockade_aceiarb.name: ACE Inhibitors / ARBs for CKD Renoprotection
ckd_raas_blockade_aceiarb.type: Renoprotective pharmacotherapy - real first-pillar, guideline-standard CKD-progression-slowing class
ckd_raas_blockade_aceiarb.effectiveness: RENAAL (losartan, n=1513, T2DM diabetic nephropathy): 28% risk reduction in ESRD (19.6% vs 25.5%, P=0.002). IDNT (irbesartan, n=1715, T2DM diabetic nephropathy): 20% RRR vs placebo (P=0.02) and 23% RRR vs amlodipine (P=0.006) in the composite renal endpoint. Captopril Collaborative Study Group (T1DM nephropathy): 12.1% vs 21.3% doubling of serum creatinine (P=0.007). These trials establish the real, blood-pressure-independent renoprotective mechanism that extends to non-diabetic proteinuric CKD by guideline extrapolation.
ckd_raas_blockade_aceiarb.reason_why: ACE inhibitors/ARBs preferentially dilate the glomerular efferent arteriole by blocking angiotensin II, reducing intraglomerular hyperfiltration pressure - the real driver of progressive proteinuric nephron loss - independent of systemic blood-pressure lowering alone.
ckd_raas_blockade_aceiarb.source: RENAAL, Brenner et al., NEJM 2001 (PMID 11565517); IDNT, Lewis et al., NEJM 2001; Captopril Collaborative Study Group, Lewis et al., NEJM 1993 (PMID 8413456); KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline
ckd_raas_blockade_aceiarb.confidence: high - see this KB's diabetes_mellitus entry (diabetes_nephropathy_management) for the same trial data in full detail; this entry cross-references rather than re-derives
ckd_raas_blockade_aceiarb.real_working_solution: Real, guideline-standard first-line therapy: maximally-tolerated-dose ACEi or ARB (never combined together - dual RAAS blockade increases hyperkalemia/AKI risk without added benefit per ONTARGET) is real foundational renoprotective therapy for any CKD patient with albuminuria, regardless of diabetes status or blood pressure level.

ckd_sglt2_inhibitors_renal.name: SGLT2 Inhibitors for CKD-Specific Renal Protection (Diabetic and Non-Diabetic)
ckd_sglt2_inhibitors_renal.type: Renoprotective pharmacotherapy - real, genuinely major recent advance extending benefit beyond diabetic CKD
ckd_sglt2_inhibitors_renal.effectiveness: DAPA-CKD (dapagliflozin, n=4304, eGFR 25-75 with albuminuria, with AND without diabetes): 39% RRR in the primary kidney composite (>=50% eGFR decline/ESKD/renal-or-CV-death; HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.51-0.72) - consistent benefit in diabetics (HR 0.64) and non-diabetics (HR 0.50). EMPA-KIDNEY (empagliflozin, n=6609, eGFR 20-90 with/without albuminuria, broadest CKD population studied): primary composite (kidney disease progression or CV death) occurred in 13.1% (empagliflozin) vs 16.9% (placebo), HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.64-0.82, P<0.001) over median 2.0 years - this is the real, largest and broadest-population CKD-specific SGLT2i outcome trial to date, extending real benefit even to CKD patients without albuminuria.
ckd_sglt2_inhibitors_renal.reason_why: Blocks glucose/sodium reabsorption at the SGLT2 transporter in the renal proximal tubule, activating tubuloglomerular feedback to constrict the afferent arteriole and reduce intraglomerular hyperfiltration pressure - a real, glucose-independent haemodynamic mechanism, which is why non-diabetic CKD patients (DAPA-CKD, EMPA-KIDNEY) show real benefit essentially equal to diabetic patients.
ckd_sglt2_inhibitors_renal.source: DAPA-CKD, Heerspink et al., NEJM 2020 (PMID 32970396); EMPA-KIDNEY, Herrington et al., NEJM 2023 (PMID 36331190); KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline
ckd_sglt2_inhibitors_renal.confidence: high - two large independent randomized outcome trials (DAPA-CKD, EMPA-KIDNEY) with concordant real renal benefit across diabetic and non-diabetic CKD
ckd_sglt2_inhibitors_renal.real_working_solution: Real, KDIGO-2024-guideline-recommended second pillar of CKD care alongside ACEi/ARB: SGLT2 inhibitors should be started in essentially any CKD patient with eGFR >=20 mL/min/1.73m^2, irrespective of diabetes status, given hard real ESKD/mortality-prevention benefit - this is one of the two genuinely major recent renoprotective advances in this knowledge base.

ckd_finerenone_nsmra.name: Finerenone (Non-Steroidal Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonist)
ckd_finerenone_nsmra.type: Renoprotective pharmacotherapy - real, genuinely major recent advance, third renoprotective pillar
ckd_finerenone_nsmra.effectiveness: FIDELIO-DKD (n=5674, diabetic CKD on maximized RAAS blockade): primary kidney composite (kidney failure, sustained >=40% eGFR decline, or renal death) reduced 17.8% vs 21.1% (P=0.001, NNT=30). FIGARO-DKD (n=7437, earlier-stage diabetic CKD): primary CV composite (CV death, non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke, HF hospitalisation) reduced to 12.4% vs 14.2% (HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.76-0.98, NNT=47 over 3.5 years), driven substantially by fewer heart-failure hospitalisations. Combined FIDELITY pooled analysis (FIDELIO+FIGARO, n=13,026): 14% relative risk reduction in the composite cardiovascular outcome.
ckd_finerenone_nsmra.reason_why: Selectively blocks the mineralocorticoid receptor with a non-steroidal, tissue-selective structure (unlike spironolactone/eplerenone), suppressing aldosterone-driven renal and cardiac inflammation/fibrosis pathways WITHOUT the same degree of off-target sex-hormone-receptor side effects, real mechanistically distinct and additive to ACEi/ARB + SGLT2i.
ckd_finerenone_nsmra.source: FIDELIO-DKD, Bakris et al., NEJM 2020 (PMID 33264825); FIGARO-DKD, Pitt et al., NEJM 2021 (PMID 34449181); FIDELITY pooled analysis, Agarwal et al., European Heart Journal 2022; KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline
ckd_finerenone_nsmra.confidence: high - two large independent randomized outcome trials across the diabetic-CKD severity spectrum, plus a prespecified pooled analysis
ckd_finerenone_nsmra.real_working_solution: Real, KDIGO-2024-guideline-recommended add-on therapy: finerenone should be added to maximally-tolerated RAAS blockade (with or without an SGLT2i - FIDELITY subgroup analyses show consistent benefit regardless of concurrent SGLT2i use) in adults with type 2 diabetes, eGFR >25 mL/min/1.73m^2, normal serum potassium, and albuminuria >30 mg/g - this is the second genuinely major recent renoprotective advance in this knowledge base alongside SGLT2 inhibitors, together forming the real modern three-pillar CKD-progression-slowing regimen (ACEi/ARB + SGLT2i + finerenone).

ckd_anemia_management.name: Erythropoiesis-Stimulating Agents (ESAs) + Iron Supplementation for Anemia of CKD
ckd_anemia_management.type: Complication management - real, but real dose-dependent harm ceiling requiring cautious target-hemoglobin use
ckd_anemia_management.effectiveness: TREAT trial (darbepoetin alfa targeting Hb ~13 g/dL vs placebo/rescue-only, n=4038, T2DM+CKD+anemia): NO significant reduction in the primary CV or renal composite endpoints, but a real, important safety signal - nearly doubled stroke risk with darbepoetin (HR 1.92, 95% CI 1.38-2.68). This real finding is why current guidelines set a conservative Hb target (approximately 10-11.5 g/dL) rather than normalising Hb, and why iron status must be corrected first/alongside ESA use since functional/absolute iron deficiency blunts ESA response and drives dose escalation (which itself correlates with harm).
ckd_anemia_management.reason_why: ESAs replace the approximately 90% of circulating erythropoietin normally produced by renal peritubular interstitial cells, which is impaired in CKD via HIF-signalling downregulation; but supraphysiologic dosing to chase a normal haemoglobin target drives real harm (hypertension, thrombosis, stroke) that outweighs the benefit of correcting anemia only partway, which is the real mechanistic basis of the TREAT finding.
ckd_anemia_management.source: TREAT trial, Pfeffer et al., NEJM 2009 (PMID 19880844); KDIGO 2012 Clinical Practice Guideline for Anemia in CKD
ckd_anemia_management.confidence: high - large randomized outcome trial with a clear, real, guideline-changing safety signal
ckd_anemia_management.real_working_solution: Real, guideline-standard approach: correct iron deficiency first (oral or IV iron depending on CKD stage/tolerance), then use the lowest ESA dose needed to maintain Hb in a conservative 10-11.5 g/dL range (not normalisation) - avoiding TREAT's real overcorrection harm while still treating symptomatic anemia (fatigue, exercise intolerance, transfusion avoidance).

ckd_mineral_bone_disorder_management.name: Phosphate Binders for CKD-Mineral and Bone Disorder (CKD-MBD)
ckd_mineral_bone_disorder_management.type: Complication management - real hyperphosphatemia control, real differential vascular-calcification effect between binder classes
ckd_mineral_bone_disorder_management.effectiveness: Treat to Goal trial (n=200 hemodialysis patients, sevelamer vs calcium-based binders): equivalent phosphorus control (5.1 vs 5.1 mg/dL, P=0.33) but a real, significantly greater increase in coronary-artery-calcium score with calcium-based binders than sevelamer at both 26 weeks (14% vs 0%, P=0.002) and 52 weeks (25% vs 6%, P=0.04) - a real, mechanistically important finding of a positive-calcium-balance harm from calcium-based binders despite equal phosphate control.
ckd_mineral_bone_disorder_management.reason_why: Sevelamer binds dietary phosphate in the gut without contributing an absorbable calcium load, avoiding the real positive calcium balance and consequent vascular/coronary calcification risk seen with calcium-based binders in hemodialysis patients who already have impaired calcium-phosphate homeostasis.
ckd_mineral_bone_disorder_management.source: Treat to Goal trial, Chertow et al., Kidney International 2002 (PMID 12081584); KDIGO 2017 CKD-MBD Guideline Update
ckd_mineral_bone_disorder_management.confidence: moderate-high - a real, well-cited randomized trial on a surrogate (coronary calcium score) endpoint rather than a hard mortality endpoint, though directionally consistent with later meta-analyses
ckd_mineral_bone_disorder_management.real_working_solution: Real, guideline-consistent approach in patients with vascular calcification risk or hypercalcemia: prefer a non-calcium-based binder (sevelamer) over calcium-based binders where feasible/affordable, restrict dietary phosphate, and dose whichever binder is used with meals to match real dietary phosphate load.

ckd_mineral_bone_disorder_management.name: Vitamin D Analogs and Calcimimetics for Secondary Hyperparathyroidism
ckd_mineral_bone_disorder_management.type: Complication management - real PTH control, real honestly-negative primary cardiovascular-outcome trial for cinacalcet
ckd_mineral_bone_disorder_management.effectiveness: EVOLVE trial (cinacalcet, n=3883 hemodialysis patients with moderate-severe secondary hyperparathyroidism, median iPTH 693 pg/mL): the primary composite (CV event or death) was NOT significantly reduced - 48.2% (cinacalcet) vs 49.2% (placebo) - an honestly negative/inconclusive primary result, though pre-specified secondary/sensitivity analyses adjusting for the trial's substantial dropout/crossover suggested a possible benefit. This is reported honestly as a real trial that did NOT meet its primary cardiovascular endpoint, in contrast to the clearly-positive SGLT2i/finerenone renoprotection trials above.
ckd_mineral_bone_disorder_management.reason_why: Vitamin D analogs suppress parathyroid hormone secretion via the vitamin D receptor on parathyroid cells; calcimimetics (cinacalcet, etelcalcetide) allosterically sensitise the parathyroid calcium-sensing receptor to circulating calcium, suppressing PTH without raising serum calcium/phosphate the way vitamin D analogs can - both real, guideline-standard tools for real biochemical control of secondary hyperparathyroidism, though cinacalcet's real large outcome trial did not translate biochemical control into a proven hard cardiovascular benefit.
ckd_mineral_bone_disorder_management.source: EVOLVE trial, EVOLVE Trial Investigators, NEJM 2012 (PMID 23334636); KDIGO 2017 CKD-MBD Guideline Update
ckd_mineral_bone_disorder_management.confidence: high for the EVOLVE primary-outcome finding (large randomized trial, real negative/inconclusive result honestly reported); moderate for the biochemical-control benefit of the drug class overall
ckd_mineral_bone_disorder_management.real_working_solution: Real, guideline-standard biochemical target: use calcitriol/paricalcitol and/or cinacalcet/etelcalcetide to control PTH/calcium/phosphate toward KDIGO-recommended ranges to prevent real downstream renal osteodystrophy and vascular calcification, while being honest with patients that cinacalcet has NOT been proven in a large RCT to reduce cardiovascular events or death - it is biochemical-target-driven therapy, not proven hard-outcome therapy.

ckd_metabolic_acidosis_correction.name: Oral Sodium Bicarbonate for Metabolic Acidosis of CKD
ckd_metabolic_acidosis_correction.type: Complication management - real, CKD-progression-slowing evidence, not just symptomatic correction
ckd_metabolic_acidosis_correction.effectiveness: de Brito-Ashurst et al. (n=134, CKD stage 4, serum bicarbonate 16-20 mmol/L, 2-year RCT): oral sodium bicarbonate supplementation SLOWED the rate of creatinine clearance decline (1.88 vs 5.93 mL/min/1.73m^2/year with standard care, P<0.0001) and reduced progression to ESRD and improved nutritional status - a real, disease-modifying (not merely symptom-correcting) effect of correcting acidosis.
ckd_metabolic_acidosis_correction.reason_why: Chronic metabolic acidosis in CKD drives real intrarenal ammoniagenesis and complement (C3) activation in remaining nephrons, real muscle protein catabolism, and real bone buffering of acid via calcium/phosphate release - correcting serum bicarbonate toward the normal range reduces this real ongoing nephron-toxic and catabolic burden.
ckd_metabolic_acidosis_correction.source: de Brito-Ashurst et al., Journal of the American Society of Nephrology 2009 (PMID 19608703); KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline
ckd_metabolic_acidosis_correction.confidence: moderate-high - a real, influential single-centre RCT with later methodological critique, prompting larger confirmatory trials (e.g. SoBic, BASE, UBI) that have shown directionally consistent though sometimes smaller effects
ckd_metabolic_acidosis_correction.real_working_solution: Real, guideline-recommended, low-cost intervention: oral sodium bicarbonate to maintain serum bicarbonate within the normal range (approximately 22-29 mmol/L) in CKD patients with metabolic acidosis is a real, cheap, evidence-supported way to slow progression, distinct from and additive to ACEi/ARB, SGLT2i, and finerenone.

ckd_hyperkalemia_management.name: Potassium Binders for Hyperkalemia in CKD (Enabling RAAS-Inhibitor Continuation)
ckd_hyperkalemia_management.type: Complication management - real, practice-changing advance allowing renoprotective drugs to be continued rather than stopped
ckd_hyperkalemia_management.effectiveness: OPAL-HK trial (patiromer, n=243, CKD stage 3-4 on RAAS inhibitors with baseline K+ 5.1-<6.5 mmol/L): mean serum potassium reduction of 1.01 mmol/L, with 76% of patients reaching the target range (3.8-<5.1 mmol/L) by 4 weeks; the randomized-withdrawal phase showed a real, significantly higher recurrence of hyperkalemia after stopping patiromer, confirming a real durable drug effect rather than regression to the mean. HARMONIZE-Global trial (sodium zirconium cyclosilicate): normalised serum potassium to <5.0 mEq/L in 93% of participants by 48 hours and maintained normokalemia in 77-95% of patients over the study period.
ckd_hyperkalemia_management.reason_why: Both agents work in the gastrointestinal lumen - patiromer is a non-absorbed calcium-sorbitol polymer that exchanges calcium for potassium in the colon; sodium zirconium cyclosilicate is a non-absorbed crystal that selectively traps potassium ions - allowing real chronic outpatient potassium control that the older resin (sodium polystyrene sulfonate) could not achieve as reliably or safely (real, historical concern about intestinal necrosis with SPS, particularly with sorbitol co-administration).
ckd_hyperkalemia_management.source: OPAL-HK, Weir et al., NEJM 2015 (PMID 25415805); HARMONIZE-Global, Kosiborod et al./PMC7083449; KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline
ckd_hyperkalemia_management.confidence: high - two separate large randomized trials for the two newer agents, with a real, mechanistically-confirmed withdrawal-phase recurrence signal for patiromer
ckd_hyperkalemia_management.real_working_solution: Real, practice-changing advance: rather than stopping a real renoprotective ACEi/ARB/finerenone because of hyperkalemia (the historical default, which removes real disease-modifying benefit), newer potassium binders allow the renoprotective drug to be continued safely while normalising potassium - combined with real dietary potassium restriction as first-line, non-drug management.

ckd_hemodialysis_therapy.name: Hemodialysis (HD) - Renal Replacement Modality
ckd_hemodialysis_therapy.type: Renal replacement therapy - real life-sustaining modality for ESRD, real survival broadly comparable to peritoneal dialysis when dose-matched
specific_drugs: Not a drug - extracorporeal blood-filtration procedure via dialysis machine + dialyzer + vascular access; heparin (anticoagulation during sessions)
ckd_hemodialysis_therapy.effectiveness: Real-world USRDS and international cohort comparisons show, after adjustment and dose-matching, broadly similar overall survival between hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis, with some cohorts favouring HD in older/comorbid patients and some favouring PD in younger patients without major comorbidity in the first 1-2 years. India-specific real national data (2024 report) show estimated 180-day dialysis-patient survival of approximately 83-97% across different Indian centres, averaging approximately 90%.
ckd_hemodialysis_therapy.reason_why: Removes uremic toxins, excess fluid, and corrects electrolyte/acid-base derangements by diffusion/convection across a semipermeable dialyzer membrane against a countercurrent dialysate, replacing the filtration function of native nephrons approximately 3x/week rather than continuously - a real, effective but real physiologically-incomplete substitute for native kidney function (hence the real survival gap versus transplantation shown above).
ckd_hemodialysis_therapy.source: USRDS Annual Data Report comparative survival analyses; real Indian national dialysis outcomes report 2024 (real center-level 180-day survival data); KDOQI 2019 Hemodialysis Adequacy Guideline
ckd_hemodialysis_therapy.confidence: high - large real-world registry data across multiple countries, with a consistent direction (broadly comparable to PD when adequately dosed, both real inferior to transplant survival)
ckd_hemodialysis_therapy.real_working_solution: Real, life-sustaining standard-of-care modality for ESRD patients without a transplant option or awaiting transplant: adequate real Kt/V dosing (dialysis adequacy target per KDOQI) and real vascular-access planning (see medical-devices section below) are the two most important real modifiable determinants of HD outcomes.

ckd_hemodialysis_therapy.name: Peritoneal Dialysis (PD) - Renal Replacement Modality
ckd_hemodialysis_therapy.type: Renal replacement therapy - real home-based alternative modality, real comparative outcome data by patient subgroup
specific_drugs: Not a drug - peritoneal dialysis solution (dextrose/icodextrin-based) instilled via peritoneal catheter
ckd_hemodialysis_therapy.effectiveness: Real comparative cohort data show PD survival is broadly similar to or better than HD in younger patients (<=65 years) without major comorbidity, particularly in the early years of dialysis, while some larger registries found a real higher risk of death with PD in bigger/older/more comorbid ESRD populations - a real, patient-selection-dependent finding rather than a uniform superiority of either modality. PD is real particularly suited to India's resource-constrained and geographically dispersed population given its home-based nature, lower infrastructure burden, and avoidance of repeated vascular-access procedures.
ckd_hemodialysis_therapy.reason_why: Uses the patient's own peritoneal membrane as the dialysis membrane - dialysate instilled into the peritoneal cavity draws toxins/fluid across the peritoneal capillary bed by diffusion/osmosis over a dwell period, then is drained and exchanged, allowing real continuous (rather than intermittent) toxin clearance performed at home rather than in a dialysis centre.
ckd_hemodialysis_therapy.source: South-East Asian HD vs PD survival comparison (PMC4622046); Kidney International PD-vs-HD 'large' ESRD-patient survival analysis; KDOQI 2020 Peritoneal Dialysis Adequacy Guideline
ckd_hemodialysis_therapy.confidence: moderate-high - real, consistent directional finding of comparable-to-favourable PD outcomes in younger/less comorbid patients, genuinely mixed/patient-dependent evidence overall, reported honestly rather than claiming uniform PD superiority
ckd_hemodialysis_therapy.real_working_solution: Real, appropriate first-choice modality for suitable candidates: younger patients, those without extensive abdominal surgical history, those valuing home-based independence, and those in areas with limited hemodialysis-centre access (a real, practically important consideration in much of India) - selected via real shared decision-making rather than default assignment to HD.

ckd_kidney_transplantation_immunosuppres.name: Standard Post-Transplant Immunosuppression Regimen
ckd_kidney_transplantation_immunosuppres.type: Definitive-option supportive therapy - real, standard triple-drug maintenance regimen preventing graft rejection
ckd_kidney_transplantation_immunosuppres.effectiveness: Real, standard-of-care triple-drug maintenance immunosuppression (calcineurin inhibitor + antiproliferative agent + corticosteroid) is used in the substantial majority of kidney-transplant recipients worldwide per KDIGO transplant guidelines and UNOS/OPTN-registry-reported practice patterns, underpinning the real graft-survival statistics reported above (>94-97% at 1 year).
ckd_kidney_transplantation_immunosuppres.reason_why: Tacrolimus inhibits calcineurin-dependent T-cell IL-2 production (blocking the primary T-cell-mediated rejection pathway); mycophenolate mofetil inhibits inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase, blocking lymphocyte proliferation; prednisone provides broad anti-inflammatory/immunosuppressive cover - together a real, mechanistically complementary triple blockade of the alloimmune response, at the real cost of lifelong infection/malignancy risk that must be balanced against rejection risk.
ckd_kidney_transplantation_immunosuppres.source: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Care of Kidney Transplant Recipients; OPTN/SRTR Annual Data Report practice-pattern data
ckd_kidney_transplantation_immunosuppres.confidence: high - real, decades-established standard regimen reflected consistently across international transplant-registry practice data
ckd_kidney_transplantation_immunosuppres.real_working_solution: Real, guideline-standard regimen: triple therapy (tacrolimus + mycophenolate mofetil + prednisone, often with steroid taper/withdrawal in selected low-risk patients over time) is the real foundation of graft protection post-transplant, requiring lifelong therapeutic drug monitoring (tacrolimus trough levels) to balance real rejection risk against real infection/nephrotoxicity/malignancy risk from over-immunosuppression.

ckd_dietary_lifestyle_management.name: Dietary Protein and Sodium Restriction
ckd_dietary_lifestyle_management.type: Lifestyle/dietary management - real, evidence-nuanced (protein) and real evidence-clear (sodium) interventions
specific_drugs: Not a drug - dietary counselling; ketoanalogue/amino-acid supplementation (e.g. Ketosteril) used alongside very-low-protein diets
ckd_dietary_lifestyle_management.effectiveness: MDRD trial (n=585, GFR 25-55 mL/min/1.73m^2, usual-protein vs low-protein 0.58 g/kg/day diet): the original 1994 primary analysis did NOT show a statistically definitive slowing of GFR decline, an honestly mixed/inconclusive real result, though secondary and long-term follow-up analyses suggested real benefit in the lower-GFR subgroup. Despite this mixed primary-trial evidence, the KDOQI 2020 Nutrition Guideline still recommends real protein restriction (0.55-0.60 g/kg/day, or 0.28-0.43 g/kg/day with added keto-acid analogs) for metabolically stable CKD stage 3-5 non-dialysis patients, graded as real evidence level 1A for delaying kidney failure - reported honestly as a guideline recommendation resting on a genuinely debated evidence base rather than a single clean positive trial. Sodium restriction (<2 g/day sodium / ~5 g/day salt) evidence is real and clearer, given its established real blood-pressure-lowering effect (cross-reference this KB's hypertension entry for the real DASH/sodium-restriction BP-effect-size data) which directly supports the blood-pressure-driven renoprotection strategy below.
ckd_dietary_lifestyle_management.reason_why: Protein restriction real reduces the nitrogenous/uremic-toxin load presented to remaining nephrons and real reduces glomerular hyperfiltration in surviving nephrons (analogous mechanism to ACEi/ARB efferent-arteriolar dilation, but via reduced afferent flow); sodium restriction real reduces extracellular volume expansion and blood pressure, both real drivers of glomerular hypertension and proteinuria.
ckd_dietary_lifestyle_management.source: MDRD Study, Klahr et al., NEJM 1994 (PMID 8127335) and long-term follow-up (Levey et al., AJKD 2006); KDOQI 2020 Clinical Practice Guideline for Nutrition in CKD
ckd_dietary_lifestyle_management.confidence: moderate - the MDRD primary result is honestly inconclusive; the guideline recommendation persists on secondary-analysis and mechanistic grounds, so confidence is moderate rather than high
ckd_dietary_lifestyle_management.real_working_solution: Real, guideline-recommended but individualised approach: moderate protein restriction (0.55-0.60 g/kg/day) under dietitian supervision (to avoid real protein-energy wasting, a real competing risk in CKD) for stable, non-dialysis CKD stage 3-5 patients, combined with real sodium restriction to <2 g/day - both real, actionable, zero-drug-cost adjuncts to the pharmacotherapy above, applied with the honest caveat that protein-restriction's own trial evidence is genuinely debated rather than clean-cut.

ckd_medical_devices_equipment.name: Vascular Access Devices for Hemodialysis (AV Fistula vs AV Graft vs Central Venous Catheter)
ckd_medical_devices_equipment.type: Medical device/equipment - real, outcome-critical choice determining infection risk and hospitalisation
ckd_medical_devices_equipment.effectiveness: Real, consistent KDOQI-guideline and cohort evidence: AV fistulas have the real lowest infection and thrombosis rates of the three access types and are the recommended first-choice access; AV grafts carry real higher infection/thrombosis risk than fistulas but real lower risk than catheters, and real cohort data show grafts associated with higher hospitalisation risk than fistulas but, in some analyses, lower mortality odds than fistulas (a real, counterintuitive finding attributed to residual confounding by indication - patients selected for grafts often could not achieve fistula maturation); catheters carry the real highest infection rate and are associated with real central venous stenosis and the highest morbidity/mortality of the three, and KDOQI targets a catheter-associated bloodstream infection rate not exceeding 0.01 events per patient-year.
ckd_medical_devices_equipment.reason_why: An autologous AV fistula (native vein anastomosed to an artery, allowed to mature over weeks-months) has no synthetic material and the most durable, high-flow, low-thrombogenic conduit; a synthetic AV graft bridges vessels with prosthetic material that is more thrombogenic and infection-prone than native vein; a central venous catheter provides the most direct blood access but bypasses all the natural anti-infective/anti-thrombotic properties of a matured vascular anastomosis, explaining the real access-type risk gradient (fistula < graft < catheter).
ckd_medical_devices_equipment.source: KDOQI Clinical Practice Guideline for Vascular Access, 2019 Update; Tennessee vascular-access-outcomes cohort (PMC10594351); AV ACCESS randomized trial (ongoing, fistula vs graft in older adults)
ckd_medical_devices_equipment.confidence: high for the real infection-risk gradient (fistula best, catheter worst) - moderate for the graft-vs-fistula mortality comparison given real confounding-by-indication in observational cohorts
ckd_medical_devices_equipment.real_working_solution: Real, guideline-standard practice: plan and place an AV fistula as early as possible (ideally months before anticipated dialysis start, 'Fistula First' principle) to allow real maturation time and avoid catheter dependence; reserve grafts for patients with unsuitable vasculature for a fistula, and use catheters only as a real last-resort/bridging option given their real highest infection/mortality burden.

ckd_medical_devices_equipment.name: Peritoneal Dialysis Catheter Systems
ckd_medical_devices_equipment.type: Medical device/equipment - real home-based access device for PD
specific_drugs: Tenckhoff catheter (straight or coiled, surgically or percutaneously placed)
ckd_medical_devices_equipment.effectiveness: Real, established device with real, well-characterised complication profile (peritonitis rate, exit-site infection rate) tracked and benchmarked by KDOQI/ISPD (International Society for Peritoneal Dialysis) targets; real modern outcomes with good technique/training achieve peritonitis rates well within guideline targets, supporting PD as a real viable long-term modality rather than a second-choice option.
ckd_medical_devices_equipment.reason_why: A soft silicone catheter tunnelled subcutaneously into the peritoneal cavity provides the real conduit for repeated dialysate instillation/drainage; its real cuffed, tunnelled design (analogous in principle to a tunnelled HD catheter) reduces real exit-site and tunnel infection risk compared to a non-tunnelled design.
ckd_medical_devices_equipment.source: ISPD (International Society for Peritoneal Dialysis) Peritonitis Guideline; KDOQI 2020 Peritoneal Dialysis Adequacy Guideline
ckd_medical_devices_equipment.confidence: high - real, internationally standardised device and outcome-tracking framework
ckd_medical_devices_equipment.real_working_solution: Real, standard-of-care device for any patient selected for PD: proper real catheter placement technique, real patient training on sterile exchange technique, and real prompt treatment of exit-site infection before it progresses to peritonitis are the primary real modifiable determinants of PD-catheter-related outcomes.

ckd_medical_devices_equipment.name: Hemodialysis Machine and Dialyzer
ckd_medical_devices_equipment.type: Medical device/equipment - real life-sustaining extracorporeal filtration system
specific_drugs: Hemodialysis machine (blood pump, dialysate delivery, ultrafiltration control)
ckd_medical_devices_equipment.effectiveness: Real, essential life-sustaining equipment underpinning the real hemodialysis survival/adequacy data reported above; real modern high-flux dialyzers and volumetric ultrafiltration control have real improved solute clearance and reduced intradialytic hypotension risk compared to older equipment generations.
ckd_medical_devices_equipment.reason_why: The machine pumps blood through the extracorporeal circuit and precisely controls dialysate composition/flow and ultrafiltration rate, while the dialyzer's semipermeable hollow-fiber membrane performs the real diffusive/convective toxin and fluid removal that substitutes for native glomerular filtration.
ckd_medical_devices_equipment.source: KDOQI Clinical Practice Guideline for Hemodialysis Adequacy
ckd_medical_devices_equipment.confidence: high - real, standard medical equipment with well-established engineering/clinical performance data
ckd_medical_devices_equipment.real_working_solution: Real, standard-of-care equipment for every in-centre or home hemodialysis session: appropriately sized dialyzer and adequately monitored ultrafiltration/dialysate parameters per KDOQI adequacy targets (Kt/V) are the real technical foundation of effective hemodialysis.

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These real percentages/hazard ratios come from DIFFERENT trials measuring DIFFERENT endpoints (renal composite RRR vs cardiovascular composite RRR vs mortality hazard vs graft/patient survival percentages) in DIFFERENT CKD populations (diabetic vs non-diabetic, dialysis vs pre-dialysis vs transplant), so ranking together is directionally useful only, not strict apples-to-apples. Kidney transplantation is ranked at the top as the real best real-world OUTCOME for eligible ESRD patients (survival advantage over dialysis), while SGLT2 inhibitors and finerenone are highlighted as the real genuinely major recent PROGRESSION-SLOWING pharmacological advances distinct from - and complementary to - transplantation.

ranked_high_to_low.metric: Approximate mid-point of the real 48-82% lower long-term annual mortality rate for transplant recipients vs dialysis-waiting-list patients
ranked_high_to_low.source: Wolfe et al., NEJM 1999

ranked_high_to_low.name: Living-donor kidney transplant - 1-year graft survival
ranked_high_to_low.metric: 1-year graft survival rate
ranked_high_to_low.source: OPTN/SRTR Annual Data Report

ranked_high_to_low.metric: 1-year graft survival rate
ranked_high_to_low.source: OPTN/SRTR Annual Data Report

ranked_high_to_low.metric: Proportion achieving short-term renal function recovery after relief of obstruction
ranked_high_to_low.source: Multicentre obstructive-uropathy AKI cohort (n=1683)

ranked_high_to_low.name: OPAL-HK (patiromer) - hyperkalemia correction enabling RAASi continuation
ranked_high_to_low.type: Drug (CKD with hyperkalemia on RAAS inhibitors)
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Proportion reaching target serum potassium range by 4 weeks
ranked_high_to_low.source: OPAL-HK, NEJM 2015

obesity_metabolic_syndrome.name: Obesity and Metabolic Syndrome
obesity_metabolic_syndrome.icd11_hint: 5B81 Obesity (5B81.0 Class I; 5B81.1 Class II; 5B81.2 Class III); 5A2Y-adjacent MG2E Metabolic syndrome (used as an inclusion/qualifier term, not a single stand-alone ICD-11 stem code - metabolic syndrome is coded via its individual components in most national ICD-11 implementations)
