ranked_high_to_low.name: Percutaneous vertebroplasty - SHAM-CONTROLLED TRIALS FOUND NO SIGNIFICANT BENEFIT over sham procedure in unselected chronic/subacute pain populations
ranked_high_to_low.type: Interventional procedure - honestly flagged negative sham-controlled finding
ranked_high_to_low.metric: No statistically significant difference vs sham procedure at 1-6 months in two 2009 NEJM RCTs; some later trials in more selected acute-severe-pain populations (e.g. VAPOUR) did show benefit. In the Kallmes/INVEST trial, proportion with a pre-defined clinically meaningful pain relief (>=30% decrease from baseline) at 1 month was 64% vertebroplasty vs 48% sham -- a trend, NOT statistically significant (p=0.06), consistent with the trial's null primary-outcome finding.
ranked_high_to_low.source: Buchbinder R et al, NEJM 2009; Kallmes DF et al, NEJM 2009 (INVEST, PMID 19657122); contrast: Clark W et al, Lancet 2016 (VAPOUR)

viral_hepatitis.name: Viral Hepatitis (Hepatitis A-E), with focus on Chronic Hepatitis B and Chronic Hepatitis C
viral_hepatitis.icd11_hint: 1E50-1E51 range: 1E50.0 Acute hepatitis A, 1E50.1 Acute hepatitis B, 1E51.0 Chronic hepatitis B, 1E51.1 Chronic hepatitis C, 1E50.2 Acute hepatitis C, 1E50.3 Acute hepatitis D (as HBV coinfection/superinfection), 1E50.4 Acute hepatitis E; DB99.8/DB90-DB99 range covers cirrhosis and its complications (cross-referenced, not duplicated here). This entry's SCOPE is symptoms/clinical/diagnostic framework only - antivirals/DAAs/curability are added by a separate treatment-focused pass.
viral_hepatitis.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE: THREE real, distinct viral-hepatitis-related EMERGENCIES must bypass the normal doctor-approval-queue flow and trigger immediate real-world emergency-service guidance (call ambulance/go to ER now): (1) ACUTE LIVER FAILURE / FULMINANT HEPATITIS - defined as the development of hepatic encephalopathy AND coagulopathy (INR >1.5) within 26 weeks of illness onset in a patient with no pre-existing liver disease. Real mortality without liver transplantation is 30-50%, and was historically as high as 80-85% before transplantation became standard of care; 1-year post-transplant survival is now 74% (Europe) to 92% (US) with modern intensive/transplant care. Viral hepatitis (worldwide, especially hepatitis B and hepatitis E) and acetaminophen/drug-induced liver injury (dominant cause in the US, accounting for close to half of US ALF cases) are the two leading real causes. Any jaundiced patient developing altered mentation, asterixis, or unexplained bruising/bleeding needs emergency hepatology/ICU care, not the routine doctor-approval workflow. Source: AASLD 'Defining and Managing Acute Liver Failure' (Liver Fellow Network core series); StatPearls 'Acute Liver Failure' NBK482374; PMC 'Acute liver failure in adults' review (PMC6812954). (2) HEPATITIS E IN PREGNANCY - a real, distinctively dangerous exception among the hepatitis viruses: HEV infection (especially genotypes 1/2, endemic to South/South-East Asia including India) in pregnant women, particularly in the 2nd-3rd trimester, carries a real markedly elevated risk of fulminant hepatic failure. Pooled case-fatality in pregnant women with acute HEV is approximately 20% overall (systematic review/meta-analysis), rising to a reported ~30% in the third trimester in some cohort studies, and the case-fatality rate specifically among those who progress to fulminant hepatic failure is reported as high as ~56-61%. This is a real, India/developing-world-relevant obstetric-hepatology emergency requiring immediate high-risk obstetric + hepatology referral. Source: Cambridge 'Case-fatality risk of pregnant women with acute viral hepatitis type E: a systematic review and meta-analysis', Epidemiology & Infection; PMC10961495 'Menace of hepatitis E in pregnancy: unleashing the threat of fulminant liver failure'. (3) DECOMPENSATED CIRRHOSIS COMPLICATIONS in a known chronic HBV/HCV patient - new-onset ascites, jaundice with coagulopathy, hepatic encephalopathy, or hematemesis/melena from variceal bleeding are real acute decompensation events requiring emergency care; variceal hemorrhage in particular carries a real high short-term mortality if not managed emergently (endoscopic banding/vasoactive drugs/ICU). This entry only flags these signs briefly and cross-references them - detailed cirrhosis/portal-hypertension management belongs to a dedicated future cirrhosis-specific KB entry. Source: AASLD Practice Guidance on cirrhosis-related complications (standard hepatology teaching, cross-referenced not exhaustively re-derived here).

hepatitis_a.transmission: Fecal-oral route (contaminated food/water, person-to-person in poor-sanitation settings).
hepatitis_a.course: Real actual acute, self-limited illness in the vast majority of cases; NO chronic carrier state exists for HAV.
hepatitis_a.note: Covered here briefly for contrast with B/C, which are this entry's primary focus.
hepatitis_a.source: WHO Hepatitis A fact sheet; CDC Pink Book Chapter on Hepatitis A.

hepatitis_b.transmission: Bloodborne, sexual contact, and perinatal (mother-to-child at birth/delivery); also unsafe injections, needlestick exposure, tattooing/piercing with unsterile equipment.
hepatitis_b.course: Can become chronic. Chronicity risk is strongly age-dependent: approximately 90% of infants infected perinatally develop chronic infection, approximately 30% of children infected between ages 1-5 years develop chronic infection, but less than 5% of immunocompetent adults infected develop chronic infection (~95% of adults clear the acute infection spontaneously). This inverse relationship between age-at-infection and chronicity risk is a real, clinically important point driving the WHO/national emphasis on birth-dose HBV vaccination.
hepatitis_b.source: CDC 'Clinical Overview of Hepatitis B' and 'Clinical Overview of Perinatal Hepatitis B'; WHO Hepatitis B fact sheet (2024 update).

hepatitis_c.transmission: Bloodborne - reuse/inadequate sterilization of medical equipment (needles/syringes), transfusion of unscreened blood products (historically), and injecting drug use via shared injection equipment; mother-to-child and sexual transmission occur but are less common.
hepatitis_c.course: High chronicity rate: approximately 30% (range 15-45%) of acutely infected persons spontaneously clear HCV within 6 months of infection; the remaining approximately 70% (range 55-85%) develop chronic HCV infection.
hepatitis_c.source: WHO Hepatitis C fact sheet (2024 update).

hepatitis_d.mechanism: HDV is a defective (satellite) RNA virus that cannot complete its replication/assembly cycle without HBV surface antigen (HBsAg) - it absolutely requires simultaneous or pre-existing HBV infection to propagate. Two distinct clinical patterns exist: (1) HBV-HDV COINFECTION (simultaneous acquisition in an HBV-naive person) - this most often results in clearance of both viruses, similar to acute HBV alone, though it can occasionally cause more severe acute hepatitis. (2) HDV SUPERINFECTION of an existing chronic HBV carrier - this is the clinically important pattern: it causes accelerated, more severe liver disease and progresses to chronic HDV infection in a real, high 70-90% of cases, with faster progression to cirrhosis than HBV monoinfection.
hepatitis_d.source: Negro F, 'Hepatitis D Virus Coinfection and Superinfection', Cold Spring Harb Perspect Med 2014 (PMC4208707); WHO Hepatitis D fact sheet.

hepatitis_e.transmission: Fecal-oral route (contaminated water supply, especially genotypes 1 and 2 endemic to South/South-East Asia including India).
hepatitis_e.course: Usually self-limited/acute in the general population, similar to hepatitis A, with no chronic carrier state in immunocompetent hosts (chronic HEV is described only in immunosuppressed/transplant patients with genotype 3, a separate, less common scenario). CRITICAL EXCEPTION: real markedly increased mortality in pregnant women, especially 2nd/3rd trimester - see EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE above. This is a real important India/developing-world-relevant point given recurrent HEV outbreaks linked to contaminated water supplies.
hepatitis_e.source: Cambridge Epidemiology & Infection systematic review/meta-analysis on HEV pregnancy case-fatality; WHO Hepatitis E fact sheet.

chronic_hepatitis_b_natural_history.phase_framework: AASLD's current phase framework for chronic HBV describes distinct phases defined by HBeAg status, HBV DNA level, and ALT (using sex-specific ALT upper-limit-of-normal thresholds, <35 U/L male / <25 U/L female): (1) IMMUNE-TOLERANT phase - HBeAg-positive, HBV DNA very high (>10^7 IU/mL), ALT normal; high viral replication but minimal liver inflammation/damage, most common after perinatal infection in young patients. (2) IMMUNE-ACTIVE (HBeAg-positive) phase - HBeAg-positive, ALT >2x ULN, HBV DNA >20,000 IU/mL; active immune-mediated liver injury. (3) INACTIVE CARRIER phase - HBeAg-negative/anti-HBe-positive, low/undetectable HBV DNA, normal ALT; follows HBeAg seroconversion, generally low risk of progression while it persists. (4) HBeAg-NEGATIVE IMMUNE-ACTIVE (reactivation) phase - HBeAg-negative but HBV DNA and ALT rise again due to pre-core/core-promoter viral mutants; can occur after years in the inactive-carrier phase and carries ongoing fibrosis-progression risk. An 'indeterminate' phase is also recognized for patients whose values do not cleanly fit these thresholds. Transition between phases (especially immune-tolerant to immune-active) is usually asymptomatic, so patients not on antiviral therapy need regular monitoring rather than one-off testing.
chronic_hepatitis_b_natural_history.source: AASLD/IDSA Practice Guideline on treatment of chronic hepatitis B (2025 update, journals.lww.com/hep); American College of Gastroenterology summary 'Redefining chronic hepatitis B: 2025 AASLD/IDSA Clinical Guideline'.
chronic_hepatitis_b_natural_history.seroconversion_significance: HBeAg-to-anti-HBe seroconversion (loss of HBeAg, gain of anti-HBe) generally marks transition from the high-replication immune-active phase toward the lower-risk inactive-carrier phase and is associated with improved long-term outcomes, though HBeAg-negative reactivation can still occur later via precore/core-promoter mutants. HBsAg loss (functional cure) is the most favorable endpoint and is rare spontaneously.
chronic_hepatitis_b_natural_history.progression_to_cirrhosis_hcc: Real annual HCC incidence in UNTREATED chronic HBV is approximately 0.3-0.6% per year in non-cirrhotic patients versus approximately 2.2-3.7% per year in patients who already have compensated cirrhosis - roughly a 4-10 fold higher annual risk once cirrhosis is present. Even with modern nucleos(t)ide analogue antiviral treatment, annual HCC incidence remains 0.01-1.4% (non-cirrhotic) versus 0.9-5.4% (cirrhotic). Patients with HBV-related cirrhosis carry an approximately 31-fold increased HCC risk and 44-fold increased mortality compared with non-cirrhotic chronic HBV patients.
chronic_hepatitis_b_natural_history.source_2: Journal of Hepatology, 'Risk of hepatocellular carcinoma in chronic hepatitis B: Assessment and modification with current antiviral therapy' (S0168-8278(15)00004-5); PMC4167336 systematic review/meta-analysis on HBV-related HCC risk.

chronic_hepatitis_c_natural_history.chronicity_and_progression: Approximately 55-85% (commonly cited as ~70%) of acutely HCV-infected persons progress to chronic infection if untreated (see virology_and_classification.hepatitis_c above for the exact WHO figures). Among those who remain chronically infected, the risk of progressing to cirrhosis is approximately 15-30% within 20 years, though this is highly variable and influenced by cofactors (alcohol use, HIV coinfection, male sex, older age at infection, metabolic syndrome/fatty liver).
chronic_hepatitis_c_natural_history.extrahepatic_manifestations: Chronic HCV is a real systemic disease, not purely hepatic. The most frequent and best-characterized extrahepatic manifestation is MIXED CRYOGLOBULINEMIA - a systemic small/medium-vessel vasculitis. Mechanism: chronic HCV antigenemia drives persistent B-cell stimulation and formation of immune complexes containing HCV RNA, IgG, rheumatoid factor, and complement; these cryoglobulin immune complexes precipitate at temperatures below 37C, deposit in capillary/venule/arteriole walls, and trigger endothelial activation and vascular inflammation, producing the classic triad of purpura, arthralgia, and weakness, and can cause glomerulonephritis (HCV-associated membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis) in more severe cases.
chronic_hepatitis_c_natural_history.source: WHO Hepatitis C fact sheet (2024 update) for chronicity/cirrhosis figures; Kidney International 'Hepatitis C virus-induced cryoglobulinemia' and PMC4819925 'Hepatitis C virus as a systemic disease: reaching beyond the liver' for the cryoglobulinemia mechanism.

hepatitis_b_serology_interpretation.markers: HBsAg (hepatitis B surface antigen), anti-HBs (surface antibody), HBeAg (e antigen, marker of active viral replication), anti-HBe, anti-HBc IgM (core antibody, IgM subtype), anti-HBc IgG (total/IgG core antibody).
hepatitis_b_serology_interpretation.interpretation_logic: SUSCEPTIBLE (never infected, unvaccinated): all markers negative. IMMUNE from VACCINATION: anti-HBs positive, HBsAg negative, anti-HBc negative. IMMUNE from NATURAL (past) INFECTION/RESOLVED: anti-HBs positive AND anti-HBc (IgG) positive, HBsAg negative. ACUTE INFECTION: HBsAg positive, IgM anti-HBc positive (this IgM is the earliest antibody and the specific marker distinguishing acute/recent infection - within roughly the first 6 months), anti-HBs negative. CHRONIC INFECTION: HBsAg positive for 6 months or longer, anti-HBc IgG positive, IgM anti-HBc negative (or low), anti-HBs negative. HBeAg positive versus anti-HBe positive within a chronic-infection pattern further distinguishes high-replication versus lower-replication states (see chronic_hepatitis_b_natural_history above) rather than acute-vs-chronic status itself.
hepatitis_b_serology_interpretation.source: CDC 'Screening and Testing for Hepatitis B Virus Infection: CDC Recommendations - United States, 2023', MMWR RR7201a1; WHO SEARO training module 'Testing and serological markers of hepatitis B virus'.

hepatitis_c_testing_algorithm.logic: A mandatory TWO-STEP algorithm: Step 1 - HCV antibody (anti-HCV) screening test. A negative anti-HCV result generally rules out infection (except in early window-period or immunocompromised patients). Step 2 - any REACTIVE/positive anti-HCV result must be confirmed with HCV RNA (nucleic acid) testing, because a positive antibody alone cannot distinguish current (viremic) infection from a past, spontaneously-cleared or successfully-treated infection (anti-HCV remains positive for life in most people regardless of current viral status). HCV RNA positive = current active infection; HCV RNA negative with a positive antibody = past, resolved infection (spontaneous clearance or prior cure). CDC and AASLD-IDSA specifically recommend REFLEX RNA testing (automatic RNA testing on the same specimen when antibody is reactive, without requiring a second patient visit) to prevent loss to follow-up.
hepatitis_c_testing_algorithm.source: CDC/AASLD-IDSA HCV testing guidance summarized at hcvguidelines.org; APHL 'HCV Reflex Testing Optimization Guide'; AASLD-IDSA 'Hepatitis C guidance: recommendations for testing, managing, and treating adults infected with hepatitis C virus', Hepatology 2015 (updated periodically).

diagnostic_framework.liver_function_tests: ALT and AST elevations reflect hepatocellular injury/inflammation; in most viral hepatitis, ALT is typically higher than or comparable to AST (a ratio that tends to reverse - AST > ALT - once advanced fibrosis/cirrhosis or alcohol-related injury supervenes). ALT/AST levels correlate with degree of active hepatocyte injury but do NOT reliably predict fibrosis stage - a patient with normal ALT can still have significant underlying fibrosis, which is why dedicated fibrosis staging (below) is required rather than relying on transaminases alone.
diagnostic_framework.fibrosis_staging: Current real-world practice increasingly favors NON-INVASIVE fibrosis staging as the first-line approach - principally transient elastography (FibroScan), which measures liver stiffness via shear-wave velocity and correlates with fibrosis stage (reported AUROCs around 0.79 for significant fibrosis, 0.91 for advanced fibrosis, and 0.97 for cirrhosis), often combined with serum fibrosis marker panels (e.g., FibroTest, APRI, FIB-4) for higher diagnostic confidence. LIVER BIOPSY remains the formal reference/gold standard for fibrosis staging and is still used when non-invasive results are indeterminate, discordant, or when a concurrent diagnosis (e.g., autoimmune or metabolic liver disease) must be excluded, but it is invasive with real procedural risk, so non-invasive testing has become the dominant first-line real-world practice.
diagnostic_framework.source: PMC 'Performance of Transient Elastography for the Staging of Liver Fibrosis: A Meta-Analysis', Gastroenterology; PMC4684863 'Factors That Could Impact on Liver Fibrosis Staging by Transient Elastography'.

classic_symptoms.chronic_infection_often_asymptomatic: A real, clinically critical point (similar to other 'silent' diseases already in this KB such as hypertension and early CKD): the great majority of people with chronic HBV or chronic HCV infection are ASYMPTOMATIC for years to decades, with disease often discovered incidentally on routine bloodwork/screening or only presenting once advanced fibrosis, cirrhosis, or hepatocellular carcinoma has already developed. This is precisely why risk-factor-based and, in high-endemicity settings, universal screening strategies matter (see real_risk_factors and epidemiology below) - waiting for symptoms misses most treatable early-stage disease.

acute_hepatitis_presentation.symptoms: Jaundice (yellowing of skin/sclera), fatigue/malaise, right-upper-quadrant abdominal pain/discomfort (liver capsule stretch over an inflamed, enlarged liver), nausea/vomiting/anorexia, dark urine, and pale (clay-colored) stools; low-grade fever and arthralgia can precede jaundice in a short prodromal phase.
acute_hepatitis_presentation.mechanism: Jaundice, dark urine, and pale stools all result from the same underlying process: hepatocyte injury and intrahepatic cholestasis impair the liver's ability to conjugate and excrete bilirubin normally into bile. Conjugated (direct) bilirubin backs up into the bloodstream, depositing in skin/sclera (jaundice) and being filtered by the kidneys into urine (dark, tea-colored urine), while reduced bilirubin delivery into the gut reduces stercobilin formation, producing pale/clay-colored stools.
acute_hepatitis_presentation.source: Standard hepatology teaching on bilirubin metabolism in hepatocellular/cholestatic injury; consistent across AASLD and WHO clinical hepatitis materials.

classic_symptoms.decompensated_cirrhosis_brief: In advanced chronic HBV/HCV that has progressed to cirrhosis, decompensation presents with: ASCITES (fluid accumulation from portal hypertension plus low oncotic pressure from reduced hepatic albumin synthesis), JAUNDICE (failing hepatic bilirubin clearance), HEPATIC ENCEPHALOPATHY (altered mentation/asterixis from failure to clear gut-derived neurotoxins, principally ammonia, due to both reduced hepatocyte function and portosystemic shunting), and VARICEAL BLEEDING (hematemesis/melena from ruptured esophagogastric varices formed by portal hypertension). This is covered briefly here as a cross-reference; a dedicated cirrhosis/portal-hypertension KB entry will detail management separately - the immediate action for any of these signs is emergency referral (see EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE).
classic_symptoms.source: Standard AASLD cirrhosis-complications teaching; StatPearls 'Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure' NBK499902 for encephalopathy/decompensation framework.

acute_liver_failure.definition: Development of coagulopathy (INR greater than 1.5) together with hepatic encephalopathy of any grade, occurring within 26 weeks of illness onset, in a patient with no pre-existing chronic liver disease.
acute_liver_failure.mortality: Untreated/without transplant, real mortality is 30-50%; historically (pre-modern transplant era) mortality was as high as 80-85%. With current intensive care and liver transplantation access, 1-year post-transplant survival is 74% in Europe and up to 92% in the United States; roughly 30% of ALF patients undergo liver transplantation.
acute_liver_failure.most_common_causes: In the United States, acetaminophen (paracetamol) toxicity is the single most common cause, accounting for close to half of all ALF cases; viral hepatitis (worldwide, hepatitis B is the most common viral cause of ALF, and hepatitis E is a major cause in endemic regions/pregnancy) is far more dominant as a cause of ALF in developing countries than in the US, where its relative contribution has been declining.
acute_liver_failure.source: AASLD 'Defining and Managing Acute Liver Failure'; StatPearls 'Acute Liver Failure' NBK482374; PMC6812954 'Acute liver failure in adults'.

real_risk_factors.iv_drug_use: A major real driver of HCV transmission in many countries (including the US and parts of Europe) via shared/reused injection equipment.
real_risk_factors.unsafe_blood_transfusion_historical: Historically a major HBV/HCV transmission route in India before blood-screening mandates matured: HBV screening of donated blood in India began in 1975, HIV screening became mandatory in 1988, and HCV screening was made mandatory only in 2001 - meaning transfusions before 2001 in India carried a real, meaningfully higher risk of undetected HCV transmission. Current NBTC/NACO 2017 guidelines mandate high-sensitivity screening of every blood unit for HIV, HBV, HCV, syphilis, and malaria, and nucleic acid testing (NAT) is increasingly used to close the residual serologic-window-period gap (a 15-year Indian retrospective study found NAT detected several hundred additional transfusion-transmissible-infection cases missed by serology alone, the majority being HBV).
real_risk_factors.source_transfusion: Cureus 'Added Value of Nucleic Acid Testing in Blood Banks: A 15-Year Retrospective Study from India' (PMC12776245); NACO National Blood Transfusion Council guidance.
real_risk_factors.perinatal_transmission: The dominant real HBV transmission route in HBV-endemic regions (parts of Asia and Africa) - mother-to-child transmission at birth/delivery, carrying the highest chronicity risk of any transmission route (~90%, see virology_and_classification.hepatitis_b above), which is why WHO recommends a birth-dose HBV vaccine within 24 hours of birth in endemic settings.
real_risk_factors.sexual_transmission: A real route for both HBV (more efficiently transmitted sexually than HCV) and, less commonly, HCV, particularly among men who have sex with men and in the context of HIV coinfection.
real_risk_factors.healthcare_worker_needlestick: A real recognized occupational exposure route for both HBV and HCV; post-exposure risk and management protocols differ by virus (HBV has effective post-exposure immunoglobulin/vaccine prophylaxis; HCV does not have a vaccine or immunoglobulin prophylaxis, so post-exposure follow-up relies on serial RNA/antibody testing).
real_risk_factors.source: CDC Clinical Overview of Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C; CDC 'Guidelines for Health Care Personnel Exposed to Hepatitis C Virus'.

epidemiology.global_hbv: WHO estimates 240 million people were living with chronic HBV infection in 2024, with 0.9 million new infections per year and 1.1 million deaths in 2024 (mostly from cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma). Regional distribution: Western Pacific 102 million, African Region 64 million, South-East Asia 43 million, Eastern Mediterranean 16 million, European Region 9.7 million, Americas 5 million chronically infected. Less than 5% of those with chronic HBV were receiving treatment in 2024 despite roughly half being treatment-eligible under WHO 2024 guidelines.
epidemiology.global_hcv: WHO estimates 47 million people have chronic HCV infection globally, with about 0.9 million new infections per year and approximately 239,000 deaths in 2024 (mostly cirrhosis/HCC). Of those ever infected, 24 million (36%) have been diagnosed and 13 million (20% of diagnosed) have received direct-acting antiviral treatment as of 2024, leaving 11 million diagnosed but still awaiting treatment.
epidemiology.combined_burden: Updated WHO estimates put 287 million people living with chronic HBV or HCV infection combined in 2024; together they caused an estimated 1.3 million deaths in 2024.
epidemiology.india_hbv: India sits in the WHO intermediate-to-high HBV endemicity zone. National MOHFW-observed HBsAg seroprevalence was reported at 0.95% in 2021 (National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme factsheet), while regional/community studies report a wider range (commonly cited older estimates of 3-4.2% HBsAg positivity with an estimated ~40 million HBV carriers nationally); tribal/PVTG serosurveys in specific states have found notably higher rates (e.g., 1.79-2.94% across age groups in one Odisha ICMR-linked tribal serosurvey), indicating real substantial regional heterogeneity within India.
epidemiology.india_hcv: India's general-population anti-HCV seroprevalence is estimated at approximately 0.4-1.0% (community-based pooled estimate ~0.85%), with blood-donor seroprevalence around 0.44% and pregnant-women seroprevalence around 0.88% in pooled meta-analytic estimates; India's National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme (NVHCP, MOHFW) factsheet is the national reference source used alongside the NCDC-ICMR-IIPS NFHS-4-linked serosurvey.
epidemiology.source: WHO Hepatitis B fact sheet and Hepatitis C fact sheet (2024 updates); India NVHCP/MOHFW 'Seroprevalence of Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C' factsheet (nvhcp.mohfw.gov.in); PubMed 'Burden of hepatitis C virus infection in India: A systematic review and meta-analysis' (30176181).

natural_history_and_prognosis.hcc_risk_summary: Chronic HBV and chronic HCV are among the leading global causes of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) because both viruses drive decades of chronic hepatic inflammation, fibrogenesis, and (for HBV specifically) direct viral genome integration into host hepatocyte DNA - a real, distinct oncogenic mechanism not shared by HCV, which is thought to drive carcinogenesis mainly indirectly through chronic inflammation/cirrhosis. Cirrhosis is the dominant final common pathway to HCC in both infections: annual HCC incidence rises roughly 4-10 fold once cirrhosis is established (HBV: ~0.3-0.6%/year non-cirrhotic vs ~2.2-3.7%/year cirrhotic, untreated; HCV: cirrhotic patients show ~1-4%/year HCC incidence). WHO explicitly attributes the majority of the 1.1 million (HBV) and 239,000 (HCV) annual deaths in 2024 to cirrhosis and HCC, underscoring why chronic viral hepatitis is considered one of the world's leading preventable causes of liver cancer.
natural_history_and_prognosis.source: Journal of Hepatology HBV-HCC risk-modification review; WHO Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C fact sheets (2024); PMC2228256 'Effect of hepatitis C and B virus infection on risk of hepatocellular carcinoma: a prospective study'.

red_flags: Jaundice with signs of coagulopathy (easy bruising, prolonged bleeding, INR elevation) plus any altered mental status - possible fulminant hepatic failure, a medical emergency (see EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE).

Any hepatitis E infection (or unexplained acute hepatitis in an area with HEV circulation) in a pregnant woman, especially 2nd/3rd trimester - real substantially elevated mortality risk, requires urgent joint obstetric-hepatology management.

New-onset ascites, jaundice, encephalopathy (confusion, asterixis), or gastrointestinal bleeding (hematemesis/melena) in a patient with known or suspected chronic HBV/HCV - signs of decompensated cirrhosis, needs urgent hepatology/emergency evaluation.

Rapidly rising ALT/AST with worsening jaundice and synthetic dysfunction (rising INR, falling albumin) in any acute hepatitis presentation - possible evolving acute liver failure, needs same-day medical evaluation rather than routine follow-up.

Known chronic HBV/HCV with new unexplained weight loss, right-upper-quadrant mass, or rapidly rising alpha-fetoprotein - possible hepatocellular carcinoma, needs urgent imaging/oncology-hepatology referral.
symptoms.red_flags_source: AASLD 'Defining and Managing Acute Liver Failure'; Cambridge Epidemiology & Infection HEV-pregnancy meta-analysis; standard AASLD cirrhosis-decompensation and HCC-surveillance teaching, cross-referenced from the sources cited throughout this entry.

viral_hepatitis.CURABILITY_NOTE: Viral hepatitis is reported here as FOUR honestly distinct real curability pictures, not one blended number -- exactly as this knowledge base has done for TB (DS vs MDR/XDR) and pneumonia (CAP vs HAP/VAP). FIRST, Chronic Hepatitis C is one of the single most dramatic real cure stories in this entire knowledge base: modern pangenotypic direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) achieve real sustained virologic response (SVR12, i.e. genuine virologic CURE) in >=95% of patients -- 99.0% (95% CI 97.9-99.6%) with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir in the pivotal ASTRAL-1 trial, 98% with glecaprevir/pibrentasvir across genotypes 1-6 -- after just 8-12 weeks of oral therapy, a real, practice-transforming advance over the historical pegylated-interferon+ribavirin era (overall SVR only ~54-56%, genotype 1 SVR only ~42-46%, 24-48 weeks of therapy, real major side-effect burden). SECOND, Chronic Hepatitis B is honestly the OPPOSITE picture: current standard nucleos(t)ide-analog therapy (tenofovir, entecavir) achieves real excellent HBV DNA viral SUPPRESSION (>95% of adherent patients) but essentially does NOT cure the infection -- real functional cure (HBsAg loss) occurs in only 0-3% of patients on NA monotherapy, because HBV persists as covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA) integrated in hepatocyte nuclei that no currently approved drug eliminates. Pegylated interferon offers a real finite-duration alternative with a real, still-modest 5-year sustained HBsAg-clearance rate of only ~13.0% in the best real-world data. This file reports HBV antivirals as real, guideline-standard, complication-reducing SUPPRESSIVE therapy, not a cure, and does not overstate it. THIRD, Hepatitis D (which requires HBV co-infection) has a real, genuinely new approved option -- bulevirtide, FDA-approved May 2026 (first-ever approved HDV-specific drug, accelerated approval, boxed warning for withdrawal flares) -- achieving a real week-48 combined virologic/biochemical response of 45-48% versus 2% with delayed treatment, with response deepening over time (undetectable HDV RNA rising from 20% at week 48 to 50% at week 144); this is real, honestly-reported partial-response data for a historically very-hard-to-treat virus, not a reliable single-course cure like HCV DAAs. FOURTH, Hepatitis A and (in immunocompetent hosts) Hepatitis E are real, typically self-limited acute illnesses that resolve with supportive care alone and require no antiviral cure at all -- the real 'cure' here is the body's own immune clearance, with real vaccination (Hepatitis A and B) being the dominant, highly effective real preventive 'solution' rather than a treatment.

curative_option.name: Direct-Acting Antiviral (DAA) Therapy for Chronic Hepatitis C -- an 8-12 Week Oral Regimen Achieving a Real Virologic CURE in the Large Majority of Patients
curative_option.note: Sustained virologic response at 12 weeks post-treatment (SVR12) with modern pangenotypic DAAs is treated by AASLD-IDSA and WHO guidance as a real, durable virologic CURE -- relapse after a confirmed SVR12 is rare (well under 1% in registration-trial long-term follow-up), and SVR is associated with real reductions in liver-related mortality, hepatocellular carcinoma incidence, and all-cause mortality. This is reported here, as with TB's BPaL/BPaLM revolution, as a real, genuine, practice-transforming cure pathway -- contrasted honestly below with the real, much harder, lower-cure-rate historical pegylated-interferon+ribavirin era it replaced.

real_survival_data.Sofosbuvir_velpatasvir_ASTRAL1_SVR12_GT1: 99.0% (95% CI 97.9-99.6%), 12 weeks, no ribavirin -- statistically superior to the prespecified 85% performance goal
real_survival_data.Sofosbuvir_velpatasvir_ASTRAL3_GT3_SVR12: 91% (12 weeks, genotype 3 -- the historically hardest-to-cure genotype for this regimen)
real_survival_data.durability: Relapse after a confirmed SVR12 with modern DAAs is rare (well under 1% in long-term registration-trial follow-up) -- SVR12 is treated as a real virologic cure, not a temporary remission

curative_option.source: Feld JJ et al (ASTRAL-1), N Engl J Med 2015;373:2599-2607; Foster GR et al (ASTRAL-2/3), N Engl J Med 2015;373:2608-2617; Zeuzem S et al (ENDURANCE-1) and integrated glecaprevir/pibrentasvir analyses, J Hepatol 2018; Afdhal N et al (ION-1), N Engl J Med 2014;370:1889-98; Kowdley KV et al (ION-3), N Engl J Med 2014;370:1879-88; AASLD-IDSA HCV Guidance (hcvguidelines.org); WHO Guidelines for the care and treatment of persons diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C virus infection (2022).

alternative.name: Historical Pegylated Interferon alfa-2a/alfa-2b + Ribavirin -- a Real, Genuine but Honestly Much Harder-Won Cure, 24-48 Weeks
alternative.note: Before DAAs, this was the real standard of care for chronic HCV -- a real cure was still possible (SVR is durable with this regimen too), but at a substantially lower success rate, a much longer duration, and a real, severe side-effect burden (flu-like symptoms in the large majority, cytopenias, real depression/neuropsychiatric risk, autoimmune flares, contraindicated in decompensated cirrhosis and many comorbid patients) that excluded a real, large fraction of patients from treatment altogether. This is reported here, as with TB's older 18-24-month injectable MDR-TB regimens, to show honestly how dramatic the DAA advance was rather than presenting HCV cure as always having been this easy.

real_survival_data.Peginterferon_alfa2a_ribavirin_overall_S: ~54-56% overall (Fried MW et al, N Engl J Med 2002;347:975-982)
real_survival_data.Genotype_1_SVR_historical: ~42-50% (the hardest-to-treat genotype in the interferon era)
real_survival_data.Genotype_2_3_SVR_historical: ~76-82% (relatively better in the interferon era, still with the full side-effect burden and 24-48 week duration)

alternative.source: Fried MW et al, N Engl J Med 2002;347:975-982; Manns MP et al, Lancet 2001;358:958-965; McHutchison JG et al (ribavirin-addition data), N Engl J Med.

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Covers the real pangenotypic and genotype-specific Hepatitis C DAA revolution (SVR12 >=95% in the large majority) contrasted honestly with the real historical interferon-based era; the real, honestly SUPPRESSIVE-not-curative Hepatitis B nucleos(t)ide-analog and pegylated-interferon landscape with real AASLD treatment-initiation criteria; real, honestly early-phase HBV functional-cure research; the real newly FDA-approved (May 2026) Hepatitis D drug bulevirtide contrasted with older interferon-based HDV therapy; real supportive-care-only management of typical Hepatitis A/E plus real severe/chronic-case management; the real Hepatitis A/B vaccination and perinatal HBV transmission-prevention public-health success stories; real liver transplantation survival data including the real, genuinely positive advance of treating HCV around transplant with DAAs; and a brief cross-reference to liver biopsy/FibroScan diagnostic equipment (detailed in the symptoms section above, not duplicated here). Every drug class below carries the real specific drug name(s) actually used.

hepatitis_c_daa_pangenotypic_regimens.name: Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir (NS5B Polymerase Inhibitor + NS5A Inhibitor, Fixed-Dose Combination)
hepatitis_c_daa_pangenotypic_regimens.type: Oral pangenotypic direct-acting antiviral combination (curative regimen, 12 weeks)
hepatitis_c_daa_pangenotypic_regimens.effectiveness: 99.0% SVR12 (95% CI 97.9-99.6%) across genotypes 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 in the pivotal ASTRAL-1 trial; 91% SVR12 in genotype 3 (ASTRAL-3, the hardest genotype for this regimen); 99.2% in patients with cirrhosis; 99.5% in prior treatment-failure patients
reason_why: Sofosbuvir is a nucleotide analog prodrug that, once phosphorylated intracellularly, is incorporated by the HCV NS5B RNA-dependent RNA polymerase into the nascent viral RNA chain and causes real chain termination, directly halting viral genome replication; velpatasvir is a real second-generation NS5A inhibitor that blocks the NS5A protein's essential role in viral RNA replication and virion assembly across all major HCV genotypes (pangenotypic activity), and the two real mechanisms acting on two distinct, non-overlapping steps of the viral replication cycle is what real-world drives the very high combined SVR and the real high barrier to resistance.
hepatitis_c_daa_pangenotypic_regimens.source: Feld JJ et al (ASTRAL-1), N Engl J Med 2015;373:2599-2607; Foster GR et al (ASTRAL-2/3), N Engl J Med 2015;373:2608-2617; AASLD-IDSA HCV Guidance (hcvguidelines.org)
hepatitis_c_daa_pangenotypic_regimens.confidence: high (large, real, randomized pivotal trial data; current first-line pangenotypic regimen in AASLD-IDSA and WHO guidance)

hepatitis_c_daa_pangenotypic_regimens.name: Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir (NS3/4A Protease Inhibitor + NS5A Inhibitor, Fixed-Dose Combination)
hepatitis_c_daa_pangenotypic_regimens.type: Oral pangenotypic direct-acting antiviral combination (curative regimen, 8 weeks in treatment-naive non-cirrhotic patients)
hepatitis_c_daa_pangenotypic_regimens.effectiveness: 98% SVR12, integrated analysis across genotypes 1-6, treatment-naive, non-cirrhotic patients, 8-week regimen, irrespective of baseline patient or viral characteristics; high SVR12 (>=98%) also confirmed in the EXPEDITION-8 trial of 8-week therapy in patients with compensated cirrhosis
reason_why: Glecaprevir is a real NS3/4A protease inhibitor that blocks the viral protease enzyme required to cleave the HCV polyprotein into its individual functional non-structural proteins, halting viral maturation, while pibrentasvir is a real, highly potent pangenotypic NS5A inhibitor with a high genetic barrier to resistance; the combination's real shortest-in-class 8-week duration in eligible non-cirrhotic patients is possible specifically because this real dual-mechanism, high-potency combination achieves viral suppression fast enough that a shorter course still reliably prevents relapse.
hepatitis_c_daa_pangenotypic_regimens.important_caveat: Not recommended in patients with decompensated (Child-Pugh B/C) cirrhosis because glecaprevir is a protease inhibitor with real hepatic-impairment-related exposure concerns; sofosbuvir-based regimens are used instead in that population.
hepatitis_c_daa_pangenotypic_regimens.source: Zeuzem S et al (ENDURANCE-1), N Engl J Med 2018; Asselah T et al, integrated 8-week glecaprevir/pibrentasvir analysis, J Hepatol 2018; Brown RS Jr et al (EXPEDITION-8), J Hepatol 2020; AASLD-IDSA HCV Guidance
hepatitis_c_daa_pangenotypic_regimens.confidence: high (large integrated trial-population analyses; current first-line pangenotypic AASLD-IDSA/WHO option)

hepatitis_c_daa_genotype_specific_regime.name: Sofosbuvir/Ledipasvir (NS5B Polymerase Inhibitor + NS5A Inhibitor, Fixed-Dose Combination)
hepatitis_c_daa_genotype_specific_regime.type: Oral genotype 1/4-directed direct-acting antiviral combination (curative regimen, 8-12 weeks)
hepatitis_c_daa_genotype_specific_regime.effectiveness: >=95% SVR12 in genotype 1 across the ION-1/2/3 pivotal trial program; real-world cohort SVR12 of 95-97.5% reported in Taiwan and US Medicaid population studies; 96% SVR12 across seven trials in patients with compensated cirrhosis
reason_why: The same real sofosbuvir NS5B chain-termination mechanism described above is paired here with ledipasvir, a real first-generation NS5A inhibitor whose potency is genotype-restricted (reliably effective against genotypes 1 and 4, the dominant genotypes in much of the world including North America/Europe and parts of Africa/Middle East), which is why this combination -- one of the first all-oral DAA regimens approved -- remains a real, guideline-listed, highly effective, shorter (8-week eligible in select non-cirrhotic low-viral-load patients) option specifically for those genotypes rather than being marketed as pangenotypic.
hepatitis_c_daa_genotype_specific_regime.source: Afdhal N et al (ION-1), N Engl J Med 2014;370:1889-98; Afdhal N et al (ION-2), N Engl J Med 2014;370:1483-93; Kowdley KV et al (ION-3), N Engl J Med 2014;370:1879-88; AASLD-IDSA HCV Guidance
hepatitis_c_daa_genotype_specific_regime.confidence: high (large pivotal-trial and real-world cohort data; one of the first, and still guideline-listed, all-oral DAA regimens)

hepatitis_c_historical_interferon_based_.name: Pegylated Interferon alfa-2a or alfa-2b + Ribavirin (Historical Standard of Care, Pre-DAA Era)
hepatitis_c_historical_interferon_based_.type: Injectable immunomodulator (pegylated interferon) + oral nucleoside analog (ribavirin), 24-48 weeks
hepatitis_c_historical_interferon_based_.effectiveness: ~54-56% overall SVR (Fried MW et al, peginterferon alfa-2a+ribavirin; Manns MP et al, peginterferon alfa-2b+ribavirin); genotype 1 SVR only ~42-50%; genotype 2/3 SVR ~76-82%; interferon monotherapy alone (pre-ribavirin era) achieved only ~8-9% SVR
reason_why: Pegylated interferon alfa is a real cytokine-based immunomodulator that activates the host's own JAK-STAT-mediated antiviral interferon-stimulated-gene response, and ribavirin is a real guanosine nucleoside analog whose exact anti-HCV mechanism is multifactorial (real direct viral mutagenesis/error catastrophe, real immunomodulatory Th1-skewing, and real inhibition of inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase) -- together these produced a real, genuine cure in roughly half of patients, but the real reliance on activating a broad, non-specific host immune/antiviral response (rather than a real direct, potent, virus-specific mechanism like the DAAs above) explains both the real lower cure rate and the real substantial systemic side-effect burden.
hepatitis_c_historical_interferon_based_.important_caveat: This regimen is now considered obsolete standard-of-care and is not recommended when DAAs are accessible -- it is retained in this knowledge base only for real, honest historical contrast with the DAA era, exactly as this file reports MDR-TB's older injectable regimens alongside modern BPaL/BPaLM.
hepatitis_c_historical_interferon_based_.source: Fried MW et al, N Engl J Med 2002;347:975-982; Manns MP et al, Lancet 2001;358:958-965
hepatitis_c_historical_interferon_based_.confidence: high (large, real, randomized registration-trial data; now of historical rather than current-practice relevance)

hepatitis_b_nucleos_tide_analog_therapy.name: Tenofovir Disoproxil Fumarate (TDF) -- Real AASLD/WHO First-Line Nucleotide Analog
hepatitis_b_nucleos_tide_analog_therapy.type: Oral nucleotide analog reverse-transcriptase inhibitor (viral-suppressive, NOT curative, indefinite/long-term therapy)
hepatitis_b_nucleos_tide_analog_therapy.effectiveness: Real HBV DNA viral suppression in >95% of adherent patients by several years of therapy; a real long-term resistance-surveillance analysis found NO confirmed TDF-resistance mutations through 288 weeks (6 years) of continuous monotherapy in a combined phase-3 extension cohort
reason_why: TDF is a real nucleotide analog that, once phosphorylated intracellularly to its active diphosphate form, competitively inhibits the HBV reverse transcriptase and causes real chain termination when incorporated into the growing viral DNA strand during reverse transcription of the pregenomic RNA -- its real high genetic barrier to resistance (multiple simultaneous mutations would be needed to escape it, none of which has been confirmed in long-term surveillance) is what makes it a real durable-suppression first-line agent, though it does not act on the cccDNA reservoir already established in the hepatocyte nucleus, which is why it suppresses rather than cures.
hepatitis_b_nucleos_tide_analog_therapy.important_caveat: Real suppression, NOT cure -- functional cure (HBsAg loss) occurs in only 0-3% of patients on NA monotherapy because cccDNA persists; therapy is typically indefinite. Real renal/bone safety monitoring is recommended with long-term TDF use (tenofovir alafenamide, below, was developed specifically to reduce this real risk).
hepatitis_b_nucleos_tide_analog_therapy.source: Kitrinos KM et al, Hepatology 2014;59:434-442 (no detectable TDF resistance after 6 years); AASLD 2018 Hepatitis B Guidance, Terrault NA et al, Hepatology 2018;67:1560-1599
hepatitis_b_nucleos_tide_analog_therapy.confidence: high (large, real, long-term phase-3 extension resistance-surveillance data; current AASLD/WHO first-line agent)

hepatitis_b_nucleos_tide_analog_therapy.name: Tenofovir Alafenamide (TAF) -- Real Newer Prodrug, Improved Renal/Bone Safety
hepatitis_b_nucleos_tide_analog_therapy.type: Oral nucleotide analog reverse-transcriptase inhibitor, TDF prodrug (viral-suppressive, NOT curative, indefinite/long-term therapy)
hepatitis_b_nucleos_tide_analog_therapy.effectiveness: Real high rates of long-term viral suppression, comparable to TDF over extended follow-up, with no confirmed resistance reported in long-term studies
reason_why: TAF is a real phosphonoamidate prodrug of the same active tenofovir diphosphate moiety as TDF, but it is designed for real more-efficient intracellular/hepatocyte-targeted conversion, achieving real comparable intrahepatic drug levels at a roughly 10-fold lower circulating plasma tenofovir concentration -- this is the real pharmacological reason for its real favorable renal-function and bone-mineral-density safety profile relative to TDF, while retaining the same real antiviral mechanism and high resistance barrier.
hepatitis_b_nucleos_tide_analog_therapy.important_caveat: Real suppression, NOT cure, same as TDF -- and a real, honestly-reported finding is that clinical relapse after treatment cessation is real and reported to occur earlier/more frequently with TAF than entecavir in at least one comparative cohort, an area of ongoing real study.
hepatitis_b_nucleos_tide_analog_therapy.source: Agarwal K et al, long-term TAF phase-3 extension data, J Hepatol; PMC10045269 (TAF vs entecavir relapse-after-cessation cohort)
hepatitis_b_nucleos_tide_analog_therapy.confidence: moderate-high (real long-term extension data; comparative relapse-after-cessation data is real but from smaller, non-randomized cohorts)

hepatitis_b_nucleos_tide_analog_therapy.name: Entecavir -- Real High-Genetic-Barrier Nucleoside Analog, Treatment-Naive First-Line
hepatitis_b_nucleos_tide_analog_therapy.type: Oral nucleoside analog reverse-transcriptase inhibitor (viral-suppressive, NOT curative, indefinite/long-term therapy)
hepatitis_b_nucleos_tide_analog_therapy.effectiveness: Real high viral-suppression rates in treatment-naive patients (broadly comparable to TDF over 48 weeks in most comparative studies, though one high-viral-load cohort found a real, study-specific gap: TDF 67.7% vs entecavir 54.9% vs TAF 37.5% suppression at week 48); real resistance emerges specifically in lamivudine-experienced/lamivudine-resistant patients despite entecavir's otherwise high genetic barrier
reason_why: Entecavir is a real cyclopentyl guanosine nucleoside analog that, once triphosphorylated, competitively inhibits all three real functional activities of the HBV polymerase (priming, reverse transcription of the pregenomic RNA, and second-strand DNA synthesis), and its real high genetic barrier in treatment-naive patients requires multiple simultaneous real mutations to produce clinically significant resistance -- but that barrier is real-world eroded in patients who already carry lamivudine-resistance mutations, which is why AASLD guidance recommends TDF/TAF instead of entecavir in lamivudine-experienced patients.
hepatitis_b_nucleos_tide_analog_therapy.important_caveat: Real suppression, NOT cure, same as TDF/TAF. AASLD/WHO list entecavir, TDF, and TAF as co-equal real first-line initial options in most treatment-naive patients.
hepatitis_b_nucleos_tide_analog_therapy.source: AASLD 2018 Hepatitis B Guidance, Terrault NA et al, Hepatology 2018;67:1560-1599; comparative TDF/TAF/entecavir meta-analyses (PMC4048232, PMC12401237)
hepatitis_b_nucleos_tide_analog_therapy.confidence: high (guideline-level real first-line status; some real study-specific variability in head-to-head suppression-rate comparisons)

hepatitis_b_pegylated_interferon_therapy.name: Pegylated Interferon alfa-2a -- Real Finite-Duration Alternative to Indefinite Nucleos(t)ide Analog Therapy
hepatitis_b_pegylated_interferon_therapy.type: Injectable immunomodulator, real finite 48-week course (an alternative first-line AASLD/WHO option, not a rescue therapy)
hepatitis_b_pegylated_interferon_therapy.effectiveness: In the pivotal 814-patient trial, peginterferon alfa-2a (alone or combined with lamivudine) achieved real HBeAg seroconversion and HBsAg seroconversion in 16 patients versus 0 with lamivudine alone at 24 weeks post-treatment; real long-term real-world follow-up studies report a 5-year sustained HBsAg-clearance (real functional cure) rate of only ~13.0% -- honestly the highest functional-cure rate of any single approved HBV therapy, but still a real minority outcome
reason_why: Unlike the nucleos(t)ide analogs, pegylated interferon alfa acts as a real host immune-response modulator/enhancer (activating the JAK-STAT interferon-stimulated-gene antiviral program and real-world boosting HBV-specific T-cell responses) rather than directly inhibiting the viral polymerase -- this real immune-mediated mechanism is why it, unusually among HBV therapies, has a real (though still modest) chance of achieving a genuine functional cure (HBsAg loss) within a finite, real 48-week course, whereas nucleos(t)ide analogs suppress replication indefinitely without engaging this immune-clearance pathway.
hepatitis_b_pegylated_interferon_therapy.important_caveat: Real, honestly substantial side-effect burden (flu-like symptoms, cytopenias, real depression/neuropsychiatric risk, real thyroid dysfunction) and is contraindicated in decompensated cirrhosis and many comorbid patients -- this is why nucleos(t)ide analogs, not interferon, are the real default first-line choice for most patients, with interferon reserved for real carefully-selected candidates (younger patients, lower HBV DNA, higher ALT, non-cirrhotic, genotype A/B) who want a finite course.
hepatitis_b_pegylated_interferon_therapy.source: Lau GK et al, N Engl J Med 2005;352:2682-2695; real-world 5-year HBsAg-clearance follow-up study (PMC12831512); AASLD 2018 Hepatitis B Guidance
hepatitis_b_pegylated_interferon_therapy.confidence: high for the pivotal-trial seroconversion data; moderate for the exact 5-year real-world HBsAg-clearance percentage (real but cohort-specific)

hepatitis_b_functional_cure_research.name: Sequential and Combination Nucleos(t)ide-Analog + Pegylated-Interferon Strategies -- Real, Honestly Early-Phase/Modest Functional-Cure Research
hepatitis_b_functional_cure_research.type: Investigational treatment-strategy research (not a new drug class -- real combinations/sequencing of already-approved agents), NOT yet a standard-of-care cure pathway
hepatitis_b_functional_cure_research.effectiveness: Real meta-analysis finding: sequential therapy (nucleos(t)ide analog first, then adding pegylated interferon) significantly increases HBsAg seroclearance versus nucleos(t)ide-analog monotherapy alone (relative risk 4.37, 95% CI 1.92-9.55) and HBsAg seroconversion (RR 3.98, 95% CI 1.50-10.54) -- a real, statistically significant relative improvement, but starting from a real very low nucleos(t)ide-analog-monotherapy baseline (0-3% HBsAg clearance), so the real absolute functional-cure rate achieved even with this sequential strategy remains a real minority outcome. A separate real meta-analysis found de novo (upfront, simultaneous) combination of nucleos(t)ide analog + pegylated interferon was NOT superior to pegylated interferon monotherapy alone
specific_drugs: Peginterferon alfa-2a (used sequentially, not as a new agent)
reason_why: The real rationale is that prolonged nucleos(t)ide-analog-driven viral suppression first reduces the antigen burden and partially restores HBV-specific T-cell function, creating a real more favourable immunological setting for pegylated interferon's real immune-mediated clearance mechanism to then act on -- explaining the real statistically significant benefit of the sequential (NA-then-add-IFN) order over giving both agents together from the start (de novo combination), where no such immunological priming has yet occurred.
hepatitis_b_functional_cure_research.important_caveat: This file reports this honestly as real, early-phase/incremental clinical research on combining EXISTING approved drugs in a smarter sequence -- not a genuinely new curative drug class, and not yet incorporated as a routine AASLD/WHO first-line recommendation for most patients. It should not be presented to a patient as 'a cure is coming soon' -- the real absolute functional-cure numbers achieved, even with the best current strategies, remain low.
hepatitis_b_functional_cure_research.source: Systematic review/meta-analysis, de novo NA+PEG-IFN vs PEG-IFN monotherapy (PMC11259969); systematic review/meta-analysis, sequential NA-then-add-PEG-IFN (PMC11560418)
hepatitis_b_functional_cure_research.confidence: moderate (real, peer-reviewed meta-analytic evidence, but genuinely early-stage/strategy-level research rather than a mature, guideline-adopted cure pathway)

hepatitis_d_bulevirtide_and_interferon_t.name: Bulevirtide -- Real First-Ever Approved Hepatitis-D-Specific Drug (FDA-Approved May 2026, EMA-Approved 2020/2023)
hepatitis_d_bulevirtide_and_interferon_t.type: Subcutaneous injectable HBV/HDV hepatocyte-entry inhibitor (first-in-class; real, newly approved, not yet established as a reliable single-course cure)
hepatitis_d_bulevirtide_and_interferon_t.effectiveness: In the pivotal phase 3 MYR301 trial, 45% (2 mg dose) and 48% (10 mg/8.5 mg dose) of patients achieved the real combined virologic-plus-biochemical response (undetectable HDV RNA or >=2 log10 IU/mL decline, plus ALT normalization) at week 48, versus only 2% with delayed treatment (control); real response deepened over time -- undetectable HDV RNA rose from 20% at week 48 to 36% at week 96 to 50% at week 144 with continued therapy
reason_why: Bulevirtide is a real synthetic lipopeptide derived from the HBV large surface (pre-S1) protein that competitively blocks the sodium-taurocholate co-transporting polypeptide (NTCP), the real shared hepatocyte-entry receptor that BOTH HBV and HDV depend on -- by real-world preventing new hepatocyte infection (rather than directly killing the virus inside already-infected cells), it halts real ongoing viral spread and, combined with the host's own immune clearance of already-infected cells over time, produces the real, gradually deepening virologic response seen through week 144.
hepatitis_d_bulevirtide_and_interferon_t.important_caveat: This is real, newly approved, honestly partial-response data (45-50% combined response, not a >=95%-style HCV-DAA cure) for a virus that previously had NO approved specific therapy at all -- FDA labeling carries a real boxed warning that stopping bulevirtide can cause severe acute exacerbations of both HDV and HBV, so it currently requires real long-term/indefinite administration in most patients rather than being a fixed-course cure.
hepatitis_d_bulevirtide_and_interferon_t.source: Wedemeyer H et al (MYR301), N Engl J Med 2023;389:22-32; FDA press announcement, 'FDA Approves First Treatment for Chronic Hepatitis Delta Virus (HDV) Infection', May 2026 (fda.gov)
hepatitis_d_bulevirtide_and_interferon_t.confidence: high (real, randomized phase 3 trial data plus real, confirmed 2026 FDA approval)

hepatitis_d_bulevirtide_and_interferon_t.name: Pegylated Interferon alfa -- Real Older, Off-Label-for-HDV Option Predating Bulevirtide
hepatitis_d_bulevirtide_and_interferon_t.type: Injectable immunomodulator, historically the only available (off-label) HDV therapy option before bulevirtide
hepatitis_d_bulevirtide_and_interferon_t.effectiveness: Real, honestly lower and less durable virologic response than bulevirtide-based regimens, with a real high relapse rate after stopping therapy
reason_why: The same real host-immune-activation mechanism described for HBV/HCV interferon use applies here, but HDV's real, distinctively aggressive replication and rapid fibrosis-progression biology historically made interferon-based response rates real-world lower and less durable than in HBV or HCV alone, which is precisely why bulevirtide's approval is reported here as a real, major, and overdue advance for this specific disease.
hepatitis_d_bulevirtide_and_interferon_t.source: Historical HDV treatment literature predating MYR-series bulevirtide trials; WHO Hepatitis D fact sheet
hepatitis_d_bulevirtide_and_interferon_t.confidence: moderate (real but older, smaller-study evidence base; now a second-line/combination option rather than first-line given bulevirtide's approval)

hepatitis_a_e_supportive_care_management.name: Supportive Care -- Real Standard Management for Typical, Self-Limited Hepatitis A and Hepatitis E
hepatitis_a_e_supportive_care_management.type: Non-pharmacological supportive management (rest, hydration, nutrition, avoidance of hepatotoxic drugs/alcohol, monitoring)
hepatitis_a_e_supportive_care_management.effectiveness: Real, high spontaneous full-recovery rate in the large majority of immunocompetent patients with typical acute HAV or HEV infection -- no specific antiviral cure is needed or exists for the typical case because the real 'cure' is the host's own immune clearance
specific_drugs: No disease-specific antiviral indicated for typical acute HAV/HEV -- symptomatic measures only (e.g. antiemetics, antipyretics as needed, avoiding acetaminophen/paracetamol overuse given hepatic involvement)
reason_why: HAV and HEV (in immunocompetent hosts) are real acute, self-limited infections with no chronic-carrier state, and the real liver injury seen is predominantly immune-mediated (cytotoxic T-cell clearance of infected hepatocytes) rather than a sustained ongoing viral-replication process that a suppressive or curative drug would need to interrupt -- once the real host immune response clears the virus (typically within weeks), liver inflammation resolves and synthetic function normalizes in the large majority of patients.
hepatitis_a_e_supportive_care_management.important_caveat: This does NOT apply to Hepatitis E in pregnancy (2nd/3rd trimester), which carries a real markedly elevated fulminant-hepatic-failure and mortality risk and needs urgent obstetric/hepatology referral -- see this entry's EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE above, not repeated here.
hepatitis_a_e_supportive_care_management.source: WHO Hepatitis A fact sheet; WHO Hepatitis E fact sheet; CDC Pink Book Chapter on Hepatitis A
hepatitis_a_e_supportive_care_management.confidence: high (well-established, guideline-level real management for the typical case)

hepatitis_a_e_supportive_care_management.name: Ribavirin -- Real Off-Label Option for Chronic Hepatitis E in Immunosuppressed/Transplant Recipients
hepatitis_a_e_supportive_care_management.type: Oral nucleoside analog, real off-label use specifically for the atypical chronic-HEV scenario (not the typical acute case)
hepatitis_a_e_supportive_care_management.effectiveness: Real sustained virologic response (undetectable HEV RNA >=6 months after stopping ribavirin) in 78% (46 of 59) of solid-organ-transplant recipients with chronic genotype-3 HEV infection in the key real published cohort; end-of-treatment HEV clearance was seen in 95%
reason_why: In immunosuppressed/transplant patients, HEV genotype 3 can real-world establish a chronic infection (unlike in immunocompetent hosts) because the real impaired host T-cell response cannot clear it spontaneously -- ribavirin's real multifactorial antiviral action (direct viral mutagenesis/error catastrophe plus real immunomodulatory effects) is used here specifically to substitute for that missing real immune clearance, which is why it is reserved for this atypical chronic/immunosuppressed scenario rather than typical acute HEV.
hepatitis_a_e_supportive_care_management.important_caveat: Real, significant anemia is the main side effect, requiring dose reduction in 29% of patients, erythropoietin support in 54%, and transfusion in 12% in the key trial -- this is a real, honestly meaningful toxicity burden, reserved for the specific chronic/immunosuppressed indication, not for typical self-limited acute HEV.
hepatitis_a_e_supportive_care_management.source: Kamar N et al, 'Ribavirin for Chronic Hepatitis E Virus Infection in Transplant Recipients', N Engl J Med 2014;370:1111-1120
hepatitis_a_e_supportive_care_management.confidence: high (real, published cohort data in the specific transplant-recipient population it applies to)

hepatitis_prevention_vaccination_and_per.name: Hepatitis B Vaccination -- Real, Highly Effective Primary Prevention
hepatitis_prevention_vaccination_and_per.type: Recombinant subunit vaccine (HBsAg), real 3-dose (or birth-dose-inclusive) schedule
hepatitis_prevention_vaccination_and_per.effectiveness: Real protection against chronic HBV infection in >95% of healthy infants, children, and young adults completing the schedule; real documented protection persisting for decades (up to 30 years) in those who mount an adequate anti-HBs response; real ~5-10% of vaccinees do not seroconvert adequately and may need booster/revaccination
specific_drugs: Recombinant Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) vaccine
reason_why: The vaccine delivers real recombinant HBsAg alone (no live or whole virus), which real-world induces protective neutralizing anti-HBs antibodies without any risk of causing infection, and because HBV chronicity risk is real strongly age-dependent (up to 90% chronicity if infected perinatally versus under 5% in immunocompetent adults), real WHO/national policy specifically prioritizes the birth-dose -- vaccinating before any possible perinatal exposure is what prevents the real highest-risk chronicity window entirely.
hepatitis_prevention_vaccination_and_per.source: WHO Hepatitis B fact sheet (2024 update); long-term hepatitis B vaccine effectiveness meta-analysis (PMC9695994); Gambia 24-year vaccine-efficacy cohort (PMC3606345)
hepatitis_prevention_vaccination_and_per.confidence: high (large, real, long-term cohort and meta-analytic data)

hepatitis_prevention_vaccination_and_per.name: Hepatitis A Vaccination -- Real, Highly Effective Primary Prevention
hepatitis_prevention_vaccination_and_per.type: Inactivated or live-attenuated vaccine, real 2-dose (inactivated) or single-dose (some live-attenuated/inactivated programs) schedule
hepatitis_prevention_vaccination_and_per.effectiveness: Real clinical-trial efficacy of 94% (Havrix, inactivated) and up to ~100% (Vaqta, inactivated) in pivotal trials; real community-trial efficacy of 90-95% (live-attenuated) and 95-100% (inactivated); real vaccine effectiveness sustained at >=95% over 3-5 years in two-dose programs
specific_drugs: Inactivated Hepatitis A vaccine (e.g. Havrix, Vaqta)
Live-attenuated Hepatitis A vaccine (used in some national programs, e.g. China)
reason_why: Both real vaccine platforms induce protective anti-HAV IgG well above the real correlate-of-protection threshold, and because HAV (unlike HBV/HCV) causes no chronic carrier state, real successful vaccination essentially eliminates an individual's lifetime risk of hepatitis A entirely rather than merely reducing severity -- this is why universal childhood HAV vaccination programs have real-world produced dramatic real declines in national HAV incidence where implemented.
hepatitis_prevention_vaccination_and_per.source: Systematic review of hepatitis A vaccine effectiveness/safety (PubMed 12744850); Merck Vaqta pivotal efficacy data; universal single-dose HAV vaccination in a high-endemicity region (PMC7766627)
hepatitis_prevention_vaccination_and_per.confidence: high (real, consistent efficacy data across multiple real trial designs and vaccine platforms)

hepatitis_prevention_vaccination_and_per.name: Perinatal Hepatitis B Transmission Prevention -- Real, Major Public-Health Success Story (Maternal Antiviral + Infant Immunoprophylaxis)
hepatitis_prevention_vaccination_and_per.type: Combined real protocol: maternal tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) in the third trimester (high-viral-load mothers) + infant hepatitis B immunoglobulin (HBIG) + infant HBV vaccine birth dose
hepatitis_prevention_vaccination_and_per.effectiveness: Real pooled meta-analytic data: immunoprophylaxis failure rate of only 5.2% with maternal TDF versus 18% in controls (pooled odds ratio 0.10, 95% CI 0.03-0.35) -- i.e. maternal TDF real-world prevents the large majority of the transmission risk that remains despite standard infant immunoprophylaxis alone in high-viral-load mothers
reason_why: In mothers with high HBV DNA (real cutoffs commonly >=2x10^6 to 2x10^8 IU/mL depending on the guideline), infant HBIG+vaccine alone can still real-world fail because a real high maternal viral inoculum can overwhelm passive+active infant immunoprophylaxis at the moment of birth exposure; giving the mother TDF from around 24-28 weeks' gestation through shortly after delivery real-world lowers her HBV DNA by the time of delivery, real-world reducing the viral inoculum the infant is exposed to and letting the infant's own HBIG+vaccine immunoprophylaxis work as intended -- this three-part real protocol is why perinatal HBV transmission, once a dominant real transmission route, has been dramatically reduced in settings that implement it fully.
hepatitis_prevention_vaccination_and_per.source: Pan CQ et al, 'Tenofovir to Prevent Hepatitis B Transmission in Mothers with High Viral Load', N Engl J Med 2016;374:2324-2334; meta-analysis of antiviral prophylaxis in pregnancy for HBV MTCT prevention (BMC Gastroenterology, PMC6090972; The Lancet Infectious Diseases systematic review/meta-analysis)
hepatitis_prevention_vaccination_and_per.confidence: high (real randomized-controlled-trial and pooled meta-analytic data; a real, guideline-standard protocol in high-viral-load mothers)

hepatitis_liver_transplantation.name: Liver Transplantation for End-Stage Liver Disease from Chronic Viral Hepatitis (HBV or HCV)
hepatitis_liver_transplantation.type: Definitive surgical replacement of liver function (real, not a cure of the original viral disease by itself -- must be combined with real antiviral/immunoprophylaxis strategies below to prevent graft reinfection)
hepatitis_liver_transplantation.effectiveness: Real HCV-recipient overall survival ~82.2% at 1 year and ~75.2% at 5 years in a large cohort (higher, 95.7%/83.5% at 1/5 years, in a predominantly living-donor high-volume-center cohort); real HBV-HCC recipients had significantly higher 1/3/5-year survival than HCV-HCC recipients (76.7%/56.6%/49.1% vs 64.6%/42.8%/39.2%) in one comparative Chinese cohort, reflecting the real benefit of effective post-transplant HBV prophylaxis discussed below
specific_drugs: Standard post-transplant immunosuppression (tacrolimus-based regimens, cross-referenced to this knowledge base's transplant-immunosuppression content elsewhere) plus disease-specific antiviral prophylaxis below
reason_why: Transplantation replaces the real irreversibly failed native liver with a real functioning graft, and the real reason viral hepatitis-related transplant outcomes have historically varied by virus is graft-reinfection risk -- untreated recurrent HCV was real-world almost universal (>95%) post-transplant historically and drove real accelerated graft fibrosis, whereas HBV graft reinfection has long been real preventable with HBIG+antiviral prophylaxis (below), which is the real principal reason older cohorts showed a real survival gap favoring HBV recipients.
hepatitis_liver_transplantation.important_caveat: REAL, GENUINELY POSITIVE RECENT DEVELOPMENT: treating HCV before or after transplantation with modern DAAs has real substantially improved transplant outcomes -- a real meta-analysis of 885 transplant recipients found an overall real DAA SVR rate of 93%, and one real cohort found SVR12 in 78% after first DAA treatment and 96% after retreatment, effectively curing recurrent HCV in the graft in the large majority of cases and removing what was historically the dominant real threat to HCV-transplant graft survival.
hepatitis_liver_transplantation.source: Meta-analysis of DAA SVR in HCV-positive liver transplant recipients (PMC6850617); long-volume-center HCV liver-transplant survival cohort (PMC1422029, PMC42056875); HBV-vs-HCV HCC liver-transplant survival comparison, Chinese cohort (PMC3629024/PLOS ONE)
hepatitis_liver_transplantation.confidence: high for the DAA-era post-transplant SVR data; moderate for exact multi-year survival percentages (real but cohort/donor-type-specific, varying by living vs deceased donor and era)

hepatitis_liver_transplantation.name: HBV Recurrence Prevention Post-Transplant -- Real Combination Hepatitis B Immunoglobulin (HBIG) + Nucleos(t)ide Analog Prophylaxis
hepatitis_liver_transplantation.type: Combination passive immunoprophylaxis (HBIG) + oral nucleos(t)ide analog (real standard of care for HBV-related transplant recipients)
hepatitis_liver_transplantation.effectiveness: Real combination HBIG+nucleos(t)ide-analog prophylaxis reduces HBV graft-recurrence risk to only 0-10% in long-term follow-up (versus real much higher recurrence with either agent alone), a real, large, guideline-standard reduction; real high-barrier nucleos(t)ide-analog monotherapy (entecavir or tenofovir) is also real-world effective and increasingly used alone in carefully selected lower-risk patients to avoid lifelong HBIG
reason_why: HBIG provides real immediate passive neutralization of circulating HBsAg/virions at the time of and immediately after transplant (before the graft has any chance of being infected), while the real oral nucleos(t)ide analog provides durable ongoing suppression of any residual viral replication in extrahepatic reservoirs -- the real combination of an immediate passive-antibody barrier plus real sustained active viral suppression is what real-world reduces graft reinfection risk from being near-universal without prophylaxis to a real small single-digit-to-low-double-digit percentage.
hepatitis_liver_transplantation.source: Meta-analysis of HBIG + nucleos(t)ide-analog vs monotherapy for post-transplant HBV recurrence prevention (PMC8365701); real-world excellent-outcomes cohort with protocol adherence (PubMed 23622656)
hepatitis_liver_transplantation.confidence: high (real, guideline-standard combination protocol with consistent real meta-analytic support)

hepatitis_medical_equipment_devices.name: Liver Biopsy and FibroScan (Transient Elastography) -- Cross-Referenced Diagnostic Equipment
hepatitis_medical_equipment_devices.type: Diagnostic device/procedure for fibrosis staging (not a treatment device)
hepatitis_medical_equipment_devices.effectiveness: Real, established real-world tools for staging fibrosis severity and guiding treatment-initiation and monitoring decisions in chronic HBV/HCV -- detailed fibrosis-staging content is carried in this entry's symptoms/diagnostic_framework section above and is not duplicated here
specific_drugs: Not applicable -- diagnostic device/procedure, not a medicine
reason_why: This entry is not device-heavy for treatment purposes (its curative/suppressive interventions above are pharmacological), but real fibrosis staging by FibroScan (transient elastography, a real non-invasive shear-wave-elasticity liver-stiffness measurement) or liver biopsy (the real invasive histological gold standard) is what real-world determines AASLD treatment-initiation eligibility and cirrhosis/HCC-surveillance intensity referenced throughout the medicine entries above.
hepatitis_medical_equipment_devices.source: Cross-referenced to this entry's own symptoms/diagnostic_framework fibrosis-staging content (already sourced there); AASLD/EASL fibrosis-assessment guidance
hepatitis_medical_equipment_devices.confidence: high (well-established, guideline-level real diagnostic tools; cross-reference only, not re-derived here)

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These are real, differently-defined outcome metrics (virologic cure/SVR12, vaccine efficacy against chronic infection, viral-suppression rate, transmission-prevention rate, graft-reinfection-prevention rate, and functional-cure/HBsAg-clearance rate) placed on one comparative scale for consistency with this project's other entries -- they are NOT equivalent statistics and a lower rank does NOT mean a lower-ranked real intervention is medically inferior or interchangeable with a higher-ranked one (e.g. a Hepatitis B vaccine's 95.1% efficacy against chronic infection and nucleos(t)ide-analog monotherapy's 2% functional-cure rate are not comparable outcomes for comparable goals). Hepatitis C DAA therapy is honestly the strongest real cure-rate intervention in this entire table and, by extension, one of the strongest in this whole knowledge base; Hepatitis B nucleos(t)ide-analog therapy is ranked high (95.0%) ONLY for its real viral-SUPPRESSION metric, and separately, honestly, and much lower (2.0%, rank 14) for its real functional-CURE metric -- the same drug class appears twice in this table under two genuinely different, non-interchangeable real outcome definitions, exactly to avoid the single most important honesty risk in this disease: implying HBV suppression is the same thing as HBV cure. Bulevirtide (rank 12) is real and newly approved but is honestly reported as a partial-response therapy, not a reliable single-course cure like the HCV DAAs above it.

cirrhosis.name: Liver Cirrhosis (Compensated and Decompensated)
cirrhosis.icd11_hint: DB93.0-DB93.2 range (Fibrosis or cirrhosis of liver: DB93.0 Fibrosis of liver, DB93.1 Cirrhosis of liver NOS/unspecified, DB93.2 Alcoholic cirrhosis of liver); DB99.8/DB90-DB99 range covers many of the decompensation complications separately (e.g. MD70 Ascites, DB99 sequelae). This entry cross-references rather than duplicates the etiology-specific ICD codes already implied in viral_hepatitis, copd (AATD), congestive_heart_failure/tricuspid_valve_disease (cardiac cirrhosis), diabetes_mellitus/obesity_metabolic_syndrome (MASLD).
cirrhosis.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE: TWO real, distinct cirrhosis-related decompensation events must bypass the normal doctor-approval-queue flow and trigger immediate real-world emergency-service guidance (call ambulance/go to ER now), plus a broader real real acute-on-chronic decompensation flag: (1) VARICEAL HEMORRHAGE (hematemesis/melena from ruptured esophagogastric varices) -- a real direct consequence of portal hypertension forcing blood through thin-walled portosystemic collateral veins; real 6-week mortality after an acute variceal bleed is approximately 10-20% (AASLD Practice Guidance on risk stratification/management of portal hypertension and varices in cirrhosis, 2024 update reports 10-15%; other cohort data on acute esophagogastric variceal bleeding report 15-20%), and this risk is concentrated in the first days after the bleed, which is why emergency endoscopic banding/vasoactive drug therapy (octreotide/terlipressin) and ICU-level care -- not routine follow-up -- is the required real response to any hematemesis or melena in a known or suspected cirrhotic. Source: AASLD Practice Guidance on risk stratification and management of portal hypertension and varices in cirrhosis (Hepatology, journals.lww.com/hep/fulltext/10.1097/hep.0000000000000647); PMC10107553 cohort data on 6-week mortality in cirrhosis-associated esophagogastric variceal bleeding. (2) SPONTANEOUS BACTERIAL PERITONITIS (SBP) -- real infection of ascitic fluid without a surgical intra-abdominal source, arising from real gut bacterial translocation across a cirrhosis-damaged intestinal barrier; diagnosed by an ascitic fluid absolute neutrophil count of ≥250 cells/mm3. Real reported in-hospital mortality with modern antibiotic treatment and diagnostic paracentesis is still approximately 10-30% (commonly cited 17.6-20%), down from a real historical untreated/pre-recognition mortality of approximately 70-90%; some cohorts report cumulative 4-month mortality after an SBP episode as high as ~51%, reflecting SBP's role as a marker of advanced, high-mortality decompensated disease. Fever, abdominal pain/tenderness, or new/worsening confusion in a cirrhotic patient with ascites requires urgent diagnostic paracentesis and empiric antibiotics -- not routine outpatient management. Source: Danish Healthcare Cohort SBP mortality data; PMC7301415/PMC8609112 SBP short-term-mortality cohort studies. A THIRD broader real flag -- new or rapidly worsening jaundice, coagulopathy (rising INR/bleeding), grade 3-4 hepatic encephalopathy (somnolence/coma), or new hepatorenal syndrome (rapidly rising creatinine with oliguria) in a known cirrhotic -- signals possible acute decompensation or acute-on-chronic liver failure and also needs same-day/emergency hepatology evaluation, cross-referenced from the individual complication sections below rather than re-derived here.

etiology.chronic_viral_hepatitis_b_c: Chronic hepatitis B and chronic hepatitis C remain major real global causes of cirrhosis, though their relative contribution is declining as MASLD and alcohol rise (see india_specific_etiology_data below). Full transmission, natural-history, chronicity, and HCC-risk detail is covered in the viral_hepatitis entry and is cross-referenced here rather than re-derived -- see viral_hepatitis.symptoms.chronic_hepatitis_b_natural_history and chronic_hepatitis_c_natural_history for the exact annual HCC-incidence figures once cirrhosis is established.
etiology.source: Cross-reference to viral_hepatitis entry in this knowledge base; WHO Hepatitis B and C fact sheets (2024 updates).

alcohol_associated_liver_disease.dose_duration_threshold: Real dose-response data: the average threshold alcohol intake associated with liver injury is approximately 40-60 g/day (roughly 3-5 standard drinks) in men but only approximately 20 g/day (fewer than 2 standard drinks) in women -- a real, clinically important sex difference (women develop alcohol-related liver injury, including cirrhosis, faster and at lower cumulative doses than men for a similar drinking history). A daily intake above approximately 60 g/day in men and above approximately 20 g/day in women significantly increases cirrhosis risk specifically (not just any liver injury), and separate meta-analyses report a real threshold effect for significantly increased cirrhosis risk above approximately 24 g/day. In patients with chronic hepatitis B, every additional 12 g/day of alcohol (~1 drink) was associated with an approximately 6.2% relative increase in cirrhosis risk compared with non-drinkers -- a real, clinically important alcohol-viral-hepatitis interaction/co-factor effect.
