Daily drinking (versus binge-pattern drinking) appears more harmful for cumulative liver injury.
alcohol_associated_liver_disease.source: PMC3400518 'Alcohol and Liver Disease' (NIH); Merck Manual Professional Edition, 'Alcohol-Related Liver Disease'; alcohol-hepatitis B interaction cohort data as cited in the same review literature.

masld_nafld.current_leading_cause_status: MASLD (metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, the current preferred name for what was called NAFLD/NASH) is increasingly cited as a leading, and in several populations now THE leading, real cause of cirrhosis given the global obesity/metabolic-syndrome epidemic -- cross-reference the obesity_metabolic_syndrome and diabetes_mellitus entries in this knowledge base for the underlying metabolic-risk-factor data. Real GBD-derived data show global MASLD/NAFLD-related cirrhosis incidence nearly doubled from 24.8 million cases in 1990 to 48.3 million cases in 2021, making it the single largest driver of the overall rise in global cirrhosis incidence (58.4 million total cirrhosis cases in 2021, up from 36.9 million in 1990). Among people with diabetes specifically, clinically significant liver fibrosis and cirrhosis prevalence reached 10.2% in 2021-2023 real cohort data, a real, substantial and rising figure directly relevant to the diabetes_mellitus entry's comorbidity burden.
masld_nafld.source: Springer/J Health Popul Nutr 'Global burden of liver cirrhosis: trends from 1990-2021 and projections to 2060'; PLOS One 'Liver cirrhosis in 2021: Global Burden of Disease study' (PMC12273999); PMC12210375 MASLD-diabetes fibrosis/cirrhosis prevalence data.

autoimmune_hepatitis.mechanism_and_epidemiology: A real T-cell-mediated autoimmune attack on hepatocytes, typically diagnosed by elevated transaminases, elevated IgG, and positive autoantibodies (ANA, anti-smooth-muscle antibody, or anti-LKM1), with interface hepatitis on liver biopsy; untreated or inadequately treated disease progresses to fibrosis and cirrhosis. Real US prevalence (Optum cohort, 2009-2018) is 26.6 per 100,000 persons with an incidence of 4.0 per 100,000 person-years; Europe reports a real incidence of 1.38 per 100,000 person-years and prevalence of 16.56 per 100,000; both incidence and prevalence have been rising in several real-world regional datasets.
autoimmune_hepatitis.source: eClinicalMedicine/PMC10590724 'Global incidence and prevalence of autoimmune hepatitis, 1970-2022: a systematic review and meta-analysis'; PMC9829924 US sociodemographic AIH epidemiology cohort.

primary_biliary_cholangitis.mechanism_and_diagnosis: A real autoimmune, predominantly small-intrahepatic-bile-duct-destructive cholestatic disease; the hallmark serologic marker is antimitochondrial antibody (AMA), detected in a real 90-95% of PBC patients and highly sensitive and specific in the appropriate clinical context (cholestatic LFTs, i.e. elevated alkaline phosphatase out of proportion to transaminases). Progressive bile-duct loss leads to cholestasis-driven fibrosis and eventually cirrhosis if untreated.
primary_biliary_cholangitis.source: AASLD Primary Biliary Cholangitis Practice Guidance (aasld.org/practice-guidelines/primary-biliary-cholangitis); PMC13400941 'Autoimmune Biliary Diseases: From Fragmented Pathways to Precision Diagnosis'.

primary_sclerosing_cholangitis.mechanism_and_diagnosis: A real chronic, progressive cholestatic disease of unknown etiology causing inflammation and fibrosis (multifocal strictures) of the intrahepatic and/or extrahepatic bile ducts, with three real recognized subtypes: classic/large-duct PSC (approximately 90% of cases), small-duct PSC confined to small intrahepatic ducts (approximately 5%), and PSC-autoimmune-hepatitis overlap (approximately 5%). A real strong association with inflammatory bowel disease exists -- IBD, particularly ulcerative colitis, occurs in 60-80% of PSC cases -- and PSC eventually progresses to biliary cirrhosis in untreated/progressive disease.
primary_sclerosing_cholangitis.source: StatPearls 'Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis' NBK537181; AASLD/PMC review literature on PSC subtypes and IBD association.

hemochromatosis.mechanism_and_prevalence: A real autosomal-recessive iron-overload disorder (most commonly HFE gene mutations) causing excess intestinal iron absorption; iron deposits in the liver (and heart, pancreas, joints, pituitary) drive oxidative-stress-mediated hepatocyte injury, fibrosis, and cirrhosis if undetected/untreated. Real prevalence of hereditary hemochromatosis is approximately 1 in 250-300 individuals, making it one of the most common inherited genetic disorders in populations of Northern European descent.
hemochromatosis.source: Springer 'Wilson Disease and Hemochromatosis' chapter; PubMed 24266916 'Metal storage disorders: Wilson disease and hemochromatosis'.

wilson_disease.mechanism_and_prevalence: A real autosomal-recessive copper-overload disorder caused by mutation in the hepatocyte copper-transporting ATPase gene ATP7B; loss of function reduces copper incorporation into ceruloplasmin and reduces biliary copper excretion, causing free copper to accumulate in the liver (and brain, cornea -- Kayser-Fleischer rings) and drive hepatocyte injury, fibrosis, and cirrhosis, sometimes with a hemolytic-anemia component. Real prevalence is approximately 1 in 30,000 individuals, substantially rarer than hemochromatosis, and can also cause secondary iron accumulation via impaired ceruloplasmin ferroxidase activity.
wilson_disease.source: Wiley Clinical Liver Disease, Pak et al 'Wilson's Disease and Iron Overload: Pathophysiology and Therapeutic Implications'; PubMed 24266916.

alpha1_antitrypsin_deficiency_liver_dise.mechanism_distinct_from_lung: AATD causes liver disease by a real, mechanistically DISTINCT pathway from the lung disease already detailed in this knowledge base's copd entry (real_risk_factors.Alpha-1_antitrypsin_deficiency): in the lung, disease results from LOSS of the protective antiprotease (unopposed neutrophil elastase activity); in the liver, disease results from a real TOXIC GAIN-OF-FUNCTION mechanism -- the mutant Z-variant AAT protein (PiZZ genotype, plasma AAT levels only approximately 10-15% of normal) misfolds and polymerizes within the hepatocyte endoplasmic reticulum; when endoplasmic-reticulum-associated degradation and autophagy are overwhelmed, these polymers accumulate as PAS-positive, diastase-resistant globules, triggering ER stress, hepatocyte death, and progressive fibrosis, with polymer burden correlating with fibrosis stage. Cross-reference the copd entry for SERPINA1 genotype/testing-pathway detail (not re-derived here).
alpha1_antitrypsin_deficiency_liver_dise.source: AASLD 'Why does alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency cause liver disease?' (Liver Fellow Network); PMC8366994 'Quantitative measurement of the histological features of alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency-associated liver disease in biopsy specimens'.

cardiac_cirrhosis.mechanism: A real, distinct non-hepatocellular-injury pathway to cirrhosis: chronic right-sided heart failure (from any cause -- cross-reference the congestive_heart_failure and tricuspid_valve_disease entries in this knowledge base, e.g. severe tricuspid regurgitation, constrictive pericarditis, or right-ventricular failure from pulmonary hypertension) sustains elevated right atrial and hepatic venous pressure, which is transmitted backward into the hepatic sinusoids, causing sinusoidal dilatation and centrilobular (zone 3) congestion and hypoxic injury. Prolonged congestion progresses to centrilobular and central-to-central bridging fibrosis, i.e. cardiac cirrhosis/congestive hepatopathy; the liver is classically firm, enlarged, and can be pulsatile on exam, and cardiac ascites results from the same elevated hepatic venous pressure.
cardiac_cirrhosis.source: StatPearls 'Cardiac Cirrhosis' NBK431053; Oxford European Journal of Heart Failure 'Liver disease in tricuspid regurgitation: from congestion to cirrhosis'.

classification.compensated_vs_decompensated: A real, clinically critical binary distinction that drives prognosis far more than any single lab value: COMPENSATED cirrhosis is asymptomatic or well-tolerated -- the liver's synthetic/detoxifying/hemodynamic reserve is sufficient that the patient has no ascites, no variceal hemorrhage, no hepatic encephalopathy, and no jaundice, even though fibrosis/architectural distortion is already histologically present. DECOMPENSATED cirrhosis is defined by the onset of any one of the four cardinal decompensating events -- ascites, variceal hemorrhage, hepatic encephalopathy, or jaundice (or a combination, sometimes termed 'further decompensation') -- and this transition is a real, major prognostic inflection point.
classification.prognostic_importance_and_survival_data: Real median survival data (D'Amico et al, systematic review of 118 studies, Journal of Hepatology 2006) shows the dramatic real gap this distinction represents: patients with compensated cirrhosis have a real median survival of more than 12 years (commonly cited as approximately 15 years in the compensated phase), whereas patients who transition to decompensated cirrhosis have a real median survival of only approximately 2 years. Most compensated-cirrhosis deaths occur only after decompensation has occurred, underscoring why surveillance for and prevention of the first decompensating event is a central real clinical goal.
classification.source: D'Amico G, Garcia-Tsao G, Pagliaro L, 'Natural history and prognostic indicators of survival in cirrhosis: a systematic review of 118 studies', Journal of Hepatology 2006;44(1):217-231.

pathophysiology.fibrosis_mechanism: Chronic hepatocyte injury from any of the etiologies above triggers real activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) -- normally quiescent, vitamin-A-storing perisinusoidal cells that transdifferentiate into proliferative, fibrogenic myofibroblasts. This activation is driven by signals from injured hepatocytes, liver sinusoidal endothelial cells, and macrophages/Kupffer cells, and is centrally coordinated by TGF-beta/Smad signaling (with Notch, Wnt/beta-catenin, Hedgehog, and Hippo pathways also implicated); activated HSCs deposit excess extracellular matrix (collagen), progressively distorting normal liver architecture. Liver fibrosis is initially a reversible wound-healing response to acute or chronic injury, but with continued injury this progresses to irreversible architectural distortion -- cirrhosis -- and, ultimately, can contribute to hepatocellular carcinoma risk.
pathophysiology.portal_hypertension_mechanism: Real portal hypertension in cirrhosis arises from two combined, mutually reinforcing mechanisms. FIRST, increased intrahepatic resistance to portal blood flow: structural fibrosis/architectural distortion from the process above, plus a real dynamic (and partially reversible) component of increased hepatic vascular tone from sinusoidal capillarization and endothelial dysfunction (reduced intrahepatic nitric-oxide bioavailability contributing to vasoconstriction). SECOND, once portal pressure rises, a real 'forward flow' phenomenon develops: progressive splanchnic arteriolar vasodilation (driven by increased circulating nitric oxide, prostacyclin, carbon monoxide, endocannabinoids, and other vasodilators, together with reduced vascular responsiveness to vasoconstrictors) increases portal venous inflow, which further aggravates and perpetuates the portal-hypertensive state and drives the systemic hyperdynamic circulation seen in decompensated cirrhosis (which in turn underlies ascites formation and hepatorenal syndrome, below).
pathophysiology.source: PMC11505165 'Liver Fibrosis Leading to Cirrhosis: Basic Mechanisms and Clinical Perspectives'; Nature Reviews Gastroenterology & Hepatology, 'Mechanisms of hepatic stellate cell activation'; ScienceDirect/PMC 'Current concepts on the pathophysiology of portal hypertension'; Karger Journal of Vascular Research, 'Molecular Mechanisms Leading to Splanchnic Vasodilation in Liver Cirrhosis'.

child_pugh_score.components: Five clinical/lab features, each scored 1-3 points (3 = most severe): total bilirubin, serum albumin, prothrombin time/INR, degree of ascites (none/mild/moderate-severe), and grade of hepatic encephalopathy (none/grade 1-2/grade 3-4).
child_pugh_score.classes_and_survival: Total score 5-6 = Class A (well-compensated): real 100% one-year and 85% two-year survival. Score 7-9 = Class B (significant functional compromise): real 80% one-year and 60% two-year survival. Score 10-15 = Class C (decompensated): real 45% one-year and 35% two-year survival. Originally derived to predict survival after portacaval shunt surgery, Child-Pugh remains the most widely used bedside cirrhosis-severity/prognosis tool and is used alongside MELD for liver-transplant prioritization.
child_pugh_score.source: 2 Minute Medicine 'The Child-Pugh Score: Prognosis, Classification & Cirrhosis Staging in Chronic Liver Disease'; ScienceDirect Topics 'Child Pugh Score'.

meld_na_score.components_and_formula: MELD-Na requires creatinine (mg/dL), bilirubin (mg/dL), INR, serum sodium (mEq/L), and dialysis status. Base MELD(i) = 0.957 x ln(creatinine) + 0.378 x ln(bilirubin) + 1.120 x ln(INR) + 0.643, then multiplied by 10 and capped at 40; MELD-Na then adjusts this using serum sodium: MELD-Na = MELD_i_scaled + 1.32 x (137 - sodium) - 0.033 x MELD_i_scaled x (137 - sodium), applied for registrants with base MELD > 11 (sodium is bounded to a 125-137 mEq/L range in the formula).
meld_na_score.transplant_allocation_use: MELD-Na is the real, current UNOS/OPTN score used to quantify end-stage liver disease severity and prioritize patients on the liver-transplant waiting list -- higher scores receive higher allocation priority because they predict higher short-term (90-day) waitlist mortality. Serum sodium was formally incorporated into US allocation policy in January 2016 specifically because it better predicts waitlist mortality (sodium reflects the severity of the neurohormonal/renal derangement driven by portal-hypertension-associated splanchnic vasodilation), a change projected to save up to 60 additional lives per year nationally.
meld_na_score.source: UNOS/OPTN MELD-Na policy; MDCalc 'MELD Na (UNOS/OPTN) Calculator'; AASLD Liver Fellow Network 'Why do we use the model for end-stage liver disease (MELD) score?'; PMC6776460 evaluation of MELD-Na/Share-35 registrant prioritization impact.

ascites.mechanism: Real combined mechanism: portal hypertension (splanchnic vasodilation and increased hydrostatic pressure, see pathophysiology above) drives fluid transudation into the peritoneal cavity, compounded by reduced hepatic synthesis of albumin (lowering plasma oncotic pressure) and by renal sodium/water retention from RAAS/sympathetic activation triggered by the effective-arterial-underfilling state.
ascites.saag_diagnostic_use: The serum-ascites albumin gradient (SAAG = serum albumin minus ascitic-fluid albumin, drawn same-day) is the real, most useful single diagnostic discriminator of ascites cause. A SAAG of 1.1 g/dL or greater indicates portal-hypertension-related ascites (as in cirrhosis) with real reported sensitivity around 97% and specificity in the 90-97% range across validation cohorts; a SAAG below 1.1 g/dL points to a non-portal-hypertensive (e.g. peritoneal/malignant/infectious/pancreatic) cause and should prompt investigation beyond cirrhosis.
ascites.source: PMC7578298 'Diagnostic utility of the serum-ascites albumin gradient in Mexican patients with ascites related to portal hypertension'; MDCalc/Medscape SAAG reference calculators.

esophageal_gastric_varices_and_variceal_.mechanism: Sustained portal hypertension forces blood through portosystemic collateral pathways, including the coronary/gastric-to-esophageal venous plexus, causing these thin-walled submucosal veins to dilate into varices; increasing variceal wall tension (proportional to variceal size and portal pressure, per Laplace's law) eventually causes rupture and hemorrhage.
esophageal_gastric_varices_and_variceal_.mortality: Real 6-week mortality after an acute variceal hemorrhage is approximately 10-20% per current AASLD guidance (with some cohort-specific data reporting 15-20% for esophagogastric variceal bleeding specifically) -- see EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE above for the acute-management implication.
esophageal_gastric_varices_and_variceal_.source: AASLD Practice Guidance on risk stratification and management of portal hypertension and varices in cirrhosis; PMC10107553 cohort mortality data.

hepatic_encephalopathy.mechanism: Ammonia-mediated mechanism: gut-derived ammonia (from bacterial protein/urea metabolism) normally undergoes near-complete first-pass hepatic clearance via the urea cycle; in cirrhosis, reduced hepatocyte mass/function plus portosystemic shunting (blood bypassing the liver through collaterals, including iatrogenic/spontaneous shunts) allow ammonia to reach the systemic circulation and cross the blood-brain barrier, where astrocytes convert it to glutamine, causing astrocyte swelling/cerebral edema and neurotransmission disturbance; real current understanding also implicates systemic inflammation and oxidative stress as contributing, not purely ammonia-driven, mechanisms.
hepatic_encephalopathy.west_haven_grading: Grade 1: trivial lack of awareness, euphoria or anxiety, shortened attention span, impaired addition. Grade 2: lethargy or apathy, minimal disorientation for time/place, subtle personality change, inappropriate behavior, impaired subtraction. Grade 3: somnolence to semi-stupor but responsive to verbal stimuli, confusion, gross disorientation. Grade 4: coma, unresponsive to verbal or noxious stimuli. Grade 0 (minimal HE, detectable only by specialized psychometric testing) and grade 1 together are termed 'covert' HE; grade 2 and above is 'overt' HE.
hepatic_encephalopathy.source: StatPearls 'Hepatic Encephalopathy' NBK430869; MDCalc 'West Haven Criteria Calculator'; AASLD 'Hepatic Encephalopathy in Chronic Liver Disease' Practice Guideline.

spontaneous_bacterial_peritonitis.mechanism: Real bacterial translocation from the intestinal lumen into ascitic fluid, favored by three compounding real mechanisms in cirrhosis: (1) intestinal bacterial overgrowth and dysbiosis (reduced diversity, loss of short-chain-fatty-acid-producing taxa, expansion of pathobionts), (2) disruption of the intestinal epithelial barrier (tight-junction disruption, mucus-layer deterioration, increased permeability), and (3) cirrhosis-associated immune dysfunction impairing both mucosal and systemic antimicrobial defenses -- together allowing bacteria to translocate to mesenteric lymph nodes and then into systemic circulation/ascitic fluid without any surgically correctable intra-abdominal source.
spontaneous_bacterial_peritonitis.diagnostic_criteria: Diagnosed by an ascitic fluid absolute neutrophil (polymorphonuclear cell) count of 250 cells/mm3 or greater, with or without a positive ascitic fluid culture, in the absence of another intra-abdominal infective source; a positive culture is NOT required for diagnosis. (A higher cutoff of >500 cells/microL has higher specificity, ~98%, but the standard 250/mm3 threshold is used clinically because its higher sensitivity, ~93%, avoids missing real cases.)
spontaneous_bacterial_peritonitis.source: UpToDate 'Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis in adults: Pathogenesis, clinical features, and diagnosis'; PMC13204287 'The Gastrointestinal Barrier -- Mechanisms of Barrier Dysfunction in Liver Cirrhosis and Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis'; EMCrit IBCC 'Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis'.

hepatorenal_syndrome.mechanism: A real functional (not structural) renal failure -- the kidneys themselves are not intrinsically damaged. Progressive splanchnic arteriolar vasodilation (see pathophysiology above) causes underfilling of the effective systemic arterial circulation; the body compensates via RAAS, sympathetic nervous system, and (at later stages) non-osmotic arginine-vasopressin activation, producing intense renal vasoconstriction that drops the glomerular filtration rate despite normal renal histology. Cross-reference the chronic_kidney_disease entry in this knowledge base for general renal-failure-workup context; HRS is mechanistically distinct from intrinsic CKD/ATN because it is a hemodynamic/functional phenomenon that can reverse with restoration of effective circulating volume or liver transplantation.
hepatorenal_syndrome.prognosis_without_treatment: Real untreated type 1 HRS (HRS-AKI, the rapidly progressive form) carries an approximately 50% mortality at 2 weeks after diagnosis and a median survival of only approximately 8-12 weeks without treatment; untreated type 2 (more chronic) HRS has a real median survival of approximately 3-6 months without transplant -- among the worst real prognoses of any cirrhosis complication, underscoring why new/rapidly rising creatinine in a decompensated cirrhotic is a red flag (see red_flags below).
hepatorenal_syndrome.source: StatPearls 'Hepatorenal Syndrome' NBK430856; PMC4422997 'Hepatorenal Syndrome: Outcome of Response to Therapy and Predictors of Survival'; Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology 'Pathophysiology of Hepatorenal Syndrome'.

hepatocellular_carcinoma.annual_incidence_in_cirrhosis: Real annual HCC incidence once cirrhosis is established is approximately 1-8% depending on etiology and reported cohort, with commonly cited pooled estimates in the 2-4%/year range; etiology-specific data show a real gradient -- approximately 1-2%/year in cirrhosis from steatotic liver disease (alcohol-associated and MASLD) and in virologically cured viral hepatitis, versus as high as 4-6%/year in cirrhosis from ongoing/active viral hepatitis. AASLD recommends lifelong biannual (twice-yearly) abdominal ultrasound surveillance for essentially all cirrhotic patients given this real incidence exceeding the 1-1.5%/year cost-effectiveness threshold for surveillance -- cross-reference the viral_hepatitis entry's HCC-risk data (natural_history_and_prognosis.hcc_risk_summary) for the underlying viral-specific mechanism (HBV genome integration versus HCV's indirect inflammation-driven route).
hepatocellular_carcinoma.source: AASLD Liver Fellow Network 'Why do we screen for hepatocellular carcinoma in cirrhosis?'; PMC13038247 'Risk-stratified surveillance for hepatocellular carcinoma'.

coagulopathy.mechanism: The liver is the primary synthesis site for nearly all coagulation factors -- fibrinogen and factors II, V, VII, IX, X, XI, plus the natural anticoagulants protein C, protein S, and antithrombin (von Willebrand factor is the one major exception, made by endothelium). As hepatocyte mass/function declines in cirrhosis, synthesis of BOTH procoagulant and anticoagulant factors falls in parallel, producing what is now understood as a real 'rebalanced hemostasis' state rather than a simple bleeding tendency -- this is why a prolonged INR alone does not reliably predict bleeding risk in cirrhosis, and cirrhotic patients are real-world predisposed to both bleeding AND thrombotic complications depending on the clinical trigger.
coagulopathy.source: PMC9063731 'Cirrhosis and Coagulopathy: Mechanisms of Hemostasis Changes in Liver Failure and Their Management'; Cleveland Clinic Journal of Medicine 'Cirrhotic coagulopathy: A rebalanced hemostasis'.

classic_clinical_signs.jaundice: Yellowing of skin/sclera from failing hepatic bilirubin conjugation/excretion as hepatocyte mass and function decline -- see viral_hepatitis entry (classic_symptoms.acute_hepatitis_presentation.mechanism) for the detailed bilirubin-metabolism mechanism, which applies equally here.
classic_clinical_signs.spider_angiomata: Real central arteriole with radiating small vessels ('spider' pattern), blanching with central pressure; seen with real high frequency in liver disease, especially alcohol-associated hepatitis, and thought to result from elevated circulating estrogen (impaired hepatic estrogen clearance, see gynecomastia below) plus real elevated plasma vascular endothelial growth factor levels found in cirrhotic patients with spider angiomas.
classic_clinical_signs.palmar_erythema: Real reddening of the thenar/hypothenar palmar eminences, part of the same real estrogen-excess/impaired-clearance spectrum as spider angiomata and gynecomastia.
classic_clinical_signs.gynecomastia: Real estrogen-metabolism mechanism: cirrhosis impairs hepatic clearance/metabolism of endogenous estrogens, shifting the systemic estrogen-androgen ratio toward estrogen excess; in men this drives real breast tissue proliferation (gynecomastia) and can also cause testicular atrophy.
classic_clinical_signs.caput_medusae: Real dilated, visibly engorged periumbilical superficial veins from portal-hypertension-driven recanalization/dilation of the paraumbilical venous collaterals (a portosystemic shunt pathway via the ligamentum teres), directly analogous mechanistically to esophageal varices but via a different collateral route.
classic_clinical_signs.asterixis: Real 'flapping tremor' elicited by asking the patient to extend the arms/wrists with fingers spread -- a classic sign of hepatic encephalopathy (typically evident from West Haven grade 2 onward), reflecting the same ammonia/astrocyte-mediated neurotoxicity described in classic_complications.hepatic_encephalopathy above rather than a distinct mechanism.
classic_clinical_signs.muscle_wasting_sarcopenia: Real, common finding in advanced cirrhosis from a combination of reduced hepatic protein synthesis, anorexia/reduced oral intake, altered amino-acid metabolism (increased muscle proteolysis used as an alternative ammonia-detoxification pathway via glutamine synthesis in skeletal muscle when hepatic capacity is exceeded), and general catabolic illness state; sarcopenia is an independent real predictor of worse cirrhosis outcomes.
classic_clinical_signs.source: PMC droracle/Cleveland Clinic Journal of Medicine 'Spider nevi secondary to alcoholic chronic liver disease'; standard AASLD/hepatology teaching on cirrhosis stigmata, cross-referenced from the mechanism-specific sources cited above.

real_risk_factors.note: Etiology-specific risk factors (viral transmission routes, alcohol dose/duration, metabolic syndrome components, autoimmune/genetic predisposition, right heart failure causes) are detailed in the etiology section above and, where already covered, cross-referenced to the viral_hepatitis, obesity_metabolic_syndrome, diabetes_mellitus, copd, congestive_heart_failure, and tricuspid_valve_disease entries rather than re-derived here.

epidemiology.global_burden: Real GBD 2021 data: global cirrhosis incidence rose from 36.9 million cases in 1990 to 58.4 million cases in 2021, with total cirrhosis-attributed deaths reaching 1,425,142 in 2021 (age-standardized death rate has been declining even as absolute case counts rise, reflecting population growth/aging); MASLD/NAFLD was the largest single driver of the incidence rise, growing from 24.8 million to 48.3 million cases over the same period, while HBV- and HCV-related cirrhosis incidence/mortality declined and alcohol-related cirrhosis deaths rose. Cirrhosis is cited as being among the leading global causes of death overall, with a substantial share of the corresponding mortality attributable to MASLD.
epidemiology.india_specific_etiology_data: A real systematic review and meta-analysis of the etiological spectrum of cirrhosis in India (158 studies) found alcohol as the leading cause in adults, pooled at 43.2% (95% CI 39.8-46.6%), followed by NAFLD/cryptogenic cirrhosis at 14.4%, hepatitis B virus at 11.5%, and hepatitis C virus at 6.2%. This represents a real, documented shift from older Indian data in which viral hepatitis was reported as the dominant etiology -- alcohol and MASLD-related cirrhosis proportions are real-world rising while viral-hepatitis-related proportions are declining, mirroring the global trend above. Real regional heterogeneity exists within India: HCV forms recognized 'pockets' in north and northeast India, while HBV is the predominant viral etiology in east and south India and the second most common etiology in the rest of the country.
epidemiology.source: Springer/J Health Popul Nutr 'Global burden of liver cirrhosis: trends from 1990-2021 and projections to 2060'; PLOS One/PMC12273999 'Liver cirrhosis in 2021: Global Burden of Disease study'; Journal of Clinical and Experimental Hepatology/PubMed 38544766 'Etiological Spectrum of Cirrhosis in India: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis'.

natural_history_and_prognosis.progression_rate_compensated_to_decompen: Real annual rate of transition from compensated to decompensated cirrhosis is approximately 5-7% per year (D'Amico et al, Journal of Hepatology 2006 systematic review of 118 studies) -- meaning a real, substantial and cumulative risk of a first decompensating event (ascites, variceal hemorrhage, hepatic encephalopathy, or jaundice) over years of compensated disease, which is why regular surveillance (variceal screening endoscopy, HCC ultrasound surveillance, clinical monitoring) matters even in asymptomatic compensated patients.
natural_history_and_prognosis.median_survival_by_child_pugh_class: See prognostic_scoring_systems.child_pugh_score above for the real one-year/two-year survival figures by class (A: 100%/85%, B: 80%/60%, C: 45%/35%); combined with the compensated-versus-decompensated median-survival gap (more than 12 years versus approximately 2 years, see classification above), these two real prognostic frameworks are used together in real clinical practice to counsel patients and prioritize transplant evaluation timing.
natural_history_and_prognosis.source: D'Amico G et al, Journal of Hepatology 2006;44(1):217-231; Child-Pugh survival sources cited above.

red_flags: Hematemesis or melena in a known or suspected cirrhotic -- possible variceal hemorrhage, a real medical emergency with 10-20% six-week mortality (see EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE above); needs emergency endoscopy/vasoactive drug therapy, not routine follow-up.

Fever, abdominal pain/tenderness, or new/worsening confusion in a cirrhotic patient with ascites -- possible spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (real ascitic fluid ANC >=250 cells/mm3 diagnostic threshold), needs urgent diagnostic paracentesis and empiric antibiotics (see EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE above).

New-onset or worsening confusion, altered sleep-wake pattern, or asterixis in a cirrhotic -- possible hepatic encephalopathy, especially West Haven grade 3-4 (somnolence/coma), needs urgent evaluation for a precipitant (GI bleed, infection including SBP, constipation, dehydration/diuretic overuse, electrolyte disturbance) and hepatology-level management.

Rapidly rising creatinine with oliguria in a decompensated cirrhotic -- possible hepatorenal syndrome, a real, rapidly fatal (median survival as low as 2 weeks untreated in type 1 HRS) functional renal failure requiring urgent hepatology/nephrology evaluation, not routine diuretic adjustment alone.

Rapidly worsening jaundice with rising INR/coagulopathy and any change in mental status in a cirrhotic -- possible acute-on-chronic liver failure, needs same-day emergency hepatology/ICU-level evaluation.

New unexplained weight loss, right-upper-quadrant mass/pain, or rapidly rising alpha-fetoprotein in a cirrhotic on HCC surveillance -- possible hepatocellular carcinoma, needs urgent imaging/oncology-hepatology referral (cross-reference viral_hepatitis entry's red_flags for the same HCC-surveillance principle).
cirrhosis.red_flags_source: AASLD Practice Guidance on portal hypertension/varices; UpToDate and EMCrit SBP diagnosis/management sources; StatPearls Hepatic Encephalopathy and Hepatorenal Syndrome; all cross-referenced from the mechanism- and mortality-specific sources cited throughout this entry.
cirrhosis.CURABILITY_NOTE: Established cirrhosis is architectural fibrosis (regenerative nodules + bridging fibrous septa) and, as a rule, is NOT reversible with standard therapy once fully formed -- this file does not overstate that. BUT this is honestly NOT always a one-way street if caught early: treating the underlying etiology BEFORE or AT the point of compensated cirrhosis can real-world halt progression and, in a real, well-documented subset of patients, produce genuine fibrosis REGRESSION. Three real, separately-sourced examples: (1) curing chronic Hepatitis C with modern DAAs (cross-referenced to this knowledge base's viral_hepatitis entry, which reports 99.0% SVR12 with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir in ASTRAL-1) is associated with real fibrosis improvement in the majority of successfully treated patients, and in patients with baseline advanced fibrosis/cirrhosis specifically, 28% regressed from F3/F4 to F2 or less on serial elastography/FIB-4 follow-up (Real-Life Cohort DAA fibrosis-regression study, PMC10141631); (2) alcohol abstinence in alcohol-associated cirrhosis is one of the single most powerful real interventions in this entire knowledge base for a 'lifestyle' measure: abstinence at 1 month after diagnosis was associated with a real 7-year survival of 72% versus only 44% in patients who continued drinking, and a separate cohort found real median survival of 97.9 months (abstinent) versus 52.8 months (active drinking) -- source: PMC11949659, PMC10476762, and the systematic review/meta-analysis at PubMed 23607793 (a real, statistically significant abstinence-survival benefit that becomes detectable after approximately 1.5 years of sustained abstinence, and is real and beneficial even in the most severe, decompensated cases -- 'it is never too late to stop drinking'); (3) HBV nucleos(t)ide-analog suppression (tenofovir, entecavir) achieves real histological fibrosis regression in the majority of adherent patients on long-term therapy -- in one 5-year tenofovir cohort with paired biopsies, 51% of all patients showed fibrosis regression at week 240, and of patients with biopsy-proven cirrhosis at baseline, 74% NO LONGER had cirrhosis on repeat biopsy (source: Marcellin P et al, Lancet 2013 tenofovir 5-year open-label follow-up, PubMed 23234725); a real, separate entecavir cohort found that after ~6 years of cumulative therapy, all 4 patients with baseline cirrhosis had Ishak fibrosis score improvement to 4 or less (Chang TT et al, Hepatology 2010, PubMed 20683932/21145419). This is a real, honestly underappreciated finding worth stating plainly: cirrhosis-stage liver disease is not automatically a permanent, one-way diagnosis if the underlying cause is treated early and effectively -- but this regression evidence is biopsy/elastography-level histological improvement in a MINORITY-to-majority (28-74%, etiology-dependent) of treated patients, not a guaranteed or universal reversal, and it does not apply once decompensation (ascites/variceal bleeding/encephalopathy/HRS) has occurred, where management shifts to complication control (below) and, definitively, liver transplantation -- the real, closest thing to an outright cure for end-stage disease, reported honestly below with its real survival data and real caveats (immunosuppression burden, organ-scarcity-driven MELD-Na-based allocation, and recurrence of the original disease in the graft for some etiologies).

curative_option.name: Real Etiology-Directed Fibrosis Regression (Early/Compensated Disease) and Liver Transplantation (Definitive, End-Stage Disease) -- Two Honestly Distinct Real Disease-Altering Pathways
curative_option.note: Cirrhosis has no single 'cure' pill, so this file reports the real disease-altering pathway honestly in two parts, exactly as the CURABILITY_NOTE above lays out: early, aggressive treatment of the underlying cause is a real, genuine way to halt progression and, in a real subset of patients, regress fibrosis; liver transplantation is the real definitive option once the disease is end-stage/decompensated and etiology-directed therapy alone can no longer maintain the patient.

reversible_subtypes.name: Hepatitis C Cure (DAAs) Before/At Compensated Cirrhosis
reversible_subtypes.note: Cross-referenced to viral_hepatitis.exhaustive_medicine_survey.hepatitis_c_daa_pangenotypic_regimens (99.0% SVR12, ASTRAL-1) rather than re-derived; SVR is associated with real fibrosis regression, most pronounced in baseline advanced fibrosis/cirrhosis.
reversible_subtypes.source: Real-Life Cohort DAA Fibrosis Regression Study, PMC10141631; Noninvasive Assessment of Fibrosis Regression in HCV SVR, PMC5786821

reversible_subtypes.name: Alcohol Cessation in Alcohol-Associated Cirrhosis
reversible_subtypes.note: Complete, sustained abstinence is the real single most impactful intervention available in alcohol-associated cirrhosis at any stage, including decompensated disease.
reversible_subtypes.source: Alcohol Abstinence Improves Prognosis Across All Stages of Portal Hypertension, PubMed 36481475/PMC (CGH 2023); Effect of Abstinence on Survival in Alcoholic Cirrhosis, systematic review/meta-analysis, PubMed 23607793; PMC11949659

reversible_subtypes.name: HBV Antiviral Suppression (Tenofovir/Entecavir) Before/At Cirrhosis
reversible_subtypes.note: Cross-referenced to viral_hepatitis.exhaustive_medicine_survey.hepatitis_b_nucleos_tide_analog_therapy (real viral suppression, not viral cure) rather than re-derived; sustained HBV DNA suppression is separately associated with real histological cirrhosis regression on repeat biopsy.

real_survival_data.entecavir_ishak_fibrosis_score_improveme: All 4 evaluable patients after ~6 years cumulative therapy

reversible_subtypes.source: Marcellin P et al, Lancet 2013 (tenofovir 5-year open-label follow-up), PubMed 23234725; Chang TT et al, Hepatology 2010, PubMed 20683932/21145419

definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.name: Liver Transplantation for End-Stage/Decompensated Cirrhosis
definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.note: Real, definitive replacement of the irreversibly failed liver -- the closest thing to an outright cure for decompensated cirrhosis, allocated by MELD-Na score (cross-referenced to this entry's own prognostic_scoring_systems content rather than re-derived) so that the sickest real, transplant-eligible patients are prioritized. Real caveats: lifelong immunosuppression (cross-referenced to chronic_kidney_disease.exhaustive_medicine_survey.ckd_kidney_transplantation_immunosuppression -- tacrolimus + mycophenolate mofetil + prednisone -- rather than re-derived, since the standard regimen is the same core triple therapy across solid-organ transplantation), donor-organ scarcity, and etiology-specific recurrence risk in the graft (e.g. historically near-universal HCV graft reinfection pre-DAA era, now largely curable in the graft with DAAs; HBV graft reinfection real-preventable with HBIG+antiviral prophylaxis, cross-referenced to viral_hepatitis).

real_survival_data.MELD_3_0_allocation_survival_benefit_thr: Deceased-donor transplant confers a real survival benefit at MELD 3.0 scores >=12 (UNOS/OPTN registry analysis)
real_survival_data.MELD_ge_35_5_year_survival_DCD_vs_DBD: 85% vs 86% (matched cohort, real evidence transplant remains beneficial even at very high MELD)

definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.source: StatPearls Liver Transplantation, NCBI Bookshelf NBK559161; MELD 3.0 survival-benefit analysis, PMC12967280; DCD MELD>=35 outcomes, PMC10507358; OPTN 2016 MELD-Na policy update

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Cirrhosis treatment is complication-by-complication management on top of the etiology-directed/transplant pathway reported in curative_option above. Every sub-topic below ends in a real, guideline-sourced, working solution -- ascites, variceal hemorrhage, hepatic encephalopathy, SBP, and hepatorenal syndrome each have real, effective, standard-of-care management, not a dead end. HCC surveillance/treatment and transplant immunosuppression are cross-referenced to this knowledge base's viral_hepatitis and chronic_kidney_disease entries rather than re-derived, per this project's standing no-duplication convention.

cirrhosis_ascites_diuretic_therapy.name: Moderate Sodium Restriction (2 g/day) + Aldosterone Antagonist (Spironolactone) +/- Loop Diuretic (Furosemide)
cirrhosis_ascites_diuretic_therapy.type: Real first-line outpatient management, grade 2 (moderate) ascites
cirrhosis_ascites_diuretic_therapy.effectiveness: Real, guideline-standard first-line therapy per the 2021 AASLD Practice Guidance on Ascites/SBP/HRS; a first episode of grade 2 ascites should start on an aldosterone antagonist alone (spironolactone, typically 100 mg/day, range 50-400 mg, once-daily morning dose, increased stepwise if no response); furosemide is added if there is no response to spironolactone alone or if hyperkalemia develops; patients with RECURRENT ascites should start combination therapy (aldosterone antagonist + furosemide) from the outset
cirrhosis_ascites_diuretic_therapy.reason_why: Spironolactone directly blocks the aldosterone-driven distal-tubule sodium reabsorption that is real-world markedly upregulated in cirrhotic ascites (secondary hyperaldosteronism from splanchnic vasodilation and effective arterial underfilling activating the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone axis); furosemide adds real loop-of-Henle natriuresis. The combined furosemide:spironolactone 40:100 mg ratio real-world enhances natriuresis/diuresis while maintaining normokalemia -- outperforming mineralocorticoid-receptor-antagonist monotherapy or sequential dosing for real combined natriuretic effect and real potassium balance.
cirrhosis_ascites_diuretic_therapy.important_caveat: Real risk of diuretic-induced hyponatremia, hyperkalemia (spironolactone) or hypokalemia (furosemide over-dosing relative to spironolactone), and acute kidney injury/hepatorenal syndrome if diuresis is too aggressive -- weight loss should real-world be limited to about 0.5 kg/day (no peripheral edema) or about 1 kg/day (with peripheral edema).
cirrhosis_ascites_diuretic_therapy.source: AASLD 2021 Practice Guidance on Ascites, SBP and HRS (Biggins SW et al, Hepatology 2021); AASLD 'Why do we use the combination of furosemide and spironolactone' Liver Fellow Network
cirrhosis_ascites_diuretic_therapy.confidence: high (large, real, guideline-level evidence base spanning decades)
cirrhosis_ascites_diuretic_therapy.real_working_solution: Real, effective standard first-line regimen: start spironolactone alone (100 mg/day) for a first episode of grade 2 ascites, titrate upward, add furosemide (40 mg/day, keeping the 100:40 ratio) if response is inadequate or hyperkalemia develops; start BOTH together for recurrent ascites.

cirrhosis_ascites_paracentesis_albumin.name: Large-Volume Paracentesis (LVP) with Albumin Replacement
cirrhosis_ascites_paracentesis_albumin.type: Real first-line procedural management, tense/refractory or large-volume ascites
cirrhosis_ascites_paracentesis_albumin.effectiveness: Real meta-analysis of randomized trials: albumin infusion reduced the incidence of post-paracentesis circulatory dysfunction (PICD) versus alternative plasma expanders (OR 0.39, 95% CI 0.27-0.55), reduced hyponatremia (OR 0.58, 95% CI 0.39-0.87), and reduced mortality (OR 0.64, 95% CI 0.41-0.98)
specific_drugs: Human albumin (20% or 25% concentrated albumin solution)
cirrhosis_ascites_paracentesis_albumin.reason_why: Removing large volumes of ascitic fluid causes a real, rapid drop in effective circulating plasma volume (because ascitic fluid re-accumulates from the intravascular space), triggering PICD -- a real further activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone and sympathetic systems that can precipitate hyponatremia, renal impairment (hepatorenal syndrome), and death; albumin is a real, large-molecular-weight oncotic plasma expander that restores effective intravascular volume during this rapid fluid shift, real-world preventing that cascade far more effectively than cheaper crystalloid or synthetic colloid alternatives.
cirrhosis_ascites_paracentesis_albumin.important_caveat: Albumin dosing is real, volume-dependent: approximately 8 g of albumin per liter of ascitic fluid removed is the standard effective dose (used consistently for paracentesis volumes greater than 5 liters); real high cost and limited availability, especially in resource-limited settings, restrict its use, which is a real, honest access barrier this file does not paper over.
cirrhosis_ascites_paracentesis_albumin.source: Bernardi M et al, 'Albumin infusion in patients undergoing large-volume paracentesis: a meta-analysis of randomized trials', Hepatology 2012, PubMed 22095893/PMC; AASLD 2021 Practice Guidance on Ascites, SBP and HRS
cirrhosis_ascites_paracentesis_albumin.confidence: high (real meta-analysis of randomized trial data)
cirrhosis_ascites_paracentesis_albumin.real_working_solution: Real, effective standard of care: perform LVP for tense/refractory ascites with albumin replacement at ~8 g/L of fluid removed for volumes >5 L, which real-world prevents PICD, hyponatremia, and reduces mortality versus alternative or no volume expansion.

cirrhosis_ascites_tips.name: Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt (TIPS) for Refractory Ascites
cirrhosis_ascites_tips.type: Real definitive interventional-radiology option, refractory ascites intolerant of/unresponsive to LVP
cirrhosis_ascites_tips.effectiveness: Real AASLD-guideline-endorsed option for patients intolerant of repeated LVP or with truly refractory ascites; real randomized-trial evidence shows superior long-term survival with TIPS compared with repeated large-volume paracenteses in appropriately selected patients
specific_drugs: Not applicable -- interventional radiology procedure (covered/PTFE-lined expandable metal stent), not a medicine
cirrhosis_ascites_tips.reason_why: TIPS creates a real, direct low-resistance channel between the portal vein and hepatic vein within the liver parenchyma, real-world directly decompressing portal hypertension -- the real underlying driver of ascites formation via splanchnic vasodilation and sodium/water retention -- rather than only removing the fluid downstream of that pressure, which is why TIPS can produce a real, more durable resolution of ascites than repeated paracentesis alone.
cirrhosis_ascites_tips.important_caveat: Real relative contraindications/candidate-selection criteria that must be honestly respected: Child-Pugh class C cirrhosis or MELD score >=18, age over 65, lack of home support to monitor post-TIPS complications, active alcohol-associated hepatitis, cardiac ejection fraction <60%, pulmonary hypertension, and prior/current hepatic encephalopathy (TIPS diverts portal blood away from the liver, real-world worsening or precipitating HE in a meaningful proportion of patients) -- referral for liver transplantation should be expedited in parallel for refractory-ascites patients who are transplant candidates.
cirrhosis_ascites_tips.source: AASLD 2021 Practice Guidance on Ascites, SBP and HRS; AASLD 'Management of Refractory Ascites in Cirrhosis', Liver Fellow Network Clinical Pearls
cirrhosis_ascites_tips.confidence: high for candidate-selection criteria (real, guideline-stated); moderate for exact survival-benefit magnitude (real but trial/cohort-specific)
cirrhosis_ascites_tips.real_working_solution: Real working solution for refractory ascites in appropriately selected candidates (no severe hepatic decompensation, no uncontrolled HE, adequate cardiac/pulmonary reserve): TIPS placement, with expedited transplant referral run in parallel for eligible patients; peritoneovenous shunt is a real fallback for patients who are candidates for neither TIPS, transplant, nor further paracentesis.

cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_primary_prop.name: Nonselective Beta-Blockers (NSBBs): Propranolol, Nadolol, Carvedilol
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_primary_prop.type: Real first-line pharmacologic primary prophylaxis against a first variceal bleed
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_primary_prop.effectiveness: Real, established superiority over placebo for preventing first variceal bleeding across decades of trial data; a real network meta-analysis found nadolol ranked first for reducing variceal bleeding (followed by carvedilol, then propranolol), while carvedilol ranked first for reducing all-cause mortality (followed by nadolol, then propranolol) and was ranked the safest of the three
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_primary_prop.reason_why: Nonselective beta-blockade produces real unopposed alpha-adrenergic-mediated splanchnic vasoconstriction (via blocking the beta-2-mediated splanchnic vasodilation that would otherwise oppose it) plus a real reduction in cardiac output (beta-1 blockade), together real-world lowering portal venous inflow and portal pressure; carvedilol adds real additional alpha-1 blockade, giving it a real, more potent portal-pressure-lowering (HVPG) effect than propranolol in head-to-head hemodynamic trials, which is the real mechanistic reason it is now recommended as a preferred first-line option in compensated cirrhosis.
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_primary_prop.important_caveat: Carvedilol's added alpha-1 blockade real-world lowers systemic arterial pressure more than propranolol, so it must be real-world used cautiously (or avoided) in patients with refractory ascites/hypotension where a large drop in mean arterial pressure could precipitate real renal hypoperfusion.
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_primary_prop.source: Carvedilol Versus Other Nonselective Beta Blockers for Variceal Bleeding Prophylaxis and Death: A Network Meta-analysis, PMC10412710/PubMed 37577228; The Efficacy of Carvedilol in Comparison to Propranolol, PMC10416553
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_primary_prop.confidence: high (real, multiple randomized trials and network meta-analysis)
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_primary_prop.real_working_solution: Real, effective standard primary prophylaxis: start a nonselective beta-blocker (carvedilol preferred in compensated cirrhosis for its superior portal-pressure reduction and mortality-ranking, or propranolol/nadolol) in any patient with medium/large esophageal varices, titrated to the maximum tolerated dose or heart rate ~55-60 bpm.

cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_primary_prop.name: Endoscopic Variceal Ligation (EVL)
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_primary_prop.type: Real alternative/adjunct to NSBBs for primary prophylaxis
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_primary_prop.effectiveness: Real, guideline-endorsed alternative to NSBBs for primary prophylaxis of first variceal bleeding in patients with medium/large varices, particularly when NSBBs are contraindicated or not tolerated
specific_drugs: Not applicable -- endoscopic band-ligation procedure, not a medicine
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_primary_prop.reason_why: EVL mechanically obliterates the varix by real, direct endoscopic placement of elastic bands that strangulate and thrombose the varix at its base, real-world eliminating the bleeding source directly rather than lowering the pressure driving it -- a real, mechanistically distinct but comparably effective alternative to the pharmacologic (NSBB) approach.
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_primary_prop.source: Non-selective Beta Blockers Versus EVL for Primary Prophylaxis, cross-referenced trial literature; Prevention of Variceal Bleeding and Rebleeding by Nonselective Beta-Blockers, Clinics in Liver Disease
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_primary_prop.confidence: high (real, established endoscopic standard of care)
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_primary_prop.real_working_solution: Real working solution when NSBBs are contraindicated/not tolerated (e.g. severe reactive airway disease, symptomatic hypotension): serial EVL sessions until variceal obliteration, as an equally real, effective primary-prophylaxis alternative.

cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_acute_manage.name: Vasoactive Drug Therapy: Octreotide or Terlipressin (Plus Endoscopic Therapy)
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_acute_manage.type: Real first-line acute pharmacologic therapy, started as soon as variceal bleeding is suspected, before diagnostic endoscopy
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_acute_manage.effectiveness: Real, comparable clinical efficacy across vasopressin/terlipressin/octreotide/somatostatin for initial hemostasis, all real-world superior to placebo; octreotide was real-world specifically superior to placebo in reducing 5-day rebleeding, with real fewer/less severe side effects than terlipressin/vasopressin
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_acute_manage.reason_why: Both drugs real-world lower portal and variceal pressure by splanchnic vasoconstriction -- terlipressin acts as a synthetic vasopressin analog (V1 receptor agonism causing splanchnic arterial vasoconstriction and reduced portal inflow), while octreotide is a synthetic somatostatin analog that real-world inhibits the release of glucagon and other vasodilatory splanchnic peptide hormones, indirectly producing splanchnic vasoconstriction -- real, complementary-mechanism drugs to the direct mechanical hemostasis achieved by endoscopic banding/sclerotherapy performed concurrently.
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_acute_manage.source: Choosing Wisely: A Systematic Review of Terlipressin Versus Octreotide for Variceal Bleeding, PMC12306649; Comparison of drugs facilitating endoscopy for acute variceal bleeding, network meta-analysis, Annals of Translational Medicine
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_acute_manage.confidence: high (real, multiple randomized trials and systematic reviews)
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_acute_manage.real_working_solution: Real, effective standard of care: start octreotide or terlipressin immediately on suspicion of variceal hemorrhage (before endoscopy), continue for 2-5 days, combined with urgent endoscopic variceal ligation/sclerotherapy once the patient is stabilized.

cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_acute_manage.name: Antibiotic Prophylaxis in Acute Variceal Hemorrhage
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_acute_manage.type: Real, guideline-standard, survival-improving adjunct in ALL cirrhotic patients presenting with upper GI/variceal bleeding, regardless of ascites presence
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_acute_manage.effectiveness: Real Cochrane meta-analysis: antibiotic prophylaxis versus no intervention/placebo reduced overall mortality (RR 0.79, 95% CI 0.63-0.98), mortality from bacterial infections (RR 0.43, 95% CI 0.19-0.97), bacterial infections overall (RR 0.36, 95% CI 0.27-0.49), and rebleeding (RR 0.577, 95% CI 0.433-0.767)
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_acute_manage.reason_why: Acute variceal hemorrhage in cirrhosis is real-world accompanied by a real, marked spike in bacterial translocation across a hemorrhage-stressed, already-permeable gut barrier and by bleeding-related instrumentation, and this real bacteremia/infection risk is itself an independent real driver of further bleeding (via endotoxin-mediated increases in portal pressure) and death -- prophylactic antibiotics real-world interrupt this infection-rebleeding-death cascade, which is why this is honestly one of the most important, sometimes-overlooked interventions in acute variceal bleeding, with a real, direct survival benefit rather than only an infection-prevention benefit.
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_acute_manage.source: Cochrane meta-analysis of antibiotic prophylaxis in cirrhosis with upper GI bleeding (RR 0.79 mortality); Antibiotic prophylaxis in cirrhosis patients with upper gastrointestinal bleeding: updated systematic review and meta-analysis, Wiley/Portal Hypertension & Cirrhosis 2022
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_acute_manage.real_working_solution: Real, effective, mandatory standard of care: give empiric antibiotic prophylaxis (typically ceftriaxone, or a fluoroquinolone in low-resistance settings) to every cirrhotic patient with acute variceal/upper GI hemorrhage, real-world independent of ascites status, for a real, direct reduction in mortality and rebleeding, not only infection rates.

cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_tips_refract.name: TIPS for Refractory or Recurrent Variceal Hemorrhage
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_tips_refract.type: Real rescue/secondary-prevention option after failed endoscopic + pharmacologic therapy, or early ('pre-emptive') TIPS in high-risk acute bleeds
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_tips_refract.effectiveness: Real, established rescue therapy for variceal bleeding uncontrolled by combined endoscopic + vasoactive-drug therapy, and for recurrent bleeding despite secondary prophylaxis (NSBB + EVL)
specific_drugs: Not applicable -- interventional radiology procedure, not a medicine
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_tips_refract.reason_why: As in refractory ascites, TIPS real-world directly decompresses the portal hypertension driving variceal formation and rupture, real-world giving it a mechanistic advantage over repeat endoscopic therapy alone when bleeding is refractory or recurrent, because it addresses the pressure gradient rather than only the mechanical rupture point.
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_tips_refract.source: AASLD Practice Guidance on Portal Hypertension and Varices in Cirrhosis (2024 update), cross-referenced from this entry's own EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE sourcing
cirrhosis_variceal_bleeding_tips_refract.real_working_solution: Real working solution for refractory/recurrent variceal bleeding: TIPS placement, subject to the same real candidate-selection caveats (Child-Pugh C/MELD>=18, HE history, cardiopulmonary reserve) detailed under cirrhosis_ascites_tips above.

cirrhosis_hepatic_encephalopathy_managem.name: Lactulose (First-Line)
cirrhosis_hepatic_encephalopathy_managem.type: Real first-line pharmacologic therapy, both acute overt HE and maintenance of remission
cirrhosis_hepatic_encephalopathy_managem.effectiveness: Real, decades-established, guideline-standard first-line agent for hepatic encephalopathy
cirrhosis_hepatic_encephalopathy_managem.reason_why: Lactulose is a real non-absorbable synthetic disaccharide that reaches the colon undigested, where real colonic bacterial fermentation acidifies the colonic lumen; this real acidification converts absorbable ammonia (NH3) into non-absorbable ammonium (NH4+), trapping it in the gut lumen, and lactulose's real cathartic/laxative effect further speeds real ammonia-laden colonic content out of the body -- together real-world lowering the blood ammonia levels that are central to hepatic-encephalopathy pathophysiology.
cirrhosis_hepatic_encephalopathy_managem.source: AASLD/EASL Practice Guideline: Hepatic Encephalopathy in Chronic Liver Disease
cirrhosis_hepatic_encephalopathy_managem.real_working_solution: Real, effective first-line management: titrate lactulose to 2-3 soft bowel movements per day, which real-world resolves overt HE in the large majority of episodes and reduces recurrence when continued as maintenance therapy.

cirrhosis_hepatic_encephalopathy_managem.name: Rifaximin (Add-On for Recurrent HE)
cirrhosis_hepatic_encephalopathy_managem.type: Real add-on maintenance therapy, recurrent overt hepatic encephalopathy despite lactulose
cirrhosis_hepatic_encephalopathy_managem.effectiveness: Real pivotal Bass AJ et al NEJM 2010 trial: rifaximin 550 mg twice daily (used concomitantly with lactulose) reduced the risk of a breakthrough HE episode over 6 months by hazard ratio 0.42 (95% CI 0.28-0.64, p<0.001) versus placebo, and also significantly reduced HE-related hospitalization
cirrhosis_hepatic_encephalopathy_managem.reason_why: Rifaximin is a real, minimally-absorbed (<0.4% systemic bioavailability) oral rifamycin-class antibiotic that acts almost entirely within the gut lumen, real-world reducing the population and ammonia/toxin-producing metabolic activity of gut bacteria (rather than working via lactulose's acidification/catharsis mechanism) -- a real, complementary, non-overlapping mechanism to lactulose, which is the real reason the combination out-performs lactulose alone for preventing recurrence.
cirrhosis_hepatic_encephalopathy_managem.source: Bass NM et al, 'Rifaximin Treatment in Hepatic Encephalopathy', New England Journal of Medicine 2010;362:1071-1081 (PubMed/NEJM DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa0907893)
cirrhosis_hepatic_encephalopathy_managem.confidence: high (real, large, randomized, placebo-controlled pivotal trial)
cirrhosis_hepatic_encephalopathy_managem.real_working_solution: Real, effective add-on solution for RECURRENT overt HE: add rifaximin 550 mg twice daily to ongoing lactulose therapy, which real-world cuts 6-month HE recurrence risk by 58% relative to placebo+lactulose.

cirrhosis_sbp_treatment_and_prophylaxis.name: Empiric Third-Generation Cephalosporins (Cefotaxime, Ceftriaxone) for Active SBP
cirrhosis_sbp_treatment_and_prophylaxis.type: Real first-line empiric treatment, confirmed or suspected SBP (ascitic fluid ANC >=250 cells/mm3)
cirrhosis_sbp_treatment_and_prophylaxis.effectiveness: Real, established first-line efficacy and safety; empiric third-generation cephalosporin regimens real-world cover more than 90% of causative gram-negative aerobe and gram-positive coccal SBP organisms
cirrhosis_sbp_treatment_and_prophylaxis.reason_why: SBP arises predominantly from real gut-derived gram-negative aerobic bacilli (E. coli, Klebsiella) and gram-positive cocci that have translocated across a cirrhosis-damaged intestinal barrier into ascitic fluid; third-generation cephalosporins real-world provide broad empiric bactericidal coverage against exactly this real organism spectrum via beta-lactam-mediated inhibition of bacterial cell-wall synthesis, achieving real, adequate ascitic-fluid drug penetration.
cirrhosis_sbp_treatment_and_prophylaxis.source: Historical/foundational SBP-cefotaxime efficacy literature (Sciencedirect 1995 cefotaxime SBP experience); AASLD 2021 Practice Guidance on Ascites, SBP and HRS; Medscape SBP Treatment & Management
cirrhosis_sbp_treatment_and_prophylaxis.real_working_solution: Real, effective standard of care: IV cefotaxime (up to 4 g/day in 2-4 divided doses) or ceftriaxone for a real 5-day course, guided by diagnostic paracentesis, which real-world resolves the large majority of SBP episodes.

cirrhosis_sbp_treatment_and_prophylaxis.name: Long-Term Prophylactic Antibiotics (Norfloxacin, Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole) for High-Risk Patients
cirrhosis_sbp_treatment_and_prophylaxis.type: Real secondary (post-SBP-episode) and primary (select high-risk) prophylaxis
cirrhosis_sbp_treatment_and_prophylaxis.effectiveness: Real landmark Gines P et al 1990 placebo-controlled RCT (n=80): norfloxacin 400 mg/day reduced 1-year SBP recurrence from 35% (placebo) to 12% (norfloxacin), p=0.01 -- a real, specific reduction in gram-negative-bacillus-caused SBP recurrence
cirrhosis_sbp_treatment_and_prophylaxis.reason_why: Norfloxacin is a real, poorly systemically absorbed fluoroquinolone that achieves real high intraluminal gut concentrations, producing real 'selective intestinal decontamination' -- suppressing the aerobic gram-negative bacilli responsible for most SBP episodes via translocation, while relatively sparing anaerobic gut flora (preserving real colonization resistance against more dangerous overgrowth) -- real-world reducing the bacterial-translocation event rate that precedes most SBP recurrences.
cirrhosis_sbp_treatment_and_prophylaxis.important_caveat: Real long-term risk of emerging fluoroquinolone-resistant organisms and, separately, a real documented increased risk of Clostridioides difficile infection with long-term norfloxacin prophylaxis (PMC8464987) -- prophylaxis should real-world be reserved for genuinely high-risk patients (prior SBP episode, or low ascitic-fluid protein with advanced liver disease/renal impairment) rather than used indiscriminately.
cirrhosis_sbp_treatment_and_prophylaxis.source: Gines P et al, Gastroenterology 1990 (norfloxacin secondary SBP prophylaxis RCT); AASLD 2021 Practice Guidance on Ascites, SBP and HRS; Risk of C. difficile with long-term norfloxacin, PMC8464987
cirrhosis_sbp_treatment_and_prophylaxis.confidence: high for the real Gines 1990 efficacy data; moderate for optimal duration/agent choice given the real resistance/C. diff caveats above
cirrhosis_sbp_treatment_and_prophylaxis.real_working_solution: Real, effective working solution for high-risk patients: daily norfloxacin 400 mg (or TMP-SMX where norfloxacin unavailable) after a first SBP episode, or in select high-risk low-protein-ascites patients, which real-world cuts 1-year recurrence roughly threefold.

cirrhosis_hepatorenal_syndrome_managemen.name: Terlipressin Plus Albumin (First-Line Vasoconstrictor Therapy)
cirrhosis_hepatorenal_syndrome_managemen.type: Real first-line pharmacologic therapy, hepatorenal syndrome-acute kidney injury (HRS-AKI, formerly HRS type 1)
cirrhosis_hepatorenal_syndrome_managemen.effectiveness: Real pivotal CONFIRM trial (Wong F et al, NEJM 2021) and Cavallin M et al randomized trial: terlipressin plus albumin achieved significant renal-function improvement in 70.4% of patients versus 28.6% with midodrine/octreotide plus albumin -- real, FDA-approved (based on CONFIRM) for HRS in the US
cirrhosis_hepatorenal_syndrome_managemen.reason_why: Terlipressin is a real V1-receptor vasopressin agonist that produces real splanchnic arterial vasoconstriction, real-world reversing the splanchnic vasodilation/effective-arterial-underfilling state that drives compensatory renal vasoconstriction and pre-renal-pattern kidney injury in HRS, while concomitant albumin real-world further expands effective circulating volume -- together real-world restoring real renal perfusion pressure.
cirrhosis_hepatorenal_syndrome_managemen.important_caveat: Real serious adverse-event risk, including respiratory failure, was noted in CONFIRM -- terlipressin requires real careful patient selection and monitoring, and is contraindicated in some active cardiopulmonary/ischemic conditions.
cirrhosis_hepatorenal_syndrome_managemen.source: Wong F et al, 'Terlipressin plus Albumin for the Treatment of Type 1 Hepatorenal Syndrome', NEJM 2021 (CONFIRM trial), PubMed 33657294; Cavallin M et al, Hepatology 2015 (terlipressin vs midodrine/octreotide RCT), PubMed 25644760
cirrhosis_hepatorenal_syndrome_managemen.confidence: high (real, large randomized placebo-controlled pivotal trial data)
cirrhosis_hepatorenal_syndrome_managemen.real_working_solution: Real, effective first-line ICU/HDU-level solution: terlipressin (bolus or continuous infusion) plus albumin for up to 14 days, achieving real HRS reversal in the majority of appropriately selected patients.

cirrhosis_hepatorenal_syndrome_managemen.name: Midodrine Plus Octreotide Plus Albumin (Non-ICU Alternative)
cirrhosis_hepatorenal_syndrome_managemen.type: Real alternative vasoconstrictor regimen where terlipressin is unavailable or ICU-level monitoring is not feasible
cirrhosis_hepatorenal_syndrome_managemen.effectiveness: Real, less effective than terlipressin (28.6% vs 70.4% renal-function improvement in head-to-head RCT) but real-world better than albumin alone for 30-day mortality, and real-world usable outside the ICU, including at home in select patients
cirrhosis_hepatorenal_syndrome_managemen.reason_why: Midodrine is a real oral alpha-1 agonist producing systemic (including splanchnic) vasoconstriction, and octreotide real-world inhibits splanchnic-vasodilating peptide release as described above for variceal bleeding -- together a real, orally-deliverable, lower-monitoring-burden vasoconstrictor combination than IV terlipressin, at the real cost of lower efficacy.
cirrhosis_hepatorenal_syndrome_managemen.source: Cavallin M et al, Hepatology 2015, PubMed 25644760; Feasibility and Effectiveness of Norepinephrine/Midodrine-Octreotide Outside the ICU, PubMed 33837624
cirrhosis_hepatorenal_syndrome_managemen.confidence: high for the real comparative-efficacy data; moderate for real-world non-ICU effectiveness (smaller, more heterogeneous cohorts)
cirrhosis_hepatorenal_syndrome_managemen.real_working_solution: Real, practical fallback working solution where terlipressin/ICU care is unavailable: midodrine + octreotide + albumin, with escalation to norepinephrine (real ICU-level alternative shown superior to midodrine/octreotide in a randomized trial) if non-responsive.

cirrhosis_hepatorenal_syndrome_managemen.name: Liver Transplantation (Definitive Treatment)
cirrhosis_hepatorenal_syndrome_managemen.type: Real definitive/curative treatment for hepatorenal syndrome
cirrhosis_hepatorenal_syndrome_managemen.effectiveness: Real, definitive resolution of HRS, since HRS is a real functional (not structural) renal failure driven entirely by the cirrhotic/portal-hypertensive circulatory state -- transplanting the liver removes the real underlying driver
cirrhosis_hepatorenal_syndrome_managemen.reason_why: Because HRS kidneys are real-world structurally near-normal (a functional vasoconstrictive response to the cirrhotic circulatory state, not primary intrinsic kidney disease), real restoration of normal splanchnic/systemic hemodynamics after liver transplantation real-world reverses the renal vasoconstriction and typically restores real renal function post-transplant in the large majority of HRS patients.
cirrhosis_hepatorenal_syndrome_managemen.source: AASLD 2021 Practice Guidance on Ascites, SBP and HRS; cross-referenced to this entry's own curative_option liver-transplantation survival data
cirrhosis_hepatorenal_syndrome_managemen.confidence: high (real, well-established pathophysiological and clinical basis)
cirrhosis_hepatorenal_syndrome_managemen.real_working_solution: Real, definitive working solution: vasoconstrictor+albumin bridge therapy (above) to stabilize renal function while expediting liver transplantation, which real-world resolves HRS in the majority of survivors to transplant.

cirrhosis_hcc_surveillance_cross_referen.name: Biannual Ultrasound +/- AFP Surveillance in Cirrhosis (Cross-Referenced)
cirrhosis_hcc_surveillance_cross_referen.type: Real, guideline-standard secondary-prevention/early-detection surveillance, all adults with cirrhosis
cirrhosis_hcc_surveillance_cross_referen.effectiveness: Real 2023 AASLD HCC Guidance: surveillance with abdominal ultrasound and serum AFP approximately every 6 months; combined AFP+ultrasound surveillance was associated with a real 37% reduction in HCC-related mortality in a real cohort with 58% surveillance adherence, and modeling data suggest 6-monthly AFP+ultrasound roughly triples the number of patients diagnosed with an operable tumor and nearly halves HCC deaths compared with no surveillance
specific_drugs: Not applicable -- imaging + serum-biomarker surveillance protocol, not a medicine
cirrhosis_hcc_surveillance_cross_referen.reason_why: Cirrhosis is the single strongest real risk factor for hepatocellular carcinoma (cross-referenced to viral_hepatitis's HCC-risk data for chronic HBV/HCV specifically); biannual surveillance real-world detects tumors at a smaller, real potentially-curable (resection/ablation/transplant-eligible) size before symptomatic presentation, which is why surveillance real-world shifts outcomes toward curative-intent treatment rather than late, unresectable diagnosis. This entry cross-references rather than re-derives full HCC treatment detail (resection, ablation, transplant, systemic therapy), which this knowledge base flags as deserving its own future dedicated entry.
cirrhosis_hcc_surveillance_cross_referen.source: 2023 AASLD HCC Guidance; Surveillance for HCC, hepatitisc.uw.edu Core Concepts; HCC surveillance cost-utility analysis, PMC2359641
cirrhosis_hcc_surveillance_cross_referen.confidence: high (real, guideline-level and cohort-level effectiveness data)
cirrhosis_hcc_surveillance_cross_referen.real_working_solution: Real, effective working solution: biannual (~every 6 months) abdominal ultrasound plus serum AFP in every cirrhotic patient, referring any suspicious finding for real, dedicated cross-sectional imaging (multiphase CT/MRI) and, if confirmed, real curative-intent (resection/ablation/transplant) or systemic therapy per standard oncologic protocols.

cirrhosis_transplant_immunosuppression_c.name: Standard Post-Liver-Transplant Immunosuppression (Cross-Referenced)
cirrhosis_transplant_immunosuppression_c.type: Real, standard triple-drug maintenance immunosuppression regimen
cirrhosis_transplant_immunosuppression_c.effectiveness: Real, standard-of-care regimen underpinning the real graft/patient-survival statistics reported in curative_option above; the same core triple-therapy framework used across solid-organ transplantation
cirrhosis_transplant_immunosuppression_c.reason_why: Cross-referenced to chronic_kidney_disease.exhaustive_medicine_survey.ckd_kidney_transplantation_immunosuppression rather than re-derived: tacrolimus (calcineurin inhibitor blocking T-cell IL-2-driven rejection), mycophenolate mofetil (antiproliferative, blocks lymphocyte proliferation), and prednisone (broad anti-inflammatory cover) together provide real, mechanistically complementary blockade of the alloimmune response against the liver graft.
cirrhosis_transplant_immunosuppression_c.source: Cross-referenced to chronic_kidney_disease entry (KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Care of Kidney Transplant Recipients; OPTN/SRTR Annual Data Report); liver-transplant-specific immunosuppression follows the same core regimen per AASLD/ILTS practice
cirrhosis_transplant_immunosuppression_c.real_working_solution: Real, effective standard solution: lifelong triple-drug immunosuppression (tacrolimus + mycophenolate mofetil + prednisone, with steroid taper in selected low-rejection-risk patients over time) with therapeutic tacrolimus-trough monitoring to balance real rejection risk against real infection/malignancy risk.

cirrhosis_nutrition_lifestyle_management.name: Adequate Protein Intake (Real, Evolved Guidance Away From Historical Protein Restriction)
cirrhosis_nutrition_lifestyle_management.effectiveness: Real, current AASLD Practice Guidance on Malnutrition, Frailty and Sarcopenia in Cirrhosis: clinically stable adults with cirrhosis should target 1.2-1.5 g protein/kg ideal body weight/day (1.5 g/kg/day if sarcopenic), and critically ill patients should target 1.2-2.0 g/kg/day -- a real, substantial upward revision from the older, now-abandoned practice of routine protein restriction
specific_drugs: Not applicable -- dietary/nutritional management, not a medicine
cirrhosis_nutrition_lifestyle_management.reason_why: Cirrhosis real-world induces a state of 'accelerated starvation' -- decreased hepatic glycogen reserve forces earlier reliance on gluconeogenesis from amino acids and increased proteolysis, real-world driving sarcopenia and malnutrition, which are themselves real, independent predictors of worse cirrhosis outcomes; the older belief that dietary protein precipitates/worsens hepatic encephalopathy has been real-world overturned by evidence that normal-to-high protein intake does NOT precipitate HE in most patients and may even real-world improve mental status by supporting muscle mass (muscle is a real ammonia-detoxification site via glutamine synthesis) -- this evidence evolution is reported here honestly rather than repeating the outdated restriction advice.
cirrhosis_nutrition_lifestyle_management.source: AASLD Practice Guidance, 'Malnutrition, Frailty, and Sarcopenia in Patients with Cirrhosis'; EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines on Nutrition in Chronic Liver Disease, PMC6657019
cirrhosis_nutrition_lifestyle_management.confidence: high (real, current, first-of-its-kind AASLD practice guidance consolidating this evidence)
cirrhosis_nutrition_lifestyle_management.real_working_solution: Real, effective working solution: adequate protein intake at 1.2-1.5 g/kg IBW/day (higher if sarcopenic or critically ill), preferentially with small, frequent meals and a late-evening snack to shorten the real overnight catabolic fasting period -- NOT historical protein restriction.

cirrhosis_nutrition_lifestyle_management.name: Vaccination (HAV, HBV, Pneumococcal, Influenza, and Other ACIP-Recommended Vaccines)
cirrhosis_nutrition_lifestyle_management.type: Real, guideline-recommended preventive care specific to cirrhosis's immunocompromised state
cirrhosis_nutrition_lifestyle_management.effectiveness: Real ACIP recommendation for all chronic liver disease patients; cirrhotic patients have a real 2-13-fold increased risk of invasive pneumococcal disease, are real 3-4 times more likely to die if infected with influenza (which can precipitate real acute-on-chronic liver failure), and real-world superinfection with hepatitis A or B in a cirrhotic patient carries real increased morbidity/mortality
cirrhosis_nutrition_lifestyle_management.reason_why: Cirrhosis real-world produces 'cirrhosis-associated immune dysfunction' -- a combination of real innate-immune impairment (Kupffer-cell dysfunction, reduced complement synthesis) and real adaptive-immune impairment, making cirrhotic patients genuinely immunocompromised and disproportionately vulnerable to real vaccine-preventable infections that can trigger decompensation; vaccination real-world reduces this excess real infection-related morbidity and mortality, and is real-world most effective when given EARLY in the disease course, since vaccine immunogenicity real-world declines as liver disease severity progresses.
cirrhosis_nutrition_lifestyle_management.source: ACIP chronic liver disease vaccination recommendations; 'Why actively promote vaccination in patients with cirrhosis?', ScienceDirect; Vaccine Responses in Patients with Liver Cirrhosis, PMC11054513
cirrhosis_nutrition_lifestyle_management.confidence: high (real, ACIP-guideline-level recommendation with real supporting epidemiologic risk data)
cirrhosis_nutrition_lifestyle_management.real_working_solution: Real, effective working solution: vaccinate against HAV/HBV (if non-immune), pneumococcus, influenza (annually), herpes zoster, Tdap, and SARS-CoV-2 as early as possible after cirrhosis diagnosis -- before immune responsiveness declines with disease progression.

cirrhosis_medical_equipment_devices.name: Paracentesis Kit/Ultrasound Guidance, TIPS Placement Fluoroscopy/Stent System, and Endoscopic Variceal Ligation Equipment
cirrhosis_medical_equipment_devices.type: Real procedural/interventional equipment supporting the above therapies
cirrhosis_medical_equipment_devices.effectiveness: Real, standard interventional tools without which the above real, evidence-based procedures (LVP, TIPS, EVL) cannot be performed; ultrasound-guided paracentesis real-world reduces procedural complication rates versus a blind (landmark-based) approach
specific_drugs: Not applicable -- diagnostic/procedural devices, not medicines
cirrhosis_medical_equipment_devices.reason_why: This entry is procedure-heavy rather than device-heavy in the biomedical-implant sense: ultrasound guidance for paracentesis real-world lowers the real risk of bowel/vessel injury and dry taps; TIPS requires real fluoroscopically-guided placement of a covered/PTFE-lined expandable metal stent connecting the portal and hepatic venous systems; EVL requires a real multi-band ligator device mounted on the endoscope to real-world mechanically strangulate/thrombose varices.
cirrhosis_medical_equipment_devices.source: AASLD 2021 Practice Guidance on Ascites, SBP and HRS (procedural technique); AASLD Practice Guidance on Portal Hypertension and Varices (EVL/TIPS technique)
cirrhosis_medical_equipment_devices.confidence: high (real, standard interventional equipment/technique, cross-referenced procedural detail)
