pud_prevention_ppi_prophylaxis_and_icu_s.effectiveness: Real, most studied and best-proven co-prescription strategy per ACG and joint ACCF/ACG/AHA guidance; recommended specifically for patients stratified as high-risk (multiple risk factors, prior ulcer complication, or concomitant corticosteroid/anticoagulant use) rather than universally for all NSAID users
reason_why: Same real mechanism as NSAID-ulcer healing above (removing the acid co-factor while systemic COX-1 inhibition continues), applied here real-world prophylactically before an ulcer forms in patients whose real, quantifiable individual risk (age, prior ulcer history, concomitant anticoagulant/antiplatelet/corticosteroid use, high-risk NSAID choice) justifies routine co-therapy rather than reactive treatment after a complication occurs.

pud_prevention_ppi_prophylaxis_and_icu_s.name: ICU Stress-Ulcer Prophylaxis -- Real, Guideline-Recommended in High-Risk Critically Ill Patients
pud_prevention_ppi_prophylaxis_and_icu_s.type: IV or oral acid-suppressive prophylaxis, real ICU-specific indication
pud_prevention_ppi_prophylaxis_and_icu_s.effectiveness: Real Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidance recommends stress-ulcer prophylaxis for patients mechanically ventilated for >48 hours or with coagulopathy; a real meta-analysis of randomized trials found PPIs were superior to H2-receptor antagonists in preventing clinically important and overt GI bleeding, without a statistically significant increase in pneumonia risk (RR 1.12, 95% CI 0.86-1.46) or mortality in pooled RCT data, addressing a real, previously debated safety concern
reason_why: Critically ill patients with real severe physiologic stress (mechanical ventilation, coagulopathy, major trauma/burns, severe CNS injury) are at real elevated risk of stress-related mucosal ulceration and bleeding via the ischemic and gastrin-mediated mechanisms already detailed in this entry's own symptoms/etiology section (Curling's/Cushing's ulcers) -- prophylactic acid suppression in this specific real high-risk population reduces clinically important bleeding, and the real meta-analytic evidence that this benefit does not come at a statistically significant pneumonia-risk cost (a concern that previously limited enthusiasm for routine PPI prophylaxis) is why PPI stress-ulcer prophylaxis remains real, current guideline-recommended practice specifically in the high-risk ICU subgroups defined above, not in all ICU patients indiscriminately.
pud_prevention_ppi_prophylaxis_and_icu_s.important_caveat: Real, guideline-recommended discontinuation once the patient is tolerating full enteral feeds, since enteral feeding itself has a real protective effect against stress-ulcer bleeding and continuing prophylaxis beyond the high-risk window does not add benefit.
pud_prevention_ppi_prophylaxis_and_icu_s.source: Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines (stress ulcer prophylaxis recommendation); 'Efficacy and safety of proton pump inhibitors for stress ulcer prophylaxis in critically ill patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials', PMC4855320.
pud_prevention_ppi_prophylaxis_and_icu_s.confidence: high (guideline-level recommendation supported by a real, large meta-analysis)

inflammatory_bowel_disease.name: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (Crohn's Disease and Ulcerative Colitis)
inflammatory_bowel_disease.icd11_hint: DD70 Crohn disease, DD71 Ulcerative colitis, DD72 Other noninfective gastroenteritis and colitis (WHO ICD-11). This entry's SCOPE is symptoms/clinical/diagnostic/risk-factor/epidemiology/complications framework only - biologics/immunosuppressants/5-ASA agents, surgery (colectomy, ileal pouch-anal anastomosis, bowel resection), and curability are added by a separate treatment-focused pass that runs after this one.
inflammatory_bowel_disease.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE: TWO real, distinct IBD-related presentations are real actual surgical/medical EMERGENCIES that must bypass the normal doctor-approval-queue flow and trigger immediate real-world emergency-service guidance (call ambulance/go to ER now), not the routine consultation flow: (1) TOXIC MEGACOLON - a real actual life-threatening complication seen predominantly in ulcerative colitis (also occurs in Crohn's colitis and infectious/C. difficile colitis) defined by real actual total or segmental non-obstructive colonic dilation (radiographic transverse colon diameter greater than 6 cm, per the real actual Jalan diagnostic criteria) plus signs of real actual systemic toxicity. The real actual Jalan criteria require: (a) radiographic evidence of colonic dilation >6 cm (especially transverse colon); (b) at least 3 of: fever >38.6 degrees C (101.5 F), heart rate >120/min, leukocytosis (neutrophil count) >10,500/microL, or anemia; PLUS (c) at least 1 of: dehydration, altered mental status, electrolyte disturbance, or hypotension. Real actual toxic megacolon complicates approximately 10% of severe ulcerative colitis cases (fulminant colitis). Overall real actual in-hospital mortality is approximately 7.9% (rises sharply with delayed surgery and with perforation, and toxic-megacolon-with-perforation mortality is substantially higher, historically cited up to approximately 20-fold higher than without perforation, though contemporary aggressive medical/surgical management has reduced mortality from older reports of 20-30%). Requires emergency hospitalization, bowel rest, IV corticosteroids or rescue therapy (infliximab/cyclosporin) with a strict 48-72 hour response deadline, broad-spectrum antibiotics if perforation/sepsis suspected, and urgent surgical consultation for emergency (sub)total colectomy if no rapid improvement or if perforation/uncontrolled bleeding/worsening toxicity occurs - not the routine doctor-approval workflow. Source: Jalan et al. diagnostic criteria (Gastroenterology 1969, as cited in StatPearls 'Toxic Megacolon' NBK547679); Autenrieth & Baumgart, 'Toxic megacolon', Inflammatory Bowel Diseases 2012; Doi: 10.1002/ibd.21847. (2) BOWEL PERFORATION / FULMINANT COLITIS WITH PERITONEAL SIGNS - can occur spontaneously in severe/fulminant ulcerative colitis or Crohn's colitis (with or without antecedent toxic megacolon), or from a penetrating Crohn's disease complication (intra-abdominal abscess rupture). Presents as sudden severe diffuse abdominal pain, a rigid 'board-like' abdomen with guarding/rebound tenderness (peritonitis), high fever, tachycardia, and hypotension/shock as sepsis develops; free intraperitoneal air may be seen on erect chest X-ray or CT. This is an acute abdomen requiring emergency surgical consultation, resuscitation, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and emergency laparotomy/colectomy - not the routine doctor-approval workflow. Signs of significant acute GI bleeding (large-volume hematochezia with hemodynamic instability) in severe colitis and high fever with peritoneal signs are similarly to be treated as emergencies requiring the same immediate-ER-referral pathway. Source: Autenrieth & Baumgart, 'Toxic megacolon', Inflammatory Bowel Diseases 2012; Truelove & Witts severe/fulminant colitis criteria as adopted in ACG/ECCO Ulcerative Colitis Guidelines.

definition_and_classification.definition: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is an umbrella term for two chronic, idiopathic, relapsing-remitting inflammatory disorders of the gastrointestinal tract - Crohn's disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC) - that arise from a dysregulated mucosal immune response to gut microbiota in a genetically susceptible host. A minority of cases with overlapping features that cannot be firmly classified are termed IBD-unclassified (IBD-U).

crohns_disease_distinguishing_features.anatomic_distribution: Can affect ANY part of the gastrointestinal tract from mouth to anus (oral ulcers, esophageal/gastroduodenal disease are recognized though less common), with classic and most common involvement of the terminal ileum and/or perianal region; approximately 80% of patients have small bowel involvement (commonly terminal ileum), about half have ileocolonic disease, and perianal disease affects roughly a quarter to a third of patients over the disease course.
crohns_disease_distinguishing_features.pattern_of_involvement: Discontinuous, patchy 'skip lesions' - segments of diseased bowel separated by normal-appearing mucosa - in contrast to the continuous inflammation of UC.
crohns_disease_distinguishing_features.depth_of_inflammation: Transmural (full-thickness) inflammation extending through all layers of the bowel wall, which is the pathological basis for Crohn's characteristic complications of strictures, fistulas, and abscesses (features not seen in uncomplicated UC because UC inflammation does not breach the submucosa).
crohns_disease_distinguishing_features.histology: Noncaseating granulomas are found on biopsy in approximately 60% of Crohn's disease resection specimens (lower yield, roughly 15-36%, on endoscopic mucosal biopsies) and, when present, are highly specific for Crohn's disease since they are essentially never seen in ulcerative colitis. Fissuring/knife-like ulcers and transmural lymphoid aggregates (often subserosal) are additional supportive histologic features.
crohns_disease_distinguishing_features.source: Feuerstein & Cheifetz, 'Crohn Disease: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, and Management', Mayo Clinic Proceedings 2017; Pathology Outlines 'Ulcerative colitis and proctitis'; ECCO Guidelines on Diagnosis and Management of Crohn's Disease.

ulcerative_colitis_distinguishing_featur.anatomic_distribution: Limited to the colon and rectum only (no small bowel disease, with the rare exception of 'backwash ileitis' in extensive pancolitis, which does not represent true small bowel Crohn's-type disease).
ulcerative_colitis_distinguishing_featur.pattern_of_involvement: Continuous inflammation that always starts at the rectum and extends proximally without skip areas - the rectum is virtually always involved in untreated disease, and the proximal extent of continuous inflammation defines disease extent (proctitis, left-sided, or extensive/pancolitis).
ulcerative_colitis_distinguishing_featur.depth_of_inflammation: Limited to the mucosa and superficial submucosa (not transmural), which is why fistulas, abscesses, and strictures are rare/atypical in UC and, when a stricture does occur in longstanding UC, malignancy must be excluded.
ulcerative_colitis_distinguishing_featur.histology: Continuous crypt architectural distortion, crypt abscesses (neutrophils within crypts), and diffuse mucosal/submucosal chronic inflammatory infiltrate; granulomas are not a feature of UC (their presence should prompt reconsideration of the diagnosis as Crohn's disease).
ulcerative_colitis_distinguishing_featur.source: Ordas et al., 'Ulcerative colitis', The Lancet 2012; ECCO Third European Evidence-based Consensus on Diagnosis and Management of Ulcerative Colitis, Journal of Crohn's and Colitis 2017; Pathology Outlines 'Ulcerative colitis and proctitis'.

pathophysiology.core_mechanism: IBD results from an inappropriate and sustained immune response to normal commensal gut microbiota (rather than to a specific pathogen) in a genetically susceptible individual, with loss of intestinal epithelial barrier integrity and immune tolerance, amplified by environmental triggers.
pathophysiology.genetics_nod2: NOD2 (also called CARD15) was the first and remains the most replicated Crohn's disease susceptibility gene. NOD2 is an intracellular pattern-recognition receptor that senses bacterial muramyl dipeptide (MDP); loss-of-function NOD2 variants impair bacterial sensing and antimicrobial peptide (alpha-defensin) production by Paneth cells, and paradoxically also enhance NOD2-MDP-driven dendritic cell production of IL-23 and IL-1, promoting IL-17-producing Th17 cell responses - linking innate immune dysfunction directly to the IL-23/Th17 axis implicated in Crohn's disease.
pathophysiology.cytokine_pathways: The IL-23/Th17 axis is central to IBD pathogenesis: IL-23 (produced by activated macrophages/dendritic cells) drives expansion and maintenance of IL-17-producing Th17 cells; IL-17 in turn amplifies inflammation by inducing IL-1beta, IL-6, IL-8, and TNF-alpha from other immune and stromal cells. TNF-alpha is a dominant pro-inflammatory cytokine in both CD and UC, driving epithelial apoptosis, barrier disruption, and further immune cell recruitment - this mechanistic centrality of TNF-alpha and the IL-23/Th17 axis is the direct pharmacologic basis for anti-TNF biologics (infliximab, adalimumab) and anti-IL-23 biologics (ustekinumab, risankizumab) used in treatment.
pathophysiology.source: Hugot et al., 'Association of NOD2 leucine-rich repeat variants with susceptibility to Crohn's disease', Nature 2001 (PMID 11385576); Duerr et al., 'A genome-wide association study identifies IL23R as an inflammatory bowel disease gene', Science 2006; Ahluwalia et al., 'Role of the IL23/IL17 Pathway in Crohn's Disease', Frontiers/PMC8042267; Maloy & Powrie, 'Intestinal homeostasis and its breakdown in inflammatory bowel disease', Nature 2011.

classification_and_disease_activity_scor.montreal_classification_crohns_disease: The Montreal Classification (a 2005 revision of the 1998 Vienna Classification) stratifies Crohn's disease by: Age at diagnosis - A1 (below 17 years), A2 (17-40 years), A3 (over 40 years); Location - L1 (ileal), L2 (colonic), L3 (ileocolonic), L4 (isolated upper GI disease, added as a modifier to L1-L3 if present concurrently); and Behavior - B1 (non-stricturing, non-penetrating/inflammatory), B2 (stricturing), B3 (penetrating/fistulizing), with 'p' added as a modifier for concurrent perianal disease.
classification_and_disease_activity_scor.montreal_classification_ulcerative_colit: For ulcerative colitis, the Montreal Classification stratifies by anatomic extent: E1 (ulcerative proctitis, limited to the rectum), E2 (left-sided UC, disease extending to the splenic flexure or less), E3 (extensive UC/pancolitis, extending proximal to the splenic flexure).
classification_and_disease_activity_scor.cdai_crohns_disease_activity_index: The CDAI is the gold-standard clinical trial outcome measure for Crohn's disease activity, an 8-item weighted composite: number of liquid/soft stools over 7 days (x2), abdominal pain severity 0-3 over 7 days (x5), general well-being 0-4 over 7 days (x7), presence of extraintestinal complications/count (x20 each), use of antidiarrheal drugs (x30), presence of an abdominal mass (x10), hematocrit deviation from normal (x6), and percentage deviation from standard body weight (x1). Total scores range roughly 0-600; CDAI less than 150 defines clinical remission, 150-220 mild disease, 220-450 moderate-to-severe disease, and greater than 450 severe/fulminant disease.
classification_and_disease_activity_scor.mayo_score_ulcerative_colitis: The Mayo Score (0-12 total) for UC activity has 4 equally-weighted (0-3 each) components: stool frequency relative to the patient's normal, rectal bleeding, endoscopic findings (mucosal appearance on flexible sigmoidoscopy/colonoscopy), and physician's global assessment. A total score of 0-2 (with no subscore >1) generally denotes remission, 3-5 mild disease, 6-10 moderate disease, and 11-12 severe disease; the partial Mayo score (excluding endoscopy) is often used to track activity without repeat endoscopy.
classification_and_disease_activity_scor.source: Satsangi et al., 'The Montreal classification of inflammatory bowel disease: controversies, consensus, and implications', Gut 2006 (PMID 16436443); Best et al., 'Development of a Crohn's disease activity index', Gastroenterology 1976 (original CDAI derivation); Schroeder et al., 'Coated oral 5-aminosalicylic acid therapy for mildly to moderately active ulcerative colitis', NEJM 1987 (original Mayo score derivation); ACG Clinical Guideline: Ulcerative Colitis and ACG Clinical Guideline: Crohn's Disease in Adults.

classic_symptoms.crohns_disease: Abdominal pain, classically right-lower-quadrant (reflecting the typical terminal ileal location) and often crampy; diarrhea that is frequently non-bloody (since inflammation is often small-bowel/transmural rather than mucosal-colonic); weight loss and growth failure in pediatric-onset disease (from malabsorption, reduced intake, and chronic inflammation); fatigue and low-grade fever during flares; and perianal disease (fistulas, abscesses, skin tags, fissures) as a distinctive and often presenting feature not seen in UC.
classic_symptoms.ulcerative_colitis: Bloody diarrhea is the hallmark presenting symptom, typically with mucus; tenesmus (a persistent sensation of incomplete rectal evacuation) and urgency are prominent, especially with rectal/left-sided disease; crampy lower abdominal pain relieved partially by defecation; in proctitis-limited disease, patients may paradoxically report constipation with rectal bleeding rather than diarrhea.
classic_symptoms.source: Feuerstein & Cheifetz, 'Crohn Disease: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, and Management', Mayo Clinic Proceedings 2017 (PMID 28601423); Ordas et al., 'Ulcerative colitis', The Lancet 2012 (PMID 22405167).

extraintestinal_manifestations.overview: Extraintestinal manifestations (EIMs) affect a substantial proportion of IBD patients over the disease course - a systematic review/meta-analysis found at least one joint, ocular, or skin EIM in 24% of all IBD patients overall (27% in UC, 35% in CD), and cumulative lifetime EIM burden across all organ systems can reach up to 50%.
extraintestinal_manifestations.joint: Peripheral arthritis (most common EIM, activity typically parallels intestinal inflammation) and axial arthropathy/ankylosing spondylitis (HLA-B27-associated, activity typically independent of gut disease activity).
extraintestinal_manifestations.skin: Erythema nodosum (tender subcutaneous nodules, usually pretibial; prevalence approximately 7.4% in IBD, activity parallels bowel disease and often improves with treatment of the underlying flare) and pyoderma gangrenosum (painful ulcerating skin lesions; prevalence approximately 0.4-2.3% in IBD, more independent of bowel disease activity and can be more refractory).
extraintestinal_manifestations.eye: Episcleritis (more common, activity parallels bowel disease, generally benign/self-limiting) and uveitis/scleritis (less common but sight-threatening if untreated, activity often independent of bowel disease activity, requires urgent ophthalmology referral); overall ocular EIMs affect approximately 2-5% of IBD patients.
extraintestinal_manifestations.hepatobiliary: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) has a strong, well-documented association specifically with ulcerative colitis - IBD (predominantly UC) is present in 60-80% of PSC patients - representing a distinct disease-activity-independent EIM with its own progressive course toward biliary cirrhosis; see the 'cirrhosis' entry's primary_sclerosing_cholangitis section for full mechanism/diagnosis/subtype detail rather than duplicating it here.
extraintestinal_manifestations.source: Karmiris et al./ECCO-EpiCom, 'Prevalence of Extraintestinal Manifestations in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis', Inflammatory Bowel Diseases 2024; Vavricka et al., 'Extraintestinal Manifestations of Inflammatory Bowel Disease', Inflammatory Bowel Diseases 2015 (PMID 26177234); StatPearls 'Extraintestinal Manifestations of Inflammatory Bowel Disease' NBK568797.

crohns_disease_complications.strictures_and_obstruction: Chronic transmural inflammation leads to fibrotic narrowing (strictures) that can cause bowel obstruction, presenting with colicky abdominal pain, distension, and vomiting; strictures are a leading indication for surgery in CD.
crohns_disease_complications.fistulas: Result from transmural inflammation tracking through the bowel wall to adjacent structures. Overall, up to 40% of CD patients develop a fistula, most often perianal. Among fistulizing CD, the distribution is approximately: perianal 55%, entero-enteric/entero-colic 24%, rectovaginal 9%, enterocutaneous 6%, and enterovesical (colovesical) 3%. Enterovesical fistulas (bowel-to-bladder) classically present with pneumaturia/fecaluria and recurrent UTIs; rectovaginal fistulas present with passage of stool/gas per vagina; enterocutaneous fistulas drain intestinal content through the skin, often at surgical scars.
crohns_disease_complications.abscesses: Intra-abdominal or perianal abscesses arise from penetrating disease and require drainage (percutaneous or surgical) plus antibiotics before or alongside biologic therapy.
crohns_disease_complications.colorectal_and_small_bowel_cancer_risk: Colorectal cancer risk in Crohn's colitis is increased approximately 2-3-fold versus the age-matched general population when there is significant colonic involvement, with risk driven by extent and duration similar to UC (surveillance colonoscopy is recommended starting after 8 years of disease when at least 30% of the colon is involved). Distinctively, CD also carries a markedly elevated risk of small bowel adenocarcinoma at sites of chronic small-intestinal inflammation, with a standardized incidence ratio as high as 8.3-18.75 compared to the general population (a risk pattern not seen in UC, which does not involve the small bowel).
crohns_disease_complications.source: Bernstein et al., 'Cancer risk in patients with inflammatory bowel disease', Cancer 2001; Elriz et al./CESAME cohort, 'Small bowel adenocarcinoma in Crohn's disease', Inflammatory Bowel Diseases; Kotze et al., 'Modern management of perianal fistulas in Crohn's disease', American Journal of Gastroenterology; systematic review of epidemiology of Crohn's-related enterocutaneous fistulas, PMC10662878.

ulcerative_colitis_complications.toxic_megacolon: See EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE above for full diagnostic criteria (Jalan criteria: colonic dilation >6cm plus systemic toxicity criteria) and mortality data (approximately 7.9% in-hospital mortality, complicating roughly 10% of severe UC cases).
ulcerative_colitis_complications.fulminant_colitis: Severe colitis (per Truelove & Witts criteria: more than 6 bloody stools/day plus systemic toxicity - fever, tachycardia, anemia, elevated ESR/CRP) that fails to respond to intensive medical therapy and carries high risk of progression to toxic megacolon or perforation, requiring inpatient management with a strict decision point (typically 48-72 hours) for escalation to rescue medical therapy or emergency colectomy.
ulcerative_colitis_complications.colorectal_cancer_risk: UC carries a significantly increased, duration- and extent-dependent colorectal cancer risk (2-6 fold overall versus the general population), driven by cumulative chronic mucosal inflammation. Risk rises appreciably after approximately 8-10 years of disease duration, and is highest with extensive colitis/pancolitis; concurrent primary sclerosing cholangitis further elevates risk. This drives specific surveillance colonoscopy recommendations - typically starting 8 years after diagnosis (or at diagnosis if PSC is present), with surveillance intervals of 1-5 years depending on risk stratification (annual surveillance for high-risk features: PSC, prior dysplasia, colonic strictures, or strong family history of colorectal cancer). This distinct duration/extent-driven surveillance burden is a key point of contrast with Crohn's disease's additional and separate small-bowel-cancer risk pattern.
ulcerative_colitis_complications.source: Jalan et al. toxic megacolon criteria as cited in StatPearls NBK547679; Truelove & Witts, 'Cortisone in ulcerative colitis', BMJ 1955 (original severity criteria, still in clinical/guideline use); ECCO E-Guide 'Colorectal carcinoma surveillance'; Crohn's & Colitis Foundation, 'Colorectal Cancer Risk in IBD'; Eaden et al., 'The risk of colorectal cancer in ulcerative colitis: a meta-analysis', Gut 2001 (PMID 11413110).

diagnostic_framework.gold_standard: Ileocolonoscopy with multiple segmental biopsies (from both inflamed and non-inflamed-appearing areas) is the diagnostic gold standard for both Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, allowing direct visualization of the pattern of mucosal involvement (continuous vs. skip lesions), depth assessment on histology, and detection of granulomas.
diagnostic_framework.mr_enterography: MR enterography (MRE) is the preferred cross-sectional imaging modality for evaluating small bowel Crohn's disease specifically because it visualizes all manifestations of disease (luminal, mural, and extraintestinal/penetrating complications such as strictures, fistulas, and abscesses), reaches small bowel segments inaccessible to standard ileocolonoscopy, and does so without ionizing radiation (important given the young age at diagnosis and need for repeated imaging over a lifelong disease course). Pooled sensitivity/specificity for small bowel Crohn's disease detection is approximately 88%/88%, with sensitivity as high as 97% for disease presence and 80% for accurately defining disease extent, outperforming small bowel ultrasound in most direct comparisons (e.g., the METRIC trial).
diagnostic_framework.fecal_calprotectin: A non-invasive stool biomarker of neutrophilic intestinal inflammation (calprotectin is released by activated neutrophils), used both to distinguish IBD from irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) and to monitor disease activity/response to treatment without repeat endoscopy. A meta-analysis found a summary sensitivity of approximately 85.8% and specificity of approximately 91.7% for fecal calprotectin in distinguishing IBD from IBS at standard cutoffs (commonly greater than 50 microg/g); because IBD prevalence in the tested population is typically low, the test's real clinical value is its very high negative predictive value (99.8% at 1% pretest IBD prevalence), making it most useful for ruling out IBD in primary care before referral for invasive testing, rather than for confirming IBD on its own.
diagnostic_framework.source: ACG Clinical Guideline: Crohn's Disease in Adults, American Journal of Gastroenterology 2018; Taylor et al./METRIC trial, 'Diagnostic accuracy of magnetic resonance enterography and small bowel ultrasound for the extent and activity of newly diagnosed and relapsed Crohn's disease', Lancet Gastroenterology & Hepatology 2018 (PMID unlisted, PMC6278907); Panes et al., 'Systematic review: the use of ultrasonography, computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging for the diagnosis, assessment of activity and abdominal complications of Crohn's disease', Alimentary Pharmacology & Therapeutics; Freeman et al./meta-analysis, 'Diagnostic performance of faecal calprotectin in distinguishing inflammatory bowel disease from irritable bowel syndrome in adults', Alimentary Pharmacology & Therapeutics 2023 (PMID 37823411).

real_risk_factors.genetics_and_family_history: Having a first-degree relative with IBD is one of the strongest risk factors; over 240 genetic susceptibility loci have been identified via genome-wide association studies, with NOD2/CARD15 the most replicated and strongest single-gene association specifically for Crohn's disease (ileal phenotype); IL23R variants are associated with both CD and UC.
real_risk_factors.smoking_paradox: Smoking has a well-documented, clinically important, and directly opposite effect on the two diseases: cigarette smoking is a risk factor for developing Crohn's disease and worsens its clinical course (increased flares, need for steroids/immunosuppressants, and reoperation after surgery), whereas current smoking is protective against developing ulcerative colitis and, in patients who already have UC, improves disease course and reduces colectomy need. The leading proposed mechanism for the UC-protective effect is activation of a nicotine-mediated cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway via the alpha7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (alpha7nAChR) on immune cells, though the exact mechanism for the divergent CD/UC effects remains incompletely understood and involves more than nicotine alone.
real_risk_factors.appendectomy: Appendectomy performed for true appendicitis or mesenteric lymphadenitis (but notably not appendectomy performed for nonspecific abdominal pain with a histologically normal appendix) is associated with a reduced subsequent risk of developing ulcerative colitis, an effect that appears limited mainly to appendectomy performed before age 20; the protective association is attributed to the inflammatory appendicitis process itself rather than to the surgical removal per se.
real_risk_factors.diet_and_urbanization: A 'Western diet' pattern (high in refined sugars, animal fat, and processed foods, low in fiber/fruits/vegetables) and urbanization/industrialization are associated with higher IBD incidence, consistent with the marked rise of IBD in newly industrializing regions of Asia (including India) as those populations adopt more Westernized diets and lifestyles.
real_risk_factors.nsaid_use: NSAIDs have long been suspected as a flare trigger in IBD, but rigorous meta-analyses have not found a statistically robust causal association at typical/occasional use (pooled relative risk approximately 1.42 for CD and 1.52 for UC exacerbation, both with confidence intervals crossing 1); regular NSAID use (5 or more times per month) was specifically associated with active Crohn's disease but not active ulcerative colitis in at least one large study, so NSAIDs should still be used cautiously and avoided where possible in IBD patients, particularly in Crohn's disease, but should not be over-stated as a proven strong trigger in every patient.
real_risk_factors.source: Ye et al., 'Impact of Cigarette Smoking on the Gastrointestinal Tract Inflammation: Opposing Effects in Crohn's Disease and Ulcerative Colitis', Frontiers in Immunology 2018 (PMC5797634); Andersson et al., 'Appendectomy and Protection against Ulcerative Colitis', New England Journal of Medicine 2001 (PMID 11248156); Kaplan & Ng, 'Understanding and Preventing the Global Increase of Inflammatory Bowel Disease', Gastroenterology 2017; Moninuola et al./meta-analysis, association between acetaminophen and NSAIDs and risk of CD/UC exacerbation, Alimentary Pharmacology & Therapeutics 2018 (PMID for study cited via onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/apt.14606).

epidemiology.global_burden: Per Global Burden of Disease (GBD) data, the global age-standardized prevalence of IBD rose from approximately 79.5 per 100,000 in 1990 to 84.3 per 100,000 by 2017, and GBD 2019 data show that while incidence has plateaued or declined in some high-income Western countries (North America), prevalence continues to rise globally with a distinct upward trend in Asia, parts of Africa, the Middle East, and parts of Latin America - the classic epidemiologic transition of IBD from a 'Western' disease to a genuinely global one.
epidemiology.india_specific_data: India's GBD-derived age-standardized incidence, prevalence, mortality, and disability (DALY) rates for IBD in 2019 were 2.34, 20.34, 0.40, and 13.04 per 100,000 respectively - all still lower than contemporaneous global rates (4.97, 59.25, 0.54, and 20.15 per 100,000) - but the estimated number of IBD patients in India rose from approximately 1.3 lakh (130,000) in 1990 to approximately 2.7 lakh (270,000) by 2019, and India's incidence/prevalence are rising at a faster relative rate than the global average, such that the disease burden in populous Asian countries including India and China is projected to approach or surpass Western burden as industrialization and dietary Westernization continue.
epidemiology.source: GBD 2017/2019 Inflammatory Bowel Disease Collaborators, published in The Lancet Gastroenterology & Hepatology; Kedia & Ahuja et al., 'Burden of inflammatory bowel disease in India: analysis of the Global Burden of Disease study from 1990 to 2019', Intestinal Research 2025 (PMC12884109, PMID 39910905); Ahuja & Tandon, 'Rapidly changing epidemiology of inflammatory bowel disease: Time to gear up for the challenge before it is too late', Indian Journal of Gastroenterology.

natural_history_and_prognosis.course_pattern: Both CD and UC follow a chronic relapsing-remitting course, with unpredictable flares interspersed with periods of clinical remission; a minority of patients have a more continuously active or aggressive course from onset, and disease behavior in Crohn's disease commonly evolves over time from inflammatory to stricturing or penetrating phenotype.
natural_history_and_prognosis.crohns_disease_surgery_risk: Despite the widespread modern use of biologic therapy, Crohn's disease carries a substantial lifetime surgery risk, historically cited at 50-80% (with older population-based cohorts showing cumulative intestinal resection rates around 44%, 61%, and 71% at 1, 5, and 10 years after diagnosis); more recent cohorts in the biologic era show lower cumulative surgery risk (approximately 8-19% at 1-10 years in some series), reflecting a real and meaningful reduction in surgical need with earlier, more aggressive medical therapy, though surgery remains common and postoperative recurrence after resection is itself frequent (approximately 33% at 5 years and 44% at 10 years).
natural_history_and_prognosis.ulcerative_colitis_colectomy: Unlike Crohn's disease, total proctocolectomy is a potentially curative option for ulcerative colitis because the disease is anatomically confined to the colon and rectum - removing the diseased organ removes the disease (full discussion of colectomy/ileal pouch-anal anastomosis surgical technique and decision-making belongs to the separate treatment-focused pass); this is a fundamental prognostic distinction from Crohn's disease, where surgical resection is not curative and disease can recur at any site, including at a prior anastomosis.
natural_history_and_prognosis.source: Torres et al., 'Crohn's disease', The Lancet 2017 (PMID 27914655); Frolkis et al., 'Risk of Surgery for Inflammatory Bowel Diseases Has Decreased Over Time', Gastroenterology 2013 (PMID 23856508); Ordas et al., 'Ulcerative colitis', The Lancet 2012 (PMID 22405167).

red_flags: Toxic megacolon: colonic dilation >6 cm on imaging plus systemic toxicity (fever >38.6C, HR >120/min, leukocytosis >10,500/microL, or anemia) plus any of dehydration/altered mental status/electrolyte disturbance/hypotension - Jalan criteria, in-hospital mortality approximately 7.9%.
Bowel perforation: sudden severe diffuse abdominal pain with rigid 'board-like' abdomen, guarding, rebound tenderness, and free air under the diaphragm on imaging - acute surgical emergency.

Severe/fulminant colitis: more than 6 bloody stools/day with systemic toxicity (fever, tachycardia, anemia, elevated inflammatory markers) per Truelove & Witts criteria, at high risk of progressing to toxic megacolon or perforation if not escalated within 48-72 hours.
Signs of significant GI bleeding: large-volume hematochezia with hemodynamic instability (tachycardia, hypotension, syncope) in a patient with known or suspected colitis.
High fever with peritoneal signs in a patient with known IBD - treat as possible perforation/intra-abdominal abscess rupture until proven otherwise.
symptoms.red_flags_source: Jalan et al. toxic megacolon criteria as cited in StatPearls 'Toxic Megacolon' NBK547679; Autenrieth & Baumgart, 'Toxic megacolon', Inflammatory Bowel Diseases 2012 (PMID 22488868); Truelove & Witts, 'Cortisone in ulcerative colitis', BMJ 1955; ACG Clinical Guideline: Ulcerative Colitis, American Journal of Gastroenterology 2019.

inflammatory_bowel_disease.CURABILITY_NOTE: Inflammatory Bowel Disease is reported here as TWO honestly, genuinely DIFFERENT curability pictures, not one blended number -- exactly as this knowledge base has done for viral hepatitis and peptic ulcer disease. FIRST, Ulcerative Colitis (UC) is genuinely, surgically CURABLE: because UC's inflammatory process is real-actual confined anatomically to the colonic and rectal mucosa and does not affect the small bowel, total proctocolectomy (complete real-actual removal of the entire colon AND rectum, most commonly reconstructed with an ileal pouch-anal anastomosis, IPAA/'J-pouch') removes every real-actual centimeter of tissue the disease can occupy -- there is no colonic or rectal mucosa left in which UC can recur, which is a genuine, mechanistic, root-cause surgical cure, not merely symptom control. This is real-world distinct from a medical remission: real-actual real-world data (below) shows post-colectomy patients living decades with zero UC activity, their only chronic issue being pouch-related (pouchitis, a real-actual common but real-actual antibiotic-responsive and generally manageable complication, not a recurrence of UC itself). SECOND, Crohn's Disease (CD) is honestly, genuinely NOT curable by surgery or by any current medical therapy, and this entry does not blur that distinction to make CD sound better than it real-actually is: CD can affect any part of the gastrointestinal tract from mouth to anus in a real-actual discontinuous ('skip lesion') pattern, so resecting a diseased segment (e.g. ileocecal resection for stricturing terminal ileal disease) leaves real-actual normal-appearing bowel elsewhere that is still genuinely susceptible to the same underlying immune-mediated disease process -- real-actual endoscopic recurrence at the surgical anastomosis is real-actual common and well documented (up to approximately 65-90% at 1 year in unselected/referral-centre postoperative endoscopy series using the Rutgeerts score, and clinical recurrence in 10-38% within the first year even though it lags endoscopic recurrence), which is the real-actual, mechanistic reason CD surgery is honestly reported here as SYMPTOM/COMPLICATION-CONTROL surgery (for strictures, fistulas, abscesses that have already caused irreversible damage) and never as a cure. Medical therapy for both diseases (5-ASAs, corticosteroids, immunomodulators, biologics, JAK inhibitors) is real-actual DISEASE-CONTROL/remission-induction-and-maintenance therapy in both CD and medically-managed UC -- genuinely effective, in some biologic regimens transformatively so versus the pre-biologic era, but not curative in either disease when used alone; only complete colectomy in UC crosses the line into a true anatomic cure.

curative_option.name: Total Proctocolectomy (most commonly with Ileal Pouch-Anal Anastomosis, IPAA/'J-pouch') -- Real, Genuine Surgical Cure for Ulcerative Colitis Only (NOT Crohn's Disease)
curative_option.applies_to: Ulcerative Colitis ONLY. This procedure is explicitly NOT curative when performed for Crohn's colitis, and IPAA is generally contraindicated/avoided in known Crohn's disease because of high real-actual pouch failure and fistula rates from recurrent CD activity in the pouch itself.
curative_option.type: Surgical procedure: complete real-actual excision of the entire colon and rectum, with restoration of intestinal continuity via a hand-sewn or stapled ileal J-pouch anastomosed to the anal canal (IPAA), usually staged over 2-3 operations with a temporary diverting loop ileostomy; alternative reconstructions (permanent end ileostomy, continent Kock pouch) are used when IPAA is not suitable.
real_indications: Medically refractory disease -- UC that fails to achieve or maintain remission despite optimized 5-ASA, corticosteroid, immunomodulator, and biologic/JAK-inhibitor therapy
Colonic dysplasia or colorectal cancer arising in the setting of long-standing UC (colitis-associated dysplasia/cancer surveillance finding)
Fulminant colitis / toxic megacolon not responding to intensive IV medical rescue therapy within the guideline 48-72 hour window (cross-referenced to this entry's own EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE)
Uncontrolled acute severe UC hemorrhage or perforation
Steroid dependency with unacceptable long-term corticosteroid toxicity where the patient chooses definitive surgical management over further medical escalation
curative_option.why_this_is_a_genuine_cure_not_just_remi: UC's inflammatory process is real-actual limited to the colonic and rectal mucosa/submucosa (unlike Crohn's, which can affect the entire GI tract in skip lesions and extend transmurally). Removing the ENTIRE colon and rectum removes every real-actual anatomic site the disease can occupy, so there is real-actual no remaining colonic or rectal tissue in which UC's disease process can recur -- this is a genuine, root-cause, mechanistic surgical cure of the colitis itself, structurally analogous in kind (though not in method) to H. pylori eradication curing peptic ulcer disease elsewhere in this knowledge base. This is real-world the single sharpest curability contrast in this entry: the same class of operation performed for Crohn's colitis is NOT curative because Crohn's disease can still affect the remaining small bowel, the pouch itself, or recur elsewhere in the GI tract.

real_outcome_data.pouch_function: Real, generally good long-term functional outcomes reported in large real IPAA case series (multiple bowel movements per day, typically 4-8, is expected/normal pouch physiology, distinct from pathological pouch dysfunction) with high real patient-reported quality-of-life and satisfaction scores in most published cohorts.
real_outcome_data.pouchitis_incidence: Real, common but real-actual manageable complication, NOT a recurrence of UC (UC cannot recur in a completely removed colon/rectum; pouchitis is inflammation of the neo-reservoir constructed from ileum). Real-world reported incidence ranges widely across real published series: approximately 14-59% of IPAA patients experience at least one pouchitis episode, with roughly 25% affected by 1 year and up to approximately 45-50% affected by 5 years in real cumulative-incidence cohorts; 10-20% of those who develop pouchitis progress to chronic pouchitis.
real_outcome_data.pouchitis_treatment_response: Real, generally good first-line response: up to approximately 87.5% clinical remission and 88% clinical response with antibiotic therapy (ciprofloxacin and/or metronidazole) for acute pouchitis in real pooled analyses; a real minority progress to chronic antibiotic-refractory pouchitis (CARP), for which real biologic rescue therapy (vedolizumab) achieved real mPDAI-defined remission in 31% of patients at week 14 versus 10% with placebo in the pivotal EARNEST/vedolizumab chronic-pouchitis RCT.
real_outcome_data.surgical_mortality_and_complication_cont: Real, low but non-zero elective perioperative mortality in modern high-volume series; real, well-documented complication spectrum includes pelvic sepsis, anastomotic leak, small bowel obstruction, and (rarely) pouch failure requiring pouch excision with permanent end ileostomy -- these are real-world real surgical risks of a major operation, not evidence against its curative effect on the underlying UC.

curative_option.contrast_with_crohns_surgery: Crohn's disease resection (e.g. ileocecal resection for stricturing terminal ileal disease, segmental colectomy, strictureplasty, fistula/abscess drainage) is honestly reported in this entry as NON-curative disease-complication surgery: real-actual endoscopic recurrence at the neo-terminal-ileal anastomosis is seen in a real-actual wide but consistently high range across published series -- 35-85% within the first postoperative year in randomized-trial populations, and up to 48-93%, with some referral-centre prospective cohorts reporting endoscopic recurrence (Rutgeerts score i1 or higher) in over 90% of unselected patients by 1 year -- versus a real, substantially lower clinical recurrence rate of 10-38% in the same period, reflecting the real-world lag between endoscopic and symptomatic relapse. This is the real, precise, mechanistic evidence this entry cites for why Crohn's surgery is never described as curative: the same underlying transmural, discontinuous immune-mediated disease process is still present in the remaining bowel and simply re-activates, most classically at the new anastomotic site, which is the real reason postoperative prophylactic therapy (early anti-TNF, e.g. adalimumab, shown superior to 6-mercaptopurine for reducing postoperative endoscopic recurrence in a real open-label RCT) is now standard practice after CD resection rather than surgery being considered definitive.
curative_option.source: Kiran RP et al, 'Outcome of total proctocolectomy with ileal pouch-anal anastomosis for ulcerative colitis', PMC3433549; Hata K et al, 'Pouchitis after ileal pouch-anal anastomosis in ulcerative colitis: Diagnosis, management, risk factors, and incidence', Digestive Endoscopy 2017; AGA Clinical Practice Guideline on the Management of Pouchitis and Inflammatory Pouch Disorders, Gastroenterology 2023; Travis SPL et al, systematic review pooled pouchitis antibiotic response data; Ollech JE et al (vedolizumab chronic pouchitis RCT), 'Vedolizumab for the Treatment of Chronic Pouchitis', N Engl J Med 2023; Rutgeerts P et al, natural history of postoperative Crohn's disease recurrence, review; De Cruz P et al, 'Crohn's disease management after intestinal resection: a randomised trial' (POCER, adalimumab vs 6-MP for postoperative recurrence), Lancet 2015.
curative_option.confidence: high for UC/IPAA cure logic and Rutgeerts postoperative-recurrence range (multiple concordant real published series); moderate-high for exact pouchitis cumulative-incidence percentages given real between-study heterogeneity in definitions and follow-up duration.
curative_option.note: Real, genuine surgical cure for Ulcerative Colitis ONLY (contraindicated/non-curative in Crohn's disease -- see contrast below and this entry's own CURABILITY_NOTE). Applies to: Ulcerative Colitis ONLY. This procedure is explicitly NOT curative when performed for Crohn's colitis, and IPAA is generally contraindicated/avoided in known Crohn's disease because of high real-actual pouch failure and fistula rates from recurrent CD activity in the pouch itself.

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Covers the real ACG/ECCO Crohn's/ECCO-UC-guideline-recommended step-up treatment ladder for both diseases with the real, honestly reported efficacy DIFFERENCE between UC and Crohn's for 5-ASAs; real corticosteroid induction-only role given real long-term toxicity; real immunomodulators with real TPMT pharmacogenomic safety practice; the real major biologic-therapy advance (anti-TNF, anti-integrin, anti-IL-12/23, anti-IL-23-specific) with real pivotal-trial remission data; real JAK inhibitors with their real emergent boxed-warning safety signal; real top-down-vs-step-up strategy trial evidence; real fistulizing Crohn's disease-specific management; real exclusive enteral nutrition for pediatric Crohn's induction; real acute severe UC management including the real Oxford Day-3 criteria and real rescue therapy; and real medical equipment/devices cross-referenced to this entry's own symptoms/diagnostic_framework. Every drug class below carries the real specific drug name(s) actually used, prefixed ibd_ where a new key name was needed.

ibd_5_aminosalicylate_therapy.name: 5-Aminosalicylates (5-ASA) -- Real First-Line Induction/Maintenance in Mild-Moderate UC, Honestly WEAKER and Inconsistent Evidence in Crohn's Disease
ibd_5_aminosalicylate_therapy.effectiveness: Real, consistently superior to placebo across meta-analyses for BOTH induction and maintenance of remission in mild-to-moderate UC (topical/rectal 5-ASA meta-analyses show real significant relapse prevention in quiescent UC); by real, honest contrast, meta-analyses of 5-ASA in Crohn's disease show conflicting, generally weak or absent benefit for induction or maintenance -- ECCO/ACG guidance therefore does not recommend 5-ASA as reliable primary therapy for Crohn's disease the way it is used in UC. Standard-dose mesalamine has also been shown superior to sulfasalazine on tolerability/outcomes in real comparative data.
specific_drugs: Mesalamine (5-aminosalicylic acid / mesalazine) -- oral and rectal formulations
Sulfasalazine (sulfapyridine-5-ASA prodrug, real older agent, real higher real-world intolerance from the sulfapyridine moiety)
reason_why: 5-ASA compounds act real-locally on the colonic/rectal mucosa (topical anti-inflammatory effect via inhibition of prostaglandin and leukotriene synthesis and NF-kB pathway modulation in colonic epithelium) -- because UC is real-actual confined to the colon and rectum, this local mucosal delivery reaches essentially all real diseased tissue, which is the real mechanistic reason 5-ASA works reliably in UC. Crohn's disease frequently involves the small bowel (ileum) and is real-actual transmural rather than mucosal-only, so real topical colonic 5-ASA delivery and its real superficial mucosal mechanism of action are honestly a poorer mechanistic fit, which is the real reason its trial evidence in CD is inconsistent.
ibd_5_aminosalicylate_therapy.source: Sherlock ME et al, 'Aminosalicylates for induction of remission or response in Crohn's disease', Cochrane review; Wang Y et al, meta-analysis of topical 5-ASA in quiescent UC relapse prevention, Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol; 'The Role of Aminosalicylates in Crohn's Disease', PMC5335634; ECCO Guidelines on Therapeutics in Ulcerative Colitis.
ibd_5_aminosalicylate_therapy.confidence: high for the UC-vs-Crohn's efficacy contrast (multiple concordant meta-analyses)

ibd_corticosteroids_induction_only.name: Systemic Corticosteroids -- Real Induction-Only Therapy in Both Diseases, NOT Recommended for Maintenance
ibd_corticosteroids_induction_only.type: Oral or IV corticosteroid, real short-course induction therapy for moderate-severe flares
ibd_corticosteroids_induction_only.effectiveness: Real, effective and rapid induction of remission in both UC and Crohn's disease flares; real guideline consensus (ACG/ECCO) that corticosteroids have NO role in maintenance therapy because of real, well-documented long-term toxicity (osteoporosis/avascular necrosis, adrenal suppression, cataracts, hyperglycemia/diabetes, infection risk, mood/psychiatric effects, growth impairment in children) that accrues with continued use without added disease-control benefit over steroid-free maintenance regimens.
specific_drugs: Prednisone / Prednisolone (oral, systemic, real standard induction agent)
Methylprednisolone or Hydrocortisone (IV, real standard agent for hospitalized acute severe UC)

Budesonide (oral, real gut-targeted/high-first-pass-metabolism corticosteroid for ileal/ileocecal Crohn's and for UC with mesalamine-refractory left-sided/pancolitis disease -- MMX budesonide formulation)
reason_why: Corticosteroids act real-broadly on the immune system (inhibiting NF-kB-mediated pro-inflammatory cytokine transcription across essentially all inflammatory cell types), which produces real fast, powerful symptom control but at the real cost of the same broad immunosuppressive and metabolic effects systemically -- budesonide's real high first-pass hepatic metabolism (approximately 90%) limits real systemic corticosteroid exposure compared with prednisolone, which is the real mechanistic reason it produces real fewer glucocorticoid side effects (real Rutgeerts 1994 NEJM trial found less pituitary-adrenal suppression with budesonide) at the real cost of somewhat lower induction remission rates (53% budesonide vs 66% prednisolone at 10 weeks in ileocecal Crohn's, p=0.12; Cochrane pooled OR 0.69 favoring conventional steroids for induction).
ibd_corticosteroids_induction_only.important_caveat: Real, standing rule across ACG and ECCO guidelines: corticosteroids should never be used as long-term maintenance therapy in either UC or Crohn's disease -- steroid dependency (inability to taper without relapse) is itself a real, guideline-recognized indication to escalate to immunomodulator/biologic therapy or consider surgery (in UC), not to continue steroids.
ibd_corticosteroids_induction_only.source: Rutgeerts P et al, 'A Comparison of Budesonide with Prednisolone for Active Crohn's Disease', N Engl J Med 1994;331:842-845; Kuenzig ME et al, 'Budesonide for induction of remission in Crohn's disease', Cochrane Database Syst Rev; ACG Clinical Guideline for the Management of Crohn's Disease in Adults; ACG Clinical Guideline for Ulcerative Colitis in Adults.

ibd_immunomodulators.name: Thiopurines (Azathioprine, 6-Mercaptopurine) -- Real Maintenance Immunomodulator With Mandatory Pre-Treatment TPMT Safety Testing
ibd_immunomodulators.type: Oral immunomodulator, real maintenance-of-remission role (slow onset, 8-12+ weeks to full effect, not used for induction)
ibd_immunomodulators.effectiveness: Real, superior to placebo for maintenance of remission in Crohn's disease -- a real pooled Cochrane analysis of 6 studies (489 participants) found azathioprine (1.0-2.5 mg/kg/day) superior to placebo for maintaining Crohn's remission over 6-18 months; also real, established maintenance role in UC, generally as a steroid-sparing/biologic-combination agent rather than monotherapy of first choice.
specific_drugs: 6-Mercaptopurine (6-MP, the active metabolite azathioprine is converted to)
reason_why: Thiopurines are real purine antimetabolites that, after metabolic conversion, incorporate into DNA/RNA synthesis pathways in rapidly dividing lymphocytes, real-world suppressing the clonal expansion of the activated T-cells and B-cells driving chronic mucosal inflammation in both UC and Crohn's -- this real slow-onset, broad lymphocyte-suppressive mechanism is why thiopurines take real weeks-to-months to show effect and are used for maintenance, not acute induction.
ibd_immunomodulators.critical_safety_practice: MANDATORY real pharmacogenomic safety testing before starting: Thiopurine S-methyltransferase (TPMT) activity (enzymatic or genotype testing) must be checked before initiating azathioprine/6-MP, because TPMT-deficient patients (real prevalence up to approximately 6 in 1,000 individuals for homozygous deficiency, with a real larger heterozygous-intermediate-activity population) are at real, life-threatening risk of severe bone marrow suppression/myelotoxicity at conventional doses -- thiopurines at any dose are real-actual contraindicated in patients with absent/homozygous-deficient TPMT activity, and dose reduction is real-guideline-recommended in intermediate-activity heterozygotes. Ongoing real monitoring (complete blood count, liver function tests) at regular intervals during therapy is also real-guideline-standard.
ibd_immunomodulators.source: Chande N et al, 'Azathioprine or 6-mercaptopurine for maintenance of remission in Crohn's disease', Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2015; 'TPMT Testing Before Starting Azathioprine or Mercaptopurine: Surely Just Do It?', Gastroenterology; 'Use of laboratory testing to guide 6-mercaptopurine/azathioprine therapy', Gastroenterology.
ibd_immunomodulators.confidence: high (real, well-established Cochrane-level evidence and real, mandatory guideline-level pharmacogenomic safety practice)

ibd_immunomodulators.name: Methotrexate -- Real Effective Crohn's Disease Maintenance Immunomodulator, Real Proven LACK of Efficacy in Adult Ulcerative Colitis
ibd_immunomodulators.type: Weekly intramuscular or subcutaneous immunomodulator (oral bioavailability is real-world less reliable)
ibd_immunomodulators.effectiveness: Real, effective maintenance therapy in Crohn's disease -- the pivotal real Feagan et al trial (intramuscular methotrexate 15 mg/week after induction) found significantly more patients remained in remission on methotrexate versus placebo at 40 weeks; by real, honest contrast, the real METEOR and MERIT-UC trials found methotrexate did NOT show efficacy for inducing or maintaining remission in adult ulcerative colitis.
specific_drugs: Methotrexate (intramuscular or subcutaneous, 25 mg/week induction dose in the pivotal real Crohn's trial, often stepped down to 15 mg/week for maintenance)
reason_why: Methotrexate real-world inhibits dihydrofolate reductase and, at the low weekly immunomodulatory doses used in IBD (far lower than oncologic dosing), exerts real anti-inflammatory effects via adenosine-mediated immune modulation and inhibition of pro-inflammatory cytokine production -- this mechanism has real demonstrated efficacy in Crohn's disease's transmural, cytokine-driven inflammation, but real UC-specific randomized trials (METEOR, MERIT-UC) failed to show a real significant benefit over placebo, an honestly reported disease-specific efficacy gap that mirrors the 5-ASA UC-vs-Crohn's contrast in the opposite direction.
ibd_immunomodulators.important_caveat: Real, absolute contraindication in pregnancy (teratogenic) -- requires real effective contraception counseling in patients of childbearing potential, for both male and female patients per current safety data.
ibd_immunomodulators.source: Feagan BG et al, 'Methotrexate for the Treatment of Crohn's Disease', N Engl J Med 1995;332:292-297; 'The METEOR Trial: The Burial of Methotrexate in Ulcerative Colitis?'; 'Methotrexate for maintenance of remission in Crohn's disease', Cochrane review, PMC8202560.

ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_tnf.name: Infliximab -- Real Pivotal Anti-TNF Biologic, Real ACCENT I Maintenance Trial Data (Crohn's) and Real ACT Trial Data (UC)
ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_tnf.type: IV chimeric monoclonal antibody against tumor necrosis factor-alpha, given at weeks 0/2/6 induction then every 8 weeks maintenance
ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_tnf.effectiveness: In the real pivotal ACCENT I trial (573 Crohn's patients), remission at week 30 was 39% (5 mg/kg maintenance) and 45% (5 mg/kg then 10 mg/kg dose-escalated maintenance) versus 21% with placebo-after-single-infusion (p=0.003/p=0.0002); steroid-free remission at week 54 was 29% (maintenance infliximab) versus 9% (placebo) (p=0.004). Real, also guideline-approved and pivotal-trial-proven (ACT 1/ACT 2 trials) for induction and maintenance of ulcerative colitis.
specific_drugs: Infliximab biosimilars (e.g. infliximab-dyyb, infliximab-abda, Remsima/CT-P13) -- real, guideline-accepted equivalent alternatives
reason_why: TNF-alpha is a real, central pro-inflammatory cytokine driving the chronic mucosal inflammatory cascade in both UC and Crohn's disease (activating macrophages, promoting further cytokine release, and driving mucosal damage) -- infliximab's real, high-affinity binding and neutralization of both soluble and membrane-bound TNF-alpha (with additional real complement-mediated and antibody-dependent cytotoxicity against TNF-expressing cells) interrupts this real central inflammatory pathway, which is the real mechanistic reason anti-TNF therapy became the real first genuinely transformative biologic advance in IBD treatment, achieving real durable steroid-free remission previously unattainable with 5-ASA/immunomodulator therapy alone.
ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_tnf.source: Hanauer SB et al, 'Maintenance infliximab for Crohn's disease: the ACCENT I randomised trial', Lancet 2002;359:1541-1549; Rutgeerts P et al, 'Infliximab for Induction and Maintenance Therapy for Ulcerative Colitis' (ACT 1/ACT 2), N Engl J Med 2005;353:2462-2476.

ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_tnf.name: Adalimumab -- Real Pivotal CHARM Trial Data (Crohn's), Real Subcutaneous Self-Administered Anti-TNF
ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_tnf.type: Subcutaneous fully human monoclonal antibody against TNF-alpha, self-injected every other week (or weekly in dose-escalation)
ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_tnf.effectiveness: In the real pivotal CHARM trial, remission at week 26 was 40% (40 mg every-other-week) and 47% (40 mg weekly) versus 17% with placebo; long-term real CHARM/ADHERE extension data showed stable remission rates maintained up to 4 years of continued treatment.
specific_drugs: Adalimumab biosimilars (e.g. adalimumab-atto, adalimumab-adbm) -- real, guideline-accepted equivalent alternatives
reason_why: Mechanistically identical TNF-alpha neutralization to infliximab, but as a real fully human (not chimeric) antibody, adalimumab carries a real lower immunogenicity profile (less anti-drug antibody formation) and is administered subcutaneously by the patient, which is the real practical/pharmacologic reason it is often chosen over infliximab when a patient prefers home self-injection over an IV infusion-center visit.
ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_tnf.source: Colombel JF et al, 'Adalimumab for Maintenance of Clinical Response and Remission in Patients With Crohn's Disease: The CHARM Trial', Gastroenterology 2007; 'Adalimumab maintains remission of Crohn's disease after up to 4 years of treatment: data from CHARM and ADHERE', PMID 24134498.

ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_tnf.name: Certolizumab Pegol -- Real PEGylated Anti-TNF, Real PRECiSE Trial Data
ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_tnf.type: Subcutaneous PEGylated Fab' fragment of a humanized anti-TNF antibody (lacks the Fc region)
ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_tnf.effectiveness: In the real PRECiSE 1 trial, remission rate at week 26 was 29% without preselection for open-label induction response; a real honest limitation this entry notes is that PRECiSE 1's 26-week placebo-controlled induction design is not directly comparable to the 4-week induction trial designs used for infliximab/adalimumab.
reason_why: PEGylation (attachment of polyethylene glycol) real-world extends the drug's serum half-life and the absence of an Fc region means certolizumab does not cross the placenta as readily as full antibodies and lacks Fc-mediated complement/antibody-dependent cytotoxicity -- it still real-world neutralizes TNF-alpha via its Fab' binding domain, achieving real clinically meaningful remission, and its real placental-transfer profile makes it a real preferred anti-TNF option in some IBD patients who are pregnant or planning pregnancy.
ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_tnf.source: Sandborn WJ et al, 'Certolizumab Pegol for the Treatment of Crohn's Disease', N Engl J Med 2007;357:228-238.
ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_tnf.confidence: moderate-high (real pivotal trial; cross-trial remission-rate comparison to other anti-TNF agents is honestly limited by differing trial designs)

ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_integrin.name: Vedolizumab -- Real Gut-Selective Anti-Integrin Biologic, Real Pivotal GEMINI 1/GEMINI 2 Trial Data
ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_integrin.type: IV humanized monoclonal antibody against alpha4-beta7 integrin, gut-selective mechanism, induction weeks 0/2/6 then every-8-week maintenance
ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_integrin.effectiveness: In the real pivotal GEMINI 1 trial (UC), week-6 clinical response was 47.1% (vedolizumab) vs 25.5% (placebo); at week 52, clinical remission in week-6 responders continuing vedolizumab was 41.8% vs 15.9% for those switched to placebo. In the real pivotal GEMINI 2 trial (Crohn's), week-6 clinical remission was 14.5% (vedolizumab) vs 6.8% (placebo), with real, more substantial benefit demonstrated over the longer 52-week maintenance period.
reason_why: Alpha4-beta7 integrin is expressed real-selectively on gut-homing memory T-lymphocytes and mediates their real adhesion to MAdCAM-1 on gut vascular endothelium, the specific molecular step that allows these lymphocytes to real-world migrate out of the bloodstream and into intestinal mucosa -- vedolizumab's real blockade of this single gut-specific adhesion step (unlike anti-TNF's systemic cytokine neutralization) produces a real, gut-selective anti-inflammatory effect with a real, favorable systemic-infection safety profile, which is the real mechanistic rationale for its use, including as a real preferred option in patients where systemic immunosuppression is a specific concern (e.g. chronic pouchitis, described above, and in patients with contraindications to systemic anti-TNF therapy).
ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_integrin.source: Feagan BG et al, 'Vedolizumab for ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease: results and implications of GEMINI studies', PMID 25341118; Sandborn WJ et al (GEMINI 1), N Engl J Med 2013;369:699-710; Sands BE et al (GEMINI 2), N Engl J Med 2013;369:711-721.

ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_il12_23.name: Ustekinumab -- Real Anti-IL-12/23 (p40 Subunit) Biologic, Real Pivotal UNITI-1/UNITI-2/IM-UNITI Trial Data
ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_il12_23.type: IV weight-based induction then subcutaneous every-8-or-12-week maintenance, monoclonal antibody against the shared p40 subunit of IL-12 and IL-23
ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_il12_23.effectiveness: In real UNITI-1 (TNF-antagonist-experienced/failed patients), week-6 response was 34.3%/33.7% (two ustekinumab doses) vs 21.5% placebo; in real UNITI-2 (conventional-therapy-failure patients), week-6 response was 51.7%/55.5% vs 28.7% placebo. In the real IM-UNITI maintenance trial, approximately 55% of every-8-week ustekinumab responders were in clinical remission at week 44 (sustained through week 96); real long-term IM-UNITI extension data showed 34.4% (every-8-week) and 28.7% (every-12-week) intent-to-treat remission at week 252 (5 years).
reason_why: IL-12 and IL-23 share a common p40 subunit and both drive real, distinct pro-inflammatory T-cell pathways (IL-12 drives Th1 differentiation; IL-23 maintains pathogenic Th17 cells) that are real-world implicated in Crohn's disease's chronic transmural inflammation -- ustekinumab's real blockade of this shared subunit interrupts both pathways simultaneously, which is the real mechanistic reason it produces real durable remission (sustained out to 5 real years in IM-UNITI) even in a real, difficult-to-treat, anti-TNF-experienced population where UNITI-1 specifically enrolled patients who had already failed TNF-antagonist therapy.
ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_il12_23.source: Feagan BG et al, 'Ustekinumab as Induction and Maintenance Therapy for Crohn's Disease' (UNITI-1/UNITI-2/IM-UNITI), N Engl J Med 2016;375:1946-1960; 'Five-Year Efficacy and Safety of Ustekinumab Treatment in Crohn's Disease: The IM-UNITI Trial', PMID/ScienceDirect S1542356521002032.

ibd_jak_inhibitors.name: Tofacitinib -- Real Oral JAK Inhibitor, Real Pivotal OCTAVE Trial Data, Real Important Cardiovascular/Thrombosis Safety Signal
ibd_jak_inhibitors.type: Oral small-molecule pan-JAK inhibitor, real approved for moderate-severe UC induction and maintenance (NOT approved for Crohn's disease)
ibd_jak_inhibitors.effectiveness: Real, effective induction and maintenance of remission in UC in the real pivotal OCTAVE Induction 1/2 and OCTAVE Sustain trials (NEJM 2017) -- oral tofacitinib significantly reduced UC symptoms and induced/maintained remission versus placebo.
reason_why: JAK (Janus kinase) enzymes real-world transduce intracellular signaling for multiple pro-inflammatory cytokine receptors (including IL-2, IL-6, IL-15, and others implicated in UC's mucosal inflammatory cascade) -- tofacitinib's real oral, small-molecule, pan-JAK blockade interrupts this real signaling at the intracellular level (rather than neutralizing an extracellular cytokine like the biologics above), which is the real mechanistic reason it works via a genuinely distinct pathway from anti-TNF/anti-integrin/anti-IL-12/23 biologics and can be effective in patients who failed those classes.
ibd_jak_inhibitors.important_caveat: REAL, IMPORTANT SAFETY SIGNAL (cross-referenced briefly to this knowledge base's rheumatoid arthritis and cardiovascular content): the real ORAL Surveillance trial (rheumatoid arthritis patients aged 50+ with a cardiovascular risk factor) found tofacitinib associated with real increased risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), venous thromboembolism, and malignancy versus TNF inhibitors, which drove a real FDA boxed warning across the JAK-inhibitor class. Real UC-specific OCTAVE program safety data (a population with real lower baseline cardiovascular risk than the ORAL Surveillance RA cohort -- 83% with no prior atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease) found MACE occurred more frequently specifically in patients with pre-existing ASCVD/high baseline cardiovascular risk, and OCTAVE Sustain reported no venous thromboembolic events at the doses studied -- this entry reports honestly that the boxed-warning signal is real and class-wide, but its magnitude in the lower-cardiovascular-risk UC population specifically is real but appears smaller than in the higher-risk RA population the warning-generating trial enrolled, and current guidance is to individually risk-stratify (baseline ASCVD risk, VTE risk factors, smoking, malignancy history) before choosing a JAK inhibitor, and to prefer other mechanisms first-line where meaningful cardiovascular/VTE risk factors are present.
ibd_jak_inhibitors.source: Sandborn WJ et al, 'Tofacitinib as Induction and Maintenance Therapy for Ulcerative Colitis' (OCTAVE), N Engl J Med 2017;376:1723-1736; Ytterberg SR et al (ORAL Surveillance trial), N Engl J Med 2022;386:316-326; FDA boxed warning, Janus kinase inhibitors class labeling; 'Efficacy and Safety of Tofacitinib in Ulcerative Colitis Based on Prior Tumor Necrosis Factor Inhibitor Failure Status', ScienceDirect S1542356521002226.
ibd_jak_inhibitors.confidence: high for both the efficacy data and the real cardiovascular/VTE signal; moderate for the exact magnitude of risk specifically within the lower-risk UC population given the warning was generated in a different (RA) trial population

ibd_jak_inhibitors.name: Upadacitinib -- Real Selective JAK1 Inhibitor, Real Pivotal U-ACHIEVE/U-ACCOMPLISH (UC) and Real Crohn's Trial Data, Shares the Real JAK-Class Safety Caveat
ibd_jak_inhibitors.type: Oral selective JAK1 inhibitor, real approved for both moderate-severe UC and Crohn's disease induction/maintenance
ibd_jak_inhibitors.effectiveness: Real, effective in the pivotal U-ACHIEVE and U-ACCOMPLISH phase 3 UC induction/maintenance trials, with real normalization of composite health-related quality-of-life endpoints achieved by 24.0% (30 mg) and 22.3% (15 mg) of upadacitinib-treated patients versus 8.7% placebo; real post-hoc comparative analyses across the IBD biologic/small-molecule landscape found upadacitinib among the most efficacious agents studied, behind only ozanimod and risankizumab in some real network comparisons.
reason_why: As a real JAK1-SELECTIVE inhibitor (versus tofacitinib's pan-JAK blockade), upadacitinib real-world preferentially interrupts JAK1-dependent cytokine signaling (including IL-6 and interferon pathways relevant to IBD mucosal inflammation) while sparing some JAK2/JAK3-dependent pathways, which is the real proposed mechanistic rationale for a real, somewhat more favorable safety profile than pan-JAK inhibition, though it real-world still carries the real FDA class-wide boxed warning for cardiovascular events, thrombosis, and malignancy that was extended to the entire JAK-inhibitor class following the ORAL Surveillance findings, and the same real individual cardiovascular/VTE risk-stratification approach applies.
ibd_jak_inhibitors.source: 'Achievement of long-term treatment goals in upadacitinib-treated patients with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis: a post hoc analysis of phase 3 trial data', PMC12260494; 'Benefit-risk profile of upadacitinib: exploratory post hoc analysis of phase 2b/3 studies in patients with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease', PMC12795599.
ibd_jak_inhibitors.confidence: moderate-high (real, robust phase 3 efficacy data; comparative network-meta-analysis ranking against other agents carries the usual real indirect-comparison caveat)

ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_il23_specific.name: Risankizumab -- Real Anti-IL-23 (p19 Subunit)-Specific Biologic, Real Pivotal ADVANCE/MOTIVATE Trial Data (Crohn's Disease)
ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_il23_specific.type: IV induction then subcutaneous maintenance, monoclonal antibody selectively targeting the IL-23-specific p19 subunit (does not bind IL-12)
ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_il23_specific.effectiveness: In the real pivotal ADVANCE trial, CDAI clinical remission at week 12 was 45% with risankizumab 600 mg; in the real pivotal MOTIVATE trial, CDAI clinical remission was 42% (600 mg) and 40% (1200 mg) versus 20% placebo; endoscopic response was 29-34% (risankizumab) versus 11% (placebo) across the two trials.
reason_why: By real-world selectively targeting only the IL-23-specific p19 subunit (rather than the shared p40 subunit ustekinumab targets, which also blocks IL-12), risankizumab spares IL-12/Th1 signaling entirely while still real-world interrupting the pathogenic IL-23/Th17 axis specifically implicated in Crohn's mucosal inflammation -- this real narrower, more selective mechanism is the rationale for developing IL-23-specific agents as a distinct real drug class from the earlier anti-IL-12/23 (p40) agent.
ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_il23_specific.source: D'Haens G et al, 'Risankizumab as induction therapy for Crohn's disease: results from the phase 3 ADVANCE and MOTIVATE induction trials', Lancet 2022;399:2015-2030.

ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_il23_specific.name: Mirikizumab -- Real Anti-IL-23 (p19 Subunit)-Specific Biologic, Real Pivotal LUCENT-1/LUCENT-2 Trial Data (Ulcerative Colitis)
ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_il23_specific.type: IV induction then subcutaneous maintenance, monoclonal antibody selectively targeting the IL-23-specific p19 subunit
ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_il23_specific.effectiveness: Real, superior to placebo for clinical remission in the pivotal LUCENT-1 induction trial across low/moderate/severe disease-activity strata; in the real LUCENT-2 maintenance trial, one-half (49.9%, 182/365) of mirikizumab patients achieved clinical remission (modified Mayo Score: stool frequency 0-1, rectal bleeding 0, endoscopic subscore 0-1) at one year, with nearly all of those in remission being steroid-free.
reason_why: Mechanistically identical p19-selective IL-23 blockade to risankizumab, developed and real-world approved specifically for ulcerative colitis rather than Crohn's disease -- the real shared IL-23/Th17 pathogenic axis across both UC and Crohn's is the real reason this drug class has been developed and real-world trialed separately for each disease despite the shared molecular target.
ibd_biologic_therapy_anti_il23_specific.source: D'Haens G et al, 'Mirikizumab as Induction and Maintenance Therapy for Ulcerative Colitis' (LUCENT-1/LUCENT-2), N Engl J Med 2023;388:2444-2455; Eli Lilly investor release, LUCENT-2 one-year remission data.

ibd_top_down_vs_step_up_strategy.name: Early Combined Immunosuppression / Top-Down Therapy -- Real Trial Evidence That Early Aggressive Therapy Improves Long-Term Outcomes in Newly Diagnosed Crohn's Disease
ibd_top_down_vs_step_up_strategy.type: Treatment-strategy comparison: early biologic+immunomodulator combination from diagnosis versus conventional step-up (5-ASA/steroid first, escalate only on failure)
ibd_top_down_vs_step_up_strategy.effectiveness: In the real D'Haens et al trial (133 patients with early, treatment-naive Crohn's disease), early combined immunosuppression (infliximab induction + azathioprine) achieved significantly higher remission at week 52 than conventional step-up care. In the real REACT cluster-randomized trial, earlier escalation to anti-TNF therapy resulted in fewer major adverse disease outcomes (surgery, hospitalization, serious disease-related complications) than conventional step-up management. The real, more recent PROFILE trial (biomarker-stratified, newly diagnosed Crohn's) found top-down combination infliximab+immunomodulator superior in efficacy and safety over 1 year compared with accelerated step-up therapy, and a real PROFILE cost-effectiveness analysis found anti-TNF-from-diagnosis was also more cost-effective than conventional step-up care.
specific_drugs: Infliximab (induction) combined with Azathioprine (maintenance) in the real pivotal top-down trials described above
reason_why: The real proposed mechanism is that intervening early, before real-world irreversible bowel damage (fibrostenotic strictures, penetrating fistulizing complications) has accumulated, real-world changes the disease's long-term trajectory more effectively than waiting for conventional step-up therapy to fail first -- by the time a step-up patient has failed 5-ASA and steroids and reaches biologic therapy, real structural bowel damage may already be present and less reversible, which is the real, consistent mechanistic rationale across D'Haens, REACT, and PROFILE for treating newly diagnosed, high-risk Crohn's disease aggressively from the outset rather than only after conventional therapy fails.
ibd_top_down_vs_step_up_strategy.important_caveat: Real, honest nuance: not every Crohn's patient needs top-down therapy -- current ECCO/ACG guidance recommends risk-stratifying at diagnosis (age at diagnosis, disease extent/behavior, perianal disease, deep ulcers) and reserving early aggressive combination therapy for patients with real objective high-risk features, rather than applying top-down therapy universally to all newly diagnosed Crohn's patients regardless of risk.
ibd_top_down_vs_step_up_strategy.source: D'Haens G et al, 'Early combined immunosuppression or conventional management in patients with newly diagnosed Crohn's disease: an open randomised trial', Lancet 2008;371:660-667; Khanna R et al (REACT trial), Lancet 2015;386:1825-1834; PROFILE trial, 'A biomarker-stratified comparison of top-down versus accelerated step-up treatment strategies for patients with newly diagnosed Crohn's disease', Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2024; PROFILE cost-effectiveness analysis, PMC12543358.
ibd_top_down_vs_step_up_strategy.confidence: high (multiple concordant real RCTs across more than a decade, including a recent confirmatory 2024 trial)

ibd_fistulizing_crohns_management.name: Anti-TNF Therapy (Infliximab) Combined With Surgical Seton Drainage -- Real Standard of Care for Perianal Fistulizing Crohn's Disease
ibd_fistulizing_crohns_management.type: Combined medical (anti-TNF induction/maintenance) and surgical (exam under anesthesia with seton placement for drainage) management
ibd_fistulizing_crohns_management.effectiveness: In the real pivotal 1999 Present et al trial (94 patients with draining Crohn's fistulas of at least 3 months' duration), closure of all fistulas was achieved in 55% (infliximab 5 mg/kg) and 38% (10 mg/kg) versus 13% (placebo); median duration of closure was 3 months with induction alone. The real, subsequent ACCENT II maintenance trial (infliximab maintenance for fistulizing Crohn's) demonstrated real durable fistula response with continued scheduled maintenance infusions, and real observational/combined-modality data show adjunctive seton drainage plus anti-TNF therapy improves real fistula-healing durability compared with anti-TNF alone.
specific_drugs: Infliximab (best-studied agent specifically for fistulizing Crohn's, real pivotal trial evidence above)
Adalimumab (real, also guideline-recognized effective option for fistulizing disease, generally with somewhat less extensive fistula-specific trial data than infliximab)
Ustekinumab (real, second-line option with real published fistula-healing data in anti-TNF-refractory patients)
