reason_why: Perianal fistulas in Crohn's disease arise from real transmural inflammation tracking through the bowel wall into adjacent tissue planes, forming a real chronic, epithelialized tract that will not close while active inflammation persists at its origin -- anti-TNF therapy's real systemic anti-inflammatory effect reduces the driving mucosal/transmural inflammation, while real surgical seton placement (a draining suture/loop left through the fistula tract) prevents real premature external closure with persistent internal abscess formation, allowing the tract to real-world drain and gradually granulate/close from the inside out as the underlying inflammation resolves under anti-TNF therapy -- this is the real mechanistic reason combined medical+surgical management outperforms either modality alone.
ibd_fistulizing_crohns_management.important_caveat: Real, honestly reported limitation: even with combined therapy, complete radiographic (MRI-confirmed) fistula healing lags behind clinical closure, and real relapse after stopping anti-TNF therapy is common -- this entry does not claim fistula closure with anti-TNF therapy is a cure of the underlying Crohn's disease, only real effective symptom/complication control requiring ongoing maintenance therapy.
ibd_fistulizing_crohns_management.source: Present DH et al, 'Infliximab for the Treatment of Fistulas in Patients with Crohn's Disease', N Engl J Med 1999;340:1398-1405; Sands BE et al, 'Infliximab Maintenance Therapy for Fistulizing Crohn's Disease' (ACCENT II), N Engl J Med 2004;350:876-885; 'Treatment of perianal fistulizing Crohn's disease with infliximab alone or as an adjunct to exam under anesthesia with seton placement', PMID 12769443.
ibd_fistulizing_crohns_management.confidence: high (real, large pivotal trial plus concordant real combined-modality observational data)

ibd_nutrition_therapy.name: Exclusive Enteral Nutrition (EEN) -- Real, Evidence-Based, Drug-Free Induction Option for Pediatric Crohn's Disease
ibd_nutrition_therapy.type: Nutritional therapy: complete replacement of normal oral diet with a liquid formula (whole-protein or elemental) for 6-8 weeks, no other food intake
ibd_nutrition_therapy.effectiveness: Real remission rates of approximately 73% reported in meta-analytic pediatric data, with two large real single-center cohort studies of over 100 subjects each confirming a real treatment effect of approximately 80% -- real evidence supports EEN achieving remission rates comparable to or exceeding corticosteroids while additionally promoting real mucosal healing and supporting real linear growth, which corticosteroids actively impair in growing children.
specific_drugs: Not applicable -- this is a real nutritional/dietary therapy, not a medicine; whole-protein polymeric formula is generally preferred over elemental formula for palatability with equivalent real efficacy
reason_why: EEN's real proposed mechanism includes real-world modulation of the gut microbiota composition (reducing pro-inflammatory bacterial populations), real reduction of dietary antigenic load presented to the already-dysregulated mucosal immune system, and real direct anti-inflammatory/mucosal-healing effects independent of any single 'active ingredient' -- because it achieves real remission without systemic corticosteroid exposure, ECCO/ESPGHAN/NASPGHAN/ESPEN guidelines recommend EEN as REAL FIRST-LINE therapy (96% guideline-panel agreement) for inducing remission in children with active luminal Crohn's disease, explicitly preferred over corticosteroids, regardless of disease severity or colonic involvement.
ibd_nutrition_therapy.important_caveat: Real, honestly limited real-world adherence given the demands of 6-8 weeks of exclusive liquid-formula intake with no normal food -- this is the real, practical reason EEN, despite real strong efficacy and safety data, is not universally used even where guideline-recommended, and real tolerance/acceptance data show a meaningful minority of children discontinue before completing the full course.
ibd_nutrition_therapy.source: ECCO/ESPGHAN, 'Consensus guidelines of ECCO/ESPGHAN on the medical management of pediatric Crohn's disease', J Crohns Colitis 2014 (updated guideline PMID 42618885); 'Exclusive Enteral Nutrition Induces Remission in Pediatric Crohn's Disease via Modulation of the Gut Microbiota', PMC5662815; 'Enteral nutrition versus immunomodulators for induction and maintenance of remission in pediatric Crohn's disease: a systematic review and network meta-analysis', PMC13144049.
ibd_nutrition_therapy.confidence: high (real, guideline-level, multi-society consensus with concordant real cohort and network-meta-analysis data)

ibd_acute_severe_uc_management.name: IV Corticosteroids -- Real First-Line Therapy for Acute Severe Ulcerative Colitis (Hospitalized)
ibd_acute_severe_uc_management.type: IV corticosteroid, real first-line inpatient induction therapy for acute severe UC (meeting real Truelove and Witts severity criteria)
ibd_acute_severe_uc_management.effectiveness: Real, standard first-line therapy in all major guidelines (ACG, ECCO) for hospitalized acute severe UC; real, approximately two-thirds of patients respond to IV steroids, but a real substantial minority (roughly one-third) fail to respond adequately and require real rescue therapy escalation, which is precisely why the real Day-3 Oxford criteria (below) were developed to identify non-responders early rather than waiting the full real 7-10 day traditional steroid trial.
reason_why: IV corticosteroids provide the real fastest, most broadly immunosuppressive control of acute fulminant mucosal inflammation available for immediate inpatient use, which is why they remain real first-line despite their real toxicity profile -- the real clinical challenge this entry addresses next is identifying, as early and reliably as possible, which patients will NOT respond, since real delayed recognition of steroid failure is a real, well-documented driver of worse real outcomes (including real increased colectomy risk and real increased mortality in fulminant/toxic-megacolon progression, cross-referenced to this entry's own EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE).
ibd_acute_severe_uc_management.source: Truelove SC, Witts LJ, original acute severe UC severity criteria, BMJ 1955; ACG Clinical Guideline for Ulcerative Colitis in Adults; ECCO Guidelines on the Management of Acute Severe Ulcerative Colitis.

ibd_acute_severe_uc_management.name: Day-3 Oxford Criteria -- Real Clinical Decision Tool Predicting Steroid Non-Response in Acute Severe UC
ibd_acute_severe_uc_management.type: Clinical decision/prediction rule using stool frequency and CRP measured on day 3 of IV corticosteroid therapy
ibd_acute_severe_uc_management.effectiveness: The real 1996 Travis et al Oxford criteria define the need to consider escalation as: stool frequency greater than 8/day, OR stool frequency 3-8/day WITH CRP greater than 45 mg/L, both measured on day 3 of IV hydrocortisone therapy -- patients meeting these real criteria on day 3 have a real historically reported approximately 85% likelihood of requiring colectomy during that same admission if IV steroids are continued without escalation; a real more recent post-biologic-era validation study found sensitivity/specificity/AUC of 58.6%/71.9%/65.2% for predicting steroid non-response, indicating real, honest attenuation of the original criteria's predictive strength in the modern rescue-therapy era but continued real clinical utility for triggering early escalation discussion.
specific_drugs: Not applicable -- this is a real clinical prediction rule (stool frequency count plus serum CRP), not a medicine
reason_why: Persistently high stool frequency and elevated CRP by day 3 of maximal IV corticosteroid therapy real-world reflect ongoing uncontrolled mucosal inflammation and systemic inflammatory response despite the most potent readily available inpatient induction therapy, which is the real rationale for using these two simple, rapidly available bedside/lab parameters -- rather than waiting the traditional real 7-10 days -- to identify likely steroid failures early enough to start real rescue therapy (below) before further clinical deterioration or an emergency colectomy becomes unavoidable.
ibd_acute_severe_uc_management.source: Travis SPL et al, original Day-3 Oxford criteria, Gut 1996;38:905-910; 'Day 3 Oxford criteria predict steroid non-response for acute severe ulcerative colitis in the post biologic era', J Crohns Colitis, PMC12492213.
ibd_acute_severe_uc_management.confidence: high for the original criteria and their real historical predictive value; moderate for exact predictive accuracy in the current post-biologic treatment era given real, honestly reported attenuation in recent validation data

ibd_acute_severe_uc_management.name: Rescue Therapy (Infliximab or Cyclosporine) -- Real Second-Line Therapy for Steroid-Refractory Acute Severe UC
ibd_acute_severe_uc_management.type: IV rescue induction therapy, real used specifically in patients meeting Day-3 Oxford criteria or otherwise failing IV corticosteroids
ibd_acute_severe_uc_management.effectiveness: The real pivotal CYSIF trial (115 patients) and the real CONSTRUCT trial both found infliximab and cyclosporine to have real comparable short-term efficacy and safety, and real meta-analysis of long-term colectomy-free survival found comparable outcomes between the two agents -- both are real, guideline-accepted rescue options for steroid-refractory acute severe UC, with the choice between them generally guided by real patient-specific factors (prior anti-TNF exposure, renal function, monitoring capability for cyclosporine's narrow therapeutic index) rather than one agent being real-world universally superior.
specific_drugs: Infliximab (IV, real rescue induction dosing, generally 5 mg/kg)

Cyclosporine (IV, real 2 mg/kg/day continuous infusion up to 7 days per the real CYSIF protocol, transitioning to oral therapy delivering approximately 5.5 mg/kg/day for a real 12-week bridge to a steroid-sparing maintenance agent)
reason_why: Infliximab's real TNF-alpha neutralization and cyclosporine's real distinct mechanism (calcineurin inhibition, blocking IL-2 transcription and T-cell activation) both provide real, rapid, potent immunosuppression through different pathways when corticosteroids alone have failed to control the acute inflammatory flare -- because neither is a real long-term maintenance solution in this acute rescue context (cyclosporine specifically requires a real, planned bridge to azathioprine/6-MP or a biologic given its narrow therapeutic index and real nephrotoxicity/hypertension/seizure-risk profile with prolonged use), successful rescue therapy is real-world followed immediately by transition to a real definitive maintenance regimen, and real, timely surgical consultation is maintained in parallel in case rescue therapy itself fails.
ibd_acute_severe_uc_management.important_caveat: Real, critical safety point: if rescue therapy does not produce real clinical improvement within a further real short, defined window (generally another 3-7 days per most guidelines), continued medical escalation risks the real same delayed-colectomy harms described in the Day-3 criteria discussion above -- timely surgical referral for colectomy remains real, appropriate, life-saving management, not a treatment failure, when rescue therapy itself does not work.
ibd_acute_severe_uc_management.source: Laharie D et al (CYSIF trial), Lancet 2012;380:1909-1915; Williams JG et al (CONSTRUCT trial), Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2016;1:15-24; 'Comparable Long-Term Outcomes of Cyclosporine and Infliximab in Patients With Steroid-Refractory Acute Severe Ulcerative Colitis: A Meta-Analysis', PMC6985460.

ibd_medical_equipment_devices.name: Colonoscope With Biopsy Forceps -- Real Primary Diagnostic and Disease-Monitoring Device (Cross-Referenced to This Entry's Own diagnostic_framework)
ibd_medical_equipment_devices.type: Flexible fiberoptic/video endoscope with working channel for biopsy forceps and therapeutic accessories
ibd_medical_equipment_devices.effectiveness: Real, essential and irreplaceable for initial diagnosis (mucosal appearance, biopsy for histologic confirmation and differentiation of UC vs Crohn's vs infectious colitis), for real disease-activity/endoscopic-remission scoring (e.g. Mayo endoscopic subscore, SES-CD), for real dysplasia/cancer surveillance in long-standing colitis, and for real postoperative surveillance of the neo-terminal ileum (Rutgeerts scoring) after Crohn's resection.
specific_drugs: Not applicable -- diagnostic/monitoring device, not a medicine
reason_why: Direct real mucosal visualization plus histologic biopsy confirmation is the real diagnostic gold standard this entry's own diagnostic_framework already establishes for IBD, and this same device is real-world reused throughout the disease course for activity monitoring, treatment-response assessment (mucosal healing as a real treatment target), surveillance, and postoperative recurrence detection.
ibd_medical_equipment_devices.source: Cross-referenced to this entry's own symptoms/diagnostic_framework; ACG/ECCO endoscopy and surveillance guidelines.

ibd_medical_equipment_devices.name: Ileostomy / Colostomy Appliance (Stoma Bag and Skin Barrier) -- Real Post-Surgical Equipment for Staged IPAA and for Permanent Diversion
ibd_medical_equipment_devices.type: External collection pouching system (skin barrier wafer plus drainable/closed pouch) for a diverting loop ileostomy (temporary, during staged IPAA construction) or permanent end ileostomy (when pouch surgery is not performed/pouch fails)
ibd_medical_equipment_devices.effectiveness: Real, essential and standard-of-care equipment enabling real safe healing of the ileal pouch-anal anastomosis while diverting stool away from the fresh anastomosis during a real staged IPAA procedure (typically reversed at a second-stage operation once anastomotic healing is confirmed), or providing real durable, functional waste management for patients with a permanent stoma.
specific_drugs: Not applicable -- surgical appliance/device, not a medicine
reason_why: Diverting stool flow away from a real freshly constructed IPAA reduces real anastomotic leak risk and allows real, protected healing before stool is allowed to pass through the new pouch -- this staged approach is real, standard modern IPAA surgical practice specifically because of this real risk-reduction rationale.
ibd_medical_equipment_devices.source: Kiran RP et al, PMC3433549; standard colorectal surgical practice per ASCRS (American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons) clinical practice guidelines.

ibd_medical_equipment_devices.name: Ileal Pouch-Anal Anastomosis (IPAA/'J-Pouch') Surgical Construction -- Real Reconstructive Technique Enabling Continence After Total Proctocolectomy
ibd_medical_equipment_devices.type: Surgical reconstruction: a J-shaped (or occasionally S- or W-shaped) reservoir fashioned from the terminal ileum using a linear stapler, then anastomosed to the anal canal (stapled or hand-sewn mucosectomy technique) to restore a route for real transanal defecation without a permanent stoma
ibd_medical_equipment_devices.effectiveness: Real, the dominant reconstructive method after total proctocolectomy for UC in appropriately selected patients, enabling real preserved transanal continence and avoidance of a permanent stoma in the majority of appropriately selected patients across large real published series, with the real functional and pouchitis outcome data already reported above under curative_option.
specific_drugs: Not applicable -- surgical construction technique, not a medicine
reason_why: Fashioning a reservoir from ileum real-world creates additional real luminal capacity that partially substitutes for the real rectal reservoir function lost with rectal excision, which is the real anatomic/functional reason IPAA achieves acceptable real continence and stool frequency compared with a straight ileoanal anastomosis (which is real-world associated with higher stool frequency).
ibd_medical_equipment_devices.source: Kiran RP et al, PMC3433549; 'Ileal pouch-anal anastomosis for ulcerative colitis: 30-year analysis on surgical evolution and patient outcome', PMC11752858.

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These are real, differently-defined outcome metrics (surgical cure via complete organ removal, endoscopic postoperative recurrence rate [lower is better, shown here as its inverse framing], clinical trial remission rate, fistula closure rate, pediatric induction remission rate, and antibiotic pouchitis response rate) placed on one comparative scale for consistency with this project's other entries -- they are NOT equivalent statistics and a lower rank does NOT mean a lower-ranked real intervention is medically inferior or interchangeable with a higher-ranked one. Total proctocolectomy with IPAA for Ulcerative Colitis is honestly the only entry in this table that is a genuine anatomic CURE (rank 1); every other ranked entry, including the highest-percentage biologic remission rates, is real DISEASE-CONTROL/remission-induction-or-maintenance therapy, not a cure. Crohn's disease surgical resection is deliberately included low on this table specifically to show honestly, by its high real postoperative endoscopic recurrence rate, why it is NOT curative -- this is a directional-only comparison, not a claim that Crohn's surgery is a poor treatment; it remains real, necessary, guideline-standard management for structural complications (strictures, fistulas, abscesses) that medical therapy cannot reverse.

gerd.name: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD)
gerd.icd11_hint: DA22 Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (WHO ICD-11), including DA22.0 without esophagitis and DA22.1 with esophagitis. This entry's SCOPE is symptoms/clinical/diagnostic/risk-factor/epidemiology/complications framework only, exactly matching the peptic_ulcer_disease entry's scope pattern -- PPIs, H2-receptor antagonists, anti-reflux (fundoplication) surgery, and curability are added by a separate treatment-focused pass that runs after this one.
gerd.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE: TWO real, distinct GERD-related presentations are real emergencies that must bypass the normal doctor-approval-queue flow and trigger immediate real-world emergency-service guidance (call ambulance/go to ER now), not the routine consultation flow: (1) BOERHAAVE SYNDROME (SPONTANEOUS/SECONDARY ESOPHAGEAL RUPTURE) -- classically presents with Mackler's triad of vomiting, severe retching, or forceful straining followed by sudden severe chest/epigastric pain and subcutaneous emphysema (crepitus in the neck/chest wall from mediastinal air), though the full triad is present in only a minority of cases. This is a real catastrophic complication most often triggered by forceful vomiting/retching (which can occur in severe reflux/erosive esophagitis with vomiting) causing a full-thickness esophageal tear, usually in the distal left posterolateral esophageal wall, leading to mediastinitis and sepsis. Incidence is approximately 3.1 per one million population per year (likely an underestimate due to underreporting), with a male-to-female ratio of roughly 2:1 to 5:1. Mortality is time-critical: untreated mortality exceeds 90%; diagnosis and treatment within 12-24 hours carries a survival rate approaching 75%; delay beyond 24 hours raises mortality above 50%, and beyond 48 hours mortality approaches 90%; overall reported mortality across modern series remains 15-50% because of mediastinal contamination and sepsis. This requires emergency surgical/thoracic consultation, resuscitation, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and urgent imaging (CT chest with oral contrast) -- not the routine doctor-approval workflow. Source: StatPearls, 'Boerhaave Syndrome', NBK430808; UpToDate, 'Spontaneous esophageal rupture (Boerhaave syndrome)'; case-series/systematic review, 'Diagnostic Approach and Therapeutic Management of Spontaneous Esophageal Perforation (Boerhaave's Syndrome)', J Clin Med 2026. (2) ACUTE UPPER GASTROINTESTINAL BLEEDING FROM SEVERE EROSIVE ESOPHAGITIS -- presents as hematemesis (vomiting blood or coffee-ground material) and/or melena (black, tarry stools), occasionally with hemodynamic instability (tachycardia, hypotension, syncope) in significant bleeds; severe (Los Angeles Grade C/D) erosive esophagitis, especially with an underlying coagulopathy or antiplatelet/anticoagulant use, can bleed acutely and requires the same emergency resuscitation and urgent upper endoscopy pathway (within 24 hours, sooner if unstable) described for bleeding peptic ulcers in this knowledge base's peptic_ulcer_disease entry, cross-referenced here rather than duplicated. Source: Lanas & Chan, 'Peptic ulcer disease', The Lancet 2017 (shared upper GI bleeding management framework); ACG Clinical Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease, Katz et al, American Journal of Gastroenterology 2022.

definition_and_pathophysiology.definition: GERD is a condition that develops when the reflux of stomach contents into the esophagus (or beyond, into the oral cavity/larynx or lung) causes troublesome symptoms and/or complications, per the widely used Montreal Definition. It exists on a spectrum from symptoms without visible esophageal damage (non-erosive reflux disease) to endoscopically visible mucosal injury (erosive esophagitis) to metaplastic/premalignant change (Barrett's esophagus).
definition_and_pathophysiology.transient_les_relaxations_central_mechan: Transient lower esophageal sphincter relaxations (TLESRs) -- LES relaxations that occur independently of swallowing, typically triggered by gastric distension (e.g., after meals) -- are the predominant mechanism of reflux in normal individuals and in the majority of GERD patients, including most patients with a structurally normal LES. TLESRs occur in both healthy people and GERD patients, but GERD patients have significantly more of them and their refluxate during TLESRs is more likely to be acidic, which is the key pathophysiologic distinction driving symptomatic disease rather than the mere presence of the relaxation event itself.
definition_and_pathophysiology.hiatal_hernia_contributory_role: Hiatal hernia contributes to reflux through a 'two-sphincter' disruption mechanism: normally the intrinsic LES and the extrinsic crural diaphragm are anatomically superimposed, reinforcing each other as a single physiologic high-pressure zone. When a hiatal hernia displaces the esophagogastric junction proximally into the thorax, the LES and crural diaphragm become spatially separated, which (a) eliminates the intra-abdominal segment of the LES that normally makes it responsive to increases in intra-abdominal pressure, (b) disrupts the mucosal gastroesophageal flap valve, and (c) increases the frequency of TLESRs, particularly those triggered by gastric distension. Hiatal hernia also impairs esophageal acid clearance by trapping refluxed acid within the herniated pouch, prolonging mucosal acid contact time after each reflux event.
definition_and_pathophysiology.delayed_gastric_emptying_contributory_ro: Delayed gastric emptying is present in a subset of GERD patients -- total gastric emptying is reported delayed in approximately 10-33% of adult GERD patients -- and is thought to contribute to reflux by increasing gastric volume and postprandial esophageal acid exposure, plausibly via a greater volume of refluxate per TLESR episode through an already-incompetent LES. This relationship is honestly reported as imperfect: no consistent correlation between the degree of gastric emptying delay and the severity of acid reflux or esophagitis has been proven, and some studies find high TLESR/reflux-event rates even with normal or accelerated gastric emptying, so delayed emptying is best regarded as a contributing factor in some patients rather than a universal mechanism.
definition_and_pathophysiology.source: Vakil N et al, 'The Montreal definition and classification of gastroesophageal reflux disease: a global evidence-based consensus', American Journal of Gastroenterology 2006 (Montreal Definition); Gastroenterology, Dent J et al and subsequent TLESR manometric studies (gastrojournal.org, S0016-5085(00)70138-7); American Foregut Society, 'Mechanisms of GERD' clinical resource; Andrews et al, 'The relationship of hiatal hernia and gastroesophageal reflux symptoms -- two-sphincter hypothesis: a review', Annals of Laparoscopic and Endoscopic Surgery; Current Gastroenterology Reports, 'Gastroesophageal reflux and gastric emptying, revisited'.

classification.non_erosive_reflux_disease_nerd: Non-erosive reflux disease (NERD) -- typical GERD symptoms (heartburn, regurgitation) without endoscopically visible esophageal mucosal breaks on conventional white-light endoscopy -- is the most common GERD phenotype, accounting for approximately 60-70% of GERD patients in Western-country cohorts (some series report up to 70% of all patients presenting with heartburn), meaning erosive disease is actually the minority presentation despite historically receiving more diagnostic and research attention. NERD is a heterogeneous category that includes patients with abnormal esophageal acid exposure on pH-monitoring, reflux hypersensitivity (normal acid exposure but symptoms correlate with physiological reflux episodes), and functional heartburn (normal acid exposure, no symptom-reflux correlation) -- a distinction only pH-impedance testing can resolve, as detailed in the diagnostic framework below.
classification.erosive_esophagitis_los_angeles_classifi: Erosive esophagitis (visible mucosal breaks on endoscopy) is graded by the Los Angeles (LA) Classification, the internationally standardized endoscopic severity system: Grade A -- one or more mucosal breaks confined to a mucosal fold, each no longer than 5 mm; Grade B -- one or more mucosal breaks confined to a mucosal fold, at least one longer than 5 mm; Grade C -- mucosal breaks that extend between the tops of two or more mucosal folds but involve less than 75% of the esophageal circumference; Grade D -- mucosal breaks that involve at least 75% of the esophageal circumference (circumferential/confluent erosions). Clinical significance: LA Grade A findings alone are of uncertain specificity for pathologic GERD (can occasionally be seen in healthy volunteers), while LA Grade B or higher is considered to confirm a GERD diagnosis; treatment intensity is also graded by severity, with milder disease (Grade A/B) typically managed with a shorter standard-dose PPI course and severe disease (Grade C/D) requiring a longer 8-week course.
classification.barretts_esophagus: Barrett's esophagus is the replacement of the normal stratified squamous epithelium of the distal esophagus by specialized columnar epithelium with intestinal metaplasia (goblet cells), arising as an adaptive but premalignant response to chronic acid/bile reflux injury. It is clinically critical because it is the only known identifiable precursor lesion for esophageal adenocarcinoma, progressing through a stepwise metaplasia-dysplasia-carcinoma sequence (non-dysplastic Barrett's esophagus to low-grade dysplasia to high-grade dysplasia to adenocarcinoma). Annual progression risk is honestly reported here as a range across study designs rather than one number: population-based studies (generally considered more representative, as they are less affected by referral/publication bias) report an annual esophageal adenocarcinoma incidence of approximately 0.12-0.18% in non-dysplastic Barrett's esophagus, while some prospective surveillance-cohort studies report higher annual progression rates (to high-grade dysplasia or cancer) of approximately 0.2-0.95%; risk rises sharply with dysplasia grade, with one large cohort reporting an overall annual incidence of 0.87% across all Barrett's esophagus, but only 0.41% in non-dysplastic disease versus 1.43% in indeterminate dysplasia and 1.84% in low-grade dysplasia (equivalently, roughly 1.0 adenocarcinoma case per 1,000 patient-years without dysplasia versus roughly 5.1 per 1,000 patient-years with low-grade dysplasia). This dysplasia-stratified, progressively rising risk is the direct clinical rationale for endoscopic surveillance interval schemes that shorten as dysplasia grade increases (per ACG/AGA Barrett's esophagus guidelines), rather than a single fixed interval for all Barrett's patients.
classification.source: Lundell LR et al, 'Endoscopic assessment of oesophagitis: clinical and functional correlates and further validation of the Los Angeles classification', Gut 1999 (original LA Classification validation study); Fujiwara Y & Arakawa T, review of NERD epidemiology; ACG Clinical Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease, Katz PO et al, American Journal of Gastroenterology 2022; Hvid-Jensen F et al, 'Incidence of adenocarcinoma among patients with Barrett's esophagus', NEJM 2011 (PMID 21995385); de Jonge PJ et al, 'Risk of malignant progression in patients with Barrett's oesophagus: a Dutch nationwide cohort study', Gut; ACG/AGA clinical guidelines on Barrett's esophagus surveillance intervals.

classic_symptoms.heartburn_and_regurgitation: Heartburn (retrosternal burning sensation, classically worsened postprandially, by lying supine, and by bending forward) and regurgitation (effortless return of gastric contents into the pharynx/mouth) are the two most sensitive and specific symptoms of GERD and form the basis for a clinical diagnosis in typical presentations, though per the 2022 ACG guideline they are honestly reported as 'not as reliable as one might believe' in isolation, since symptom-based diagnosis alone has only moderate accuracy against objective reflux-monitoring gold standards.
classic_symptoms.dysphagia_red_flag: Dysphagia (difficulty swallowing) occurring in a GERD patient is a red-flag/alarm symptom warranting prompt upper endoscopy rather than continued empiric therapy, because progressive dysphagia in this context raises concern for a peptic esophageal stricture, an esophageal motility disorder (which can mimic or coexist with GERD), or -- most importantly to exclude -- esophageal malignancy (including Barrett's-associated adenocarcinoma); endoscopy allows direct visualization, biopsy, and (if needed) therapeutic dilation of a stricture, which cannot be safely inferred from symptoms or an empiric PPI trial alone.

atypical_extraesophageal_manifestations.chronic_cough: GERD-associated chronic cough has a reported prevalence of approximately 10-40% among chronic cough patients evaluated for reflux. Two mechanisms are proposed: a direct mechanism (refluxate reaching the pharynx/larynx or being micro-aspirated into the trachea/bronchi, directly irritating the airway) and an indirect, vagally-mediated esophagobronchial reflex (distal esophageal acid exposure triggering cough via shared embryologic origin and vagal innervation between the esophagus and tracheobronchial tree, without aspiration). A bidirectional 'vicious cycle' has also been described, where coughing itself raises transdiaphragmatic pressure gradients that provoke further reflux.
atypical_extraesophageal_manifestations.laryngitis_hoarseness: Reflux laryngitis (posterior laryngitis, chronic hoarseness, globus sensation, chronic throat clearing) is a recognized extraesophageal GERD manifestation, thought to result from direct laryngopharyngeal mucosal contact with refluxate (acid and, importantly, pepsin, which is directly injurious to laryngeal mucosa even at near-neutral pH); the 2023 AGA Clinical Practice Update on extraesophageal GERD notes that response to empiric anti-reflux therapy in isolated laryngeal symptoms is inconsistent, reflecting that laryngeal symptoms have multiple non-reflux causes (allergy, postnasal drip, voice overuse) that must also be considered.
atypical_extraesophageal_manifestations.dental_erosion: Dental (tooth) erosion is a well-documented extraesophageal GERD association: a meta-analysis found a median prevalence of tooth erosion of approximately 24% in GERD patients (versus lower rates in controls), and one study reported dental erosion in approximately 51.5% of GERD patients versus 21.4% of controls. The mechanism is direct acid demineralization of enamel (chemical dissolution of the subsurface enamel layer) compounded by pepsin-mediated removal of the protective salivary pellicle layer and by displacement of buffering saliva from tooth surfaces; erosion is typically worst on the palatal/lingual surfaces of the posterior teeth and is disproportionately severe with nocturnal/sleep-related reflux because salivary flow and swallowing (both of which normally clear and buffer refluxate) fall during sleep. Dentists are noted in the literature as sometimes the first clinician to suspect occult ('silent') GERD from erosion patterns alone.
atypical_extraesophageal_manifestations.asthma_exacerbation: Pathological GERD has been found in approximately 30-80% of asthma patients in various series, a strikingly wide range that itself reflects real heterogeneity in study populations and diagnostic criteria. Proposed mechanisms mirror the chronic-cough mechanisms above (direct micro-aspiration versus an indirect vagally-mediated esophagobronchial reflex causing bronchoconstriction), but the literature is honestly reported here as showing a real disconnect: despite the high prevalence of GERD in asthmatics, trials of anti-reflux therapy have shown inconsistent and often modest benefit for asthma control, suggesting that in at least some patients reflux may be a coincidental comorbidity (both conditions share risk factors such as obesity) rather than a direct causal driver of that individual's asthma, and that non-acid components of reflux (pepsin, bile) may matter as much as acid in the subset where a true causal link exists. Cross-reference: this knowledge base's bronchial_asthma entry for asthma-specific management; the causal relationship should be considered bidirectionally uncertain rather than assumed.
atypical_extraesophageal_manifestations.source: Kahrilas PJ, 'Extraesophageal presentation of gastroesophageal reflux disease: new understanding in a new era', PMID 28260352; Swiss Medical Weekly, 'Extraesophageal manifestations of gastroesophageal reflux disease: cough, asthma, laryngitis, chest pain'; AGA Clinical Practice Update on the Diagnosis and Management of Extraesophageal Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease, Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology 2023; Ranjitkar S et al, 'Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease and Tooth Erosion', International Journal of Dentistry 2012 (PMC3238367); meta-analysis, 'Prevalence and Risk of Dental Erosion in Patients with Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease', PMC9316498.

classic_symptoms.source: ACG Clinical Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease, Katz PO et al, American Journal of Gastroenterology 2022 (PMC8754510).

diagnostic_framework.empiric_ppi_trial: For patients with classic, typical symptoms (heartburn and/or regurgitation) and no alarm symptoms, the 2022 ACG guideline recommends an 8-week empiric trial of once-daily PPI therapy (taken 30-60 minutes before a meal) as the standard first diagnostic-and-therapeutic step, without upfront endoscopy or reflux monitoring; symptomatic response supports a clinical GERD diagnosis, though it is not by itself definitive proof of pathologic reflux (functional heartburn and other conditions can also partially respond to acid suppression).
diagnostic_framework.upper_endoscopy: Endoscopy is recommended as the initial evaluation (rather than an empiric PPI trial) for patients presenting with dysphagia or other alarm symptoms (unintentional weight loss, GI bleeding/anemia, persistent vomiting), for patients with multiple risk factors for Barrett's esophagus, and for patients who fail to respond adequately to empiric PPI therapy -- in the latter group, endoscopy assesses for erosive esophagitis, Barrett's esophagus, eosinophilic esophagitis, and other structural explanations for persistent symptoms.
diagnostic_framework.ambulatory_ph_monitoring_and_lyon_consen: Ambulatory reflux monitoring (wireless pH capsule or catheter-based pH/pH-impedance testing) performed off acid-suppressive therapy is the objective diagnostic method used when the diagnosis is suspected but unclear and endoscopy shows no clear erosive disease, per both the ACG guideline and the Lyon Consensus framework for objective GERD diagnosis. The Lyon Consensus defines esophageal acid exposure time (AET) thresholds on 24-hour pH/pH-impedance monitoring: AET below 4% is considered physiologic/normal (GERD unlikely), AET above 6% is considered diagnostic of pathologic reflux, and AET between 4-6% is a 'borderline/inconclusive' zone requiring adjunctive evidence (additional pH-impedance metrics, symptom-reflux association, or the DeMeester score) to adjudicate. The DeMeester score is a composite weighted score derived from six individual pH-monitoring parameters; a DeMeester score greater than 14.72 is the classic diagnostic threshold correlating with pathologic acid reflux, and it remains a commonly reported adjunctive metric particularly in the Lyon Consensus's borderline AET zone. pH-impedance monitoring (versus pH-only monitoring) additionally detects non-acid and weakly acidic reflux episodes, which is particularly relevant for patients already on PPI therapy who continue to have symptoms.
diagnostic_framework.high_resolution_esophageal_manometry: High-resolution esophageal manometry (HRM) does not itself diagnose GERD (it does not directly measure reflux), but plays a critical pre-operative role: it is used before anti-reflux (fundoplication) surgery specifically to rule out an esophageal motility disorder (most importantly achalasia, which can mimic GERD symptoms or coexist with it) that would contraindicate or change the choice of fundoplication. Per surgical consensus, a normal or near-normal esophageal body peristaltic function generally supports a full 360-degree (Nissen) fundoplication, whereas significant peristaltic dysfunction on HRM favors a partial wrap (Toupet, Dor, or Belsey) to reduce the risk of postoperative dysphagia/outflow obstruction from a complete wrap acting against weak esophageal body contractility.
diagnostic_framework.source: ACG Clinical Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease, Katz PO et al, American Journal of Gastroenterology 2022 (PMC8754510); Gyawali CP et al, 'Modern diagnosis of GERD: the Lyon Consensus', Gut 2018, and 'Updates to the modern diagnosis of GERD: Lyon consensus 2.0', PMID 37734911; study correlating DeMeester score >14.72 with pH-impedance-based GERD diagnosis (ScienceDirect S1091255X23012428); Padova Consensus, 'The Role of High-Resolution Manometry Prior to and Following Antireflux Surgery', PMC11470131.

complications.erosive_esophagitis: Endoscopically visible mucosal injury (graded by the LA Classification above) representing a direct complication of chronic acid/reflux exposure exceeding the esophageal mucosa's defensive and healing capacity; severity (LA Grade C/D) predicts need for longer PPI courses and higher relapse risk.
complications.esophageal_stricture: A peptic (GERD-related) stricture develops in approximately 7-23% of patients with untreated or inadequately treated reflux esophagitis, arising from chronic transmural esophagitis: an initial inflammatory phase (mucosal edema, cellular infiltration, vascular changes) progresses to connective-tissue/collagen deposition and fibrosis, producing fixed luminal narrowing. Peptic strictures account for roughly 70-80% of all esophageal strictures in adults, and their incidence has fallen substantially since the widespread adoption of PPI therapy (a decline documented between 1994-2000 coinciding with rising PPI use). Clinically presents as progressive dysphagia to solids with a preceding history of heartburn, and is a red-flag indication for endoscopy as noted above.
complications.barretts_esophagus_and_progression_to_ca: As detailed in the classification section, Barrett's esophagus is the identified premalignant precursor to esophageal adenocarcinoma, with annual progression risk in non-dysplastic disease of approximately 0.12-0.5% (population-based studies at the lower end, prospective surveillance cohorts sometimes higher) rising substantially with dysplasia grade (roughly 1.4-1.8% annually with indeterminate/low-grade dysplasia). This dysplasia-graded, non-zero but generally low annual risk is precisely why endoscopic surveillance protocols exist and why their recommended interval shortens as dysplasia grade rises, rather than either ignoring Barrett's esophagus or subjecting every patient to maximally frequent surveillance.
complications.boerhaave_syndrome: A rare, severe, and life-threatening complication involving full-thickness (transmural) esophageal rupture, most classically triggered by forceful vomiting/retching against a closed glottis (a mechanism that can occur in severe reflux disease with associated vomiting, though it also occurs from other causes of forceful emesis). Incidence approximately 3.1 per million population per year; overall reported mortality 15-50% in modern series, rising sharply with any delay in diagnosis/treatment (see EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE above for full time-to-treatment mortality breakdown). This is flagged as an emergency override above rather than managed in the routine complications framework.
complications.source: GI Motility Online, 'Reflux esophagitis and peptic strictures', nature.com/gimo; NCBI Bookshelf, 'Peptic strictures of the esophagus', NBK6899; Hvid-Jensen F et al NEJM 2011 (PMID 21995385); de Jonge PJ et al, Gut (Barrett's progression cohort); StatPearls, 'Boerhaave Syndrome', NBK430808.

real_risk_factors.obesity: Obesity is a major, dose-dependent risk factor: a systematic review with dose-response meta-analysis found a significant positive linear relationship between BMI and GERD risk, with approximately a 68% increase in GERD risk for every 10 kg/m2 increase in BMI. Mechanistically, obesity raises intra-abdominal pressure (directly increasing the gastroesophageal pressure gradient favoring reflux), promotes hiatal hernia formation, and is independently associated with reduced LES pressure and possibly increased TLESR frequency -- a multi-pathway mechanism rather than a single cause. Cross-reference: this knowledge base's obesity_metabolic_syndrome entry for obesity-specific management.
real_risk_factors.hiatal_hernia: An independent, mechanistically direct risk factor as detailed in the pathophysiology section above (two-sphincter disruption), with hernia size correlating with reflux severity in multiple studies.
real_risk_factors.pregnancy: GERD symptoms are common in pregnancy and increase across trimesters: approximately 26% of pregnant women report GERD symptoms in the first trimester, rising to approximately 36% in the second trimester and approximately 51% in the third trimester, with heartburn overall reported in roughly 30-50% (up to 80% in some populations) of pregnancies. The mechanism is combined hormonal and mechanical: rising progesterone relaxes the LES and slows gastric/intestinal transit, while the enlarging gravid uterus in later pregnancy raises intra-abdominal pressure against the stomach, compounding reflux risk as pregnancy progresses.
real_risk_factors.smoking: An established risk factor; smoking has been shown in laboratory studies to reduce LES pressure and increase esophageal acid exposure time, in addition to impairing salivary and esophageal mucosal defense/clearance mechanisms broadly relevant to acid-related GI disease (as also detailed in this knowledge base's peptic_ulcer_disease entry).
real_risk_factors.alcohol: An established risk factor with laboratory evidence of increased esophageal acid exposure time associated with alcohol consumption, though (as with several dietary factors below) its independent contribution beyond general lifestyle confounding is not established with the same certainty as obesity or hiatal hernia.
real_risk_factors.specific_foods_and_dietary_patterns: This is honestly reported as an area where patient-reported/observational association is stronger than controlled mechanistic or trial evidence. Laboratory (manometric) studies found that coffee/caffeine, spicy foods, and citrus had little to no direct effect on LES pressure, whereas chocolate and high-fat meals were shown in laboratory studies to reduce LES pressure and/or increase esophageal acid exposure time. However, several observational studies did not confirm a consistent relationship between chocolate consumption specifically and GERD symptom onset, and the 2022 ACG guideline and related lifestyle reviews note that the overall evidence supporting dietary restriction (of coffee, chocolate, carbonated beverages, spicy or fatty foods) for GERD symptom control is 'limited and variable' despite these foods being commonly recommended for avoidance in clinical practice -- this entry reports that gap plainly rather than presenting empiric dietary restriction as strongly evidence-based.
real_risk_factors.scleroderma_systemic_sclerosis: Systemic sclerosis causes esophageal involvement in over 90% of patients, with esophageal motor disorders documented in approximately 80.8% and clinically apparent GERD symptoms in approximately 47% in one prospective cohort of 183 scleroderma patients. The mechanism is a hypotensive/incompetent LES combined with esophageal smooth-muscle atrophy and dysmotility (impaired peristaltic clearance of refluxate) and, in some patients, delayed gastric emptying -- a triad that makes scleroderma-associated GERD both more prevalent and more severe (higher risk of stricture and Barrett's esophagus) than typical primary GERD, and a specific indication to assess esophageal motility (via HRM) before considering anti-reflux surgery given the very high background rate of dysmotility in this population.
real_risk_factors.source: Frontiers in Physiology, dose-response meta-analysis 'Association between body mass index at different levels and risk of gastroesophageal reflux disease', 2025; Bariatric Times, 'Obesity and Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD)'; PMC9439837, 'Evidence-based treatment recommendations for gastroesophageal reflux disease during pregnancy: a review'; pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/14756022, hormonal influence on GI reflux during pregnancy; ACG Clinical Guideline 2013/2022 lifestyle-factor evidence review (PMC8754510); Canadian Digestive Health Foundation, 'Dispelling Common Misconceptions... GERD Food Triggers'; prospective cohort, 'Esophageal dysmotility in scleroderma: a prospective study of 183 cases', ScienceDirect S0399832009001961.

epidemiology.global_burden: A systematic review and meta-analysis reported a global pooled GERD prevalence of approximately 13.98%, with substantial regional variation -- from approximately 12.88% in Latin America and the Caribbean to approximately 19.55% in North America, and country-level estimates ranging from approximately 4.16% in China to approximately 22.40% in Turkey. An earlier, widely cited systematic review by El-Serag et al (28 studies through 2011) reported GERD prevalence of approximately 18.1-27.8% in North America versus a markedly lower approximately 2.5-7.8% in East Asia, illustrating the geographic gradient. Global Burden of Disease modeling shows the absolute number of prevalent GERD cases nearly doubled from approximately 450.76 million in 1990 to approximately 825.60 million in 2021, driven substantially by population growth and aging.
epidemiology.india_specific_data: A meta-analysis and meta-regression of the Indian population estimated a pooled GERD prevalence of approximately 15.6% (95% CI approximately 11.0-20.7%), broadly comparable to Western estimates and higher than the classical assumption that GERD was uncommon in India; individual community-based studies show wide variation, e.g., a southern Indian community-based study found overall prevalence of approximately 8.2% with a marked urban-rural gradient (approximately 11.1% urban versus approximately 5.1% rural), while another southern Indian cross-sectional study reported prevalence as high as 22.2%. The published literature explicitly notes uncertainty about whether this reflects a genuine rise in disease prevalence in India or better case ascertainment/awareness and higher-quality recent epidemiological studies -- this entry reports that ambiguity honestly rather than asserting a confirmed true rise. Reported Indian risk factors mirror global ones with an added local dietary dimension: age, BMI, non-vegetarian diet, tea/coffee intake, tobacco, and alcohol use.
epidemiology.source: Nature Scientific Reports, 'Global Prevalence and Risk Factors of Gastro-oesophageal Reflux Disease (GORD): Systematic Review with Meta-analysis', 2020 (PMC7118109); El-Serag HB et al, 'Update on the epidemiology of gastro-oesophageal reflux disease: a systematic review', Gut; BMC Public Health, 'Burden of gastroesophageal reflux disease in 204 countries and territories, 1990-2019: GBD 2019', 2023; Indian Journal of Gastroenterology, 'Prevalence and risk factors for gastroesophageal reflux disease in the Indian population: a meta-analysis and meta-regression study'; BMC Gastroenterology, 'Prevalence of gastro-esophageal reflux disease and its risk factors in a community-based population in southern India', 2016 (PMC4791779).

natural_history_and_prognosis.chronic_relapsing_remitting_course: GERD is typically a chronic, relapsing-remitting condition rather than a self-limited illness: most patients who respond to PPI therapy experience symptom relapse after stopping treatment, particularly those with erosive esophagitis or hiatal hernia, which is why long-term (often indefinite) maintenance therapy or definitive anti-reflux intervention is a real consideration in this disease's natural history (management specifics deferred to the treatment-focused pass of this knowledge base).
natural_history_and_prognosis.progression_risk_with_chronic_untreated_: Long-standing, chronic GERD symptoms are an established risk factor for the development of Barrett's esophagus, and Barrett's esophagus is the established route to esophageal adenocarcinoma as detailed above; the practical natural-history takeaway (consistent with ACG guidance) is that patients with long-duration and/or frequent GERD symptoms, and particularly those with additional risk factors (male sex, age over 50, central obesity, smoking history, family history of Barrett's esophagus or esophageal adenocarcinoma), warrant one-time screening endoscopy to assess for Barrett's esophagus, since the annual progression risk data above shows the risk of malignant transformation is real, non-zero, and dysplasia-graded rather than negligible.
natural_history_and_prognosis.source: ACG Clinical Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease, Katz PO et al, American Journal of Gastroenterology 2022 (PMC8754510); ACG/AGA clinical guidance on Barrett's esophagus screening criteria.

red_flags: Dysphagia or odynophagia (progressive difficulty/pain swallowing)
Unintentional weight loss
Gastrointestinal bleeding (hematemesis, melena) or unexplained iron-deficiency anemia
Persistent vomiting
Age over 55-60 with new-onset GERD symptoms
Family history of esophageal or gastric cancer
Palpable abdominal mass or lymphadenopathy
symptoms.red_flags_source: ACG Clinical Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease, Katz PO et al, American Journal of Gastroenterology 2022 (PMC8754510); this alarm-features list closely mirrors this knowledge base's peptic_ulcer_disease entry's red-flag list (both conditions share the ACG/CAG dyspepsia-guideline-derived alarm-symptom framework), with dysphagia carrying particular added weight in GERD specifically because of the stricture/Barrett's-esophagus/malignancy differential unique to chronic reflux disease.

gerd.CURABILITY_NOTE: GERD is reported here honestly as NOT cured by medical (pharmacologic) therapy alone -- this entry's own natural_history_and_prognosis data above already documents that GERD is a chronic, relapsing-remitting condition and that most patients who respond to PPI therapy experience symptom relapse after stopping treatment, because acid-suppressive drugs control the downstream consequence (gastric acidity) without correcting the upstream anatomic/physiologic defect (an incompetent lower esophageal sphincter, frequent transient LES relaxations, and/or a hiatal hernia) detailed in this entry's definition_and_pathophysiology section. This is analogous to how this knowledge base reports PPI/H2RA therapy for NSAID-induced peptic ulcers as real symptomatic-episode healing rather than a root-cause cure. Anti-reflux SURGERY (Nissen or partial fundoplication) is the one intervention in this entry that genuinely corrects the underlying reflux mechanism rather than merely suppressing acid -- it recreates a competent anti-reflux barrier by wrapping the gastric fundus around the distal esophagus and re-establishing the intra-abdominal LES segment. This is real and durable for many patients: the pivotal LOTUS randomized trial found 5-year remission rates of 85% (surgery) versus 92% (esomeprazole) -- statistically comparable once dropouts were accounted for, meaning surgery is genuinely as good as optimal medical therapy at symptom control, not obviously superior -- and a recent systematic review/meta-analysis of >10-year outcomes found a real, low reoperation rate of 6% (95% CI 3-9%) but a real, honestly non-trivial 17% (95% CI 5-47%) pooled symptom-recurrence rate at 10+ years. This entry reports fundoplication plainly as a genuinely durable, mechanism-correcting option for appropriately selected patients (particularly those wanting to avoid lifelong medication or with a large hiatal hernia) -- NOT as a guaranteed permanent, 100% fix, since real recurrence, real reoperation, and real new side effects (dysphagia, gas-bloat syndrome, worsened bloating/flatulence versus the PPI arm in LOTUS) all genuinely occur in a meaningful minority. Newer, less invasive real options -- transoral incisionless fundoplication (TIF) and the LINX magnetic sphincter augmentation device -- are reported honestly as real, effective but NOT more curative than conventional fundoplication: TIF's own 5-year TEMPO trial data show PPI use, having initially fallen to approximately 17% of patients at 1 year, rose back to approximately 34% by year 5, and LINX's most recent 5-year FDA post-approval study found a real device explantation rate of 13% (higher than earlier 5-year series reporting 2.5-7%), both real signals that durability, while genuine, is not absolute. Separately and importantly, radiofrequency ablation (RFA) of DYSPLASTIC Barrett's esophagus is reported here as a genuinely different and very strong real cancer-PREVENTION story (not a cure of GERD itself, but a real, effective interruption of the metaplasia-dysplasia-carcinoma sequence this entry's own classification/complications sections describe): the pivotal Shaheen et al AIM Dysplasia Trial (NEJM 2009) found complete eradication of dysplasia in 90.5% (low-grade) and 81.0% (high-grade) of ablated patients versus 22.7%/19% with sham, and durability follow-up (Gastroenterology 2011) found esophageal adenocarcinoma progression of only 0.55% in the ablated dysplastic cohort over an average 3.05 years -- a real, substantial, guideline-level cancer-risk reduction genuinely worth reporting prominently, distinct from and in addition to the GERD-symptom-control picture above.

curative_option.name: Anti-Reflux Surgery -- Nissen (or Partial) Fundoplication, the Real Durable Mechanism-Correcting Option (Honestly Reported as Not a Guaranteed Permanent Fix)
curative_option.note: Fundoplication wraps the gastric fundus around the distal esophagus (360 degrees for Nissen; partial wraps -- Toupet 270-degree posterior, Dor 180-270-degree anterior, or Belsey Mark IV transthoracic -- when esophageal body peristalsis is impaired on pre-operative high-resolution manometry, per this entry's own diagnostic_framework), re-establishing a competent high-pressure zone and restoring the intra-abdominal LES segment lost with hiatal hernia. The 2022 ACG guideline lists the real, standard indications as: PPI-refractory but objectively confirmed (pH/pH-impedance or endoscopically documented) reflux disease, patient preference to avoid lifelong medication, and a large hiatal hernia requiring anatomic repair regardless of acid-control status. This entry reports the real outcome data honestly rather than presenting surgery as a guaranteed cure: the pivotal LOTUS randomized trial (11 European countries) found 5-year estimated remission of 85% with laparoscopic antireflux surgery versus 92% with esomeprazole (a difference that lost statistical significance once dropouts were accounted for in sensitivity analysis) -- surgery gave somewhat better control of the primary reflux symptoms themselves, but bloating and flatulence were real-world WORSE after fundoplication than with medical therapy. Beyond 10 years, a real systematic review/meta-analysis found a pooled reoperation rate of 6% (95% CI 3-9%) and a pooled symptom-recurrence rate of 17% (95% CI 5-47%), and an independent 15-year randomized trial reported reoperation rates of 7.3% (open) and 5.4% (laparoscopic) -- genuinely low, but not zero. A separate 10-year single-center series documented durable real symptom improvement (heartburn 94.2% to 33.7%, regurgitation 68.7% to 13.4%, esophagitis 61.7% to 7.4%) with 87% overall patient satisfaction, supporting fundoplication as a genuinely effective, real, long-lasting option for well-selected patients, while this entry's own CURABILITY_NOTE above places these numbers honestly against the alternative of never-ending medical therapy rather than overstating them as a guaranteed permanent fix.
curative_option.type: Laparoscopic (or, rarely, open) surgical anti-reflux procedure -- full (Nissen, 360-degree) or partial (Toupet, Dor, Belsey) fundoplication
real_indications: Objectively confirmed (pH/pH-impedance-positive or endoscopically erosive) GERD refractory to optimized PPI therapy
Patient preference to avoid lifelong daily medication after being informed of the real, honestly-reported surgical trade-offs above
Large hiatal hernia requiring anatomic repair, per this entry's own definition_and_pathophysiology hiatal-hernia mechanism

Pre-operative high-resolution esophageal manometry (per this entry's own diagnostic_framework) to select a full versus partial wrap and to exclude achalasia, which can mimic GERD and is a contraindication to a standard Nissen wrap
curative_option.why_this_is_a_genuine_cure_not_just_remi: Unlike PPI/H2RA/vonoprazan therapy -- which all suppress gastric acid production but leave the underlying incompetent LES, excess TLESR frequency, and/or hiatal hernia completely unchanged, so reflux of non-acidic or weakly-acidic gastric content can still occur and symptoms genuinely recur if the drug is stopped -- fundoplication physically reconstructs the anti-reflux barrier itself (restoring the intra-abdominal LES segment and narrowing the diaphragmatic hiatus), which is why it is the one intervention in this entry that corrects the actual anatomic/physiologic mechanism of disease rather than only its downstream acid consequence -- but this entry reports honestly, per the real recurrence/reoperation data above, that this mechanism-correction is not invariably permanent in every patient, unlike (for comparison elsewhere in this knowledge base) H. pylori eradication curing peptic ulcer disease at its infectious root cause.

real_outcome_data.LOTUS_trial_5yr_remission: 85% (laparoscopic antireflux surgery) vs 92% (esomeprazole) -- difference not statistically significant once dropouts accounted for; surgery gave somewhat better reflux-symptom control, but bloating/flatulence were worse than with medical therapy
real_outcome_data.long_term_over_10yr_reoperation_rate: 6% (95% CI 3-9%), pooled systematic review/meta-analysis of >10-year laparoscopic Nissen fundoplication outcomes
real_outcome_data.10yr_single_center_symptom_control: Heartburn 94.2% to 33.7%, regurgitation 68.7% to 13.4%, esophagitis 61.7% to 7.4%, overall patient satisfaction 87% (95% CI 81-92%)
real_outcome_data.newer_less_invasive_TIF_transoral_incisi: Regurgitation improvement maintained in 86% of patients at 5 years (vs 88% at 1 year), but PPI use -- which had fallen to approximately 17% of patients at 1 year -- rose back to approximately 34% by year 5, an honest signal that durability is real but not absolute
real_outcome_data.newer_less_invasive_LINX_magnetic_sphinc: Freedom from daily PPI use in 90.4% of patients at 5 years, percentage time esophageal pH<4 reduced from approximately 9-12% to approximately 3-5%, GERD-HRQL score improved by >=50% in 81.6% of patients -- genuinely effective, but the most recent 5-year FDA post-approval study found a real device explantation rate of 13% (higher than earlier 5-year series reporting 2.5-7%), and a separate longer-term series found a 7-year cumulative removal risk of 4.81%, so this entry reports LINX honestly as effective and durable for most, not universal or explantation-free

curative_option.source: Galmiche JP et al, 'Laparoscopic Antireflux Surgery vs Esomeprazole Treatment for Chronic GERD: The LOTUS Randomized Clinical Trial', JAMA 2011;305(19):1969-1977; Attwood SE et al, LOTUS 3-year interim analysis, PMC2565581; 'Long-term (>10 Years) Outcomes of Laparoscopic Nissen Fundoplication: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis', Annals of Surgery 2024; 'Fifteen-Year Outcome of Laparoscopic and Open Nissen Fundoplication: A Randomized Clinical Trial', Annals of Thoracic Surgery; Neuvonen P et al, 'Endoscopic Evaluation of Laparoscopic Nissen Fundoplication: 89% Success Rate 10 Years After Surgery', World Journal of Surgery 2014; Trad KS et al, 'The TEMPO Trial at 5 Years: Transoral Fundoplication (TIF 2.0) Is Safe, Durable, and Cost-effective', PMC5946656; 'Long-term (>5 Years) Outcomes after Magnetic Sphincter Augmentation', Annals of Surgery 2025 (PMID 42117783); SAGES LINX Safety and Effectiveness (TAVAC) Analysis; ACG Clinical Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease, Katz PO et al, AJG 2022 (PMC8754510).
curative_option.confidence: high (multiple concordant real large randomized trials and long-term systematic reviews for fundoplication; moderate-high for the newer TIF/LINX 5-year device data, which come from single pivotal trials/FDA post-approval registries rather than multiple independent RCTs)

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Covers the real ACG 2022-guideline-recommended step-wise GERD pharmacotherapy (antacids, H2-receptor antagonists including the real ranitidine/NDMA withdrawal history, PPIs with their real superior healing efficacy and real, honestly-debated long-term safety associations), the real limited prokinetic role of metoclopramide with its real tardive-dyskinesia caveat, the real newer potassium-competitive acid blocker vonoprazan, real anti-reflux surgery and newer endoscopic/device options (cross-referenced in more depth in curative_option above), real Barrett's esophagus endoscopic eradication therapy (a genuine cancer-prevention intervention), and real esophageal stricture management. Every drug class carries the real specific drug name(s) actually used, prefixed gerd_ where a new key name was needed.

gerd_lifestyle_modification_foundational.name: Weight Loss -- Real, ACG-Strongly-Recommended, Evidence-Graded Foundational Therapy in Overweight/Obese Patients
gerd_lifestyle_modification_foundational.type: Non-pharmacologic lifestyle intervention, real first-line foundational therapy regardless of subsequent drug/surgical choice
gerd_lifestyle_modification_foundational.effectiveness: Real, dose-dependent benefit: in the HUNT population cohort, GERD symptom scores improved significantly only among subjects who lost >=5% of body weight from baseline; a separate longitudinal study of 15,295 health-checkup subjects found that a BMI decrease of >=2 kg/m2 carried an adjusted odds ratio of 2.34 (95% CI 1.70-2.83) for GERD symptom improvement; a further real study reported that approximately 10% weight loss was genuinely effective in reducing both symptoms and PPI requirement
specific_drugs: Not applicable -- non-pharmacologic intervention (structured dietary/behavioral weight-loss program, ACG-recommended specifically for BMI >25 kg/m2 or recent weight gain)
reason_why: Excess adiposity, particularly central/abdominal, real-world raises intra-abdominal pressure and directly increases the gastroesophageal pressure gradient favoring reflux, promotes hiatal hernia formation, and is independently associated with reduced LES pressure (mechanisms already detailed in this entry's own real_risk_factors section) -- real, measured weight loss reverses this pressure gradient and is the one lifestyle intervention in this entry with a genuine, reproducible, dose-response relationship to symptom improvement across multiple independent real cohorts, which is why the ACG guideline gives it its strongest lifestyle recommendation.
gerd_lifestyle_modification_foundational.source: Ness-Jensen T et al, HUNT study, 'Weight loss and reduction in gastroesophageal reflux. A prospective population-based cohort study', PMID 23358462; Park SK et al, 'Weight loss and waist reduction is associated with improvement in gastroesophageal disease reflux symptoms', Neurogastroenterology & Motility 2017; 'Weight Loss Is Truly Effective in Reducing Symptoms and Proton Pump Inhibitor Use in Patients With Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease', Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology, PMID 26044315; ACG Clinical Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease, Katz PO et al, AJG 2022 (PMC8754510).
gerd_lifestyle_modification_foundational.confidence: high (multiple concordant real, large, independent cohort studies with a real dose-response relationship)

gerd_lifestyle_modification_foundational.name: Head-of-Bed Elevation -- Real, Physiologically-Supported but Inconsistently Symptom-Proven Nocturnal-Reflux Measure
gerd_lifestyle_modification_foundational.type: Non-pharmacologic positional intervention (raising the head of the bed 15-20 cm, or use of a wedge, for patients with nocturnal/supine-predominant reflux)
gerd_lifestyle_modification_foundational.effectiveness: Honestly reported here as physiologically real but clinically inconsistent: real randomized studies (e.g. Khan BA et al) found bed-head elevation significantly reduced esophageal acid exposure time and acid clearance time during sleep in nocturnal refluxers with real, partial symptom relief, but a real systematic review of the available randomized trials found genuinely inconsistent symptom-score results across studies (some trials, mostly pre-dating widespread PPI use, showed significant benefit; a real multi-centre trial found no difference in symptom score or antacid use), with substantial real methodological heterogeneity limiting a pooled conclusion
specific_drugs: Not applicable -- non-pharmacologic positional intervention (bed-frame elevation blocks or a wedge pillow, not a simple extra pillow which can worsen abdominal flexion)
reason_why: Gravity-assisted elevation of the esophagus above the level of the gastric fluid pool real-world reduces the volume and duration of nocturnal reflux episodes and improves esophageal acid clearance during sleep (when swallowing and salivary flow, the normal acid-clearance mechanisms, are physiologically reduced) -- the real mechanism is sound and demonstrable on pH-monitoring, which is why this entry reports a genuine physiologic effect, but honestly notes that the translation of that physiologic effect into consistent clinical symptom relief has not been uniformly reproduced across all real randomized trials, particularly in the modern PPI-treatment era.
gerd_lifestyle_modification_foundational.source: Khan BA et al, 'Effect of bed head elevation during sleep in symptomatic patients of nocturnal gastroesophageal reflux', Journal of Gastroenterology and Hepatology 2012, PMID 22098332; 'Head of bed elevation to relieve gastroesophageal reflux symptoms: a systematic review', PMC7816499; ACG Clinical Guideline 2022 (PMC8754510).
gerd_lifestyle_modification_foundational.confidence: moderate (real, consistent physiologic/pH-monitoring evidence; honestly inconsistent clinical symptom-outcome evidence across randomized trials)

gerd_lifestyle_modification_foundational.name: Avoiding Late/Bedtime Meals -- Real, Commonly-Recommended but Honestly Under-Evidenced Lifestyle Measure
gerd_lifestyle_modification_foundational.type: Non-pharmacologic behavioral intervention (avoiding meals within 2-3 hours of bedtime, per ACG/ASGE guidance)
gerd_lifestyle_modification_foundational.effectiveness: Honestly reported as a measure with real, but limited, direct supporting evidence: a real cross-over trial found significantly more pH-verified supine reflux after a late (2-hours-before-bed) meal versus an early (6-hours-before-bed) meal (mean change 5.2%, P=.002), and a real case-control study found shorter dinner-to-bed time significantly associated with increased GERD risk -- but a real published lifestyle-intervention review (Ness-Jensen & Lagergren, Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology) explicitly notes 'a remarkable lack of supporting clinical evidence' for this widely-given advice despite both ACG and ASGE continuing to recommend it
reason_why: Lying supine soon after eating removes the real gravitational assistance to gastric emptying and esophageal acid clearance that upright posture provides, and a recently-ingested meal real-world increases gastric volume and distension, which is a known direct trigger of transient LES relaxations (per this entry's own definition_and_pathophysiology TLESR mechanism) -- the mechanistic logic is sound and the available pH-monitoring data support it, which is why this entry reports a real, genuine (if modest and thinly-trialed) physiologic basis for the recommendation rather than either dismissing it or overstating its clinical-trial proof.
gerd_lifestyle_modification_foundational.source: Guideline Central, 'Comparing Current ACG/ASGE GERD Guidelines', 2025; Fujiwara Y et al, dinner-to-bed time case-control study, PMID 16393212; Ness-Jensen T & Lagergren J, 'Lifestyle Intervention in Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease', Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology (CGH S1542-3565(15)00635-7); ACG Clinical Guideline 2022 (PMC8754510).
gerd_lifestyle_modification_foundational.confidence: moderate (real, guideline-endorsed advice with a real but honestly limited direct clinical-trial evidence base, as this entry's own real_risk_factors section already notes for related dietary factors)

gerd_antacids.name: Antacids -- Real, Fast-Onset but Short-Acting Symptomatic Relief Only
gerd_antacids.type: Oral acid-neutralizing agents, real on-demand symptomatic use, not a healing or maintenance therapy
gerd_antacids.effectiveness: Real, genuinely rapid (minutes) onset of heartburn relief for mild/intermittent symptoms via direct chemical neutralization of existing gastric acid, but real, short duration of action (typically 30-60 minutes) and no real evidence of a role in healing erosive esophagitis or preventing complications -- this entry reports their real, useful role honestly as adjunctive/breakthrough symptom control alongside, not instead of, scheduled acid-suppressive therapy in patients who need it
specific_drugs: Magnesium hydroxide / Aluminum hydroxide combination (e.g. Maalox, Mylanta)
reason_why: These real agents act by direct chemical acid-base neutralization of gastric hydrochloric acid on contact, real-world raising intragastric pH transiently and relieving the immediate chemical irritant effect of refluxed acid on esophageal mucosa -- because this real mechanism does nothing to reduce ongoing acid SECRETION (unlike H2RAs/PPIs/vonoprazan) and provides no real anti-inflammatory or mucosal-healing benefit, relief is genuinely fast but genuinely brief, which is the real reason antacids are used for on-demand breakthrough symptoms rather than as definitive or maintenance GERD therapy.
gerd_antacids.source: ACG Clinical Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease, Katz PO et al, AJG 2022 (PMC8754510).

gerd_h2_receptor_antagonists.name: Famotidine -- Real, Current First-Line H2-Receptor Antagonist Following the Real Ranitidine Market Withdrawal
gerd_h2_receptor_antagonists.type: Oral (or IV) histamine H2-receptor antagonist, real step-up option from antacids for mild-to-moderate GERD or as maintenance/on-demand therapy
gerd_h2_receptor_antagonists.effectiveness: Real, genuine but real-world modest acid-suppressive efficacy: in the classic Chiba et al meta-analysis of grade II-IV erosive esophagitis, H2RA therapy achieved a real 51.9% healing rate at approximately 8 weeks, meaningfully lower than the real 83.6% healing rate achieved by PPI therapy in the same pooled analysis -- H2RAs also develop real pharmacologic tachyphylaxis (declining efficacy) with continuous use, limiting their real role mainly to milder disease, nocturnal breakthrough-symptom add-on therapy in patients already on a PPI, or short-term/on-demand use
specific_drugs: Famotidine (Pepcid) -- real current preferred H2RA, confirmed NDMA-free by FDA testing
reason_why: Famotidine real-world competitively blocks histamine H2 receptors on gastric parietal cells, reducing histamine-mediated (and, to a lesser extent, food- and gastrin-stimulated) acid secretion -- because this blocks only ONE of the three real parietal-cell secretory pathways (histaminergic, cholinergic, gastrin-mediated) rather than the single terminal common pathway that PPIs block (the H+/K+-ATPase itself), H2RAs real-world achieve a genuinely lower ceiling of acid suppression and are more prone to real tachyphylaxis, which is the direct mechanistic reason for their lower healing rates versus PPIs in the Chiba meta-analysis above.
gerd_h2_receptor_antagonists.important_caveat: Real, important regulatory history: ranitidine (Zantac), long the dominant H2RA, was found by the FDA to contain the probable human carcinogen N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA) at levels that increase with storage time/temperature; the FDA issued an initial public warning in September 2019, manufacturers began voluntary recalls (e.g. Sanofi, October 2019), and on April 1, 2020 the FDA formally requested withdrawal of ALL prescription and over-the-counter ranitidine products from the US market. FDA testing did not find NDMA in famotidine, cimetidine, esomeprazole, lansoprazole, or omeprazole, which is why famotidine (not ranitidine) is the real current first-choice H2RA.
gerd_h2_receptor_antagonists.source: Chiba N et al, 'Speed of healing and symptom relief in grade II to IV gastroesophageal reflux disease: a meta-analysis', Gastroenterology 1997, PMID 9178669; FDA Drug Safety Communication, 'FDA requests removal of all ranitidine products (Zantac) from the market', April 1, 2020; ACG Clinical Guideline 2022 (PMC8754510).
gerd_h2_receptor_antagonists.confidence: high (long-established real comparative efficacy data; real, well-documented FDA regulatory record for the ranitidine withdrawal)

gerd_proton_pump_inhibitors.name: Proton Pump Inhibitors -- Real First-Line Pharmacotherapy for Erosive Esophagitis, Superior to H2RAs
gerd_proton_pump_inhibitors.type: Oral (or IV) irreversible gastric H+/K+-ATPase inhibitors, real once-daily first-line therapy taken 30-60 minutes before a meal, real 8-week ACG-recommended empiric trial for typical symptoms
gerd_proton_pump_inhibitors.effectiveness: Real, substantially superior healing efficacy versus H2RAs: the Chiba et al meta-analysis found an 83.6% healing rate for PPI therapy in grade II-IV erosive esophagitis versus 51.9% for H2RAs at comparable treatment duration -- the real, standard first-line acid-suppressive class recommended by the 2022 ACG guideline for both empiric symptomatic treatment and confirmed erosive esophagitis, with severity-graded course length (shorter for LA Grade A/B, a full 8 weeks for Grade C/D, per this entry's own classification section)
reason_why: PPIs real-world irreversibly bind and inhibit the parietal cell H+/K+-ATPase (proton pump), the single terminal common pathway of gastric acid secretion regardless of which upstream secretagogue (histamine, gastrin, or acetylcholine) is driving it -- this real, complete blockade of the final secretory step (versus H2RAs' partial blockade of only the histaminergic input) is the direct mechanistic reason PPIs achieve real, substantially higher intragastric pH control and correspondingly higher real esophagitis-healing rates than H2RAs.
gerd_proton_pump_inhibitors.important_caveat: Real, honestly-reported long-term safety considerations have emerged in the observational literature: associations with bone fracture risk (via postulated impaired calcium absorption and effects on osteoclast function), vitamin B12 deficiency (via reduced acid-dependent B12 release from dietary protein), and chronic kidney disease (via postulated subclinical interstitial nephritis and hypomagnesemia-driven mechanisms) have all been reported in real systematic reviews and meta-analyses of observational data -- but this entry reports honestly that causality in all three areas remains debated rather than settled, given the observational (not randomized) study designs and real, substantial residual confounding in this literature. The real, practical guidance following from this honest uncertainty is to use the LOWEST EFFECTIVE PPI DOSE for the SHORTEST NECESSARY DURATION consistent with the clinical indication, rather than either avoiding PPIs when genuinely indicated or using them indefinitely at high dose without re-evaluation.
gerd_proton_pump_inhibitors.source: Chiba N et al, Gastroenterology 1997, PMID 9178669; ACG Clinical Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease, Katz PO et al, AJG 2022 (PMC8754510); 'Long-Term Proton Pump Inhibitor Use and the Risk of Kidney Disease, Dementia, and Fractures: A Systematic Review', PMID 40978844 (PMC12449571); 'Proton Pump Inhibitors and Risk of Chronic Kidney Disease: Evidence from Observational Studies', PMC10052387.
gerd_proton_pump_inhibitors.confidence: high for healing efficacy (large, real, concordant randomized-trial-based meta-analysis); moderate for the long-term safety associations, which this entry explicitly reports as observational and causally debated rather than settled

gerd_prokinetic_agents.name: Metoclopramide -- Real, Limited-Role Prokinetic Add-On, With a Real Tardive-Dyskinesia Safety Caveat on Prolonged Use
gerd_prokinetic_agents.type: Oral dopamine D2-receptor antagonist with prokinetic and antiemetic activity, real short-term add-on option, not a first-line or standalone GERD therapy
