gout_acute_flare_adjunct_ice.name: Topical Ice Therapy as an Adjunct - Small Randomised Trial Shows Added Pain Relief; Conditionally Guideline-Recommended
specific_drugs: Topical ice / cold pack applied to the affected joint (adjunct only)
Background regimen used in the trial: prednisone 30 mg tapered over 6 days plus colchicine 0.6 mg/day
gout_acute_flare_adjunct_ice.effectiveness: Schlesinger 2002 (19 patients, one-week follow-up): with a background of oral prednisone (30 mg tapered) and colchicine, ice therapy reduced pain by 7.75 cm (SD 2.58) on a 10-cm scale versus 4.42 cm (SD 2.96) without ice (p=0.021); joint circumference and synovial fluid volume trended better but not significantly. The 2020 ACR guideline conditionally recommends topical ice as an adjuvant.
gout_acute_flare_adjunct_ice.reason_why: Cooling the inflamed joint reduces local blood flow, oedema and nerve conduction, adding analgesia on top of anti-inflammatory drugs.
gout_acute_flare_adjunct_ice.important_caveat: Only 19 patients; the trial could not show an effect beyond analgesia. It is an adjunct, not a treatment of the crystal deposit.
gout_acute_flare_adjunct_ice.real_working_solution: Apply ice as an add-on to, never a replacement for, an anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID, colchicine or glucocorticoid).
gout_acute_flare_adjunct_ice.source: Schlesinger N et al., 'Local ice therapy during bouts of acute gouty arthritis', J Rheumatol 2002;29:331-334 (PMID 11838852); FitzGerald JD et al., '2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout', Arthritis Care Res (Hoboken) 2020;72:744-760 (PMID 32391934)

gout_ult_treat_to_target_strategy.name: Treat-to-Target Urate-Lowering Strategy (Serum Urate <6 mg/dL; <5 mg/dL if Severe/Tophaceous) With Nurse-Led Education - 95% Versus 30% Reaching Target at 2 Years
gout_ult_treat_to_target_strategy.type: Management strategy: titrate urate-lowering drug against serial serum urate measurements, with patient education and engagement
specific_drugs: Allopurinol (first-line xanthine-oxidase inhibitor, titrated to serum urate target)
gout_ult_treat_to_target_strategy.effectiveness: Nottingham Gout Treatment Trial (Doherty 2018; 517 patients, nurse-led care 255 versus GP-led usual care 262): 95% versus 30% had serum urate below 360 umol/L (6 mg/dL) at 2 years (RR 3.18, 95% CI 2.42-4.18, p<0.0001); all secondary outcomes (flares in year 2, tophi, quality of life) favoured nurse-led care; cost per QALY gained GBP 5,066. Follow-up of the same trial (Fuller 2020, 82% questionnaire response): nurse-led participants were more likely to be on urate-lowering therapy (adjusted RR 1.19, 1.09-1.30) and had fewer flares in the previous 12 months (median 0 versus 1, p<0.001). Pooled analysis of two RCTs (Stamp 2022): between months 12 and 24, 91 of 343 (27%) serum-urate responders had a flare versus 156 of 245 (64%) non-responders (adjusted OR 0.29, 95% CI 0.17-0.51). Retrospective 267-patient cohort (Shoji 2004): lower follow-up serum urate (OR 0.42) and antihyperuricaemic drug use (OR 0.22) each associated with fewer attacks. 2020 ACR: strongly recommends a treat-to-target strategy with dose titration guided by serial serum urate (moderate evidence) and a target below 6 mg/dL (high evidence); 2016 EULAR: keep serum urate <6 mg/dL, and <5 mg/dL in severe gout.
gout_ult_treat_to_target_strategy.reason_why: Urate crystals form and dissolve according to the tissue urate saturation threshold; keeping serum urate below the threshold lets crystal deposits dissolve, so flares and tophi stop - a dose that never reaches the target cannot do this.
gout_ult_treat_to_target_strategy.important_caveat: Indications: the ACR 2020 strongly recommends urate-lowering therapy for tophi, radiographic damage or frequent flares; it conditionally recommends against starting it after a first flare and against pharmacological treatment of asymptomatic hyperuricaemia, and conditionally recommends starting it in patients with infrequent flares (<2 per year). The 95%/30% figures come from a single UK trial and a nurse-led programme that may not transfer unchanged to other health systems.
gout_ult_treat_to_target_strategy.real_working_solution: Measure serum urate, titrate the urate-lowering drug stepwise until serum urate is below 6 mg/dL (below 5 mg/dL if tophi), then keep it there; a nurse-led programme of education plus titration raised target attainment from 30% to 95%.
gout_ult_treat_to_target_strategy.source: Doherty M et al. (Nottingham Gout Treatment Trial), 'Efficacy and cost-effectiveness of nurse-led care involving education and engagement of patients and a treat-to-target urate-lowering strategy versus usual care for gout', Lancet 2018;392:1403-1412 (PMID 30343856); Fuller A et al., 'Nurse-led care is preferred over GP-led care of gout and improves gout outcomes: results of Nottingham Gout Treatment Trial follow-up study', Rheumatology (Oxford) 2020;59:575-579 (PMID 31410473); Stamp LK et al., 'Association between serum urate and flares in people with gout and evidence for surrogate status: a secondary analysis of two randomised controlled trials', Lancet Rheumatol 2022;4:e53-e60 (PMID 38288731); Shoji A et al., 'A retrospective study of the relationship between serum urate level and recurrent attacks of gouty arthritis', Arthritis Rheum 2004;51:321-325 (PMID 15188314); FitzGerald JD et al., '2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout', Arthritis Care Res (Hoboken) 2020;72:744-760 (PMID 32391934); Richette P et al., '2016 updated EULAR evidence-based recommendations for the management of gout', Ann Rheum Dis 2017;76:29-42 (PMID 27457514)

gout_ult_treat_to_target_strategy.name: Starting Urate-Lowering Therapy During an Acute Flare - RCT Shows No Worsening of Pain or Flares; ACR Conditionally Prefers Starting During the Flare
gout_ult_treat_to_target_strategy.type: Timing strategy for initiating urate-lowering therapy
specific_drugs: Allopurinol 300 mg daily (as tested; ACR advises a low starting dose <=100 mg/day, lower in CKD)
Indomethacin 50 mg three times daily as background flare treatment
Colchicine 0.6 mg twice daily as background prophylaxis
gout_ult_treat_to_target_strategy.effectiveness: Taylor 2012 (57 men with crystal-proven gout, 51 evaluable): allopurinol 300 mg versus placebo for 10 days on top of indomethacin and 90 days of colchicine prophylaxis - mean pain scores did not differ at any point from day 1 to day 10 (day 10: 0.18 versus 0.27, p=0.54), subsequent flares by day 30 in 2 (allopurinol) versus 3 (placebo) patients, and inflammatory markers were similar. The 2020 ACR guideline conditionally recommends starting urate-lowering therapy during the flare over waiting until it resolves (moderate evidence).
gout_ult_treat_to_target_strategy.reason_why: Serum urate can be lowered without prolonging the flare; delaying therapy mostly delays the start of crystal dissolution and risks the patient never returning for it.
gout_ult_treat_to_target_strategy.important_caveat: One small single-centre trial with 51 evaluable patients; the tested allopurinol dose (300 mg) is higher than the low starting dose the guidelines now advise.
gout_ult_treat_to_target_strategy.real_working_solution: There is no need to wait for the flare to settle: start (at low dose, with anti-inflammatory cover) at the visit where gout is diagnosed and the indication for urate-lowering therapy is met.
gout_ult_treat_to_target_strategy.source: Taylor TH et al., 'Initiation of allopurinol at first medical contact for acute attacks of gout: a randomized clinical trial', Am J Med 2012;125:1126-1134 (PMID 23098865); FitzGerald JD et al., '2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout', Arthritis Care Res (Hoboken) 2020;72:744-760 (PMID 32391934)

gout_ult_treat_to_target_strategy.name: Stopping Versus Continuing Urate-Lowering Therapy After Crystals Have Cleared - Withdrawal Has Been Studied Only in Selected Patients; ACR Conditionally Advises Continuing
gout_ult_treat_to_target_strategy.effectiveness: Perez-Ruiz 2011 (prospective cohort of 211 gout patients whose urate-lowering therapy was withdrawn after 5 years without tophi or 5 years after the last tophus resolved): none of the patients whose average serum urate after withdrawal stayed below 7 mg/dL had a crystal-proven recurrence; weight loss and losartan or fenofibrate use were associated with staying below 7 mg/dL, and diuretic use with failing to. Perez-Ruiz 2006: patients whose average serum urate was below 5.05 mg/dL on therapy and below 8.75 mg/dL after withdrawal had the longest (>4 years) symptom-free interval. The 2020 ACR guideline conditionally recommends continuing urate-lowering therapy indefinitely rather than stopping.
gout_ult_treat_to_target_strategy.reason_why: Tissue urate stores take years to deplete; once depleted, a lower rate of new crystal formation may keep crystals away for years if serum urate stays modest - but the underlying urate overload persists and the pool refills when serum urate rises.
gout_ult_treat_to_target_strategy.important_caveat: Both Perez-Ruiz studies are observational and single-centre; there is no randomised withdrawal trial.
gout_ult_treat_to_target_strategy.real_working_solution: Default to lifelong therapy; discuss supervised withdrawal only for a patient with a long, well-documented period at target, no tophi, and factors that keep untreated serum urate low (weight loss, no diuretic, possibly losartan), with regular serum urate checks after stopping.
gout_ult_treat_to_target_strategy.source: Perez-Ruiz F et al., 'A two-stage approach to the treatment of hyperuricemia in gout: the dirty dish hypothesis', Arthritis Rheum 2011;63:4002-4006 (PMID 21898351); Perez-Ruiz F et al., 'Using serum urate levels to determine the period free of gouty symptoms after withdrawal of long-term urate-lowering therapy: a prospective study', Arthritis Rheum 2006;55:786-790 (PMID 17013833); FitzGerald JD et al., '2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout', Arthritis Care Res (Hoboken) 2020;72:744-760 (PMID 32391934)

gout_ult_allopurinol.name: Allopurinol - First-Line Urate-Lowering Drug: Start Low, Titrate to Target; Fixed 300 mg Often Fails, Dose Escalation Works (Stamp RCT 69% Versus 32%)
gout_ult_allopurinol.type: Xanthine-oxidase inhibitor (purine analogue), oral once daily
specific_drugs: Allopurinol 100 mg and 300 mg tablets (Zyloprim; in India Zyloric, GlaxoSmithKline Pharmaceuticals)
gout_ult_allopurinol.effectiveness: Label dosing: start 100 mg daily and increase by 100 mg at weekly intervals until serum urate is 6 mg/dL or less (maximum 800 mg daily); 50 mg daily start in impaired kidney function; baseline uric acid, blood count, liver and kidney tests; prophylaxis for flares recommended. Dose-escalation RCT (Stamp 2017; 183 participants, 52% with creatinine clearance <60 mL/min, 12 months): serum urate <6 mg/dL in 69% of the dose-escalation group versus 32% of controls; mean urate change -1.5 versus -0.34 mg/dL; no difference in renal function change; the 24-month extension confirmed most people tolerate doses above creatinine-clearance-based limits, with fewer flares and smaller tophi in both groups. A fixed 300 mg dose underperforms: in APEX only 22% of allopurinol 300 mg (100 mg in renal impairment) patients had the last three monthly serum urates <6.0 mg/dL at 28 weeks versus 48% (febuxostat 80 mg) and 65% (120 mg); in Reinders 2009 only 20 of 82 (24%) reached <=5.0 mg/dL after 2 months on 300 mg. 2020 ACR: strongly recommends allopurinol as preferred first-line, including in moderate-to-severe CKD, starting at <=100 mg/day (lower in CKD) and titrating above 300 mg/day as needed. Starting dose matters: Stamp 2012 (54 hypersensitivity cases, 157 controls) found 91% of cases versus 36% of controls started at >=1.5 mg per unit eGFR, top-quintile starting dose OR 23.2.
gout_ult_allopurinol.reason_why: Allopurinol and its metabolite oxypurinol inhibit xanthine oxidase, blocking the last two steps of purine degradation (hypoxanthine to xanthine to uric acid), so less urate enters the blood.
gout_ult_allopurinol.important_caveat: Allopurinol also interacts with azathioprine and mercaptopurine (dose reduction needed), capecitabine (avoid), and with pegloticase (stop allopurinol when pegloticase is started) - see the interactions category.
gout_ult_allopurinol.real_working_solution: Start allopurinol at 100 mg/day (50 mg or an eGFR-scaled dose in CKD), raise the dose stepwise against serum urate (100 mg weekly per the label; monthly in the Stamp trial) until <6 mg/dL (<5 mg/dL if tophi), and cover the first 3-6 months with colchicine or another anti-inflammatory; do not leave the patient on 300 mg without checking serum urate.
gout_ult_allopurinol.source: FDA, allopurinol tablets prescribing information, sections 2, 5.1, 7 (openFDA drug label API, label versions effective 2024-07-08 and 2026-06-03, accessed 2026-09-21); Stamp LK et al., 'A randomised controlled trial of the efficacy and safety of allopurinol dose escalation to achieve target serum urate in people with gout', Ann Rheum Dis 2017;76:1522-1528 (PMID 28314755); Stamp LK et al., 'Allopurinol dose escalation to achieve serum urate below 6 mg/dL: an open-label extension study', Ann Rheum Dis 2017;76:2065-2070 (PMID 28830881); Schumacher HR Jr et al. (APEX), 'Effects of febuxostat versus allopurinol and placebo in reducing serum urate in subjects with hyperuricemia and gout: a 28-week, phase III trial', Arthritis Rheum 2008;59:1540-1548 (PMID 18975369); Reinders MK et al., 'Efficacy and tolerability of urate-lowering drugs in gout: a randomised controlled trial of benzbromarone versus probenecid after failure of allopurinol', Ann Rheum Dis 2009;68:51-56 (PMID 18250112); FitzGerald JD et al., '2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout', Arthritis Care Res (Hoboken) 2020;72:744-760 (PMID 32391934); Stamp LK et al., 'Starting dose is a risk factor for allopurinol hypersensitivity syndrome: a proposed safe starting dose of allopurinol', Arthritis Rheum 2012;64:2529-2536 (PMID 22488501); Retail listings for Zyloric (allopurinol, GlaxoSmithKline Pharmaceuticals Ltd) 100 mg and 300 mg tablets (truemeds.in, medplusmart.com, accessed 2026-09-21)

gout_ult_allopurinol.name: HLA-B*58:01 Screening and Allopurinol Hypersensitivity - Strong Genetic Risk Marker; Screening Removed Severe Reactions in a Taiwanese Prospective Cohort
specific_drugs: Febuxostat (alternate xanthine-oxidase inhibitor for HLA-B*58:01 carriers)
Benzbromarone or probenecid (uricosuric alternatives, where available)
gout_ult_allopurinol.effectiveness: Hung 2005 (Han Chinese; 51 allopurinol severe cutaneous adverse reaction cases, 135 tolerant patients, 93 healthy controls): HLA-B*5801 present in 51 of 51 (100%) reaction cases versus 20 of 135 (15%) tolerant patients (OR 580.3, 95% CI 34.4-9,780.9) and 19 of 93 (20%) healthy subjects. Ko 2015 (Taiwan, 2,926 people needing allopurinol, 2,910 genotyped): 571 (19.6%) tested positive and were steered to an alternative; none of the 2,339 test-negative patients given allopurinol developed a severe cutaneous reaction versus 7 expected from the historical national incidence (0.30% per year; p=0.0026); mild rash occurred in 97 (3%). 2020 ACR: conditionally recommends HLA-B*5801 testing for patients of Southeast Asian descent (e.g. Han Chinese, Korean, Thai) and African American patients, and conditionally recommends against testing in others. Label: serious dermatologic reactions (TEN, SJS, DRESS) occur in about 5 in 10,000 (0.05%) allopurinol patients; stop at the first rash; thiazide diuretics, ampicillin/amoxicillin and bendamustine can raise skin-reaction risk.
gout_ult_allopurinol.reason_why: HLA-B*58:01 presents allopurinol/oxypurinol-derived peptides to T cells, triggering a delayed cytotoxic T-cell reaction against the skin and other organs in carriers.
gout_ult_allopurinol.important_caveat: Ko 2015 compared screening against a historical incidence estimate, not a concurrent randomised control. For India, this knowledge base's symptoms entry cites a single North Indian typing study with an allele frequency of about 15% (moderate confidence; not independently re-verified in this pass); the availability and cost of HLA-B*58:01 testing in India and any Indian guidance recommending screening were not found and are unverified.
gout_ult_allopurinol.real_working_solution: Test HLA-B*58:01 before allopurinol in the ACR-listed high-risk ancestries; if positive, choose an alternative such as febuxostat or a uricosuric; in everyone, start allopurinol low, escalate slowly, and stop it at the first rash.
gout_ult_allopurinol.source: Hung SI et al., 'HLA-B*5801 allele as a genetic marker for severe cutaneous adverse reactions caused by allopurinol', Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 2005;102:4134-4139 (PMID 15743917); Ko TM et al., 'Use of HLA-B*58:01 genotyping to prevent allopurinol induced severe cutaneous adverse reactions in Taiwan: national prospective cohort study', BMJ 2015;351:h4848 (PMID 26399967); FitzGerald JD et al., '2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout', Arthritis Care Res (Hoboken) 2020;72:744-760 (PMID 32391934); FDA, allopurinol tablets prescribing information, sections 2, 5.1, 7 (openFDA drug label API, label versions effective 2024-07-08 and 2026-06-03, accessed 2026-09-21)

gout_ult_febuxostat.name: Febuxostat - Stronger Urate Lowering Than Fixed-Dose Allopurinol (FACT, APEX) and 5-Year Durability (FOCUS)
gout_ult_febuxostat.type: Non-purine selective xanthine-oxidase inhibitor, oral once daily
specific_drugs: Indian brands: Febutaz and Febuget (Sun Pharmaceutical), Febugood (Torrent), Febucip (Cipla), Febuxor (Intas), Febumac (Macleods)
gout_ult_febuxostat.effectiveness: APEX (Schumacher 2008; 1,072 subjects, 28 weeks): last three monthly serum urates <6.0 mg/dL in 48% (febuxostat 80 mg), 65% (120 mg) and 69% (240 mg) versus 22% (allopurinol 300 or 100 mg by renal function) and 0% (placebo); in impaired renal function 4 of 9 (44%), 5 of 11 (45%) and 3 of 5 (60%) versus 0 of 10 (0%) on allopurinol 100 mg. FACT (Becker 2005; 760 patients, 507 febuxostat and 253 allopurinol, 52 weeks): flare incidence in weeks 9-52 similar (64% febuxostat 80 mg, 70% 120 mg, 64% allopurinol); median tophus-area reduction 83%, 66% and 50%. FOCUS 5-year extension (116 enrolled): 93% (54 of 58 remaining) had serum urate <6.0 mg/dL at 5 years, flares nearly abolished, and baseline tophi resolved in 69% (18 of 26); but 50% of subjects discontinued prematurely (38 in the first year) - completer bias. The FDA label restricts use to patients with an inadequate response to a maximally titrated allopurinol dose, intolerance to allopurinol, or for whom allopurinol is not advisable.
gout_ult_febuxostat.reason_why: Febuxostat is a non-purine selective xanthine-oxidase inhibitor, chemically unrelated to the purine-analogue allopurinol, and at 80-120 mg it lowers serum urate further than fixed-dose allopurinol 300 mg (APEX).
gout_ult_febuxostat.important_caveat: Head-to-head wins are against fixed-dose allopurinol 300 mg; a dose-escalated allopurinol reaches 69% (Stamp 2017), so the 22% comparator overstates febuxostat's real advantage.
gout_ult_febuxostat.real_working_solution: Use febuxostat when allopurinol, titrated to dose, has failed or is not tolerated (or is unsuitable because of hypersensitivity risk) - and only after weighing the cardiovascular signal described in the next entry.
gout_ult_febuxostat.source: Schumacher HR Jr et al. (APEX), 'Effects of febuxostat versus allopurinol and placebo in reducing serum urate in subjects with hyperuricemia and gout: a 28-week, phase III trial', Arthritis Rheum 2008;59:1540-1548 (PMID 18975369); Becker MA et al. (FACT), 'Febuxostat compared with allopurinol in patients with hyperuricemia and gout', N Engl J Med 2005;353:2450-2461 (PMID 16339094); Schumacher HR Jr et al. (FOCUS), 'Febuxostat in the treatment of gout: 5-yr findings of the FOCUS efficacy and safety study', Rheumatology (Oxford) 2009;48:188-194 (PMID 19141576); FDA, Uloric (febuxostat) prescribing information, boxed warning and indications (openFDA drug label API, label effective 2025-12-24, accessed 2026-09-21); 1mg.com, Febuxostat generic page listing Indian brands and manufacturers (1mg.com/generics/febuxostat-209871, accessed 2026-09-21)

gout_ult_febuxostat.name: Febuxostat Cardiovascular Safety - CARES Signal (Higher CV and All-Cause Death) Versus FAST (Non-Inferior) and the FDA Boxed Warning
gout_ult_febuxostat.type: Safety evidence and regulatory restriction for a xanthine-oxidase inhibitor
specific_drugs: Allopurinol (the comparator and preferred first-line drug)
gout_ult_febuxostat.effectiveness: CARES (White 2018; 6,190 patients with gout and major cardiovascular disease, median 32 months): primary composite 10.8% (335) febuxostat versus 10.4% (321) allopurinol (HR 1.03, one-sided 98.5% CI upper limit 1.23, non-inferior); all-cause mortality HR 1.22 (1.01-1.47) and cardiovascular death HR 1.34 (1.03-1.73) higher with febuxostat; 56.6% stopped the trial regimen and 45.0% left follow-up, limiting interpretation. FAST (Mackenzie 2020; 6,128 patients aged >=60 already on allopurinol with a further CV risk factor, median 4.0 years, open-label, lead-in optimising allopurinol): on-treatment primary composite 1.72 versus 2.05 events per 100 patient-years, adjusted HR 0.85 (0.70-1.03), non-inferior; deaths 222 (7.2%) febuxostat versus 263 (8.6%) allopurinol; 32.4% versus 16.5% discontinued randomised therapy. The current FDA label carries a boxed warning: gout patients with established CV disease treated with febuxostat had a higher rate of CV death than with allopurinol; use only when allopurinol at a maximally titrated dose is inadequate, not tolerated, or not advisable.
gout_ult_febuxostat.reason_why: The mechanism of the excess CV death in CARES is not established by these trials; the two trials differ in population (CARES: gout with established major cardiovascular disease; FAST: patients aged 60 or older already on allopurinol, excluding recent MI/stroke and severe heart failure) and in follow-up.
gout_ult_febuxostat.important_caveat: CARES and FAST disagree on direction (HR 1.34 for CV death versus a non-inferior composite and numerically fewer deaths); the boxed warning follows CARES.
gout_ult_febuxostat.real_working_solution: Prefer allopurinol first; keep febuxostat for allopurinol failure or intolerance, and in patients with established cardiovascular disease weigh the boxed-warning signal explicitly against the alternatives (uricosuric, or pegloticase for refractory disease).
gout_ult_febuxostat.source: White WB et al. (CARES), 'Cardiovascular safety of febuxostat or allopurinol in patients with gout', N Engl J Med 2018;378:1200-1210 (PMID 29527974); Mackenzie IS et al. (FAST), 'Long-term cardiovascular safety of febuxostat compared with allopurinol in patients with gout', Lancet 2020;396:1745-1757 (PMID 33181081); FDA, Uloric (febuxostat) prescribing information, boxed warning and indications (openFDA drug label API, label effective 2025-12-24, accessed 2026-09-21); FitzGerald JD et al., '2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout', Arthritis Care Res (Hoboken) 2020;72:744-760 (PMID 32391934)

gout_ult_uricosurics.name: Probenecid and Benzbromarone (Uricosurics) - Benzbromarone 200 mg Reached Target in 92% After Allopurinol Failure; Hepatotoxicity Caveat
gout_ult_uricosurics.type: Uricosuric agents (inhibit renal tubular urate reabsorption, URAT1/OAT), oral
specific_drugs: Benzbromarone 200 mg daily (Reinders 2009 dose; withdrawn by the originator in 2003, still used in Japan, China, Singapore and other countries)
gout_ult_uricosurics.effectiveness: Reinders 2009 (96 gout patients entered; 82 evaluable on allopurinol 300 mg for 2 months - only 20 (24%) reached serum urate <=0.30 mmol/L (5.0 mg/dL) and 9 (11%) stopped for adverse drug reactions; 62 non-responders/intolerant were then randomised): target reached in 22 of 24 (92%) with benzbromarone 200 mg/day versus 20 of 31 (65%) with probenecid 2 g/day (p=0.03); mean serum urate fall 64% versus 50% (p<0.001). Cochrane 2014: moderate-quality evidence that benzbromarone is probably as good as allopurinol and better than probenecid for serum urate normalisation, and benzbromarone caused fewer withdrawals and adverse events than probenecid. Perez-Ruiz 2002 (63 patients with tophaceous gout): tophus size reduced faster with benzbromarone or combined allopurinol plus benzbromarone than with allopurinol alone, and the velocity of reduction was linearly related to the mean serum urate during therapy. EULAR 2016: if the target cannot be reached with allopurinol, consider febuxostat, a uricosuric, or a xanthine-oxidase inhibitor combined with a uricosuric.
gout_ult_uricosurics.reason_why: Uricosurics block URAT1 and related transporters in the proximal tubule so more filtered urate is excreted in urine, lowering serum urate by increasing renal clearance rather than reducing production.
gout_ult_uricosurics.important_caveat: Benzbromarone was withdrawn by Sanofi in 2003 after reports of serious hepatotoxicity (Lee 2008 argues the case evidence was limited); use requires liver monitoring. The ACR 2020 guideline conditionally prefers switching to an alternate xanthine-oxidase inhibitor over adding a uricosuric. Availability of benzbromarone and probenecid in India was not verified.
gout_ult_uricosurics.real_working_solution: If a titrated xanthine-oxidase inhibitor fails to reach target or is not tolerated, a uricosuric (benzbromarone where legally available, otherwise probenecid), alone or combined with allopurinol, is an evidence-supported next step.
gout_ult_uricosurics.source: Reinders MK et al., 'Efficacy and tolerability of urate-lowering drugs in gout: a randomised controlled trial of benzbromarone versus probenecid after failure of allopurinol', Ann Rheum Dis 2009;68:51-56 (PMID 18250112); Kydd AS et al., 'Uricosuric medications for chronic gout', Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2014;CD010457 (PMID 25392987); Perez-Ruiz F et al., 'Effect of urate-lowering therapy on the velocity of size reduction of tophi in chronic gout', Arthritis Rheum 2002;47:356-360 (PMID 12209479); Richette P et al., '2016 updated EULAR evidence-based recommendations for the management of gout', Ann Rheum Dis 2017;76:29-42 (PMID 27457514); Lee MH et al., 'A benefit-risk assessment of benzbromarone in the treatment of gout. Was its withdrawal from the market in the best interest of patients?', Drug Saf 2008;31:643-665 (PMID 18636784); Zhang MY et al., 'Liver failure associated with benzbromarone: a case report and review of the literature', World J Clin Cases 2019;7:1717 (PMID 31367632; PMC6658378)

gout_ult_uricosurics.name: Lesinurad (Zurampic) Plus Xanthine-Oxidase Inhibitor - Higher Urate Target Rates, But Withdrawn From the US Market in 2019
gout_ult_uricosurics.type: Selective uric acid reabsorption inhibitor (URAT1 inhibitor), add-on to a xanthine-oxidase inhibitor
specific_drugs: Lesinurad 200 mg daily with allopurinol (no longer marketed in the US)
Lesinurad 200 mg or 400 mg with febuxostat (CRYSTAL trial)
gout_ult_uricosurics.effectiveness: CLEAR 1 (Saag 2017; 603 patients on stable allopurinol, mean 306.6 mg/day, 6 months): serum urate <6.0 mg/dL in 54.2% (lesinurad 200 mg) and 59.2% (400 mg) versus 27.9% with allopurinol alone (p<0.0001); no significant benefit on flare rate or complete tophus resolution; reversible creatinine elevations. CLEAR 2 (Bardin 2017; 610 patients) tested the same design. CRYSTAL (Dalbeth 2017; 324 tophaceous patients on febuxostat): serum urate <6 mg/dL at month 6 in 76.1% (lesinurad 400 mg, p<0.0001), 56.6% (200 mg, not significant at month 6) versus 46.8% with febuxostat alone; total target-tophus area reduction 50.1% and 52.9% versus 28.3%; complete tophus resolution not different. Ironwood discontinued marketing of lesinurad (Zurampic) and lesinurad-allopurinol (Duzallo) in the US effective 1 February 2019; per the company reports this was a business decision after market testing, and lesinurad carried a boxed warning for acute renal failure.
gout_ult_uricosurics.reason_why: Lesinurad selectively inhibits URAT1 and OAT4, adding a renal-excretion route on top of xanthine-oxidase inhibition, which is why it improved serum urate only when combined with an XOI.
gout_ult_uricosurics.important_caveat: Reported for completeness and honest history: it improved serum urate targets but showed no significant flare or tophus-resolution advantage in the pivotal trials.
gout_ult_uricosurics.real_working_solution: Lesinurad is no longer an available option in the US; a patient on a xanthine-oxidase inhibitor who cannot reach target should consider dose escalation, a switch to febuxostat, benzbromarone/probenecid, or referral for pegloticase.
gout_ult_uricosurics.source: Saag KG et al. (CLEAR 1), 'Lesinurad combined with allopurinol: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in gout patients with an inadequate response to standard-of-care allopurinol (a US-based study)', Arthritis Rheumatol 2017;69:203-212 (PMID 27564409); Bardin T et al. (CLEAR 2), 'Lesinurad in combination with allopurinol: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in patients with gout with inadequate response to standard of care', Ann Rheum Dis 2017;76:811-820 (PMID 27821644); Dalbeth N et al. (CRYSTAL), 'Lesinurad, a selective uric acid reabsorption inhibitor, in combination with febuxostat in patients with tophaceous gout', Arthritis Rheumatol 2017;69:1903-1913 (PMID 28597604); Fierce Pharma, 'Ironwood dumps AstraZeneca gout drug Zurampic and lays off 125 in the process' (fiercepharma.com, accessed 2026-09-21)

gout_ult_refractory_pegloticase.name: Pegloticase (Krystexxa) 8 mg IV Every 2 Weeks - 42% Pooled Responders in GOUT1/GOUT2 (0% Placebo) for Refractory Gout, With Boxed Warnings
gout_ult_refractory_pegloticase.type: PEGylated recombinant uricase, intravenous infusion every 2 weeks (specialist-supervised)
specific_drugs: Pegloticase 8 mg intravenous every 4 weeks (studied alternative arm)
gout_ult_refractory_pegloticase.effectiveness: GOUT1/GOUT2 (Sundy 2011; two 6-month placebo-controlled trials, chronic gout refractory to allopurinol): responders were defined as plasma uric acid <6.0 mg/dL in months 3 and 6. Trial C0405: 20 of 43 (47%) biweekly, 8 of 41 (20%) monthly, 0 of 20 placebo; trial C0406: 16 of 42 (38%) biweekly, 21 of 43 (49%) monthly, 0 of 23 placebo. Pooled: 36 of 85 (42%) biweekly, 29 of 84 (35%) monthly, 0 of 43 (0%) placebo (p<0.001). The FDA boxed warning covers anaphylaxis and infusion reactions (administer in a healthcare setting, premedicate with antihistamines and corticosteroids), and G6PD-deficiency-associated haemolysis and methaemoglobinaemia (contraindicated in G6PD deficiency); serum uric acid must be checked before each infusion and treatment stopped if it rises above 6 mg/dL, particularly on two consecutive readings. 2020 ACR: strongly recommends pegloticase for patients in whom xanthine-oxidase inhibitors, uricosurics and other interventions have failed to reach target and who have frequent flares or non-resolving subcutaneous tophi, and strongly recommends against it in patients with infrequent flares (<2/year) and no tophi; 2016 EULAR: pegloticase for refractory gout. The allopurinol label directs stopping allopurinol when pegloticase is started.
gout_ult_refractory_pegloticase.reason_why: Humans lack uricase; pegloticase converts urate to the highly soluble allantoin, so serum urate drops to near zero within hours and existing crystal deposits dissolve rapidly.
gout_ult_refractory_pegloticase.important_caveat: About 58% of pooled patients on pegloticase alone (biweekly) did not meet the response definition, and MIRROR showed higher anti-drug antibody positivity and infusion reactions without methotrexate; pegloticase availability, price and approval in India were not verified.
gout_ult_refractory_pegloticase.real_working_solution: For a patient with refractory, tophaceous or frequently flaring gout who has failed every oral option, pegloticase (ideally with methotrexate, next entry) is the only agent with a large controlled-trial responder rate; it is a specialist, infusion-centre therapy.
gout_ult_refractory_pegloticase.source: Sundy JS et al. (GOUT1/GOUT2, C0405/C0406), 'Efficacy and tolerability of pegloticase for the treatment of chronic gout in patients refractory to conventional treatment: two randomized controlled trials', JAMA 2011;306:711-720 (PMID 21846852); FDA, Krystexxa (pegloticase) prescribing information, boxed warning (openFDA drug label API, label effective 2026-07-09, accessed 2026-09-21); FitzGerald JD et al., '2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout', Arthritis Care Res (Hoboken) 2020;72:744-760 (PMID 32391934); Richette P et al., '2016 updated EULAR evidence-based recommendations for the management of gout', Ann Rheum Dis 2017;76:29-42 (PMID 27457514); FDA, allopurinol tablets prescribing information, sections 2, 5.1, 7 (openFDA drug label API, label versions effective 2024-07-08 and 2026-06-03, accessed 2026-09-21)

gout_ult_refractory_pegloticase.name: Pegloticase With Methotrexate Co-Therapy (MIRROR RCT) - 71.0% Versus 38.5% Responders at Month 6
gout_ult_refractory_pegloticase.type: Immunomodulation of pegloticase to reduce anti-drug antibodies
specific_drugs: Methotrexate 15 mg orally once weekly (MIRROR dose)
Folic acid 1 mg daily (MIRROR open-label study co-medication)
gout_ult_refractory_pegloticase.effectiveness: MIRROR RCT (Botson 2023; 152 patients with uncontrolled gout randomised 2:1 to methotrexate 15 mg/week 100 versus placebo 52, for 52 weeks): month-6 responders (serum urate <6 mg/dL for >=80% of the month) 71.0% (71/100) versus 38.5% (20/52), difference 32.3% (95% CI 16.3-48.3), p<0.0001; infusion-reaction rate 4.2% versus 30.6% (p<0.001); anti-drug antibody positivity lower with methotrexate. 12-month findings: response 60.0% (60/100) versus 30.8% (16/52), difference 29.1% (13.2-44.9), p=0.0003; discontinuation for serum-urate monitoring 22.9% versus 63.3%; complete resolution of >=1 tophus 53.8% (28/52) versus 31.0% (9/29) at week 52 (p=0.048). The earlier open-label MIRROR study (14 patients) had 11 of 14 (78.6%) responders at 6 months versus the previously reported 42% with pegloticase alone. Gout flares were the commonest adverse event (66.7% versus 69.4% in the first 6 months).
gout_ult_refractory_pegloticase.reason_why: Methotrexate suppresses the immune response to the PEGylated foreign protein, so anti-pegloticase antibodies form less often and the drug keeps working (and causes fewer infusion reactions).
gout_ult_refractory_pegloticase.important_caveat: The ACR 2020 guideline pre-dates the MIRROR RCT and contains no methotrexate co-therapy recommendation; methotrexate co-therapy use is trial-based, not yet a graded guideline recommendation in the sources reviewed.
gout_ult_refractory_pegloticase.real_working_solution: When pegloticase is chosen, co-prescribe oral methotrexate (started before the first infusion in the open-label study); this roughly doubled the number of patients keeping serum urate below 6 mg/dL.
gout_ult_refractory_pegloticase.source: Botson JK et al. (MIRROR RCT), 'A randomized, placebo-controlled study of methotrexate to increase response rates in patients with uncontrolled gout receiving pegloticase: primary efficacy and safety findings', Arthritis Rheumatol 2023;75:293-304 (PMID 36099211); Botson JK et al. (MIRROR RCT), '12-month findings', ACR Open Rheumatol 2023;5:407-418 (PMID 37385296); Botson JK et al. (MIRROR OL), 'Pegloticase in combination with methotrexate in patients with uncontrolled gout: a multicenter, open-label study', J Rheumatol 2021;48:767-774 (PMID 32934137)

gout_investigational_and_regional_agents.name: Investigational Urate-Lowering Agents - SEL-212 (Pegadricase Plus Sirolimus Nanoparticles) and Pozdeutinurad (AR882, URAT1 Inhibitor) - Company-Reported Phase 3 Data, Not Yet Prescribing Options
gout_investigational_and_regional_agents.type: Investigational uricase-tolerisation combination and investigational selective URAT1 inhibitor
specific_drugs: SEL-212 (pegadricase plus ImmTOR sirolimus nanoparticle; once-monthly infusion)
Pozdeutinurad (AR882) 50 mg and 75 mg once daily
gout_investigational_and_regional_agents.effectiveness: SEL-212 DISSOLVE I (US study): response (serum urate <6 mg/dL for at least 80% of month 6) in 56% (0.15 mg/kg ImmTOR) and 48% (0.1 mg/kg) versus 4% placebo; DISSOLVE II (global): 47% and 41% versus 12% placebo (company press release, 21 March 2023). Pozdeutinurad REDUCE 2 topline (company press release, 21 May 2026): serum urate <6 mg/dL at month 6 in 69.2% (75 mg) and 56.6% (50 mg) versus 8.1% placebo (p<0.0001 for both).
gout_investigational_and_regional_agents.reason_why: SEL-212 pairs a PEGylated uricase with sirolimus-loaded nanoparticles to blunt anti-drug antibodies; pozdeutinurad selectively blocks URAT1 to raise renal urate excretion.
gout_investigational_and_regional_agents.important_caveat: Both data sets are company topline press releases, not peer-reviewed publications, and their current regulatory status was not verified (the 2023 release only anticipated a US submission in the first half of 2024); they are not prescribing options.
gout_investigational_and_regional_agents.real_working_solution: These are pipeline agents; the real working options today remain the licensed ones in this survey (allopurinol first, then febuxostat or a uricosuric, then pegloticase).
gout_investigational_and_regional_agents.source: Sobi, 'Phase 3 DISSOLVE program of SEL-212 in chronic refractory gout meets primary endpoint', press release 21 March 2023 (sobi.com, accessed 2026-09-21); Sobi, 'Positive topline results from the pivotal Phase 3 REDUCE 2 study of pozdeutinurad in gout', press release 21 May 2026 (sobi.com, accessed 2026-09-21)

gout_investigational_and_regional_agents.name: Dotinurad (URECE) - Selective URAT1 Inhibitor Approved in Japan (January 2020) Only; Regional Agent, Not Available as a Standard Option Elsewhere
specific_drugs: Benzbromarone (older uricosuric with liver-injury and CYP2C9-interaction problems that dotinurad was developed to avoid)
gout_investigational_and_regional_agents.effectiveness: Dotinurad was approved for gout and hyperuricaemia in Japan in January 2020; the review reports it was developed because benzbromarone has drug-induced liver injury and CYP2C9-inhibition problems, and that dotinurad potently inhibits URAT1 in transporter-expressing cells. No response-rate percentage from a peer-reviewed trial was retrieved for this entry.
gout_investigational_and_regional_agents.reason_why: Dotinurad inhibits URAT1 in the renal proximal tubule, reducing urate reabsorption, with less off-target liver and drug-interaction liability than benzbromarone.
gout_investigational_and_regional_agents.important_caveat: Approval outside Japan and availability in India were not verified.
gout_investigational_and_regional_agents.real_working_solution: Outside Japan it is not a standard option; use the licensed alternatives in this survey.
gout_investigational_and_regional_agents.source: Taniguchi T et al., 'Pharmacological properties and clinical efficacy of dotinurad (URECE tablets), a novel hypouricemic agent', Nihon Yakurigaku Zasshi 2020;155:426-434 (PMID 33132262)

gout_flare_prophylaxis_during_ult_initia.name: Colchicine Prophylaxis When Starting Allopurinol or Febuxostat - Borstad RCT: 0.52 Versus 2.91 Flares; 6 Months Outperforms 8 Weeks
gout_flare_prophylaxis_during_ult_initia.type: Anti-inflammatory prophylaxis during urate-lowering therapy initiation
specific_drugs: Colchicine 0.6 mg twice daily (Borstad 2004 regimen); label prophylaxis dose 0.6 mg once or twice daily, maximum 1.2 mg/day
gout_flare_prophylaxis_during_ult_initia.effectiveness: Borstad 2004 (43 patients starting allopurinol, colchicine 0.6 mg twice daily versus placebo for 3 months beyond reaching serum urate <6.5 mg/dL, double-blind): total flares 0.52 versus 2.91 per patient (p=0.008; 82% fewer, computed (2.91-0.52)/2.91); flares months 0-3 0.57 versus 1.91 (p=0.022); months 3-6 0 versus 1.05 (p=0.033); flare severity on a visual analogue scale 3.64 versus 5.08 (p=0.018). Wortmann 2010 (analysis of three phase III febuxostat trials, 4,101 patients): flare rates rose sharply to as much as 40% after 8 weeks of prophylaxis was stopped and then declined slowly, whereas rates stayed at 3-5% at the end of 6 months of prophylaxis, with no increase in adverse events with the longer duration. 2020 ACR: strongly recommends anti-inflammatory prophylaxis for at least 3-6 months when starting urate-lowering therapy. The colchicine and allopurinol labels both recommend prophylaxis when urate-lowering therapy is started.
gout_flare_prophylaxis_during_ult_initia.reason_why: Lowering serum urate mobilises crystals from tissue stores, which briefly increases crystal-triggered inflammation; colchicine dampens the neutrophil response while the store empties.
gout_flare_prophylaxis_during_ult_initia.important_caveat: Colchicine interaction and renal-dose cautions apply (see interactions category); the Borstad trial was small (43 patients).
gout_flare_prophylaxis_during_ult_initia.real_working_solution: Give colchicine 0.6 mg once or twice daily (or an alternative in the next entry) from the day urate-lowering therapy starts and continue for at least 3-6 months, not 8 weeks.
gout_flare_prophylaxis_during_ult_initia.source: Borstad GC et al., 'Colchicine for prophylaxis of acute flares when initiating allopurinol for chronic gouty arthritis', J Rheumatol 2004;31:2429-2432 (PMID 15570646); Wortmann RL et al., 'Effect of prophylaxis on gout flares after the initiation of urate-lowering therapy: analysis of data from three phase III trials', Clin Ther 2010;32:2386-2397 (PMID 21353107); FitzGerald JD et al., '2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout', Arthritis Care Res (Hoboken) 2020;72:744-760 (PMID 32391934); FDA, Colcrys (colchicine) prescribing information, sections 2.1, 4, 7 (openFDA drug label API, label effective 2022-10-01, accessed 2026-09-21); FDA, allopurinol tablets prescribing information, sections 2, 5.1, 7 (openFDA drug label API, label versions effective 2024-07-08 and 2026-06-03, accessed 2026-09-21)

gout_flare_prophylaxis_during_ult_initia.name: Alternatives for Flare Prophylaxis (Low-Dose NSAID or Low-Dose Prednisone/Prednisolone) When Colchicine Cannot Be Used
specific_drugs: Naproxen (prophylactic dose used in the febuxostat phase III trials)
gout_flare_prophylaxis_during_ult_initia.effectiveness: The 2020 ACR guideline lists colchicine, NSAIDs and prednisone/prednisolone as acceptable prophylactic anti-inflammatory therapies for at least 3-6 months (dose limits for prednisone/prednisolone were not confirmed in the retrieved text). In the three febuxostat phase III trials prophylaxis with colchicine or naproxen was chosen by the investigator, with patients having an estimated creatinine clearance below 50 mL/min not to receive naproxen (Wortmann 2010).
gout_flare_prophylaxis_during_ult_initia.reason_why: Any of the three classes dampens crystal-mobilisation flares; the choice follows renal, gastrointestinal and cardiovascular risk.
gout_flare_prophylaxis_during_ult_initia.important_caveat: No head-to-head trial of prophylaxis agents was retrieved; the low-dose prednisone/prednisolone dose limit is unverified here.
gout_flare_prophylaxis_during_ult_initia.real_working_solution: If colchicine is contraindicated or not tolerated, use a low-dose NSAID (with gastroprotection where indicated and only when renal function allows) or a low-dose glucocorticoid for the same 3-6 months.
gout_flare_prophylaxis_during_ult_initia.source: FitzGerald JD et al., '2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout', Arthritis Care Res (Hoboken) 2020;72:744-760 (PMID 32391934); Wortmann RL et al., 'Effect of prophylaxis on gout flares after the initiation of urate-lowering therapy: analysis of data from three phase III trials', Clin Ther 2010;32:2386-2397 (PMID 21353107)

gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.name: Weight Loss in Overweight/Obese Gout Patients - Real but Low-Quality Evidence: 71% Fewer Monthly Attacks in a 13-Man Pilot; Bariatric Surgery Can Transiently Worsen Flares
specific_drugs: Calorie restriction to about 1,600 kcal/day with 40% carbohydrate, 30% protein, 30% fat (Dessein 2000 regimen)
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.effectiveness: Dessein 2000 (13 non-diabetic men, 16 weeks): mean weight loss 7.7 kg, monthly attacks fell from 2.1 to 0.6 (median; 71% reduction, computed (2.1-0.6)/2.1), serum urate fell from 0.57 to 0.47 mmol/L and normalised in 7 of 12 (58%) patients with a raised baseline level. Nielsen 2017 systematic review (10 studies, one randomised): serum urate change ranged from -168 to +30 umol/L, 0% to 60% of patients reached the <360 umol/L target, 6 of 8 studies (75%) showed fewer attacks; GRADE evidence low for serum urate, moderate for target achievement and low for attacks; bariatric surgery temporarily increased serum urate and attacks in the short term. 2020 ACR: conditionally recommends weight loss for overweight/obese patients (very low evidence).
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.reason_why: Weight loss reduces insulin resistance and hepatic urate production and improves renal urate excretion.
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.important_caveat: Evidence quality is low; rapid crash dieting or bariatric surgery can transiently raise urate and flares.
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.real_working_solution: Advise gradual weight loss as an adjunct to urate-lowering drugs, not as a substitute; average urate effects are modest and the best data come from a tiny uncontrolled pilot.
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.source: Dessein PH et al., 'Beneficial effects of weight loss associated with moderate calorie/carbohydrate restriction, and increased proportional intake of protein and unsaturated fat on serum urate and lipoprotein levels in gout: a pilot study', Ann Rheum Dis 2000;59:539-543 (PMID 10873964); Nielsen SM et al., 'Weight loss for overweight and obese individuals with gout: a systematic review of longitudinal studies', Ann Rheum Dis 2017;76:1870-1882 (PMID 28866649); FitzGerald JD et al., '2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout', Arthritis Care Res (Hoboken) 2020;72:744-760 (PMID 32391934)

gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.name: Limiting Alcohol - Beer Carries the Highest Gout Risk (RR 1.49 per Serving per Day); Moderate Wine Was Not Associated
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.effectiveness: Choi 2004 (47,150 US men, 12 years, 730 incident gout cases): relative risk of gout versus non-drinkers 1.32 (0.99-1.75) for 10.0-14.9 g/day, 1.49 (1.14-1.94) for 15.0-29.9 g/day, 1.96 (1.48-2.60) for 30.0-49.9 g/day and 2.53 (1.73-3.70) for >=50 g/day; per serving per day beer 1.49 (1.32-1.70), spirits 1.15 (1.04-1.28), wine 1.04 (0.88-1.22). 2020 ACR: conditionally recommends limiting alcohol (low evidence).
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.reason_why: Alcohol (especially beer, which also supplies guanosine purines) raises urate production and lowers renal urate excretion.
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.important_caveat: Prospective cohort of men (no randomisation); the effect size is a risk association, not a proven treatment effect.
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.real_working_solution: Advise stopping or sharply cutting beer and spirits; the observational data suggest moderate wine is less harmful, but no trial tests this.
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.source: Choi HK et al., 'Alcohol intake and risk of incident gout in men: a prospective study', Lancet 2004;363:1277-1281 (PMID 15094272); FitzGerald JD et al., '2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout', Arthritis Care Res (Hoboken) 2020;72:744-760 (PMID 32391934)

gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.name: Limiting Sugar-Sweetened Drinks and High-Fructose Intake - RR 1.85 for Two or More Servings Daily; Diet Drinks Not Associated
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.type: Lifestyle: fructose and sugar-sweetened drink reduction
specific_drugs: Fruit juice and fructose-rich fruits (associated with higher risk at high intake)
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.effectiveness: Choi 2008 (prospective cohort of men, 12 years, 755 incident cases): compared with <1 serving a month, RR of gout 1.29 (1.00-1.68) for 5-6 servings a week, 1.45 (1.02-2.08) for one a day and 1.85 (1.08-3.16) for two or more a day; RR across fifths of fructose intake 1.00, 1.29, 1.41, 1.84, 2.02 (1.49-2.75); diet soft drinks not associated. 2020 ACR: conditionally recommends limiting high-fructose corn syrup (very low evidence).
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.reason_why: Fructose metabolism consumes ATP in the liver and drives purine degradation to uric acid.
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.important_caveat: Observational data in men; effect of stopping on established gout is not tested by an RCT.
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.real_working_solution: Replace sugar-sweetened soft drinks and fruit juices with water; the association is with sweetened drinks and fructose load, not with diet drinks.
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.source: Choi HK, Curhan G, 'Soft drinks, fructose consumption, and the risk of gout in men: prospective cohort study', BMJ 2008;336:309-312 (PMID 18244959); FitzGerald JD et al., '2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout', Arthritis Care Res (Hoboken) 2020;72:744-760 (PMID 32391934)

gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.name: Purine-Rich Meat and Seafood Versus Dairy - Meat RR 1.41, Seafood RR 1.51, Dairy RR 0.56; Purine-Rich Vegetables and Protein Not Associated
specific_drugs: Low-fat dairy products (associated with lower risk)
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.effectiveness: Choi 2004 NEJM (47,150 men, 12 years, 730 cases): highest versus lowest quintile RR of gout 1.41 (1.07-1.86) for meat, 1.51 (1.17-1.95) for seafood and 0.56 (0.42-0.74) for dairy products; purine-rich vegetables and total protein were not associated. 2020 ACR: conditionally recommends limiting purine intake (low evidence).
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.reason_why: Animal-source purines add to the urate pool, while milk proteins are mildly uricosuric.
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.important_caveat: Observational cohort; it shows risk associations, not treatment effects.
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.real_working_solution: Moderate red meat and seafood and favour dairy and vegetables; do not restrict vegetables on 'purine' grounds.
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.source: Choi HK et al., 'Purine-rich foods, dairy and protein intake, and the risk of gout in men', N Engl J Med 2004;350:1093-1103 (PMID 15014182); FitzGerald JD et al., '2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout', Arthritis Care Res (Hoboken) 2020;72:744-760 (PMID 32391934)

gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.name: DASH-Type Diet - Randomised Feeding Trial Lowered Serum Urate by 0.25 mg/dL; Cohort Shows 32% Lower Gout Risk
specific_drugs: DASH diet (fruits, vegetables, low-fat dairy, reduced saturated fat)
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.effectiveness: Juraschek 2021 (secondary analysis of the DASH feeding trial, 327 participants, 8 weeks, weight kept constant): serum urate lowered by 0.25 mg/dL (95% CI -0.43 to -0.08, p=0.004) versus the control diet; by baseline serum urate the fall was 0.08, 0.12, 0.42, 0.44 and 0.73 mg/dL for <5, 5-5.9, 6-6.9, 7-7.9 and >=8 mg/dL. Rai 2017 (men followed 26 years, 1,731 incident cases): adjusted relative risk for extreme fifths of the DASH score 0.68 (0.57-0.80, p trend <0.001); Western pattern RR 1.42 (1.16-1.74). The 2020 ACR guideline text retrieved makes no DASH recommendation.
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.reason_why: The pattern combines less fructose/red meat and more dairy and plant food, all directionally lowering serum urate.
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.important_caveat: Trial participants were largely not gout patients (mean baseline urate 5.7 mg/dL); a dedicated gout dietary RCT was called for by the authors.
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.real_working_solution: A DASH-like diet is a sensible healthy pattern for gout patients with hypertension or high urate, but the urate effect (about 0.25 mg/dL) is small compared with a urate-lowering drug (allopurinol dose escalation lowers about 1.5 mg/dL).
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.source: Juraschek SP et al., 'Effects of dietary patterns on serum urate: results from a randomized trial of the effects of diet on hypertension', Arthritis Rheumatol 2021;73:1014-1020 (PMID 33615722); Rai SK et al., 'The Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet, Western diet, and risk of gout in men: prospective cohort study', BMJ 2017;357:j1794 (PMID 28487277); Stamp LK et al., 'A randomised controlled trial of the efficacy and safety of allopurinol dose escalation to achieve target serum urate in people with gout', Ann Rheum Dis 2017;76:1522-1528 (PMID 28314755)

gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.name: Cherry Consumption - Case-Crossover Study: 35% Lower Odds of an Attack (OR 0.65); Observational, Not Guideline-Recommended
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.effectiveness: Zhang 2012 (633 gout patients followed online for 1 year, case-crossover design): cherry intake over a 2-day window associated with a 35% lower risk of gout attacks (OR 0.65, 95% CI 0.50-0.85); cherry extract OR 0.55 (0.30-0.98); cherries plus allopurinol OR 0.25 (0.15-0.42), i.e. 75% lower than periods without either. The 2020 ACR guideline text retrieved makes no cherry recommendation (insufficient evidence).
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.reason_why: Cherry anthocyanins and polyphenols have anti-inflammatory and mild urate-lowering properties (proposed).
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.important_caveat: Self-reported observational study; no randomised trial in the sources retrieved.
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.real_working_solution: Cherries are a harmless optional dietary addition, but they are not a treatment: keep taking the urate-lowering drug and prophylaxis.
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.source: Zhang Y et al., 'Cherry consumption and decreased risk of recurrent gout attacks', Arthritis Rheum 2012;64:4004-4011 (PMID 23023818); FitzGerald JD et al., '2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout', Arthritis Care Res (Hoboken) 2020;72:744-760 (PMID 32391934)

gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.name: Vitamin C Supplementation - Real Negative Trial: 500 mg/day for 8 Weeks Cut Serum Urate by Only 0.23 mg/dL; ACR Conditionally Recommends Against
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.effectiveness: Stamp 2013 (pilot RCT in gout patients): vitamin C 500 mg/day for 8 weeks lowered serum urate by only 0.014 mmol/L (0.23 mg/dL) versus 0.118 mmol/L (1.9 mg/dL) with starting or increasing allopurinol (p<0.001), despite plasma ascorbate rising; baseline urate about 8.4 mg/dL. 2020 ACR: conditionally recommends against adding vitamin C (low evidence).
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.reason_why: Vitamin C is weakly uricosuric in healthy hyperuricaemic subjects but the effect in gout patients is small.
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.important_caveat: Small pilot trial; the negative result is reported so vitamin C is not mistakenly used in place of urate-lowering drugs.
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.real_working_solution: Do not use vitamin C to treat gout; titrate the urate-lowering drug instead.
gout_lifestyle_diet_measures.source: Stamp LK et al., 'Clinically insignificant effect of supplemental vitamin C on serum urate in patients with gout: a pilot randomized controlled trial', Arthritis Rheum 2013;65:1636-1642 (PMID 23681955); FitzGerald JD et al., '2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout', Arthritis Care Res (Hoboken) 2020;72:744-760 (PMID 32391934)

gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.name: Antihypertensive Choice - Losartan and Calcium Channel Blockers Lower Gout Risk; Diuretics Raise It 2.4-Fold
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.type: Comorbidity management: switch urate-raising for urate-neutral or urate-lowering antihypertensives
specific_drugs: Amlodipine (a calcium channel blocker; class RR 0.87)
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.effectiveness: Wurzner 2001 (hypertensive hyperuricaemic gout patients, crossover): losartan 50 mg once daily lowered serum uric acid from 538 to 491 umol/L (8.7% fall, computed 47/538; p<0.01) whereas irbesartan had no effect; 50 mg twice daily did not lower it further. Choi 2012 (population case-control, 29,138 hypertensive patients): relative risk of incident gout 0.87 (0.82-0.93) with calcium channel blockers, 0.81 (0.70-0.94) with losartan, 2.36 (2.21-2.52) with diuretics, 1.48 (1.40-1.57) with beta blockers, 1.24 (1.17-1.32) with ACE inhibitors and 1.29 (1.16-1.43) with non-losartan ARBs. 2020 ACR: conditionally recommends switching hydrochlorothiazide to an alternate antihypertensive and choosing losartan preferentially when feasible (very low evidence). Perez-Ruiz 2011: diuretic use was associated with failing to keep serum urate below 7 mg/dL after urate-lowering therapy withdrawal.
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.reason_why: Losartan (unlike irbesartan in Wurzner 2001) is uricosuric; thiazide and loop diuretics and loop diuretics reduce renal urate excretion.
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.important_caveat: Case-control and small crossover data; the effect of losartan on serum urate is small (8.7%).
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.real_working_solution: In a gout patient with hypertension prefer losartan or a calcium channel blocker, and replace a thiazide where blood pressure allows; this adds a modest urate-lowering effect but does not replace urate-lowering therapy.
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.source: Wurzner G et al., 'Comparative effects of losartan and irbesartan on serum uric acid in hypertensive patients with hyperuricaemia and gout', J Hypertens 2001;19:1855-1860 (PMID 11593107); Choi HK et al., 'Antihypertensive drugs and risk of incident gout among patients with hypertension: population based case-control study', BMJ 2012;344:d8190 (PMID 22240117); FitzGerald JD et al., '2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout', Arthritis Care Res (Hoboken) 2020;72:744-760 (PMID 32391934); Perez-Ruiz F et al., 'A two-stage approach to the treatment of hyperuricemia in gout: the dirty dish hypothesis', Arthritis Rheum 2011;63:4002-4006 (PMID 21898351)

gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.name: Fenofibrate - FIELD Post-Hoc: Uric Acid Lowered 20.1% and First Gout Events HR 0.54; ACR Conditionally Advises Against Adding It Solely for Gout
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.type: Lipid-lowering PPAR-alpha agonist with a urate-lowering side effect
specific_drugs: Allopurinol (background urate-lowering; the effect persisted in patients on it)
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.effectiveness: Waldman 2018 (post-hoc of the FIELD RCT in type 2 diabetes): plasma uric acid 20.1% lower (18.5-21.7%, p<0.0001) with fenofibrate; first gout events 81 (2%) versus 151 (3%) over 5 years (HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.41-0.70, p<0.0001); all gout events HR 0.48 (0.37-0.60); cumulative first-gout-event incidence in patients with baseline urate >0.42 mmol/L 13.9% with placebo versus 5.7% with fenofibrate. 2020 ACR: conditionally recommends against adding or switching to fenofibrate as a urate-lowering strategy. Perez-Ruiz 2011: fenofibrate use was associated with staying below 7 mg/dL after urate-lowering therapy withdrawal.
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.reason_why: Fenofibrate is uricosuric (increases renal urate clearance) in addition to lowering triglycerides.
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.important_caveat: FIELD was not designed to test gout (post-hoc); the ACR advises against using fenofibrate as a urate-lowering strategy.
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.real_working_solution: In a gout patient who also needs a fibrate for hypertriglyceridaemia, fenofibrate is a reasonable choice with a small urate-lowering bonus; do not add it only to treat gout.
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.source: Waldman B et al., 'Effect of fenofibrate on uric acid and gout in type 2 diabetes: a post-hoc analysis of the randomised, controlled FIELD study', Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2018;6:310-318 (PMID 29496472); FitzGerald JD et al., '2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout', Arthritis Care Res (Hoboken) 2020;72:744-760 (PMID 32391934); Perez-Ruiz F et al., 'A two-stage approach to the treatment of hyperuricemia in gout: the dirty dish hypothesis', Arthritis Rheum 2011;63:4002-4006 (PMID 21898351)

gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.name: SGLT2 Inhibitors in Type 2 Diabetes With Gout - Serum Urate Lowered by About 38 umol/L; Gout Incidence HR 0.62 and Recurrent Flares Rate Ratio 0.67 Versus Sulfonylureas
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.type: Comorbidity management: glucose-lowering drugs with urate-lowering effect
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.effectiveness: Zhao 2018 meta-analysis (62 RCTs, 34,941 patients): SGLT2 inhibitors lowered serum uric acid by a weighted mean of -37.73 umol/L (95% CI -40.51 to -34.95), empagliflozin -45.83 umol/L (-53.03 to -38.63); the effect persisted long term but was abolished in patients with eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2. McCormick 2024 (target-trial emulation, 34,604 matched adults with type 2 diabetes on metformin): gout incidence 4.27 versus 6.91 events per 1,000 person-years (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.48-0.80); recurrent flares among gout patients rate ratio 0.67 (0.55-0.82); MACE HR 0.87 (0.77-0.98).
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.reason_why: SGLT2 inhibitors increase urinary glucose excretion, which is thought to raise urinary urate excretion and lower serum urate.
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.important_caveat: The gout-risk data are observational cohort emulations; the urate effect is lost at eGFR <60.
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.real_working_solution: For a patient with type 2 diabetes and gout, an SGLT2 inhibitor is a good glucose-lowering choice that also modestly lowers serum urate and flare risk; it is not a stand-alone gout treatment.
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.source: Zhao Y et al., 'Effects of sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors on serum uric acid level: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials', Diabetes Obes Metab 2018;20:458-462 (PMID 28846182); McCormick N et al., 'Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors vs sulfonylureas for gout prevention among patients with type 2 diabetes receiving metformin', JAMA Intern Med 2024;184:650-660 (PMID 38619822)

gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.name: Chronic Kidney Disease and Gout - Allopurinol Remains Preferred Even in CKD Stage >3 (ACR Strong); Titrate Up; Colchicine and NSAID Cautions
specific_drugs: Allopurinol (start 50 mg in impaired kidney function per label; titrate to target)
Anakinra (effective in CKD 4-5 in a retrospective series)
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.effectiveness: 2020 ACR: allopurinol is the strongly preferred first-line agent including in moderate-to-severe CKD (stage >3), and CKD patients may still need doses above 300 mg/day to reach target. Stamp 2017: 52% of trial participants had creatinine clearance <60 mL/min and dose escalation was well tolerated with no difference in renal-function change between arms. Loustau 2018: anakinra was effective in all 31 gout patients with stage 4-5 CKD or kidney transplant (one serious infection). Naproxen was not to be given to patients with estimated creatinine clearance <50 mL/min in the febuxostat phase III trials (Wortmann 2010). The Colcrys label contraindicates P-gp or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors in patients with renal or hepatic impairment.
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.reason_why: Allopurinol/oxypurinol is renally cleared, so dose is scaled to kidney function but still escalated to target; NSAIDs and colchicine accumulate or worsen kidney function in CKD.
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.important_caveat: Colchicine renal dose adjustment details were not retrieved; refer to the full label.
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.real_working_solution: In CKD, keep treating to target with allopurinol (start low, go slow, escalate), use glucocorticoids or an IL-1 inhibitor for flares when NSAIDs are unsuitable, and dose-adjust colchicine.
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.source: FitzGerald JD et al., '2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout', Arthritis Care Res (Hoboken) 2020;72:744-760 (PMID 32391934); Stamp LK et al., 'A randomised controlled trial of the efficacy and safety of allopurinol dose escalation to achieve target serum urate in people with gout', Ann Rheum Dis 2017;76:1522-1528 (PMID 28314755); Loustau C et al., 'Effectiveness and safety of anakinra in gout patients with stage 4-5 chronic kidney disease or kidney transplantation', Joint Bone Spine 2018;85:755-760 (PMID 29654950); Wortmann RL et al., 'Effect of prophylaxis on gout flares after the initiation of urate-lowering therapy: analysis of data from three phase III trials', Clin Ther 2010;32:2386-2397 (PMID 21353107); FDA, Colcrys (colchicine) prescribing information, sections 2.1, 4, 7 (openFDA drug label API, label effective 2022-10-01, accessed 2026-09-21)

gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.name: Clinically Important Drug Interactions in Gout Treatment - Azathioprine/Mercaptopurine With Allopurinol, Colchicine With P-gp/CYP3A4 Inhibitors and Statins, Pegloticase With Allopurinol
specific_drugs: Allopurinol with azathioprine or mercaptopurine (reduce the thiopurine dose)
Colchicine with clarithromycin, protease inhibitors or other strong CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitors
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.effectiveness: Allopurinol label: azathioprine or mercaptopurine doses must be reduced (older label: to about one-third to one-quarter of the usual dose when allopurinol 300-600 mg/day is given); capecitabine should be avoided; when pegloticase is started, allopurinol is to be discontinued; thiazide diuretics, ampicillin/amoxicillin and bendamustine may increase serious skin reactions. Colcrys label: colchicine is a P-gp and CYP3A4 substrate; fatal drug interactions have been reported; in patients with renal or hepatic impairment colchicine is contraindicated with P-gp or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (including all protease inhibitors except fosamprenavir); statins (atorvastatin, fluvastatin, lovastatin, pravastatin, simvastatin) can cause myopathy and rhabdomyolysis when combined.
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.reason_why: Allopurinol blocks xanthine oxidase, which normally inactivates thiopurines; colchicine exposure rises when its P-gp/CYP3A4 clearance is inhibited.
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.real_working_solution: Screen every gout prescription against this list before starting: adjust or avoid the interacting drug, or choose a different flare/urate-lowering agent.
gout_comorbidity_and_drug_interaction_ma.source: FDA, allopurinol tablets prescribing information, sections 2, 5.1, 7 (openFDA drug label API, label versions effective 2024-07-08 and 2026-06-03, accessed 2026-09-21); FDA, Colcrys (colchicine) prescribing information, sections 2.1, 4, 7 (openFDA drug label API, label effective 2022-10-01, accessed 2026-09-21)

gout_diagnostic_and_monitoring_devices.name: Diagnostic and Monitoring Tools - Synovial Fluid Microscopy for MSU Crystals, Ultrasound Double-Contour Sign, Dual-Energy CT, Serum Urate Assay, HLA-B*58:01 Genotyping
gout_diagnostic_and_monitoring_devices.type: Diagnostic, imaging and monitoring devices supporting treatment decisions
specific_drugs: Polarised-light microscopy of synovial fluid or tophus aspirate (monosodium urate crystal identification)
gout_diagnostic_and_monitoring_devices.effectiveness: 2015 ACR/EULAR classification criteria (Neogi 2015): MSU crystals in a symptomatic joint/bursa or a tophus is sufficient to classify as gout; the full criteria have sensitivity 92% and specificity 89%. Ogdie 2015 meta-analysis (11 studies, crystal-confirmed gold standard, mostly established disease): ultrasound double-contour sign pooled sensitivity 0.83 (0.72-0.91) and specificity 0.76 (0.68-0.83); ultrasound tophus 0.65 and 0.80; dual-energy CT urate deposition sensitivity 0.87 (0.79-0.93) and specificity 0.84 (0.75-0.90). Serial serum urate is the monitoring tool for treat-to-target (Doherty 2018).
gout_diagnostic_and_monitoring_devices.reason_why: Crystal identification proves the diagnosis and separates gout from septic and other arthritis; imaging shows deposited urate when fluid cannot be obtained; serum urate tells whether the target that dissolves crystals is being met.
gout_diagnostic_and_monitoring_devices.important_caveat: Imaging performance figures come mostly from patients with long-standing disease; the added value of imaging over clinical criteria in early disease is uncertain (Ogdie 2015).
gout_diagnostic_and_monitoring_devices.real_working_solution: Aspirate and identify crystals whenever feasible; use ultrasound or dual-energy CT when fluid is unobtainable or disease is atypical; measure serum urate to titrate therapy.
gout_diagnostic_and_monitoring_devices.source: Neogi T et al., '2015 gout classification criteria: an American College of Rheumatology/European League Against Rheumatism collaborative initiative', Arthritis Rheumatol 2015;67:2557-2568 (PMID 26352873); Ogdie A et al., 'Imaging modalities for the classification of gout: systematic literature review and meta-analysis', Ann Rheum Dis 2015;74:1868-1874 (PMID 24915980); Doherty M et al. (Nottingham Gout Treatment Trial), 'Efficacy and cost-effectiveness of nurse-led care involving education and engagement of patients and a treat-to-target urate-lowering strategy versus usual care for gout', Lancet 2018;392:1403-1412 (PMID 30343856)

gout_tophi_and_surgical_care.name: Tophus Resolution With Sustained Urate Lowering - Faster at Lower Serum Urate; 69% Resolved in 5-Year FOCUS; 53.8% Complete Resolution of at Least One Tophus With Pegloticase Plus Methotrexate
specific_drugs: Allopurinol, febuxostat, benzbromarone (single or combined to reach serum urate <5 mg/dL)
Pegloticase plus methotrexate (for refractory tophaceous gout)
Lesinurad plus febuxostat (no longer marketed in the US; reduced tophus area by 50-53% versus 28%)
gout_tophi_and_surgical_care.effectiveness: Perez-Ruiz 2002 (63 patients): velocity of tophus reduction was linearly related to mean serum urate during therapy - the lower the urate, the faster the tophus shrank - and benzbromarone or combined therapy shrank tophi faster than allopurinol alone. FOCUS 5-year: tophus resolution in 69% (18 of 26). FACT: median tophus-area reduction 83% (febuxostat 80 mg), 66% (120 mg) and 50% (allopurinol) at 52 weeks. CRYSTAL: target tophus area reduction 50.1-52.9% with lesinurad plus febuxostat versus 28.3% with febuxostat alone. MIRROR: complete resolution of >=1 tophus 53.8% versus 31.0% at week 52. 2016 EULAR: serum urate below 5 mg/dL in severe (tophaceous) gout.
gout_tophi_and_surgical_care.reason_why: Below the tissue urate saturation threshold crystals in tophi dissolve at a rate proportional to how far serum urate is below it.
gout_tophi_and_surgical_care.real_working_solution: Aim for serum urate below 5 mg/dL in tophaceous gout and be patient - resolution takes months to years; escalate (uricosuric or pegloticase) when tophi persist.
gout_tophi_and_surgical_care.source: Perez-Ruiz F et al., 'Effect of urate-lowering therapy on the velocity of size reduction of tophi in chronic gout', Arthritis Rheum 2002;47:356-360 (PMID 12209479); Schumacher HR Jr et al. (FOCUS), 'Febuxostat in the treatment of gout: 5-yr findings of the FOCUS efficacy and safety study', Rheumatology (Oxford) 2009;48:188-194 (PMID 19141576); Becker MA et al. (FACT), 'Febuxostat compared with allopurinol in patients with hyperuricemia and gout', N Engl J Med 2005;353:2450-2461 (PMID 16339094); Dalbeth N et al. (CRYSTAL), 'Lesinurad, a selective uric acid reabsorption inhibitor, in combination with febuxostat in patients with tophaceous gout', Arthritis Rheumatol 2017;69:1903-1913 (PMID 28597604); Botson JK et al. (MIRROR RCT), '12-month findings', ACR Open Rheumatol 2023;5:407-418 (PMID 37385296); Richette P et al., '2016 updated EULAR evidence-based recommendations for the management of gout', Ann Rheum Dis 2017;76:29-42 (PMID 27457514)

gout_tophi_and_surgical_care.name: Surgical Tophus Excision - Evidence Limited to Small Retrospective Series; Medical Urate Lowering Comes First
specific_drugs: Surgical tophus excision (e.g. elbow olecranon region)
Sustained urate-lowering therapy (allopurinol, febuxostat) before and after surgery
gout_tophi_and_surgical_care.effectiveness: Kirschenbaum 2022 (6 men, 7 elbow procedures; indications failure of medical management, skin ulceration or large tophi): no intraoperative or immediate wound complications; no tophus recurrence at mean 30.8 months (range 14.0-43.5); pain-free physiologic range of motion. Xiao 2026 (retrospective series of surgery for ulcerated tophi in Hainan): favourable wound healing, lower inflammatory markers and pain scores, low infection rate; authors propose indications of functional impairment, chronic non-healing wounds, refractory pain or large tophi (>1.5 cm) and advise avoiding surgery during acute flares and in patients with uncontrolled comorbidities. No randomised or comparative surgical trial was found in the sources searched.
gout_tophi_and_surgical_care.reason_why: Removing a large mechanically obstructing or ulcerated urate deposit gives immediate functional and wound benefit that slow dissolution by drugs cannot provide.
gout_tophi_and_surgical_care.important_caveat: Very small, retrospective, uncontrolled series; no comparative evidence exists in the sources retrieved.
gout_tophi_and_surgical_care.real_working_solution: Consider surgical excision only for tophi that are ulcerated, infected, disabling or refractory to adequate urate lowering, always alongside continued urate-lowering therapy.
gout_tophi_and_surgical_care.source: Kirschenbaum JD et al., 'Operative management of gouty tophi in the region of the olecranon: a case series', JSES Int 2022;6:550-554 (PMID 35572418); Xiao W et al., 'A retrospective analysis of the surgical efficacy for tophi wounds in Hainan province', Front Surg 2026;13:1752070 (PMID 42147384)

gout_india_availability_and_access.name: India Availability - Generic Allopurinol, Febuxostat and Colchicine Are Marketed; Specialist Biologics and Some Uricosurics Could Not Be Verified
specific_drugs: Allopurinol: Zyloric 100 mg and 300 mg tablets (GlaxoSmithKline Pharmaceuticals Ltd)
Febuxostat: Febutaz and Febuget (Sun Pharmaceutical), Febugood (Torrent), Febucip (Cipla), Febuxor (Intas), Febumac (Macleods), FBX (Albert David), Febutax (Leeford)
Colchicine 0.5 mg: Zycolchin and other brands
gout_india_availability_and_access.effectiveness: Retail/pharmacy listings show allopurinol (Zyloric, GlaxoSmithKline Pharmaceuticals, 100 mg and 300 mg), at least ten febuxostat brands (Febutaz, Febutax, Foxstat, FBX, Febumac, Febucip, Febuget, Febugood, Febutac, Febuxor) and colchicine 0.5 mg tablets (Zycolchin and others) in the Indian market. Not verified in the sources searched and therefore not claimed: CDSCO approval status of individual brands; India availability of pegloticase, canakinumab, anakinra, benzbromarone and probenecid; availability and cost of HLA-B*58:01 testing (an Indian allele-frequency figure is cited separately in this knowledge base's symptoms entry and was not re-verified here); and an Indian national gout guideline (a search for an Indian Rheumatology Association gout guideline returned none).
gout_india_availability_and_access.reason_why: Indian pharmacies stock xanthine-oxidase inhibitors and colchicine, so the trial-proven core (allopurinol titration to target, colchicine or NSAID cover, febuxostat second-line) is deliverable locally.
gout_india_availability_and_access.important_caveat: Brand and manufacturer names come from retail listings and may change; prices are omitted because they vary. Indian colchicine tablets are 0.5 mg, whereas the trial and label regimens (1.2 mg then 0.6 mg) assume 0.6 mg tablets.
gout_india_availability_and_access.real_working_solution: Use generic allopurinol titrated to a serum urate below 6 mg/dL, colchicine or NSAID prophylaxis for 3-6 months, and febuxostat only for allopurinol failure or intolerance; check current local availability of biologics and uricosurics with the dispensing pharmacy.
gout_india_availability_and_access.source: 1mg.com, Febuxostat generic page listing Indian brands and manufacturers (1mg.com/generics/febuxostat-209871, accessed 2026-09-21); Retail listings for Zyloric (allopurinol, GlaxoSmithKline Pharmaceuticals Ltd) 100 mg and 300 mg tablets (truemeds.in, medplusmart.com, accessed 2026-09-21); Retail listings for Zycolchin (colchicine 0.5 mg) and other Indian colchicine 0.5 mg brands (medibuddy.in, medplusmart.com, accessed 2026-09-21)

gout_negative_or_neutral_evidence.name: Allopurinol for Cardiovascular or Kidney Protection Without Gout - ALL-HEART and CKD-FIX Were Neutral; Treat Gout by Gout Criteria
gout_negative_or_neutral_evidence.type: Negative/neutral trial evidence for allopurinol beyond gout
gout_negative_or_neutral_evidence.effectiveness: ALL-HEART (Mackenzie 2022; 5,721 patients aged >=60 with ischaemic heart disease and no gout, mean follow-up 4.8 years): primary composite of non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke or cardiovascular death 314 (11.0%) allopurinol versus 325 (11.3%) usual care (HR 1.04, 95% CI 0.89-1.21, p=0.65); all-cause death HR 1.02 (0.87-1.20). CKD-FIX (Badve 2020; 363 patients with chronic kidney disease at high risk of progression, mean eGFR 31.7): eGFR decline -3.33 versus -3.23 mL/min/1.73 m2 per year (difference -0.10, 95% CI -1.18 to 0.97, p=0.85). 2020 ACR conditionally recommends against starting pharmacological urate-lowering therapy for asymptomatic hyperuricaemia.
gout_negative_or_neutral_evidence.reason_why: Lowering urate with allopurinol does not, in these trials, change heart or kidney outcomes in people without gout.
gout_negative_or_neutral_evidence.real_working_solution: Prescribe allopurinol for gout (and its guideline indications), not as a cardio-renal protective drug; for gout patients with CKD, the reason to treat is gout control, not kidney protection.
gout_negative_or_neutral_evidence.source: Mackenzie IS et al. (ALL-HEART), 'Allopurinol versus usual care in UK patients with ischaemic heart disease', Lancet 2022;400:1195-1205 (PMID 36216006); Badve SV et al. (CKD-FIX), 'Effects of allopurinol on the progression of chronic kidney disease', N Engl J Med 2020;382:2504-2513 (PMID 32579811); FitzGerald JD et al., '2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout', Arthritis Care Res (Hoboken) 2020;72:744-760 (PMID 32391934)

gout_negative_or_neutral_evidence.name: Rilonacept for the Acute Flare - Real Low-Quality Evidence That It Gives Less Pain Relief Than Indomethacin
specific_drugs: Rilonacept 320 mg (evaluated in a trial versus indomethacin)
Indomethacin 50 mg three times daily (the superior comparator)
