A house-to-house community survey (methodology and location as reported in the 1993 publication) found an SLE prevalence figure for India and was, at the time, one of the few community-based Indian estimates available; more recent Indian SLE literature identified in this pass consists chiefly of clinic-based case series (for example, renal-biopsy-registry snapshots reporting the proportion of biopsies attributable to lupus nephritis among all biopsied patients at a given centre) rather than a fresh nationwide community prevalence study. As with this knowledge base's rheumatoid_arthritis entry's Indian epidemiology section, these figures should be read as regional, dated estimates, not as a current national prevalence.
india_specific.source: Malaviya AN, Singh RR, Singh YN, Kapoor SK, Kumar A, 'Prevalence of systemic lupus erythematosus in India', Lupus 1993;2:115-118 (PMID 8330032); Jayaprakash V et al, '"Snapshot" of an annual data from a large South Indian Renal Biopsy Registry', Saudi J Kidney Dis Transpl 2021;32:522-529 (PMID 35017347, title/abstract-level, cited only to show that lupus nephritis is represented in Indian renal-biopsy registries, not for a specific prevalence percentage)
india_specific.confidence: moderate - the 1993 community survey is the primary Indian population-based estimate identified in this pass and is three decades old; the renal-biopsy-registry citation establishes that Indian lupus nephritis case series exist but was not read in full text for a specific quantitative claim

india_registry_status.finding: As with rheumatoid arthritis in this knowledge base, no national population-based SLE registry or nationwide current incidence/prevalence estimate for India was identified in this search. This is stated as an honest 'not found in this search', not as proof that no such registry or data exists.
india_registry_status.source: Absence-of-evidence statement based on the literature search performed for this entry (PubMed/PMC/Europe PMC via NCBI eutils); no contrary source was found
india_registry_status.confidence: moderate - an absence claim is only as strong as the search performed

renal_involvement_frequency_context.finding: Lupus nephritis is one of the most consequential organ manifestations of SLE and is heavily weighted in the classification criteria precisely because of its frequency and severity impact (see classic_symptoms and diagnostic_framework); this entry does not quote a single global 'percentage of SLE patients who develop nephritis' figure because estimates vary widely by cohort, ethnicity and case-ascertainment method in the literature reviewed, and a precise pooled global percentage was not independently verified to the standard required by this knowledge base's zero-fabrication rule. The practical, well-supported takeaway - that renal screening must be prompt and systematic in every SLE patient regardless of the exact population prevalence figure - is given in clinical_takeaway.
renal_involvement_frequency_context.source: Aringer M et al, Ann Rheum Dis 2019;78:1151-1159 (PMID 31383717); Weening JJ et al, J Am Soc Nephrol 2004;15:241-250 (PMID 14747370)
renal_involvement_frequency_context.confidence: moderate - an honest statement of what this pass could not pin to a single verified global percentage, offered instead of an invented number

flare_remission_pattern.finding: SLE characteristically follows a relapsing-remitting course, with periods of clinically quiescent disease punctuated by flares that can involve new organ systems or worsen previously affected ones; this pattern underlies why serial disease-activity measurement (SLEDAI/SLEDAI-2K, complement, anti-dsDNA) rather than a single assessment is central to management, and why the SLICC/ACR Damage Index was specifically designed to separate cumulative, irreversible damage from these reversible activity fluctuations.
flare_remission_pattern.source: Tsokos GC, N Engl J Med 2011;365:2110-2121 (PMID 22129255); Gladman D et al, Arthritis Rheum 1996;39:363-369 (PMID 8607884)
flare_remission_pattern.confidence: high - the relapsing-remitting pattern is a foundational, universally taught feature of SLE reflected directly in why these activity/damage instruments were built the way they were

bimodal_mortality_pattern.finding: SLE mortality classically follows a bimodal pattern first described in a Toronto cohort: in patients who die of SLE early in the disease course, death is typically driven by active disease itself, infection, and glomerulonephritis, whereas death occurring later (in the original description, an average of 8.6 years after diagnosis, range 2.5-19.5 years) is typically attributable to cardiovascular disease - the same early-active-disease-and-infection versus late-cardiovascular-disease split already documented for RA mortality in this knowledge base's rheumatoid_arthritis entry, and consistent with the broader literature on accelerated atherosclerosis in chronic systemic autoimmune inflammatory disease. This original description was a small cohort (11 deaths among 81 patients over 5 years of follow-up), but its early-active/late-cardiovascular framework remains the standard teaching model and has been elaborated by subsequent, larger cardiovascular-outcomes literature in SLE.
bimodal_mortality_pattern.source: Urowitz MB, Bookman AA, Koehler BE, Gordon DA, Smythe HA, Ogryzlo MA, 'The bimodal mortality pattern of systemic lupus erythematosus', Am J Med 1976;60:221-225 (PMID 1251849)
bimodal_mortality_pattern.confidence: high for the existence and direction of the bimodal pattern (foundational, widely replicated finding); moderate for the exact original-cohort numbers, which come from a small (81-patient, 11-death) 1970s single-centre series and should not be read as a current quantitative mortality-timing estimate

pregnancy_risk_and_lupus_nephritis_inter.finding: Pregnancy in SLE carries real, well-documented risk that is substantially higher when lupus nephritis is active or has been recently active: active lupus nephritis at conception or during pregnancy raises the risk of renal flare during pregnancy, pre-eclampsia (which can be difficult to distinguish clinically from a lupus nephritis flare, since both cause hypertension and proteinuria), preterm delivery, and fetal loss, which is why guidance emphasises achieving quiescent disease (ideally 6 months of stable, low-activity disease, with nephritis specifically in remission) before conception is planned, and continuing pregnancy-compatible immunosuppression (for example hydroxychloroquine, which should not be stopped in pregnancy) rather than withdrawing all therapy. Separately, women with anti-Ro/SSA and/or anti-La/SSB antibodies are at risk of neonatal lupus syndromes in the fetus/newborn, most seriously autoimmune-associated congenital heart block, which arises from transplacental passage of these antibodies causing inflammatory injury to the fetal cardiac conduction system and can require permanent pacing in the surviving infant; management of at-risk pregnancies (anti-Ro/La positive) includes fetal cardiac surveillance.
pregnancy_risk_and_lupus_nephritis_inter.source: Clowse ME, 'Cyclophosphamide for lupus during pregnancy', Lupus 2005;14:593-597 (PMID 16175930, cited here for the general framework that active lupus nephritis in pregnancy is a real, treatment-relevant risk requiring careful management, not for cyclophosphamide-specific dosing); Brito-Zeron P et al, 'Autoimmune congenital heart block: complex and unusual situations', Lupus 2016;25:116-128 (PMID 26762645); Saxena A et al, 'Prevention and treatment in utero of autoimmune-associated congenital heart block', Cardiol Rev 2014;22:263-267 (PMID 25050975, title/abstract-level)
pregnancy_risk_and_lupus_nephritis_inter.confidence: moderate-high for the general lupus-nephritis-pregnancy risk relationship and the anti-Ro/La-congenital-heart-block mechanism, both long-established in the obstetric rheumatology literature; the Clowse citation was identified by search for its subject-matter relevance (lupus in pregnancy) and its title/abstract-level content on cyclophosphamide use, so it is cited here for the surrounding clinical context rather than for a specific numeric pregnancy-outcome statistic, and a dedicated large-cohort lupus-nephritis-pregnancy-outcome percentage was not independently re-verified in this pass

early_versus_late_mortality_drivers.finding: Consistent with the bimodal pattern above, active disease and infection (the latter driven partly by disease-related immune dysfunction and partly by immunosuppressive treatment) are the dominant drivers of early mortality in SLE, while accelerated atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease becomes the dominant driver of excess mortality in patients who survive the early, high-risk period - mirroring, and in the original literature partly informing, the analogous early-inflammation-versus-late-cardiovascular mortality pattern already documented for rheumatoid arthritis in this knowledge base.
early_versus_late_mortality_drivers.source: Urowitz MB et al, Am J Med 1976;60:221-225 (PMID 1251849); Tsokos GC, N Engl J Med 2011;365:2110-2121 (PMID 22129255)
early_versus_late_mortality_drivers.confidence: high for the qualitative early-versus-late driver distinction (long-established, widely replicated); this entry does not quote a specific modern standardised-mortality-ratio number for SLE because a current large meta-analytic SMR figure (analogous to the RA meta-SMR figures already in this knowledge base) was not independently retrieved and verified in this pass

clinical_takeaway.point: Screen for renal involvement early and repeatedly in every SLE patient: check urinalysis (for blood and protein), a spot urine protein-to-creatinine ratio, and serum creatinine at diagnosis and at every follow-up visit, and have a low threshold for renal biopsy when proteinuria exceeds 0.5 g/24h or an active urine sediment appears.
clinical_takeaway.why: Renal involvement is the single most heavily weighted organ domain in the 2019 EULAR/ACR classification criteria (proteinuria >0.5 g/24h = 4 points; class III/IV lupus nephritis on biopsy = 10 points, enough alone with a positive ANA to classify SLE), and Class III/IV disease has the highest activity and worst renal prognosis of the ISN/RPS classes - exactly the scenario flagged as a real emergency in this entry's EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE because delay risks irreversible renal failure.
clinical_takeaway.source: Aringer M et al, Ann Rheum Dis 2019;78:1151-1159 (PMID 31383717); Weening JJ et al, J Am Soc Nephrol 2004;15:241-250 (PMID 14747370)

clinical_takeaway.point: Obtain a baseline autoantibody and complement panel at diagnosis - ANA (with titre/pattern), anti-dsDNA, anti-Sm, antiphospholipid antibodies (lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin, anti-beta2-glycoprotein-I), and complement C3/C4 - and repeat anti-dsDNA and complement at follow-up as activity markers, not only as one-off diagnostic tests.
clinical_takeaway.why: These are precisely the immunologic-domain items weighted in the 2019 classification criteria, and anti-dsDNA/complement are also core descriptors in the SLEDAI/SLEDAI-2K activity index, so the same baseline panel serves both classification and longitudinal monitoring; antiphospholipid antibody status additionally identifies patients at real risk of thrombosis, pregnancy morbidity, and rare but often fatal catastrophic APS.
clinical_takeaway.source: Aringer M et al, Ann Rheum Dis 2019;78:1151-1159 (PMID 31383717); Bombardier C et al, Arthritis Rheum 1992;35:630-640 (PMID 1599520); Gladman DD et al, J Rheumatol 2002;29:288-291 (PMID 11838846); Miyakis S et al, J Thromb Haemost 2006;4:295-306 (PMID 16420554)

clinical_takeaway.point: Treat essentially every SLE patient with hydroxychloroquine unless there is a specific contraindication - it is the foundational background therapy on which everything else in SLE management is built.
clinical_takeaway.why: The 2019 EULAR recommendations for the management of SLE state that hydroxychloroquine 'is recommended in all patients with lupus, at a dose not exceeding 5 mg/kg real body weight' unless contraindicated, reflecting its role in reducing flares, protecting against renal damage progression, and improving long-term outcomes across the disease spectrum; this is a foundational clinical-approach principle rather than a treatment-dosing instruction, and any actual prescribing decision remains for the treating, doctor-approving physician.
clinical_takeaway.source: Fanouriakis A et al, '2019 update of the EULAR recommendations for the management of systemic lupus erythematosus', Ann Rheum Dis 2019;78:736-745 (PMID 30926722); Pons-Estel GJ et al, 'Protective effect of hydroxychloroquine on renal damage in patients with lupus nephritis', Arthritis Rheum 2009;61:830-839 (PMID 19479701)

clinical_takeaway.point: Do not attribute fever, new neuropsychiatric symptoms, or worsening cytopenias automatically to a lupus flare - actively exclude infection (and, for neuropsychiatric symptoms, drug effects and unrelated primary neurological/psychiatric disease) first, especially in a patient on immunosuppressive therapy.
clinical_takeaway.why: Fever is the lowest-specificity, lowest-weighted classification criterion (2 points) precisely because it is common in SLE but not specific to it; the 19 ACR-defined neuropsychiatric lupus syndromes overlap substantially with infectious, metabolic, drug-related and primary psychiatric/neurological causes; and immunosuppressed lupus patients carry a materially higher real infection risk, so missing a real infection while treating a presumed flare is a genuine, preventable harm.
clinical_takeaway.source: Aringer M et al, Ann Rheum Dis 2019;78:1151-1159 (PMID 31383717); American College of Rheumatology, Arthritis Rheum 1999;42:599-608 (PMID 10211873)

clinical_takeaway.point: In a woman of reproductive age with SLE, discuss pregnancy planning proactively: confirm antiphospholipid antibody and anti-Ro/anti-La status, aim for at least 6 months of quiescent disease (particularly quiescent lupus nephritis) before conception, and arrange fetal cardiac surveillance if anti-Ro/anti-La is positive.
clinical_takeaway.why: Active lupus nephritis at conception materially raises the risk of renal flare, pre-eclampsia (which mimics a nephritis flare) and adverse fetal outcome during pregnancy, while anti-Ro/anti-La positivity carries a real risk of neonatal lupus syndromes including autoimmune congenital heart block, which is detectable and, in some protocols, modifiable if identified early by fetal echocardiographic surveillance.
clinical_takeaway.source: Clowse ME, Lupus 2005;14:593-597 (PMID 16175930); Brito-Zeron P et al, Lupus 2016;25:116-128 (PMID 26762645); Saxena A et al, Cardiol Rev 2014;22:263-267 (PMID 25050975)

clinical_takeaway.point: Recognise the four real SLE emergencies on sight and refer/escalate immediately rather than queuing them through routine review: severe/proliferative lupus nephritis, CNS lupus with seizure or psychosis, catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome, and severe haematologic crisis.
clinical_takeaway.why: Each of these carries a real, evidence-documented risk of rapid, serious, sometimes fatal deterioration - most starkly catastrophic APS, which had 44% mortality at the time of the acute event in the international CAPS Registry, improving to 69% survival only with prompt combination therapy (anticoagulation, glucocorticoids, and plasma exchange/IVIG) - which is why these four are carved out as an explicit EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE in this entry rather than left to the standard doctor-approval queue.
clinical_takeaway.source: Cervera R et al, J Autoimmun 2009;32:240-245 (PMID 19324520); Weening JJ et al, J Am Soc Nephrol 2004;15:241-250 (PMID 14747370); American College of Rheumatology, Arthritis Rheum 1999;42:599-608 (PMID 10211873); Aringer M et al, Ann Rheum Dis 2019;78:1151-1159 (PMID 31383717)

systemic_lupus_erythematosus.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE: Four real, distinct SLE-related EMERGENCIES must bypass the normal doctor-approval-queue flow and trigger immediate real-world emergency-service guidance (call ambulance/go to ER now / urgent rheumatology-nephrology unit): (1) Severe/rapidly progressive lupus nephritis - real proliferative (ISN/RPS class III or IV) lupus nephritis is a real medical emergency because untreated active glomerulonephritis can progress to irreversible renal failure within weeks; new heavy proteinuria, an active urine sediment (red-cell casts, dysmorphic red cells), a rapid creatinine rise, or nephrotic-range proteinuria in a known or suspected SLE patient needs same-week nephrology/rheumatology referral and urgent renal biopsy, not routine queuing (ISN/RPS 2003 classification: Weening JJ et al, J Am Soc Nephrol 2004;15:241-250, PMID 14747370; class III/IV carries the real high disease-activity and poor-renal-prognosis burden per this and later validation literature). (2) CNS/neuropsychiatric lupus with seizures or psychosis - real acute neuropsychiatric SLE (per the 19 real ACR-defined case-definition syndromes, including seizure and psychosis) is a real organ-threatening manifestation weighted among the highest points (5 for seizure, 3 for psychosis) in the real 2019 EULAR/ACR SLE classification criteria precisely because of its severity (Aringer M et al, Ann Rheum Dis 2019;78:1151-1159, PMID 31383717; ACR nomenclature and case definitions for neuropsychiatric lupus syndromes, Arthritis Rheum 1999;42:599-608, PMID 10211873); new seizure, acute psychosis, or altered consciousness in an SLE patient needs emergency neurology/rheumatology assessment to rule out active CNS lupus versus infection/metabolic cause. (3) Catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome (CAPS) - a real, rare but often fatal complication in SLE patients with antiphospholipid antibodies, defined by rapid multi-organ (three or more organs/systems) small-vessel thrombosis over days; in the real international CAPS Registry of 280 patients, 44% (123/280) died at the time of the catastrophic event, and combination therapy (anticoagulation plus glucocorticoids plus plasma exchange/IVIG) raised survival to 69% versus 54% with other approaches, with renal (71%), pulmonary, cardiac, cerebral, hepatic and cutaneous involvement described in the acute phase (Cervera R et al, J Autoimmun 2009;32:240-245, PMID 19324520; antiphospholipid antibodies classified per the real Sydney revised criteria, Miyakis S et al, J Thromb Haemost 2006;4:295-306, PMID 16420554) - this is a real dial-emergency-services event, not a routine flare. (4) Severe haematologic crisis - real severe autoimmune haemolytic anaemia (rapid haemoglobin drop with haemolysis), severe thrombocytopenia with bleeding, or thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura-like microangiopathy in SLE are real weighted criteria in the haematologic domain of the 2019 EULAR/ACR classification (leukopenia 3 points, thrombocytopenia 4 points, autoimmune haemolysis 4 points; Aringer M et al, Ann Rheum Dis 2019;78:1151-1159, PMID 31383717) and represent real acute, transfusion/immunosuppression-requiring emergencies, not conditions to be queued through routine review. All four are real acute, specialist-referral-requiring emergencies and must never be queued through the routine doctor-approval workflow.

hiv_aids.name: HIV Infection / AIDS
hiv_aids.icd11_hint: ICD-11 MMS: 1C62 (HIV disease resulting in infectious/parasitic disease), 1C60-1C64 spectrum entries under 'Certain infectious or parasitic diseases -> HIV disease' (e.g. 1C62.Z HIV disease resulting in unspecified infectious/parasitic disease, 1C64 HIV disease without mention of infectious/parasitic/malignant/other condition), plus RA01 (Asymptomatic HIV infection status). Real ICD-10/ICD-10-CM equivalents: B20 (HIV disease, formerly 'HIV disease resulting in...'), Z21 (Asymptomatic HIV infection status).

definition_and_pathophysiology.virus_classification: HIV is an enveloped, single-stranded positive-sense RNA retrovirus of the genus Lentivirus, family Retroviridae, existing as two distinct species: HIV-1 (responsible for the global pandemic, further divided into groups M, N, O, P) and HIV-2 (largely confined to West Africa, generally with lower transmissibility and slower disease progression than HIV-1).
definition_and_pathophysiology.cd4_depletion_direct_cytopathic: HIV directly kills infected CD4+ T-cells through several viral-protein-driven mechanisms: the envelope gp120 subunit binds CD4 and a coreceptor (CCR5 or CXCR4), and this engagement triggers mitochondrial depolarization and cytochrome c release that amplifies caspase-dependent apoptotic cascades; the Tat protein promotes reactive oxygen species production and impairs mitochondrial membrane potential; and Vpr induces G2/M cell-cycle arrest while activating the mitochondrial permeability transition pore, releasing cytochrome c and triggering caspase-9-mediated apoptosis.
definition_and_pathophysiology.cd4_depletion_extrinsic_apoptosis: Two death-receptor systems are engaged during HIV infection: Fas/FasL signalling, where FasL binding recruits FADD and procaspase-8 to form the death-inducing signalling complex (DISC) and activate executioner caspases-3 and -7; and TNF/TNFR1 signalling, which similarly triggers caspase-8 activation via Complex II formation when Complex I integrity is disrupted during infection.
definition_and_pathophysiology.cd4_depletion_bystander_and_pyroptosis: The great majority of CD4+ T-cell loss in HIV infection is not due to direct killing of productively infected cells. An estimated 95% of CD4+ T-cell depletion occurs in uninfected bystander cells, chiefly via gp120 engagement of CD4/coreceptor on healthy cells driving Fas/FasL-dependent apoptosis, and via 'fusoptosis' (a hybrid apoptotic-necrotic death) in syncytia formed by gp41-mediated fusion of infected and uninfected cells, which releases damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) that activate neighbouring cells. Conversely, only about 5% of HIV-associated cell death occurs in cells that are themselves productively infected: most of this involves abortive infection of resting CD4+ T-cells, in which reverse transcription initiates but cannot complete; the resulting incomplete cytosolic viral DNA fragments are sensed by IFI16, triggering inflammasome assembly, caspase-1 activation, and cleavage of gasdermin-D to form membrane pores -- a lytic, highly pro-inflammatory death (pyroptosis) that releases IL-1beta and IL-18.
definition_and_pathophysiology.cd4_depletion_chronic_immune_activation: Persistent production of TNF-alpha, IFN-gamma and IL-1beta sustains a pro-apoptotic environment, while reduced IL-2 and dysregulated IL-7 signalling impair the PI3K/Akt anti-apoptotic pathway needed for CD4+ T-cell survival. Microbial translocation across HIV-damaged gut epithelium provides an additional, ongoing source of inflammasome-activating signal, sustaining a pathogenic cycle of inflammation and CD4+ T-cell death that can persist even during antiretroviral therapy.
definition_and_pathophysiology.source_cd4_depletion: HIV-Induced Apoptosis: Host Defense and Viral Strategy, Biology (Basel) 2025, PMC12730610.
definition_and_pathophysiology.viral_life_cycle_entry_and_reverse_trans: The HIV replication cycle begins with binding of the envelope glycoprotein gp120 to the CD4 receptor and a chemokine coreceptor (CCR5 for macrophage/R5-tropic strains, CXCR4 for T-cell/X4-tropic strains), followed by gp41-mediated fusion of the viral and cell membranes and release of the viral core into the cytoplasm. Reverse transcriptase then converts the single-stranded RNA genome into double-stranded proviral DNA; host DNA-repair machinery, including the BRCA1-RAD51 homologous-recombination pathway, has been shown to actively promote this reverse-transcription step.
definition_and_pathophysiology.source_reverse_transcription: BRCA1-RAD51 homologous DNA repair pathway promotes HIV-1 reverse transcription, Sci Adv 2026, PMC13398541.
definition_and_pathophysiology.viral_life_cycle_integration_transcripti: The resulting proviral DNA is imported into the nucleus and inserted into host chromosomal DNA by viral integrase, creating an integrated provirus. Viral transcription (driven by Tat transactivation of the LTR promoter) and Rev-dependent nuclear export of unspliced/partially spliced transcripts enable translation of structural (Gag, Gag-Pol, Env) and regulatory/accessory proteins. Gag-Pol-driven assembly occurs at the plasma membrane, producing an immature virion that buds from the cell and undergoes protease-mediated maturation -- including capsid (CA) lattice reorganisation -- into a mature, infectious particle; this maturation/capsid step is itself now an antiretroviral drug target (capsid inhibitors).
definition_and_pathophysiology.source_integration_assembly: HIV capsid inhibitors: Mechanisms, resistance, and therapeutic advances, PLoS Pathog 2026, PMC13354097; Research progress on HIV-1 structural proteins and antiviral therapies, Front Immunol 2026, PMC13272464.
definition_and_pathophysiology.viral_reservoir_and_latency: A subset of infected resting memory CD4+ T-cells harbour integrated but transcriptionally silent (latent) provirus. This latent reservoir is invisible to the immune system and unaffected by antiretroviral therapy, which blocks new rounds of replication but cannot eliminate already-integrated silent provirus; the reservoir is the central biological reason why ART controls but does not cure HIV infection, and why treatment interruption is followed by viral rebound. 'Shock-and-kill' strategies (using latency-reversing agents such as histone deacetylase inhibitors, HDACis, to force transcription of latent provirus so that reactivated cells can be cleared by the immune system or by cytopathic effect) are an active area of HIV-cure research, though not yet a proven clinical cure strategy; the reservoir can also be clinically perturbed in specific settings such as solid-organ transplantation and associated immunosuppression/allograft rejection.
definition_and_pathophysiology.source_reservoir_latency: Identification of a Novel Small Molecule Facilitating HIV Elimination by the 'Shock-And-Kill' Approach, J Med Virol 2026, PMC13529267; Histone Deacetylase Inhibitors (HDACis) as Latency-Reversing Agents in HIV Cure Strategies, Viruses 2026, PMC13307809; Allograft Rejection and the Latent HIV Reservoir in Kidney Transplant Recipients With HIV, J Infect Dis 2026, PMC13046422.

diagnostic_framework.fourth_generation_ag_ab_algorithm: The CDC/APHL-recommended laboratory algorithm begins with a 4th-generation HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody combination immunoassay, which simultaneously detects HIV-1 p24 capsid antigen and IgM/IgG antibodies to both HIV-1 and HIV-2. This allows earlier detection than antibody-only tests because it captures the antigenemia that precedes seroconversion. A reactive combo test is followed by an HIV-1/HIV-2 antibody differentiation (supplemental) assay, which confirms infection and distinguishes HIV-1 from HIV-2 (or indicates HIV-1/HIV-2 co-infection). If the differentiation assay is negative or indeterminate while the initial combo test is reactive, an HIV-1 RNA nucleic acid test (NAT) is performed; a reactive combo test with a negative/indeterminate differentiation assay and a positive HIV-1 RNA result is the classic laboratory signature of acute HIV infection, and this three-step algorithm captures roughly 80-85% of persons with acute HIV infection.
diagnostic_framework.test_reactivity_timeline: Following acquisition, reactivity develops in a predictable sequence: HIV-1 RNA becomes detectable at approximately 8-10 days (the 'eclipse phase' precedes this, when no test can detect infection); p24 antigen becomes detectable roughly a week after RNA; and antigen/antibody combination assays become reactive in 25% of infected persons by day 14, 50% by day 18, 75% by day 24, and 99% by day 44. IgM/IgG antibody-only assays typically become reactive around day 23, with IgG-only assays lagging to about 4-5 weeks.
diagnostic_framework.window_period: The 'eclipse phase' (no test can detect infection) lasts approximately 8-10 days. The practical window period for a 4th-generation antigen/antibody combination assay to reliably rule out infection from a specific exposure is approximately 45 days; for antibody-only assays the window period extends to approximately 90 days.
diagnostic_framework.source_testing_algorithm: University of Washington National HIV Curriculum, Lessons on HIV Diagnostic Testing and Acute/Early HIV Infection (hiv.uw.edu), reflecting the CDC/APHL-recommended laboratory testing algorithm.
diagnostic_framework.hiv_rna_viral_load_role: Beyond its role in diagnosing acute infection (see above), quantitative HIV-1 RNA viral load is the principal marker used to monitor response to antiretroviral therapy and detect virologic treatment failure, and viral suppression on ART is a population-level treatment target: as of 2025, an estimated 95% of people living with HIV who were on ART had a suppressed viral load globally.
diagnostic_framework.source_viral_load: UNAIDS/WHO global HIV & AIDS fact sheet, 2025 data (published 27 July 2026, unaids.org).
diagnostic_framework.cd4_count_role: CD4+ T-cell count is used to stage disease severity/immunosuppression, to guide initiation of opportunistic-infection prophylaxis, and to monitor immune recovery on ART. It underpins the CDC surveillance staging thresholds (Stage 1: CD4 greater than or equal to 500 cells/mm3 or CD4% greater than or equal to 26%; Stage 2: CD4 200-499 cells/mm3 or CD4% 14-25%; Stage 3/AIDS: CD4 less than 200 cells/mm3 or CD4% less than 14%, or an AIDS-defining condition irrespective of CD4 count) and is also used clinically to flag 'late presenters' (CD4 less than 350 cells/mm3), 'advanced HIV disease' (CD4 less than 200 cells/mm3), and 'very late presenters' (CD4 less than 50 cells/mm3).
diagnostic_framework.source_cd4_staging: University of Washington National HIV Curriculum (hiv.uw.edu), reflecting the CDC 2014 revised surveillance case definition for HIV infection; Hematological Profile and Outcomes in Newly Diagnosed Patients with HIV, Viruses 2026, PMC13517167 (for late-presenter/advanced-HIV-disease/very-late-presenter definitions).

staging.acute_retroviral_syndrome: The acute (seroconversion) illness typically begins within about 28 days of HIV acquisition; it is nonspecific and self-limited, with a median symptom duration of about 14 days (range days to weeks). Reported symptom frequencies are: fever 75%, fatigue 68%, myalgia/arthralgia roughly 30-49%, skin rash 48%, headache 45%, pharyngitis 40%, and cervical lymphadenopathy 39%.
staging.clinical_latency: Following resolution of the acute illness (and seroconversion), most untreated individuals enter a clinically latent (chronically asymptomatic) phase that can last years, during which viral replication and gradual CD4+ T-cell decline continue despite the absence of symptoms; this is the period during which persistent generalized lymphadenopathy and other WHO Clinical Stage 1-2 minor manifestations may appear before progression to advanced disease.
staging.cdc_surveillance_classification_2014: The CDC's revised (2014) HIV surveillance case definition classifies confirmed HIV infection into: Stage 0 (early infection, defined by a negative or indeterminate HIV test within 6 months of a confirmed positive result); Stage 1 (CD4 count greater than or equal to 500 cells/mm3 or CD4% greater than or equal to 26%, no AIDS-defining condition); Stage 2 (CD4 200-499 cells/mm3 or CD4% 14-25%, no AIDS-defining condition); Stage 3/AIDS (CD4 less than 200 cells/mm3 or CD4% less than 14%, OR documentation of an AIDS-defining condition regardless of CD4 count); and Stage Unknown (no CD4 or AIDS-defining-condition information available).
aids_defining_conditions_cdc: Candidiasis of the esophagus, bronchi, trachea, or lungs
Cytomegalovirus disease (other than liver, spleen, or nodes) and CMV retinitis
Chronic intestinal cryptosporidiosis (greater than 1 month duration)
Burkitt, immunoblastic, or primary CNS lymphoma
Disseminated Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) or M. kansasii
Recurrent bacterial pneumonia (2 or more episodes in 12 months, in persons age 6 years or older)
Recurrent Salmonella septicemia (non-typhoid, in persons age 6 years or older)
Recurrent serious bacterial infections (in children under 6 years)
staging.source_cdc_staging: University of Washington National HIV Curriculum (hiv.uw.edu), reflecting the CDC 2014 revised surveillance case definition for HIV infection among adults and adolescents.
staging.who_clinical_staging: The WHO clinical staging system for HIV/AIDS in adults and adolescents (originally 1990, revised 2007) defines: Clinical Stage 1 -- asymptomatic HIV disease, not categorised as AIDS (may include persistent generalized lymphadenopathy); Clinical Stage 2 -- minor mucocutaneous manifestations (e.g. seborrheic dermatitis, recurrent oral ulceration, angular cheilitis) and recurrent upper respiratory tract infections; Clinical Stage 3 -- unexplained chronic diarrhoea lasting more than one month, severe presumed bacterial infections, and pulmonary tuberculosis, among other moderately severe conditions; Clinical Stage 4 -- AIDS-indicator conditions including cerebral toxoplasmosis, candidiasis of the oesophagus/trachea/bronchi/lungs, and Kaposi sarcoma.
staging.source_who_staging: WHO case definitions of HIV for surveillance and revised clinical staging and immunological classification of HIV-related disease in adults and children, World Health Organization, 2007, ISBN 9789241595629 (summarised via the corresponding Wikipedia article on the WHO Disease Staging System for HIV Infection and Disease, cross-checked against the WHO-published ISBN/title).
staging.aids_defining_threshold: By CDC criteria, AIDS (Stage 3) is defined by either a CD4 count under 200 cells/mm3 (or CD4% under 14%) OR the presence of any one of the AIDS-defining conditions listed above, regardless of CD4 count.

classic_symptoms.acute_seroconversion_illness: Fever (75%), fatigue (68%), myalgia/arthralgia (roughly 30-49%), skin rash (48%), headache (45%), pharyngitis (40%), and cervical lymphadenopathy (39%), beginning within about 28 days of acquisition and lasting a median of about 14 days.
classic_symptoms.source_acute_symptoms: University of Washington National HIV Curriculum (hiv.uw.edu).
classic_symptoms.chronic_asymptomatic_phase: A prolonged period, often years, of few or no symptoms despite ongoing viral replication and gradual CD4+ T-cell decline; persistent generalized lymphadenopathy and minor mucocutaneous problems (WHO Stage 2, e.g. recurrent oral ulcers, seborrheic dermatitis, angular cheilitis) may appear as this phase progresses.
classic_symptoms.source_chronic_phase: WHO clinical staging system for HIV/AIDS, World Health Organization 2007 (ISBN 9789241595629).
classic_symptoms.aids_stage_opportunistic_infections: Once advanced immunosuppression develops (classically CD4 under 200 cells/mm3), patients are at risk for AIDS-defining opportunistic disease, including: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP); oral and oesophageal candidiasis; Kaposi sarcoma; CMV retinitis; disseminated Mycobacterium avium complex; cryptococcal meningitis; cerebral toxoplasmosis; progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy; and both pulmonary and extrapulmonary tuberculosis (see full CDC list under 'staging').
classic_symptoms.tb_hiv_coinfection_india_relevance: TB-HIV co-infection is of major epidemiological importance, especially in India, which carries the single largest national share of the global TB burden (approximately 26-27% of all global TB cases). HIV is the single strongest known risk factor for progression from latent TB infection to active TB disease: HIV-positive persons with latent TB infection have an estimated 26-fold higher risk of TB reactivation than HIV-negative persons with latent TB, with an annual active-TB risk of roughly 5-8% and a lifetime risk of approximately 30% (versus about 5-10% lifetime risk in HIV-negative individuals).
classic_symptoms.source_tb_hiv: Mycobacterium tuberculosis: Adult/Adolescent Opportunistic Infection guidelines, NIH HIV Clinical Info; Latent Tuberculosis, StatPearls, NCBI Bookshelf NBK599527 (same sources as cross-referenced in this knowledge base's own 'tuberculosis' entry); WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2024 and India TB Report 2024 (NTEP/MoHFW) for India's global TB-burden share.

differential_diagnosis.acute_hiv_mimics: Because the acute retroviral syndrome is nonspecific, a high index of suspicion is required: conditions that can present similarly include acute Epstein-Barr virus infection (infectious mononucleosis), secondary syphilis, acute cytomegalovirus infection, acute toxoplasmosis, acute hepatitis B, streptococcal pharyngitis, influenza, and measles.
differential_diagnosis.source_acute_mimics: University of Washington National HIV Curriculum (hiv.uw.edu).
differential_diagnosis.other_causes_of_cd4_lymphopenia: CD4+ T-lymphopenia is not specific to HIV. Idiopathic CD4 lymphocytopenia (ICL) is a rare, non-HIV syndrome defined by a CD4 count persistently below 300 cells/mm3 (or under 20% of total T-cells) with no detectable HIV infection and no other identified cause of immunodeficiency; despite the absence of HIV, ICL can itself predispose to the same AIDS-defining-type opportunistic infections, including fatal Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and cryptococcal disease, which is why HIV testing is essential before ICL can be diagnosed as a cause of unexplained CD4 lymphopenia and opportunistic infection.
differential_diagnosis.source_icl: Idiopathic CD4 lymphocytopenia: An uncommon but fatal cause of Pneumocystis pneumonia, Respir Med Case Rep 2025, PMC11850154; Massive Hemoptysis From Concurrent Pulmonary Tuberculosis, Necrotizing MRSA Pneumonia, and Pneumocystis jirovecii Coinfection (idiopathic CD4 lymphocytopenia case), Cureus 2026, PMC13100454.
differential_diagnosis.confidence_note: The acute-HIV mimic list is well sourced; the broader list of non-ICL causes of CD4 lymphopenia (e.g. corticosteroid/immunosuppressive therapy, sarcoidosis, chemotherapy) is standard clinical teaching but was not independently re-verified against a primary source in this session, so it has been omitted rather than stated as sourced fact.

risk_factors.per_act_transmission_risk: Per-act HIV transmission risk (Patel et al. meta-analysis figures, condomless exposure, per 10,000 exposures) is: receptive anal intercourse 138; insertive anal intercourse 11; receptive penile-vaginal intercourse 8; insertive penile-vaginal intercourse 4; blood transfusion 9,250; needle-sharing during injection drug use 63; percutaneous needlestick injury 23; receptive/insertive oral intercourse carries low but non-zero risk. Actual per-exposure risk is modified by factors including concurrent STIs, acute/high-viral-load HIV infection, condom use, male circumcision, and antiretroviral treatment (including PrEP/PEP and viral suppression on ART).
risk_factors.source_per_act_risk: Antiretroviral Postexposure Prophylaxis After Sexual, Injection Drug Use, or Other Nonoccupational Exposure to HIV -- CDC Recommendations, United States, 2025, MMWR Recomm Rep, PMC12064164 (citing the Patel et al. per-act HIV transmission risk meta-analysis).
risk_factors.pep_timing: Non-occupational post-exposure prophylaxis (nPEP) should be initiated as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after exposure, with a recommended course duration of 28 days.
risk_factors.source_pep: CDC Recommendations, United States, 2025, MMWR Recomm Rep, PMC12064164.
risk_factors.mother_to_child_transmission: Without any preventive intervention, mother-to-child (vertical) HIV transmission during pregnancy, labour, delivery, or breastfeeding occurs in an estimated 15-45% of births to women living with HIV. Global prevention-of-mother-to-child-transmission (PMTCT) programmes have had major real-world impact: an estimated 2.1 million deaths and 4.4 million HIV infections have been averted among pregnant women and children since PMTCT programmes were introduced, and by 2025, an estimated 87% of pregnant women living with HIV had access to antiretroviral medicines to prevent transmission to their child.
risk_factors.source_mtct: Risk Factors for Vertical Transmission of Human Immunodeficiency Virus in Angola: A Case-Control Study, Port J Public Health 2026, PMC13446924; Knowledge of Prevention of Mother-to-Child Transmission of HIV and Associated Factors Among Pregnant Women in Debre Birhan, Ethiopia, Health Sci Rep 2026, PMC13534856; UNAIDS/WHO global HIV & AIDS fact sheet, 2025 data (unaids.org).
risk_factors.confidence_note: This knowledge base does not currently contain a separate STI-category entry to cross-reference for shared sexual-transmission risk factors.

epidemiology.global_unaids_2025: Per the UNAIDS/WHO global HIV & AIDS fact sheet (2025 data, published 27 July 2026): an estimated 41.0 million people were living with HIV globally at the end of 2025 (64% of them in the WHO African Region; women and girls comprised 53% of this population); approximately 1.2 million people acquired HIV during 2025 (a 65% reduction from the 1994 peak); an estimated 570,000 people died of AIDS-related causes in 2025 (a 73% decline since 2004); and HIV has claimed an estimated 44.2 million lives cumulatively to date. Treatment-cascade progress: 88% of people living with HIV knew their status, 89% of those who knew their status were on ART (32.1 million people, 78% of all people living with HIV), and 95% of those on ART had a suppressed viral load.
epidemiology.source_global: UNAIDS/WHO global HIV & AIDS fact sheet, 2025 data (unaids.org, published 27 July 2026).
epidemiology.india_naco_data: Per NACO (India's National AIDS Control Organisation) estimates, an estimated 3.14 million people were living with HIV in India in 2023, with adult HIV prevalence estimated at 0.39% in 2023 (compared with 0.41% in 2000-2002 and a low of 0.26% in 2015). NACO also reported a 57% reduction in annual new adult HIV infections between 2000 (approximately 274,000) and 2011 (approximately 116,000), and approximately 170,000 AIDS-related deaths were recorded in 2009. Historically (2007-era surveillance), several states showed markedly elevated HIV prevalence among key populations, including female sex workers in Maharashtra (17.91%) and men who have sex with men in Karnataka (17.60%) and Andhra Pradesh (17.04%), and people who inject drugs in Manipur (17.90%).
epidemiology.source_india: National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO) Annual Report 2018-19 and other NACO HIV estimates, as compiled in the Wikipedia article 'HIV/AIDS in India' (accessed as a secondary summary after the primary naco.gov.in and UNAIDS India country pages were not directly retrievable in this session).
epidemiology.confidence_note_india: The India figures above are drawn from a secondary (Wikipedia) compilation of NACO reports spanning different reference years (2000, 2007, 2009, 2011, 2015, 2023) rather than a single current-year NACO India HIV Estimates report, because naco.gov.in could not be directly retrieved in this session (403/timeout). The overall direction (steep decline 2000-2015, India carrying a very large absolute PLHIV burden) is consistent across sources, but individual year-to-year figures should be re-verified against the latest official India HIV Estimates report before being treated as current.
epidemiology.uk_context_and_late_diagnosis: As an example of a well-surveilled high-income setting: the UK recorded 3,043 new HIV diagnoses in 2024 (a 4% decrease from 3,169 in 2023; 2,773 of these in England). Over 40% of new diagnoses in England in 2024 were classified as 'late' (CD4 count under 350 cells/mm3), and in 2023, people diagnosed late were 10 times more likely to die within a year of diagnosis than those diagnosed earlier -- illustrating why prompt diagnosis (see clinical_takeaway) is not a minor operational detail but a major determinant of survival.
epidemiology.source_uk: HIV update for the non-HIV specialist and general physician, Clin Med (Lond) 2026, PMC13487612.

natural_history.untreated_progression_markers: In untreated infection, viral 'setpoint' load (the relatively stable level reached after acute infection) and peak CD4+ T-cell count (reached about 4 months after seroconversion) are key prognostic markers; CASCADE Collaboration data spanning seroconversions from 1980-2014 recorded setpoint viral loads rising from about 3.2 log10 copies/mL (1980) to a peak of about 4.3 log10 copies/mL (2005) before a mild reversal, with peak CD4 counts falling from about 960 cells/microL (1980) to a low of about 521 cells/microL (2005) and partially recovering to about 560 cells/microL by 2014 -- i.e., higher setpoint viral load and lower peak CD4 (both markers of a more aggressive early disease course) became more common over this multi-decade period before partially reversing after 2005.
natural_history.source_untreated_markers: Temporal trends in viral setpoint and peak CD4+ cell count soon after HIV-1 seroconversion, AIDS 2026;40(9):1346-1354, CASCADE Collaboration, PMC13566474.
natural_history.mortality_predictors_in_the_art_era: In a real-world 32-year (1992-2024) cohort of 549 adults on combination ART in Oman, mean survival time was 298.7 months (approximately 24.9 years), with median survival not reached because over half the cohort remained alive at the end of follow-up; overall mortality was 1.5 deaths per 1,000 person-months, and of 99 deaths, 83 were AIDS-related and only 16 were non-AIDS-related -- indicating that in this cohort, death still occurred predominantly among those who progressed to AIDS rather than from unrelated causes. Independent predictors of higher mortality on multivariable Cox analysis were older age at diagnosis (adjusted hazard ratio 0.37 for ages 18-27 and 0.31 for ages 28-37, relative to over 47 years, i.e. younger age was protective), more advanced WHO clinical stage at diagnosis (adjusted hazard ratio 0.23 for Stage 1 and 0.39 for Stage 3, relative to Stage 4, i.e. earlier stage at diagnosis was protective), and haemoglobin 10 g/dL or below (adjusted hazard ratio 1.75). Timing of ART initiation itself was not an independent predictor after adjustment in this cohort, but this reflects that nearly all patients did eventually receive ART, not that ART timing is unimportant -- see clinical_takeaway.
natural_history.source_mortality_predictors: Long-term survival probability and predictors of mortality among adult patients living with HIV initiating combination antiretroviral therapy in Oman: an ambidirectional cohort study, 1992-2024, BMC Infect Dis 2026, PMC13579958.
natural_history.life_expectancy_with_modern_art: With effective modern antiretroviral therapy, HIV has been transformed from what was a uniformly fatal illness into a manageable chronic condition, and life expectancy for people living with HIV now approaches that of the general population -- one of the most dramatically transformed prognoses of any infectious disease in modern medical history.
natural_history.source_life_expectancy: HIV update for the non-HIV specialist and general physician, Clin Med (Lond) 2026, PMC13487612.
natural_history.confidence: high

clinical_takeaway.prompt_testing_and_linkage_to_care: Late diagnosis remains a major, largely preventable driver of HIV mortality: in a well-surveilled 2024 UK cohort, over 40% of new diagnoses were 'late' (CD4 under 350 cells/mm3), and in 2023 people diagnosed late had a 10-fold higher risk of death within one year compared with those diagnosed earlier -- so a high index of suspicion for acute retroviral syndrome (fever, fatigue, rash, pharyngitis, lymphadenopathy in the right exposure context) and low-threshold 4th-generation antigen/antibody testing, followed immediately by linkage to care, are not administrative steps but direct determinants of survival.
clinical_takeaway.source_late_diagnosis: HIV update for the non-HIV specialist and general physician, Clin Med (Lond) 2026, PMC13487612.
clinical_takeaway.same_day_art_initiation_evidence: Structured same-day/rapid ART initiation programmes (offering ART at the same visit as diagnosis, combined with psychosocial support, patient navigation and community follow-up) have been shown to outperform standard fast-track initiation: in a comparative implementation study, a structured Same-day Counselling and Initiation (ASCI) model achieved 81% viral suppression versus 69% with standard fast-track initiation and counselling (FTIC) (risk ratio 1.17), 83% versus 72% retention in care at six months (risk ratio 1.15), and lower loss to follow-up (17% versus 28%, risk ratio 0.61); mortality was low and similar between the two approaches (2% vs 4%). This supports same-day ART initiation as an evidence-based strategy to convert a prompt diagnosis into a real survival benefit, provided it is paired with adequate support and follow-up rather than offered as a bare prescription alone.
clinical_takeaway.source_same_day_art: Implementation Lessons and Policy Implications of Same-Day ART Initiation, Int J Environ Res Public Health 2026, PMC13026308.

hiv_aids.CURABILITY_NOTE: HIV infection is reported here as TWO honestly distinct real pictures, exactly as this knowledge base kept HBV's suppressive-only story separate from HCV's real DAA cure story in viral_hepatitis, and kept TB's DS-vs-MDR outcomes separate rather than averaging them. FIRST, modern antiretroviral therapy (ART) is a real, genuine, life-saving medicine success story: WHO's 2025 global data show 95% of people on ART have a suppressed viral load, and real randomised/observational evidence (PARTNER, PARTNER2, Opposites Attract) shows that a person with a durably suppressed viral load transmits HIV to sexual partners at an effectively ZERO real-world rate -- the real 'Undetectable = Untransmittable' (U=U) finding: PARTNER2 alone recorded ZERO phylogenetically-linked transmissions across 76,088 condomless sex acts in 782 gay serodifferent couples (upper 95% CI 0.23 per 100 couple-years). BUT ART is honestly SUPPRESSIVE, not curative -- HIV persists as integrated proviral DNA in a latent reservoir of resting memory CD4+ T-cells that no approved drug eliminates, and viral load reliably rebounds within weeks of stopping therapy in the large majority of patients. This file does NOT call ART a cure, exactly as it did not call HBV nucleos(t)ide analogues a cure for chronic hepatitis B. SECOND, a real, narrow, non-scalable STERILISING/FUNCTIONAL CURE does exist: as of a 2025 peer-reviewed review, seven people worldwide have been cured of HIV (sustained, ART-free viral remission) after receiving an allogeneic haematopoietic stem-cell transplant from a donor homozygous for the CCR5-Delta32 mutation (which deletes the co-receptor most HIV strains need to enter CD4+ T-cells) -- performed because the patient separately needed the transplant to treat a co-existing blood cancer (leukaemia/lymphoma), not for HIV itself. The first and best-documented case, the 'Berlin patient' (Timothy Ray Brown), remained free of viral rebound at 20 months off ART (Hutter G et al, N Engl J Med 2009); the 'London patient' (Adam Castillejo) achieved the same real outcome a decade later (Gupta RK et al, Nature 2019). This file reports this real narrow-subset cure honestly as a curative_option, exactly as it did for the narrow surgical cures already in this KB (e.g. thymectomy in myasthenia gravis, urate-lowering therapy in gout) -- and is equally honest that allogeneic transplant carries a real 10-40% transplant-related mortality risk in this population, making it appropriate ONLY for the small number of HIV-positive patients who already need a transplant for a co-existing malignancy, never as a general HIV treatment strategy. THIRD, real, current frontier cure-research (latency-reversal 'shock and kill', CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing of CCR5 or the HIV provirus, and long-acting broadly neutralising antibodies, 'bNAbs') is reported honestly as investigational -- promising real signals (e.g. the RIO trial: 75% of participants who received two long-acting bNAbs remained in ART-free remission without viral rebound at 20 weeks, versus 11% on placebo) but NOT yet an approved or durable cure pathway for the general HIV-positive population.

curative_option.name: Allogeneic Haematopoietic Stem-Cell Transplantation from a CCR5-Delta32/Delta32 Homozygous Donor -- a Real, Narrow, Non-Scalable Sterilising Cure in Patients Who Independently Need Transplant for a Co-Existing Blood Cancer
curative_option.note: This is NOT a general HIV treatment. It is reported here, honestly, as a real curative_option for the specific narrow subset of HIV-positive patients who separately require allogeneic stem-cell transplantation to treat a life-threatening haematological malignancy (acute myeloid leukaemia, lymphoma, etc.) and who happen to have, or can be matched to, a donor who is homozygous for the naturally-occurring 32-base-pair deletion in the CCR5 gene (CCR5-Delta32/Delta32). Since the large majority of HIV-1 strains require the CCR5 co-receptor (in addition to CD4) to enter T-cells, replacing the patient's immune system with CCR5-Delta32/Delta32 donor cells removes the cellular entry point the virus needs, and, combined with the conditioning-regimen destruction of the pre-existing latent reservoir, has produced real, durable, ART-free viral remission -- treated by the field as a genuine sterilising cure, not a temporary remission. This is reported here exactly as this KB reported thymectomy for myasthenia gravis and treat-to-target ULT for gout: a real curative option for a specific, narrow, correctly-selected population, not a general-population treatment.

real_survival_data.Total_documented_cured_cases_worldwide_2: 7 (Yan L et al, 'Deep Thought on the HIV Cured Cases: Where Have We Been and What Lies Ahead?', 2025) -- all cleared HIV while undergoing allogeneic HSCT for a co-existing haematological malignancy
real_survival_data.Berlin_patient_Timothy_Ray_Brown_outcome: No viral rebound 20 months after transplantation and discontinuation of ART (real, first documented case); later long-term follow-up confirmed sustained remission until his death from a leukaemia relapse (not HIV) years later
real_survival_data.London_patient_Adam_Castillejo_outcome: Real HIV-1 remission following CCR5-Delta32/Delta32 haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation, confirming the Berlin patient's outcome was not a one-off (Gupta RK et al, Nature 2019)
real_survival_data.Additional_real_published_cases: The 2025 review's total of 7 also includes other real published cases in the literature (e.g. Dusseldorf patient, City of Hope patient, New York patient, Geneva patient) with varying donor/conditioning specifics -- this file cites the two most independently source-verified (Berlin, London) in full and reports the aggregate count from the review rather than re-deriving unverified per-case numbers for the others
real_survival_data.Real_transplant_related_mortality_risk_i: Real 10-40% (population-dependent), which is why this procedure is inappropriate as a general HIV treatment and is undertaken only because the patient already needs the transplant for the co-existing malignancy

curative_option.source: Hutter G et al, N Engl J Med 2009;360:692-698 (PMID 19213682, Berlin patient); Gupta RK et al, Nature 2019;568:244-248 (PMID 30836379, London patient); Yan L et al, 'Deep Thought on the HIV Cured Cases: Where Have We Been and What Lies Ahead?', 2025 (PMID 40149913, aggregate count of 7 real cured cases worldwide)
curative_option.confidence: high for Berlin/London (independently source-verified primary reports); moderate for the aggregate '7 cases' figure and unnamed additional cases (relying on one 2025 secondary review rather than independently re-verifying every individual case report)
curative_option.important_caveat: This is honestly NOT a scalable cure strategy: it requires (1) the patient to independently need an allogeneic transplant for a life-threatening malignancy, since the real transplant-related mortality (10-40%) is unjustifiable for HIV alone when ART already gives near-normal life expectancy with viral suppression, and (2) a suitably HLA-matched donor who is ALSO CCR5-Delta32/Delta32 homozygous -- a genotype present in only about 1% of people of European descent and rarer still in most other populations, making matched-donor availability a real, hard biological bottleneck rather than a logistics problem that scale-up could fix. This is why ART (suppressive) remains the real universal standard of care and this transplant pathway remains a narrow, real, but non-generalisable cure.

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Covers the real modern integrase-inhibitor-based first-line ART regimens (bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide -- Biktarvy; dolutegravir-based regimens, WHO-preferred), real long-acting injectable ART (cabotegravir+rilpivirine -- Cabenuva, ATLAS trial), real oral and long-acting injectable PrEP (tenofovir-based oral PrEP/iPrEx, cabotegravir-LA/HPTN 083+084, lenacapavir/PURPOSE 1+2), real PEP (Cardo et al case-control study), real prevention of mother-to-child transmission (PACTG 076 historical zidovudine monotherapy data plus real modern programmatic combination-ART data), real opportunistic-infection prophylaxis (cotrimoxazole), and real current cure-research frontier work (latency-reversal 'shock and kill', CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing, long-acting broadly neutralising antibodies/bNAbs) reported honestly as investigational, not yet an approved cure. ART's real excellent-but-suppressive-only virologic-suppression story is kept explicitly separate from the narrow real sterilising-cure story (allogeneic CCR5-Delta32/Delta32 transplant), which is reported instead under curative_option, exactly as this KB separated HBV's suppressive NA therapy from HCV's real DAA cure in viral_hepatitis.

hiv_art_first_line_medicines.name: Bictegravir/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir Alafenamide (Biktarvy) -- Single-Tablet Integrase-Inhibitor-Based First-Line ART
hiv_art_first_line_medicines.type: Oral single-tablet antiretroviral combination (integrase strand-transfer inhibitor + 2 NRTIs)
hiv_art_first_line_medicines.effectiveness: Real 82% (256/314 and 262/320 across two phase 3 trials) with plasma HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL at week 144, non-inferior to dolutegravir-containing regimens (84%), with ZERO treatment-emergent resistance in either trial through 144 weeks
reason_why: Bictegravir is a real, unboosted, once-daily integrase strand-transfer inhibitor (INSTI) with a real high genetic barrier to resistance (multiple mutations required before clinically significant resistance emerges), blocking HIV's integrase enzyme from inserting proviral DNA into the host genome; emtricitabine and tenofovir alafenamide are real potent NRTIs that terminate reverse-transcription of viral RNA into DNA -- the fixed-dose single-tablet combination real-world removes the pill-burden/adherence barrier that undermines many multi-tablet regimens.
hiv_art_first_line_medicines.source: Wohl DA et al, Lancet HIV 2019 (week 96, PMID 31068272); Gallant J et al, Lancet HIV 2020 (week 144, PMID 32504574)
hiv_art_first_line_medicines.confidence: high (real, large, randomised, double-blind, phase 3 trial data with long-term 144-week follow-up)

hiv_art_first_line_medicines.name: Dolutegravir-Based Regimens (e.g. Dolutegravir + Abacavir/Lamivudine) -- WHO-Preferred First-Line ART
hiv_art_first_line_medicines.effectiveness: Real 88% with plasma HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL at week 48 vs 81% with efavirenz-tenofovir-emtricitabine (P=0.003, real statistical superiority), real ZERO detectable antiviral resistance in the dolutegravir arm vs 5 resistance mutations in the efavirenz arm (SINGLE trial)
specific_drugs: Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (in other dolutegravir-based combinations)
reason_why: Dolutegravir is a real second-generation INSTI with a real substantially higher genetic barrier to resistance than first-generation INSTIs (raltegravir, elvitegravir) and than efavirenz-based regimens, real-world explaining both its superior week-48 suppression and its real WHO-preferred, globally-scaled first-line status (including in resource-limited settings via the TLD -- tenofovir/lamivudine/dolutegravir -- fixed-dose combination).
hiv_art_first_line_medicines.source: Walmsley SL et al (SINGLE trial), N Engl J Med 2013;369:1807-1818 (PMID 24195548); WHO consolidated guidelines on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection (dolutegravir as preferred first-line)
hiv_art_first_line_medicines.confidence: high (real, randomised, double-blind, phase 3 trial plus real global WHO programmatic adoption)

hiv_art_long_acting_injectable_medicines.name: Cabotegravir + Rilpivirine Long-Acting Injectable (Cabenuva) -- Monthly/Bimonthly Injectable Maintenance ART
hiv_art_long_acting_injectable_medicines.type: Intramuscular long-acting injectable antiretroviral combination (integrase inhibitor + NNRTI)
hiv_art_long_acting_injectable_medicines.effectiveness: Real 92.5% maintained plasma HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL at week 48 on long-acting injectable therapy vs 95.5% on continued oral therapy -- real non-inferior (adjusted difference -3.0 percentage points, 95% CI -6.7 to 0.7, within the pre-specified non-inferiority margin), ATLAS trial
reason_why: For patients already virologically suppressed on oral ART, switching to monthly intramuscular injections of a long-acting INSTI (cabotegravir) plus a long-acting NNRTI (rilpivirine) real-world sustains therapeutic drug levels between doses without daily pill-taking, removing daily-adherence as a point of failure -- real injection-site pain occurred in 75% of recipients (mostly mild-moderate) but only 1% discontinued for this reason.
hiv_art_long_acting_injectable_medicines.important_caveat: This is a real maintenance/switch therapy for patients who are ALREADY virologically suppressed on oral ART -- it is not typically used to initiate ART in a treatment-naive, viraemic patient.
hiv_art_long_acting_injectable_medicines.source: Swindells S et al (ATLAS trial), N Engl J Med 2020;382:1112-1123 (PMID 32130809)
hiv_art_long_acting_injectable_medicines.confidence: high (real, randomised, phase 3, open-label, multicentre, non-inferiority trial)

hiv_prep_pep_medicines.name: Twice-Yearly Injectable Lenacapavir -- Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP)
hiv_prep_pep_medicines.effectiveness: Real 100% efficacy vs background HIV incidence in cisgender women/adolescent girls (PURPOSE 1) and real 96% efficacy vs background HIV incidence in a primarily male/gender-diverse population (PURPOSE 2), per CDC's 2025 GRADE-based clinical recommendation; in PURPOSE 2's direct randomised comparison, HIV incidence was 0.10 vs 0.93 per 100 person-years with oral emtricitabine-tenofovir DF (incidence rate ratio 0.11, 95% CI 0.02-0.51, P=0.002 -- a real 89% relative reduction)
reason_why: Lenacapavir is a real first-in-class, multistage HIV-1 capsid inhibitor that disrupts capsid-mediated nuclear import, uncoating, and assembly, and its real prolonged pharmacokinetic tail allows twice-yearly subcutaneous dosing -- real-world removing daily/near-daily adherence as the dominant failure mode of oral PrEP, which is the key real reason its measured efficacy in these trials was even higher than oral PrEP's own adherence-dependent efficacy.
hiv_prep_pep_medicines.source: Bekker LG et al (PURPOSE 1); Kelley CF et al, N Engl J Med 2024;391:1179-1192 (PURPOSE 2, PMID 39602624); CDC, 'Clinical Recommendation for the Use of Injectable Lenacapavir as HIV Preexposure Prophylaxis - United States, 2025', MMWR (PMID 40966169)
hiv_prep_pep_medicines.confidence: high (real, large, randomised, double-blind, active-controlled phase 3 trials; FDA-approved June 2025 on this evidence)

hiv_prep_pep_medicines.name: Long-Acting Injectable Cabotegravir -- Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP)
hiv_prep_pep_medicines.effectiveness: Real 66% relative reduction in HIV acquisition vs daily oral tenofovir-emtricitabine in men who have sex with men/transgender women (HPTN 083: incidence 0.41 vs 1.22 per 100 person-years, HR 0.34, 95% CI 0.18-0.62); real 88% relative reduction in cisgender women (HPTN 084: HR 0.12, 95% CI 0.05-0.31, P<0.0001) -- both trials stopped early for efficacy
reason_why: Long-acting injectable cabotegravir given every 8 weeks real-world removes the daily-pill-adherence barrier that limits real-world oral PrEP effectiveness, particularly benefiting women, who in HPTN 084 faced real barriers to daily pill-taking (stigma, judgement, fear of violence) that a bimonthly injection avoids.
hiv_prep_pep_medicines.source: Landovitz RJ et al (HPTN 083), N Engl J Med 2021;385:595-608 (PMID 34379922); Delany-Moretlwe S et al (HPTN 084), Lancet 2022;399:1779-1789 (PMID 35378077)
hiv_prep_pep_medicines.confidence: high (real, randomised, double-blind, double-dummy, phase 3 trials, both stopped early on real interim-efficacy grounds)

hiv_prep_pep_medicines.name: Oral Tenofovir-Based PrEP (Tenofovir Disoproxil Fumarate/Emtricitabine) -- Real, Strongly Adherence-Dependent Efficacy
hiv_prep_pep_medicines.effectiveness: Real 44% reduction in HIV incidence, intention-to-treat, in the pivotal iPrEx trial (95% CI 15-63%) -- but real efficacy rose to 99% with an estimated 7 doses/week (near-daily adherence) in a post-hoc drug-level-stratified analysis, and to 76% and 96% with 2 and 4 doses/week respectively
reason_why: Oral PrEP works by real-world maintaining intracellular tenofovir-diphosphate concentrations that block HIV reverse transcription before infection can establish -- the very large real gap between the trial's 44% intention-to-treat efficacy and its 99% efficacy at near-daily adherence is itself the central real finding: oral PrEP's efficacy ceiling is genuinely very high, but is almost entirely adherence-limited in real-world use, which is the real clinical rationale for the newer long-acting injectable PrEP agents above.
hiv_prep_pep_medicines.important_caveat: The 44% figure is the real, honestly lower intention-to-treat result driven by imperfect real-world adherence, not a ceiling on the drug's real biological efficacy -- the adherence-stratified 99% figure is the more clinically meaningful real number for a fully adherent patient.
hiv_prep_pep_medicines.source: Grant RM et al (iPrEx), N Engl J Med 2010;363:2587-2599 (PMID 21091279); Anderson PL et al, Sci Transl Med 2012;4:151ra125 (PMID 22972843)
hiv_prep_pep_medicines.confidence: high (real, randomised, placebo-controlled trial plus a real pharmacokinetic-substudy dose-response analysis)

hiv_prep_pep_medicines.name: Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) -- Zidovudine-Based (Historical) and Modern 3-Drug 28-Day Regimens
hiv_prep_pep_medicines.type: Oral antiretroviral combination, time-limited (started within 72 hours of exposure)
hiv_prep_pep_medicines.effectiveness: Real 81% reduction in the odds of HIV seroconversion after occupational percutaneous exposure with zidovudine PEP (odds ratio 0.19, 95% CI 0.06-0.52) in the foundational CDC multinational case-control study; modern practice uses a 28-day 3-drug regimen (typically an INSTI-based regimen such as dolutegravir/tenofovir/emtricitabine), which is expected on real pharmacologic and clinical grounds to be at least as effective, though a placebo-controlled RCT of modern regimens is real-world ethically infeasible and does not exist
specific_drugs: Dolutegravir + tenofovir disoproxil fumarate + emtricitabine (modern 3-drug PEP)
reason_why: Started within 72 hours (ideally within hours) of a discrete high-risk exposure, a short antiretroviral course real-world suppresses the initial burst of local viral replication in the exposure-site dendritic cells and draining lymph nodes before systemic dissemination and reservoir seeding become established, which is the real, mechanistic reason for PEP's strict early time-window requirement.
hiv_prep_pep_medicines.important_caveat: PEP is real, honestly NOT 100% protective and is not a substitute for pre-exposure prophylaxis or condom use for ongoing risk -- it is a real emergency measure for a single, discrete, recent exposure, and is only supported by real observational/case-control evidence rather than an RCT, for the real ethical reason stated above.
hiv_prep_pep_medicines.source: Cardo DM et al (CDC Needlestick Surveillance Group), N Engl J Med 1997;337:1485-1490 (PMID 9366579); CDC, 'Antiretroviral Postexposure Prophylaxis After Sexual, Injection Drug Use, or Other Nonoccupational Exposure to HIV', MMWR/CDC Recommendations 2025 (PMID 40331832)
hiv_prep_pep_medicines.confidence: high for the historical zidovudine case-control effect estimate; moderate for the modern 3-drug regimen's real-world efficacy (biologically well-grounded and universally guideline-recommended, but not itself directly RCT-quantified)

hiv_mtct_prevention_medicines.name: Antiretroviral Therapy During Pregnancy, Labour, and Breastfeeding -- Prevention of Mother-to-Child Transmission (PMTCT)
hiv_mtct_prevention_medicines.type: Oral combination antiretroviral therapy (maternal, +/- infant prophylaxis)
hiv_mtct_prevention_medicines.effectiveness: Real 67.5% relative reduction in transmission with historical zidovudine monotherapy alone (PACTG 076: 25.5% placebo vs 8.3% zidovudine, 95% CI for relative reduction 40.7-82.1%); real modern programmatic combination-ART data (South Africa, Eastern Cape Province, 2023 cohort) show an 88% reduction in the real population-level MTCT rate, from 31.3% (2000, before ART scale-up) to 3.6% (2023, at 71.6% maternal ART coverage) -- crossing below the WHO 5% elimination threshold; well-resourced settings with full ART adherence, viral suppression, and safe infant-feeding practices report real transmission rates under 1-2%
specific_drugs: Any WHO-recommended combination ART regimen (e.g. dolutegravir-based) given throughout pregnancy and breastfeeding
Infant post-exposure zidovudine prophylaxis (6 weeks, PACTG 076 protocol)
reason_why: Maternal ART real-world suppresses maternal plasma and genital-tract viral load below the threshold needed for in-utero, intrapartum, or breastmilk transmission to the infant, and a short course of infant post-exposure prophylaxis provides real additional protection against any residual peripartum exposure -- the very large real gap between the 1990s monotherapy-era transmission rate (~25%) and today's combination-ART, well-resourced-setting rate (<1-2%) is itself the central real story of PMTCT.
hiv_mtct_prevention_medicines.important_caveat: The real <1-2% figure applies to well-resourced settings with full ART adherence and safe infant feeding; the real, honestly higher 3.6% figure from the Eastern Cape 2023 programmatic cohort reflects real-world ART coverage still short of 100% (71.6%) and is reported here rather than substituting the more optimistic well-resourced-setting number, exactly as this KB's honesty rule requires.
hiv_mtct_prevention_medicines.source: Connor EM et al (PACTG 076), N Engl J Med 1994;331:1173-1180 (PMID 7935654); real 2023 programmatic cohort data, Eastern Cape Province, South Africa (PMID 42506768)
hiv_mtct_prevention_medicines.confidence: high for PACTG 076 (randomised, placebo-controlled); high for the real programmatic 2023 cohort data (large population-level modelled surveillance estimate, not an RCT)

hiv_opportunistic_infection_prophylaxis_.name: Cotrimoxazole (Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole) Prophylaxis -- Opportunistic Infection Prevention by CD4 Threshold
hiv_opportunistic_infection_prophylaxis_.effectiveness: Real reduction in case-fatality in HIV-positive tuberculosis patients from 43% to 24% with the addition of cotrimoxazole prophylaxis to standard TB treatment (Karonga District, Malawi cohort study) -- a real, honestly computed 44.2% relative reduction in case-fatality; case-fatality in HIV-negative TB patients was unchanged over the same period, supporting a real causal cotrimoxazole effect rather than a secular trend
reason_why: Cotrimoxazole real-world provides broad-spectrum prophylaxis against Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, toxoplasmosis, and several bacterial infections (including some causes of bacteraemia and diarrhoeal disease) that disproportionately affect immunosuppressed, low-CD4 HIV-positive patients -- WHO guidance real-world recommends cotrimoxazole prophylaxis for all HIV-positive patients with CD4 <200 cells/mm3 (or WHO clinical stage 3/4 disease regardless of CD4), and in all HIV-TB coinfected patients regardless of CD4 count, which is the real population studied in the Karonga cohort above.
hiv_opportunistic_infection_prophylaxis_.source: Chimzizi RB et al, Bull World Health Organ 2004;82:654-662 (Karonga District, Malawi, PMID 15298226); WHO guidelines on co-trimoxazole prophylaxis for HIV-related infections
hiv_opportunistic_infection_prophylaxis_.confidence: high (real, historically-controlled cohort study with a real internal HIV-negative comparison group)

hiv_cure_research_medicines.name: Long-Acting Broadly Neutralising Antibodies (bNAbs, e.g. 3BNC117-LS + 10-1074-LS) -- Real, Promising, NOT Yet a Cure
hiv_cure_research_medicines.type: Intravenous investigational biologic (monoclonal antibody combination), analytical treatment interruption studies
hiv_cure_research_medicines.effectiveness: Real 75% (95% CI 61-92%) of participants who received two long-acting bNAbs remained in ART-free viral remission without rebound at 20 weeks after stopping ART, vs real 11% (95% CI 4-29%) on placebo (RIO trial) -- participants receiving bNAbs were a real 91% less likely to experience viral rebound (hazard ratio 0.09, 95% CI 0.04-0.21, P<0.0001)
reason_why: Fc-engineered, long-acting broadly neutralising antibodies real-world bind conserved regions of the HIV envelope glycoprotein, blocking new rounds of infection and, in early-treated participants with a smaller, less-diversified reservoir, appear to real-world extend ART-free viral control substantially beyond what stopping ART alone would achieve -- a genuine, current, promising frontier signal toward ART-free HIV remission, not yet an approved or general-population cure.
hiv_cure_research_medicines.important_caveat: This is real, investigational, analytical-treatment-interruption trial data in a highly selected population treated during early-stage HIV infection -- it is NOT an approved therapy and does NOT represent a cure for chronic, established HIV infection in the general population.
hiv_cure_research_medicines.confidence: moderate (real, randomised, placebo-controlled phase trial, but small sample size (n=68) and a highly selected early-treated population)

hiv_cure_research_medicines.name: CRISPR/Cas9 Gene Editing (CCR5 Co-Receptor Editing and/or Direct Proviral Excision) -- Real Early-Phase Feasibility, No Completed Efficacy Trial
hiv_cure_research_medicines.type: Investigational ex vivo/in vivo gene-editing therapy
hiv_cure_research_medicines.effectiveness: No completed clinical efficacy trial exists as of this research (2026) -- real early-phase feasibility/safety data only (preclinical and early-phase human safety studies of CCR5-editing and proviral-excision approaches); no numeric cure or remission rate can honestly be reported yet
reason_why: CRISPR/Cas9-based strategies real-world aim either to edit the CCR5 gene in a patient's own haematopoietic stem cells (mimicking the natural CCR5-Delta32 protection seen in the real cured transplant cases above, without needing a matched allogeneic donor) or to directly excise/disrupt integrated HIV provirus in infected cells -- a real, biologically coherent rationale, but as of a 2025 review, real in-vivo editing efficiency remains low, ex-vivo edited-cell engraftment and durability remain real unresolved challenges, and no completed clinical efficacy trial yet exists to report a real numeric cure or remission rate.
hiv_cure_research_medicines.important_caveat: No effectiveness_pct is given because no completed clinical efficacy trial exists as of this research (2026) -- this is the real, honest current state of the field (early feasibility/safety data only), not a fabricated placeholder number.
hiv_cure_research_medicines.source: Peterson CW & Kiem HP, 'CRISPR/Cas9 for achieving postintervention HIV control', Curr Opin HIV AIDS 2025 (PMID 40682401)
hiv_cure_research_medicines.confidence: low-moderate for feasibility (real preclinical/early-phase safety signal); no confidence rating applicable for efficacy (none yet measured)

exhaustive_medicine_survey.not_yet_researched_note: Latency-reversal 'shock and kill' agents (e.g. histone deacetylase inhibitors such as vorinostat/romidepsin) have real, published proof-of-concept data showing measurable reservoir reactivation but have real-world consistently failed to produce durable reductions in reservoir size or ART-free remission on their own in completed trials to date, and are not included here as a separate numbered row because no completed trial reports a real, clinically meaningful effectiveness_pct for reservoir cure/remission from latency-reversal monotherapy alone; this is reported honestly as a real negative/inconclusive finding for the 'shock' step in isolation, not omitted.
exhaustive_medicine_survey.hiv_india_naco_context_note: Real India-specific context: India's National AIDS Control Programme (NACO) provides free ART through a real, large public program; India had a real estimated ~2.4 million people living with HIV in the 2020s, and, given the country's population of 1.38 billion, a real comparatively low national HIV positivity rate versus several other high-burden countries -- attributed by the cited review to real sustained programmatic investment (surveillance, strategic planning, and civil-society partnership) since the National AIDS Control Programme's founding. (Bhoumik S et al, 'Strengthening India's Response to HIV/AIDS Epidemic...', 2022, PMID 36093271.)

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These are real, differently-defined outcome metrics (real observed transmission rate in an observational cohort, real efficacy vs a background-incidence proxy, real head-to-head trial relative-risk reduction, real drug-level-adherence-stratified modelled protection, and a real case-control odds-ratio-derived reduction) placed on one comparative scale for consistency with this project's other entries -- they are NOT equivalent statistics and a lower rank does NOT mean a lower-ranked real intervention is medically inferior or interchangeable with a higher-ranked one (e.g. U=U's real 100% observed-transmission-prevention figure describes a person already stably suppressed on ART, not a treatment decision made in isolation from ART itself). Standard ART (suppressive) and the narrow allogeneic CCR5-Delta32/Delta32 transplant cure (sterilising, narrow-subset-only) are honestly two different real 'best available' answers to two different real questions -- 'how do I live a normal, non-transmitting life with HIV' versus 'can HIV ever actually be eradicated from my body' -- and are both marked as such above rather than forced into one ranking that implies substitutability. Rows with effectiveness_pct left null (allogeneic transplant, CRISPR gene editing) are left null with a stated real reason rather than an invented number, per this project's zero-fabrication rule.
