pso_phototherapy_narrowband_uvb.reason_why: Narrowband UVB (311-313 nm) induces apoptosis of pathogenic skin-infiltrating T cells and Langerhans cells and directly reduces keratinocyte hyperproliferation, without the systemic immunosuppression of oral/biologic drugs.
pso_phototherapy_narrowband_uvb.important_caveat: This is a real, systemic-drug-free option but requires 2-3 clinic visits per week for many weeks (a genuine access/adherence barrier), carries a real long-term cumulative skin-cancer risk with extensive lifetime UV exposure (lower than PUVA but not zero), and is less effective than PUVA per this same review.
pso_phototherapy_narrowband_uvb.real_working_solution: NB-UVB is a real, systemic-therapy-sparing option for moderate-to-severe plaque or guttate psoriasis, particularly useful where access to a phototherapy unit exists and where injectable/oral systemic therapy is undesired, contraindicated, or not yet accessible; expect roughly two-thirds of patients to reach substantial clearance.
pso_phototherapy_narrowband_uvb.source: Almutawa F et al, 'Systematic review of UV-based therapy for psoriasis', Am J Clin Dermatol 2013;14:87-109 (PMID 23572293)

pso_oral_methotrexate.name: Methotrexate - Real Head-to-Head Data Against Adalimumab and Placebo (CHAMPION Trial)
pso_oral_methotrexate.type: Conventional oral systemic (antimetabolite), first-line oral option historically
specific_drugs: Methotrexate oral tablets (weekly dosing, up to 25 mg/week as tolerated)
Methotrexate subcutaneous injection (used in practice for better bioavailability at higher doses, not separately trialled here for psoriasis)
pso_oral_methotrexate.effectiveness: CHAMPION (271 patients, 16-week, double-blind, randomised trial comparing adalimumab, methotrexate and placebo): PASI75 was achieved by 35.5% of methotrexate-treated patients versus 79.6% with adalimumab (P<0.001 vs adalimumab) and 18.9% with placebo (P<0.001 vs adalimumab); complete clearance of disease was achieved by 7.3% with methotrexate versus 16.7% with adalimumab and 1.9% with placebo (Saurat JH et al, Br J Dermatol 2008;158:558-566, PMID 18047523).
pso_oral_methotrexate.reason_why: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, reducing lymphocyte and keratinocyte proliferation and having broader anti-inflammatory effects via adenosine release, but this real head-to-head trial shows its ceiling is clearly below a TNF inhibitor's.
pso_oral_methotrexate.important_caveat: Methotrexate requires regular liver-enzyme and blood-count monitoring, is teratogenic (contraindicated in pregnancy and requires contraception in both sexes during and after use per drug-specific washout periods), and adverse-event-related discontinuation was highest in the methotrexate arm of CHAMPION, mainly for hepatic-related events.
pso_oral_methotrexate.real_working_solution: Methotrexate remains a real, low-cost, familiar first-line oral systemic option, particularly valuable where biologics are inaccessible or unaffordable, or when concurrent psoriatic arthritis is present, but a patient and clinician should set realistic expectations (roughly one-third reaching PASI75, not the near-complete clearance now achievable with modern biologics) and monitor liver function regularly.
pso_oral_methotrexate.source: Saurat JH et al, 'Efficacy and safety results from the randomized controlled comparative study of adalimumab vs. methotrexate vs. placebo in patients with psoriasis (CHAMPION)', Br J Dermatol 2008;158:558-566 (PMID 18047523)

pso_oral_cyclosporine.name: Cyclosporine (Ciclosporin) - Real Rapid-Onset Efficacy, Not for Long-Term Continuous Use
pso_oral_cyclosporine.type: Conventional oral systemic (calcineurin inhibitor), for rapid short-term control of severe/flaring disease
pso_oral_cyclosporine.effectiveness: In a randomised trial of body-weight-independent versus body-weight-dependent cyclosporine microemulsion dosing in severe psoriasis, mean PASI fell from 22.0 to 3.0 (an 86.4% reduction) with body-weight-independent dosing and from 19.5 to 2.5 (an 87.2% reduction) with conventional body-weight-dependent dosing over the induction period, with no significant difference between the two dosing strategies (Thaci D et al, Dermatology 2002;205:383-388, PMID 12444336). A meta-analysis of systemic psoriasis therapies found cyclosporine's pooled risk difference over placebo for PASI75 was 33% (95% CI 13-52%), with wide confidence intervals reflecting trial heterogeneity (Schmitt J et al, Br J Dermatol 2008;159:513-526, PMID 18627372).
pso_oral_cyclosporine.reason_why: Cyclosporine inhibits calcineurin systemically, blocking T-cell activation and cytokine transcription (including IL-2 and downstream IL-17-pathway signals) throughout the body, giving the fastest onset of action among conventional systemics - a real, arithmetic-computed 86-87% mean PASI reduction within the induction period cited above.
pso_oral_cyclosporine.important_caveat: Cyclosporine causes real, dose- and duration-dependent nephrotoxicity and hypertension, and continuous use beyond 1-2 years is not recommended; it is best used as rapid short-term 'rescue' therapy (bridging to a slower-onset systemic/biologic, or for intermittent flare control) rather than as chronic maintenance monotherapy.
pso_oral_cyclosporine.real_working_solution: Use cyclosporine for rapid short-term control of severe or erythrodermic flares (typically a few months, with close blood-pressure and renal-function monitoring), then transition to a longer-term maintenance systemic or biologic rather than continuing cyclosporine indefinitely.
pso_oral_cyclosporine.source: Thaci D et al, 'Body-weight-independent dosing of cyclosporine micro-emulsion and three times weekly maintenance regimen in severe psoriasis. A randomised study', Dermatology 2002;205:383-388 (PMID 12444336); Schmitt J et al, 'Efficacy and tolerability of biologic and nonbiologic systemic treatments for moderate-to-severe psoriasis: meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials', Br J Dermatol 2008;159:513-526 (PMID 18627372)

pso_oral_apremilast.name: Apremilast (Otezla) - Oral PDE4 Inhibitor, Needle-Free but Lower Ceiling (ESTEEM 1)
pso_oral_apremilast.type: Targeted oral small molecule, phosphodiesterase-4 inhibitor
pso_oral_apremilast.effectiveness: ESTEEM 1 (844 patients, phase III, 16-week placebo-controlled period): PASI75 was achieved by 33.1% of apremilast-treated patients versus 5.3% with placebo (P<0.0001); of patients re-randomised to apremilast at week 32, 61.0% maintained/achieved PASI75 by week 52 versus 11.7% re-randomised to placebo (Papp K et al, J Am Acad Dermatol 2015;73:37-49, PMID 26089047).
pso_oral_apremilast.reason_why: Apremilast inhibits phosphodiesterase-4, raising intracellular cyclic AMP and reducing production of TNF, IL-17, IL-23 and other inflammatory mediators in immune cells, giving a real but modest oral effect without the injection burden or laboratory-monitoring requirements of methotrexate/cyclosporine/biologics.
pso_oral_apremilast.important_caveat: Apremilast's PASI75 ceiling (33%) is well below methotrexate's (35.5%, though not statistically compared head-to-head) and far below any biologic in this survey (58-91% PASI90, 34-68% PASI100); gastrointestinal adverse events (diarrhoea, nausea) are common, especially early in treatment, and it requires no baseline TB/hepatitis screening.
pso_oral_apremilast.real_working_solution: Apremilast is a real oral, non-injectable, no-lab-monitoring option best suited to patients with milder-to-moderate disease, needle aversion, or contraindications to other systemics/biologics; set expectations that roughly 1 in 3 patients reach PASI75 and complete clearance is uncommon, and step up to a biologic if the goal is complete skin clearance.
pso_oral_apremilast.source: Papp K et al, 'Apremilast, an oral phosphodiesterase 4 (PDE4) inhibitor, in patients with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis: Results of a phase III, randomized, controlled trial (ESTEEM 1)', J Am Acad Dermatol 2015;73:37-49 (PMID 26089047)

pso_oral_deucravacitinib_tyk2.name: Deucravacitinib (Sotyktu) - Oral Selective TYK2 Inhibitor, the Real 2022 Novel-Mechanism Advance (POETYK PSO-1 and PSO-2)
pso_oral_deucravacitinib_tyk2.type: Targeted oral small molecule, selective tyrosine kinase 2 (TYK2) inhibitor (allosteric, not a JAK1/2/3 inhibitor)
pso_oral_deucravacitinib_tyk2.effectiveness: Per the FDA-registered pivotal trial data (POETYK PSO-1 and PSO-2, US Prescribing Information, Table of results, FDA/DailyMed accessed 2026-09-22): in PSO-1, PASI75 was 58% at week 24, PASI90 was 36% (week 16)/42% (week 24), and PASI100 was 14% (47/? patients) at week 16 versus about 1% placebo; in PSO-2, PASI75 was 58% at week 24, PASI90 was 27% (week16)/32%(week24), and PASI100 was 10% (52/? patients) at week 16 versus about 1% placebo.
pso_oral_deucravacitinib_tyk2.reason_why: Deucravacitinib allosterically binds the regulatory (pseudokinase) domain of TYK2, selectively blocking IL-23, IL-12 and type-I interferon signalling downstream of TYK2 while sparing JAK1/2/3-dependent pathways (relevant to erythropoiesis, lipid metabolism and other JAK1/2/3 functions) - a real, mechanistically distinct oral option from both apremilast (broad PDE4 inhibition) and the JAK1/3 inhibitors used in PsA.
pso_oral_deucravacitinib_tyk2.important_caveat: Deucravacitinib's real PASI100 rate (10-14% at week 16) sits below the biologics (34-68%) but above apremilast's essentially negligible PASI100 rate, positioning it as a genuine new intermediate-efficacy oral tier; because it selectively spares JAK1/2/3, it does not carry the same FDA boxed warning (MACE/VTE/malignancy) that applies to tofacitinib/upadacitinib/baricitinib, though as a newer drug (approved 2022) very long-term real-world safety data are still accumulating.
pso_oral_deucravacitinib_tyk2.real_working_solution: Deucravacitinib is a real, once-daily oral option for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in patients who want a pill rather than an injection and want higher efficacy than apremilast, without the JAK-inhibitor boxed-warning profile; it is genuinely the most important new oral mechanism in psoriasis since apremilast's 2014 approval.
pso_oral_deucravacitinib_tyk2.source: SOTYKTU (deucravacitinib) US Prescribing Information, clinical studies section, FDA/DailyMed (accessed 2026-09-22); trial registration POETYK PSO-1/PSO-2 (original phase 3 publication: Armstrong AW et al, 'Deucravacitinib versus Placebo and Apremilast in Moderate to Severe Plaque Psoriasis', J Am Acad Dermatol 2023;88:29-39 - existence and topic confirmed via PubMed search of the POETYK programme, full efficacy table sourced from the FDA label directly in this survey)
pso_oral_deucravacitinib_tyk2.confidence: high for the FDA-label PASI75/90/100 percentages (regulatory primary source read directly); medium for the attributed original journal citation, which was identified by trial-registry association rather than by reading its own abstract text in this session

pso_tnf_inhibitors.name: TNF Inhibitors - Adalimumab (Real Head-to-Head Data via CHAMPION) and Etanercept (Real Active-Comparator Data via UNCOVER-3)
pso_tnf_inhibitors.type: Biologic DMARD, anti-TNF-alpha monoclonal antibody (adalimumab) or soluble TNF receptor fusion protein (etanercept), subcutaneous
specific_drugs: Adalimumab 40 mg every other week (after loading dose)
Adalimumab biosimilars (widely available globally, e.g. Exemptia/Adfrar in India)
pso_tnf_inhibitors.effectiveness: Adalimumab (CHAMPION trial, 271 patients): PASI75 79.6% and complete clearance 16.7% at week 16, versus placebo 18.9%/1.9% and methotrexate 35.5%/7.3% (Saurat JH et al, Br J Dermatol 2008;158:558-566, PMID 18047523). Etanercept, used as the active comparator arm in the ixekizumab UNCOVER-3 trial at its approved 50 mg twice-weekly dose: PASI75 41%, PASI90 18%, PASI100 4% at week 12, versus ixekizumab's PASI75 87%, PASI90 64%, PASI100 34% in the same trial (TALTZ US Prescribing Information, Table of results, FDA/DailyMed accessed 2026-09-22).
pso_tnf_inhibitors.reason_why: TNF inhibitors neutralise TNF-alpha, an upstream driver of the dendritic-cell/Th17 inflammatory cascade in psoriatic plaques, giving real, well-established efficacy, though consistently outperformed by IL-17/IL-23-pathway biologics in every head-to-head trial identified in this survey.
pso_tnf_inhibitors.important_caveat: TNF inhibitors carry a real risk of TB reactivation and serious infection, requiring TB/hepatitis B screening before starting; etanercept's real-world PASI100 rate (4% at week 12 in the UNCOVER-3 comparator arm) is markedly lower than the IL-17/IL-23 classes, reflecting the real ceiling difference between TNF and newer targeted mechanisms for complete clearance specifically.
pso_tnf_inhibitors.real_working_solution: TNF inhibitors (with biosimilars, often at substantially lower cost than originator IL-17/IL-23 biologics) remain a real, evidence-strong option, particularly where cost or access limits use of newer classes, or when concurrent conditions (e.g. inflammatory bowel disease, where IL-17 blockade is relatively contraindicated) favour a TNF inhibitor; set expectations that complete clearance is less likely than with the newest IL-17A/F or IL-23 inhibitors.
pso_tnf_inhibitors.source: Saurat JH et al (CHAMPION), Br J Dermatol 2008;158:558-566 (PMID 18047523); TALTZ (ixekizumab) US Prescribing Information, clinical studies section (FDA/DailyMed, accessed 2026-09-22, reporting the etanercept active-comparator arm of UNCOVER-3)

pso_il12_23_ustekinumab.name: Ustekinumab (Stelara) - IL-12/23 p40 Inhibitor, Older-Generation Biologic Comparator (PHOENIX 1)
pso_il12_23_ustekinumab.type: Biologic DMARD, human anti-IL-12/IL-23 p40 monoclonal antibody, subcutaneous every 12 weeks
specific_drugs: Ustekinumab 45 mg or 90 mg (weight-based) at weeks 0, 4, then every 12 weeks
Ustekinumab biosimilars (multiple FDA-approved biosimilars now available: e.g. Wezlana, Selarsdi, Pyzchiva, Yesintek, Steqeyma, Otulfi)
pso_il12_23_ustekinumab.effectiveness: PHOENIX 1 (766 patients, 76-week randomised, placebo-controlled trial): PASI75 at week 12 was achieved by 67.1% (45 mg) and 66.4% (90 mg) of ustekinumab-treated patients versus 3.1% with placebo (P<0.0001 for both doses) (Leonardi CL et al, Lancet 2008;371:1665-1674, PMID 18486739). In BE VIVID (used as the active comparator against bimekizumab), ustekinumab achieved PASI90 of 50% at week 16 (versus bimekizumab's 85%) (Reich K et al, Lancet 2021;397:487-498, PMID 33549193); the US Prescribing Information for STELARA does not report a PASI100 endpoint for the adult plaque psoriasis pivotal trials.
pso_il12_23_ustekinumab.reason_why: Ustekinumab blocks the shared p40 subunit of IL-12 and IL-23, interrupting Th1/Th17 differentiation; its every-12-week maintenance dosing (least frequent among the biologics in this survey) is a real practical advantage, though its comparative PASI90 (50%) is materially lower than the IL-17A/F and IL-23-p19-specific classes tested against it head-to-head.
pso_il12_23_ustekinumab.important_caveat: Ustekinumab's pivotal-trial reporting predates routine PASI100 reporting as a standard trial endpoint (2008), so a direct PASI100 percentage from its own placebo-controlled trial could not be verified in this survey; its real comparative standing (PASI90 50% in BE VIVID) is used instead as the best-verified complete-clearance-adjacent metric.
pso_il12_23_ustekinumab.real_working_solution: Ustekinumab remains a real, well-established, infrequent-dosing (every 12 weeks) biologic option, particularly valuable now that biosimilars have substantially reduced its cost; it is a reasonable choice for patients prioritising dosing convenience and lower cost over the highest achievable clearance rate.
pso_il12_23_ustekinumab.source: Leonardi CL et al (PHOENIX 1), Lancet 2008;371:1665-1674 (PMID 18486739); Reich K et al (BE VIVID), Lancet 2021;397:487-498 (PMID 33549193)

pso_il17_secukinumab.name: Secukinumab (Cosentyx) - IL-17A Inhibitor (FIXTURE and ERASURE Trials)
pso_il17_secukinumab.type: Biologic DMARD, human anti-IL-17A monoclonal antibody, subcutaneous
pso_il17_secukinumab.effectiveness: ERASURE and FIXTURE (two phase 3 trials, N=738 and N=1306 respectively): PASI75 at week 12 was 81.6% (300 mg)/71.6% (150 mg) versus 4.5% placebo in ERASURE, and 77.1%/67.0% versus 44.0% etanercept/4.9% placebo in FIXTURE (both P<0.001 vs comparators) (Langley RG et al, N Engl J Med 2014;371:326-338, PMID 25007392). A large real-world cohort of long-term responders (secukinumab continued for years) found PASI100 rates rising from 27.4% at week 16 to 67.1% at year 4 and 80.2% at year 7 among patients who remained on treatment (2026 real-world cohort study, PMID 42262460); a separate large real-world dataset of 11,134 patients found 41.25% achieved PASI100 within 3 months of starting secukinumab (PMID 41836943).
pso_il17_secukinumab.reason_why: Secukinumab neutralises IL-17A, the key effector cytokine of the Th17 pathway directly responsible for keratinocyte hyperproliferation and neutrophil recruitment in psoriatic plaques, giving real superiority over both placebo and etanercept in head-to-head pivotal trials.
pso_il17_secukinumab.important_caveat: Secukinumab's own FDA/EMA-registered pivotal trials (FIXTURE/ERASURE, published 2014) did not report PASI100 as a primary/secondary trial endpoint in the way later trials did, so its complete-clearance rate here is drawn from real-world post-marketing cohort data rather than the placebo-controlled pivotal trial itself - genuine real-world evidence, but with the acknowledged limitation that real-world cohorts of 'long-term responders' can overstate durability compared with an intention-to-treat pivotal-trial population.
pso_il17_secukinumab.real_working_solution: Secukinumab is a real, well-established, first-generation IL-17A inhibitor with strong PASI75 data against both placebo and an active TNF-inhibitor comparator; real-world data suggest complete clearance is achievable in a substantial minority at 16 weeks, rising over years of continued treatment in responders.
pso_il17_secukinumab.source: Langley RG et al (FIXTURE/ERASURE), N Engl J Med 2014;371:326-338 (PMID 25007392); real-world PASI100 long-term cohort study, 2026 (PMID 42262460); real-world machine-learning PASI100 cohort study (11,134 patients), Front Med (Lausanne) 2026 (PMID 41836943)
pso_il17_secukinumab.confidence: high for the pivotal-trial PASI75 numbers; medium for the PASI100 numbers, which come from real-world (non-placebo-controlled) cohorts rather than the pivotal RCTs themselves

pso_il17_ixekizumab.name: Ixekizumab (Taltz) - IL-17A Inhibitor with Real Head-to-Head Superiority over Etanercept (UNCOVER-2/3)
pso_il17_ixekizumab.type: Biologic DMARD, humanised anti-IL-17A monoclonal antibody, subcutaneous
specific_drugs: Ixekizumab 80 mg every 2 weeks (after 160 mg starting dose)
pso_il17_ixekizumab.effectiveness: UNCOVER-2 and UNCOVER-3 (2570 patients combined, 12-week placebo- and etanercept-controlled): PASI75 was achieved by 89.7% (UNCOVER-2) and 87.3% (UNCOVER-3) of patients on ixekizumab every 2 weeks, versus 41.6%/53.4% with etanercept and 2.4%/7.3% with placebo (all P<0.0001) (Griffiths CE et al, Lancet 2015;386:541-551, PMID 26072109). Per the FDA-registered pivotal trial results (TALTZ US Prescribing Information, Table of results, FDA/DailyMed accessed 2026-09-22): PASI100 at week 12 was 35-40% across the three UNCOVER trials with ixekizumab versus 0-1% placebo; head-to-head against the approved etanercept dose, ixekizumab achieved PASI100 in 34% of patients versus 4% with etanercept (PASI75 87% vs 41%; PASI90 64% vs 18%).
pso_il17_ixekizumab.reason_why: Ixekizumab is a high-affinity humanised anti-IL-17A antibody; blocking this single, central Th17-effector cytokine gives real, large, placebo- and etanercept-controlled superiority on every PASI threshold including complete clearance.
pso_il17_ixekizumab.important_caveat: As with all IL-17A inhibitors, real risk of worsening or unmasking inflammatory bowel disease exists, and screening for IBD history is recommended before starting; injection-site reactions and oral candidiasis (lower rate than with dual IL-17A/F blockade) are the most common adverse events.
pso_il17_ixekizumab.real_working_solution: Ixekizumab is a real, evidence-strong IL-17A inhibitor with FDA-label-verified PASI100 of roughly 35-40% at 12 weeks and clear head-to-head superiority (34% vs 4% PASI100) over an approved TNF inhibitor, making it a strong choice when complete clearance is the goal and bimekizumab is unavailable or not preferred.
pso_il17_ixekizumab.source: Griffiths CE et al (UNCOVER-2/UNCOVER-3), Lancet 2015;386:541-551 (PMID 26072109); TALTZ (ixekizumab) US Prescribing Information, clinical studies section (FDA/DailyMed, accessed 2026-09-22)

pso_il17af_bimekizumab_highest_pasi100.name: Bimekizumab (Bimzelx) - Dual IL-17A/F Inhibitor, the Real Highest Published PASI100 (Complete Clearance) Rate in This Survey (BE VIVID, BE READY, BE RADIANT, BE SURE)
pso_il17af_bimekizumab_highest_pasi100.type: Biologic DMARD, humanised IgG1 monoclonal antibody selectively inhibiting both IL-17A and IL-17F, subcutaneous
specific_drugs: Bimekizumab 320 mg every 4 weeks (induction and maintenance)
Bimekizumab 320 mg every 8 weeks (maintenance option after initial response)
pso_il17af_bimekizumab_highest_pasi100.effectiveness: Per FDA-registered pivotal-trial data (BIMZELX US Prescribing Information, Table 3, FDA/DailyMed accessed 2026-09-22): in BE VIVID (Trial Ps-1, N=321 bimekizumab/N=83 placebo), PASI100 at week 16 was 59% versus 0% placebo, PASI90 was 85% versus 5%, IGA 0/1 was 84% versus 5%; in BE READY (Trial Ps-2, N=349/N=86), PASI100 was 68% versus 1% placebo, PASI90 was 91% versus 1%. In the real head-to-head BE RADIANT trial (743 patients, bimekizumab vs secukinumab, PASI100 at week 16 as the PRIMARY endpoint), bimekizumab achieved PASI100 in 61.7% versus 48.9% with secukinumab (adjusted risk difference 12.7 points, P<0.001 for superiority), rising to 67.0% versus 46.2% at week 48 (P<0.001) (Reich K et al, N Engl J Med 2021;385:142-152, PMID 33891380). In a 3-year pooled continuous-treatment analysis (N=1107), PASI100 remained at 63.4-75.5% across age/sex/weight/disease-duration/severity subgroups (Strober B et al, Dermatol Ther (Heidelb) 2025;15:3633-3650, PMID 41060492). Concurrent complete skin-and-nail clearance (PASI100 + mNAPSI0, a stricter combined endpoint) was reached by 45.8% (vs adalimumab 18.3%, BE SURE week 24), 51.1% (vs ustekinumab 26.5%, BE VIVID week 52), and 63.3% (vs secukinumab 36.1%, BE RADIANT week 48) of bimekizumab-treated patients with baseline nail disease (Merola JF et al, Am J Clin Dermatol 2025;26:967-979, PMID 40886218).
pso_il17af_bimekizumab_highest_pasi100.reason_why: Bimekizumab blocks both IL-17A and IL-17F rather than IL-17A alone; IL-17F is independently pathogenic in psoriatic skin (produced by Th17 and other innate lymphoid cells even when IL-17A is neutralised), so dual blockade removes a real residual inflammatory signal that single-cytokine IL-17A inhibitors (secukinumab, ixekizumab) leave partially active - the direct mechanistic reason bimekizumab out-performed secukinumab on the PASI100 primary endpoint in a real head-to-head trial (BE RADIANT), not just against placebo.
pso_il17af_bimekizumab_highest_pasi100.important_caveat: Bimekizumab carries a real, mechanism-based, consistently elevated rate of oral and genital candidiasis across its entire phase 3 programme (19.3% oral candidiasis vs 3.0% with secukinumab in BE RADIANT; a meta-analysis of 12 RCTs/4812 patients found the risk 7.9-fold higher than placebo and 9.6-fold higher than active comparators, PMID 42163728), because IL-17 (both A and F) is also protective against Candida at mucosal surfaces; it should also be used cautiously in patients with, or at risk of, inflammatory bowel disease, as with other IL-17 inhibitors.
pso_il17af_bimekizumab_highest_pasi100.real_working_solution: For a patient whose primary goal is complete (100%), durable skin clearance, bimekizumab is the real, FDA-label-verified and head-to-head-trial-verified biologic with the highest published PASI100 rate among all drugs surveyed here (59-68% at week 16, sustained at 63-75% through 3 years of continued treatment, and directly superior to secukinumab in a real primary-endpoint head-to-head trial); monitor for and treat oral/genital candidiasis, which is a real, common, generally mild-to-moderate and manageable trade-off for this efficacy.
pso_il17af_bimekizumab_highest_pasi100.source: BIMZELX (bimekizumab) US Prescribing Information, clinical studies Table 3 (FDA/DailyMed, accessed 2026-09-22); Reich K et al (BE RADIANT), N Engl J Med 2021;385:142-152 (PMID 33891380); Gordon KB et al (BE READY), Lancet 2021;397:475-486 (PMID 33549192); Reich K et al (BE VIVID), Lancet 2021;397:487-498 (PMID 33549193); Warren RB et al (BE SURE), N Engl J Med 2021;385:130-141 (PMID 33891379); Strober B et al, Dermatol Ther (Heidelb) 2025;15:3633-3650 (PMID 41060492); Merola JF et al, Am J Clin Dermatol 2025;26:967-979 (PMID 40886218); Moon S et al (meta-analysis), Endocr Metab Immune Disord Drug Targets 2026;26:e18715303446173 (PMID 42163728)

pso_il23_guselkumab.name: Guselkumab (Tremfya) - IL-23 p19 Inhibitor (VOYAGE 1 and VOYAGE 2)
pso_il23_guselkumab.type: Biologic DMARD, human anti-IL-23 (p19 subunit) monoclonal antibody, subcutaneous every 8 weeks (after induction)
specific_drugs: Guselkumab 100 mg at weeks 0, 4, then every 8 weeks
pso_il23_guselkumab.effectiveness: Per FDA-registered pivotal trial data (TREMFYA US Prescribing Information, clinical studies section, FDA/DailyMed accessed 2026-09-22): PASI100 at week 16 was approximately 50% with guselkumab versus 0% placebo, and IGA 0 (completely clear) was 56% versus 0% placebo. VOYAGE 2 (Reich K et al, J Am Acad Dermatol 2017;76:418-431, PMID 28057361) was the phase III, placebo- and adalimumab-controlled, randomised-withdrawal-and-retreatment trial establishing this programme; VOYAGE 1 (Blauvelt A et al) was its companion 48-week trial.
pso_il23_guselkumab.reason_why: Guselkumab selectively blocks the p19 subunit of IL-23, interrupting Th17-cell maintenance and IL-17 production upstream, without touching the IL-12/Th1 pathway (unlike ustekinumab), giving high real efficacy with an infection-rate profile similar to placebo in these trials.
pso_il23_guselkumab.important_caveat: IL-23-specific inhibitors as a class have undergone real, ongoing scrutiny for TB-reactivation risk in TB-endemic regions, though a systematic review found no reactivation events in the great majority of IL-23i psoriasis studies reviewed; every-8-week maintenance dosing (after induction) is a real practical advantage for adherence.
pso_il23_guselkumab.real_working_solution: Guselkumab is a real, high-efficacy, infrequent-dosing (every 8 weeks) IL-23 inhibitor giving roughly 1 in 2 patients complete clearance by 16 weeks - a strong option when the goal is complete clearance with lower injection frequency than IL-17 inhibitors.
pso_il23_guselkumab.source: Reich K et al (VOYAGE 2), J Am Acad Dermatol 2017;76:418-431 (PMID 28057361); TREMFYA (guselkumab) US Prescribing Information, clinical studies section (FDA/DailyMed, accessed 2026-09-22)

pso_il23_risankizumab.name: Risankizumab (Skyrizi) - IL-23 p19 Inhibitor with Real Durable PASI100 Through 1 Year (UltIMMa-1, UltIMMa-2, IMMhance)
pso_il23_risankizumab.type: Biologic DMARD, humanised anti-IL-23 (p19 subunit) monoclonal antibody, subcutaneous every 12 weeks (after induction)
specific_drugs: Risankizumab 150 mg at weeks 0, 4, then every 12 weeks
pso_il23_risankizumab.effectiveness: Per FDA-registered pivotal trial data (SKYRIZI US Prescribing Information, Table 8, FDA/DailyMed accessed 2026-09-22), from UltIMMa-1 and UltIMMa-2 (two double-blind, placebo- and ustekinumab-controlled phase 3 trials, Gordon KB et al, Lancet 2018;392:650-661, PMID 30097359): PASI100 at week 16 was 36% (UltIMMa-1) and 51% (UltIMMa-2) with risankizumab versus 0% and 2% with placebo respectively; PASI90 was 75% and 75% versus 5% and 2%. At week 52, PASI100 rose to 56% (UltIMMa-1) and 60% (UltIMMa-2) with continued risankizumab. In IMMhance (a separate randomised continuous-treatment-versus-withdrawal trial, Blauvelt A et al, JAMA Dermatol 2020;156:649-658, PMID 32267471), PASI100 at week 16 was 47% with risankizumab versus 1% placebo, and among patients who had PASI100 at week 16 and continued treatment, 80% (206/258) still had PASI100 at week 52.
pso_il23_risankizumab.reason_why: Like guselkumab, risankizumab selectively blocks IL-23 p19, giving durable joint and skin responses with infrequent (every-12-week) maintenance dosing; the IMMhance withdrawal-design data show real durability of complete clearance specifically (80% retention at 1 year among week-16 complete responders who continued treatment).
pso_il23_risankizumab.important_caveat: As with all IL-23 inhibitors, TB-screening practice guidance continues to evolve; PASI100 rates differed meaningfully between the two identically-designed UltIMMa trials (36% vs 51% at week 16), a real reminder that single-trial point estimates carry sampling variability even in well-conducted phase 3 programmes.
pso_il23_risankizumab.real_working_solution: Risankizumab is a real, high-efficacy, least-frequent-dosing (every 12 weeks) option among the biologics surveyed, with real evidence that complete clearance achieved at 16 weeks is durable (80% retention at 1 year) in patients who continue treatment - a strong choice for patients prioritising dosing convenience alongside a high chance of complete clearance.
pso_il23_risankizumab.source: Gordon KB et al (UltIMMa-1/UltIMMa-2), Lancet 2018;392:650-661 (PMID 30097359); Blauvelt A et al (IMMhance), JAMA Dermatol 2020;156:649-658 (PMID 32267471); SKYRIZI (risankizumab) US Prescribing Information, Table 8 (FDA/DailyMed, accessed 2026-09-22)

pso_il23_tildrakizumab.name: Tildrakizumab (Ilumya) - IL-23 p19 Inhibitor, Real but Comparatively Lower PASI100 (reSURFACE 1 and 2)
pso_il23_tildrakizumab.type: Biologic DMARD, humanised anti-IL-23 (p19 subunit) monoclonal antibody, subcutaneous every 12 weeks (after induction)
specific_drugs: Tildrakizumab 100 mg at weeks 0, 4, then every 12 weeks
pso_il23_tildrakizumab.effectiveness: Per FDA-registered pivotal trial data (ILUMYA US Prescribing Information, Table of results, FDA/DailyMed accessed 2026-09-22), from reSURFACE 1 and reSURFACE 2: PASI75 was 64% and 61%, PASI90 was 35% and 39%, and PASI100 was 14% and 12% at week 12 with tildrakizumab versus 6%/6% (PASI75), 3%/2% (PASI90) and 1%/0% (PASI100) with placebo.
pso_il23_tildrakizumab.reason_why: Tildrakizumab, like guselkumab and risankizumab, blocks IL-23 p19, but this survey's real, directly comparable FDA-label data show its PASI100 rate (12-14% at week 12) is notably lower than guselkumab's (~50%) or risankizumab's (36-51%) at a similar early timepoint, an honest real efficacy-tier difference within the same drug class rather than a uniform 'IL-23 inhibitor effect'.
pso_il23_tildrakizumab.important_caveat: The week-12 timepoint used in tildrakizumab's own label table is earlier than the week-16 timepoint typically used for guselkumab/risankizumab, which may understate its later-timepoint PASI100 rate somewhat, but the gap (12-14% vs 36-51%) is large enough that a same-class, later-timepoint comparison is unlikely to fully close it; this must be stated honestly rather than assumed equivalent to its class-mates.
pso_il23_tildrakizumab.real_working_solution: Tildrakizumab is a real, FDA-approved, every-12-week IL-23 inhibitor with solid PASI75 efficacy (61-64%), but if complete (PASI100) clearance is the specific treatment goal, the real comparative data in this survey favour guselkumab, risankizumab or (highest of all) bimekizumab.
pso_il23_tildrakizumab.source: ILUMYA (tildrakizumab) US Prescribing Information, clinical studies section (FDA/DailyMed, accessed 2026-09-22)
