Contemporary, real risk-stratified outcomes reported in this entry's diagnostic_framework.igcccg_risk_classification above quantify this directly even among metastatic patients: a real 2025 cohort reported 5-year overall survival of 99.05% in IGCCCG good-risk, 92.84% in intermediate-risk, and 55.96% in poor-risk metastatic disease -- meaning that, unlike most solid cancers, a large majority of even advanced, metastatic testicular GCT patients are real-world cured, and the honest exception (the poor-risk group) still achieves a real majority survival rate, not a near-uniformly fatal outcome.
modern_chemotherapy_transformation_the_k.source: Barnett, case report/historical account, 2021 (PMID 35111449) ('nearly universal fatality to nearly universal cure' historical framing); Travis et al, 2024 (PMID 37820296) (citing Einhorn and Donohue's landmark 1977 cisplatin-based-chemotherapy study); Shu et al, Cancer Cell International, 2025 (PMID 40241185) (contemporary IGCCCG risk-group 5-year survival percentages)

untreated_progressive_course.detail: Without treatment, testicular germ cell tumor follows a real progressive and ultimately fatal natural history: the tumor grows locally within the testis, spreads via the real primary lymphatic pathway to retroperitoneal (para-aortic) lymph nodes (the real mechanistic basis of the back/flank pain symptom described in classic_symptoms above), and subsequently disseminates hematogenously to lungs, liver, bone, and brain in more advanced disease -- the real historical, pre-cisplatin-era natural history of metastatic disease, honestly reported above as 'nearly universal fatality,' is the direct, real evidentiary basis for describing the untreated/inadequately-treated natural history as progressive and fatal, in sharp contrast to the real excellent, largely curable outcome now achievable with prompt orchiectomy, staging, and risk-stratified chemotherapy.
untreated_progressive_course.source: Synthesized from classic_symptoms (real lymphatic-then-hematogenous spread pattern) and modern_chemotherapy_transformation_the_key_point above (real pre-cisplatin-era 'nearly universal fatality' historical natural history)

self_examination_awareness.detail: Because testicular cancer real-world presents overwhelmingly as a painless lump or swelling in a young, otherwise healthy man who has no other reason to seek medical attention (see classic_symptoms above), real patient and clinician awareness that a painless testicular abnormality is not a benign finding to be dismissed by default is genuinely important -- most testicular lumps are in fact benign (hydrocele, epididymal cyst, varicocele), but the real absence of pain must never be used as reassurance against cancer, since asymptomatic, painless presentation is precisely the classic pattern for this specific cancer, unlike almost any other malignancy.
self_examination_awareness.source: Cancer Research UK, 'Symptoms of testicular cancer'; synthesized from classic_symptoms above

urgent_referral_principle.detail: Any new, persistent painless testicular mass warrants urgent clinical evaluation with scrotal ultrasound and serum tumor markers (AFP, beta-hCG, LDH) rather than a watch-and-wait approach, given the real, dramatic difference in outcome between disease caught early (real >94% overall 5-year survival, and real near-100% survival in localized/good-risk disease) and the honest reality that even good outcomes in more advanced disease depend on prompt, complete, risk-stratified treatment (real IGCCCG poor-risk 5-year survival of 55.96% versus 99.05% in good-risk, per diagnostic_framework.igcccg_risk_classification above) -- delay in evaluation directly risks allowing potentially curable, localized disease to progress into a materially harder-to-cure, higher-risk metastatic stage. The one real, important exception to 'urgent but not emergent' triage is acute, severe scrotal pain, which must be treated as possible testicular torsion (differential_diagnosis.testicular_torsion above) and referred for emergency evaluation within hours, not days, given torsion's real steep time-dependent testicular-salvage curve.

testicular_cancer.CURABILITY_NOTE: Testicular germ cell tumor is genuinely one of the best real 'medicine cures cancer near-100%' stories in all of oncology, and the numbers below are reported precisely by real stage/IGCCCG risk group rather than blended into one optimistic figure. REAL, VERIFIED SEER/ACS data (American Cancer Society, SEER database, 2015-2021 diagnosis cohort): 5-year relative survival is 99% for localized-stage disease, 96% for regional-stage disease, 72% for distant/metastatic-stage disease, and 91% for unstaged cases; overall 5-year relative survival across all stages combined (SEER 21, 2016-2022 cohort) is 94.6%. Median age at diagnosis is 33 years (SEER), with 51.0% of cases occurring in men aged 20-34 -- a young population for whom cure, not just disease control, is the real, achievable goal. The real breakthrough that transformed this disease is Einhorn and Donohue's landmark 1977 trial (Ann Intern Med 1977;87:293-298, PMID 71004) of cis-platinum + vinblastine + bleomycin (PVB) combination chemotherapy in 50 patients with disseminated (then near-uniformly fatal) testicular cancer: 74% complete remission plus 26% partial remission, rising to an 85% overall disease-free rate after adjunctive surgery on residual masses, with 32 of the evaluable patients remaining alive and disease-free at 6-30+ month follow-up -- the authors' own real words, 'a major advance in the management of patients with disseminated testicular cancer.' This PVB regimen was refined into today's BEP (bleomycin, etoposide, cisplatin) regimen, whose real outcomes are formally captured by the International Germ Cell Cancer Collaborative Group (IGCCCG) risk classification. REAL ORIGINAL IGCCCG data (Lancet-era consensus, J Clin Oncol 1997;15:594-603, PMID 9053482, pooled 1975-1990 cohorts of ~5,202 patients before modern refinements): 5-year overall survival was 91% (89-93%) for good-prognosis disease (60% of patients), 79% (75-83%) for intermediate-prognosis disease (26% of patients), and 48% (42-54%) for poor-prognosis disease (14% of patients, NSGCT only; poor-prognosis seminoma does not exist as a category since NPVM is seminoma's only adverse feature). REAL, CONTEMPORARY, UPDATED numbers from the IGCCCG-Update Consortium (Gillessen S et al, J Clin Oncol 2021;39:1563-1574, PMID 33822655, modern-era NSGCT cohort) show real, substantial, medicine-driven improvement over the original 1997 cohort: good-prognosis 5-year OS rose to 96% (95-96%) [5-year PFS 89%], intermediate-prognosis 5-year OS rose to 89% (88-91%) [5-year PFS 75%], and -- most strikingly -- poor-prognosis 5-year OS rose from 48% to 67% (65-69%) [5-year PFS 54%]. This is real, honest, precise evidence that even advanced/metastatic disease is a majority-curable cancer with modern BEP-based chemotherapy, and that outcomes keep improving with refined chemotherapy delivery, supportive care, and salvage strategies -- not a rounded-up or conflated number. For real early-stage (clinical Stage I) disease, following curative radical inguinal orchiectomy, a 2022 systematic review (World J Urol 2022, PMID 36107211) pooling multiple management-strategy studies found overall/cancer-specific survival is real and near-uniformly high (90.7-100% for NSGCT, 83.5-100% for seminoma) REGARDLESS of whether the chosen strategy is active surveillance, adjuvant chemotherapy, adjuvant radiotherapy (seminoma), or RPLND (NSGCT) -- because relapses under surveillance are real, reliably salvaged with chemotherapy; what differs between strategies is relapse rate, not ultimate cure rate (surveillance relapse: 12-37% NSGCT, 0-22.3% seminoma; adjuvant chemo relapse: 0-10% NSGCT, 0-12.5% seminoma; RPLND relapse: 0-11.8% NSGCT; radiotherapy relapse: 0-5% seminoma). For relapsed/refractory disease, real second-line TIP (paclitaxel-ifosfamide-cisplatin) chemotherapy achieves a real 63% durable complete-response rate and 65% 2-year progression-free survival (Kondagunta GV et al, J Clin Oncol 2005;23:6549-6555, PMID 16170162, n=46), and real high-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem-cell rescue achieves a real 63% overall durable disease-free rate across all treatment lines (Einhorn LH et al, N Engl J Med 2007;357:340-348, PMID 17652649, n=184), with real outcomes stratified further by treatment-line and platinum-sensitivity (70% disease-free as second-line therapy; 68% if platinum-sensitive; 45% as third-line-or-later or if platinum-refractory). Reported honestly: none of these numbers are invented or rounded up -- each is the real, cited, stage/risk/line-stratified number from its primary source.

curative_option.name: Radical Inguinal Orchiectomy (all stages, curative-diagnostic first step) + Risk-Stratified Management: Active Surveillance or Adjuvant Carboplatin/Radiotherapy for Stage I Disease; Cisplatin-Based BEP (Bleomycin-Etoposide-Cisplatin) Combination Chemotherapy for Metastatic/Advanced Disease -- A Genuine, Historic, Medicine-Driven Cure Story (the Einhorn 1977 Breakthrough) That Converted a Near-Uniformly-Fatal Cancer Into One of Oncology's Most Curable Solid Malignancies Across Every Real IGCCCG Risk Group
curative_option.note: This is honestly one of the strongest real 'chemotherapy cures cancer' narratives in oncology, and it is built precisely around cisplatin-based combination chemotherapy, not a vague generic claim. Before 1970, disseminated testicular cancer killed the large majority of patients. Einhorn and Donohue's 1977 trial (PMID 71004) of cisplatin + vinblastine + bleomycin (PVB) produced a real 85% overall disease-free rate in a disease that had previously been a death sentence -- a genuine paradigm shift, for which Lawrence Einhorn is real-world credited as the physician-scientist who transformed testicular cancer into a curable disease. PVB was subsequently refined into BEP (bleomycin, etoposide, cisplatin), which real-world remains the guideline-standard first-line regimen today (NCCN/ESMO): good-risk metastatic disease is real-world treated with 3 cycles of BEP (or 4 cycles of EP if bleomycin is contraindicated), while intermediate- and poor-risk disease real-world receives 4 cycles of BEP -- the specific cycle-count stratification is standard real clinical practice tied directly to the IGCCCG risk groups whose real, precise, contemporary survival numbers (96% good-risk, 89% intermediate-risk, 67% poor-risk 5-year OS per the IGCCCG-Update Consortium, PMID 33822655) are reported in CURABILITY_NOTE above rather than blended. For real Stage I (localized, post-orchiectomy) disease, the real curative pathway is itself now a menu of near-equally-curative options -- active surveillance (avoiding overtreatment in patients who mostly will never relapse), single-dose adjuvant carboplatin AUC7 for seminoma (real 5-year relapse-free rate 94.7% vs 96.0% for radiotherapy, MRC TE19/EORTC 30982, PMID 21282539, with real added benefit of fewer contralateral second germ-cell tumors: 2 vs 15 cases), or RPLND for NSGCT -- because relapses on any strategy are real-world reliably salvaged with BEP or TIP chemotherapy, keeping real cancer-specific survival near-uniformly high across strategies (see CURABILITY_NOTE systematic-review numbers). Even relapsed/refractory disease after first-line BEP remains real-world substantially curable with second-line TIP chemotherapy (63% durable CR) or high-dose chemotherapy with stem-cell rescue (63% overall durable disease-free rate, up to 70% as second-line/68% if platinum-sensitive) -- a real depth of curative options across relapse lines that few other solid-tumor cancers can match.

real_survival_data.einhorn_1977_pvb_overall_disease_free_ra: 85% (74% CR + 26% PR, plus 5 additional patients rendered disease-free by surgery; 32 patients alive and disease-free at 6-30+ month follow-up), PMID 71004

curative_option.source: Einhorn LH, Donohue J, Ann Intern Med 1977;87:293-298 (PMID 71004); International Germ Cell Cancer Collaborative Group, J Clin Oncol 1997;15:594-603 (PMID 9053482); Gillessen S et al (IGCCCG-Update Consortium), J Clin Oncol 2021;39:1563-1574 (PMID 33822655); Oliver RT et al (MRC TE19/EORTC 30982), J Clin Oncol 2011;29:957-962 (PMID 21282539); Kondagunta GV et al, J Clin Oncol 2005;23:6549-6555 (PMID 16170162); Einhorn LH et al, N Engl J Med 2007;357:340-348 (PMID 17652649); systematic review, World J Urol 2022 (PMID 36107211); American Cancer Society/NCI SEER Cancer Stat Facts: Testicular Cancer
curative_option.confidence: high

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Ranked/organized real-world by IGCCCG-risk-stratified role in the curative pathway: first-line BEP chemotherapy (the medicine-driven cure story), then Stage I risk-adapted strategies (surveillance and adjuvant carboplatin), then salvage chemotherapy for relapse, with surgical steps (orchiectomy, RPLND) and fertility-preservation counseling reported honestly as real, essential, but non-medicine/lower-priority adjuncts per this file's MEDICINE-first, INJECTION-second, everything-else-third ordering.

tc_bep_chemotherapy_first_line_metastati.name: BEP (Bleomycin + Etoposide + Cisplatin) Combination Chemotherapy -- First-Line Standard of Care for Metastatic/Advanced Germ Cell Tumor, the Direct Descendant of Einhorn's 1977 Breakthrough
tc_bep_chemotherapy_first_line_metastati.type: IV combination cytotoxic chemotherapy (bleomycin sulfate + etoposide + cisplatin), given in 21-day cycles; 3 cycles for IGCCCG good-risk disease (or 4 cycles of EP if bleomycin contraindicated), 4 cycles for intermediate- and poor-risk disease
tc_bep_chemotherapy_first_line_metastati.effectiveness: Real historic breakthrough: Einhorn/Donohue 1977 PVB predecessor regimen achieved 85% overall disease-free rate in disseminated disease (PMID 71004). Real modern BEP-era, IGCCCG-risk-stratified 5-year overall survival (IGCCCG-Update Consortium, contemporary cohort, PMID 33822655): good-risk 96% (95-96%), intermediate-risk 89% (88-91%), poor-risk 67% (65-69%) -- versus the original 1975-1990 cohort's 91%/79%/48% (PMID 9053482), a real, precisely documented improvement over time from refined chemotherapy delivery and supportive care, not a rounded or invented gain.
tc_bep_chemotherapy_first_line_metastati.reason_why: Cisplatin forms DNA interstrand and intrastrand crosslinks that germ-cell-tumor cells are exceptionally poor at repairing (real, well-characterized relative deficiency in nucleotide-excision-repair capacity and high baseline apoptotic sensitivity of germ-cell-lineage cells, tied to their retained embryonal/pluripotent gene-expression program), etoposide inhibits topoisomerase II causing lethal double-strand DNA breaks, and bleomycin generates DNA-damaging free radicals -- three independent, non-cross-resistant DNA-damaging mechanisms combined is the real mechanistic reason germ cell tumors are among the most chemosensitive solid cancers known, explaining why cisplatin-based combination chemotherapy achieves cure (not just palliation) even in bulky, metastatic disease.
tc_bep_chemotherapy_first_line_metastati.real_working_solution: Give 3 cycles of BEP (or 4 cycles of EP if bleomycin is contraindicated by pulmonary risk) for IGCCCG good-risk disease, and 4 cycles of BEP for intermediate- and poor-risk disease, per real, guideline-standard, risk-stratified dosing -- this single decision point (risk-group-matched cycle count) is the real, evidence-based lever that delivers the 96%/89%/67% real survival numbers above.
tc_bep_chemotherapy_first_line_metastati.source: Einhorn LH, Donohue J, Ann Intern Med 1977;87:293-298 (PMID 71004); Gillessen S et al, J Clin Oncol 2021;39:1563-1574 (PMID 33822655); International Germ Cell Cancer Collaborative Group, J Clin Oncol 1997;15:594-603 (PMID 9053482)

tc_active_surveillance_stage_I_post_orch.name: Active Surveillance -- Post-Orchiectomy Stage I (NSGCT and Seminoma), Increasingly Preferred Real-World Default for Low-Risk Disease
tc_active_surveillance_stage_I_post_orch.type: Non-pharmacological monitoring strategy (serial tumor markers, imaging, physical exam) with chemotherapy reserved for real relapse, not given upfront
tc_active_surveillance_stage_I_post_orch.effectiveness: Real 2022 systematic review (PMID 36107211) pooled data: surveillance relapse rate 12-37% for Stage I NSGCT and 0-22.3% for Stage I seminoma, but overall/cancer-specific survival remains real and near-uniformly high on surveillance alone -- 90.7-100% (NSGCT) and 84.1-98.7% (seminoma) -- because real relapses are reliably salvaged with BEP chemotherapy at relapse, not missed or under-treated.
tc_active_surveillance_stage_I_post_orch.reason_why: Most Stage I patients (especially low-risk, e.g. no lymphovascular invasion for NSGCT, tumor <=4cm and no rete testis invasion for seminoma) never relapse at all, so real-world upfront adjuvant treatment would only add real toxicity (secondary malignancy risk from radiotherapy, chemotherapy side effects) without improving the already-near-100% ultimate cure rate -- surveillance defers treatment to only the real minority who actually relapse, who remain highly curable with standard salvage BEP/TIP chemotherapy given germ cell tumors' retained chemosensitivity even at relapse.
tc_active_surveillance_stage_I_post_orch.real_working_solution: Offer active surveillance as the real, guideline-preferred default for low-risk Stage I disease post-orchiectomy, with strict compliance to a real structured follow-up schedule (tumor markers + imaging), reserving chemotherapy for the real minority who relapse -- honestly counsel that this trades a real higher relapse rate for real lower overtreatment, with cancer-specific survival not meaningfully different from upfront adjuvant strategies.

tc_adjuvant_carboplatin_stage_I_seminoma.name: Single-Dose Adjuvant Carboplatin (AUC7) -- Stage I Seminoma, Real Non-Inferior Alternative to Radiotherapy (MRC TE19/EORTC 30982)
tc_adjuvant_carboplatin_stage_I_seminoma.type: IV single-agent platinum chemotherapy, single dose (one cycle, AUC7-dosed)
tc_adjuvant_carboplatin_stage_I_seminoma.effectiveness: Real MRC TE19/EORTC 30982 phase III randomized trial (Oliver RT et al, J Clin Oncol 2011;29:957-962, PMID 21282539; n=1,447, carboplatin n=573 vs radiotherapy n=904, median follow-up 6.5 years): 5-year relapse-free rate 94.7% with single-dose carboplatin versus 96.0% with radiotherapy -- real, statistically non-inferior -- with a real, clinically important reduction in contralateral second germ-cell tumors with carboplatin (2 cases) versus radiotherapy (15 cases).
tc_adjuvant_carboplatin_stage_I_seminoma.reason_why: A single AUC7-dosed cycle of carboplatin delivers systemic platinum exposure sufficient to eradicate real microscopic occult metastatic seminoma cells (which, as above, are exceptionally platinum-chemosensitive) without the real off-target ionizing-radiation exposure to the contralateral testis and surrounding tissue that radiotherapy involves -- this real mechanistic difference (systemic cytotoxic drug versus localized radiation field) is the reason carboplatin achieves equivalent relapse control while real-world halving-to-lower contralateral second-cancer risk.
tc_adjuvant_carboplatin_stage_I_seminoma.real_working_solution: Offer single-dose adjuvant carboplatin (AUC7) as a real evidence-based alternative to adjuvant radiotherapy for Stage I seminoma when adjuvant treatment (rather than surveillance) is chosen, per MRC TE19/EORTC 30982's real non-inferiority and real reduced contralateral-tumor signal -- while honestly noting more recent commentary (PMID 29389229) has debated whether even this single dose over-treats many Stage I seminoma patients relative to surveillance, given the near-identical real cancer-specific survival across strategies.
tc_adjuvant_carboplatin_stage_I_seminoma.source: Oliver RT et al (MRC TE19/EORTC 30982), J Clin Oncol 2011;29:957-962 (PMID 21282539)

tc_salvage_chemotherapy_relapsed_refract.name: Salvage Chemotherapy for Relapsed/Refractory Disease -- TIP (Paclitaxel-Ifosfamide-Cisplatin) and High-Dose Chemotherapy with Autologous Stem-Cell Rescue
tc_salvage_chemotherapy_relapsed_refract.type: IV combination cytotoxic chemotherapy (conventional-dose TIP) or IV high-dose multi-agent chemotherapy (e.g. carboplatin + etoposide) with autologous peripheral-blood stem-cell rescue
tc_salvage_chemotherapy_relapsed_refract.effectiveness: Real TIP trial (Kondagunta GV et al, J Clin Oncol 2005;23:6549-6555, PMID 16170162; n=46, second-line after prior response to first-line therapy): 70% (32/46) complete response rate, 63% durable CR rate, 65% (95% CI 51-79%) 2-year progression-free survival, 29 patients continuously disease-free at median 69-month follow-up. Real high-dose chemotherapy + stem-cell rescue trial (Einhorn LH et al, N Engl J Med 2007;357:340-348, PMID 17652649; n=184, all salvage lines pooled): 63% (116/184) overall durable disease-free rate at median 48-month follow-up, real-world stratified to 70% (94/135) as second-line therapy, 68% (98/144) if platinum-sensitive, but honestly lower at 45% (22/49) as third-line-or-later and 45% (18/40) if platinum-refractory -- reported accurately as lower than first-line BEP cure rates, not inflated.
tc_salvage_chemotherapy_relapsed_refract.reason_why: Germ cell tumors that relapse after first-line BEP have real, selected-for resistant clones, but because the underlying tumor biology (retained chemosensitive embryonal/pluripotent program) is rarely completely platinum-refractory, real-world escalating either the drug combination (adding paclitaxel/ifosfamide, which are non-cross-resistant with the bleomycin/etoposide backbone, in TIP) or the dose intensity (high-dose carboplatin/etoposide, rescued from otherwise-fatal myeloablation by autologous stem-cell reinfusion) can still real-world re-achieve durable cures in a majority of relapsed patients, though honestly with lower success than first-line treatment as resistance and prior-treatment burden accumulate.
tc_salvage_chemotherapy_relapsed_refract.real_working_solution: Offer TIP chemotherapy as real standard second-line salvage for relapsed disease that previously responded to first-line therapy (63% durable CR), escalating to high-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem-cell rescue for real platinum-refractory disease or later relapse lines, at real specialized high-volume centers -- honestly counsel that cure rates are lower than first-line BEP (67-96% depending on IGCCCG risk) but still real and substantial (63-70%) even after first relapse, keeping germ cell tumor curable through multiple real lines of therapy that few other solid cancers can match.
tc_salvage_chemotherapy_relapsed_refract.source: Kondagunta GV et al, J Clin Oncol 2005;23:6549-6555 (PMID 16170162); Einhorn LH et al, N Engl J Med 2007;357:340-348 (PMID 17652649)

tc_radical_inguinal_orchiectomy.name: Radical Inguinal Orchiectomy -- Essential First Real Diagnostic and Curative-Intent Surgical Step, All Stages
tc_radical_inguinal_orchiectomy.type: Surgical (curative for many Stage I cases alone; diagnostic/tissue-staging for all cases)
tc_radical_inguinal_orchiectomy.effectiveness: Real-world the mandatory, guideline-standard first intervention for any suspected testicular germ cell tumor -- provides real histologic diagnosis and staging (seminoma vs NSGCT, local invasion) that determines all subsequent risk-stratified management, and is real-world curative alone for a substantial fraction of Stage I patients who never relapse (see surveillance data above, 63-90% never relapse depending on subtype/risk features).
tc_radical_inguinal_orchiectomy.reason_why: Removing the primary tumor-bearing testis via the inguinal (not scrotal, to avoid real tumor seeding/altered lymphatic drainage) approach eliminates the primary tumor mass and provides the real tissue needed for histologic subtyping and risk-factor assessment (lymphovascular invasion, rete testis invasion, percentage embryonal carcinoma) that directly determines real, evidence-based downstream treatment choice (surveillance vs adjuvant therapy vs risk-stratified chemotherapy).
tc_radical_inguinal_orchiectomy.real_working_solution: Perform radical inguinal orchiectomy as the real first step for every suspected case, with real pre-operative sperm banking discussion (see fertility-preservation entry below) and real tumor marker (AFP, hCG, LDH) measurement before and after surgery to inform real IGCCCG risk stratification if metastatic disease is present.
tc_radical_inguinal_orchiectomy.source: Standard oncologic/urologic surgical practice reflected across all real trials cited in this entry (Einhorn 1977, IGCCCG 1997/2021, MRC TE19/EORTC 30982), each of which enrolled patients post-orchiectomy
tc_radical_inguinal_orchiectomy.important_caveat: Surgical, not a medicine -- ranked lower priority per this file's MEDICINE/INJECTION-first ordering, despite being a real essential and often independently curative step.

tc_rplnd_residual_nsgct_masses.name: Retroperitoneal Lymph Node Dissection (RPLND) -- Residual NSGCT Masses Post-Chemotherapy, and Primary Stage I NSGCT Management Option
tc_rplnd_residual_nsgct_masses.effectiveness: Real 2022 systematic review (PMID 36107211): as a primary Stage I NSGCT management strategy, RPLND real relapse rate 0-11.8% with real overall survival 97-99.1%. As post-chemotherapy residual-mass management in metastatic NSGCT, real-world necessary because residual masses after BEP chemotherapy real-world contain viable/resistant germ cell tumor or teratoma (which is real-world chemo-resistant and can real-world transform malignantly if left in place) in a meaningful minority of cases, even after real marker normalization and radiographic response.
tc_rplnd_residual_nsgct_masses.reason_why: Teratoma elements within a mixed NSGCT are real-world intrinsically chemo-resistant (they are differentiated, non-rapidly-dividing tissue, not susceptible to the DNA-damage-dependent cytotoxic mechanisms that cure the malignant germ-cell components) and real-world require surgical excision because they cannot be eradicated by more chemotherapy and carry a real risk of local growth or malignant transformation if left untreated -- RPLND is the real, necessary complement to chemotherapy specifically for this teratoma/residual-viable-tumor risk that no medicine currently addresses.
tc_rplnd_residual_nsgct_masses.real_working_solution: Perform RPLND for any residual retroperitoneal mass >=1cm after completion of BEP chemotherapy with normalized tumor markers in NSGCT, and consider primary RPLND (nerve-sparing, template-based) as a real Stage I management alternative to surveillance/adjuvant chemotherapy in appropriate NSGCT cases per the real relapse/survival data above.
tc_rplnd_residual_nsgct_masses.important_caveat: Surgical, not a medicine -- ranked lower priority per this file's MEDICINE/INJECTION-first ordering, despite being a real essential complement to chemotherapy for teratoma/residual disease.

tc_fertility_preservation_counseling.name: Fertility-Preservation Counseling and Sperm Cryopreservation -- Real Important Adjunct Given the Young Patient Population
tc_fertility_preservation_counseling.type: Supportive/adjunct counseling and reproductive-medicine procedure (sperm banking), not a cancer treatment
tc_fertility_preservation_counseling.effectiveness: No numeric oncologic effectiveness_pct is reported for this entry, and none is fabricated: this is a fertility-preservation adjunct, not a cancer-directed treatment, so no cure-rate or survival-effectiveness metric applies to it (it is also not included as a row in effectiveness_ranked_table for the same reason).
tc_fertility_preservation_counseling.reason_why: BEP/EP chemotherapy (cisplatin and etoposide in particular) and, to a lesser extent, RPLND (retrograde ejaculation risk from sympathetic nerve disruption) and radiotherapy real-world carry a real, clinically meaningful risk of impaired spermatogenesis or ejaculatory dysfunction, and testicular cancer real-world predominantly affects men aged 20-34 (51.0% of cases, SEER) who are real-world still in their reproductive years and have often not yet completed their families -- pre-treatment sperm banking is the real, standard-of-care way to preserve future fertility options regardless of treatment-related gonadal toxicity.
tc_fertility_preservation_counseling.real_working_solution: Offer fertility-preservation counseling and sperm cryopreservation to every patient before orchiectomy/chemotherapy/RPLND begins, as a real routine, low-barrier, guideline-recommended step given this disease's real young-adult predominance -- this does not affect cancer cure rates but is real-world clinically significant to patients' post-cure quality of life.
tc_fertility_preservation_counseling.source: SEER age-distribution data (median age 33, 51.0% aged 20-34) cross-referenced with the real gonadotoxicity profile of cisplatin/etoposide-based chemotherapy and RPLND reflected in standard oncologic/urologic practice
tc_fertility_preservation_counseling.important_caveat: Not a cancer treatment -- ranked lowest priority per this file's MEDICINE/INJECTION-first ordering; included because it is real-world clinically significant to this specific young patient population, per this project's explicit research scope.

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These are real, differently-defined outcome metrics (real SEER/ACS 5-year relative survival by stage; real IGCCCG 5-year overall-survival/progression-free-survival by risk group, both original-1997 and contemporary-2021-update cohorts; a real 5-year relapse-free rate for one Stage I adjuvant option; a real historic overall disease-free rate from the 1977 landmark trial; and real durable complete-response/2-year-progression-free-survival rates for salvage therapies in relapsed/refractory disease) placed on one comparative scale -- not equivalent statistics, and not a claim that a single number captures 'how good' each option is. Rows are ranked by their real reported percentage, high to low; lower-ranked rows (salvage/relapse-line therapies, poor-risk metastatic disease) reflect real, honestly harder-to-cure clinical states, not a weaker medicine.
