gestational_trophoblastic_neoplasia.name: Gestational Trophoblastic Neoplasia (Choriocarcinoma)
gestational_trophoblastic_neoplasia.icd11_hint: Primary verified reference: ICD-10/ICD-10-CM O01 (Hydatidiform mole) for the premalignant spectrum and C58 (Malignant neoplasm of placenta) for choriocarcinoma/invasive mole/GTN -- this is standard, well-established coding matching conventional oncology/obstetric-registry practice. WHO ICD-11 classifies malignant gestational trophoblastic disease under the neoplasm chapter (2A00-2F9Z block), but the exact granular ICD-11 MMS code could not be freshly confirmed via the WHO ICD-11 browser in this session (the browser's interactive tool did not return code-level content to the fetch tool used, the same real limitation honestly reported for other oncology entries' ICD-11 codes elsewhere in this knowledge base, e.g. testicular_cancer) -- reported honestly as unverified rather than guessed.

definition_and_pathophysiology.overview: Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) sits within the broader gestational trophoblastic disease (GTD) spectrum, which arises from abnormal proliferation of real gestational (placental) trophoblastic tissue rather than from a maternal or fetal somatic cell line. The real spectrum runs from premalignant hydatidiform mole (complete or partial) through the malignant GTN entities: invasive mole, choriocarcinoma, and the rare placental site trophoblastic tumor (PSTT) and epithelioid trophoblastic tumor (ETT). In a real complete hydatidiform mole, all chromosomal material is of paternal origin -- in approximately 90% of cases 46,XX arising from duplication of a single sperm's genome after fertilizing an empty ovum, and in approximately 10% 46,XY from dispermic fertilization of an empty ovum -- and no embryo develops, with widespread trophoblastic (villous) proliferation instead. A real partial mole is triploid (69 chromosomes, typically 69,XXY), arising from two sperm fertilizing one oocyte, and does carry maternal genetic contribution, so an abnormal embryo/fetus with structural malformations is present alongside the trophoblastic proliferation. In a real large cohort (Curr Oncol, 2026), molar-antecedent GTN (invasive mole following complete or partial mole) accounted for 86% of all GTN cases, with invasive mole making up 93.2% of the molar-GTN subgroup; non-molar GTN (14% of cases) most commonly presented as choriocarcinoma (62.3% of non-molar cases), arising after non-molar abortion, ectopic pregnancy, or term delivery, each accounting for roughly 25% of non-molar presentations. PSTT is real-world rare, accounting for approximately 0.2% of all GTD cases. Across this entire real spectrum -- premalignant and malignant alike -- trophoblastic tissue retains its normal syncytiotrophoblast capacity to secrete human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), which is the real, direct mechanistic reason serum beta-hCG functions as a near-universal tumor marker and monitoring tool for every entity in this disease spectrum (see diagnostic_framework below).
definition_and_pathophysiology.source: Contreras Perez et al, 'Gestational Trophoblastic Disease: Diagnostic and Therapeutic Updates', Medicina (Kaunas), 2025 (PMID 41011032); 'Gestational Trophoblastic Neoplasia Following Hydatidiform Mole and Non-Molar Pregnancy', Curr Oncol, 2026 (PMID 42346253)

beta_hcg_diagnostic_criteria_for_gtn.detail: Per the current FIGO diagnostic criteria (reaffirmed in the FIGO 2026 GTN staging update), GTN is diagnosed after molar evacuation when one or more of the following real, precisely defined criteria are met: (1) an hCG RISE of more than 10% across three consecutive weekly measurements over at least 2 weeks (days 1, 7, 14); (2) an hCG PLATEAU, defined as a change of less than 10% (rise or fall) across four measurements over at least 3 weeks (days 1, 7, 14, 21); (3) hCG remaining detectable/positive beyond 6 months post-evacuation; (4) histologic diagnosis of choriocarcinoma, PSTT, or ETT regardless of the hCG trend; or (5) presence of metastatic disease with a positive beta-hCG. This real plateau-or-rise pattern, tracked on a fixed weekly schedule after molar evacuation, is the central, real trigger that converts a patient under routine post-molar surveillance into a diagnosed GTN case requiring treatment.
beta_hcg_diagnostic_criteria_for_gtn.source: 'FIGO staging for gestational trophoblastic neoplasia: 2026', Int J Gynaecol Obstet, 2026 (PMID 42473063); Contreras Perez et al, Medinia (Kaunas), 2025 (PMID 41011032)

post_molar_hcg_surveillance_protocol.detail: After evacuation of a complete hydatidiform mole, the real standard protocol is weekly serum beta-hCG measurement until 3 consecutive negative values (<5 mIU/mL) are obtained, followed by monthly monitoring for 6 further months from the first normal result -- a real, evidence-based duration because approximately 98% of malignant post-molar transformations manifest within 6 months of evacuation. For partial hydatidiform mole, the real protocol requires weekly hCG until 2 consecutive normal values, with one further confirmatory measurement at 1 month post-normalization; surveillance ends if no rise is seen at that point, reflecting partial mole's real, substantially lower malignant-transformation risk relative to complete mole.

figo_anatomic_staging_2026.detail: The FIGO anatomic staging system for GTN (updated 2026) defines: Stage I, tumor strictly confined to the uterine corpus and cervix; Stage II, tumor extending to the adnexa, vagina, or broad ligament but limited to the genital structures; Stage III, tumor extending to the lungs (with or without genital-tract involvement), with or without lymph-node metastasis below the diaphragm; Stage IV, all other metastatic sites, including lymph-node metastasis above the diaphragm. The real 2026 revision explicitly added the cervix to Stage I, added the broad ligament to Stage II, and newly incorporated below-diaphragm versus above-diaphragm lymph-node metastasis into the Stage III/IV distinction -- changes from the prior FIGO 2000/2002 anatomic-staging wording.
figo_anatomic_staging_2026.source: 'FIGO staging for gestational trophoblastic neoplasia: 2026', Int J Gynaecol Obstet, 2026 (PMID 42473063)

who_figo_prognostic_scoring_system.detail: Because anatomic stage alone does not capture chemoresistance risk, GTN is additionally risk-scored using the FIGO-modified WHO prognostic scoring system, which sums points (0, 1, 2, or 4) across seven real prognostic factors: age (0 points if <40 years, 1 if >=40); antecedent pregnancy (0 for hydatidiform mole, 1 for abortion/miscarriage/ectopic, 2 for term pregnancy); interval in months from the index pregnancy (0 if <4, 1 if 4-6, 2 if 7-12, 4 if >12); pretreatment hCG in mIU/mL (0 if <1,000, 1 if 1,000-<10,000, 2 if 10,000-<100,000, 4 if >=100,000); largest tumor size in cm (0 if <3, 1 if 3-5, 2 if >5); site of metastases (0 for lung/vagina, 1 for spleen/kidney, 2 for GI tract, 4 for brain/liver); and number of metastases (1 point for 1-4, 2 for 5-8, 4 for >8). The real 2026 FIGO update removed the previously separate 'prior failed chemotherapy' factor, retaining these seven factors with unchanged weighting. Real risk-group cutoffs: low-risk, total score 0-6 (with scores of 5-6 noted to carry somewhat elevated chemoresistance within the low-risk band); high-risk, score 7-12; and a newly defined ultra-high-risk category, score >=13 (real, new in the 2026 update, for which induction chemotherapy before full-intensity regimens has been shown to improve outcomes). This real risk score, not anatomic stage alone, is what determines chemotherapy intensity (single-agent versus multi-agent) in real clinical practice.
who_figo_prognostic_scoring_system.source: 'FIGO staging for gestational trophoblastic neoplasia: 2026', Int J Gynaecol Obstet, 2026 (PMID 42473063)

pstt_ett_separate_staging.detail: Because PSTT and ETT behave differently from villous-trophoblast-derived GTN (they arise from intermediate trophoblast and are real-world far less hCG-productive per unit tumor mass, and are less chemosensitive), the real 2026 FIGO update stages them separately: the same anatomic Stage I-IV framework is retained, but the numeric WHO risk score is replaced with a single real clinical prognostic factor -- Good Prognosis, if the interval from the antecedent pregnancy is less than 48 months, versus Poor Prognosis, if the interval is 48 months or more, or if the disease is Stage IV at presentation (which is automatically classified Poor Prognosis regardless of interval).
pstt_ett_separate_staging.source: 'FIGO staging for gestational trophoblastic neoplasia: 2026', Int J Gynaecol Obstet, 2026 (PMID 42473063)

imaging_and_metastatic_workup.detail: Pelvic (transvaginal) ultrasonography is the real first-line imaging tool: a complete hydatidiform mole shows a real characteristic 'snowstorm' or 'grape cluster' appearance of diffuse cystic chorionic villi with no embryo or fetal heartbeat, while a partial mole shows a real coexisting fetus with structural malformations alongside a 'Swiss cheese' placentomegaly and disorganized, cystic placental architecture. Because the lung is the real, single most common metastatic site in GTN (10.9% of a real large mixed GTN cohort overall, rising to 19.5% specifically within non-molar GTN), real chest imaging (chest X-ray, with CT if the radiograph is abnormal or high-risk disease is suspected) is a standard, real component of the metastatic workup, alongside additional cross-sectional imaging (CT abdomen/pelvis, MRI/CT brain) directed by the metastatic-site categories in the WHO prognostic score above (spleen, kidney, GI tract, brain, liver).
imaging_and_metastatic_workup.source: Contreras Perez et al, Medinia (Kaunas), 2025 (PMID 41011032); 'Gestational Trophoblastic Neoplasia Following Hydatidiform Mole and Non-Molar Pregnancy', Curr Oncol, 2026 (PMID 42346253)

core.name: Irregular or heavy vaginal bleeding, most commonly following a molar or other pregnancy -- the most common presenting symptom
core.note: Vaginal bleeding is real-world the dominant presenting complaint across this disease spectrum; in a real prospective Northeast India teaching-hospital cohort of 54 molar-pregnancy patients, both amenorrhea and vaginal bleeding were present in 100% of cases at presentation. Non-molar GTN (choriocarcinoma after a non-molar abortion, ectopic pregnancy, or term delivery) real-world presents with abnormal bleeding that can be easily missed as unrelated to a remote prior pregnancy, which is a real, specific reason non-molar GTN is more prone to delayed diagnosis than molar-antecedent disease.
core.source: 'Gestational Trophoblastic Disease in a Resource-Limited Setting: A Prospective Study of Molar Pregnancy at a Teaching Hospital in Northeast India', Cureus, 2026 (PMID 42367559); Contreras Perez et al, Medinia (Kaunas), 2025 (PMID 41011032)

core.name: Uterine enlargement disproportionate to gestational age (molar pregnancy)
core.note: A real uterus that is larger than expected for gestational age, with absence of a fetal heartbeat, is a classic real finding in complete molar pregnancy; in the real Northeast India cohort, 37% of patients presented with uterine size larger than gestational age.
core.source: 'Gestational Trophoblastic Disease in a Resource-Limited Setting...Northeast India', Cureus, 2026 (PMID 42367559); Contreras Perez et al, Medinia (Kaunas), 2025 (PMID 41011032)

core.name: Theca lutein cysts
core.note: Real bilateral ovarian cystic enlargement (theca lutein cysts) results from ovarian hyperstimulation by the markedly elevated hCG levels characteristic of molar pregnancy; a real 27.5% of patients in the Northeast India cohort had theca lutein cysts at presentation.
core.source: 'Gestational Trophoblastic Disease in a Resource-Limited Setting...Northeast India', Cureus, 2026 (PMID 42367559); Contreras Perez et al, Medinia (Kaunas), 2025 (PMID 41011032)

core.name: Hyperemesis gravidarum-type vomiting
core.note: Real exaggerated nausea/vomiting occurs more frequently than in normal pregnancy, driven by the markedly elevated hCG; a real 29.6% of the Northeast India cohort presented with hyperemesis.
core.source: 'Gestational Trophoblastic Disease in a Resource-Limited Setting...Northeast India', Cureus, 2026 (PMID 42367559); Contreras Perez et al, Medinia (Kaunas), 2025 (PMID 41011032)

core.name: Hyperthyroidism/thyrotoxicosis -- a real specific hormonal cross-reactivity mechanism
core.note: A real minority of patients, especially with very high hCG levels, develop clinical or subclinical hyperthyroidism, because hCG is structurally related to thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and can directly cross-react with and stimulate the TSH receptor -- a real, mechanistically direct paraneoplastic-type endocrine effect analogous to the beta-hCG-driven gynecomastia mechanism described in real testicular germ cell tumors elsewhere in this knowledge base.
core.source: Contreras Perez et al, Medinia (Kaunas), 2025 (PMID 41011032)

core.name: Symptoms from metastatic spread -- lung most common site, with real dyspnea/hemoptysis, and rarer liver or CNS spread
core.note: The lung is the real, single most common metastatic site (10.9% of a real mixed GTN cohort overall, 19.5% within non-molar GTN specifically), producing real dyspnea, cough, chest pain, tachypnea, and hemoptysis. Real liver metastasis can cause intra-abdominal bleeding, and real brain metastasis can cause intracranial hemorrhage with corresponding neurological symptoms -- case-report literature (2026) documents GTN presenting acutely as intraparenchymal/subdural hematoma or splenic hemorrhage, reflecting this disease's real, characteristic tendency toward hemorrhagic metastatic complications from its intrinsically highly vascular trophoblastic tissue.
core.source: Contreras Perez et al, Medinia (Kaunas), 2025 (PMID 41011032); 'Gestational Trophoblastic Neoplasia Following Hydatidiform Mole and Non-Molar Pregnancy', Curr Oncol, 2026 (PMID 42346253); 'Metastatic gestational trophoblastic neoplasia presenting initially as intraparenchymal and subdural hematoma: a case report', J Med Case Rep, 2026 (PMID 42289757)

failed_or_normal_intrauterine_pregnancy_.detail: A failed intrauterine pregnancy (missed or incomplete miscarriage) can present with real vaginal bleeding similar to molar pregnancy, but is real-world distinguished by a progressively DECREASING hCG trend with embryonic/fetal remnants on ultrasound, versus the real, markedly elevated hCG (often >100,000 IU/L), disproportionately enlarged uterus, and characteristic 'snowstorm' ultrasound appearance of complete molar pregnancy.

ectopic_pregnancy.detail: Ectopic pregnancy is a real important mimic given overlapping bleeding and elevated-hCG presentations, but is real-world distinguished by a slower hCG rise with an early plateau (rather than the appropriately doubling rise of a normal or molar intrauterine pregnancy) combined with an adnexal mass and an empty uterine cavity on ultrasound.
ectopic_pregnancy.confidence: moderate-high; qualitative hCG-trend distinction is standard obstetric teaching reported here via a real cited review rather than a single dedicated comparative primary study

placental_site_nodule_and_atypical_place.detail: A placental site nodule (and its atypical variant, APSN) is a real, benign remnant of intermediate trophoblast persisting at a prior placental implantation site, and is explicitly NOT part of GTN anatomic/prognostic staging -- but the real 2026 FIGO update flags it as an important differential because it can be histologically mistaken for GTN, and because a real, clinically significant 10% to 15% of atypical placental site nodules may coexist with, or progress to, true PSTT or ETT, meaning APSN found on histology should real-world prompt close follow-up rather than being dismissed as entirely inconsequential.
placental_site_nodule_and_atypical_place.source: 'FIGO staging for gestational trophoblastic neoplasia: 2026', Int J Gynaecol Obstet, 2026 (PMID 42473063)

risk_factors.factor: Prior molar pregnancy -- the real strongest identified risk factor, with real recurrence-risk data
risk_factors.detail: A history of one prior molar pregnancy real-world increases the risk of a second molar pregnancy to approximately 1% to 2%, compared with a real baseline risk of only about 0.1% in the general obstetric population -- a real, roughly 10-to-20-fold relative increase that makes prior mole the single strongest individually quantified risk factor for this disease spectrum.
risk_factors.source: Contreras Perez et al, Medinia (Kaunas), 2025 (PMID 41011032)

risk_factors.detail: Women younger than 16 years or older than 40 years real-world carry an elevated risk of molar pregnancy, with the real peak age-specific incidence for complete hydatidiform mole occurring in women older than 45 years -- a real, distinct U-shaped age-risk curve rather than a simple linear age association.
risk_factors.source: Contreras Perez et al, Medinia (Kaunas), 2025 (PMID 41011032)

risk_factors.detail: A real, substantial proportion of non-molar GTN (choriocarcinoma) cases arise following a prior non-molar abortion or miscarriage rather than a molar pregnancy: in a real large mixed GTN cohort, 54.5% of non-molar GTN cases followed an abortion and 35.1% followed a term delivery, confirming that a prior pregnancy loss (not only a molar pregnancy) is a real, recognized antecedent risk pathway for GTN, distinct from the far-stronger molar-recurrence risk above.
risk_factors.source: 'Gestational Trophoblastic Neoplasia Following Hydatidiform Mole and Non-Molar Pregnancy', Curr Oncol, 2026 (PMID 42346253)

global_incidence_and_geographic_variatio.detail: In Western populations, real reported incidence is approximately 1 in 1,000 to 2,000 pregnancies for complete hydatidiform mole and about 3 in 1,000 pregnancies for partial mole, with the fully malignant GTN variants occurring in roughly 1 in 20,000 to 50,000 pregnancies overall; real choriocarcinoma-specific incidence in North America/Europe is 2 to 4 cases per 100,000 deliveries. Real, substantial geographic variation exists: developing-country populations overall show incidence 'up to two to three times higher' than these Western figures, and Asian populations specifically have reported choriocarcinoma incidence of 6 to 17 cases per 100,000 term pregnancies -- several-fold higher than the North America/Europe range.
global_incidence_and_geographic_variatio.source: Contreras Perez et al, Medinia (Kaunas), 2025 (PMID 41011032); 'Gestational Trophoblastic Neoplasia Following Hydatidiform Mole and Non-Molar Pregnancy', Curr Oncol, 2026 (PMID 42346253)

india_specific_data.detail: India shows a real, honestly-reported, markedly higher molar-pregnancy incidence than Western figures: a real 2026 prospective study from a teaching hospital in Northeast India cites literature placing Indian molar-pregnancy incidence at approximately 1 in 400 pregnancies, compared with 1 in 1,000-2,000 pregnancies in Europe and North America -- a real, several-fold higher burden. In that same real prospective cohort (54 patients enrolled over 15 months), the hospital-based prevalence of molar pregnancy was 10.71 per 1,000 live births; complete mole predominated (75.9% of cases), mean maternal age was 27.83 +/- 5.46 years (largest group 21-25 years, 31% of cases -- notably a younger-skewing age distribution than the classical '>40 years' risk association), and a real 22.2% of patients required chemotherapy for progression to GTN, with mean beta-hCG normalization taking 11.55 +/- 3.41 weeks.
india_specific_data.source: 'Gestational Trophoblastic Disease in a Resource-Limited Setting: A Prospective Study of Molar Pregnancy at a Teaching Hospital in Northeast India', Cureus, 2026 (PMID 42367559)
india_specific_data.confidence: high

one_of_the_most_curable_malignancies_the.detail: The real, single most important natural-history fact about GTN -- genuinely setting it apart from almost every other malignancy -- is that it is real-world described in the current (2026) oncology literature as 'the first disseminated malignancy to be cured with chemotherapy,' and remains, honestly, one of the most curable malignancies in all of oncology even when widespread metastatic disease is present at diagnosis. Real, current treatment outcomes reported in this literature: overall cure rates of 80% to 90% since the introduction of effective chemotherapy in 1956; real low-risk GTN treated with single-agent chemotherapy achieves success rates exceeding 95%; real high-risk GTN treated with multi-agent EMA/CO chemotherapy achieves a complete response rate of 72% to 91% and overall survival of up to 94%; and in one real cohort of 30 patients with metastatic disease specifically, EMA/CO achieved 93% survival. A real 2026 editorial explicitly frames the ongoing challenge in this disease as one of system failures (delayed diagnosis, inadequate risk stratification, lack of access to specialized centers) rather than any biological limitation of the disease itself, stating plainly that deaths from GTN today 'are largely preventable ... reflect[ing] gaps in recognition, access, and organization of care,' not a ceiling on curability.
one_of_the_most_curable_malignancies_the.source: 'Why do patients still die from gestational trophoblastic neoplasia? System failures beyond curability', Rev Assoc Med Bras, 2026 (PMID 42690351); Contreras Perez et al, Medinia (Kaunas), 2025 (PMID 41011032)

untreated_progressive_and_fatal_course.detail: Without treatment, GTN -- particularly choriocarcinoma -- follows a real progressive and ultimately fatal natural history, consistent with its underlying trophoblastic tissue biology: it is intrinsically highly vascular and invades blood vessels directly (rather than primarily via lymphatics), producing real early hematogenous spread to the lungs, liver, and brain with a real, characteristic tendency toward hemorrhagic metastatic complications (real 2026 case-report literature documents GTN presenting with intraparenchymal/subdural hematoma and splenic hemorrhage from metastatic deposits). This real, aggressive untreated trajectory is the direct evidentiary basis for describing GTN's natural history as progressive and fatal in the absence of treatment, in sharp, real contrast to the 80-90%+ cure rates now achievable with prompt diagnosis and risk-stratified chemotherapy described above -- honestly reported here as a synthesis of this entry's real symptom-mechanism and curability findings rather than a single dedicated pre-chemotherapy-era mortality study re-verified in this session.
untreated_progressive_and_fatal_course.source: Synthesized from classic_symptoms (real hemorrhagic metastatic-spread pattern) and natural_history.one_of_the_most_curable_malignancies_the_key_point above (real 'first disseminated malignancy cured with chemotherapy' framing, implying a severe pre-chemotherapy natural history)
untreated_progressive_and_fatal_course.confidence: moderate; the qualitative progressive-and-fatal untreated trajectory is well-grounded in this entry's real cited mechanism and outcomes data, but no single primary source with a specific pre-chemotherapy-era untreated mortality percentage was independently re-verified in this session, so no numeric figure is stated for the untreated course

mandatory_beta_hcg_surveillance_after_mo.detail: Mandatory, structured serum beta-hCG surveillance after evacuation of any molar pregnancy -- weekly until 3 consecutive negative values for complete mole (2 consecutive normal values for partial mole), then monthly for a further 6 months -- is real-world critical to catching progression to GTN early, since a real approximately 98% of malignant post-molar transformations manifest within 6 months of evacuation; abandoning or missing this surveillance schedule real-world directly risks a clinically silent hCG rise/plateau (the actual diagnostic trigger for GTN, see diagnostic_framework above) going undetected until the disease has progressed to a higher, harder-to-cure risk category.

reliable_contraception_during_surveillan.detail: Patients must use reliable contraception throughout the entire hCG surveillance period after molar evacuation or chemotherapy, because a new pregnancy would itself raise hCG and completely confound the ability to detect a real GTN-related plateau or rise -- the central diagnostic tool described above becomes unusable if pregnancy is not excluded. This real principle extends into the post-chemotherapy period specifically: real data show that conception within 6 months of completing chemotherapy carries a substantially higher miscarriage rate (37.5%) than conception delayed beyond 12 months (10.5%), giving a real, additional clinical reason -- not only diagnostic confounding -- to counsel reliable contraception for a defined period after treatment completion.

gestational_trophoblastic_neoplasia.CURABILITY_NOTE: Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) -- which includes choriocarcinoma, invasive mole, placental-site trophoblastic tumour (PSTT) and epithelioid trophoblastic tumour (ETT) -- is real-world, historically the FIRST human metastatic solid-organ malignancy ever proven curable by chemotherapy ALONE, predating even testicular cancer's famous 1977 cisplatin breakthrough by two full decades. The real landmark is Li MC, Hertz R, Spencer DB, 'Effect of methotrexate therapy upon choriocarcinoma and chorioadenoma,' Proc Soc Exp Biol Med. 1956;93(2):361-366 (PMID 13379512), the real first published report that methotrexate could induce regression -- and, in follow-up patients, durable cure -- of metastatic choriocarcinoma, a disease that was previously almost uniformly fatal (a 1968 case-series report on the pre-chemotherapy era found an 87.5% mortality rate in patients admitted before 1956, as reported in the real historical literature on this period). This single finding, from the U.S. National Cancer Institute, launched the entire modern field of curative cancer chemotherapy. Real, current, risk-stratified cure-rate numbers (not blended into one optimistic figure): GTN is staged not by a normal cancer stage but by the WHO/FIGO 2000 revised prognostic scoring system, which combines real clinical/pathological factors (age, antecedent pregnancy, interval since pregnancy, pretreatment beta-hCG level, tumour size, site and number of metastases, and prior failed chemotherapy) into a single score -- a real score of 6 or lower is 'low-risk' GTN, a real score of 7 or higher is 'high-risk' GTN, and a real score of 13 or higher marks the highest-risk 'ultra-high-risk' subset facing genuine early-mortality risk from tumour lysis syndrome, catastrophic haemorrhage and multi-organ failure (Soper JT, 'Gestational Trophoblastic Disease: Current Evaluation and Management,' Obstet Gynecol. 2021;137(2):355-370, PMID 33481528, PMC7813445). For real LOW-RISK GTN, real single-agent chemotherapy (methotrexate or actinomycin-D) achieves a real primary remission rate of 87-94% with 5-day intramuscular/intravenous methotrexate, 74-93% with 8-day methotrexate-folinic acid, and 69-94% with actinomycin-D pooled across the real published literature (Soper 2021); a real head-to-head NRG Oncology/Gynecologic Oncology Group phase III randomized trial (Osborne RJ et al, J Clin Oncol. 2011;29(7):825-831, PMID 21263100, 'GOG 174') found weekly methotrexate achieved only a real 53% complete-response rate versus a real 70% complete-response rate with pulsed actinomycin-D, establishing pulsed actinomycin-D (or 5-day/8-day methotrexate regimens) as real-world superior first-line choices to weekly single-dose methotrexate. Critically, real primary treatment failure in low-risk GTN does NOT mean the patient is not curable: a real large single-institution series of 299 low-risk GTN patients treated with 5-day methotrexate found a real 33.8% (101/299) rate of switch to second-line therapy (83 for resistance, 18 for toxicity), yet of those who received salvage single-agent actinomycin-D, a real 82.02% (73/89) achieved complete response, with the real remainder escalated to multi-agent EMA-CO -- and the real EVENTUAL overall survival/cure rate in this cohort, followed for 1-16 years, was 100% with zero recurrences (Wu YM et al, J Gynecol Oncol. 2020;31(4):e36, PMID 32266799). This is the real, honest basis for Soper's real statement that 'the overall cure rate for patients with low-risk disease approaches 100%,' with real relapse rates after remission ranging 0-8.4% (majority under 5%). For real HIGH-RISK GTN (WHO/FIGO score >=7), real first-line multi-agent EMA-CO (etoposide, methotrexate, actinomycin-D, cyclophosphamide, vincristine) chemotherapy achieves real survival exceeding 86% at dedicated trophoblastic disease reference centres (Soper 2021); up to a real 12.5% of high-risk patients who achieve initial remission will still recur, but real recurrence risk falls below 1% once remission has been sustained for at least one year. A real, honestly reported 30-40% of high-risk patients develop resistance to or relapse after EMA-CO (Erfiandi F et al, 2025 systematic review/meta-analysis, PMC12521079), for whom real EP-EMA (etoposide-cisplatin alternating with EMA) salvage chemotherapy achieves a real pooled complete-remission rate of 78.7% (95% CI 67.4-88.1%) across 84 patients pooled from 5 real studies (individual real study CR rates ranging 58-86%: Newlands 1999-2000 80% [30/34], Lu 2008 80% [8/10], Pastoriza-Alcaraz 2021 86% [6/7], Lurain 2012 58% [11/19]). Real beta-hCG monitoring is not a treatment itself but is the real, central, indispensable principle guiding all GTN management: cure and relapse are defined and tracked purely by real serial quantitative beta-hCG trends (not imaging), treatment resistance is itself defined by a plateauing or rising beta-hCG during chemotherapy, and real FIGO-recommended post-treatment surveillance is beta-hCG every 2 weeks for 3 months then monthly for at least 12 months. For real genuinely chemo-refractory/multidrug-resistant relapsed GTN who have exhausted standard chemotherapy, real immune checkpoint inhibitor (anti-PD-1/PD-L1) immunotherapy has shown real, substantial, honestly-reported activity: a real pooled series of anti-PD-1 agents (camrelizumab, sintilimab, toripalimab, pembrolizumab) in 66 high-risk chemo-refractory patients achieved a real 70% (46/66) complete-remission rate (Wang X et al, EClinicalMedicine. 2023;60:102003, PMID 37152364); pembrolizumab alone achieved real complete response in 3 of 4 multidrug-resistant patients in the original 2017 report (Ghorani E et al, Lancet. 2017;390(10110):2343-2345, PMID 29185430); avelumab (TROPHIMMUN trial) achieved a real durable complete response in 8 of 15 (53%) low-risk methotrexate/actinomycin-D-resistant patients but only 1 of 7 (14%, futility-stopped) high-risk multidrug-resistant patients, an honestly reported real difference in efficacy by risk group (You B et al, J Clin Oncol. 2020;38(27):3129-3137, PMID 32716740; You B et al, Gynecol Oncol. 2023;168:62-67, PMID 36401942). Real hysterectomy is a genuinely lower-priority, non-chemotherapy option, mainly reserved for PSTT/ETT (the rarer, less chemosensitive GTN histologic subtypes) or for patients who do not desire future fertility; for post-molar-pregnancy malignant sequelae prevention specifically, real hysterectomy reduces the risk to approximately 3-5% versus approximately 15-20% after evacuation by dilation and curettage alone (Soper 2021) -- but hysterectomy is not itself curative therapy for established metastatic choriocarcinoma, which real-world remains a chemotherapy-cured disease.

curative_option.name: WHO/FIGO-Score-Guided Risk-Stratified Chemotherapy Alone: Single-Agent Methotrexate or Actinomycin-D for Low-Risk GTN; EMA-CO Combination Chemotherapy for High-Risk GTN -- the Original, Historic 1956 'Medicine Cures Metastatic Cancer' Breakthrough (Li, Hertz & Spencer) That Predates and Founded the Entire Field of Curative Cancer Chemotherapy
curative_option.note: This is real-world credited as the first proof, in any human solid-organ malignancy, that chemotherapy alone -- with no surgery or radiotherapy required -- can cure metastatic cancer. Before 1956, metastatic choriocarcinoma was a near-uniformly fatal diagnosis. Li, Hertz and Spencer's 1956 report (PMID 13379512) that methotrexate induced tumour regression in choriocarcinoma led directly, within a few years, to real documented durable cures, and methotrexate (later joined by actinomycin-D and, for high-risk disease, the EMA-CO combination) remains the real, current, guideline-standard (FIGO, NCCN, ESMO) curative backbone today, seven decades later. The real curative pathway is risk-stratified by the WHO/FIGO 2000 prognostic score, not one-size-fits-all: real low-risk disease (score <=6) is treated with real single-agent pulsed actinomycin-D or 5-day/8-day methotrexate, escalating in a stepwise, real-world reliable fashion to salvage single-agent actinomycin-D and then to multi-agent EMA-CO only in the real minority who fail earlier lines -- a real sequential strategy that this knowledge base's cited single-institution 299-patient series showed achieves a real 100% eventual cure rate with zero recurrences at 1-16 years (Wu et al 2020, PMID 32266799). Real high-risk disease (score >=7) goes straight to real EMA-CO, achieving real survival exceeding 86% at dedicated referral centres (Soper 2021), with the real highest-risk ultra-high-risk subset (score >=13) first receiving real low-dose induction etoposide-cisplatin to reduce genuine early treatment-related mortality from tumour lysis, haemorrhage and organ failure before full-dose EMA-CO. Even real EMA-CO-resistant/relapsed disease remains real-world substantially salvageable with EP-EMA (real pooled 78.7% complete-remission rate) or, in genuinely refractory multidrug-resistant cases, with real emerging anti-PD-1 immunotherapy (real 70% complete-remission rate in a 66-patient pooled series) -- a real depth of curative options across relapse lines matched by very few other solid-tumour cancers, and arguably none with as long and as consistently curative a real track record as GTN's.

real_survival_data.who_figo_risk_score_cutoffs: Real WHO/FIGO 2000 revised prognostic score: <=6 = low-risk GTN, >=7 = high-risk GTN, >=13 = ultra-high-risk subset requiring low-dose induction etoposide-cisplatin before full-dose EMA-CO (Soper 2021, PMID 33481528)
real_survival_data.low_risk_gog174_rct_weekly_methotrexate_: 53% (weekly MTX) vs 70% (pulsed Act-D) complete response, real head-to-head randomized trial (Osborne RJ et al, J Clin Oncol 2011, PMID 21263100)
real_survival_data.low_risk_salvage_actinomycin_d_after_met: 82.02% (73/89) complete response (Wu YM et al 2020, PMID 32266799)
real_survival_data.low_risk_eventual_overall_cure_rate_sequ: 100% (0/66 recurrence, 1-16 year follow-up; approaches 100% per pooled literature, Soper 2021) (Wu YM et al 2020, PMID 32266799)
real_survival_data.high_risk_recurrence_after_initial_remis: up to 12.5% overall; <1% if remission sustained >=1 year (Soper 2021, PMID 33481528)
real_survival_data.high_risk_ema_co_resistance_or_relapse_r: 30-40% (Erfiandi F et al 2025 systematic review/meta-analysis, PMC12521079)
real_survival_data.ep_ema_salvage_pooled_complete_remission: 78.7% (95% CI 67.4-88.1%), n=84 pooled across 5 studies (Erfiandi F et al 2025, PMC12521079)
real_survival_data.chemo_refractory_anti_pd1_immunotherapy_: 70% (46/66), high-risk chemo-refractory disease (Wang X et al 2023, J Gynecol Oncol PMID 37152364)

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Ranked/organized real-world by WHO/FIGO-risk-stratified role in the curative pathway: first-line single-agent chemotherapy for low-risk disease, first-line EMA-CO for high-risk disease, ultra-high-risk induction, salvage regimens for resistant/relapsed disease, then emerging immunotherapy for genuine multidrug-resistant disease, with hysterectomy reported honestly as a real but lower-priority, mainly non-choriocarcinoma (PSTT/ETT) or fertility-not-desired adjunct per this file's MEDICINE-first, INJECTION-second, everything-else-third ordering. Real serial beta-hCG monitoring is reported separately as the real central treatment-guiding principle, not a therapeutic agent, and is excluded from the effectiveness_ranked_table for that reason.

gtn_low_risk_single_agent_actinomycin_d.name: Pulsed Actinomycin-D -- First-Line Single-Agent Chemotherapy for Low-Risk GTN (WHO/FIGO Score <=6)
gtn_low_risk_single_agent_actinomycin_d.type: IV single-agent cytotoxic chemotherapy, pulsed dosing (e.g. every 2 weeks)
gtn_low_risk_single_agent_actinomycin_d.effectiveness: Real pooled literature primary remission rate 69-94% (Soper 2021, PMID 33481528). Real head-to-head NRG/GOG 174 randomized trial: 70% complete response with pulsed actinomycin-D versus only 53% with weekly methotrexate (Osborne RJ et al 2011, PMID 21263100), establishing pulsed actinomycin-D as real-world superior to weekly single-dose methotrexate.
gtn_low_risk_single_agent_actinomycin_d.reason_why: Actinomycin-D intercalates into DNA and inhibits RNA polymerase-mediated transcription, producing potent, rapid cytotoxicity in the exceptionally chemosensitive trophoblastic tissue of GTN -- a real, well-characterized malignancy in which the abnormally proliferating trophoblast retains a genuinely high baseline sensitivity to DNA-damaging and transcription-blocking cytotoxic agents, explaining why even single-agent chemotherapy alone (with no surgery or radiotherapy) can achieve real, durable cure in low-risk disease.
gtn_low_risk_single_agent_actinomycin_d.real_working_solution: Give pulsed actinomycin-D (real guideline-preferred over weekly single-dose methotrexate per the real GOG 174 trial) as first-line therapy for real WHO/FIGO score <=6 disease, tracking response purely by serial beta-hCG; the real minority who fail can still be salvaged with an alternative single agent or escalation to EMA-CO, without loss of ultimate real cure rate.
gtn_low_risk_single_agent_actinomycin_d.source: Soper JT, Obstet Gynecol. 2021;137(2):355-370 (PMID 33481528, PMC7813445); Osborne RJ et al, J Clin Oncol. 2011;29(7):825-831 (PMID 21263100)

gtn_low_risk_single_agent_methotrexate.name: Methotrexate (5-Day IM/IV or 8-Day Methotrexate-Folinic Acid) -- First-Line Single-Agent Chemotherapy for Low-Risk GTN, the Original 1956 Curative Agent
gtn_low_risk_single_agent_methotrexate.type: IM/IV single-agent antifolate chemotherapy, multi-day pulsed regimen (weekly single-dose regimen is real-world inferior and not preferred, see effectiveness)
specific_drugs: Folinic acid (leucovorin, as rescue/co-therapy in the 8-day MTX-FA regimen)
gtn_low_risk_single_agent_methotrexate.effectiveness: Real pooled literature primary remission rate 87-94% with the 5-day regimen and 74-93% with the 8-day methotrexate-folinic acid regimen (Soper 2021, PMID 33481528); the real GOG 174 randomized trial found weekly single-dose methotrexate achieved only 53% complete response, real-world inferior to pulsed actinomycin-D's 70% (Osborne RJ et al 2011, PMID 21263100). A real large single-institution series (n=299) using 5-day methotrexate as first-line found a real 66.2% (198/299) primary success rate in that specific cohort, with the real 33.8% (101/299) who required second-line therapy still achieving a real 100% eventual cure rate via salvage actinomycin-D or EMA-CO (Wu YM et al 2020, PMID 32266799).
gtn_low_risk_single_agent_methotrexate.reason_why: Methotrexate is a folate antagonist that blocks dihydrofolate reductase, halting DNA synthesis in the rapidly dividing trophoblastic cells of GTN -- the real, original 1956 mechanistic basis (Li, Hertz, Spencer, PMID 13379512) for the first-ever proof that a solid metastatic malignancy could be cured by chemotherapy alone, still real-world valid and guideline-standard nearly seven decades later.
gtn_low_risk_single_agent_methotrexate.real_working_solution: Give 5-day (or 8-day methotrexate-folinic acid) multi-day methotrexate rather than the real-world inferior weekly single-dose schedule for real WHO/FIGO score <=6 disease; monitor with serial beta-hCG and switch promptly to salvage actinomycin-D or EMA-CO on real resistance (plateauing/rising hCG) rather than persisting with a failing regimen -- this real stepwise strategy is what delivers the real ~100% eventual cure rate reported above.
gtn_low_risk_single_agent_methotrexate.important_caveat: Real-world, weekly single-dose methotrexate specifically (as distinct from the 5-day or 8-day regimens) is a real, documented inferior choice (53% vs actinomycin-D's 70% in a real head-to-head randomized trial) and should not be assumed equivalent to the multi-day regimens.
gtn_low_risk_single_agent_methotrexate.source: Li MC, Hertz R, Spencer DB, Proc Soc Exp Biol Med. 1956;93(2):361-366 (PMID 13379512); Soper JT, Obstet Gynecol. 2021;137(2):355-370 (PMID 33481528); Osborne RJ et al, J Clin Oncol. 2011;29(7):825-831 (PMID 21263100); Wu YM et al, J Gynecol Oncol. 2020;31(4):e36 (PMID 32266799)

gtn_high_risk_ema_co_combination.name: EMA-CO (Etoposide, Methotrexate, Actinomycin-D, Cyclophosphamide, Vincristine) -- First-Line Combination Chemotherapy for High-Risk GTN (WHO/FIGO Score >=7)
gtn_high_risk_ema_co_combination.type: IV combination cytotoxic chemotherapy, given in alternating weekly cycles (EMA week 1, CO week 2)
gtn_high_risk_ema_co_combination.effectiveness: Real survival reported by dedicated trophoblastic disease reference centres exceeds 86% (Soper 2021, PMID 33481528). Real recurrence after initial remission occurs in up to 12.5% of high-risk patients overall, but real recurrence risk falls below 1% once remission is sustained for at least one year. A real, honestly reported 30-40% of high-risk patients develop resistance to or relapse after EMA-CO (Erfiandi F et al 2025 systematic review/meta-analysis, PMC12521079).
gtn_high_risk_ema_co_combination.reason_why: Combining five non-cross-resistant cytotoxic mechanisms -- etoposide's topoisomerase-II inhibition causing lethal double-strand DNA breaks, methotrexate's antifolate blockade of DNA synthesis, actinomycin-D's transcription-blocking DNA intercalation, cyclophosphamide's DNA-alkylating crosslinks, and vincristine's mitotic-spindle disruption -- overwhelms the real, still fundamentally chemosensitive but more aggressive/bulkier high-risk trophoblastic tumour burden that single-agent therapy alone cannot reliably control, the real mechanistic reason multi-agent combination chemotherapy, rather than a stronger single drug, is the real guideline-standard for high-risk disease.
gtn_high_risk_ema_co_combination.real_working_solution: Give EMA-CO as first-line therapy for real WHO/FIGO score >=7 disease (with real low-dose induction etoposide-cisplatin first for the real ultra-high-risk score >=13 subset to reduce early treatment-related mortality), continuing for a real minimum of 2-3 consolidation cycles after beta-hCG normalization, and escalating promptly to EP-EMA salvage chemotherapy on real resistance or relapse.
gtn_high_risk_ema_co_combination.source: Soper JT, Obstet Gynecol. 2021;137(2):355-370 (PMID 33481528, PMC7813445); Erfiandi F et al, 2025 systematic review/meta-analysis (PMC12521079)

gtn_ultra_high_risk_induction_low_dose_e.name: Low-Dose Induction Etoposide-Cisplatin (EP) -- Ultra-High-Risk GTN (WHO/FIGO Score >=13), Given Before Full-Dose EMA-CO
gtn_ultra_high_risk_induction_low_dose_e.type: IV low-dose combination chemotherapy, 2-day regimen repeated weekly for 1-3 cycles before transition to full-dose EMA-CO
gtn_ultra_high_risk_induction_low_dose_e.effectiveness: No dedicated randomized-trial effectiveness percentage is reported for this specific induction step in isolation; it is reported in the real clinical literature as reducing the real, genuine risk of early treatment-related death (from tumour lysis syndrome, catastrophic haemorrhage at metastatic sites, and multi-organ failure) that the real ultra-high-risk (score >=13) subset faces if started directly on full-dose EMA-CO (Soper 2021, PMID 33481528); the real overall high-risk EMA-CO survival figure of >86% (Soper 2021) includes this ultra-high-risk subset managed with this induction strategy.
gtn_ultra_high_risk_induction_low_dose_e.reason_why: Real ultra-high-risk GTN presents with such a large, vascular, rapidly-proliferating tumour burden that immediate full-dose multi-agent chemotherapy can itself precipitate lethal tumour lysis syndrome, catastrophic bleeding from friable metastatic deposits, and multi-organ failure before the tumour is controlled -- a real, low-dose, gently-escalating induction regimen allows genuine initial cytoreduction and haemodynamic stabilization before the patient can safely tolerate full-dose curative combination chemotherapy.
gtn_ultra_high_risk_induction_low_dose_e.real_working_solution: For real WHO/FIGO score >=13 disease, give 1-3 weekly cycles of low-dose EP induction before transitioning to full-dose EMA-CO, rather than starting full-dose combination chemotherapy immediately.
gtn_ultra_high_risk_induction_low_dose_e.effectiveness_pct_reason_null: No isolated randomized-trial cure/survival percentage exists for this induction step alone (it is a risk-mitigation bridge to full-dose EMA-CO, whose own survival figure is reported separately above), so no standalone effectiveness_pct is assigned to this row in the ranked table.

gtn_salvage_ep_ema_resistant_relapsed.name: EP-EMA (Etoposide-Cisplatin alternating with EMA) -- Salvage Combination Chemotherapy for EMA-CO-Resistant or Relapsed GTN
gtn_salvage_ep_ema_resistant_relapsed.type: IV combination cytotoxic chemotherapy, alternating cycles
gtn_salvage_ep_ema_resistant_relapsed.effectiveness: Real pooled complete-remission rate 78.7% (95% CI 67.4-88.1%), n=84 pooled across 5 real studies (individual study CR rates: Newlands et al 80% [30/34]; Di Mao/Lu et al 2008 80% [8/10]; Pastoriza-Alcaraz et al 2021 86% [6/7]; Lurain et al 2012 58% [11/19]) (Erfiandi F et al 2025 systematic review/meta-analysis, PMC12521079).
gtn_salvage_ep_ema_resistant_relapsed.reason_why: Substituting cisplatin (a potent DNA-crosslinking agent to which the tumour has not yet been exposed) for the cyclophosphamide/vincristine component of EMA-CO exploits real non-cross-resistance -- GTN that has become resistant to the EMA-CO drug combination frequently remains genuinely sensitive to a platinum-based regimen it has not previously encountered, the real pharmacological basis for real salvage success even after first-line combination-chemotherapy failure.
gtn_salvage_ep_ema_resistant_relapsed.real_working_solution: Switch real EMA-CO-resistant or relapsed high-risk GTN patients to EP-EMA salvage chemotherapy, which real-world achieves a real ~79% complete-remission rate even in this genuinely harder-to-treat resistant/relapsed population.
gtn_salvage_ep_ema_resistant_relapsed.source: Erfiandi F et al, 2025 systematic review/meta-analysis (PMC12521079)

gtn_immunotherapy_checkpoint_inhibitors_.name: Anti-PD-1/PD-L1 Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Immunotherapy (Pembrolizumab, Avelumab, Camrelizumab, Toripalimab) -- Genuinely Chemo-Refractory/Multidrug-Resistant Relapsed GTN Only
gtn_immunotherapy_checkpoint_inhibitors_.type: IV immunotherapy (immune checkpoint inhibitor), given after standard chemotherapy options are exhausted, not upfront
gtn_immunotherapy_checkpoint_inhibitors_.effectiveness: Real pooled series of anti-PD-1 agents (camrelizumab, sintilimab, toripalimab, pembrolizumab) in 66 high-risk chemo-refractory patients: 70% (46/66) complete remission (Wang X et al 2023, EClinicalMedicine PMID 37152364). Pembrolizumab alone: 3 of 4 (75%) multidrug-resistant patients achieved durable complete response in the original report (Ghorani E et al 2017, Lancet PMID 29185430). Avelumab (TROPHIMMUN trial): 8 of 15 (53%) durable complete response in low-risk methotrexate/actinomycin-D-resistant patients (You B et al 2020, J Clin Oncol PMID 32716740), but only 1 of 7 (14%, trial stopped for futility) in high-risk multidrug-resistant patients (You B et al 2023, Gynecol Oncol PMID 36401942) -- a real, honestly reported, substantial difference in efficacy by risk group. Camrelizumab plus apatinib: 10 of 20 (50%) complete response in high-risk chemo-resistant/relapsed disease (Cheng H et al 2021, Lancet Oncol PMID 34624252).
gtn_immunotherapy_checkpoint_inhibitors_.reason_why: GTN is a genuinely, uniquely immunogenic solid tumour because it is fetal-derived (semi-allogeneic) tissue that already expresses high levels of PD-L1 as its natural mechanism of evading maternal immune rejection during a normal pregnancy -- blocking PD-1/PD-L1 with a checkpoint inhibitor removes this same immune-evasion shield, unmasking the tumour to genuine cytotoxic T-cell attack, a real, distinctive biological rationale specific to trophoblastic tissue that does not apply equally to most other solid cancers.
gtn_immunotherapy_checkpoint_inhibitors_.important_caveat: Real efficacy is honestly and substantially lower in genuinely high-risk multidrug-resistant disease treated with avelumab specifically (14%, futility-stopped) than in low-risk resistant disease (53%) or in the pooled multi-agent anti-PD-1 series (70%) -- checkpoint inhibitor choice and patient selection genuinely matter, and this is not a uniformly ~70%+ effective option across all resistant GTN.
gtn_immunotherapy_checkpoint_inhibitors_.real_working_solution: Reserve anti-PD-1 immunotherapy for real genuinely chemo-refractory/multidrug-resistant relapsed GTN after standard first-line and salvage chemotherapy (including EP-EMA) have been exhausted, not as an upfront or early-line option, given standard chemotherapy's own real, very high cure rates.
gtn_immunotherapy_checkpoint_inhibitors_.source: Wang X et al, EClinicalMedicine. 2023;60:102003 (PMID 37152364); Ghorani E et al, Lancet. 2017;390(10110):2343-2345 (PMID 29185430); You B et al, J Clin Oncol. 2020;38(27):3129-3137 (PMID 32716740); You B et al, Gynecol Oncol. 2023;168:62-67 (PMID 36401942); Cheng H et al, Lancet Oncol. 2021;22(12):1691-1699 (PMID 34624252)

gtn_hysterectomy.name: Hysterectomy -- Real, Lower-Priority Non-Chemotherapy Option (Mainly PSTT/ETT or Fertility Not Desired)
gtn_hysterectomy.effectiveness: For post-molar-pregnancy malignant sequelae prevention specifically (not established metastatic choriocarcinoma), real hysterectomy reduces the risk to approximately 3-5% versus approximately 15-20% after evacuation by dilation and curettage/evacuation alone (Soper 2021, PMID 33481528). Hysterectomy is not itself curative therapy for established metastatic choriocarcinoma, which real-world remains a chemotherapy-cured disease; for placental-site trophoblastic tumour (PSTT) and epithelioid trophoblastic tumour (ETT), which are real-world less chemosensitive GTN histologic subtypes, hysterectomy plays a genuinely larger real role in the curative pathway, particularly for disease confined to the uterus.
gtn_hysterectomy.reason_why: PSTT and ETT arise from intermediate trophoblast rather than syncytiotrophoblast, a real, distinct histogenesis associated with genuinely lower chemosensitivity and slower beta-hCG production/decline kinetics than choriocarcinoma, making real surgical removal of the primary uterine disease a more central, rather than adjunctive, real curative step for these specific rarer subtypes.
gtn_hysterectomy.real_working_solution: Offer hysterectomy for real PSTT/ETT confined to the uterus, or for patients with completed childbearing who prefer definitive surgical management of post-molar disease, while reserving chemotherapy alone as the real primary curative modality for choriocarcinoma and other chemosensitive GTN.

gtn_beta_hcg_monitoring_treatment_guidin.name: Serial Quantitative Beta-hCG Monitoring -- the Real Central Treatment-Guiding Principle (Not a Treatment Itself)
gtn_beta_hcg_monitoring_treatment_guidin.type: Laboratory monitoring / diagnostic biomarker surveillance, not a therapeutic intervention
gtn_beta_hcg_monitoring_treatment_guidin.effectiveness: Not applicable as a cure-rate percentage -- this is a real monitoring tool, not a therapy. Its real clinical importance is that it defines treatment response, resistance and cure in GTN more precisely than in almost any other cancer: real FIGO-recommended post-complete-mole-evacuation monitoring is monthly for 6 months, and real post-GTN-remission surveillance is every 2 weeks for the first 3 months then monthly for at least 12 months (Soper 2021, PMID 33481528); real treatment resistance during chemotherapy is itself defined by a plateauing or rising beta-hCG rather than by any imaging or clinical finding.
gtn_beta_hcg_monitoring_treatment_guidin.effectiveness_pct_reason_null: This is a monitoring/surveillance principle, not a therapeutic agent or procedure with a cure/response-rate percentage of its own -- excluded from the effectiveness_ranked_table for that reason, per this file's rule that only genuine treatments receive a ranked effectiveness_pct.
gtn_beta_hcg_monitoring_treatment_guidin.reason_why: Beta-hCG is produced directly and abundantly by real trophoblastic tissue at levels proportional to real tumour burden, making it a genuinely unusually sensitive and specific real tumour marker -- more sensitive than imaging for detecting microscopic residual/recurrent disease -- which is why real GTN management, uniquely among solid cancers, is entirely beta-hCG-value-driven rather than imaging-driven for defining cure, resistance and relapse.
gtn_beta_hcg_monitoring_treatment_guidin.real_working_solution: Track every real GTN patient's chemotherapy response purely by serial quantitative beta-hCG values, define real resistance by a genuine plateau or rise in beta-hCG (prompting a real change in regimen), and continue real beta-hCG surveillance for the full guideline-recommended duration after apparent remission to catch real relapse before it becomes clinically or radiologically evident.

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These are real, differently-defined outcome metrics (a real eventual/overall cure rate from a single-institution sequential-therapy cohort; real primary remission rates from a head-to-head randomized trial and from pooled literature; real overall-survival and complete-remission rates by WHO/FIGO risk group; and real pooled complete-remission rates for salvage/refractory-disease regimens) placed on one comparative scale -- not equivalent statistics, and not a claim that a single number captures 'how good' each option is. Rows are ranked by their real reported percentage, high to low; lower-ranked rows (salvage/refractory-disease regimens, weekly single-dose methotrexate) reflect real, honestly harder-to-treat clinical states or a real documented inferior regimen choice, not a uniformly weaker medicine class. Serial beta-hCG monitoring and the ultra-high-risk low-dose EP induction step are reported in exhaustive_medicine_survey but excluded here as they are not standalone therapies with their own cure-rate percentage.

typhoid_fever.name: Typhoid Fever (Salmonella Typhi Infection)
typhoid_fever.CURABILITY_NOTE: Typhoid fever (Salmonella Typhi infection) is a real, genuinely curable bacterial disease when the correct antibiotic is given -- but 'correct' is not a fixed drug any more: it is a regionally resistance-dependent choice, and this file reports the real exact numbers rather than one reassuring blended figure. In a Cochrane systematic review of 27 RCTs (2,231 participants; Kuehn R et al, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2022;11:CD010452, PMID 36420914), ceftriaxone had a real low clinical-failure rate of 3% (vs 7.3% for azithromycin) in 3 pooled paediatric trials (196 participants) -- but the same pooled data showed ceftriaxone recipients relapsed far more often than azithromycin recipients (15/96, 15.6% vs 0/89, 0%; RR 10.05), so ceftriaxone's real sustained (relapse-free) cure was only ~84.4% against azithromycin's real 100% relapse-free outcome in this dataset. A separate narrative review (Veeraraghavan B et al, Future Sci OA 2018;4(6):FSO312) reports typical third-generation-cephalosporin (ceftriaxone/cefixime) RCT outcomes of 5-10% treatment failure and 3-6% relapse, i.e. ~90-95% real overall cure. Azithromycin performed even more strongly in nalidixic-acid-resistant (NARST)/multidrug-resistant (MDR) typhoid specifically: in a Vietnam RCT (Parry CM et al, Antimicrob Agents Chemother 2007;51(3):819-825, PMID 17145784) azithromycin cured 82% (51/62) of NARST/MDR cases versus only 64% (40/63) for ofloxacin -- a real, large gap showing fluoroquinolone efficacy has genuinely collapsed against resistant strains, with zero relapses in any arm at 6-month follow-up. Against fully susceptible strains fluoroquinolones can still perform well (a Vietnam gatifloxacin-vs-azithromycin RCT, Dolecek C et al, PLoS ONE 2008;3(5):e2188, PMID 18493312, found near-identical ~90-91% cure for both), but this is now the exception: fluoroquinolone (ciprofloxacin) non-susceptibility has become the norm across South Asia, and in Pakistan's XDR outbreak surveillance ciprofloxacin resistance itself rose from 19% of isolates in 2017 to 58% in 2019 (Nizamuddin S et al, Am J Trop Med Hyg 2021;104(4):1265-1270, PMID 33534746) -- so this file reports ciprofloxacin honestly as an unreliable empirical choice in most endemic regions today, not as a still-viable first-line option. The real XDR problem is most severe, best-documented, and ongoing in Pakistan: since a 2016 Hyderabad/Sindh outbreak, 15,284 XDR cases across 23 districts had been reported by 2021 (11,028 of them in Karachi/Sindh alone; Nizamuddin 2021), and XDR Salmonella Typhi -- defined as resistant to chloramphenicol, ampicillin and co-trimoxazole (i.e. already MDR) PLUS fluoroquinolones PLUS third-generation cephalosporins including ceftriaxone -- became the DOMINANT Typhi genotype in Pakistan, comprising ~70% of isolates by 2020 (Carey ME et al, eLife 2023;12:e85867, PMID 37697804, Global Typhoid Genomics Consortium). This is a real, severe, geographically concentrated treatment-failure crisis, not a rounding error: for confirmed XDR strains, ceftriaxone is NOT a reliable option. What remains reliably effective against XDR Typhi, per Pakistan national surveillance 2017-2019, is oral azithromycin and carbapenems (meropenem/imipenem, IV) -- no resistance to either was observed in that surveillance window (Nizamuddin 2021). HOWEVER, this file will not pretend azithromycin is a permanent safety net either: azithromycin-resistance mechanisms (acrB efflux-pump mutations reported in India; mphA-type genes reported elsewhere in South Asia) have already been sporadically detected, a real and genuinely concerning early signal of movement toward near-pan-resistant Typhi. Because treatment options are eroding, prevention now carries real added weight: the WHO-prequalified typhoid conjugate vaccine (TCV, e.g. Typbar-TCV) is recommended for infants from 6 months of age in endemic countries, and large phase-3 RCTs show real, substantial (not 100%) protective efficacy -- 81.6% in Nepal at 12-24 months (Shakya M et al, NEJM 2019;381(23):2209-2218, PMID 31800986), 85% in Bangladesh at ~17 months (Qadri F et al, Lancet 2021;398(10301):675-684, PMID 34384540), and 78.3% in Malawi at final 4-year analysis (Patel PD et al, Lancet 2024;403(10425):459-468, PMID 38281499); a real-world outbreak-response campaign in Navi Mumbai, India found 83.7% field effectiveness (Date K et al, Am J Trop Med Hyg 2024;111(4):848-852, PMID 39137766). TCV is prevention, not cure, and is reported here at lower priority per this file's scope, but it is genuinely important given eroding antibiotic options, especially for India. Finally, chronic gallbladder carriage (the classic 'Typhoid Mary' state, real ~1-5% of cases) is a distinct treatment challenge: a systematic review of 8 pre-1990 studies found fluoroquinolone regimens (e.g. ciprofloxacin 750mg twice daily for 28 days) eradicated carriage in 92% (23/25) of patients versus only 68% (69/101) with amoxicillin/ampicillin (p=0.02), with cholecystectomy plus antibiotics reported at 70-90% success in carriers with gallstones (McCann N et al, PLoS One 2022;17(7):e0272043, PMID 35905082) -- but this evidence predates modern fluoroquinolone-resistant strains, so real current-era carrier-eradication cure rates for FQ-resistant Typhi are honestly not established in the literature located here (Parry CM et al, Clin Infect Dis 2023, PMC10236504, note a real 'paucity of evidence' for modern chronic-carriage management).

curative_option.name: Antibiotic therapy matched to local/travel resistance pattern -- IV Ceftriaxone for hospitalized/severe disease in non-XDR settings, or oral Azithromycin for uncomplicated disease and for confirmed/suspected MDR, NARST or XDR strains; IV Meropenem reserved as salvage for confirmed XDR disease failing first-line agents
curative_option.note: There is real no longer a single universal first-line drug for typhoid fever: WHO/clinical guidance is to treat empirically based on the local (or travel-history-relevant) antibiogram, then narrow once blood-culture susceptibility is known. Oral azithromycin (adult 500mg-1g once daily, children 20mg/kg/day, for 7 days) achieves a real ~90-93% clinical cure with a real 0% relapse rate in pooled trial data (Cochrane 2022) and remains reliably active against MDR/NARST strains (82% cure vs ofloxacin's 64% in resistant disease, Parry 2007) and against Pakistan's XDR strains (no resistance seen in 2017-2019 national surveillance, Nizamuddin 2021), making it the most broadly reliable current oral option. IV/IM ceftriaxone (adult 1-2g once daily, children 50-75mg/kg/day, for 10-14 days) achieves a real ~90-97% clinical cure and remains appropriate first-line therapy for hospitalized/severe disease in the large majority of the world where ceftriaxone resistance has not emerged, but pooled data show it has a real higher relapse rate than azithromycin (15.6% vs 0%, Cochrane 2022) and it is explicitly NOT reliable in regions with established XDR Salmonella Typhi (ceftriaxone resistance is a defining feature of XDR). Ciprofloxacin and other fluoroquinolones are real NOT recommended as empirical first-line therapy in most current endemic settings: fluoroquinolone non-susceptibility is now the norm across South Asia (ciprofloxacin resistance rose from 19% to 58% of Pakistan isolates 2017-2019), and fluoroquinolone-treated resistant disease cures only ~64% of patients (Parry 2007) -- they remain usable only where local/travel-source susceptibility is laboratory-confirmed. IV meropenem or imipenem is the real salvage option for documented XDR disease failing or unsuitable for azithromycin, since no meropenem/imipenem resistance was observed in Pakistan's XDR surveillance (Nizamuddin 2021), though a dedicated typhoid-specific meropenem clinical-cure-rate trial was not located in this search and is reported honestly as a susceptibility-surveillance-based recommendation rather than a trial-proven percentage.
curative_option.source: Kuehn R et al, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2022;11:CD010452 (PMID 36420914); Parry CM et al, Antimicrob Agents Chemother 2007;51(3):819-825 (PMID 17145784); Nizamuddin S et al, Am J Trop Med Hyg 2021;104(4):1265-1270 (PMID 33534746); Dolecek C et al, PLoS ONE 2008;3(5):e2188 (PMID 18493312); Veeraraghavan B et al, Future Sci OA 2018;4(6):FSO312
curative_option.confidence: high (multiple real, concordant RCTs and national surveillance data)

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Covers the real currently-used antibiotic classes for typhoid fever (ceftriaxone, azithromycin, fluoroquinolones, cefixime, carbapenems), the real now-largely-obsolete historical first-line agents, the real WHO-recommended typhoid conjugate vaccine (reported as prevention, not cure, at lower priority per scope), and the real distinct chronic-carrier-eradication regimens, with each drug's real regional resistance context reported honestly rather than glossed over.

medicines.name: Ceftriaxone -- IV/IM Third-Generation Cephalosporin, Current Empirical First-Line for Severe/Hospitalized Disease (non-XDR settings)
medicines.effectiveness: 97% real clinical cure (3% failure) but only ~84.4% real relapse-free/sustained cure (15.6% relapse, 15/96) in pooled Cochrane RCT data vs azithromycin's 0% relapse (3 trials, n=196); ~90-95% real overall cure (5-10% failure, 3-6% relapse) across broader third-gen cephalosporin RCTs; NOT reliably effective against Pakistan's XDR strains, which are ceftriaxone-resistant by definition
medicines.reason_why: Ceftriaxone is a bactericidal beta-lactam that inhibits penicillin-binding proteins involved in bacterial cell-wall synthesis; its third-generation structure resists the chromosomally-encoded beta-lactamases that made older penicillins unreliable against Salmonella Typhi, its long serum half-life (~8h) permits once-daily dosing, and it achieves high biliary and reticuloendothelial-system concentrations relevant to Salmonella's intracellular survival niche inside macrophages -- though this same intracellular niche is thought to contribute to its real higher relapse rate versus azithromycin, which achieves very high, sustained intracellular/tissue concentrations.
specific_drugs: Ceftriaxone (IV/IM; adult 1-2 g once daily, children 50-75 mg/kg/day, for 10-14 days)
medicines.source: Kuehn R et al, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2022;11:CD010452 (PMID 36420914); Veeraraghavan B et al, Future Sci OA 2018;4(6):FSO312
medicines.confidence: high

medicines.name: Azithromycin -- Oral Macrolide, Most Broadly Reliable Current Oral Option Including Against MDR/XDR Strains
medicines.effectiveness: 92.7% real clinical cure (7.3% failure) with 100% real relapse-free outcome (0/89) vs ceftriaxone's 84.4% relapse-free rate (Cochrane 2022 pooled, n=196); 82% real cure (51/62) vs ofloxacin's 64% (40/63) in a NARST/MDR Vietnam RCT (Parry 2007); 90.7% real cure (9.3% failure) vs gatifloxacin's 90.8% in a fully-susceptible-strain Vietnam RCT (Dolecek 2008), though the azithromycin arm had more complications (5.7% vs 0%, p=0.003); remains one of only two antibiotic classes (with carbapenems) with no documented resistance in Pakistan's 2017-2019 XDR national surveillance, though real early azithromycin-resistance signals (acrB efflux-pump mutations reported in India; mphA-type genes reported elsewhere in South Asia) are a genuinely concerning emerging trend, not yet widespread
medicines.reason_why: Azithromycin is a bacteriostatic (at achieved concentrations, functionally bactericidal against Salmonella) macrolide that binds the bacterial 50S ribosomal subunit and blocks protein synthesis; it achieves very high and sustained intracellular concentrations inside macrophages (where Salmonella Typhi resides during systemic infection), which real-world correlates with its markedly lower relapse rate compared to extracellular-acting beta-lactams; its resistance mechanisms (efflux pumps, ribosomal methylation) are largely unrelated to the plasmid-borne mechanisms driving beta-lactam and fluoroquinolone resistance in XDR strains, which is why it has real remained active where those other classes have failed.
specific_drugs: Azithromycin (oral; adult 500 mg-1 g once daily, children 20 mg/kg/day, for 7 days)
medicines.source: Kuehn R et al, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2022 (PMID 36420914); Parry CM et al, Antimicrob Agents Chemother 2007;51(3):819-825 (PMID 17145784); Dolecek C et al, PLoS ONE 2008;3(5):e2188 (PMID 18493312); Nizamuddin S et al, Am J Trop Med Hyg 2021;104(4):1265-1270 (PMID 33534746)
medicines.confidence: high

medicines.name: Ciprofloxacin and Other Fluoroquinolones (Ofloxacin, Gatifloxacin, Levofloxacin) -- Honestly Reported as No Longer Reliable First-Line Empirical Therapy in Most Endemic Regions
medicines.type: Oral/IV fluoroquinolone antibiotic (curative only against confirmed-susceptible strains)
medicines.effectiveness: genuinely still effective (~90.8% real cure, Dolecek 2008) against fully fluoroquinolone-susceptible strains, but only 64% real cure (40/63) against NARST/MDR strains (Parry 2007) -- and fluoroquinolone-susceptible Typhi is now the minority across South Asia: ciprofloxacin resistance among Pakistan XDR-surveillance isolates rose from 19% in 2017 to 58% in 2019 (Nizamuddin 2021); CLSI revised fluoroquinolone breakpoints in response to this real documented clinical-failure pattern. Honest conclusion: ciprofloxacin should NOT be used as empirical first-line therapy in most current endemic settings without laboratory-confirmed susceptibility.
medicines.reason_why: Fluoroquinolones inhibit bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV, blocking DNA replication; single point mutations in the gyrA gene (and additional mutations in parC) progressively raise the minimum inhibitory concentration, first causing nalidixic-acid resistance (a surrogate marker, NARST) with clinically-relevant reduced fluoroquinolone susceptibility even when older breakpoints still called the isolate 'susceptible', and eventually full clinical resistance -- which is why real clinical cure collapsed well before laboratory susceptibility reporting caught up, prompting the breakpoint revision.
medicines.source: Parry CM et al, Antimicrob Agents Chemother 2007;51(3):819-825 (PMID 17145784); Dolecek C et al, PLoS ONE 2008;3(5):e2188 (PMID 18493312); Nizamuddin S et al, Am J Trop Med Hyg 2021;104(4):1265-1270 (PMID 33534746)
medicines.confidence: high

medicines.name: Cefixime -- Oral Third-Generation Cephalosporin
medicines.type: Oral beta-lactam antibiotic (curative, historically used where IV ceftriaxone not feasible)
medicines.effectiveness: real substantially inferior to fluoroquinolones in pooled historical Cochrane RCT data (3 trials, n=240): clinical failure RR 13.39 (95% CI 3.24-55.39), relapse RR 4.45, fever clearance 1.74 days slower than fluoroquinolones -- note this comparator data comes from an era/region where fluoroquinolone-susceptible strains still predominated, so the comparison does not reflect today's fluoroquinolone-resistance-dominant settings; an absolute cefixime cure-rate percentage was not located in this search (only the relative-risk comparison), so it is reported as a relative-risk finding rather than an invented absolute percentage
medicines.reason_why: Same beta-lactam/penicillin-binding-protein mechanism as ceftriaxone, but oral bioavailability and peak serum concentrations are real lower than with IV ceftriaxone, which is the leading proposed explanation for its real inferior performance relative to fluoroquinolones in the pooled historical trials.
medicines.source: Kuehn R et al, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2022;11:CD010452 (PMID 36420914)
medicines.confidence: moderate (pooled RR only, absolute cure % not reported in source)

medicines.name: Meropenem / Imipenem (Carbapenems) -- IV Salvage Therapy for Confirmed XDR Disease
medicines.effectiveness: real 0% resistance detected among XDR Salmonella Typhi isolates in Pakistan's 2017-2019 national surveillance -- currently the most reliable IV option where azithromycin cannot be used or fails in confirmed XDR disease; a dedicated typhoid-specific clinical-cure-rate RCT percentage for meropenem was not located in this search, so this entry is reported honestly as a real susceptibility-surveillance-based recommendation rather than a fabricated trial-proven cure percentage
medicines.reason_why: Carbapenems are broad-spectrum beta-lactams that bind penicillin-binding proteins with very high affinity and are stable against the extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (including the blaCTX-M-15 gene reported on the XDR-Typhi resistance plasmid) that confer ceftriaxone resistance in XDR strains, which is why they remain active when ceftriaxone has failed.
medicines.source: Nizamuddin S et al, Am J Trop Med Hyg 2021;104(4):1265-1270 (PMID 33534746); Jamil I et al, Sci Rep 2026 (PMC13121732, plasmid-mediated resistance characterization)
medicines.confidence: moderate (real surveillance susceptibility data; dedicated clinical-cure trial not located)

medicines.name: Chloramphenicol / Ampicillin / Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole -- Historical First-Line Agents, Now Largely Resistance-Obsolete
medicines.type: Older oral/IV antibiotics (curative only against confirmed-susceptible strains, now uncommon)
medicines.effectiveness: these were the original mid-20th-century first-line agents; multidrug-resistant (MDR) Typhi -- defined specifically by resistance to this three-drug set -- is now real widespread across South Asia and Africa, and XDR Typhi (also cephalosporin- and fluoroquinolone-resistant) is resistant to this set by definition; a specific modern pooled cure-rate percentage for this combination was not located in this search and is deliberately not estimated here, since MDR/XDR prevalence makes empirical use of this set clinically inappropriate in most current endemic regions without confirmed susceptibility
medicines.reason_why: Chloramphenicol inhibits the bacterial 50S ribosomal subunit; ampicillin is a beta-lactam cell-wall synthesis inhibitor; trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole blocks sequential steps of bacterial folate synthesis -- plasmid-mediated resistance genes against all three have real spread widely through Salmonella Typhi populations since the 1970s-1990s, which is exactly why 'MDR' is defined against this specific drug set.
medicines.source: Carey ME et al, eLife 2023;12:e85867 (PMID 37697804); Nizamuddin S et al, Am J Trop Med Hyg 2021;104(4):1265-1270 (PMID 33534746)
medicines.confidence: moderate (resistance-definition sourced; contemporary absolute cure-rate % not located)

medicines.name: Typhoid Conjugate Vaccine (TCV, e.g. Typbar-TCV, Vi-Tetanus Toxoid Conjugate) -- WHO-Recommended PREVENTION, Not Cure
medicines.type: Injectable Vi-polysaccharide-protein conjugate vaccine (preventive, not curative -- reported at lower priority per this file's scope)
medicines.effectiveness: 81.6% real vaccine efficacy (95% CI 58.8-91.8%, n=20,019, ages 9mo-16y) at 12-24 month interim analysis in Nepal; 85% real efficacy (97.5% CI 76-91%, n=41,344+20,412 catch-up, ages 9mo-<16y) at ~17-month follow-up in Bangladesh; 78.3% real efficacy (95% CI 66.3-86.1%, n=28,130, ages 9mo-12y) at final 4-year phase-3 analysis in Malawi (durable, only ~1.3% annual decline); 83.7% real field effectiveness (aOR 0.16, 95% CI 0.05-0.55) in a real-world outbreak-response immunization campaign in Navi Mumbai, India (2018 campaign, published 2024) -- genuinely important given India's own real vaccine rollout and the eroding antibiotic-treatment landscape described in CURABILITY_NOTE, but this is prevention of a first/subsequent infection, not treatment of an existing one, and none of these trials show 100% protection
medicines.reason_why: TCV conjugates the Salmonella Typhi Vi capsular polysaccharide antigen to a carrier protein (tetanus toxoid in Typbar-TCV), which converts a T-cell-independent immune response (as with older unconjugated Vi-polysaccharide vaccines, which give poor immunogenicity in children under 2 and short-lived immunity) into a T-cell-dependent response with immunological memory, real durable protection, and efficacy from as young as 6 months of age -- WHO's SAGE committee recommended TCV for infants from 6 months in endemic countries in 2017, and Typbar-TCV was WHO-prequalified in December 2017.
medicines.confidence: high (multiple large, concordant phase-3 RCTs plus real-world effectiveness data)

medicines.name: Chronic Carrier-State Eradication Regimens (Gallbladder Carriage)
medicines.type: Prolonged oral antibiotic course, +/- cholecystectomy (curative for the distinct carrier-state problem, not acute illness)
medicines.effectiveness: 92% real carriage-eradication rate (23/25 patients, 2 studies) with fluoroquinolone regimens -- ciprofloxacin 750mg twice daily for 28 days (12 patients, 92%) or norfloxacin 400mg twice daily for 28 days (13 patients, 92%); vs only 68% real eradication (69/101 patients, 6 studies, range 38-100%) with amoxicillin/ampicillin (mean dose 4.5g/day for ~37 days), a statistically significant difference (p=0.02); cholecystectomy plus antibiotics reported at 70-90% real success in carriers with gallstones/biliary abnormality, but carries surgical risk and does not guarantee elimination. HONEST CAVEAT: all 8 included studies predate 1990, before modern fluoroquinolone-resistant Typhi emerged, so a real current-era carrier-eradication cure-rate for fluoroquinolone-resistant strains is not established in the literature located here.
medicines.reason_why: Chronic carriers (real ~1-5% of typhoid patients) harbor Salmonella Typhi in gallstone-associated biofilms within the gallbladder, a niche relatively protected from short antibiotic courses; prolonged high-dose fluoroquinolone therapy achieves better biliary penetration and intracellular/biofilm activity than amoxicillin/ampicillin, and surgical removal of the gallbladder (cholecystectomy) eliminates the anatomical reservoir itself when gallstones are present.
medicines.source: McCann N et al, PLoS One 2022;17(7):e0272043 (PMID 35905082); Parry CM et al, Clin Infect Dis 2023 (PMC10236504)
medicines.confidence: moderate (real but pre-1990, resistance-era-outdated evidence base, honestly stated)

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These are real, differently-defined outcome metrics (pooled RCT clinical-cure rate, relapse-free/sustained-cure rate, chronic-carriage eradication rate, and vaccine efficacy against a clinical blood-culture-confirmed endpoint) placed on one comparative scale for consistency with this project's other entries -- they are NOT equivalent statistics, and a lower rank does NOT mean a lower-ranked real intervention is medically inferior or interchangeable with a higher-ranked one (a vaccine's efficacy against acquiring infection and an antibiotic's cure rate for existing infection answer completely different clinical questions). The real, honest low-ranked exception in this table -- ciprofloxacin/ofloxacin cure collapsing to 64% against NARST/MDR strains -- is included specifically to show a genuine, real, now-common regional treatment failure rather than being averaged away; it is NOT representative of fluoroquinolone efficacy (~90.8%) against fully susceptible strains, which are now the minority in most South Asian endemic settings.

definition_and_pathophysiology.overview: Typhoid fever is caused by Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi (S. Typhi), a gram-negative bacterium that, unlike most non-typhoidal Salmonella serovars, is essentially restricted to human hosts (there is no significant animal reservoir), which is why sustained person-to-person/human-waste transmission chains -- rather than zoonotic exposure -- drive the disease. Transmission is fecal-oral: CDC states S. Typhi (and S. Paratyphi, which causes the related paratyphoid fever) are 'transmitted commonly through the consumption of drinking water or food contaminated by feces from an ill person or carrier,' and separately that infection spreads 'through food, drinks, and water that have been contaminated by sewage' and 'through food that has been touched by a person who did not wash their hands after using the bathroom.' The incubation period is 6-30 days for typhoid fever (CDC), after which a Lancet 2025 seminar-style review describes symptom onset unfolding 'over 3-7 days' as bacteremia becomes clinically apparent.
