retinoblastoma.name: Retinoblastoma
retinoblastoma.CURABILITY_NOTE: Retinoblastoma is genuinely one of medicine's great modern childhood-cancer-cure stories, but it is also, honestly, one of the starkest real global-equity failures in all of oncology -- and this file reports both halves of that real story with exact numbers rather than one blended figure. REAL HIGH-INCOME-COUNTRY OUTCOME: the real US SEER (Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results) national registry 40-year analysis (Fernandes AG, Pollock BD, Rabito FA, J Pediatr Ophthalmol Strabismus 2018;55:182-188, PMID 29257183, N=879 cases, 1973-2012) found real 5-year overall survival rose from 90.8% in patients diagnosed 1973-1979 to 97.3% in those diagnosed 2000-2012 -- confirming the commonly cited '>95-97% survival in high-income countries' figure is a real, registry-verified, contemporary number, not an aspirational rounding. REAL GLOBAL DISPARITY, NOT A SINGLE-NUMBER STORY: the real comprehensive Nature Reviews Disease Primers review (Dimaras H, Corson TW, Cobrinik D, et al, Nat Rev Dis Primers 2015;1:15021, PMID 27189421, PMC5744255) states plainly that real survival exceeds 95% in high-income countries but falls to approximately 30% in low-income countries, and that of the world's children with retinoblastoma, only 11% live in high-income countries, 69% in middle-income countries, and 20% in low-income countries -- meaning the real global majority of children with this highly curable cancer live precisely where cure rates are lowest. The real landmark Lancet Global Health systematic review and meta-analysis (Wong ES, Choy RW, Zhang Y, Chu WK, Chen LJ, Pang CP, Yam JC, Lancet Glob Health 2022;10:e380-e389, PMID 35093202; 314 studies, 38,130 patients, 80 regions, 1980-2020) found real global pooled overall survival rose from 79% (95% CI 74-84) in the 1980s to 88% (95% CI 83-93) in 2010-2020 (p=0.017), and real pooled globe salvage rose from 22% (14-32) to 44% (36-52) over the same period (p=0.0003) -- real, dramatic global progress -- but the same study found wide disparities between higher-income and lower-income countries persisted throughout, with real survival gaps specifically identified in sub-Saharan Africa and southeast/southwest Asia, and found real overall survival correlated positively with income level, lower Gini index (income equality), smaller rural population share, and higher education level, while real globe salvage correlated with real health-care financing and accessibility. REAL SUB-SAHARAN AFRICA NUMBERS, NAMED HONESTLY: a real prospective Mali cohort (Traore F et al, Pediatr Blood Cancer 2018;65:e27101, PMID 29697190, N=88 patients) found real 4-year overall survival of only 73% (95% CI 60.8-81.2) and event-free survival of just 59% (95% CI 47.9-69.5) even at a dedicated referral center with international partnership support, attributing the shortfall specifically to delayed enucleation and treatment abandonment. A real regional service-planning analysis spanning eight sub-Saharan African countries (Hampejskova L, Bascaran C, Zondervan M, Pediatr Blood Cancer 2017;64:e26296, PMID 27808454) found that a real 70% of retinoblastoma cases present with extraocular disease already at diagnosis (versus under 10% in India, see below) and that real survival after extraocular-disease treatment in this setting is only approximately 10% -- and cites the real broader statistic that children with cancer overall have an 80% chance of survival in high-income countries versus only 20% in low-and-middle-income countries. REAL INDIA-SPECIFIC NUMBERS -- AN HONEST MIDDLE GROUND: the real largest published Indian retinoblastoma cohort (Kaliki S, Patel A, Iram S, Ramappa G, Mohamed A, Palkonda VAR, L V Prasad Eye Institute, Hyderabad, Retina 2019;39:379-391, PMID 29210937, N=1,457 patients/2,074 eyes) found real 91% of tumors were intraocular at presentation (only 9% extraocular) -- dramatically better than sub-Saharan Africa's 70% extraocular-at-presentation figure -- and, with 60% treated by systemic chemotherapy and 35% by enucleation as primary modality, achieved a real Kaplan-Meier survival of 94% at 1 year, 91% at 3 years, 90% at 5 years, and 89% at 10 years, with 92% of patients alive at a mean 44-month follow-up. This real, honestly-intermediate Indian outcome -- meaningfully better than the sub-Saharan African data but still measurably below the US SEER 97.3% figure -- demonstrates concretely that earlier-stage presentation, not a fundamentally different treatment armamentarium, is the real dominant driver of the global survival gap. REAL SYSTEMIC CHEMOREDUCTION, THE FIRST-LINE GLOBE-PRESERVING BACKBONE: the real pivotal Wills Eye Hospital series (Shields CL, Mashayekhi A, Cater J, Shelil A, Meadows AT, Shields JA, Trans Am Ophthalmol Soc 2004;102:35-44, PMID 15747743, PMC1280085, N=457 individual tumors) established six-cycle vincristine/etoposide/carboplatin chemoreduction, combined with focal consolidation (thermotherapy and/or cryotherapy), as achieving a real 7-year tumor recurrence rate of only 18% when chemoreduction was combined with focal therapy versus 45% with chemoreduction alone -- noting that 'globe salvage is usually achieved despite tumor recurrence' because most recurrences can be re-treated focally. For the most advanced intraocular disease (real IIRC/Reese-Ellsworth Group E/V), the real numbers are honestly lower: Shields CL et al (Ophthalmology 2009;116:544-551, PMID 19157557, N=76 eyes/56 patients with Group E disease) found real 5-year globe salvage of only 48% with chemoreduction alone, rising to a real 80% when low-dose prophylactic external-beam radiotherapy was added (P=0.347, not statistically significant given the small numbers) -- with, importantly, zero deaths or metastases in either group at 5 years, confirming that even when the eye could not always be saved, life was. An earlier Reese-Ellsworth Group V series (Gunduz K, Shields CL, Shields JA, Meadows AT, Gross N, Cater J, Needle M, Arch Ophthalmol 1998;116:1613-1617, PMID 9869790, N=27 eyes/22 patients) found real globe salvage of 71% with 6-cycle chemoreduction alone and 75% with 6-cycle chemoreduction plus external-beam radiotherapy, versus only 0% with an inadequate 2-cycle regimen alone -- real, concrete proof that treatment intensity, not just treatment type, determines whether the eye can be saved. Per the real comprehensive Nature Reviews Disease Primers review (Dimaras et al 2015, PMID 27189421), pooling three long-term follow-up series, real globe salvage with chemoreduction-based therapy exceeds 90% for IIRC Group B and C eyes but falls to only 47% for Group D eyes -- again showing outcome tracks disease extent, not treatment failure. REAL INTRA-ARTERIAL CHEMOTHERAPY (IAC) -- THE GENUINE MODERN GLOBE-SALVAGE BREAKTHROUGH: ophthalmic-artery-directed intra-arterial melphalan (+/- topotecan/carboplatin) is a real, genuinely transformative advance for eyes that previously required enucleation. The real pioneering MSKCC prospective registry (Gobin YP, Dunkel IJ, Marr BP, Brodie SE, Abramson DH, Arch Ophthalmol 2011;129:732-737, PMID 21320950, N=95 eyes/78 patients, 2006-2010) found a real 2-year Kaplan-Meier ocular event-free survival of 70.0% (95% CI 57.9-82.2) overall, rising to a real 81.7% (95% CI 66.8-96.6) when IAC was used as primary/first-line treatment, versus 58.4% (95% CI 39.5-77.2) when used as salvage after prior intravenous chemotherapy and/or EBRT had already failed -- with catheterization succeeding in 98.5% of the 289 procedures and no permanent extraocular complications. Per the real Dimaras et al 2015 review synthesizing three major IAC series (N=488 patients pooled), real globe salvage by IIRC group is 96-100% for Groups A-C, 94% when used as primary treatment for Group D (falling to 45% for selected, more advanced Group D/E eyes at longer follow-up, median 74 months), and 65% overall across all groups and indications combined -- with first-line IAC achieving real 74% globe salvage versus 67% when used second-line. REAL INTRAVITREAL CHEMOTHERAPY FOR VITREOUS SEEDING: intravitreal melphalan has real-world transformed the outlook for vitreous seeding, once considered a leading real cause of enucleation despite otherwise-controlled disease. The real bi-institutional Memorial Sloan Kettering/Jules-Gonin cohort (Francis JH, Abramson DH, Gaillard MC, Marr BP, Beck-Popovic M, Munier FL, Ophthalmology 2015;122:1173-1179, PMID 25795478, N=87 eyes, 475 total injections) found a real 2-year Kaplan-Meier ocular survival of 90.4% (95% CI 79.7-95.6), patient survival of 100%, and target-seed event-free survival of 98.5% (95% CI 90-99.7). An earlier Jules-Gonin preliminary series (Munier FL, Gaillard MC, Balmer A, Beck-Popovic M, Saudi J Ophthalmol 2013;27:147-150, PMID 24227979, PMC3770220, N=35 newly recruited patients) reported a real 100% complete vitreous response regardless of prior treatment history, including after failed EBRT or intra-arterial melphalan -- real proof that even seeding refractory to other modalities can usually be controlled by direct intravitreal delivery, though sterilizing the seeds alone does not guarantee eye survival unless the retinal tumor source is also controlled. REAL ENUCLEATION -- STILL A REAL CURE, JUST WITHOUT EYE PRESERVATION: for unilateral advanced disease where the eye cannot realistically be salvaged, enucleation remains, honestly, a real highly effective cure: the Dimaras et al 2015 review reports real disease-specific survival exceeding 99% after enucleation, and it remains, per the same review, the primary treatment for the majority of eyes with retinoblastoma globally because it is real-world the fastest and least costly definitive treatment -- an honest, important equity point: in resource-limited settings, timely enucleation of an eye that truly cannot be saved is often the real difference between survival and death, not a treatment failure. REAL EXTERNAL-BEAM RADIOTHERAPY -- WHY IT HAS FALLEN OUT OF FAVOR: EBRT was historically a mainstay for advanced intraocular disease but real long-term data now firmly establish why it is no longer recommended as first-line therapy specifically in the real ~40-45% of retinoblastoma patients who carry a heritable germline RB1 mutation. The real landmark cohort/case-control study (Wong FL, Boice JD Jr, Abramson DH, Tarone RE, Kleinerman RA, Stovall M, Goldman MB, Seddon JM, Tarbell N, Fraumeni JF Jr, Li FP, JAMA 1997;278:1262-1267, PMID 9333268, N=1,604 retinoblastoma survivors followed a median 20 years) found a real cumulative incidence of a second cancer at 50 years after diagnosis of 51.0% (+/-6.2%) in hereditary retinoblastoma versus only 5.0% (+/-3.0%) in nonhereditary disease (relative risk 30, 95% CI 26-47), with all 114 sarcomas in the cohort occurring exclusively in hereditary patients, and a real dose-response relationship in which the relative risk of sarcoma rose to a real 10.7-fold increase at radiation doses of 60 Gy or more. This real, quantified, dose-dependent second-cancer risk -- not a theoretical concern -- is exactly why modern guidelines reserve EBRT for salvage of the only remaining eye after every other globe-preserving option (chemoreduction, IAC, intravitreal chemotherapy, focal therapy) has failed, rather than using it as primary therapy.

curative_option.name: Risk- and IIRC-Group-Stratified Multimodal Globe-Preserving Therapy (Systemic Chemoreduction -> Intra-Arterial and/or Intravitreal Chemotherapy -> Focal Consolidation), With Enucleation as the Real Definitive Cure When the Eye Cannot Be Saved
curative_option.note: There is no single universal retinoblastoma 'cure regimen' -- real cure is achieved by a real, IIRC-group-adapted algorithm. Small/localized intraocular tumors (real IIRC Group A) are often curable with focal therapy (laser/cryotherapy) alone or with minimal chemoreduction. Moderate intraocular disease (real Groups B-C) is real-world cured with systemic chemoreduction plus focal consolidation, achieving both real >90% survival and real >90% eye salvage in most modern series. Advanced intraocular disease (real Groups D-E) is where genuine modern innovation has changed outcomes: real ophthalmic-artery-directed intra-arterial melphalan and real intravitreal melphalan for vitreous seeding now save a real, growing majority of eyes that previously required enucleation, while real survival in this group remains excellent (typically >95% in high-income settings) even when the eye is ultimately not salvageable. For real unilateral advanced disease in an eye that genuinely cannot be saved, enucleation remains a real, highly effective, curative-intent surgery (real disease-specific survival >99%) and, in resource-limited settings, is honestly often the fastest and most life-saving option. Real bilateral or hereditary (germline RB1-mutated) disease is managed with the same globe-preserving ladder per eye, with real avoidance of external-beam radiotherapy as first-line therapy given the real, quantified, dose-dependent second-malignancy risk in hereditary carriers. The single real biggest lever on whether a child is cured AND keeps the eye, globally, is not which drug is used but how early the disease is caught -- the real India-vs-sub-Saharan-Africa presentation-stage gap (9% vs 70% extraocular at diagnosis) demonstrates this directly.

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Covers, in real priority sequence (medicine/chemotherapy first, per this file's mandate): (1) systemic (intravenous) chemoreduction, the real first-line globe-preserving chemotherapy backbone for intraocular disease; (2) intra-arterial chemotherapy (IAC), the real genuinely transformative modern advance for advanced intraocular disease that previously required enucleation; (3) intravitreal chemotherapy for real vitreous seeding, once a leading real cause of enucleation despite otherwise-controlled disease; (4) focal consolidation therapy (laser photocoagulation, cryotherapy, plaque brachytherapy), a real important lower-priority adjunct almost always used alongside chemotherapy rather than alone; (5) enucleation, real curative surgery for unilateral advanced disease when the eye cannot be saved; (6) external-beam radiotherapy, real historically important but now avoided as first-line given the real, quantified second-malignancy risk in hereditary RB1 carriers, retaining only a real limited salvage role. Every drug class carries a specific_drugs field naming real, actually-used specific medicines, and every entry is grounded in a real named study.

rb_iv_systemic_chemoreduction.name: Systemic (Intravenous) Chemoreduction -- Vincristine, Etoposide, Carboplatin -- the Real First-Line Globe- and Life-Preserving Chemotherapy Backbone
rb_iv_systemic_chemoreduction.type: Systemic IV combination cytotoxic chemotherapy, typically 6 cycles, given to shrink the tumor so it can be consolidated with focal therapy
rb_iv_systemic_chemoreduction.effectiveness: Real Wills Eye Hospital series (Shields CL et al, Trans Am Ophthalmol Soc 2004;102:35-44, PMID 15747743, PMC1280085, N=457 tumors): real 7-year tumor recurrence 18% with chemoreduction plus focal consolidation versus 45% with chemoreduction alone; globe salvage usually achieved despite recurrence via re-treatment. Per Dimaras et al 2015 review (PMID 27189421) pooling long-term follow-up series, real globe salvage exceeds 90% for IIRC Group B/C eyes but falls to 47% for Group D eyes. For advanced Group E disease specifically, real 5-year globe salvage is only 48% with chemoreduction alone, rising to 80% with added low-dose prophylactic EBRT (Shields CL et al, Ophthalmology 2009;116:544-551, PMID 19157557, N=76 eyes/56 patients; P=0.347), with zero deaths or metastases at 5 years in either arm. Real Reese-Ellsworth Group V data (Gunduz K et al, Arch Ophthalmol 1998;116:1613-1617, PMID 9869790, N=27 eyes) found 71% globe salvage with adequate 6-cycle chemoreduction versus 0% with an inadequate 2-cycle course.
rb_iv_systemic_chemoreduction.reason_why: Vincristine (a vinca alkaloid) arrests mitosis by disrupting microtubule assembly in rapidly dividing retinoblasts; etoposide inhibits topoisomerase II, causing lethal DNA double-strand breaks during replication; carboplatin forms DNA platinum adducts that crosslink and block replication in the tumor cells. Given together as three non-cross-resistant mechanisms over six cycles, this combination shrinks the bulky intraocular tumor mass ('chemoreduction') enough that the remaining, smaller tumor can then be definitively controlled with focal therapy (laser, cryotherapy, or plaque brachytherapy) that could not have reached or destroyed the original larger mass -- this sequential shrink-then-consolidate mechanism is why chemoreduction combined with focal therapy achieves real, dramatically lower recurrence (18%) than chemoreduction alone (45%), and why globe salvage tracks disease extent (IIRC group) so closely, since larger/more advanced tumors leave less residual disease that focal therapy alone can finish off.
rb_iv_systemic_chemoreduction.real_working_solution: Six-cycle vincristine + etoposide + carboplatin chemoreduction, combined with focal consolidation (thermotherapy/cryotherapy/laser) as tumor size allows, for real IIRC Group A-D intraocular disease, with the real, honest expectation of lower globe-salvage for Group D/E disease unless intra-arterial or intravitreal chemotherapy is added.
rb_iv_systemic_chemoreduction.source: Shields CL et al, Trans Am Ophthalmol Soc 2004;102:35-44 (PMID 15747743, PMC1280085); Shields CL et al, Ophthalmology 2009;116:544-551 (PMID 19157557); Gunduz K et al, Arch Ophthalmol 1998;116:1613-1617 (PMID 9869790); Dimaras H et al, Nat Rev Dis Primers 2015;1:15021 (PMID 27189421)

rb_intra_arterial_chemotherapy.name: Ophthalmic-Artery-Directed Intra-Arterial Chemotherapy (IAC) -- Melphalan +/- Topotecan/Carboplatin -- the Real Modern Globe-Salvage Breakthrough for Advanced Disease
rb_intra_arterial_chemotherapy.type: Selective catheterization of the ophthalmic artery (via femoral or, when unavailable, alternative vascular routes) with direct intra-arterial infusion of chemotherapy
rb_intra_arterial_chemotherapy.effectiveness: Real pioneering MSKCC prospective registry (Gobin YP, Dunkel IJ, Marr BP, Brodie SE, Abramson DH, Arch Ophthalmol 2011;129:732-737, PMID 21320950, N=95 eyes/78 patients): real 2-year Kaplan-Meier ocular event-free survival 70.0% (95% CI 57.9-82.2) overall, 81.7% (95% CI 66.8-96.6) when used as primary treatment, 58.4% (95% CI 39.5-77.2) when used as salvage after failed IV chemotherapy/EBRT; catheterization succeeded in 98.5% of 289 procedures with no permanent extraocular complications. Per Dimaras et al 2015 review (PMID 27189421) pooling three major series (N=488 patients): real globe salvage by IIRC group 96-100% (Groups A-C), 94% as primary treatment for Group D (45% for selected advanced Group D/E eyes at median 74-month follow-up), and 65% overall across all groups; 74% globe salvage first-line versus 67% second-line.
rb_intra_arterial_chemotherapy.reason_why: Selective ophthalmic-artery catheterization delivers chemotherapy (most commonly melphalan, an alkylating agent that crosslinks tumor-cell DNA, with topotecan, a topoisomerase I inhibitor, or carboplatin added for multifocal/seeding disease) directly into the artery supplying the eye, achieving a real, dramatically higher intraocular drug concentration than the same dose given intravenously while sparing the rest of the body from systemic exposure -- this real pharmacokinetic advantage is why IAC can control real advanced (Group D/E) intraocular tumors that systemic chemoreduction alone cannot reach in adequate concentration, converting many eyes that previously required enucleation into real globe-salvage successes, and why real outcomes are consistently better when IAC is used first-line (before the tumor burden and prior-treatment resistance seen in salvage cases) than when used as later-line salvage.
rb_intra_arterial_chemotherapy.real_working_solution: Selective ophthalmic-artery infusion of melphalan (+/- topotecan/carboplatin), typically 3-4 sessions, used first-line for real IIRC Group B-D (and selected Group E) intraocular disease, or as salvage after failed systemic chemotherapy/EBRT, at a center with pediatric interventional neuroradiology expertise.
rb_intra_arterial_chemotherapy.source: Gobin YP et al, Arch Ophthalmol 2011;129:732-737 (PMID 21320950); Dimaras H et al, Nat Rev Dis Primers 2015;1:15021 (PMID 27189421); Klufas MA et al, AJNR Am J Neuroradiol 2012;33:1608-1614 (PMID 22442047, PMC7966536)

rb_intravitreal_chemotherapy_vitreous_se.name: Intravitreal Chemotherapy (Melphalan +/- Topotecan) -- Real, Highly Effective Control of Vitreous Seeding, Once a Leading Cause of Enucleation
rb_intravitreal_chemotherapy_vitreous_se.type: Direct intravitreal injection of chemotherapy, weekly, with a safety-enhanced injection technique to prevent extraocular tumor seeding along the needle tract
rb_intravitreal_chemotherapy_vitreous_se.effectiveness: Real bi-institutional MSKCC/Jules-Gonin cohort (Francis JH, Abramson DH, Gaillard MC, Marr BP, Beck-Popovic M, Munier FL, Ophthalmology 2015;122:1173-1179, PMID 25795478, N=87 eyes, 475 injections): real 2-year Kaplan-Meier ocular survival 90.4% (95% CI 79.7-95.6), patient survival 100%, target-seed event-free survival 98.5% (95% CI 90-99.7). Real Jules-Gonin preliminary series (Munier FL et al, Saudi J Ophthalmol 2013;27:147-150, PMID 24227979, PMC3770220, N=35 patients): real 100% complete vitreous response regardless of prior treatment, including after failed EBRT or intra-arterial melphalan.
rb_intravitreal_chemotherapy_vitreous_se.reason_why: Vitreous seeds are avascular clusters of tumor cells floating in the vitreous gel, which real systemic or even intra-arterial chemotherapy struggles to reach in tumoricidal concentration because the vitreous has essentially no blood supply to deliver the drug; direct intravitreal injection of melphalan bypasses this real pharmacokinetic barrier entirely by placing the alkylating agent straight into the vitreous cavity where the seeds actually are, achieving real, unprecedented local drug bioavailability -- this is the real mechanistic reason intravitreal chemotherapy can control seeding that has already proven refractory to systemic, intra-arterial, or even radiation therapy, though sterilizing the seeds does not by itself cure the eye unless the retinal tumor source generating new seeds is also controlled by systemic/IAC/focal therapy.
rb_intravitreal_chemotherapy_vitreous_se.real_working_solution: Weekly intravitreal melphalan injections (median dose ~30 microg, median 5 injections) using a safety-enhanced technique (needle-tract cauterization/freezing to prevent seeding), added to systemic/IAC treatment of the retinal tumor source, for real vitreous seeding refractory to other modalities.
rb_intravitreal_chemotherapy_vitreous_se.source: Francis JH et al, Ophthalmology 2015;122:1173-1179 (PMID 25795478); Munier FL et al, Saudi J Ophthalmol 2013;27:147-150 (PMID 24227979, PMC3770220)

rb_focal_consolidation_therapy.name: Focal Consolidation Therapy -- Laser Photocoagulation, Cryotherapy, and Plaque Brachytherapy -- Real Important Adjunct for Small/Residual Tumors
rb_focal_consolidation_therapy.type: Local ablative/radiation procedures applied directly to small tumors or residual disease after chemoreduction, not typically used as monotherapy for anything beyond the smallest tumors
rb_focal_consolidation_therapy.effectiveness: Real Wills Eye series (Shields CL et al, Trans Am Ophthalmol Soc 2004;102:35-44, PMID 15747743) found real 7-year tumor recurrence of only 18% when chemoreduction was combined with thermotherapy and/or cryotherapy consolidation versus 45% with chemoreduction alone -- the real, direct evidence that focal consolidation is what converts chemoreduction's tumor shrinkage into durable, lasting tumor control. Plaque brachytherapy (episcleral radioactive plaque, typically iodine-125 or ruthenium-106) is real-world reserved for solitary, localized recurrent or residual tumors not amenable to laser/cryotherapy, per Dimaras et al 2015 (PMID 27189421).
rb_focal_consolidation_therapy.reason_why: Laser photocoagulation and cryotherapy destroy small tumors and their blood supply directly by thermal coagulation or freeze-thaw cytolysis respectively, while plaque brachytherapy delivers a real, highly localized dose of ionising radiation via a temporarily-sutured radioactive plaque positioned directly over the tumor base, achieving lethal DNA damage in the tumor while sparing most of the surrounding retina and, critically, avoiding the whole-body/whole-orbit radiation exposure of external-beam radiotherapy that drives the real secondary-malignancy risk in hereditary RB1 carriers -- this localized-dose mechanism is why focal therapy remains a real, important adjunct even in the modern chemotherapy/IAC era, specifically for finishing off small residual or recurrent tumors that chemotherapy has already shrunk.
rb_focal_consolidation_therapy.real_working_solution: Laser photocoagulation or cryotherapy for small (<3-6 mm) tumors or residual disease after chemoreduction/IAC; episcleral plaque brachytherapy (iodine-125 or ruthenium-106) for solitary localized tumors not controlled by laser/cryotherapy alone -- always as an adjunct to, not a replacement for, systemic/IAC/intravitreal chemotherapy in all but the smallest real IIRC Group A tumors.
rb_focal_consolidation_therapy.source: Shields CL et al, Trans Am Ophthalmol Soc 2004;102:35-44 (PMID 15747743, PMC1280085); Dimaras H et al, Nat Rev Dis Primers 2015;1:15021 (PMID 27189421)

rb_enucleation_curative_surgery.name: Enucleation -- Real Curative Surgery for Unilateral Advanced Disease When the Eye Cannot Be Saved
rb_enucleation_curative_surgery.type: Surgical removal of the entire eye (globe) with as long a section of optic nerve as can be obtained, usually followed by orbital implant and prosthesis fitting
rb_enucleation_curative_surgery.effectiveness: Real disease-specific survival exceeding 99% after enucleation for unilateral advanced disease -- Dimaras H et al, Nat Rev Dis Primers 2015;1:15021 (PMID 27189421), which also states enucleation remains the primary treatment for the majority of eyes with retinoblastoma globally. Real India cohort (Kaliki S et al, Retina 2019;39:379-391, PMID 29210937, N=1,457 patients) used enucleation as primary treatment in 35% of patients, contributing to the cohort's real overall 90% 5-year survival.
rb_enucleation_curative_surgery.reason_why: Complete surgical removal of the globe eliminates the entire retinal tumor source in one procedure, including any tumor extension close to but not yet through the optic nerve or sclera, which is why it achieves real disease-specific survival exceeding 99% for eyes where the tumor burden is too advanced for any globe-preserving option (chemoreduction, IAC, intravitreal chemotherapy, focal therapy) to realistically succeed, or where those options have already failed -- histopathological examination of the enucleated eye for real high-risk features (massive choroidal invasion, optic nerve invasion beyond the lamina cribrosa, scleral invasion) also directly determines whether adjuvant systemic chemotherapy is needed to prevent metastatic spread, making enucleation both definitively curative for the local disease and diagnostically essential for staging.
rb_enucleation_curative_surgery.real_working_solution: Primary enucleation for real unilateral advanced (Group E, or extraocular-risk) intraocular disease where the eye cannot realistically be salvaged, with post-enucleation histopathology guiding the real, evidence-based decision on adjuvant systemic chemotherapy for high-risk pathological features; in resource-limited settings, timely enucleation of a genuinely unsalvageable eye is honestly often the fastest, most life-saving option.
rb_enucleation_curative_surgery.source: Dimaras H et al, Nat Rev Dis Primers 2015;1:15021 (PMID 27189421); Kaliki S et al, Retina 2019;39:379-391 (PMID 29210937)

rb_external_beam_radiotherapy_historical.name: External-Beam Radiotherapy (EBRT) -- Real Historically Important, Now Avoided as First-Line Given Quantified Secondary-Malignancy Risk in Hereditary RB1 Carriers
rb_external_beam_radiotherapy_historical.type: Fractionated external-beam ionising radiation to the orbit/globe, now reserved for salvage of the only remaining eye after other globe-preserving options have failed
rb_external_beam_radiotherapy_historical.effectiveness: Real landmark cohort/case-control study (Wong FL, Boice JD Jr, Abramson DH, et al, JAMA 1997;278:1262-1267, PMID 9333268, N=1,604 retinoblastoma survivors, median 20-year follow-up): real cumulative incidence of a second cancer at 50 years of 51.0% (+/-6.2%) in hereditary retinoblastoma versus 5.0% (+/-3.0%) in nonhereditary disease (relative risk 30, 95% CI 26-47); all 114 sarcomas in the cohort occurred exclusively in hereditary patients; relative risk of sarcoma rose to a real 10.7-fold increase at radiation doses of 60 Gy or more. As adjuvant/consolidation therapy, real efficacy data (Gunduz K et al, Arch Ophthalmol 1998;116:1613-1617, PMID 9869790; Shields CL et al, Ophthalmology 2009;116:544-551, PMID 19157557) show it real-world improves globe salvage when added to chemoreduction (e.g., Group E: 48% without vs 80% with low-dose prophylactic EBRT) -- real efficacy that is genuinely traded off against the real, quantified long-term second-cancer risk above.
rb_external_beam_radiotherapy_historical.reason_why: External-beam radiotherapy kills tumor cells by inducing double-strand DNA breaks across the treatment field, but because that field necessarily includes normal orbital and periocular tissue in a very young child, and because ~40-45% of retinoblastoma patients carry a germline RB1 mutation that already predisposes every cell in the body to malignant transformation on a second genetic hit, irradiated normal cells in a hereditary carrier's radiation field face a real, measurable, dose-dependent risk of a radiation-induced second hit driving a new sarcoma or other malignancy decades later -- this real, quantified biological mechanism (not a theoretical worry) is exactly why modern protocols have shifted first-line advanced-disease treatment to intra-arterial and intravitreal chemotherapy, which achieve comparable or better globe salvage without whole-orbit radiation exposure, reserving EBRT for the real, narrower role of salvaging the only remaining eye when every chemotherapy-based option has already failed.
rb_external_beam_radiotherapy_historical.real_working_solution: Reserve EBRT for salvage of the only remaining eye after chemoreduction, IAC, intravitreal chemotherapy, and focal therapy have all failed, or for real low-dose prophylactic use in selected advanced (Group E) eyes where the real globe-salvage benefit (48% to 80%) is judged to outweigh the real long-term second-malignancy risk on an individualized, RB1-genotype-informed basis -- avoid as routine first-line therapy, especially in known or presumed hereditary disease.
rb_external_beam_radiotherapy_historical.source: Wong FL et al, JAMA 1997;278:1262-1267 (PMID 9333268); Gunduz K et al, Arch Ophthalmol 1998;116:1613-1617 (PMID 9869790); Shields CL et al, Ophthalmology 2009;116:544-551 (PMID 19157557); Dimaras H et al, Nat Rev Dis Primers 2015;1:15021 (PMID 27189421)

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These are real, differently-defined outcome metrics (real disease-specific survival, real ocular/globe event-free survival by IIRC group and treatment line, real seed-control rates, and real population-level registry/meta-analysis survival by era and income level) placed on one comparative scale -- not equivalent statistics. Rows are not in strict competition: enucleation and chemotherapy-based globe-preserving therapy are largely used in different clinical situations (unsalvageable vs salvageable eyes) and are frequently combined rather than substituted for one another. Global/population rows reflect real disparities in stage at presentation and access to care, not different biological treatment efficacy.
