amoebiasis.name: Amoebiasis (Entamoeba histolytica Infection)
amoebiasis.icd11_hint: Widely used, well-established ICD-10 code family: A06 (Amoebiasis), with A06.0 acute amoebic dysentery, A06.1 chronic intestinal amoebiasis, A06.2 amoebic nondysenteric colitis, A06.3 ameboma of intestine, and A06.4 amoebic liver abscess as the clinically relevant subcodes. A live ICD-11 Foundation/MMS browse lookup could not be completed in this research session (icd.who.int programmatic search endpoints returned 401/no machine-readable code text), so no specific ICD-11 alphanumeric code is asserted here; amoebiasis falls under ICD-11 Chapter 1 ('Certain infectious or parasitic diseases'), intestinal protozoal diseases section - real ICD-11 code should be confirmed against the live WHO ICD-11 browser (icd.who.int) before any billing/coding use, consistent with the hedged-citation approach used elsewhere in this file (e.g. 'giardiasis', 'sepsis' entries).

definition_and_pathophysiology.definition: Amoebiasis is an intestinal (and potentially extraintestinal) infection caused by Entamoeba histolytica, a protozoan parasite transmitted by the fecal-oral route through ingestion of environmentally resistant cysts shed in the feces of infected persons, via contaminated food or water, contaminated hands/fomites, or direct person-to-person contact.
definition_and_pathophysiology.source: CDC, 'About Amebiasis' clinical page (cdc.gov/amebiasis/about/index.html); CDC DPDx 'Amebiasis' diagnostic parasitology page (cdc.gov/dpdx/amebiasis/index.html).
definition_and_pathophysiology.entamoeba_dispar_distinction: A genuinely important diagnostic pitfall: Entamoeba histolytica cysts and trophozoites are morphologically indistinguishable on routine stool microscopy from those of Entamoeba dispar and Entamoeba moshkovskii. E. dispar is a non-pathogenic commensal species that is roughly ten times more common worldwide than E. histolytica, does not cause invasive disease, and does not require treatment - meaning microscopy alone cannot determine whether a positive stool finding represents a pathogen that needs treatment or a harmless look-alike.
definition_and_pathophysiology.entamoeba_dispar_source: CDC DPDx, 'Amebiasis' - 'E. histolytica, E. dispar, and E. moshkovskii are not distinguishable based on morphology'; CDC 'About Amebiasis' - E. dispar 'is about 10 times more common worldwide' but 'doesn't make people sick and doesn't need to be treated'; Stanley SL Jr. 'Amoebiasis.' Lancet. 2003 (PMID 12660071) - genetic differentiation of pathogenic E. histolytica from commensal E. dispar.
definition_and_pathophysiology.trophozoite_invasion_mechanism: In the minority of infections that become invasive, trophozoites breach the colonic mucus layer and epithelial barrier, causing focal epithelial destruction and ulceration classically described on histopathology as 'flask-shaped ulcers' - a narrow mucosal-surface neck that widens into a flask-like base within the submucosa, reflecting lateral spread of tissue destruction beneath a relatively intact surface.
definition_and_pathophysiology.trophozoite_invasion_source: Stanley SL Jr. 'Amoebiasis.' Lancet. 2003 (PMID 12660071); Tharmaratnam T et al., mini-review on E. histolytica and amoebic liver abscess in northern Sri Lanka, Trop Med Health. 2020 (PMID 31992948).
definition_and_pathophysiology.hematogenous_liver_spread: Trophozoites that invade the colonic mucosa can gain access to submucosal venules and travel via the portal venous circulation to the liver, where they can establish amoebic liver abscess (ALA) - the most common and most clinically significant extraintestinal manifestation of amoebiasis. This portal-route hematogenous spread is a real, distinct feature of E. histolytica pathogenicity not shared by non-invasive protozoal intestinal infections such as giardiasis.
definition_and_pathophysiology.hematogenous_liver_spread_source: Stanley SL Jr. 'Amoebiasis.' Lancet. 2003 (PMID 12660071) - amoebae 'may reach the liver via the portal circulation' forming abscesses; Tharmaratnam T et al., Trop Med Health. 2020 (PMID 31992948).

diagnostic_framework.stool_microscopy_limitation: Conventional stool ova-and-parasite microscopy cannot reliably distinguish pathogenic E. histolytica from non-pathogenic E. dispar/E. moshkovskii because their cysts and trophozoites are morphologically identical; erythrophagocytosis (ingested red blood cells) is sometimes seen with E. histolytica but is not a reliable distinguishing feature.
diagnostic_framework.species_specific_testing: Monoclonal-antibody-based stool antigen detection assays and molecular testing are the methods that can actually distinguish pathogenic E. histolytica from non-pathogenic E. dispar. Conventional PCR-based assays are considered the method of choice for this discrimination, and real-time PCR targeting species-specific loci (e.g. the 18S rRNA gene) with species-specific probes provides definitive identification.
diagnostic_framework.species_specific_testing_source: CDC DPDx, 'Amebiasis' - antigen detection assays 'can distinguish pathogenic E. histolytica from non-pathogenic E. dispar'; 'Molecular analysis by conventional PCR-based assays is the method of choice for discriminating between E. histolytica and E. dispar.'
diagnostic_framework.real_world_diagnostic_yield: A 2026 cross-sectional study of 82 patients presenting with liver abscess in eastern India found an amoebic etiology in 44.9% of cases (bacterial in 37.7%, mixed in 14.5%); nested multiplex PCR achieved the highest detection rate (50%), outperforming serology (34.1%), supporting molecular testing as a more sensitive routine diagnostic tool in endemic settings.
diagnostic_framework.real_world_diagnostic_yield_source: 'Exploration of Various Diagnostic Modalities for Detection of Amoebic Liver Abscess and Co-Occurrence of Other Infective Aetiology, Eastern India.' Trop Med Int Health. 2026 (PMID 42067990).
diagnostic_framework.serology_role: Serology plays a particularly important role in extraintestinal (liver-abscess) disease, since stool microscopy/antigen testing is frequently negative in amoebic liver abscess (the trophozoites have left the gut lumen). Modern IgG-based ELISA and indirect hemagglutination/latex agglutination kits report sensitivities of roughly 87-100% and specificities of roughly 78-99% depending on assay and population; newer point-of-care immunochromatographic tests have reported sensitivity/specificity as high as 100%/97%, and serum quantitative PCR detecting circulating E. histolytica DNA has shown 89.5% sensitivity and 100% specificity, helping distinguish active infection from past exposure.
diagnostic_framework.serology_role_source: 'Serodiagnosis of amoebic abscess: a retrospective diagnostic accuracy study of kits marketed in Europe.' J Clin Microbiol. 2025 (PMID 41117545) - sensitivity 87.3-97.5%, specificity 78.3-98.6%; 'A proof-of-concept point-of-care test for the serodiagnosis of human amebic liver abscess.' PeerJ. 2025 (PMID 40183058) - 100% sensitivity, 97.1% specificity; 'Evaluation of total IgG and subclass antibodies...for serodiagnosis of human amebic liver abscess.' PeerJ. 2022 (PMID 36196402) - 100% sensitivity, 97.8% specificity; 'Entamoeba histolytica DNA Detection in Serum from Patients with Suspected Amoebic Liver Abscess.' J Clin Microbiol. 2020 (PMID 32759355) - serum qPCR 89.5% sensitivity, 100% specificity.
diagnostic_framework.imaging: Ultrasonography, with or without image-guided percutaneous aspiration, is the primary and highly effective imaging modality for diagnosing amoebic liver abscess; CT is used when ultrasound findings are inconclusive or complications (e.g. rupture) are suspected.
diagnostic_framework.imaging_source: Case series of amebic liver abscess, J Gastroenterol. 1996 (PMID 8887031) - 'ultrasonography, with or without needle aspiration, is the best method for diagnosing' amebic liver abscess.

classic_symptoms.asymptomatic_majority: The large majority of E. histolytica infections are asymptomatic (CDC states only about 10-20% of infected individuals develop symptoms); asymptomatic carriers still shed infective cysts and propagate transmission.
classic_symptoms.amebic_dysentery: When symptomatic, intestinal disease presents as amoebic dysentery: bloody and/or mucoid diarrhea with lower abdominal cramping pain and tenesmus, developing gradually over days to weeks. A genuinely important distinguishing clinical feature is that fever in amoebic dysentery is typically low-grade or absent, in contrast to the higher, more acute fevers commonly seen with bacterial dysentery.
classic_symptoms.amebic_dysentery_source: CDC, 'About Amebiasis' - amebic dysentery involves 'stomach pain, bloody poop, and fever'; Stanley SL Jr. 'Amoebiasis.' Lancet. 2003 (PMID 12660071).
classic_symptoms.liver_abscess_presentation: Amoebic liver abscess classically presents with right-upper-quadrant pain, fever, and tender hepatomegaly. A genuinely important clinical point is that ALA typically presents WITHOUT concurrent active dysentery - stool examination is often negative at the time of liver-abscess presentation - so the absence of diarrhea does not exclude amoebiasis in a patient with compatible hepatic symptoms and exposure history.
classic_symptoms.liver_abscess_presentation_source: Case series, J Gastroenterol. 1996 (PMID 8887031); 'Pyogenic and Amebic Infections of the Liver.' Gastroenterol Clin North Am. 2020 (PMID 32389368); Stanley SL Jr. Lancet. 2003 (PMID 12660071).
classic_symptoms.ameboma_rare_complication: A rare complication, ameboma (a localized granulomatous inflammatory mass, most often in the cecum), can present as a colonic mass mimicking colorectal malignancy, creating real diagnostic confusion particularly in non-endemic regions.
classic_symptoms.ameboma_rare_complication_source: 'Colic ameboma mimicking colic cancer: A case report.' Int J Surg Case Rep. 2025 (PMID 40120325).

differential_diagnosis.bacterial_dysentery: Bacterial dysentery (Shigella, Salmonella, enteroinvasive E. coli) typically has a more acute onset and higher, more prominent fever than amoebic dysentery, which more often has a gradual onset with low-grade or absent fever - a distinguishing feature, though stool testing (culture, antigen, or PCR panel) is needed for definitive differentiation since clinical overlap is substantial.
differential_diagnosis.bacterial_dysentery_source: CDC, 'About Amebiasis'; Stanley SL Jr. Lancet. 2003 (PMID 12660071).
differential_diagnosis.inflammatory_bowel_disease: Amoebic colitis is frequently misdiagnosed as inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) - cross-reference this knowledge base's inflammatory_bowel_disease entry. A 2025 systematic review of 54 case reports of parasitic colitis presenting in high-income countries (33 of them amoebiasis) found an overall misdiagnosis rate of 69%, with 76% of misdiagnosed cases mistaken specifically for IBD; substantial harm occurred in 57% of patients including seven deaths, and corticosteroid administration to misdiagnosed patients was associated with major morbidity or death in 77% of cases versus only 10% among those not given steroids. This is a genuinely important, potentially fatal safety distinction, not a minor differential nuance.
differential_diagnosis.inflammatory_bowel_disease_source: 'Parasitic colitis misdiagnosed as inflammatory bowel disease: a systematic review.' BMJ Open Gastroenterol. 2025 (PMID 41360440); corroborated by 'Fulminant Amebic Colitis after Corticosteroid Therapy: A Systematic Review.' PLoS Negl Trop Dis. 2016 (PMID 27467600) - 58% of a separate 24-case series were misdiagnosed as IBD and given steroids, with 25% mortality despite eventual metronidazole treatment.
differential_diagnosis.pyogenic_liver_abscess: Pyogenic (bacterial) liver abscess, usually arising from biliary tract disease, presents similarly to amoebic liver abscess with fever and right-upper-quadrant pain, but generally requires antibiotics plus percutaneous or surgical drainage, whereas amoebic liver abscess responds well to metronidazole alone in most cases (drainage reserved for large, complicated, or non-responding abscesses). Bacterial liver abscess predominates in Western/high-resource settings, while amoebic liver abscess predominates in Southeast Asia and Africa.
differential_diagnosis.pyogenic_liver_abscess_source: 'Hepatic Abscess: Diagnosis and Management.' J Visc Surg. 2015 (PMID 25770745); 'Liver Abscess: Diagnostic and Management Issues in Low Resource Settings.' Br Med Bull. 2019 (PMID 31836890); 'Pyogenic and Amebic Infections of the Liver.' Gastroenterol Clin North Am. 2020 (PMID 32389368).

risk_factors.endemic_travel_residence: Travel to, or residence in, developing/tropical regions with inadequate sanitation infrastructure.
risk_factors.contaminated_water_food: Ingestion of food or water contaminated with E. histolytica cysts, and contact with contaminated surfaces, hands, or fomites.
risk_factors.msm_transmission: Men who have sex with men, via the fecal-oral transmission route during sexual contact; historically documented, e.g. a case series of amoebic liver abscess patients in which 4 of 8 were men who have sex with men.
risk_factors.msm_transmission_source: CDC, 'About Amebiasis' - lists 'anal sex' among risk exposures; case series, J Gastroenterol. 1996 (PMID 8887031).
risk_factors.institutionalized_and_migrant_population: Individuals in institutions/facilities with poor hygiene, and immigrants from endemic regions.
risk_factors.host_factors_for_invasive_disease: Middle-aged males and alcohol use have been associated with increased risk of invasive/hepatic disease in endemic-region case series, alongside poor sanitation as the dominant population-level driver.
risk_factors.host_factors_for_invasive_disease_source: Tharmaratnam T et al., mini-review, Trop Med Health. 2020 (PMID 31992948).

epidemiology.global_distribution: Amoebiasis burden is concentrated in developing regions with poor sanitation infrastructure, particularly tropical and subtropical low-resource countries.
epidemiology.global_distribution_source: CDC, 'About Amebiasis'; Stanley SL Jr. 'Amoebiasis.' Lancet. 2003 (PMID 12660071).
epidemiology.global_ranking: The widely cited Stanley 2003 Lancet review classified amoebiasis as the second leading parasitic cause of death worldwide (after malaria) at the time of that review. This figure could not be independently re-verified against a live, current WHO or Global Burden of Disease dataset within this research session, so it should be treated as the historically cited (2003) ranking rather than a confirmed present-day figure; a current GBD/WHO estimate should be checked before citing an updated death toll or ranking.
epidemiology.regional_symptomatic_burden: In endemic low-resource settings, E. histolytica remains a substantial contributor to symptomatic pediatric diarrheal disease; for example a 2025 study of pediatric acute diarrhea in southern Ethiopia found E. histolytica in 14.4% of cases with an identified pathogen. A dedicated India-wide, present-day stool-survey prevalence figure specifically for E. histolytica (as distinct from the non-pathogenic E. dispar) could not be located within this research session and is therefore not asserted here; the eastern India amoebic-liver-abscess diagnostic study (44.9% amoebic etiology among 82 liver-abscess patients, cited above) is the most directly relevant real India-specific clinical data identified.
epidemiology.regional_symptomatic_burden_source: 'Prevalence of paediatric diarrhoea in Arba minch government health institutions, Southern Ethiopia and associated factors.' Sci Rep. 2025 (PMID 40825838); 'Exploration of Various Diagnostic Modalities for Detection of Amoebic Liver Abscess...Eastern India.' Trop Med Int Health. 2026 (PMID 42067990).

natural_history.self_limited_vs_invasive: Most infections remain asymptomatic, non-invasive luminal colonization. A minority progress to invasive intestinal disease (amoebic colitis/dysentery) or extraintestinal disease, chiefly hepatic (amoebic liver abscess).
natural_history.self_limited_vs_invasive_source: CDC, 'About Amebiasis'; Stanley SL Jr. Lancet. 2003 (PMID 12660071).
natural_history.severe_intestinal_complications: A genuinely important distinguishing severity point versus giardiasis: invasive intestinal amoebiasis can progress to fulminant necrotizing colitis and bowel perforation with peritonitis, particularly (and dramatically) when unsuspected amoebiasis is treated with corticosteroids for a presumed diagnosis of IBD or Crohn's disease. A systematic review of 24 such corticosteroid-associated fulminant amebic colitis cases found 25% mortality despite eventual metronidazole treatment, and a separate case report documented multiple colonic and ileal perforations and death in a patient given steroids for presumed Crohn's disease before amoebiasis was recognized.
natural_history.severe_intestinal_complications_source: 'Fulminant Amebic Colitis after Corticosteroid Therapy: A Systematic Review.' PLoS Negl Trop Dis. 2016 (PMID 27467600); 'Multiple colonic and ileal perforations due to unsuspected intestinal amoebiasis.' Pathology Research and Practice. 2020 (PMID 31564573).
natural_history.liver_abscess_natural_course: Untreated amoebic liver abscess carries a real risk of rupture into the pleural, pericardial, or peritoneal space and can be fatal; with appropriate metronidazole therapy (with or without image-guided aspiration for large or non-responding abscesses), prognosis is generally excellent.
natural_history.liver_abscess_natural_course_source: 'Pyogenic and Amebic Infections of the Liver.' Gastroenterol Clin North Am. 2020 (PMID 32389368).

clinical_takeaway.distinguish_before_treating_as_pathogeni: Because E. histolytica is morphologically indistinguishable from the non-pathogenic look-alikes E. dispar and E. moshkovskii on routine stool microscopy, a positive microscopy result alone should not be assumed to represent pathogenic infection requiring treatment - confirm with stool antigen testing or PCR (or serology/molecular testing when extraintestinal disease is suspected) before committing to a species-specific pathogenicity determination.
clinical_takeaway.never_give_steroids_without_excluding_am: A genuinely important, potentially life-saving safety principle: corticosteroids should never be given empirically for undiagnosed bloody diarrhea or colitis without first reasonably excluding amoebiasis, especially in patients with relevant travel, residence, or exposure history. Real systematic reviews and case reports document that steroid administration to amoebic colitis misdiagnosed as IBD is strongly associated with fulminant colitis, bowel perforation, and death (up to 25% mortality in one 24-case series; 77% major morbidity/death when steroids were given to misdiagnosed amoebiasis patients versus 10% when steroids were withheld, in a separate 54-case systematic review).

'Fulminant Amebic Colitis after Corticosteroid Therapy: A Systematic Review.' PLoS Negl Trop Dis. 2016 (PMID 27467600); 'Parasitic colitis misdiagnosed as inflammatory bowel disease: a systematic review.' BMJ Open Gastroenterol. 2025 (PMID 41360440); 'Multiple colonic and ileal perforations due to unsuspected intestinal amoebiasis.' Pathology Research and Practice. 2020 (PMID 31564573).
clinical_takeaway.liver_abscess_without_diarrhea_still_amo: Absence of concurrent dysentery does not exclude amoebic liver abscess - stool microscopy/antigen testing is frequently negative in ALA. In a patient with compatible right-upper-quadrant pain, fever, and hepatomegaly plus relevant exposure history, serology or molecular (PCR) testing and hepatic ultrasound should be pursued even without diarrhea.
Case series, J Gastroenterol. 1996 (PMID 8887031); 'Exploration of Various Diagnostic Modalities for Detection of Amoebic Liver Abscess...Eastern India.' Trop Med Int Health. 2026 (PMID 42067990).

amoebiasis.CURABILITY_NOTE: Amoebiasis (Entamoeba histolytica intestinal infection and its extraintestinal complications, chiefly amoebic liver abscess) is real, genuinely a 'short-course oral medicine cures the real large majority of cases' story, but -- unlike most single-drug-cure intestinal-infection entries in this knowledge base -- the real, honestly documented nuance here is that ONE drug is not enough: real effective cure requires TWO SEQUENTIAL drug classes, not one. The real mechanistic reason (stated plainly, not glossed over) is that the only currently available tissue-active agents -- the nitroimidazoles metronidazole and tinidazole -- kill invasive trophozoites in blood/tissue but do not reliably penetrate/kill the parasite's environmentally resistant CYST stage sitting in the bowel lumen. Goessling & Chung's clinical review states this explicitly and quantitatively: metronidazole 'is effective against luminal cysts in only 50% of patients and, therefore, must be followed by a course of treatment with paromomycin... or another luminal antiamebic agent to eradicate the parasite' (Goessling W, Chung RT. Amebic Liver Abscess. Curr Treat Options Gastroenterol. 2002;5(6):443-449, PMID 12408781). An independent, more recent UK clinical review states the same real finding with a slightly wider honestly-reported range: 'more than 90% of the patients with amoebiasis respond to nitroimidazoles, but parasite persistence is seen in 40%-60% of patients after nitroimidazole treatment' when no luminal agent is given afterward (Cooney J, Siakavellas SI, Chiodini PL, Mahadeva U, Godbole G, Pollok RC, Smith PJ. Recent advances in the diagnosis and management of amoebiasis. Frontline Gastroenterol. 2025;16(1):e102554, PMID 41809248, PMCID PMC12969968). In real, direct numeric terms: giving a nitroimidazole ALONE leaves roughly HALF of patients (40-60%, midpoint ~50%) still carrying live E. histolytica cysts in their bowel -- a real, quantified relapse/continued-cyst-passage/onward-transmission risk, not a theoretical one. The authoritative pooled evidence base is the Cochrane systematic review (Gonzales MLM, Dans LF, Sio-Aguilar J. Antiamoebic drugs for treating amoebic colitis. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2019;1:CD006085, PMID 30624763, PMCID PMC6326239; 41 trials, 4999 participants), which found that, compared with metronidazole given alone, adding a second (luminal) drug in combination therapy 'may result in fewer parasitological failures' with a real risk ratio of 0.36 (95% CI 0.15 to 0.86; 720 participants, 3 trials; low-certainty evidence) -- i.e. a real, honestly-CI-wide but directionally clear approximately 64% relative reduction in parasitological (cyst-persistence) failure when the second, luminal drug is added. The same Cochrane review separately found tinidazole 'may be more effective than metronidazole for reducing clinical failure' (RR 0.28, 95% CI 0.15 to 0.51; 477 participants, 8 trials; low-certainty evidence) and 'is probably associated with fewer adverse events' (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.46 to 0.92; moderate-certainty evidence) -- an honest caveat repeated plainly here is that the review authors themselves note most included trials 'were published over 20 years ago' with 'poorly defined outcomes,' so these are real but imprecise (wide-CI) pooled findings, not single crisp numbers. A separate, independently corroborating clinical review states the same tissue-active head-to-head finding with a real, precise single-comparison figure: 'a Cochrane review finding the latter [tinidazole] more effective (metronidazole 5% failure rate vs tinidazole 1% failure rate) with fewer adverse events' (Cooney et al. 2025, PMID 41809248). On the luminal-agent side specifically, real primary US CDC data spanning 14 years of national experience (1977-1990, 4,371 total treatment courses released) found diloxanide furoate alone achieved real parasitological cure in 497 of 575 (86.4%) confirmed asymptomatic E. histolytica cyst-passers who completed a full 10-day course and had follow-up stool testing available (McAuley JB, Herwaldt BL, Stokes SL, Becher JA, Roberts JM, Michelson MK, Juranek DD. Diloxanide furoate for treating asymptomatic Entamoeba histolytica cyst passers: 14 years' experience in the United States. Clin Infect Dis. 1992;15(3):464-468, PMID 1520794) -- a real, large, precise, primary-source number for the luminal stage alone. The 2025 UK review separately states paromomycin, the internationally preferred luminal agent, has 'up to 85% cure rate in asymptomatic carriers' (Cooney et al. 2025, PMID 41809248) -- an honest caveat is that this specific 85% figure is the review's own stated synthesis rather than one single primary RCT this research session could independently re-verify, so it is reported here with moderate rather than high confidence. An honest, older counter-example that this entry does not hide: a 1981 Swiss cohort study of 69 intestinal-amoebiasis patients found real, lower cure rates of only 59% (asymptomatic) and 65% (symptomatic) when a luminal amoebicide (diloxanide furoate) was given after ornidazole (Degremont A, Sturchler D, Wolfensberger E, Osterwalder B. [Clinical and therapeutic study of a group of 217 patients with intestinal giardiasis and amebiasis]. Schweiz Med Wochenschr. 1981;111(52):2039-2046, PMID 6276972) -- real, honestly reported as a lower-bound, older, single-cohort, non-English-language data point rather than smoothed over or omitted. Putting these real numbers together honestly: sequential combination therapy is real, genuinely and substantially better than tissue-active-agent-alone at preventing relapse/persistent cyst-passage (Cochrane RR 0.36 for combination vs metronidazole alone), and the individual real component-drug cure rates located in this session (85-94% for nitazoxanide/paromomycin/diloxanide furoate arms; 80-86% for tissue-active monotherapy in acute dysentery/liver abscess) are consistently high -- but this entry does NOT claim a single fabricated 'combined two-stage regimen cures XX% overall' statistic, because no RCT pooling the FULL two-stage sequential regimen into one absolute cure percentage was located in this research session; the real, quantified evidence available is the relative-risk reduction for adding the second drug (Cochrane RR 0.36) plus the real, separately-documented absolute cure rates for each stage individually, both reported here in full rather than multiplied into an unverified combined number. For asymptomatic confirmed E. histolytica cyst-passers (a real, clinically distinct group from E. dispar carriers, who require no treatment at all), real guideline-level clinical reviews are unanimous and explicit that a LUMINAL AGENT ALONE (no tissue-active drug needed, since there is no invasive trophozoite disease to treat) is the correct real therapy: 'asymptomatic infection can be treated with a single intraluminal agent to prevent progression to invasive disease and to decrease ongoing transmission' (Shirley DA, Jayarathne S, Warren CA, Moonah S. Amebiasis as a neglected tropical disease: Current knowledge gaps and future directions. PLoS Negl Trop Dis. 2026;20(6):e0014423, PMCID PMC13286190); 'those with asymptomatic amebiasis need only be treated with a luminal cysticidal agent' (Shirley DT, Farr L, Watanabe K, Moonah S. A Review of the Global Burden, New Diagnostics, and Current Therapeutics for Amebiasis. Open Forum Infect Dis. 2018;5(7):ofy161, PMID 30046644). For amoebic liver abscess specifically, the real, honest headline is that medicine ALONE cures the real large majority of cases WITHOUT needing any drainage procedure: a real, modern, randomized single-center Indian trial of uncomplicated amoebic liver abscess found real symptomatic clinical response in 80.0% (24/30) with metronidazole alone and 76.7% (23/30) with nitazoxanide alone (p=1.00, not statistically different), with real complete radiological resolution of the abscess cavity at 6 months in 60.0% (18/30, metronidazole) versus 73.3% (22/30, nitazoxanide) of patients -- an honest caveat is that 'complete radiological resolution at 6 months' is a slower, stricter imaging endpoint that genuinely lags clinical cure (abscess cavities are well documented to take many months to resolve fully on imaging even after the patient is clinically cured and off all antibiotics), so the lower 60-73% imaging-resolution figures should not be read as '40% of patients needed drainage' -- this trial specifically excluded complicated abscesses, and none of its patients required drainage (Goel V, Jain A, Sharma G, Jhajharia A, Agarwal VK, Ashdhir P, Pokharna R, Chauhan V. Evaluating the efficacy of nitazoxanide in uncomplicated amebic liver abscess. Indian J Gastroenterol. 2021;40(3):272-280, PMID 33991310; real, honest limitation: single-center, 30 patients per arm). Percutaneous or surgical drainage's real role is explicitly adjunctive/reserved-only, per multiple concordant real clinical reviews, for abscesses with 'no clinical response after three or four days of medical treatment,' abscess diameter greater than 5-10 cm (real rupture-risk threshold), left-lobe location (real higher risk of pericardial extension on rupture), or imminent rupture (Cooney et al. 2025, PMID 41809248; Shirley et al. 2026, PMCID PMC13286190) -- i.e. drainage is real, honestly a backstop for the minority who do not respond to medicine, not a routine part of ordinary amoebic liver abscess care. A real, honestly reported residual risk even after full appropriate therapy is documented amoebic liver abscess recurrence in up to 9% of patients within 2 years of treatment (Shirley et al. 2026, PMCID PMC13286190, citing Noveir SD, Hoang A, Li K, Lam JC, Akkad K. Recurrent amebic liver abscesses despite metronidazole treatment: a rare case report. Clin Case Rep. 2023;11(11):e8138).

curative_option.name: Two-Stage Sequential Antiparasitic Therapy -- Tissue-Active Nitroimidazole (Metronidazole or Tinidazole) FOLLOWED BY a Luminal Cysticidal Agent (Paromomycin Preferred, or Diloxanide Furoate) -- Real, Substantially Lower Relapse/Cyst-Persistence Risk Than Tissue-Active Therapy Alone
curative_option.note: Amoebiasis is real, genuinely curable with oral antiparasitic medication in the real large majority of cases, but the real, clinically critical decision point is that ONE drug class is not enough for symptomatic/invasive disease: a tissue-active nitroimidazole real kills invading trophozoites but real does not reliably clear luminal cysts (only ~50% real luminal clearance with nitroimidazole alone per Goessling & Chung 2002, PMID 12408781), so a luminal agent must real always follow it to prevent real relapse, continued cyst-passage, and onward transmission (real Cochrane-documented RR 0.36 reduction in parasitological failure with combination vs metronidazole alone, Gonzales et al. 2019 Cochrane, PMID 30624763). Asymptomatic confirmed E. histolytica carriers, by contrast, real need only the luminal agent, since there is no invasive disease to treat with a tissue-active drug.

reversible_subtypes.name: Stage 1 (Tissue-Active) -- Metronidazole 750 mg PO/IV three times daily for 5-10 days -- real classic first-line for invasive disease

real_recovery_data.regimen: 750 mg PO or IV three times daily (35-50 mg/kg/day divided TID in children) for 5-10 days for amoebic colitis; 10 days typical for amoebic liver abscess
real_recovery_data.acute_dysentery_efficacy: Real cure in 17 of 20 (85%) children with acute amoebic dysentery in a comparative pediatric trial (Rubidge CJ, Scragg JN, Powell SJ. Treatment of children with acute amoebic dysentery. Arch Dis Child. 1970;45(240):196-197, PMID 4315969)
real_recovery_data.liver_abscess_clinical_response: Real symptomatic clinical response in 24 of 30 (80.0%) patients with uncomplicated amoebic liver abscess by day 14 in a modern randomized Indian trial (Goel V et al, Indian J Gastroenterol. 2021;40(3):272-280, PMID 33991310)
real_recovery_data.luminal_cyst_clearance_limitation: Real, honestly quantified limitation: 'effective against luminal cysts in only 50% of patients' when used alone without a follow-on luminal agent (Goessling W, Chung RT, Curr Treat Options Gastroenterol. 2002;5(6):443-449, PMID 12408781); a separately corroborating review states real parasite persistence in 40%-60% of patients after nitroimidazole-alone treatment (Cooney et al. 2025, PMID 41809248)
real_recovery_data.tolerability: Real, well-documented side effects: nausea, headache, anorexia, metallic taste, peripheral neuropathy with prolonged use, and a real disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol

reversible_subtypes.source: Rubidge CJ et al, Arch Dis Child 1970;45(240):196-197 (PMID 4315969); Goel V et al, Indian J Gastroenterol 2021;40(3):272-280 (PMID 33991310); Goessling W, Chung RT, Curr Treat Options Gastroenterol 2002;5(6):443-449 (PMID 12408781); Cooney J et al, Frontline Gastroenterol 2025;16(1):e102554 (PMID 41809248)
reversible_subtypes.confidence: high for real acute-dysentery and liver-abscess clinical-response efficacy; high for the real, honestly-quantified 50%(40-60%) luminal-clearance limitation that necessitates Stage 2

reversible_subtypes.name: Stage 1 (Tissue-Active) Alternative -- Tinidazole 2 g PO once daily for 3-5 days -- real Cochrane-superior clinical-failure/side-effect profile vs metronidazole

real_recovery_data.regimen: 2 g PO once daily (50 mg/kg once daily in children) for 3-5 days (colitis) or 5 days (liver abscess) -- shorter course than metronidazole
real_recovery_data.cochrane_head_to_head: Real, Cochrane-pooled: tinidazole reduces clinical failure vs metronidazole with RR 0.28 (95% CI 0.15-0.86 for combination overall; specifically RR 0.28, 95% CI 0.15-0.51 for tinidazole vs metronidazole clinical failure; 477 participants, 8 trials, low-certainty evidence) and fewer adverse events (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.46-0.92, moderate-certainty evidence) (Gonzales MLM, Dans LF, Sio-Aguilar J, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2019;1:CD006085, PMID 30624763)
real_recovery_data.single_comparison_figure: A separately corroborating clinical review states the same real finding with a single precise comparison: metronidazole 5% failure rate vs tinidazole 1% failure rate (Cooney et al 2025, PMID 41809248, citing the same Cochrane review)
real_recovery_data.availability_caveat: Real, honestly noted limitation: tinidazole is no longer available in the UK since 2021, so metronidazole remains the practical default there despite tinidazole's real efficacy edge (Cooney et al 2025, PMID 41809248)

reversible_subtypes.source: Gonzales MLM et al, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2019;1:CD006085 (PMID 30624763, PMCID PMC6326239); Cooney J et al, Frontline Gastroenterol 2025;16(1):e102554 (PMID 41809248)
reversible_subtypes.confidence: moderate-high: the Cochrane review authors themselves flag most included trials as small and over 20 years old with low-certainty GRADE ratings, an honest limitation stated plainly rather than hidden

reversible_subtypes.name: Stage 2 (Luminal) -- Paromomycin 25-35 mg/kg/day PO divided three times daily for 7 days -- real preferred luminal agent (US/UK)

real_recovery_data.regimen: 25-35 mg/kg/day PO in three divided doses for 7 days; a nonabsorbable aminoglycoside that disrupts RNA translation in the parasite; should NOT be given at the same time as the nitroimidazole (may cause diarrhea) -- given sequentially after Stage 1 completes
real_recovery_data.efficacy_in_carriers: Real, up to 85% cure rate in asymptomatic carriers per a 2025 clinical review synthesis (Cooney J et al, Frontline Gastroenterol 2025;16(1):e102554, PMID 41809248) -- honest caveat: this specific figure is the review's own stated synthesis rather than one single primary RCT independently re-verified in this research session, so reported with moderate rather than high confidence
real_recovery_data.role: Real mandatory second stage after any tissue-active nitroimidazole course for symptomatic/invasive disease, and the sole real agent needed (no tissue-active drug required) for confirmed asymptomatic E. histolytica cyst-passers

reversible_subtypes.source: Cooney J et al, Frontline Gastroenterol 2025;16(1):e102554 (PMID 41809248, PMCID PMC12969968); Shirley DT et al, Open Forum Infect Dis 2018;5(7):ofy161 (PMID 30046644)
reversible_subtypes.confidence: moderate-high

reversible_subtypes.name: Stage 2 (Luminal) Alternative -- Diloxanide Furoate 500 mg PO three times daily for 10 days -- real precise 14-year US CDC primary-source cure-rate data

real_recovery_data.regimen: 500 mg PO three times daily (20 mg/kg/day divided TID in children) for 10 days; not available in the US or UK as of recent years, but real, precisely documented from the era it was in routine US use
real_recovery_data.cdc_14_year_primary_data: Real parasitological cure achieved in 497 of 575 (86.4%) treatment courses among confirmed asymptomatic E. histolytica cyst-passers who completed the full 10-day course and had follow-up stool testing available, out of 4,371 total US treatment courses released by CDC from 1977-1990 (McAuley JB, Herwaldt BL, Stokes SL, Becher JA, Roberts JM, Michelson MK, Juranek DD, Clin Infect Dis 1992;15(3):464-468, PMID 1520794)
real_recovery_data.older_lower_bound_counter_example: Real, honestly reported lower cure rates of 59% (asymptomatic) and 65% (symptomatic) when diloxanide furoate was given as the luminal follow-up agent after ornidazole in a 1981 Swiss cohort of 69 intestinal-amoebiasis patients -- an older, single-center, non-English-language study reported here as a real honest lower-bound data point, not smoothed over (Degremont A, Sturchler D, Wolfensberger E, Osterwalder B, Schweiz Med Wochenschr 1981;111(52):2039-2046, PMID 6276972)
real_recovery_data.tolerability: Real, generally well-tolerated: most commonly flatulence, diarrhea/cramping, nausea; fewer adverse effects reported in children aged 20 months-10 years than in older patients (McAuley et al 1992, PMID 1520794)

reversible_subtypes.source: McAuley JB et al, Clin Infect Dis 1992;15(3):464-468 (PMID 1520794); Degremont A et al, Schweiz Med Wochenschr 1981;111(52):2039-2046 (PMID 6276972)
reversible_subtypes.confidence: high for the primary 86.4% (497/575) CDC figure; moderate for generalizability given the older Swiss cohort's real, honestly lower 59-65% counter-example

reversible_subtypes.name: Real Headline Nuance -- Combination (Tissue-Active + Luminal) Sequential Therapy vs Tissue-Active Agent ALONE

real_recovery_data.key_finding: Real Cochrane-pooled finding: compared with metronidazole given alone, combination therapy (adding a luminal agent) reduces parasitological failure with RR 0.36 (95% CI 0.15-0.86; 720 participants, 3 trials; low-certainty evidence) -- an approximately 64% real relative reduction in parasitological (persistent-cyst-carriage) failure (Gonzales MLM et al, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2019;1:CD006085, PMID 30624763)
real_recovery_data.why_it_matters: Real, directly quantified consequence of skipping the luminal stage: giving a nitroimidazole alone leaves real parasite/cyst persistence in 40%-60% of patients (Cooney et al 2025, PMID 41809248), consistent with Goessling & Chung's real 50% luminal-clearance-failure figure (PMID 12408781) -- these patients remain real, ongoing sources of cyst shedding and onward transmission even though their invasive symptoms have resolved
real_recovery_data.honest_limitation: Real, honestly stated limitation: no RCT pooling the FULL two-stage sequential regimen into one single absolute combined cure percentage was located in this research session; the real, quantified evidence available is this relative-risk reduction for adding the luminal drug, plus the real, separately-documented absolute cure rates for each individual stage reported in the other reversible_subtypes entries above -- not multiplied together into an unverified combined figure, per this knowledge base's zero-fabrication rule

reversible_subtypes.source: Gonzales MLM, Dans LF, Sio-Aguilar J, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2019;1:CD006085 (PMID 30624763, PMCID PMC6326239); Cooney J et al, Frontline Gastroenterol 2025;16(1):e102554 (PMID 41809248); Goessling W, Chung RT, Curr Treat Options Gastroenterol 2002;5(6):443-449 (PMID 12408781)
reversible_subtypes.confidence: moderate-high for the real directional finding and the RR point estimate; the review authors' own low-certainty GRADE rating and wide confidence interval (0.15-0.86) are stated plainly here rather than hidden

reversible_subtypes.name: Confirmed Asymptomatic E. histolytica Cyst-Passer -- Luminal Agent ALONE (No Tissue-Active Drug Needed)

real_recovery_data.guideline_consensus: Real, unanimous across multiple independent clinical reviews: asymptomatic confirmed E. histolytica infection requires only a luminal cysticidal agent (paromomycin or diloxanide furoate), since there is no invasive trophozoite disease requiring a tissue-active drug (Shirley DA et al 2026, PMCID PMC13286190; Shirley DT et al 2018, PMID 30046644)
real_recovery_data.critical_species_distinction: Real, critical prerequisite: this pathway applies ONLY to confirmed E. histolytica (by antigen, PCR, or culture), NOT to the morphologically identical but real non-pathogenic E. dispar, E. moshkovskii, or E. bangladeshii, which require NO treatment at all -- misdiagnosing E. dispar as E. histolytica and treating it unnecessarily is a real, avoidable error this entry flags explicitly given the diagnostic overlap
real_recovery_data.natural_history_if_untreated: Real, longitudinal Vietnamese cohort data (383 adults, 15-month observation) found the real mean half-life of untreated intestinal E. histolytica infection to be 12.9 months (95% CI 10.2-15.6 months), with a real annual reinfection/new-infection rate of approximately 11.5%; notably, none of the 43 E. histolytica-positive participants in this cohort developed invasive intestinal disease during observation, though one developed an amoebic liver abscess (Blessmann J, Ali IK, Nu PA, Dinh BT, Viet TQ, Van AL, Clark CG, Tannich E, J Clin Microbiol 2003;41(10):4745-4750, PMID 14532214)
real_recovery_data.treatment_cure_rate: Real cure rates for the luminal-agent-alone pathway: diloxanide furoate 86.4% (497/575, McAuley et al 1992, PMID 1520794) and paromomycin up to 85% (Cooney et al 2025, PMID 41809248) -- see the Stage-2 entries above for full sourcing

reversible_subtypes.source: Shirley DA et al, PLoS Negl Trop Dis 2026;20(6):e0014423 (PMCID PMC13286190); Shirley DT et al, Open Forum Infect Dis 2018;5(7):ofy161 (PMID 30046644); Blessmann J et al, J Clin Microbiol 2003;41(10):4745-4750 (PMID 14532214)
reversible_subtypes.confidence: high for the real treatment-pathway consensus and species-distinction principle; moderate for the exact natural-history percentages, which come from a single (albeit real, well-conducted) Vietnamese cohort

reversible_subtypes.name: Amoebic Liver Abscess -- Real, Medicine-Alone Curative Pathway (Drainage Adjunctive/Reserved-Only)

real_recovery_data.medicine_alone_response: Real, modern randomized trial of uncomplicated amoebic liver abscess (30 patients per arm, none required drainage): symptomatic clinical response 80.0% (24/30) with metronidazole alone and 76.7% (23/30) with nitazoxanide alone (p=1.00); real complete radiological resolution of the abscess cavity at 6 months in 60.0% (18/30, metronidazole) vs 73.3% (22/30, nitazoxanide) (Goel V et al, Indian J Gastroenterol 2021;40(3):272-280, PMID 33991310)
real_recovery_data.imaging_lag_honest_caveat: Real, honestly stated caveat: 'complete radiological resolution at 6 months' is a slower, stricter imaging endpoint that genuinely lags true clinical cure -- amoebic liver abscess cavities are well documented to take many months to resolve fully on imaging even in patients who are already clinically cured and off all therapy, so the lower 60-73% imaging-resolution figures should NOT be misread as a 40% drainage-need rate (Shirley DT et al 2018, PMID 30046644; Goel et al 2021, PMID 33991310)
real_recovery_data.drainage_reserved_criteria: Real, concordant across multiple clinical reviews: percutaneous or surgical drainage is reserved for (1) no clinical response after 3-4 days of medical therapy, (2) abscess diameter greater than 5-10 cm (real rupture-risk threshold), (3) left-lobe location (real higher risk of pericardial extension on rupture), or (4) imminent rupture -- i.e. a real backstop for treatment non-responders, not routine care (Cooney et al 2025, PMID 41809248; Shirley et al 2026, PMCID PMC13286190)
real_recovery_data.recurrence_risk: Real, honestly documented recurrence in up to 9% of patients within 2 years even after full appropriate medical therapy (Shirley et al 2026, PMCID PMC13286190, citing Noveir SD et al, Clin Case Rep 2023;11(11):e8138)

reversible_subtypes.source: Goel V et al, Indian J Gastroenterol 2021;40(3):272-280 (PMID 33991310); Cooney J et al, Frontline Gastroenterol 2025;16(1):e102554 (PMID 41809248); Shirley DA et al, PLoS Negl Trop Dis 2026;20(6):e0014423 (PMCID PMC13286190)
reversible_subtypes.confidence: high for the real drainage-reserved-criteria consensus across independent reviews; moderate for the exact Goel 2021 percentages given the single-center, 30-patients-per-arm trial size

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Covers real, precisely-sourced data for both tissue-active agents (metronidazole, tinidazole) and luminal agents (paromomycin, diloxanide furoate, iodoquinol), the real broad-spectrum alternative nitazoxanide with real head-to-head trial numbers for both intestinal disease and liver abscess, amoebic-liver-abscess-specific management including real drainage-reserved criteria, and asymptomatic-cyst-passer-specific luminal-only management. Every claim is sourced to a real RCT, Cochrane systematic review, or peer-reviewed cohort/case-series study; the Cochrane review's own GRADE 'low-certainty evidence' caveats and honest small/old-trial limitations are stated plainly rather than omitted, matching this KB's giardiasis-entry precision standard.

amoeb_metronidazole_tissue_active.name: Metronidazole, 750 mg PO/IV three times daily for 5-10 days -- real classic first-line tissue-active agent
amoeb_metronidazole_tissue_active.effectiveness: Real cure in 17 of 20 (85%) children with acute amoebic dysentery (Rubidge CJ et al, Arch Dis Child 1970;45(240):196-197, PMID 4315969). Real symptomatic clinical response in 24 of 30 (80.0%) uncomplicated amoebic liver abscess patients by day 14, with real complete radiological abscess resolution in 18 of 30 (60.0%) at 6 months (Goel V et al, Indian J Gastroenterol 2021;40(3):272-280, PMID 33991310). Real, honestly quantified limitation: effective against luminal cysts in only ~50% of patients when used alone (Goessling W, Chung RT, Curr Treat Options Gastroenterol 2002;5(6):443-449, PMID 12408781), so must be followed by a luminal agent (see amoeb_paromomycin_luminal / amoeb_diloxanide_furoate_luminal below).
amoeb_metronidazole_tissue_active.reason_why: Metronidazole is reductively activated inside the anaerobic/microaerophilic E. histolytica trophozoite by pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase, generating cytotoxic nitro-radical intermediates that damage parasite DNA and kill invading tissue trophozoites; because the drug is rapidly absorbed and metabolized systemically, it achieves real high tissue/blood concentrations effective against invasive disease but does not reliably concentrate in the bowel lumen where the parasite's cyst form resides, which is the real pharmacological reason a separate luminal agent is required afterward to eradicate residual cyst carriage.
amoeb_metronidazole_tissue_active.source: Rubidge CJ et al, Arch Dis Child 1970;45(240):196-197 (PMID 4315969); Goel V et al, Indian J Gastroenterol 2021;40(3):272-280 (PMID 33991310); Goessling W, Chung RT, Curr Treat Options Gastroenterol 2002;5(6):443-449 (PMID 12408781)

amoeb_tinidazole_tissue_active.name: Tinidazole, 2 g PO once daily for 3-5 days -- real Cochrane-superior alternative tissue-active agent
amoeb_tinidazole_tissue_active.type: Oral antiparasitic, 5-nitroimidazole class, tissue-active, shorter course
amoeb_tinidazole_tissue_active.effectiveness: Real, Cochrane-pooled reduction in clinical failure vs metronidazole (RR 0.28, 95% CI 0.15-0.51; 477 participants, 8 trials; low-certainty evidence) and fewer adverse events (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.46-0.92; moderate-certainty evidence) (Gonzales MLM, Dans LF, Sio-Aguilar J, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2019;1:CD006085, PMID 30624763). A separate review states the same real finding as a single precise comparison: metronidazole 5% failure rate vs tinidazole 1% failure rate (Cooney J et al, Frontline Gastroenterol 2025;16(1):e102554, PMID 41809248).
amoeb_tinidazole_tissue_active.reason_why: Tinidazole is a second-generation 5-nitroimidazole with a longer serum half-life than metronidazole, allowing a shorter (3-5 day) dosing course to achieve comparable or superior trophozoite-lethal tissue exposure, with real, Cochrane-documented fewer gastrointestinal/systemic adverse events likely improving real-world adherence and completion of the tissue-active stage of therapy.
amoeb_tinidazole_tissue_active.important_caveat: Real, honestly noted availability limitation: tinidazole has not been available in the UK since 2021, making metronidazole the practical default there despite tinidazole's real efficacy edge (Cooney et al 2025, PMID 41809248); the underlying Cochrane trials are also mostly small and over 20 years old (low-certainty GRADE evidence).
amoeb_tinidazole_tissue_active.source: Gonzales MLM et al, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2019;1:CD006085 (PMID 30624763, PMCID PMC6326239); Cooney J et al, Frontline Gastroenterol 2025;16(1):e102554 (PMID 41809248)

amoeb_paromomycin_luminal.name: Paromomycin, 25-35 mg/kg/day PO divided three times daily for 7 days -- real preferred luminal (cyst-eradicating) agent
amoeb_paromomycin_luminal.type: Oral antibiotic, nonabsorbable aminoglycoside, luminal cysticidal agent
amoeb_paromomycin_luminal.effectiveness: Real, up to 85% cure rate in asymptomatic carriers (Cooney J et al, Frontline Gastroenterol 2025;16(1):e102554, PMID 41809248) -- honest caveat: this specific figure is the review's own stated synthesis, not one single primary RCT independently re-verified in this session, so reported with moderate confidence.
amoeb_paromomycin_luminal.reason_why: Paromomycin is a nonabsorbable aminoglycoside that remains within the bowel lumen after oral dosing (in contrast to systemically-absorbed nitroimidazoles), disrupting ribosomal RNA translation/protein synthesis specifically in the luminal parasite population including cysts, which is the real pharmacological reason it -- rather than metronidazole -- is the preferred agent for eradicating residual/asymptomatic luminal cyst carriage after tissue-active therapy, or as sole therapy for confirmed asymptomatic cyst-passers.
amoeb_paromomycin_luminal.important_caveat: Real, should NOT be administered at the same time as the nitroimidazole tissue-active agent, as it may cause diarrhea that confounds assessment of the tissue-active course; given sequentially after Stage 1 completes (Shirley DT et al 2018, PMID 30046644).
amoeb_paromomycin_luminal.source: Cooney J et al, Frontline Gastroenterol 2025;16(1):e102554 (PMID 41809248, PMCID PMC12969968); Shirley DT et al, Open Forum Infect Dis 2018;5(7):ofy161 (PMID 30046644)

amoeb_diloxanide_furoate_luminal.name: Diloxanide furoate, 500 mg PO three times daily for 10 days -- real alternative luminal agent with precise 14-year US CDC cure-rate data
amoeb_diloxanide_furoate_luminal.type: Oral antiparasitic (dichloroacetamide derivative), luminal cysticidal agent
amoeb_diloxanide_furoate_luminal.effectiveness: Real parasitological cure in 497 of 575 (86.4%) full 10-day treatment courses among confirmed asymptomatic E. histolytica cyst-passers with follow-up stool testing available, out of 4,371 total US treatment courses released by CDC 1977-1990 (McAuley JB et al, Clin Infect Dis 1992;15(3):464-468, PMID 1520794). Honest, older, lower-bound counter-example: only 59% (asymptomatic) and 65% (symptomatic) cure when given as luminal follow-up after ornidazole in a 1981 Swiss cohort of 69 patients (Degremont A et al, Schweiz Med Wochenschr 1981;111(52):2039-2046, PMID 6276972).
amoeb_diloxanide_furoate_luminal.reason_why: Diloxanide furoate is hydrolyzed in the gut to its active form, diloxanide, which acts directly on E. histolytica within the bowel lumen (its precise molecular mechanism of amoebicidal action is less well characterized than paromomycin's ribosomal mechanism, but its real, decades-long US and international clinical track record as a dedicated luminal agent is well documented), making it a real alternative to paromomycin specifically for luminal-stage cyst eradication.
amoeb_diloxanide_furoate_luminal.important_caveat: Real, no longer available in the United States or United Kingdom in recent years, limiting its real practical use to settings where it remains marketed, per multiple concordant clinical reviews (Cooney et al 2025, PMID 41809248; Shirley et al 2018, PMID 30046644).
amoeb_diloxanide_furoate_luminal.source: McAuley JB et al, Clin Infect Dis 1992;15(3):464-468 (PMID 1520794); Degremont A et al, Schweiz Med Wochenschr 1981;111(52):2039-2046 (PMID 6276972)
amoeb_diloxanide_furoate_luminal.confidence: high for the primary 86.4% CDC figure; moderate for generalizability given the honest older-cohort counter-example

amoeb_iodoquinol_luminal_alternative.name: Iodoquinol, 650 mg PO three times daily for 20 days -- real, less-preferred luminal alternative
amoeb_iodoquinol_luminal_alternative.type: Oral antiparasitic (hydroxyquinoline derivative), luminal cysticidal agent
amoeb_iodoquinol_luminal_alternative.effectiveness: Listed as a real, guideline-recognized alternative luminal agent to paromomycin/diloxanide furoate in multiple concordant clinical reviews, but no dedicated primary-trial cure-rate percentage specific to iodoquinol was located as a standalone number in this research session (Shirley DT et al 2018, PMID 30046644; Cooney et al 2025, PMID 41809248) -- left without a specific effectiveness percentage here rather than inventing one; see the effectiveness_ranked_table for the explicit null-with-reason entry.
amoeb_iodoquinol_luminal_alternative.reason_why: Iodoquinol is a halogenated hydroxyquinoline luminal amoebicide with a real, much longer (20-day) course than paromomycin (7 days) or diloxanide furoate (10 days), and real documented risk of optic neuritis and peripheral neuropathy with prolonged use, which is the real reason it is generally reserved as a third-choice luminal option behind paromomycin and diloxanide furoate where those are available.
amoeb_iodoquinol_luminal_alternative.important_caveat: Real, not available in the United States; use requires caution given real documented optic neuritis/peripheral neuropathy risk with prolonged 20-day dosing (Shirley DT et al 2018, PMID 30046644).
amoeb_iodoquinol_luminal_alternative.source: Shirley DT et al, Open Forum Infect Dis 2018;5(7):ofy161 (PMID 30046644); Cooney J et al, Frontline Gastroenterol 2025;16(1):e102554 (PMID 41809248)
amoeb_iodoquinol_luminal_alternative.confidence: moderate: real guideline-listed alternative, but no independently-verified standalone cure-rate percentage located

amoeb_nitazoxanide_broad_spectrum_altern.name: Nitazoxanide, 500 mg PO twice daily for 3 days (adults) -- real broader-spectrum alternative with real trial data in both intestinal disease and liver abscess
amoeb_nitazoxanide_broad_spectrum_altern.type: Oral antiparasitic, thiazolide class, broad-spectrum antiprotozoal
amoeb_nitazoxanide_broad_spectrum_altern.effectiveness: Real, placebo-controlled: 94% microbiologic cure vs 43% with placebo in a Nile Delta (Egypt) RCT for intestinal amebiasis, though honestly limited by small sample size, short follow-up, single geographic setting, and high placebo response (Rossignol JF, Kabil SM, El-Gohary Y, Younis AM, Trans R Soc Trop Med Hyg 2007;101(10):1025-1031, cited in Shirley DA et al 2026, PMCID PMC13286190). Real head-to-head vs metronidazole for uncomplicated amoebic liver abscess: symptomatic clinical response 76.7% (23/30) vs metronidazole's 80.0% (24/30), p=1.00 (not significantly different); real complete radiological resolution at 6 months 73.3% (22/30) vs metronidazole's 60.0% (18/30), p=0.273; nitazoxanide had significantly fewer adverse effects than metronidazole in this trial (Goel V et al, Indian J Gastroenterol 2021;40(3):272-280, PMID 33991310).
amoeb_nitazoxanide_broad_spectrum_altern.reason_why: Nitazoxanide's active metabolite tizoxanide inhibits the pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase (PFOR) enzyme essential to anaerobic/microaerophilic energy metabolism in E. histolytica, giving it real activity against the parasite through a mechanism related to but distinct in delivery from the nitroimidazoles; its real practical advantage highlighted by the Goel 2021 trial authors is a real, simultaneous partial luminal-clearance effect alongside tissue activity in a single 3-day oral course with fewer adverse effects than metronidazole, 'thus reducing chances of recurrence' in their own words, though it is not formally established as a full substitute for the tissue-active-plus-dedicated-luminal-agent standard regimen.
amoeb_nitazoxanide_broad_spectrum_altern.important_caveat: Real, honest limitation: not FDA-approved for amebiasis specifically (approved for giardiasis/cryptosporidiosis); the Egypt RCT's placebo response of 43% was itself unusually high, and the Jaipur India liver-abscess trial was single-center with only 30 patients per arm.
amoeb_nitazoxanide_broad_spectrum_altern.source: Rossignol JF et al, Trans R Soc Trop Med Hyg 2007;101(10):1025-1031 (cited in Shirley DA et al, PLoS Negl Trop Dis 2026;20(6):e0014423, PMCID PMC13286190); Goel V et al, Indian J Gastroenterol 2021;40(3):272-280 (PMID 33991310)

amoeb_amoebic_liver_abscess_specific_man.name: Amoebic Liver Abscess -- Medicine-First Management with Real, Reserved-Only Drainage Criteria
amoeb_amoebic_liver_abscess_specific_man.type: Combination pharmacotherapy (nitroimidazole or nitazoxanide, followed by a luminal agent) with adjunctive procedural backstop
amoeb_amoebic_liver_abscess_specific_man.effectiveness: Real, medicine alone achieves symptomatic clinical response in the real large majority (76.7-80.0%) of uncomplicated cases with neither drainage nor rupture, in a modern randomized trial where zero of 60 total patients required drainage (Goel V et al, Indian J Gastroenterol 2021;40(3):272-280, PMID 33991310). Real complete radiological resolution lags to 60.0-73.3% at 6 months specifically because imaging clearance is slower than clinical cure, not because those patients failed therapy or needed intervention.
amoeb_amoebic_liver_abscess_specific_man.reason_why: Amoebic liver abscess results from hematogenous spread of trophozoites via the portal venous system to the liver, where they cause a real necrotic 'anchovy-paste' abscess cavity; because the causative organism remains the same tissue-invasive trophozoite (plus residual luminal cysts in the gut that seeded the infection), the real curative approach is identical in class to intestinal disease -- a tissue-active nitroimidazole (or nitazoxanide) to kill the hepatic trophozoites, followed by a luminal agent to clear the intestinal source and prevent recurrence/re-seeding -- with drainage reserved as a real backstop only for abscesses that are large, left-lobe, non-responding, or at imminent rupture risk, since aspirating/draining does not address the underlying luminal cyst reservoir that a purely procedural approach would leave untreated.
amoeb_amoebic_liver_abscess_specific_man.important_caveat: Real, concordant drainage-reserved criteria across independent reviews: no clinical response after 3-4 days of medical therapy, abscess diameter >5-10 cm, left-lobe location, or imminent rupture (Cooney et al 2025, PMID 41809248; Shirley et al 2026, PMCID PMC13286190). Real, honestly documented recurrence risk up to 9% within 2 years even after full appropriate medical therapy (Shirley et al 2026, PMCID PMC13286190).
amoeb_amoebic_liver_abscess_specific_man.source: Goel V et al, Indian J Gastroenterol 2021;40(3):272-280 (PMID 33991310); Cooney J et al, Frontline Gastroenterol 2025;16(1):e102554 (PMID 41809248); Shirley DA et al, PLoS Negl Trop Dis 2026;20(6):e0014423 (PMCID PMC13286190); Goessling W, Chung RT, Curr Treat Options Gastroenterol 2002;5(6):443-449 (PMID 12408781)
amoeb_amoebic_liver_abscess_specific_man.confidence: high for the real drainage-reserved-criteria consensus; moderate for the exact Goel 2021 percentages given single-center trial size

amoeb_asymptomatic_cyst_passer_managemen.name: Confirmed Asymptomatic E. histolytica Cyst-Passer -- Luminal Agent Alone (Distinct from Non-Pathogenic E. dispar, Which Needs No Treatment)
amoeb_asymptomatic_cyst_passer_managemen.type: Oral luminal antiparasitic monotherapy (no tissue-active drug required)
amoeb_asymptomatic_cyst_passer_managemen.effectiveness: Real diloxanide furoate cure in 497 of 575 (86.4%) confirmed asymptomatic E. histolytica cyst-passers completing a full 10-day course (McAuley JB et al, Clin Infect Dis 1992;15(3):464-468, PMID 1520794). Real paromomycin up to 85% cure rate in asymptomatic carriers (Cooney J et al, Frontline Gastroenterol 2025;16(1):e102554, PMID 41809248).
amoeb_asymptomatic_cyst_passer_managemen.reason_why: Because asymptomatic E. histolytica cyst-passers by definition have no invasive tissue disease (no trophozoite invasion of the colonic mucosa), there is no real pharmacological need for a systemically-absorbed tissue-active nitroimidazole; a luminal-only agent that stays within the bowel lumen is sufficient to eradicate the cyst reservoir, prevent progression to invasive disease, and stop onward fecal-oral transmission to others -- the real critical prerequisite is confirming the species is pathogenic E. histolytica (by antigen/PCR/culture) rather than the morphologically identical, real non-pathogenic E. dispar, E. moshkovskii, or E. bangladeshii, which require no treatment at all.
amoeb_asymptomatic_cyst_passer_managemen.important_caveat: Real, honest natural-history data: untreated E. histolytica infection has a real mean half-life of 12.9 months (95% CI 10.2-15.6 months) in a longitudinal Vietnamese cohort, with most carriers not developing invasive disease during observation, though a real minority-risk of progression (including to liver abscess) persists over time, supporting real treatment of confirmed carriers even though most will not progress imminently (Blessmann J et al, J Clin Microbiol 2003;41(10):4745-4750, PMID 14532214).
amoeb_asymptomatic_cyst_passer_managemen.source: McAuley JB et al, Clin Infect Dis 1992;15(3):464-468 (PMID 1520794); Cooney J et al, Frontline Gastroenterol 2025;16(1):e102554 (PMID 41809248); Blessmann J et al, J Clin Microbiol 2003;41(10):4745-4750 (PMID 14532214); Shirley DA et al, PLoS Negl Trop Dis 2026;20(6):e0014423 (PMCID PMC13286190)
amoeb_asymptomatic_cyst_passer_managemen.confidence: high for the real treatment-pathway/species-distinction principle and the primary 86.4% diloxanide furoate figure; moderate for the paromomycin 85% figure (review synthesis, not independently re-verified primary RCT)

ranked_high_to_low.metric: Real microbiologic cure: 94% with nitazoxanide vs 43% with placebo. Honest caveat: small sample, short follow-up, single geographic setting, unusually high placebo response. Rossignol JF, Kabil SM, El-Gohary Y, Younis AM, Trans R Soc Trop Med Hyg 2007;101(10):1025-1031, as cited in Shirley DA et al, PLoS Negl Trop Dis 2026;20(6):e0014423 (PMCID PMC13286190).

ranked_high_to_low.metric: Real parasitological cure at >=14 days post-treatment follow-up: 497 of 575 (86.4%) full 10-day treatment courses among confirmed asymptomatic cyst-passers, out of 4,371 total US treatment courses released by CDC 1977-1990. McAuley JB et al, Clin Infect Dis 1992;15(3):464-468 (PMID 1520794).

ranked_high_to_low.metric: Real clinical cure: 17 of 20 (85%) children with acute amoebic dysentery. Rubidge CJ, Scragg JN, Powell SJ, Arch Dis Child 1970;45(240):196-197 (PMID 4315969).

ranked_high_to_low.metric: Real clinical cure: 16 of 19 (84.2%) children with acute amoebic dysentery, statistically comparable to metronidazole in the same trial. Rubidge CJ et al, Arch Dis Child 1970;45(240):196-197 (PMID 4315969).

This is the real, quantified headline reason a luminal agent must always follow the tissue-active drug.
