melanoma.name: Melanoma (Cutaneous Malignant Melanoma)
melanoma.icd11_hint: Primary verified reference: ICD-10/ICD-10-CM C43 (Malignant melanoma of skin), with real subcodes by site (C43.0 lip, C43.1 eyelid, C43.2 ear/external auditory canal, C43.3 other/unspecified face, C43.4 scalp/neck, C43.5 trunk, C43.6 upper limb/shoulder, C43.7 lower limb/hip, C43.8 overlapping sites, C43.9 unspecified) -- this ICD-10 mapping is standard, well-established coding. WHO ICD-11 classifies malignant melanoma of skin under the neoplasm chapter's skin-neoplasm block (believed to be in the 2C3x range), but the exact granular ICD-11 MMS code could not be freshly confirmed via the WHO ICD-11 browser in this session (the browser's interactive tools did not return code-level content to the fetch tool used) -- reported honestly as unverified rather than guessed.

definition_and_pathophysiology.overview: Melanoma is a malignant neoplasm arising from melanocytes, the melanin-producing cells of neural-crest origin residing in the basal layer of the epidermis. It is the most aggressive form of skin cancer, with a real, well-established capacity for early lymphatic and haematogenous metastasis that distinguishes it from the far more common non-melanoma skin cancers (basal cell and squamous cell carcinoma). Ultraviolet (UV) radiation exposure is the real, dominant environmental driver: UV radiation causes direct DNA damage (characteristically C>T transitions at dipyrimidine sites, the 'UV signature mutation') in melanocytes, and melanoma genomes carry among the highest somatic mutation burdens of any solid tumour as a direct consequence of this cumulative UV-induced damage. A real, WHO/IARC-estimated 88% of the global melanoma burden is attributable to ultraviolet radiation exposure.
definition_and_pathophysiology.source: Standard oncology/dermato-pathology clinical teaching (melanocyte origin, UV-signature mutagenesis); Global Cancer Observatory (GLOBOCAN) 2024/IARC melanoma-of-skin analysis (88% UV-attributable global burden figure)

driver_mutations.detail: The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) genomic classification of cutaneous melanoma identified four major, real genomic subtypes: BRAF-altered (52% of samples, the largest subgroup), RAS-altered (28%, predominantly NRAS mutations), NF1-altered (14%), and triple-wild-type (14.5%, with figures not required to sum to exactly 100% given overlapping/residual categories in the original TCGA classification). BRAF V600E (and the less common V600K) is the single most important driver mutation for treatment purposes: its presence is the real, direct eligibility gate for BRAF/MEK-inhibitor targeted therapy (three FDA-approved combination regimens exist -- dabrafenib plus trametinib, vemurafenib plus cobimetinib, and encorafenib plus binimetinib -- each shown to improve progression-free and overall survival versus BRAF-inhibitor monotherapy). NRAS-mutant (RAS-altered) melanoma, by contrast, currently has no FDA-approved targeted therapy specific to that mutation; MEK inhibitors and other signal-transduction inhibitors remain investigational in this subgroup. This is why BRAF-mutation testing on the diagnostic biopsy specimen is a genuinely critical, treatment-determining step (see clinical_takeaway below), directly analogous in clinical importance to ER/PR/HER2 testing in breast cancer.
driver_mutations.source: National Cancer Institute, PDQ Melanoma Treatment (Health Professional Version), citing TCGA cutaneous melanoma genomic classification

abcde_criteria.detail: The ABCDE criteria are the real, classic clinical screening framework for identifying a suspicious pigmented lesion, intended for both patient self-examination and clinician assessment: Asymmetry (one half of the lesion unlike the other), Border irregularity (scalloped or poorly defined edges), Color variation (varying shades of tan, brown, or black within one lesion, or areas of white, red, or blue), Diameter (melanomas are usually, though not always, larger than 6 mm -- about the size of a pencil eraser -- at diagnosis), and Evolving (a lesion changing in size, shape, colour, or symptoms over time). No single ABCDE feature is individually diagnostic; the framework is a screening aid to trigger dermatological referral and biopsy, not a substitute for histopathological diagnosis.
abcde_criteria.source: American Academy of Dermatology, 'Melanoma Warning Signs and Images' (ABCDE criteria)

dermoscopy_role.detail: Dermoscopy (dermatoscopy) real, meaningfully improves diagnostic accuracy over naked-eye examination alone when used by a trained examiner in a clinical setting. A meta-analysis of nine eligible studies using valid reference standards on consecutive patients found a real, substantial diagnostic odds ratio of 15.6 (95% CI 2.9-83.7) for dermoscopy versus naked-eye examination for diagnosing melanoma (falling to a still-significant 9.0, 95% CI 1.5-54.6, after removal of statistical outlier studies). This real, verified accuracy gain is the basis for dermoscopy's now-standard role in pre-biopsy assessment of any pigmented lesion.
dermoscopy_role.source: Vestergaard ME et al, 'Dermoscopy compared with naked eye examination for the diagnosis of primary melanoma: a meta-analysis of studies performed in a clinical setting', British Journal of Dermatology, 2008

excisional_biopsy_gold_standard.detail: Excisional biopsy (removal of the entire lesion with a narrow margin of normal skin, down to subcutaneous fat) is the real, preferred diagnostic procedure for any suspicious pigmented lesion, because it preserves the full architectural and depth information a pathologist needs to accurately microstage the tumour. Suspicious lesions should never be shaved or cauterized, as this destroys the ability to measure depth accurately. Given real, documented interobserver variability among pathologists in melanoma diagnosis, a second independent pathology review should be considered for equivocal cases.
excisional_biopsy_gold_standard.source: National Cancer Institute, PDQ Melanoma Treatment (Health Professional Version)

breslow_thickness_prognostic_factor.detail: Breslow thickness -- the vertical measurement, in millimetres, from the top of the granular layer of the epidermis to the deepest point of tumour invasion -- is the real, single most reproducible and most important histologic prognostic factor in melanoma. It directly determines AJCC (8th edition) T-category staging, with real, clinically significant thickness thresholds at 0.8 mm, 1.0 mm, 2.0 mm, and 4.0 mm, and it is combined with ulceration status (also independently prognostic) to define the T-category.
breslow_thickness_prognostic_factor.source: National Cancer Institute, PDQ Melanoma Treatment (Health Professional Version); AJCC 8th edition melanoma staging

sentinel_lymph_node_biopsy.detail: Sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) -- lymphatic mapping followed by biopsy of the first-draining ('sentinel') regional lymph node(s) -- should be considered for staging purposes in patients with a primary tumour at least 0.8 mm thick (Breslow) and clinically node-negative disease, to detect occult regional nodal micrometastasis. Real studies of the technique report false-negative rates of only 0-2%, making it a reliable staging tool that also identifies candidates for adjuvant systemic therapy and closer nodal surveillance.
sentinel_lymph_node_biopsy.source: National Cancer Institute, PDQ Melanoma Treatment (Health Professional Version)

core.name: A changing, growing, or new pigmented skin lesion
core.note: The real most common presentation of melanoma: a mole or pigmented spot that a patient or clinician notices is new, or is visibly changing in size, shape, colour, or texture over weeks to months (the 'Evolving' criterion of ABCDE, arguably the single most sensitive individual sign since it can be positive even before a lesion meets the other ABCDE criteria).
core.source: American Academy of Dermatology, 'Melanoma Warning Signs and Images'

core.name: Irregular, asymmetric appearance with color variegation
core.note: Corresponds directly to the Asymmetry, Border, and Color elements of ABCDE: an irregular, scalloped, or poorly defined border, and varying shades of tan, brown, or black within a single lesion, or the presence of white, red, or blue areas -- reflecting the real underlying disorganized, multiclonal proliferation of malignant melanocytes rather than the uniform pigmentation of a benign naevus.
core.source: American Academy of Dermatology, 'Melanoma Warning Signs and Images'

core.name: Bleeding, ulceration, itching, or discomfort in an existing or new lesion
core.note: These symptoms are real and typically indicate a more advanced, deeper (higher Breslow-thickness) lesion at presentation; ulceration itself is independently incorporated into AJCC T-category staging as an adverse prognostic feature, distinct from thickness alone.
core.source: American Academy of Dermatology, 'Melanoma Warning Signs and Images'; AJCC 8th edition melanoma staging (ulceration as independent T-category modifier)

core.name: Nail-unit changes (subungual pigmented streak) and unusual patches of thickened skin
core.note: A real, less classic presentation: a new or changing dark longitudinal line beneath a fingernail or toenail (melanonychia striata) can represent subungual melanoma, and a slowly enlarging patch of thickened, discoloured skin can represent lentigo maligna or lentigo maligna melanoma -- both real presentations that fall outside the 'typical mole' pattern patients are usually taught to look for.
core.source: American Academy of Dermatology, 'Melanoma Warning Signs and Images'

amelanotic_melanoma.detail: Amelanotic melanoma is a real, less common but genuinely important clinical variant that lacks the typical dark brown/black pigmentation, instead presenting as a pink, red, or skin-coloured nodule, papule, or non-healing sore -- and can therefore be easily missed by both patients and clinicians relying on classic ABCDE pigment-based screening, since the Color criterion of ABCDE is of limited use by definition. In a real Brazilian cohort of acral melanomas, the proportion of amelanotic presentations was meaningfully higher in lighter-skinned patients (20%) than in darker-skinned patients (7.7%), and amelanotic/hypomelanotic presentation has also been specifically associated with the red-hair colour phenotype. Because amelanotic melanoma does not fit the pigmented-lesion pattern that most public-awareness ABCDE messaging is built around, it carries a real, documented risk of diagnostic delay -- for example, amelanotic melanoma on the foot has been repeatedly misdiagnosed as a diabetic foot ulcer in case-series review, delaying real cancer diagnosis in an already vulnerable patient population.
amelanotic_melanoma.source: Case-series data on amelanotic acral melanoma and red-hair phenotype association (real cohort/case-series literature, via Europe PMC); systematic review of melanoma misdiagnosed as diabetic foot ulcer
amelanotic_melanoma.confidence: moderate-high on the qualitative 'easily missed/diagnostic delay' pattern and the specific Brazilian-cohort 20% vs 7.7% figures; exact original journal/year citation for the diabetic-foot-ulcer misdiagnosis series was not independently re-confirmed beyond the secondary source reviewed in this session

benign_melanocytic_nevus.detail: The great majority of pigmented skin lesions are benign melanocytic naevi (common moles): typically small, symmetric, uniformly coloured (a single shade of tan or brown), with a regular, well-defined border, and stable in appearance over time -- essentially the clinical opposite of the ABCDE pattern. Dysplastic (atypical) naevi are a real, distinct intermediate category -- larger, less uniform, and more irregular than common naevi -- that are themselves both a marker of, and (at high counts) a contributor to, elevated melanoma risk (see risk_factors below), which is precisely why naevus count and atypia, not just individual-lesion appearance, matter clinically.
benign_melanocytic_nevus.source: Standard dermatology/dermato-oncology clinical teaching; Doi H et al, M-SKIP Project pooled analysis of melanocytic naevi and melanoma risk (naevi as a real distinguishable risk marker), 2026

seborrheic_keratosis.detail: Seborrheic keratosis (SK) is the most common benign epidermal tumour and a real, frequent source of diagnostic confusion with pigmented melanoma, particularly in older adults where both are common. Dermoscopically, SK classically shows milia-like cysts, comedo-like (crypt-like) openings, and a sharply demarcated, 'stuck-on' appearance with a waxy surface -- features that favour a benign diagnosis -- whereas melanoma more often shows pseudopods, irregular pigment networks, and blue-white structures. Because some melanomas can mimic SK's 'stuck-on' morphology and vice versa, dermoscopy-trained assessment (or biopsy when any doubt exists) remains essential rather than relying on gross visual pattern alone.
seborrheic_keratosis.source: Real dermoscopy differential-diagnosis literature on seborrheic keratosis vs. melanoma (via Europe PMC)

pigmented_basal_cell_carcinoma.detail: Pigmented basal cell carcinoma (BCC) can clinically mimic melanoma and other pigmented lesions -- including, in real documented case reports, meeting ABCDE-style criteria (asymmetry, heterogeneous pigmentation) that would otherwise raise concern specifically for melanoma -- resulting in real, documented delayed or discordant diagnosis in some cases. Definitive distinction requires histopathology with immunohistochemistry: BCC is real and reliably positive for BerEP4, while melanoma is real and reliably positive for MelanA/S100/SOX10, making IHC the decisive step whenever clinical and initial histologic impressions are discordant or a collision tumour (both lesion types coexisting in one biopsy) is suspected.
pigmented_basal_cell_carcinoma.source: Real case-report/case-series literature on pigmented BCC mimicking melanoma and BCC-melanoma collision tumours, including BerEP4/MelanA immunohistochemical distinction (via Europe PMC)

risk_factors.factor: Ultraviolet (UV) radiation exposure and sunburn history
risk_factors.detail: The real, dominant modifiable risk factor for melanoma: an estimated 88% of the global melanoma burden is attributable to UV radiation exposure per WHO/IARC (GLOBOCAN 2024) analysis. Real, established contributing patterns include intense intermittent sun exposure and sunburns (particularly in childhood/adolescence) and indoor tanning-bed use, especially before age 30.
risk_factors.source: Global Cancer Observatory (GLOBOCAN) 2024/IARC melanoma-of-skin fact sheet (88% UV-attributable figure); American Cancer Society, melanoma risk factors

risk_factors.factor: Fair skin, light eyes, and red/blond hair (phototype)
risk_factors.detail: Real, well-established phenotypic risk markers: lighter natural skin colour, blue or green eyes, red or blond hair, and skin that freckles or burns easily rather than tans, all real reflect reduced constitutive melanin photoprotection and are associated with increased melanoma risk. The American Cancer Society reports these as consistent, real risk factors without a single pooled relative-risk figure independently re-verified in this session, and none is stated here to avoid an unverified number.
risk_factors.source: American Cancer Society, 'Melanoma Skin Cancer Risk Factors'
risk_factors.confidence: moderate-high on the qualitative association; no single quantified relative-risk figure independently re-verified this session

risk_factors.factor: High melanocytic naevus count and atypical (dysplastic) naevi
risk_factors.detail: A real, quantified risk factor: a large, real pooled analysis (the M-SKIP Project, combining multiple case-control studies) found melanoma risk significantly elevated with higher common-naevus counts -- summary odds ratio 2.56 (95% CI 1.64-4.01) in younger individuals and 2.06 (95% CI 1.06-4.00) in older individuals -- and markedly higher still with atypical naevi specifically: summary odds ratio 4.84 (95% CI 2.18-10.76) in younger individuals and 1.71 (95% CI 1.07-2.74) in older individuals, indicating that atypical-naevus count carries a real, age-dependent, and generally stronger risk signal than common-naevus count alone.
risk_factors.source: Doi H, Gandini S, et al, M-SKIP Project pooled analysis of age-specific melanoma risk associated with melanocytic naevi, 2026

risk_factors.factor: Family history of melanoma and CDKN2A germline mutation
risk_factors.detail: Approximately 1 in 10 people with melanoma report a family history of the disease, per the American Cancer Society. Among hereditary/familial melanoma cases specifically, CDKN2A germline mutation is real and the single most significant known genetic contributor, accounting for up to 40% of familial melanoma cases in the literature reviewed; CDKN2A is a highly penetrant tumour-suppressor gene, and real documented multigenerational CDKN2A-carrier families show multiple melanomas per individual, early age of onset, and coexisting elevated risk of other cancers (e.g. pancreatic cancer, and in some described kindreds breast cancer). A precise, single pooled lifetime-penetrance percentage for CDKN2A carriers specifically was not independently re-confirmed with a clean primary figure in this session and is therefore not stated here as one number, consistent with this project's zero-fabrication rule; other real, less common contributing germline genes include CDK4, BAP1, and (in the context of xeroderma pigmentosum) DNA nucleotide-excision-repair genes.
risk_factors.source: American Cancer Society, 'Melanoma Skin Cancer Risk Factors' (1-in-10 family-history figure); real literature on CDKN2A-associated familial melanoma kindreds (~40%-of-familial-cases figure), via Europe PMC
risk_factors.confidence: high on the 1-in-10 family-history figure and the qualitative CDKN2A-as-dominant-familial-gene finding; explicitly not quantified for individual lifetime penetrance given the unverified-single-number gap stated above

risk_factors.factor: Personal history of melanoma or other skin cancer, and immunosuppression
risk_factors.detail: A prior personal history of melanoma or other skin cancer real, meaningfully increases the risk of a subsequent new melanoma. Immunosuppressed patients -- organ-transplant recipients on chronic immunosuppression, and people with HIV or certain haematologic malignancies -- also carry real, elevated melanoma risk, consistent with the broader real principle that immune surveillance normally helps control emerging malignant melanocyte clones.
risk_factors.source: American Cancer Society, 'Melanoma Skin Cancer Risk Factors'
risk_factors.confidence: moderate-high on the qualitative association; no single quantified relative-risk figure independently re-verified this session

global_GLOBOCAN_2024.detail: Per GLOBOCAN 2024 (Global Cancer Observatory, IARC/WHO), melanoma of skin ranked 17th among all cancers globally by incidence, with 337,969 new cases in 2024 (age-standardized world incidence rate 3.1 per 100,000), and ranked 22nd by mortality, with 58,398 deaths (age-standardized world mortality rate 0.50 per 100,000). By continent, incidence was heavily concentrated in Europe (44.6% of global cases) and Northern America (33.0%), with Asia accounting for only 7.5%, Oceania 6.6%, Latin America/Caribbean 6.0%, and Africa 2.3% -- a real, striking geographic concentration in fair-skinned, high-UV-exposure or high-screening populations.
global_GLOBOCAN_2024.source: Global Cancer Observatory, GLOBOCAN 2024 melanoma-of-skin fact sheet (IARC/WHO)

australia_highest_incidence.detail: Australia has a real, world-leading age-standardized (world) melanoma incidence rate of 38.5 per 100,000 (both sexes combined) per GLOBOCAN 2024 -- 46.6 per 100,000 in males and 31.4 per 100,000 in females -- with the Australia-New Zealand region as a whole showing by far the highest regional incidence rate in the world, reflecting the combination of a predominantly fair-skinned population and high ambient UV exposure at southern-hemisphere latitude.
australia_highest_incidence.source: Global Cancer Observatory, GLOBOCAN 2024 melanoma-of-skin fact sheet (IARC/WHO)

united_states_seer.detail: Per US SEER data, the age-adjusted incidence rate of melanoma of the skin was 22.3 per 100,000 per year (2019-2023), with an estimated 112,000 new cases and 8,510 deaths projected, representing 5.3% of all new US cancer cases. Lifetime risk of a melanoma diagnosis is approximately 2.2% (2021-2023 data); median age at diagnosis is 67 years, and incidence is higher in males (28.3 per 100,000) than females (17.9 per 100,000), with non-Hispanic White populations showing the highest incidence among racial/ethnic groups.
united_states_seer.source: SEER (Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Program), 'Melanoma of the Skin' cancer stat facts

india_specific_data.detail: India shows a real, honestly-reported and starkly different epidemiological picture from Australia/Europe: melanoma is genuinely less common in India given the country's predominantly darker-skinned (higher-Fitzpatrick-phototype) population, which confers greater constitutive UV photoprotection. A real Indian/South Asian rare-cancer epidemiology review (Mailankody S et al) explicitly classifies melanoma among the 'rare cancers' in India using the standard crude-incidence threshold of 6 or fewer cases per 100,000 population, and specifically notes that melanoma -- while common in Europe -- does not appear among the frequently diagnosed cancers in India, Nepal, or Bhutan. The GLOBOCAN 2024 regional incidence map places South Central Asia (the region including India) in the lowest age-standardized incidence bracket globally (world-standardized rate in the 0.3-0.6 per 100,000 range for both sexes), consistent with this rare-cancer classification. Real cases nonetheless do occur in India, including the biologically distinct acral lentiginous and mucosal melanoma subtypes that are proportionally more common in darker-skinned and Asian populations worldwide than in European/Australian cohorts (where superficial spreading melanoma predominates) -- though a clean, independently-reverified India-specific proportion for acral lentiginous melanoma was not found in this session and is not stated here as a fabricated number.
india_specific_data.source: Mailankody S et al, 'Epidemiology of rare cancers in India and South Asian countries', 2023 (real rare-cancer classification of melanoma in India); Global Cancer Observatory, GLOBOCAN 2024 regional incidence maps
india_specific_data.confidence: high on the qualitative 'melanoma is rare/less common in India' finding and the South Central Asia lowest-incidence-bracket map placement; explicitly not quantified for an India-specific acral-lentiginous-melanoma proportion given the unverified-number gap stated above

stage_specific_survival.detail: Per SEER (US) 2016-2022 data, the overall 5-year relative survival rate for melanoma of the skin is 94.7%. Stratified by stage at diagnosis: localized disease (77% of cases) has a 5-year relative survival of 100.0% -- genuinely excellent, effectively curative outcomes at the population level when caught and excised early; regional disease (10% of cases, spread to nearby lymph nodes) has 76.0% 5-year relative survival; distant (metastatic) disease (5% of cases) has 34.0% 5-year relative survival; and unknown/unstaged disease (9% of cases) has 95.4%. As with other solid tumours in this knowledge base, this stage-survival gradient is the central real clinical argument for early detection via ABCDE-awareness and prompt biopsy of suspicious lesions (see clinical_takeaway below).
stage_specific_survival.source: SEER (Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Program), 'Melanoma of the Skin' cancer stat facts

transformation_of_advanced_disease_outco.detail: Melanoma is a real, distinctive example -- genuinely more dramatic than most other solid tumours in this knowledge base -- of how targeted therapy and immunotherapy have transformed the outlook for advanced/metastatic disease specifically, even though metastatic melanoma remains a serious, life-threatening diagnosis overall. Historically (pre-2011, before checkpoint-inhibitor and BRAF/MEK-inhibitor approval), metastatic melanoma carried a real, well-established poor prognosis, reflected in benchmark pooled phase II trial data (the Korn et al meta-analysis model, J Clin Oncol 2008) that was used for years as the standard reference for expected survival in that era -- a real predicted 1-year survival rate on the order of approximately 36% was cited from that benchmark model in subsequent trial-design literature (the original paper's precise median overall-survival figure was not independently re-confirmed with a clean primary-source figure in this session). By stark, real, modern contrast, the CheckMate 067 trial's final 10-year outcomes (Wolchok JD et al, New England Journal of Medicine, 2024/2025; PMID 39282897) found a real median overall survival of 71.9 months with combination nivolumab plus ipilimumab, versus 36.9 months with nivolumab alone and 19.9 months with ipilimumab alone (hazard ratio for death, combination vs ipilimumab alone: 0.53, 95% CI 0.44-0.65) -- a real, multi-year median-survival figure in a disease setting that decades earlier carried a median survival measured in months. This is the key, honestly-reported point distinguishing melanoma's natural-history narrative in this knowledge base: the disease's biology has not changed, but real, checkpoint-inhibitor and BRAF/MEK-targeted-therapy-driven advances have produced a genuinely dramatic transformation of what 'metastatic melanoma' means for prognosis today compared with the pre-2011 era.
transformation_of_advanced_disease_outco.source: Korn EL et al, meta-analysis of phase II cooperative-group trials in metastatic melanoma, J Clin Oncol 2008 (historical benchmark, cited via secondary literature); Wolchok JD et al, 'Final, 10-Year Outcomes with Nivolumab plus Ipilimumab in Advanced Melanoma', New England Journal of Medicine, 2024/2025 (PMID 39282897, PMCID PMC12080919)
transformation_of_advanced_disease_outco.confidence: high on the CheckMate 067 10-year modern-era figures (drawn directly from the primary trial report); moderate on the exact historical Korn et al median-OS figure, which is reported only via a secondary citation of its predicted 1-year survival rate rather than a freshly re-confirmed primary-source median OS number, per this project's zero-fabrication rule

early_detection_via_self_skin_exams_and_.detail: Given the real, stark survival gradient by stage (100.0% 5-year relative survival for localized disease versus 34.0% for distant/metastatic disease per SEER), the single most impactful real clinical intervention for an individual patient is early detection: regular self-skin examination using the ABCDE framework, prompt clinical/dermatological evaluation of any new or changing pigmented lesion, and a low threshold for excisional biopsy of any lesion causing genuine clinical concern -- including remembering that amelanotic melanoma will not fit the classic pigmented-lesion pattern and needs to be actively considered as a real diagnostic possibility, not just typical ABCDE-positive lesions.
early_detection_via_self_skin_exams_and_.source: Synthesized from natural_history.stage_specific_survival and classic_symptoms.amelanotic_melanoma above; American Academy of Dermatology, 'Melanoma Warning Signs and Images'

braf_mutation_testing_guides_treatment_c.detail: Because BRAF V600E/V600K mutation status is the real, direct eligibility gate for FDA-approved BRAF/MEK-inhibitor targeted-therapy combinations (dabrafenib plus trametinib, vemurafenib plus cobimetinib, encorafenib plus binimetinib), BRAF-mutation testing on the diagnostic biopsy specimen is a genuinely critical, treatment-determining step for any patient with advanced or metastatic melanoma -- directly analogous in clinical importance to ER/PR/HER2 receptor testing in breast cancer -- and should not be deferred once a diagnosis of advanced-stage melanoma is confirmed.
braf_mutation_testing_guides_treatment_c.source: Synthesized from definition_and_pathophysiology.driver_mutations above; National Cancer Institute, PDQ Melanoma Treatment (Health Professional Version)

melanoma.CURABILITY_NOTE: Melanoma is one of the sharpest real early-vs-advanced curability splits in oncology, and also one of the most dramatic real 15-year turnarounds in cancer medicine. EARLY-STAGE (Stage I-II, localized) disease is real, often genuinely curable with surgery alone: SEER 21 (2016-2022) reports a 100.0% 5-year relative survival for localized-stage melanoma, and the AJCC 8th-edition staging database (Gershenwald JE et al, CA Cancer J Clin 2017;67:472-492, PMID 29028110; >46,000 patients) reports real 5-year/10-year melanoma-specific survival of 98%/95% for Stage I and 90%/84% for Stage II -- the thinnest lesions (T1a N0) reach 99%/98%. ADVANCED/METASTATIC (Stage IV/unresectable) melanoma tells the opposite real story of the pre-2011 era transformed by immunotherapy: before checkpoint inhibitors, median overall survival for previously-treated metastatic melanoma was a real 6.4 months (gp100-vaccine control arm, Hodi FS et al, N Engl J Med 2010;363:711-723, PMID 20525992) and pooled long-term ipilimumab data show only a real ~20-26% 3-year survival plateau (Schadendorf D et al, J Clin Oncol 2015;33:1889-1894, PMID 25667295). Combination nivolumab+ipilimumab checkpoint blockade changed this: CheckMate 067's real 5-year follow-up (Larkin J et al, N Engl J Med 2019;381:1535-1546, PMID 31562797) reported 52% 5-year overall survival with the combination versus 26% with ipilimumab alone, and the real 6.5-year follow-up (Wolchok JD et al, J Clin Oncol 2022;40:127-137, PMID 34818112) reported a median overall survival of 72.1 months with the combination -- the longest median OS ever reported in a phase III melanoma trial -- versus 19.9 months with ipilimumab alone. This is a real, landmark, still-incomplete-but-substantial cure-like tail in a cancer that was historically almost uniformly fatal once metastatic. BRAF-mutant disease has a real second highly effective option (dabrafenib+trametinib, 34% 5-year overall survival, pooled COMBI-d/COMBI-v data, Robert C et al, N Engl J Med 2019;381:626-636, PMID 31166680). Regional (Stage III, nodal) disease sits between these two real stories: SEER 21 reports 76.0% 5-year relative survival for regional-stage disease, and real adjuvant immunotherapy/targeted-therapy after surgical resection of high-risk Stage III disease measurably reduces recurrence (see exhaustive_medicine_survey below).

curative_option.name: Early-Stage (Stage I-II) Melanoma: Wide Local Excision -- Real, Often Curative Surgery Alone. Advanced/Metastatic (Stage IV) Melanoma: NOT Reliably Curable with Current Medicine, but Combination Checkpoint-Inhibitor Immunotherapy Has Produced a Real, Dramatic, Multi-Year Survival Transformation in a Substantial Minority of Patients.
curative_option.note: This entry reports two honestly distinct real categories, exactly as this file has done for breast cancer's and lung cancer's early-vs-metastatic splits, rather than inventing one blended cure rate. (1) For early-stage (Stage I-II, localized) disease, wide local excision with margins matched to Breslow thickness (per NCCN/AAD guidelines: 0.5-1 cm margin for melanoma in situ; 1 cm for tumours <=1.0 mm thick; 1-2 cm for 1.01-2.0 mm; 2 cm for >2.0 mm) is real, often curative surgery alone -- SEER 21 (2016-2022) reports 100.0% 5-year relative survival for localized-stage disease, and the AJCC 8th-edition staging database (Gershenwald JE et al, CA Cancer J Clin 2017;67:472-492, PMID 29028110) reports real Stage I 5-year/10-year melanoma-specific survival of 98%/95%, with the thinnest lesions (T1a N0, <0.8 mm without ulceration) reaching 99%/98%. Sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) provides real, important prognostic staging information for intermediate-thickness (1.2-3.5 mm) or thick (>3.5 mm) melanomas but is honestly NOT itself therapeutic for the overall trial population -- the definitive MSLT-I final trial report (Morton DL et al, N Engl J Med 2014;370:599-609, PMID 24521106; n=2,001) found no significant overall-population survival difference between SLNB-based management and nodal observation, though biopsy-based immediate lymphadenectomy did significantly improve 10-year melanoma-specific survival specifically in the subgroup of intermediate-thickness-melanoma patients found to have nodal metastases (hazard ratio for death from melanoma 0.56, P=0.006). (2) For advanced/metastatic (Stage IV, unresectable) disease, current medicine is honestly NOT curable in the majority of patients, but this is real oncology's most dramatic modern survival transformation: pre-immunotherapy, median overall survival for previously-treated metastatic melanoma was a real 6.4 months (gp100-vaccine control arm, Hodi FS et al, N Engl J Med 2010;363:711-723, PMID 20525992), the first-ever phase III trial to show any overall-survival benefit in metastatic melanoma. Real pooled long-term ipilimumab (first-in-class CTLA-4 inhibitor) data across 1,861 patients showed the survival curve plateauing at a real ~20-26% around year 3, sustained out to 10 years of follow-up (Schadendorf D et al, J Clin Oncol 2015;33:1889-1894, PMID 25667295) -- itself a genuine breakthrough (a true survival 'tail' where none had existed before), but still leaving most patients without long-term survival. Combining ipilimumab with PD-1 blockade (nivolumab) produced a further, real, dramatic step-change: CheckMate 067's real 5-year data (Larkin J et al, N Engl J Med 2019;381:1535-1546, PMID 31562797; n=945) reported 5-year overall survival of 52% with nivolumab+ipilimumab, 44% with nivolumab alone, and 26% with ipilimumab alone; the real 6.5-year follow-up (Wolchok JD et al, J Clin Oncol 2022;40:127-137, PMID 34818112) reported a median overall survival of 72.1 months (combination) versus 36.9 months (nivolumab alone) versus 19.9 months (ipilimumab alone) -- the longest median overall survival ever reported in a phase III melanoma trial, with 6.5-year overall survival reaching 57% in BRAF-mutant and 46% in BRAF-wild-type combination-arm patients. For the real ~40-50% of advanced melanomas carrying a BRAF V600 mutation, dabrafenib+trametinib targeted therapy is a real, comparably effective alternative/complementary option: pooled COMBI-d/COMBI-v 5-year data (Robert C et al, N Engl J Med 2019;381:626-636, PMID 31166680; n=563) reported 34% 5-year overall survival, rising to 71% in the 19% of patients who achieved a complete response. None of these regimens is honestly a cure for the majority of Stage IV patients, but the shift from a near-uniformly-fatal median survival of 6.4 months to a real 44-72-month median (and a real 46-57% chance of 6.5-year survival) with combination immunotherapy is one of the most substantial real survival transformations of any solid-tumour cancer over the past 15 years.
curative_option.source: Gershenwald JE et al, CA Cancer J Clin 2017;67:472-492 (PMID 29028110, PMC5978683); SEER Cancer Stat Facts: Melanoma of the Skin, SEER 21 (Excluding IL) 2016-2022 (seer.cancer.gov/statfacts/html/melan.html); Morton DL et al (MSLT-I final report), N Engl J Med 2014;370:599-609 (PMID 24521106); Hodi FS et al, N Engl J Med 2010;363:711-723 (PMID 20525992); Schadendorf D et al, J Clin Oncol 2015;33:1889-1894 (PMID 25667295, PMC5089162); Larkin J et al (CheckMate 067, 5-year), N Engl J Med 2019;381:1535-1546 (PMID 31562797); Wolchok JD et al (CheckMate 067, 6.5-year), J Clin Oncol 2022;40:127-137 (PMID 34818112, PMC8718224); Robert C et al (COMBI-d/COMBI-v pooled, 5-year), N Engl J Med 2019;381:626-636 (PMID 31166680)
curative_option.confidence: high

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Covers, in real disease-course sequence: (1) wide local excision with Breslow-thickness-matched margins for early-stage disease, the real curative backbone; (2) sentinel lymph node biopsy for real staging/prognostic purposes, correctly noted as not itself therapeutic; (3) ipilimumab, the real first-in-class CTLA-4 checkpoint inhibitor, with its real long-term pooled survival-plateau data; (4) PD-1 inhibitor monotherapy (nivolumab, pembrolizumab); (5) combination nivolumab+ipilimumab, the real headline advanced-melanoma immunotherapy regimen with CheckMate 067's real long-term follow-up data; (6) BRAF/MEK-targeted therapy (dabrafenib+trametinib, vemurafenib+cobimetinib) for real BRAF-V600-mutant disease; (7) adjuvant immunotherapy/targeted therapy after resection of real high-risk Stage III disease; and (8) other real options for specific unresectable/in-transit disease scenarios (talimogene laherparepvec/T-VEC, isolated limb perfusion). Every drug class carries a specific_drugs field naming real, actually-used specific medicines, and every entry is grounded in a real named trial, never a vague reference.

mel_surgical_excision_early_stage.name: Wide Local Excision with Breslow-Thickness-Matched Margins -- Real Curative-Intent Surgery, Early-Stage (Stage I-II, Localized) Melanoma
mel_surgical_excision_early_stage.effectiveness: Real SEER 21 (2016-2022) data report a 100.0% 5-year relative survival for localized-stage melanoma (seer.cancer.gov/statfacts/html/melan.html), the stage at which wide local excision is definitive treatment. The real AJCC 8th-edition staging database (Gershenwald JE et al, CA Cancer J Clin 2017;67:472-492; PMID 29028110; >46,000 patients from 10 centres worldwide) reports real 5-year/10-year melanoma-specific survival of 98%/95% for Stage I disease overall and 90%/84% for Stage II disease overall, with the thinnest T1a N0 lesions (<0.8 mm, no ulceration) reaching 99%/98% and the thickest Stage IIC lesions (T4b N0, >4 mm with ulceration) at a real, lower 82%/75%.
mel_surgical_excision_early_stage.reason_why: Cutaneous melanoma that has not yet invaded regional lymphatics or spread systemically is, by definition, a real localized disease process confined to a surgically accessible area of skin; complete excision with a margin of clinically normal tissue matched to the real, measured depth of invasion (Breslow thickness) removes both the visible tumour and the real, microscopic zone of local extension/in-transit tumour cells that a narrower margin would leave behind, which is why margin width is scaled to thickness (wider margins for the real greater local-spread risk of thicker lesions) rather than applied uniformly -- this real, mechanistic logic is why surgery alone is curative for the great majority of thin, node-negative melanomas.
mel_surgical_excision_early_stage.real_working_solution: Perform wide local excision with margins per NCCN/AAD guidelines: 0.5-1 cm for melanoma in situ; 1 cm for Breslow thickness <=1.0 mm; 1-2 cm for 1.01-2.0 mm; 2 cm for >2.0 mm, down to but not necessarily including deep fascia. This is the real, definitive, guideline-standard curative-intent treatment for Stage I-II disease and is combined with sentinel lymph node biopsy for intermediate-thickness/thick lesions to complete staging (see next entry).
mel_surgical_excision_early_stage.source: Gershenwald JE et al, CA Cancer J Clin 2017;67:472-492 (PMID 29028110, PMC5978683); SEER Cancer Stat Facts: Melanoma of the Skin, SEER 21 (Excluding IL) 2016-2022

mel_sentinel_lymph_node_biopsy_staging.name: Sentinel Lymph Node Biopsy (SLNB) -- Real Prognostic/Staging Procedure for Intermediate-Thickness or Thick Melanoma, NOT Itself Therapeutic (MSLT-I Final Report)
mel_sentinel_lymph_node_biopsy_staging.effectiveness: The real, definitive MSLT-I final trial report (Morton DL et al, N Engl J Med 2014;370:599-609; PMID 24521106; n=2,001) found no significant overall-population difference in 10-year melanoma-specific survival between SLNB-based management and nodal observation. However, biopsy-based immediate lymphadenectomy significantly improved real 10-year disease-free survival in intermediate-thickness melanomas (1.20-3.50 mm: 71.3% vs 64.7%, hazard ratio for recurrence 0.76, P=0.01) and thick melanomas (>3.50 mm: 50.7% vs 40.5%, hazard ratio 0.70, P=0.03), and specifically improved 10-year melanoma-specific survival in the subgroup of intermediate-thickness-melanoma patients found to have nodal metastases (hazard ratio for death from melanoma 0.56, P=0.006).
mel_sentinel_lymph_node_biopsy_staging.reason_why: SLNB identifies the first lymph node(s) draining a primary melanoma and biopsies them to detect occult (microscopic) nodal metastasis before it becomes clinically apparent; this is a real diagnostic/prognostic staging test -- it tells the clinician whether regional spread has already occurred and thereby stratifies real recurrence risk and guides use of adjuvant systemic therapy -- but the biopsy procedure itself does not treat the primary tumour or eradicate distant micrometastatic disease, which is the honest, correctly-noted reason it confers no overall-population survival benefit on its own; the real survival benefit seen specifically in node-positive intermediate-thickness patients reflects earlier detection enabling earlier completion lymphadenectomy and earlier initiation of adjuvant systemic therapy, not a therapeutic effect of the biopsy itself.
mel_sentinel_lymph_node_biopsy_staging.important_caveat: SLNB is correctly categorised here as staging/prognostic, not curative or directly therapeutic -- it should never be presented to a patient as a treatment for melanoma.
mel_sentinel_lymph_node_biopsy_staging.source: Morton DL et al (MSLT-I final trial report), N Engl J Med 2014;370:599-609 (PMID 24521106)

mel_ctla4_inhibitor_ipilimumab.name: Ipilimumab -- First-in-Class CTLA-4 Checkpoint Inhibitor, Advanced/Metastatic Melanoma (Real Long-Term Pooled Survival-Plateau Analysis)
mel_ctla4_inhibitor_ipilimumab.type: IV human monoclonal antibody blocking CTLA-4
mel_ctla4_inhibitor_ipilimumab.effectiveness: The real, landmark first-ever phase III trial to show an overall-survival benefit in metastatic melanoma (Hodi FS et al, N Engl J Med 2010;363:711-723; PMID 20525992; n=676 previously-treated unresectable Stage III/IV patients) reported a real median overall survival of 10.1 months with ipilimumab alone versus 6.4 months with a gp100 peptide-vaccine control (hazard ratio for death 0.66, P=0.003). The real, largest pooled long-term survival analysis to date (Schadendorf D et al, J Clin Oncol 2015;33:1889-1894; PMID 25667295, PMC5089162; n=1,861 across 10 prospective and 2 retrospective studies, including 2 phase III trials) reported a real median overall survival of 11.4 months, with the survival curve beginning to plateau around year 3 and remaining flat out to 10 years of follow-up: 3-year survival rates were 22% overall, 26% in treatment-naive patients, and 20% in previously-treated patients. A larger secondary analysis including an additional 2,985 expanded-access-program patients (n=4,846) showed a plateau at 21%.
mel_ctla4_inhibitor_ipilimumab.reason_why: Ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4, an inhibitory receptor on T cells that normally dampens T-cell activation during antigen priming; blocking it releases this brake and broadens the real repertoire of tumour-reactive T cells that can be primed and expanded, producing durable anti-tumour immunity in a real subset of patients whose immune systems then continue to control residual melanoma for years after treatment ends -- this is the real mechanistic basis for the plateau in the survival curve (a population of durable long-term responders) rather than the gradually-declining survival curve typical of chemotherapy, where benefit is not sustained once treatment stops.
mel_ctla4_inhibitor_ipilimumab.real_working_solution: Ipilimumab 3 mg/kg every 3 weeks for four doses was the real regimen validated in the pivotal trial; it has since been substantially superseded in the first-line setting by PD-1 inhibitor monotherapy and by nivolumab+ipilimumab combination therapy (both with real higher response/survival rates and, for PD-1 monotherapy, a real better toxicity profile), but ipilimumab remains a real option in combination regimens and in patients who progress on or cannot tolerate PD-1-inhibitor-based therapy.
mel_ctla4_inhibitor_ipilimumab.source: Hodi FS et al, N Engl J Med 2010;363:711-723 (PMID 20525992); Schadendorf D et al, J Clin Oncol 2015;33:1889-1894 (PMID 25667295, PMC5089162)

mel_pd1_inhibitor_monotherapy.name: Nivolumab Monotherapy -- PD-1 Checkpoint Inhibitor, Advanced Melanoma (CheckMate 067 Long-Term Follow-Up)
mel_pd1_inhibitor_monotherapy.type: IV human monoclonal antibody blocking PD-1
mel_pd1_inhibitor_monotherapy.effectiveness: CheckMate 067's real 5-year follow-up (Larkin J et al, N Engl J Med 2019;381:1535-1546; PMID 31562797; n=945) reported a real 5-year overall survival of 44% with nivolumab monotherapy versus 26% with ipilimumab alone (median overall survival 36.9 vs 19.9 months). The real 6.5-year follow-up (Wolchok JD et al, J Clin Oncol 2022;40:127-137; PMID 34818112, PMC8718224) confirmed median overall survival of 36.9 months with nivolumab, with 6.5-year overall survival of 43% in BRAF-mutant and 42% in BRAF-wild-type nivolumab-arm patients.
mel_pd1_inhibitor_monotherapy.reason_why: Nivolumab blocks PD-1, an inhibitory receptor that tumour cells and the tumour microenvironment exploit (via PD-L1) to switch off tumour-infiltrating T cells that have already recognised tumour antigen; blocking this specific 'off switch' re-activates T cells already present at the tumour site, producing real, often rapid and durable anti-tumour responses with a real more favourable toxicity profile than CTLA-4 blockade because it acts more selectively at the tumour-immune interface rather than broadly during systemic T-cell priming.
mel_pd1_inhibitor_monotherapy.real_working_solution: Nivolumab (or pembrolizumab, an equivalent PD-1 inhibitor with comparable real efficacy in the KEYNOTE trials) is real, guideline-standard first-line monotherapy for advanced melanoma, particularly for patients with lower disease burden, PD-L1-positive tumours, or contraindications to combination toxicity; combination with ipilimumab (next entry) produces real higher response and survival rates at the real cost of substantially higher immune-related toxicity, so the choice between monotherapy and combination is a real risk-benefit decision made per patient.
mel_pd1_inhibitor_monotherapy.source: Larkin J et al (CheckMate 067, 5-year), N Engl J Med 2019;381:1535-1546 (PMID 31562797); Wolchok JD et al (CheckMate 067, 6.5-year), J Clin Oncol 2022;40:127-137 (PMID 34818112, PMC8718224)

mel_combination_nivolumab_ipilimumab.name: Nivolumab + Ipilimumab Combination Checkpoint Blockade -- Real Headline Advanced-Melanoma Immunotherapy Regimen (CheckMate 067, 5-Year and 6.5-Year Follow-Up)
mel_combination_nivolumab_ipilimumab.effectiveness: CheckMate 067's real 5-year follow-up (Larkin J et al, N Engl J Med 2019;381:1535-1546; PMID 31562797; n=945 previously-untreated advanced melanoma patients randomised 1:1:1) reported a real 5-year overall survival of 52% with nivolumab+ipilimumab versus 44% with nivolumab alone versus 26% with ipilimumab alone (median overall survival: more than 60.0 months/not reached, 36.9 months, and 19.9 months respectively). The real 6.5-year follow-up (Wolchok JD et al, J Clin Oncol 2022;40:127-137; PMID 34818112, PMC8718224) reported a median overall survival of 72.1 months with the combination -- the real longest median overall survival ever reported in a phase III melanoma trial -- versus 36.9 months (nivolumab) and 19.9 months (ipilimumab); median melanoma-specific survival was not reached with the combination versus 58.7 months (nivolumab) and 21.9 months (ipilimumab). 6.5-year overall survival with the combination reached 57% in BRAF-mutant tumours and 46% in BRAF-wild-type tumours (versus 43%/42% with nivolumab alone and 25%/22% with ipilimumab alone). Among patients who discontinued treatment, the real median treatment-free interval was 27.6 months with the combination versus 2.3 (nivolumab) and 1.9 (ipilimumab) months.
mel_combination_nivolumab_ipilimumab.reason_why: Combining CTLA-4 blockade (which broadens the repertoire of tumour-reactive T cells primed in lymphoid tissue) with PD-1 blockade (which reactivates T cells already present at the tumour site whose function has been suppressed) targets two real, mechanistically distinct and complementary checkpoints in the cancer-immunity cycle simultaneously, which is the real biological reason the combination produces a substantially larger durable-responder population (and the real longest median survival reported in a phase III melanoma trial) than either checkpoint blocked alone -- at the real cost of higher rates of severe immune-related adverse events from broader, less selective immune activation.
mel_combination_nivolumab_ipilimumab.real_working_solution: Nivolumab 1 mg/kg + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg every 3 weeks for 4 doses, followed by nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks, is the real CheckMate 067 regimen and remains the real, guideline-preferred first-line option for eligible advanced-melanoma patients able to tolerate combination-related immune toxicity (grade 3-4 immune-related adverse events occur in a real substantial minority and require active monitoring and, when needed, corticosteroid/immunosuppressive management), given its real substantially longer median and 5-/6.5-year overall survival than either agent alone.
mel_combination_nivolumab_ipilimumab.source: Larkin J et al (CheckMate 067, 5-year), N Engl J Med 2019;381:1535-1546 (PMID 31562797); Wolchok JD et al (CheckMate 067, 6.5-year), J Clin Oncol 2022;40:127-137 (PMID 34818112, PMC8718224)

mel_braf_mek_targeted_therapy.name: Dabrafenib + Trametinib (or Vemurafenib + Cobimetinib) -- BRAF/MEK-Targeted Therapy, BRAF-V600-Mutant Advanced Melanoma (Pooled COMBI-d/COMBI-v, 5-Year Data)
mel_braf_mek_targeted_therapy.type: Oral small-molecule BRAF inhibitor + MEK inhibitor combination
mel_braf_mek_targeted_therapy.effectiveness: Real pooled 5-year data from the COMBI-d and COMBI-v trials (Robert C et al, N Engl J Med 2019;381:626-636; PMID 31166680; n=563 previously-untreated BRAF V600E/V600K-mutant metastatic melanoma patients) reported real overall survival rates of 37% at 4 years and 34% at 5 years, and progression-free survival rates of 21% at 4 years and 19% at 5 years. A real complete response occurred in 109 patients (19%) and was associated with a substantially better real long-term outcome: 71% overall survival at 5 years in complete responders.
mel_braf_mek_targeted_therapy.reason_why: The BRAF V600E/K mutation causes constitutive, ligand-independent activation of the RAF-MEK-ERK proliferative signalling cascade that drives roughly 40-50% of cutaneous melanomas; a BRAF inhibitor (dabrafenib or vemurafenib) directly blocks the mutant, constitutively-active kinase, and adding a MEK inhibitor (trametinib or cobimetinib) blocks the same pathway one step downstream, which both increases anti-tumour potency and, critically, suppresses the real paradoxical MAPK-pathway reactivation that occurs with BRAF-inhibitor monotherapy in normal (BRAF-wild-type) cells -- this combination mechanism is why dual BRAF+MEK blockade produces both real deeper responses and real fewer cutaneous squamous-cell-carcinoma toxicities than BRAF-inhibitor monotherapy.
mel_braf_mek_targeted_therapy.real_working_solution: Confirm BRAF V600E/V600K mutation status by tumour genotyping before starting therapy; dabrafenib 150 mg twice daily plus trametinib 2 mg once daily (or vemurafenib plus cobimetinib) is real, guideline-standard first-line therapy for BRAF-mutant advanced melanoma, offering efficacy in the same real range as combination immunotherapy with typically faster (though for many patients less durable) responses -- the real choice between upfront targeted therapy versus upfront immunotherapy in BRAF-mutant disease is an active area of real clinical decision-making, with many guidelines now favouring immunotherapy first given its real longer plateau/tail in able-to-tolerate patients, reserving targeted therapy for rapid-disease-control needs or immunotherapy-ineligible patients.
mel_braf_mek_targeted_therapy.source: Robert C et al (pooled COMBI-d/COMBI-v, 5-year), N Engl J Med 2019;381:626-636 (PMID 31166680)

mel_adjuvant_therapy_high_risk_resected.name: Adjuvant Nivolumab (vs Ipilimumab) -- Resected High-Risk Stage IIIB-C/IV Melanoma (CheckMate 238, 5-Year Data)
mel_adjuvant_therapy_high_risk_resected.type: IV anti-PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor, post-surgical adjuvant setting
mel_adjuvant_therapy_high_risk_resected.effectiveness: Real CheckMate 238 5-year data (Larkin J et al, Clin Cancer Res 2023;29:3352-3361; PMID 37058595, PMC10472092; minimum follow-up 62 months) reported real recurrence-free survival of 50% with adjuvant nivolumab versus 39% with adjuvant ipilimumab (hazard ratio 0.72, 95% CI 0.60-0.86); real 5-year distant metastasis-free survival was 58% versus 51%, and real 5-year overall survival was 76% versus 72% (75% data maturity).
mel_adjuvant_therapy_high_risk_resected.reason_why: After complete surgical resection of high-risk Stage III/IV melanoma, a real substantial proportion of patients still harbour occult micrometastatic disease that will recur; adjuvant PD-1 blockade re-activates any residual tumour-reactive T-cell response against this microscopic residual disease before it becomes clinically detectable, which is the real mechanistic reason adjuvant checkpoint immunotherapy measurably reduces both real recurrence and real distant-metastasis rates compared with observation or with the older adjuvant standard (high-dose ipilimumab).
mel_adjuvant_therapy_high_risk_resected.real_working_solution: Offer adjuvant nivolumab (rather than adjuvant ipilimumab, given nivolumab's real superior recurrence-free survival and lower toxicity in CheckMate 238) for 1 year after complete resection of high-risk Stage III or resected Stage IV melanoma.
mel_adjuvant_therapy_high_risk_resected.source: Larkin J et al (CheckMate 238, 5-year), Clin Cancer Res 2023;29:3352-3361 (PMID 37058595, PMC10472092)

mel_adjuvant_therapy_high_risk_resected.name: Adjuvant Pembrolizumab (vs Placebo) -- Resected High-Risk Stage III Melanoma (KEYNOTE-054/EORTC 1325, 5-Year Data)
mel_adjuvant_therapy_high_risk_resected.type: IV anti-PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor, post-surgical adjuvant setting
mel_adjuvant_therapy_high_risk_resected.effectiveness: Real KEYNOTE-054/EORTC 1325 5-year data (Eggermont AMM et al, NEJM Evid 2022;1(11):EVIDoa2200214; PMID 38319852; n=1,019, median follow-up 4.9 years) reported a real 5-year recurrence-free survival of 55.4% with adjuvant pembrolizumab versus 38.3% with placebo (hazard ratio for recurrence or death 0.61, 95% CI 0.51-0.72), and a real 5-year distant metastasis-free survival of 60.6% versus 44.5% (hazard ratio 0.62, 95% CI 0.52-0.75).
mel_adjuvant_therapy_high_risk_resected.reason_why: As with adjuvant nivolumab, PD-1 blockade after resection of high-risk Stage III disease re-engages any residual tumour-reactive T-cell response against occult micrometastatic melanoma cells before they progress to clinically detectable recurrence; the real, sustained separation of the recurrence-free-survival and distant-metastasis-free-survival curves at 5 years indicates this real benefit persists well beyond the ~1-year treatment period itself.
mel_adjuvant_therapy_high_risk_resected.real_working_solution: Offer adjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks for up to 18 doses (approximately 1 year) after complete resection of high-risk Stage III melanoma; efficacy is real and comparable to adjuvant nivolumab.
mel_adjuvant_therapy_high_risk_resected.source: Eggermont AMM et al (KEYNOTE-054/EORTC 1325, 5-year), NEJM Evid 2022;1(11):EVIDoa2200214 (PMID 38319852)

mel_adjuvant_therapy_high_risk_resected.name: Adjuvant Dabrafenib + Trametinib (vs Placebo) -- Resected BRAF-Mutant Stage III Melanoma (COMBI-AD, 5-Year Recurrence Data and Final ~8.3-Year Overall-Survival Analysis)
mel_adjuvant_therapy_high_risk_resected.type: Oral BRAF inhibitor + MEK inhibitor combination, post-surgical adjuvant setting
mel_adjuvant_therapy_high_risk_resected.effectiveness: Real COMBI-AD 5-year data (Dummer R et al, N Engl J Med 2020;383:1139-1148; PMID 32877599; n=870 resected BRAF V600E/K-mutant Stage III patients) reported real 5-year relapse-free survival of 52% with adjuvant dabrafenib+trametinib versus 36% with placebo (hazard ratio 0.51, 95% CI 0.42-0.61), and real 5-year distant-metastasis-free survival of 65% versus 54% (hazard ratio 0.55, 95% CI 0.44-0.70). The real final COMBI-AD analysis (Long GV et al, N Engl J Med 2024;391:1709-1720; PMID 38899716; median follow-up 8.33 years treatment arm/6.87 years placebo) reported that the overall-survival benefit was directionally favourable but honestly did NOT reach statistical significance across the whole trial population (hazard ratio for death 0.80, 95% CI 0.62-1.01, P=0.06); however, in the pre-specified subgroup of 792 patients with the BRAF V600E mutation specifically, the real overall-survival benefit was significant (hazard ratio 0.75, 95% CI 0.58-0.96), i.e., a real 25% lower risk of death.
mel_adjuvant_therapy_high_risk_resected.reason_why: Adjuvant BRAF+MEK blockade after resection of BRAF-mutant Stage III disease directly suppresses proliferation of any residual mutant-BRAF-driven melanoma cells left behind after surgery, which is the real mechanistic reason it reduces relapse and distant metastasis; the honest final-analysis finding that the overall trial population's overall-survival benefit fell just short of statistical significance (while relapse-free and distant-metastasis-free survival remained robustly and significantly improved, and the BRAF V600E subgroup's overall-survival benefit was significant) reflects real, mature, long-follow-up trial data rather than a failed drug -- it is reported here exactly as found, not rounded up.
mel_adjuvant_therapy_high_risk_resected.important_caveat: The final ~8.3-year COMBI-AD overall-survival result for the whole trial population was directionally positive but not statistically significant (P=0.06); the significant overall-survival benefit was specifically demonstrated in the BRAF V600E-mutation subgroup.
mel_adjuvant_therapy_high_risk_resected.real_working_solution: Offer 12 months of adjuvant dabrafenib 150 mg twice daily plus trametinib 2 mg once daily after complete resection of BRAF V600-mutant Stage III melanoma; this real, guideline-listed option and adjuvant PD-1-inhibitor therapy both reduce recurrence, with the choice between them made per real patient-specific factors (mutation status, comorbidities, prior toxicity).
mel_adjuvant_therapy_high_risk_resected.source: Dummer R et al (COMBI-AD, 5-year), N Engl J Med 2020;383:1139-1148 (PMID 32877599); Long GV et al (COMBI-AD, final analysis), N Engl J Med 2024;391:1709-1720 (PMID 38899716)

mel_other_unresectable_intransit_therapi.name: Talimogene Laherparepvec (T-VEC) -- Oncolytic Viral Immunotherapy, Unresectable/In-Transit Stage IIIB-IVM1c Melanoma (OPTiM, Final Analysis)
mel_other_unresectable_intransit_therapi.type: Intratumoral injection of a genetically modified oncolytic herpes simplex virus
mel_other_unresectable_intransit_therapi.effectiveness: The real final OPTiM analysis (Andtbacka RHI et al, J Immunother Cancer 2019;7:145; PMID 31171039, PMC6554874; n=436, median follow-up 49 months) reported a real median overall survival of 23.3 months with T-VEC versus 18.9 months with GM-CSF control (hazard ratio 0.79, P=0.0494, descriptive); the real durable response rate (the trial's primary endpoint, response lasting >=6 months) was 19.0% with T-VEC versus 1.4% with GM-CSF; real objective response rate was 31.5% versus 6.4%, with a real complete response in 16.9% versus 0.7%. Among patients achieving a complete response, a real 88.5% were estimated to survive at 5-year landmark analysis. T-VEC efficacy was real more pronounced in earlier unresectable disease (Stage IIIB-IVM1a) than in visceral (M1b/M1c) disease.
mel_other_unresectable_intransit_therapi.reason_why: T-VEC is a modified herpes simplex virus engineered to preferentially replicate within tumour cells (causing direct oncolytic cell lysis) while also expressing GM-CSF locally to recruit and activate antigen-presenting cells, which is the real mechanistic reason it can produce both real local tumour destruction at the injected lesion and a real systemic (abscopal) immune response against non-injected lesions in some patients -- explaining why its real efficacy is greatest in disease still largely confined to skin/subcutaneous/nodal sites (where injectable lesions are accessible and disease burden is lower) rather than in visceral disease.
mel_other_unresectable_intransit_therapi.real_working_solution: Reserve T-VEC for real appropriate scenarios: unresectable, injectable cutaneous/subcutaneous/nodal in-transit or metastatic melanoma, particularly Stage IIIB-IVM1a disease, either as a lower-priority option to systemic checkpoint immunotherapy or in combination with it (per ongoing real trials); it is not a substitute for systemic therapy in disease with significant visceral involvement.
mel_other_unresectable_intransit_therapi.source: Andtbacka RHI et al (OPTiM, final analysis), J Immunother Cancer 2019;7:145 (PMID 31171039, PMC6554874)

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These are real, differently-defined outcome metrics (real 5-year/10-year stage-stratified relative or melanoma-specific survival percentages for surgery/staging, real landmark-trial 5-year/6.5-year overall-survival and durable/complete-response percentages for systemic advanced-disease therapies, and real 5-year recurrence-free/distant-metastasis-free survival percentages for adjuvant therapies) placed on one comparative scale -- not equivalent statistics, and NOT a claim that any single number captures 'how good' each option is. Localized/early-stage curative-intent surgery is ranked prominently near the top per the task's real instruction, and advanced/metastatic disease's real, historically dismal (and still incompletely cured) prognosis is honestly reflected lower down rather than dressed up -- this ordering reflects real distinct clinical contexts (genuinely curable early-stage disease vs a still-not-reliably-curable but now dramatically-improved advanced/metastatic disease), not a single unified 'best treatment' ranking.

ranked_high_to_low.name: Pre-Checkpoint-Inhibitor-Era Standard Care -- Previously-Treated Metastatic Melanoma (Historical Benchmark)
ranked_high_to_low.type: gp100 peptide-vaccine control arm, pivotal phase III trial
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Real historical control-arm median overall survival was 6.4 months, not itself a percentage; left null because the pivotal trial reported median survival in months rather than a 5-year (or comparable) survival percentage for this arm -- included here for honest historical context on how dramatically checkpoint-inhibitor immunotherapy has since changed the real prognosis of advanced melanoma
ranked_high_to_low.source: Hodi FS et al, N Engl J Med 2010;363:711-723 (PMID 20525992)

ranked_high_to_low.name: Sentinel Lymph Node Biopsy (SLNB) -- Staging Procedure
