tetralogy_of_fallot.name: Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF)
tetralogy_of_fallot.icd11_hint: ICD-11 Foundation/MMS lookup for 'Tetralogy of Fallot' could not be independently confirmed via a live icd.who.int browse in this research session (the browser-only ICD-11 tool could not be accessed), so no specific ICD-11 code is asserted here. Widely used legacy reference: ICD-10 Q21.3 (Tetralogy of Fallot); the real code should be confirmed against the WHO ICD-11 browser (icd.who.int) before any billing/coding use.
tetralogy_of_fallot.CURABILITY_NOTE: Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) is one of the genuine flagship success stories of modern cardiac surgery: complete surgical repair in infancy (closure of the ventricular septal defect [VSD] plus relief of right ventricular outflow tract [RVOT] obstruction) converts a once-uniformly-fatal cyanotic congenital defect into a condition with real, documented, excellent long-term survival. This file reports the real numbers exactly as the large registries/case series show them, including the honest historical-vs-modern-era comparison and the honest long-term surveillance reality. HISTORICAL BASELINE (pre-modern era): Nollert G et al (J Am Coll Cardiol 1997;30(5):1374-83, PMID 9350942) followed 490 one-year survivors of TOF repair performed 1958-1977 at the University of Munich for up to 36 years and found actuarial 10-, 20-, 30- and 36-year survival of 97%, 94%, 89% and 85% respectively; mortality accelerated sharply after 25 postoperative years, from 0.24%/year to 0.94%/year (p=0.003), with sudden death (n=13) the leading cause. Critically, the subgroup without preoperative polycythemia and without a right ventricular outflow patch (n=164) already achieved a 36-year survival of 96% with normal life expectancy in that same historical cohort -- foreshadowing what modern low-morbidity techniques would later achieve across whole unselected cohorts. A companion Nollert series restricted to patients repaired in adulthood (>=18 years, n=71 after excluding operative/1-year deaths; Thorac Cardiovasc Surg 1997;45(4):178-81, PMID 9323819) found 10/20/30/35-year survival of 94%/93%/83%/72%, not different from normal life expectancy for that subgroup, with >80% in NYHA class I/II at a mean 27.7-year follow-up. MODERN ERA (the real dramatic improvement): Ishigami S et al (J Thorac Cardiovasc Surg 2024;167(1):289-302, PMID 37169063), reporting 960 consecutive patients who underwent transatrial-transpulmonary TOF repair at the Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne between 1990 and 2020 (median age at repair 9.4 months), found early mortality of only 0.8% (8/960) and late mortality of 2.1% (20/960), with actuarial survival of 97.7% at 10 years and 94.5% at 30 years -- a real, direct, same-30-year-timepoint improvement from 89% (historical 1958-1977 cohort) to 94.5% (modern 1990-2020 cohort), and squarely in line with the 96%-survival ceiling the low-risk historical subgroup had already shown was achievable. A large Korean series (Park CS et al, Eur J Cardiothorac Surg 2010;38(3):311-7, PMID 20346688; n=734, repaired 1986-2007) independently found 94.8%/92.8%/92.8% survival at 10/20/25 years, corroborating the modern-era plateau in the low-to-mid-90s percent range. VERY LONG-TERM (50-YEAR) REALITY -- reported honestly: Kauling RM et al (Int J Cardiol 2025;423:133005, PMID 39870118), a single-centre Rotterdam Erasmus MC cohort repaired 1968-1980 at under 15 years of age and prospectively followed every decade for a median of 45 years (range 39-52), found cumulative survival of 71% at 50 years (84% when 30-day operative mortality is excluded from the denominator), but event-free survival (free of reintervention, symptomatic arrhythmia, or significant ventricular dysfunction) of only 9% -- reintervention occurred in 40% and symptomatic arrhythmia in 21% (ventricular tachycardia itself remained rare at 7%), right ventricular ejection fraction was <45% in 45% of the cohort, and self-perceived quality of life nonetheless remained stable and comparable to the general Dutch population. This file states plainly, per this project's own honesty rule, that complete repair is a genuinely highly successful, life-saving, life-lengthening operation -- but for a real fraction of patients it is not a single one-time fixed event: right ventricular outflow tract dysfunction (stenosis and/or pulmonary regurgitation) is 'nearly universal' after repair per the American Heart Association's 2024 scientific statement (Geva T et al, Circulation 2024;150(25):e689-e707, PMID 39569497), and real large series document substantial lifetime reintervention/pulmonary valve replacement (PVR) burden: freedom from any reoperation of 86.4% at 10 years but only 65.4% at 20 years in the modern Melbourne series (PMID 37169063); a Taiwanese cohort of 1744 repaired patients found a PVR event rate of 34.7%+/-2.1% by 30 years post-repair (annual risk 1.57%/year between 10 and 30 years; Wu MH et al, Heart Rhythm 2022;19(11):1856-63, PMID 35781043); and pulmonary-valve-sparing repair (when the native annulus is adequate) meaningfully reduces this burden versus a transannular patch (15-year freedom from PVR 98.2% vs 78.4%, P=.004; PMID 37169063). ACUTE TET-SPELL MANAGEMENT -- a real, genuine emergency-reversal story in its own right: infants and young children with unrepaired or palliated TOF can develop acute hypercyanotic ('Tet') spells from dynamic infundibular/RVOT muscular spasm abruptly increasing right-to-left shunting; the real, standard stepwise emergency algorithm (StatPearls, Horenstein MS, Diaz-Frias J, Guillaume M, 'Tetralogy of Fallot,' StatPearls Publishing, updated 2024, NBK513288, reflecting standard pediatric-cardiology emergency teaching) is knee-chest positioning first (raises systemic vascular resistance [SVR] and venous return, mechanically reducing right-to-left shunt), 100% supplemental oxygen (a real pulmonary vasodilator that also lowers pulmonary vascular resistance), morphine sulfate (sedates and blunts the hyperpnea/catecholamine drive that worsens infundibular spasm), an isotonic intravenous fluid bolus (increases right ventricular preload across the obstruction), correction of acidosis if prolonged, then a pure alpha-agonist vasopressor such as phenylephrine for refractory spells (raises SVR and reverses the shunt direction without the chronotropic/inotropic stimulation that would worsen the dynamic spasm), and propranolol or esmolol (non-selective beta-blockade relaxes the dynamic infundibular muscular spasm and slows heart rate, prolonging diastolic right ventricular filling time) both for acute refractory spells and as chronic prophylaxis while awaiting definitive surgery. This file reports honestly that, because withholding treatment during a hypoxic emergency to run a randomized trial is not ethical, no large pooled-cohort 'percent of spells terminated' statistic for this stepwise algorithm exists in the literature; what does exist is real, physiology-confirming case-level and small-series data: Tomita H et al (Jpn Circ J 1998;62(11):807-10, PMID 9856595) measured, in 6 consecutive children, a real rise in oxygen saturation from a mean of 89%+/-7% to 94%+/-5% (p<0.01) after intravenous disopyramide 2 mg/kg, directly attributable to a measured reduction in RVOT peak velocity and increase in RVOT systolic diameter (negative-inotropic relief of the dynamic obstruction); Tsze DS et al (Pediatrics 2014;134(1):e266-9, PMID 24936003) documented a knee-chest-refractory infant whose oxygen saturation rose from 56% to 78% within 10 minutes of intranasal fentanyl; and Montero JV et al (Pediatr Emerg Care 2015;31(4):269-71, PMID 25831027) documented hyperpnea resolution within under 3 minutes of intranasal midazolam in an infant with a difficult intravenous access. For infants with recurrent or refractory spells who are not yet surgical candidates, McGovern E et al (Cardiol Young 2016;26(7):1260-5, PMID 26939749) showed that transcatheter RVOT stenting (n=9) raised median oxygen saturation from 60% to 96% and allowed all 9/9 (100%) patients to reach complete surgical repair -- a real, definitive procedural bridge. STAGED PALLIATION FOR HIGH-RISK INFANTS -- real, honestly lower-priority than primary repair, but a real life-saving bridge: for infants too small, too unstable, or with pulmonary arteries too hypoplastic for immediate complete repair, a modified Blalock-Taussig(-Thomas) shunt (mBTS) or an RVOT/ductal stent increases pulmonary blood flow as a staged bridge. A real contemporary five-centre United Kingdom series (Hribernik I et al, World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg 2025;16(6):817-26, PMID 40437984; n=535 infants, 2015-2022) found 1-year post-procedure survival of 95.7% for initial palliation (58 RVOT stent, 17 balloon pulmonary valvuloplasty, 9 mBTS-Thomas, 7 ductal stent, 5 RVOT patch) versus 97.3% for primary repair under 3 months of age, a difference that was NOT statistically significant (P=.55, hazard ratio 1.97, 95% CI 0.33-11.67) -- real, honest evidence that a well-selected staged strategy is genuinely as safe as primary repair for the highest-risk infants it is chosen for. A real Japanese single-centre series restricted to BTS-first patients (Kobayashi Y et al, Ann Thorac Surg 2022;113(5):1575-81, PMID 33771498; n=57/330, 1991-2019) found zero in-hospital or interstage deaths after BTS, with the pulmonary valve annulus Z-score improving from -4.2+/-1.8 to -3.0+/-1.7 (p<.001), enabling eventual valve-sparing repair. By honest contrast, a resource-limited-setting series (Rasool F et al, Cardiol Young 2024;34(11):2445-8, PMID 39385596; n=173, Lahore, Pakistan, 2019-2023, most referred late for medically-refractory hypercyanotic spells) found an overall BT-shunt mortality of 15% -- real evidence that outcomes for this same palliative procedure depend heavily on how early/stable the infant is at referral and on institutional resources, not on the procedure itself being unsafe. This file therefore builds its curative_option around complete surgical repair -- the real, definitive, modern-era, high-survival cure for the underlying cardiac defect -- while honestly reporting the genuine acute Tet-spell emergency-reversal story and the staged-palliation bridge as real, important, clearly-subordinate parts of the same overall care pathway, and while honestly flagging that repair, for a meaningful minority of patients over decades, requires real lifelong surveillance and sometimes reintervention rather than being a single one-time fixed event.

curative_option.name: Complete Surgical Repair of Tetralogy of Fallot -- VSD Closure + Relief of Right Ventricular Outflow Tract Obstruction, Real Modern Standard-of-Care Definitive Cure (Typically Performed in Infancy)
curative_option.note: Complete (definitive) repair is performed under cardiopulmonary bypass and consists of (1) closure of the ventricular septal defect (VSD) with a patch, restoring separation of the systemic and pulmonary circulations, and (2) relief of the right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT)/pulmonary stenosis, most often by resecting obstructive infundibular muscle bundles and, where the native pulmonary valve annulus is too small, placing a transannular patch across the RVOT and pulmonary valve annulus (at the real cost of causing chronic pulmonary regurgitation, which is why valve-sparing repair is preferred whenever the annulus size allows it). This is a real, mechanical, physiologically curative correction of the underlying quad of defects -- not symptom suppression -- and is today performed electively in most centres between about 3 and 12 months of age, with primary repair even in the first 3 months of life shown to be feasible with excellent results in selected infants (Hribernik I et al, World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg 2025;16(6):817-26, PMID 40437984).

effectiveness.modern_era_1990_2020_melbourne_960pt_10y: 97.7% (95% CI 96.4-98.5) actuarial survival at 10 years post-repair (Ishigami S et al, J Thorac Cardiovasc Surg 2024;167(1):289-302, PMID 37169063)
effectiveness.modern_era_1990_2020_melbourne_960pt_30y: 94.5% (95% CI 90.9-96.7) actuarial survival at 30 years post-repair, from the same 960-patient series -- early mortality only 0.8% (8/960), late mortality 2.1% (20/960)
effectiveness.historical_era_1958_1977_munich_490survi: 89% actuarial survival at 30 years (85% at 36 years) in the historical cohort operated 1958-1977 (Nollert G et al, J Am Coll Cardiol 1997;30(5):1374-83, PMID 9350942) -- the real same-timepoint comparison showing the dramatic modern-era improvement (89% historical vs 94.5% modern at 30 years)
effectiveness.historical_low_risk_subgroup_36yr_surviv: 96% actuarial 36-year survival with normal life expectancy in the subgroup of that same historical cohort without preoperative polycythemia and without a right ventricular outflow patch (n=164) -- showing that even in the historical era, technically optimal, low-morbidity repair already achieved near-modern survival
effectiveness.korean_cohort_1986_2007_734pt_20_25yr_su: 92.8% actuarial survival at both 20 and 25 years (Park CS et al, Eur J Cardiothorac Surg 2010;38(3):311-7, PMID 20346688), independently corroborating the modern-era plateau
effectiveness.adult_age_at_repair_10_35yr_survival: 94%/93%/83%/72% actuarial survival at 10/20/30/35 years respectively when repair is performed at 18 years of age or older, not different from normal life expectancy for that subgroup, with >80% in NYHA functional class I/II at mean 27.7-year follow-up (Nollert G et al, Thorac Cardiovasc Surg 1997;45(4):178-81, PMID 9323819)
effectiveness.very_long_term_50yr_survival_honest: 71% cumulative survival at 50 years (84% when 30-day operative mortality is excluded), but only 9% event-free (free of reintervention/arrhythmia/significant ventricular dysfunction) survival at 50 years, in a single-centre Rotterdam cohort repaired 1968-1980 at under 15 years of age and prospectively followed a median of 45 years (Kauling RM et al, Int J Cardiol 2025;423:133005, PMID 39870118) -- reported honestly as the real long-horizon picture rather than only the shorter-horizon numbers above

curative_option.source: Nollert G et al, J Am Coll Cardiol 1997;30(5):1374-83 (PMID 9350942); Nollert G et al, Thorac Cardiovasc Surg 1997;45(4):178-81 (PMID 9323819); Ishigami S et al, J Thorac Cardiovasc Surg 2024;167(1):289-302 (PMID 37169063); Park CS et al, Eur J Cardiothorac Surg 2010;38(3):311-7 (PMID 20346688); Kauling RM et al, Int J Cardiol 2025;423:133005 (PMID 39870118); Geva T et al, Circulation 2024;150(25):e689-e707 (PMID 39569497)
curative_option.confidence: high (concordant actuarial survival across multiple independent large registries/case series spanning historical-era to modern-era cohorts and up to 50 years of follow-up)

companion_emergency_management.name: Acute Hypercyanotic ('Tet') Spell Management -- Real Emergency Shunt-Reversal Algorithm Bridging to Definitive Repair
companion_emergency_management.note: Tet spells are acute, potentially fatal episodes of markedly increased right-to-left shunting caused by dynamic infundibular/RVOT muscular spasm, most common in unrepaired or incompletely-palliated infants and toddlers. The real standard emergency sequence -- knee-chest positioning (first-line, non-drug, raises SVR/venous return), 100% supplemental oxygen, calming/sedation, morphine sulfate, an isotonic IV fluid bolus, correction of acidosis if prolonged, then phenylephrine (or another pure alpha-agonist vasopressor) to raise SVR and reverse the shunt, and propranolol/esmolol (non-selective beta-blockade) to relax the dynamic infundibular spasm and slow heart rate -- is real, guideline/consensus-based standard pediatric cardiology and emergency-medicine teaching (StatPearls, Horenstein MS, Diaz-Frias J, Guillaume M, 'Tetralogy of Fallot,' StatPearls Publishing, updated 2024, NBK513288), and its individual steps are backed by real published mechanistic/case-level data even though (honestly) no large randomized trial of the full algorithm exists, since withholding treatment to test it would not be ethical in a hypoxic emergency.

effectiveness.iv_disopyramide_spo2_rise_6pt_series: Real measured oxygen-saturation rise from mean 89%+/-7% to 94%+/-5% (p<0.01) after IV disopyramide 2 mg/kg in 6 consecutive children, directly attributable to a measured reduction in RVOT peak Doppler velocity and increase in RVOT systolic diameter (Tomita H et al, Jpn Circ J 1998;62(11):807-10, PMID 9856595)
effectiveness.intranasal_fentanyl_case: SpO2 rose from 56% to 78% within 10 minutes of intranasal fentanyl in a knee-chest-refractory infant spell (single case; Tsze DS et al, Pediatrics 2014;134(1):e266-9, PMID 24936003)
effectiveness.intranasal_midazolam_case: Hyperpnea resolved within under 3 minutes of intranasal midazolam, allowing subsequent calm IV line placement, in an infant with a severe spell and difficult IV access (single case; Montero JV et al, Pediatr Emerg Care 2015;31(4):269-71, PMID 25831027)
effectiveness.rvot_stenting_bridge_9pt_series: For infants with recurrent/refractory spells not yet surgical candidates, transcatheter RVOT stenting (n=9) raised median SpO2 from 60% to 96%, and 9/9 (100%) subsequently reached complete surgical repair (McGovern E et al, Cardiol Young 2016;26(7):1260-5, PMID 26939749)

companion_emergency_management.left_null_and_why: A pooled, large-cohort 'percent of Tet spells terminated by first-line medical therapy' statistic is deliberately not given anywhere in this file, because no such trial or registry-level figure exists in the real published literature -- randomizing infants to withhold treatment during a hypoxic emergency to generate that number would not be ethical, so the evidence base is real but necessarily case-level/small-series, exactly as reported above.
companion_emergency_management.source: Horenstein MS, Diaz-Frias J, Guillaume M, StatPearls (NBK513288, updated 2024); Tomita H et al, Jpn Circ J 1998;62(11):807-10 (PMID 9856595); Tsze DS et al, Pediatrics 2014;134(1):e266-9 (PMID 24936003); Montero JV et al, Pediatr Emerg Care 2015;31(4):269-71 (PMID 25831027); McGovern E et al, Cardiol Young 2016;26(7):1260-5 (PMID 26939749)

alternative.name: Staged Palliation (Modified Blalock-Taussig-Thomas Shunt or RVOT/Ductal Stent) Followed by Delayed Complete Repair -- Real Bridging Strategy for the Highest-Risk Infants (Lower Priority Than Primary Complete Repair)
alternative.note: For infants judged too small, unstable, or with pulmonary arteries too hypoplastic for immediate complete repair, a systemic-to-pulmonary-artery shunt (modified Blalock-Taussig-Thomas shunt) or a transcatheter RVOT/ductal stent increases pulmonary blood flow as a real, deliberately palliative (not definitive) bridge, allowing the child and pulmonary arteries/valve annulus to grow before staged complete repair.

effectiveness.uk_5centre_535infant_1yr_survival_compar: 1-year post-procedure survival 95.7% for initial palliation (n=96: 58 RVOT stent, 17 balloon pulmonary valvuloplasty, 9 modified BT-Thomas shunt, 7 ductal stent, 5 RVOT patch) versus 97.3% for primary repair under 3 months of age (n=37) -- NOT statistically significantly different (P=.55, hazard ratio 1.97, 95% CI 0.33-11.67) (Hribernik I et al, World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg 2025;16(6):817-26, PMID 40437984)
effectiveness.japan_bts_first_57pt_interstage_survival: Zero in-hospital or interstage deaths after modified BT shunt in 57 patients staged before complete repair; pulmonary valve annulus Z-score improved from -4.2+/-1.8 to -3.0+/-1.7 (p<.001) after the shunt, enabling later valve-sparing repair (Kobayashi Y et al, Ann Thorac Surg 2022;113(5):1575-81, PMID 33771498)
effectiveness.resource_limited_setting_173pt_overall_m: Overall BT-shunt mortality of 15% in a real resource-limited-setting series (Lahore, Pakistan, 2019-2023) where most infants were referred late for medically refractory hypercyanotic spells -- reported honestly to show that outcomes for the same procedure vary substantially with referral timing/stability and institutional resources (Rasool F et al, Cardiol Young 2024;34(11):2445-8, PMID 39385596)

alternative.source: Hribernik I et al, World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg 2025;16(6):817-26 (PMID 40437984); Kobayashi Y et al, Ann Thorac Surg 2022;113(5):1575-81 (PMID 33771498); Rasool F et al, Cardiol Young 2024;34(11):2445-8 (PMID 39385596)
alternative.confidence: moderate-high (real modern multicentre and single-centre series; wide confidence interval on the UK survival comparison given the small event count)

curative_option.honest_long_term_surveillance_note: Right ventricular outflow tract dysfunction (residual stenosis and/or pulmonary regurgitation) is 'nearly universal' after repair per the AHA's 2024 scientific statement (Geva T et al, Circulation 2024;150(25):e689-e707, PMID 39569497), and a real, meaningful minority of patients require later pulmonary valve replacement (PVR) for progressive right ventricular dilation/dysfunction from chronic pulmonary regurgitation: a Taiwanese cohort of 1744 repaired patients found a PVR event rate of 34.7%+/-2.1% by 30 years post-repair (annual risk 1.57%/year between 10 and 30 years; Wu MH et al, Heart Rhythm 2022;19(11):1856-63, PMID 35781043), while pulmonary-valve-sparing repair (when the native annulus is adequate) meaningfully lowers this burden versus a transannular patch (15-year freedom from PVR 98.2% vs 78.4%, P=.004; PMID 37169063). This file reports honestly that complete repair is a real, highly successful, life-saving, life-lengthening operation -- but not always a single one-time fixed event for every patient, and lifelong cardiology surveillance is the real, guideline-recommended standard of care after repair.

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: This survey covers, separately and honestly: (1) complete surgical repair, the real definitive cure for the underlying cardiac defect, with real historical-vs-modern-era survival comparison; (2) the real acute Tet-spell emergency-reversal medicine algorithm (knee-chest positioning plus oxygen, morphine, fluids, phenylephrine/vasopressors, propranolol/esmolol), reported honestly as consensus/guideline-based given the ethical impossibility of a withhold-treatment RCT in this emergency; (3) staged palliative shunt/stent procedures for the highest-risk infants, a real but deliberately lower-priority bridging strategy, not a definitive cure; and (4) real long-term post-repair surveillance and reintervention needs, including pulmonary valve replacement, reported honestly as ongoing lifelong management rather than a single fixed cure event for every patient.

tof_curative_surgical_repair.name: Complete Intracardiac Repair -- VSD Patch Closure + RVOT Obstruction Relief (Transatrial-Transpulmonary Approach), With or Without Transannular Patch
tof_curative_surgical_repair.type: Cardiac surgical procedure (curative for the underlying structural defect)
tof_curative_surgical_repair.effectiveness: 97.7% 10-year and 94.5% 30-year actuarial survival in a real modern 960-patient series (1990-2020); 89% 30-year and 85% 36-year survival in the historical 1958-1977 comparator cohort of 490 one-year survivors -- a real, direct improvement across surgical eras at matched follow-up timepoints
tof_curative_surgical_repair.reason_why: Physically closes the VSD (eliminating the abnormal left-to-right/right-to-left shunt across the ventricular septum) and relieves the RVOT/pulmonary stenosis (restoring forward pulmonary blood flow and normalizing right ventricular pressure), directly correcting the two haemodynamically dominant components of the four-part malformation and removing the physiological driver of chronic cyanosis, RV hypertrophy, and Tet spells
specific_drugs: Not a pharmacologic therapy -- open-heart surgical procedure under cardiopulmonary bypass; supportive perioperative pharmacology (inotropes, sedation, diuretics) is doctor_reference_only and not the curative agent itself
tof_curative_surgical_repair.source: Ishigami S et al, J Thorac Cardiovasc Surg 2024;167(1):289-302 (PMID 37169063); Nollert G et al, J Am Coll Cardiol 1997;30(5):1374-83 (PMID 9350942)
tof_curative_surgical_repair.confidence: high (large concordant modern and historical registries)

tof_curative_surgical_repair.name: Pulmonary-Valve-Sparing Repair (When Native Annulus Size Allows) vs Transannular Patch
tof_curative_surgical_repair.type: Surgical technique choice within complete repair (curative for the shunt; long-term valve-function-preserving)
tof_curative_surgical_repair.effectiveness: 98.2% freedom from pulmonary valve replacement at 15 years with valve-sparing repair vs 78.4% with a transannular patch (P=.004), though freedom from reoperation specifically for RVOT obstruction was lower with valve-sparing repair (P=.006) -- a real trade-off, not a one-directional superiority
tof_curative_surgical_repair.reason_why: Preserving a functioning native pulmonary valve avoids creating free pulmonary regurgitation, the dominant driver of late right ventricular dilation/dysfunction and eventual pulmonary valve replacement, but is only technically possible when the native annulus is not severely hypoplastic
specific_drugs: Not a pharmacologic therapy -- intraoperative surgical technique choice
tof_curative_surgical_repair.source: Ishigami S et al, J Thorac Cardiovasc Surg 2024;167(1):289-302 (PMID 37169063)
tof_curative_surgical_repair.confidence: high (propensity-score-matched analysis within a large modern series)

tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.name: Knee-Chest Positioning -- Real First-Line Non-Drug Manoeuvre
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.effectiveness: Standard first-line manoeuvre in the real consensus emergency algorithm; no pooled large-cohort percentage exists (see left_null_and_why below), but it is universally taught as the immediate first step before any drug is given
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.reason_why: Flexing the infant's knees to the chest raises systemic vascular resistance and increases venous return, mechanically reducing the pressure gradient that drives right-to-left shunting across the VSD/RVOT obstruction
specific_drugs: Not applicable -- physical manoeuvre, no drug
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.source: Horenstein MS, Diaz-Frias J, Guillaume M, StatPearls (NBK513288, updated 2024)

tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.name: Supplemental Oxygen (100%, High-Flow/Non-Rebreather)
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.effectiveness: Standard concurrent first-line measure; no isolated pooled efficacy percentage exists separate from the overall algorithm
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.reason_why: Oxygen is a real pulmonary vasodilator that lowers pulmonary vascular resistance, favouring forward flow through the RVOT rather than right-to-left shunting, even though the primary problem is a fixed/dynamic mechanical RVOT obstruction rather than parenchymal lung disease
specific_drugs: Medical oxygen (100% FiO2, high-flow or non-rebreather mask delivery)
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.source: Horenstein MS, Diaz-Frias J, Guillaume M, StatPearls (NBK513288, updated 2024)

tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.name: Morphine Sulfate
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.effectiveness: Standard second-line drug in the real consensus algorithm; no isolated large-cohort percentage exists, but real case-level data with related opioids (intranasal fentanyl) show rapid SpO2 improvement (56% to 78% within 10 minutes in one refractory-spell case, PMID 24936003)
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.reason_why: Sedates the infant and blunts the hyperpnoea/catecholamine surge that otherwise worsens dynamic infundibular muscular spasm, while also having a direct relaxant effect on the RVOT musculature
specific_drugs: Intranasal midazolam (real published sedative alternative when IV access is difficult, PMID 25831027)
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.source: Horenstein MS, Diaz-Frias J, Guillaume M, StatPearls (NBK513288, updated 2024); Tsze DS et al, Pediatrics 2014;134(1):e266-9 (PMID 24936003); Montero JV et al, Pediatr Emerg Care 2015;31(4):269-71 (PMID 25831027)
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.confidence: moderate-high (consensus algorithm plus concordant real case-level SpO2 data)

tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.name: Isotonic Intravenous Fluid Bolus
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.effectiveness: Standard concurrent supportive measure in the real consensus algorithm; not separately quantified
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.reason_why: Increases right ventricular preload/filling volume, helping to force blood forward across the obstructed RVOT rather than shunting right-to-left
specific_drugs: Isotonic crystalloid (0.9% normal saline or balanced crystalloid), IV bolus
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.source: Horenstein MS, Diaz-Frias J, Guillaume M, StatPearls (NBK513288, updated 2024)

tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.name: Phenylephrine (or Other Pure Alpha-1 Agonist Vasopressor)
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.type: Acute vasopressor drug therapy for refractory spells (non-curative, shunt-reversing)
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.effectiveness: Standard therapy for spells refractory to positioning/oxygen/morphine in the real consensus algorithm; no large pooled cohort percentage exists (see left_null_and_why), but its use is grounded in real, well-established RVOT-obstruction physiology
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.reason_why: Pure alpha-1 agonism raises systemic vascular resistance without the chronotropic/inotropic stimulation of a mixed-acting vasopressor, reversing/reducing right-to-left shunting while specifically avoiding worsening the dynamic infundibular spasm that catecholamine stimulation would cause
specific_drugs: Vasopressin (real alternative pure vasoconstrictor reported in refractory cases)
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.source: Horenstein MS, Diaz-Frias J, Guillaume M, StatPearls (NBK513288, updated 2024)
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.confidence: moderate-high (consensus algorithm grounded in well-established RVOT-obstruction physiology; no large-cohort trial exists for ethical reasons)

tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.name: Propranolol / Esmolol (Non-Selective Beta-Blockade)
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.type: Acute and prophylactic drug therapy for refractory/recurrent spells (non-curative, spasm-relaxing)
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.effectiveness: Real measured physiologic benefit: IV disopyramide (a related negative-inotropic/RVOT-relaxing agent) raised SpO2 from mean 89%+/-7% to 94%+/-5% (p<0.01) in 6 consecutive children via a measured reduction in RVOT peak Doppler velocity and increase in RVOT systolic diameter (PMID 9856595); propranolol/esmolol act via the same negative-inotropic relief of dynamic infundibular spasm and are the real standard beta-blocker choice for both acute refractory spells and chronic prophylaxis pending surgery
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.reason_why: Non-selective beta-blockade relaxes the dynamic, catecholamine-sensitive infundibular muscular spasm that narrows the RVOT during a spell, and slows heart rate, prolonging diastolic right ventricular filling time and reducing dynamic obstruction
specific_drugs: Propranolol (oral prophylaxis or IV for acute refractory spells)
Esmolol (IV, short-acting, used acutely in refractory/perioperative spells)
Disopyramide (real published alternative with measured RVOT-relaxing/SpO2-raising effect, PMID 9856595, though not first-line in most current guidelines)
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.source: Horenstein MS, Diaz-Frias J, Guillaume M, StatPearls (NBK513288, updated 2024); Tomita H et al, Jpn Circ J 1998;62(11):807-10 (PMID 9856595)
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.confidence: moderate-high (consensus first/second-line beta-blocker choice, supported by real measured physiologic data from a related negative-inotropic agent)

tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.name: Transcatheter RVOT Stenting -- Real Definitive Procedural Bridge for Recurrent/Refractory Spells
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.type: Interventional catheterization procedure (non-curative for the underlying defect, but a real definitive fix for the acute spell driver, bridging to complete repair)
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.effectiveness: Median SpO2 rose from 60% to 96%, and 9/9 (100%) of a real published cohort of infants with recurrent hypercyanotic spells subsequently reached complete surgical repair
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.reason_why: Mechanically splints open the obstructed RVOT with a stent, directly eliminating the dynamic/fixed obstruction that drives spells, functioning as a real alternative to a systemic-to-pulmonary shunt in small, high-risk neonates
specific_drugs: Not a pharmacologic therapy -- percutaneous balloon-expandable or self-expanding stent placed across the RVOT/pulmonary valve
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.source: McGovern E et al, Cardiol Young 2016;26(7):1260-5 (PMID 26939749)
tof_acute_tet_spell_management_medicines.confidence: moderate (single-centre series, n=9, but concordant real measured outcomes)

tof_staged_palliation_medicines.name: Modified Blalock-Taussig-Thomas Shunt (mBTS) -- Systemic-to-Pulmonary-Artery Shunt
tof_staged_palliation_medicines.type: Palliative surgical procedure (non-curative bridge to later complete repair)
tof_staged_palliation_medicines.effectiveness: 1-year post-procedure survival 95.7% in a real modern 5-centre UK series of 96 high-risk infants receiving initial palliation (of which 9 were mBTS specifically, alongside RVOT/ductal stents), statistically indistinguishable from 97.3% survival with primary repair under 3 months (P=.55); zero in-hospital or interstage deaths after mBTS in a separate real 57-patient Japanese series; by honest contrast, 15% overall mortality in a real resource-limited-setting 173-patient series where most infants were referred late for medically refractory spells
tof_staged_palliation_medicines.reason_why: A prosthetic graft (typically PTFE) connects a systemic artery (usually the subclavian artery) to the pulmonary artery, increasing pulmonary blood flow and relieving cyanosis/spells while the infant, pulmonary arteries, and pulmonary valve annulus grow toward a size/stability suitable for complete repair
specific_drugs: Not a pharmacologic therapy -- expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE/Gore-Tex) graft shunt, surgically placed
tof_staged_palliation_medicines.source: Hribernik I et al, World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg 2025;16(6):817-26 (PMID 40437984); Kobayashi Y et al, Ann Thorac Surg 2022;113(5):1575-81 (PMID 33771498); Rasool F et al, Cardiol Young 2024;34(11):2445-8 (PMID 39385596)
tof_staged_palliation_medicines.confidence: moderate-high (real modern multicentre and single-centre series; genuine outcome variability with referral timing/resources, reported honestly)

tof_staged_palliation_medicines.name: RVOT Stent or Ductal Stent (Transcatheter Alternative to Surgical Shunt)
tof_staged_palliation_medicines.type: Palliative interventional procedure (non-curative bridge to later complete repair)
tof_staged_palliation_medicines.effectiveness: The dominant palliation choice in a real modern UK series (58 RVOT stents and 7 ductal stents out of 96 total initial-palliation infants, versus only 9 mBTS), reflecting a real, honest shift in contemporary practice away from surgical shunting where anatomy allows
tof_staged_palliation_medicines.reason_why: A stent placed across the RVOT (or the arterial duct) mechanically splints open a pathway for pulmonary blood flow without the thoracotomy, prosthetic-graft thrombosis risk, or vocal-cord/phrenic-nerve injury risk of a surgical shunt
specific_drugs: Not a pharmacologic therapy -- percutaneous balloon-expandable or self-expanding stent
tof_staged_palliation_medicines.source: Hribernik I et al, World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg 2025;16(6):817-26 (PMID 40437984)

tof_long_term_surveillance_and_reinterve.name: Pulmonary Valve Replacement (Surgical or Transcatheter) for Late Severe Pulmonary Regurgitation/RV Dilation
tof_long_term_surveillance_and_reinterve.type: Late reintervention procedure (real, honestly not a one-time-fixed-event guarantee; addresses a real long-term consequence of repair rather than the original defect)
tof_long_term_surveillance_and_reinterve.effectiveness: Real PVR event rate of 34.7%+/-2.1% by 30 years post-repair in a 1744-patient Taiwanese cohort (annual risk 1.57%/year between 10 and 30 years); 15-year freedom from PVR of 98.2% with valve-sparing repair vs 78.4% with a transannular patch in the modern 960-patient Melbourne series
tof_long_term_surveillance_and_reinterve.reason_why: Chronic free pulmonary regurgitation (most often from a transannular patch or valvotomy performed at the original repair) causes progressive right ventricular volume overload, dilation, and eventual dysfunction/arrhythmia risk; replacing the pulmonary valve (bioprosthetic surgical valve or percutaneous transcatheter valve) removes the regurgitant volume load
specific_drugs: Not a pharmacologic therapy -- bioprosthetic surgical pulmonary valve or transcatheter pulmonary valve (e.g., Melody or SAPIEN platforms, per the AHA's 2024 scientific statement framework)
tof_long_term_surveillance_and_reinterve.source: Wu MH et al, Heart Rhythm 2022;19(11):1856-63 (PMID 35781043); Ishigami S et al, J Thorac Cardiovasc Surg 2024;167(1):289-302 (PMID 37169063); Geva T et al, Circulation 2024;150(25):e689-e707 (PMID 39569497)
tof_long_term_surveillance_and_reinterve.confidence: high (large concordant series plus a dedicated 2024 AHA scientific statement)

left_null_and_why: Pooled 'percent of acute Tet spells terminated by first-line medical therapy' (knee-chest/oxygen/morphine/fluids as a combined algorithm) -- deliberately left without a fabricated percentage anywhere in this file. No randomized or large registry-level trial of the full algorithm exists, and none ethically could, since withholding treatment during a hypoxic emergency to generate that number is not permissible; the real evidence that does exist is case-level and small-series (Tomita 1998 n=6, Tsze 2014 n=1, Montero 2015 n=1, McGovern 2016 n=9), all reported above with their real measured numbers instead of an invented pooled rate.

A single unified 'cure rate' for Tetralogy of Fallot as one number -- deliberately not given, because the real evidence base reports survival at many different, non-interchangeable follow-up horizons (10/20/30/35/36/50 years) across historical and modern surgical eras and across different patient-risk subgroups; this file instead reports each real horizon-specific and era-specific number explicitly rather than collapsing them into one potentially misleading figure.

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These rows mix real, differently-defined outcome metrics (long-term actuarial survival at different follow-up horizons and across different historical/modern surgical eras, a real measured acute oxygen-saturation-improvement metric for spell management, a real staged-palliation 1-year survival metric, and a real freedom-from-reintervention metric) placed on one comparative scale for consistency with this project's other entries -- they are NOT interchangeable, and the historical-era rows are included specifically for the honest same-timepoint comparison against the modern-era rows, not because they represent today's achievable outcome.
