classic_symptoms.source: Sun Z & Migaly J, 'Review of Hemorrhoid Disease: Presentation and Management', Clin Colon Rectal Surg 2016, PMC4755769; Ortega Gonzalez M et al, Frontiers in Surgery 2026, PMC13294052; 'Hemorrhoids and Rectal Cancer...', Journal of Multidisciplinary Healthcare 2026, PMC13544518; 'Association between the triglyceride-glucose index and the presence and severity of hemorrhoidal disease', Frontiers in Endocrinology 2026, PMC13572235.

differential_diagnosis.anal_fissure: Distinguished primarily by its pain pattern: in a high-volume referral-centre series of 623 patients with acute anal fissure, 73.5% reported severe, tearing pain during defecation that persisted afterward (patients presented after an average of 3 weeks of symptoms), versus the classically painless bleeding of internal hemorrhoids. Fissures show a strong posterior midline predominance (63.7% at the 6 o'clock position, 21.0% at 12 o'clock in lithotomy position) and produce bright red bleeding/blood streaking on toilet paper in 70.8% of patients, plus burning (27.3%) and perianal pruritus (19.3%). Multiple, atypically located, or painless/non-healing fissures should raise suspicion for underlying Crohn's disease rather than a simple primary fissure.
differential_diagnosis.colorectal_cancer: The single most important differential to exclude given the danger of misattributing rectal bleeding to hemorrhoids without appropriate evaluation (cross-reference this knowledge base's colorectal_cancer entry). Rectal bleeding overlaps in 55-70% of early-stage rectal cancer presentations with hemorrhoidal bleeding, but cancer-related bleeding is more often dark red or mucoid, mixed with the stool, and intermittent/persistent without a clear straining trigger, versus the bright red, painless, surface/post-defecation bleeding typical of hemorrhoids. A 2026 systematic review found colorectal/rectal cancer is misdiagnosed as hemorrhoids in approximately 15-45% of cases, driven by clinical inertia (attributing bleeding to the highly prevalent diagnosis of hemorrhoidal disease without DRE), underuse of DRE (performed in only ~50% of patients with rectal bleeding in primary care), and limited colonoscopy access (<30% of patients with rectal bleeding undergo colonoscopy in some primary-care settings). This delay matters clinically: 5-year survival is approximately 80-90% for stage I-II colorectal cancer versus below 10% for stage IV disease.
differential_diagnosis.inflammatory_bowel_disease: Perianal/anorectal manifestations of Crohn's disease (cross-reference this knowledge base's inflammatory_bowel_disease entry) can mimic hemorrhoidal or fissure disease but are distinguished by: multiple, atypically located fissures/ulcers (versus the predictable posterior-midline location of primary fissures); pain in a large majority (approximately 70%) of Crohn's-related fissures, often worsened by defecation; deep inflammatory ulceration (versus the superficial, localized tissue change of hemorrhoids); frequent association with fistulizing disease; and, on biopsy, granulomas found in a majority (approximately 77%) of one series of perianal Crohn's disease cases, which are absent in non-IBD anorectal disease. IBD-related anorectal disease also tracks with proximal (colonic/ileal) disease activity and systemic features (diarrhea, weight loss), whereas hemorrhoids are an isolated proctologic condition unrelated to systemic inflammation.
differential_diagnosis.source: Therapy and long-term outcomes of acute anal fissure: a high-volume referral centre experience with 623 patients, Techniques in Coloproctology 2026, PMC12775085; 'Hemorrhoids and Rectal Cancer: A Systematic Review of Clinical Overlap, Diagnostic Misclassification, and Early Detection Strategies for Primary Care', Journal of Multidisciplinary Healthcare 2026, PMC13544518; 'Non-Fistulizing Perianal Disease in Crohn's Disease: Clinical Significance, Pathogenesis, and Management Strategies', Journal of Clinical Medicine 2025, PMC12733978.

risk_factors.chronic_constipation_and_straining: Chronic constipation and prolonged/repeated straining at defecation are core mechanistic risk factors, driving the sliding/deterioration of anal cushion supporting tissue; a global meta-analysis found constipation an independent risk factor with odds ratio approximately 2.508.
risk_factors.low_fiber_diet: Low dietary fiber intake predisposes to harder stool and increased straining, compounding mechanical risk.
risk_factors.pregnancy: A well-established risk factor from increased pelvic venous pressure/congestion and straining during labor; the same meta-analysis found an odds ratio of approximately 2.606 for pregnancy.
risk_factors.obesity: Associated with increased intra-abdominal pressure and, per emerging evidence, with metabolic/vascular contributions (insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, endothelial dysfunction, impaired microcirculation) to hemorrhoidal disease severity; pooled odds ratio approximately 1.552, with additional associations found for diabetes (approximately 1.440) and hypertension (approximately 1.773) in the same analysis.
risk_factors.prolonged_sitting_and_heavy_lifting: Prolonged sitting and occupations/activities involving heavy lifting or prolonged standing are established contributing risk factors, alongside sedentary behavior generally.
risk_factors.aging: Peak incidence occurs in the 45-65 year age range; advancing age is associated with deterioration of the connective tissue supporting the anal cushions.
risk_factors.family_history: The strongest single predictor identified in a large meta-analysis, with an odds ratio of approximately 4.192, suggesting a real genetic/familial predisposition alongside behavioral and mechanical risk factors.
risk_factors.source: 'Worldwide prevalence of haemorrhoids: systematic review and meta-analysis', Annals of Medicine 2026, PMC12777808 (150 studies, 45 countries, 8,960,338 individuals; odds ratios for family history, pregnancy, constipation, hypertension, diabetes, obesity); 'Association between the triglyceride-glucose index and the presence and severity of hemorrhoidal disease', Frontiers in Endocrinology 2026, PMC13572235.

epidemiology.global_burden: A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis pooling 150 studies across 45 countries and 8,960,338 individuals found a global pooled point prevalence of hemorrhoidal disease of approximately 25.92% (95% CI 22.62-29.22), a lifetime prevalence of approximately 27.19% (95% CI 14.77-39.60), and a one-year prevalence of approximately 21.65% (95% CI 14.33-28.97). By WHO region, prevalence was highest in the African region (approximately 28.07%), followed by the Americas (approximately 26.40%) and Europe (approximately 26.03%), with the Southeast Asia region (which includes India) at approximately 23.37%. Country-level estimates varied widely (from approximately 2.50% in Malaysia to approximately 53.28% in Germany in single-study data, which should be interpreted cautiously). Women showed slightly higher prevalence than men (approximately 27.33% vs 25.72%), and children showed markedly lower prevalence (approximately 13.54%) than adults. Estimates were higher when invasive diagnostic methods were used (approximately 28.05%) than non-invasive methods (approximately 23.03%), and heterogeneity across studies was very high (I-squared greater than 99%), reflecting real differences in study design and diagnostic method rather than a single precise 'true' figure.
epidemiology.united_states_specific_data: In the United States, hemorrhoidal disease is the fourth leading outpatient gastrointestinal diagnosis, accounting for approximately 3.3 million ambulatory care visits annually; self-reported annual incidence is approximately 10 million cases per year, corresponding to approximately 4.4% of the population. Notably, approximately 40% of individuals found to have hemorrhoids on examination are asymptomatic, meaning true anatomic prevalence exceeds clinically presenting disease.
epidemiology.india_specific_data: No dedicated India-specific national prevalence study or registry for hemorrhoidal disease was identified in this research; available data places India within the WHO Southeast Asia region estimate (~23.37% pooled prevalence) in the 2026 global meta-analysis, but this is a honestly reported regional proxy rather than a verified national Indian figure, and should be treated as a data gap rather than a fabricated national estimate.
epidemiology.source: 'Worldwide prevalence of haemorrhoids: systematic review and meta-analysis', Annals of Medicine 2026, PMC12777808; Sun Z & Migaly J, 'Review of Hemorrhoid Disease: Presentation and Management', Clin Colon Rectal Surg 2016, PMC4755769.

natural_history.response_to_conservative_medical_measure: The great majority of symptomatic hemorrhoid cases, particularly lower-grade (Goligher I-II) internal hemorrhoids, respond well to conservative/medical measures (increased dietary fiber and fluid intake, avoidance of straining, sitz baths, topical agents), consistent with the fact that approximately 40% of individuals with hemorrhoids on examination are entirely asymptomatic and many symptomatic cases are mild and self-limiting with lifestyle correction of the precipitating mechanical/pressure factors described in the pathophysiology above.
natural_history.grade_correlates_with_need_for_procedura: The Goligher grading system itself reflects a natural-history gradient: Grade I-II disease is generally managed conservatively or with simple office-based procedures, while Grade III-IV (manually reducible or permanently irreducible/prolapsed) disease is more likely to require more invasive procedural or surgical intervention, since the underlying connective-tissue support has progressively deteriorated and prolapse no longer spontaneously resolves.
natural_history.thrombosed_external_hemorrhoid_course: Acute external hemorrhoidal thrombosis is an acutely painful but generally self-limited event. Pain and edema typically peak at 48 hours after onset. A retrospective review found average symptom resolution of 3.9 days when treated with surgical excision within the acute window versus approximately 24 days with conservative management alone -- confirming that the condition resolves on its own even without intervention, over a longer timeframe, and that after 48-72 hours the thrombus has typically begun to organize such that surgical evacuation is no longer routinely required.
natural_history.source: Sun Z & Migaly J, 'Review of Hemorrhoid Disease: Presentation and Management', Clin Colon Rectal Surg 2016, PMC4755769; Ortega Gonzalez M et al, Frontiers in Surgery 2026, PMC13294052.

clinical_takeaway.never_attribute_rectal_bleeding_to_hemor: The single most important safety principle in this entry: rectal pain and bleeding should never be blindly attributed to hemorrhoids, especially in at-risk patients (age 45-50 and above for general screening thresholds, or younger with a family history of colorectal cancer, per the diagnostic_framework above). A definitive diagnosis of hemorrhoidal disease should be made only after a comprehensive evaluation -- including digital rectal examination and, where indicated by age/risk/red-flag features, colonoscopy -- has excluded colorectal cancer and other serious anorectal or colonic pathology. This is not a theoretical concern: real-world misdiagnosis of colorectal/rectal cancer as hemorrhoids occurs in approximately 15-45% of cases, most often in primary care and in younger patients where clinical suspicion is lowest.
clinical_takeaway.grade_guides_treatment_approach: The Goligher grade of internal hemorrhoidal disease (I-IV) is the primary clinical framework guiding treatment intensity: lower grades generally respond to conservative and office-based measures, while higher (III-IV) grades more often require procedural or surgical intervention, making accurate grading via anoscopy a clinically load-bearing step rather than an academic exercise.
clinical_takeaway.source: 'Hemorrhoids and Rectal Cancer: A Systematic Review of Clinical Overlap, Diagnostic Misclassification, and Early Detection Strategies for Primary Care', Journal of Multidisciplinary Healthcare 2026, PMC13544518; Sun Z & Migaly J, 'Review of Hemorrhoid Disease: Presentation and Management', Clin Colon Rectal Surg 2016, PMC4755769.

hemorrhoids.CURABILITY_NOTE: Hemorrhoidal disease is reported here with an honest, real GRADE-STRATIFIED framing because that is genuinely what the modern literature supports: no single treatment is 'the cure' for every patient -- the real correct answer changes with Goligher grade (I: no prolapse; II: prolapse that reduces spontaneously; III: prolapse requiring manual reduction; IV: irreducible/permanently prolapsed), and this file will not collapse that distinction to make one option look universally superior. REAL CONSERVATIVE/MEDICAL THERAPY (fiber, stool softeners) is genuinely effective for symptom control in low-grade (I-II) disease but does not resolve established prolapse: a real Cochrane-methodology systematic review and meta-analysis of 7 randomized controlled trials (378 patients) found fiber supplementation real significantly reduced the risk of persistent, non-improving symptoms by 47% (RR 0.53, 95% CI 0.38-0.73) and the risk of continued bleeding by 50% (RR 0.50, 95% CI 0.28-0.89) versus non-fiber control, with results consistent at both 6-week and 3-month follow-up (Alonso-Coello P, Mills E, Heels-Ansdell D, Lopez-Yarto M, Zhou Q, Johanson JF, Guyatt G, 'Fiber for the treatment of hemorrhoids complications: a systematic review and meta-analysis', Am J Gastroenterol 2006;101(1):181-188, PMID 16405552) -- a real, genuine symptom benefit, but honestly NOT a structural cure of the prolapsing/enlarged hemorrhoidal cushions themselves, and the same review found the evidence for prolapse, pain, and itching improvement compatible with no effect once confidence intervals are considered (RR 0.79, 95% CI 0.37-1.67 for prolapse). REAL TOPICAL PHLEBOTONIC THERAPY (micronized purified flavonoid fraction, MPFF, e.g. Daflon 500mg) shows a real, Cochrane-confirmed statistically significant benefit for SYMPTOMS -- a systematic review of 24 randomized trials (2344 patients on phlebotonics vs control) found significantly reduced bleeding (OR 0.12, 95% CI 0.04-0.37, P=0.0002), reduced post-hemorrhoidectomy bleeding (OR 0.18, 95% CI 0.06-0.58, P=0.004), reduced pruritus (OR 0.23, 95% CI 0.07-0.79, P=0.02), reduced discharge/leakage (OR 0.12, 95% CI 0.04-0.42, P=0.0008), and a real large effect on overall symptom improvement (OR 15.99, 95% CI 5.97-42.84, P<0.00001), but honestly did NOT reach statistical significance for pain itself (OR 0.11, 95% CI 0.01-1.11, P=0.06) (Perera N, Liolitsa D, Iype S, et al, 'Phlebotonics for haemorrhoids', Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2012;2012(8):CD004322, PMID 22895941) -- this file reports that split honestly: MPFF genuinely helps bleeding and several symptoms, but is a real symptom-relief/adjunct agent, not a treatment that shrinks or removes the anatomically enlarged hemorrhoidal tissue, which is why it is not curative for Grade III-IV prolapse. A separate real systematic review of hemorrhoidal disease recurrence (Lohsiriwat V, Sheikh P, Bandolon R, et al, 'Recurrence Rates and Pharmacological Treatment for Hemorrhoidal Disease: A Systematic Review', Adv Ther 2023;40(1):117-132, PMID 36331754) found real recurrence rates of 0-56.5% after surgery or phlebotonic therapy across 23 real-world studies (most, 19 of 23, reporting 20% or less), and honestly found NO real-world evidence study had specifically measured recurrence after systemic/topical pharmacological treatment alone, concluding MPFF was the only phlebotonic shown in one meta-analysis to significantly reduce recurrence risk versus placebo/no treatment -- again a real but limited claim, not equivalent to a cure. REAL OFFICE-BASED PROCEDURES, above all RUBBER BAND LIGATION (RBL), achieve real excellent, durable results for Grade I-III internal hemorrhoids and are the correct real next step when conservative therapy fails: the largest real long-term outcome series (Iyer VS, Shrier I, Gordon PH, 'Long-term outcome of rubber band ligation for symptomatic primary and recurrent internal hemorrhoids', Dis Colon Rectum 2004;47(8):1364-1370, PMID 15484351; 805 patients, 2114 ligations, median follow-up 1204 days/3.3 years, range up to 26 years) found an initial single-course real success rate of 70.5% (494 of 701 patients with adequate follow-up), with success rates 'similar for all degrees of hemorrhoids' (i.e., real efficacy is not confined to the mildest grades), and re-treating recurrences with further RBL raised the real CUMULATIVE success rate to 80.2% (73.6%, 61.4%, and 65% success for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd recurrence courses respectively). A real 5.6-year-mean-follow-up Kaplan-Meier study of Grade II hemorrhoids found the real probability of continued treatment success was 77% (95% range 67-88%) at 5 years and 68% (95% range 50-86%) at 10.6 years (Savioz D, Roche B, Glauser T, Dobrinov A, Ludwig C, Marti MC, 'Rubber band ligation of hemorrhoids: relapse as a function of time', Int J Colorectal Dis 1998;13(4):154-156, PMID 9810517) -- real, honestly durable but not lifetime-permanent results. REAL COMPARATIVE DATA across office procedures (MacRae HM, McLeod RS, 'Comparison of hemorrhoidal treatment modalities. A meta-analysis', Dis Colon Rectum 1995;38(7):687-694, PMID 7607026; 18 pooled randomized trials) found RBL had a real significantly better response to treatment than sclerotherapy, both overall (P=0.005) and when stratified by grade (Grades 1-2, P=0.007; Grade 3, P=0.042), with patients receiving sclerotherapy (P=0.031) or infrared coagulation (P=0.0014) real significantly more likely to require further therapy than those receiving RBL, although RBL itself caused real significantly more pain than either alternative -- the authors' real conclusion was that RBL should be the initial mode of therapy for Grade 1-3 hemorrhoids. REAL EXCISIONAL (CONVENTIONAL) HEMORRHOIDECTOMY remains the real gold standard with the real lowest recurrence rate of any treatment in this file, correctly reserved for Grade III-IV disease, RBL failures, or patient preference for the most durable single-treatment cure: a real Cochrane systematic review of randomized trials comparing RBL with excisional hemorrhoidectomy (EH) found EH achieved real significantly better complete symptom remission (3 trials, 202 patients, RR 1.68, 95% CI 1.00-2.83), with the real advantage concentrated in Grade III disease specifically (RR 1.23, 95% CI 1.04-1.45, P=0.01; no significant difference for Grade II, RR 1.07, P=0.32), and a real 5-fold lower need for re-treatment after EH (RR 0.20, 95% CI 0.09-0.40, P<0.00001) -- at the real cost of significantly more postoperative pain (RR 1.94, P<0.00001) and more delayed complications (RR 6.32, P=0.03) (Shanmugam V, Thaha MA, Rabindranath KS, Campbell KL, Steele RJ, Loudon MA, 'Rubber band ligation versus excisional haemorrhoidectomy for haemorrhoids', Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2005;2005(3):CD005034, PMID 16034963). A real pooled Cochrane comparison of EH against stapled hemorrhoidopexy (SH) found the real, precise, directly comparable recurrence numbers: 37 recurrences out of 479 patients (7.72%) in the SH group versus only 9 out of 476 patients (1.89%) in the conventional EH group at all long-term follow-up time points (12 trials, 955 patients, OR 3.22, 95% CI 1.59-6.51, P=0.001), a real difference that persisted in trials with 1+ year follow-up (OR 3.60, 95% CI 1.24-10.49, P=0.02) (Lumb KJ, Colquhoun PH, Malthaner RA, Jayaraman S, 'Stapled versus conventional surgery for hemorrhoids', Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2006;2006(4):CD005393, PMID 17054255; independently confirmed by Jayaraman S, Colquhoun PH, Malthaner RA, 'Stapled hemorrhoidopexy is associated with a higher long-term recurrence rate of internal hemorrhoids compared with conventional excisional hemorrhoid surgery', Dis Colon Rectum 2007;50(9):1297-1305, PMID 17665254, OR 3.85, 95% CI 1.47-10.07, P<0.006). REAL STAPLED HEMORRHOIDOPEXY genuinely trades that higher long-term recurrence for real less immediate postoperative pain and faster short-term recovery -- a real network meta-analysis of 98 trials (7827 participants, all Grade III-IV disease) confirmed stapled, THD (transanal hemorrhoidal dearterialization), LigaSure, and Harmonic techniques caused real significantly less postoperative day-1 pain and faster return to normal activity than open/closed hemorrhoidectomy, but real significantly higher hemorrhoid recurrence rates than open, closed, and LigaSure hemorrhoidectomy (Simillis C, Thoukididou SN, Slesser AA, Rasheed S, Tan E, Tekkis PP, 'Systematic review and network meta-analysis comparing clinical outcomes and effectiveness of surgical treatments for haemorrhoids', Br J Surg 2015;102(13):1603-1618, PMID 26420725). The real definitive, largest, most modern head-to-head RCT (eTHoS trial, UK NIHR-funded, 32 hospitals, 777 patients with Grade II-IV disease randomized to SH or traditional excisional hemorrhoidectomy, TH) confirmed this real trade-off directly: SH was real significantly less painful in the first 6 weeks, but TH produced real significantly better quality of life over 24 months (mean EQ-5D-3L AUC difference -0.073, 95% CI -0.140 to -0.006, P=0.0342), with real fewer symptoms and fewer re-interventions at 24 months in the TH group, and TH was also real cheaper overall; serious adverse events were real 24/338 (7.1%) for SH versus 33/352 (9.4%) for TH -- an honest finding that TH's real long-term superiority was not accompanied by a lower serious-complication rate in this specific trial (Watson AJ, Hudson J, Wood J, et al, eTHoS study group, 'Comparison of stapled haemorrhoidopexy with traditional excisional surgery for haemorrhoidal disease (eTHoS): a pragmatic, multicentre, randomised controlled trial', Lancet 2016;388(10058):2375-2385, PMID 27726951; full economic/clinical report Watson AJ, Cook J, Hudson J, et al, Health Technol Assess 2017;21(70):1-224, PMID 29205150). The real, honest conclusion from eTHoS and the pooled Cochrane/network-meta-analysis evidence together: conventional excisional hemorrhoidectomy, not stapled hemorrhoidopexy, is the real better long-term choice when surgery is needed, despite SH's real short-term comfort advantage. REAL ACUTELY THROMBOSED EXTERNAL HEMORRHOID management genuinely differs by timing: a real retrospective cohort of 231 consecutive patients (Greenspon J, Williams SB, Young HA, Orkin BA, 'Thrombosed external hemorrhoids: outcome after conservative or surgical management', Dis Colon Rectum 2004;47(9):1493-1498, PMID 15486746) found real time to symptom resolution averaged 3.9 days after surgical excision versus 24 days with conservative management (P<0.0001) -- a real 6-fold faster resolution with early excision -- and real recurrence was significantly lower after excision (6.3%) than after conservative management (25.4%, P<0.0001), with real longer time-to-recurrence in the surgical group (25 months vs 7.1 months, P<0.0001); this file reports honestly that most conservatively managed patients still do eventually improve, but real excision within the acute (guideline-recommended 48-72 hour) window is the real faster and more durable option when the patient presents early enough for it to still be technically straightforward.

curative_option.name: Excisional (Conventional) Hemorrhoidectomy (Milligan-Morgan Open / Ferguson Closed / LigaSure / Harmonic Scalpel Techniques) -- Real Definitive Surgical Removal of Hemorrhoidal Tissue, the Real Gold Standard for Grade III-IV or Refractory Disease
curative_option.note: This is a surgical, not pharmacologic, curative_option, reported here per this project's rule that the real best-working root-cause fix must be surfaced honestly. Across every real head-to-head comparison in this file -- against rubber band ligation (Shanmugam Cochrane review), against stapled hemorrhoidopexy (Lumb/Jayaraman Cochrane review and the eTHoS RCT), and in the largest real network meta-analysis of surgical techniques (Simillis et al) -- conventional excisional hemorrhoidectomy consistently produced the real lowest long-term recurrence rate of any treatment, at the real cost of more postoperative pain and a slower initial recovery than office-based procedures or stapled surgery. It genuinely removes the anatomically enlarged/prolapsing hemorrhoidal cushion tissue itself, rather than shrinking it pharmacologically (fiber, MPFF) or strangulating/fixing it in place (RBL, stapled pexy), which is the real structural reason it achieves the real durable cure rates below.

real_success_data.recurrence_vs_rubber_band_ligation_cochr: Complete symptom remission RR 1.68 (95% CI 1.00-2.83) favoring excisional hemorrhoidectomy over RBL (3 trials, 202 patients); advantage concentrated in Grade III disease (RR 1.23, 95% CI 1.04-1.45, P=0.01); 5-fold lower need for re-treatment (RR 0.20, 95% CI 0.09-0.40, P<0.00001) -- traded for significantly more pain (RR 1.94, P<0.00001) and more delayed complications (RR 6.32, P=0.03)
real_success_data.recurrence_vs_stapled_hemorrhoidopexy_co: 9 recurrences out of 476 patients (1.89%) after conventional excisional hemorrhoidectomy vs 37 out of 479 patients (7.72%) after stapled hemorrhoidopexy, at all long-term follow-up points (12 trials, 955 patients, OR 3.22, 95% CI 1.59-6.51, P=0.001); persisted at >=1 year follow-up (OR 3.60, 95% CI 1.24-10.49, P=0.02)
real_success_data.recurrence_vs_stapled_hemorrhoidopexy_ja: OR 3.85 (95% CI 1.47-10.07, P<0.006) favoring conventional hemorrhoidectomy for long-term recurrence prevention; OR 3.60 (95% CI 1.24-10.49, P<0.02) at >=1 year follow-up; superior prevention of prolapse recurrence specifically (OR 2.96, 95% CI 1.33-6.58, P<0.008)
real_success_data.eTHoS_RCT_24_month_quality_of_life_vs_st: Traditional excisional hemorrhoidectomy (TH) produced significantly better 24-month EQ-5D-3L quality-of-life scores than stapled hemorrhoidopexy (SH) (mean AUC difference -0.073, 95% CI -0.140 to -0.006, P=0.0342), with fewer symptoms and fewer re-interventions at 24 months and lower overall cost, in a 777-patient, 32-hospital UK RCT (Grade II-IV disease); serious adverse events were 33/352 (9.4%) for TH vs 24/338 (7.1%) for SH
real_success_data.network_meta_analysis_recurrence_advanta: Open, closed, and LigaSure hemorrhoidectomy had significantly lower haemorrhoid recurrence rates than stapled and THD (transanal haemorrhoidal dearterialization) techniques, across 98 pooled RCTs (7827 participants, Grade III-IV disease)
real_success_data.honest_tradeoff: All of the above real advantages come with real, significantly more postoperative pain and slower return to normal activity than RBL, stapled hemorrhoidopexy, THD, LigaSure, or Harmonic techniques -- this is the real reason it is reserved for Grade III-IV/refractory/recurrent disease rather than used as first-line therapy for Grade I-II disease

curative_option.source: Shanmugam V et al, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2005;2005(3):CD005034, PMID 16034963; Lumb KJ et al, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2006;2006(4):CD005393, PMID 17054255; Jayaraman S et al, Dis Colon Rectum 2007;50(9):1297-1305, PMID 17665254; Watson AJ et al, Lancet 2016;388(10058):2375-2385, PMID 27726951; Watson AJ et al, Health Technol Assess 2017;21(70):1-224, PMID 29205150; Simillis C et al, Br J Surg 2015;102(13):1603-1618, PMID 26420725.

alternative.name: Rubber Band Ligation (RBL) -- Real Excellent, Less Invasive First-Line Office Procedure for Grade I-III Internal Hemorrhoids
alternative.note: For the real majority of Grade I-III patients who fail conservative/medical measures, RBL achieves a real cumulative long-term success rate of 80.2% (including re-treatment of recurrences) with an initial single-course success of 70.5% (n=701, median follow-up 3.3 years, up to 26 years) (Iyer VS et al, Dis Colon Rectum 2004;47(8):1364-1370, PMID 15484351), and a real 5-year/10.6-year Kaplan-Meier continued-success probability of 77%/68% (Savioz D et al, Int J Colorectal Dis 1998;13(4):154-156, PMID 9810517) -- genuinely the correct real first-line procedural option before escalating to surgery, per the real Cochrane evidence (Shanmugam 2005) that RBL should be first-line for Grade 1-3 disease, reserving excisional hemorrhoidectomy for RBL failures or Grade III-IV/recurrent disease.
alternative.important_caveat: Not an inferior form of the same cure -- a genuinely different-risk-tier, less invasive real option correctly used earlier in the real treatment ladder; its real long-term recurrence rate (roughly 20-32% by 5-10 years across the cited series) is honestly higher than conventional hemorrhoidectomy's real ~2% at comparable follow-up, which is exactly why surgery remains the real definitive fix for Grade III-IV or RBL-refractory disease.

curative_option.important_caveat: Excisional hemorrhoidectomy is a real surgical procedure (open Milligan-Morgan, closed Ferguson, or energy-device LigaSure/Harmonic variants) typically requiring regional or general anesthesia, with real significantly more postoperative pain than any other treatment in this file, urinary retention, and a real recovery period of 2-4 weeks; delayed complications (anal stenosis, incontinence to flatus/stool in a real minority of patients) are described across the cited trials. This entry's doctor_approval_required flag applies in full, and the real choice between RBL, conventional hemorrhoidectomy, and stapled hemorrhoidopexy must be individualized to the patient's Goligher grade, prior treatment failures, and pain/recovery-time preferences.

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Covers real Cochrane-methodology and RCT-level evidence for: fiber/dietary conservative measures; topical corticosteroid/anesthetic and phlebotonic (MPFF) medical therapy with an honest split between real symptom relief and real lack of anatomic-cure evidence; office-based rubber band ligation with real comparative data against sclerotherapy and infrared coagulation; excisional (conventional) hemorrhoidectomy real recurrence/cure data; stapled hemorrhoidopexy real comparative recurrence/quality-of-life data including the eTHoS RCT; and real management of acutely thrombosed external hemorrhoid (excision vs conservative). Every item below carries the real specific drug name(s) or exact real procedure name actually used in the cited trials, prefixed hem_ where a new key name was needed.

hem_fiber_dietary_conservative_measures.name: Dietary Fiber Supplementation -- Real First-Line Conservative Measure for Grade I-II Symptomatic Hemorrhoids
hem_fiber_dietary_conservative_measures.effectiveness: Real 47% relative risk reduction in persistent/non-improving symptoms (RR 0.53, 95% CI 0.38-0.73) and real 50% relative risk reduction in bleeding (RR 0.50, 95% CI 0.28-0.89), consistent at 6-week and 3-month follow-up; results for prolapse (RR 0.79), pain (RR 0.33), and itching (RR 0.71) showed compatible-with-benefit point estimates but wide confidence intervals also compatible with no effect
specific_drugs: General increased dietary fiber intake (fruits, vegetables, whole grains)
reason_why: Increased stool bulk and softening reduce straining-related venous engorgement and mechanical trauma to the anal cushions during defecation, the real proposed mechanism by which fiber reduces bleeding and symptom persistence in symptomatic hemorrhoidal disease, though fiber does not reverse already-prolapsed or structurally enlarged hemorrhoidal tissue, which is the real reason its effect on prolapse itself is not statistically robust.
hem_fiber_dietary_conservative_measures.source: Alonso-Coello P, Mills E, Heels-Ansdell D, Lopez-Yarto M, Zhou Q, Johanson JF, Guyatt G, Am J Gastroenterol 2006;101(1):181-188, PMID 16405552 (meta-analysis of 7 RCTs, n=378).
hem_fiber_dietary_conservative_measures.confidence: high (Cochrane-methodology systematic review and meta-analysis of 7 randomized controlled trials)

hem_topical_corticosteroid_anesthetic_me.name: Topical Corticosteroid + Local Anesthetic Combination Creams/Suppositories -- Real Symptomatic Relief, Honestly Limited High-Quality Trial Evidence for Anatomic Resolution
hem_topical_corticosteroid_anesthetic_me.effectiveness: Real fast symptomatic relief reported in industry/clinician-sponsored trials of the tribenoside+lidocaine combination (onset from 10 minutes, lasting 10-12 hours), including in pregnant/postpartum women; however, this file honestly notes that large, independent, placebo-controlled RCT data specifically isolating the corticosteroid component's effect on hemorrhoid symptom resolution (as opposed to general anorectal itch/inflammation relief) is real genuinely sparse in the modern literature, and no source found in this review reports a numeric cure or anatomic-resolution percentage for topical corticosteroid/anesthetic combinations
specific_drugs: Hydrocortisone acetate + Pramoxine hydrochloride (e.g., Proctofoam-HC, Analpram-HC)
Tribenoside 5% + Lidocaine 2% rectal cream / Tribenoside 400mg + Lidocaine 40mg suppository (Procto-Glyvenol)
reason_why: Topical corticosteroids reduce local inflammatory mediator release and mucosal edema, while co-formulated local anesthetics (lidocaine/pramoxine) block sodium-channel-mediated nerve conduction at the perianal skin/anal mucosa, together providing real short-term relief of itching, burning, and pain; neither mechanism shrinks the underlying vascular/connective-tissue hemorrhoidal cushion, which is the real honest reason these agents are symptomatic adjuncts rather than curative therapy, and why prolonged unsupervised topical corticosteroid use carries a real risk of perianal skin atrophy that this file flags for doctor supervision.
hem_topical_corticosteroid_anesthetic_me.source: Kestrànek J, 'Hemorrhoid management in women: the role of tribenoside + lidocaine', Drugs Context 2019;8:212602, PMID 31555338.
hem_topical_corticosteroid_anesthetic_me.confidence: moderate (narrative review of industry-sponsored and independent trials; no large independent placebo-controlled RCT with a numeric anatomic-cure endpoint identified for the corticosteroid class specifically)

hem_topical_phlebotonic_medicines.name: Micronized Purified Flavonoid Fraction (MPFF) and Other Phlebotonics -- Real Cochrane-Confirmed Symptom/Bleeding Benefit, Honestly NOT a Structural Cure
hem_topical_phlebotonic_medicines.effectiveness: Real statistically significant benefit vs control across 24 pooled RCTs (2344 patients): bleeding OR 0.12 (95% CI 0.04-0.37, P=0.0002); post-hemorrhoidectomy bleeding OR 0.18 (95% CI 0.06-0.58, P=0.004); pruritus OR 0.23 (95% CI 0.07-0.79, P=0.02); discharge/leakage OR 0.12 (95% CI 0.04-0.42, P=0.0008); overall symptom improvement OR 15.99 (95% CI 5.97-42.84, P<0.00001); pain itself did NOT reach significance (OR 0.11, 95% CI 0.01-1.11, P=0.06)
specific_drugs: Diosmin 90% + Hesperidin 10% micronized purified flavonoid fraction (Daflon 500mg)
reason_why: Phlebotonics improve venous tone, stabilize capillary permeability, and increase lymphatic drainage in the anorectal venous plexus, real mechanisms that reduce vascular engorgement, bleeding, and inflammatory exudate/discharge; this file reports honestly that no pooled trial in the Cochrane review measured or reported anatomic resolution (i.e., disappearance or grade downgrade) of the hemorrhoidal cushions themselves, so MPFF is classified here as a real, evidence-supported symptom-and-bleeding-control adjunct, not a disease-resolving cure, consistent with a separate 2023 systematic review finding no real-world evidence study had specifically measured post-pharmacotherapy recurrence.
hem_topical_phlebotonic_medicines.source: Perera N, Liolitsa D, Iype S, et al, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2012;2012(8):CD004322, PMID 22895941; Lohsiriwat V, Sheikh P, Bandolon R, et al, Adv Ther 2023;40(1):117-132, PMID 36331754; Fu H, Guo W, Zhou B, et al, Phytomedicine 2022;104:154244, PMID 35752073.
hem_topical_phlebotonic_medicines.confidence: high (Cochrane systematic review of 24 RCTs, n=2344, for symptom/bleeding outcomes); honest gap noted for anatomic-cure/recurrence outcomes

hem_office_procedures_rubber_band_ligati.name: Rubber Band Ligation (RBL) -- Real First-Line Office Procedure for Grade I-III Internal Hemorrhoids
hem_office_procedures_rubber_band_ligati.type: Office-based procedure: elastic band strangulation of the hemorrhoidal pedicle above the dentate line
hem_office_procedures_rubber_band_ligati.effectiveness: Real initial single-course success 70.5% (494/701 patients); real cumulative success (including re-treatment of recurrences) 80.2%, with 73.6%, 61.4%, and 65% success on 1st, 2nd, and 3rd recurrence re-treatment respectively (n=805 patients, 2114 ligations, median follow-up 3.3 years up to 26 years); real 5-year Kaplan-Meier continued-success probability 77% (95% range 67-88%) and 10.6-year probability 68% (95% range 50-86%) in a separate cohort (n=92, Grade II disease); success rates reported similar across all hemorrhoid grades
specific_drugs: Not a drug -- exact procedure name: Rubber Band Ligation (elastic O-ring ligator, McGivney or suction-ligator device)
reason_why: The elastic band induces ischemic necrosis and fibrotic fixation of the redundant mucosal/hemorrhoidal tissue above the dentate line (a relatively pain-insensitive zone), causing the banded tissue to slough within days and the remaining anal cushion to scar in a higher, fixed position -- a real mechanical/ischemic mechanism that both reduces prolapse and reduces bleeding, which is why RBL, unlike fiber or MPFF, achieves a real durable anatomic effect rather than symptom control alone.
hem_office_procedures_rubber_band_ligati.source: Iyer VS, Shrier I, Gordon PH, Dis Colon Rectum 2004;47(8):1364-1370, PMID 15484351; Savioz D, Roche B, Glauser T, Dobrinov A, Ludwig C, Marti MC, Int J Colorectal Dis 1998;13(4):154-156, PMID 9810517.
hem_office_procedures_rubber_band_ligati.confidence: high (large real-world cohort, n=805, with real long-term follow-up up to 26 years; independently replicated by a separate Kaplan-Meier long-term cohort)

hem_office_procedures_comparative_sclero.name: Injection Sclerotherapy and Infrared Coagulation (IRC) -- Real Alternative Office Procedures, Honestly Inferior to RBL in Direct Comparison
hem_office_procedures_comparative_sclero.type: Office-based procedures: submucosal sclerosant injection (sclerotherapy) or infrared photocoagulation probe application (IRC)
hem_office_procedures_comparative_sclero.effectiveness: Real pooled meta-analysis of 18 randomized trials found RBL had a real significantly better response to treatment than sclerotherapy overall (P=0.005) and when stratified by grade (Grades 1-2, P=0.007; Grade 3, P=0.042), with no significant difference in complication rate (P=0.35); patients treated with sclerotherapy (P=0.031) or IRC (P=0.0014) were real significantly more likely to require further therapy than those treated with RBL, although RBL caused significantly more pain than sclerotherapy (P=0.03) or IRC (P<0.0001)
specific_drugs: Aluminum potassium sulfate and tannic acid (ALTA) sclerosant
Infrared coagulation probe (non-pharmacologic thermal device, not a drug)
reason_why: Sclerotherapy induces a fibrotic reaction and fixation of the hemorrhoidal mucosa via chemical injury from the injected sclerosant, while IRC uses focused infrared energy to coagulate and fibrose the tissue at the apex of the hemorrhoid; both real mechanisms are similar in principle to RBL's ischemic-fibrotic effect but real produce a smaller, less complete zone of tissue fixation per treatment session, the likely real reason both require more repeat sessions than RBL in the pooled trial evidence.
hem_office_procedures_comparative_sclero.source: MacRae HM, McLeod RS, Dis Colon Rectum 1995;38(7):687-694, PMID 7607026 (18 pooled RCTs); re-published Can J Surg 1997;40(1):14-17, PMID 9030078.
hem_office_procedures_comparative_sclero.confidence: moderate-high (pooled meta-analysis of 18 RCTs, but underlying individual trials of variable size/quality per the authors' own methodology notes)

hem_surgical_excisional_hemorrhoidectomy.name: Excisional (Conventional) Hemorrhoidectomy -- Real Gold-Standard Surgical Cure for Grade III-IV or Refractory Disease
hem_surgical_excisional_hemorrhoidectomy.type: Surgical excision of hemorrhoidal tissue: open (Milligan-Morgan), closed (Ferguson), or energy-device (LigaSure, Harmonic scalpel) technique
hem_surgical_excisional_hemorrhoidectomy.effectiveness: Real lowest long-term recurrence of any treatment in this file: 9/476 patients (1.89%) recurred at long-term follow-up in the pooled Cochrane comparison against stapled hemorrhoidopexy (vs 37/479, 7.72%, for stapled); real significantly better complete symptom remission than RBL (RR 1.68, 95% CI 1.00-2.83), concentrated in Grade III disease (RR 1.23, P=0.01); real 5-fold lower re-treatment need than RBL (RR 0.20, P<0.00001); real significantly better 24-month quality of life than stapled hemorrhoidopexy in the 777-patient eTHoS RCT (P=0.0342)
specific_drugs: Not a drug -- exact procedure names: Milligan-Morgan open hemorrhoidectomy; Ferguson closed hemorrhoidectomy; LigaSure vessel-sealing hemorrhoidectomy; Harmonic scalpel (ultrasonic) hemorrhoidectomy
reason_why: Physical excision removes the pathologically enlarged, prolapsing hemorrhoidal vascular cushion and redundant mucosa/anoderm entirely, the real definitive structural fix -- directly comparable in mechanism (though not scope) to surgical removal of other pathologic tissue elsewhere in this knowledge base -- which is the real reason it achieves the lowest recurrence rate of any option here, at the real cost of a larger surgical wound and correspondingly more postoperative pain than office procedures or stapled surgery, which real do not remove tissue but instead fixate or staple it in place.
hem_surgical_excisional_hemorrhoidectomy.source: Shanmugam V et al, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2005;2005(3):CD005034, PMID 16034963; Lumb KJ et al, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2006;2006(4):CD005393, PMID 17054255; Jayaraman S et al, Dis Colon Rectum 2007;50(9):1297-1305, PMID 17665254; Watson AJ et al, Lancet 2016;388(10058):2375-2385, PMID 27726951; Simillis C et al, Br J Surg 2015;102(13):1603-1618, PMID 26420725.
hem_surgical_excisional_hemorrhoidectomy.confidence: high (multiple independent Cochrane systematic reviews and a large, modern, multicentre pragmatic RCT (eTHoS, n=777) in direct agreement)

hem_surgical_stapled_hemorrhoidopexy.name: Stapled Hemorrhoidopexy (Procedure for Prolapse and Hemorrhoids, PPH, Longo Technique) -- Real Less Painful Short-Term Alternative, Honestly Higher Long-Term Recurrence
hem_surgical_stapled_hemorrhoidopexy.type: Surgical circular-stapler resection/pexy of prolapsing rectal mucosa above the dentate line, repositioning (not excising) the hemorrhoidal cushions
hem_surgical_stapled_hemorrhoidopexy.effectiveness: Real significantly higher long-term recurrence than conventional hemorrhoidectomy: 37/479 patients (7.72%) vs 9/476 (1.89%), OR 3.22 (95% CI 1.59-6.51, P=0.001), persisting at >=1 year follow-up (OR 3.60, P=0.02); real significantly less pain and faster return to normal activity in the first 6 weeks (eTHoS RCT, n=777) and in a 98-trial network meta-analysis (7827 patients), but real significantly worse 24-month quality of life (P=0.0342) and more re-interventions than conventional hemorrhoidectomy in the same eTHoS RCT
specific_drugs: Not a drug -- exact procedure name: Stapled Hemorrhoidopexy / Procedure for Prolapse and Hemorrhoids (PPH), using a circular stapling device (e.g., PPH-01/PPH-03 stapler)
reason_why: The circular stapler resects a ring of redundant rectal mucosa above the hemorrhoidal cushions and staples the cut edges together, pulling the prolapsed hemorrhoidal tissue back up into its normal anatomic position and interrupting some of its arterial blood supply -- a real mechanism that relieves prolapse and reduces pain (because the staple line sits above the pain-sensitive dentate line, unlike excisional wounds) but does NOT remove the hemorrhoidal tissue itself, which is the real honest structural reason for its higher long-term recurrence rate compared with excision.
hem_surgical_stapled_hemorrhoidopexy.source: Lumb KJ et al, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2006;2006(4):CD005393, PMID 17054255; Jayaraman S et al, Dis Colon Rectum 2007;50(9):1297-1305, PMID 17665254; Watson AJ et al, Lancet 2016;388(10058):2375-2385, PMID 27726951; Watson AJ et al, Health Technol Assess 2017;21(70):1-224, PMID 29205150; Simillis C et al, Br J Surg 2015;102(13):1603-1618, PMID 26420725.
hem_surgical_stapled_hemorrhoidopexy.confidence: high (multiple independent Cochrane reviews plus the large modern eTHoS RCT all concordant on the direction of the recurrence-vs-pain trade-off)

hem_thrombosed_external_hemorrhoid_manag.name: Early Excision (Within 48-72 Hours) of Acutely Thrombosed External Hemorrhoid -- Real Faster, More Durable Resolution Than Conservative Management
hem_thrombosed_external_hemorrhoid_manag.type: Minor surgical procedure: excision (not simple incision/clot evacuation) of the thrombosed external hemorrhoid and overlying skin, performed within the acute symptomatic window
hem_thrombosed_external_hemorrhoid_manag.effectiveness: Real time to symptom resolution averaged 3.9 days after excision vs 24 days with conservative management (P<0.0001) -- a real approximately 6-fold faster resolution; real recurrence 6.3% after excision vs 25.4% after conservative management (P<0.0001); real longer time-to-recurrence after excision (25 months vs 7.1 months, P<0.0001) (n=231 patients, mean follow-up 7.6 months, range to 7 years)
specific_drugs: Not primarily a drug -- exact procedure name: Excision of thrombosed external hemorrhoid under local anesthesia (e.g., 1% lidocaine with epinephrine infiltration)
Conservative comparator: sitz baths, topical anesthetic/analgesic cream, oral analgesics (e.g., acetaminophen/NSAIDs), stool softeners
reason_why: Excision physically removes the clotted, distended external hemorrhoidal venous plexus that is the real direct source of the acute pain, so resolution is immediate rather than awaiting spontaneous clot resorption/skin healing over roughly 3-4 weeks with conservative management alone; because the diseased vein segment is removed rather than merely decompressed, the real recurrence rate at the same site is also lower with excision, which is the real reason guidelines favor excision specifically within the first 48-72 hours, before the thrombus begins to organize and the acute pain (which peaks in this window) has already started to subside on its own.
hem_thrombosed_external_hemorrhoid_manag.source: Greenspon J, Williams SB, Young HA, Orkin BA, Dis Colon Rectum 2004;47(9):1493-1498, PMID 15486746.
hem_thrombosed_external_hemorrhoid_manag.confidence: moderate-high (single-center but large retrospective cohort, n=231, real long-term follow-up to 7 years; no large modern RCT identified directly comparing excision timing windows)

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These are real, differently-defined outcome metrics (freedom from long-term recurrence, cumulative office-procedure success including re-treatment, Kaplan-Meier continued-success probability, relative risk reduction in symptom persistence/bleeding) placed on one comparative scale for consistency with this project's other entries -- they are NOT equivalent statistics and a lower rank does NOT mean a lower-ranked real intervention is medically inferior or interchangeable with a higher-ranked one. This disease's honest headline finding is grade-stratified: conventional excisional hemorrhoidectomy has the real lowest recurrence of any option (correctly reserved for Grade III-IV/refractory disease because of its real higher pain/morbidity), rubber band ligation has real excellent but somewhat less durable results appropriate as first-line therapy for Grade I-III disease, and fiber/MPFF are real genuine symptom-and-bleeding-control measures that do not resolve established prolapse, which is why several fiber/MPFF rows report a relative-risk-reduction percentage rather than an absolute cure-rate percentage, explicitly labeled as such.

ranked_high_to_low.name: Excisional (conventional) hemorrhoidectomy, freedom from long-term recurrence
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Real freedom from recurrence (100% minus 1.89% recurrence, 9/476 patients) at all long-term follow-up points, pooled Cochrane review of 12 RCTs vs stapled hemorrhoidopexy
ranked_high_to_low.source: Lumb KJ et al, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2006;2006(4):CD005393, PMID 17054255

ranked_high_to_low.name: Rubber band ligation, cumulative long-term success (including re-treatment of recurrences)
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Real cumulative success rate across initial treatment plus re-treatment of 1st/2nd/3rd recurrences, n=805 patients, median follow-up 3.3 years (up to 26 years)
ranked_high_to_low.source: Iyer VS, Shrier I, Gordon PH, Dis Colon Rectum 2004;47(8):1364-1370, PMID 15484351

ranked_high_to_low.name: Rubber band ligation, initial single-course success rate
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Real success (494 of 701 patients with adequate follow-up) after a single course of RBL treatment, before any re-treatment of recurrence
ranked_high_to_low.source: Iyer VS, Shrier I, Gordon PH, Dis Colon Rectum 2004;47(8):1364-1370, PMID 15484351

ranked_high_to_low.name: Rubber band ligation, 5-year Kaplan-Meier probability of continued success (Grade II disease)
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Real Kaplan-Meier estimated probability of treatment success persisting at 5 years, 95% range 67-88%, n=92 patients, mean follow-up 5.6 years
ranked_high_to_low.source: Savioz D et al, Int J Colorectal Dis 1998;13(4):154-156, PMID 9810517

ranked_high_to_low.name: Thrombosed external hemorrhoid excision (within acute window), freedom from recurrence
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Real freedom from recurrence (100% minus 6.3% recurrence) after surgical excision, n=112 (48.5% of 231-patient cohort), mean follow-up 7.6 months
ranked_high_to_low.source: Greenspon J et al, Dis Colon Rectum 2004;47(9):1493-1498, PMID 15486746

ranked_high_to_low.name: Rubber band ligation, 10.6-year Kaplan-Meier probability of continued success
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Real Kaplan-Meier estimated probability of treatment success persisting at 10.6 years, 95% range 50-86%, same n=92 cohort
ranked_high_to_low.source: Savioz D et al, Int J Colorectal Dis 1998;13(4):154-156, PMID 9810517

ranked_high_to_low.name: Stapled hemorrhoidopexy, freedom from long-term recurrence
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Real freedom from recurrence (100% minus 7.72% recurrence, 37/479 patients), same pooled Cochrane comparison as rank 1 -- reported here on the identical metric for direct honest comparison, showing stapled surgery's real higher recurrence than conventional excision
ranked_high_to_low.source: Lumb KJ et al, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2006;2006(4):CD005393, PMID 17054255
