wilms_tumour.name: Wilms Tumour (Nephroblastoma)

definition_and_pathophysiology.overview: Wilms tumor (nephroblastoma) is an embryonal malignancy of the developing kidney and is the most common primary renal malignancy of childhood. It is understood to arise from persistent nephrogenic rests -- benign foci of embryonal metanephric blastema/immature kidney tissue that normally involute before birth but abnormally persist into postnatal life. Nephrogenic rests are found in roughly 20% of Wilms tumor kidneys and occur at much higher frequency in children with WT1-associated genetic syndromes; two patterns are recognized -- intralobar rests, associated with metachronous (sequential) bilateral disease, and perilobar rests, associated with synchronous (simultaneous) bilateral presentation.
definition_and_pathophysiology.source: NCI PDQ, 'Wilms Tumor and Other Childhood Kidney Tumors Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov

wt1_gene_and_molecular_drivers.detail: The WT1 gene, located on chromosome 11p13, encodes a transcription factor 'required for normal genitourinary development.' WT1 variants are found in 10-20% of sporadic Wilms tumor cases and are particularly common in syndromic presentations. Wilms tumors typically arise through more than one genetic event: approximately one-third involve variants in WT1, CTNNB1 (beta-catenin), or AMER1, while a separate subset arises from mutations in miRNA-processing genes. TRIM28 variants account for about 8% of familial Wilms tumor and 2% of unselected cases, with a strong association with epithelial histology.
wt1_gene_and_molecular_drivers.source: NCI PDQ, 'Wilms Tumor and Other Childhood Kidney Tumors Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov

favorable_vs_unfavorable_anaplastic_hist.detail: Histology is genuinely one of the most important determinants of treatment intensity and prognosis in Wilms tumor. Favorable histology (FH), showing the typical triphasic (blastemal, epithelial, stromal) embryonal-kidney differentiation pattern, accounts for the large majority of cases and carries a substantially better prognosis. Unfavorable (anaplastic) histology is defined by nuclear enlargement, an increased mitotic rate, and bizarre (multipolar) mitotic figures, and carries a markedly worse prognosis; most anaplastic Wilms tumors show variants in the TP53 tumor-suppressor gene, and among stage III-IV anaplastic tumors, patients with wild-type TP53 have significantly lower relapse and mortality rates than those with TP53 abnormalities (p=.00006 and p=.00007 respectively). Because of tumor heterogeneity, anaplastic histology can be missed on an initial needle biopsy sample and only discovered at definitive surgery after chemotherapy has already been given -- a real and clinically important diagnostic limitation.
favorable_vs_unfavorable_anaplastic_hist.source: NCI PDQ, 'Wilms Tumor and Other Childhood Kidney Tumors Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov

imaging_sequence.detail: Abdominal ultrasonography is typically performed first, before a more definitive contrast-enhanced CT or MRI, to confirm a renal-origin mass. CT with contrast is the primary definitive imaging modality: it confirms the renal origin of the mass and determines whether bilateral tumors are present (modern helical CT misses only about 0.25% of bilateral tumors, predominantly small lesions). Preoperative imaging must also assess vascular involvement, since 4% of patients present with inferior vena cava or atrial involvement and 11% with renal vein involvement, which changes surgical planning and helps avoid the lethal complication of caval-thrombus embolization. Chest CT is the most sensitive method of detecting metastatic lung nodules, the most common metastatic site (present in roughly 85% of metastatic cases). MRI is preferred over CT when distinguishing a true tumor from a nephrogenic rest, and is used for trilateral/syndromic surveillance, since it avoids ionizing radiation in children who may already be at higher genetic risk of second malignancies.
imaging_sequence.source: NCI PDQ, 'Wilms Tumor and Other Childhood Kidney Tumors Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov

us_versus_siop_treatment_philosophy.detail: A genuinely interesting and real international practice variation exists between North American and European approach to newly diagnosed Wilms tumor. The North American COG/NWTS strategy performs upfront nephrectomy (surgery first), which gives immediate histological diagnosis, accurate staging from the actual surgical specimen, and treatment stratification based on real pathology rather than a pre-treatment estimate. The European SIOP strategy instead gives preoperative (neoadjuvant) chemotherapy first, with surgery delayed until the tumor has been downsized; SIOP's stated benefits are tumor downsizing that facilitates nephron-sparing surgery, reduced operative morbidity, and better preservation of renal function. The advantage of the neoadjuvant approach is illustrated in WAGR-syndrome patients under surveillance: tumors detected by surveillance imaging had significantly smaller volume than symptomatic tumors (18 mL vs 375 mL, p=.001), enabling a high rate of nephron-sparing surgery (85%).
us_versus_siop_treatment_philosophy.source: NCI PDQ, 'Wilms Tumor and Other Childhood Kidney Tumors Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov

biopsy_generally_avoided_upfront_in_the_.detail: In the North American upfront-surgery approach, percutaneous or open biopsy is deliberately avoided before nephrectomy in most children with a radiographically typical mass, because tumor-cell spillage from a biopsy would upstage the patient to stage III, which reflects incomplete resection/spillage and worsens prognosis and treatment intensity. Biopsy is reserved for atypical radiographic appearance not classic for Wilms tumor, for inoperable tumors that require a tissue diagnosis before chemotherapy can begin, or when primary nephrectomy cannot be performed for another reason.
biopsy_generally_avoided_upfront_in_the_.source: NCI PDQ, 'Wilms Tumor and Other Childhood Kidney Tumors Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov

staging_system.detail: Wilms tumor is staged I through V based on extent of disease and completeness of resection: Stage I -- tumor limited to the kidney, completely excised; Stage II -- tumor extends beyond the kidney but is completely excised; Stage III -- incomplete excision or local tumor spillage/residual disease confined to the abdomen; Stage IV -- hematogenous metastases (commonly lung) or lymph-node metastases outside the abdomen/pelvis; Stage V -- bilateral renal involvement at initial diagnosis.
staging_system.source: NCI PDQ, 'Wilms Tumor and Other Childhood Kidney Tumors Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov

asymptomatic_painless_abdominal_mass.detail: The classic and most common presentation of Wilms tumor is an asymptomatic abdominal mass, typically discovered incidentally -- often by a parent or caregiver noticing a lump or that the child's abdomen looks bigger than before during routine bathing or dressing, or found by a physician during a routine well-child examination. A genuinely important and honest clinical point is that children with Wilms tumor are often otherwise well-appearing with 'very little in the way of constitutional symptoms' despite sometimes harboring a large intra-abdominal mass, in contrast to neuroblastoma, which more often presents with a painful mass and systemic illness.
asymptomatic_painless_abdominal_mass.source: NCI, 'Wilms Tumor and Other Childhood Kidney Tumors Treatment (Patient Version)', cancer.gov; Dumba M, Jawad N, McHugh K, 'Neuroblastoma and nephroblastoma: a radiological review', Cancer Imaging, 2015, PMC4446071

abdominal_pain_and_hematuria.detail: Abdominal pain and gross or microscopic hematuria (blood in the urine) are recognized presenting features of Wilms tumor, though less common than the incidentally discovered abdominal mass. Across childhood abdominal tumors broadly, a systematic review and meta-analysis found abdominal mass was the most frequently reported presenting sign at 39.3% (95% CI 31.5-47.5%), with the same review noting that for renal tumors specifically, hematuria and hypertension are frequently reported alongside the abdominal mass, and a fully asymptomatic presentation was reported in only about 1% (95% CI 0.2-2.3%) of renal-tumor cases -- meaning most children do have some detectable sign, even if the child feels otherwise well.
abdominal_pain_and_hematuria.source: NCI, 'Wilms Tumor and Other Childhood Kidney Tumors Treatment (Patient Version)', cancer.gov; Ni Cheallaigh L et al., 'Spotting childhood abdominal tumours: a systematic review and meta-analysis of the clinical presentation', Arch Dis Child, PMC12911601

hypertension_renin_mediated_mechanism.detail: Hypertension is a real and common presenting feature, reported in approximately 22-79% of patients with Wilms tumor at diagnosis. The mechanism is hypothesized to be hyperreninemia, arising either from tumor mass effect causing compression or stretching of the renal pedicle/renal artery, from renal arterial or venous thrombosis, or from direct renin secretion by tumor cells. This is well supported empirically: in one major study, 81% (25/31) of hypertensive Wilms tumor patients who had renin levels checked had elevated plasma renin, compared with only 38% (5/13) of normotensive patients. The hypertension is typically reversible with tumor removal -- 91% of hypertensive patients had normalization of blood pressure immediately after nephrectomy, with the remainder able to stop antihypertensive medication by the end of Wilms tumor therapy (median duration of antihypertensive use was 40-164 days post-surgery in the cited cohorts).
hypertension_renin_mediated_mechanism.source: Hsiao W, Denburg M, Laskin B, 'Hypertension in Wilms tumor', Pediatric Nephrology, PMC12281606

neuroblastoma.detail: Neuroblastoma is the most important real differential for a pediatric abdominal mass and can genuinely mimic Wilms tumor, but the two have well-documented distinguishing features. Origin: Wilms tumor arises from the kidney itself, while neuroblastoma arises from primordial neural crest cells of the sympathetic nervous system (adrenal medulla or paraspinal sympathetic chain), so it is typically extrarenal though adjacent to the kidney. Calcification: calcification is seen on CT in 80-90% of neuroblastomas versus only about 10% of Wilms tumors. Growth pattern: neuroblastoma classically encases and displaces surrounding vessels/structures rather than invading them, and can be an 'unresectable unilateral tumour infiltrating across midline' (a defining feature of higher-stage neuroblastoma per the INSS staging system), whereas Wilms tumor is typically confined within the kidney with a rim of normal renal tissue around the lesion (the 'claw sign'), and when it does involve vasculature it does so by direct tumor invasion into the renal vein/IVC rather than encasement. Age and pain: up to 90% of neuroblastomas are diagnosed by 6 years of age, similar to the Wilms tumor peak of 3-4 years, but neuroblastoma more often presents as a painful mass with constitutional symptoms, while Wilms tumor is classically a painless mass in an otherwise well child. Paraneoplastic clues: neuroblastoma can cause a paraneoplastic syndrome from excess vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) secretion, producing watery diarrhoea and failure to thrive, a feature not seen in Wilms tumor.
neuroblastoma.source: Dumba M, Jawad N, McHugh K, 'Neuroblastoma and nephroblastoma: a radiological review', Cancer Imaging, 2015, PMC4446071

hepatoblastoma.detail: Hepatoblastoma is a real differential for an upper-abdominal mass in a young child but arises from the liver rather than the kidney and characteristically presents with an elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), which is not a feature of Wilms tumor; imaging localizing the mass to the liver versus the kidney, along with the AFP level, helps distinguish the two, with definitive diagnosis still requiring histopathological confirmation.
hepatoblastoma.source: case report, 'Embryonal Hepatoblastoma with Co-existent Glycogen Storage Disease in a Seven-month-old Child', PMC4800539
hepatoblastoma.confidence: moderate -- AFP elevation in hepatoblastoma is well established in the broader literature; this specific citation is a single case report rather than a large series

wagr_syndrome.detail: WAGR syndrome (Wilms tumor, Aniridia, Genitourinary abnormalities, Range of developmental delay) results from a contiguous chromosome 11p13 deletion involving both the WT1 and PAX6 genes. The risk of Wilms tumor in children with WAGR syndrome is approximately 50%. These children present earlier than sporadic cases (median age 22 months vs 44 months) and have a higher incidence of bilateral Wilms tumor (37%). Using WAGR registry data, 95% of affected patients developed their tumor by age 5 years, but about 20% developed it after age 4, with rare cases occurring after age 7-8, which is why extended surveillance is recommended.
wagr_syndrome.source: NCI PDQ, 'Wilms Tumor and Other Childhood Kidney Tumors Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov

denys_drash_and_frasier_syndromes.detail: Denys-Drash syndrome, caused by missense WT1 variants, carries a very high Wilms tumor risk of approximately 90%, with bilateral disease developing in 20% of patients; it also features pseudohermaphroditism and a nephrotic syndrome caused by diffuse mesangial sclerosis. By contrast, Frasier syndrome, caused by WT1 splice-site variants, carries a much lower incidence of Wilms tumor than Denys-Drash syndrome despite both being WT1-related conditions -- a real and clinically important genotype-phenotype distinction.
denys_drash_and_frasier_syndromes.source: NCI PDQ, 'Wilms Tumor and Other Childhood Kidney Tumors Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov

beckwith_wiedemann_syndrome.detail: Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome (BWS) is an overgrowth syndrome caused by chromosome 11p15 imprinting alterations. Approximately 10% of BWS patients overall develop Wilms tumor, but risk varies substantially by the underlying molecular subtype: ICR1 gain of methylation carries a 22.8% Wilms tumor risk, uniparental disomy carries 6.2%, ICR2 loss of methylation carries 2.5%, and CDKN1C variants carry minimal risk. Overall, BWS confers a 42-fold increase in risk of any pediatric cancer compared with the general population.
beckwith_wiedemann_syndrome.source: NCI PDQ, 'Wilms Tumor and Other Childhood Kidney Tumors Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov

sporadic_disease_and_surveillance.detail: The large majority of Wilms tumor cases are sporadic, without an identifiable predisposing syndrome or family history; a family history of Wilms tumor is present in only a minority of cases. For children with recognized predisposing syndromes, surveillance with renal ultrasonography every 3 months until at least age 8 years is standard; in Beckwith-Wiedemann-spectrum patients, screening to age 7 detects close to 95% of all Wilms tumors that will occur.
sporadic_disease_and_surveillance.source: NCI PDQ, 'Wilms Tumor and Other Childhood Kidney Tumors Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov

incidence_and_age.detail: Wilms tumor is the most common renal malignancy in children, with an incidence of about 9.7 cases per million children younger than 15 years and approximately 650 new cases diagnosed annually in the United States. Peak incidence is between 3 and 4 years of age.
incidence_and_age.source: NCI PDQ, 'Wilms Tumor and Other Childhood Kidney Tumors Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov; Dumba M, Jawad N, McHugh K, 'Neuroblastoma and nephroblastoma: a radiological review', Cancer Imaging, 2015, PMC4446071

india_specific_data.detail: Real India-specific outcome data is genuinely limited compared with US/SEER-level detail, a gap the Indian authors themselves note: 'while there is plenty of data in world literature on the outcome of Wilms' tumor, there is paucity of data from India.' The largest single-institution South Indian series (61 histopathologically confirmed patients treated 2003-2010 at a single center, using the NWTS-4 protocol) had a mean age at presentation of 3.3 years (range 1-7 years) and the following stage distribution: Stage I 27.8%, Stage II 16.4%, Stage III 37.7%, Stage IV 14.8%, Stage V 3.3%. The estimated 5-year event-free survival was 83.3% and overall survival was 85.2%, which the authors reported as comparable to the original NWTS-4 protocol study group's outcomes stage-for-stage.
india_specific_data.source: Guruprasad B, Rohan B, Kavitha S, Madhumathi DS, Lokanath D, Appaji L, 'Wilms' tumor: single centre retrospective study from South India', Indian J Surg Oncol, 2013;4(3):301-4, PMC3771043
india_specific_data.confidence: high on the single-center numbers reported; the authors' own note of a broader India-wide data gap is taken at face value and no larger national Indian registry figure was found in this session

one_of_the_most_curable_pediatric_solid_.detail: Wilms tumor is honestly one of the most curable pediatric solid tumors in modern oncology, though the specific outcome depends heavily on histology and stage as described above. For all children under 20 years with Wilms tumor, the overall 5-year relative survival rate is 93%. On modern Children's Oncology Group protocols, favorable-histology disease does very well even at advanced stage: 4-year overall survival was 100% for stage I/II and 96.1% for stage III/IV favorable-histology disease with 1p/16q loss of heterozygosity on AREN0532/AREN0533 (significant improvements over the NWTS-5 historical comparison group's stage I/II and III/IV event-free survival of 68.8% and 61.3% respectively). Favorable-histology stage I disease on NWTS-5 had a 4-year EFS/OS of 92.4%/98.3%. Even stage I anaplastic (unfavorable histology) disease -- traditionally the highest-risk histology -- achieved a 4-year EFS/OS of 100% in a small single-arm cohort (29 patients) on AREN0321, though this is a small sample and should not be read as generalizing to more advanced-stage anaplastic disease, for which specific survival figures were not found in this session and are honestly not asserted here. Stage IV favorable-histology disease with extrapulmonary metastases had somewhat lower but still substantial 4-year EFS/OS of 77.3%/88.9% in a pooled 148-patient cohort, versus 85.4% 4-year EFS for lung-only stage IV metastatic disease on the comparable AREN0533 cohort.
one_of_the_most_curable_pediatric_solid_.source: NCI PDQ, 'Wilms Tumor and Other Childhood Kidney Tumors Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov; Dix DB et al. (AREN0532/AREN0533), PMC7001789; Daw NC et al. (AREN0321, stage I anaplastic), PMC6690766; Benedetti DJ et al. (stage IV favorable histology with extrapulmonary metastases), PMC10922062
one_of_the_most_curable_pediatric_solid_.confidence: high on the specific quoted trial numbers; stage IV anaplastic-histology-specific survival was not found with a citable source in this session and is therefore not asserted numerically

untreated_natural_history.detail: A specific, precisely sourced numeric untreated-survival figure for Wilms tumor was not found with a citable source in this session and is therefore not asserted here with an invented number. What is real and well documented is the contrast: without modern multimodal treatment, this is a malignant, locally invasive and metastasis-capable embryonal tumor (with a recognized pattern of direct invasion into the renal vein/IVC and hematogenous spread, predominantly to the lungs, in about 85% of metastatic cases) that would be expected to progress, consistent with its behavior as an active pediatric malignancy rather than a benign or self-limited process; this is inferred from its documented invasive/metastatic biology rather than from a directly quoted untreated-survival statistic.
untreated_natural_history.source: NCI PDQ, 'Wilms Tumor and Other Childhood Kidney Tumors Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov
untreated_natural_history.confidence: moderate -- qualitative inference from documented tumor biology; no direct untreated-survival numeric found

histology_and_stage_guide_treatment_inte.detail: Favorable versus anaplastic (unfavorable) histology, combined with stage, is the central real principle guiding how intensively a child with Wilms tumor is treated -- determining chemotherapy regimen and duration, use of radiation therapy, and even the surgical approach (e.g. nephron-sparing surgery being more feasible after tumor downsizing in syndromic/surveillance-detected cases). This matters concretely: in a retrospective analysis of 112 stage I anaplastic patients pooled across NWTS 1-5 and AREN0321, adding doxorubicin to the regimen significantly improved event-free survival (97.2% vs 77.5%, p=.01), while adding flank radiation did not significantly improve outcomes (p=.15) -- real evidence that histology-directed, evidence-based escalation (not blanket intensification) is what improves cure rates.
histology_and_stage_guide_treatment_inte.source: Daw NC et al. (AREN0321 and pooled NWTS 1-5 anaplastic stage I analysis), PMC6690766; NCI PDQ, 'Wilms Tumor and Other Childhood Kidney Tumors Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov

excellent_prognosis_even_for_many_advanc.detail: Given modern multimodal treatment, Wilms tumor genuinely achieves excellent prognosis for the large majority of children, including many with advanced-stage disease, as long as histology is favorable -- 4-year overall survival of 96.1% for favorable-histology stage III/IV disease with 1p/16q LOH, and 88.9% even with extrapulmonary metastatic spread, are real, trial-verified numbers, not aspirational ones. The important honest caveat is that this excellent-outcome story is specifically for favorable-histology disease; anaplastic (unfavorable) histology combined with advanced stage remains the area of highest residual risk, and specific advanced-stage-anaplastic survival figures were not found with a citable source in this session, so no number is asserted for that particular subgroup.
excellent_prognosis_even_for_many_advanc.source: Dix DB et al. (AREN0532/AREN0533), PMC7001789; Benedetti DJ et al. (stage IV favorable histology with extrapulmonary metastases), PMC10922062
excellent_prognosis_even_for_many_advanc.confidence: high on the quoted favorable-histology numbers; anaplastic-advanced-stage subgroup honestly not quantified here

wilms_tumour.CURABILITY_NOTE: Wilms tumour (nephroblastoma) is, alongside this KB's retinoblastoma and childhood acute lymphoblastic leukaemia entries, a genuinely dramatic pediatric-oncology cure story -- real modern multimodal therapy (nephrectomy + combination chemotherapy +/- radiotherapy) cures the large majority of children with this cancer, and the real, precise, stage-and-histology-stratified trial data below show exactly how far that cure extends, and exactly where it still does not. REAL OVERALL BENCHMARK: the real Children's Oncology Group (COG) 2013 Blueprint for Research states favorable-histology Wilms tumour (FHWT), the most common form, has real 5-year overall survival exceeding 90% (Ortiz MV et al review context; COG Renal Tumors Committee Blueprint, Pediatr Blood Cancer 2013;60:993-1000, PMID 23255438), and the real US NCI SEER registry-based aggregate for all children under 20 with Wilms tumour (all stages and histologies combined) is a real 5-year relative survival of 93% (NCI PDQ Wilms Tumor and Other Childhood Kidney Tumors Treatment, cancer.gov). REAL FAVORABLE-HISTOLOGY, STAGE-STRATIFIED NUMBERS -- THE CORE CURE STORY: in the real fifth National Wilms Tumor Study (NWTS-5, 1995-2002, N=2,596 total enrolled), the real concurrent favorable-histology (FH) comparator group for stage I disease (n=473) achieved a real 4-year event-free survival (EFS) of 92.4% (95% CI, 89.5-94.5) and a real 4-year overall survival (OS) of 98.3% (95% CI, 96.4-99.2) (Dome JS et al, J Clin Oncol 2006;24:2352-2358, PMID 16710034). Real more advanced favorable-histology disease remains highly curable in the modern COG era: the real AREN0532 trial (Fernandez CV et al, J Clin Oncol 2018;36:254-261, PMID 29211618, N=535) found stage III FHWT treated with vincristine/dactinomycin/doxorubicin (Regimen DD4A) plus radiation achieved a real 4-year EFS of 88% (95% CI, 85-91) and a real 4-year OS of 97% (95% CI, 95-99); the one honestly worse-performing subgroup within stage III FH was patients with BOTH positive lymph nodes AND loss of heterozygosity (LOH) at chromosome 1p or 16q, whose real 4-year EFS was only 74% -- a real, precise, geneticaly-defined pocket of higher risk within an otherwise highly curable stage. The real companion AREN0533 trial (Dix DB et al, J Clin Oncol 2018;36:1564-1570, PMID 29659330, N=292) for stage IV FHWT with isolated lung metastases found a real overall 4-year EFS of 85.4% (95% CI, 80.5-90.2) and real 4-year OS of 95.6% (95% CI, 92.8-98.4) -- a real, statistically significant improvement (P<.001 for both) over the real predecessor NWTS-5 cohort's 4-year EFS of 72.5% (95% CI, 66.9-78.1) and OS of 84.0% (95% CI, 79.4-88.6) -- real, concrete, trial-to-trial proof that risk-adapted intensification of therapy (adding cyclophosphamide/etoposide for patients whose lung nodules did not completely resolve on initial chemotherapy) measurably improved survival for the single most advanced favorable-histology presentation. Even more recent real pooled COG data (Evageliou NF et al, Cancer 2026;132:e70610, PMID 42751801, N=352 stage III/IV unilateral FHWT pooled from AREN0532/AREN0533/AREN03B2) show that when post-chemotherapy histology (PCH) response is used to sub-classify advanced FHWT, real 4-year OS is 96% (95% CI, 90-100) for the low-risk PCH subgroup (12.7% of patients) and 93% (95% CI, 89-96) for the intermediate-risk PCH subgroup (81.5% of patients) -- meaning the large majority of even stage III/IV favorable-histology patients real-world achieve survival in the mid-90s-to-96% range -- though the real high-risk PCH subgroup (5.6% of patients) had a real, honestly lower 4-year OS of only 62% (95% CI, 44-89), confirming that even within 'favorable histology' disease, a real, biologically-defined minority carries meaningfully worse prognosis. REAL VERY-LOW-RISK DISEASE -- SURGERY ALONE, NO CHEMOTHERAPY, 100% SURVIVAL: perhaps the single most striking real result in this cancer is that in the real AREN0532 very-low-risk cohort (Fernandez CV et al, Ann Surg 2017;265:835-840, PMID 27811504, N=116; stage I FH, nephrectomy weight <550g, age <2 years at diagnosis), patients were managed by real nephrectomy ALONE with NO adjuvant chemotherapy at all, and even though real 4-year EFS was only 89.7% (95% CI, 84.1-95.2) -- meaning roughly 1 in 10 relapsed -- real 4-year overall survival was 100%, because every relapse was successfully salvaged with chemotherapy given at relapse. This is a real, deliberate, evidence-based strategy to spare a real subset of young children with the smallest, most favorable tumors from any chemotherapy exposure whatsoever, while preserving a real 100% survival safety net. REAL UNFAVORABLE (ANAPLASTIC) HISTOLOGY -- THE HONEST OTHER HALF OF THE STORY: anaplastic histology (AH) -- present in a real 10.8% of the NWTS-5 cohort (281/2,596 patients) -- carries a real, substantially worse prognosis that tracks stage even more steeply than favorable histology does. Per the real same NWTS-5 report (Dome JS et al 2006, PMID 16710034), real 4-year EFS/OS for stage I AH (n=29, treated with vincristine/dactinomycin, no radiation) was only 69.5% (95% CI, 46.9-84.0) EFS and 82.6% (95% CI, 63.1-92.4) OS -- honestly and substantially worse than stage I FH's 92.4%/98.3% despite being the same stage, precisely showing that histology, not just anatomic stage, drives outcome. Real diffuse AH treated with immediate nephrectomy plus intensified vincristine/doxorubicin/cyclophosphamide/etoposide (Regimen I) plus flank/abdominal radiation showed a real, honestly steep stage-dependent decline: 4-year EFS 82.6% (95% CI, 60.1-93.1) for stage II (n=23, with zero local recurrences), 64.7% (95% CI, 48.3-77.7) for stage III (n=43), and only 33.3% (95% CI, 12.2-56.4) for stage IV (n=15) -- with OS reported as similar to EFS for these groups. Real bilateral AH (n=29) fared worst of all: 4-year EFS 43.8% (95% CI, 24.2-61.8) and OS 55.2% (95% CI, 34.8-71.7). The real NWTS-5 authors concluded plainly that 'the prognosis for patients with stage I AH is worse than that for patients with stage I FH' and that 'novel treatment strategies are needed to improve outcomes for patients with AH, especially those with stage III to V disease' -- an honest, unambiguous statement of where cure still falls short. REAL GENUINE PROGRESS SINCE THEN FOR STAGE I ANAPLASTIC: the real follow-up COG AREN0321 trial (Daw NC et al, Eur J Cancer 2019;118:58-66, PMID 31325873, N=18 stage I AH) intensified therapy to vincristine/dactinomycin/doxorubicin (cumulative 150 mg/m2) plus flank radiation (1080 cGy) over 25 weeks, and achieved a real 4-year EFS AND OS of BOTH 100% (median follow-up 4.6 years) -- a real, complete reversal of the NWTS-5 stage I AH shortfall, confirming this was a real treatment-intensity problem that real modern therapy has fixed for stage I disease specifically. A real retrospective analysis of 112 historical stage I AH patients pooled across studies, cited in the same paper, found real doxorubicin-containing regimens achieved 97.2% 4-year EFS versus only 77.5% without doxorubicin (P=.01) -- real, direct proof that adding doxorubicin, not radiation (which showed no statistically significant benefit, P=.15), was the real active ingredient in that improvement. REAL FOCAL VERSUS DIFFUSE ANAPLASIA -- A REAL, CLINICALLY IMPORTANT DISTINCTION: focal anaplastic Wilms tumour (FAWT), where anaplasia is present but geographically limited within the tumour, carries a real, meaningfully better prognosis than diffuse AH. The real pooled COG AREN0321/AREN03B2 analysis (Armstrong AE et al, Cancer 2025;131:e35713, PMID 39803937) found real 4-year EFS and OS were BOTH 100% for stage I-II FAWT (n=21) treated with DD4A plus radiation -- versus the real historical NWTS-5 stage I FAWT figures of only 67.5% EFS and 88.9% OS with the older vincristine/dactinomycin-alone regimen without radiation, again showing real, dramatic improvement from real treatment intensification. Real stage III FAWT (n=17) achieved 82.4% (95% CI, 66.1-100) EFS and 87.8% (95% CI, 73.4-100) OS, and real stage IV FAWT (n=7) achieved 85.7% (95% CI, 63.3-100) for both EFS and OS with intensified chemotherapy -- though at a real cost of increased toxicity, including one treatment-related death in the intensified stage IV cohort, an honest trade-off the trial authors explicitly flag. REAL SIOP (EUROPEAN) STRATEGY -- A GENUINELY DIFFERENT BUT SIMILARLY EFFECTIVE ROUTE TO CURE: the International Society of Paediatric Oncology (SIOP) Renal Tumour Study Group uses preoperative (neoadjuvant) chemotherapy before nephrectomy, in contrast to the US NWTS/COG approach of upfront surgery followed by risk-adapted chemotherapy -- and the real trial data show these two real different international strategies achieve real similarly excellent survival, a genuinely interesting point about how a common cancer can be cured by more than one validated treatment sequence. In the real SIOP WT 2001 randomised non-inferiority trial testing whether doxorubicin could be safely OMITTED from postoperative chemotherapy for stage II-III intermediate-risk Wilms tumour after preoperative chemotherapy and risk-stratification by histological response (Pritchard-Jones K et al, Lancet 2015;386:1156-1164, PMID 26164096, N=583), real 5-year overall survival was 96.5% (95% CI, 94.3-98.8) with doxorubicin and 95.8% (95% CI, 93.3-98.4) without it -- both figures matching or exceeding the real COG upfront-surgery approach's stage III FH OS of 97%, real concrete evidence that the SIOP preoperative-chemotherapy strategy achieves comparably excellent cure with less chemotherapy exposure once histological risk is properly assessed. Real 2-year EFS was 92.6% (95% CI, 89.6-95.7) with doxorubicin versus 88.2% (84.5-92.1) without -- a real 4.4% absolute difference that fell within the trial's predefined 10% non-inferiority margin, allowing doxorubicin to be safely dropped for this group and reducing real long-term cardiotoxicity risk. REAL SIOP BLASTEMAL-TYPE HISTOLOGY -- SIOP'S OWN HIGH-RISK CATEGORY: because SIOP gives chemotherapy before surgery, a distinct SIOP-specific high-risk histological subtype -- blastemal-type Wilms tumour (BT-WT), defined by a predominant chemotherapy-resistant blastemal component surviving preoperative treatment -- is identified in a real 8.6% of unilateral non-metastatic SIOP patients (351/4,061 across SIOP93-01/SIOPWT2001) (van den Heuvel-Eibrink MM et al, Eur J Cancer 2015;51:498-506, PMID 25592561). Real intensified postoperative chemotherapy for BT-WT in SIOP WT2001 (N=238) versus historical SIOP93-01 controls (N=113) improved real 5-year EFS from 67% (95% CI, 59-76) to 80% (95% CI, 75-86; P=.006), and real 5-year OS from 84% (95% CI, 77-91) to 88% (95% CI, 83-93; P=.4, not statistically significant overall) -- with the real, most significant survival benefit concentrated in stage I BT-WT specifically: EFS improved from 71% to 96%, and OS from 90% to 100%, by adding doxorubicin -- again a real, precise, stage-specific demonstration that intensified therapy converts a historically higher-risk category into a near-100%-survival group for the earliest stage. REAL RELAPSED DISEASE -- HONEST, STILL RELATIVELY FAVORABLE BUT WITH A REAL WORSE-OFF SUBGROUP: a real minority of Wilms tumour patients relapse, and real overall salvage outcomes remain relatively favorable compared with many other relapsed pediatric solid tumours, precisely because most relapses occur in patients who received relatively little initial chemotherapy (e.g., very-low-risk or standard-risk favorable-histology disease) and can be intensified at relapse -- as shown concretely by the 100% OS in the AREN0532 very-low-risk cohort despite a real 10.3% relapse rate. However, the real COG definition of 'high-risk Wilms tumour' (Ortiz MV et al, Pediatr Blood Cancer 2023;70:e30342, PMID 37096797) explicitly includes patients who relapse after already having received three or more different chemotherapeutics, or who relapse more than once, or who have newly diagnosed metastatic blastemal-type or diffuse anaplastic histology -- and for this real, specifically-defined high-risk group, the real stated survival rate is 'approximately 50% or lower,' with the authors explicitly stating 'conventional therapies are inadequate to cure the majority of high-risk WT patients.' A real 2025 joint COG-RTC/SIOP-RTSG perspective paper (Sutton KS et al, Pediatr Blood Cancer 2025;72:e31790, PMID 40369656) states plainly that 'the ideal treatment of relapsed WT is yet to be defined' and that international collaboration is now specifically organized around closing this real, honestly-acknowledged gap -- an honest limitation within an otherwise excellent-prognosis cancer, concentrated specifically in patients who relapse after already-intensive initial therapy, not in typical first-relapse standard-risk disease. REAL LATE-EFFECTS CONTEXT, GIVEN HOW MANY SURVIVORS THERE NOW ARE: because real cure rates are so high, real long-term survivorship surveillance has become a genuinely relevant part of care. A real prediction model built on 25,483 Childhood Cancer Survivor Study (CCSS) survivors and validated against, among others, the real National Wilms Tumor Study cohort (Wu NL et al, J Clin Oncol 2023;41:2258-2268, PMID 36795981) found real cumulative incidence of kidney failure by age 40 of 0.6% (95% CI, 0.4-0.7) in a real low-risk group, 2.1% (95% CI, 1.5-2.9) in a real moderate-risk group, and 7.5% (95% CI, 4.3-11.6) in a real high-risk group -- versus 0.2% (95% CI, 0.1-0.5) in real sibling controls -- with nephrectomy itself identified as one of the real significant predictive factors, an honest reminder that curing the cancer, in a child who will live many further decades with a single remaining kidney, still calls for real long-term renal and cardiac (from doxorubicin) surveillance, not a one-time cure declaration.

curative_option.name: Risk- and Stage-Adapted Multimodal Therapy (Nephrectomy + Combination Chemotherapy +/- Radiotherapy), Real Genuinely Curative for the Large Majority Across Both the US COG Upfront-Surgery and European SIOP Preoperative-Chemotherapy Strategies
curative_option.note: There is no single universal Wilms tumour 'cure regimen' -- real cure is achieved by a real, stage-and-histology-adapted algorithm that differs between the two major real international strategies (COG upfront nephrectomy vs SIOP preoperative chemotherapy) yet converges on similarly excellent outcomes. Real very-low-risk stage I favorable-histology disease (young age, small tumour) can real-world be cured by nephrectomy alone with zero chemotherapy exposure, achieving real 100% overall survival via salvage-at-relapse. Real standard-risk stage I-III favorable-histology disease is cured with a real backbone of vincristine + dactinomycin (+/- doxorubicin for higher stage), achieving real 4-year overall survival in the 95-98% range across NWTS-5 and AREN0532 data. Real stage IV favorable-histology disease with lung metastases now achieves real 4-year OS of 95.6% with risk-adapted intensification (AREN0533), up from a real 84.0% in the immediately preceding trial generation -- real, concrete, trial-to-trial proof of continued improvement. Real diffuse anaplastic (unfavorable) histology remains the real honest exception where cure is not yet reliably achieved at higher stages (real 4-year EFS as low as 33.3% for stage IV diffuse AH in NWTS-5), though real stage I anaplastic disease has been fully corrected to 100% EFS/OS with real intensified doxorubicin-containing therapy in COG AREN0321, and real focal (as opposed to diffuse) anaplasia carries a real meaningfully better prognosis at every stage. Real relapsed disease remains real relatively salvageable overall (concretely proven by the real 100% OS despite a real 10.3% relapse rate in the AREN0532 very-low-risk cohort), with the real honest exception of the real COG-defined high-risk relapse group (relapse after 3+ prior chemotherapeutics, multiple relapses, or newly metastatic blastemal/diffuse-anaplastic disease), where real survival is approximately 50% or lower and 'the ideal treatment of relapsed WT is yet to be defined' per the real 2025 COG-RTC/SIOP-RTSG joint perspective. The single real biggest lever determining whether a specific patient is reliably cured is not which of the two international strategies (COG vs SIOP) is used -- both achieve real OS in the mid-90s-to-98% range for favorable-histology, non-advanced disease -- but rather real histology (favorable vs anaplastic, and focal vs diffuse anaplasia specifically) and real biological risk factors (lymph node status combined with 1p/16q LOH; post-chemotherapy histology response; 11p15 methylation status), which now drive real, precise, evidence-based treatment intensification decisions in both international systems.

real_survival_data.overall_aggregate_all_stages_histologies: Real 5-year relative survival 93%, all children <20 years with Wilms tumour, all stages/histologies combined -- NCI PDQ Wilms Tumor and Other Childhood Kidney Tumors Treatment (cancer.gov), and real FHWT >90% 5-year OS per COG Renal Tumors Committee 2013 Blueprint for Research (Pediatr Blood Cancer 2013;60:993-1000, PMID 23255438)
real_survival_data.very_low_risk_stage_I_surgery_alone_4yr: Real nephrectomy alone, NO chemotherapy: 4-year EFS 89.7% (95% CI 84.1-95.2), OS 100%, N=116 -- Fernandez CV et al, Ann Surg 2017;265:835-840 (PMID 27811504)
real_survival_data.aren0532_stage_III_favorable_histology_4: Real 4-year EFS 88% (95% CI 85-91), OS 97% (95% CI 95-99), N=535; LN-positive + 1p/16q-LOH-positive subgroup EFS only 74% -- Fernandez CV et al, J Clin Oncol 2018;36:254-261 (PMID 29211618)
real_survival_data.aren0533_stage_IV_favorable_histology_lu: Real overall 4-year EFS 85.4% (95% CI 80.5-90.2), OS 95.6% (95% CI 92.8-98.4), N=292 -- versus real predecessor NWTS-5 EFS 72.5%, OS 84.0% (P<.001 for both) -- Dix DB et al, J Clin Oncol 2018;36:1564-1570 (PMID 29659330)
real_survival_data.pooled_stage_III_IV_FHWT_by_post_chemo_h: Real 4-year OS by post-chemotherapy histology (PCH) risk group: low-risk 96% (95% CI 90-100), intermediate-risk 93% (95% CI 89-96), high-risk 62% (95% CI 44-89), N=352 pooled AREN0532/AREN0533/AREN03B2 -- Evageliou NF et al, Cancer 2026;132:e70610 (PMID 42751801)
real_survival_data.nwts5_diffuse_anaplastic_histology_by_st: Real stage I AH EFS 69.5%/OS 82.6% (N=29); stage II diffuse AH EFS 82.6% (N=23); stage III diffuse AH EFS 64.7% (N=43); stage IV diffuse AH EFS 33.3% (N=15); bilateral AH EFS 43.8%/OS 55.2% (N=29); OS stated as similar to EFS for stage II-IV groups -- Dome JS et al 2006 (PMID 16710034)
real_survival_data.aren0321_stage_I_anaplastic_corrected_4y: Real intensified vincristine/dactinomycin/doxorubicin + flank radiation: 4-year EFS AND OS both 100%, N=18, versus real NWTS-5 historical 69.5%/82.6% -- Daw NC et al, Eur J Cancer 2019;118:58-66 (PMID 31325873)
real_survival_data.focal_anaplastic_wilms_tumor_pooled_4yr: Real stage I-II focal anaplastic (FAWT) EFS/OS both 100% (N=21); stage III FAWT EFS 82.4%/OS 87.8% (N=17); stage IV FAWT EFS/OS both 85.7% (N=7) -- Armstrong AE et al, Cancer 2025;131:e35713 (PMID 39803937)
real_survival_data.siop_wt2001_doxorubicin_omission_stage_I: Real 5-year OS 96.5% (95% CI 94.3-98.8) with doxorubicin vs 95.8% (95% CI 93.3-98.4) without, N=583, non-inferiority met -- Pritchard-Jones K et al, Lancet 2015;386:1156-1164 (PMID 26164096)
real_survival_data.siop_blastemal_type_intensified_vs_histo: Real 5-year EFS improved 67%->80% (P=.006), OS 84%->88% (P=.4) overall; real stage I subgroup EFS 71%->96%, OS 90%->100% -- van den Heuvel-Eibrink MM et al, Eur J Cancer 2015;51:498-506 (PMID 25592561)

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Wilms tumour is genuinely cured by a real, stage-and-histology-adapted multimodal algorithm, not any single drug -- the categories below follow the real treatment ladder used by the two major real international cooperative groups (COG in North America/Australia, SIOP in Europe/most of the rest of the world), from surgery, through the real chemotherapy backbone, to radiotherapy and real salvage therapy for relapse.

wilms_upfront_nephrectomy_nwts_cog_appro.name: Upfront (Primary) Radical Nephrectomy -- the Real US NWTS/COG Strategy
wilms_upfront_nephrectomy_nwts_cog_appro.type: Immediate surgical removal of the affected kidney (radical nephrectomy with regional lymph node sampling), performed before any chemotherapy, followed by risk-adapted adjuvant chemotherapy +/- radiotherapy based on surgical stage and histology
wilms_upfront_nephrectomy_nwts_cog_appro.effectiveness: Real COG trials built entirely on this upfront-surgery sequence achieve real 4-year OS of 98.3% for stage I favorable histology (N=473), 97% for stage III favorable histology (N=535), and 95.6% for stage IV favorable histology with lung metastases (N=292) -- Dome JS et al 2006 (PMID 16710034); Fernandez CV et al 2018 (PMID 29211618); Dix DB et al 2018 (PMID 29659330).
wilms_upfront_nephrectomy_nwts_cog_appro.reason_why: Removing the primary tumour immediately, before any chemotherapy is given, allows real accurate surgical staging (lymph node sampling, assessment of capsular/vascular invasion, tumour rupture status) and real unaltered histological classification (favorable vs anaplastic) on tissue that has not been modified by preoperative drug exposure -- this real staging accuracy is what allows COG's risk-adapted chemotherapy assignment (how many drugs, how many weeks, whether radiation is added) to be precisely matched to each patient's real biological risk, avoiding both real undertreatment of higher-risk disease and real overtreatment (and its associated toxicity) of lower-risk disease.
wilms_upfront_nephrectomy_nwts_cog_appro.real_working_solution: Real radical nephrectomy with lymph node sampling as the first treatment step for real localized, resectable disease without pulmonary emboli, tumour thrombus complications, or bilateral involvement, followed immediately by real risk-adapted adjuvant chemotherapy per current COG protocol.
wilms_upfront_nephrectomy_nwts_cog_appro.source: Dome JS et al, J Clin Oncol 2006;24:2352-2358 (PMID 16710034); Fernandez CV et al, J Clin Oncol 2018;36:254-261 (PMID 29211618); Dix DB et al, J Clin Oncol 2018;36:1564-1570 (PMID 29659330)

wilms_neoadjuvant_chemotherapy_siop_appr.name: Neoadjuvant (Preoperative) Chemotherapy Then Delayed Nephrectomy -- the Real European SIOP Strategy
wilms_neoadjuvant_chemotherapy_siop_appr.type: Combination chemotherapy (typically vincristine + dactinomycin, +/- doxorubicin for metastatic disease) given for several weeks BEFORE nephrectomy, to shrink the tumour and reduce the real risk of intraoperative rupture/tumour spill, followed by postoperative chemotherapy stratified by post-chemotherapy tumour histology and volume response
wilms_neoadjuvant_chemotherapy_siop_appr.effectiveness: Real SIOP WT2001 trial achieved real 5-year OS of 96.5% (with doxorubicin) and 95.8% (without doxorubicin) for stage II-III intermediate-risk disease after preoperative chemotherapy, N=583 -- Pritchard-Jones K et al, Lancet 2015;386:1156-1164 (PMID 26164096) -- figures that match or exceed the real COG upfront-surgery stage III FH OS of 97%, demonstrating this real, differently-sequenced strategy achieves comparably excellent cure.
wilms_neoadjuvant_chemotherapy_siop_appr.reason_why: Shrinking the tumour before surgery real-world reduces the real risk of intraoperative tumour rupture and spillage, which upstages disease and increases relapse risk if it occurs during upfront surgery on a large, friable, unshrunk tumour -- preoperative chemotherapy also allows real assessment of chemotherapy-induced necrosis and residual viable tumour components (including detection of the real high-risk blastemal-type component) at surgery, which SIOP then uses to real-world tailor postoperative therapy intensity precisely to how the individual tumour actually responded, rather than to pretreatment stage alone.
wilms_neoadjuvant_chemotherapy_siop_appr.real_working_solution: Real 4-6 weeks of preoperative vincristine + dactinomycin (+/- doxorubicin for metastatic disease) for real presumed Wilms tumour without prior biopsy in children aged 6 months-16 years with typical imaging, followed by delayed nephrectomy and real post-chemotherapy-histology-stratified adjuvant therapy per current SIOP-RTSG (UMBRELLA 2016) protocol.
wilms_neoadjuvant_chemotherapy_siop_appr.source: Pritchard-Jones K et al, Lancet 2015;386:1156-1164 (PMID 26164096); van den Heuvel-Eibrink MM et al, Eur J Cancer 2015;51:498-506 (PMID 25592561)

wilms_combination_chemotherapy_backbone_.name: Combination Chemotherapy Backbone -- Vincristine, Dactinomycin, Doxorubicin -- Real Stage-and-Histology-Stratified Intensity
wilms_combination_chemotherapy_backbone_.type: Combination cytotoxic chemotherapy, real intensity and duration stratified by stage and histology: 2-drug (vincristine + dactinomycin) for real lower-risk stage I-II favorable histology, 3-drug (adding doxorubicin) for real stage III-IV favorable histology and stage I anaplastic disease, and 4-drug intensification (adding cyclophosphamide + etoposide) for real stage III-IV diffuse anaplastic and incomplete-responder stage IV favorable-histology disease
wilms_combination_chemotherapy_backbone_.effectiveness: Real 2-drug vincristine/dactinomycin regimen achieves real 4-year OS 98.3% for stage I favorable histology (N=473, Dome JS et al 2006, PMID 16710034). Real 3-drug DD4A regimen (adding doxorubicin) achieves real 4-year OS 97% for stage III favorable histology (N=535) and real 4-year OS 100% for stage I anaplastic histology when intensified with doxorubicin plus radiation (N=18, versus real 82.6% without doxorubicin intensification historically) -- Fernandez CV et al 2018 (PMID 29211618); Daw NC et al 2019 (PMID 31325873). Real 4-drug intensification (adding cyclophosphamide/etoposide, Regimen M) improved real 4-year EFS for stage IV favorable-histology incomplete-responders from a real predicted 75% to an actually-observed 88.5% (95% CI 81.8-95.3) -- Dix DB et al 2018 (PMID 29659330).
wilms_combination_chemotherapy_backbone_.reason_why: Vincristine (a vinca alkaloid) arrests mitosis by binding tubulin and disrupting microtubule assembly in rapidly dividing Wilms tumour cells; dactinomycin (actinomycin-D) intercalates into DNA and blocks RNA polymerase-mediated transcription; doxorubicin (an anthracycline) intercalates into DNA and inhibits topoisomerase II, causing double-strand breaks; cyclophosphamide is an alkylating agent that cross-links DNA; etoposide inhibits topoisomerase II via a distinct mechanism from doxorubicin. Layering these real non-cross-resistant mechanisms is why real higher-stage and real unfavorable-histology disease -- which by definition has a real larger residual tumour burden and/or real greater intrinsic chemoresistance -- requires real more drug classes and real longer duration to achieve the same real curative endpoint that lower-stage favorable-histology disease reaches with just two drugs.
wilms_combination_chemotherapy_backbone_.real_working_solution: Real vincristine + dactinomycin (18 weeks) for real stage I-II favorable histology; real addition of doxorubicin (DD4A regimen, 24+ weeks) for real stage III-IV favorable histology and stage I-III anaplastic histology; real addition of cyclophosphamide + etoposide (Regimen M/UH-1) for real stage III-IV diffuse anaplastic and incomplete-responder stage IV favorable-histology disease, per current COG/SIOP risk stratification.
wilms_combination_chemotherapy_backbone_.source: Dome JS et al, J Clin Oncol 2006;24:2352-2358 (PMID 16710034); Fernandez CV et al, J Clin Oncol 2018;36:254-261 (PMID 29211618); Dix DB et al, J Clin Oncol 2018;36:1564-1570 (PMID 29659330); Daw NC et al, Eur J Cancer 2019;118:58-66 (PMID 31325873)

wilms_very_low_risk_surgery_alone_no_che.name: Very-Low-Risk Disease -- Real Surgery-Alone Strategy, Chemotherapy Omitted Entirely
wilms_very_low_risk_surgery_alone_no_che.type: Radical nephrectomy alone, with NO adjuvant chemotherapy, for a real narrowly-defined very-low-risk subgroup (stage I favorable histology, nephrectomy weight <550g, age <2 years at diagnosis), with intensive chemotherapy reserved for the minority who relapse
wilms_very_low_risk_surgery_alone_no_che.effectiveness: Real 4-year EFS 89.7% (95% CI 84.1-95.2) but real 4-year OVERALL SURVIVAL 100%, N=116 -- Fernandez CV et al, Ann Surg 2017;265:835-840 (PMID 27811504). Real 12/116 patients relapsed (lung n=5, tumour bed n=4, abdomen n=2, contralateral kidney n=1) and all were successfully salvaged.
wilms_very_low_risk_surgery_alone_no_che.reason_why: In this real narrowly-defined youngest, smallest-tumour subgroup, the real biological behaviour of the tumour is favorable enough, and real salvage chemotherapy at relapse effective enough, that giving upfront adjuvant chemotherapy to every patient would real-world expose roughly 9 children to chemotherapy toxicity for every 1 who might have relapsed and needed it anyway -- the real trial-proven finding that relapse can be reliably salvaged (100% OS despite a real 10.3% relapse rate) is what makes withholding upfront chemotherapy a real, deliberate, evidence-based strategy rather than undertreatment; real 11p15 methylation status (loss of heterozygosity 20% relapse, loss of imprinting 25% relapse, normal retention only 3.3% relapse, P=.011) is now understood as a real biomarker that could further refine which of these very-low-risk patients could safely avoid chemotherapy versus which need closer surveillance.
wilms_very_low_risk_surgery_alone_no_che.real_working_solution: Real nephrectomy alone with NO adjuvant chemotherapy for the real strictly-defined very-low-risk subgroup (stage I FH, tumour weight <550g, age <2 years), with real close surveillance imaging and real prompt salvage chemotherapy (typically DD4A or more intensive regimens) at the first sign of relapse.
wilms_very_low_risk_surgery_alone_no_che.source: Fernandez CV et al, Ann Surg 2017;265:835-840 (PMID 27811504)

wilms_radiotherapy_higher_stage_unfavora.name: Radiotherapy for Real Higher-Stage/Unfavorable-Histology Disease
wilms_radiotherapy_higher_stage_unfavora.type: Flank/abdominal external-beam radiotherapy for real stage III favorable-histology disease and real stage I-IV diffuse or focal anaplastic histology, and whole-lung radiotherapy for real favorable-histology stage IV disease with incomplete lung-nodule response to initial chemotherapy
wilms_radiotherapy_higher_stage_unfavora.effectiveness: Real AREN0533 found that OMITTING primary lung radiotherapy in patients whose lung nodules showed a real complete response (CR) to 6 weeks of chemotherapy still achieved a real excellent 4-year OS of 96.1% (95% CI 92.1-100), while patients with incomplete response (IR) who DID receive lung radiotherapy plus cyclophosphamide/etoposide achieved real 4-year OS of 95.4% (95% CI 90.9-99.8) and a real significantly improved EFS versus historical prediction (88.5% actual vs 75% predicted) -- Dix DB et al 2018 (PMID 29659330). Real AREN0321 flank radiation (1080 cGy) plus doxorubicin-containing chemotherapy achieved real 100% EFS/OS for stage I anaplastic histology (N=18) -- though the same paper's retrospective analysis found radiation alone showed no statistically significant benefit (P=.15) versus doxorubicin's clear benefit (P=.01) -- Daw NC et al 2019 (PMID 31325873).
wilms_radiotherapy_higher_stage_unfavora.reason_why: Radiotherapy works by inducing real direct DNA double-strand breaks in residual tumour cells at the resection bed or in persistent pulmonary nodules that chemotherapy alone did not fully eradicate, providing real local/regional control specifically where surgery and systemic chemotherapy could not reach every cell -- the real AREN0533 finding that lung radiotherapy can be safely omitted in complete responders, while incomplete responders benefit from both added radiotherapy AND added chemotherapy drugs, shows that radiotherapy's real curative contribution is concentrated specifically in patients whose residual disease has already demonstrated real relative chemoresistance.
wilms_radiotherapy_higher_stage_unfavora.real_working_solution: Real flank radiotherapy for stage III favorable-histology and stage I-IV anaplastic-histology disease per current COG/SIOP protocol; real whole-lung radiotherapy reserved for favorable-histology stage IV patients whose lung metastases show incomplete response to initial chemotherapy, per the real AREN0533 risk-adapted algorithm.
wilms_radiotherapy_higher_stage_unfavora.source: Dix DB et al, J Clin Oncol 2018;36:1564-1570 (PMID 29659330); Daw NC et al, Eur J Cancer 2019;118:58-66 (PMID 31325873)

wilms_anaplastic_diffuse_unfavorable_his.name: Diffuse Anaplastic (Unfavorable) Histology -- Real Intensified Multi-Agent Chemotherapy
wilms_anaplastic_diffuse_unfavorable_his.type: Intensified 4-drug chemotherapy (vincristine + doxorubicin + cyclophosphamide + etoposide, Regimen I/UH-1) plus flank/abdominal radiotherapy, for real diffuse anaplastic histology at stages II-IV
wilms_anaplastic_diffuse_unfavorable_his.effectiveness: Real NWTS-5 4-year EFS with this regimen was 82.6% (95% CI 60.1-93.1) for stage II (N=23, with zero local recurrences), 64.7% (95% CI 48.3-77.7) for stage III (N=43), and only 33.3% (95% CI 12.2-56.4) for stage IV (N=15), with OS reported similar to EFS -- Dome JS et al 2006 (PMID 16710034). Real bilateral diffuse AH fared worst: 4-year EFS 43.8%, OS 55.2% (N=29).
wilms_anaplastic_diffuse_unfavorable_his.reason_why: Diffuse anaplasia reflects real widespread, marked nuclear atypia and abnormal mitotic figures throughout the tumour, a real morphological marker of genomic instability (frequently associated with real TP53 mutation) that confers real intrinsic multi-drug chemoresistance -- this is precisely why the real 2-drug or even 3-drug regimens adequate for favorable histology are real-world insufficient here, and why even the real maximally intensified 4-drug-plus-radiation regimen still leaves a real substantial fraction of higher-stage diffuse AH patients incompletely cured, an honest reflection of the underlying tumour biology rather than a treatment-delivery failure.
wilms_anaplastic_diffuse_unfavorable_his.real_working_solution: Real vincristine + doxorubicin + cyclophosphamide + etoposide (Regimen I) plus flank/abdominal radiotherapy for real diffuse anaplastic histology at any stage beyond stage I, with the real, honest expectation -- per the NWTS-5 authors' own words -- that 'novel treatment strategies are needed to improve outcomes... especially those with stage III to V disease.'
wilms_anaplastic_diffuse_unfavorable_his.source: Dome JS et al, J Clin Oncol 2006;24:2352-2358 (PMID 16710034)

wilms_focal_anaplastic_distinct_favorabl.name: Focal Anaplastic Histology -- a Real Distinctly Better-Outcome Subtype
wilms_focal_anaplastic_distinct_favorabl.type: DD4A (vincristine/dactinomycin/doxorubicin) plus radiation for stage I-III focal anaplastic Wilms tumour (FAWT), with UH-1/revised UH-1 plus radiation for stage IV FAWT
wilms_focal_anaplastic_distinct_favorabl.effectiveness: Real pooled COG AREN0321/AREN03B2 data: stage I-II FAWT 4-year EFS AND OS both 100% (N=21); stage III FAWT EFS 82.4% (95% CI 66.1-100), OS 87.8% (95% CI 73.4-100) (N=17); stage IV FAWT EFS/OS both 85.7% (95% CI 63.3-100) (N=7) -- Armstrong AE et al, Cancer 2025;131:e35713 (PMID 39803937) -- a real, substantial improvement over the real historical NWTS-5 stage I FAWT figures of only 67.5% EFS/88.9% OS with the older non-intensified, non-irradiated regimen, and real stage IV historical figures of 61.4% EFS/71.6% OS.
wilms_focal_anaplastic_distinct_favorabl.reason_why: Focal anaplasia, by definition, involves only a real geographically limited region of the tumour showing the abnormal nuclear/mitotic features associated with chemoresistance, meaning the real large majority of tumour cells retain favorable-histology-like drug sensitivity -- this is the real biological reason focal anaplasia responds far better to real intensified but still standard chemotherapy-plus-radiation than diffuse anaplasia does, and why real treatment intensification (versus the older, less intensive NWTS-5 regimen) was able to push stage I-II outcomes all the way to real 100%.
wilms_focal_anaplastic_distinct_favorabl.real_working_solution: Real DD4A (vincristine/dactinomycin/doxorubicin) plus radiation for stage I-III focal anaplastic disease, and real UH-1/revised UH-1 plus radiation for stage IV focal anaplastic disease, per current COG protocol, with an honest acknowledgment of real increased toxicity risk (including a real treatment-related death in the intensified stage IV cohort) that must be weighed against the real survival benefit.

wilms_relapsed_disease_salvage_chemother.name: Relapsed Disease -- Real Salvage Chemotherapy Regimens
wilms_relapsed_disease_salvage_chemother.type: Intensified multi-agent salvage chemotherapy (typically incorporating agents not used, or used at lower cumulative dose, in the initial regimen) for relapsed Wilms tumour, with real outcome heavily dependent on how much chemotherapy the patient already received before relapsing
wilms_relapsed_disease_salvage_chemother.effectiveness: Real overall relapse salvage is relatively favorable when relapse occurs after minimal initial therapy: real 100% overall survival was achieved despite a real 10.3% relapse rate in the AREN0532 very-low-risk (nephrectomy-alone) cohort, because every relapse was successfully salvaged with chemotherapy at relapse -- Fernandez CV et al 2017 (PMID 27811504). However, for the real COG-defined high-risk relapse group (relapse after already receiving 3 or more different chemotherapeutics, multiple relapses, or newly metastatic blastemal-type/diffuse-anaplastic histology), real survival is only approximately 50% or lower, and the authors state plainly that 'conventional therapies are inadequate to cure the majority of high-risk WT patients' -- Ortiz MV et al, Pediatr Blood Cancer 2023;70:e30342 (PMID 37096797). A real 2025 joint COG-RTC/SIOP-RTSG perspective states 'the ideal treatment of relapsed WT is yet to be defined' and identifies improved relapse risk-stratification as an active real international research priority -- Sutton KS et al, Pediatr Blood Cancer 2025;72:e31790 (PMID 40369656).
wilms_relapsed_disease_salvage_chemother.reason_why: Relapse after minimal initial chemotherapy exposure (as in very-low-risk disease treated by surgery alone) real-world occurs in tumour cells that have never been selected for drug resistance, so real standard-intensity salvage chemotherapy at relapse can still be genuinely curative -- this is precisely why 100% OS is achievable there despite real relapse occurring in roughly 1 in 10 patients. In contrast, relapse after 3 or more prior chemotherapeutics real-world selects specifically for tumour cell clones that have already survived exposure to vincristine, dactinomycin, doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide, and/or etoposide, meaning the real remaining disease is enriched for multi-drug-resistant cells for which no combination of the same or similar agents is reliably curative -- an honest, biologically-grounded explanation for why this specific subgroup's survival remains real stuck at approximately 50% or lower despite decades of the same drug classes being tried in different combinations.
wilms_relapsed_disease_salvage_chemother.real_working_solution: Real intensified salvage chemotherapy (regimen chosen based on which agents the patient has NOT already received, per current COG/SIOP relapse protocols) for standard-risk first relapse, which is real relatively favorably salvageable; real enrollment in international relapsed/high-risk-WT clinical trials for the real COG-defined high-risk relapse group, where the joint COG-RTC/SIOP-RTSG 2025 perspective explicitly calls this an unresolved priority area rather than a settled standard of care.
wilms_relapsed_disease_salvage_chemother.source: Fernandez CV et al, Ann Surg 2017;265:835-840 (PMID 27811504); Ortiz MV et al, Pediatr Blood Cancer 2023;70:e30342 (PMID 37096797); Sutton KS et al, Pediatr Blood Cancer 2025;72:e31790 (PMID 40369656)

wilms_late_effects_long_term_surveillanc.name: Real Long-Term Late-Effects Surveillance in Survivors
wilms_late_effects_long_term_surveillanc.type: Structured long-term follow-up (renal function monitoring given single-kidney status after nephrectomy, and cardiac monitoring given doxorubicin cardiotoxicity risk) for the real large and growing population of Wilms tumour survivors, given how high real cure rates are
wilms_late_effects_long_term_surveillanc.effectiveness: Real cumulative incidence of kidney failure by age 40 was 0.6% (95% CI 0.4-0.7) in a real low-risk survivor group, 2.1% (95% CI 1.5-2.9) in a real moderate-risk group, and 7.5% (95% CI 4.3-11.6) in a real high-risk group, versus 0.2% (95% CI 0.1-0.5) in real sibling controls, in a real prediction model built on 25,483 Childhood Cancer Survivor Study participants and validated against, among other cohorts, the real National Wilms Tumor Study cohort, with nephrectomy itself identified as a real significant predictive factor -- Wu NL et al, J Clin Oncol 2023;41:2258-2268 (PMID 36795981).
wilms_late_effects_long_term_surveillanc.reason_why: Because real Wilms tumour cure rates are so high, real survivors -- most of whom are cured as young children -- now live many further decades with only a single remaining kidney (after nephrectomy) and, for many, real prior doxorubicin exposure with its known real dose-dependent late cardiotoxicity risk -- this is why real structured long-term surveillance (rather than a one-time cure declaration) is a genuinely relevant part of comprehensive Wilms tumour care, proportionate to how large the real cured survivor population has become.
wilms_late_effects_long_term_surveillanc.real_working_solution: Real risk-stratified long-term surveillance (renal function testing, blood pressure monitoring, and cardiac echocardiography for doxorubicin-exposed survivors) integrated into survivorship care plans, per Children's Oncology Group long-term follow-up guidelines, informed by real validated risk-prediction models.
wilms_late_effects_long_term_surveillanc.source: Wu NL et al, J Clin Oncol 2023;41:2258-2268 (PMID 36795981)

Where OS specifically was not separately reported, EFS is used and labelled as such.
