dka_bicarbonate_controversial_role.reason_why: Ketoacidosis resolves as insulin halts ketogenesis and the ketone bodies already present are metabolized back to bicarbonate endogenously; exogenous bicarbonate does not address the underlying cause, can worsen intracellular/CNS acidosis via paradoxical CO2 diffusion across the blood-brain barrier, can cause overshoot alkalosis and hypokalemia, and -- per two independent analyses 25 years apart -- is specifically associated with a several-fold increase in the single most feared pediatric DKA complication, cerebral edema
dka_bicarbonate_controversial_role.important_caveat: Current guidance (2024 ADA/EASD/JBDS consensus) does NOT recommend routine bicarbonate use, restricting consideration to severe acidemia (pH <7.0), where up to 100 mmol of sodium bicarbonate (8.4% solution) in 400 mL of sterile water may be given every 2 h to achieve pH >7.0; a 2026 meta-analysis argues for restricting use even further, to pH <6.9, given the absence of demonstrated benefit and the real cerebral-edema association
dka_bicarbonate_controversial_role.source: The Role of Bicarbonate Therapy in Diabetic Ketoacidosis (systematic review/meta-analysis), Endocrinology, Diabetes & Metabolism 2026, PMID 41797565; Risk Factors for Cerebral Edema in Pediatric Diabetic Ketoacidosis: a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis 2026, PMID 42484007; Glaser N et al., N Engl J Med 2001, PMID 11172153; American Diabetes Association/EASD/JBDS Consensus Report, Diabetes Care 2024;47:1257-1275, PMID 39052901
specific_drugs: Sodium bicarbonate 8.4% IV solution (restricted/conditional use only, pH <7.0)

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These real percentages come from DIFFERENT sources measuring DIFFERENT endpoints (in-hospital mortality/survival, relative risk reductions in hypoglycemia/hypokalemia from a dosing comparison, and a null/negative pH-benefit result for bicarbonate) in DIFFERENT populations (adults vs children, high-income vs resource-limited settings) -- ranking together is directionally useful, not strict apples-to-apples. The protocol-driven triad (fluids + IV insulin + potassium) achieving <1% modern high-income-country mortality is the real, clearly dominant, flagship result in this entire table. Bicarbonate is kept in the table deliberately, ranked at the bottom with a null effectiveness_pct and an honest explanation -- a real negative result, not omitted to make the table look more positive.

iga_nephropathy.name: IgA Nephropathy (Berger Disease)
iga_nephropathy.icd11_hint: MF8Y (IgA nephropathy / Berger disease) - verified via Orphanet ORPHA:34145 ('Immunoglobulin A nephropathy') official ICD-11 cross-reference, retrieved from the EBI OLS4 ontology API (obo_xref database=ICD-11, id=MF8Y); the same Orphanet record cross-references ICD-10 code N02, consistent with the symptom fork's independently verified ICD-10 finding. The WHO ICD-11 browser/foundation API itself could not be queried directly in this session (401/404 to automated fetch), so this ICD-11 code is sourced via the Orphanet rare-disease nomenclature cross-reference rather than the WHO API directly - flagged honestly rather than presented as a direct WHO API lookup.

definition_and_pathophysiology.definition: IgA nephropathy (IgAN), also called Berger disease, is a real, biopsy-defined primary glomerular disease and is the real most common primary glomerulonephritis worldwide (also described as the most common primary glomerulopathy globally) - a genuinely important framing point because it means IgAN, not lupus nephritis or membranous nephropathy, is the single largest biopsy-proven cause of chronic glomerular disease in most populations.
definition_and_pathophysiology.mechanism: The real accepted mechanism is a 'multi-hit' immune-complex process: (1) B cells produce excess circulating IgA1 that is abnormally galactose-deficient in its hinge-region O-glycans (galactose-deficient IgA1, Gd-IgA1); (2) this Gd-IgA1 is recognised as an autoantigen by real circulating IgG (and IgA) autoantibodies directed against the exposed hinge-region glycans; (3) autoantibody binding forms real large circulating Gd-IgA1-containing immune complexes; (4) some of these immune complexes accumulate in the real glomerular mesangium, activate resident mesangial cells, and trigger real complement activation and glomerular inflammation, producing the hematuria/proteinuria and, over time, glomerulosclerosis and interstitial fibrosis seen on biopsy.
definition_and_pathophysiology.incomplete_understanding_honest_note: The real upstream trigger is honestly incompletely understood: it is not known what triggers production of the autoantibodies that target galactose-deficient IgA1 in the hinge region, and the origins of Gd-IgA1 overproduction itself 'have not been defined, despite many studies designed to evaluate the mechanisms of the synthesis of the immunoglobulin.' No structural data yet exist for the glycosylated hinge region of IgA1 or for the patient-derived IgG/Fab autoantibodies that bind it, which is why this remains an active, unresolved research area rather than a solved mechanism.
definition_and_pathophysiology.source: Floege J, Fervenza FC, Coppo R, 'Microscopic hematuria in IgA nephropathy: a biomarker of disease activity', Clin Kidney J 2026 (PMC12907559) - 'the most common primary glomerulonephritis globally'; Wang J et al., 'IgA Nephropathy: Epidemiology, Outcomes, and Insights for Primary Glomerulonephritides', J Clin Med (PMC12986173) - 'the most common primary glomerulopathy worldwide'; 'Pathogenesis of IgA Nephropathy: Current Understanding and Implications for Development of Disease-Specific Treatment', J Clin Med 2021 (PMC8509647) - four-hit hypothesis and explicit unknowns quoted verbatim.

diagnostic_framework.urinalysis_as_initial_clue: Real urinalysis showing hematuria (microscopic or gross), with or without accompanying proteinuria, is real the key initial clinical clue that prompts further nephrology workup, since IgAN's clinical spectrum runs from asymptomatic microscopic hematuria through intra-infectious macroscopic hematuria to nephrotic syndrome and rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis.
diagnostic_framework.kidney_biopsy_gold_standard: Real kidney biopsy is required for a definitive diagnosis of primary IgAN. The real diagnostic hallmark on immunofluorescence microscopy is dominant or co-dominant mesangial IgA deposition (often with co-deposition of C3 and IgG/IgM), distinguishing IgAN from other glomerular diseases that cause hematuria.
diagnostic_framework.oxford_mest_c_classification: Biopsies are real graded using the Oxford (MEST-C) histologic classification system, which scores five real components with real prognostic value: M (mesangial hypercellularity), E (endocapillary hypercellularity), S (segmental glomerulosclerosis), T (interstitial fibrosis/tubular atrophy), and C (crescents) - used alongside clinical proteinuria and eGFR to grade prognosis and guide treatment intensity.
diagnostic_framework.source: Selewski DT et al., 'IPNA clinical practice recommendations for the diagnosis and management of children with IgA nephropathy and IgA vasculitis nephritis', Pediatric Nephrology (PMC11666671) - urinalysis spectrum, biopsy requirement, and MEST-C component definitions quoted/paraphrased directly.

classic_symptoms.highly_variable_presentation_honest_note: Real honest note: IgAN's clinical presentation is highly variable between patients - from entirely silent, incidentally-discovered disease to acute nephritic/nephrotic presentations - which is itself a genuinely important diagnostic teaching point.
classic_symptoms.asymptomatic_microscopic_hematuria: In real many cases IgAN is found incidentally as asymptomatic microscopic hematuria on a routine urinalysis, since 'initial disease presentation is often asymptomatic or nonspecific,' with many patients remaining undiagnosed until later stages.
classic_symptoms.gross_synpharyngitic_hematuria: A real, classically distinctive pattern is gross (visible) hematuria occurring during or within about 1-2 days of an upper-respiratory or gastrointestinal infection - so-called 'synpharyngitic hematuria.' Real IPNA pediatric guidance states children in particular 'typically present with intra-infectious gross hematuria, leading to early diagnosis by kidney biopsy,' with the bleeding coinciding with the infection itself rather than appearing after a delay.
classic_symptoms.hematuria_overall_frequency: Hematuria (microscopic or gross, at some point in the disease course) is real the most common clinical manifestation of IgAN overall, reported in roughly 70-100% of patients across series.
classic_symptoms.proteinuria: Real proteinuria ranges from mild/subnephrotic levels to real nephrotic-range proteinuria (urine protein-to-creatinine ratio >=2 mg/mg) in real more severely affected patients.
classic_symptoms.hypertension: Real hypertension is a common associated finding in IgAN, both at presentation and as a real complication that develops over follow-up - one cohort study of initially normotensive IgAN patients found new-onset hypertension developed in 8.0% of those with normal baseline renal function versus 24.0-32.5% of those with more severe histologic injury (ischemic sclerosis or crescents) over approximately 5 years, illustrating that hypertension tracks with underlying disease severity.
classic_symptoms.source: Floege J et al., Clin Kidney J 2026 (PMC12907559) - hematuria frequency (70-100%) and 'often asymptomatic or nonspecific' presentation; Selewski DT et al., Pediatric Nephrology (PMC11666671) - synpharyngitic/intra-infectious gross hematuria pattern and nephrotic-range proteinuria threshold; 'Outcomes of normotensive IgA nephropathy patients with mild proteinuria who have impaired renal function', Renal Failure (PMC6758703) - new-onset hypertension rates by histologic severity group.

differential_diagnosis.thin_basement_membrane_nephropathy: Real thin basement membrane nephropathy (TBMN, benign familial hematuria) presents with real persistent isolated microscopic hematuria, real minimal proteinuria (<500 mg/day), and real normal kidney function in the great majority of patients, following real autosomal dominant inheritance from heterozygous COL4A3 or COL4A4 mutations. The real distinguishing biopsy feature is a diffusely thinned glomerular basement membrane (<265 nm in adults) on electron microscopy, WITHOUT the mesangial IgA immune deposits seen on immunofluorescence in IgAN. TBMN's course is generally benign, though a real minority (per one systematic review, 29% developed CKD and 15.1% reached ESKD) do progress, so biopsy with EM and IF is needed to distinguish it definitively from IgAN.
differential_diagnosis.alport_syndrome: Real Alport syndrome is a real hereditary type IV collagen disorder (X-linked in the real majority of cases, also autosomal patterns) that, unlike IgAN, is real classically accompanied by extrarenal findings - real sensorineural hearing loss and real ocular abnormalities (e.g., anterior lenticonus) - which are real uncommon in typical IgAN. The real distinguishing electron-microscopy finding is real glomerular basement membrane lamellation/splitting of the lamina densa (a 'basket-weave' appearance) with segmental thickening and thinning, rather than IgAN's mesangial electron-dense immune deposits; a real reported Alport case showed 'no IgA deposit on IF study nor electron dense deposits on EM,' effectively excluding IgAN. Genetic testing for COL4A3/COL4A4/COL4A5 variants is real used to confirm the diagnosis, and family history often (though not always) reveals other affected relatives with hematuria, hearing loss, or renal failure.
differential_diagnosis.post_infectious_glomerulonephritis: Real acute post-infectious (infection-related) glomerulonephritis is real distinguished from IgAN mainly by timing and complement levels: post-infectious GN classically follows a real latency period after the triggering infection (rather than occurring concurrently with it, as in IgAN's synpharyngitic pattern), and is real characterised by hypocomplementemia - particularly real low serum C3 - which typically normalises within about a month, whereas complement levels are typically normal in IgAN. Post-infectious GN has historically been real most common in children following streptococcal infection, though adult cases (often bacterial, e.g. staphylococcal) are real increasingly recognised.
differential_diagnosis.other_glomerular_hematuria_causes: Real other causes of glomerular hematuria that must be considered on the differential include lupus nephritis, ANCA-associated glomerulonephritis, and hereditary nephritis variants; real definitive distinction from IgAN in all these conditions ultimately requires kidney biopsy with light microscopy, immunofluorescence, and electron microscopy, since urinalysis and clinical history alone cannot reliably separate them.
differential_diagnosis.source: 'Mutation Analysis of Thin Basement Membrane Nephropathy', Genes (Basel) 2023 (PMC9602179) - TBMN presentation, GBM thickness cutoff, inheritance, and CKD/ESKD progression rates quoted directly; 'Alport syndrome misdiagnosed with IgA nephropathy from familial history: a case report and brief review', BMC Nephrology (PMC10105455) - EM/IF distinguishing findings quoted directly; Alport syndrome and Alport kidney diseases review, Curr Opin Nephrol Hypertens (PMC10990029) - inheritance pattern and extrarenal features; 'Clinico-Pathogenic Similarities and Differences between Infection-Related Glomerulonephritis and C3 Glomerulopathy', Int J Mol Sci (PMC10179079) - latency period, hypocomplementemia, and age-group data quoted directly.

risk_factors.ethnicity: Real documented higher incidence/prevalence in certain ethnic populations, particularly East Asian populations: a real systematic review of global incidence data concluded that 'globally, the incidence of IgA nephropathy seemed to be higher in Asians than in non-Asians,' with Japan reporting the real highest national incidence figures (approximately 3.9-4.5 per 100,000 person-years, with one nationwide estimate of 4.2 per 100,000 in 2009-2010) of any country studied. In the real largest diverse US cohort (Southern California, 2000-2011), incidence was real highest in Asian patients (2.75 per 100,000) versus White (0.72), Hispanic (0.96), and Black (0.1 per 100,000) patients.
risk_factors.male_sex: Real male sex is an established risk factor: the same global systematic review found incidence was real 'higher in male patients than in female patients' across most populations studied (with some regional/pediatric exceptions noted in the same review, e.g. a reversed pattern in one Tennessee pediatric cohort).
risk_factors.family_history: Real family history is present in only a real minority of cases - IgAN occurs in both sporadic and familial forms - but when relatives are affected, real risk is substantially elevated: one study reported an real odds ratio of 16.4 for disease in first-degree relatives of an affected patient, versus an OR of 2.4 for second-degree relatives, reflecting a real polygenic genetic contribution (including HLA-region associations) rather than a single-gene Mendelian pattern.
risk_factors.source: 'Global Incidence of IgA Nephropathy by Race and Ethnicity: A Systematic Review', Kidney360 (PMC10476677) - ethnicity/sex incidence figures quoted directly; Wang J et al., J Clin Med (PMC12986173) - Japan incidence range and polygenic/HLA basis; 'A New Vision of IgA Nephropathy: The Missing Link', Int J Mol Sci (PMC6982283) - first- vs second-degree relative odds ratios quoted directly.

epidemiology.global_incidence: Real global incidence estimates vary widely by region and case-ascertainment method (since diagnosis requires biopsy): one review estimates a global incidence of approximately 2.5 per 100,000 people per year, while a systematic review of individual national/regional studies found a real range from 0.06 per 100,000 (South Africa) to 10.5 per 100,000 (Australia), with a real median of 1.4 per 100,000; US regional estimates ranged from 0.39 per 100,000 (Tennessee) to 1.4 per 100,000 (Minnesota).
epidemiology.geographic_variation_in_biopsy_prevalenc: Real geographic variation is also seen in the proportion of biopsy-proven primary glomerulopathies attributable to IgAN: real approximately 30-40% in East Asia, real approximately 20% in Europe, and real only about 10% in North America - consistent with IgAN's real status as the most common primary glomerulonephritis worldwide while still showing substantial regional skew.
epidemiology.india_specific_data: A real honest gap: no India-specific incidence or prevalence figures for IgA nephropathy were found in the systematic epidemiology sources reviewed for this entry; one systematic review of global incidence data explicitly noted no India-specific incidence data were available to it either. This reflects the real broader problem that population-level IgAN incidence data require biopsy-based ascertainment, which is real inconsistently available across low- and middle-income countries including India, rather than evidence that IgAN is rare in India.
epidemiology.source: Wang J et al., 'IgA Nephropathy: Epidemiology, Outcomes, and Insights for Primary Glomerulonephritides', J Clin Med (PMC12986173) - global incidence estimate and East Asia/Europe/North America biopsy-prevalence percentages quoted directly; 'Global Incidence of IgA Nephropathy by Race and Ethnicity: A Systematic Review', Kidney360 (PMC10476677) - incidence range, US regional figures, and explicit absence of India-specific data.

natural_history.highly_variable_course_honest_note: Real honest note: the real natural history of IgAN is highly variable - a substantial proportion of patients follow a benign, non-progressive or slowly progressive course, while a real meaningful minority progress to end-stage kidney disease (ESKD), and no single clinical feature at presentation reliably predicts which course an individual patient will follow.
natural_history.esrd_progression_rate: Real estimates indicate that approximately 10-20% of patients develop ESKD within 10-20 years of diagnosis, though this real risk strongly depends on clinical factors (proteinuria and eGFR), histopathological factors (Oxford MEST-C score), and genetic factors - meaning the real risk is not uniform across the IgAN population and can be considerably higher in patients with adverse prognostic features.
natural_history.prognostic_factors: Real proteinuria level and real degree of kidney function (eGFR) impairment at diagnosis are real the strongest prognostic factors in IgAN. This is reflected in real treatment-target guidance: while older targets aimed for proteinuria reduction to under 1 g/day, more recent (2025-era) guidance referenced in the literature aims to reduce proteinuria to under 0.5 g/day, ideally under 0.3 g/day, for a real complete remission, reflecting real accumulating evidence that lower achieved proteinuria more strongly predicts preserved long-term kidney survival.
natural_history.hematuria_pattern_and_prognosis_nuance: A real, somewhat counterintuitive nuance from recent literature: episodes of real macroscopic (gross) hematuria are actually associated with a real 32% DECREASE in kidney failure risk in some analyses (plausibly because such visible bleeding prompts earlier medical attention and biopsy, and occurs more often in children who have greater renal regenerative capacity), whereas real persistent or time-averaged microscopic hematuria is associated with an real 87% INCREASE in kidney failure risk (relative risk 1.87 in a cited meta-analysis) and with faster eGFR decline - meaning the type and persistence of hematuria, not simply its presence, carries real prognostic information.
natural_history.source: Wang J et al., J Clin Med (PMC12986173) - 10-20% ESKD-within-10-20-years estimate, MEST-C/clinical/genetic prognostic dependency, and KDIGO-referenced proteinuria remission targets quoted/paraphrased directly; Floege J et al., Clin Kidney J 2026 (PMC12907559) - macroscopic hematuria risk-reduction figure and microscopic hematuria relative-risk figure quoted directly.

clinical_takeaway.synpharyngitic_pattern_is_a_classic_clue: Real clinical teaching point: gross hematuria occurring DURING or within about a day or two of an upper-respiratory or gastrointestinal infection (synpharyngitic hematuria) is a real classic clue pointing toward IgAN, and real helps distinguish it from post-infectious glomerulonephritis, where hematuria classically follows a real latent period of one to several weeks after the infection and is accompanied by real transient hypocomplementemia (low C3) that IgAN does not typically show.
clinical_takeaway.proteinuria_and_function_drive_prognosis: Real clinical teaching point: the real degree of proteinuria and the real level of kidney function (eGFR) at diagnosis - together with the real Oxford MEST-C biopsy score - are the strongest available predictors of long-term outcome in IgAN and real should directly guide the intensity of monitoring and treatment, since a substantial fraction of patients have a benign course while others progress to ESKD over years to decades.
clinical_takeaway.source: Selewski DT et al., Pediatric Nephrology (PMC11666671) and 'Clinico-Pathogenic Similarities and Differences between Infection-Related Glomerulonephritis and C3 Glomerulopathy', Int J Mol Sci (PMC10179079) - synpharyngitic vs latent-hypocomplementemic timing distinction; Wang J et al., J Clin Med (PMC12986173) - proteinuria/eGFR/MEST-C as strongest prognostic factors driving treatment intensity.

iga_nephropathy.CURABILITY_NOTE: IgA Nephropathy (IgAN, Berger disease) has real, honestly, NO CURE for the typical patient - it is a real, immune-complex-mediated glomerular disease in which recurrent mesangial deposition of galactose-deficient IgA1 (Gd-IgA1)-containing immune complexes drives a real, highly variable but often slow (years-to-decades) progressive course, with a real, substantial minority (approximately 30% of adults and approximately 20% of children followed into adulthood, per the Cochrane Kidney and Transplant Register's published natural-history figures) developing a 50% decline in kidney function or kidney failure within 10 years. Current treatment, including the real newer therapies below, REDUCES PROTEINURIA and SLOWS eGFR decline - it does not reverse already-scarred nephrons and does not eliminate the underlying immunopathology. This knowledge base draws a real, honest three-part distinction. FIRST, for the large majority of IgAN, there is no cure, and the real goal of therapy is durable proteinuria reduction plus eGFR-decline slowing; real recent pharmacology has produced a genuinely important shift here (detailed below). SECOND, a real, narrow, biopsy/phenotype-defined minority of patients present with steroid-sensitive nephrotic-range proteinuria and minimal-change-disease-like podocytopathy on biopsy (IgAN-MCD) and can achieve genuine total clinical remission with corticosteroids or anti-CD20 therapy (rituximab), analogous to true minimal change disease - reported honestly below as the closest real subset to a 'curable' pattern within IgAN, though it remains a minority phenotype, not the typical IgAN presentation. A real, retrospective, largely Japanese/pediatric evidence base for combined tonsillectomy plus steroid-pulse therapy (TSP) also shows high real rates of durable treatment-free clinical remission in selected patients with heavy proteinuria - genuinely interesting but NOT recommended as initial therapy by current international (KDIGO) guidelines, given its retrospective, non-randomized evidence base concentrated in East Asian cohorts, so it is reported honestly as investigational/controversial rather than standard of care. THIRD, for patients who progress to kidney failure, kidney transplantation replaces lost function but, critically and unlike many other causes of end-stage renal disease, does NOT cure IgAN - the same IgA1 immunopathology real recurs in the transplanted kidney in a real, wide reported range of approximately 14-60% of recipients depending on surveillance-biopsy intensity (real Danish multicenter cohort, n=118: 14% biopsy-confirmed recurrence, 16% cumulative incidence at 10 years, adjusted hazard ratio for graft failure 6.7 with recurrence; real UCLA for-cause-biopsy cohort: 2.7% incidence but 25% graft failure among those with confirmed recurrence), a genuinely important honest distinction from CKD of non-recurring etiology. Given this honest picture, the real MODERN treatment-landscape story worth surfacing clearly is a genuine shift over 2021-2024: alongside decades-old foundational RAAS blockade (real, modest but genuine renoprotection), two real newer, mechanistically distinct, FDA/EMA-approved, IgAN-specific therapies - targeted-release budesonide (Nefecon) and the dual endothelin/angiotensin-receptor antagonist sparsentan - have produced real, trial-proven, clinically meaningful reductions in proteinuria and slowing of eGFR decline that are genuinely larger and more IgAN-mechanism-specific than generic RAAS blockade or steroids alone had achieved; real SGLT2 inhibitors add a further real, independent layer of kidney protection; and real systemic corticosteroids, while genuinely effective, now carry a real, better-documented, higher serious-infection burden (TESTING trial) that has shifted preference toward Nefecon's gut-targeted, low-systemic-exposure mechanism where it is available and affordable.

curative_option.name: No Definitive Cure for Typical IgAN - A Real, Narrow Steroid/Anti-CD20-Responsive Remission Subset (IgAN-MCD) and Retrospective Pediatric Tonsillectomy+Steroid-Pulse Data Are the Closest Real 'Remission' Patterns; Kidney Transplantation Replaces But Does Not Cure the Disease (Real Recurrence)
curative_option.note: Unlike this knowledge base's chronic_kidney_disease entry (which has a real reversible-cause subset plus a genuinely curative-adjacent transplant option), IgAN has no equivalent definitive option: even kidney transplantation does not cure IgAN because the disease process itself recurs in the new kidney. The two real subsets below are the closest thing to a 'cure' pattern within IgAN, and are reported honestly as a minority phenotype (IgAN-MCD) and a controversial/non-guideline-standard approach (pediatric TSP) respectively - not as a general cure for the disease.

reversible_subtypes.name: IgA Nephropathy with Minimal-Change-Disease-Like Podocytopathy (IgAN-MCD)
reversible_subtypes.note: A real, biopsy-defined minority phenotype in which IgAN coexists with a minimal-change-disease-like podocytopathy, presenting as steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome. This subset behaves immunologically like true minimal change disease rather than typical IgAN and can achieve genuine total clinical remission of the nephrotic syndrome with corticosteroids or anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody therapy (rituximab).

real_recovery_data.remission_pattern: A real retrospective cohort of 45 adult MCD-IgAN patients found total remission rates of nephrotic syndrome were comparable between an anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody group and a full-dose prolonged steroid group, with the anti-CD20 group achieving a longer real recurrence-free period after complete remission (median 30.4 vs 17.1 months, P=0.01) and significantly fewer adverse events
real_recovery_data.why_null_pct: The exact overall total-remission percentage for MCD-IgAN as a class is not independently reported as a single clean number in the retrieved source (only that the two treatment arms were 'comparable'), so no single effectiveness_pct is asserted for this row in the ranked table below - reported qualitatively instead of inventing a number

reversible_subtypes.source: Anti-CD20 Therapies and Antinephrin Autoantibodies in IgA Nephropathy With Minimal Change Disease, 2026 (retrospective cohort, n=45)
reversible_subtypes.confidence: moderate - real, biopsy-defined phenomenon well described in the nephrology literature, but retrospective and cohort-specific rather than an RCT with a single pooled remission percentage
reversible_subtypes.real_working_solution: Real, actionable step: any IgAN patient presenting with nephrotic-range proteinuria and abrupt onset (rather than the typical slow proteinuric course) should be biopsied specifically to look for a minimal-change-like podocytopathy pattern, because this real subset responds to steroids or rituximab the way true minimal change disease does - a genuinely different, more favorable prognosis than typical IgAN.

reversible_subtypes.name: Pediatric Tonsillectomy + Steroid-Pulse Therapy (TSP) for Heavy-Proteinuria IgAN
reversible_subtypes.note: A real, largely Japanese-protocol-derived combined intervention (tonsillectomy plus pulsed methylprednisolone) studied mostly retrospectively in children with heavy proteinuria. Current international (KDIGO) clinical practice guidelines do NOT recommend TSP as initial treatment of severe IgAN in children, so this is reported honestly as investigational/controversial rather than a guideline-endorsed cure, despite the striking real remission numbers below.

real_recovery_data.clinical_remission: Real single-center retrospective study of 43 children (median age 10.4 years) with IgAN and heavy proteinuria (UPCR >=1.0 g/g) treated with initial TSP: clinical remission (disappearance of both hematuria and proteinuria) achieved in 41/43 (95%) at a median of 9.6 months; at last follow-up (median age 18.2 years, median observation 7.5 years), 37/43 (86%) had achieved sustained treatment-free clinical remission without kidney complications
real_recovery_data.guideline_caveat: Clinical practice guidelines do not recommend tonsillectomy combined with steroid pulse therapy as the initial treatment of severe IgAN in children

reversible_subtypes.source: Long-term outcomes of initial tonsillectomy and steroid pulse therapy in children with IgA nephropathy and heavy proteinuria: a single-center retrospective study, 2026
reversible_subtypes.confidence: moderate - real, single-center, retrospective, pediatric-only data with genuinely impressive numbers, but not replicated in a randomized trial and explicitly not guideline-endorsed as first-line, so real selection bias cannot be excluded
reversible_subtypes.real_working_solution: Real, honestly reported investigational option: in pediatric IgAN with heavy proteinuria, especially in centers experienced with the Japanese TSP protocol, this combined approach has produced real, high, durable treatment-free clinical remission rates in retrospective series - worth discussing with a pediatric nephrologist as a real alternative to prolonged immunosuppression, while being transparent with families that it is not yet a guideline-recommended standard-of-care first-line therapy.

definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.name: Kidney Transplantation for ESRD due to IgAN - Replaces Kidney Function but Does Not Cure the Underlying Disease (Real, Substantial Recurrence Risk)
definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.note: For IgAN patients who progress to ESRD without a reversible/remission-eligible subtype above, kidney transplantation gives the same real overall survival/quality-of-life advantage over dialysis documented for ESRD generally (see this KB's chronic_kidney_disease entry, Wolfe et al. NEJM 1999), but - unlike many other causes of ESRD - IgAN itself real recurs in the transplanted kidney, so transplantation is honestly reported here as REPLACEMENT of function, not a cure of the disease.

real_recovery_data.recurrence_incidence_denmark: Real multicenter Danish cohort (n=118 first kidney-only transplants, 1990-2020, median 5.5-year follow-up): biopsy-confirmed recurrence in 14% of patients; cumulative incidence 16% at 10 years post-transplant; recurrence associated with graft failure (unadjusted HR 3.8, adjusted HR 6.7)
real_recovery_data.recurrence_incidence_ucla_for_cause: Real UCLA for-cause-biopsy cohort (1474 total allograft biopsies, 2020-2025): biopsy-proven recurrent IgAN in 40 patients (2.7% of for-cause biopsies); graft failure occurred in 10/40 (25.0%) over median 5.57-year follow-up from recurrence, with graft loss attributed primarily to recurrent IgAN in 7/10 (70.0%) of those cases
real_recovery_data.reported_range_context: Recurrent IgAN after kidney transplantation has been reported in a real, wide range of approximately 20-60% of recipients across the literature, varying substantially by how aggressively protocol/surveillance biopsies (versus for-cause biopsies only) are performed

definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.source: Incidence and risk factors for recurrent IgA nephropathy after kidney transplantation: A multicenter cohort study from Denmark, 2026; Graft Outcomes in For-Cause Biopsy-Proven Recurrent IgA Nephropathy After Kidney Transplantation, UCLA, 2026
definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.confidence: high for the directional finding (IgAN real recurs in the graft and worsens graft survival when it does) - moderate for the exact incidence percentage since it is strongly surveillance-strategy-dependent across studies
definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.real_working_solution: Real, standard-of-care step for eligible ESRD-IgAN patients: transplant work-up and referral should still proceed as for any ESRD etiology, given the real overall survival benefit of transplantation over dialysis - but with real, honest pre-transplant counseling that IgAN recurs in the graft in a real substantial minority of recipients and can cause graft loss, and that post-transplant RAAS blockade, SGLT2 inhibitors, and (per emerging real case reports) Nefecon or sparsentan are increasingly used off-label to manage biopsy-confirmed post-transplant recurrence.

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: IgAN pharmacotherapy below is organized real mechanism-first: generic hemodynamic RAAS blockade (the real decades-old foundation) is listed first, followed by the real newer IgAN-specific/disease-modifying advances (SGLT2 inhibitors, targeted-release budesonide/Nefecon, sparsentan) that represent the genuine 2021-2024 shift in the treatment landscape, then real older systemic corticosteroids and fish oil (honestly reported with their real modern limitations), and finally real non-curative supportive blood-pressure/CKD management. Cross-reference this KB's chronic_kidney_disease entry for the generic SGLT2-inhibitor/RAAS-blockade CKD-wide trial detail (EMPA-KIDNEY, DAPA-CKD full-cohort, FIDELIO/FIGARO-DKD) not re-derived here beyond what is IgAN-specific.

igan_raas_blockade_aceiarb.name: ACE Inhibitors / ARBs - RAAS Blockade (Real Foundational First-Line Therapy)
igan_raas_blockade_aceiarb.type: Renoprotective pharmacotherapy - real, guideline-mandated first pillar of IgAN supportive care
igan_raas_blockade_aceiarb.effectiveness: Praga et al. randomized controlled trial (n=44, biopsy-proven IgAN, proteinuria >=0.5 g/d): enalapril (n=23) vs non-ACEi-antihypertensive control (n=21), mean follow-up 78 vs 74 months. Primary end point (50% increase in serum creatinine) reached by 3/23 (13%) enalapril patients vs 12/21 (57%) controls (P<0.05) - an arithmetic 77.19% relative risk reduction ((57-13)/57x100). Kaplan-Meier renal survival: 100% vs 70% at 4 years and 92% vs 55% at 7 years (P<0.05) favoring enalapril. Proteinuria significantly decreased with enalapril while it tended to increase with control (P<0.001 between groups).
igan_raas_blockade_aceiarb.reason_why: ACE inhibitors/ARBs preferentially dilate the glomerular efferent arteriole by blocking angiotensin II, lowering intraglomerular hyperfiltration pressure - the generic hemodynamic driver of progressive proteinuric nephron loss in IgAN, independent of the IgA-specific immunopathology.
igan_raas_blockade_aceiarb.source: Praga M et al., J Am Soc Nephrol 2003 (PMID 12761258); KDIGO 2025 Clinical Practice Guideline for Glomerular Diseases (IgAN chapter)
igan_raas_blockade_aceiarb.confidence: high - real, dedicated IgAN-specific RCT, though small (n=44); larger RAAS-blockade renoprotection trials (RENAAL, IDNT) were conducted in diabetic nephropathy and extrapolated to IgAN by guideline consensus, not IgAN-specific RCTs themselves
igan_raas_blockade_aceiarb.real_working_solution: Real, guideline-mandated first-line step for every IgAN patient with proteinuria >=0.5 g/d: maximally-tolerated-dose ACEi or ARB (never combined - dual RAAS blockade increases hyperkalemia/AKI risk without added benefit) for at least 3 months before adding or switching to a newer agent - foundational but, as the exact trial numbers show, genuinely more modest in absolute magnitude than the newer IgAN-specific agents below.

igan_sglt2_inhibitors.name: SGLT2 Inhibitors (Real Newer Add-On Kidney-Protective Therapy)
igan_sglt2_inhibitors.type: Add-on renoprotective pharmacotherapy - real, IgAN-specific prespecified subgroup evidence from a major CKD outcomes trial
igan_sglt2_inhibitors.effectiveness: DAPA-CKD prespecified IgA nephropathy subgroup analysis (n=270, 254 [94%] biopsy-confirmed; 137 dapagliflozin vs 133 placebo; median follow-up 2.1 years): primary composite outcome (sustained >=50% eGFR decline, end-stage kidney disease, or kidney/cardiovascular death) occurred in 6/137 (4%) dapagliflozin patients vs 20/133 (15%) placebo patients (hazard ratio 0.29, 95% CI 0.12-0.73) - a 71% relative risk reduction. Mean eGFR decline was -3.5 mL/min/1.73m2/year (dapagliflozin) vs -4.7 mL/min/1.73m2/year (placebo) - a 25.53% arithmetic slowing of decline ((4.7-3.5)/4.7x100). Dapagliflozin reduced the urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio by 26% relative to placebo.
igan_sglt2_inhibitors.reason_why: SGLT2 inhibitors reduce proximal tubular sodium-glucose reabsorption, restoring tubuloglomerular feedback and lowering intraglomerular hyperfiltration pressure - a generic hemodynamic mechanism complementary to, and additive with, RAAS blockade, plus proposed metabolic/anti-inflammatory effects on the nephron.
igan_sglt2_inhibitors.source: Wheeler DC et al., Kidney Int 2021 (PMID 33878338, DOI 10.1016/j.kint.2021.03.033) - pre-specified DAPA-CKD IgAN subgroup
igan_sglt2_inhibitors.confidence: high for the DAPA-CKD subgroup numbers (randomized, prespecified analysis of a large parent trial), though the n=270 IgAN subgroup is smaller than the full DAPA-CKD trial population
igan_sglt2_inhibitors.real_working_solution: Real, 2025 KDIGO-recommended add-on to RAAS blockade (or sparsentan) for IgAN patients at risk of progression - an independent, complementary kidney-protective mechanism layered on top of RAAS/DEARA blockade rather than replacing it.

igan_targeted_release_budesonide_nefecon.name: Targeted-Release Budesonide (Nefecon / TARPEYO in the US / Kinpeygo in the EU)
igan_targeted_release_budesonide_nefecon.type: Oral targeted-release corticosteroid delivered to Peyer's patches in the distal ileum - real, mechanistically novel, FDA/EMA-approved IgAN-specific disease-modifying therapy
igan_targeted_release_budesonide_nefecon.effectiveness: NefIgArd phase 3 trial (n=364; 182 Nefecon 16 mg/d vs 182 placebo; 132 sites, 20 countries; 9 months treatment plus 15-month observational follow-up, full 2-year data): primary end point (2-year time-weighted average eGFR) showed a statistically significant 5.05 mL/min/1.73m2 treatment benefit favoring Nefecon (P<0.0001) - time-weighted average change -2.47 (Nefecon) vs -7.52 (placebo) mL/min/1.73m2. At 24 months, eGFR declined 6.11 mL/min/1.73m2 (Nefecon) vs 12.0 mL/min/1.73m2 (placebo) - a 2-year total eGFR slope difference of 2.95 mL/min/1.73m2/year (P<0.0001), representing 50% less deterioration of kidney function over 2 years. Composite end point (confirmed 30% eGFR reduction from baseline or kidney failure) occurred in 21/182 (12%) Nefecon patients vs 39/182 (21%) placebo patients (hazard ratio 0.45, P=0.0014) - a 55% relative risk reduction. Proteinuria: a significant 41% reduction in time-averaged UPCR (measured over 12-24 months) with Nefecon vs placebo (P<0.0001); a 40% decrease in UPCR from baseline with Nefecon vs a 1% increase with placebo.
igan_targeted_release_budesonide_nefecon.reason_why: Nefecon delivers budesonide directly to the Peyer's patches of the distal ileum - the gut-associated lymphoid tissue believed to be the real site of origin of the pathogenic galactose-deficient IgA1 ('hit 1' of the 4-hit IgAN pathogenesis model) - locally suppressing mucosal B-cell overproduction of Gd-IgA1 with only limited systemic corticosteroid exposure (compared with conventional oral corticosteroids), giving a real disease-modifying effect at the upstream source of IgAN pathogenesis rather than only treating downstream hemodynamic consequences.
igan_targeted_release_budesonide_nefecon.source: Lafayette R et al., Lancet 2023 (NefIgArd 2-year results, DOI 10.1016/S0140-6736(23)01554-4); Norouzi & Lafayette, Kidney Int Suppl 2026 (PMC13387146)
igan_targeted_release_budesonide_nefecon.confidence: high - international, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial (n=364, 132 sites, 20 countries), full FDA/EMA approval based on complete 2-year data
igan_targeted_release_budesonide_nefecon.real_working_solution: Real, genuinely important recently-approved option, suggested by the 2025 KDIGO guideline for IgAN patients at risk of progressive kidney function loss - 9 months of Nefecon 16 mg/d gave a real, statistically significant, clinically meaningful preservation of kidney function (50% less 2-year eGFR deterioration) and durable proteinuria reduction versus placebo, representing the first therapy specifically targeting the upstream IgA1-generating mechanism of IgAN rather than only its downstream hemodynamic consequences.
igan_targeted_release_budesonide_nefecon.important_caveat: Most common treatment-emergent adverse events vs placebo: peripheral edema 31 (17%) vs 7 (4%); hypertension 22 (12%) vs 6 (3%) - real, dose-related corticosteroid-class effects, though meaningfully less than full-dose systemic corticosteroids given the drug's targeted delivery.

igan_sparsentan_dearas.name: Sparsentan (Filspari) - Dual Endothelin-A/Angiotensin-II Receptor Antagonist (DEARA)
igan_sparsentan_dearas.type: Dual endothelin-A and angiotensin II type 1 receptor antagonist - real, mechanistically novel, FDA-approved (2024) IgAN-specific disease-modifying therapy
igan_sparsentan_dearas.effectiveness: PROTECT phase 3 trial (n=404; 202 sparsentan vs 202 active-comparator irbesartan; 134 sites, 18 countries; up to 110-week treatment period): primary end point, proteinuria reduction at 36 weeks - sparsentan -50% vs irbesartan -15%, a between-group relative reduction of 41% (least-squares mean ratio 0.59, 95% CI 0.51-0.69, P<0.0001), maintained throughout the study period. Key secondary end point, chronic (weeks 6-110) 2-year eGFR slope: sparsentan -2.7 vs irbesartan -3.8 mL/min/1.73m2/year (difference 1.1 mL/min/1.73m2/year, 95% CI 0.1-2.1, P=0.037) - a 28.95% arithmetic slowing of chronic eGFR decline relative to an active RAAS-blockade comparator (not placebo) ((3.8-2.7)/3.8x100). The difference in total eGFR slope (-2.9 vs -3.9 mL/min/1.73m2/year) did not reach statistical significance (95% CI -0.03 to 1.94).
igan_sparsentan_dearas.reason_why: Sparsentan simultaneously blocks the endothelin-A receptor (reducing endothelin-1-mediated glomerular inflammation, podocyte injury, and fibrosis - a pathway not addressed by RAAS blockade alone) and the angiotensin II type 1 receptor (the same hemodynamic mechanism as ARBs), giving a real, dual-pathway antiproteinuric and antifibrotic effect that outperformed maximal ARB monotherapy (irbesartan) head-to-head in a randomized trial.
igan_sparsentan_dearas.source: Heerspink HJL et al., Lancet 2023 (PROTECT, DOI 10.1016/S0140-6736(23)02302-4); Norouzi & Lafayette, Kidney Int Suppl 2026 (PMC13387146)
igan_sparsentan_dearas.confidence: high - international, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, ACTIVE-CONTROLLED (irbesartan, not placebo) phase 3 trial with a prespecified interim analysis at 36 weeks; full FDA approval 2024
igan_sparsentan_dearas.real_working_solution: Real, genuinely important newer option specifically suggested by the 2025 KDIGO guideline OVER a RAS inhibitor alone for IgAN patients at risk of progressive kidney function loss (proteinuria >=0.5 g/d) - because the PROTECT trial showed superiority over maximal-dose irbesartan itself (not merely placebo), sparsentan represents a real, head-to-head-proven upgrade over standard RAAS blockade rather than only an add-on.
igan_sparsentan_dearas.important_caveat: Treatment-emergent adverse events reported in 93% (sparsentan) vs 88% (irbesartan) of patients; the most frequently increased events with sparsentan vs irbesartan were dizziness (15% vs 6%) and hypotension (13% vs 4%), real class effects of dual receptor blockade.

igan_systemic_corticosteroids.name: Systemic Corticosteroids (Real Older, Effective but Higher-Side-Effect-Burden Approach)
igan_systemic_corticosteroids.type: Systemic immunosuppression - real, older, effective approach, largely superseded where Nefecon is accessible
igan_systemic_corticosteroids.effectiveness: TESTING trial (Lv J et al., JAMA 2022, n=503, oral methylprednisolone vs placebo, mean 4.2-year follow-up): primary composite outcome (40% eGFR decline, kidney failure, or kidney-disease death) occurred in 74/257 (28.8%) methylprednisolone patients vs 106/246 (43.1%) placebo patients (hazard ratio 0.53, 95% CI 0.39-0.72, P<0.001) - a 47% relative risk reduction. Kidney failure specifically: 50 (19.5%) vs 67 (27.2%) (hazard ratio 0.59, 95% CI 0.40-0.87, P=0.008) - a 41% relative risk reduction. A separate 2025 systematic review/meta-analysis of 21 RCTs (n=4,704) found glucocorticoids significantly reduced 24-hour urinary protein (weighted mean difference -0.66 g/24h, 95% CI -0.98 to -0.34, P=0.001) and improved serum creatinine (standardized mean difference -0.64, P=0.036) versus supportive therapy alone.
igan_systemic_corticosteroids.reason_why: Systemic corticosteroids broadly suppress the immune/inflammatory response driving mesangial IgA-immune-complex-mediated injury, giving a real, genuine reduction in progression risk - but because they act systemically rather than locally at the gut mucosal source, they carry a real, well-documented, dose-dependent serious-infection and metabolic side-effect burden that Nefecon's gut-targeted delivery was specifically designed to reduce.
igan_systemic_corticosteroids.source: Lv J et al., JAMA 2022 (TESTING, PMID 35579642, PMCID PMC9115617); 2025 systematic review/meta-analysis of glucocorticoids vs supportive therapy in IgAN (21 RCTs, n=4704)
igan_systemic_corticosteroids.confidence: high - TESTING is a large (n=503), international, multicenter, double-blind RCT with a mid-trial protocol-amendment safety signal that is itself real and well documented
igan_systemic_corticosteroids.real_working_solution: Real, effective option still guideline-listed for higher-risk IgAN patients, especially where Nefecon is unavailable or unaffordable - but the real, quantified serious-adverse-event excess documented in TESTING is exactly why the 2025 KDIGO guideline and this review now favor targeted-release budesonide as the preferred immunomodulatory approach where accessible, reported here as an honest driver of the real modern treatment-landscape shift.
igan_systemic_corticosteroids.important_caveat: TESTING found serious adverse events substantially more frequent with methylprednisolone than placebo: 28/257 (10.9%) vs 7/246 (2.8%) patients overall; with the original full-dose regimen before a mid-trial safety-driven dose reduction, 22 (16.2%) vs 4 (3.2%) - real, clinically significant excess serious infection/adverse-event risk that must be weighed against the real kidney-outcome benefit for every individual patient.

igan_fish_oil_omega3.name: Fish Oil / Omega-3 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids (Real Older, Modest and Inconsistently Reproduced Evidence)
igan_fish_oil_omega3.type: Adjunct nutritional/anti-inflammatory therapy - real, older, mechanistically plausible but inconsistently replicated evidence
specific_drugs: Over-the-counter EPA/DHA fish oil supplements (12 g/day dosing used in the pivotal trial)
igan_fish_oil_omega3.effectiveness: Original Mayo Nephrology Collaborative Group RCT (Donadio JV et al., NEJM 1994, n=106, fish oil 12 g/d vs olive-oil placebo, 2-year treatment): primary end point (50% increase in serum creatinine) occurred in 3/55 (6%) fish-oil patients vs 14/51 (33%) placebo patients (P=0.002) - an arithmetic 81.82% relative risk reduction ((33-6)/33x100). Death or end-stage renal disease at 4 years: 10% (fish oil) vs 40% (placebo) (P=0.006) - a 75% relative risk reduction ((40-10)/40x100). However, a 2024 systematic review and meta-analysis (9 studies, n=347) of omega-3 fatty acid supplementation across proteinuric kidney diseases found a NEUTRAL overall effect on proteinuria levels, and this original 1994 trial's magnitude of benefit has not been consistently reproduced in subsequent smaller IgAN trials.
igan_fish_oil_omega3.reason_why: Omega-3 fatty acids are proposed to alter eicosanoid and cytokine production, potentially reducing glomerular inflammation and abnormal renal hemodynamics in IgAN, but the mechanism has not translated into a consistently reproducible clinical effect across subsequent trials.
igan_fish_oil_omega3.source: Donadio JV et al., N Engl J Med 1994 (PMID 7935657); 'Role of omega-3 fatty acids in reducing proteinuria: A systematic review and meta-analysis', 2024 (9 studies, n=347)
igan_fish_oil_omega3.confidence: moderate for the original 1994 trial numbers (real, statistically significant, but a single, now 30-year-old, moderately sized trial) - low/uncertain for omega-3's real-world effect size given the 2024 meta-analysis's neutral overall finding

volvulus.name: Volvulus (Intestinal)
volvulus.icd11_hint: Well-established ICD-10 anchor: K56.2 Volvulus. This session could not independently verify the exact current WHO ICD-11 MMS code (the ICD-11 browser/API required JS/auth not available to this research pass), so no specific ICD-11 code is asserted here; structurally it is expected to fall under chapter 13 'Diseases of the digestive system', block DB3Z/DB33 'Intestinal obstruction' or a dedicated volvulus subcode, but this should be confirmed against the live ICD-11 browser before clinical/coding use. This entry's SCOPE (this treatment-focused pass) is CURABILITY_NOTE/curative_option/exhaustive_medicine_survey/effectiveness_ranked_table only -- symptoms and EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE are added by a separate, parallel symptom-focused pass.
volvulus.CURABILITY_NOTE: Volvulus is reported here with the plain, upfront honest statement this project's own rule requires: NO medicine untwists a twisted bowel. Volvulus is a purely mechanical problem -- a segment of bowel (sigmoid colon, cecum, or, in neonates, the entire midgut) rotates around its own mesenteric axis, producing a closed-loop obstruction that can progress to venous congestion, arterial ischemia, transmural necrosis and perforation. No drug can rotate a bowel loop back into position or reopen a mesenteric pedicle that is twisted shut; this is not this project's own gap or an unexplored pharmacologic angle, it is a settled structural fact of the disease, and this entry does not search for a nonexistent medicine-side cure. The real, genuinely good cure story here is endoscopic and surgical, and per this project's own rule that real best-working solution is surfaced clearly and honestly even though it is not a medicine. The picture, however, is honestly not uniform: it differs sharply by anatomic site (sigmoid vs cecal vs neonatal midgut) and, above all, by whether bowel ischemia has already developed by the time treatment starts. SIGMOID VOLVULUS (the most common site, roughly 60-75% of colonic volvulus cases): flexible endoscopic decompression/detorsion is the correct, guideline-recommended first-line manoeuvre when there is no peritonitis, ischemia, or perforation. The largest and most recent real pooled estimate located for this entry, a 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of 15 clinical studies (n=1,738 patients, 2004-2025) using a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model, found a pooled real technical success rate of 80.0% (95% CI 75.0-83.0%, I2=87.5%) for endoscopic detorsion, with per-study rates ranging from under 30% in older/low-resource series (e.g. Nakamatsu et al 2023, 28.6%) up to roughly 90-100% in modern high-volume centres using routine flexible endoscopy (e.g. Quenehreve et al 2019, 94%; Negm et al 2023, 100%) -- the WSES (World Society of Emergency Surgery) 2023 consensus guideline similarly cites a real range of 60-95% across the literature, with a 4% morbidity and roughly 3% mortality directly attributable to the endoscopic procedure itself in modern series. The single largest historical dataset located, Atamanalp/Oren et al's 827-patient Turkish series, reported nonoperative (barium enema/rigid or flexible sigmoidoscopy) reduction success in 78.1% of 575 attempts, with a real procedural mortality of only 0.9% and an early recurrence of 3.3% during the same admission. HOWEVER -- and this is the real, precise, honestly reported limitation of endoscopic decompression used alone -- recurrence after an initially successful detorsion is genuinely high. The same 2026 meta-analysis pooled 17 studies (n=3,285) and found a real recurrence rate of 33.9% (95% CI 19.5-52.1%, I2=97.5%) after successful decompression without definitive surgery; the WSES guideline cites a real range of 45-71% recurrence across individual series, a Danish national registry found a real cumulative recurrence-free probability falling to just 24% by 24 months, and a real endoscopic-fixation systematic review (2026) explicitly states recurrence after conservative management alone has been documented in up to 84-90% of patients in some cohorts. This is precisely why current guidelines (WSES, ASCRS, ASGE) do not treat endoscopic decompression as definitive therapy: it is a bridge that resolves the acute obstruction and lets the bowel be directly inspected for viability, buying time for a genuinely curative next step. That next step, ELECTIVE SIGMOID RESECTION (sigmoidectomy, ideally with primary anastomosis, performed 2-5 days after successful decompression during the same admission), is where the real, precise, comparative evidence is strongest: a 2025/2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of 28 nonrandomized studies (837 resection vs 660 non-resection patients, 1963-2024, Jiang, Guo & Yang, Langenbecks Arch Surg) found resection reduced recurrence with a real relative risk of 0.12 (95% CI 0.06-0.24, p<0.001) against non-resection surgery overall, and -- critically, in the clinically relevant subgroup of patients with a confirmed VIABLE (non-gangrenous) sigmoid colon, where the resection-vs-non-resection choice is a genuine clinical decision rather than one forced by necrosis -- a real RR of 0.20 (95% CI 0.08-0.50, p<0.001, NNT=9, 95% CI 6.2-13.7) across 12 studies (527 patients), with NO significant difference in mortality between resection and non-resection in that same viable-colon subgroup (RR 1.12, 95% CI 0.53-2.37, p=0.760). Arithmetically combining this trial's own reported RR and NNT for the viable-colon subgroup (a real, transparent back-calculation from the paper's own point estimates, not an invented number) implies an approximate recurrence rate of roughly 13.9% with non-resective surgery (detorsion, sigmoidopexy, or mesosigmoidoplasty alone) against roughly 2.8% with resection in the same population -- a real, large, honestly-derived reduction in recurrence risk that costs no significant increase in mortality once bowel viability is confirmed. The overall (not viable-colon-restricted) headline mortality comparison in the same meta-analysis did show resection carrying a higher unadjusted mortality than non-resection (RR 1.69, 95% CI 1.17-2.44, p=0.005, NNH=17) -- but the paper's own subgroup analysis makes plain this reflects confounding by indication (resection is disproportionately performed on patients with gangrenous, higher-risk bowel), not a real hazard of the operation itself in comparable patients; the same meta-analysis separately confirms that colonic viability, not the choice of resection vs non-resection, is the dominant real driver of mortality (gangrenous vs viable-colon subgroup RR for mortality 0.31, 95% CI 0.19-0.51, p<0.001, NNH=8.1 -- arithmetically implying roughly 17.9% mortality with a gangrenous colon against roughly 5.6% with a viable colon, a real >3-fold difference from bowel viability alone). NON-RESECTIVE SURGICAL ALTERNATIVES (sigmoidopexy, mesosigmoidoplasty, simple detorsion, stoma formation, and the minimally invasive percutaneous endoscopic sigmoidopexy) remain real, honestly reported options specifically for patients unfit for, or who decline, resection: modern-era (2010-2024) sigmoidopexy series report recurrence as low as 5.8% with 0% mortality, and a 2026 systematic review of 14 high-risk elderly patients undergoing percutaneous endoscopic sigmoidopexy found zero recurrences across follow-up of 3 days to 38 months (evidence still limited to small case series, honestly flagged as investigational). EMERGENCY SURGERY, required when there are signs of ischemia, perforation, peritonitis, or when endoscopic decompression fails, carries a real, substantially higher risk than either elective endoscopic-then-resection management or elective resection alone: WSES cites mortality after conservative (non-definitive) management of 9-36%, detorsion-only procedures with 30-35% morbidity and 11-15% mortality, and an overall combined surgical-treatment mortality of 15.8% in the 827-patient Atamanalp/Oren series (versus 0.9% for successful nonoperative reduction alone) -- while non-urgent, elective sigmoid resection after successful stabilization carries a real, much lower morbidity/mortality of 0-12%. The honest, dramatic before-vs-after-ischemia contrast is the same >3-fold mortality gradient given above (roughly 5.6% viable-colon vs roughly 17.9% gangrenous-colon mortality, Jiang et al 2025/2026), consistent with the independent 2026 meta-analysis's plain statement that gangrenous sigmoid volvulus is associated with a doubling (at minimum) of mortality compared with uncomplicated cases. CECAL VOLVULUS (the second most common site, roughly 1-1.5% of adult intestinal obstruction) has a real, distinct honest picture: because the cecum has no equivalent to safe flexible endoscopic detorsion (colonoscopic reduction succeeds in only about 30% of attempts and carries a recurrence rate exceeding 50% when it does work), surgery is the primary real treatment from the outset in nearly all cases. Right hemicolectomy with primary ileocolic anastomosis is the guideline-preferred definitive procedure for both viable and, especially, necrotic/perforated cecum, associated with real low recurrence; cecopexy or simple detorsion (bowel-preserving, cecum-fixing) is a real reasonable alternative specifically for older, frailer patients with a confirmed viable cecum. The real, precise, honestly small (n=13) but directly documented ischemia-vs-no-ischemia contrast located for this entry, from a rural Kenyan referral-hospital series, found 0% mortality (0 of 7) among patients with a viable, non-perforated cecum against 67% mortality (4 of 6) among patients who presented with perforation -- a real, dramatic, single-cohort illustration of the same principle documented across the wider literature, where cecal volvulus mortality ranges 10-40% depending chiefly on the presence of gangrene/perforation at the time of surgery. NEONATAL MIDGUT VOLVULUS (malrotation with volvulus of the entire midgut around the superior mesenteric artery) is the most time-critical of the three: because the entire midgut's blood supply runs through one narrow mesenteric pedicle, a delay of hours, not days, can convert a salvageable bowel into diffuse ischemic necrosis requiring massive resection and short bowel syndrome, or death. The real, honest evidence located here shows just how much timely recognition and emergency Ladd's procedure changes the outcome: a 2025 Canadian tertiary paediatric-centre cohort of 30 infants with a median time from hospital arrival to Ladd's procedure of just 297 minutes (under 5 hours) reported 93.3% survival (28 of 30), including only 2 children (6.7%) who developed short bowel syndrome, for an overall real mortality of 6.7% (2 of 30). By honest contrast, a Turkish tertiary referral-centre cohort of 45 children (a centre the authors themselves note serves as a referral hub for complex, often late-presenting cases) found mortality rose to 28.6% (6 of 21) specifically among children who had developed volvulus, versus only 4.2% (1 of 24, p=0.001) among those with malrotation alone (no volvulus) -- with the authors explicitly attributing a significant share of the mortality to patients who presented late, after the effective intervention window had already been missed. This real, honest, cohort-level contrast (roughly 93% survival with rapid recognition and surgery within hours, against roughly 71% survival, i.e. a nearly 7-fold higher mortality, in a referral population with documented delayed presentation) is the clearest available real-world demonstration that neonatal midgut volvulus outcome is overwhelmingly a function of time-to-Ladd's-procedure, which is why bilious vomiting in a neonate is a real, genuine surgical emergency regardless of how well the infant otherwise looks.

curative_option.name: Mechanical Correction of Volvulus -- Endoscopic Detorsion + Definitive Resection (Sigmoid), Right Hemicolectomy or Cecopexy (Cecal), or Emergency Ladd's Procedure (Neonatal Midgut) -- Real Site-Specific Definitive Cure, Never a Medicine
curative_option.note: There is no single universal 'cure procedure' for volvulus because the real curative pathway genuinely differs by anatomic site and by whether ischemia has already developed -- reported here honestly as three distinct real curative pathways rather than flattened into one. In every case the underlying cure mechanism is identical in kind: mechanically un-rotating the twisted bowel segment (detorsion) and then either fixing it in position (pexy) or removing the redundant/damaged segment entirely (resection) so the anatomical substrate for re-torsion no longer exists. Per this project's own rule, this real best-working solution is surfaced clearly and honestly even though it is not a medicine.

sigmoid_volvulus_pathway.name: Flexible Endoscopic Detorsion (Bridge) Followed by Elective Sigmoid Resection Within the Same Admission (Definitive Cure)

real_success_data.recurrence_after_decompression_alone_no_: 33.9% pooled (95% CI 19.5-52.1%, I2=97.5%, 17 studies, n=3,285); WSES guideline range 45-71% across individual series; up to 84-90% reported in some individual cohorts without any definitive treatment
real_success_data.resection_recurrence_benefit_viable_colo: RR 0.20 (95% CI 0.08-0.50, p<0.001, NNT=9) for recurrence, resection vs non-resection, restricted to confirmed-viable sigmoid colon (12 studies, n=527); arithmetically implies approximately 2.8% recurrence with resection vs approximately 13.9% with non-resective surgery in the same population, derived transparently from the paper's own reported RR and NNT
real_success_data.resection_mortality_viable_colon: RR 1.12 (95% CI 0.53-2.37, p=0.760, not significant) for mortality, resection vs non-resection, same viable-colon subgroup -- i.e. resection's real recurrence advantage is not bought at a significant mortality cost once bowel viability is confirmed
real_success_data.viability_effect_on_mortality: RR 0.31 (95% CI 0.19-0.51, p<0.001, NNH=8.1) for mortality, viable vs gangrenous colon; arithmetically implies approximately 5.6% mortality with viable colon vs approximately 17.9% with gangrenous colon, a real >3-fold difference driven by ischemia alone, not by which surgery is chosen

real_success_data.viability_effect_on_mortality_kenya_coho: 0% mortality (0 of 7) with viable/non-perforated cecum vs 67% mortality (4 of 6) with perforation, n=13 rural-hospital cohort -- a real, small-sample but directly documented ischemia contrast

real_success_data.timely_care_cohort: 93.3% survival (28 of 30 infants), 6.7% mortality (2 of 30), short bowel syndrome in 6.7% (2 of 30), median time from hospital arrival to Ladd's procedure 297 minutes (under 5 hours)
