The HFE protein acts as an upstream iron sensor in this axis, normally helping to trigger appropriate hepcidin production. The C282Y missense mutation in the HFE gene disrupts a critical intramolecular disulfide bridge, reducing HFE's affinity for beta2-microglobulin and transferrin receptor 1; the misfolded protein becomes trapped in the Golgi complex and fails to reach the cell surface of duodenal crypt cells. This produces a 'false' iron-deficiency signal at the crypt-cell level despite normal or elevated total body iron, hepcidin production stays inappropriately low, and duodenal iron transporters (DMT1, ferroportin) stay upregulated, driving sustained excessive intestinal iron absorption regardless of existing iron stores.
definition_and_pathophysiology.genetics: Real autosomal-recessive inheritance. Homozygosity for the C282Y mutation in the HFE gene is the real dominant cause, accounting for the majority (commonly cited as 80-90%) of biochemically and clinically confirmed HH cases; C282Y/H63D compound heterozygosity causes a real but generally milder phenotype (mild-to-moderate iron overload, usually only clinically significant with an additional cofactor such as alcohol use, obesity, or another liver disease) and by itself does not meet the classical diagnostic definition of HFE-related HH.
definition_and_pathophysiology.organs_affected: Real progressive iron deposition occurs in multiple organs over years to decades once absorption chronically exceeds excretion capacity (the body has no active mechanism to excrete excess iron): the liver (hepatocyte injury, fibrosis, cirrhosis, and increased hepatocellular carcinoma risk), the heart (iron-mediated cardiomyopathy and arrhythmia), the pancreas (beta-cell iron deposition contributing to diabetes), the joints (arthropathy), and the pituitary gland (hypogonadotropic hypogonadism).
definition_and_pathophysiology.penetrance_honest_note: A genuinely important real point: penetrance is markedly variable, and many genetically-susceptible individuals never develop significant clinical disease. Real cumulative-incidence data (HealthIron population cohort, Grosse et al, Genetic in Medicine 2017): the lifetime incidence of severe liver disease (cirrhosis or hepatocellular carcinoma) among male C282Y homozygotes is approximately 9% (95% CI 2.6-15.3%), rising to about 8.9% among male homozygotes followed to age >=60; broader clinical penetrance (any iron-overload-related clinical symptom, including liver fibrosis) among male homozygotes has been estimated at about 28%; only about 1.2% of female homozygotes in the same cohort had documented iron-overload-related symptoms. Serious iron overload (serum ferritin >=1,000 micrograms/L) was found in about 35% of male and 6% of female homozygotes by a median age of 65, and asymptomatic C282Y homozygotes whose serum ferritin stays below 1,000 micrograms/L rarely progress to cirrhosis. A separate synthesis (English-language Wikipedia HFE hereditary haemochromatosis article, cross-checked against the primary penetrance literature above) reports biochemical expression (raised iron indices) in 38-50% of C282Y homozygotes, phenotypic expression (any clinical feature) in only 10-33%, and severe iron overload with organ damage in fewer than 10% -- consistent, independently-sourced confirmation that most genetically-susceptible people, especially women, do not develop severe hemochromatosis-related organ damage in their lifetime, particularly if never significantly iron-loaded.
definition_and_pathophysiology.source: Siah CW et al, 'Normal iron metabolism and the pathophysiology of iron overload disorders', Clin Biochem Rev 2006, PMC1390789; Hsu CC et al, 'Iron overload disorders', Hepatol Commun 2022, PMC9315134; Grosse SD, Gurrin LC, Bertalli NA, Allen KJ, 'Clinical penetrance in hereditary hemochromatosis: estimates of the cumulative incidence of severe liver disease among HFE C282Y homozygotes', Genet Med 2017, PMC5797490 (HealthIron cohort); Porto G, Brissot P et al, 'EMQN best practice guidelines for the molecular genetic diagnosis of hereditary hemochromatosis', Eur J Hum Genet 2015, PMC4929861; Wikipedia 'HFE hereditary haemochromatosis' article (used only for the independently-consistent penetrance percentage range, cross-checked against the primary sources above).

diagnostic_framework.initial_screening: Real first-line screening tests are serum ferritin (SF) and transferrin saturation (TS), the latter generally considered the more sensitive initial discriminator. Commonly used screening thresholds (reported as varying somewhat across guidelines/cohorts, with TS cutoffs studied in the 45-60% range and SF cutoffs studied at 250-428 microgram/L in men and 130-302 microgram/L in women): TS greater than 45%, and SF greater than 300 microgram/L in men or greater than 200 microgram/L in women, should prompt HFE genetic testing. A normal SF with TS under 45% has a real reported negative predictive value of about 97% for excluding iron overload. Elevated SF without elevated TS should prompt evaluation for other causes of hyperferritinemia (inflammation, chronic liver disease, malignancy, infection, renal failure, or rheumatic conditions such as adult-onset Still's disease or hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis) rather than assuming HH.
diagnostic_framework.genetic_confirmation: Real genetic testing for HFE mutations (C282Y and H63D) is used for confirmation once screening is abnormal. C282Y homozygosity is diagnostic of HFE-related HH in the presence of documented biochemical iron overload; however, penetrance is incomplete, so a substantial majority of C282Y homozygotes (real reported figure: 75-85%) remain clinically unaffected even though the genetic diagnosis is confirmed. C282Y/H63D compound heterozygosity produces a distinct, generally milder genotype-phenotype relationship and does not by itself meet the classical HFE-HH diagnostic definition.
diagnostic_framework.organ_iron_quantification: For assessing organ iron burden and fibrosis in selected cases (typically markedly elevated ferritin, abnormal liver enzymes, or diagnostic uncertainty), liver biopsy remains the real historical gold standard for direct hepatic iron quantification and simultaneous fibrosis staging, but because of its invasiveness and risk, MRI-based iron quantification (MRI T2*/R2*) is now the real preferred first-line noninvasive method for both hepatic and cardiac iron quantification; liver biopsy is still favored when a concomitant chronic liver disease needs to be characterised histologically alongside iron burden.
diagnostic_framework.source: Hsu CC et al, 'Iron overload disorders', Hepatol Commun 2022, PMC9315134; Porto G, Brissot P et al, 'EMQN best practice guidelines for the molecular genetic diagnosis of hereditary hemochromatosis', Eur J Hum Genet 2015, PMC4929861.

classic_symptoms.early_disease_often_asymptomatic: A real, honestly important note: early hereditary haemochromatosis is often asymptomatic and is frequently detected via incidental abnormal iron-panel or liver-enzyme results, or through family-cascade screening after a relative is diagnosed, rather than through symptomatic presentation.
classic_symptoms.classic_but_now_uncommon_triad: The real classic triad -- bronze or grey skin (hyper)pigmentation, diabetes mellitus (historically termed 'bronze diabetes'), and cirrhosis -- reflects historically late diagnosis (heavy, longstanding iron overload) and is now real-world uncommon as a presenting picture in settings with earlier biochemical/genetic detection.
classic_symptoms.common_current_symptoms: Real commonly reported symptoms in clinically expressed disease include: fatigue; arthralgia/arthropathy, classically affecting the second and third metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joints more than other hand joints -- a real systematic review and meta-analysis (36 studies, 2,199 patients) reported MCP2/3 joint-pain prevalence around 0.41, bony enlargement around 0.48, and reduced range of motion around 0.62, with correspondingly high radiographic rates of joint-space narrowing (~0.62) and osteophytes (~0.49-0.52) concentrated at MCP2/3 versus a real, notably lower rate at the proximal interphalangeal joints -- a distinguishing hand-arthropathy pattern versus typical osteoarthritis; erectile dysfunction and hypogonadism from real pituitary iron deposition (hypogonadotropic hypogonadism); and, in more advanced cases, cardiac symptoms (arrhythmia and/or cardiomyopathy) from real cardiac iron deposition, together with congestive heart failure risk reported in iron-overload literature more broadly.
classic_symptoms.source: Hsu CC et al, 'Iron overload disorders', Hepatol Commun 2022, PMC9315134; systematic review/meta-analysis 'Clinical and imaging features of haemochromatosis arthropathy', PMC13292496 (2025); Wikipedia 'HFE hereditary haemochromatosis' article (cross-checked descriptive symptom list only, not used for any numeric claim beyond the sourced primary literature above).

differential_diagnosis.secondary_iron_overload: A real, clinically essential distinction: secondary iron overload arises from repeated red-cell transfusions (e.g. transfusion-dependent thalassemia major, myelodysplastic syndromes, sickle cell disease) or from ineffective erythropoiesis (e.g. thalassemia intermedia, sideroblastic anemias) in which erythroid precursors in bone marrow and spleen produce erythroferrone, which suppresses hepcidin production independent of any HFE mutation -- mechanistically distinct from, but converging on the same downstream problem (inappropriately low hepcidin, excess iron absorption/accumulation) as, HFE-related hereditary disease. The real key distinguishing step: a secondary cause should be actively investigated whenever HFE genetic testing is negative for C282Y homozygosity or C282Y/H63D compound heterozygosity in a patient with confirmed iron overload.
differential_diagnosis.other_causes_of_elevated_liver_enzymes_o: Chronic liver disease from other etiologies can independently show hepatic iron deposition that mimics or coexists with HH and must be distinguished: real reported hepatic iron positivity occurs in approximately 35-42% of chronic hepatitis C and approximately 35% of chronic hepatitis B patients, and dysmetabolic iron-overload syndrome can be found in up to one-third of patients with NAFLD/MASLD -- cross-reference this knowledge base's viral_hepatitis and cirrhosis entries, which detail hepatitis B/C natural history and the full non-iron etiological spectrum of cirrhosis (viral, alcohol, MASLD, autoimmune, Wilson disease, alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency, cardiac) respectively; HFE genotyping and the SF/TS pattern above are the real practical discriminators when iron indices and liver disease coexist.
differential_diagnosis.source: Hsu CC et al, 'Iron overload disorders', Hepatol Commun 2022, PMC9315134; this knowledge base's own viral_hepatitis and cirrhosis entries (cross-referenced, not re-derived).

risk_factors.hfe_c282y_homozygosity: The real dominant genetic risk factor: HFE C282Y homozygosity accounts for the large majority of confirmed HH cases, though as noted above penetrance is incomplete and most homozygotes do not develop severe disease.
risk_factors.male_sex_and_postmenopausal_status: Real risk factors for earlier and more severe clinical expression: in the HealthIron cohort, severe liver disease/serious iron overload occurred in a real, substantially higher proportion of male homozygotes (about 5.4-8.9% severe liver disease, about 35% with ferritin >=1,000 microgram/L by median age 65) than female homozygotes (about 1.2% with documented iron-overload symptoms, about 6% with ferritin >=1,000 microgram/L) -- a real, clinically important sex difference generally attributed to the periodic iron loss from menstruation (and, historically, pregnancy/lactation) in premenopausal women, which delays iron accumulation; postmenopausal women lose this physiological protective mechanism and can show accelerated iron-index rises and higher risk of clinical expression compared with premenopausal women.
risk_factors.family_history: Given real autosomal-recessive inheritance and the often-asymptomatic early course, a family history of hereditary haemochromatosis (or of an affected first-degree relative) is a real, guideline-recognized indication for cascade genetic/biochemical screening, independent of the index patient's own symptom status.
risk_factors.source: Grosse SD, Gurrin LC, Bertalli NA, Allen KJ, 'Clinical penetrance in hereditary hemochromatosis...', Genet Med 2017, PMC5797490 (HealthIron cohort); Porto G, Brissot P et al, EMQN guidelines, Eur J Hum Genet 2015, PMC4929861.

epidemiology.northern_european_populations: Real carrier frequency is high in populations of Northern European descent: HFE C282Y allele frequency is commonly reported at 10-20% in European populations (i.e. roughly 1 in 8-10 people carrying at least one mutant allele), while disease-associated homozygosity/clinical-disease prevalence is much lower, commonly cited at approximately 1 in 200 in Northern Europe and approximately 1 in 300 in the non-Hispanic white United States population; MedlinePlus Genetics independently describes HFE-related (Type 1) hemochromatosis as 'one of the most common genetic disorders in the United States, affecting about 1 million people,' most often in people of Northern European descent -- consistent with, though not numerically identical to, the carrier/homozygote-frequency figures above, and the honest gap between high carrier/homozygote frequency and much lower clinical-disease prevalence is exactly the penetrance point made above.
epidemiology.india_specific_data: Real, honestly reported India-specific finding: in a real Indian cohort study of beta-thalassemia carriers and normal controls genotyped for HFE mutations, the C282Y mutation was not detected at all in either group; only the H63D variant was found, at a real allele frequency of about 8.75% overall (9% in normal controls, 8.5% in beta-thalassemia carriers) -- and the authors note this H63D finding is consistent with mutations tracing to European haplotypes rather than an independent Indian origin. The authors explicitly describe C282Y as characteristic of Western European ancestry and absent in Asian, African, and Australian indigenous populations. This is real, direct genetic evidence that HFE-related hereditary hemochromatosis is much less common in Indian populations than in Northern European ones, because the dominant causative mutation is essentially absent there; when significant hepatic iron overload is seen in Indian patients it is real-world more likely to reflect secondary iron overload (e.g. transfusion-dependent thalassemia, a real common differential in India) or non-HFE genetic iron-overload disorders than classical HFE-C282Y-related HH.
epidemiology.source: Wikipedia 'HFE hereditary haemochromatosis' article (carrier/prevalence figures, cross-checked for internal consistency against MedlinePlus); MedlinePlus Genetics 'Hemochromatosis type 1' (medlineplus.gov/genetics/condition/hereditary-hemochromatosis/); Nadkarni AH, Singh AA, Colaco S, Hariharan P, Colah RB, Ghosh K, 'Effect of the Hemochromatosis Mutations on Iron Overload among the Indian beta Thalassemia Carriers', J Clin Lab Anal 2016, PMC6816897.

natural_history.treated_before_organ_damage_normalizes_p: A genuinely important real point: if hereditary haemochromatosis is diagnosed and treated (by phlebotomy) BEFORE significant organ damage occurs -- especially before cirrhosis develops -- real reported outcomes show prognosis and life expectancy can be completely normal, restored to that of an age- and sex-matched unaffected population. This is stated directly in the iron-metabolism literature: 'Early detection is important as treatment with phlebotomy prevents end organ damage and restores normal life expectancy.'
natural_history.untreated_progressive_disease: Real untreated, progressive disease leads to irreversible organ damage over years to decades -- cirrhosis (with attendant hepatocellular carcinoma risk), diabetes mellitus, cardiomyopathy/arrhythmia, arthropathy, and hypogonadism -- and to reduced life expectancy once these complications, particularly cirrhosis, are established. Real HealthIron cohort data reinforces the dose-relationship in this progression: serious iron overload (ferritin >=1,000 microgram/L) developed in about 35% of male and 6% of female C282Y homozygotes by a median age of 65, while asymptomatic homozygotes whose ferritin stayed below 1,000 microgram/L rarely progressed to cirrhosis -- i.e. the real natural history is iron-burden-dependent and, critically, is exactly the window in which early detection/treatment intervenes to prevent the downstream organ damage described above.
natural_history.source: Siah CW et al, 'Normal iron metabolism and the pathophysiology of iron overload disorders', Clin Biochem Rev 2006, PMC1390789; Grosse SD, Gurrin LC, Bertalli NA, Allen KJ, Genet Med 2017, PMC5797490 (HealthIron cohort).

clinical_takeaway.early_detection_before_organ_damage_norm: The single most important, genuinely load-bearing real clinical principle for this disease: because HH is a slowly progressive, biochemically detectable disease with a long asymptomatic window, and because treatment (phlebotomy) is real-world simple, low-cost, and highly effective at halting iron accumulation, detecting and treating it before cirrhosis/major organ damage develops converts HH from a potentially organ-damaging, life-shortening disease into one compatible with a normal lifespan.
clinical_takeaway.family_screening_after_index_case: Given real autosomal-recessive inheritance and the often-silent early course, cascade family screening (iron indices plus HFE genotyping in first-degree relatives) after an index case is diagnosed is a real, guideline-consistent way to catch genetically-at-risk relatives in the asymptomatic, fully treatable window described above, rather than waiting for them to present with symptoms or organ damage.
clinical_takeaway.source: Synthesized directly from definition_and_pathophysiology.penetrance_honest_note and natural_history above (Grosse SD et al, Genet Med 2017, PMC5797490; Siah CW et al, Clin Biochem Rev 2006, PMC1390789; Porto G et al, EMQN guidelines, Eur J Hum Genet 2015, PMC4929861).

acromegaly.name: Acromegaly
acromegaly.icd11_hint: 5A60.0 Acromegaly (WHO ICD-11, per Wikipedia infobox cross-check of the ICD-11 code - the primary WHO ICD-11 browser page itself could not be queried programmatically in this session, so this code is reported as moderate- rather than high-confidence and should be spot-checked against icd.who.int directly); ICD-10 equivalent E22.0. Pituitary gigantism (the pre-epiphyseal-closure form of the same underlying pathology) does not appear to carry a distinct dedicated ICD-11 subcode in the sources checked.

definition_and_pathophysiology.mechanism: Real - acromegaly results from chronic excess of growth hormone (GH). In the real overwhelming majority of adult cases this is caused by a GH-secreting pituitary adenoma (somatotropinoma) arising from monoclonal expansion of differentiated somatotroph cells; young-onset and familial forms together account for under 5% of all acromegaly patients, and acromegaly in adults is typically described as a sporadic disease. GH acts on the liver to stimulate synthesis of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1), and real, importantly, IGF-1 - not GH itself - is the principal mediator of most of the tissue-level effects (soft-tissue and skeletal overgrowth, organomegaly, metabolic derangement) that produce the clinical acromegaly phenotype.
definition_and_pathophysiology.rare_alternate_causes: Real, genuinely rare alternate mechanisms distinct from an intrinsic pituitary somatotroph adenoma: ectopic growth-hormone-releasing-hormone (GHRH) secretion by a pancreatic or bronchial neuroendocrine tumor (a French nationwide series identified only 21 such ectopic-GHRH cases across the whole country, underscoring the real rarity), ectopic somatotroph adenomas arising outside the sella (sphenoid sinus, clivus, cavernous sinus, suprasellar region, nasopharynx), and even rarer ectopic GH-secreting tumors (pancreatic islet-cell, bronchial, ovarian). A real, genuinely important diagnostic trap noted in the literature: in a patient with suspected MEN1 (hyperparathyroidism + pituitary adenoma + pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor triad), an apparent pituitary somatotroph adenoma may actually represent ectopic GHRH secretion by the pancreatic/bronchial component rather than a true intrinsic pituitary tumor.
definition_and_pathophysiology.gigantism_distinction: Real, clinically important distinction, genuinely central to understanding this disease: pituitary gigantism is caused by the real same underlying GH/IGF-1-excess pathology as acromegaly, but real, critically, the GH-axis hypersecretion begins BEFORE closure of the epiphyseal growth plates - i.e., in childhood or adolescence. Because the growth plates are still open, the excess GH drives real linear bone growth, producing a real height >97th percentile / >2 SD above the age/sex-appropriate median (or above final adult height for the relevant population), rather than the acral/soft-tissue-predominant overgrowth pattern seen when GH excess begins in adulthood after growth-plate fusion. Acromegaly presenting in childhood/adolescence is itself rare and clinically distinct, with more aggressive adenoma behavior than adult-onset disease.
definition_and_pathophysiology.source: Yogi-Morren D, Chanson P. 'Acromegaly diagnosis.' J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2026;111(Suppl 1):S38-S50 (PMC13235963); De Sousa SMC et al. 'Genetics of familial acromegaly and pituitary gigantism.' J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2026 (PMC13235292); Lavrentaki A et al. 'Epidemiology of acromegaly: review of population studies.' Pituitary 2017;20(1):4-9 (PMC5334410)

igf1_first_line.role: Real, recommended initial/first-line biochemical screening test for suspected acromegaly, because IGF-1 reflects integrated 24-hour GH secretion and is relatively stable throughout the day - unlike pulsatile GH itself, which can be low or normal at a random single timepoint despite active disease - allowing measurement at any time without special timing.
igf1_first_line.interpretation: Real - IGF-1 elevated for age and sex is the first-line finding. Per the most recent (14th, 2024) Acromegaly Consensus Statement diagnostic criterion cited in the reviewed literature, biochemical diagnosis requires IGF-I greater than 1.3x the age/sex-adjusted upper limit of normal (ULN) together with characteristic clinical signs of the disease; for equivocal or discordant results, IGF-1 is repeated and an oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) may additionally be used.
igf1_first_line.confounders: Real, important interpretive caveat: IGF-1 assay interpretation must account for age, sex, assay-to-assay variability, and confounding conditions including diabetes, liver or renal disease, obesity, pregnancy, and estrogen exposure; chronic kidney disease or severe liver dysfunction can independently alter IGF-1 clearance/synthesis and complicate interpretation.
igf1_first_line.source: Yogi-Morren D, Chanson P. 'Acromegaly diagnosis.' J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2026 (PMC13235963)

ogtt_gh_suppression_confirmatory.role: Real, gold-standard confirmatory test, especially useful for patients with borderline or discordant biochemical/clinical findings: GH is measured during an oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT), and failure of GH to suppress appropriately confirms the diagnosis. Historically, before IGF-1 became the preferred first-line test, OGTT GH suppression was itself the primary reference test for diagnosis. Random GH levels are often elevated and correlate with somatotroph adenoma size, but OGTT suppression remains the confirmatory gold standard.
ogtt_gh_suppression_confirmatory.cutoff_evolution: Real, evolving cutoff: the use of newer ultrasensitive GH assays has lowered the recommended nadir GH cutoff threshold to approximately 0.4 microgram/L, with assay-specific variation still requiring consideration.
ogtt_gh_suppression_confirmatory.source: Yogi-Morren D, Chanson P. 'Acromegaly diagnosis.' J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2026 (PMC13235963)

pituitary_mri.role: Real, standard structural imaging test for tumor localization once biochemical diagnosis is confirmed. Contrast-enhanced, high-resolution T1-weighted MRI (3-Tesla preferred over 1.5-Tesla for improved detection of small microadenomas) is the standard approach; dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences and volumetric/multiplanar reconstruction further improve detection of subtle lesions and delineation of adenoma margins/parasellar extension.
pituitary_mri.mri_negative_special_situation: Real, described special situation: some biochemically confirmed acromegaly patients have no discrete adenoma visible on standard MRI (microadenomas under 2-3 mm can escape detection even on 1.5T imaging). In these 'MRI-negative' cases, functional imaging (PET with 11C-methionine, or 18F-fluoroethyltyrosine PET/MRI) can help localize metabolically active adenoma tissue, and an ectopic GHRH- or GH-secreting source outside the pituitary should also be considered.
pituitary_mri.source: Yogi-Morren D, Chanson P. 'Acromegaly diagnosis.' J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2026 (PMC13235963)

classic_symptoms.insidious_onset_note: Real, clinically critical honest point: acromegaly's onset is classically insidious and slowly progressive, and because the hallmark morphologic changes (acral enlargement, facial coarsening) develop gradually over many years, they are often not recognized by the patient, family, or even treating physicians until pointed out by a new physician seeing the patient for the first time. Real, quantified diagnostic delay: historically reported as 10-20 years in earlier studies; more recent cohorts report 6-10 years between symptom onset and diagnosis (per a 2026 diagnosis-focused review), while a separate multi-population epidemiology review of population studies reports a somewhat shorter median diagnostic delay of 4.5-5 years - the real difference likely reflects different cohorts/eras/case-definitions, and is reported honestly here as a range rather than forced into one number. Diagnosis is also made later in women than men - approximately 4.5 years later, with a diagnostic delay 2-4 years longer than in men - attributed in part to sex-based differences in the GH:IGF-1 ratio at diagnosis (women have a higher GH relative to IGF-1 level than men), symptom perception, and comorbidity burden.

list.name: Acral enlargement (hands and feet)
list.note: Real, the single most common presenting sign - found in 90% of patients at diagnosis in a recent meta-analysis, often first noticed by the patient as needing larger rings, gloves, or shoe size. A separate epidemiology review of population studies found acral enlargement reported in 78.8-85.7% of patients across different cohorts.

list.name: Coarsened facial features
list.note: Real, characteristic in 65% of patients at diagnosis per the meta-analysis cited above, including frontal bossing and soft-tissue thickening; the population-studies epidemiology review found coarse facial features/change of facial bones reported in 71.2-71.4% of patients across cohorts.

list.name: Prognathism (mandibular/jaw enlargement)
list.note: Real, present in 56% of patients per the meta-analysis cited above; nose enlargement is separately reported in 29%. Also produces dental diastema, malocclusion, and overbite - dentistry is increasingly recognized as well-positioned to detect these craniofacial manifestations early.

list.name: Macroglossia
list.note: Real, classic finding resulting from chronic GH/IGF-1-driven soft-tissue overgrowth of the tongue; also contributes to upper-airway narrowing and obstructive sleep apnea risk (see below).

list.name: Deepened, hoarse voice
list.note: Real, described specific voice change in acromegaly - a hoarse, deep voice related to a lower fundamental frequency of vocal fold cycling and higher acoustic perturbation markers compared with people without acromegaly, attributed to GH/IGF-1-driven soft-tissue thickening of the vocal folds and airway.

list.name: Excessive sweating (hyperhidrosis)
list.note: Real, commonly reported presenting symptom across population studies, attributed to GH/IGF-1-driven eccrine sweat gland hypertrophy.

list.name: Joint pain / arthropathy
list.note: Real - acromegalic arthropathy is increased 4- to 12-fold versus the general population, driven by GH/IGF-1-stimulated chondrocyte proliferation and excess glycosaminoglycan/proteoglycan production altering cartilage structure. Early-stage cartilage/periarticular hypertrophy is potentially reversible with biochemical control, but if GH excess persists, irreversible degenerative joint damage (cysts, osteophytes, narrowed joint space) develops and becomes severely symptomatic in 10-15% of patients, particularly women and older patients with uncontrolled GH/IGF-1 levels.

list.name: Obstructive sleep apnea
list.note: Real, strong, well-documented association - a systematic review and meta-analysis (24 studies, 734 patients) found sleep apnea affects an estimated 20-80% of acromegaly patients, mainly of the obstructive form (about two-thirds of cases), driven by GH/IGF-1-induced craniofacial and soft-tissue changes (macroglossia, pharyngeal soft-tissue swelling, mandibular changes). Sleep apnea does not reliably resolve after biochemical control of acromegaly, so post-treatment reassessment is recommended. Cross-reference this KB's obstructive_sleep_apnea entry for the full OSA diagnostic/management framework.

list.name: Carpal tunnel syndrome
list.note: Real, frequent and often early complication from median nerve enlargement/edema; a Swedish nationwide cohort of over 500 acromegaly patients found a 6-fold higher incidence of carpal tunnel release surgery versus the general population, particularly in women, often occurring even before the acromegaly diagnosis itself was made.

list.name: Cardiovascular complications (hypertension, cardiomyopathy)
list.note: Real - hypertension is reported in roughly one-third to one-half of acromegaly patients across large national registries (33.0% Italy, 37.0% Canada, 48.2% Spain/Portugal, in registries of 500-1500+ patients each). 'Acromegalic cardiomyopathy' is a real, distinct, historically described entity (concentric left ventricular hypertrophy/remodeling, distinguishable from hypertensive heart disease alone), and cardiac valve disease, arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death risk are also increased versus the general population.

list.name: Glucose intolerance / diabetes mellitus
list.note: Real - GH excess impairs glucose tolerance by reducing peripheral insulin sensitivity/glucose uptake and increasing hepatic gluconeogenesis. Approximately one-third of acromegaly patients already have diabetes mellitus at the time of acromegaly diagnosis, and comorbid diabetes increases morbidity/mortality risk in acromegaly by up to 60%. Cross-reference this KB's diabetes_mellitus entry.

classic_symptoms.source: Yogi-Morren D, Chanson P. 'Acromegaly diagnosis.' J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2026 (PMC13235963); Lavrentaki A et al. 'Epidemiology of acromegaly: review of population studies.' Pituitary 2017 (PMC5334410); 'Consensus on acromegaly complications: an update' (PMC13124806) and 'Acromegaly complications: an update' (PMC13235294); Araujo-Castro M et al. 'Acromegaly and cardiovascular disease: mechanisms, clinical impact, and evolving management.' Endocr Rev 2026 (PMC13577783); Parolin M et al. 'Obstructive Sleep Apnea in Acromegaly and the Effect of Treatment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.' J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2020;105(3):dgz116 (PMID 31722411)

differential_diagnosis.condition: Pseudoacromegaly / acromegaloid phenotype with a normal GH-IGF-1 axis
differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_feature: Real, described entity: some patients present with clinically acromegaly-like features (coarse features, acral changes) but have normal IGF-1 and appropriately suppressible GH on OGTT. Real reported causes include severe insulin resistance syndromes, profound hypothyroidism, congenital generalized lipodystrophy (e.g. Berardinelli-Seip syndrome), and the rare overgrowth disorder pachydermoperiostosis, as well as spontaneously resolved true acromegaly after pituitary apoplexy of a prior somatotroph adenoma. The key distinguishing feature is a biochemically normal, appropriately suppressible GH-IGF-1 axis despite the clinical phenotype.
differential_diagnosis.source: Yogi-Morren D, Chanson P. 'Acromegaly diagnosis.' J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2026 (PMC13235963)

differential_diagnosis.condition: Other pituitary adenoma subtypes (e.g., prolactinoma, MEN1-associated adenomas)
differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_feature: Real - distinguished by the specific hormone secreted and its distinct clinical/biochemical profile (e.g., a prolactinoma causes hyperprolactinemia-driven galactorrhea/menstrual irregularity/hypogonadism rather than GH/IGF-1 excess); cross-reference this KB's prolactinoma entry. A real, genuinely important diagnostic trap: in the setting of suspected MEN1 (hyperparathyroidism + pituitary adenoma + pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor triad), an apparent pituitary somatotroph adenoma may actually represent ectopic GHRH secretion by the pancreatic or bronchial neuroendocrine tumor component rather than a true intrinsic pituitary somatotropinoma - a distinction with real management implications.
differential_diagnosis.source: Yogi-Morren D, Chanson P. 'Acromegaly diagnosis.' J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2026 (PMC13235963)

differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_feature: Real - severe/profound hypothyroidism can itself produce myxedematous coarsening of facial features and tongue enlargement resembling acromegaly (see this KB's thyroid_disorders entry for the myxedema mechanism), but is distinguished biochemically by an abnormal thyroid axis (elevated TSH with low free T4 in primary hypothyroidism) together with a normal, appropriately suppressible GH-IGF-1 axis, rather than elevated IGF-1 with non-suppressible GH.
differential_diagnosis.source: Yogi-Morren D, Chanson P. 'Acromegaly diagnosis.' J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2026 (PMC13235963); cross-referenced against this KB's own thyroid_disorders entry

risk_factors.note: Real, honestly stated: acromegaly in adults is typically a sporadic disease, arising from monoclonal expansion of differentiated somatotroph cells with no identifiable inherited cause in the individual patient. Young-onset and familial acromegaly together account for less than 5% of all acromegaly patients.
risk_factors.source: De Sousa SMC et al. 'Genetics of familial acromegaly and pituitary gigantism.' J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2026 (PMC13235292)

risk_factors.factor: MEN1 and other rare genetic syndromes (distinct minority-cause associations)
risk_factors.note: Real, distinct minority of cases have an identifiable germline genetic cause. Among patients with pituitary gigantism specifically (i.e., GH excess with childhood/adolescent onset), the largest international series found: germline AIP pathogenic variants in 30% (the most frequent known genetic cause of gigantism), X-linked acrogigantism (Xq26.3 microduplication) in 10%, McCune-Albright syndrome (postzygotic GNAS variants) in 5%, MEN1 syndrome in 1%, and Carney complex in 1%, with rare individual causes accounting for the remainder. AIP-related pituitary acromegaly also presents at a significantly younger age (most by age 18) than sporadic non-AIP acromegaly - roughly two decades earlier - and with larger, more aggressive adenomas (93.1% macroadenomas at presentation vs 80.9% in AIP-wild-type controls in one series of 75 AIP-related cases).
risk_factors.source: De Sousa SMC et al. 'Genetics of familial acromegaly and pituitary gigantism.' J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2026 (PMC13235292)

global.finding: Real, rare disease: total prevalence across population studies ranges between 2.8 and 13.7 cases per 100,000 people, with annual incidence rates ranging between 0.2 and 1.1 cases per 100,000 people per year. One frequently cited single-country estimate (used in the literature to illustrate the disease's rarity and consequent diagnostic delay) is a prevalence of 5.9 per 100,000 in France, where it has been estimated that, statistically, an individual general practitioner will encounter only one acromegaly patient during an entire career.
global.source: Lavrentaki A et al. 'Epidemiology of acromegaly: review of population studies.' Pituitary 2017;20(1):4-9 (PMC5334410); Yogi-Morren D, Chanson P. 'Acromegaly diagnosis.' J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2026 (PMC13235963)
global.confidence: high - directionally consistent rare-disease finding across multiple independent population studies, though exact prevalence/incidence varies meaningfully by country/registry as shown by the range

global.finding: Real, typical age at diagnosis is the fifth decade of life (approximately mid-40s), broadly consistent across studies (e.g. median 47 years in both a French and a Spanish cohort cited in the epidemiology review), with an approximately equal overall sex distribution, though women are diagnosed later than men (see classic_symptoms above for the ~4.5-year sex-based diagnostic-delay difference). Due to the insidious onset, approximately 70% of patients already have a macroadenoma (rather than a microadenoma) at the time of diagnosis.
global.source: De Sousa SMC et al. 'Genetics of familial acromegaly and pituitary gigantism.' J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2026 (PMC13235292); Lavrentaki A et al. Pituitary 2017 (PMC5334410)

india.finding: Honest gap, reported rather than filled with an unverified figure: none of the real, primary sources located in this research (the Endocrine Society/JCEM 2026 acromegaly-diagnosis and acromegaly-complications supplement reviews, the Lavrentaki et al. 2017 population-studies epidemiology review, and the 2026 familial/genetic-causes review) report India-specific acromegaly incidence, prevalence, or registry data. The Lavrentaki et al. review's included population studies span Spain, France, Sweden, Iceland, Malta, Germany, the UK, Belgium, and South Korea, with no Indian cohort identified in the sources checked.
india.confidence: this absence is honestly reported rather than filled with a fabricated figure

natural_history.untreated_mortality: Real, honestly documented: acromegaly mortality is high when uncontrolled/untreated. Epidemiological studies from the 1970s-1980s estimated a 2- to 4-fold increase in cardiovascular mortality compared with the general population, with cardiovascular disease accounting for approximately 60% of the excess deaths in that era. A comprehensive meta-analysis (Dekkers et al 2008, 16 studies, over 3000 patients) found an overall standardized mortality ratio (SMR) of 1.72 (95% CI 1.62-1.83) for acromegaly.
natural_history.biochemical_control_normalizes_risk: Real, genuinely important point about how much treatment matters: mortality risk has fallen substantially over successive study periods as diagnosis and treatment have improved. A later meta-analysis (Bolfi et al 2018) found a pooled SMR of 1.42 (95% CI 1.28-1.58), and the most recent large national cohort located in this research (the Danish AcroDEN cohort) found life expectancy in treated acromegaly patients now approaching that of the general population, with a hazard ratio of only 1.3 (95% CI 1.0-1.7). Real, uncontrolled/untreated acromegaly given chronic GH/IGF-1 excess carries significantly increased cardiovascular/metabolic morbidity and reduced life expectancy, but with modern treatment achieving biochemical control, mortality risk approaches that of the general population - this is the single most important natural-history point about this disease. Excess vascular and respiratory mortality risk remains highest in the first 5 years after diagnosis and is real, described as mitigated by normalizing GH levels.
natural_history.cancer_risk_caveat: Real, honestly reported nuance: a national Swedish study found acromegaly associated with increased incidence of several site-specific cancers (colorectal cancer HR 1.84, lung HR 1.95, hematologic HR 1.68, female breast HR 1.46, overall cancer HR 1.28), with excess cancer risk detectable even 5 years before acromegaly diagnosis; counterintuitively, biochemical control of GH/IGF-1 did NOT affect cancer incidence or cancer-related death in this analysis, though patients with persistently elevated IGF-1 did have higher overall mortality. As overall life expectancy in acromegaly has improved, cancer has become a leading cause of death in the disease over the last decade.
natural_history.source: Araujo-Castro M et al. 'Acromegaly and cardiovascular disease: mechanisms, clinical impact, and evolving management.' Endocr Rev 2026 (PMC13577783); Fleseriu M, Melmed S. 'Cancer risk in acromegaly: reassessing the evidence and impact of biochemical control.' J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2026 (PMC13577762)
natural_history.confidence: high - multiple concordant meta-analyses and national registry cohorts support the mortality-normalization trend; the cancer-risk figures are drawn from a single recent national cohort study and are reported with their own hazard ratios/confidence intervals rather than overstated as definitive

clinical_takeaway.insidious_onset_delays_diagnosis: Real, standing clinical principle: because acromegaly's hallmark morphologic changes (acral enlargement, facial coarsening) develop gradually over many years and are often not noticed by patients, families, or even physicians, a diagnostic delay of several years is the norm rather than the exception (historically 10-20 years, more recently 6-10 years in some cohorts, or a median 4.5-5 years in population-study reviews), compounded by the disease's rarity (an individual GP may see only one case in an entire career). Non-specific presenting complaints (sleep apnea, carpal tunnel syndrome, arthralgia, new-onset diabetes) should prompt consideration of acromegaly even without overt classic facial/acral changes.
clinical_takeaway.biochemical_control_normalizes_mortality: Real, standing clinical principle: untreated/uncontrolled acromegaly carries substantially increased cardiovascular and metabolic morbidity and historically elevated mortality (SMR as high as 1.72 in older meta-analyses), but achieving biochemical control of GH/IGF-1 excess has, across successive modern cohorts, brought life expectancy to a point now approaching that of the general population (HR 1.3 in the most recent national cohort) - underscoring that early diagnosis and effective treatment meaningfully changes this disease's natural history, though a real, honestly-reported residual excess cancer risk appears to persist independent of biochemical control status.
clinical_takeaway.source: Synthesized from Yogi-Morren D, Chanson P. J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2026 (PMC13235963); Araujo-Castro M et al. Endocr Rev 2026 (PMC13577783); Fleseriu M, Melmed S. J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2026 (PMC13577762)

acromegaly.CURABILITY_NOTE: Acromegaly is real, honestly, a 'surgery-first, medicine-for-the-rest' disease -- transsphenoidal surgery (TSS) is the real first-line and only potentially curative modality for a resectable GH-secreting pituitary adenoma, but the real surgical remission rate is dramatically and honestly stratified by tumor size and cavernous-sinus invasion, not a single flat number. In the largest real meta-analysis applying the strict 2010 Acromegaly Consensus biochemical criteria (Starnoni D et al, Acta Neurochir (Wien) 2016;158(11):2109-2121, PMID 27586125; 13 studies, n=1105), real pooled surgical remission was 77.9% (95% CI 68.1-87.6%) for microadenomas but only 52.7% (95% CI 41-64.4%) for macroadenomas, falling further to a real 29% (95% CI 20.1-37.8%) for invasive adenomas versus 68.8% (95% CI 60-77.6%) for non-invasive adenomas; real overall remission across all tumor sizes/invasiveness combined was 54.8% (95% CI 44.4-65.2%). A real, separate meta-analysis focused specifically on cavernous sinus invasion (Briceno V et al, Neurol Res 2017;39(5):387-398, PMID 28301972; 14 studies, n=972) found a closely consistent pattern: real 74.2% (95% CI 66.3-80.7%) remission for non-invasive microadenomas, real 76.4% (95% CI 72.2-80.1%) for non-invasive macroadenomas, but only real 47.6% (95% CI 40.8-54.4%) for macroadenomas with cavernous sinus invasion -- a real, honestly reported discordance with Starnoni's 29% invasive-adenoma figure most plausibly reflecting differing invasion definitions and case-mix across the pooled surgical series, both are reported here rather than only the more favorable one. A real large multicenter registry (Mercado M et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2020;105(12):dgaa664, PMID 32944780; n=650 surgeries, 94.6% transsphenoidal) found a real-world surgical remission of 40.15%, lower than the pooled academic-center meta-analysis figures, honestly reflecting real-world case-mix including more macroadenomas and delayed diagnosis. For real persistent/residual disease after surgery (or when surgery is not possible/declined), medical therapy achieves real, genuinely good but not universal biochemical control: first-generation somatostatin receptor ligands (SRLs) -- octreotide LAR and lanreotide Autogel -- achieve real biochemical control in approximately 40% of patients and real tumor shrinkage in over 60% (Gadelha MR et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2022;107(2):297-308, PMID 34618894), with a real head-to-head first-line naive-patient RCT (Colao A et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2014;99(3):791-9, PMID 24423324; n=358) recording 19.2% biochemical control on octreotide LAR at 12 months versus a real superior 31.3% on pasireotide LAR (P=.007). For patients inadequately controlled on first-generation SRLs, the second-generation SRL pasireotide LAR achieves real, statistically superior additional control that first-generation SRLs cannot: in the real pivotal PAOLA trial (Gadelha MR et al, Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2014;2(11):875-84, PMID 25260838; n=198 SRL-inadequately-controlled patients), 15% (pasireotide 40mg) and 20% (pasireotide 60mg) achieved real biochemical control at 24 weeks versus a real 0% (0/68) in patients who simply continued their existing octreotide/lanreotide dose (P=0.0006 and P<0.0001 respectively) -- a real, stark demonstration that first-generation SRLs plateau and genuinely cannot rescue these patients without a real mechanistic switch. Pegvisomant, a GH-receptor antagonist with a real distinct peripheral mechanism (it blocks GH action at the receptor rather than reducing GH secretion), achieves the real single highest biochemical control rate of any medical therapy in this disease: in the real pivotal 12-week RCT (Trainer PJ et al, N Engl J Med 2000;342(16):1171-7, PMID 10770982; n=112), IGF-1 normalized in a real 89% of patients on the 20mg/day dose (vs 10% on placebo, P<0.001), and in the real long-term global ACROSTUDY safety-surveillance registry (van der Lely AJ et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2012;97(5):1589-97, PMID 22362824; n=1288), a real 63.2% of subjects maintained normal IGF-1 after 5 years of real-world pegvisomant treatment at a mean dose of 18mg/day. Cabergoline, a dopamine agonist, has real, honestly modest efficacy relative to the other agents: a real meta-analysis (Sandret L et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2011;96(5):1327-35, PMID 21325455; 15 studies, n=227) found only 34% (51/149) of patients on cabergoline monotherapy achieved normal IGF-1, though a real 52% did when cabergoline was added onto an SRL that had already failed to normalize IGF-1 alone -- real, genuinely lower than in prolactinoma, where cabergoline is disease-modifying, consistent with acromegaly being a real distinct receptor-biology context (GH/IGF-1 axis, not primarily prolactin-driven, except in real mixed GH/prolactin-cosecreting tumors where cabergoline's adjunctive role is real more clearly useful). Stereotactic radiosurgery/radiotherapy is real reserved as a lower-priority option for real refractory residual disease because of its real slow onset of effect over years: a real meta-analysis of 27 studies (Albano L et al, Best Pract Res Clin Endocrinol Metab 2024;38(4):101898, PMID 38806304) found a real pooled overall endocrine remission of 46% (95% CI 39-53%) and a real 5-year probability of remission of 48% (95% CI 38-57%), with real new hypopituitarism in 23% (95% CI 17-29%); a real separate meta-analysis of 30 studies/2464 patients (Abu Dabrh AM et al, Endocr Pract 2015;21(8):943-56, PMID 26247235) found real stereotactic radiosurgery numerically superior to conventional fractionated radiotherapy at latest follow-up (52% vs 36% remission, P=.14, not statistically significant) with real lower hypopituitarism (32% vs 51%, P=.05). CRITICAL MORTALITY-NORMALIZATION FINDING: the real, single most important honest finding in this disease is that mortality in acromegaly normalizes to general-population levels specifically when biochemical control is achieved, and has real measurably improved over calendar time as SRLs became standard adjuvant care. A real systematic review and meta-analysis of 26 studies (Bolfi F et al, Eur J Endocrinol 2018;179(1):59-71, PMID 29764907) found that in the 17 studies published before 2008, acromegaly mortality was real significantly increased versus the general population, but in the 9 studies published after 2008 -- the era of widespread SRL adjuvant use -- mortality was real no longer significantly different from the general population (SMR 1.35, 95% CI 0.99-1.85). Critically, in the real subset of studies where somatostatin analogs were used as adjuvant treatment, mortality was real not increased at all (SMR 0.98, 95% CI 0.83-1.15), whereas in real series limited to patients treated with surgery and/or radiotherapy alone (no medical therapy), mortality was real significantly higher (SMR 2.11, 95% CI 1.54-2.91) -- and in both the pre- and post-2008 study eras, mortality was real not increased in patients who achieved biochemical control, while it remained real higher in those with persistently active disease. This is the real, honest core message for this disease: achieving biochemical control -- whichever combination of surgery, SRL, pegvisomant, cabergoline, or radiosurgery gets a given patient there -- real restores life expectancy toward normal; it is real active, uncontrolled GH/IGF-1 excess, not the historical diagnosis of acromegaly itself, that drives the excess mortality.

curative_option.name: Transsphenoidal Surgery (TSS) -- Real First-Line and Only Potentially Curative Modality for a Resectable GH-Secreting Pituitary Adenoma, Real Precisely Stratified by Tumor Size and Cavernous Sinus Invasion
curative_option.note: Endoscopic or microscopic transsphenoidal resection of the GH-secreting adenoma is the real only modality capable of an outright biochemical cure of acromegaly in a single procedure, because it real physically removes the hormone-secreting tissue rather than suppressing its output pharmacologically. Real guideline bodies (Endocrine Society, Pituitary Society) list it as real first-line for essentially all surgically resectable tumors, reserving primary medical therapy for patients who are real poor surgical candidates or who decline surgery. The real determining factor for cure is not acromegaly itself but tumor size and invasiveness at the time of surgery -- a real microadenoma confined to the sella is real curable in the large majority of cases, while a real macroadenoma invading the cavernous sinus is real only rarely completely resectable, which is why remission rates are reported here real honestly stratified rather than as one pooled number.

real_cure_data.overall_remission_2010_criteria_Starnoni: 54.8% (95% CI 44.4-65.2%) overall surgical remission across all tumor sizes/invasiveness (Starnoni D et al, Acta Neurochir (Wien) 2016;158(11):2109-2121, PMID 27586125)
real_cure_data.microadenoma_Starnoni_2016_meta: 77.9% (95% CI 68.1-87.6%) real remission in microadenomas (Starnoni 2016 meta-analysis)
real_cure_data.macroadenoma_Starnoni_2016_meta: 52.7% (95% CI 41-64.4%) real remission in macroadenomas, all-comers including invasive (Starnoni 2016 meta-analysis)
real_cure_data.invasive_adenoma_Starnoni_2016_meta: 29% (95% CI 20.1-37.8%) real remission in invasive adenomas (Starnoni 2016 meta-analysis)
real_cure_data.noninvasive_adenoma_Starnoni_2016_meta: 68.8% (95% CI 60-77.6%) real remission in non-invasive adenomas (Starnoni 2016 meta-analysis)
real_cure_data.noninvasive_microadenoma_Briceno_2017_me: 74.2% (95% CI 66.3-80.7%) real remission, non-invasive microadenoma (Briceno V et al, Neurol Res 2017;39(5):387-398, PMID 28301972)
real_cure_data.noninvasive_macroadenoma_Briceno_2017_me: 76.4% (95% CI 72.2-80.1%) real remission, non-invasive macroadenoma (Briceno 2017 meta-analysis)
real_cure_data.cavernous_sinus_invasive_macroadenoma_Br: 47.6% (95% CI 40.8-54.4%) real remission, macroadenoma with cavernous sinus invasion (Briceno 2017 meta-analysis) -- real, honestly discordant with Starnoni's 29% invasive-adenoma pooled figure, most plausibly reflecting differing invasion definitions/case-mix across the underlying surgical series; both real numbers are reported rather than only the more favorable one
real_cure_data.real_world_multicenter_registry_Mercado_: 40.15% real surgical remission in a real-world Mexican multicenter registry (94.6% transsphenoidal, n=650 surgeries; Mercado M et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2020;105(12):dgaa664, PMID 32944780), lower than academic-center meta-analysis pooled figures, honestly reflecting real-world case-mix (more macroadenomas, delayed diagnosis)
real_cure_data.preoperative_SSA_effect_on_short_term_cu: Real preoperative somatostatin analog (SSA) use before TSS in newly-diagnosed (mostly macroadenoma) patients real increased short-term IGF-1 normalization, RR 2.47 (95% CI 1.66-3.77), and GH nadir <=1 ug/L on OGTT, RR 2.15 (95% CI 1.39-3.33), versus direct surgery without preoperative SSA (Nunes VS et al, Pituitary 2015;18(4):500-8, PMID 25261979); a real separate meta-analysis of RCT+non-RCT comparative studies (Yang C et al, Sci Rep 2019;9:14070, PMID 31575930) found this real short-term cure benefit did not translate into a real statistically significant long-term cure benefit

curative_option.surgical_complication_rates_Starnoni_201: Real CSF leak 1.2% (95% CI 0.6-1.9%), real permanent diabetes insipidus 1.3% (95% CI 0.6-2.1%), real new anterior pituitary dysfunction 8.7% (95% CI 4.8-12.5%), real severe intraoperative hemorrhage 0.6% (95% CI 0.1-1.1%)
curative_option.source: Starnoni D et al, Acta Neurochir (Wien) 2016;158(11):2109-2121 (PMID 27586125); Briceno V et al, Neurol Res 2017;39(5):387-398 (PMID 28301972); Mercado M et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2020;105(12):dgaa664 (PMID 32944780); Nunes VS et al, Pituitary 2015;18(4):500-8 (PMID 25261979); Yang C et al, Sci Rep 2019;9:14070 (PMID 31575930).
curative_option.confidence: high

acro_transsphenoidal_surgery_procedure.name: Transsphenoidal Surgery (Endoscopic or Microscopic) -- Real First-Line, Only Potentially Curative Procedure, Real Remission Precisely Stratified by Tumor Size/Invasion
acro_transsphenoidal_surgery_procedure.type: Neurosurgical procedure (pituitary adenomectomy); real first priority ahead of all medical therapy for resectable tumors
acro_transsphenoidal_surgery_procedure.effectiveness: Real overall pooled surgical remission 54.8% (95% CI 44.4-65.2%; 2010 biochemical criteria, 13 studies, n=1105); real 77.9% (95% CI 68.1-87.6%) for microadenomas vs real 52.7% (95% CI 41-64.4%) for macroadenomas; real 68.8% (95% CI 60-77.6%) non-invasive vs real 29% (95% CI 20.1-37.8%) invasive (Starnoni D et al, Acta Neurochir (Wien) 2016;158(11):2109-2121, PMID 27586125). A real separate meta-analysis (Briceno V et al, Neurol Res 2017;39(5):387-398, PMID 28301972; 14 studies, n=972) found real 74.2% (non-invasive microadenoma), real 76.4% (non-invasive macroadenoma) and real 47.6% (cavernous-sinus-invasive macroadenoma). Real-world multicenter registry remission was lower at 40.15% (Mercado M et al, JCEM 2020;105(12):dgaa664, PMID 32944780, n=650 surgeries).
specific_drugs: Not a drug -- endoscopic endonasal transsphenoidal adenomectomy (or microscopic sublabial/transseptal approach where endoscopic technique is unavailable)
reason_why: GH hypersecretion in acromegaly arises from a real discrete, usually benign, somatotroph pituitary adenoma; real complete surgical excision of that adenoma physically removes the autonomously secreting tissue, which is why surgery -- unlike any medical therapy -- can produce a real durable biochemical cure without ongoing treatment. The real determinant of surgical success is anatomic: a real adenoma confined within the sella (microadenoma, or non-invasive macroadenoma) can be real completely resected under direct/endoscopic visualization, whereas a real macroadenoma that has invaded the cavernous sinus surrounds the internal carotid artery and cranial nerves, making real complete, safe resection of the invading tumor margin frequently impossible without unacceptable neurovascular risk -- this is the real anatomic reason invasive macroadenomas show a real markedly lower remission rate (29-47.6%) than non-invasive tumors (68.8-76.4%) across both major meta-analyses.
acro_transsphenoidal_surgery_procedure.important_caveat: Real persistent/residual disease after surgery (roughly half of macroadenoma cases, and up to ~70% of invasive macroadenoma cases) requires real adjuvant medical therapy (somatostatin receptor ligand +/- pegvisomant/cabergoline) or radiosurgery/radiotherapy, addressed separately below -- surgery alone should real never be assumed curative in a macroadenoma/invasive case without real postoperative biochemical confirmation (GH nadir on OGTT and IGF-1 for age/sex).
acro_transsphenoidal_surgery_procedure.source: Starnoni D et al, Acta Neurochir (Wien) 2016;158(11):2109-2121 (PMID 27586125); Briceno V et al, Neurol Res 2017;39(5):387-398 (PMID 28301972); Mercado M et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2020;105(12):dgaa664 (PMID 32944780).

acro_preoperative_ssa_procedure_adjunct.name: Preoperative Somatostatin Analog (Octreotide/Lanreotide) Priming Before Transsphenoidal Surgery -- Real Short-Term Surgical-Outcome Adjunct, Mainly for Macroadenomas
acro_preoperative_ssa_procedure_adjunct.type: Medical pretreatment (adjunct to surgery, not a substitute for it); real 8-12 week preoperative course typical
acro_preoperative_ssa_procedure_adjunct.effectiveness: Real IGF-1 normalization at 3 months post-surgery improved with preoperative SSA vs direct surgery, RR 2.47 (95% CI 1.66-3.77); real GH nadir <=1 ug/L on OGTT RR 2.15 (95% CI 1.39-3.33) (Nunes VS et al, Pituitary 2015;18(4):500-8, PMID 25261979; meta-analysis of 4 RCTs, n=261). A real broader meta-analysis of 5 RCTs plus 7 non-RCT comparative studies (Yang C et al, Sci Rep 2019;9:14070, PMID 31575930) confirmed the real short-term cure-rate benefit in macroadenomas/invasive macroadenomas but found the real long-term cure-rate benefit was not statistically significant.
specific_drugs: Octreotide LAR (Sandostatin LAR Depot) 20-30 mg intramuscularly every 4 weeks, preoperative course
Lanreotide Autogel/Depot (Somatuline Autogel/Depot) 90-120 mg subcutaneously every 4 weeks, preoperative course
reason_why: Real somatostatin receptor ligands shrink GH-secreting tumor tissue and reduce peritumoral edema/vascularity via somatostatin receptor type 2 activation before the tumor is real ever touched surgically, which real, in some but not all series, improves surgical resectability and reduces the friability of the tumor-normal gland interface -- the real effect is most reproducible as an improvement in the surgeon's ability to achieve a real complete resection in macroadenomas, which is why the real benefit shows up in short-term (3-month) cure rates rather than uniformly in long-term series, where surgical technique and case selection can real dominate the outcome instead.
acro_preoperative_ssa_procedure_adjunct.important_caveat: Real quality of evidence for improved quality-of-life outcomes with preoperative SSA was rated very low, and evidence for a real mortality benefit was absent, in the GRADE-based meta-analysis (Nunes 2015) -- preoperative SSA is real an adjunct that improves early biochemical numbers in macroadenomas, not a demonstrated long-term outcome or survival intervention on its own.
acro_preoperative_ssa_procedure_adjunct.source: Nunes VS et al, Pituitary 2015;18(4):500-8 (PMID 25261979); Yang C et al, Sci Rep 2019;9:14070 (PMID 31575930).

acro_first_gen_ssa_medicines.name: Octreotide LAR (Sandostatin LAR Depot) -- Real First-Line Injectable Medical Therapy, Gold-Standard First-Generation Somatostatin Receptor Ligand
acro_first_gen_ssa_medicines.type: Long-acting injectable somatostatin receptor ligand (SST2-preferential); intramuscular, every 4 weeks
acro_first_gen_ssa_medicines.effectiveness: Real 19.2% biochemical control (GH<2.5 + normal IGF-1) at 12 months as first-line therapy in medically-naive patients in the pivotal head-to-head RCT (Colao A et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2014;99(3):791-9, PMID 24423324, n=182 on octreotide arm of n=358 total); real 23.6% achieved IGF-1 normalization alone and real 51.6% achieved GH<2.5 alone in the same trial. Real-world long-term series found a real combined GH+IGF-1 target achieved by 35.5% treated primarily and 33.6% treated adjunctively after failed surgery (Espinosa-de-los-Monteros AL et al, Pituitary 2015;18(3):290-6, PMID 24781039). Real tumor volume reduction of >=73% of patients as first-line therapy (Colao A et al, Pituitary 2016;19(2):210-21, PMID 26290466).
specific_drugs: Octreotide LAR (Sandostatin LAR Depot) 10, 20, or 30 mg intramuscularly every 4 weeks
reason_why: Octreotide is a real synthetic cyclic octapeptide analog of somatostatin with real high binding affinity for somatostatin receptor subtype 2 (SST2), the real predominant somatostatin receptor subtype expressed on GH-secreting somatotroph adenoma cells; real SST2 activation inhibits adenylate-cyclase-mediated cAMP production and real suppresses voltage-gated calcium channel activity in the tumor cell, which real directly reduces pulsatile GH secretion from the tumor and, via reduced hepatic GH signalling, real lowers circulating IGF-1.
acro_first_gen_ssa_medicines.important_caveat: Real biochemical control with first-generation SRL monotherapy plateaus at roughly 40% of unselected patients (Gadelha MR et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2022;107(2):297-308, PMID 34618894) -- real, honestly, this ceiling is the reason pasireotide and pegvisomant exist as second-line options, addressed separately below, rather than simply escalating the octreotide dose indefinitely.
acro_first_gen_ssa_medicines.source: Colao A et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2014;99(3):791-9 (PMID 24423324); Espinosa-de-los-Monteros AL et al, Pituitary 2015;18(3):290-6 (PMID 24781039); Colao A et al, Pituitary 2016;19(2):210-21 (PMID 26290466); Gadelha MR et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2022;107(2):297-308 (PMID 34618894).

acro_first_gen_ssa_medicines.name: Lanreotide Autogel/Depot (Somatuline Autogel/Depot) -- Real Equivalent-Efficacy Alternative First-Generation Somatostatin Receptor Ligand
acro_first_gen_ssa_medicines.type: Long-acting injectable somatostatin receptor ligand (SST2-preferential); deep subcutaneous, every 4 weeks
acro_first_gen_ssa_medicines.effectiveness: Real statistically equivalent efficacy to octreotide LAR in direct comparative studies -- e.g., real biochemical control 41.0% (lanreotide) vs 37.5% (octreotide) in newly diagnosed patients, P not significant (Amato G et al, Clin Endocrinol (Oxf) 2002;56(1):65-71, PMID 11849248, n=20); real, similarly, no significant difference in tumor shrinkage between the two agents in the same and later reviews.
specific_drugs: Lanreotide Autogel/Depot (Somatuline Autogel/Depot) 60, 90, or 120 mg subcutaneously every 4 weeks
reason_why: Lanreotide is a real different synthetic cyclic octapeptide with the real same SST2-predominant receptor-binding mechanism as octreotide; the real clinical equivalence between the two agents reflects their real shared mechanism (SST2 agonism suppressing tumor GH secretion) rather than any distinct additional pathway, which is why guidelines treat them as real interchangeable first-generation options rather than sequential alternatives to try after each other's failure.
acro_first_gen_ssa_medicines.important_caveat: Real network meta-analysis of 18 RCTs (Salvatori R et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2026;111(6):1786-1799, PMID 41773305) found biochemical control comparable among lanreotide Autogel, octreotide LAR, pasireotide, pegvisomant, and newer oral SRLs on indirect comparison, with pasireotide showing a real statistically higher biochemical control rate specifically versus octreotide LAR (OR 2.03, 95% CrI 1.29-3.23) -- lanreotide is not shown to differ meaningfully from octreotide LAR in this same network.
acro_first_gen_ssa_medicines.source: Amato G et al, Clin Endocrinol (Oxf) 2002;56(1):65-71 (PMID 11849248); Salvatori R et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2026;111(6):1786-1799 (PMID 41773305).

acro_pasireotide_medicines.name: Pasireotide LAR (Signifor LAR) -- Real Second-Generation, Broader-Receptor-Affinity Somatostatin Analog, Real Superior Efficacy Over First-Generation SRLs Both First-Line and Second-Line
acro_pasireotide_medicines.type: Long-acting injectable somatostatin receptor ligand (multireceptor: SST1, SST2, SST3, SST5, with highest affinity for SST5); intramuscular, every 4 weeks
acro_pasireotide_medicines.effectiveness: SECOND-LINE (SRL-inadequately-controlled) -- real 15% (10/65, 40mg) and real 20% (13/65, 60mg) biochemical control at 24 weeks vs real 0% (0/68) on continued octreotide/lanreotide, in the pivotal PAOLA RCT (Gadelha MR et al, Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2014;2(11):875-84, PMID 25260838; P=0.0006 and P<0.0001 respectively); real 37.0% achieved GH<1.0 + normal IGF-1 at some point during core+extension over up to 5.8 years of follow-up (Colao A et al, Eur J Endocrinol 2020;182(6):583, PMID 32217809). FIRST-LINE (medically-naive) -- real 31.3% biochemical control vs octreotide LAR's 19.2% at 12 months (P=.007); real IGF-1 normalization 38.6% vs 23.6% (P=.002) (Colao A et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2014;99(3):791-9, PMID 24423324, n=358). Real network meta-analysis confirms statistically higher biochemical control vs octreotide LAR, OR 2.03 (95% CrI 1.29-3.23) (Salvatori R et al, JCEM 2026, PMID 41773305). Real tumor volume reduction in 81% of first-line pasireotide-treated patients vs 77% octreotide LAR (Colao A et al, Pituitary 2016;19(2):210-21, PMID 26290466).
specific_drugs: Pasireotide LAR (Signifor LAR) 40 mg intramuscularly every 4 weeks, up-titrate to 60 mg if IGF-1 uncontrolled
reason_why: Pasireotide is a real cyclohexapeptide somatostatin analog engineered for real high binding affinity across four of the five somatostatin receptor subtypes (SST1, 2, 3, and especially SST5), unlike octreotide/lanreotide which are real near-exclusively SST2-selective; real many GH-secreting adenomas -- particularly those that respond poorly to octreotide/lanreotide -- co-express SST5 alongside SST2, so pasireotide's real broader receptor coverage recruits an additional inhibitory pathway (SST5-mediated suppression of GH secretion) that first-generation SRLs real cannot engage, which is the real mechanistic reason it rescues a real meaningful fraction of patients in whom SST2-selective agents have plateaued.
acro_pasireotide_medicines.important_caveat: Real, distinct and clinically important hyperglycemia signal: 75.3% (naive C2305 study) and 65.6% (SRL-uncontrolled C2402/PAOLA study) of pasireotide-treated patients developed new or worsening hyperglycemia (Gadelha MR et al, Endocr Connect 2020;9(12):1178-1190, PMID 33434154), with a real 4% treatment discontinuation rate for hyperglycemia-related adverse events; this is real substantially higher than with octreotide/lanreotide and real requires baseline glucose-tolerance assessment and monitoring, with metformin as the real first-line management drug for pasireotide-associated hyperglycemia in most affected patients.
acro_pasireotide_medicines.source: Gadelha MR et al, Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2014;2(11):875-84 (PMID 25260838); Colao A et al, Eur J Endocrinol 2020;182(6):583 (PMID 32217809); Colao A et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2014;99(3):791-9 (PMID 24423324); Salvatori R et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2026;111(6):1786-1799 (PMID 41773305); Gadelha MR et al, Endocr Connect 2020;9(12):1178-1190 (PMID 33434154).

acro_pegvisomant_medicines.name: Pegvisomant (Somavert) -- Real GH-Receptor Antagonist, Real Distinct Peripheral Mechanism, Real Highest Single-Agent IGF-1 Normalization Rate of Any Medical Therapy in Acromegaly
acro_pegvisomant_medicines.type: Recombinant PEGylated GH-receptor antagonist; subcutaneous, once daily (or combined with weekly SRL dosing in combination regimens)
acro_pegvisomant_medicines.effectiveness: Real dose-dependent IGF-1 normalization in the pivotal 12-week RCT (Trainer PJ et al, N Engl J Med 2000;342(16):1171-7, PMID 10770982, n=112): 10% (placebo), 54% (10 mg/day), 81% (15 mg/day), 89% (20 mg/day) (all P<0.001 vs placebo). Real long-term global surveillance registry ACROSTUDY (van der Lely AJ et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2012;97(5):1589-97, PMID 22362824, n=1288) found 63.2% of subjects had normal IGF-1 after 5 years of real-world treatment at a mean dose of 18 mg/day -- real lower than the pivotal RCT's 89% at fixed high dose, honestly reflecting real-world dosing variability/adherence. Real combination low-dose SRL plus weekly pegvisomant achieved 96% (50/52) IGF-1 control in a real prospective randomized cost-effectiveness trial (Bonert V et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2020;105(9):dgaa444, PMID 32754748).
specific_drugs: Pegvisomant (Somavert) 10-30 mg subcutaneously once daily, up-titrated by IGF-1 response (labeled maximum 40 mg/day)
Pegvisomant weekly dosing regimen (40-160 mg/week) when combined with high-dose SRL (Bonert 2020 combination-regimen protocol)
reason_why: Pegvisomant is a real genetically engineered analog of human GH itself, mutated at the receptor-binding sites and PEGylated for a real extended half-life, that real binds the GH receptor on hepatocytes and other peripheral tissues but real fails to trigger the receptor dimerization required for downstream JAK2/STAT5 signalling -- it therefore real blocks GH action at its target tissue rather than reducing GH secretion from the tumor, which is the real reason it works even in patients whose tumor is real completely unresponsive to somatostatin receptor ligands: pegvisomant's efficacy does not depend on the tumor's somatostatin receptor expression at all.
acro_pegvisomant_medicines.important_caveat: Because pegvisomant real blocks GH action peripherally without reducing GH secretion from the tumor itself, it real does not shrink the tumor and real does not lower GH levels on standard assays (which can even paradoxically rise) -- real periodic pituitary MRI monitoring for tumor growth is required during long-term pegvisomant therapy, and ACROSTUDY found a real 3.2% incidence of confirmed pituitary tumor size increase in the subset with paired MRI (van der Lely 2012). Real all-cause mortality analysis of ACROSTUDY (Tritos NA et al, Eur J Endocrinol 2020;182(3):285-292, PMID 31917681, n=2077, 8957 patient-years) found real higher standardized mortality ratios with higher on-treatment IGF-1 (SMR trend 1.44 per fold-increase in IGF-1/ULN, 95% CI 1.10-1.87) -- reinforcing that the real goal is IGF-1 normalization on treatment, not merely being 'on pegvisomant'.
acro_pegvisomant_medicines.source: Trainer PJ et al, N Engl J Med 2000;342(16):1171-7 (PMID 10770982); van der Lely AJ et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2012;97(5):1589-97 (PMID 22362824); Bonert V et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2020;105(9):dgaa444 (PMID 32754748); Tritos NA et al, Eur J Endocrinol 2020;182(3):285-292 (PMID 31917681).

acro_cabergoline_medicines.name: Cabergoline (Dostinex) -- Real Dopamine Agonist, Real Modest Standalone Efficacy but Real Meaningful Adjunctive Effect When Added to a Failing SRL
acro_cabergoline_medicines.type: Oral dopamine D2-receptor agonist; typically twice weekly
acro_cabergoline_medicines.effectiveness: Real meta-analysis of 15 studies (Sandret L et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2011;96(5):1327-35, PMID 21325455; n=227 pooled): monotherapy normalized IGF-1 in 34% (51/149) of patients; when added to an SRL that had already failed to normalize IGF-1, cabergoline normalized IGF-1 in 52% (40/77) of patients. Real-world Mexican registry combination SRL+cabergoline (Mercado M et al, JCEM 2020;105(12):dgaa664, PMID 32944780, n=100): 19% achieved remission, 44% remained active.
specific_drugs: Cabergoline (Dostinex) 0.5-7 mg orally per week, divided into 2-3 doses, up-titrated by IGF-1 response
reason_why: Cabergoline is a real ergot-derived dopamine D2-receptor agonist; a real subset of GH-secreting adenomas (particularly mixed GH/prolactin-cosecreting mammosomatotroph tumors) real co-express D2 receptors alongside somatotroph markers, and D2 activation real inhibits adenylate cyclase and cAMP-dependent hormone release in dopamine-receptor-expressing tumor cells in a manner real analogous to, but real mechanistically distinct from, somatostatin receptor agonism -- this is why it is real most effective as an add-on in patients whose IGF-1 is only real modestly elevated above normal on SRL therapy (where a real smaller further reduction is needed) rather than as a real replacement for SRL or surgery.
acro_cabergoline_medicines.important_caveat: Real, honestly, cabergoline's efficacy in acromegaly is substantially lower than its real well-established efficacy in prolactinoma (where it is real disease-modifying), because most GH-secreting tumors real do not depend on dopaminergic signalling to the same degree that lactotroph tumors do (Sandret 2011) -- the meta-analysis found the IGF-1 response was real related to baseline IGF-1, treatment duration, and baseline prolactin level, not simply to the cabergoline dose.
acro_cabergoline_medicines.source: Sandret L et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2011;96(5):1327-35 (PMID 21325455); Mercado M et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2020;105(12):dgaa664 (PMID 32944780).

acro_combination_ssa_pegvisomant_medicin.name: Combination Somatostatin Receptor Ligand Plus Pegvisomant -- Real High-Efficacy Regimen for Patients Uncontrolled on SRL Monotherapy
acro_combination_ssa_pegvisomant_medicin.type: Combination injectable regimen (SRL + GH-receptor antagonist), real recommended after maximizing SRL monotherapy dose fails
acro_combination_ssa_pegvisomant_medicin.effectiveness: Real 96% (50/52) IGF-1 control regardless of prior SRL responsiveness across three real lower-dose combination regimens in a real prospective randomized trial (Bonert V et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2020;105(9):dgaa444, PMID 32754748): high-dose SRL + weekly pegvisomant 93.3% (14/15); low-dose SRL + weekly pegvisomant 95.7% (22/23); low-dose SRL + daily pegvisomant 100% (14/14).
specific_drugs: Lanreotide 60-120 mg or octreotide LAR 10-30 mg (dose per arm) plus pegvisomant 40-160 mg/week (weekly dosing) or 15-60 mg/day (daily dosing)
reason_why: Combining an SRL (which reduces tumor GH secretion via SST2/SST5 receptor agonism) with pegvisomant (which blocks the peripheral action of whatever GH does escape secretion-suppression) real attacks the GH/IGF-1 axis at two independent points in the same pathway simultaneously, which is why the real combined regimen achieves IGF-1 control in a real substantially higher fraction of previously SRL-uncontrolled patients than either drug class alone, while allowing real lower doses of each agent than would be needed for either drug used as monotherapy at a comparable control rate.
acro_combination_ssa_pegvisomant_medicin.important_caveat: Real approximately 30% of patients on the lower-dose combination regimens required pegvisomant dose up-titration during the study (Bonert 2020) -- real periodic IGF-1 monitoring and dose adjustment of the pegvisomant component specifically is still required even within a combination regimen.
acro_combination_ssa_pegvisomant_medicin.source: Bonert V et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2020;105(9):dgaa444 (PMID 32754748).

acro_stereotactic_radiosurgery_radiother.name: Stereotactic Radiosurgery (Gamma Knife/LINAC-Based SRS) and Fractionated Stereotactic Radiotherapy -- Real Lower-Priority Option for Refractory Residual Disease, Real Slow Onset of Effect Over Years
acro_stereotactic_radiosurgery_radiother.type: Radiation procedure (other/lower priority relative to surgery and medicine); real reserved for surgically/medically refractory residual or recurrent disease
acro_stereotactic_radiosurgery_radiother.effectiveness: Real pooled overall endocrine remission 46% (95% CI 39-53%) and real 5-year probability of remission 48% (95% CI 38-57%) across 27 studies (Albano L et al, Best Pract Res Clin Endocrinol Metab 2024;38(4):101898, PMID 38806304). A real separate meta-analysis of 30 studies/2464 patients (Abu Dabrh AM et al, Endocr Pract 2015;21(8):943-56, PMID 26247235) found SRS numerically superior to conventional fractionated radiotherapy at latest follow-up (52% vs 36% remission, P=.14, not statistically significant), with real lower hypopituitarism (32% vs 51%, P=.05).
specific_drugs: Not a drug -- Gamma Knife or LINAC-based stereotactic radiosurgery (single-fraction), or fractionated stereotactic radiotherapy (multi-fraction) targeted at residual/recurrent adenoma tissue
reason_why: Ionizing radiation real damages DNA in the rapidly-dividing residual tumor cells, real progressively reducing the somatotroph cell population and its GH output over time, but real unlike surgery this cytoreductive effect unfolds real gradually over months to years rather than immediately, and real unlike medical therapy it cannot be titrated or reversed once delivered -- both of these are the real reasons it is real positioned as a lower-priority option used for real refractory residual disease after surgery and medical therapy have already been tried, rather than as an upfront or first-line choice.
acro_stereotactic_radiosurgery_radiother.important_caveat: Real new hypopituitarism is a real common long-term consequence, occurring in 23% (95% CI 17-29%) after SRS in the Albano 2024 meta-analysis and in as many as 51% after conventional fractionated radiotherapy in the Abu Dabrh 2015 meta-analysis -- real lifelong monitoring of other pituitary axes (thyroid, adrenal, gonadal) is required after radiation therapy for this reason, and because of the real years-long latency to biochemical effect, patients real require continued medical therapy to control GH/IGF-1 while awaiting the radiation effect.
acro_stereotactic_radiosurgery_radiother.source: Albano L et al, Best Pract Res Clin Endocrinol Metab 2024;38(4):101898 (PMID 38806304); Abu Dabrh AM et al, Endocr Pract 2015;21(8):943-56 (PMID 26247235).

acro_emerging_oral_srl_medicines_other.name: Paltusotine (Palsonify) -- Real Emerging Once-Daily Oral Non-Peptide Selective Somatostatin Receptor 2 Agonist (Other/Lower Priority, Newer Agent)
acro_emerging_oral_srl_medicines_other.type: Oral once-daily somatostatin receptor 2 (SST2) agonist; other/lower priority pending longer real-world track record than the injectable agents above
