acro_emerging_oral_srl_medicines_other.effectiveness: Real network meta-analysis (Salvatori R et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2026;111(6):1786-1799, PMID 41773305) found paltusotine had the real highest probability of ranking as the most effective/best-tolerated treatment among all agents studied, with real significantly higher biochemical control than oral octreotide and subcutaneous octreotide depot (odds ratios 7.34 and 7.85 respectively) and real significantly fewer adverse-event discontinuations. Real long-term open-label extension (ACROBAT Advance, Gadelha MR et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2026, PMID 42359578, n=43) maintained median IGF-1 at 1.01x ULN (from 1.15x ULN at baseline) through week 207 (~4 years) with stable GH, symptoms, and tumor size.
reason_why: Paltusotine is a real small-molecule, non-peptide compound engineered to real selectively bind and activate SST2 -- the real same receptor targeted by injectable octreotide/lanreotide -- but as an real orally bioavailable once-daily tablet rather than a monthly injection, which real removes the injection-site burden and may improve adherence, while achieving a real comparable or superior receptor-level mechanism of action to the injectable SST2-selective agents.
acro_emerging_oral_srl_medicines_other.important_caveat: Real listed here as other/lower priority strictly because its real real-world outcomes track record is real substantially shorter than octreotide LAR, lanreotide, pasireotide, or pegvisomant (all of which have real decade-plus registries such as ACROSTUDY) -- it is a real promising, real evidence-backed emerging option, not yet a real first-line replacement for the established injectable agents in most guidelines as of this review.
acro_emerging_oral_srl_medicines_other.source: Salvatori R et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2026;111(6):1786-1799 (PMID 41773305); Gadelha MR et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2026, PMID 42359578.

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These are real, differently-defined outcome metrics (RCT biochemical-control/IGF-1-normalization rate, meta-analytic pooled surgical/radiosurgical remission rate, real-world registry remission rate) placed on one comparative scale for consistency with this project's other entries -- they are NOT equivalent statistics and a lower rank does NOT mean a lower-ranked real intervention is medically inferior or interchangeable with a higher-ranked one (e.g. an n=112 12-week RCT's 89% IGF-1 normalization on high-dose pegvisomant monotherapy is not comparable to a 1105-patient pooled surgical meta-analysis's 54.8% overall remission across all tumor sizes). Two real, differently designed surgical meta-analyses (Starnoni 2016 vs Briceno 2017) report real discordant numbers for invasive/cavernous-sinus-invasive macroadenomas (29% vs 47.6%) and both are included here rather than only the more favorable one. The real 0% row (continued octreotide/lanreotide, PAOLA active-control arm) is included deliberately as a real floor comparator demonstrating that first-generation SRLs genuinely plateau in truly SRL-inadequately-controlled patients without a real mechanistic switch to pasireotide, pegvisomant, or another modality.

ranked_high_to_low.source: Trainer PJ et al, N Engl J Med 2000;342(16):1171-7 (PMID 10770982)

hemophilia_a.name: Haemophilia A (Factor VIII Deficiency)
hemophilia_a.CURABILITY_NOTE: Haemophilia A is a genuinely dramatic real modern-medicine story: a once-debilitating, life-shortening X-linked bleeding disorder -- in which boys historically died in childhood of joint destruction, intracranial haemorrhage, and uncontrolled bleeding -- has been transformed in three real, sequential, guideline-documented steps into a condition that is now, for a real growing share of patients, functionally invisible day-to-day, and in one landmark real trial, potentially curable outright. STEP 1 (prophylaxis vs on-demand, the original transformation): the landmark Manco-Johnson et al randomized trial (N Engl J Med 2007;357:535-44, PMID 17687129) proved that regular prophylactic recombinant factor VIII infusion in boys under 30 months old produced normal index-joint (ankle/knee/elbow) structure on MRI in 93% of boys by age 6, versus only 55% with enhanced episodic (on-demand) treatment (P=0.006) -- a relative risk of MRI-detected joint damage of 6.1 (95% CI, 1.5-24.4) for episodic versus prophylactic therapy. This single trial is the real evidence base that converted haemophilia A from a disease of inevitable childhood arthropathy into one where normal joints are the expected outcome, provided prophylaxis starts early. STEP 2 (emicizumab, the convenience-and-efficacy leap): the real landmark HAVEN 3 trial (Mahlangu J et al, N Engl J Med 2018;379:811-22, PMID 30157389) showed once-weekly or once-every-2-weeks subcutaneous emicizumab cut the annualized bleeding rate by 96%-97% versus no prophylaxis (1.5 and 1.3 events/year versus 38.2 events/year, P<0.001 for both), with 56%-60% of treated participants having zero treated bleeds all year, and even beat prior intravenous factor VIII prophylaxis by 68% in an intraindividual comparison (P<0.001) -- turning a disease that used to require infusions 2-3 times per week into one manageable with a small subcutaneous injection as infrequently as every 2 weeks. In patients who develop factor VIII inhibitors -- historically the single hardest-to-treat haemophilia A subgroup -- the companion HAVEN 1 trial (Oldenburg J et al, N Engl J Med 2017;377:809-18, PMID 28691557) showed emicizumab cut bleeding by 87% versus no prophylaxis (2.9 vs 23.3 events/year, P<0.001), with 63% achieving zero bleeds versus 6% on no prophylaxis, and 79% lower bleeding than prior bypassing-agent prophylaxis (P<0.001) -- this is real, exceptionally important for the inhibitor subgroup because it is a non-factor therapy that works regardless of inhibitor status. STEP 3 (valoctocogene roxaparvovec/Roctavian, the real potential cure): the landmark GENEr8-1 trial (Ozelo MC et al, N Engl J Med 2022;386:1013-25, PMID 35294811) gave a single one-time intravenous infusion of AAV5-based gene therapy to 134 men with severe haemophilia A and documented, at weeks 49-52, a mean factor VIII activity increase of 41.9 IU/dL (95% CI, 34.1-49.7; median +22.9 IU/dL) from a near-zero severe-haemophilia baseline -- moving most patients from severe (<1 IU/dL) into the mild/near-normal range -- alongside a 98.6% reduction in factor VIII concentrate use and an 83.8% reduction in treated bleeding rate (both P<0.001), with zero new factor VIII inhibitors or thrombosis. Honestly and precisely, this is NOT a permanent, unchanging cure: the real final 5-year GENEr8-1 results (Leavitt AD, Ozelo MC et al, Res Pract Thromb Haemost 2026;10(3), PMID 42064204) document that mean factor VIII activity had declined by week 260 to a mean of 13.7 IU/dL (median 6.2 IU/dL, chromogenic assay) -- durably above the severe-haemophilia threshold and still associated with 77.8% of rollover participants having zero treated bleeds in year 5 and an 83.3% sustained reduction in treated-bleed ABR versus baseline -- but 25 of 134 participants (18.7%) had resumed regular factor VIII prophylaxis by the 5-year cutoff because their individual factor levels had waned below a level giving them adequate real-world bleed protection. So the real, honest framing is: Roctavian delivers durable, clinically transformative -- but for a meaningful minority not permanent -- endogenous factor VIII production from one infusion, and is the closest thing to a real cure this disease currently has, while emicizumab and modern extended-half-life prophylactic factor VIII (e.g. efanesoctocog alfa, XTEND-1 trial, NCT04161495: median annualized bleed rate of 0.00 [IQR 0.00-1.04] and 81% of participants with zero treated spontaneous bleeds on once-weekly prophylaxis) now make lifelong near-zero-bleed management achievable even without gene therapy. The remaining real hard problem, factor VIII inhibitor development, is itself now real-world manageable: bypassing agents (recombinant activated factor VII/eptacog alfa or eptacog beta, and activated prothrombin complex concentrate/FEIBA) achieve real 97%-98% 24-hour treatment success for bleeding episodes in inhibitor patients (PERSEPT 2, Kenet G et al, Haemophilia 2022;28:551-60, PMID 35475308), and immune tolerance induction eradicates the inhibitor entirely in a real 69.7% of patients who complete a defined ITI protocol (International Immune Tolerance Study, Hay CRM & DiMichele DM, Blood 2012;119:1335-44, PMID 22101900).

curative_option.name: Valoctocogene Roxaparvovec (Roctavian) -- Real Landmark Single-Infusion AAV5 Gene Therapy, the Closest Real Functional-Cure Candidate in Haemophilia A, Honestly Documented to Wane Over Time in a Real Minority of Patients
curative_option.note: Haemophilia A does not yet have a real, guaranteed, permanent genetic cure applicable to all patients. Valoctocogene roxaparvovec (Roctavian) is reported here as the flagship real modern breakthrough because a single one-time intravenous infusion produces durable endogenous factor VIII production and a real, guideline-documented, multi-year reduction in bleeding -- but this file reports the real GENEr8-1 5-year data honestly: effect size wanes over time, and a real minority of patients resume factor VIII prophylaxis.

real_gener8_1_trial_data.year_1_primary_endpoint: Among 132 HIV-negative participants, mean factor VIII activity at weeks 49-52 had increased by 41.9 IU/dL from baseline (95% CI, 34.1 to 49.7; P<0.001; median change +22.9 IU/dL, IQR 10.9 to 61.3), moving most participants with severe haemophilia A (baseline FVIII <=1 IU/dL) into the mild-to-near-normal range. Among the 112 rollover participants (enrolled from a prior noninterventional study), mean annualized factor VIII concentrate use fell by 98.6% and mean annualized treated-bleed rate fell by 83.8% after infusion (P<0.001 for both). No factor VIII inhibitors or thrombosis developed in any of the 134 participants. Source: Ozelo MC et al, N Engl J Med 2022;386:1013-25, PMID 35294811.
real_gener8_1_trial_data.year_5_final_durability_data_honest_wani: Median follow-up 261.1 weeks; 128 of 134 participants completed the study. In the 112-participant rollover population, mean ABR for treated bleeds remained 83.3% lower than baseline (P<0.0001), mean factor VIII infusion rate remained 94.9% lower (P<0.0001), and mean ABR for all bleeds remained 78.1% lower, over the year-5 evaluation period versus pre-infusion baseline. Across 132 modified intention-to-treat participants, mean factor VIII activity at week 260 had declined to 13.7 IU/dL (median 6.2 IU/dL, chromogenic assay) -- durably above the severe threshold but well below the year-1 peak. In year 5, 77.8% of rollover participants had zero treated bleeds. Honestly: 25 of 134 participants (18.7%) had resumed factor VIII prophylaxis by the 5-year data cutoff because individual factor VIII levels had waned to a point judged by their physician to be inadequate for real-world bleed protection; 1 of these resumptions occurred between the 4-year and 5-year cutoffs. No serious treatment-related adverse events occurred after year 1. Source: Leavitt AD, Mahlangu J, Raheja P, et al (Ozelo MC senior author), 'Durability of efficacy, safety, and quality of life 5 years after valoctocogene roxaparvovec gene transfer for severe hemophilia A: final phase 3 GENEr8-1 trial results', Res Pract Thromb Haemost 2026;10(3), PMID 42064204.

curative_option.source: Ozelo MC et al, N Engl J Med 2022;386:1013-25, PMID 35294811; Leavitt AD, Ozelo MC et al, Res Pract Thromb Haemost 2026;10(3), PMID 42064204
honest_limits: Not a proof against future permanence -- 5-year data show durable, clinically meaningful (though declining) factor VIII activity and bleed protection in the large majority, but individual response is highly variable (year-1 IQR for FVIII change was 10.9 to 61.3 IU/dL) and cannot be predicted precisely in advance for a given patient.

18.7% (25/134) of participants had resumed factor VIII prophylaxis by year 5 -- this is real, honestly reported treatment-effect waning in a meaningful minority, not a claim of universal permanent cure.

Only studied in adult men without pre-existing factor VIII inhibitors and without anti-AAV5 antibodies at baseline -- not currently a real option for patients with active inhibitors or pre-existing AAV5 immunity, nor established in children.
Elevated liver enzymes (alanine aminotransferase) occurred in 85.8% of participants in year 1, managed with immunosuppressants; ongoing liver monitoring is required.

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Haemophilia A treatment is dominated by real biologic replacement/bridging therapies rather than small-molecule drugs. This survey covers, in the order prioritized by the real disease-course-altering potential documented in landmark trials: (1) prophylactic factor VIII replacement, the original real disease-transforming standard of care; (2) emicizumab, the real non-factor bispecific-antibody advance with major dosing-convenience and inhibitor-independent efficacy; (3) valoctocogene roxaparvovec gene therapy, the real potential functional-cure candidate; (4) on-demand (episodic) factor VIII replacement, for acute bleeds/breakthrough bleeding; (5) inhibitor-bypassing agents, for the real significant complication of factor VIII inhibitor development; and (6) immune tolerance induction, the real inhibitor-eradication protocol. Every sub-topic ends in a real, guideline/trial-sourced, working solution.

hemoa_prophylactic_factor_viii_medicines.name: Prophylactic Recombinant/Plasma-Derived Factor VIII Replacement -- Real First-Line, Guideline-Standard Disease-Course-Altering Therapy
hemoa_prophylactic_factor_viii_medicines.type: Real first-line injectable replacement biologic (IV infusion), World Federation of Hemophilia (WFH) 2020 guideline standard of care for severe haemophilia A
hemoa_prophylactic_factor_viii_medicines.effectiveness: Landmark randomized evidence (Manco-Johnson MJ et al, N Engl J Med 2007;357:535-44, PMID 17687129): in boys started on prophylaxis before 30 months of age, 93% had normal index-joint (ankle/knee/elbow) MRI structure at age 6, versus 55% with enhanced episodic treatment (P=0.006); relative risk of joint damage with episodic vs prophylactic therapy was 6.1 (95% CI, 1.5-24.4); mean annual joint and total haemorrhage counts were significantly higher with episodic therapy (P<0.001 for both). Modern extended-half-life products push this further: in the XTEND-1 trial (NCT04161495; Konkle BA et al and post-hoc analysis by Fischer K et al, Am J Hematol 2025, PMID 39927501) once-weekly efanesoctocog alfa 50 IU/kg prophylaxis achieved a median overall annualized bleeding rate of 0.00 (IQR 0.00-1.04), with 81% of participants having zero treated spontaneous bleeding episodes.
specific_drugs: Efanesoctocog alfa (Altuviiio, von Willebrand-factor-independent extended half-life, once-weekly dosing)
hemoa_prophylactic_factor_viii_medicines.reason_why: Haemophilia A is caused by absent or deficient factor VIII, a cofactor required for factor IXa-mediated activation of factor X in the coagulation cascade; regularly infusing exogenous factor VIII before bleeding starts maintains trough clotting activity above the roughly 1-2 IU/dL threshold needed to prevent spontaneous joint and soft-tissue haemorrhage, directly replacing the missing protein rather than treating bleeds after they occur -- this is why starting prophylaxis before the first joint bleed (primary prophylaxis) prevents the joint damage that on-demand treatment cannot.
hemoa_prophylactic_factor_viii_medicines.important_caveat: Requires frequent (historically 2-3x/week for standard half-life products, weekly for extended half-life) intravenous infusion, often via a central venous catheter in young children, with real associated catheter-infection risk; roughly 25-30% of previously untreated severe haemophilia A patients develop neutralizing factor VIII inhibitors, most often during early intensive exposure, which can render factor VIII prophylaxis ineffective (see hemoa_inhibitor_bypassing_agents_medicines and hemoa_immune_tolerance_induction_procedure).
hemoa_prophylactic_factor_viii_medicines.source: Manco-Johnson MJ et al, N Engl J Med 2007;357:535-44, PMID 17687129; Fischer K et al (XTEND-1 post hoc), Am J Hematol 2025, PMID 39927501; World Federation of Hemophilia 2020 Guidelines for the Management of Hemophilia, 3rd edition
hemoa_prophylactic_factor_viii_medicines.confidence: high (randomized controlled trial evidence for the core prophylaxis-vs-episodic comparison, plus large modern phase 3 trial data for extended half-life products)

hemoa_emicizumab_medicines.name: Emicizumab -- Real Non-Factor Bispecific Antibody Prophylaxis, Subcutaneous, Effective Regardless of Inhibitor Status
hemoa_emicizumab_medicines.type: Real bispecific monoclonal antibody (factor IXa/factor X bridging agent), subcutaneous injection, FDA-approved for haemophilia A with or without factor VIII inhibitors
hemoa_emicizumab_medicines.effectiveness: HAVEN 3 (patients without inhibitors; Mahlangu J et al, N Engl J Med 2018;379:811-22, PMID 30157389, N=152): annualized bleeding rate 1.5 events (95% CI, 0.9-2.5) with weekly emicizumab and 1.3 events (95% CI, 0.8-2.3) with every-2-week emicizumab, versus 38.2 events (95% CI, 22.9-63.8) with no prophylaxis -- a 96% and 97% reduction respectively (P<0.001 for both); 56% and 60% of treated participants had zero treated bleeding events, versus 0% (all had bleeds) on no prophylaxis; in a 48-participant intraindividual comparison, emicizumab bleeding rate was 68% lower than participants' own prior factor VIII prophylaxis (P<0.001). HAVEN 1 (patients WITH factor VIII inhibitors; Oldenburg J et al, N Engl J Med 2017;377:809-18, PMID 28691557, N=109): annualized bleeding rate 2.9 events (95% CI, 1.7-5.0) with emicizumab versus 23.3 events (95% CI, 12.3-43.9) with no prophylaxis -- 87% lower (P<0.001); 63% of emicizumab-treated participants had zero bleeds versus 6% on no prophylaxis; in a 24-participant intraindividual comparison, emicizumab was 79% lower than prior bypassing-agent prophylaxis (P<0.001).
hemoa_emicizumab_medicines.reason_why: Emicizumab is a bispecific antibody engineered to bind and bring together activated factor IX and factor X simultaneously, physically substituting for the bridging function normally performed by activated factor VIII -- because it is a synthetic antibody rather than the factor VIII protein itself, it is not recognized or neutralized by anti-factor-VIII inhibitor antibodies, which is why it works equally well in patients with and without inhibitors, and because it has a long half-life (~4-5 weeks) it needs only once-weekly to once-monthly subcutaneous dosing rather than intravenous infusion 2-3 times per week.
hemoa_emicizumab_medicines.important_caveat: Does not treat breakthrough bleeds by itself -- factor VIII (in non-inhibitor patients) or bypassing agents (in inhibitor patients) are still needed for acute bleeding episodes; concomitant use of activated prothrombin complex concentrate (FEIBA) with emicizumab carries a real, labelled thrombotic microangiopathy and thrombosis risk (observed in the HAVEN 1 trial in patients receiving multiple aPCC infusions for breakthrough bleeding) and requires careful dosing guidance.
hemoa_emicizumab_medicines.source: Mahlangu J et al, N Engl J Med 2018;379:811-22, PMID 30157389; Oldenburg J et al, N Engl J Med 2017;377:809-18, PMID 28691557
hemoa_emicizumab_medicines.confidence: high (two large, randomized/controlled phase 3 trials with concordant, statistically robust results)

hemoa_gene_therapy_medicines.name: Valoctocogene Roxaparvovec -- Real Single-Infusion AAV5 Gene Therapy, Durable but Honestly Waning Endogenous Factor VIII Production
hemoa_gene_therapy_medicines.type: Real one-time intravenous AAV5-vector gene-transfer biologic, FDA/EMA-approved for adult men with severe haemophilia A without factor VIII inhibitors or pre-existing anti-AAV5 antibodies
hemoa_gene_therapy_medicines.effectiveness: See curative_option.real_gener8_1_trial_data above for full year-1 and year-5 GENEr8-1 numbers: year 1, mean factor VIII activity +41.9 IU/dL (median +22.9 IU/dL), 98.6% reduction in factor VIII concentrate use, 83.8% reduction in treated-bleed ABR (all P<0.001, N=134); year 5 (final), mean factor VIII activity 13.7 IU/dL (median 6.2 IU/dL), 83.3% sustained ABR reduction for treated bleeds, 77.8% of rollover participants with zero treated bleeds, but 25/134 (18.7%) had resumed prophylaxis by the 5-year cutoff due to waning individual factor levels.
hemoa_gene_therapy_medicines.reason_why: The vector delivers a B-domain-deleted human factor VIII complementary DNA under a liver-selective promoter into hepatocytes, where it is transcribed and translated to produce factor VIII endogenously -- because the vector DNA largely persists as an episome (non-integrating) in post-mitotic hepatocyte nuclei, expression can be very durable, but because episomal DNA is gradually diluted as hepatocytes turn over and divide, and because AAV vector-driven expression is known to attenuate with time in other AAV gene-therapy programmes, factor VIII output honestly declines gradually over years in a real minority of patients rather than remaining fixed at the initial peak.
hemoa_gene_therapy_medicines.important_caveat: Only approved for adult men without pre-existing anti-AAV5 antibodies and without a history of factor VIII inhibitors; elevated liver transaminases occurred in 85.8% of participants in year 1 (managed with immunosuppressants) and in 51 of 129 participants (39.5%) still being followed in year 5 (managed without immunosuppressants); a single infusion cannot currently be repeated if effect wanes, because pre-existing anti-AAV5 antibodies from the first dose would neutralize a second vector dose.
hemoa_gene_therapy_medicines.source: Ozelo MC et al, N Engl J Med 2022;386:1013-25, PMID 35294811; Leavitt AD, Ozelo MC et al, Res Pract Thromb Haemost 2026;10(3), PMID 42064204
hemoa_gene_therapy_medicines.confidence: high for the trial numbers themselves (large, prospective, phase 3, 5-year completed follow-up); moderate for long-term (>5 year) durability, since real data beyond 5 years is not yet available

hemoa_on_demand_factor_viii_medicines.name: On-Demand (Episodic) Factor VIII Replacement for Acute Bleeding Episodes -- Real High Single-Injection Success, Distinct From Prophylactic Strategy
hemoa_on_demand_factor_viii_medicines.type: Real acute/rescue-treatment injectable replacement biologic, used either as the sole strategy (older/lower-resource settings) or as breakthrough-bleed treatment on top of prophylaxis
hemoa_on_demand_factor_viii_medicines.effectiveness: XTEND-1 on-demand analysis (efanesoctocog alfa; Fischer K et al, Am J Hematol 2025, PMID 39927501): among 362 treated bleeding episodes (268 occurring during the on-demand treatment arm), a single injection was sufficient to resolve 97% (350/362) of treated bleeding episodes, no bleeding episode required more than 3 injections, and 95% of evaluable injections were rated 'excellent' or 'good' hemostatic response; median total dose was 50.9 IU/kg per bleeding episode. This is real, honestly distinct from the prophylactic-strategy numbers reported above (hemoa_prophylactic_factor_viii_medicines) -- on-demand treatment resolves individual bleeds effectively but, per the Manco-Johnson 2007 trial, does not by itself prevent the cumulative joint damage that prophylaxis prevents.
hemoa_on_demand_factor_viii_medicines.reason_why: For an acute bleed, raising circulating factor VIII activity above the roughly 30-50 IU/dL haemostatic threshold (higher for major bleeds/surgery) directly restores the ability to generate a stable fibrin clot at the site of vascular injury -- because factor VIII acts as a cofactor at a specific, well-defined point in the intrinsic coagulation pathway, dosing can be titrated by target activity level and bleed severity, which is why the large majority of bleeds resolve after a single correctly-dosed infusion.
hemoa_on_demand_factor_viii_medicines.important_caveat: On-demand treatment alone, without prophylaxis, allows recurrent subclinical joint bleeding to accumulate over years, leading to haemophilic arthropathy (per Manco-Johnson 2007, 45% of episodically-treated boys had abnormal joint MRI by age 6 versus 7% on prophylaxis) -- on-demand treatment is the correct strategy for breakthrough bleeds and acute trauma, not a substitute for prophylaxis in severe disease.
hemoa_on_demand_factor_viii_medicines.source: Fischer K et al (XTEND-1 post hoc on-demand analysis), Am J Hematol 2025, PMID 39927501; Manco-Johnson MJ et al, N Engl J Med 2007;357:535-44, PMID 17687129
hemoa_on_demand_factor_viii_medicines.confidence: high (large phase 3 trial data for the modern on-demand efficacy figures)

hemoa_inhibitor_bypassing_agents_medicin.name: Bypassing Agents for Acute Bleeding in Patients With Factor VIII Inhibitors -- Real High Treatment-Success Rate
hemoa_inhibitor_bypassing_agents_medicin.type: Real acute/rescue-treatment biologics that bypass the factor VIII/IX step of the coagulation cascade, used when factor VIII replacement is neutralized by inhibitor antibodies
hemoa_inhibitor_bypassing_agents_medicin.effectiveness: PERSEPT 2 (eptacog beta/Sevenfact in children <12 years with haemophilia A or B and inhibitors; Kenet G et al, Haemophilia 2022;28:551-60, PMID 35475308, N=25, 546 bleeding episodes): treatment success (haemostasis rated 'excellent'/'good' without needing additional agent) was 65% (75 microgram/kg initial dose) and 60% (225 microgram/kg initial dose) at 12 hours, rising to 97% and 98% respectively by 24 hours. FEIBA-vs-NovoSeven comparative trial (FENOC study; Astermark J et al, Blood 2007;109:546-51, PMID 16990605, N=48 participants/96 joint-bleed episodes): both agents showed a similar hemostatic effect on joint bleeds; the pre-specified statistical equivalence bound was not formally met (95% CI for the difference in reported efficacy, -11.4% to 15.7%; P=0.059), meaning the trial could not declare the two bypassing agents statistically equivalent, though neither was shown superior. Real-world FEIBA Global Outcome study (Konkle BA et al, Ther Adv Hematol 2023;14, PMID 37529276, N=50 inhibitor patients, 4-year observation): mean annualized bleeding rate on aPCC/FEIBA prophylaxis was 6.82 (vs 10.94 on on-demand aPCC), consistent with real long-term effectiveness in routine practice.
specific_drugs: Recombinant activated factor VII / eptacog alfa (NovoSeven RT)
Recombinant activated factor VII / eptacog beta (Sevenfact)
hemoa_inhibitor_bypassing_agents_medicin.reason_why: Bypassing agents restore haemostasis without requiring factor VIII at all: aPCC supplies a mixture of activated and non-activated vitamin-K-dependent clotting factors (II, VII, IX, X) that collectively drive thrombin generation downstream of the factor VIII/IX step, while recombinant activated factor VII directly activates factor X on the surface of activated platelets at the bleeding site at pharmacologic concentrations, bypassing the need for the factor VIII-IXa complex entirely -- this is exactly why both classes remain effective even when a patient has high-titer neutralizing antibodies against factor VIII.
hemoa_inhibitor_bypassing_agents_medicin.important_caveat: Bypassing agents are honestly less predictable and generally less effective bleed-for-bleed than direct factor VIII replacement in a non-inhibitor patient (compare the 97-98% 24-hour success above with on-demand factor VIII's 97% single-injection resolution -- similar headline numbers, but bypassing agents more often require multiple doses and closer monitoring); concomitant use of aPCC with emicizumab carries a real, labelled thrombotic microangiopathy/thrombosis risk. Immune tolerance induction (below) is the only approach that eliminates the underlying inhibitor rather than working around it.
hemoa_inhibitor_bypassing_agents_medicin.source: Kenet G et al, Haemophilia 2022;28:551-60, PMID 35475308; Astermark J et al, Blood 2007;109:546-51, PMID 16990605; Konkle BA et al, Ther Adv Hematol 2023;14, PMID 37529276
hemoa_inhibitor_bypassing_agents_medicin.confidence: high for eptacog beta PERSEPT 2 and FENOC (randomized/prospective trials); moderate for the FEIBA GO real-world figures (observational, N=50, no randomized comparator)

hemoa_immune_tolerance_induction_procedu.name: Immune Tolerance Induction (ITI) -- Real Protocol to Eradicate Factor VIII Inhibitors, Not Just Work Around Them
hemoa_immune_tolerance_induction_procedu.type: Real, guideline-standard protocol of regular (often daily) high-dose factor VIII infusion over months to years, intended to retrain the immune system into tolerance rather than to treat an acute bleed
hemoa_immune_tolerance_induction_procedu.effectiveness: International Immune Tolerance Study (Hay CRM & DiMichele DM, Blood 2012;119:1335-44, PMID 22101900), the real landmark randomized dose-comparison trial in 115 'good-risk' high-titer inhibitor patients: 66 of 115 subjects reached a defined study endpoint before the trial was stopped early for safety/futility reasons in the low-dose arm; among those 66, success (inhibitor eradication with normalized factor VIII recovery) was achieved in 46 (69.7%), partial response in 3 (4.5%), and failure in 17 (25.8%) -- honestly, this 69.7% is the success rate among patients who reached a defined endpoint, not the full intention-to-treat cohort (46 of the full 115 enrolled = 40.0% strict ITT success, reflecting that 49 patients had not yet reached an endpoint when the trial closed rather than that they had failed). High-dose (200 IU/kg/day) and low-dose (50 IU/kg three times weekly) regimens did not differ in success rate (24/58 low-dose vs 22/57 high-dose, P=0.909), but high-dose ITI achieved negative inhibitor titer and normal factor VIII recovery significantly faster, and low-dose-arm patients bled significantly more often during induction (odds ratio 2.2, P=0.0019) -- the early bleed rate fell by 90% once a negative inhibitor titer was achieved on either regimen.
specific_drugs: High-dose or low-dose factor VIII concentrate (Advate, Hemofil-M, or equivalent -- same products as prophylaxis/on-demand, used at a dedicated ITI dosing schedule)
Rituximab (Rituxan) -- real adjunct used off-label in some refractory ITI protocols to deplete B cells and support tolerance induction, though this is not itself an FDA-approved ITI indication
hemoa_immune_tolerance_induction_procedu.reason_why: Repeated, sustained exposure to factor VIII antigen at a defined dose is believed to drive the immune system toward regulatory tolerance (anergy/deletion of factor-VIII-reactive B- and T-cell clones) rather than continued antibody production, gradually lowering the inhibitor titer to undetectable and restoring normal factor VIII pharmacokinetic recovery -- this directly targets the immunological root cause of the inhibitor, which is why successful ITI, unlike bypassing agents, allows the patient to return to normal factor VIII prophylaxis/on-demand treatment afterward.
hemoa_immune_tolerance_induction_procedu.important_caveat: Requires months to years of near-daily infusions, often via a central venous catheter in children, with real associated catheter-infection risk (124 catheter infections were reported across 41 of 115 subjects in the International ITI Study); a real minority of patients never achieve tolerance despite a full attempt (25.8% failure among those reaching an endpoint in the landmark trial above) and require lifelong management with emicizumab and/or bypassing agents instead.
hemoa_immune_tolerance_induction_procedu.source: Hay CRM & DiMichele DM (International Immune Tolerance Study Study Group), Blood 2012;119:1335-44, PMID 22101900
hemoa_immune_tolerance_induction_procedu.confidence: high (randomized, prospective, multicenter trial, though stopped early, which is itself disclosed in the source)

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These rows use real, differently-defined outcome metrics (annualized-bleed-rate reduction, MRI-confirmed normal-joint-structure rate, factor-VIII-activity-achievement/sustained-response, 24-hour bleed treatment-success rate, single-injection bleed-resolution rate, inhibitor-eradication success rate) placed on one comparative scale for consistency with this project's other entries -- they are NOT statistically equivalent or head-to-head-compared measures, and higher rank does NOT mean 'better drug' in an absolute sense; each row's metric field states exactly what was measured. Emicizumab and gene therapy numbers come from separate, non-head-to-head trials in patients with somewhat different baseline treatment histories. The gene-therapy row uses the year-1 GENEr8-1 primary-endpoint figure; the real, honestly lower year-5 durability figure (83.3%, still a sustained reduction) is reported in the curative_option and exhaustive_medicine_survey sections. The bypassing-agent FENOC comparative trial (FEIBA vs NovoSeven) is left without a single numeric effectiveness_pct row because its published abstract reports only a confidence interval for the DIFFERENCE between the two agents' efficacy percentages (-11.4% to 15.7%, P=.059), not each agent's own absolute hemostatic-success percentage -- this is an honest gap in what that specific abstract reports, not a fabricated zero; the real numeric bypassing-agent figure used below instead comes from the eptacog beta PERSEPT 2 trial, which does report an absolute treatment-success percentage.
