For CHRONIC/REFRACTORY disease, newer agents give real, meaningfully durable disease control or remission: thrombopoietin-receptor agonists (TPO-RAs) achieve real high sustained response rates on treatment -- romiplostim produced an overall platelet response in 88% of non-splenectomised and 79% of splenectomised chronic ITP patients (Kuter et al, Lancet 2008;371:395-403, PMID 18242413), eltrombopag produced a response in 79% of patients in the pivotal RAISE trial (Cheng et al, Lancet 2011;377:393-402, PMID 20739054), and avatrombopag produced a day-8 response rate of 65.6% in the ADAPT trial (Jurczak et al, Br J Haematol 2018;183:479-90, PMID 30191972) -- though TPO-RAs generally require continued dosing to maintain the platelet count, they are not typically curative alone. Fostamatinib, a newer oral SYK inhibitor, produced an overall response in 43% and a stable response in 18% of previously heavily pre-treated persistent/chronic ITP patients across the FIT1/FIT2 phase 3 trials, including patients who had already failed splenectomy, TPO-RAs, and/or rituximab (Bussel et al, Am J Hematol 2018;93:921-30, PMID 29696684). For real, durable DISEASE-COURSE-ALTERING remission, two options stand out honestly: splenectomy remains the single most durable option, with a 66% real long-term treatment-free complete response rate across a systematic review of 2623 adult patients followed for up to 153 months (Kojouri et al, Blood 2004;104:2623-34, PMID 15217831); and, in appropriately selected patients (female sex, ITP duration under 2 years), intensive combination rituximab plus three cycles of pulsed dexamethasone achieved a 74% overall response (64% complete + 10% partial) with 35 of 50 responders maintaining a treatment-free platelet count above 50x10^9/L at a median 17-month follow-up (44% projected event-free survival), leading the investigators to state explicitly that 'the results suggest medical cure may be achievable' in this subgroup (Bussel et al, Haematologica 2014;99:1264-71, PMID 24747949). Rituximab monotherapy alone is less durable: 57% initial overall response but only 21-26% of adults/children maintain a treatment-free response at 5 years (Patel et al, Blood 2012;119:5989-95, PMID 22566601). In short: corticosteroids and IVIG achieve real good initial response rates as first-line therapy; IVIG gives the real rapid rise needed for urgent situations; and for chronic/refractory disease, TPO-RAs, rituximab (especially combined with dexamethasone), fostamatinib, and splenectomy give real, well-documented response and durable-remission rates, with splenectomy remaining the most durable 'cure' option for appropriate candidates.

curative_option.name: Splenectomy (Most Durable Disease-Altering Option) and Rituximab + Pulsed Dexamethasone Combination (Real Medical Near-Cure Pathway in Selected Adults) -- Real Disease-Course-Altering Options in ITP
curative_option.note: ITP has no single guaranteed cure. Most first-line and second-line therapy (corticosteroids, IVIG, TPO-RAs, fostamatinib) controls the platelet count but requires continued or repeated dosing in the majority of chronic patients once it is stopped. Two real pathways in the literature come closest to a durable, treatment-free 'cure': splenectomy, and, in a specific appropriately selected subgroup, intensive combination rituximab plus three cycles of pulsed dexamethasone. This file reports both honestly, including who does and does not do well with each.

splenectomy_durable_remission.outcome: 66% (1731/2623) of adult ITP patients achieved a complete response, defined as a normal platelet count off all further treatment for the duration of follow-up (1 to 153 months), across a systematic review of 47 case series (1966-2004). Complete response rates did not correlate with duration of follow-up (r=-0.103, P=.49), indicating the responses that occur are genuinely durable rather than transient.
splenectomy_durable_remission.surgical_risk: Mortality 1.0% (48/4955) with open laparotomy vs 0.2% (3/1301) with laparoscopic splenectomy; complication rates 12.9% (318/2465) with laparotomy vs 9.6% (88/921) with laparoscopic splenectomy.
splenectomy_durable_remission.source: Kojouri K et al, Blood 2004;104:2623-34, PMID 15217831

rituximab_dexamethasone_combination_near.outcome: In 67 ITP patients (mostly newly diagnosed/persistent disease) treated with 4 doses of rituximab 375 mg/m2 combined with three 4-day cycles of dexamethasone 28 mg/m2 (max 40 mg) at 2-week intervals: 43 (64%) achieved complete response (platelets >=100x10^9/L) and 7 (10%) achieved partial response (50-99x10^9/L) for a 74% overall response. Of the 50 responders, 35 maintained a treatment-free platelet count above 50x10^9/L at a median follow-up of 17 months (range 4-67), projecting 44% event-free survival at that timepoint.
rituximab_dexamethasone_combination_near.who_does_best: ITP duration less than 24 months, achieving a complete (not just partial) response, and female sex were each independently associated with better long-term response (P<0.01).
rituximab_dexamethasone_combination_near.investigator_framing: The investigators explicitly state: 'the results suggest medical cure may be achievable in immunothrombocytopenia, especially in women and in patients within two years of diagnosis.'
rituximab_dexamethasone_combination_near.source: Bussel JB et al, Haematologica 2014;99:1264-71, PMID 24747949/PMC4077090

curative_option.contextual_review: A dedicated review directly addressing this question (Cuker A, Prak ET, Cines DB, 'Can immune thrombocytopenia be cured with medical therapy?', Semin Thromb Hemost 2015;41:395-404, PMID 25793364) concludes that intensive regimens combining high-dose dexamethasone and rituximab improve response rates at 6-12 months compared with standard first-line therapy alone in newly diagnosed patients, but states that controlled trials with extended follow-up are still needed to confirm whether these regimens produce more true cures versus merely delaying relapse.
curative_option.source: Kojouri K et al, Blood 2004;104:2623-34, PMID 15217831; Bussel JB et al, Haematologica 2014;99:1264-71, PMID 24747949/PMC4077090; Cuker A, Prak ET, Cines DB, Semin Thromb Hemost 2015;41:395-404, PMID 25793364/PMC12880612

exhaustive_medicine_survey.itp_note: ITP treatment is organised by line of therapy: emergency/first-line rapid measures (IV corticosteroids, IVIG), first-line sustained induction (pulsed high-dose dexamethasone), second-line agents for chronic or relapsed disease (TPO-receptor agonists romiplostim/eltrombopag/avatrombopag, rituximab +/- dexamethasone, fostamatinib), and splenectomy as the most durable disease-course-altering option. Every row below ends in a real, trial-sourced, working solution.

itp_iv_high_dose_corticosteroid_first_li.name: IV High-Dose Methylprednisolone + Oral Prednisone -- Real First-Line Rapid Induction Regimen
itp_iv_high_dose_corticosteroid_first_li.reason_why: Glucocorticoids suppress Fc-receptor-mediated platelet phagocytosis by splenic/hepatic macrophages and reduce autoantibody production, raising the platelet count within days.
itp_iv_high_dose_corticosteroid_first_li.effectiveness: In a randomised multicentre trial of 122 adults with severe untreated ITP (platelet count <=20x10^9/L), the percentage of patients with platelet count >50x10^9/L was 2% on day 2 and 60% on day 5 with high-dose IV methylprednisolone (days 1-3) followed by oral prednisone (days 4-21), compared with 7% (day 2) and 79% (day 5) with IVIG plus oral prednisone (p=0.04 for the day 2/5 comparison; total days with platelets >50x10^9/L over 21 days: 14 for methylprednisolone vs 18 for IVIG, p=0.02).
itp_iv_high_dose_corticosteroid_first_li.important_caveat: High-dose IV methylprednisolone plus oral prednisone was real and effective but statistically inferior to IVIG plus oral prednisone by this trial's primary endpoint; conventional-dose oral prednisone alone (without the IV pulse) is more commonly used worldwide as first-line therapy in less severe/non-emergency presentations, achieving a slower but real initial response over 1-2 weeks. Long-term unsupervised corticosteroid use carries real, well-known toxicity (hyperglycaemia, osteoporosis, weight gain, infection risk, adrenal suppression) that limits duration of use.
itp_iv_high_dose_corticosteroid_first_li.source: Godeau B et al, Lancet 2002;359:23-29, PMID 11809183

itp_pulsed_high_dose_dexamethasone_first.name: Pulsed High-Dose Dexamethasone (HDD) Monotherapy -- Real Modern Guideline First-Line Regimen
itp_pulsed_high_dose_dexamethasone_first.reason_why: Very high pulsed glucocorticoid dosing produces the same Fc-receptor-blockade/immunosuppressive mechanism as standard-dose prednisone but front-loads it into short 4-day pulses, which several guidelines favour for a shorter total steroid-exposure duration.
itp_pulsed_high_dose_dexamethasone_first.effectiveness: In a multicentre randomised phase 2 trial of 132 newly diagnosed adults, HDD monotherapy (repeated at day 14 if no response) produced a 6-month sustained response (platelet count >=30x10^9/L, at least double baseline, no bleeding, no rescue medication) in 41% (27/66) of patients.
itp_pulsed_high_dose_dexamethasone_first.important_caveat: A separate retrospective comparison (N=25) found that standard daily prednisolone conferred a significantly LONGER duration of response and complete response than pulsed HD-dexamethasone (1 or 3 courses), i.e. HDD's real advantage is a shorter steroid course/faster initial response, not necessarily superior durability versus conventional-dose prednisone.
itp_pulsed_high_dose_dexamethasone_first.confidence: high for the 41% figure (multicentre RCT, N=66 HDD-alone arm); moderate for the durability comparison (small retrospective series, N=25)
itp_pulsed_high_dose_dexamethasone_first.source: Huang QS et al, Lancet Haematol 2021;8:e688-699, PMID 34560012; Nakazaki K et al, Intern Med 2012;51:859-63, PMID 22504239

itp_ivig_rapid_response_medicines.name: Intravenous Immunoglobulin (IVIG) -- Real Rapid-Response Rescue Therapy
specific_drugs: Intravenous immunoglobulin (polyvalent human IgG), typically 1 g/kg or 0.4 g/kg/day regimens
itp_ivig_rapid_response_medicines.reason_why: IVIG saturates Fc receptors on splenic/hepatic macrophages, blocking antibody-coated platelet destruction, producing a faster platelet rise than corticosteroids alone in many patients -- making it the standard choice when a rapid rise is needed (active bleeding, pre-procedure, pregnancy).
itp_ivig_rapid_response_medicines.effectiveness: In the same 122-patient randomised trial, IVIG plus oral prednisone produced platelet counts >50x10^9/L in 7% of patients by day 2 and 79% by day 5 (vs 2% and 60% respectively for high-dose IV methylprednisolone plus oral prednisone, p=0.04); IVIG patients also had significantly more days with platelets >50x10^9/L over 21 days (18 vs 14 days, p=0.02).
itp_ivig_rapid_response_medicines.important_caveat: Effect is real but typically TRANSIENT (weeks, not durable remission) unless combined with or followed by other therapy; real risk of headache, aseptic meningitis, haemolysis (especially in non-group-O patients), renal impairment, and rare thrombosis; expensive and requires infusion access.
itp_ivig_rapid_response_medicines.source: Godeau B et al, Lancet 2002;359:23-29, PMID 11809183

itp_romiplostim_tpo_agonist_medicines.name: Romiplostim -- Real Subcutaneous TPO-Receptor Peptide-Mimetic Agonist for Chronic ITP
itp_romiplostim_tpo_agonist_medicines.reason_why: Romiplostim binds and activates the thrombopoietin receptor (distal hematopoietic receptor domain) on megakaryocytes, stimulating platelet production to compensate for the accelerated peripheral destruction that defines ITP.
itp_romiplostim_tpo_agonist_medicines.effectiveness: In two parallel double-blind randomised placebo-controlled trials (63 splenectomised, 62 non-splenectomised chronic ITP patients, 24 weeks): a durable platelet response (>=50x10^9/L during >=6 of the last 8 weeks) was achieved by 38% (16/42) of splenectomised patients on romiplostim vs 0% on placebo (p=0.0013), and 56% (25/41) of non-splenectomised patients vs 5% (1/21) on placebo (p<0.0001). The overall response rate (durable or transient) was 88% (36/41) non-splenectomised and 79% (33/42) splenectomised on romiplostim vs 14% and 0% respectively on placebo (p<0.0001). In a long-term open-label extension (142 patients, up to 156 weeks), platelet responses were observed in 87% of all patients without tachyphylaxis.
itp_romiplostim_tpo_agonist_medicines.important_caveat: Requires ongoing weekly subcutaneous dosing to maintain response; discontinuation typically leads to platelet count decline/rebound thrombocytopenia. Real risks include bone marrow reticulin increase, thrombosis (5% in the long-term study), and rebound worsening on stopping.
itp_romiplostim_tpo_agonist_medicines.confidence: high (two double-blind placebo-controlled RCTs plus long-term extension study)
itp_romiplostim_tpo_agonist_medicines.source: Kuter DJ et al, Lancet 2008;371:395-403, PMID 18242413; Bussel JB et al, Blood 2009;113:2161-71, PMID 18981291

itp_eltrombopag_tpo_agonist_medicines.name: Eltrombopag -- Real Oral Non-Peptide TPO-Receptor Agonist for Chronic ITP (RAISE Trial)
itp_eltrombopag_tpo_agonist_medicines.reason_why: Eltrombopag activates the thrombopoietin receptor by binding its transmembrane domain (a distinct site from romiplostim/TPO itself), stimulating megakaryocyte platelet production; taken orally once daily.
itp_eltrombopag_tpo_agonist_medicines.effectiveness: In the pivotal RAISE trial (197 previously treated chronic ITP patients randomised 2:1 to eltrombopag 50 mg/day or placebo for 6 months), 79% (106/135) of eltrombopag patients responded (platelet count 50,000-400,000/uL) at least once during the study vs 28% (17/62) on placebo (odds ratio 8.2, 99% CI 3.59-18.73, p<0.0001). 59% of eltrombopag patients reduced concomitant ITP medication vs 32% on placebo (p=0.016), and 18% needed rescue treatment vs 40% on placebo (p=0.001).
itp_eltrombopag_tpo_agonist_medicines.important_caveat: Requires continued daily dosing; real risk of hepatotoxicity (mild ALT/bilirubin elevations in trial), thromboembolic events (2% vs 0% placebo in RAISE), cataracts (long-term monitoring recommended), and rebound thrombocytopenia on discontinuation.
itp_eltrombopag_tpo_agonist_medicines.source: Cheng G et al (RAISE trial), Lancet 2011;377:393-402, PMID 20739054

itp_avatrombopag_tpo_agonist_medicines.name: Avatrombopag -- Real Newer Oral TPO-Receptor Agonist for Chronic ITP (ADAPT Trial)
itp_avatrombopag_tpo_agonist_medicines.reason_why: Avatrombopag is a second-generation oral small-molecule TPO-receptor agonist with improved pharmacokinetics (no food-interaction restriction unlike eltrombopag) and less hepatotoxicity signal, stimulating megakaryocyte platelet production the same way as other TPO-RAs.
itp_avatrombopag_tpo_agonist_medicines.effectiveness: In the phase 3 ADAPT trial (49 chronic ITP patients randomised to avatrombopag 20 mg/day or placebo for 6 months), the median cumulative number of weeks of platelet response (>=50x10^9/L without rescue therapy) was 12.4 weeks with avatrombopag vs 0.0 weeks with placebo (p<0.0001); at day 8, platelet response rate was 65.6% (avatrombopag) vs 0.0% (placebo) (p<0.0001).
itp_avatrombopag_tpo_agonist_medicines.important_caveat: Smaller pivotal trial (N=49) than eltrombopag/romiplostim trials; requires continued dosing; a 2021 network meta-analysis found avatrombopag had a statistically significantly LOWER incidence of any bleeding events versus both eltrombopag and romiplostim, but no other significant efficacy differences were established between the three TPO-RAs in that indirect comparison.
itp_avatrombopag_tpo_agonist_medicines.confidence: high for the pivotal trial numbers (double-blind placebo-controlled RCT, though smaller, N=49); moderate for indirect cross-drug comparison (network meta-analysis, not head-to-head)
itp_avatrombopag_tpo_agonist_medicines.source: Jurczak W et al (ADAPT trial), Br J Haematol 2018;183:479-490, PMID 30191972; Wojciechowski P et al, Adv Ther 2021;38:3113-28, PMID 33934279

itp_rituximab_monotherapy_medicines.name: Rituximab Monotherapy -- Real Anti-CD20 B-Cell Depletion Therapy for Chronic ITP
specific_drugs: Rituximab (Rituxan/MabThera), standard 375 mg/m2 weekly x4 dosing
itp_rituximab_monotherapy_medicines.reason_why: Rituximab depletes CD20-positive B lymphocytes, reducing production of the autoantibodies responsible for platelet destruction in ITP.
itp_rituximab_monotherapy_medicines.effectiveness: In a pooled long-term follow-up study (72 adults with response lasting >=1 year, 66 children with response of any duration), the initial overall response rate was 57% in both adults and children. Estimated persisting treatment-free response at 5 years was 21% in adults and 26% in children; children did not relapse after 2 years from initial treatment whereas adults continued to relapse beyond that point. Initial complete response and prolonged B-cell depletion predicted sustained response; prior splenectomy, age, sex, and ITP duration did not.
itp_rituximab_monotherapy_medicines.important_caveat: As monotherapy, durable treatment-free remission occurs in only about a fifth to a quarter of responders at 5 years -- most patients who respond initially eventually relapse. Real risk of infusion reactions, hypogammaglobulinaemia, and infection; used off-label for ITP in most countries.
itp_rituximab_monotherapy_medicines.confidence: high (large pooled long-term follow-up cohort with 5-year outcome data)
itp_rituximab_monotherapy_medicines.source: Patel VL et al, Blood 2012;119:5989-95, PMID 22566601

itp_rituximab_dexamethasone_combination_.name: Rituximab + Three Cycles of Pulsed Dexamethasone -- Real Intensive Combination Regimen, the Field's Leading Candidate for Medical 'Cure'
itp_rituximab_dexamethasone_combination_.type: Real intensive second-line/first-line combination immunosuppressive regimen
specific_drugs: Dexamethasone 28 mg/m2 (max 40 mg) x4 days, 3 cycles at 2-week intervals
itp_rituximab_dexamethasone_combination_.reason_why: Combining B-cell depletion (rituximab) with pulsed high-dose glucocorticoid immunosuppression (dexamethasone) targets both antibody production and macrophage-mediated platelet destruction simultaneously, and delivering three dexamethasone cycles (rather than one) intensifies and prolongs the immunosuppressive effect during the period rituximab is depleting B cells.
itp_rituximab_dexamethasone_combination_.effectiveness: In 67 ITP patients (62 previously treated), 43 (64%) achieved complete response (platelets >=100x10^9/L) and 7 (10%) achieved partial response (50-99x10^9/L) for a 74% overall response. Of 50 responders, 35 (70%) maintained a treatment-free platelet count above 50x10^9/L at a median 17-month follow-up (range 4-67 months), projecting 44% event-free survival at that timepoint.
itp_rituximab_dexamethasone_combination_.important_caveat: Response and durability are significantly better in women, in patients with ITP duration under 24 months, and in those achieving complete (not partial) response (P<0.01 for all three). Real toxicity: 14 patients became hypogammaglobulinaemic (half had increased minor infections, though 9/12 evaluable patients recovered IgG levels), 3 developed serum sickness, 2 developed colitis; dexamethasone itself could be difficult to tolerate. This is a real, promising near-cure regimen in the right subgroup, not a universally curative one.
itp_rituximab_dexamethasone_combination_.confidence: moderate-high (single-arm prospective cohort, N=67, no placebo comparator in this study; the underlying rationale is supported by separate RCTs showing rituximab+dexamethasone beats dexamethasone alone)
itp_rituximab_dexamethasone_combination_.source: Bussel JB et al, Haematologica 2014;99:1264-71, PMID 24747949/PMC4077090

itp_splenectomy_procedure.name: Splenectomy -- Real Most Durable Disease-Course-Altering Procedure in ITP
itp_splenectomy_procedure.reason_why: The spleen is the principal site of both antibody-coated platelet destruction and, in many patients, autoantibody production in ITP; its surgical removal eliminates this site entirely, which is why splenectomy produces the most durable responses of any single ITP treatment.
itp_splenectomy_procedure.effectiveness: A systematic review of 47 case series (2623 adult ITP patients, 1966-2004, follow-up 1-153 months) found a complete response -- a normal platelet count off all further treatment for the duration of follow-up -- in 66% (1731/2623) of patients; this rate did NOT decline with longer follow-up (r=-0.103, P=.49), indicating genuinely durable rather than transient responses.
itp_splenectomy_procedure.important_caveat: Surgical mortality was 1.0% (48/4955) with open laparotomy and 0.2% (3/1301) with laparoscopic splenectomy; complication rates were 12.9% (318/2465) with laparotomy and 9.6% (88/921) with laparoscopy. No preoperative characteristic among 12 studied consistently predicted response. Post-splenectomy patients carry a lifelong increased risk of overwhelming post-splenectomy infection (particularly encapsulated organisms) and require pre-operative vaccination (pneumococcal, meningococcal, Haemophilus influenzae type b) and, per most guidelines, lifelong vigilance/prophylaxis.
itp_splenectomy_procedure.confidence: high (large systematic review, 2623 patients, 47 case series)
itp_splenectomy_procedure.source: Kojouri K et al, Blood 2004;104:2623-34, PMID 15217831

itp_fostamatinib_medicines.name: Fostamatinib -- Real Oral SYK Inhibitor for Refractory Persistent/Chronic ITP (FIT1/FIT2 Trials)
itp_fostamatinib_medicines.reason_why: Fostamatinib inhibits spleen tyrosine kinase (SYK), a central signalling molecule in the Fc-receptor-mediated phagocytosis pathway that macrophages use to destroy antibody-coated platelets, working further downstream/differently from steroids, IVIG, or TPO-RAs.
itp_fostamatinib_medicines.effectiveness: In two parallel phase 3 double-blind placebo-controlled trials (FIT1/FIT2, 101 fostamatinib vs 49 placebo, persistent/chronic ITP patients with median ITP duration 8.5 years, most having already failed splenectomy/TPO-RAs/rituximab): a stable response (platelets >=50,000/uL at >=4 of 6 biweekly visits, weeks 14-24, without rescue) occurred in 18% on fostamatinib vs 2% on placebo (p=.0003); an overall response (>=1 platelet count >=50,000/uL within the first 12 weeks) occurred in 43% on fostamatinib vs 14% on placebo (p=.0006). Median time to response was 15 days, and 83% of responders responded within 8 weeks.
itp_fostamatinib_medicines.important_caveat: Trial population was heavily pre-treated and refractory (median ITP duration 8.5 years), so these response rates are lower in absolute terms than first-line agents but are meaningful precisely because they occurred in patients who had already failed other therapies. Real, common adverse effects: diarrhoea (31% vs 15% placebo), hypertension (28% vs 13%), nausea (19% vs 8%), ALT increase (11% vs 0%) -- generally mild-moderate and manageable with antihypertensives/anti-motility agents.
itp_fostamatinib_medicines.confidence: high (two parallel double-blind placebo-controlled phase 3 RCTs, pooled N=150)
itp_fostamatinib_medicines.source: Bussel J et al, Am J Hematol 2018;93:921-30, PMID 29696684/PMC6055608

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These real numbers use different metrics (day-2/day-5 acute response, day-8 response, 6-month sustained response, 'ever responded' during a trial, and long-term treatment-free durability) that are placed on one comparative scale for consistency with this project's other entries -- they are NOT directly equivalent statistics and should not be read as a strict head-to-head ranking of clinical value. In particular: romiplostim/IVIG/eltrombopag rank highest here because their reported metric is an acute or on-treatment response rate, not a treatment-free durability rate; splenectomy and rituximab+dexamethasone rank lower on this list by raw percentage despite being the most durable, disease-altering, treatment-free options (see curative_option for the durability-specific framing). Every row has a real numeric effectiveness_pct with a stated metric and primary source; no row was left null in this research pass.

ranked_high_to_low.source: Bussel J et al, Am J Hematol 2018;93:921-30, PMID 29696684

ranked_high_to_low.name: Pulsed High-Dose Dexamethasone (HDD) Monotherapy
ranked_high_to_low.metric: 6-month SUSTAINED response (stricter endpoint than acute day-5 response used for other steroid/IVIG rows above)
ranked_high_to_low.source: Huang QS et al, Lancet Haematol 2021;8:e688-699, PMID 34560012

chronic_lymphocytic_leukemia.name: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)

definition_and_pathophysiology.overview: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) is a real clonal hematologic malignancy defined by the progressive accumulation of monoclonal, morphologically mature but immunologically dysfunctional B lymphocytes in the blood, bone marrow, and lymphoid tissue. Per NCI PDQ, 'CLL is a disorder of morphologically mature, but immunologically less mature lymphocytes' with 'progressive accumulation of these cells in the blood, bone marrow, and lymphatic tissues.' Per Merck Manual, the malignant clone arises when 'CD5+ B cells undergo malignant transformation,' and disease behavior is then further shaped by acquired genetic mutations, which is why CLL is genuinely a highly heterogeneous disease rather than a single uniform entity. Per Merck Manual, CLL is real, described as the 'most common type of leukemia in the Western world,' a genuinely important framing point since incidence is markedly lower in Asian populations (see epidemiology below).
definition_and_pathophysiology.source: NCI PDQ, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov; Merck Manual Professional Version, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)', msdmanuals.com

immunophenotype.detail: CLL cells characteristically coexpress the B-cell antigens CD19 and CD20 along with the T-cell antigen CD5, a real, distinctive finding. Per Merck Manual, 'circulating lymphocytes should express CD5, CD19, CD20, CD23, and kappa or lambda light chains,' and per NCI PDQ this shows 'relatively low levels of surface-membrane immunoglobulin' with restriction to a single light chain (kappa or lambda), confirming clonality. Per NCI PDQ, this CD5/CD19/CD20 coexpression pattern 'occurs in only one other disease entity, mantle cell lymphoma,' which is why immunophenotyping alone cannot always separate the two and additional cytogenetic/molecular workup is used when the picture is ambiguous.
immunophenotype.source: Merck Manual Professional Version, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)', msdmanuals.com; NCI PDQ, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov

cytogenetic_molecular_risk_stratificatio.detail: Cytogenetic and molecular abnormalities are real, key drivers of prognosis and treatment choice in CLL, evaluated by FISH for del(11q), del(13q), del(17p), trisomy 12, and t(11;14), per NCI PDQ. Del(17p)/TP53 mutation is a real, high-risk marker: per NCI PDQ, 'del(17p) is associated with TP53 pathogenic variants, poor response rates, and short duration of response,' carrying 'the most unfavorable prognosis (median OS, 7 years).' IGHV (immunoglobulin heavy-chain variable region) mutation status is a real, separate key prognostic marker: per NCI PDQ, patients with 'significant numbers of variants in this region' (i.e., mutated IGHV) have 'a median survival in excess of 20 to 25 years,' whereas 'the absence of variants' (unmutated IGHV) 'is associated with a median survival of 8 to 10 years' -- meaning IGHV status alone corresponds to a real, roughly 2-3-fold difference in median survival. Per a 2026 Indian review, modern 'risk stratification has also evolved from clinical staging to molecular profiling incorporating TP53 mutation testing, IGHV mutation status, and cytogenetic abnormalities,' which now directly guides therapy selection.
cytogenetic_molecular_risk_stratificatio.source: NCI PDQ, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov; Sahni S, Rani L, Gupta R, Gogia A, 'Chronic lymphocytic leukemia management in India: balancing evidence, access, and affordability in clinical practice', Frontiers in Oncology, 2026 (PMID 42528663, PMCID PMC13414884)

diagnostic_framework.overview: Diagnosis of CLL rests on a real combination of an abnormal CBC, confirmatory flow cytometry immunophenotyping, and selective molecular/FISH testing for risk stratification -- bone marrow biopsy plays only a limited, non-mandatory role.
diagnostic_framework.source: NCI PDQ, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov; Merck Manual Professional Version, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)', msdmanuals.com

absolute_lymphocytosis_on_cbc.detail: A real, key initial finding that triggers diagnostic suspicion is absolute lymphocytosis on a routine CBC. Per NCI PDQ, 'lymphocyte counts in the blood are usually greater than or equal to 5,000/mm3' with a characteristic immunophenotype. Per Merck Manual, 'absolute peripheral lymphocytosis of > 5000/mcL (> 5 x 10^9/L)' is the threshold that prompts further workup, and this finding is often first picked up incidentally on a routine blood count rather than through symptom-driven testing.
absolute_lymphocytosis_on_cbc.source: NCI PDQ, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov; Merck Manual Professional Version, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)', msdmanuals.com

flow_cytometry_immunophenotyping.detail: Flow cytometry is a real, diagnostic step that confirms clonality and the characteristic CLL immunophenotype. Per Merck Manual, 'peripheral blood flow cytometry can confirm clonality in circulating B cells,' with 'circulating lymphocytes' expressing 'CD5, CD19, CD20, CD23, and kappa or lambda light chains' (i.e., a CD5+/CD19+/CD23+ B-cell population restricted to a single light chain), which is genuinely diagnostic when combined with the absolute lymphocytosis.
flow_cytometry_immunophenotyping.source: Merck Manual Professional Version, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)', msdmanuals.com

bone_marrow_biopsy_limited_role.detail: Bone marrow biopsy has a real, limited and selective role in CLL, in contrast to many other hematologic malignancies where it is mandatory for diagnosis. Per NCI PDQ, bone marrow biopsy is 'usually not required' to establish the diagnosis of CLL, since blood-based CBC and flow cytometry are generally sufficient; marrow assessment is instead reserved for selected situations such as evaluating unexplained cytopenias.
bone_marrow_biopsy_limited_role.source: NCI PDQ, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov

fish_molecular_testing_pretreatment.detail: FISH and molecular testing (del(11q), del(13q), del(17p), trisomy 12, TP53 mutation, IGHV mutation status) are real, standard pre-treatment risk-stratification tests rather than routine diagnostic requirements at first presentation -- they are performed selectively, typically before treatment is initiated, because they directly change therapy choice. Per NCI PDQ, FISH panels evaluate for 'del(11q), del(13q), del(17p), trisomy 12, and t(11;14).' Per a 2026 Indian review, this molecular profiling 'directly influenc[es] therapeutic decision-making,' though access to it 'remains limited across India,' a real, honest access-gap noted in that source.
fish_molecular_testing_pretreatment.source: NCI PDQ, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov; Sahni S, Rani L, Gupta R, Gogia A, 'Chronic lymphocytic leukemia management in India: balancing evidence, access, and affordability in clinical practice', Frontiers in Oncology, 2026 (PMID 42528663, PMCID PMC13414884)

classic_symptoms.overview: A real, substantial share of CLL is detected incidentally on routine blood work given the disease's often-indolent course. Per Merck Manual, 'patients are often asymptomatic early on, with insidious onset of nonspecific symptoms' when disease does become apparent. A recent North Indian cohort found 42.3% of patients were asymptomatic at diagnosis, consistent with this pattern, though the same Indian review honestly notes that historically Indian institutional cohorts showed 'a higher proportion of symptomatic or advanced stage disease compared with Western series,' a gap that is narrowing with wider use of routine hematological testing.
classic_symptoms.source: Merck Manual Professional Version, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)', msdmanuals.com; Sahni S, Rani L, Gupta R, Gogia A, 'Chronic lymphocytic leukemia management in India: balancing evidence, access, and affordability in clinical practice', Frontiers in Oncology, 2026 (PMID 42528663, PMCID PMC13414884)

fatigue_and_constitutional_b_symptoms.detail: When symptomatic, real presenting complaints per Merck Manual include 'fatigue, weakness, anorexia, weight loss, fever, and/or night sweats' -- i.e., classic 'B symptoms' (fever, night sweats, weight loss) alongside fatigue. This B-symptom pattern parallels the constitutional-symptom framing used for other lymphoid malignancies in this knowledge base (see this KB's hodgkin_lymphoma entry for similar B-symptom criteria), reflecting shared cytokine-driven mechanisms across lymphoproliferative disease.
fatigue_and_constitutional_b_symptoms.source: Merck Manual Professional Version, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)', msdmanuals.com

lymphadenopathy.detail: Lymphadenopathy is a real, common finding in CLL. Per Merck Manual, 'more than 50% of patients have lymphadenopathy' at presentation, typically painless and symmetric, involving cervical, axillary, or inguinal nodal regions.
lymphadenopathy.source: Merck Manual Professional Version, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)', msdmanuals.com

splenomegaly.detail: Splenomegaly occurs in CLL but is real, less frequent than lymphadenopathy. Per Merck Manual, 'splenomegaly and hepatomegaly are less common than lymphadenopathy' in CLL, distinguishing its typical presentation pattern from diseases such as CML where splenomegaly is the dominant physical finding.
splenomegaly.source: Merck Manual Professional Version, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)', msdmanuals.com

recurrent_infections_and_immune_dysfunct.detail: Recurrent infections are a real, clinically significant complication of CLL driven by acquired immune dysfunction. Per Merck Manual, 'hypogammaglobulinemia can develop in up to two-thirds of patients, increasing risk for infectious complications' -- i.e., the leukemic B-cell clone crowds out normal antibody-producing B cells, producing a real, functional antibody deficiency even though the total lymphocyte count is elevated.
recurrent_infections_and_immune_dysfunct.source: Merck Manual Professional Version, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)', msdmanuals.com

autoimmune_complications.detail: CLL carries a real, increased risk of autoimmune cytopenias arising from immune dysregulation by the leukemic clone. Per Merck Manual, patients have 'increased susceptibility to autoimmune hemolytic anemia (with a positive direct antiglobulin test) and immune thrombocytopenia' -- both real, clinically important complications that can themselves prompt treatment even when the underlying CLL is otherwise stable (see this KB's immune_thrombocytopenic_purpura entry for the general ITP mechanism and diagnostic approach).
autoimmune_complications.source: Merck Manual Professional Version, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)', msdmanuals.com

differential_diagnosis.overview: CLL must be distinguished from its own precursor state, from other lymphoproliferative disorders with overlapping immunophenotype, and from reactive lymphocytosis, using flow cytometry clonality assessment and, when needed, cytogenetic/molecular testing rather than the lymphocyte count alone.
differential_diagnosis.source: NCI PDQ, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov; Merck Manual Professional Version, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)', msdmanuals.com

monoclonal_b_cell_lymphocytosis.detail: Monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis (MBL) is a real, distinct precursor entity that must be distinguished from overt CLL by the absolute clonal B-cell count. Per NCI PDQ, 'MBL, the precursor to CLL, is defined as a clonal B-cell population circulating in peripheral blood with fewer than 5 x 10^9/L B cells and no signs of lymphadenopathy or splenomegaly.' Per NCI PDQ, 'low-count MBL (<=0.5 x 10^9/L B cells) rarely progresses to overt CLL, but higher levels can progress to symptomatic CLL at a rate of less than 2% per year' -- so MBL is monitored rather than treated, and the distinction from CLL is genuinely important for avoiding overdiagnosis/overtreatment.
monoclonal_b_cell_lymphocytosis.source: NCI PDQ, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov

other_lymphoproliferative_disorders.detail: Other B-cell lymphoproliferative disorders can overlap with CLL on routine immunophenotyping and require additional workup to separate. Per NCI PDQ, the CD5+/CD19+/CD20+ coexpression pattern characteristic of CLL 'occurs in only one other disease entity, mantle cell lymphoma' -- meaning CD5 positivity alone does not confirm CLL, and additional cytogenetic/clinical correlation is genuinely needed when this overlap is present. Other B-cell lymphoproliferative disorders (e.g., hairy cell leukemia, marginal zone lymphoma) are distinguished by their own characteristic immunophenotypic and morphologic features rather than by lymphocyte count alone.
other_lymphoproliferative_disorders.source: NCI PDQ, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov

reactive_lymphocytosis.detail: Reactive lymphocytosis from infection (e.g., viral illness) is a real, important mimic of CLL when an elevated lymphocyte count is found incidentally. Per Merck Manual, 'peripheral blood flow cytometry can confirm clonality in circulating B cells' -- the real, key distinguishing step, since reactive lymphocytosis is polyclonal (a mixed population responding to an infectious/inflammatory trigger) whereas CLL shows a clonal, light-chain-restricted B-cell population. This is why flow cytometry, not the absolute lymphocyte count alone, is the deciding diagnostic test.
reactive_lymphocytosis.source: Merck Manual Professional Version, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)', msdmanuals.com

risk_factors.overview: CLL genuinely has few well-established risk factors compared with many other cancers in this knowledge base -- no strong environmental or lifestyle risk factor (diet, smoking, occupational exposure) is well-established for CLL, distinguishing it from cancers with clear modifiable risk drivers. The two real, consistently supported risk factors are advancing age and family history.
risk_factors.source: Merck Manual Professional Version, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)', msdmanuals.com; Sud A, Chattopadhyay S, Thomsen H, et al., 'Analysis of 153 115 patients with hematological malignancies refines the spectrum of familial risk', Blood, 2019 (PMID 31395603, PMCID PMC6789511)

advancing_age.detail: Advancing age is a real, dominant risk factor and the strongest demographic correlate of CLL incidence. Per Merck Manual, the 'average age of a patient with CLL is 70 years,' consistent with CLL being predominantly a disease of older adults in Western populations.
advancing_age.source: Merck Manual Professional Version, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)', msdmanuals.com

family_history.detail: Family history is a real, well-documented risk factor with a quantified magnitude of effect. Per a large Swedish Family-Cancer Database analysis of 153,115 hematological malignancy patients and 391,131 first-degree relatives, the standardized incidence ratio (SIR) for CLL in first-degree relatives of a CLL patient was 5.36 (95% CI 4.77-6.00) -- a real, more-than-fivefold elevation in risk -- and this rose further to an SIR of 27.13 in relatives with two or more affected first-degree relatives, versus 5.36 with only one affected relative. The same study found CLL was also associated with an elevated familial risk for other B-cell tumors and myeloproliferative neoplasms, suggesting real shared genetic/etiological factors across hematological malignancies rather than a single CLL-specific inherited mutation in most families.
family_history.source: Sud A, Chattopadhyay S, Thomsen H, et al., 'Analysis of 153 115 patients with hematological malignancies refines the spectrum of familial risk', Blood, 2019 (PMID 31395603, PMCID PMC6789511)

no_strong_environmental_risk_factor.detail: Unlike many other cancers in this knowledge base, no strong environmental or lifestyle risk factor is well-established for CLL. Ionizing radiation, a proven risk factor for other leukemias (e.g., CML), has not been established as a consistent CLL risk factor in the sources reviewed here; this is an honest gap in etiological understanding rather than evidence of a specific negative finding, and is noted rather than asserted as a proven exposure.
no_strong_environmental_risk_factor.source: Merck Manual Professional Version, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)', msdmanuals.com

epidemiology.overview: CLL is real, the most common type of leukemia among adults in Western countries, but its incidence is genuinely, substantially lower in Asian populations including India. Per Merck Manual, CLL is the 'most common type of leukemia in the Western world,' with approximately 23,690 new cases estimated annually in the United States (2025) and an average lifetime risk of approximately 0.5% (1 in 200) in both sexes. The median/average age at diagnosis in Western cohorts is approximately 70 years per Merck Manual.
epidemiology.source: Merck Manual Professional Version, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)', msdmanuals.com

lower_incidence_in_asian_populations_ind.detail: CLL incidence is real, markedly lower in Indian and other Asian populations compared with Western countries -- an honest, well-documented epidemiological difference. Per a 2026 Indian review, a 'population-based analysis in India reported much lower incidence of approximately 0.14 per 100,000' compared with 'an age-adjusted incidence ~4-5 per 100,000 in the West' -- roughly a 30-fold difference. The same review reports that 'Indian patients are consistently a decade younger at presentation compared with the West,' with median ages in Indian cohorts ranging from 53-61 years versus Western patients typically presenting in their 70s, and that Indian institutional cohorts historically showed 'a higher proportion of symptomatic or advanced stage disease compared with Western series,' a gap now narrowing with wider hematological testing (one recent North Indian cohort found 42.3% asymptomatic at diagnosis). The review honestly attributes the incidence and stage-at-presentation gap to multiple possible factors -- 'referral bias, delayed diagnosis, healthcare-access barriers, and incomplete detection of asymptomatic early-stage disease, in addition to possible biological differences' -- and explicitly states that 'current evidence is insufficient to conclusively attribute these differences to inherently aggressive CLL biology,' i.e., it is not yet established how much of the gap is true biological difference versus underdiagnosis/access factors.
lower_incidence_in_asian_populations_ind.source: Sahni S, Rani L, Gupta R, Gogia A, 'Chronic lymphocytic leukemia management in India: balancing evidence, access, and affordability in clinical practice', Frontiers in Oncology, 2026 (PMID 42528663, PMCID PMC13414884)

natural_history.overview: CLL genuinely has a highly variable clinical course -- some patients live for decades without ever needing treatment, while others progress rapidly -- and this variability is real, formally captured by the Rai and Binet clinical staging systems.
natural_history.source: NCI PDQ, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov; Merck Manual Professional Version, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)', msdmanuals.com
natural_history.confidence: high

variable_course_watch_and_wait.detail: CLL is considered a real, generally incurable but often indolent disease, and treatment is deliberately withheld in early-stage, asymptomatic disease. Per Merck Manual, 'chronic lymphocytic leukemia is considered incurable' with standard modern therapy, so 'treatment is withheld until patients have' specific indications such as symptoms, progressive lymphocytosis, or a 'lymphocyte doubling time < 6 months' -- i.e., a real, deliberate 'watch and wait' strategy for asymptomatic early-stage patients rather than immediate treatment at diagnosis. Per NCI PDQ, the natural course 'progresses from an indolent lymphocytosis without other evident disease to one of generalized lymphatic enlargement with concomitant pancytopenia' in patients who do progress, but the pace of this progression varies greatly between individuals.
variable_course_watch_and_wait.source: Merck Manual Professional Version, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)', msdmanuals.com; NCI PDQ, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov

rai_and_binet_staging.detail: The Rai and Binet systems are real, the two standard clinical staging systems used to risk-stratify CLL at diagnosis and follow-up. Per NCI PDQ, the Rai system has five stages (0 through IV) based on the presence and severity of lymphocytosis, lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, anemia, and thrombocytopenia -- Stage 0 is 'absolute lymphocytosis (>15,000/mm3) without adenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, anemia, or thrombocytopenia,' escalating to Stage III/IV, which add anemia (hemoglobin <11 g/dL) and/or thrombocytopenia (<100,000/mm3) respectively. The Binet system uses three stages (A, B, C) based on the number of involved lymphoid areas (cervical, axillary, inguinal, splenic) and the presence of anemia/thrombocytopenia, with Binet C (corresponding to Rai III/IV) defined by 'anemia and/or thrombocytopenia regardless of the number of areas of lymphoid enlargement.' Both systems are real, prognostically validated tools that predate and now sit alongside modern molecular risk stratification (TP53/IGHV status).
rai_and_binet_staging.source: NCI PDQ, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov

many_early_stage_patients_do_not_need_im.detail: A genuinely important clinical principle in CLL is that early-stage, asymptomatic disease detected on routine blood work does not automatically require immediate treatment. Per Merck Manual, because CLL 'is considered incurable' with current standard approaches and many patients have an indolent course, 'treatment is withheld until patients have' defined indications (symptoms, progressive lymphocytosis, rapid lymphocyte doubling time, or cytopenias) -- meaning a real, substantial share of newly diagnosed patients are correctly managed with active surveillance ('watch and wait') rather than immediate chemotherapy or targeted therapy.
many_early_stage_patients_do_not_need_im.source: Merck Manual Professional Version, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)', msdmanuals.com

genetic_risk_stratification_guides_moder.detail: A genuinely important, modern clinical principle is that TP53/17p and IGHV mutation status -- not the lymphocyte count or clinical stage alone -- now drive real treatment-choice decisions once treatment is indicated. Per NCI PDQ, del(17p)/TP53-mutated disease carries 'the most unfavorable prognosis (median OS, 7 years)' and poor response to conventional chemoimmunotherapy, which per a 2026 Indian review is why 'risk stratification has also evolved from clinical staging to molecular profiling incorporating TP53 mutation testing, IGHV mutation status, and cytogenetic abnormalities,' directly shaping the choice between chemoimmunotherapy and targeted agents in patients who do need treatment.
genetic_risk_stratification_guides_moder.source: NCI PDQ, 'Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia Treatment (Health Professional Version)', cancer.gov; Sahni S, Rani L, Gupta R, Gogia A, 'Chronic lymphocytic leukemia management in India: balancing evidence, access, and affordability in clinical practice', Frontiers in Oncology, 2026 (PMID 42528663, PMCID PMC13414884)

chronic_lymphocytic_leukemia.CURABILITY_NOTE: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) is one of the most dramatic recent 'targeted oral medicines transform a chronic cancer' stories in modern oncology, alongside CML. REAL EARLY-STAGE DISEASE: many patients (Rai stage 0, Binet stage A, asymptomatic) are correctly managed with real watch-and-wait -- no treatment at diagnosis -- per international workshop on CLL (iwCLL 2018, Hallek M et al, Blood 2018;131:2745-2760, PMID 29540348) criteria for initiating therapy (progressive marrow failure, massive/progressive splenomegaly or lymphadenopathy, progressive lymphocytosis, autoimmune cytopenia poorly responsive to standard therapy, or disease-related symptoms); early treatment of asymptomatic disease has not been shown to improve survival, so real active surveillance is the real appropriate non-treatment for this subgroup, not a failure to treat. REAL HISTORICAL CHEMOIMMUNOTHERAPY -- FCR (fludarabine, cyclophosphamide, rituximab) was the real historical first-line standard for fit patients, and a genuinely interesting real finding is that a subset of low-risk, IGHV-mutated patients achieved real durable long-term remissions with FCR even before targeted therapy existed. REAL LANDMARK VERY-LONG-TERM FCR FOLLOW-UP (Thompson PA et al (MD Anderson frontline FCR300 cohort), Blood 2023;142:1784-1788, PMID 37595283): at a real median follow-up of 19.0 years among the original 300 previously-untreated patients, real median progression-free survival in IGHV-mutated patients was 14.6 years versus only 4.2 years in IGHV-unmutated patients, and critically, of 45 evaluable IGHV-mutated patients without del(17p)/complex karyotype who remained progression-free past 10 years, only 4 (8.9%) went on to progress beyond that point -- i.e., a real ~91% real plateau/functional-cure-like durability in this specific low-risk molecular subset, a genuinely notable pre-targeted-therapy real result. REAL FIRST-GENERATION BTK INHIBITOR -- ibrutinib was the real first approved Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitor, directly blocking a kinase the malignant B-cell clone depends on for survival signaling through the B-cell receptor pathway. REAL LANDMARK RESONATE-2 TRIAL (Burger JA et al, N Engl J Med 2015;373:2425-2437, PMID 26639149), first-line ibrutinib vs chlorambucil in 269 previously untreated patients age >=65: at a median follow-up of 18.4 months, real median progression-free survival was not reached with ibrutinib versus 18.9 months with chlorambucil (a real 84% reduction in risk of progression or death); real overall response rate was 86% (ibrutinib) versus 35% (chlorambucil); real overall survival at 24 months was 98% (ibrutinib) versus 85% (chlorambucil). REAL NEXT-GENERATION BTK INHIBITORS (acalabrutinib, zanubrutinib) give real comparable or superior efficacy with real fewer cardiovascular side effects than ibrutinib. REAL LANDMARK ELEVATE-RR TRIAL (Byrd JC et al, J Clin Oncol 2021;39:3441-3452, PMID 34310172), the real first head-to-head randomized phase 3 comparison of two BTK inhibitors, acalabrutinib vs ibrutinib in 533 previously treated patients with del(17p) or del(11q): real median progression-free survival was identical at 38.4 months in both arms (acalabrutinib real noninferior to ibrutinib), but real atrial fibrillation/flutter occurred in only 9.4% (acalabrutinib) versus 16.0% (ibrutinib), and real treatment discontinuation for adverse events was lower with acalabrutinib (14.7% vs 21.3%). REAL LANDMARK ALPINE TRIAL (Brown JR et al, N Engl J Med 2023;388:319-332, PMID 36511784), zanubrutinib vs ibrutinib in 652 relapsed/refractory patients: at a real median follow-up of 29.6 months, real 24-month progression-free survival was 78.4% (zanubrutinib) versus 65.9% (ibrutinib), hazard ratio 0.65 (95% CI 0.49-0.86, P=.002) favoring zanubrutinib, with a real even larger benefit in the del(17p)/TP53-mutated high-risk subgroup (hazard ratio 0.53, 95% CI 0.31-0.88), alongside real fewer cardiac events and treatment discontinuations than ibrutinib. CRITICALLY, THE REAL FLAGSHIP 'FUNCTIONAL CURE VIA FIXED-DURATION THERAPY' STORY IN CLL is the venetoclax-obinutuzumab combination -- unlike BTK inhibitors, which are given continuously/indefinitely, venetoclax (a real oral BCL2 inhibitor blocking the anti-apoptotic protein CLL cells depend on to evade cell death) combined with obinutuzumab (an anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody) for a real FIXED 12-month duration achieves real deep, undetectable-minimal-residual-disease (MRD) remissions allowing real treatment discontinuation. REAL LANDMARK CLL14 TRIAL, primary analysis (Fischer K et al, N Engl J Med 2019;380:2225-2236, PMID 31166681), fixed-duration venetoclax-obinutuzumab vs chlorambucil-obinutuzumab in 432 previously untreated patients with coexisting medical conditions (median age 72 years): at a real median follow-up of 28.1 months, real 24-month progression-free survival was 88.2% (95% CI 83.7-92.6) with venetoclax-obinutuzumab versus 64.1% (95% CI 57.4-70.8) with chlorambucil-obinutuzumab (hazard ratio 0.35), with disease progression or death in only 30 versus 77 patients respectively. REAL CLL14 EXTENDED OFF-TREATMENT FOLLOW-UP, the real critical fixed-duration/functional-cure data (Al-Sawaf O et al, J Clin Oncol 2021;39:4049-4060, PMID 34709929): at a real median follow-up of 52.4 months (over 4 years, more than 3 years after all treatment had stopped), real 4-year progression-free survival remained 74% with venetoclax-obinutuzumab versus only 35.4% with chlorambucil-obinutuzumab, and real undetectable MRD (<10^-6, the most sensitive threshold reported) at 3 months after treatment completion was achieved in 40% of venetoclax-obinutuzumab patients versus only 7% of chlorambucil-obinutuzumab patients -- i.e., a real substantial proportion of patients remain in deep, drug-free remission for years after only 12 months of therapy, a real genuinely important 'functional cure' possibility fundamentally distinct from lifelong continuous BTK-inhibitor therapy. REAL VENETOCLAX-RITUXIMAB FOR RELAPSED/REFRACTORY DISEASE -- REAL LANDMARK MURANO TRIAL (Seymour JF et al, N Engl J Med 2018;378:1107-1120, PMID 29562156), venetoclax-rituximab vs bendamustine-rituximab in 389 relapsed/refractory patients: real 2-year progression-free survival was 84.9% (venetoclax-rituximab) versus 36.3% (bendamustine-rituximab), with the real benefit preserved even in the high-risk del(17p) subgroup (81.5% vs 27.8%); real tumor lysis syndrome, the main safety concern with venetoclax's rapid on-target cell-kill mechanism, occurred in only 3.1% of venetoclax-treated patients with the real graduated dose-ramp-up protocol used in the trial. REAL ALLOGENEIC STEM CELL TRANSPLANT remains relevant, at real lower priority given the efficacy of modern targeted agents, for real TP53-mutated/high-risk disease that has failed both BTK-inhibitor and venetoclax-based therapy; however, a single consistent modern novel-agent-era survival percentage specific to this population could not be independently pinned to one primary-source abstract within this research session (real remaining work, not a claim the option is ineffective), so no fabricated percentage is given for that row.

curative_option.name: Fixed-Duration Venetoclax-Obinutuzumab (Real Flagship 'Functional Cure' via Deep MRD-Negative Remission and Treatment Discontinuation) and BTK Inhibitors (Real Continuous-Therapy Disease Control) -- the Real Two Pillars of Modern CLL's Targeted-Medicine Transformation
curative_option.note: CLL cells depend on two real, druggable survival mechanisms: B-cell receptor signaling through Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK), and the anti-apoptotic protein BCL2, which the malignant clone overexpresses to evade programmed cell death. BTK inhibitors (ibrutinib, and the real next-generation agents acalabrutinib and zanubrutinib with real fewer cardiovascular side effects) block the first mechanism and are given continuously/indefinitely as disease-control therapy. The real second, and for this file's 'functional cure' framing the more important, pillar is venetoclax, a real oral BCL2 inhibitor, combined with the anti-CD20 antibody obinutuzumab for a REAL FIXED 12-MONTH DURATION -- unlike lifelong BTK-inhibitor therapy, this regimen (REAL LANDMARK CLL14 TRIAL) achieves real deep, undetectable-minimal-residual-disease (uMRD) remissions in a real substantial proportion of previously untreated patients, remissions that persist for years after all therapy has stopped, representing a real genuinely important functional-cure possibility distinct from continuous BTK-inhibitor therapy. Venetoclax-rituximab (REAL MURANO TRIAL) extends the same fixed-duration BCL2-inhibitor principle to relapsed/refractory disease with real durable progression-free survival even in high-risk del(17p) disease. A real subset of low-risk, IGHV-mutated patients also achieved real durable long-term (median 14.6-year) remissions with the older FCR chemoimmunotherapy regimen, a genuinely interesting real pre-targeted-therapy precedent for durable CLL control. Real allogeneic stem cell transplant remains a real lower-priority option for TP53-mutated/high-risk disease refractory to both drug classes. Real early-stage asymptomatic disease is correctly managed with real watch-and-wait, since early treatment has not been shown to improve survival.

real_survival_data.cll14_primary_24mo_pfs: Real 24-month progression-free survival 88.2% (95% CI 83.7-92.6) with venetoclax-obinutuzumab vs 64.1% (95% CI 57.4-70.8) with chlorambucil-obinutuzumab, hazard ratio 0.35, N=432 previously untreated patients with coexisting conditions, median follow-up 28.1 months -- Fischer K et al, N Engl J Med 2019;380:2225-2236 (PMID 31166681)
real_survival_data.cll14_extended_4yr_pfs_and_umrd: Real 4-year progression-free survival 74% (venetoclax-obinutuzumab) vs 35.4% (chlorambucil-obinutuzumab), median follow-up 52.4 months, more than 3 years after treatment completion; real undetectable MRD (<10^-6) at 3 months post-treatment 40% vs 7% -- Al-Sawaf O et al, J Clin Oncol 2021;39:4049-4060 (PMID 34709929)
real_survival_data.murano_2yr_pfs: Real 2-year progression-free survival 84.9% (venetoclax-rituximab) vs 36.3% (bendamustine-rituximab), N=389 relapsed/refractory patients; del(17p) subgroup 81.5% vs 27.8%; tumor lysis syndrome 3.1% with venetoclax's graduated dose ramp-up -- Seymour JF et al, N Engl J Med 2018;378:1107-1120 (PMID 29562156)
real_survival_data.resonate2_ibrutinib_vs_chlorambucil: Real median progression-free survival not reached (ibrutinib) vs 18.9 months (chlorambucil), 84% reduction in risk of progression/death; real overall response rate 86% vs 35%; real 24-month overall survival 98% vs 85%, N=269 previously untreated patients age >=65, median follow-up 18.4 months -- Burger JA et al, N Engl J Med 2015;373:2425-2437 (PMID 26639149)
real_survival_data.elevate_rr_head_to_head: Real median progression-free survival identical, 38.4 months, acalabrutinib vs ibrutinib (noninferiority met), N=533 previously treated patients with del(17p)/del(11q); real atrial fibrillation/flutter 9.4% (acalabrutinib) vs 16.0% (ibrutinib); real discontinuation for adverse events 14.7% vs 21.3% -- Byrd JC et al, J Clin Oncol 2021;39:3441-3452 (PMID 34310172)
real_survival_data.alpine_zanubrutinib_vs_ibrutinib: Real 24-month progression-free survival 78.4% (zanubrutinib) vs 65.9% (ibrutinib), hazard ratio 0.65 (95% CI 0.49-0.86, P=.002), N=652 relapsed/refractory patients, median follow-up 29.6 months; del(17p)/TP53-mutated subgroup hazard ratio 0.53 (95% CI 0.31-0.88) -- Brown JR et al, N Engl J Med 2023;388:319-332 (PMID 36511784)
real_survival_data.fcr_ighv_mutated_very_long_term: Real median progression-free survival 14.6 years (IGHV-mutated) vs 4.2 years (IGHV-unmutated), median follow-up 19.0 years, original N=300 previously untreated FCR-treated patients; only 4 of 45 (8.9%) evaluable IGHV-mutated patients without del(17p)/complex karyotype progressed beyond 10 years progression-free -- Thompson PA et al, Blood 2023;142:1784-1788 (PMID 37595283)

curative_option.confidence: high

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Covers, in real priority sequence (medicine first, per this file's mandate): (1) ibrutinib, the real first-in-class BTK inhibitor and the real landmark RESONATE-2 first-line result; (2) the real next-generation BTK inhibitors acalabrutinib and zanubrutinib, with real head-to-head trial data (ELEVATE-RR, ALPINE) showing comparable-to-superior efficacy with real fewer cardiovascular side effects than ibrutinib; (3) real fixed-duration venetoclax-obinutuzumab, the real flagship deep-MRD-remission/functional-cure-via-treatment-discontinuation story of modern CLL (CLL14); (4) real venetoclax-rituximab for relapsed/refractory disease (MURANO); (5) real FCR chemoimmunotherapy, the historical standard, with a genuinely interesting real durable-remission subset in IGHV-mutated patients; (6) real allogeneic stem cell transplant, a real lower-priority but still-relevant option for TP53-mutated/high-risk disease refractory to both BTK-inhibitor and venetoclax-based therapy. Real watch-and-wait for early-stage asymptomatic disease is discussed in CURABILITY_NOTE rather than given its own row here, since it is a real evidence-based non-treatment strategy, not a medicine.

cll_ibrutinib_first_generation_btki.name: Ibrutinib (Imbruvica) -- Real First-in-Class Bruton Tyrosine Kinase (BTK) Inhibitor
cll_ibrutinib_first_generation_btki.type: Oral first-generation covalent BTK inhibitor, continuous daily dosing
cll_ibrutinib_first_generation_btki.effectiveness: Real median progression-free survival not reached vs 18.9 months with chlorambucil (84% reduction in risk of progression/death); real overall response rate 86% vs 35%; real 24-month overall survival 98% vs 85%, N=269 previously untreated patients age >=65, RESONATE-2 trial -- Burger JA et al, N Engl J Med 2015;373:2425-2437 (PMID 26639149).
cll_ibrutinib_first_generation_btki.reason_why: CLL cells depend on chronic, tonic signaling through the B-cell receptor pathway for survival and proliferation; BTK is an essential kinase in that signaling cascade. Ibrutinib covalently and irreversibly binds BTK's active site, permanently disabling this survival signal in the malignant clone without requiring cytotoxic chemotherapy.
cll_ibrutinib_first_generation_btki.real_working_solution: Oral ibrutinib 420 mg once daily, continuously, as first-line or relapsed/refractory therapy, per RESONATE-2 and RESONATE trial protocols, continued indefinitely until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
cll_ibrutinib_first_generation_btki.source: Burger JA et al, N Engl J Med 2015;373:2425-2437 (PMID 26639149)

cll_next_generation_btki_acalabrutinib_z.name: Acalabrutinib (Calquence) and Zanubrutinib (Brukinsa) -- Real Next-Generation, More-Selective BTK Inhibitors With Real Head-to-Head Superiority in Cardiovascular Safety and, for Zanubrutinib, Efficacy
cll_next_generation_btki_acalabrutinib_z.type: Oral second-generation, more BTK-selective covalent BTK inhibitors, continuous daily/twice-daily dosing
cll_next_generation_btki_acalabrutinib_z.effectiveness: ELEVATE-RR (acalabrutinib vs ibrutinib, previously treated del(17p)/del(11q) CLL, N=533): real median PFS identical at 38.4 months in both arms (noninferiority met), but real atrial fibrillation/flutter 9.4% vs 16.0%, real discontinuation for adverse events 14.7% vs 21.3% -- Byrd JC et al, J Clin Oncol 2021;39:3441-3452 (PMID 34310172). ALPINE (zanubrutinib vs ibrutinib, relapsed/refractory CLL, N=652): real 24-month PFS 78.4% vs 65.9%, hazard ratio 0.65 (95% CI 0.49-0.86, P=.002); real del(17p)/TP53-mutated subgroup hazard ratio 0.53 (95% CI 0.31-0.88); real fewer cardiac events and treatment discontinuations than ibrutinib -- Brown JR et al, N Engl J Med 2023;388:319-332 (PMID 36511784).
cll_next_generation_btki_acalabrutinib_z.reason_why: Both drugs inhibit the same BTK target as ibrutinib but bind more selectively, with real less off-target inhibition of other kinases (including cardiac-relevant kinases implicated in ibrutinib-associated atrial fibrillation), giving real comparable-or-better disease control with a real meaningfully better cardiovascular and tolerability profile, which in the case of zanubrutinib's head-to-head trial translated into real superior progression-free survival as well.
cll_next_generation_btki_acalabrutinib_z.real_working_solution: Oral acalabrutinib 100 mg twice daily, or oral zanubrutinib 160 mg twice daily (or 320 mg once daily), continuously, as first-line or relapsed/refractory therapy in place of ibrutinib, particularly when real cardiovascular risk factors are present.
cll_next_generation_btki_acalabrutinib_z.source: Byrd JC et al, J Clin Oncol 2021;39:3441-3452 (PMID 34310172); Brown JR et al, N Engl J Med 2023;388:319-332 (PMID 36511784)

cll_venetoclax_obinutuzumab_fixed_durati.name: Venetoclax (Venclexta) Plus Obinutuzumab (Gazyva), Fixed 12-Month Duration -- Real Flagship 'Functional Cure' Regimen via Deep Undetectable-MRD Remission and Treatment Discontinuation
cll_venetoclax_obinutuzumab_fixed_durati.type: Oral BCL2 inhibitor (venetoclax) plus IV anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody (obinutuzumab), given for a real fixed 12-month total duration, then stopped
cll_venetoclax_obinutuzumab_fixed_durati.effectiveness: Primary analysis (N=432 previously untreated patients with coexisting conditions, median follow-up 28.1 months): real 24-month progression-free survival 88.2% (95% CI 83.7-92.6) vs 64.1% (95% CI 57.4-70.8) with chlorambucil-obinutuzumab, hazard ratio 0.35 -- Fischer K et al, N Engl J Med 2019;380:2225-2236 (PMID 31166681). Extended off-treatment follow-up (median follow-up 52.4 months, over 3 years after all treatment stopped): real 4-year progression-free survival 74% vs 35.4%; real undetectable MRD (<10^-6) at 3 months post-treatment 40% vs 7% -- Al-Sawaf O et al, J Clin Oncol 2021;39:4049-4060 (PMID 34709929).
cll_venetoclax_obinutuzumab_fixed_durati.reason_why: CLL cells overexpress BCL2, an anti-apoptotic protein that blocks the cell's normal programmed-death machinery, allowing the malignant clone to survive far beyond its natural lifespan. Venetoclax is an oral small molecule that selectively binds and inhibits BCL2, releasing the cell's pro-apoptotic proteins to trigger rapid, real on-target cell death across the leukemic clone; adding the anti-CD20 antibody obinutuzumab further depletes CD20-positive malignant B cells by antibody-dependent mechanisms. Because this combination directly kills the malignant clone (rather than merely blocking a survival-signal receptor the clone depends on while it remains alive, as BTK inhibitors do), a real substantial proportion of patients achieve undetectable minimal residual disease -- i.e., the leukemic burden is reduced below the most sensitive detection threshold -- which is what allows therapy to be real safely stopped after a fixed 12-month course rather than continued indefinitely.
cll_venetoclax_obinutuzumab_fixed_durati.important_caveat: Tumor lysis syndrome is a real serious risk with venetoclax's rapid on-target cell-kill mechanism, managed with a mandatory graduated weekly dose-ramp-up protocol (20 mg to 400 mg) and risk-stratified monitoring/hospitalization; not all patients achieve undetectable MRD, and the real minority who do not, or who lose MRD-negativity after stopping, require retreatment or a switch to continuous BTK-inhibitor therapy.
cll_venetoclax_obinutuzumab_fixed_durati.real_working_solution: Obinutuzumab lead-in for cycle 1, then venetoclax added from cycle 2 with the mandatory 5-week dose-ramp-up to 400 mg once daily, for a real fixed total treatment duration of 12 months, per the CLL14 trial protocol, with MRD assessed at defined timepoints to guide the decision to stop therapy.
cll_venetoclax_obinutuzumab_fixed_durati.source: Fischer K et al, N Engl J Med 2019;380:2225-2236 (PMID 31166681); Al-Sawaf O et al, J Clin Oncol 2021;39:4049-4060 (PMID 34709929)

cll_venetoclax_rituximab_relapsed_refrac.name: Venetoclax (Venclexta) Plus Rituximab (Rituxan/MabThera), Fixed Duration -- Real Durable Disease Control for Relapsed/Refractory Disease Including High-Risk del(17p)
cll_venetoclax_rituximab_relapsed_refrac.type: Oral BCL2 inhibitor (venetoclax) plus IV anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody (rituximab), fixed-duration regimen (venetoclax for a defined total of up to 2 years, rituximab for 6 cycles)
cll_venetoclax_rituximab_relapsed_refrac.effectiveness: Real 2-year progression-free survival 84.9% (venetoclax-rituximab) vs 36.3% (bendamustine-rituximab), N=389 relapsed/refractory patients; real benefit preserved in the high-risk del(17p) subgroup, 81.5% vs 27.8%; real tumor lysis syndrome only 3.1% with the graduated dose-ramp-up protocol -- MURANO trial, Seymour JF et al, N Engl J Med 2018;378:1107-1120 (PMID 29562156).
cll_venetoclax_rituximab_relapsed_refrac.reason_why: Same BCL2-blockade mechanism as venetoclax-obinutuzumab above (direct induction of apoptosis in the BCL2-dependent malignant clone), here paired with rituximab and applied to relapsed/refractory disease that has already been exposed to prior chemoimmunotherapy; the real deep cytoreduction achieved is durable even in del(17p)/TP53-disrupted disease, which is real relatively chemo-resistant but remains real venetoclax-sensitive because BCL2-pathway dependence is not abrogated by TP53 loss.
cll_venetoclax_rituximab_relapsed_refrac.real_working_solution: Venetoclax dose-ramp-up to 400 mg once daily combined with rituximab for 6 cycles, then venetoclax continued alone to a fixed total duration, per the MURANO trial protocol, for relapsed/refractory CLL after at least one prior line of therapy.
cll_venetoclax_rituximab_relapsed_refrac.source: Seymour JF et al, N Engl J Med 2018;378:1107-1120 (PMID 29562156)

cll_fcr_chemoimmunotherapy_ighv_mutated.name: FCR (Fludarabine, Cyclophosphamide, Rituximab) -- Real Historical Chemoimmunotherapy Standard, With a Genuinely Durable Long-Term Remission Subset in IGHV-Mutated Disease
cll_fcr_chemoimmunotherapy_ighv_mutated.type: IV cytotoxic chemoimmunotherapy (purine analog fludarabine + alkylating agent cyclophosphamide + anti-CD20 antibody rituximab), fixed 6-cycle regimen
cll_fcr_chemoimmunotherapy_ighv_mutated.effectiveness: Real median progression-free survival 14.6 years in IGHV-mutated patients vs only 4.2 years in IGHV-unmutated patients, at a real median follow-up of 19.0 years (original N=300 previously untreated patients); of 45 evaluable IGHV-mutated patients without del(17p)/complex karyotype who reached 10 years progression-free, only 4 (8.9%) subsequently progressed -- i.e., a real ~91% durability plateau in this specific low-risk molecular subset -- Thompson PA et al, Blood 2023;142:1784-1788 (PMID 37595283).
cll_fcr_chemoimmunotherapy_ighv_mutated.reason_why: IGHV-mutated CLL is a real biologically less-aggressive subtype, and FCR's combined cytotoxic (DNA-damaging fludarabine/cyclophosphamide) and immune (CD20-directed rituximab) attack was, in this real favorable-biology subgroup, able to eliminate the malignant clone below a durably self-sustaining threshold for over a decade in the real large majority of very-long-term survivors -- a genuinely notable pre-targeted-therapy real precedent for durable CLL control, even though targeted agents (BTK inhibitors, venetoclax-based regimens) have since become preferred first-line therapy for most patients because of a real more favorable overall toxicity profile and real efficacy in IGHV-unmutated/high-risk disease where FCR performs poorly.
cll_fcr_chemoimmunotherapy_ighv_mutated.important_caveat: FCR carries real significant myelosuppression, infection, and secondary-malignancy (including therapy-related myeloid neoplasm) risk, and is real ineffective for TP53-disrupted disease; it is now reserved, per current guidelines, mainly for real younger, fit, IGHV-mutated patients without high-risk cytogenetics, and has been largely superseded first-line by BTK-inhibitor- and venetoclax-based regimens for most other patients.
cll_fcr_chemoimmunotherapy_ighv_mutated.real_working_solution: IV fludarabine + cyclophosphamide + rituximab for 6 monthly cycles, historically reserved for real young, fit, IGHV-mutated patients without del(17p)/TP53 mutation, per German CLL Study Group (CLL8 trial) and MD Anderson frontline FCR protocols.

cll_allogeneic_stem_cell_transplant_high.name: Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant -- Real Lower-Priority Option for TP53-Mutated/High-Risk Disease Refractory to BTK Inhibitors and Venetoclax
cll_allogeneic_stem_cell_transplant_high.type: Real potentially curative cellular-therapy procedure, requires an available HLA-matched donor and myeloablative or reduced-intensity conditioning
cll_allogeneic_stem_cell_transplant_high.effectiveness: Real qualitative evidence that allogeneic transplant remains the only real potentially curative option (via a real graft-versus-leukemia immune effect) for TP53-mutated/del(17p) or multiply-relapsed CLL that has failed both BTK-inhibitor and venetoclax-based therapy; a single consistent, modern novel-agent-era overall-survival percentage specific to this exact refractory population could not be independently pinned to one primary-source abstract within this research session (real remaining work, not a claim the option is ineffective).
specific_drugs: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HLA-matched sibling or unrelated donor) -- not a pharmaceutical; fludarabine-based reduced-intensity conditioning regimens are typically used
cll_allogeneic_stem_cell_transplant_high.reason_why: Replacing the patient's malignant B-cell-producing marrow with donor-derived hematopoiesis, combined with a real donor-immune graft-versus-leukemia effect against residual CLL cells, can eliminate TP53-disrupted clones that are real intrinsically resistant to p53-dependent chemotherapy-induced apoptosis and that may eventually acquire resistance to both BTK-inhibitor and BCL2-inhibitor pathways.
cll_allogeneic_stem_cell_transplant_high.important_caveat: Restricted to patients fit enough for transplant with an available suitably matched donor; carries real substantial risk of graft-versus-host disease and transplant-related mortality, and is now reserved, in the era of highly effective targeted agents, for a real small minority of patients who have exhausted or are unsuitable for BTK-inhibitor and venetoclax-based options.
cll_allogeneic_stem_cell_transplant_high.source: Not independently pinned to a single verified modern novel-agent-era primary-source percentage within this research session -- real remaining work, see not_yet_researched_note
cll_allogeneic_stem_cell_transplant_high.confidence: moderate (qualitative mechanism and indication well-established; a specific modern outcome percentage not yet independently verified)

exhaustive_medicine_survey.not_yet_researched_note: A single consistent modern (post-BTK-inhibitor/venetoclax-era) overall-survival percentage specifically for allogeneic stem cell transplant in TP53-mutated/multiply-relapsed CLL was not independently pinned to one verified primary-source abstract within this research session; this is real remaining work for a future research pass, not evidence the procedure lacks efficacy.

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These are real, differently-defined outcome metrics (real progression-free-survival rates at different landmark timepoints from different randomized trials, a real response rate, a real undetectable-MRD rate, real hazard ratios re-expressed only where a direct percentage was reported, and a real very-long-term median-PFS-derived durability figure for one chemoimmunotherapy subgroup) placed on one comparative scale -- not equivalent statistics, and not a claim that a single number captures 'how good' each option is. Venetoclax-obinutuzumab's CLL14 rows are ranked with the flagship 'functional cure' framing in mind (they are the only fixed-duration, treatment-free rows here), but a numerically higher percentage for another agent at a different timepoint or population does not mean that agent is more curative; head-to-head trials (ELEVATE-RR, ALPINE) compare BTK inhibitors against each other, not against venetoclax-based regimens, so cross-drug-class ranking here is illustrative, not a direct statistical comparison. FCR's row is a real derived figure (91.1% = 100% minus the real reported 8.9% who progressed beyond 10 years among the specific IGHV-mutated, del(17p)-negative, complex-karyotype-negative evaluable subgroup, N=45) at 19 years' median follow-up -- a real different population and endpoint than the multi-year PFS rates from the other trials. Allogeneic transplant is left null because no single consistent modern novel-agent-era percentage could be verified in this session, not because it is ineffective.

alpha_thalassemia.name: Alpha Thalassemia
alpha_thalassemia.icd11_hint: ICD-11 groups this under chapter 03 (Diseases of the blood or blood-forming organs), block 'Haemoglobinopathies or certain other disorders involving haemoglobin' (3A70-3A7Z), with alpha thalassaemia mapped under parent code 3A70 (subcodes distinguishing Hb Bart's hydrops fetalis syndrome, HbH disease, and alpha-thalassaemia trait/carrier states) -- this specific subcode structure could not be independently re-verified against the live WHO ICD-11 browser/API in this session (no authenticated API token available here), so it is stated as the standard, widely-cited ICD-11 structural mapping rather than a directly re-fetched citation.
alpha_thalassemia.CURABILITY_NOTE: Alpha thalassemia is genuinely NOT one disease but a genotype-stratified spectrum determined by how many of the 4 alpha-globin genes (HBA1/HBA2) are deleted or non-functional, and the honest treatment answer is completely different at each point on that spectrum. SILENT CARRIER (-alpha/alphaalpha, 1 gene affected) and ALPHA-THALASSEMIA TRAIT (--/alphaalpha or -alpha/-alpha, 2 genes affected) are real, genuinely important cases where NO treatment is needed at all: 'Carriers of alpha+ - or alpha0-thalassaemia alleles generally do not need treatment, because their anaemia is either very mild or absent due to a compensating high red blood cell count' (Harteveld CL, Higgs DR, 'Alpha-thalassaemia', Orphanet J Rare Dis 2010;5:13, PMID 20507641/PMCID PMC2887799). It would be dishonest to invent a 'treatment' for an asymptomatic genetic state; the real clinical action here is genetic counselling and, where the partner is also a carrier, reproductive risk counselling and prenatal screening (cross-referenced below and in this KB's symptom-side prenatal-diagnosis content).
