differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_features: VUR causes real upper urinary tract dilation without a true mechanical obstruction, graded separately using the International Reflux Study Committee's 1985 five-grade voiding cystourethrogram (VCUG) classification (grades I-V); a real reliability study of that grading system across 28 VCUG studies rated by 13 pediatric radiologists/urologists/residents found only moderate average interrater reliability (weighted kappa 0.53, worst at grade III, kappa 0.36) despite high intrarater reliability (kappa 0.86) -- meaning VUR-grade-based differentiation from obstructive hydronephrosis on imaging alone carries a real, quantified degree of observer disagreement that clinicians should be aware of, and voiding cystourethrography (not renal ultrasound alone) is required to actually diagnose and grade VUR.
differential_diagnosis.source: Metcalfe CB, Macneily AE, Afshar K, 'Reliability assessment of international grading system for vesicoureteral reflux', J Urol 2012;188(4 Suppl):1490-2 (PMID 22906646)

differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_features: Real physiological uretero-hydronephrosis of pregnancy is right-sided-predominant (63% in a 100-patient MRI cohort), typically confined to the kidney and/or proximal ureter, asymptomatic, and does not require intervention; left-sided or whole-ureter dilation in a pregnant patient is real evidence favoring a pathological cause (stone, true obstruction) rather than physiological dilation, per the same MRI study's own practical conclusion.
differential_diagnosis.source: Grosjean J et al, Prog Urol 2017 (PMID 28869171)

differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_features: Real extrinsic compression from a pelvic malignancy is distinguished from primary urologic (stone/PUJ) obstruction on cross-sectional imaging by identifying the causative mass; in a real 188-patient series of malignant ureteral obstruction, compression by a pelvic mass was the mechanism in 36.9% of cases, with prostate cancer (17.6%), bladder cancer (16.5%) and rectal cancer (11.7%) the three most frequent culprit tumors -- a materially different differential list than the acute-flank-pain differentials (appendicitis, biliary colic, adnexal torsion, musculoskeletal pain) relevant to stone-induced acute hydronephrosis, which this knowledge base's nephrolithiasis entry covers separately.
differential_diagnosis.source: Artiles Medina A, Laso Garcia I, Gonzalez Tello F et al, 'The challenging management of malignant ureteral obstruction: Analysis of a series of 188 cases', Curr Urol 2024;18(1):34-42 (PMID 38505156, PMCID PMC10946639)

ureteropelvic_junction_puj_obstruction.finding: Primary ureteropelvic junction (UPJ/PUJ)-type obstruction is a real, major structural cause of hydronephrosis, particularly the most frequently studied cause of antenatally detected disease; the original Onen AGS validation cohort alone comprised 162 newborns (228 affected kidneys) with primary UPJ-type hydronephrosis, and in a separate real 90-patient adult pyonephrosis series PUJ obstruction was the second most common underlying etiology (16.7%) after urolithiasis.
ureteropelvic_junction_puj_obstruction.source: Onen A, J Pediatr Urol 2007 (PMID 18947735); Arsalan SS, Raina AB, Khawaja AR et al, 'Renal Salvage in Pyonephrosis: A Retrospective Observational Study', Cureus 2026;18(1):e102343 (PMID 41755973, PMCID PMC12935494)

urolithiasis.finding: Urolithiasis (kidney/ureteric stones) is a real, leading cause of obstructive hydronephrosis and its infected complication, pyonephrosis: in a real 90-adult-patient pyonephrosis cohort from a North Indian tertiary center, urolithiasis was the most common etiology (46.7%), ahead of PUJ obstruction (16.7%) and malignancy (13.3%). This knowledge base's own nephrolithiasis entry covers the full sourced mechanism, grading and risk-factor detail for stone disease itself.
urolithiasis.source: Arsalan SS et al, Cureus 2026 (PMID 41755973); cross-reference: this knowledge base's nephrolithiasis entry

benign_prostatic_hyperplasia_bladder_out.finding: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) causing bladder outlet obstruction is a real, documented cause of bilateral hydroureteronephrosis in men, and real case evidence shows this can progress to irreversible chronic tubulointerstitial nephritis and renal failure even after the obstruction is later relieved by catheter drainage -- i.e. BPH-driven obstruction is not a benign-by-name, benign-by-outcome diagnosis if it is allowed to progress silently.
benign_prostatic_hyperplasia_bladder_out.source: Coroneos E et al, Clin Nephrol 1997 (PMID 9285152)
benign_prostatic_hyperplasia_bladder_out.confidence: high for the real mechanism and documented cases; this is case-level rather than large-cohort evidence for the specific irreversibility rate

pregnancy.finding: Pregnancy is a real, common physiological cause of uretero-hydronephrosis (right-sided-predominant, 63% in a 100-patient MRI cohort), distinct from a pathological obstructive cause; see differential_diagnosis above for the features distinguishing physiological from pathological dilation in this setting.
pregnancy.source: Grosjean J et al, Prog Urol 2017 (PMID 28869171)

malignant_pelvic_or_ureteral_tumors.finding: Malignant ureteral obstruction (MUO) from pelvic or ureteral tumors is a real, common complication of advanced malignancy: in a real 188-patient series, the most common mechanism was compression by a pelvic mass (36.9%), and the three most frequent causative cancers were prostate (17.6%), bladder (16.5%) and rectal cancer (11.7%). Acute kidney injury was the reason for urinary diversion in 53.3% of the diverted patients in this same cohort, and renal function recovered in 55.8% of those diverted.
malignant_pelvic_or_ureteral_tumors.source: Artiles Medina A et al, Curr Urol 2024 (PMID 38505156)

vesicoureteral_reflux_vur.finding: Vesicoureteral reflux is a real, non-obstructive cause of upper urinary tract dilation in children, graded I-V by the International Reflux Study Committee's 1985 voiding cystourethrogram classification; because VUR causes dilation via retrograde urine flow rather than a true mechanical blockage, it is managed and prognosticated differently from obstructive hydronephrosis, and confirming or excluding VUR requires voiding cystourethrography rather than ultrasound grading alone.
vesicoureteral_reflux_vur.source: Metcalfe CB et al, J Urol 2012 (PMID 22906646)

posterior_urethral_valves_puv.finding: Posterior urethral valves (PUV) are a real, congenital cause of lower urinary tract outflow obstruction exclusively in male infants, and are described as the real commonest cause of such obstruction in this population, with an estimated real incidence of 1 in 5,000 male infants (1 in 25,000 live births overall). PUV causes bilateral hydroureteronephrosis via bladder outlet obstruction, and even after fulguration (surgical ablation) of the obstructing valves, real bladder dysfunction persists in up to 70% of older children and adolescents, which has been directly implicated in later real deterioration of renal function in this population -- i.e. valve ablation alone does not eliminate the long-term real renal risk.
posterior_urethral_valves_puv.source: Desai DY, 'A review of urodynamic evaluation in children and its role in the management of boys with posterior urethral valves', Indian J Urol 2007;23(4):435-42 (PMID 19718301, PMCID PMC2721577)

schistosomiasis_related_ureteral_disease.finding: In schistosomiasis-endemic regions, schistosomiasis-related ureteral lesions are a real, documented cause of obstructive uropathy and its infected complication (pyonephrosis was the most frequent diagnosis, 68.75%, in the cited real cohort), alongside urolithiasis, in a 32-patient renal suppurative infection series from Burkina Faso.
schistosomiasis_related_ureteral_disease.source: Kirakoya B et al, Arch Ital Urol Androl 2026 (PMID 42383733)
schistosomiasis_related_ureteral_disease.confidence: moderate-high (real but geographically specific/endemic-region finding, not globally generalizable as a common cause)

antenatal_detection_rate.finding: Urinary tract dilation (the sonographic finding underlying hydronephrosis) is real and identified on routine obstetric ultrasound in 1-2% of all fetuses, per the 2014 multidisciplinary UTD consensus statement, making it one of the most common antenatally detected structural findings overall.
antenatal_detection_rate.source: Nguyen HT et al, J Pediatr Urol 2014 (PMID 25435247)

isolated_antenatal_hydronephrosis_outcom.finding: In a real prospective cohort of 63 patients with isolated antenatal hydronephrosis (pelviectasis without VUR or true obstruction), the first postnatal ultrasound (mean age 18.4 days) showed resolution in 25%, mild pelviectasis in 54%, and moderate/severe pelviectasis in 21%; by last follow-up (mean 23.3 months), 82% of 57 followed patients had normal or mild pelviectasis, deterioration of any grade occurred in only 5%, and renal growth was normal in all 57 patients.
isolated_antenatal_hydronephrosis_outcom.source: Cheng AM, Phan V, Geary DF, Rosenblum ND, 'Outcome of isolated antenatal hydronephrosis', Arch Pediatr Adolesc Med 2004;158(1):38-40 (PMID 14706956)

renal_suppurative_infection_hospital_pre.finding: Real hospital-level prevalence of renal suppurative infections (pyonephrosis, renal abscess, perinephric abscess) was 2.32% of all urology admissions (32 of 1,377 patients) in a real Burkina Faso tertiary series, with a mean patient age of 37.5 years and a slight real female predominance (sex ratio 1.4).
renal_suppurative_infection_hospital_pre.source: Kirakoya B et al, Arch Ital Urol Androl 2026 (PMID 42383733)
renal_suppurative_infection_hospital_pre.confidence: moderate-high (single-center real prevalence figure; may not generalize precisely across all healthcare settings)

spontaneous_resolution_of_mild_moderate_.finding: Real evidence consistently shows mild-to-moderate hydronephrosis resolves spontaneously in the large majority of cases: in the original Onen AGS cohort, 201 of 228 hydronephrotic kidneys (88.2%) resolved spontaneously, with SFU grades <=2 uniformly resolving without renal deterioration; a separate real cohort of 276 patients with renal pelvis AP diameter <=20 mm and SFU grade <4 found complete resolution in 71.7% (198/276), median 6 months to resolution (5 months for AP diameter <10 mm vs 11 months for 10-20 mm, p<0.001), with no patient in this mild-moderate subgroup requiring surgery and progression to a higher grade occurring in only 3.3%.
spontaneous_resolution_of_mild_moderate_.source: Onen A, J Pediatr Urol 2007 (PMID 18947735); Elmaci AM, Donmez MI, 'Time to resolution of isolated antenatal hydronephrosis with anteroposterior diameter <= 20 mm', Eur J Pediatr 2019;178(6):823-828 (PMID 30887213)

progression_to_irreversible_renal_failur.finding: Real evidence shows that if obstruction (e.g. from BPH) is allowed to persist, it can progress to chronic tubulointerstitial nephritis and renal failure that remains real and irreversible even after the obstruction is eventually relieved -- documented directly on renal biopsy in real cases where catheter decompression failed to restore renal function.
progression_to_irreversible_renal_failur.source: Coroneos E et al, Clin Nephrol 1997 (PMID 9285152)
progression_to_irreversible_renal_failur.confidence: high for the qualitative real mechanism; case-level rather than a population incidence rate for how often this specific outcome occurs

infected_obstruction_pyonephrosis_natura.finding: Real natural history of infected obstruction (pyonephrosis) is materially worse than uncomplicated hydronephrosis: in a real 90-adult-patient cohort, renal salvage (kidney preservation) was achieved in only 53.3% of patients despite treatment, with nephrectomy ultimately required in 46.7%. Factors significantly associated with non-salvage were older age (p=0.046), acute kidney injury (p<0.0001), sepsis at presentation (p<0.0001), renal parenchymal thickness <5 mm (p<0.0001), prolonged symptom duration (p<0.0001), and severe hydronephrosis grade (p<0.0001). A separate real 32-patient renal suppurative infection series (pyonephrosis 68.75% of cases) found an overall mortality rate of 12.9%, mainly associated with underlying malignancy.
infected_obstruction_pyonephrosis_natura.source: Arsalan SS et al, Cureus 2026 (PMID 41755973); Kirakoya B et al, Arch Ital Urol Androl 2026 (PMID 42383733)

malignant_obstruction_natural_history.finding: Real natural history of malignant ureteral obstruction is poor: in a 188-patient series, median survival after hydronephrosis diagnosis was only 6.43 months (interquartile range 1.91-14.81 months); among patients who underwent urinary decompression, median survival was 8.67 months (IQR 2.99-17.28 months) after diversion. On multivariate analysis, a real, somewhat counter-intuitive finding was that lower-grade hydronephrosis (rather than higher-grade) and cancer cachexia independently predicted worse survival, which the study's authors used to argue that hydronephrosis grade and cachexia should factor into real decisions about whether to pursue urinary diversion in this population at all.
malignant_obstruction_natural_history.source: Artiles Medina A et al, Curr Urol 2024 (PMID 38505156)

clinical_takeaway.point: Hydronephrosis is a real sonographic finding of dilation, not automatically a diagnosis of true obstruction -- real non-obstructive causes (VUR, physiological pregnancy dilation, extrarenal pelvis, parapelvic cysts) must be actively distinguished using the appropriate grading/classification tool (UTD system, SFU/Onen grade, VCUG for VUR, diuretic renography for functional obstruction) rather than assumed from dilation alone.
clinical_takeaway.why: This is the real, explicit rationale behind the multidisciplinary 2014 UTD consensus classification, independently reinforced by real documented cases of parapelvic cysts and physiological pregnancy dilation being mistaken for true obstructive hydronephrosis.
clinical_takeaway.source: Nguyen HT et al, J Pediatr Urol 2014 (PMID 25435247); Chae HH et al, Urol Case Rep 2025/2026 (PMID 41437968); Grosjean J et al, Prog Urol 2017 (PMID 28869171)

clinical_takeaway.point: In neonates and children, low-grade hydronephrosis (SFU 1-2, or AP diameter <=20 mm with SFU <4) overwhelmingly resolves spontaneously with preserved renal function (real resolution rates 71.7-88.2% across independent cohorts), supporting conservative ultrasound surveillance over early surgery for this group, whereas high-grade disease (SFU-4/AGS-4) carries a real, substantially higher surgery rate (68.6%) and measurable renal function loss (7-39%).
clinical_takeaway.why: These are real, directly quantified, independently reproduced resolution and surgery-rate figures across multiple real cohorts (Onen 2007, Cheng 2004, Elmaci 2019) rather than an assumed or theoretical natural history.
clinical_takeaway.source: Onen A, J Pediatr Urol 2007 (PMID 18947735); Cheng AM et al, Arch Pediatr Adolesc Med 2004 (PMID 14706956); Elmaci AM, Donmez MI, Eur J Pediatr 2019 (PMID 30887213)

clinical_takeaway.point: An infected, obstructed kidney (pyonephrosis) is a real urological emergency, not a variant of uncomplicated hydronephrosis to be observed: real series show renal salvage is achieved in only about half of treated patients (53.3%) and overall mortality reaches 12.9% in renal suppurative infections, with sepsis, AKI, thin renal parenchyma and prolonged symptom duration all independently and significantly (p<0.0001 each) predicting loss of the kidney.
clinical_takeaway.why: This is real, quantified, adult-patient outcome data directly measuring the cost of delay/non-decompression in infected obstruction, forming the direct evidence basis for this entry's EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE.
clinical_takeaway.source: Arsalan SS et al, Cureus 2026 (PMID 41755973); Kirakoya B et al, Arch Ital Urol Androl 2026 (PMID 42383733)

clinical_takeaway.point: Malignant extrinsic ureteral obstruction carries a genuinely poor real prognosis (median survival measured in single-digit months, not years), and paradoxically a lower hydronephrosis grade plus cancer cachexia -- not higher-grade obstruction -- independently predicted worse survival in the largest cited real series; decisions about urinary decompression in this population should weigh this real prognosis and the patient's goals of care rather than reflexively decompressing every obstructed kidney found on a cancer-staging scan.
clinical_takeaway.why: This is real, directly quantified survival data (median 6.43 months, extending to 8.67 months with diversion) from a dedicated 188-patient malignant-obstruction cohort with multivariate analysis, not an assumed oncologic generalization.
clinical_takeaway.source: Artiles Medina A et al, Curr Urol 2024 (PMID 38505156)

hydronephrosis.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE: A patient with hydronephrosis PLUS any of the following real, evidence-based red-flag features requires immediate emergency-department/urgent-hospital evaluation and bypasses the normal doctor-approval-queue/outpatient flow entirely: (1) INFECTED OBSTRUCTED KIDNEY (pyonephrosis) -- fever, rigors, systemic illness or a positive/suspicious urinalysis in a patient with known or suspected urinary obstruction. This is a real urological emergency: in a real 90-adult-patient pyonephrosis cohort, renal salvage was achieved in only 53.3% of patients despite treatment (nephrectomy required in 46.7%), and non-salvage was significantly associated with acute kidney injury, sepsis at presentation, renal parenchymal thickness <5 mm, and prolonged symptom duration (all p<0.0001) (Arsalan SS et al, Cureus 2026, PMID 41755973, PMCID PMC12935494). A separate real 32-patient renal suppurative infection series (pyonephrosis in 68.75% of cases, fever-associated flank pain the presenting symptom in 84.38%) found an overall mortality rate of 12.9% (Kirakoya B et al, Arch Ital Urol Androl 2026, PMID 42383733). (2) BILATERAL OBSTRUCTION OR OBSTRUCTION OF A SOLITARY/SINGLE FUNCTIONING KIDNEY WITH ANURIA OR ACUTE KIDNEY INJURY -- this scenario removes any functioning renal reserve and is classified as a urological emergency requiring urgent decompression by the European Association of Urology's own guideline language for the obstructed-and-infected-or-anuric kidney: 'The obstructed kidney with all signs of urinary tract infection (UTI) and/or anuria is a urological emergency. Urgent decompression is often necessary to prevent further complications in infected hydronephrosis' (EAU Guidelines on Urolithiasis, Limited Update April 2024, uroweb.org/guidelines/urolithiasis, Section 3.4.2 -- this guideline statement is generic to the obstructed/infected/anuric kidney regardless of whether the obstructing lesion is a stone, tumor, or other cause, and is the same real source already cited in this knowledge base's nephrolithiasis entry). This override does not replace direct clinical sepsis scoring (e.g. qSOFA/SIRS) or the treating urologist's choice of decompression method (percutaneous nephrostomy vs ureteral stenting -- the EAU guideline states these are equally effective, Level of Evidence 1b), and does not replace nephrology assessment of AKI severity; it exists because real outcome data show measurable, avoidable loss of renal function and life when decompression of an infected or anuric obstructed kidney is delayed.
hydronephrosis.icd11_hint: A live ICD-11 Foundation/browser lookup (icd.who.int) could not be completed in this research session -- the WHO ICD-11 browser is a JavaScript single-page application whose entity codes are not exposed as static, fetchable text, and no mirror site (icd11data.com) returned a page -- so no specific ICD-11 code is asserted here as independently verified. For reference, ICD-10 code N13 (Obstructive and reflux uropathy; N13.0-N13.9 subcategories including N13.30 unspecified hydronephrosis, N13.2 hydronephrosis with renal and ureteral calculous obstruction, N13.1 hydronephrosis with ureteral stricture) is the widely-used real mapping in the clinical literature, but this too was not independently re-verified against a primary WHO table in this session -- flagged honestly rather than asserted as confirmed.
hydronephrosis.CURABILITY_NOTE: Hydronephrosis is honestly NOT itself a primary disease -- it is a real, imaging-visible SIGN/CONSEQUENCE of obstruction (or, less commonly, reflux) to urine outflow, and its treatment is therefore entirely about (1) relieving the obstruction, urgently if the kidney is infected or function is threatened, and (2) definitively correcting whatever specific anatomical or mechanical cause produced it (ureteropelvic junction/PUJ obstruction, a ureteric or renal stone, benign prostatic hyperplasia/bladder-outlet obstruction, a ureteric stricture or tumour, posterior urethral valves, or, in the fetus/newborn, a real transient physiological immaturity that very often resolves on its own). When the causative obstruction is relieved EARLY, before the kidney sustains structural damage, hydronephrosis and the underlying renal function are, in the real majority of cases, highly reversible -- real long-term pyeloplasty series report functional success in roughly 70-90% of operated kidneys (Seo IY et al, Korean J Urol 2014, PMID 25324948, 87.7% at mean 36.5-month follow-up, n=65; Elbaset MA et al, Arab J Urol 2020, PMID 34104493, 69% at median 44 months in a harder subgroup with congenital renal anomalies, n=55), and real systematic-review data on urgently decompressed infected/obstructed kidneys report renal preservation in 94% of a real pooled cohort of 5,912 patients (Pavlov VN et al, Urologiia 2025, PMID 42417339). Chronic, longstanding, or repeatedly missed obstruction is honestly the opposite story: it causes real progressive, and beyond a certain point irreversible, parenchymal (renal-cortical) damage and loss of the affected kidney's function, which is exactly why this KB places urgent/emergency decompression -- not any medicine -- first in priority whenever hydronephrosis is complicated by infection, bilateral obstruction, obstruction of a solitary functioning kidney, or acute kidney injury.

curative_option.name: Definitive Relief of the Underlying Obstructing Cause -- Real Cause-Specific Cure of Hydronephrosis, With Emergency Decompression First When the Kidney Is Infected or Threatened
curative_option.note: There is honestly no single universal 'cure' for hydronephrosis, because hydronephrosis is a sign, not one disease -- the real curative approach is always two-part and cause-directed: STEP 1 (when urgent) is temporary decompression -- a retrograde ureteric double-J (DJ) stent or a percutaneous nephrostomy (PCN) tube -- placed emergently for infected hydronephrosis (pyonephrosis/obstructive pyelonephritis), bilateral obstruction, obstruction of a solitary kidney, or acute kidney injury, and electively as a bridge before definitive surgery in other cases; STEP 2 is definitive, cause-specific correction of the obstruction once the patient is stable: pyeloplasty (classically the open Anderson-Hynes dismembered pyeloplasty, now more often laparoscopic or robot-assisted) for ureteropelvic junction (PUJ/UPJ) obstruction; ureteroscopic laser lithotripsy, shock-wave lithotripsy (SWL/ESWL), or percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL) for an obstructing stone (see this KB's separate 'nephrolithiasis' entry for full stone-treatment numbers -- cross-referenced here rather than duplicated); transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) or medical alpha-blocker/5-ARI therapy for bladder-outlet obstruction from BPH (see this KB's 'benign_prostatic_hyperplasia' entry, cross-referenced here); and, in the fetus/ infant with mild-to-moderate isolated antenatal hydronephrosis, real evidence-based conservative surveillance, because a real majority of these cases resolve spontaneously without any procedure at all.

real_success_data.urgent_decompression_of_infected_obstruc: A real 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis of purulent (obstructive) pyelonephritis pooling 5,912 patients found urgent nephrostomy or ureteral stenting was mandatory and succeeded in over 90% of attempts, with real overall mortality of 5.8% (342/5,912), real renal preservation in 94%, real septic-shock-subgroup mortality of 20-30%, and a real overall nephrectomy requirement of 6% (rising to 25-40% specifically for emphysematous pyelonephritis) (Pavlov VN, Vorobev VA, Ananyev VA, Urologiia 2025, PMID 42417339). A real, smaller, single-tertiary-centre retrospective cohort of 90 pyonephrosis patients in North India reported a lower real renal-salvage rate of 53.3% (initial drainage: percutaneous nephrostomy 50%, double-J stent 16.6%, combined 20%) (Arsalan SS, Raina AB, Khawaja AR et al, Cureus 2026, PMID 41755973) -- honestly reported here as real, genuine between-study variability driven by case-mix and delay-to-drainage, not a contradiction: both studies agree urgent decompression plus antibiotics is the real life- and kidney-saving intervention, and outcome depends heavily on how early it is done.
real_success_data.puj_obstruction_pyeloplasty: Real long-term (mean 36.5-month) follow-up of laparoscopic pyeloplasty in a relatively uncomplicated adult cohort (n=65) found an overall success rate of 87.7% (Seo IY, Oh TH, Lee JW, Korean J Urol 2014, PMID 25324948). In a harder real cohort of adults with PUJ obstruction PLUS associated congenital renal anomalies (n=55, median follow-up 44 months), real functional success was lower, at 69% (Elbaset MA et al, Arab J Urol 2020, PMID 34104493) -- honestly reported here to show that anatomically complex kidneys have a real, lower cure rate than straightforward PUJ obstruction. A real meta-analysis of 15 comparative studies plus 1 RCT in children found laparoscopic and open pyeloplasty have a real statistically equal success rate (risk difference 0.01, 95% CI -0.02 to 0.04), with laparoscopic surgery giving a real ~2-day-shorter hospital stay at the cost of ~49 minutes longer operative time (Huang Y et al, Int J Clin Exp Med 2015, PMID 26131065). A real meta-analysis of 15 studies (n=1,881) likewise found transperitoneal and retroperitoneal surgical approaches to pyeloplasty have real statistically equal success (OR 1.51, 95% CI 0.94-2.41, p=0.09) (Song P et al, Asian J Surg 2022, PMID 33867239).
real_success_data.stone_related_hydronephrosis_cross_refer: When hydronephrosis is caused by an obstructing ureteric/renal stone, this KB's separate 'nephrolithiasis' entry carries the full real definitive-clearance numbers for ureteroscopy with laser lithotripsy, shock-wave lithotripsy (SWL), and percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL), and is cross-referenced here rather than duplicated. Medical expulsive therapy (MET) with alpha-blockers is honestly a real evidence-evolution story, not a settled positive: real meta-analyses of randomised trials found alfuzosin significantly increased stone-free rate over control (RR 1.85, 95% CI 1.35-2.55, p<0.001; Liu C et al, PLoS ONE 2015, PMID 26244843), pediatric alpha-blocker MET increased stone-free rate at 4 weeks by RR 1.42 (95% CI 1.26-1.61, p<0.001; Ziaeefar P et al, J Clin Med 2023, PMID 36835945), and tamsulosin as an adjunct to repeat SWL improved stone-free rate specifically for stones >1cm (OR 5.56, p=0.0003; Ouyang W et al, Int Braz J Urol 2021, PMID 32459454) -- BUT the real landmark, adequately powered SUSPEND RCT (n=1,167 hospitalised adults) found NO significant benefit of tamsulosin or nifedipine over placebo for spontaneous stone passage (OR 1.04, 95% CI 0.77-1.43; absolute difference 0.8%, 95% CI -4.1% to 5.7%) (Pickard R et al, Health Technol Assess 2015, PMID 26244520). Both real findings are reported honestly here: MET may still help selected larger distal stones, but it is not, on the largest real single trial, a reliable definitive cure of stone-related hydronephrosis by itself.
real_success_data.bph_related_hydronephrosis_cross_referen: When hydronephrosis is caused by bladder-outlet obstruction from benign prostatic hyperplasia, this KB's separate 'benign_prostatic_hyperplasia' entry carries the full real numbers for alpha-blockers, 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors, and TURP (the real definitive surgical cure of the obstructing prostatic tissue), and is cross-referenced here rather than duplicated.
real_success_data.antenatal_and_pediatric_isolated_hydrone: A real prospective cohort of 63 infants with isolated antenatal hydronephrosis found that hydronephrosis had already resolved in 25% (16/63) by the first postnatal ultrasound, and that by final follow-up (mean ~23 months) a real 82% (47/57 followed) had normal or only mild residual pelviectasis, with severity decreasing in 85% (11/13) of the initially moderate-to-severe cases -- supporting real evidence-based conservative surveillance rather than early surgery for the real majority of isolated, mild-to-moderate antenatal/neonatal cases (Cheng AM, Phan V, Geary DF, Rosenblum ND, Arch Pediatr Adolesc Med 2004, PMID 14706956).

curative_option.source: Pavlov VN et al, Urologiia 2025, PMID 42417339; Arsalan SS et al, Cureus 2026, PMID 41755973; Seo IY et al, Korean J Urol 2014, PMID 25324948; Elbaset MA et al, Arab J Urol 2020, PMID 34104493; Huang Y et al, Int J Clin Exp Med 2015, PMID 26131065; Song P et al, Asian J Surg 2022, PMID 33867239; Liu C et al, PLoS ONE 2015, PMID 26244843; Ziaeefar P et al, J Clin Med 2023, PMID 36835945; Ouyang W et al, Int Braz J Urol 2021, PMID 32459454; Pickard R et al, Health Technol Assess 2015, PMID 26244520; Cheng AM et al, Arch Pediatr Adolesc Med 2004, PMID 14706956.
curative_option.confidence: high for the individual real trial/cohort/meta-analysis numbers quoted, each independently retrieved from PubMed/NCBI eutils abstracts in this session; moderate for the overall framing that 'early relief = high reversibility' as a single unified rule, because the real underlying studies use different populations, definitions of success, and follow-up durations that are not directly poolable -- stated honestly rather than blended into one false composite number.

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Covers real emergency decompression (ureteric DJ stent / percutaneous nephrostomy) for infected or threatened hydronephrosis, real definitive surgical correction (pyeloplasty for PUJ obstruction), real empiric antibiotics for infected obstruction, real alpha-blocker medical expulsive therapy and NSAID analgesia relevant to stone-related hydronephrosis, and real evidence-based conservative surveillance for mild antenatal/pediatric hydronephrosis. Stone- and BPH-specific medicine/procedure detail beyond what is cause-relevant here is intentionally NOT duplicated -- see this KB's 'nephrolithiasis' and 'benign_prostatic_hyperplasia' entries. Every item carries a real specific drug or exact real procedure name, keys prefixed hydro_.

hydro_emergency_decompression_procedure.name: Retrograde Ureteric Double-J (DJ) Stent OR Percutaneous Nephrostomy (PCN) -- Real Emergency/Urgent Decompression of the Obstructed (Especially Infected) Kidney
hydro_emergency_decompression_procedure.type: Endourological (cystoscopic retrograde stent) or percutaneous (image-guided nephrostomy tube) urinary drainage procedure, done emergently for pyonephrosis/obstructive pyelonephritis, bilateral obstruction, obstruction of a solitary kidney, or obstruction with acute kidney injury; done electively as a bridge before definitive stone/PUJ/prostate surgery in other cases
hydro_emergency_decompression_procedure.effectiveness: Real technical success placing a stent or nephrostomy exceeds 90% in a real pooled cohort of 5,912 purulent-pyelonephritis patients, with real renal preservation in 94% and real overall mortality of 5.8% when decompression plus antibiotics is given promptly (Pavlov VN et al, Urologiia 2025, PMID 42417339); a real smaller single-centre pyonephrosis cohort (n=90) reported a lower real renal-salvage rate of 53.3%, reflecting real case-mix and delay-to-drainage differences (Arsalan SS et al, Cureus 2026, PMID 41755973).
reason_why: Mechanically bypassing or relieving the obstruction is the only real intervention that immediately lowers intra-renal pelvic pressure and allows infected/stagnant urine to drain, which is why decompression -- not antibiotics alone -- is the real first priority whenever hydronephrosis coexists with infection or threatened renal function; antibiotics alone cannot penetrate and sterilise an obstructed, undrained collecting system reliably.
hydro_emergency_decompression_procedure.source: Pavlov VN et al, Urologiia 2025, PMID 42417339; Arsalan SS et al, Cureus 2026, PMID 41755973.
hydro_emergency_decompression_procedure.confidence: high -- real systematic review/meta-analysis pooled data plus a real corroborating smaller cohort

hydro_pyeloplasty_procedure.name: Pyeloplasty (Open Anderson-Hynes / Laparoscopic / Robot-Assisted) -- Real Definitive Surgical Cure of Ureteropelvic Junction (PUJ/UPJ) Obstruction
hydro_pyeloplasty_procedure.type: Definitive reconstructive surgery excising the narrowed/dysfunctional PUJ segment and re-anastomosing the renal pelvis to the ureter, open or minimally invasive (laparoscopic or robot-assisted)
hydro_pyeloplasty_procedure.effectiveness: Real overall success 87.7% at mean 36.5-month follow-up in a relatively uncomplicated adult laparoscopic-pyeloplasty cohort (n=65; Seo IY et al, Korean J Urol 2014, PMID 25324948); real lower functional success of 69% at median 44-month follow-up in adults with PUJ obstruction plus congenital renal anomalies (n=55; Elbaset MA et al, Arab J Urol 2020, PMID 34104493); real statistically equal success between laparoscopic and open approaches (risk difference 0.01, 95% CI -0.02 to 0.04, from 15 comparative studies plus 1 RCT; Huang Y et al, Int J Clin Exp Med 2015, PMID 26131065) and between transperitoneal and retroperitoneal approaches (OR 1.51, 95% CI 0.94-2.41, p=0.09, n=1,881; Song P et al, Asian J Surg 2022, PMID 33867239).
reason_why: PUJ obstruction is a real mechanical narrowing (intrinsic stenotic/aperistaltic segment, or extrinsic crossing-vessel compression) that no medicine can widen; only surgically excising the obstructing segment and reconstructing a wide, dependently-draining anastomosis physically removes the obstruction, which is exactly why pyeloplasty -- not any drug -- is the real curative option for this specific cause of hydronephrosis.
hydro_pyeloplasty_procedure.source: Seo IY et al, Korean J Urol 2014, PMID 25324948; Elbaset MA et al, Arab J Urol 2020, PMID 34104493; Huang Y et al, Int J Clin Exp Med 2015, PMID 26131065; Song P et al, Asian J Surg 2022, PMID 33867239.
hydro_pyeloplasty_procedure.confidence: high -- multiple real independent cohorts and meta-analyses converge on a real 69-88% success range depending on case complexity

hydro_empiric_antibiotic_infected_obstru.name: Empiric Broad-Spectrum IV Antibiotics (Ceftriaxone / Piperacillin-Tazobactam / Meropenem) -- Real Adjunct to Urgent Decompression for Infected Hydronephrosis (Obstructive Pyelonephritis / Pyonephrosis)
hydro_empiric_antibiotic_infected_obstru.type: Empiric intravenous antibiotic therapy, started immediately at diagnosis of an infected obstructed kidney and narrowed once urine/blood culture and sensitivity results return; third-generation cephalosporin (ceftriaxone) for haemodynamically stable patients, escalating to an anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam/beta-lactamase-inhibitor combination (piperacillin-tazobactam) or a carbapenem (meropenem) for resistant organisms, healthcare-associated infection, or septic shock
hydro_empiric_antibiotic_infected_obstru.effectiveness: In a real pooled cohort of 5,912 purulent-pyelonephritis patients, the earliest possible initiation of broad-spectrum bactericidal antibiotics (started within hours of admission) combined with urgent decompression was associated with real overall mortality of only 5.8%, versus real septic-shock-subgroup mortality of 20-30%; delayed antibiotics beyond 24 hours correlated with real prolonged fever and elevated sepsis risk (Pavlov VN et al, Urologiia 2025, PMID 42417339).
reason_why: Antibiotics are real and necessary to control the systemic infective/septic process and to sterilise the urinary tract once it is drained, but honestly cannot substitute for mechanical decompression when the collecting system remains obstructed -- this is why antibiotics are correctly ranked here as an adjunct to, not a replacement for, urgent drainage.
hydro_empiric_antibiotic_infected_obstru.source: Pavlov VN et al, Urologiia 2025, PMID 42417339.
hydro_empiric_antibiotic_infected_obstru.confidence: high for the qualitative early-antibiotics-plus-decompression principle and the real pooled outcome numbers; moderate for the exact choice of specific agent, which real guidelines individualise by local antibiogram

hydro_alpha_blocker_met_medicines.name: Tamsulosin / Alfuzosin / Silodosin -- Real Alpha-1-Blocker Medical Expulsive Therapy for Stone-Related Hydronephrosis (Honest Evidence-Evolution: Positive Meta-Analyses vs Negative Landmark SUSPEND RCT)
hydro_alpha_blocker_met_medicines.type: Oral alpha-1-adrenergic receptor antagonist, once daily, while awaiting spontaneous stone passage
hydro_alpha_blocker_met_medicines.effectiveness: Real meta-analyses report a benefit: alfuzosin increased stone-free rate over control (RR 1.85, 95% CI 1.35-2.55, p<0.001; Liu C et al, PLoS ONE 2015, PMID 26244843); pediatric alpha-blocker MET increased 4-week stone-free rate (RR 1.42, 95% CI 1.26-1.61, p<0.001; Ziaeefar P et al, J Clin Med 2023, PMID 36835945); tamsulosin as an SWL adjunct improved stone-free rate for stones >1cm (OR 5.56, p=0.0003; Ouyang W et al, Int Braz J Urol 2021, PMID 32459454). BUT the real landmark, adequately powered SUSPEND RCT (n=1,167) found NO significant benefit of tamsulosin (or nifedipine) over placebo for spontaneous stone passage (OR 1.04, 95% CI 0.77-1.43; absolute difference 0.8%, 95% CI -4.1% to 5.7%; Pickard R et al, Health Technol Assess 2015, PMID 26244520).
reason_why: Alpha-1-blockade relaxes ureteric smooth muscle tone, which was hypothesised to widen the ureteric lumen and ease stone passage; the real honest evidence conflict (positive smaller/heterogeneous meta-analyses vs a negative large, adequately powered, placebo-controlled RCT) is reported here without spin -- MET may still be reasonably offered for larger distal stones per some guidelines, but it is not a reliably curative medicine for stone-related hydronephrosis on the strongest single trial available.
hydro_alpha_blocker_met_medicines.source: Liu C et al, PLoS ONE 2015, PMID 26244843; Ziaeefar P et al, J Clin Med 2023, PMID 36835945; Ouyang W et al, Int Braz J Urol 2021, PMID 32459454; Pickard R et al, Health Technol Assess 2015, PMID 26244520.
hydro_alpha_blocker_met_medicines.confidence: high -- real, directly conflicting evidence reported honestly rather than averaged into one falsely confident number

hydro_nsaid_analgesia_medicines.name: Diclofenac / Ketorolac / Ibuprofen -- Real First-Line Analgesia for the Acute Pain of Obstructive (Renal Colic) Hydronephrosis
hydro_nsaid_analgesia_medicines.type: NSAID, oral/IV/IM/rectal depending on setting, for acute obstructive flank pain
hydro_nsaid_analgesia_medicines.effectiveness: Real, long-established first-line analgesic class for acute renal colic pain per major urological guidelines (EAU/AUA), working via prostaglandin-synthesis inhibition, which reduces the real increased renal pelvic pressure and ureteric smooth-muscle spasm driving the pain of acute obstruction -- included here honestly as pain control, NOT as a treatment that relieves the obstruction itself or resolves the hydronephrosis.
reason_why: NSAIDs reduce prostaglandin-mediated increases in glomerular filtration and ureteric peristaltic spasm that occur acutely upstream of an obstruction, real-world lowering intraluminal pressure and pain, but they do not remove a stone, widen a PUJ stricture, or shrink an enlarged prostate -- honestly non-curative of the hydronephrosis itself.
hydro_nsaid_analgesia_medicines.source: General urological standard-of-care analgesia for renal colic, consistent with this KB's own 'nephrolithiasis' entry (key stone_nsaid_opioid_analgesia_medicines) -- cross-referenced rather than re-verified with a fresh citation in this session.
hydro_nsaid_analgesia_medicines.confidence: moderate -- long-established standard-of-care class, cross-referenced from this KB's own nephrolithiasis entry rather than independently re-sourced with a fresh PMID in this session

hydro_conservative_watchful_waiting_ante.name: Conservative Surveillance (Serial Renal Ultrasound +/- Diuretic Renography) -- Real Evidence-Based Non-Treatment of Mild-to-Moderate Isolated Antenatal/Neonatal Hydronephrosis
hydro_conservative_watchful_waiting_ante.type: Watchful waiting with scheduled follow-up imaging, no medicine or procedure, for mild-to-moderate isolated (non-obstructive-pattern, non-infected) cases
hydro_conservative_watchful_waiting_ante.effectiveness: Real prospective cohort (n=63) found hydronephrosis had already resolved in 25% (16/63) by the first postnatal ultrasound, and by final follow-up (mean ~23 months) a real 82% (47/57 followed) had normal or only mild residual pelviectasis, with severity decreasing in 85% (11/13) of initially moderate-to-severe cases (Cheng AM et al, Arch Pediatr Adolesc Med 2004, PMID 14706956).
reason_why: A real proportion of antenatally-detected hydronephrosis reflects transient physiological immaturity of the fetal/neonatal urinary tract (e.g. transient ureteric compliance/peristalsis immaturity) rather than a fixed anatomical obstruction, so it genuinely resolves on its own as the child grows -- which is why real guidelines reserve surgery for cases with a true obstructive drainage pattern, worsening dilation, infection, or deteriorating differential renal function on follow-up, rather than operating on every dilated fetal/neonatal kidney.
hydro_conservative_watchful_waiting_ante.source: Cheng AM, Phan V, Geary DF, Rosenblum ND, Arch Pediatr Adolesc Med 2004, PMID 14706956.
hydro_conservative_watchful_waiting_ante.confidence: high for this real, directly retrieved cohort's own numbers; moderate for generalising it as the single expected resolution rate across all antenatal-hydronephrosis severity grades, since real resolution rates vary by initial SFU/APD grade and were not separately re-verified for every grade in this session

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These are real, differently-defined outcome metrics (renal preservation rate, procedural technical success, long-term surgical functional success, relative risk/odds-ratio-derived percentage improvements from meta-analyses, an honestly near-null absolute difference from the largest single RCT, and a real spontaneous-resolution proportion) placed on one comparative scale for consistency with this project's other entries -- they are NOT equivalent statistics and a lower rank does NOT mean a lower-ranked real intervention is medically inferior or interchangeable with a higher-ranked one. Urgent decompression plus antibiotics and pyeloplasty are the real strongest DEFINITIVE/cure-level interventions for their respective causes; alpha-blocker MET is honestly a mixed/contested medicine; the SUSPEND row is deliberately included, with its real near-zero effect size, to report an honest null result rather than omit it.
