other_established_risk_factors.finding: Additional established or strongly associated risk factors, cited across the sources above and standard vascular-dementia reviews, include: smoking, hyperlipidaemia, obesity, physical inactivity, low educational attainment, older age, and genetic small-vessel disease syndromes such as CADASIL (NOTCH3 mutation) for early-onset cases. These act largely through the same shared mechanism of cumulative macrovascular and cerebral small-vessel injury as stroke, atrial fibrillation, diabetes and hypertension.
other_established_risk_factors.source: O'Brien JT, Thomas A, Lancet 2015;386:1698-1706 (PMID 26595643); Chabriat H et al., Lancet Neurol 2009;8:643-653 (PMID 19539236)
other_established_risk_factors.confidence: moderate-high - qualitative risk-factor list is well supported; this entry does not state a pooled quantitative relative risk for smoking/hyperlipidaemia/obesity specifically because none was verified this session (see report)

second_most_common_cause.finding: Vascular dementia is one of the most common causes of dementia after Alzheimer's disease, causing around 15% of dementia cases in the cited Western epidemiological synthesis; subcortical ischaemic vascular dementia (small-vessel disease) is now recognised as the more common vascular subtype than classic multi-infarct dementia in most population-based series.
second_most_common_cause.confidence: high for the '2nd most common, ~15%' figure as reported in this major review; this entry does not additionally assert region-specific prevalence percentages (e.g. for East Asian populations, sometimes reported as higher) because a separate verified source for those region-specific figures was not obtained this session

prevalence_rises_with_stroke_burden.finding: Because vascular dementia risk is directly tied to cerebrovascular event burden, prevalence estimates are highly dependent on stroke history: roughly 10% of stroke patients have pre-existing dementia, roughly 10% develop new dementia shortly after a first stroke, and this rises to over a third after a recurrent stroke, meaning population vascular-dementia burden will track population stroke incidence and recurrence rates.
prevalence_rises_with_stroke_burden.source: Pendlebury ST, Rothwell PM, Lancet Neurol 2009;8:1006-1018 (PMID 19782001)

mixed_dementia_prevalence.finding: Pure vascular dementia is less common at autopsy than mixed AD-plus-vascular pathology; in one community autopsy series only 12% of dementia cases had vascular dementia pathology alone, while 38% had AD pathology plus infarcts, indicating that the true population burden of vascular contribution to dementia (pure plus mixed) is substantially higher than the ~15% clinical-diagnosis figure for 'pure' vascular dementia alone.

natural_history.finding: Course depends heavily on subtype: classic multi-infarct vascular dementia tends to progress in a stepwise fashion, with periods of stability punctuated by abrupt declines coincident with new vascular events (and therefore is, in principle, more preventable/haltable by aggressive vascular risk-factor control after each event than a purely neurodegenerative process); subcortical small-vessel vascular dementia more often progresses gradually, resembling neurodegenerative dementias in trajectory. Recurrent stroke substantially worsens prognosis and cognitive trajectory (over a third of patients with recurrent stroke had dementia in the pooled analysis above), and survival after post-stroke dementia is reduced compared with post-stroke patients without dementia. There are no medications licensed specifically for vascular dementia itself (per O'Brien & Thomas), which is why the evidence-based focus of care is aggressive control of the causative vascular risk factors and secondary stroke prevention rather than a vascular-dementia-specific disease-modifying drug; this symptoms-and-diagnosis entry does not itself cover treatment, which is addressed in a separate treatment-focused pass on this same disease entry.
natural_history.source: O'Brien JT, Thomas A, Lancet 2015;386:1698-1706 (PMID 26595643); Pendlebury ST, Rothwell PM, Lancet Neurol 2009;8:1006-1018 (PMID 19782001)
natural_history.confidence: high

clinical_takeaway.finding: Vascular dementia should be actively suspected whenever cognitive decline is accompanied by a documented stroke/TIA temporally linked to the decline, a stepwise or fluctuating (rather than smoothly progressive) course, early gait disturbance or urinary incontinence, prominent executive/processing-speed impairment out of proportion to memory loss, focal neurological signs, or an imaging burden of infarcts/white-matter disease disproportionate to hippocampal atrophy. Because vascular dementia and Alzheimer's pathology very commonly co-exist (mixed dementia), and because vascular risk factors (hypertension, diabetes, atrial fibrillation, prior stroke, smoking, hyperlipidaemia) are the only currently modifiable levers proven to reduce cognitive decline risk (SPRINT MIND) or known to sharply raise it (stroke, AF, diabetes), the highest-value real clinical action is aggressive identification and control of these vascular risk factors and secondary stroke prevention, applied whether the dementia is judged 'pure' vascular or mixed.
clinical_takeaway.source: Synthesised from Roman GC et al. (PMID 8094895), Sachdev P et al. (PMID 24632990), O'Brien JT & Thomas A (PMID 26595643), Williamson JD et al. (PMID 30688979), and the risk-factor sources cited above

vascular_dementia.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE: Any sudden (minutes-to-hours) worsening of cognition, new focal neurological deficit (facial droop, arm/leg weakness, slurred speech, vision loss, severe imbalance), or new severe headache in a patient with known or suspected vascular dementia MUST be treated as a possible acute stroke/TIA and bypass the normal doctor-approval-queue flow entirely - call emergency services / go to the ER immediately (time-critical for thrombolysis/thrombectomy eligibility), the same way any acute stroke is a real medical emergency. Separately, any rapid (days-to-weeks) cognitive decline, especially with fluctuating consciousness, must prompt urgent medical evaluation to rule out treatable causes that mimic or worsen vascular dementia (delirium/infection, subdural haematoma, normal-pressure hydrocephalus, hypoglycaemia, medication toxicity, thyroid or B12 deficiency, non-convulsive seizure) before the decline is attributed to progression of the underlying vascular dementia itself.
vascular_dementia.CURABILITY_NOTE: Vascular dementia (VaD) is NOT curable and NOT reversible once neuronal/white-matter injury from infarcts, haemorrhage or chronic small-vessel disease has occurred - this must be stated plainly, exactly as for Alzheimer's disease in this knowledge base. Unlike Alzheimer's disease, however, VaD has no even-modest disease-modifying drug: cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine, which have real (if small) benefit in Alzheimer's, show only inconsistent, mostly non-significant-on-global-function benefit when tested specifically in VaD, and none is FDA/EMA-approved for this indication - donepezil (Black SE et al., Stroke 2003;34:2323-2330, PMID 12970516; Wilkinson D et al., Neurology 2003;61:479-486, PMID 12939421) and galantamine (Erkinjuntti T et al., Lancet 2002;359:1283-1290, PMID 11965273) produced small, statistically significant ADAS-cog gains but the pooled meta-analysis (Kavirajan H, Schneider LS, Lancet Neurol 2007;6:782-792, PMID 17689146; 9 RCTs, 3093 active vs 2090 placebo) rated the benefit 'of uncertain clinical significance', with only low-dose donepezil showing any global-function improvement; memantine (Orgogozo JM et al., Stroke 2002;33:1834-1839, PMID 12105362; Wilcock G et al., Int Clin Psychopharmacol 2002;17:297-305, PMID 12409683) improved ADAS-cog by ~2 points in both pivotal trials but produced NO significant improvement in global clinical impression (CIBIC-plus/CGI-C) in either trial. The real, achievable goal in VaD is therefore not treating the cognitive deficit that has already occurred, but halting FURTHER vascular injury through aggressive risk-factor control - the closest thing to 'preventing more of the disease'. The strongest real evidence for this is SPRINT MIND (9361 participants, intensive [target systolic BP <120mmHg] vs standard [<140mmHg] BP control): a significant 15% reduction in combined MCI-or-probable-dementia (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.74-0.97) and 19% reduction in MCI alone (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.69-0.95), though the probable-dementia-alone endpoint itself narrowly missed significance (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.67-1.04) (Williamson JD et al., JAMA 2019;321:553-561, PMID 30688979). In patients with prior stroke/TIA, PROGRESS (6105 participants, perindopril+indapamide) cut cognitive decline 19% (P=0.01) and dementia-with-recurrent-stroke 34% (P=0.03), though overall dementia risk alone was reduced only a non-significant 12% (P=0.2) (Tzourio C et al., Arch Intern Med 2003;163:1069-1075, PMID 12742805). Honesty requires reporting that not every plausible vascular-protective drug has trial-proven cognitive benefit: a Cochrane review found NO eligible randomised trial evidence that aspirin treats or slows VaD (Williams PS et al., Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2000, PMID 11034710), and statins showed no significant cognitive benefit even in Alzheimer's disease, with zero RCTs identified specifically in VaD (McGuinness B et al., Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2014, PMID 25004278). Antihypertensive treatment in the general older hypertensive population without prior cerebrovascular disease also failed to show a significant dementia-prevention benefit in an earlier Cochrane review (OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.74-1.07, not significant) (McGuinness B et al., Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2009, PMID 19821318) - the positive SPRINT MIND/PROGRESS results above are more recent, larger, and used stricter/earlier intervention targets or higher-risk (post-stroke) populations, which is the real, honest explanation for why they succeeded where the older review did not. REAL WORKING SOLUTION for the person who already has VaD: (1) aggressive, guideline-target control of BP, glucose and lipids, antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapy for atrial fibrillation, statin therapy for secondary vascular-event prevention, and smoking cessation - proven to reduce recurrent stroke and, per SPRINT MIND/PROGRESS, to measurably cut further cognitive decline, even though this does not reverse damage already done; (2) a cautious trial of donepezil, galantamine or memantine where a mixed AD-vascular picture is suspected or the family wants to try for a small, real, but inconsistent symptomatic benefit, with an honest discussion that the evidence in pure VaD is weaker than in Alzheimer's disease and that these drugs are being used off-label for this specific indication; (3) the same non-drug BPSD, falls, delirium, dysphagia, caregiver-support and advance-care-planning measures used in Alzheimer's disease, since these complications - not the cognitive test score - drive most of the morbidity and mortality in dementia of any cause.

curative_option.name: Aggressive Vascular Risk-Factor Control - Not a Cure for Existing Damage, the Real Ceiling for Halting Further Vascular Injury
curative_option.note: There is no procedure or drug that reverses infarcted brain tissue or established white-matter ischaemic damage. The real, evidence-based 'closest to a cure' in VaD is aggressive secondary/primary vascular-risk-factor control, which measurably reduces further cognitive decline and recurrent vascular events, even though it cannot restore tissue already lost. This is fundamentally a prevention-of-further-disease strategy, not a treatment for the cognitive deficit already present.

definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.name: Intensive Blood Pressure Control + Post-Stroke Secondary Prevention (Antihypertensive/Antiplatelet-Anticoagulant/Statin/Smoking Cessation)
definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.note: Intensive BP control (target systolic BP <120 mmHg vs standard <140 mmHg) in SPRINT MIND, and perindopril+indapamide BP lowering after stroke/TIA in PROGRESS, are the two largest real randomised trials directly demonstrating that vascular risk-factor control slows the cognitive trajectory that would otherwise progress to more VaD - this is real, statistically-significant, guideline-relevant evidence, not a symptomatic drug effect.

real_survival_data.sprint_mind_mci_or_probable_dementia_com: HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.74-0.97), 20.2 vs 24.1 events per 1000 person-years, intensive vs standard BP control, 9361 participants, median intervention 3.34y (Williamson JD et al., JAMA 2019;321:553-561, PMID 30688979)
real_survival_data.sprint_mind_mci_alone: HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.69-0.95), 14.6 vs 18.3 per 1000 person-years - statistically significant
real_survival_data.sprint_mind_probable_dementia_alone: HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.67-1.04), 7.2 vs 8.6 per 1000 person-years - did NOT reach statistical significance as a standalone endpoint
real_survival_data.progress_cognitive_decline_poststroke: 19% relative risk reduction (9.1% vs 11.0%, 95% CI 4-32%, P=0.01), perindopril+indapamide vs placebo, 6105 participants with prior stroke/TIA, mean follow-up 3.9y (Tzourio C et al., Arch Intern Med 2003;163:1069-1075, PMID 12742805)
real_survival_data.progress_dementia_alone_all_participants: 12% relative risk reduction (6.3% vs 7.1%, 95% CI -8% to 28%, P=0.2) - NOT statistically significant

definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.safety_note: Honest caveat: neither trial's PRIMARY standalone 'probable dementia' or 'dementia' endpoint reached statistical significance alone (SPRINT MIND HR 0.83, P not significant; PROGRESS RRR 12%, P=0.2) - the significant, reproducible benefit is on the composite MCI-or-dementia outcome, MCI alone, and cognitive-decline/dementia-with-recurrent-stroke endpoints. An earlier Cochrane review of BP-lowering in the GENERAL hypertensive population without prior cerebrovascular disease found no significant dementia-prevention benefit at all (OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.74-1.07) (McGuinness B et al., Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2009, PMID 19821318) - the real, honest interpretation is that intensive BP targets and treatment in HIGHER-RISK (already-hypertensive-to-SPRINT's-degree, or post-stroke) populations produced the significant results, not BP lowering as a universal dementia-prevention intervention in unselected older adults.
definitive_option_nonreversible_majority.source: Williamson JD et al., JAMA 2019;321:553-561, PMID 30688979; Tzourio C et al., Arch Intern Med 2003;163:1069-1075, PMID 12742805; McGuinness B et al., Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2009, PMID 19821318

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: This survey covers every real, sourced treatment-side intervention specifically studied in vascular dementia (VaD): the three cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine (all off-label for this indication - none holds FDA/EMA approval for VaD), and the vascular risk-factor-control drugs (antihypertensives, statins, antiplatelets) whose real evidence is for PREVENTING further vascular injury, not treating the existing cognitive deficit. Mixed/honest negative results are reported in full rather than omitted, per this knowledge base's standing policy.

vd_cholinesterase_inhibitor_galantamine.name: Galantamine - Largest and Most Positive Cholinesterase-Inhibitor Trial in Probable VaD / Mixed AD+CVD
specific_drugs: Galantamine (Reminyl/Razadyne and generics, 24 mg/day target dose, titrated from 8 mg/day)
vd_cholinesterase_inhibitor_galantamine.effectiveness: 6-month double-blind RCT, 592 participants (396 galantamine, 196 placebo) with probable VaD or AD-with-cerebrovascular-disease: ADAS-cog improved -1.7 (SE 0.4) with galantamine vs worsened +1.0 (SE 0.5) with placebo, a 2.7-point treatment difference (P<0.0001); CIBIC-plus stable-or-improved in 74% (213/288 evaluable) on galantamine vs 59% (95/161) on placebo (P=0.0001); activities of daily living improved (P=0.002) and behavioural symptoms improved (P=0.016).
vd_cholinesterase_inhibitor_galantamine.reason_why: VaD, like Alzheimer's disease, frequently involves a cholinergic deficit (loss of cholinergic projection fibres from ischaemic damage to periventricular white matter and basal forebrain nuclei), and mixed AD-vascular pathology is very common at autopsy in clinically-diagnosed dementia; galantamine reversibly inhibits acetylcholinesterase and allosterically modulates nicotinic receptors to increase cholinergic transmission.
vd_cholinesterase_inhibitor_galantamine.important_caveat: Nearly a third of this trial's population had AD-with-cerebrovascular-disease rather than pure probable VaD, so this positive result cannot be assumed to generalise fully to pure multi-infarct or subcortical small-vessel VaD without comorbid AD pathology. Galantamine is NOT FDA/EMA-approved for vascular dementia; this use is off-label.
vd_cholinesterase_inhibitor_galantamine.real_working_solution: Where a mixed AD-vascular clinical picture is suspected (very common in real practice), a supervised trial of galantamine 8 mg/day titrated to 16-24 mg/day over 4 weeks is reasonable, continuing only if the family/clinician perceive a real functional benefit at reassessment.
vd_cholinesterase_inhibitor_galantamine.source: Erkinjuntti T et al., Lancet 2002;359:1283-1290, PMID 11965273

vd_cholinesterase_inhibitor_donepezil.name: Donepezil - Two Large Pivotal 24-Week RCTs (Studies 307 and 308), Real But Small and Inconsistent Global-Function Benefit
specific_drugs: Donepezil (Aricept and generics, 5 mg/day and 10 mg/day)
vd_cholinesterase_inhibitor_donepezil.effectiveness: Study 307 (Black SE et al, 603 participants, 70.5% probable/29.5% possible VaD): ADAS-cog improved -1.90 (5 mg, P=0.001) and -2.33 (10 mg, P<0.001) vs placebo; CIBIC-Plus improved with 5 mg (P=0.014), CDR-Sum-of-Boxes improved with 10 mg (P=0.007); ADFACS (ADL) improved with both doses (P=0.02). Study 308 (Wilkinson D et al, 616 participants, 76% probable VaD): ADAS-cog improved -1.65 (5 mg, P=0.003) and -2.09 (10 mg, P=0.0002); CIBIC-Plus responder rate 39% (5 mg, P=0.004) and 32% (10 mg, P=0.047) vs 25% placebo.
vd_cholinesterase_inhibitor_donepezil.reason_why: Same cholinergic-deficit rationale as galantamine: donepezil reversibly and selectively inhibits acetylcholinesterase, increasing synaptic acetylcholine to partially compensate for ischaemic damage to cholinergic pathways.
vd_cholinesterase_inhibitor_donepezil.important_caveat: Global-function/ADAS-cog benefit did not scale cleanly with dose across the two trials (5 mg outperformed 10 mg on some global measures), and treatment-related withdrawal rose with 10 mg (21.8% vs 11.1% placebo in Study 307, P=0.005). The pooled meta-analysis rated the overall clinical significance of this benefit as uncertain (see meta-analysis entry below). Donepezil is NOT FDA/EMA-approved for vascular dementia; this use is off-label.
vd_cholinesterase_inhibitor_donepezil.real_working_solution: Start at 5 mg/day; only escalate to 10 mg/day if 5 mg is well tolerated and reassess for a genuine functional benefit at 3 months, given the higher discontinuation rate at 10 mg without a consistently larger global-function benefit.
vd_cholinesterase_inhibitor_donepezil.source: Black S et al., Stroke 2003;34:2323-2330, PMID 12970516; Wilkinson D et al., Neurology 2003;61:479-486, PMID 12939421

vd_cholinesterase_inhibitor_rivastigmine.name: Rivastigmine - Smallest Pooled Effect Size Among the Cholinesterase Inhibitors Studied in VaD
specific_drugs: Rivastigmine (Exelon and generics, oral capsule or transdermal patch) - off-label in VaD
vd_cholinesterase_inhibitor_rivastigmine.effectiveness: Pooled in the Kavirajan & Schneider meta-analysis of 9 RCTs (one rivastigmine trial included): ADAS-cog mean difference -1.10 points (95% CI -2.15 to -0.05) versus placebo - statistically significant (CI excludes 0) but the smallest effect size among all agents reviewed (donepezil 10 mg: -2.17; galantamine and donepezil 5 mg intermediate).
vd_cholinesterase_inhibitor_rivastigmine.reason_why: Same cholinergic-deficit-compensation mechanism as donepezil and galantamine.
vd_cholinesterase_inhibitor_rivastigmine.important_caveat: No large, independently-verified pivotal head-to-head VaD trial for rivastigmine was located in this research pass beyond its inclusion in the pooled meta-analysis; this entry is therefore sourced to the meta-analysis rather than a dedicated primary trial. Not FDA/EMA-approved for vascular dementia.
vd_cholinesterase_inhibitor_rivastigmine.real_working_solution: Reasonable alternative to donepezil/galantamine if GI tolerability with those agents is poor (the transdermal patch reduces cholinergic GI side effects versus oral dosing), but expect the smallest effect size of the class based on current pooled evidence.
vd_cholinesterase_inhibitor_rivastigmine.source: Kavirajan H, Schneider LS, Lancet Neurol 2007;6:782-792, PMID 17689146

vd_nmda_antagonist_memantine.name: Memantine - Two Pivotal RCTs (MMM300, MMM500): Real Cognitive Test Improvement, No Significant Global-Function Benefit
vd_nmda_antagonist_memantine.effectiveness: MMM300 (Orgogozo JM et al, 28 weeks, 321 randomised/288 ITT): ADAS-cog memantine +0.4 vs placebo -1.6, a 2.0-point treatment difference (95% CI 0.49-3.60); CIBIC-plus improved-or-stable in 60% memantine vs 52% placebo (P=0.227, NOT significant); MMSE significantly better with memantine (P=0.003). MMM500 (Wilcock G et al, 28 weeks, 579 randomised/548 ITT, 54 UK centres): ADAS-cog difference -1.75 points (95% CI -3.02 to -0.49) favouring memantine; CGI-C showed NO significant difference between groups.
vd_nmda_antagonist_memantine.reason_why: Chronic ischaemia and excitotoxic glutamate release are proposed contributors to neuronal injury in VaD; memantine is a low-to-moderate-affinity, voltage-dependent NMDA-receptor antagonist intended to reduce excitotoxic calcium influx while preserving physiological glutamatergic signalling needed for learning and memory.
vd_nmda_antagonist_memantine.important_caveat: Both pivotal VaD trials are a textbook example of a real, statistically significant cognitive-test-score improvement that did NOT translate into a significant global clinical (CIBIC-plus/CGI-C) benefit - this must be reported honestly rather than presented as a clear clinical win. Memantine is NOT FDA/EMA-approved for vascular dementia; this use is off-label.
vd_nmda_antagonist_memantine.real_working_solution: Reasonable to trial in moderate-severe VaD or when cholinesterase inhibitors are not tolerated, given its favourable adverse-event profile (dizziness the most common event, 11% vs 8% placebo in MMM500) and NICE TA217-style precedent from AD, but families should be told plainly that the pivotal VaD trials did not show a significant global-function benefit despite the ADAS-cog gain.
vd_nmda_antagonist_memantine.source: Orgogozo JM et al., Stroke 2002;33:1834-1839, PMID 12105362; Wilcock G et al., Int Clin Psychopharmacol 2002;17:297-305, PMID 12409683

vd_overall_cholinesterase_memantine_meta.name: Pooled Meta-Analysis Across All Cholinesterase Inhibitors and Memantine in VaD - Honest Overall Verdict
vd_overall_cholinesterase_memantine_meta.type: Meta-analysis / evidence synthesis (not a drug itself)
vd_overall_cholinesterase_memantine_meta.effectiveness: 9 RCTs, 3093 participants on active drug vs 2090 on placebo (3 donepezil, 2 galantamine, 1 rivastigmine, 2 memantine trials, one further study). ADAS-cog mean differences ranged from -1.10 (rivastigmine) to -2.17 (donepezil 10 mg) points, all nominally significant, but only low-dose donepezil showed a significant CGI-C functional improvement (OR 1.51); cholinesterase inhibitors caused significantly more dropouts and GI adverse effects (anorexia, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, insomnia) than placebo; memantine had a comparatively safer profile.
vd_overall_cholinesterase_memantine_meta.reason_why: Pooling increases statistical power across individually underpowered trials in a pathologically heterogeneous condition (multi-infarct, strategic single-infarct, subcortical small-vessel/Binswanger-type, and mixed AD-vascular VaD all differ in cholinergic and glutamatergic pathophysiology), giving the most reliable aggregate estimate of a real but small class effect.
vd_overall_cholinesterase_memantine_meta.important_caveat: The authors' own conclusion, quoted directly: these drugs produce cognitive benefits of 'uncertain clinical significance' in VaD - this is the single most authoritative honest verdict on cognitive-enhancer drugs in VaD and is why none is approved for this indication despite the individually significant trial results above.
vd_overall_cholinesterase_memantine_meta.source: Kavirajan H, Schneider LS, Lancet Neurol 2007;6:782-792, PMID 17689146

vd_antihypertensive_intensive_bp_control.name: Intensive Blood Pressure Control (SPRINT MIND) - Real, Significant Reduction in MCI/Combined Cognitive-Decline Outcome
vd_antihypertensive_intensive_bp_control.type: Antihypertensive (vascular risk-factor control, not symptomatic cognitive treatment)
specific_drugs: Any guideline antihypertensive regimen achieving intensive systolic BP target <120 mmHg (SPRINT protocol commonly used thiazide-type diuretics e.g. chlorthalidone, ACE inhibitors/ARBs, calcium-channel blockers e.g. amlodipine, and beta-blockers as needed, individualised per patient)
vd_antihypertensive_intensive_bp_control.effectiveness: 9361 participants, intensive (<120 mmHg) vs standard (<140 mmHg) systolic BP target, median treatment 3.34 years, total follow-up 5.11 years: combined MCI-or-probable-dementia HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.74-0.97, significant); MCI alone HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.69-0.95, significant); probable dementia alone HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.67-1.04, NOT significant as a standalone endpoint).
vd_antihypertensive_intensive_bp_control.reason_why: Chronic hypertension drives cerebral small-vessel disease (lipohyalinosis, lacunar infarcts, white-matter hyperintensities) that is the direct anatomical substrate of subcortical VaD; lowering BP more aggressively reduces the rate of new ischaemic injury accruing over time.
vd_antihypertensive_intensive_bp_control.important_caveat: The trial's own primary dementia endpoint did not reach significance alone - report the composite/MCI results honestly as the significant finding, not as if probable dementia itself was significantly reduced.
vd_antihypertensive_intensive_bp_control.real_working_solution: In patients able to tolerate it, target a systolic BP closer to <120 mmHg rather than the older <140 mmHg goal, individualised for orthostatic/frailty risk, as real, guideline-relevant vascular-injury prevention.
vd_antihypertensive_intensive_bp_control.source: Williamson JD et al., JAMA 2019;321:553-561, PMID 30688979

vd_antihypertensive_intensive_bp_control.name: BP Lowering in General Older Hypertensive Population Without Prior Cerebrovascular Disease - Real Negative Cochrane Finding
specific_drugs: Various antihypertensive drug classes pooled across 4 trials, unselected older hypertensive adults
vd_antihypertensive_intensive_bp_control.effectiveness: 4 RCTs, 15,936 hypertensive participants, mean age 75.4y, mean baseline BP 171/86 mmHg: dementia incidence 236/7767 (treatment) vs 259/7660 (placebo), OR 0.89 (95% CI 0.74-1.07) - NOT statistically significant despite significant BP reduction achieved.
vd_antihypertensive_intensive_bp_control.reason_why: Same vascular-injury-prevention mechanism as above, but this earlier review pooled trials in an UNSELECTED general hypertensive population (not the higher-risk, intensive-target or post-stroke populations of SPRINT MIND/PROGRESS), which is the authors' own proposed reason the benefit was not detected here.
vd_antihypertensive_intensive_bp_control.important_caveat: Cochrane's own conclusion, quoted directly: 'There is no convincing evidence from the trials identified that blood pressure lowering in late-life prevents the development of dementia or cognitive impairment in hypertensive patients with no apparent prior cerebrovascular disease.' Reported here in full for honesty, contrasting with the later, larger, intensive-target SPRINT MIND result above.
vd_antihypertensive_intensive_bp_control.source: McGuinness B et al., Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2009, PMID 19821318

vd_antihypertensive_secondary_prevention.name: Perindopril + Indapamide Post-Stroke BP Lowering (PROGRESS) - Real Significant Cognitive-Decline Reduction in a Higher-Risk Population
vd_antihypertensive_secondary_prevention.effectiveness: 6105 participants with prior stroke or TIA, mean follow-up 3.9 years: cognitive decline reduced 19% (9.1% vs 11.0%, 95% CI 4-32%, P=0.01); dementia occurring with recurrent stroke reduced 34% (P=0.03); overall dementia risk alone reduced only a non-significant 12% (193/3051, 6.3% vs 217/3054, 7.1%; 95% CI -8% to 28%, P=0.2).
vd_antihypertensive_secondary_prevention.reason_why: In a population that has already had a cerebrovascular event, further BP-driven ischaemic injury (and recurrent stroke, the strongest single driver of incident VaD) is directly reduced by BP lowering.
vd_antihypertensive_secondary_prevention.important_caveat: As with SPRINT MIND, the standalone 'dementia' endpoint (independent of recurrent stroke) did not reach significance - the real, significant, reproducible benefit is on cognitive decline and on the dementia-with-recurrent-stroke composite.
vd_antihypertensive_secondary_prevention.real_working_solution: In any patient with a prior stroke/TIA, guideline-target BP lowering with an ACE inhibitor/thiazide-type combination (or equivalent) is real, sourced secondary prevention against further cognitive decline, not merely against a second stroke.
vd_antihypertensive_secondary_prevention.source: Tzourio C et al., Arch Intern Med 2003;163:1069-1075, PMID 12742805

vd_statin_secondary_prevention.name: Statins - Proven for Secondary Vascular/Stroke Prevention, But Real Negative Evidence for Treating Established Cognitive Decline
specific_drugs: Rosuvastatin (used per standard cardiovascular/stroke secondary-prevention guidelines, not for cognitive treatment)
vd_statin_secondary_prevention.effectiveness: Cochrane review of statins FOR THE TREATMENT of existing dementia (4 RCTs, 1154 participants, all diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease - zero RCTs identified specifically in vascular dementia): ADAS-cog mean difference -0.26 (95% CI -1.05 to 0.52, P=0.51, NOT significant); MMSE mean difference -0.32 (95% CI -0.71 to 0.06, P=0.10, NOT significant); no significant difference in behaviour, global function or activities of daily living.
vd_statin_secondary_prevention.reason_why: Statins lower LDL cholesterol and have pleiotropic anti-inflammatory/endothelial effects that reduce atherosclerotic plaque burden and recurrent ischaemic vascular events - a real mechanism for preventing FURTHER vascular injury - but there is no verified mechanism by which they reverse cognition already lost to prior infarcts.
vd_statin_secondary_prevention.important_caveat: Do not present statins as a 'VaD cognitive treatment' - the honest evidence base shows no benefit on cognition even in Alzheimer's disease, and no dedicated VaD cognitive trial exists at all. Their real, correct indication in a VaD patient is standard secondary cardiovascular/stroke-risk-factor control (per usual lipid/statin guidelines for atherosclerotic disease), not cognitive treatment.
vd_statin_secondary_prevention.real_working_solution: Prescribe a statin for its real, guideline-based indication - secondary prevention of recurrent stroke/vascular events in a patient with cerebrovascular disease - and do not market it to the family as a dementia treatment.
vd_statin_secondary_prevention.source: McGuinness B et al., Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2014, PMID 25004278

vd_antiplatelet_secondary_prevention.name: Antiplatelet Therapy (Aspirin) - Proven for Secondary Stroke Prevention, Real Zero-RCT-Evidence Gap for Treating VaD Cognition
specific_drugs: Clopidogrel (alternative/dual therapy per standard stroke secondary-prevention guidelines)
vd_antiplatelet_secondary_prevention.effectiveness: A dedicated Cochrane review searching specifically for RCT evidence of aspirin's effect ON VaD found ZERO eligible randomised controlled trials despite aspirin being widely prescribed for this population; verbatim conclusion: 'There is no evidence that aspirin is effective in treating patients with a diagnosis of vascular dementia.'
vd_antiplatelet_secondary_prevention.reason_why: Antiplatelet therapy is well established for reducing recurrent ischaemic stroke and cardiovascular events (the proven anatomical driver of incident/worsening VaD) via inhibition of platelet aggregation, but this benefit for stroke recurrence has never been formally tested as a cognitive endpoint in a dedicated VaD RCT.
vd_antiplatelet_secondary_prevention.important_caveat: This is a genuine evidence gap, not proof of no effect - the Cochrane authors explicitly called for trials of aspirin's effect on cognition, behaviour and quality of life in VaD, and also flagged the real, unresolved safety question of cerebral/GI haemorrhage risk in this population. Widespread clinical use is based on the general stroke-prevention literature, not on VaD-specific cognitive trial evidence.
vd_antiplatelet_secondary_prevention.real_working_solution: Use antiplatelet (or anticoagulant, e.g. a DOAC, if atrial fibrillation is present) therapy for its real, guideline-proven indication of secondary stroke/vascular-event prevention in a patient with cerebrovascular disease - this is sound practice - while being honest with families that it is not a proven cognitive treatment for VaD itself.
vd_antiplatelet_secondary_prevention.source: Williams PS et al., Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2000, PMID 11034710

ranked_high_to_low.name: Galantamine 24 mg/day (probable VaD / AD+CVD)
ranked_high_to_low.metric: CIBIC-plus stable-or-improved in 74% (galantamine) vs 59% (placebo) at 6 months, P=0.0001; ADAS-cog treatment effect 2.7 points (P<0.0001); off-label, not FDA/EMA-approved for VaD
ranked_high_to_low.source: Erkinjuntti T et al., Lancet 2002;359:1283-1290, PMID 11965273

ranked_high_to_low.name: Memantine 20 mg/day (mild-moderate VaD) - CIBIC-plus responder rate
ranked_high_to_low.metric: CIBIC-plus improved-or-stable 60% memantine vs 52% placebo, P=0.227 NOT significant (MMM300, N=321); ADAS-cog improved by ~2 points in both MMM300 and MMM500 (significant) but CGI-C/global function NOT significantly different from placebo in either pivotal trial; off-label, not FDA/EMA-approved for VaD
ranked_high_to_low.source: Orgogozo JM et al., Stroke 2002;33:1834-1839, PMID 12105362; Wilcock G et al., Int Clin Psychopharmacol 2002;17:297-305, PMID 12409683

ranked_high_to_low.name: Rivastigmine (oral/transdermal) - pooled ADAS-cog effect
ranked_high_to_low.metric: ADAS-cog mean difference -1.10 points (95% CI -2.15 to -0.05) vs placebo - smallest effect size of the cholinesterase-inhibitor class reviewed; no dedicated large pivotal VaD trial independently verified this session; off-label, not FDA/EMA-approved for VaD
ranked_high_to_low.source: Kavirajan H, Schneider LS, Lancet Neurol 2007;6:782-792, PMID 17689146

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These real metrics come from DIFFERENT trials measuring DIFFERENT endpoints (ADAS-cog points, CIBIC-plus/CIBIC-Plus responder percentages, hazard ratios, relative risk reductions, or odds ratios), so the ordering is a directional judgement of real, sourced benefit size and significance, NOT a single common-scale percentage ranking; effectiveness_pct is populated only where a genuine, directly reported responder/event percentage or convertible relative-risk figure exists (None where no such number exists, e.g. rivastigmine's meta-analysis-only point-scale result). Rows 7-9 (effectiveness_pct 0.0) are REAL NEGATIVE OR ZERO-EVIDENCE Cochrane findings, reported in full rather than omitted - they are not proof the underlying drug class (antihypertensives generally, statins, antiplatelets) is useless, only that the SPECIFIC endpoint/population tested did not show significant cognitive benefit; each drug class remains correctly indicated for its own proven vascular/stroke-prevention role (see curative_option and the corresponding exhaustive_medicine_survey entries). None of rows 1, 2, 5 or 6 (the cognitive-enhancer drugs) is FDA/EMA-approved specifically for vascular dementia - all represent off-label use supported by the individual trial evidence quoted, and the pooled meta-analysis (Kavirajan & Schneider 2007, PMID 17689146) rates their overall class benefit in VaD as 'of uncertain clinical significance'.

glioma.name: Glioma (Brain Tumour)
glioma.icd11_hint: 2A00 Gliomas of brain (ICD-10 equivalent C71.9 Malignant neoplasm of brain, unspecified) - could not be independently re-verified against the live WHO ICD-11 browser in this session because icd.who.int is a JavaScript-rendered application that returned no code text to automated fetch; flagged moderate confidence pending manual confirmation on the ICD-11 MMS browser.
glioma.CURABILITY_NOTE: Glioma outcomes are genuinely bimodal by molecular subtype and grade, and the honest answer must lead with the real best-case group rather than hide it: WHO grade 2-3 IDH-mutant, 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendroglioma treated with maximal safe resection plus radiotherapy and PCV chemotherapy (procarbazine, lomustine, vincristine) has a REAL median overall survival of 14.7 years in the 1p/19q-codeleted subgroup of RTOG 9402 (vs 7.3 years with radiotherapy alone, HR 0.59, P=.03; Cairncross JG et al., J Clin Oncol 2013;31:337-343, PMID 23071247), and in the companion EORTC 26951 trial the codeleted subgroup's median survival with PCV+RT was NOT YET REACHED at long-term follow-up versus 112 months (9.3 years) with radiotherapy alone (HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.31-1.03; van den Bent MJ et al., J Clin Oncol 2013;31:344-350, PMID 23071237) - a meaningful minority of these patients live one to two decades or longer with a real chance of durable, cure-like disease control, especially with complete resection. This is the real working solution for the most favourable molecular subtype and it is stated first, honestly, because it is true and verifiable, not because it generalises to all glioma. The harder truth, which must equally be stated and not hidden, is that glioblastoma (IDH-wildtype, WHO grade 4, the most common adult glioma) remains genuinely difficult to cure despite the best available therapy: even with maximal safe resection plus the Stupp protocol (concurrent radiotherapy + temozolomide, then 6 cycles of adjuvant temozolomide), median overall survival is only 14.6 months (vs 12.1 months with radiotherapy alone), 2-year survival 26.5% (vs 10.4%), and 5-year survival just 9.8% (vs 1.9% with radiotherapy alone) (Stupp R et al., N Engl J Med 2005;352:987-996, PMID 15758009; Stupp R et al., Lancet Oncol 2009;10:459-466, PMID 19269895). Adding tumor-treating fields (Optune) to maintenance temozolomide improves median OS further to 20.9 months (vs 16.0 months with temozolomide alone, HR 0.63, P<.001; Stupp R et al., JAMA 2017;318:2306-2316, PMID 29260225), and MGMT promoter methylation identifies a subgroup that benefits most from temozolomide (median OS 21.7 months, 95% CI 17.4-30.4, in methylated patients receiving temozolomide+radiotherapy; Hegi ME et al., N Engl J Med 2005;352:997-1003, PMID 15758010) - real, incremental, evidence-based gains, but glioblastoma is NOT curable with today's standard therapy for the great majority of patients, and this knowledge base states that plainly rather than dressing it up. The real, honest, and actionable message is therefore molecular-subtype-stratified, not one-size-fits-all: test every glioma for IDH mutation and 1p/19q codeletion status (WHO CNS5 classification; review of cIMPACT-NOW criteria, PMID 35562131) at diagnosis, because this single step tells the patient and family which of these two very different real prognostic realities they are in, and drives which of the treatments below gives the real best chance of long-term survival.

curative_option.name: Maximal Safe Surgical Resection Followed by Molecular-Subtype-Stratified Adjuvant Therapy - The Real Foundational Curative-Intent Approach Across Glioma Grades
curative_option.note: Surgery is the real first step for essentially every glioma where safe resection is feasible, both because greater extent of resection is independently associated with longer survival at every grade, and because it provides the tissue needed for the IDH-mutation/1p19q-codeletion/MGMT-methylation molecular testing that determines which adjuvant pathway below (PCV+RT for codeleted oligodendroglioma vs the Stupp protocol +/- tumor-treating fields for IDH-wildtype glioblastoma) gives the real best chance of long-term, in a minority of cases cure-like, survival.

surgical_foundation_extent_of_resection.name: Maximal Safe Resection (Gross Total Resection where achievable) vs Subtotal Resection/Biopsy
surgical_foundation_extent_of_resection.note: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 37 studies covering over 41,000 glioblastoma patients found gross total resection (GTR) substantially reduces mortality compared with subtotal resection (STR), independent of adjuvant therapy received, though the authors rated underlying evidence quality moderate-to-low by GRADE criteria because no randomised trial of GTR vs STR is ethical or feasible.

real_survival_data.one_year_mortality_relative_risk: RR 0.62 (95% CI 0.56-0.69, P<.001) for GTR vs STR; number needed to treat (NNT) = 9
real_survival_data.two_year_mortality_relative_risk: RR 0.84 (95% CI 0.79-0.89, P<.001) for GTR vs STR; NNT = 17
real_survival_data.progression_free_survival: 1-year PFS relative risk 0.66 (95% CI 0.43-0.99) favouring GTR

surgical_foundation_extent_of_resection.source: Brown TJ et al., 'Association of the Extent of Resection With Survival in Glioblastoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis', JAMA Oncol 2016;2:1460-1469, PMID 27310651

gbm_stupp_protocol_radiotherapy_concurre.name: The Stupp Protocol - Concurrent Radiotherapy + Temozolomide, then 6 Cycles Adjuvant Temozolomide (Standard of Care for IDH-Wildtype Glioblastoma)
gbm_stupp_protocol_radiotherapy_concurre.note: This is the real, guideline-defining standard of care for newly diagnosed glioblastoma worldwide since 2005, and remains the backbone onto which tumor-treating fields is now added.

real_survival_data.five_year_survival_long_term_followup: 9.8% (95% CI 6.4-14.0) with RT+TMZ vs 1.9% (95% CI 0.6-4.4) with RT alone

mgmt_methylation_predictive_biomarker.finding: MGMT promoter methylation silences the DNA-repair enzyme that otherwise reverses temozolomide's alkylating damage, so methylated tumours derive the largest benefit from temozolomide.
mgmt_methylation_predictive_biomarker.real_survival_data: Median overall survival 21.7 months (95% CI 17.4-30.4) in MGMT-methylated patients treated with temozolomide+radiotherapy; the abstract-reported differential in unmethylated patients was smaller and did not reach statistical significance.
mgmt_methylation_predictive_biomarker.source: Hegi ME et al., 'MGMT gene silencing and benefit from temozolomide in glioblastoma', N Engl J Med 2005;352:997-1003, PMID 15758010

gbm_stupp_protocol_radiotherapy_concurre.source: Stupp R et al., N Engl J Med 2005;352:987-996, PMID 15758009; Stupp R et al. (5-year follow-up), Lancet Oncol 2009;10:459-466, PMID 19269895

oligodendroglioma_1p19q_codeleted_pcv_pl.name: PCV Chemotherapy (Procarbazine + Lomustine + Vincristine) Added to Radiotherapy - Real Long-Term, in a Meaningful Minority Cure-Like, Survival in 1p/19q-Codeleted Anaplastic Oligodendroglioma
oligodendroglioma_1p19q_codeleted_pcv_pl.note: This is the real best-case molecular subtype in this knowledge base's glioma entry: two independent phase III randomised trials with over a decade of follow-up both show a doubling-or-more of median survival when PCV is added to radiotherapy specifically in tumours with 1p/19q co-deletion.

real_survival_data.rtog_9402_codeleted_subgroup: Median OS 14.7 years (PCV+RT) vs 7.3 years (RT alone), HR 0.59, P=.03
real_survival_data.eortc_26951_codeleted_subgroup: Median OS not reached (PCV+RT) vs 112 months/9.3 years (RT alone), HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.31-1.03)
real_survival_data.eortc_26951_overall_unselected_populatio: Median OS 42.3 months (PCV+RT) vs 30.6 months (RT alone)

oligodendroglioma_1p19q_codeleted_pcv_pl.source: Cairncross JG et al., J Clin Oncol 2013;31:337-343, PMID 23071247; van den Bent MJ et al., J Clin Oncol 2013;31:344-350, PMID 23071237

glioma_surgery_maximal_safe_resection.name: Maximal Safe Surgical Resection (Gross Total Resection where feasible) - Foundational Real First Step Across All Glioma Grades
glioma_surgery_maximal_safe_resection.type: Curative-intent/cytoreductive neurosurgery, often with awake craniotomy and intraoperative mapping/5-ALA fluorescence guidance to maximise resection while preserving function
glioma_surgery_maximal_safe_resection.effectiveness: Meta-analysis of 37 studies, >41,000 glioblastoma patients: GTR vs STR reduced 1-year mortality (RR 0.62, 95% CI 0.56-0.69, P<.001, NNT 9) and 2-year mortality (RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.79-0.89, P<.001, NNT 17); benefit is independent of and additive to adjuvant chemoradiotherapy.
glioma_surgery_maximal_safe_resection.reason_why: Cytoreduction lowers tumour burden before radio/chemotherapy, relieves mass effect and raised intracranial pressure, and yields the tissue needed for IDH/1p19q/MGMT molecular testing that determines the entire subsequent treatment pathway.
glioma_surgery_maximal_safe_resection.important_caveat: No randomised trial of GTR vs STR exists or is ethically feasible, so evidence is from retrospective/observational series (GRADE moderate-to-low); resection extent must always be balanced against eloquent-cortex function preservation.
glioma_surgery_maximal_safe_resection.real_working_solution: Maximal SAFE resection (not resection at any functional cost) by a specialist neuro-oncology surgical team, with intraoperative mapping in eloquent regions, is the real first-line intervention for essentially every newly diagnosed glioma amenable to surgery.
glioma_surgery_maximal_safe_resection.source: Brown TJ et al., JAMA Oncol 2016;2:1460-1469, PMID 27310651

glioma_pcv_chemotherapy_oligodendrogliom.name: PCV Chemotherapy (Procarbazine, Lomustine/CCNU, Vincristine) Added to Radiotherapy - Real Best-Case Long-Term Survival in 1p/19q-Codeleted Anaplastic Oligodendroglioma
glioma_pcv_chemotherapy_oligodendrogliom.effectiveness: RTOG 9402: in the 1p/19q-codeleted subgroup, median OS 14.7 years with PCV+RT vs 7.3 years with RT alone (HR 0.59, P=.03). EORTC 26951: codeleted subgroup median OS not reached with PCV+RT vs 112 months (9.3 years) with RT alone (HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.31-1.03); unselected overall population 42.3 vs 30.6 months.
glioma_pcv_chemotherapy_oligodendrogliom.reason_why: 1p/19q co-deletion marks a distinct oligodendroglial lineage with especially high sensitivity to alkylating chemotherapy and radiotherapy, and identifies the glioma subgroup with the best real long-term prognosis of any diffuse glioma.
glioma_pcv_chemotherapy_oligodendrogliom.important_caveat: Benefit is concentrated in the molecularly-defined 1p/19q-codeleted subgroup; PCV is myelosuppressive and neurotoxic (peripheral neuropathy from vincristine) and requires close haematologic monitoring across its ~6 cycles.
glioma_pcv_chemotherapy_oligodendrogliom.real_working_solution: Every newly diagnosed anaplastic oligodendroglioma/oligoastrocytoma should be tested for 1p/19q co-deletion; codeleted tumours should receive radiotherapy plus PCV (or, per more recent practice, temozolomide is sometimes substituted for lomustine-based regimens with better tolerability, though PCV has the longest randomised follow-up data).
glioma_pcv_chemotherapy_oligodendrogliom.source: Cairncross JG et al., J Clin Oncol 2013;31:337-343, PMID 23071247; van den Bent MJ et al., J Clin Oncol 2013;31:344-350, PMID 23071237

glioma_radiotherapy_temozolomide_stupp_p.name: Stupp Protocol - Concurrent Radiotherapy + Temozolomide, then 6 Cycles Adjuvant Temozolomide - Standard of Care for IDH-Wildtype Glioblastoma
specific_drugs: Temozolomide (Temodar/Temodal, 75 mg/m2/day concurrent with RT, then 150-200 mg/m2/day for 5 days per 28-day cycle x6 adjuvant)
glioma_radiotherapy_temozolomide_stupp_p.effectiveness: Median OS 14.6 months (RT+TMZ) vs 12.1 months (RT alone); 2-year survival 26.5% vs 10.4%; 5-year survival at long-term follow-up 9.8% (95% CI 6.4-14.0) vs 1.9% (95% CI 0.6-4.4).
glioma_radiotherapy_temozolomide_stupp_p.reason_why: Temozolomide is a small-molecule oral alkylating agent that crosses the blood-brain barrier and methylates DNA (O6-guanine), causing cytotoxic mismatch-repair-mediated cell death that synergises with radiotherapy's DNA damage.
glioma_radiotherapy_temozolomide_stupp_p.important_caveat: Benefit is concentrated in MGMT-promoter-methylated tumours (median OS 21.7 months); even with this protocol the great majority of glioblastoma patients are NOT cured, and this must be stated honestly rather than minimised.
glioma_radiotherapy_temozolomide_stupp_p.real_working_solution: This remains the real, guideline-mandated (NCCN/EANO) standard of care for newly diagnosed IDH-wildtype glioblastoma after maximal safe resection, in patients fit enough for chemoradiotherapy (typically age <70-75 with good performance status; hypofractionated RT+TMZ is used in frail/elderly patients per the Perry NEJM 2017 trial).
glioma_radiotherapy_temozolomide_stupp_p.source: Stupp R et al., N Engl J Med 2005;352:987-996, PMID 15758009; Stupp R et al., Lancet Oncol 2009;10:459-466, PMID 19269895

glioma_mgmt_methylation_biomarker_temozo.name: MGMT Promoter Methylation Testing - Real Predictive Biomarker for Temozolomide Benefit in Glioblastoma
glioma_mgmt_methylation_biomarker_temozo.type: Molecular/epigenetic biomarker test guiding chemotherapy decision (not itself a drug)
glioma_mgmt_methylation_biomarker_temozo.effectiveness: MGMT-methylated patients treated with temozolomide+radiotherapy achieved median OS 21.7 months (95% CI 17.4-30.4); the survival differential attributable to temozolomide was smaller and not statistically significant in unmethylated tumours per the original report.
glioma_mgmt_methylation_biomarker_temozo.reason_why: MGMT (O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase) is the DNA-repair enzyme that reverses temozolomide's cytotoxic alkylation; promoter methylation silences this gene, so methylated tumours cannot repair the damage and are far more sensitive to the drug.
glioma_mgmt_methylation_biomarker_temozo.important_caveat: Testing does not currently withhold temozolomide from unmethylated patients in standard practice (small benefit is still possible and few alternatives exist), but it materially changes prognostic counselling and clinical-trial eligibility.
glioma_mgmt_methylation_biomarker_temozo.real_working_solution: MGMT promoter methylation status should be tested at diagnosis in every glioblastoma to inform prognosis and counselling alongside the Stupp protocol decision.
glioma_mgmt_methylation_biomarker_temozo.source: Hegi ME et al., N Engl J Med 2005;352:997-1003, PMID 15758010

glioma_tumor_treating_fields_optune_ef14.name: Tumor Treating Fields (Optune, NovoTTF-100A) Added to Maintenance Temozolomide - Real Survival Benefit in Newly Diagnosed Glioblastoma (EF-14 Trial)
glioma_tumor_treating_fields_optune_ef14.type: Wearable scalp-applied alternating electric field device (200 kHz), used continuously (>=18 hours/day) with maintenance temozolomide
glioma_tumor_treating_fields_optune_ef14.effectiveness: EF-14 randomised trial (n=695): median OS 20.9 months (TTFields+TMZ) vs 16.0 months (TMZ alone), HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.53-0.76, P<.001).
glioma_tumor_treating_fields_optune_ef14.reason_why: Low-intensity alternating electric fields disrupt mitotic spindle formation and organelle assembly during tumour cell division, preferentially affecting rapidly dividing glioma cells while sparing quiescent normal neurons.
glioma_tumor_treating_fields_optune_ef14.important_caveat: Requires shaving the scalp and wearing the device continuously for most of the day/night for maximum benefit, which is a real adherence and quality-of-life burden; device is costly and not universally reimbursed/available outside major centres.
glioma_tumor_treating_fields_optune_ef14.real_working_solution: Added to maintenance temozolomide after completion of the Stupp protocol's concurrent phase, TTFields is now an NCCN category 1 option and gives a real, trial-proven several-month survival extension on top of standard chemoradiotherapy.

glioma_bevacizumab_recurrent_response_ra.name: Bevacizumab (+/- Irinotecan) - Real Objective Response Rate in Recurrent Glioblastoma (BRAIN Study)
glioma_bevacizumab_recurrent_response_ra.type: Anti-VEGF monoclonal antibody, alone or with topoisomerase-I-inhibitor chemotherapy
glioma_bevacizumab_recurrent_response_ra.effectiveness: Phase II BRAIN study, recurrent glioblastoma: bevacizumab alone achieved 6-month PFS 42.6% and objective response rate 28.2%; bevacizumab+irinotecan achieved 6-month PFS 50.3% and objective response rate 37.8%.
glioma_bevacizumab_recurrent_response_ra.reason_why: Glioblastoma is a highly vascular, VEGF-driven tumour; bevacizumab neutralises VEGF-A, reducing tumour vascular permeability/oedema and objectively shrinking a substantial minority of recurrent tumours on imaging.
glioma_bevacizumab_recurrent_response_ra.important_caveat: This is a response-rate/PFS benefit in the recurrent (non-curative) setting, not a proven overall-survival benefit; no randomised trial of bevacizumab in recurrent GBM has shown an OS improvement.
glioma_bevacizumab_recurrent_response_ra.real_working_solution: Bevacizumab is a real, FDA-approved (2009, accelerated approval) option for recurrent glioblastoma, particularly useful for reducing steroid-refractory peritumoural oedema and achieving objective radiographic/symptomatic response, even though it does not extend overall survival.
glioma_bevacizumab_recurrent_response_ra.source: Friedman HS et al. (BRAIN study), J Clin Oncol 2009;27:4733-4740, PMID 19720927

glioma_bevacizumab_newly_diagnosed_no_su.name: Bevacizumab Added to Radiotherapy+Temozolomide in Newly Diagnosed Glioblastoma - Real Honest Negative Overall-Survival Result (AVAglio Trial)
glioma_bevacizumab_newly_diagnosed_no_su.type: Anti-VEGF monoclonal antibody added to standard Stupp protocol
glioma_bevacizumab_newly_diagnosed_no_su.effectiveness: AVAglio randomised trial: progression-free survival improved (10.7 vs 7.3 months with placebo) but median overall survival was NOT significantly improved (15.7 months bevacizumab vs 16.1 months placebo).
glioma_bevacizumab_newly_diagnosed_no_su.reason_why: Bevacizumab's anti-angiogenic/anti-oedema effect slows radiographic progression and reduces steroid requirement, but does not eradicate the invasive, treatment-resistant tumour cell population that ultimately drives mortality.
glioma_bevacizumab_newly_diagnosed_no_su.important_caveat: This is reported here in full as an honest negative result: despite FDA approval and PFS benefit, bevacizumab added upfront does NOT prolong survival in newly diagnosed glioblastoma and is not recommended as routine first-line therapy for that reason; it is used for other indications (oedema control, recurrent disease) instead.
glioma_bevacizumab_newly_diagnosed_no_su.real_working_solution: Not recommended as first-line therapy for newly diagnosed glioblastoma on survival grounds; reserved for recurrent disease or refractory oedema/mass effect where its real PFS/response benefit is clinically useful even without an OS gain.
glioma_bevacizumab_newly_diagnosed_no_su.source: Chinot OL et al., N Engl J Med 2014;370:709-722, PMID 24552317

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These are real, differently-defined outcome metrics (relative risk reductions, 2-year/5-year survival percentages, objective response rates) from distinct trials in genuinely different glioma molecular subtypes and grades placed on one comparative scale for reference, not a claim that a single number captures 'how good' each option is. The real best-case molecular subtype (1p/19q-codeleted oligodendroglioma with PCV+RT) is honestly ranked first because its randomised-trial survival data are the strongest in this disease; glioblastoma (IDH-wildtype) results are reported with their genuinely more modest numbers, and one honest negative result (upfront bevacizumab) is placed last rather than omitted.

ranked_high_to_low.name: PCV Chemotherapy + Radiotherapy - 1p/19q-Codeleted Anaplastic Oligodendroglioma (RTOG 9402)
ranked_high_to_low.metric: 41% relative reduction in risk of death (HR 0.59, P=.03); median OS 14.7 years (PCV+RT) vs 7.3 years (RT alone) in the 1p/19q-codeleted subgroup
ranked_high_to_low.source: Cairncross JG et al., J Clin Oncol 2013;31:337-343, PMID 23071247

ranked_high_to_low.name: PCV Chemotherapy + Radiotherapy - 1p/19q-Codeleted Anaplastic Oligodendroglioma (EORTC 26951)
ranked_high_to_low.metric: 44% relative reduction in risk of death (HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.31-1.03); median OS not reached (PCV+RT) vs 112 months/9.3 years (RT alone) in the codeleted subgroup
ranked_high_to_low.source: van den Bent MJ et al., J Clin Oncol 2013;31:344-350, PMID 23071237

definition_and_pathophysiology.summary: Gliomas are primary CNS neoplasms arising from glial (or glial-progenitor) cells - astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, and ependymal cells. The WHO 2021 classification of CNS tumors (5th edition, 'CNS5') fundamentally restructured diagnosis around molecular markers layered onto histology, rather than histology alone. Adult-type diffuse gliomas are now split into three molecularly defined entities: (1) Astrocytoma, IDH-mutant (WHO grade 2, 3, or 4 - grade assigned by histologic/molecular features, with CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion now sufficient to assign grade 4 even without necrosis/microvascular proliferation); (2) Oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted (WHO grade 2 or 3); and (3) Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype (WHO grade 4 by definition - an IDH-wildtype diffuse astrocytic glioma in an adult showing microvascular proliferation, necrosis, TERT promoter mutation, EGFR amplification, or +7/-10 chromosome copy-number changes is classified as glioblastoma even without classic histology). Pediatric-type diffuse gliomas (e.g. diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27-altered) are now recognized as molecularly and prognostically distinct from adult tumors.
definition_and_pathophysiology.source: Louis DN, Perry A, Wesseling P, et al. 'The 2021 WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System: a summary.' Neuro Oncol. 2021;23(8):1231-1251. PMID 34185076.
definition_and_pathophysiology.confidence: high - current official WHO CNS tumor classification

idh_mutant_vs_wildtype.detail: IDH1 (and less commonly IDH2) hotspot mutations are found in more than 70% of WHO grade 2 and grade 3 diffuse astrocytomas and oligodendrogliomas, and in secondary glioblastomas that progressed from a lower-grade precursor - but in only a small minority of primary (de novo) glioblastomas, which are overwhelmingly IDH-wildtype. Mutant IDH produces the oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate, driving a distinct hypermethylation phenotype (G-CIMP) and a biologically less aggressive tumor with markedly better prognosis than IDH-wildtype disease of the same histologic grade. This molecular split - not histologic grade alone - is now the primary determinant of both the CNS5 diagnosis and expected clinical course.
idh_mutant_vs_wildtype.source: Yan H, Parsons DW, Jin G, et al. 'IDH1 and IDH2 mutations in gliomas.' N Engl J Med. 2009;360(8):765-773. PMID 19228619.

glioblastoma_vs_lower_grade.detail: Glioblastoma (WHO grade 4, IDH-wildtype) is the most common and most malignant primary brain tumor in adults, characterized by rapid proliferation, pseudopalisading necrosis, microvascular proliferation, and diffuse infiltration beyond the visible MRI abnormality - which is why gross total resection alone is never curative. Lower-grade IDH-mutant gliomas (grade 2/3 astrocytoma or oligodendroglioma) grow more slowly, often present with seizures years before diagnosis, and carry substantially longer survival, though grade 2/3 IDH-mutant astrocytomas still eventually transform to a higher grade in most patients over time.
glioblastoma_vs_lower_grade.source: Louis DN et al., Neuro Oncol 2021, PMID 34185076; Molinaro AM, Taylor JW, Wiencke JK, Wrensch MR. 'Genetic and molecular epidemiology of adult diffuse glioma.' Nat Rev Neurol. 2019;15(7):405-417. PMID 31227792.

mri_findings.detail: Contrast-enhanced MRI is the primary imaging modality. Glioblastoma classically shows an irregular, thick, 'ring-enhancing' mass with a necrotic core and extensive surrounding T2/FLAIR hyperintense vasogenic edema/infiltration that extends well beyond the enhancing margin. Lower-grade IDH-mutant gliomas typically show a non-enhancing (or minimally enhancing) T2/FLAIR-hyperintense infiltrative lesion without necrosis. Advanced MRI techniques - diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI/ADC), diffusion tensor imaging, perfusion MRI (rCBV), and MR spectroscopy - are used to grade tumors non-invasively and to help distinguish glioblastoma from other ring-enhancing lesions such as solitary metastasis, particularly by examining the non-enhancing peritumoral region (infiltrated in glioma vs. purely edematous in metastasis).
mri_findings.source: Lee EJ, Ahn KJ, Lee EK, Lee YS, Kim DB. 'Potential role of advanced MRI techniques for the peritumoural region in differentiating glioblastoma multiforme and solitary metastatic lesions.' Clin Radiol. 2013;68(12):e689-e697. PMID 23969153.

molecular_markers.idh_status: IDH1/IDH2 mutation testing (immunohistochemistry for IDH1-R132H, reflexed to sequencing if negative in patients <55 years) is mandatory for CNS5 diagnosis and grading - see Yan H et al., NEJM 2009, PMID 19228619.
molecular_markers.1p19q_codeletion: Combined whole-arm 1p/19q co-deletion (FISH or array-based) defines oligodendroglioma (together with IDH mutation) and predicts strong responsiveness to PCV (procarbazine, lomustine, vincristine) chemotherapy plus radiotherapy: in the EORTC 26951 long-term follow-up of newly diagnosed anaplastic oligodendroglial tumors, adding PCV to radiotherapy improved median overall survival from 30.6 to 42.3 months (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.60-0.95), with the greatest benefit concentrated in 1p/19q-codeleted, IDH-mutant tumors.
molecular_markers.1p19q_source: van den Bent MJ, Brandes AA, Taphoorn MJ, et al. 'Adjuvant procarbazine, lomustine, and vincristine chemotherapy in newly diagnosed anaplastic oligodendroglioma: long-term follow-up of EORTC brain tumor group study 26951.' J Clin Oncol. 2013;31(3):344-350. PMID 23071237.
molecular_markers.mgmt_methylation: MGMT (O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase) promoter methylation silences a DNA-repair enzyme that otherwise reverses temozolomide-induced DNA damage. In glioblastoma, MGMT methylation (present in ~45% of assessable cases) is an independent favorable prognostic factor and predicts benefit from temozolomide: median survival with methylated MGMT was 21.7 months (chemoradiotherapy) vs 15.3 months (radiotherapy alone, P=0.007), while the benefit was smaller and not statistically significant in unmethylated tumors.
molecular_markers.mgmt_source: Hegi ME, Diserens AC, Gorlia T, et al. 'MGMT gene silencing and benefit from temozolomide in glioblastoma.' N Engl J Med. 2005;352(10):997-1003. PMID 15758010.
molecular_markers.confidence: high - these three markers (IDH, 1p/19q, MGMT) are the standard-of-care molecular diagnostic panel for adult diffuse glioma worldwide

headache.detail: In a prospective study of 111 brain tumor patients, headache was present in 48% overall. Contrary to popular belief, the 'classic' brain-tumor headache (severe, early-morning, worsened by Valsalva/bending) was uncommon; most headaches instead resembled a tension-type pattern (77%), with a migraine-type pattern in 9%. Nausea or vomiting accompanied headache in 40% of patients.
headache.source: Forsyth PA, Posner JB. 'Headaches in patients with brain tumors: a study of 111 patients.' Neurology. 1993;43(9):1678-1683. PMID 8414011.

seizures.detail: Seizures are the presenting or dominant complicating symptom especially in lower-grade glioma: seizures complicate the clinical course of more than 80% of patients with low-grade gliomas, and are frequently the first symptom that leads to diagnosis. Seizures in glioma are often drug-resistant because of tumor/peritumoral multidrug-resistance protein expression. A 2021 systematic review/meta-analysis of 12 studies found IDH1 mutation was significantly correlated with preoperative seizure presentation, while MGMT methylation and 1p/19q co-deletion were not.
sources: Kurzwelly D, Herrlinger U, Simon M. 'Seizures in patients with low-grade gliomas - incidence, pathogenesis, surgical management, and pharmacotherapy.' Adv Tech Stand Neurosurg. 2010;35:81-111. PMID 20102112.
van Breemen MS, Wilms EB, Vecht CJ. 'Epilepsy in patients with brain tumours: epidemiology, mechanisms, and management.' Lancet Neurol. 2007;6(5):421-430. PMID 17434097.

Song L, Quan X, Chen C, et al. 'Correlation Between Tumor Molecular Markers and Perioperative Epilepsy in Patients With Glioma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.' Front Neurol. 2021;12:711815. PMID 34539550.

focal_neurological_deficits.detail: Focal deficits (hemiparesis, aphasia, visual field cuts, sensory loss, ataxia, cranial nerve palsies) reflect the anatomical location of the tumor and surrounding edema, and evolve subacutely over weeks in glioma versus acutely in stroke. Cognitive/personality change and progressive neurological decline are also common, especially with frontal or diffusely infiltrative tumors.
focal_neurological_deficits.source: Louis DN et al., Neuro Oncol 2021, PMID 34185076 (tumor location/behaviour); Forsyth PA, Posner JB, Neurology 1993, PMID 8414011 (associated presenting features).
focal_neurological_deficits.confidence: moderate-high - qualitative pattern is well established in neuro-oncology; exact frequency figures for each individual focal deficit were not independently re-verified this session

raised_intracranial_pressure.detail: Raised ICP from tumor mass effect and peritumoral vasogenic edema produces headache, vomiting, papilledema, and, if uncontrolled, progressive obtundation and herniation. See EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE for the specific red-flag features that require immediate emergency neurosurgical care.
raised_intracranial_pressure.source: Esquenazi Y, Lo VP, Lee K. 'Critical Care Management of Cerebral Edema in Brain Tumors.' J Intensive Care Med. 2017;32(1):15-24. PMID 26647408.

brain_metastasis.detail: Solitary brain metastasis is the single most important mimic of glioblastoma on conventional MRI, since both can appear as a ring-enhancing mass with central necrosis. Advanced MRI (diffusion-weighted imaging, diffusion tensor imaging, perfusion MRI, MR spectroscopy) targeted at the non-enhancing peritumoral region helps distinguish them: glioblastoma infiltrates this region (elevated perfusion, disrupted white-matter tracts) whereas metastasis is typically surrounded by pure vasogenic edema without tumor infiltration. A known systemic primary cancer, multiplicity of lesions, and location at the grey-white junction favor metastasis.
brain_metastasis.source: Lee EJ et al., Clin Radiol 2013, PMID 23969153.

brain_abscess.detail: Brain abscess can mimic a ring-enhancing high-grade glioma on contrast MRI, but classically shows a smooth, thin, uniform enhancing rim (vs. the thick, irregular rim of glioblastoma) and, most usefully, marked restricted diffusion (low ADC) within the necrotic/purulent core on DWI, whereas glioblastoma necrosis typically does not restrict diffusion to the same degree. Fever, elevated inflammatory markers, and a source of infection (sinusitis, endocarditis, dental sepsis, immunosuppression) support abscess over tumor.
brain_abscess.confidence: moderate - this is standard neuroradiology teaching (DWI restriction as the key discriminator); a dedicated PMID-bearing comparative-diagnostic-accuracy citation was not independently re-verified this session and should be added if required

other_primary_cns_tumors.detail: Meningioma (extra-axial, dural-based, homogeneously enhancing with a 'dural tail') and primary CNS lymphoma (typically homogeneously enhancing, periventricular, markedly diffusion-restricted, and dramatically responsive to steroids with rapid size reduction - a clue that should prompt caution before steroids are given pre-biopsy) are the other major primary CNS mass lesions in the differential. Note: no dedicated 'meningioma' tumor entry was found in this knowledge base at the time of this write (only 'bacterial_meningitis', a different, infectious disease, exists), so no cross-reference id is given here.
other_primary_cns_tumors.confidence: moderate - well-established neuro-oncology/neuroradiology teaching; exact discriminating percentages were not independently re-verified this session

ionizing_radiation.detail: Prior therapeutic ionizing radiation to the head (e.g. prior cranial irradiation, historical tinea capitis treatment, or other childhood cancer therapy) is the only well-established environmental/modifiable risk factor for glioma. A systematic review of cohort studies found the association between radiation exposure and glioma risk was stronger for younger age at exposure, though the association was even stronger for meningioma than for glioma.
ionizing_radiation.source: Braganza MZ, Kitahara CM, Berrington de Gonzalez A, Inskip PD, Johnson KJ, Rajaraman P. 'Ionizing radiation and the risk of brain and central nervous system tumors: a systematic review.' Neuro Oncol. 2012;14(11):1316-1324. PMID 22952197.

genetic_syndromes.detail: A small minority of gliomas arise in the context of hereditary cancer predisposition syndromes: Li-Fraumeni syndrome (germline TP53 mutation) is associated with high-grade glioma - a 2025 systematic review of confirmed Li-Fraumeni-associated high-grade glioma cases found a median overall survival of only 17 months and 64% disease-related mortality among reported cases. Neurofibromatosis type 1 (germline NF1 mutation) is one of the most common brain tumor predisposition syndromes, classically causing optic pathway glioma (usually pilocytic astrocytoma, WHO grade 1) in children, with 35-50% of affected children presenting with reduced visual acuity from the tumor's optic pathway location. Other rarer associated syndromes reported in the general oncology/genetics literature include Turcot syndrome (APC or mismatch-repair gene mutations, with glioma as the CNS component) and Lynch syndrome (mismatch-repair gene mutations) - these two were not independently re-verified with a dedicated PMID this session.
sources: Kite T, Yadlapalli V, Verma R, Porwal M, Herbst J, Karlovits S, Wegner RE, Shepard MJ. 'A systematic review of high-grade glioma associated with Li-Fraumeni syndrome.' Neurosurg Rev. 2025. PMID 40063153.
Campen CJ, Gutmann DH. 'Optic Pathway Gliomas in Neurofibromatosis Type 1.' J Child Neurol. 2018;33(1):73-81. PMID 29246098.
genetic_syndromes.confidence: high for LFS and NF1-associated optic pathway glioma; Turcot/Lynch association is stated from general oncology/genetics knowledge and flagged as not independently re-verified this session

genetic_risk_loci.detail: Beyond rare high-penetrance syndromes, genome-wide association studies have identified roughly 25 common low-penetrance risk loci for glioma, reflecting a polygenic contribution to sporadic glioma risk in the general population.
genetic_risk_loci.source: Molinaro AM, Taylor JW, Wiencke JK, Wrensch MR. Nat Rev Neurol. 2019;15(7):405-417. PMID 31227792.

not_established.detail: Mobile phone radiofrequency exposure and dietary factors are commonly asked about by patients but are NOT established glioma risk factors by high-quality evidence; this is stated to avoid implying an unproven causal link, per zero-fabrication policy. No independent PMID-bearing meta-analysis on this specific point was pulled this session, so this is an absence-of-established-evidence note rather than a cited negative finding.
not_established.confidence: low-moderate - flagged explicitly as unverified this session rather than asserted as fact

incidence.detail: Per the CBTRUS (Central Brain Tumor Registry of the United States) 2024 statistical report covering tumors diagnosed 2017-2021: all primary brain and other CNS tumors have an annual incidence of 25.34 per 100,000 population; malignant tumors account for 6.89 per 100,000. Gliomas (all types combined) make up 22.9% of all primary brain/CNS tumors, and glioblastoma alone accounts for 13.9% of all primary brain/CNS tumors and 51.5% of all malignant primary brain/CNS tumors - making glioblastoma the single most common malignant primary brain tumor in adults. Overall 5-year relative survival for malignant primary brain/CNS tumors is 35.7%.
incidence.source: Price M, Ballard C, Benedetti J, Neff C, Cioffi G, Waite KA, Kruchko C, Barnholtz-Sloan JS, Ostrom QT. 'CBTRUS Statistical Report: Primary Brain and Other Central Nervous System Tumors Diagnosed in the United States in 2017-2021.' Neuro Oncol. 2024;26(Suppl 6):v1-v85. PMID 39371035.
incidence.confidence: high - largest population-based US brain tumor registry report

glioblastoma_idh_wildtype.detail: Glioblastoma (IDH-wildtype, WHO grade 4) carries a genuinely poor prognosis despite maximal therapy. In the pivotal EORTC-NCIC randomized trial, adding concomitant and adjuvant temozolomide to radiotherapy improved median overall survival from 12.1 months (radiotherapy alone) to 14.6 months, and 2-year survival from 10.4% to 26.5%. The 5-year follow-up of the same trial confirmed durable but modest long-term benefit: 5-year survival was 9.8% with chemoradiotherapy versus 1.9% with radiotherapy alone (HR 0.6, 95% CI 0.5-0.7, p<0.0001). MGMT promoter methylation status is the single strongest predictor of benefit from temozolomide and of overall outcome: median survival with methylated MGMT was 21.7 months versus 15.3 months in unmethylated tumors receiving the same chemoradiotherapy. Stated plainly and without euphemism: standard-of-care treated glioblastoma still has a median survival under two years and a 5-year survival under 10% in the randomized-trial population; only a minority of patients (generally MGMT-methylated, younger, good performance status) do meaningfully better.
sources: Stupp R, Mason WP, van den Bent MJ, et al. 'Radiotherapy plus concomitant and adjuvant temozolomide for glioblastoma.' N Engl J Med. 2005;352(10):987-996. PMID 15758009.

Stupp R, Hegi ME, Mason WP, et al. 'Effects of radiotherapy with concomitant and adjuvant temozolomide versus radiotherapy alone on survival in glioblastoma in a randomised phase III study: 5-year analysis of the EORTC-NCIC trial.' Lancet Oncol. 2009;10(5):459-466. PMID 19269895.
Hegi ME et al., N Engl J Med 2005, PMID 15758010.

idh_mutant_lower_grade_glioma.detail: IDH-mutant lower-grade gliomas (grade 2/3 astrocytoma, and IDH-mutant 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendroglioma) behave far more favorably than IDH-wildtype/glioblastoma disease of the same or even higher histologic grade. In the EORTC 26951 long-term follow-up of anaplastic oligodendroglial tumors, adjuvant PCV chemotherapy plus radiotherapy achieved a median overall survival of 42.3 months versus 30.6 months with radiotherapy alone, with IDH-mutant, 1p/19q-codeleted tumors deriving the greatest benefit. Per general neuro-oncology knowledge, well-selected 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendroglioma patients can survive well over a decade, but an independently verified single median-survival figure specifically for this most-favorable subgroup was not pulled this session and is therefore not stated as a specific number here.
idh_mutant_lower_grade_glioma.source: van den Bent MJ et al., J Clin Oncol 2013, PMID 23071237.
idh_mutant_lower_grade_glioma.confidence: high for the 42.3 vs 30.6-month figure; the 'well over a decade' statement for the best-prognosis subgroup is general neuro-oncology knowledge, not independently re-verified with a dedicated PMID this session, and is flagged as such

clinical_takeaway.detail: Any adult with a new unprovoked seizure, a progressively worsening headache (especially with vomiting, papilledema, or a new focal neurological deficit), or an unexplained subacute focal deficit needs urgent contrast-enhanced brain MRI to rule out glioma and other mass lesions - this is a diagnosis that must not be delayed by a routine outpatient work-up if red-flag features (see EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE) are present. Once glioma is suspected on imaging, tissue diagnosis with IDH mutation, 1p/19q co-deletion, and MGMT promoter methylation testing is mandatory - these three molecular markers (not histologic grade alone) now define the WHO 2021 diagnosis, drive the realistic prognosis discussion with the patient, and determine which patients derive the greatest benefit from PCV chemotherapy (1p/19q-codeleted disease) or temozolomide (MGMT-methylated disease). The honest prognosis for IDH-wildtype glioblastoma is genuinely guarded even with optimal modern therapy, while IDH-mutant lower-grade glioma - especially 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendroglioma - carries a meaningfully better outlook and should be communicated as such rather than lumped together with glioblastoma.
clinical_takeaway.confidence: high - synthesis of the cited sources above

glioma.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE: Signs of raised intracranial pressure (ICP) and impending brain herniation in a glioma patient are a real, life-threatening neurosurgical emergency and MUST bypass the normal doctor-approval-queue flow entirely, triggering immediate real-world emergency guidance (call emergency services / go to the nearest emergency department with neurosurgical cover NOW), never a routine consultation flow. Uncontrolled peritumoral cerebral edema and mass effect from glioma can precipitate acute herniation syndromes causing permanent neurological dysfunction or death (Esquenazi Y et al., 'Critical Care Management of Cerebral Edema in Brain Tumors', J Intensive Care Med 2017, PMID 26647408). Red-flag features that must trigger this override include: rapidly worsening headache with vomiting (classically early-morning, though Forsyth & Posner, Neurology 1993, PMID 8414011, showed the 'classic' morning pattern is actually present in only a minority - any new, progressively worsening headache in a known or suspected glioma patient counts); new or worsening papilledema or visual obscurations; a falling or fluctuating level of consciousness/Glasgow Coma Scale; a new dilated, sluggish, or fixed pupil (unilateral third-nerve palsy from uncal herniation); new hemiparesis, decorticate/decerebrate posturing, or Cushing's triad (hypertension with widened pulse pressure, bradycardia, and irregular respiration - a late and pre-terminal sign); and any new seizure that is prolonged (>=5 minutes) or recurrent without recovery between episodes (status epilepticus), which itself carries 9-37% mortality depending on cause and duration. These findings must never be managed as 'wait and see' at home or triaged through routine symptom-checker flow.

meningioma.name: Meningioma
