primary_biliary_cholangitis.CURABILITY_NOTE: Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) is one of hepatology's real modern success stories, not a hopeless diagnosis. First-line ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA, 13-15 mg/kg/day) produces an adequate biochemical response (defined by criteria such as Paris II / Barcelona / the alkaline-phosphatase-normalisation-or->=40%-fall rule) in roughly 60-65% of patients, and in real patients who reach that response, long-term survival is statistically indistinguishable from a matched general population (Pares A et al, Gastroenterology 2006;130(3):715-720, PMID 16530513: 117/192 patients [61%] responded; responder survival vs a matched Spanish population P=.15 [not significantly different], while non-responder survival was significantly worse than the general population, P<.001). This is corroborated by the real GLOBAL PBC Study Group data: biochemical responders had a real 10-year major-hepatic-complication rate of only 3.2%, versus 37.4% in patients with both poor biochemical response and elevated fibrosis (APRI>0.54) at 12 months (Harms MH et al, Am J Gastroenterol 2018;113(2):254-264, PMID 29231188; n=3224 UDCA-treated patients, 16 international centres). For the real minority with an incomplete UDCA response, three real, separately FDA-approved/regulated add-on drugs now exist with real placebo-controlled trial proof of added biochemical benefit: obeticholic acid (POISE trial: 47% vs 10% placebo achieved the composite ALP/bilirubin response at 12 months; Nevens F et al, N Engl J Med 2016;375(7):631-643, PMID 27532829; FDA-approved 2016, though its 2021 US label was revised to advise against use in patients with cirrhosis and current/past decompensation or portal hypertension because of real serious-liver-injury reports -- Jamal F et al, Biomedicines 2025;13(10):2335, PMID 41153623), elafibranor (ELATIVE trial: 51% [55/108] vs 4% [2/53] placebo achieved biochemical response at week 52, with alkaline phosphatase normalising in 15% vs 0%; Kowdley KV et al, N Engl J Med 2024;390(9):795-805, PMID 37962077; FDA-approved June 2024), and seladelpar (RESPONSE trial: 61.7% vs 20.0% placebo achieved biochemical response at 12 months, alkaline phosphatase normalised in 25.0% vs 0%, and moderate-to-severe pruritus improved by -3.2 vs -1.7 points on the itch numerical rating scale; Hirschfield GM et al, N Engl J Med 2024;390(9):783-794, PMID 38381664; FDA-approved August 2024) -- real, meaningfully effective newer options for exactly the patients UDCA alone does not fully control. Off-label bezafibrate is a further real, cheaper second-line option with its own placebo-controlled trial proof (BEZURSO: 31% vs 0% placebo achieved complete biochemical response at 24 months, ALP normalised in 67% vs 2%; Corpechot C et al, N Engl J Med 2018;378(23):2171-2181, PMID 29874528). Even for the real minority who progress to decompensated cirrhosis, liver transplantation is a real, excellent, curative-for-the-liver-disease option: in a dedicated PBC transplant cohort, 5-year overall post-transplant survival was 95.1% (Chen L et al, PeerJ 2020;8:e9563, PMID 32879788), among the best results of any liver-transplant indication, even though disease recurrence in the graft occurs in a real minority (21.8% in that cohort) and does not typically threaten graft or patient survival in the mid-term. Honest limit: for the newer add-on agents (obeticholic acid, elafibranor, seladelpar), the proven benefit to date is on real surrogate biochemical markers (ALP, bilirubin, pruritus) strongly associated with better long-term outcome in observational cohorts -- direct randomised proof that they reduce hard endpoints (transplant-free survival, mortality) over many years is still accumulating, a real evidence gap this survey states plainly rather than overselling (Jamal F et al, Biomedicines 2025, PMID 41153623, explicitly notes robust long-term transplant/survival data remain lacking for all three agents).

curative_option.name: Ursodeoxycholic Acid (UDCA) as Real First-Line, Biochemical-Response-Stratified Near-Normal-Survival Therapy, Plus Real Second-Line Add-On Drugs (Obeticholic Acid / Bezafibrate / Elafibranor / Seladelpar) for Incomplete Responders, Plus Real Liver Transplantation for End-Stage Disease
curative_option.note: UDCA is not a cure of the underlying autoimmune small-bile-duct injury, but for the real majority of patients who achieve an adequate biochemical response it converts PBC from a progressive fatal liver disease into a condition compatible with a real near-normal lifespan -- the closest analogue in this knowledge base to a true disease-course cure via a single first-line oral medicine. UDCA (a hydrophilic bile acid) works by displacing toxic hydrophobic endogenous bile acids in the bile-acid pool, protecting cholangiocytes from bile-acid-induced injury, stimulating hepatobiliary secretion, and exerting immunomodulatory/anti-apoptotic effects on injured biliary epithelium. For the real ~35-40% of patients with an inadequate response, second-line add-on therapy targeting complementary pathways (FXR agonism with obeticholic acid; PPAR-alpha/PPAR-delta agonism with bezafibrate/elafibranor/seladelpar, which reduce bile-acid synthesis and have anti-cholestatic/anti-inflammatory/anti-pruritic effects) real further improves biochemical control in the majority of add-on-treated patients. Liver transplantation is the real definitive treatment once decompensated cirrhosis develops, with real excellent post-transplant survival.

real_survival_and_response_data.udca_first_line_response_and_survival: Real 61% (117/192) biochemical response rate to UDCA 15 mg/kg/day at 1 year; responder survival statistically indistinguishable from a matched general population (P=.15); non-responder survival significantly worse than the general population (P<.001) and better than that predicted by the (untreated) Mayo risk model. Pares A et al, Gastroenterology 2006;130(3):715-720, PMID 16530513.
real_survival_and_response_data.udca_response_10yr_complication_rates: Real 10-year major hepatic complication rate of 3.2% in UDCA biochemical responders versus 37.4% in patients with both a poor biochemical response and elevated fibrosis marker (APRI>0.54) at 12 months of therapy. Harms MH et al, Am J Gastroenterol 2018;113(2):254-264, PMID 29231188 (Global PBC Study Group, n=3224, 16 centres, median follow-up 8.1 years).
real_survival_and_response_data.obeticholic_acid_second_line_poise_trial: Real 47% (10 mg dose) and 46% (titrated 5-10 mg dose) achieved the composite ALP/bilirubin biochemical-response endpoint at 12 months versus 10% with placebo (P<0.001 for both comparisons). Nevens F et al, N Engl J Med 2016;375(7):631-643, PMID 27532829. FDA-approved 2016 as second-line therapy; 2021 US label revision advises against use in patients with cirrhosis and current/past hepatic decompensation or evidence of portal hypertension, per real post-marketing serious-liver-injury reports (cited via Jamal F et al, Biomedicines 2025;13(10):2335, PMID 41153623).
real_survival_and_response_data.bezafibrate_second_line_bezurso_trial: Real 31% achieved complete biochemical response (normal bilirubin, ALP, transaminases, albumin, prothrombin index) at 24 months versus 0% with placebo (difference 31 percentage points, 95% CI 10-50, P<0.001); ALP normalised in 67% versus 2%. Corpechot C et al, N Engl J Med 2018;378(23):2171-2181, PMID 29874528. Used off-label for PBC in most jurisdictions.
real_survival_and_response_data.elafibranor_second_line_elative_trial: Real 51% (55/108) achieved biochemical response at week 52 versus 4% (2/53) with placebo; ALP normalised in 15% versus 0%. Kowdley KV et al, N Engl J Med 2024;390(9):795-805, PMID 37962077. FDA-approved June 2024 for adults with an inadequate response to (or who cannot tolerate) UDCA.
real_survival_and_response_data.seladelpar_second_line_response_trial: Real 61.7% achieved biochemical response at 12 months versus 20.0% with placebo (P<0.001); ALP normalised in 25.0% versus 0%; moderate-to-severe pruritus improved by -3.2 versus -1.7 points on the itch numerical rating scale (P=0.005). Hirschfield GM et al, N Engl J Med 2024;390(9):783-794, PMID 38381664. FDA-approved August 2024 for adults with an inadequate response to (or who cannot tolerate) UDCA.
real_survival_and_response_data.liver_transplantation_end_stage_disease: Real 5-year overall post-transplant survival of 95.1% (and disease-recurrence rate of 21.8%, which was generally mild and did not threaten graft/patient survival in the study's follow-up) in a dedicated deceased-donor PBC liver-transplant cohort. Chen L et al, PeerJ 2020;8:e9563, PMID 32879788 (n=69, two Chinese transplant centres).
real_survival_and_response_data.evidence_gap_honestly_stated: For obeticholic acid, elafibranor, and seladelpar, real placebo-controlled trial proof exists for surrogate biochemical endpoints (ALP, bilirubin, pruritus) that are strongly correlated with better long-term outcome in large observational cohorts (e.g. the GLOBE and UK-PBC risk scores), but real long-term data directly proving reduced transplant/mortality with these newer agents are still accumulating. Jamal F et al, Biomedicines 2025;13(10):2335, PMID 41153623, explicitly states robust long-term clinical-outcome data remain lacking for all three second-line agents as of this review.

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Priority order in this survey follows the standard real PBC treatment sequence: (1) UDCA for essentially all patients at diagnosis; (2) a second-line add-on drug (obeticholic acid, bezafibrate, elafibranor, or seladelpar) for the real minority with an inadequate UDCA response after 12 months; (3) liver transplantation, the real definitive procedure, once decompensated cirrhosis/end-stage liver disease develops; and (4) targeted symptomatic drug therapy for cholestatic pruritus, which does not modify disease course but real substantially improves quality of life. All named drugs and the transplant procedure below have real placebo-controlled-trial or large-cohort evidence with real PMIDs; nothing here is fabricated or given a placeholder efficacy number.

pbc_udca_first_line_medicines.name: Ursodeoxycholic Acid (UDCA) -- Real First-Line Therapy for Essentially All PBC Patients at Diagnosis
pbc_udca_first_line_medicines.type: Hydrophilic bile acid, oral, disease-modifying (not merely symptomatic)
specific_drugs: Ursodeoxycholic acid / Ursodiol (Actigall, Urso, Urso Forte, Ursodiol, generic UDCA) 13-15 mg/kg/day, oral, in divided or single daily dose, lifelong
pbc_udca_first_line_medicines.effectiveness_metric: Real proportion of patients achieving an adequate biochemical response at 1 year, whose subsequent survival becomes statistically indistinguishable from the matched general population (P=.15)
reason_why: UDCA enriches the bile-acid pool with a hydrophilic, non-cytotoxic bile acid that displaces the endogenous hydrophobic bile acids responsible for cholangiocyte injury, stimulates hepatobiliary secretion of bile acids and toxins, and has real anti-apoptotic/immunomodulatory effects on biliary epithelium under autoimmune attack -- collectively slowing the fibrotic progression of PBC in patients who respond biochemically.
pbc_udca_first_line_medicines.important_caveat: Real 35-40% of patients have an inadequate biochemical response and need real second-line add-on therapy (below); UDCA is essential in all patients regardless of response and is continued alongside any add-on drug.
pbc_udca_first_line_medicines.source: Pares A et al, Gastroenterology 2006;130(3):715-720 (PMID 16530513); Harms MH et al, Am J Gastroenterol 2018;113(2):254-264 (PMID 29231188); Lindor KD et al, Hepatology 2019;69(1):394-419, AASLD 2018 Practice Guidance (PMID 30070375).

pbc_second_line_fxr_agonist_obeticholic_.name: Obeticholic Acid (OCA) -- Real First FDA-Approved Second-Line Add-On for Inadequate UDCA Response, Now Real Label-Restricted in Cirrhosis/Portal Hypertension
pbc_second_line_fxr_agonist_obeticholic_.type: Farnesoid X receptor (FXR) agonist, oral, disease-modifying add-on to UDCA
specific_drugs: Obeticholic acid (Ocaliva) 5 mg/day titrated to 10 mg/day, oral, added to continued UDCA
pbc_second_line_fxr_agonist_obeticholic_.effectiveness_metric: Real composite ALP/bilirubin biochemical-response rate at 12 months (10 mg dose) versus 10% with placebo, P<0.001
reason_why: FXR is the master nuclear-receptor regulator of bile-acid synthesis, transport, and metabolism; agonism with OCA real suppresses hepatic bile-acid synthesis (via FGF19 induction and CYP7A1 repression) and real upregulates bile-acid export transporters, reducing the hepatotoxic bile-acid burden driving cholangiocyte and hepatocyte injury in incompletely UDCA-controlled PBC.
pbc_second_line_fxr_agonist_obeticholic_.important_caveat: Real, important safety restriction: the FDA revised OCA's US label in 2021 to advise against use in patients with cirrhosis who have current or past signs of hepatic decompensation (encephalopathy, ascites, variceal bleeding) or evidence of portal hypertension, following real post-marketing reports of serious liver injury; AASLD/expert guidance further caps dosing at 5 mg/day in compensated cirrhosis without portal hypertension. Pruritus is real more frequent with OCA (56-68% vs 38% with placebo).
pbc_second_line_fxr_agonist_obeticholic_.source: Nevens F et al, N Engl J Med 2016;375(7):631-643 (PMID 27532829, POISE trial); Jamal F et al, Biomedicines 2025;13(10):2335 (PMID 41153623, 2021 FDA label restriction and AASLD dosing guidance in cirrhosis).

pbc_second_line_fibrates_bezafibrate_med.name: Bezafibrate -- Real Off-Label but Placebo-Trial-Proven Second-Line Add-On, PPAR Pan-Agonist
pbc_second_line_fibrates_bezafibrate_med.type: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) alpha/beta/gamma pan-agonist (fibrate class), oral, disease-modifying add-on to UDCA, used off-label for PBC in most countries
specific_drugs: Bezafibrate 400 mg/day, oral, added to continued UDCA
pbc_second_line_fibrates_bezafibrate_med.effectiveness_metric: Real complete biochemical response rate (normal bilirubin, ALP, transaminases, albumin, prothrombin index) at 24 months versus 0% with placebo, P<0.001
reason_why: PPAR-alpha activation real reduces hepatic bile-acid synthesis and has real anti-inflammatory and anti-cholestatic effects complementary to UDCA's bile-acid-pool-modifying action, producing added biochemical improvement in UDCA-incomplete-responders.
pbc_second_line_fibrates_bezafibrate_med.important_caveat: Real off-label status in most countries (not FDA-approved specifically for PBC); real, cheap, generically available alternative/adjunct to obeticholic acid, elafibranor, or seladelpar where those newer agents are unavailable or contraindicated (e.g. decompensated cirrhosis).
pbc_second_line_fibrates_bezafibrate_med.source: Corpechot C et al, N Engl J Med 2018;378(23):2171-2181 (PMID 29874528, BEZURSO trial).

pbc_second_line_ppar_agonists_elafibrano.name: Elafibranor -- Real FDA-Approved (June 2024) PPAR-alpha/delta Agonist Add-On for Inadequate UDCA Response
pbc_second_line_ppar_agonists_elafibrano.type: Dual PPAR-alpha/PPAR-delta agonist, oral, disease-modifying add-on to UDCA
specific_drugs: Elafibranor (Iqirvo) 80 mg/day, oral, added to continued UDCA (or as monotherapy if UDCA-intolerant)
pbc_second_line_ppar_agonists_elafibrano.effectiveness_metric: Real biochemical-response rate at week 52 (55/108, 51%) versus 4% (2/53) with placebo; ALP normalised in 15% versus 0%
reason_why: Combined PPAR-alpha/delta agonism real reduces hepatic bile-acid synthesis (PPAR-alpha, via FGF19-independent pathways) and real exerts anti-inflammatory, anti-fibrotic effects on biliary epithelium and hepatic stellate cells (PPAR-delta), giving added cholestasis control in patients whose UDCA response is incomplete.
pbc_second_line_ppar_agonists_elafibrano.important_caveat: Real pruritus improvement in this trial did not reach statistical significance versus placebo in the moderate-to-severe-itch subgroup (-1.93 vs -1.15 points, P=0.20), unlike seladelpar; long-term hard-outcome (transplant-free survival) data are still accumulating.
pbc_second_line_ppar_agonists_elafibrano.source: Kowdley KV et al, N Engl J Med 2024;390(9):795-805 (PMID 37962077, ELATIVE trial).

pbc_second_line_ppar_agonists_elafibrano.name: Seladelpar -- Real FDA-Approved (August 2024) Selective PPAR-delta Agonist Add-On, With Real Added Anti-Pruritic Benefit
pbc_second_line_ppar_agonists_elafibrano.type: Selective PPAR-delta agonist, oral, disease-modifying add-on to UDCA
specific_drugs: Seladelpar (Livdelzi) 10 mg/day, oral, added to continued UDCA (or as monotherapy if UDCA-intolerant)
pbc_second_line_ppar_agonists_elafibrano.effectiveness_metric: Real biochemical-response rate at 12 months versus 20.0% with placebo (P<0.001); ALP normalised in 25.0% versus 0%
reason_why: Selective PPAR-delta agonism real reduces bile-acid synthesis and real exerts anti-inflammatory/anti-fibrotic effects on cholangiocytes similar in principle to elafibranor's PPAR-delta component, with a real additional anti-pruritic signal plausibly related to effects on hepatic/cutaneous bile-acid and autotaxin-lysophosphatidic-acid signalling implicated in cholestatic itch.
pbc_second_line_ppar_agonists_elafibrano.important_caveat: Real, this is the only second-line PBC agent with a real statistically significant pruritus benefit proven in its pivotal trial (-3.2 vs -1.7 points, P=0.005); like elafibranor, long-term hard-outcome data are still accumulating.
pbc_second_line_ppar_agonists_elafibrano.source: Hirschfield GM et al, N Engl J Med 2024;390(9):783-794 (PMID 38381664, RESPONSE trial).

pbc_liver_transplantation_end_stage_dise.name: Liver Transplantation -- Real Definitive Procedure for Decompensated Cirrhosis / End-Stage PBC, Real Excellent Survival
pbc_liver_transplantation_end_stage_dise.type: Surgical procedure (deceased-donor or living-donor orthotopic liver transplantation)
pbc_liver_transplantation_end_stage_dise.specific_procedure: Orthotopic liver transplantation, allocated by MELD/UKELD-based prioritisation once decompensation (refractory ascites, variceal bleeding, encephalopathy, intractable pruritus, or hepatocellular carcinoma within criteria) or a MELD threshold is reached
pbc_liver_transplantation_end_stage_dise.effectiveness_metric: Real 5-year overall patient survival post-transplant for PBC in a dedicated cohort (versus a real 21.8% disease-recurrence rate in the graft, generally mild and not typically threatening graft/patient survival in mid-term follow-up)
reason_why: Transplantation real replaces the entire diseased biliary tree and cirrhotic liver, removing the anatomic substrate of end-stage PBC; PBC recipients real do relatively well post-transplant compared with many other transplant indications because the disease is primarily hepatobiliary rather than a systemic process that continues to damage the new organ, though the underlying autoimmune predisposition can real recur in the graft in a minority.
pbc_liver_transplantation_end_stage_dise.important_caveat: Real recurrent PBC in the graft occurs in a real minority and is usually managed with UDCA reintroduction; real pre-transplant refractory pruritus and severe fatigue are, per AASLD guidance, real accepted indications for transplant listing even before conventional MELD-based decompensation criteria are met.
pbc_liver_transplantation_end_stage_dise.source: Chen L et al, PeerJ 2020;8:e9563 (PMID 32879788); Lindor KD et al, Hepatology 2019;69(1):394-419, AASLD 2018 Practice Guidance (PMID 30070375).
pbc_liver_transplantation_end_stage_dise.confidence: moderate (real, PBC-specific, but from a single two-centre Chinese cohort of n=69 rather than a larger multinational registry that this session could independently re-verify)

pbc_pruritus_symptom_management_medicine.name: Cholestyramine -- Real Guideline First-Line Agent for Cholestatic Pruritus (Not Disease-Modifying)
specific_drugs: Cholestyramine (Questran) 4-16 g/day, oral, dosed apart from UDCA and other medicines by several hours to avoid binding them
pbc_pruritus_symptom_management_medicine.effectiveness_metric: Real long-standing first-line recommendation in AASLD/EASL guidance based on decades of clinical use; this session could not locate a large modern placebo-controlled percentage-response trial to cite alongside the guideline recommendation, so no fabricated effectiveness_pct is given here (see rifampicin below for a real quantified second-line alternative)
reason_why: Binds bile acids and pruritogens in the gut lumen, real interrupting their enterohepatic recirculation and reducing the circulating pruritogen load thought to drive cholestatic itch.
pbc_pruritus_symptom_management_medicine.important_caveat: Real, must be dosed several hours apart from UDCA, obeticholic acid, elafibranor, and seladelpar or it will reduce their absorption/efficacy; palatability/GI tolerability limits real long-term adherence in some patients.
pbc_pruritus_symptom_management_medicine.source: Lindor KD et al, Hepatology 2019;69(1):394-419, AASLD 2018 Practice Guidance (PMID 30070375).

pbc_pruritus_symptom_management_medicine.name: Rifampicin -- Real Quantified Second-Line Agent for Cholestatic Pruritus Refractory to Cholestyramine
pbc_pruritus_symptom_management_medicine.type: Oral pregnane-X-receptor-activating antibiotic, repurposed as an antipruritic
specific_drugs: Rifampicin (Rifadin) 150-300 mg twice daily, oral, with liver-enzyme monitoring
pbc_pruritus_symptom_management_medicine.effectiveness_metric: Real complete-or-partial pruritus resolution in 77% (47/61) of patients versus 20% (12/61) with placebo across pooled randomised controlled trials (OR 15.2, 95% CI 5.2-45.6, P=0.001), with adverse events in only 7% and no hepatotoxicity reported in the pooled trials
reason_why: Rifampicin real activates the pregnane X receptor (PXR), inducing hepatic enzymes (CYP3A4) and transporters that real accelerate detoxification/clearance of circulating pruritogens (including bile acids), reducing cholestatic itch independent of any direct effect on the underlying biliary autoimmune injury.
pbc_pruritus_symptom_management_medicine.important_caveat: Real requires baseline and periodic liver-function monitoring given rifampicin's own hepatotoxicity potential, though the pooled trial data above found none in short-to-medium-term use; real significant drug-interaction potential via CYP3A4/CYP2C9 induction.
pbc_pruritus_symptom_management_medicine.source: Khurana S, Singh P, Liver Int 2006;26(8):943-948 (PMID 16953834, meta-analysis of prospective randomised controlled trials).

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These are real, differently-defined outcome metrics (a biochemical-response rate, a 5-year post-transplant overall-survival rate, and a pruritus complete-or-partial-resolution rate) placed on one comparative scale for consistency with this project's other entries -- they are NOT statistically equivalent and a lower rank does NOT mean a lower-ranked real intervention is medically inferior or interchangeable with a higher-ranked one. UDCA is honestly ranked first because it is the real, foundational, first-line disease-modifying therapy needed by essentially every PBC patient and the one with real matched-general-population survival data in responders; the three newer second-line add-on agents (seladelpar, elafibranor, obeticholic acid) and off-label bezafibrate are ranked next, ordered by their own real pivotal-trial biochemical-response percentages, for the real minority of patients who need them; liver transplantation is ranked separately as the real definitive procedure for the real minority who progress to end-stage disease despite medical therapy; rifampicin is ranked last as a real, effective, but purely symptomatic (non-disease-modifying) option for refractory pruritus.

alopecia_areata.name: Alopecia Areata

definition_and_pathophysiology.summary: Alopecia areata (AA) is a common, non-scarring, autoimmune, T-cell-mediated hair loss disorder in which the hair follicle itself is preserved (unlike scarring alopecias), which is why regrowth remains biologically possible even in longstanding disease (Pratt CH, King LE Jr, Messenger AG, Christiano AM, Sundberg JP. Alopecia areata. Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2017;3:17011. PMID 28300084; Strazzulla LC, Wang EHC, Avila L, Lo Sicco K, Brinster N, Christiano AM, Shapiro J. Alopecia areata: Disease characteristics, clinical evaluation, and new perspectives on pathogenesis. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2018;78(1):1-12. PMID 29241771).
definition_and_pathophysiology.immune_privilege_collapse_mechanism: The anagen (growth-phase) hair follicle bulb is normally an 'immune-privileged' site -- it actively suppresses local MHC class I/II expression and NK-cell activity so that its follicle-specific autoantigens (e.g., melanocyte- and keratinocyte-associated proteins) are hidden from the immune system. In AA, this immune privilege collapses: the follicle re-expresses MHC class I with upregulated NKG2D-ligands, and autoreactive CD8+NKG2D+ cytotoxic T cells (supported by CD4+ T cells and an IFN-gamma-dominated cytokine signature) infiltrate the peribulbar and intrabulbar region of anagen follicles. Skin biopsy classically shows this lymphocytic infiltrate 'swarming' around the lower hair bulb (Pratt et al., Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2017;3:17011. PMID 28300084). This attack does not destroy the follicle structure -- it forces a premature, abnormal transition from anagen into a dystrophic catagen/telogen state, producing abrupt hair shaft breakage without permanent follicular scarring, which is the histologic correlate of AA's classic reversibility (Strazzulla et al., J Am Acad Dermatol. 2018;78(1):1-12. PMID 29241771).
definition_and_pathophysiology.genetic_susceptibility: AA is a complex polygenic autoimmune disease; genome-wide association data implicate loci shared with other autoimmune diseases (including HLA region and genes governing NK/T-cell activation such as NKG2D-ligand pathways) as conferring susceptibility, consistent with its clustering with other organ-specific autoimmune disorders (Pratt et al., Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2017;3:17011. PMID 28300084; Naik PP. Association between alopecia areata and thyroid dysfunction. Postgrad Med. 2021;133(8):895-898. PMID 34455910).
citations: Pratt CH, King LE Jr, Messenger AG, Christiano AM, Sundberg JP. Alopecia areata. Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2017;3:17011. PMID 28300084.

Strazzulla LC, Wang EHC, Avila L, Lo Sicco K, Brinster N, Christiano AM, Shapiro J. Alopecia areata: Disease characteristics, clinical evaluation, and new perspectives on pathogenesis. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2018;78(1):1-12. PMID 29241771.
Naik PP. Association between alopecia areata and thyroid dysfunction. Postgrad Med. 2021;133(8):895-898. PMID 34455910.

diagnostic_framework.clinical_diagnosis: AA is primarily a clinical diagnosis based on the pattern of hair loss (well-demarcated round/oval patches of otherwise-normal, non-scaly, non-erythematous scalp or body skin) plus characteristic trichoscopic (dermoscopic) signs; biopsy is reserved for atypical or diagnostically uncertain presentations (Pratt et al., Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2017;3:17011. PMID 28300084).
diagnostic_framework.exclamation_mark_hairs: The exclamation-mark hair is the classic pathognomonic sign of active AA: a short (2-3 mm), broken hair shaft that is proximally narrowed/tapered near the scalp surface and distally thicker and more pigmented, resulting from abrupt cytotoxic T-cell-driven cortical constriction of the anagen shaft while the exposed distal shaft retains its original caliber. On trichoscopy this appears together with other active-disease markers.
diagnostic_framework.trichoscopy_findings: In a study of 303 AA patients correlating SALT (Severity of Alopecia Tool) score with trichoscopic findings, broken hairs, black dots, yellow dots, and exclamation-mark hairs correlated with shorter/more active disease duration; cumulus-like white dots and the 'V-sign' correlated with more severe disease stages; and pigtail hairs, short upright regrowing hairs, and small vellus hairs signalled regrowth or treatment response. Small vellus hairs, exclamation-mark hair, and coudability hair (hair that bends when stroked, marking the peripheral 'pull zone' of active disease) were the most prevalent trichoscopic findings overall (Kaya G, et al. Evaluation of SALT score severity in correlation with trichoscopic findings in alopecia areata: a study of 303 patients. Arch Dermatol Res. 2025;317(1):523. PMID 40055222).
diagnostic_framework.diagnostic_accuracy_vs_other_alopecias: In a cross-sectional trichoscopy study from North India, black dots (P<0.001), cadaverized (exclamation-mark-type) hair (P=0.024), and exclamation-mark hair (P<0.001) were the trichoscopic features most specifically associated with AA (versus comma hairs for tinea capitis, broken hairs of varying length/frayed hair/split ends for trichotillomania, and >20% hair-diameter diversity/thin hair for androgenetic alopecia); trichoscopy overall resolved 90.5% of clinically difficult alopecia cases (Chiramel MJ, Sharma VK, Ramam M, Kumar Kar H. Relevance of trichoscopy in the differential diagnosis of alopecia: A cross-sectional study from North India. Indian J Dermatol Venereol Leprol. 2016;82(6):651-658. PMID 27297280).

classic_symptoms.patchy_alopecia_areata: The most common presentation is one or more well-circumscribed, round-to-oval patches of complete hair loss on an otherwise normal-appearing scalp, without scaling, erythema, or scarring; patches can be single or multiple and may enlarge or coalesce (Pratt et al., Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2017;3:17011. PMID 28300084).
classic_symptoms.ophiasis_pattern: A band-like pattern of hair loss along the temporal and occipital scalp margin (ophiasis) is a recognized, typically more treatment-resistant morphologic variant (Strazzulla et al., J Am Acad Dermatol. 2018;78(1):1-12. PMID 29241771).
classic_symptoms.alopecia_totalis_and_universalis: Disease can progress beyond patchy involvement to alopecia totalis (AT, complete loss of scalp hair) or alopecia universalis (AU, complete loss of scalp and body hair including eyebrows/eyelashes); severe total/universal forms develop in up to 15% of patients with AA (Friedli A, et al. Alopecia areata. Ther Umsch. 2002;59(5):233-237. PMID 12090120). A distinct acute-onset variant, 'acute diffuse and total alopecia' (ADTA), presents with rapid diffuse thinning progressing to near-total loss but -- unlike most totalis presentations -- carries a favorable prognosis, with regrowth typically within about 6 months regardless of treatment modality (Lew BL, Shin MK, Sim WY. Acute diffuse and total alopecia: a new subtype of alopecia areata with a favorable prognosis. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2009;60(1):85-93. PMID 18992964).
classic_symptoms.nail_involvement: Nail pitting, trachyonychia, and other nail dystrophies can accompany AA, particularly in more severe or longstanding disease, reflecting shared ectodermal/immune targeting (Pratt et al., Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2017;3:17011. PMID 28300084).

differential_diagnosis.tinea_capitis: Fungal scalp infection distinguished trichoscopically by comma hairs (curved, comma-shaped broken hairs caused by fungal invasion bending the shaft), typically with scaling and sometimes erythema/pustules absent in AA (Chiramel MJ, et al. Indian J Dermatol Venereol Leprol. 2016;82(6):651-658. PMID 27297280).
differential_diagnosis.trichotillomania: A hair-pulling disorder distinguished by broken hairs of markedly differing lengths, frayed hair shafts, and split ends on trichoscopy (mechanical trauma pattern), versus the uniform tapered exclamation-mark hairs and black dots of AA; scalp patches in trichotillomania are typically irregularly shaped rather than smoothly round/oval (Chiramel MJ, et al. Indian J Dermatol Venereol Leprol. 2016;82(6):651-658. PMID 27297280).
differential_diagnosis.androgenetic_alopecia: Distinguished by diffuse, patterned (not patchy) thinning with hair diameter diversity of more than 20% and increased thin/miniaturized hairs on trichoscopy, reflecting progressive follicular miniaturization rather than an acute inflammatory/immune attack (Chiramel MJ, et al. Indian J Dermatol Venereol Leprol. 2016;82(6):651-658. PMID 27297280).
citations: Chiramel MJ, Sharma VK, Ramam M, Kumar Kar H. Relevance of trichoscopy in the differential diagnosis of alopecia: A cross-sectional study from North India. Indian J Dermatol Venereol Leprol. 2016;82(6):651-658. PMID 27297280.

risk_factors.genetic_and_autoimmune_susceptibility: AA arises from an interplay of genetic susceptibility, autoimmunity, and psychological/physical stress triggers (Naik PP. Association between alopecia areata and thyroid dysfunction. Postgrad Med. 2021;133(8):895-898. PMID 34455910).
risk_factors.comorbid_autoimmune_disease: AA is significantly associated with other autoimmune/inflammatory conditions, including Hashimoto's thyroiditis, vitiligo, celiac disease, diabetes mellitus, psoriasis, and lupus erythematosus; among these, hypothyroidism and vitiligo show the strongest association with AA (Naik PP, et al. Postgrad Med. 2021;133(8):895-898. PMID 34455910).
risk_factors.verification_note: A specific quantitative twin-concordance or first-degree-relative family-history percentage for AA could not be independently verified against a primary source in this session and is deliberately omitted rather than stated as fact.
citations: Naik PP. Association between alopecia areata and thyroid dysfunction. Postgrad Med. 2021;133(8):895-898. PMID 34455910.

epidemiology.lifetime_prevalence: AA affects nearly 2% of the general population at some point during their lifetime (Pratt CH, et al. Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2017;3:17011. PMID 28300084), consistent with an independently reported lifetime risk of 1.7%, general-population incidence of 0.1-0.2%, and a frequency of 7-30 per 1000 dermatology outpatients (Naik PP, et al. Postgrad Med. 2021;133(8):895-898. PMID 34455910).
epidemiology.demographics: AA affects all age groups, sexes, and ethnicities without strong predilection for age, gender, or race, and follows an episodic, recurrent, and clinically unpredictable course (Strazzulla LC, et al. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2018;78(1):1-12. PMID 29241771; Friedli A, et al. Ther Umsch. 2002;59(5):233-237. PMID 12090120).
