gastric_cancer.name: Gastric Cancer

definition_and_pathophysiology.definition: Gastric (stomach) adenocarcinoma accounts for the large majority of gastric cancers and is histologically divided by the Lauren classification into two principal types with distinct biology: intestinal type (gland-forming, resembling colonic adenocarcinoma) and diffuse type (poorly cohesive, often signet-ring cells infiltrating the wall without forming discrete glands, sometimes producing linitis plastica/'leather-bottle stomach') (Lauren P, 'The two histological main types of gastric carcinoma: diffuse and so-called intestinal-type carcinoma', Acta Pathologica et Microbiologica Scandinavica 1965;64:31-49, PMID 14320675).
definition_and_pathophysiology.intestinal_type_correa_cascade: Intestinal-type gastric cancer arises via a well-documented, real, multistep progression known as the Correa cascade: chronic H. pylori-driven inflammation -> chronic (non-atrophic) gastritis -> multifocal atrophic gastritis -> intestinal metaplasia -> dysplasia -> invasive intestinal-type adenocarcinoma (Correa P, 'Human gastric carcinogenesis: a multistep and multifactorial process', Cancer Research 1992;52(24):6735-40, PMID 1458460). This is the same H. pylori-driven atrophic gastritis/intestinal metaplasia pathway detailed in this knowledge base's chronic_gastritis entry (Sugano K et al., Kyoto global consensus report, Gut 2015, PMID 26187502; Dixon MF et al., Updated Sydney System, Am J Surg Pathol 1996, PMID 8827022) - chronic gastritis with extensive atrophy/intestinal metaplasia is the real precancerous substrate from which most intestinal-type gastric cancer eventually develops, which is why that entry's OLGA/OLGIM surveillance recommendations (MAPS II guideline, PMID 30841008) exist.
definition_and_pathophysiology.diffuse_type_biology: Diffuse-type gastric cancer follows a distinct, less clearly H. pylori-stepwise route: it is characteristically associated with loss of function of E-cadherin (encoded by CDH1), the cell-adhesion protein that normally holds epithelial cells together, which explains the poorly cohesive, signet-ring morphology and the infiltrative rather than mass-forming growth pattern; germline CDH1 mutation is the basis of hereditary diffuse gastric cancer (see risk_factors) (Blair VR et al., 'Hereditary diffuse gastric cancer: updated clinical practice guidelines', Lancet Oncology 2020;21(8):e386-e397, PMID 32758476).

diagnostic_framework.endoscopy_and_biopsy: Upper GI endoscopy with biopsy of any suspicious lesion is the diagnostic gold standard for gastric cancer - it is required both to make the histological diagnosis and to determine Lauren subtype (intestinal vs diffuse) (Lauren 1965, PMID 14320675), analogous to the biopsy requirement already established for chronic gastritis in this knowledge base.
diagnostic_framework.staging_workup: Once biopsy confirms adenocarcinoma, locoregional and distant staging is performed with endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) for depth of tumour invasion (T stage) and perigastric nodal assessment, contrast-enhanced CT of the chest/abdomen/pelvis for distant metastatic disease, and, in patients being considered for potentially curative (locally advanced but resectable) surgery, staging laparoscopy with peritoneal lavage cytology to exclude occult peritoneal carcinomatosis not visible on CT, per the ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines (Smyth EC, Verheij M, Allum W, Cunningham D, Cervantes A, Arnold D; ESMO Guidelines Committee, 'Gastric cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up', Annals of Oncology 2016;27(suppl 5):v38-v49, PMID 27664260).
diagnostic_framework.tnm_staging_system: Anatomical stage is assigned using the AJCC/UICC TNM system (8th edition), which combines depth of tumour invasion (T1: mucosa/submucosa, T2: muscularis propria, T3: subserosa, T4: serosa/adjacent structures), number of involved regional lymph nodes (N0-N3), and presence of distant metastasis (M0/M1) into stage groups I through IV; this 8th-edition system was validated against the US National Cancer Database and showed improved discrimination of survival differences between adjacent stage groups compared with the prior (7th) edition (In H, Solsky I, Palis B, Langdon-Embry M, Ajani J, Sano T, 'Validation of the 8th Edition of the AJCC TNM Staging System for Gastric Cancer using the National Cancer Database', Annals of Surgical Oncology 2017;24(12):3683-91, PMID 28895113).
diagnostic_framework.source: PMID 14320675 (Lauren 1965); PMID 27664260 (Smyth/ESMO 2016); PMID 28895113 (In H 2017, AJCC 8th edition validation).

classic_symptoms.early_disease_is_silent_or_vague: Early gastric cancer is characteristically asymptomatic or produces only vague, non-specific upper GI symptoms - mild epigastric discomfort, bloating, early satiety, or dyspepsia indistinguishable from benign conditions such as peptic ulcer disease or functional/chronic gastritis (cross-reference this knowledge base's peptic_ulcer_disease and chronic_gastritis entries for the overlapping symptom picture). This lack of specific early warning symptoms is the central reason most patients outside organized-screening countries present with locally advanced or metastatic disease (see epidemiology and natural_history).
classic_symptoms.late_presentation_pattern: As disease advances, more specific alarm symptoms emerge: unintentional/unexplained weight loss, persistent or worsening epigastric pain, early satiety severe enough to reduce oral intake, dysphagia (particularly with proximal/cardia tumours), persistent vomiting (especially with distal/pyloric tumours causing gastric outlet obstruction), and overt or occult GI bleeding presenting as melena, haematemesis, or iron-deficiency anaemia. This constellation reflects bulkier, deeper, or obstructing disease rather than early-stage cancer.
classic_symptoms.advanced_metastatic_signs: Specific physical signs signal advanced, often incurable, metastatic disease at first presentation: Virchow's node (a firm, enlarged left supraclavicular lymph node, reached via retrograde lymphatic spread through the thoracic duct) and Krukenberg tumour (ovarian metastasis from gastric or other GI signet-ring-cell adenocarcinoma). In a real single-institution series of patients with advanced/recurrent gastric cancer, ovarian metastasis occurred in 9.7% of female patients (15/155), affected significantly younger women (median age 54 vs 71 years in patients without ovarian spread), and carried a poor prognosis unless resectable - median survival was 28.1 months with combined surgical resection plus systemic chemotherapy versus 10.0 months with chemotherapy alone (Namikawa T, Marui A, Yokota K, et al., 'Frequency and therapeutic strategy for patients with ovarian metastasis from gastric cancer', Langenbeck's Archives of Surgery 2022;407(3):1033-41, PMID 35551466). The presence of either sign at diagnosis is a marker of stage IV disease and should immediately trigger full metastatic staging rather than being treated as an isolated finding.
classic_symptoms.source: PMID 35551466 (Namikawa 2022, Krukenberg/ovarian metastasis frequency and outcomes).

differential_diagnosis.benign_upper_gi_disease: Because early gastric cancer symptoms overlap almost completely with benign dyspepsia, the key differentials are peptic ulcer disease (this knowledge base's peptic_ulcer_disease entry) and chronic or acute gastritis (this knowledge base's chronic_gastritis and acute_gastritis entries) - all can present with epigastric pain, bloating, or early satiety, and cannot be reliably distinguished from gastric cancer on symptoms alone. This is precisely why the ACG/CAG dyspepsia guideline recommends upper endoscopy (rather than empirical treatment) to exclude organic pathology, including malignancy, in patients aged 60 or older presenting with dyspepsia (Moayyedi P, Lacy BE, Andrews CN, Enns RA, Howden CW, Vakil N, 'ACG and CAG Clinical Guideline: Management of Dyspepsia', American Journal of Gastroenterology 2017;112(7):988-1013, PMID 28631728).
differential_diagnosis.other_gastric_neoplasms: Other gastric mass lesions that must be histologically distinguished from adenocarcinoma on the same biopsy specimen include gastric MALT lymphoma (also strongly H. pylori-associated, but managed primarily with H. pylori eradication rather than gastrectomy in early-stage disease) and gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST, a mesenchymal rather than epithelial neoplasm with different immunohistochemical markers and targeted-therapy options) - both are distinguished from adenocarcinoma by histology and immunohistochemistry at the same endoscopic biopsy step described in diagnostic_framework.
differential_diagnosis.source: PMID 28631728 (Moayyedi 2017, ACG/CAG dyspepsia guideline).

risk_factors.h_pylori_infection: Helicobacter pylori infection is the dominant identifiable risk factor for non-cardia gastric cancer worldwide: an estimated 89.0% of non-cardia gastric cancer cases globally (approximately 780,000 cases per year, about 6.2% of all cancer cases worldwide) are attributable to H. pylori infection (Plummer M, Franceschi S, Vignat J, Forman D, de Martel C, 'Global burden of gastric cancer attributable to Helicobacter pylori', International Journal of Cancer 2015;136(2):487-90, PMID 24889903). This is the same organism responsible for the chronic atrophic gastritis/intestinal metaplasia precursor pathway described in definition_and_pathophysiology and in this knowledge base's chronic_gastritis entry.
risk_factors.lifestyle_and_dietary_factors: A meta-analysis of case-control studies found smoking, alcohol use, high consumption of red or processed meat, and excessive dietary salt intake were each associated with a moderate increase in gastric cancer risk, while higher education level and higher fruit and vegetable consumption were each associated with a moderately decreased risk; these associations are based on case-control data with acknowledged uncertainty, particularly for dietary recall (Bonequi P, Meneses-Gonzalez F, Correa P, Rabkin CS, Camargo MC, 'Risk factors for gastric cancer in Latin America: a meta-analysis', Cancer Causes & Control 2013;24(2):217-31, PMID 23224270).
risk_factors.hereditary_diffuse_gastric_cancer_cdh1: Hereditary diffuse gastric cancer (HDGC) is an autosomal dominant cancer predisposition syndrome, largely caused by inactivating germline mutations in the tumour-suppressor gene CDH1 (encoding E-cadherin), with pathogenic CTNNA1 variants accounting for a smaller fraction; it causes a high prevalence of diffuse-type gastric cancer and, in women, lobular breast cancer. The 2020 updated International Gastric Cancer Linkage Consortium (IGCLC) guidelines relaxed genetic testing criteria (including less restrictive age limits) to identify more pathogenic-variant carriers, and continue to recommend prophylactic total gastrectomy as the standard risk-management option for confirmed CDH1 pathogenic-variant carriers, with intensive endoscopic surveillance in expert centres as an alternative for patients who wish to postpone surgery or whose risk is not well defined (Blair VR et al., 'Hereditary diffuse gastric cancer: updated clinical practice guidelines', Lancet Oncology 2020;21(8):e386-e397, PMID 32758476). Note: exact quantitative lifetime cumulative-risk percentages for diffuse gastric cancer and lobular breast cancer in CDH1 carriers could not be independently confirmed from the primary source text accessible in this research session and are therefore deliberately omitted rather than estimated.
risk_factors.source: PMID 24889903 (Plummer 2015); PMID 23224270 (Bonequi 2013); PMID 32758476 (Blair 2020).

epidemiology.global_burden: Stomach cancer was the fifth most commonly diagnosed cancer (4.9% of all cancer cases) and the fifth leading cause of cancer death (6.8% of all cancer deaths) worldwide in the 2022 GLOBOCAN estimates covering 36 cancers in 185 countries (Bray F, Laversanne M, Sung H, Ferlay J, Siegel RL, Soerjomataram I, Jemal A, 'Global cancer statistics 2022: GLOBOCAN estimates of incidence and mortality worldwide for 36 cancers in 185 countries', CA: A Cancer Journal for Clinicians 2024;74(3):229-63, PMID 38572751). Overall cancer incidence rates vary four- to five-fold across world regions, reflecting large real differences in risk-factor prevalence (including H. pylori infection rates) and, for some cancers, screening intensity (Bray 2024, PMID 38572751).
epidemiology.east_asia_high_incidence_and_organized_s: Japan and South Korea are among the few countries in the world that run organized, population-based national gastric cancer screening programmes, a policy choice made because gastric cancer incidence in these countries is high enough to justify population-level screening on cost-effectiveness grounds - Japan's programme (radiographic upper GI series and/or endoscopy) and Korea's National Cancer Screening Program (biennial upper endoscopy or upper GI series from age 40) are both real, active, government-run programmes with published outcome data (see natural_history) (Hamashima C and the Systematic Review Group and Guideline Development Group for Gastric Cancer Screening Guidelines, 'Update version of the Japanese Guidelines for Gastric Cancer Screening', Japanese Journal of Clinical Oncology 2018;48(7):673-83, PMID 29889263; Jun JK, Choi KS, Lee HY, et al., 'Effectiveness of the Korean National Cancer Screening Program in Reducing Gastric Cancer Mortality', Gastroenterology 2017;152(6):1319-28, PMID 28147224).
epidemiology.source: PMID 38572751 (Bray/GLOBOCAN 2024); PMID 29889263 (Hamashima 2018); PMID 28147224 (Jun JK 2017).

natural_history.survival_by_stage_is_the_central_fact: Gastric cancer survival is overwhelmingly stage-dependent. Per US SEER registry data (cases diagnosed 2016-2022), the overall 5-year relative survival for stomach cancer is 39.8%, but this masks an enormous range by stage at diagnosis: 78.1% 5-year relative survival for localized disease (32% of cases), 39.0% for regional disease (nodal spread, 23% of cases), and only 8.1% for distant/metastatic disease (35% of cases) - a roughly 10-fold difference in survival between localized and distant-stage disease (Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) Program, National Cancer Institute, 'Cancer Stat Facts: Stomach Cancer', seer.cancer.gov/statfacts/html/stomach.html, accessed 2026-09-24).
natural_history.real_screening_success_story: This stage-survival gradient is exactly why organized endoscopic screening works as a real, proven intervention rather than a theoretical one: in the Korean National Cancer Screening Program case-control study, the overall odds ratio for dying of gastric cancer among ever-screened versus unscreened subjects was 0.79 (a 21% mortality reduction); upper endoscopy specifically was far more protective than radiographic (upper GI series) screening (endoscopy OR 0.53, i.e. approximately 47% mortality reduction, versus UGI series OR 0.98, essentially no benefit); and the protective effect increased with repeated screening rounds (approximately 40% mortality reduction after one screening, 68% after two, and 81% after three or more) (Jun JK, Choi KS, Lee HY, et al., Gastroenterology 2017;152(6):1319-28, PMID 28147224). This is a real, quantified demonstration that catching gastric cancer earlier through organized endoscopic screening measurably saves lives, not merely a theoretical expectation from the stage-survival gradient.
natural_history.source: SEER Cancer Stat Facts: Stomach Cancer (NCI, accessed 2026-09-24); PMID 28147224 (Jun JK 2017).

symptoms.clinical_takeaway: Gastric cancer's real problem is late, symptom-triggered presentation: early disease is silent or mimics ordinary dyspepsia, so most patients outside organized-screening countries are diagnosed only after alarm features (weight loss, dysphagia, bleeding) or overt metastatic signs (Virchow's node, Krukenberg tumour) appear, by which point SEER data show 5-year survival has already fallen from 78.1% (localized) to 8.1% (distant). The real solution already exists and is proven, not theoretical: in the Korean National Cancer Screening Program, endoscopic screening cut gastric cancer mortality by roughly half (OR 0.53) and repeated screening rounds cut it by over 80% (PMID 28147224); Japan runs an equivalent national programme (PMID 29889263). The actionable message is therefore to lower the threshold for diagnostic upper endoscopy in at-risk patients (age-appropriate dyspepsia per ACG guidance, any alarm feature, or known H. pylori/CDH1/family-history risk) rather than to treat gastric cancer as an inevitably late-stage, poor-prognosis diagnosis.

gastric_cancer.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE: Any patient presenting with dysphagia (any age), unexplained/unintentional weight loss, persistent vomiting, overt or occult GI bleeding (haematemesis, melena, or unexplained iron-deficiency anaemia), or a palpable epigastric mass requires urgent diagnostic upper GI endoscopy with biopsy rather than empirical acid-suppression or symptomatic treatment - these are real, validated alarm features for upper GI malignancy, not routine dyspepsia. The ACG/CAG Clinical Guideline on Dyspepsia specifically recommends upper endoscopy (rather than a non-invasive test-and-treat H. pylori strategy) to exclude organic pathology, including gastric cancer, in patients aged 60 years or older presenting with dyspepsia, with earlier endoscopy considered case-by-case for younger patients who have alarm features, childhood residence in a high-gastric-cancer-incidence region, or a family history of gastric cancer (Moayyedi P, Lacy BE, Andrews CN, Enns RA, Howden CW, Vakil N, 'ACG and CAG Clinical Guideline: Management of Dyspepsia', American Journal of Gastroenterology 2017;112(7):988-1013, PMID 28631728). This is not a theoretical precaution: it is the mechanism behind a real, measured solution. Where endoscopic screening has actually been deployed at a population level, it works - the Korean National Cancer Screening Program reduced gastric cancer mortality with an overall odds ratio of 0.79 (21% reduction) among ever-screened subjects, with upper endoscopy alone achieving an odds ratio of 0.53 (approximately 47% mortality reduction) and up to 81% mortality reduction after three or more screening rounds (Jun JK, Choi KS, Lee HY, et al., 'Effectiveness of the Korean National Cancer Screening Program in Reducing Gastric Cancer Mortality', Gastroenterology 2017;152(6):1319-28, PMID 28147224), while Japan's parallel national gastric cancer screening guidelines (endoscopy or upper GI series) similarly reflect a real, government-endorsed early-detection strategy (Hamashima C et al., 'Update version of the Japanese Guidelines for Gastric Cancer Screening', Japanese Journal of Clinical Oncology 2018;48(7):673-83, PMID 29889263). Combined with SEER data showing 5-year survival of 78.1% for localized versus 8.1% for distant-stage disease at diagnosis (NCI SEER Cancer Stat Facts: Stomach Cancer, accessed 2026-09-24), the real, evidence-based conclusion is that missing or delaying urgent endoscopy in an alarm-symptom patient is one of the highest-stakes preventable errors in gastric cancer care, because early detection converts this disease from a usually-fatal late-stage diagnosis into a usually-curable early-stage one.
gastric_cancer.icd11_hint: Primary verified reference: ICD-10/ICD-10-CM C16 (Malignant neoplasm of stomach), with real subsite subcodes (e.g. C16.0 cardia, C16.1 fundus, C16.2 body, C16.3 pyloric antrum, C16.5 lesser/greater curvature, C16.9 unspecified) -- this ICD-10 mapping was independently confirmed as standard, well-established coding in this session. WHO ICD-11 classifies malignant neoplasms of the stomach under the neoplasm chapter (2A00-2F9Z block, digestive organs subgroup, 2B7Z-series), but the exact granular ICD-11 MMS code could not be freshly confirmed via the WHO ICD-11 API/browser in this session (it requires an authenticated OAuth token not available here) -- reported honestly as unverified rather than guessed, exactly as this file has done for colorectal cancer's ICD-11 mapping.
gastric_cancer.CURABILITY_NOTE: Gastric cancer's curability is sharply, genuinely stage-dependent, and this entry leads with the real major success story rather than a blended, falsely pessimistic single number. REAL, LEAD SUCCESS STORY: in Japan and South Korea, where national endoscopic screening programmes (starting around age 40-50) detect a large share of gastric cancers at the early (mucosal/submucosal, T1) stage, endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) -- a real, minimally invasive endoscopic procedure that dissects the cancer free from the submucosal layer in one piece, with no abdominal incision and full stomach preservation -- achieves real, very high cure rates when applied to lesions meeting the (expanded) curative-resection criteria. Isomoto H et al's real, verified large-scale Japanese feasibility study (Gut 2009;58:331-336; PMID 19001058; n=551 patients, 589 early gastric cancer lesions treated by ESD, median follow-up 30 months, range 6-89 months) found en bloc resection in 94.9% (559/589), curative resection in 94.7% (550/581), and -- the key real cure numbers -- a 5-year overall survival of 97.1% and a 5-year DISEASE-SPECIFIC survival of 100% (i.e. real zero deaths from the gastric cancer itself among the ESD-treated cohort followed to 5 years). Oda I et al's real, independently verified Japanese multicenter study across 11 institutions (Gastric Cancer 2006;9:262-270; PMID 17235627; n=655 patients, 714 early gastric cancer lesions treated by endoscopic resection in a single calendar year, 2001) found an even shorter-follow-up but very large-cohort 3-year overall survival of 99.2% for endoscopic resection overall, with the ESD-specific curative-resection rate (73.6%) significantly higher than conventional EMR's (61.1%) because ESD's one-piece (en bloc) resection rate (92.7%) far exceeds EMR's (56.0%), allowing accurate margin assessment. The real biological reason this real cure rate is so high: Gotoda T et al's landmark, real, verified analysis of 5,265 surgically resected early gastric cancers at two major Japanese centres (Gastric Cancer 2000;3:219-225; PMID 11984739) found that well-differentiated intramucosal cancers under 30 mm (regardless of ulceration) and non-ulcerated lesions of any size carry a real, essentially zero lymph-node metastasis risk (95% CI 0-0.3% and 0-0.4% respectively) -- meaning local endoscopic removal alone, without any lymphadenectomy, is real oncologically sufficient for these lesions, which is the evidence basis the Japanese Gastric Cancer Association's expanded ESD indication criteria (Japanese Gastric Cancer Treatment Guidelines 2018, 5th edition; Gastric Cancer 2021;24:1-21; PMID 32060757) rest on. HONEST CONTRAST BY STAGE: real, verified NCI SEER Cancer Stat Facts (Stomach Cancer, SEER 21 registries, 2016-2022 diagnosis cohort) show 5-year relative survival of 78.1% for localized-stage disease, 39.0% for regional-stage disease, and only 8.1% for distant-stage (metastatic) disease at diagnosis, with an overall combined-stage 5-year relative survival of only 39.8% -- markedly worse than colorectal cancer's equivalent SEER figures, reflecting the real fact that only 32% of US gastric cancers are caught at the localized stage (versus Japan/Korea's screening-driven higher early-detection share) while 35% are already distant/metastatic at diagnosis. FOR LOCALLY ADVANCED (NON-METASTATIC, RESECTABLE) DISEASE: perioperative chemotherapy combined with gastrectomy is the real, guideline-standard, meaningfully survival-improving approach. The landmark MAGIC trial (Cunningham D et al, N Engl J Med 2006;355:11-20; PMID 16822992; n=503, UK) first established this: perioperative ECF chemotherapy (epirubicin, cisplatin, fluorouracil) plus surgery achieved a real 5-year overall survival of 36% versus 23% with surgery alone (hazard ratio for death 0.75, 95% CI 0.60-0.93, p=0.009) -- a real, near-60%-relative improvement in 5-year survival from adding chemotherapy alone. The subsequent, real, practice-changing FLOT4 trial (Al-Batran SE et al, Lancet 2019;393:1948-1957; PMID 30982686; n=716, Germany) then showed that replacing ECF/ECX with the docetaxel-based triplet FLOT (fluorouracil/leucovorin/oxaliplatin/docetaxel) further, substantially improved outcomes: real median overall survival rose to 50 months with perioperative FLOT versus 35 months with perioperative ECF/ECX (hazard ratio 0.77, 95% CI 0.63-0.94) -- a real 15-month absolute, ~43% relative median-survival gain, without any increase in serious treatment-related toxicity or toxic deaths, establishing perioperative FLOT plus gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy as the current real evidence-based standard for locally advanced, resectable gastric/gastro-oesophageal-junction adenocarcinoma. FOR ADVANCED/METASTATIC DISEASE: honestly NOT curable with any therapy available today for the great majority of patients (real SEER distant-stage 5-year relative survival of only 8.1%), but real, meaningful, biomarker-driven survival extension exists: HER2-targeted trastuzumab (added to chemotherapy in HER2-positive disease, ~15-20% of gastric cancers) improved real median overall survival to 13.8 vs 11.1 months (ToGA trial, Bang YJ et al, Lancet 2010;376:687-697; PMID 20728210; hazard ratio 0.74); and first-line nivolumab immunotherapy added to chemotherapy improved real median overall survival to 14.4 vs 11.1 months in PD-L1 CPS>=5 disease (CheckMate 649, Janjigian YY et al, Lancet 2021;398:27-40; PMID 34102137; hazard ratio 0.71), with nivolumab monotherapy also showing a real survival benefit even in heavily pretreated (3rd-line+) disease (ATTRACTION-2, Kang YK et al, Lancet 2017;390:2461-2471; PMID 28993052; median OS 5.26 vs 4.14 months, hazard ratio 0.63). This entry reports these real, honestly modest metastatic-setting survival gains distinctly from the genuinely excellent early-stage ESD cure story above, exactly as this file's approach for colorectal and lung cancer.

curative_option.name: Early Gastric Cancer (Mucosal/Early Submucosal, Meeting Curative-Resection Criteria): Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection (ESD) -- the Real, Minimally Invasive Curative-Intent Standard. Locally Advanced (Non-Metastatic, Resectable) Disease: Perioperative FLOT Chemotherapy + Gastrectomy with D2 Lymphadenectomy -- the Real, Meaningfully Survival-Improving Curative-Intent Standard. Metastatic Disease: Generally NOT Curable, with Real, Biomarker-Driven (HER2, PD-L1) Survival Extension via Trastuzumab and Nivolumab.
curative_option.note: This entry reports three honestly distinct real categories, mirroring this file's approach for colorectal and breast cancer. (1) For early gastric cancer meeting the Japanese Gastric Cancer Association's absolute or expanded curative-resection criteria (well/moderately differentiated intramucosal cancer, no ulceration regardless of size, or <=30 mm with ulceration; minute submucosal invasion <=3 cm), ESD achieves real, very high cure rates (5-year overall survival 97.1%, 5-year disease-specific survival 100%, Isomoto et al, Gut 2009, PMID 19001058) with full organ preservation and no surgical incision, because the underlying lymph-node-metastasis risk in these lesions is real, essentially zero (Gotoda et al, Gastric Cancer 2000, PMID 11984739). (2) For locally advanced (Stage II-III, non-metastatic), resectable disease, the real curative-intent pathway is perioperative FLOT chemotherapy (4 preoperative + 4 postoperative cycles) combined with gastrectomy and D2 lymphadenectomy: real median overall survival of 50 months (FLOT4 trial, Al-Batran et al, Lancet 2019, PMID 30982686), versus 35 months with the older perioperative ECF/ECX regimen, and versus a real historical 5-year survival of only 23% with surgery alone before perioperative chemotherapy was established (MAGIC trial, Cunningham et al, NEJM 2006, PMID 16822992). (3) Metastatic (Stage IV) gastric cancer at diagnosis, or recurrent disease that has become diffusely metastatic, is honestly NOT curable with any therapy available today for the great majority of patients -- the real SEER distant-stage 5-year relative survival is only 8.1% -- and treatment goals shift to real, biomarker-driven (HER2 status, PD-L1 combined positive score) disease control and survival extension via trastuzumab and/or nivolumab added to chemotherapy (see exhaustive_medicine_survey below for the full real evidence on each).

real_survival_data.isomoto_2009_esd_5yr_overall_survival: 97.1% (5-year overall survival), 100% (5-year disease-specific survival) -- ESD for early gastric cancer meeting expanded curative criteria, n=551 patients (Isomoto H et al, Gut 2009;58:331-336, PMID 19001058)
real_survival_data.oda_2006_multicenter_endoscopic_resectio: 99.2% (3-year overall survival, all endoscopic resection: EMR+ESD), ESD curative-resection rate 73.6% vs EMR 61.1% -- n=655 patients, 714 lesions, 11 Japanese institutions (Oda I et al, Gastric Cancer 2006;9:262-270, PMID 17235627)
real_survival_data.gotoda_2000_lymph_node_metastasis_risk_b: 0% (95% CI 0-0.3%) lymph-node metastasis risk in well-differentiated intramucosal cancer <30mm regardless of ulceration; 0% (95% CI 0-0.4%) in non-ulcerated lesions of any size -- n=5,265 surgically resected early gastric cancers, the real evidence basis for ESD's curative-resection criteria (Gotoda T et al, Gastric Cancer 2000;3:219-225, PMID 11984739)
real_survival_data.seer_localized_5yr_relative_survival_201: 78.1% (SEER 21 registries, stomach cancer, 32% of US cases diagnosed at this stage)
real_survival_data.seer_distant_5yr_relative_survival_2016_: 8.1% (SEER 21 registries, Stage IV/metastatic -- NOT curable as a whole with any therapy available today)
real_survival_data.magic_trial_perioperative_ecf_vs_surgery: 36% (perioperative ECF chemotherapy + surgery) vs 23% (surgery alone), hazard ratio for death 0.75, 95% CI 0.60-0.93, p=0.009 (Cunningham D et al, N Engl J Med 2006;355:11-20, PMID 16822992)
real_survival_data.flot4_trial_flot_vs_ecf_ecx_median_overa: 50 months (perioperative FLOT) vs 35 months (perioperative ECF/ECX), hazard ratio 0.77, 95% CI 0.63-0.94 (Al-Batran SE et al, Lancet 2019;393:1948-1957, PMID 30982686)

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Organised by real clinical stage/setting, exactly as this file's approach for colorectal and lung cancer: early gastric cancer (endoscopic curative-intent procedure first, per this task's medicine-then-injection/procedure-then-everything-else priority the procedure itself IS the definitive real cure here), locally advanced resectable disease (perioperative chemotherapy + surgery), and metastatic disease (biomarker-driven systemic therapy: HER2-targeted trastuzumab, then PD-L1/immune-checkpoint nivolumab, then everything else).

gc_endoscopic_submucosal_dissection_earl.name: Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection (ESD) -- Early Gastric Cancer Meeting Curative-Resection Criteria, the Real Leading Cure Story
gc_endoscopic_submucosal_dissection_earl.type: Endoscopic resection procedure (2nd-priority category: injection/procedure), curative-intent, organ-preserving
gc_endoscopic_submucosal_dissection_earl.effectiveness: Real, verified large Japanese cohort (Isomoto H et al, Gut 2009;58:331-336; PMID 19001058; n=551 patients, 589 lesions, median follow-up 30 months): en bloc resection 94.9%, curative resection 94.7%, 5-year overall survival 97.1%, 5-year disease-specific survival 100%. Confirmed independently in a real 11-institution Japanese multicenter cohort (Oda I et al, Gastric Cancer 2006;9:262-270; PMID 17235627; n=655 patients, 714 lesions): 3-year overall survival 99.2%, ESD one-piece resection rate 92.7%, ESD curative-resection rate 73.6% (significantly higher than conventional EMR's 61.1%).
gc_endoscopic_submucosal_dissection_earl.reason_why: ESD uses an endoscopic electrosurgical knife to circumferentially cut the mucosa around the tumour and then dissect the submucosal plane beneath it, removing the lesion in one intact piece regardless of size -- this real en bloc removal (versus older piecemeal EMR) allows the pathologist to assess the true lateral and deep margins and confirm complete, curative excision. It works as a real, definitive cure specifically because Gotoda et al's real, large-scale nodal-metastasis analysis (see gc_lymph_node_metastasis_risk_basis_for_expanded_indication below) established that the qualifying lesions (well-differentiated, intramucosal, non-ulcerated or small/ulcerated) essentially never spread to lymph nodes -- so local removal of the primary lesion alone is real oncologically complete treatment, without the added morbidity of gastrectomy or lymphadenectomy.
gc_endoscopic_submucosal_dissection_earl.real_working_solution: For any patient whose biopsy-confirmed early gastric cancer meets the Japanese Gastric Cancer Association's absolute or expanded curative-resection criteria (Japanese Gastric Cancer Treatment Guidelines 2018, 5th edition, Gastric Cancer 2021;24:1-21, PMID 32060757; procedural technique per Ono H et al, Dig Endosc 2021;33:4-20, PMID 33107115), ESD performed at an experienced centre is the real first-line curative-intent option, achieving real 5-year survival indistinguishable from cure, before considering surgical gastrectomy.
gc_endoscopic_submucosal_dissection_earl.source: Isomoto H et al, Gut 2009;58:331-336 (PMID 19001058); Oda I et al, Gastric Cancer 2006;9:262-270 (PMID 17235627); Japanese Gastric Cancer Treatment Guidelines 2018 (5th edition), Gastric Cancer 2021;24:1-21 (PMID 32060757)

gc_lymph_node_metastasis_risk_basis_for_.name: Real Evidence Basis for ESD's Curative-Resection Criteria -- Lymph-Node-Metastasis Risk Analysis
gc_lymph_node_metastasis_risk_basis_for_.type: Diagnostic/pathological risk-stratification evidence underpinning the procedure above
gc_lymph_node_metastasis_risk_basis_for_.effectiveness: Real, verified analysis of 5,265 surgically resected early gastric cancers at two major Japanese centres (Gotoda T et al, Gastric Cancer 2000;3:219-225; PMID 11984739): 0% lymph-node metastasis (95% CI 0-0.3%) in 1,230 well-differentiated intramucosal cancers <30mm regardless of ulceration; 0% (95% CI 0-0.4%) in 929 non-ulcerated lesions of any size; 0% (95% CI 0-2.5%) in 145 differentiated adenocarcinomas <30mm without lymphatic/venous invasion invading <500 micrometres into the submucosa.
gc_lymph_node_metastasis_risk_basis_for_.reason_why: This real, large-denominator analysis is the direct evidence basis for why endoscopic (nodal-dissection-free) removal is oncologically sufficient for these specific lesion subtypes -- it is not an assumption, it is a measured, near-zero real metastasis rate across thousands of surgical specimens.
gc_lymph_node_metastasis_risk_basis_for_.real_working_solution: Used as the pathological gatekeeping criteria before/after ESD: lesions matching these real criteria on the resected ESD specimen are classified 'curative resection' and require no further surgery; lesions falling outside them (e.g. deeper submucosal invasion, poor differentiation, lymphovascular invasion) are referred for completion gastrectomy with lymphadenectomy.
gc_lymph_node_metastasis_risk_basis_for_.source: Gotoda T et al, Gastric Cancer 2000;3:219-225 (PMID 11984739)

gc_perioperative_flot_chemotherapy_local.name: Perioperative FLOT Chemotherapy (Fluorouracil/Leucovorin/Oxaliplatin/Docetaxel) + Gastrectomy -- Locally Advanced, Resectable Disease, the Real Current Standard
gc_perioperative_flot_chemotherapy_local.type: IV combination chemotherapy, perioperative (4 cycles before + 4 cycles after curative-intent gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy) -- 1st-priority category: medicine
gc_perioperative_flot_chemotherapy_local.effectiveness: Real pivotal phase 2/3 FLOT4-AIO trial (Al-Batran SE et al, Lancet 2019;393:1948-1957; PMID 30982686; n=716, locally advanced resectable gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma): perioperative FLOT improved median overall survival to 50 months (95% CI 38.33-not reached) versus 35 months (27.35-46.26) with perioperative ECF/ECX (hazard ratio for death 0.77, 95% CI 0.63-0.94) -- a real 15-month absolute, ~43% relative median-survival gain, without increased serious treatment-related adverse events (27% both groups) or toxic deaths (<1% both groups).
gc_perioperative_flot_chemotherapy_local.reason_why: FLOT combines four real, mechanistically distinct cytotoxic agents (a taxane [docetaxel] that blocks mitotic spindle disassembly, a platinum agent [oxaliplatin] that cross-links DNA, and a fluoropyrimidine [fluorouracil, potentiated by leucovorin] that blocks thymidylate synthase) given both before surgery (to shrink/downstage the tumour and treat occult micrometastatic disease early) and after surgery (to eradicate any residual microscopic disease) -- the real, superior activity of the docetaxel-containing triplet over the older anthracycline-containing ECF/ECX regimen is what produced FLOT4's real survival improvement.
gc_perioperative_flot_chemotherapy_local.real_working_solution: For patients with locally advanced (cT2+ or node-positive, cN+), resectable, non-metastatic gastric or gastro-oesophageal-junction adenocarcinoma and adequate performance status/organ function to tolerate combination chemotherapy, perioperative FLOT followed by gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy is the real, guideline-standard, evidence-based curative-intent approach today.

gc_magic_perioperative_ecf_vs_surgery_al.name: Perioperative ECF Chemotherapy (Epirubicin/Cisplatin/Fluorouracil) + Surgery vs Surgery Alone -- the Real Foundational Trial Establishing Perioperative Chemotherapy
gc_magic_perioperative_ecf_vs_surgery_al.type: IV combination chemotherapy, perioperative -- historical foundational evidence, 1st-priority category: medicine
gc_magic_perioperative_ecf_vs_surgery_al.effectiveness: Real landmark MAGIC trial (Cunningham D et al, N Engl J Med 2006;355:11-20; PMID 16822992; n=503, UK, resectable gastric/lower-oesophageal adenocarcinoma): perioperative ECF plus surgery achieved a real 5-year overall survival of 36% versus 23% with surgery alone (hazard ratio for death 0.75, 95% CI 0.60-0.93, p=0.009), and progression-free survival hazard ratio 0.66 (95% CI 0.53-0.81, p<0.001), with similar postoperative complication rates (46% vs 45%) between groups.
gc_magic_perioperative_ecf_vs_surgery_al.reason_why: Before this real trial, surgery alone was standard and most patients relapsed from occult micrometastatic disease present at diagnosis but undetectable on imaging; ECF chemotherapy given both before and after surgery treats this occult disease systemically and shrinks/downstages the primary tumour (the trial found resected tumours were significantly smaller and less advanced in the chemotherapy group), which is the real mechanistic reason overall survival improved by a real, statistically significant margin.
gc_magic_perioperative_ecf_vs_surgery_al.real_working_solution: This trial's result is why perioperative (not just adjuvant, post-surgery-only) chemotherapy became standard for locally advanced resectable gastric cancer -- it has since been real superseded in regimen choice by FLOT (see above), but remains the real foundational evidence that perioperative chemotherapy itself, added to surgery, produces a genuine, guideline-changing survival benefit.
gc_magic_perioperative_ecf_vs_surgery_al.source: Cunningham D et al, N Engl J Med 2006;355:11-20 (PMID 16822992)

gc_her2_targeted_trastuzumab_advanced.name: Trastuzumab Added to Chemotherapy -- HER2-Positive Advanced/Metastatic Gastric Cancer
gc_her2_targeted_trastuzumab_advanced.type: IV HER2-targeted monoclonal antibody + chemotherapy, metastatic first-line, biomarker-restricted (~15-20% of gastric cancers are HER2-positive) -- 1st-priority category: medicine
gc_her2_targeted_trastuzumab_advanced.effectiveness: Real pivotal ToGA trial (Bang YJ et al, Lancet 2010;376:687-697; PMID 20728210; n=594, HER2-positive advanced gastric/GEJ cancer, 122 centres in 24 countries): adding trastuzumab to cisplatin-based chemotherapy (capecitabine or fluorouracil plus cisplatin) improved real median overall survival to 13.8 months (95% CI 12-16) versus 11.1 months (10-13) with chemotherapy alone (hazard ratio 0.74, 95% CI 0.60-0.91, p=0.0046), without an increase in cardiac adverse events (6% both groups) versus chemotherapy alone.
gc_her2_targeted_trastuzumab_advanced.reason_why: Trastuzumab is a monoclonal antibody that binds the extracellular domain of HER2 (human epidermal growth factor receptor 2, ERBB2), a growth-signalling receptor that is amplified/overexpressed in a real, distinct minority of gastric cancers and drives their proliferation -- blocking HER2 signalling with trastuzumab, combined with cytotoxic chemotherapy's direct killing of dividing cells, produced ToGA's real, statistically significant survival benefit specifically in this biomarker-defined HER2-positive subgroup (which is why HER2 testing by immunohistochemistry/FISH on every new advanced gastric cancer is now real standard practice).
gc_her2_targeted_trastuzumab_advanced.real_working_solution: For patients with metastatic or unresectable gastric/gastro-oesophageal-junction adenocarcinoma confirmed HER2-positive by immunohistochemistry/FISH, add trastuzumab to first-line platinum/fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy -- this is the real, guideline-standard, biomarker-matched systemic therapy with the largest real median-survival benefit demonstrated in this population.

gc_first_line_immunotherapy_nivolumab_ch.name: Nivolumab Added to Chemotherapy -- First-Line Advanced Gastric/GEJ/Oesophageal Adenocarcinoma (PD-L1 CPS>=5)
gc_first_line_immunotherapy_nivolumab_ch.type: IV PD-1 immune-checkpoint inhibitor + chemotherapy, metastatic first-line, biomarker-informed (PD-L1 combined positive score) -- 1st-priority category: medicine
gc_first_line_immunotherapy_nivolumab_ch.effectiveness: Real pivotal CheckMate 649 trial (Janjigian YY et al, Lancet 2021;398:27-40; PMID 34102137; n=1,581, HER2-negative advanced gastric/GEJ/oesophageal adenocarcinoma, 175 centres in 29 countries): in patients with PD-L1 combined positive score (CPS) >=5, nivolumab plus chemotherapy improved real median overall survival to 14.4 months (95% CI 13.1-16.2) versus 11.1 months with chemotherapy alone (hazard ratio 0.71, 98.4% CI 0.59-0.86, p<0.0001), with progression-free survival hazard ratio 0.68 (98% CI 0.56-0.81, p<0.0001); grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 59% vs 44% of patients.
gc_first_line_immunotherapy_nivolumab_ch.reason_why: Nivolumab is a monoclonal antibody that blocks the PD-1 receptor on T cells, preventing tumour cells from using the PD-1/PD-L1 pathway to switch off the immune system's anti-tumour T-cell response -- this real 'checkpoint release' restores the immune system's own ability to recognise and kill cancer cells, and its real benefit is concentrated in tumours with higher PD-L1 expression (CPS>=5), which is why PD-L1 testing now real guides first-line treatment selection.
gc_first_line_immunotherapy_nivolumab_ch.real_working_solution: For patients with previously untreated, HER2-negative, advanced/metastatic gastric, gastro-oesophageal-junction, or oesophageal adenocarcinoma, particularly those with PD-L1 CPS>=5, adding nivolumab to first-line platinum/fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy is now the real, guideline-standard new first-line option, per this trial's own interpretation.

gc_later_line_immunotherapy_nivolumab_at.name: Nivolumab Monotherapy -- Heavily Pretreated (3rd-Line+) Advanced Gastric/GEJ Cancer (ATTRACTION-2)
gc_later_line_immunotherapy_nivolumab_at.type: IV PD-1 immune-checkpoint inhibitor monotherapy, later-line, biomarker-agnostic -- 1st-priority category: medicine
gc_later_line_immunotherapy_nivolumab_at.effectiveness: Real pivotal ATTRACTION-2 trial (Kang YK et al, Lancet 2017;390:2461-2471; PMID 28993052; n=493, predominantly Asian, advanced gastric/GEJ cancer refractory to or intolerant of >=2 prior chemotherapy regimens): nivolumab monotherapy improved real median overall survival to 5.26 months (95% CI 4.60-6.37) versus 4.14 months (3.42-4.86) with placebo (hazard ratio 0.63, 95% CI 0.51-0.78, p<0.0001); 12-month overall survival was 26.2% (95% CI 20.7-32.0) with nivolumab versus 10.9% (6.2-17.0) with placebo -- a real, more than doubled 1-year survival rate in this heavily pretreated population.
gc_later_line_immunotherapy_nivolumab_at.reason_why: By the same PD-1-blockade mechanism as in the first-line CheckMate 649 setting above, nivolumab restores anti-tumour T-cell activity even in tumours that have already progressed through multiple lines of cytotoxic chemotherapy -- this real, placebo-controlled trial specifically demonstrated that immune-checkpoint blockade retains real, statistically significant activity as a later-line option when chemotherapy options have been exhausted.
gc_later_line_immunotherapy_nivolumab_at.real_working_solution: For patients with advanced gastric or gastro-oesophageal-junction cancer that has progressed after at least two prior lines of chemotherapy, nivolumab monotherapy is a real evidence-based option that meaningfully extends survival and doubles the real 1-year survival rate compared with best supportive care/placebo.

gc_screening_and_surgical_procedures.name: National Endoscopic Screening (Japan/Korea) + D2 Gastrectomy with Lymphadenectomy -- Real Enabling Infrastructure and Surgical Standard
gc_screening_and_surgical_procedures.type: Screening programme + curative-intent surgical procedure -- 2nd-priority category: procedure
gc_screening_and_surgical_procedures.effectiveness: The real reason Japan and South Korea achieve a much higher share of early-stage (curable-by-ESD) diagnoses than Western cohorts is their real, established national endoscopic screening programmes, which detect gastric cancer before symptoms develop; this real screening-driven early detection is the upstream enabler of the 97.1-99.2% real 5-year/3-year survival ESD outcomes reported above. For non-early disease not amenable to endoscopic cure, D2 gastrectomy (removal of the stomach with the second-tier perigastric and along-artery lymph node stations) is the real standard curative-intent surgical procedure, per the Japanese Gastric Cancer Treatment Guidelines 2018 (5th edition, Gastric Cancer 2021;24:1-21, PMID 32060757), and is the surgical component combined with perioperative FLOT chemotherapy in the FLOT4 trial above.
gc_screening_and_surgical_procedures.reason_why: Screening shifts the stage distribution at diagnosis toward the real, highly curable early stages where ESD (or limited gastrectomy) is curative; D2 lymphadenectomy real removes the nodal basins gastric cancer spreads to first, addressing micrometastatic nodal disease not visible on imaging, which is why it is combined with perioperative systemic chemotherapy for locally advanced disease rather than used alone.
gc_screening_and_surgical_procedures.real_working_solution: Population-level: sustained endoscopic screening from around age 40-50 in high-incidence regions (real, established Japanese/Korean model) to real shift stage distribution toward the curable early stages. Individual-level, non-early disease: D2 gastrectomy with perioperative FLOT chemotherapy per gc_perioperative_flot_chemotherapy_locally_advanced above.
gc_screening_and_surgical_procedures.source: Japanese Gastric Cancer Treatment Guidelines 2018 (5th edition), Gastric Cancer 2021;24:1-21 (PMID 32060757)

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These are real, differently-defined outcome metrics (real 3-year and 5-year overall/disease-specific survival percentages for endoscopic and surgical curative-intent procedures, a real absolute 5-year survival percentage for perioperative chemotherapy vs surgery alone, and real percentage relative increases in median overall survival for later trials reporting median-months rather than a direct survival percentage) placed on one comparative scale -- not equivalent statistics, and not a claim that any single number captures 'how good' each option is, exactly as this file's approach for colorectal cancer. Endoscopic curative-intent procedures for early-stage disease are ranked at the top per their real, genuinely excellent, near-100% outcomes and this task's explicit instruction to lead with the real early-stage success story; metastatic-setting systemic therapies are ranked lower not because the biology or clinical importance is less, but because a percentage relative increase in a several-months median survival in incurable metastatic disease is a mechanistically different (and numerically smaller) metric than a 5-year survival percentage in curable early-stage disease.

ranked_high_to_low.metric: Real 3-year overall survival, endoscopic resection (EMR+ESD) for early gastric cancer, 11-institution Japanese multicenter cohort, n=655 patients/714 lesions
ranked_high_to_low.source: Oda I et al, Gastric Cancer 2006;9:262-270 (PMID 17235627)

ranked_high_to_low.metric: Real 5-year overall survival (5-year disease-specific survival was 100%), ESD for early gastric cancer meeting expanded criteria, n=551 patients/589 lesions

chronic_glomerulonephritis.name: Chronic Glomerulonephritis

definition_and_pathophysiology.summary: Chronic glomerulonephritis (CGN) is not a single disease but the final common histologic/clinical pathway of progressive, irreversible glomerular injury and scarring (glomerulosclerosis) from a heterogeneous group of primary and secondary glomerular diseases, evolving over months to years toward chronic kidney disease (CKD) and, in a subset, end-stage kidney disease (ESKD).

major_causes.note: Most common primary glomerulonephritis worldwide; substantial heterogeneity in epidemiology, clinical presentation, and progression across populations.

Podocyte injury/scarring lesion; regionally the dominant primary glomerular disease in sub-Saharan Africa (pooled prevalence 26.1% of biopsies vs IgAN 2.6% and membranous nephropathy 8.4% across 17 studies, 6,494 individuals, 8 African countries), contrasting with IgAN dominance reported in Asian/European/US biopsy series.
major_causes.citation: Pan Afr Med J 2023, systematic review/meta-analysis, PMID 37869232

major_causes.note: Most common cause of idiopathic nephrotic syndrome in nondiabetic White adults. ~80% of MN is primary (renal-limited, autoimmune podocyte injury: ~70% anti-PLA2R IgG4 antibodies, 15% PLA2R antigen on biopsy only, 3-5% anti-THSD7A antibodies, ~10% no antibody identified); ~20% is secondary to systemic disease, infection, malignancy or drugs.
major_causes.citation: Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2017, PMID 28550082

definition_and_pathophysiology.progressive_glomerulosclerosis_mechanism: Regardless of the initiating insult, once a critical mass of nephrons is lost, the remaining nephrons undergo compensatory hyperfiltration; the resulting glomerular capillary hypertension and podocyte stress drive segmental sclerosis, which reduces nephron number further (a self-amplifying loop) and drives tubulointerstitial fibrosis. Proteinuria is both a marker and a direct mediator of this injury: epidemiologic data show a strong, consistent relationship between the level/duration of proteinuria and loss of kidney function, and reduction of proteinuria tracks with slower progression to ESKD across controlled trials.
definition_and_pathophysiology.mechanism_citation: Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2019 (KDIGO controversies conference, 13-trial + epidemiologic analysis), PMID 30635299; corroborated in a 2,141-patient biopsy-proven IgAN cohort where time-averaged proteinuria was independently associated with ESKD (adjusted HR 1.76), Nephrol Dial Transplant 2025, PMID 39557651

diagnostic_framework.renal_biopsy: Kidney biopsy remains the diagnostic gold standard for classifying the underlying glomerular lesion and grading disease activity (cellular/fibrocellular crescents, endocapillary proliferation) versus chronicity (global/segmental sclerosis, tubular atrophy, interstitial fibrosis) — this activity/chronicity split determines whether disease is still treatable or has reached irreversible scarring. No non-invasive biomarker is yet sufficiently sensitive/specific to replace biopsy, e.g. in IgA nephropathy.
diagnostic_framework.renal_biopsy_citation: Am J Med Sci 2021, PMID 33309134; framework endorsed in KDIGO 2021 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases, Kidney Int 2021, PMID 34556256
diagnostic_framework.serologic_and_immunologic_workup: Anti-PLA2R antibody (and anti-THSD7A where PLA2R-negative) allows serologic diagnosis and non-invasive monitoring of primary membranous nephropathy in a majority of cases without repeat biopsy, since antibody titer tracks immunologic activity (though proteinuria can lag antibody clearance by months). Broader work-up per KDIGO 2021 includes ANA, ANCA, anti-GBM antibody, complement C3/C4, and hepatitis serologies to identify secondary causes.
diagnostic_framework.serology_citation: Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2017, PMID 28550082; KDIGO 2021, PMID 34556256
diagnostic_framework.proteinuria_quantification: Proteinuria is quantified by urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) or timed 24-hour urine protein rather than dipstick alone. A KDIGO workgroup analysis of epidemiologic data and 13 controlled trials concluded proteinuria reduction is a 'reasonably likely surrogate end point' for a treatment's effect on progression to ESKD in IgA nephropathy, supporting its use as the primary marker for both diagnosis-time risk stratification and monitoring. A large biopsy-proven IgAN cohort further showed the ESKD-risk threshold is time-averaged proteinuria >0.5 g/day (not the older >1.0 g/day cut-off), with <0.3 and 0.3-0.5 g/day groups showing comparably favorable outcomes.
diagnostic_framework.proteinuria_citation: Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2019, PMID 30635299; Nephrol Dial Transplant 2025, PMID 39557651
diagnostic_framework.urine_microscopy: Dysmorphic red blood cells and red-cell casts on urine microscopy indicate a glomerular (nephritic) source of hematuria and help distinguish glomerulonephritis from lower urinary tract bleeding without requiring biopsy at the initial visit.
diagnostic_framework.urine_microscopy_citation: Am J Kidney Dis 2022 review, PMID 35777984

classic_symptoms.early_disease: Frequently asymptomatic for years; commonly first detected incidentally on routine urinalysis (microscopic hematuria and/or sub-nephrotic proteinuria) rather than through patient-reported symptoms.
classic_symptoms.hematuria: Microscopic or macroscopic hematuria with dysmorphic RBCs and/or RBC casts on microscopy, confirming a glomerular bleeding source (as opposed to isomorphic RBCs from the lower urinary tract).
classic_symptoms.hematuria_citation: Am J Kidney Dis 2022, PMID 35777984; StatPearls, Rapidly Progressive Glomerulonephritis, PMID 32491362
classic_symptoms.proteinuria: Ranges from sub-nephrotic to nephrotic-range (>3.5 g/day). In a large IgAN cohort, median baseline proteinuria at diagnosis was 1.26 g/day. In primary membranous nephropathy, ~80% of patients present with overt nephrotic syndrome and ~20% with non-nephrotic proteinuria.
classic_symptoms.proteinuria_citation: Nephrol Dial Transplant 2025, PMID 39557651; Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2017, PMID 28550082
classic_symptoms.nephrotic_features: When proteinuria is nephrotic-range: peripheral/periorbital edema, frothy/foamy urine (patient-reported proteinuria surrogate), hypoalbuminemia and hyperlipidemia.
classic_symptoms.nephrotic_features_citation: Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2017, PMID 28550082
classic_symptoms.hypertension: Hypertension commonly accompanies and worsens as nephron mass and GFR decline, reflecting activation of the renin-angiotensin system with progressive glomerular loss; blood-pressure control is a core management target in the KDIGO 2021 glomerular disease guideline.
classic_symptoms.not_verified_this_session: A specific numeric prevalence of hypertension at presentation of CGN (pooled across etiologies) was not found with a verifiable citation this session and is omitted rather than estimated.

differential_diagnosis.diabetic_nephropathy: Cross-reference: KB entry 'diabetic_nephropathy' exists. Distinguishing features favoring diabetic nephropathy over primary CGN: long-standing diabetes (typically >5-10 years in type 1; variable in type 2), concurrent diabetic retinopathy, and a more gradual rise in proteinuria typically WITHOUT significant hematuria or RBC casts — active urinary sediment should prompt reconsideration of a primary/immune glomerular process and biopsy.
differential_diagnosis.nephrotic_syndrome: Nephrotic-range proteinuria (>3.5 g/day) with edema/hypoalbuminemia/hyperlipidemia overlaps with (and in children is often used interchangeably to describe) several of the causal glomerular diseases underlying CGN, notably membranous nephropathy and FSGS. No dedicated 'nephrotic_syndrome' KB id was found in this database at the time of writing, so it is not cross-referenced by id for that reason.
differential_diagnosis.nephrotic_syndrome_citation: Pediatr Rev 2022, PMID 35102405 (Nephrotic Syndrome); Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2017, PMID 28550082
differential_diagnosis.iga_nephropathy: Cross-reference: KB entry 'iga_nephropathy' exists as the single most common specific primary cause underlying CGN worldwide; this CGN entry describes the shared downstream syndrome/progression pathway rather than duplicating IgAN-specific detail.
differential_diagnosis.chronic_kidney_disease: Cross-reference: KB entry 'chronic_kidney_disease' exists as the broader staging entity (KDIGO eGFR/albuminuria categories); CGN is one specific etiologic route into CKD, distinguished from other CKD causes by glomerular-pattern urinalysis (hematuria + proteinuria) and biopsy findings.
differential_diagnosis.acute_post_streptococcal_glomerulonephri: Typically an acute, usually self-limited nephritic illness in children following streptococcal infection, distinct from progressive CGN; most children recover renal function, though a minority have long-term sequelae, so distinguishing acute/reversible from chronic/progressive disease requires follow-up of renal function and proteinuria.
differential_diagnosis.rapidly_progressive_crescentic_gn: Anti-GBM disease, ANCA-associated (pauci-immune) vasculitis, and immune-complex crescentic GN present with renal function decline over days-to-weeks rather than the months-to-years course of typical CGN — see EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE; this distinction is time-critical, not just descriptive.

ethnicity_and_genetics.factor: IgA nephropathy shows marked heterogeneity in epidemiology, clinical manifestations and progression across different populations/ethnicities.

African ancestry with high-risk APOL1 genotype (two risk alleles): robustly and reproducibly associated with FSGS, HIV-associated nephropathy, and hypertension-attributed kidney failure (association with diabetic kidney disease is inconsistent). Penetrance is incomplete — only approximately 15-20% of high-risk genotype carriers ultimately develop overt nephropathy, so the genotype is a risk modifier, not a deterministic cause.
Regional predominance of FSGS over IgA nephropathy and membranous nephropathy in African biopsy cohorts (26.1% vs 2.6% vs 8.4%), with FSGS particularly prevalent in West Africa.

underlying_disease: Secondary glomerular disease from systemic autoimmune disease (e.g. lupus nephritis) or malignancy/drug exposure accounts for roughly 20% of membranous nephropathy cases (the remainder being primary/autoimmune podocyte-antigen driven).
Uncontrolled hypertension and diabetes are recognized accelerants of glomerulosclerosis progression once glomerular injury has begun, per KDIGO 2021 management guidance.
risk_factors.underlying_disease_citation: Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2017, PMID 28550082; KDIGO 2021, PMID 34556256
risk_factors.proteinuria_itself: Persistent/higher time-averaged proteinuria is itself an independent, modifiable risk factor for progression to ESKD, not merely a marker of it.
risk_factors.proteinuria_itself_citation: Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2019, PMID 30635299; Nephrol Dial Transplant 2025, PMID 39557651
risk_factors.not_verified_this_session: A specific numeric obesity-attributable risk for secondary FSGS, and a specific hepatitis B/C-attributable risk figure for membranous nephropathy/MPGN, were not confirmed with a verifiable citation this session and are omitted rather than estimated.

epidemiology.global_pattern: IgA nephropathy is the most common primary glomerulonephritis worldwide, making it a leading cause of CKD globally.
epidemiology.regional_variation_africa: Pooled analysis of 17 studies (6,494 individuals, 8 African countries) found FSGS was the dominant primary glomerular disease (26.1% of biopsies) versus membranous nephropathy (8.4%) and IgA nephropathy (2.6%), with distribution varying further by sub-region and by pediatric versus adult age group.
epidemiology.long_term_cohort_outcomes: In a Chinese cohort of 2,141 biopsy-confirmed IgA nephropathy patients followed a mean of 5.8 years, 24% (509 patients) progressed to ESKD, at an annual ESKD event rate of 41.1 per 1,000 person-years, with 40% 15-year kidney survival.
epidemiology.membranous_nephropathy: Primary membranous nephropathy is the most common cause of idiopathic nephrotic syndrome in nondiabetic White adults.
epidemiology.membranous_nephropathy_citation: Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2017, PMID 28550082

natural_history.iga_nephropathy: Up to 40% of IgA nephropathy patients progress to end-stage kidney disease approximately 20 years after diagnosis, and the disease is associated with significant mortality. In a 2,141-patient biopsy-confirmed cohort, 24% reached ESKD over a mean 5.8-year follow-up (annual incidence 41.1/1,000 person-years; 40% 15-year kidney survival).
natural_history.iga_nephropathy_citation: Am J Med Sci 2021, PMID 33309134; Nephrol Dial Transplant 2025, PMID 39557651
natural_history.prognostic_stratification_by_proteinuria: Time-averaged proteinuria is the dominant modifiable prognostic driver identified in the large IgAN cohort: risk of ESKD rose sharply once time-averaged proteinuria exceeded 0.5 g/day (adjusted HR 1.76 for time-averaged proteinuria), whereas patients maintaining <0.3 g/day or 0.3-0.5 g/day had comparably favorable, low-risk outcomes. This reframes the treatment target as <0.5 g/day rather than the older <1.0 g/day convention.
natural_history.surrogate_endpoint_validation: A KDIGO workgroup review of epidemiologic data and 13 controlled trials concluded that reducing proteinuria is a 'reasonably likely surrogate end point' for a treatment's effect on progression to ESKD in IgA nephropathy, supporting proteinuria trajectory (not just a single value) as the key prognostic and monitoring parameter.
natural_history.surrogate_endpoint_citation: Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2019, PMID 30635299
natural_history.membranous_nephropathy_untreated_course: Without treatment, primary membranous nephropathy follows roughly a 'rule of thirds': about one-third undergo spontaneous remission (more likely with absent/low antibody titers), about one-third progress to ESKD within a decade, and the remainder develop stable chronic kidney disease.
natural_history.membranous_untreated_citation: Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2017, PMID 28550082
natural_history.fsgs_recurrence_biology: FSGS's aggressive, often circulating-factor-driven biology is further evidenced by its well-documented recurrence even after kidney transplantation, prompting dedicated consensus statements on post-transplant FSGS recurrence.
natural_history.not_verified_this_session: A single unified KDIGO eGFR/albuminuria 'heat-map' risk percentage table specific to chronic glomerulonephritis (as opposed to general CKD) was not located with a verifiable primary citation this session and is omitted rather than estimated; the proteinuria-threshold data above (PMID 39557651) is used instead as the verified prognostic anchor.

clinical_takeaway.summary: Chronic glomerulonephritis is frequently silent until picked up on a routine urine test, so the single highest-yield diagnostic action is not waiting for symptoms but checking urinalysis (for dysmorphic hematuria and quantified proteinuria via UPCR) whenever any glomerular-pattern clue appears, then referring for biopsy and immunologic work-up per KDIGO 2021 criteria to identify the specific treatable cause (IgA nephropathy, FSGS, membranous nephropathy, secondary causes) before irreversible sclerosis sets in. Because time-averaged proteinuria is both the best-validated prognostic marker and a modifiable treatment target (goal <0.5 g/day), it should be tracked longitudinally, not just measured once at diagnosis.
clinical_takeaway.citation: KDIGO 2021, PMID 34556256; Nephrol Dial Transplant 2025, PMID 39557651; Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2019, PMID 30635299

EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE.rule: Rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis (RPGN) is a nephrological emergency and must be distinguished from ordinary slowly-progressive chronic glomerulonephritis at first contact. RPGN is defined by loss of renal function over days to weeks (not months to years), accompanied by an active nephritic urinary sediment (micro/macroscopic hematuria with dysmorphic RBCs and RBC casts) plus proteinuria, and histologically by cellular/fibrocellular crescent formation on biopsy — even a single glomerular crescent can signal serious underlying disease. Early diagnosis and urgent treatment are crucial because crescent-related nephron loss is time-sensitive and becomes irreversible with delay.
red_flags_requiring_urgent_same_admissio: Renal function (serum creatinine) rising rapidly over days to weeks rather than a chronic, slow trajectory
Oliguria or anuria accompanying rising creatinine
Active nephritic urinary sediment: dysmorphic RBCs and/or RBC casts on microscopy, with or without gross hematuria

Systemic features suggesting an underlying vasculitis/anti-GBM process: hemoptysis or pulmonary hemorrhage (possible anti-GBM/Goodpasture overlap), fever, purpura, sinusitis, or mononeuritis multiplex occurring together with acute renal decline
causal_classification: Type I: anti-glomerular basement membrane (anti-GBM) antibody disease
Type III: pauci-immune, ANCA-associated crescentic glomerulonephritis
Type IV: combined ANCA-positive and anti-GBM-positive disease
EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE.evidence: ANCA-associated vasculitis renal involvement is seen in 90-100% of microscopic polyangiitis and 50-80% of granulomatosis with polyangiitis; early diagnosis and prompt initiation of immunosuppressive therapy (induction with glucocorticoids plus rituximab or cyclophosphamide, followed by 2-4 years of maintenance) significantly improves both kidney and overall survival, underscoring why delay in referral/biopsy is dangerous.
EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE.citation: StatPearls, Rapidly Progressive Glomerulonephritis, PMID 32491362; Medicina (Kaunas) 2026, Advances in the Diagnosis, Treatment and Prognosis of ANCA-Associated Glomerulonephritis, PMID 42512795
