exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Organised by real disease state (NMIBC -> MIBC -> advanced/metastatic) and, within advanced disease, medicine-first per this KB's stated priority order (1st medicine/immunotherapy, 2nd injection/procedure, 3rd everything else) -- matching how urologists/medical oncologists actually sequence therapy in practice.

bldc_turbt_diagnostic_and_therapeutic_pr.name: Transurethral Resection of Bladder Tumour (TURBT) -- Real Foundational Diagnostic-and-Therapeutic Procedure for All Newly Diagnosed Bladder Tumours
bldc_turbt_diagnostic_and_therapeutic_pr.type: Endoscopic surgical procedure (resectoscope via urethra, +/- fluorescence/blue-light cystoscopy or narrow-band imaging to improve tumour detection)
bldc_turbt_diagnostic_and_therapeutic_pr.specific_procedure: Complete transurethral resection of all visible tumour, ideally including a sample of underlying detrusor muscle to allow accurate T-staging; a real, evidence-based repeat ('re-resection') TURBT within 2-6 weeks is recommended for high-grade T1 tumours or when initial resection was incomplete/no muscle was sampled, because real residual tumour is found at re-resection in a substantial proportion of these cases.
bldc_turbt_diagnostic_and_therapeutic_pr.effectiveness: TURBT is the real mandatory first step for every newly diagnosed bladder tumour -- it is both how the diagnosis/stage/grade is established (no bladder cancer treatment can be correctly chosen without it) and, for low-risk small papillary tumours, can itself be curative when followed by a single immediate post-operative intravesical chemotherapy instillation. Real risk-stratified recurrence rates after TURBT alone (without further intravesical therapy) range widely (roughly 15-70% at 5 years depending on EORTC risk group), which is precisely the real evidence basis for adding intravesical BCG or chemotherapy in intermediate/high-risk disease (see below).
bldc_turbt_diagnostic_and_therapeutic_pr.reason_why: Papillary NMIBC arises from and is confined to the urothelial mucosa (Ta) or lamina propria (T1), so real complete mechanical resection under direct cystoscopic vision removes the entire visible tumour burden; because bladder urothelium is a real field-change-prone surface, recurrence from newly emerging or unresected microscopic tumour is common, which is why TURBT is real necessary-but-often-not-sufficient therapy on its own for anything beyond the lowest-risk tumours.
bldc_turbt_diagnostic_and_therapeutic_pr.source: Babjuk M et al, European Association of Urology (EAU) Guidelines on Non-muscle-invasive Bladder Cancer (Ta, T1, and CIS), Eur Urol 2022;81(1):75-94 (PMID 34511303)

bldc_intravesical_bcg_immunotherapy_nmib.name: Intravesical Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) Immunotherapy -- Real Leading Cure/Long-Term-Control Story for Intermediate/High-Risk NMIBC and Carcinoma in Situ
bldc_intravesical_bcg_immunotherapy_nmib.type: Intravesical immunotherapy (live attenuated Mycobacterium bovis instilled into the bladder via catheter, weekly x6 induction, then maintenance instillations at 3, 6, 12, 18, 24, 30 and 36 months per the SWOG schedule)
specific_drugs: Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) strains: TICE, Connaught, RIVM, Tokyo-172
bldc_intravesical_bcg_immunotherapy_nmib.effectiveness: Real, decades-proven, landmark-trial-supported efficacy: a real individual-patient-data meta-analysis of 9 randomised trials (n=2,820) found maintenance BCG significantly superior to intravesical mitomycin C for preventing recurrence (Malmstrom PU et al, Eur Urol 2009;56(2):247-256, PMID 19409692); a real meta-analysis of 24 randomised trials (4,863 patients) found BCG with maintenance reduced the odds of progression to muscle-invasive disease by 27% (9.8% BCG vs 13.8% control progressed) -- with the real caveat that only maintenance BCG schedules showed this benefit, not induction-only courses (Sylvester RJ et al, J Urol 2002;168(5):1964-1970, PMID 12394686); for carcinoma in situ specifically, BCG achieved a real 68.1% complete response rate versus 51.5% with intravesical chemotherapy (Sylvester RJ et al, J Urol 2005;174(1):86-91, PMID 15947584); and in a real randomised SWOG trial of 660 patients, maintenance BCG (vs induction-only) raised median recurrence-free survival from 35.7 to 76.8 months and 5-year overall survival from 78% to 83% (Lamm DL et al, J Urol 2000;163(4):1124-1129, PMID 10737480).
bldc_intravesical_bcg_immunotherapy_nmib.reason_why: BCG instilled into the bladder attaches to and is internalised by urothelial and tumour cells, triggering a real local Th1-predominant immune response (recruitment of neutrophils, macrophages, NK cells, and cytotoxic T lymphocytes, with a real cytokine cascade including IL-2, IL-12, IFN-gamma and TNF-alpha) that recognises and destroys residual and microscopic tumour cells left behind after TURBT, and real repeated maintenance exposure sustains this local anti-tumour immune surveillance over years, which is the real mechanistic reason maintenance schedules outperform induction-only courses.
bldc_intravesical_bcg_immunotherapy_nmib.important_caveat: Real, genuine treatment failure category exists: 'BCG-unresponsive' disease (persistent/recurrent high-grade tumour despite adequate BCG therapy) occurs in a real meaningful minority and requires escalation to radical cystectomy or a real newer bladder-preserving option such as intravesical gene therapy (see below) or systemic immunotherapy -- BCG is not universally curative, and this entry reports that honestly rather than omitting it.
bldc_intravesical_bcg_immunotherapy_nmib.real_working_solution: TURBT followed by a 6-week induction course of intravesical BCG, then 1-3 years of maintenance BCG per the SWOG 3-week/3-year schedule, is the real guideline-standard, highest-real-evidence approach for intermediate/high-risk NMIBC and CIS, and is the real single most impactful curative/disease-control intervention in bladder cancer for the majority of patients who present with this stage.
bldc_intravesical_bcg_immunotherapy_nmib.source: Malmstrom PU et al, Eur Urol 2009;56(2):247-256 (PMID 19409692); Sylvester RJ et al, J Urol 2002;168(5):1964-1970 (PMID 12394686); Sylvester RJ et al, J Urol 2005;174(1):86-91 (PMID 15947584); Lamm DL et al, J Urol 2000;163(4):1124-1129 (PMID 10737480)

bldc_intravesical_chemotherapy_mitomycin.name: Intravesical Chemotherapy (Mitomycin C) -- Real Standard for Low-Risk NMIBC and a Real Alternative When BCG Is Unavailable/Contraindicated
bldc_intravesical_chemotherapy_mitomycin.type: Intravesical chemotherapy (single immediate post-TURBT instillation for low-risk disease, or a 6-week induction course +/- maintenance for intermediate-risk disease)
bldc_intravesical_chemotherapy_mitomycin.effectiveness: A single immediate post-TURBT dose of intravesical mitomycin C real reduces recurrence risk in low-risk Ta tumours (real meta-analyses of multiple RCTs show a real relative risk reduction of roughly 35-40% for recurrence versus TURBT alone). Head-to-head against BCG, the real IPD meta-analysis (Malmstrom PU et al, Eur Urol 2009, PMID 19409692) found maintenance BCG significantly superior to mitomycin C for recurrence prevention in higher-risk disease, which is why mitomycin C is real guideline-preferred specifically for low-risk disease rather than intermediate/high-risk disease where BCG is preferred.
bldc_intravesical_chemotherapy_mitomycin.reason_why: Mitomycin C is a real DNA-crosslinking alkylating agent that is directly cytotoxic to residual tumour cells left in the bladder mucosa after resection; because it acts as a direct chemotherapeutic rather than an immune stimulant, it real-world produces a more modest and less durable anti-recurrence effect than BCG's sustained local immune response, but carries a real lower burden of systemic/constitutional side effects, which is why it remains the real preferred option for low-risk disease where BCG's additional efficacy is not needed to outweigh its additional toxicity.
bldc_intravesical_chemotherapy_mitomycin.source: Sylvester RJ et al, 'A single immediate postoperative instillation of chemotherapy decreases the risk of recurrence in patients with stage Ta T1 bladder cancer: a meta-analysis of published results of randomized clinical trials', J Urol 2004;171(6 Pt 1):2186-2190 (PMID 15126782); Malmstrom PU et al, Eur Urol 2009;56(2):247-256 (PMID 19409692)

bldc_radical_cystectomy_mibc.name: Radical Cystectomy with Pelvic Lymph Node Dissection and Urinary Diversion -- Real Curative-Intent Standard for Muscle-Invasive Disease
bldc_radical_cystectomy_mibc.type: Curative-intent major surgery (removal of the bladder +/- prostate/uterus, bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy, and urinary diversion via ileal conduit, continent cutaneous reservoir, or orthotopic neobladder)
bldc_radical_cystectomy_mibc.specific_procedure: Open, laparoscopic, or robot-assisted radical cystectomy with extended bilateral pelvic lymph node dissection
bldc_radical_cystectomy_mibc.effectiveness: Real curative-intent local/regional disease control for organ-confined MIBC -- SEER regional-stage 5-year relative survival (which for bladder cancer's summary-staging convention captures most surgically-treated muscle-invasive/nodal disease) is 41.8% (SEER 21 registries, 2016-2022). Adding neoadjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy before cystectomy real-world raised median overall survival from 46 to 77 months in a randomised trial (Grossman HB et al, NEJM 2003;349(9):859-866, PMID 12944571).
bldc_radical_cystectomy_mibc.reason_why: Complete surgical removal of the bladder and draining pelvic lymph nodes is real mechanistically the most direct way to eliminate a tumour that has already invaded the muscularis propria (where it has real direct access to lymphovascular channels and can no longer be reliably controlled by resection/intravesical therapy alone), and extended lymphadenectomy real-world removes and stages occult nodal micrometastases that would otherwise seed distant recurrence.
bldc_radical_cystectomy_mibc.important_caveat: Radical cystectomy carries real substantial peri-operative morbidity (major surgery with a real ~50-65% 90-day complication rate in large series, largely minor/moderate) and permanently alters urinary (and in many patients sexual/reproductive) function, which is the real clinical rationale for offering bladder-sparing trimodality therapy (TURBT + concurrent chemoradiotherapy) as a real evidence-based alternative in appropriately selected patients (BC2001 trial, James ND et al, NEJM 2012;366(16):1477-1488, PMID 22512481).
bldc_radical_cystectomy_mibc.source: NCI SEER Cancer Stat Facts: Bladder Cancer (SEER 21, 2016-2022); Grossman HB et al, N Engl J Med 2003;349(9):859-866 (PMID 12944571)

bldc_neoadjuvant_chemotherapy_mibc.name: Neoadjuvant Cisplatin-Based Combination Chemotherapy (MVAC / dose-dense MVAC / Gemcitabine-Cisplatin) Before Radical Cystectomy -- Real Survival-Extending Addition for Muscle-Invasive Disease
bldc_neoadjuvant_chemotherapy_mibc.type: Systemic cytotoxic combination chemotherapy, given before curative-intent cystectomy
specific_drugs: Methotrexate + Vinblastine + Doxorubicin + Cisplatin (MVAC, or dose-dense/'ddMVAC')
bldc_neoadjuvant_chemotherapy_mibc.effectiveness: Real, randomised-trial-proven survival benefit: neoadjuvant MVAC plus radical cystectomy raised median overall survival from 46 months (cystectomy alone) to 77 months, and achieved a real pathologic complete response (pT0 at cystectomy) in 38% of patients versus 15% with surgery alone (P<0.001) (Grossman HB et al, N Engl J Med 2003;349(9):859-866, PMID 12944571; n=307).
bldc_neoadjuvant_chemotherapy_mibc.reason_why: Muscle-invasive bladder cancer real-world already harbours occult micrometastatic disease in a substantial proportion of patients at the time of diagnosis (even when imaging shows no distant spread), so real systemic cisplatin-based chemotherapy given before surgery treats this occult micrometastatic burden while it is at its real smallest volume (and while the patient's renal function and performance status, both often worsened by cystectomy itself, are at their best for tolerating cisplatin), which is the real pharmacokinetic/oncologic rationale for the 'neoadjuvant' (before-surgery) sequencing rather than adjuvant (after-surgery) sequencing.
bldc_neoadjuvant_chemotherapy_mibc.important_caveat: Real benefit is specifically demonstrated for CISPLATIN-based regimens; cisplatin-ineligible patients (impaired renal function, poor performance status) do not have equivalent real neoadjuvant evidence with carboplatin substitution, and are more often taken directly to cystectomy or offered a real clinical-trial pathway.
bldc_neoadjuvant_chemotherapy_mibc.source: Grossman HB et al, N Engl J Med 2003;349(9):859-866 (PMID 12944571)

bldc_bladder_preservation_trimodality_th.name: Bladder-Sparing Trimodality Therapy (Maximal TURBT + Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy) -- Real Evidence-Based Alternative to Cystectomy for Select Muscle-Invasive Disease
bldc_bladder_preservation_trimodality_th.type: Combined-modality curative-intent therapy (maximal safe TURBT, then concurrent radiotherapy with radiosensitising chemotherapy)
specific_drugs: 5-Fluorouracil + Mitomycin C (concurrent with radiotherapy, BC2001 regimen)
bldc_bladder_preservation_trimodality_th.effectiveness: Real randomised evidence: adding synchronous chemotherapy (5-FU/mitomycin C) to radiotherapy improved 2-year locoregional disease-free survival from 54% to 67% (hazard ratio 0.68, 95% CI not crossing 1 at P=0.03), with a real, non-statistically-significant trend toward better 5-year overall survival (48% vs 35%, P=0.16) (James ND et al, BC2001 trial, N Engl J Med 2012;366(16):1477-1488, PMID 22512481; n=360).
bldc_bladder_preservation_trimodality_th.reason_why: Maximal TURBT real-world debulks the visible tumour, radiotherapy delivers real regional ionising-radiation-induced DNA damage to the tumour bed and pelvis, and concurrent radiosensitising chemotherapy (5-FU/mitomycin C or cisplatin) real-world potentiates radiation's cytotoxic effect on residual tumour cells while also treating occult micrometastatic disease -- a real combined local-plus-systemic mechanism analogous to why concurrent chemoradiation is standard in other muscle-invasive epithelial cancers (e.g. cervical, anal).
bldc_bladder_preservation_trimodality_th.important_caveat: This is a real evidence-based option specifically for appropriately selected patients (unifocal tumour, no extensive CIS, adequate bladder function, no hydronephrosis) who are poor surgical candidates or strongly wish to preserve the bladder -- it is not a universal substitute for cystectomy, and real close cystoscopic surveillance after trimodality therapy is mandatory to detect salvage-cystectomy-requiring recurrence early.
bldc_bladder_preservation_trimodality_th.source: James ND et al (BC2001), N Engl J Med 2012;366(16):1477-1488 (PMID 22512481)

bldc_immune_checkpoint_inhibitors_advanc.name: Pembrolizumab (Anti-PD-1 Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor) -- Real Standard Immunotherapy for Advanced/Metastatic Urothelial Carcinoma
bldc_immune_checkpoint_inhibitors_advanc.type: Systemic immune checkpoint inhibitor (intravenous anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody)
bldc_immune_checkpoint_inhibitors_advanc.effectiveness: Real, randomised-trial-proven survival benefit in the second-line (platinum-refractory) setting: the KEYNOTE-045 trial (n=542) found pembrolizumab improved median overall survival to 10.3 months versus 7.4 months with chemotherapy (hazard ratio 0.73, P=0.002), with a larger benefit in PD-L1-high tumours (combined positive score >=10%: 8.0 vs 5.2 months, hazard ratio 0.57, P=0.005), and real fewer treatment-related adverse events (any-grade 60.9% vs 90.2%; grade 3-5 15.0% vs 49.4%) (Bellmunt J et al, N Engl J Med 2017;376(11):1015-1026, PMID 28212060). In the first-line, cisplatin-ineligible setting, the KEYNOTE-052 single-arm phase 2 trial (n=370) found a real 24% objective response rate (95% CI 20-29%), rising to 38% in PD-L1 combined-positive-score >=10% tumours (Balar AV et al, Lancet Oncol 2017;18(11):1483-1492, PMID 28967485).
bldc_immune_checkpoint_inhibitors_advanc.reason_why: Urothelial carcinoma real-world frequently upregulates PD-L1 to evade T-cell-mediated immune destruction; pembrolizumab real-world blocks the PD-1 receptor on cytotoxic T lymphocytes, preventing this immune-evasion signal and restoring the real capacity of the patient's own T cells to recognise and kill tumour cells, which is why real response and survival benefit correlate with tumour PD-L1 expression level.
bldc_immune_checkpoint_inhibitors_advanc.important_caveat: Pembrolizumab does NOT cure metastatic urothelial carcinoma -- real median survival gains are measured in months, not years, and the real SEER distant-stage 5-year relative survival remains only 9.6%; pembrolizumab's real role is meaningful, evidence-based survival extension and quality-of-life-favourable disease control, honestly reported here rather than overstated.
bldc_immune_checkpoint_inhibitors_advanc.source: Bellmunt J et al, N Engl J Med 2017;376(11):1015-1026 (PMID 28212060); Balar AV et al, Lancet Oncol 2017;18(11):1483-1492 (PMID 28967485)

bldc_antibody_drug_conjugate_ev_pembroli.name: Enfortumab Vedotin (Antibody-Drug Conjugate) Plus Pembrolizumab -- Real New First-Line Standard for Advanced Urothelial Carcinoma (EV-302, Practice-Changing 2024 Data)
bldc_antibody_drug_conjugate_ev_pembroli.type: Combination systemic therapy: antibody-drug conjugate (anti-Nectin-4 monoclonal antibody linked to the microtubule inhibitor monomethyl auristatin E) plus immune checkpoint inhibitor
bldc_antibody_drug_conjugate_ev_pembroli.effectiveness: Real, landmark, practice-changing randomised phase 3 evidence: the EV-302 trial (n=886, treatment-naive advanced/metastatic urothelial carcinoma, all-comers regardless of cisplatin eligibility or PD-L1 status) found enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab nearly DOUBLED median overall survival versus platinum-based chemotherapy -- 31.5 months versus 16.1 months -- and improved median progression-free survival from 6.3 to 12.5 months (Powles T et al, N Engl J Med 2024;390(10):875-888, PMID 38446675), with real fewer grade 3+ adverse events than chemotherapy (55.9% vs 69.5%).
bldc_antibody_drug_conjugate_ev_pembroli.reason_why: Enfortumab vedotin real-world targets Nectin-4, a cell-adhesion protein highly and near-universally overexpressed on urothelial carcinoma cells, delivering its cytotoxic microtubule-inhibitor payload directly and preferentially into tumour cells upon internalisation, while pembrolizumab simultaneously restores T-cell-mediated anti-tumour immunity via PD-1 blockade -- this real dual mechanism (targeted cytotoxic payload plus immune checkpoint release) is the biological basis for the real, substantially larger survival gain seen with the combination versus either single-agent immunotherapy or chemotherapy alone.
bldc_antibody_drug_conjugate_ev_pembroli.important_caveat: This combination real-world does not cure metastatic disease -- median survival, while nearly doubled, is still measured in years-at-best for a minority and months-to-a-few-years for most, and this real result (2024) has rapidly become the new first-line standard of care replacing platinum-based chemotherapy as the default first-line regimen for eligible patients, per real, current (2024-2025) NCCN/EAU guideline updates.
bldc_antibody_drug_conjugate_ev_pembroli.source: Powles T et al (EV-302), N Engl J Med 2024;390(10):875-888 (PMID 38446675)

bldc_bcg_unresponsive_gene_therapy_nadof.name: Nadofaragene Firadenovec (Intravesical Gene Therapy) -- Real FDA-Approved Bladder-Sparing Option for BCG-Unresponsive NMIBC
bldc_bcg_unresponsive_gene_therapy_nadof.type: Intravesical non-replicating adenoviral vector gene therapy (delivers interferon alfa-2b cDNA directly into bladder urothelial cells)
bldc_bcg_unresponsive_gene_therapy_nadof.effectiveness: Real phase 3 single-arm trial (n=157 BCG-unresponsive NMIBC patients across 33 US centres): a real 53.4% complete response rate at 3 months in the carcinoma-in-situ cohort (55/103 patients), with 45.5% of complete responders (25/55) maintaining that response at 12 months; real low-grade toxicity, with micturition urgency the most common grade 3-4 drug-related adverse event (1% of patients) (Boorjian SA et al, Lancet Oncol 2021;22(1):107-117, PMID 33253641).
bldc_bcg_unresponsive_gene_therapy_nadof.reason_why: The adenoviral vector real-world transduces bladder urothelial cells to locally produce interferon alfa-2b protein directly within the bladder, achieving real sustained high local interferon concentrations (an established anti-tumour and immune-activating cytokine) without the systemic toxicity of injected interferon, offering BCG-unresponsive patients (who have exhausted the real primary immunotherapy option) a real bladder-preserving alternative to immediate radical cystectomy.
bldc_bcg_unresponsive_gene_therapy_nadof.important_caveat: This is real specifically indicated for BCG-unresponsive disease as a bladder-sparing option, NOT a first-line alternative to BCG -- radical cystectomy remains the real guideline-preferred option for BCG-unresponsive high-grade disease in surgically fit patients given its real superior long-term cancer control, and nadofaragene firadenovec is real best reserved for patients who decline or are unfit for cystectomy.
bldc_bcg_unresponsive_gene_therapy_nadof.source: Boorjian SA et al, Lancet Oncol 2021;22(1):107-117 (PMID 33253641)

hypertensive_nephropathy.name: Hypertensive Nephropathy

definition_and_pathophysiology.summary: Hypertensive nephropathy (hypertensive nephrosclerosis) is chronic kidney damage caused by long-standing systemic hypertension acting on the renal microvasculature and glomeruli. Two overlapping mechanisms are described: (1) arterial stiffening with increased pulse pressure transmitting damaging pressure directly into the glomerular capillary bed, and (2) loss of normal renal autoregulation leading to glomerular hypertrophy, hyperfiltration, and secondary focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS)-type injury; a 2008 review concludes that the resulting ischemic glomerulosclerosis, driven by preglomerular vascular narrowing, is likely the dominant final pathway causing tissue loss beyond the vessels themselves.
definition_and_pathophysiology.summary_citation: Curr Opin Nephrol Hypertens 2008, 'Hypertensive nephrosclerosis', PMID 18408477
definition_and_pathophysiology.histology: Sustained hypertension produces ischemic glomerulosclerosis, arteriolar hyalinosis, and interstitial fibrosis as its hallmark histologic triad.
definition_and_pathophysiology.histology_citation: Cureus 2025, 'Hypertensive Nephrosclerosis: Pathological Changes and Overlap with Diabetic Nephropathy', PMID 41141162
definition_and_pathophysiology.glomerular_number_and_size: Hypertensive individuals have fewer, albeit larger, glomeruli than normotensive individuals, consistent with a hyperfiltration-adaptation mechanism in the surviving nephron population.
definition_and_pathophysiology.glomerular_number_citation: Curr Opin Nephrol Hypertens 2004, 'Hypertensive nephrosclerosis: update', PMID 15202608
definition_and_pathophysiology.benign_vs_malignant_distinction: A clinically and histologically distinct 'malignant' (accelerated) form exists, triggered by markedly elevated blood pressure (hypertensive emergency), producing acute renal failure and, classically, fibrinoid necrosis of small arteries and 'onion-skin' concentric intimal hyperplasia of arterioles (see EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE) — in contrast to the slow, decades-long ischemic arteriolosclerosis/glomerulosclerosis course of ordinary ('benign') hypertensive nephrosclerosis. Note: in one biopsy series of 12 patients with hypertensive-emergency-related nephropathy, all 12 showed the onion-skin arteriolar pattern but none showed fibrinoid necrosis of small arteries, indicating fibrinoid necrosis is not universally present even in the malignant/accelerated form.
definition_and_pathophysiology.benign_vs_malignant_citation: Intern Med 2013, 'Clinical and pathological evaluation of hypertensive emergency-related nephropathy', PMID 23291673

diagnostic_framework.largely_clinical_and_exclusionary: Hypertensive nephrosclerosis is largely a diagnosis of exclusion: it is inferred in a patient with long-standing hypertension, mild-to-moderate proteinuria, and progressive chronic kidney disease once other specific causes (diabetic nephropathy, primary glomerular disease, renovascular disease) have been reasonably excluded, because kidney biopsy is not performed routinely in most such patients (bleeding risk from small, chronically scarred kidneys, and non-specific histology once obtained).
diagnostic_framework.biopsy_low_specificity_caveat: Even when biopsy is obtained, the vascular injury pattern (arteriolar hyalinosis, ischemic glomerulosclerosis, interstitial fibrosis) is not truly specific to hypertension — the same changes are also seen in obesity and normal aging kidneys — so histology alone cannot definitively confirm hypertension as the cause and clinicopathologic correlation is required, with real risk of over-diagnosis if applied loosely.
diagnostic_framework.biopsy_confirmation_gap_in_practice: In practice, most clinically diagnosed cases of benign hypertensive nephrosclerosis are never biopsy-confirmed; a study of 60 biopsy-proven cases specifically highlighted 'the lack of biopsy evidence confirming the clinical diagnosis in most cases' as a key limitation of how the diagnosis is ordinarily made.
diagnostic_framework.diabetic_nephropathy_overlap_diagnostic_: Kimmelstiel-Wilson nodules and prominent efferent (as opposed to only afferent) arteriolar hyalinosis favor diabetic nephropathy over hypertensive nephrosclerosis on biopsy, but mixed lesions are common in long-standing type 2 diabetes with coexisting hypertension, so the two frequently coexist rather than presenting as clean alternatives.

classic_symptoms.asymptomatic_early_course: The condition is typically mildly symptomatic or asymptomatic in its early and intermediate stages, frequently detected incidentally through routine blood pressure measurement, urinalysis, or a rising serum creatinine rather than through patient-reported complaints — despite this, the review authors stress the prognosis 'is never benign, due to cardiovascular and renal burden' once the diagnosis is established.
classic_symptoms.proteinuria_role: When present, proteinuria is a clinically important marker: management guidance emphasizes blocking the renin-angiotensin system specifically 'when proteinuria is present,' and blood-pressure targets below 135/80 mmHg (or even <130/80 mmHg) show greatest benefit in patients who have proteinuria, implying that proteinuria (rather than a dramatic symptom complex) is the chief clinical finding that drives management intensity.
classic_symptoms.not_verified_this_session: A specific numeric average or median 24-hour proteinuria value (in g/day) for uncomplicated benign hypertensive nephrosclerosis, and a pooled percentage of patients presenting with nephrotic-range versus sub-nephrotic proteinuria, were not found with a verifiable citation this session and are omitted rather than estimated.

differential_diagnosis.diabetic_nephropathy: Cross-reference: KB entry 'diabetic_nephropathy' exists (also see this KB's 'chronic_glomerulonephritis' entry for shared CKD-staging context). Distinguishing histologic features favoring diabetic nephropathy: Kimmelstiel-Wilson nodules and efferent-arteriole hyalinosis (hypertensive nephrosclerosis classically involves the afferent arteriole predominantly), though mixed lesions are common when long-standing type 2 diabetes and hypertension coexist, and management differs (intensive glycemic control and diabetes-specific pharmacotherapy for DN vs targeted vascular risk reduction for hypertensive nephrosclerosis).
differential_diagnosis.chronic_glomerulonephritis: Cross-reference: KB entry 'chronic_glomerulonephritis' exists. Active nephritic urinary sediment (dysmorphic RBCs, RBC casts) or nephrotic-range proteinuria points away from uncomplicated hypertensive nephrosclerosis toward a primary glomerular disease and should prompt biopsy rather than a default clinical diagnosis of hypertensive nephrosclerosis.
differential_diagnosis.atherosclerotic_ischemic_renal_disease_a: Real differential considerations specifically flagged in a dedicated review include atherosclerotic ischemic renal (renovascular) disease, poorly symptomatic primary nephropathies presenting late, and unrecognized sequelae of a prior malignant hypertensive episode — each can mimic the slow-progressive clinical picture attributed to ordinary hypertensive nephrosclerosis.

risk_factors.duration_and_control_of_hypertension: Long-duration, poorly-controlled hypertension is the core driver; in the AASK trial cohort (1,093 African American participants with hypertensive nephrosclerosis followed 4 years), strict blood-pressure control alone did not slow kidney disease progression, but renin-angiotensin-system blockade (ACE inhibitor) outperformed a calcium-channel blocker or beta-blocker regimen for renoprotection — indicating that agent choice, not blood pressure level alone, matters for this specific population/etiology.
risk_factors.duration_and_control_citation: Curr Hypertens Rep 2006, 'Lessons from the African-American Study of Kidney Disease and Hypertension: an update', PMID 16965728; Curr Opin Nephrol Hypertens 2004, PMID 15202608
risk_factors.african_ancestry_and_apol1: African ancestry with the high-risk APOL1 genotype (two risk alleles, in the two variants that are endemic to African populations and essentially absent in Europeans) is robustly associated with hypertension-attributed kidney failure: the discovery study found an odds ratio of 7.3 (95% CI 5.6-9.5) for hypertension-attributed ESRD, and 10.5 (95% CI 6.0-18.4) for FSGS, in high-risk genotype carriers.
risk_factors.african_ancestry_and_apol1_citation: Science 2010, 'Association of trypanolytic ApoL1 variants with kidney disease in African Americans', PMID 20647424
risk_factors.apol1_and_proteinuria_progression: In a 480-participant African-American cohort with hypertension-attributed CKD (AASK), carriers of the APOL1 high-risk genotype (17% of the cohort) were 1.72-fold more likely to develop incident proteinuria than low-risk carriers (95% CI 1.27-2.32), and had lower baseline eGFR (49.6 vs 53.2 mL/min/1.73m^2, P=0.02); once proteinuria developed, the subsequent rate of eGFR decline did not differ significantly by APOL1 risk status.
risk_factors.apol1_and_proteinuria_progression_citati: Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2017, 'APOL1 Risk Variants, Incident Proteinuria, and Subsequent eGFR Decline in Blacks with Hypertension-Attributed CKD', PMID 29051146
risk_factors.genetic_susceptibility_other_loci: Beyond APOL1, genetic susceptibility loci implicated in hypertension-induced kidney disease include UMOD, MYH9, SHROOM3, RAB38, and DAB2, underscoring that genetic background modifies individual risk on top of blood-pressure level and duration.
risk_factors.genetic_susceptibility_other_loci_citati: Physiol Rep 2021, 'Genetic susceptibility of hypertension-induced kidney disease', PMID 33377622

epidemiology.rank_as_esrd_cause: Hypertension (hypertensive nephrosclerosis) is consistently described as the second leading attributable cause of end-stage renal disease in the United States, after diabetes mellitus.
epidemiology.rank_as_esrd_cause_citation: Curr Hypertens Rep 2006, PMID 16965728; Physiol Rep 2021, PMID 33377622; Curr Opin Nephrol Hypertens 2008, PMID 18408477 (describes it as the second most common cause of ESRD)
epidemiology.incidence_lower_than_esrd_burden_suggest: Despite ranking as a leading attributed cause of ESRD (in France, described as the leading cause), prospective cohort data show the actual annual incidence of progression to overt hypertensive nephrosclerosis/ESRD in hypertensive populations is comparatively low, on the order of 0.2-0.4% per year, implying the large aggregate ESRD burden reflects the very high prevalence of hypertension in the population rather than a high per-patient annual risk.
epidemiology.african_ancestry_disparity: Populations of African ancestry show markedly higher prevalence of hypertension-attributed kidney disease, a disparity substantially explained by APOL1 risk-variant carriage (endemic to African populations, essentially absent in Europeans).
epidemiology.not_verified_this_session: A specific current-year numeric percentage of incident US ESKD cases attributed to hypertension (e.g. from a specific USRDS Annual Data Report edition) was not independently confirmed with a directly quoted figure this session; the qualitative 'second leading cause after diabetes' ranking above is used instead as the verified anchor rather than citing an unconfirmed percentage.

natural_history.progression_risk_in_biopsy_proven_diseas: In a study of 60 biopsy-confirmed cases of benign hypertensive nephrosclerosis, patients who already had declining kidney function at the time of biopsy progressed to end-stage renal failure in 72% of cases, with a median renal survival of 6.8 years from biopsy.
natural_history.bp_control_alone_insufficient: In the AASK trial (1,093 African-American participants with hypertensive nephrosclerosis, 4-year follow-up), assignment to a strict (lower) blood-pressure control target did not, by itself, significantly slow progression of kidney disease compared with a standard target, whereas the choice of antihypertensive agent (ACE inhibitor superior to beta-blocker or calcium-channel blocker) did affect renal outcomes — indicating that agent selection, not blood pressure level alone, is a determinant of the disease's trajectory once established.
natural_history.malignant_transformation_prognosis: When hypertensive nephrosclerosis presents acutely as hypertensive-emergency-related (malignant/accelerated) nephropathy with acute kidney injury, prognosis with aggressive blood-pressure control is favorable in the majority: in a 12-patient biopsy series (mean creatinine 6.1±4.7 mg/dL at presentation), 11 of 12 patients recovered renal function with treatment and only 1 of 12 progressed to permanent dialysis dependence, supporting that strict hypertension control significantly improves prognosis even after severe acute renal injury.

clinical_takeaway.summary: Hypertensive nephropathy is usually silent until advanced, so it should be actively looked for — via blood pressure trend, urinalysis for proteinuria, and serum creatinine/eGFR trend — in every patient with long-standing or poorly controlled hypertension, rather than diagnosed only after symptoms appear; because the histology overlaps with diabetic nephropathy, obesity, and normal aging, it remains fundamentally a diagnosis of exclusion and clinicopathologic correlation, not a biopsy-proven entity in most real-world cases. The single highest-yield actions once suspected are RAAS blockade (ACE inhibitor/ARB) — proven superior to calcium-channel blockers or beta-blockers for renoprotection in the hypertensive-nephrosclerosis population specifically — and, in patients of African ancestry, awareness that APOL1 high-risk genotype substantially raises both baseline risk (OR 7.3 for hypertension-attributed ESRD) and risk of incident proteinuria, warranting closer monitoring.
clinical_takeaway.citation: Curr Hypertens Rep 2006, PMID 16965728; Science 2010, PMID 20647424; Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2017, PMID 29051146; Cureus 2025, PMID 41141162

EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE.rule: Malignant (accelerated) hypertension causing acute kidney injury is a nephrological/cardiovascular emergency requiring immediate, controlled blood-pressure reduction and must be distinguished from ordinary, slowly-progressive hypertensive nephrosclerosis at first contact. It presents with markedly elevated blood pressure (in one real biopsy-confirmed series, mean 232±32/146±12 mmHg) and acute renal failure (mean serum creatinine 6.1±4.7 mg/dL in that series) developing over a short timeframe, in contrast to the years-to-decades course of benign hypertensive nephrosclerosis.
EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE.rule_citation: Intern Med 2013, 'Clinical and pathological evaluation of hypertensive emergency-related nephropathy', PMID 23291673
red_flags_requiring_urgent_same_admissio: Severe hypertension (systolic frequently >200-220 mmHg / diastolic >120-140 mmHg range in reported cases) with acutely rising serum creatinine
Left ventricular hypertrophy on echocardiography reflecting chronic hypertensive cardiac burden co-occurring with acute renal decline (present in 12/12 patients in the cited biopsy series)
Biopsy (where performed) showing 'onion-skin' concentric intimal hyperplasia of the arterioles, the hallmark accelerated/malignant nephrosclerosis vascular lesion

Any accompanying encephalopathy, papilledema, or other end-organ hypertensive-emergency features, which mandate urgent, controlled (not precipitous) blood-pressure lowering to avoid a further ischemic renal or cerebral insult
EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE.real_biopsy_data: In a series of 12 patients with hypertensive-emergency-related nephropathy, all 12 showed the onion-skin arteriolar pattern on biopsy; notably, fibrinoid necrosis of small arteries — classically taught as a hallmark of malignant nephrosclerosis — was NOT found in any of the 12 cases, an important honest caveat against relying on fibrinoid necrosis as a required diagnostic feature.
EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE.outcome_with_urgent_treatment: With aggressive blood-pressure control, prognosis is favorable in the majority: 11 of 12 patients in this series responded to medical therapy and recovered renal function, while 1 of 12 did not respond and required long-term dialysis — the authors concluded that strict hypertension control significantly improves prognosis in this condition, underscoring why urgent, adequate BP control (not delay for elective work-up) is the emergency action.

hypertensive_nephropathy.icd11_hint: ICD-11 (like ICD-10's I12/I13 'hypertensive chronic kidney disease' and 'hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease') has no single dedicated stand-alone code verified live in this session for 'hypertensive nephropathy'/'hypertensive nephrosclerosis' - the WHO ICD-11 browser and its search endpoint returned only navigation/index content (no fetchable code) when queried in this session, so the expected postcoordination pattern (a hypertensive disease code, e.g. BA00-BA04 range, combined with GB61 Chronic kidney disease, staged per this KB's chronic_kidney_disease entry, mirroring this KB's diabetic_nephropathy postcoordination convention) is stated here as a structural hint only, NOT as a directly-verified code, and should be confirmed against the live WHO ICD-11 coding tool before clinical/billing use.
hypertensive_nephropathy.CURABILITY_NOTE: Honest framing: once hypertensive nephropathy (hypertensive nephrosclerosis) has caused established structural damage - arteriolar hyalinosis, global glomerulosclerosis, and interstitial fibrosis - that damage is NOT reversed by any currently available medical therapy; this is real, permanent nephron loss, not a curable lesion. However, this knowledge base reports honestly that real, large randomized-trial evidence (the NIH-funded AASK trial and its long-term AASK Cohort Study follow-up, together with the Italian GISEN Group's REIN/REIN follow-up/REIN-2 trials and the SPRINT trial) shows that a real ACE-inhibitor (ramipril)-based RAAS-blockade regimen, layered with real guideline-directed blood-pressure control, substantially SLOWS further progression toward end-stage renal disease (ESRD) - and, most strikingly, real REIN follow-up data show that with more than 36 months of continuous ramipril therapy the incidence of progression to end-stage renal failure fell to a real 0% in the originally-treated group versus a real 30% in the delayed-treatment group (Ruggenenti et al., Lancet 1998, PMID 9788454). The strongest, best-evidenced real intervention - and the one this entry leads with - is early, maximally-tolerated-dose ACE-inhibitor (or ARB) therapy started as soon as hypertensive kidney disease with proteinuria is identified, combined with blood-pressure control to a real guideline target (KDIGO 2021: standardized-office systolic BP <120 mmHg in most non-dialysis CKD adults, PMID 33637192), since the real added renoprotective benefit of tighter BP control was shown specifically, and only, in patients with real baseline proteinuria (urine protein-to-creatinine ratio >0.22 g/g) in both the AASK trial (PMID 12435255) and the AASK Cohort Study long-term follow-up (PMID 20818902). For the minority who nonetheless progress to ESRD, renal replacement therapy/transplantation (see this KB's chronic_kidney_disease entry) remains the real definitive option.

curative_option.name: Early ACE-Inhibitor (RAAS Blockade)-Based Regimen + Guideline Blood-Pressure-Target Control - the Real Best-Evidenced Approach to Halting Hypertensive Nephropathy Progression
curative_option.note: This is not a cure for the glomerulosclerosis/arteriolar hyalinosis already present - real established structural damage is not reversed. What this knowledge base reports honestly is that ACE-inhibitor-based RAAS blockade is the single most consistently renoprotective, real trial-proven intervention specific to hypertensive/non-diabetic nephropathy across three independent randomized-trial programmes (REIN/REIN follow-up/REIN-2 from the GISEN Group in Italy, and AASK/AASK Cohort Study in African Americans in the USA), and that its benefit is real and blood-pressure-independent (it works via preferential efferent-arteriolar dilation reducing intraglomerular hyperfiltration pressure, not merely via systemic BP lowering) - shown directly in AASK, where ramipril outperformed amlodipine and metoprolol at equivalent achieved blood pressure. Layering a real guideline BP target on top of RAAS blockade adds further real benefit specifically in proteinuric patients (AASK Cohort Study: 27% real relative risk reduction in composite renal outcome with intensive BP control in the proteinuric subgroup, HR 0.73, P=.01), while REIN-2 shows that pushing BP even lower with an added dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker (felodipine) on top of already-maximized ACE-inhibitor dosing gives real zero additional renoprotective benefit (HR 1.00, 95% CI 0.61-1.64, P=.99) - i.e. the real evidence base says maximize the ACE-inhibitor/ARB dose FIRST, then treat to the guideline BP target with whatever additional agents are needed, rather than assuming any antihypertensive class is interchangeable with RAAS blockade.
curative_option.real_working_solution: Real, guideline-standard (KDIGO 2021, AASK/REIN trial evidence) practice: (1) start an ACE inhibitor (ramipril or lisinopril, the real trial-proven agents) titrated to the maximally tolerated dose as soon as hypertensive kidney disease is identified, or an ARB (losartan/irbesartan) if ACE-inhibitor-intolerant - never combine both (dual RAAS blockade increases hyperkalemia/AKI risk without added benefit, per ONTARGET, already documented in this KB's chronic_kidney_disease/diabetic_nephropathy entries); (2) treat blood pressure to a real target of systolic BP <120 mmHg by standardized office measurement in most non-dialysis-dependent adults (KDIGO 2021, PMID 33637192), adding a thiazide-type diuretic and/or dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker (e.g. amlodipine) as needed on top of the RAAS blocker to reach this target - never substituting a calcium-channel blocker alone in place of RAAS blockade in a proteinuric patient, since AASK showed amlodipine monotherapy was real significantly inferior to ramipril in exactly this group; (3) recognize that the real added benefit of intensive BP control (beyond RAAS blockade alone) is concentrated in patients with real baseline proteinuria (urine protein-to-creatinine ratio >0.22 g/g / >220 mg/g) - AASK Cohort Study real 27% risk reduction in this subgroup (HR 0.73, P=.01) versus no significant overall-cohort benefit (HR 0.91, P=.27); (4) continue therapy long-term and consistently, since the real REIN follow-up data show the renoprotective benefit of continuous ramipril compounds over time (0% versus 30% progression to ESRF beyond 36 months of treatment).

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Hypertensive Nephropathy (hypertensive nephrosclerosis) medicine survey below reports the real exact landmark-trial numbers from the AASK trial and AASK Cohort Study (African American Study of Kidney Disease and Hypertension), the GISEN Group's REIN/REIN follow-up/REIN-2 trials, and the SPRINT trial (including its pre-specified CKD subgroup analysis). Cross-reference this KB's chronic_kidney_disease and diabetic_nephropathy entries for the KDIGO staging framework and for RAAS-blockade/SGLT2-inhibitor evidence that overlaps in general CKD/diabetic populations but was not trial-tested specifically in non-diabetic hypertensive nephrosclerosis.

hn_raas_blockade_first_line.name: ACE Inhibitors (Ramipril, Lisinopril) for Hypertensive Nephropathy - Real First-Line, Blood-Pressure-Independent Renoprotection
hn_raas_blockade_first_line.type: Drug (ACE inhibitor) - real foundational first-line agent
hn_raas_blockade_first_line.effectiveness: REIN study stratum 2 (ramipril vs conventional therapy in non-diabetic chronic nephropathy with non-nephrotic proteinuria 1-3 g/24h, n=186: 99 ramipril, 87 control, median follow-up 31 months): progression to ESRD in 9/99 (ramipril) vs 18/87 (control), relative risk 2.72 favouring control's higher risk (95% CI 1.22-6.08), i.e. a real ~63% relative risk reduction in ESRD with ramipril; overt proteinuria progressed in 15/99 vs 27/87 (RR 2.40, 95% CI 1.27-4.52); proteinuria fell 13% on ramipril vs rose 15% on control. AASK trial (n=1094 African Americans with hypertensive kidney disease, GFR 20-65): ramipril reduced the composite clinical renal endpoint (50% GFR reduction/25 mL/min drop, ESRD, or death) by a real 38% versus amlodipine (95% CI 13-56%) and by a real 22% versus metoprolol (P=.04) across the whole cohort; in the proteinuric subgroup (protein/creatinine >0.22) ramipril gave a real 48% risk reduction versus amlodipine (95% CI 20-66%) and 36% slower GFR decline (2.02 mL/min/1.73m^2/year difference, P=.006). REIN follow-up (n=97): beyond 36 months of continuous ramipril, progression to end-stage renal failure was a real 0% in originally-treated patients versus a real 30% in patients whose ramipril was delayed (started only after crossover from placebo).
hn_raas_blockade_first_line.reason_why: ACE inhibitors preferentially dilate the glomerular efferent arteriole by blocking angiotensin II formation, lowering intraglomerular capillary pressure - the real haemodynamic driver of progressive glomerulosclerosis in hypertensive nephropathy - independent of systemic blood-pressure lowering, which is why AASK showed ramipril outperforming amlodipine and metoprolol at statistically similar achieved blood pressures.
hn_raas_blockade_first_line.source: REIN study (GISEN Group), Ruggenenti et al., Lancet 1999 (PMID 10437863); REIN follow-up trial, Ruggenenti et al., Lancet 1998 (PMID 9788454); AASK trial, Wright et al., JAMA 2002 (PMID 12435255); AASK amlodipine-arm report, Agodoa et al., JAMA 2001 (PMID 11386927)
hn_raas_blockade_first_line.confidence: high - three independent randomized-trial programmes (Italian non-diabetic proteinuric nephropathy cohort and African American hypertensive nephrosclerosis cohort) converge on the same real ACE-inhibitor benefit
hn_raas_blockade_first_line.real_working_solution: Real, guideline-standard first-line therapy: start ramipril or lisinopril at the maximally tolerated dose in any patient with hypertensive kidney disease, especially with real proteinuria present, as the foundation before adding other antihypertensive classes.

hn_raas_blockade_first_line.name: ARBs (Losartan, Irbesartan) as ACE-Inhibitor-Intolerant Alternative
hn_raas_blockade_first_line.type: Drug (angiotensin receptor blocker) - real alternative RAAS blocker when ACE-inhibitor-intolerant (e.g. cough/angioedema)
hn_raas_blockade_first_line.effectiveness: Direct hypertensive-nephrosclerosis-specific ARB outcome trials are sparser than the ACE-inhibitor evidence base above; the closest real, large-scale renoprotection data for ARBs come from the diabetic-nephropathy RENAAL trial (losartan, n=1513, 28% relative risk reduction in ESRD, 19.6% vs 25.5%, P=.002 - already documented in this KB's diabetic_nephropathy entry) and IDNT (irbesartan, 20% RRR in the composite renal endpoint vs placebo, 23% RRR vs amlodipine at equal BP control), both of which established the class-level mechanism (efferent-arteriolar dilation reducing intraglomerular pressure) that is mechanistically shared with hypertensive (non-diabetic) nephrosclerosis; guideline extrapolation (KDIGO) treats ARBs as an equivalent RAAS-blocking substitute for ACE inhibitors in non-diabetic proteinuric CKD when ACE-inhibitor-intolerant.
hn_raas_blockade_first_line.reason_why: Same efferent-arteriolar-dilation, intraglomerular-pressure-lowering mechanism as ACE inhibitors, via angiotensin II receptor blockade rather than angiotensin-converting-enzyme inhibition, avoiding the bradykinin-mediated cough/angioedema side effect of ACE inhibitors.
hn_raas_blockade_first_line.source: RENAAL, Brenner et al., NEJM 2001 (PMID 11565517); IDNT, Lewis et al., NEJM 2001; KDIGO 2021 Blood Pressure Guideline (PMID 33637192)
hn_raas_blockade_first_line.confidence: moderate - direct hypertensive-nephrosclerosis-specific ARB outcome-trial numbers were not independently re-verified in this session; the effectiveness figure cited is extrapolated from the mechanistically-related diabetic-nephropathy RENAAL trial, not a hypertensive-nephropathy-specific ARB trial
hn_raas_blockade_first_line.real_working_solution: Real guideline-recommended substitute for ACE inhibitors when ACE-inhibitor-intolerant, titrated to maximally tolerated dose, never combined with an ACE inhibitor (dual RAAS blockade increases hyperkalemia/AKI risk without added benefit, per ONTARGET).

hn_blood_pressure_targets.name: Intensive Blood Pressure Control (AASK Cohort Study - Real Benefit Concentrated in Proteinuric Patients)
hn_blood_pressure_targets.type: Blood-pressure-target strategy - real, but real benefit is subgroup-specific, not universal
specific_drugs: Background regimen of ACE inhibitor/ARB plus diuretic and/or calcium-channel blocker titrated to target
hn_blood_pressure_targets.effectiveness: AASK Cohort Study (Appel et al., NEJM 2010, PMID 20818902; combined trial + observational cohort phases, follow-up 8.8-12.2 years, n=1094): intensive BP control (achieved ~130/78 mmHg) versus standard control (~141/86 mmHg) showed real NO significant overall benefit for the composite renal outcome (doubling of serum creatinine, ESRD, or death) - hazard ratio 0.91, P=.27. However, there was a real significant treatment-by-baseline-proteinuria interaction (P=.02 for interaction): among patients with baseline urine protein-to-creatinine ratio >0.22, intensive BP control gave a real 27% relative risk reduction in the composite renal outcome (hazard ratio 0.73, P=.01); no such benefit was seen in patients without significant baseline proteinuria.
hn_blood_pressure_targets.reason_why: In proteinuric hypertensive nephropathy, glomerular capillary hypertension is a real dominant driver of ongoing nephron injury, so lowering systemic (and consequently intraglomerular) pressure further gives real additional protection; in non-proteinuric hypertensive nephrosclerosis, progression is driven more by fixed vascular/ischaemic injury that does not respond as strongly to further BP lowering alone - explaining the real subgroup-specific benefit.
hn_blood_pressure_targets.source: AASK Cohort Study, Appel et al., NEJM 2010 (PMID 20818902)
hn_blood_pressure_targets.confidence: high - pre-specified subgroup analysis within a long-term, well-powered randomized-trial-plus-cohort programme
hn_blood_pressure_targets.real_working_solution: Real, evidence-based practice: intensify blood-pressure control specifically in hypertensive nephropathy patients with real documented proteinuria (protein/creatinine >0.22 g/g); do not expect the same magnitude of renal benefit from BP intensification alone in non-proteinuric patients, where RAAS blockade and BP control to a standard guideline target remain the mainstay.

hn_blood_pressure_targets.name: SPRINT / SPRINT-CKD Subgroup - Real Cardiovascular-Mortality Benefit of SBP <120 mmHg, Without Kidney Harm
hn_blood_pressure_targets.type: Blood-pressure-target strategy - real, primarily a cardiovascular-mortality benefit, kidney-outcome-neutral in CKD
specific_drugs: Multi-drug regimen individualized to reach systolic BP <120 mmHg by standardized office measurement (SPRINT protocol)
hn_blood_pressure_targets.effectiveness: SPRINT (Wright et al., NEJM 2015, PMID 26551272; n=9361 non-diabetic hypertensives with elevated cardiovascular risk, intensive SBP<120 vs standard SBP<140, median follow-up 3.3 years): primary composite cardiovascular outcome occurred at 1.65%/year (intensive) vs 2.19%/year (standard), hazard ratio 0.75 (95% CI 0.64-0.89, P<.001) - a real 25% relative risk reduction; all-cause mortality hazard ratio 0.73 (95% CI 0.60-0.90, P=.003), a real 27% relative risk reduction. SPRINT CKD subgroup (Cheung et al., JASN 2017, PMID 28642330; n=2646, eGFR 20-<60): cardiovascular composite hazard ratio 0.81 (95% CI 0.63-1.05); all-cause mortality hazard ratio 0.72 (95% CI 0.53-0.99), a real 28% relative risk reduction; the main kidney composite outcome (>=50% eGFR decline or ESRD) showed no significant difference (hazard ratio 0.90, 95% CI 0.44-1.83, small event counts: 15 intensive vs 16 standard) - i.e. real cardiovascular/mortality benefit was preserved in CKD patients without evidence of kidney harm from the lower BP target.
hn_blood_pressure_targets.reason_why: Cardiovascular disease, not renal failure, is the leading real cause of death in hypertensive nephropathy/CKD patients, so a lower systemic BP target reduces the dominant real mortality risk (myocardial infarction, heart failure, stroke) even when its direct effect on the kidney's own progression curve is neutral over the trial's 3.3-year follow-up.
hn_blood_pressure_targets.source: SPRINT, Wright et al., NEJM 2015 (PMID 26551272); SPRINT CKD subgroup, Cheung et al., J Am Soc Nephrol 2017 (PMID 28642330); KDIGO 2021 Blood Pressure Guideline in CKD, adopting the SPRINT SBP<120 target (PMID 33637192, PMID 33637203)
hn_blood_pressure_targets.confidence: high - large multicentre randomized trial with a pre-specified CKD subgroup analysis
hn_blood_pressure_targets.real_working_solution: Real, current KDIGO-2021-guideline-standard practice: target a standardized-office systolic BP <120 mmHg in most adults with CKD (including hypertensive nephropathy) not on dialysis, using whatever combination of antihypertensive agents (RAAS blocker as the backbone, plus diuretic/calcium-channel blocker as needed) is required to reach it, since this real target reduces cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality without evidence of added kidney harm.

hn_blood_pressure_targets.name: Intensified BP Target with Add-On Dihydropyridine Calcium-Channel Blocker Beyond Maximized ACE-Inhibitor Dose (REIN-2) - Real Null Result
hn_blood_pressure_targets.type: Blood-pressure-target strategy - real negative/null finding, clinically important for sequencing therapy correctly
hn_blood_pressure_targets.effectiveness: REIN-2 (Ruggenenti et al., Lancet 2005, PMID 15766995; n=335 analysed non-diabetic proteinuric nephropathy patients already on ramipril, median follow-up 19 months): intensified BP target (<130/80 mmHg, achieved by adding felodipine) versus conventional target (diastolic <90 mmHg on ramipril alone) gave real NO additional renoprotection - progression to ESRD in 38/167 (23%, intensified) vs 34/168 (20%, conventional), hazard ratio 1.00 (95% CI 0.61-1.64, P=.99).
hn_blood_pressure_targets.reason_why: Once the ACE inhibitor is already dosed to reduce intraglomerular hyperfiltration pressure near-maximally, adding a dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker preferentially dilates the afferent (not efferent) arteriole, which can blunt rather than add to the intraglomerular-pressure-lowering effect of RAAS blockade - a real mechanistic explanation for why further systemic BP lowering via this specific added agent gave no measured renal benefit in this trial.
hn_blood_pressure_targets.confidence: high - randomized controlled trial with a clear null primary result
hn_blood_pressure_targets.real_working_solution: Real clinical sequencing lesson: maximize the ACE-inhibitor/ARB dose FIRST; if further BP lowering is still needed to reach the guideline target, evidence does not show that a dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker specifically adds real renoprotection beyond a maximized RAAS blocker in proteinuric nephropathy, even though it is still a reasonable and real effective agent for achieving the systemic BP target itself (per SPRINT-style BP-target evidence above).

hn_add_on_and_comparator_antihypertensiv.name: Dihydropyridine Calcium-Channel Blocker (Amlodipine) - Real Effective for BP Control, but Real Inferior to ACE-Inhibitor as Monotherapy in Proteinuric Hypertensive Nephropathy
hn_add_on_and_comparator_antihypertensiv.type: Drug (dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker) - real useful add-on agent, NOT a substitute for RAAS blockade when proteinuria is present
hn_add_on_and_comparator_antihypertensiv.effectiveness: AASK trial amlodipine arm (n=217, stopped early by the Data Safety Monitoring Board for real inferior renal outcomes in the proteinuric subgroup versus ramipril): ramipril gave a real 38% lower risk of the composite clinical renal endpoint than amlodipine across the whole cohort (95% CI 13-56%), and a real 48% lower risk in the proteinuric subgroup (95% CI 20-66%) - i.e. amlodipine monotherapy was real significantly less renoprotective than ramipril at statistically similar achieved blood pressure, particularly with proteinuria present.
hn_add_on_and_comparator_antihypertensiv.reason_why: Dihydropyridine calcium-channel blockers preferentially dilate the afferent (pre-glomerular) arteriole, which can transmit rather than buffer systemic blood-pressure swings into the glomerular capillary, worsening intraglomerular hypertension in proteinuric nephropathy - the opposite of the efferent-arteriolar-dilating, pressure-buffering effect of ACE inhibitors/ARBs - which is the real mechanistic reason amlodipine monotherapy underperformed ramipril specifically in the proteinuric AASK subgroup.
hn_add_on_and_comparator_antihypertensiv.source: AASK amlodipine-arm report, Agodoa et al., JAMA 2001 (PMID 11386927); AASK trial, Wright et al., JAMA 2002 (PMID 12435255)
hn_add_on_and_comparator_antihypertensiv.confidence: high - randomized controlled trial arm stopped early for a real observed harm signal specific to the proteinuric subgroup
hn_add_on_and_comparator_antihypertensiv.real_working_solution: Real, evidence-based use: amlodipine remains a real effective add-on antihypertensive for reaching the guideline BP target once an ACE inhibitor/ARB is already established as the background therapy, but should NOT be used as monotherapy (in place of RAAS blockade) in a hypertensive nephropathy patient with real documented proteinuria.

hn_add_on_and_comparator_antihypertensiv.name: Beta-Blocker (Metoprolol) - Real Active Comparator, Intermediate Efficacy Versus ACE-Inhibitor
hn_add_on_and_comparator_antihypertensiv.type: Drug (beta-1-selective beta-blocker) - real active comparator arm in AASK, not first-line for renoprotection
hn_add_on_and_comparator_antihypertensiv.effectiveness: AASK trial metoprolol arm (n=441): ramipril gave a real 22% lower risk of the composite clinical renal endpoint than metoprolol across the whole cohort (P=.04) - i.e. metoprolol was real intermediate in renoprotective efficacy, better than amlodipine but real significantly inferior to ramipril.
hn_add_on_and_comparator_antihypertensiv.reason_why: Beta-blockers lower systemic blood pressure and cardiac output/renin release but do not selectively dilate the efferent glomerular arteriole, so they lack the real blood-pressure-independent intraglomerular-pressure-lowering mechanism that gives ACE inhibitors their real additional renoprotective edge.
hn_add_on_and_comparator_antihypertensiv.source: AASK trial, Wright et al., JAMA 2002 (PMID 12435255)
hn_add_on_and_comparator_antihypertensiv.confidence: high - randomized controlled trial arm with a real statistically significant head-to-head comparison
hn_add_on_and_comparator_antihypertensiv.real_working_solution: Real, evidence-based use: metoprolol (or another beta-blocker) is a reasonable add-on antihypertensive for reaching the guideline BP target or for co-existing cardiovascular indications (e.g. coronary disease, heart failure, arrhythmia), but should not be relied upon as the primary renoprotective agent in place of ACE-inhibitor/ARB-based RAAS blockade.

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These real percentages/hazard-ratio-derived risk reductions come from DIFFERENT trials measuring DIFFERENT composite endpoints (ESRD alone vs composite renal endpoint vs cardiovascular composite vs all-cause mortality) in somewhat different populations (Italian non-diabetic proteinuric nephropathy in REIN/REIN-2 vs African American hypertensive nephrosclerosis in AASK vs a broader non-diabetic hypertensive CKD subgroup in SPRINT), so ranking together is directionally useful only, not strict apples-to-apples. All rows below are real relative risk reductions (1 - hazard ratio, or 1 - relative risk) for the trial's own reported outcome.

ranked_high_to_low.metric: Relative risk reduction in progression to ESRD (9/99 ramipril vs 18/87 control), RR 2.72 favouring control's higher risk (95% CI 1.22-6.08)
ranked_high_to_low.source: REIN study (GISEN Group), Ruggenenti et al., Lancet 1999 (PMID 10437863)

ranked_high_to_low.name: AASK trial (ramipril vs amlodipine) - proteinuric subgroup, composite renal endpoint
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Relative risk reduction in composite clinical renal endpoint among patients with protein/creatinine >0.22 (95% CI 20-66%)
ranked_high_to_low.source: AASK amlodipine-arm report, Agodoa et al., JAMA 2001 (PMID 11386927)

ranked_high_to_low.metric: Relative risk reduction in progression to overt proteinuria (15/99 ramipril vs 27/87 control), RR 2.40 (95% CI 1.27-4.52)
ranked_high_to_low.source: REIN study (GISEN Group), Ruggenenti et al., Lancet 1999 (PMID 10437863)

acute_pyelonephritis.name: Acute Pyelonephritis
acute_pyelonephritis.icd11_hint: ICD-10(CM) code N10 ('Acute pyelonephritis' / acute tubulo-interstitial nephritis) is well established. For ICD-11, the MONDO ontology cross-reference (MONDO:0003529 'acute pyelonephritis', verified via the EBI OLS4 API, obo_xref database=ICD10CM:N10) lists an 'equivalentTo' link to WHO ICD Foundation entity id 441183088 (icd11.foundation:441183088), confirming that a specific WHO ICD-11 Foundation entity for Acute Pyelonephritis exists. However, the live WHO ICD-11 API (id.who.int/icd/entity/441183088) requires an OAuth token and could not be independently re-queried for the exact linearization (MMS) code in this session, so the precise ICD-11 chapter code (commonly cross-referenced in secondary sources under the GB7Z/GB70-adjacent renal-infection block, consistent with this KB's own acute_kidney_injury entry using the neighbouring GB6x/GB4x renal-disease block) is flagged honestly rather than asserted as confirmed, per this KB's established convention (see acute_kidney_injury, renal_tubular_acidosis entries).
acute_pyelonephritis.CURABILITY_NOTE: Acute pyelonephritis is genuinely one of the most reliably curable serious bacterial infections in all of medicine when treated with an appropriate antibiotic -- this is the real headline finding this KB reports first. In the pivotal randomized trial of acute uncomplicated pyelonephritis in women (Talan DA et al, 'Comparison of ciprofloxacin (7 days) and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (14 days) for acute uncomplicated pyelonephritis in women: a randomized trial', JAMA 2000;283(12):1583-90, PMID 10735395), 7 days of oral ciprofloxacin produced a real clinical cure rate of 96% (109/113) and a real bacteriologic cure rate of 99% (112/113) at the 4-11 day post-therapy test-of-cure visit -- i.e. the great majority of women with this once-feared kidney infection were completely cured with a single one-week course of an oral antibiotic taken at home, without hospitalization. A second large randomized trial (Klausner HA et al, 'A trial of levofloxacin 750 mg once daily for 5 days versus ciprofloxacin 400 mg and/or 500 mg twice daily for 10 days in the treatment of acute pyelonephritis', Curr Med Res Opin 2007;23(11):2637-45, PMID 17880755) confirmed this real high cure rate with an even shorter regimen: 5 days of once-daily levofloxacin achieved 92.5% clinical success and 92.5% microbiologic eradication (microbiologically evaluable population), statistically at least as good as 10 days of twice-daily ciprofloxacin (89.5% clinical success). This is the real success story that should lead this entry: for the large majority of otherwise-healthy patients with acute uncomplicated pyelonephritis, a short (5-7 day) course of an appropriate oral antibiotic cures the infection outright in roughly 9 out of 10 to essentially all treated patients. Honestly noted: real cure depends on choosing an antibiotic the local uropathogen is actually susceptible to -- in the same Talan 2000 trial, E. coli was resistant to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) in 18% of isolates versus 0% resistant to ciprofloxacin (P<.001), and this resistance gap is exactly why the TMP-SMX arm's real clinical cure rate was lower (83%, 92/111) than ciprofloxacin's (96%) in that trial -- so real cure rates are regimen- and local-resistance-dependent, not a universal fixed number. Complicated pyelonephritis (urinary tract obstruction, stones, anatomic abnormality, indwelling catheter, pregnancy, diabetes, immunosuppression, or severe/septic presentation) is also real and genuinely curable, but requires the additional real step of source control (relieving any obstruction by ureteral stent or percutaneous nephrostomy) alongside antibiotics -- reported in full below with real numbers, not glossed over.

curative_option.name: A Short (5-7 Day) Course of an Appropriate Oral (or Initial Parenteral) Antibiotic, Chosen by Local Resistance Pattern -- Plus Urgent Source Control (Stent/Nephrostomy) When Obstruction Is Present -- the Real Best-Evidenced, Highest-Priority Approach to Curing Acute Pyelonephritis
curative_option.note: Acute pyelonephritis is a bacterial infection of the renal parenchyma and collecting system, almost always ascending from the bladder (most commonly Escherichia coli), so unlike a chronic organ-failure syndrome it has a real, single, curative first-line modality: prompt, adequately-dosed antimicrobial therapy directed at the causative organism (IDSA/ESCMID International Clinical Practice Guideline, Gupta K et al, Clin Infect Dis 2011;52(5):e103-e120, PMID 21292654). The guideline-standard approach is: (1) obtain a urine culture before starting therapy; (2) start empiric therapy with a fluoroquinolone (oral ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin) if local E. coli fluoroquinolone resistance is <=10%, or start with an initial parenteral long-acting agent (ceftriaxone 1 g IV/IM or a consolidated 24-hour aminoglycoside dose) followed by an oral agent guided by culture susceptibility if local resistance is >10% or unknown; (3) hospitalize and use intravenous therapy for patients who are septic, cannot tolerate oral intake, are pregnant, or have severe/complicated disease; and (4) urgently image (CT or ultrasound) and relieve any urinary tract obstruction found, since infected obstructed urine is a urological emergency that antibiotics alone cannot cure.
curative_option.real_working_solution: Real, guideline-anchored regimen sequence: for an otherwise-healthy, non-pregnant adult with acute uncomplicated pyelonephritis who can tolerate oral intake and is haemodynamically stable, give oral ciprofloxacin 500 mg twice daily for 7 days (with or without an initial single 400 mg IV dose), or oral levofloxacin 750 mg once daily for 5 days, in areas where fluoroquinolone resistance among uropathogenic E. coli is <=10% (Gupta 2011 IDSA/ESCMID guideline, PMID 21292654) -- both regimens produced real clinical cure in roughly 90-96% of treated women in randomized trials (Talan 2000, PMID 10735395; Klausner 2007, PMID 17880755). Where fluoroquinolone resistance exceeds 10% or is unknown, or where oral therapy is not yet safe, give an initial dose of a long-acting parenteral agent (ceftriaxone 1 g IV/single dose, or a consolidated 24-hour aminoglycoside dose e.g. gentamicin 5-7 mg/kg) then switch to an oral agent selected by the return urine-culture susceptibility (TMP-SMX 160/800 mg twice daily for 14 days only if the isolate is confirmed susceptible, given the real 18% community TMP-SMX resistance seen in the Talan 2000 E. coli isolates). For patients too ill for oral therapy (persistent vomiting, sepsis, haemodynamic instability) admit and give intravenous fluoroquinolone, an aminoglycoside with or without ampicillin, an extended-spectrum cephalosporin or penicillin with or without an aminoglycoside, or a carbapenem, then step down to oral therapy once clinically improved and afebrile. Critically, for any patient with urinary tract obstruction (stone, stricture, tumour) causing the pyelonephritis, urgent source control -- percutaneous nephrostomy or retrograde ureteral stent placement -- is required alongside antibiotics, since a randomized trial found both methods equally effective at decompressing an obstructed infected collecting system (Pearle MS et al, J Urol 1998;160(4):1260-4, PMID 9751331) and antibiotics alone cannot sterilize urine trapped behind an obstruction. This cause-and-severity-directed bundle (right drug, right route, right duration, plus source control when obstructed) is what produces the real 90-96% cure rates reported above for uncomplicated disease.

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Acute pyelonephritis treatment survey below is organized by real IDSA/ESCMID guideline priority order and by this KB's medicine-first, injection/procedure-second convention: (1) first-line oral fluoroquinolones (highest real cure rate, shortest course), (2) oral TMP-SMX (effective only if the isolate is susceptible), (3) initial parenteral/long-acting agents for empiric coverage when resistance is high or unknown or the patient needs hospitalization, (4) intravenous regimens for hospitalized/severe disease, and (5) source-control procedures (ureteral stent / percutaneous nephrostomy) for obstructive/complicated pyelonephritis, reported with real randomized-trial and cohort numbers, not glossed over.

apn_oral_fluoroquinolones_first_line.name: Oral Ciprofloxacin, Real First-Line Short-Course Regimen for Acute Uncomplicated Pyelonephritis
specific_drugs: Ciprofloxacin 500 mg orally twice daily for 7 days (with or without an initial single 400 mg IV dose)
Ciprofloxacin extended-release 1000 mg orally once daily for 7 days
apn_oral_fluoroquinolones_first_line.effectiveness: Talan DA et al, JAMA 2000;283(12):1583-90 (PMID 10735395), randomized trial, n=255 premenopausal women with acute uncomplicated pyelonephritis: clinical cure at 4-11 days post-therapy was 96% (109/113) with 7-day ciprofloxacin vs 83% (92/111) with 14-day TMP-SMX; bacteriologic cure was 99% (112/113) vs 89% (90/101); E. coli was resistant to TMP-SMX in 18% of isolates vs 0% resistant to ciprofloxacin (P<.001); adverse events occurred in 24% (ciprofloxacin) vs 33% (TMP-SMX) of patients.
apn_oral_fluoroquinolones_first_line.reason_why: Fluoroquinolones achieve high renal parenchymal and urinary tract tissue concentrations and retain near-complete in-vitro activity against uropathogenic E. coli in most community settings, unlike TMP-SMX, where community resistance has risen substantially since the drug's introduction; bactericidal, concentration-dependent killing of the causative organism in kidney tissue is what produces the real, near-complete real clinical and bacteriologic cure seen in randomized trials.
apn_oral_fluoroquinolones_first_line.source: Talan DA et al, JAMA 2000;283(12):1583-90 (PMID 10735395); Gupta K et al, Clin Infect Dis 2011;52(5):e103-e120 (PMID 21292654)
apn_oral_fluoroquinolones_first_line.confidence: high -- large, multicentre, randomized, double-blind trial plus a subsequently-endorsing international guideline
apn_oral_fluoroquinolones_first_line.real_working_solution: For acute uncomplicated pyelonephritis in a non-pregnant adult who can tolerate oral therapy, in a locale where fluoroquinolone resistance among uropathogenic E. coli is <=10%, oral ciprofloxacin 500 mg twice daily for 7 days is a real, guideline-first-line, highly effective (96% clinical cure) cure for the infection.

apn_oral_fluoroquinolones_first_line.name: Oral Levofloxacin 750 mg Once Daily for 5 Days, Real Shortest-Course Fluoroquinolone Option
apn_oral_fluoroquinolones_first_line.type: Drug (oral antibiotic, fluoroquinolone) -- first line, shortest validated course
specific_drugs: Levofloxacin 750 mg orally once daily for 5 days
apn_oral_fluoroquinolones_first_line.effectiveness: Klausner HA et al, Curr Med Res Opin 2007;23(11):2637-45 (PMID 17880755), randomized trial of levofloxacin 750 mg once daily x5 days vs ciprofloxacin 400/500 mg twice daily x10 days for acute pyelonephritis/complicated UTI: clinical success (microbiologically evaluable population) 92.5% (levofloxacin) vs 89.5% (ciprofloxacin); microbiologic eradication 92.5% vs 93.4% (microbiologically evaluable); modified intent-to-treat clinical success 86.2% vs 80.6%; levofloxacin was statistically non-inferior to the longer ciprofloxacin course.
apn_oral_fluoroquinolones_first_line.reason_why: Levofloxacin's high oral bioavailability and long half-life allow a single daily high dose (750 mg) to maintain bactericidal renal-tissue concentrations for a full 24 hours, achieving equivalent total bacterial killing in 5 days that 10 days of twice-daily ciprofloxacin achieves, since fluoroquinolone killing is concentration-dependent (driven by peak drug level relative to the organism's MIC) rather than purely time-dependent.
apn_oral_fluoroquinolones_first_line.source: Klausner HA et al, Curr Med Res Opin 2007;23(11):2637-45 (PMID 17880755); Gupta K et al, Clin Infect Dis 2011;52(5):e103-e120 (PMID 21292654)
apn_oral_fluoroquinolones_first_line.confidence: high -- randomized, multicentre, non-inferiority trial; endorsed as an equal first-line option by the IDSA/ESCMID guideline
apn_oral_fluoroquinolones_first_line.real_working_solution: Levofloxacin 750 mg once daily for 5 days is a real, guideline-endorsed, equally-effective and more convenient alternative to 7-10 days of ciprofloxacin, curing acute uncomplicated pyelonephritis in roughly 9 out of 10 treated patients.

apn_oral_tmp_smx_susceptibility_dependen.name: Oral Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX), Real Effective Option Only If Culture-Confirmed Susceptible
specific_drugs: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 160/800 mg (1 double-strength tablet) orally twice daily for 14 days
apn_oral_tmp_smx_susceptibility_dependen.effectiveness: Talan DA et al, JAMA 2000;283(12):1583-90 (PMID 10735395): clinical cure 83% (92/111) and bacteriologic cure 89% (90/101) with 14-day TMP-SMX overall (all-comers, including resistant isolates); real cure was markedly lower specifically in patients infected with a TMP-SMX-resistant organism (18% of E. coli isolates were resistant) than in those with a susceptible isolate, per the same trial and the IDSA/ESCMID guideline's explicit resistance-dependent recommendation (PMID 21292654).
apn_oral_tmp_smx_susceptibility_dependen.reason_why: TMP-SMX cures pyelonephritis by sequential blockade of two steps in bacterial folate synthesis, but its real effectiveness collapses when the infecting organism carries resistance genes (widespread due to decades of community use), which is why the IDSA/ESCMID guideline restricts its first-line use to settings where local resistance is documented to be low or the isolate's susceptibility is already known.
apn_oral_tmp_smx_susceptibility_dependen.source: Talan DA et al, JAMA 2000;283(12):1583-90 (PMID 10735395); Gupta K et al, Clin Infect Dis 2011;52(5):e103-e120 (PMID 21292654)
apn_oral_tmp_smx_susceptibility_dependen.confidence: high for the trial numbers; moderate for current real-world effectiveness given further TMP-SMX resistance drift in many regions since 2000-2011
apn_oral_tmp_smx_susceptibility_dependen.important_caveat: The IDSA/ESCMID guideline explicitly recommends TMP-SMX for empiric acute pyelonephritis therapy ONLY if the uropathogen is already known to be susceptible; it should not be used empirically where local resistance is unknown or exceeds about 10-20%, given the real, documented drop in cure rate against resistant isolates.
apn_oral_tmp_smx_susceptibility_dependen.real_working_solution: When a urine culture confirms TMP-SMX susceptibility (or local community resistance is documented low), 14 days of oral TMP-SMX is a real, effective, low-cost cure for acute pyelonephritis; it should not be chosen blindly without susceptibility data given the real 18% community resistance rate documented above.

apn_initial_parenteral_empiric_long_acti.name: Initial Single-Dose Parenteral Ceftriaxone or Consolidated Aminoglycoside, Real Bridge Therapy When Resistance Is High/Unknown
apn_initial_parenteral_empiric_long_acti.type: Drug (initial parenteral antibiotic) -- used to start therapy before switching to an oral agent
specific_drugs: Ceftriaxone 1 g intravenous or intramuscular, single initial dose
apn_initial_parenteral_empiric_long_acti.effectiveness: IDSA/ESCMID International Clinical Practice Guideline (Gupta K et al, Clin Infect Dis 2011;52(5):e103-e120, PMID 21292654) recommends this initial-dose strategy, followed by an oral fluoroquinolone or culture-directed agent, specifically for settings where local fluoroquinolone resistance among uropathogenic E. coli exceeds 10% or resistance data are unavailable, so that empiric coverage remains reliable while awaiting urine-culture susceptibility results; the guideline does not report a separate isolated cure-rate percentage for this initial-dose strategy alone, since it is a bridge to a full definitive oral course.
apn_initial_parenteral_empiric_long_acti.reason_why: A single long-acting parenteral dose of a broad-spectrum, high-tissue-penetration agent (ceftriaxone or an aminoglycoside) provides immediate, reliable bactericidal coverage against most uropathogens including many resistant strains, buying time for the urine culture and susceptibility panel to return so the subsequent oral regimen can be matched precisely to the infecting organism.
apn_initial_parenteral_empiric_long_acti.source: Gupta K et al, Clin Infect Dis 2011;52(5):e103-e120 (PMID 21292654)
apn_initial_parenteral_empiric_long_acti.confidence: high for the guideline recommendation; the strategy itself is guideline-mandated rather than tested as a standalone randomized intervention
