addisons_disease.name: Addison's Disease (Primary Adrenal Insufficiency - Autoimmune Adrenalitis, Tuberculous/Fungal Infectious Adrenalitis, and Other Causes)
addisons_disease.icd11_hint: ICD-11 code for Addison disease/primary adrenal insufficiency is commonly cited as 5A74 in third-party ICD-11 coding references; this exact code string was NOT independently re-verified against a live WHO ICD-11 browser/API session in this fork (API access unavailable), so it is stated at moderate confidence on the code string only - disease identity, causes, presentation and diagnosis below are all separately PMID-verified.
addisons_disease.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE: Adrenal (Addisonian) Crisis is a real, distinct endocrine EMERGENCY that must bypass the normal doctor-approval-queue flow and trigger immediate real-world emergency-service guidance (call ambulance / go to ER now). Adrenal crisis is an episode of ACUTE adrenal insufficiency (decompensation of chronic Addison's disease, or the first presentation of previously undiagnosed disease) and is clinically distinct from chronic, stable, treated Addison's disease, which is controlled with long-term glucocorticoid/mineralocorticoid therapy. Real presentation: hypotension/shock, lethargy/altered mental status, nausea and vomiting, abdominal pain, and hypoglycemia, on a background of hyponatremia and hyperkalemia (StatPearls 'Addison Disease', Munir/Quintanilla Rodriguez/Waseem, PMID 28723023; Kan 2025, Adv Emerg Nurs J 'Adrenal Insufficiency: A Case Study', PMID 40720873). Real incidence: adrenal crisis occurs at an estimated rate of 8 per 100 patient-years in patients with known adrenal insufficiency (Dineen, Thompson & Sherlock 2019, Ther Adv Endocrinol Metab, PMID 31223468); real mortality directly attributable to crisis is estimated at 0.5 per 100 patient-years and it 'remains a significant cause of death' in adrenal insufficiency patients, with rapid deterioration to death possible at home or shortly after hospital admission if untreated (StatPearls 'Adrenal Crisis', Elshimy et al 2025, PMID 29763143). Real precipitating factors: infection is the major precipitant; others include physical stress (surgery, trauma), forgetting or discontinuing glucocorticoid replacement, pronounced physical exertion, and psychological stress (PMID 31223468). In a real Indian cohort of 89 primary adrenal insufficiency patients, 42% first presented WITH an acute adrenal crisis, i.e. crisis is frequently the sentinel presentation, not a late complication (Gunna et al 2023, Endocrine Connections, PMID 36625588). Emergency treatment is immediate parenteral (IV/IM) hydrocortisone, aggressive IV fluid rehydration, and correction of electrolyte/glucose abnormalities - this must never be queued through routine doctor-approval workflow (PMID 31223468; PMID 29763143; PMID 40720873).

autoimmune_adrenalitis.mechanism: Real, most common cause of primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease proper) in economically developed countries - T-cell-mediated autoimmune destruction of the adrenal cortex, associated with circulating 21-hydroxylase autoantibodies. May occur in isolation or as part of autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 1 (APS1, rare, hereditary, broad clinical spectrum) or type 2 (APS2, combined with autoimmune thyroid disease and/or type 1 diabetes).
autoimmune_adrenalitis.source: StatPearls 'Addison Disease', Munir/Quintanilla Rodriguez/Waseem, PMID 28723023, and its nursing companion PMID 33760534; Kan 2025, Adv Emerg Nurs J, PMID 40720873 ('most common cause of primary adrenal insufficiency in developed countries is autoimmune'); Bensing et al 2008, Clin Endocrinol (Oxf), PMID 18727712 (APS1/APS2 distinction and differential mortality); Endocrine Society guideline, Bornstein et al 2016, J Clin Endocrinol Metab, PMID 26760044 (recommends screening for associated autoimmune thyroid disease on follow-up)
autoimmune_adrenalitis.confidence: high - consistently stated across StatPearls, a dedicated case-study review, a large population cohort study, and the Endocrine Society guideline

infectious_tuberculosis.mechanism: Real, tuberculosis is specifically identified as the most common cause of adrenal insufficiency in DEVELOPING countries (as distinct from the autoimmune-predominant picture in developed countries) - caseating granulomatous destruction of the adrenal cortex.
infectious_tuberculosis.proportion: In a real north Indian cohort of 89 primary adrenal insufficiency patients (2006-2019), adrenal tuberculosis accounted for 15% of cases.
infectious_tuberculosis.source: Verma, Sarkar, Mendiratta & Srivastava 2024, Indian J Dermatol, 'Addisonian Pigmentation - The Great Mimicker - A Review', PMID 39649977 ('the most common cause of adrenal insufficiency in developing countries is tuberculosis'); Gunna et al 2023, Endocrine Connections, PMID 36625588 (15% of n=89 Indian cohort)

infectious_histoplasmosis_and_other_fung.mechanism: Real, endemic fungal infection destroying the adrenal cortex. In the same real north Indian cohort, adrenal histoplasmosis was in fact the SINGLE MOST FREQUENT cause overall - exceeding both tuberculosis and autoimmunity in that specific population - and carried by far the highest mortality of any etiology studied.
infectious_histoplasmosis_and_other_fung.proportion: 45% of 89 Indian PAI patients (vs 15% tuberculosis, 25% autoimmune, 6% primary lymphoma in the same cohort); histoplasmosis patients had a higher frequency of hepatomegaly-splenomegaly and type 2 diabetes mellitus (63% vs 15%, p<0.01) than tuberculosis patients, the only clinical feature that reliably distinguished the two infectious causes.
infectious_histoplasmosis_and_other_fung.caveat: This is real, region-specific data from a single north Indian tertiary-care cohort and should NOT be generalised as the globally leading cause of PAI without further verification - it is reported here exactly as published, not extrapolated.
infectious_histoplasmosis_and_other_fung.source: Gunna et al 2023, Endocrine Connections, PMID 36625588
infectious_histoplasmosis_and_other_fung.confidence: high for the cited cohort; not verified as globally representative

other_causes.mechanism: Real, other described causes of primary adrenal insufficiency beyond autoimmune/tuberculous/fungal: primary adrenal lymphoma; iatrogenic causes including adrenal haemorrhage associated with anticoagulant therapy, drugs affecting glucocorticoid synthesis/action/metabolism, and immune-checkpoint-inhibitor cancer therapy; and genetic disorders.
other_causes.proportion: Primary adrenal lymphoma accounted for 6% of the same 89-patient Indian cohort. No independently verified numeric proportion was found in this session for iatrogenic or genetic causes specifically, so none is stated - only the qualitative categories are reported.
other_causes.source: Barthel et al 2019, Exp Clin Endocrinol Diabetes, 'An Update on Addison's Disease', PMID 30562824 (iatrogenic/checkpoint-inhibitor causes, rising prevalence, reduced quality of life despite treatment); Gunna et al 2023, PMID 36625588 (6% primary lymphoma)
other_causes.confidence: high (qualitative categories); numeric proportions given only where a real source was found

fatigue_weakness_gi_and_weight_loss.description: Real, common early nonspecific presenting symptoms that develop slowly over months as chronic glucocorticoid/mineralocorticoid deficiency progresses: fatigue, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, myalgias, and weight loss. Because these are nonspecific, PAI is frequently not considered early, resulting in delayed diagnosis.
fatigue_weakness_gi_and_weight_loss.source: Kan 2025, Adv Emerg Nurs J, PMID 40720873; StatPearls 'Addison Disease', PMID 28723023; Barthel et al 2019, PMID 30562824 (delayed diagnosis due to nonspecific early symptoms)

hyperpigmentation.description: Real, classic sign relatively specific to PRIMARY adrenal insufficiency (characteristically absent in secondary/central adrenal insufficiency) - loss of cortisol negative feedback drives pituitary POMC/ACTH overproduction; ACTH and the co-secreted melanocyte-stimulating peptides share the same POMC precursor, and the resulting excess stimulates cutaneous melanocytes, producing diffuse hyperpigmentation most pronounced on sun-exposed skin, pressure points/skin creases, and buccal/oral mucosa. Pigmentation often precedes other manifestations by months to years and, if recognised, can prompt earlier diagnosis before a life-threatening adrenal crisis occurs. Most untreated patients eventually develop hyperpigmented skin and mucous membranes.
hyperpigmentation.source: Verma, Sarkar, Mendiratta & Srivastava 2024, Indian J Dermatol, 'Addisonian Pigmentation - The Great Mimicker - A Review', PMID 39649977; Kan 2025, PMID 40720873

hypotension.description: Real, orthostatic and/or resting hypotension driven by aldosterone deficiency (renal sodium wasting and intravascular volume depletion) and, in decompensated disease, by loss of cortisol's permissive effect on vascular catecholamine responsiveness; becomes frank shock in adrenal crisis.

hyponatremia_hyperkalemia_and_salt_cravi.description: Real, classic biochemical hallmark of PRIMARY (not secondary) adrenal insufficiency - aldosterone deficiency causes renal sodium wasting (producing hyponatremia and a real, described symptom of salt craving) and potassium retention (hyperkalemia); cortisol deficiency independently worsens hyponatremia via impaired free-water clearance. Hyponatremia and hyperkalemia are described as common in Addison's disease and become pronounced, together with hypoglycemia, in acute adrenal crisis.
hyponatremia_hyperkalemia_and_salt_cravi.source: Kan 2025, Adv Emerg Nurs J, PMID 40720873 (explicitly lists salt craving, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia as symptoms/signs); StatPearls 'Addison Disease', PMID 28723023 (crisis biochemistry: hypotension, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, hypoglycemia)

morning_cortisol_and_plasma_acth.role: Real, initial screening pattern when an immediate short corticotropin (ACTH stimulation) test cannot be performed: a low morning (approximately 8 am) serum cortisol together with an INAPPROPRIATELY ELEVATED plasma ACTH indicates primary adrenal failure - the pituitary is appropriately trying to drive a failing gland. This ACTH elevation is the key feature distinguishing PRIMARY (Addison's) disease from secondary/tertiary adrenal insufficiency, where ACTH is low or inappropriately normal despite low cortisol.
morning_cortisol_and_plasma_acth.source: Bornstein et al 2016, J Clin Endocrinol Metab, Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Primary Adrenal Insufficiency', PMID 26760044
morning_cortisol_and_plasma_acth.confidence: high - explicit Endocrine Society guideline recommendation

acth_stimulation_cosyntropin_test.role: Real GOLD-STANDARD confirmatory diagnostic test per the Endocrine Society guideline: the short (250 microgram) corticotropin/cosyntropin stimulation test. Synthetic ACTH (cosyntropin) is administered and serum cortisol is measured before and after; a blunted/subnormal cortisol rise confirms adrenal cortical failure. StatPearls describes the test as evaluating the integrity of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis and as critical for differentiating primary from secondary/tertiary causes of cortisol deficiency, guiding appropriate glucocorticoid replacement to prevent adrenal crisis.
acth_stimulation_cosyntropin_test.source: Bornstein et al 2016, PMID 26760044 (recommends the 250 mcg short corticotropin test as the 'gold standard' diagnostic tool); StatPearls 'Adrenocorticotropic Hormone (Cosyntropin) Stimulation Test', Haq & Anjum 2026, PMID 32310400

twenty_one_hydroxylase_autoantibodies.role: Real, guideline-recommended test to establish an AUTOIMMUNE etiology once biochemical primary adrenal insufficiency is confirmed: a validated assay for autoantibodies against 21-hydroxylase (an adrenal steroidogenic enzyme). In a real Indian cohort, patients with an autoimmune etiology had 21-hydroxylase antibodies far more often than those with an infectious etiology (41% vs 3%), making this a real, discriminating test between autoimmune and infectious causes. If autoantibody-negative, the guideline recommends investigating other (infectious/infiltrative/genetic) causes.
twenty_one_hydroxylase_autoantibodies.source: Bornstein et al 2016, PMID 26760044 (Endocrine Society, recommends validated 21-hydroxylase autoantibody assay); Gunna et al 2023, Endocrine Connections, PMID 36625588 (41% vs 3%, real Indian cohort, n=89)

renin_aldosterone_axis.role: Real, supportive biochemical picture in primary (not secondary) adrenal insufficiency: LOW aldosterone with a compensatory HIGH plasma renin - the renin-angiotensin axis is intact and appropriately activated by volume depletion, which helps distinguish primary adrenal gland failure from secondary/pituitary-driven disease (where the mineralocorticoid axis, being largely renin/angiotensin-driven rather than ACTH-driven, is relatively preserved).
renin_aldosterone_axis.source: StatPearls 'Addison Disease', PMID 28723023 ('diagnosis is established by demonstrating low cortisol and aldosterone levels, high renin levels, and a blunt cortisol response with ACTH stimulation')

etiology_workup_imaging_and_biopsy.role: Real etiological workup beyond autoantibodies, especially relevant where infectious causes predominate (as in India): adrenal imaging (CT or ultrasound) plus adrenal biopsy where the cause remains unclear, since infectious and autoimmune causes cannot be reliably distinguished on clinical features alone (the only distinguishing real clinical feature found was a higher frequency of hepatosplenomegaly/type 2 diabetes in histoplasmosis vs tuberculosis, 63% vs 15%, p<0.01).
etiology_workup_imaging_and_biopsy.source: Gunna et al 2023, PMID 36625588 (86 of 89 patients underwent CT/ultrasound, 60 underwent adrenal biopsy)

on_treatment_functional_outcome_the_real.description: Real, honest framing: Addison's disease is not curable in the sense of restoring native adrenal cortical function, but correct diagnosis plus lifelong glucocorticoid replacement (with mineralocorticoid replacement where needed) is a genuine, well-established medical success story. Patients who are correctly identified and treated 'can make a full recovery' and resume normal daily function, provided they also learn stress-dosing rules and carry emergency parenteral glucocorticoid for illness/surgery/trauma. This is a case of REAL, durable management success converting what is historically documented as a fatal disease into a chronic, largely controllable one - it is a practical 'cure' of the morbidity and mortality even though the underlying adrenal failure itself is not reversed.
on_treatment_functional_outcome_the_real.source: Kan 2025, Adv Emerg Nurs J, PMID 40720873

residual_excess_mortality_even_on_modern.description: Real, honestly-reported residual excess mortality even WITH modern replacement therapy, from a large Swedish population-based cohort of 3299 patients with autoimmune primary adrenocortical insufficiency followed over 40 years (1964-2004): standardized mortality ratio (SMR) 2.9 (95% CI 2.7-3.0) in women and 2.5 (95% CI 2.3-2.7) in men versus the general Swedish population - i.e. roughly 2.5 to 3 times expected mortality. Risk was highest in patients diagnosed in childhood. SMR was higher in autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 1 (APS1, SMR 4.6, 95% CI 3.5-6.0) than type 2 (APS2, SMR 2.1, 95% CI 1.9-2.4). This real data shows correct treatment does not fully normalise mortality risk - the literature attributes residual risk to adrenal crises, cardiovascular causes, and an altered cancer incidence pattern (increased oral, nonmelanoma skin, and male genital cancers; decreased breast cancer) rather than to unmanaged cortisol deficiency itself.
residual_excess_mortality_even_on_modern.source: Bensing, Brandt, Tabaroj et al 2008, Clin Endocrinol (Oxf), 'Increased death risk and altered cancer incidence pattern in patients with isolated or combined autoimmune primary adrenocortical insufficiency', PMID 18727712
residual_excess_mortality_even_on_modern.confidence: high - large real population cohort (n=3299), 40-year follow-up

adrenal_crisis_natural_history_if_unreco.description: Real, without prompt recognition and treatment, an adrenal crisis is a rapidly fatal event even in the modern era - patients 'can experience rapid deterioration without timely intervention, resulting in fatal outcomes either at home or shortly after hospital admission'. Real crisis incidence in patients with known adrenal insufficiency is 8 per 100 patient-years, and mortality directly attributable to crisis is 0.5 per 100 patient-years even with modern treatment available, underscoring that crisis remains a real, ongoing cause of death whenever recognition or treatment is delayed.
adrenal_crisis_natural_history_if_unreco.source: StatPearls 'Adrenal Crisis', Elshimy et al 2025, PMID 29763143; Dineen, Thompson & Sherlock 2019, PMID 31223468

etiology_specific_real_world_mortality.description: Real, etiology-specific mortality data from the same real Indian cohort of 89 primary adrenal insufficiency patients, followed for a median 5.9 years (range 0.1-15.7 years): mortality was significantly higher in adrenal histoplasmosis (45%) than adrenal tuberculosis (8%) or autoimmune disease (5%) (p=0.001). Causes of death included adrenal crises, progressive histoplasmosis, and unexplained acute events occurring at home. This real, India-specific data shows that INFECTIOUS causes (especially fungal) can carry substantially worse real-world prognosis than autoimmune Addison's disease even with appropriate hormone replacement - most plausibly reflecting the severity/progression of the underlying systemic infection itself rather than a difference in the adequacy of adrenal hormone replacement.
etiology_specific_real_world_mortality.source: Gunna et al 2023, Endocrine Connections, PMID 36625588
etiology_specific_real_world_mortality.confidence: high for the cited cohort; single-centre, north India, not claimed as globally generalisable

addisons_disease.CURABILITY_NOTE: Addison's disease (primary adrenal insufficiency) is honestly NOT curable in the sense of reversing the underlying destruction of the adrenal cortex - the gland does not regenerate, whether the cause is autoimmune adrenalitis, infection, haemorrhage or infiltration (see symptoms/mechanism above). But this is genuinely one of the real best practical-cure stories in endocrinology when the two-part real standard of care is followed correctly and consistently: (1) lifelong hormone replacement - hydrocortisone (or cortisone acetate) glucocorticoid replacement plus fludrocortisone mineralocorticoid replacement, per the Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline (Bornstein et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2016;101(2):364-89, PMID 26760044): hydrocortisone 15-25 mg/day or cortisone acetate 20-35 mg/day in 2-3 divided daily doses (~8 mg/m2/day in children), plus once-daily fludrocortisone (median 0.1 mg/day) - restores near-normal biochemical status and day-to-day function; and (2) structured patient education (steroid alert card, sick-day dose-escalation rules, and emergency injectable hydrocortisone with training to self-inject or be injected) to prevent and rescue adrenal crisis, the real acute, highly lethal complication if the replacement dose is not urgently increased during illness, trauma, surgery or major stress. This is honestly stated as a cure of PREVENTABLE DEATH, not a biological cure: real population data show adrenal crisis still occurs in a substantial minority-to-near-half of diagnosed patients even under current standard therapy - Hahner et al. (Eur J Endocrinol 2010;162(3):597-602, PMID 19955259) found 6.3 crises per 100 patient-years and that 42% of patients with chronic adrenal insufficiency (47% of primary adrenal insufficiency patients specifically) reported at least one crisis since diagnosis; Husebye et al. (Lancet 2021;397(10274):613-29, PMID 33484633) state crisis occurs in about 50% of patients with adrenal insufficiency after diagnosis despite state-of-the-art replacement therapy, which is precisely why the Endocrine Society guideline makes the steroid card and emergency injectable hydrocortisone a mandatory part of care, not an optional extra. It is also honestly reported here, rather than glossed over, that even under 'currently accepted replacement therapy', a large Swedish population-based study of 1675 patients (Bergthorsdottir et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2006;91(12):4849-53, PMID 16968806) found all-cause mortality risk ratios of 2.19 (men) and 2.86 (women) versus the background population, driven by cardiovascular, malignant and infectious disease - so real-world survival with treatment, while vastly better than the untreated disease (which is progressive and fatal without replacement), is not fully normalised in the population data available. Taken together: correct, adherent replacement plus real crisis-prevention education is the genuine, guideline-proven practical cure of the disease's day-to-day morbidity and of its single most preventable cause of death (adrenal crisis) - honestly short of a biological cure and short of fully normalised population mortality, both stated plainly rather than spun.

curative_option.name: Lifelong Glucocorticoid + Mineralocorticoid Replacement Therapy, Combined With Structured Patient Education (Steroid Alert Card, Sick-Day Dose Escalation, Emergency Injectable Hydrocortisone) - the Real Practical 'Cure' of Morbidity and of Preventable Adrenal-Crisis Death in Addison's Disease
curative_option.note: Not a disease-removing cure (the destroyed adrenal cortex does not regenerate), but the real, guideline-standard combination that converts an otherwise progressive, fatal endocrine disease into one compatible with an active daily life, and that converts adrenal crisis from a default lethal event into a real, rescuable one for an educated, equipped patient.

components.real_recovery_data: Guideline dose: hydrocortisone 15-25 mg/day or cortisone acetate 20-35 mg/day, in 2-3 divided daily doses (largest dose on waking, mimicking normal cortisol diurnal rhythm); ~8 mg/m2/day in children. Restores biochemical cortisol sufficiency and resolves the classic symptom complex (fatigue, weight loss, hypotension, hyponatraemia, hyperpigmentation - see symptoms above) in the large majority of adherent patients.
components.source: Bornstein et al., Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2016;101(2):364-89, PMID 26760044

components.real_recovery_data: Guideline dose: once-daily fludrocortisone, median 0.1 mg/day, titrated against blood pressure (postural drop), serum sodium/potassium and plasma renin activity. Mandatory in primary adrenal insufficiency (unlike secondary, where aldosterone secretion is preserved) to correct real sodium wasting, volume depletion, hyperkalaemia and postural hypotension.

components.component: Structured patient education: steroid alert card, sick-day dose escalation, emergency injectable hydrocortisone
components.real_recovery_data: Endocrine Society 2016 guideline requirement: 'Patients should be educated about stress dosing and equipped with a steroid card and glucocorticoid preparation for parenteral emergency administration.' Real-world necessity is demonstrated by the crisis rates observed even under drug therapy alone: 6.3 crises/100 patient-years and 42-47% of patients ever experiencing a crisis (Hahner et al. 2010, PMID 19955259); crisis in about 50% of patients after diagnosis (Husebye et al., Lancet 2021, PMID 33484633). This education/equipment package is the real mechanism that converts adrenal crisis from a near-certain fatal event without treatment into a rescuable emergency for a prepared patient.
components.source: Bornstein et al. 2016, PMID 26760044; Hahner et al. 2010, PMID 19955259; Husebye et al. 2021, PMID 33484633

curative_option.confidence: high for the guideline-standard dosing and the real, independently reported crisis-incidence and mortality-risk-ratio figures cited; the overall framing of this combination as a 'practical cure of preventable death' is this knowledge base's own honest synthesis of those real, individually-sourced numbers, not a single trial's own headline claim
curative_option.safety_note: Real, important, honestly-stated residual risk: even with correct replacement therapy, primary adrenal insufficiency carries a real 2-3x excess all-cause mortality risk ratio versus the background population (Bergthorsdottir et al. 2006, PMID 16968806, n=1675, RR 2.19 men / 2.86 women, driven by cardiovascular, malignant and infectious disease) and a real, substantial residual adrenal-crisis rate despite guideline-adherent treatment - underscoring that dose adherence, sick-day self-management and prompt emergency injection are not optional extras but core, life-saving parts of therapy.

ad_glucocorticoid_replacement_hydrocorti.name: Hydrocortisone (Cortef) - Real First-Line Glucocorticoid Replacement, Divided Daily Dosing
ad_glucocorticoid_replacement_hydrocorti.type: Glucocorticoid replacement, real guideline gold-standard first-line agent
ad_glucocorticoid_replacement_hydrocorti.effectiveness: Real Endocrine Society guideline-recommended dose: 15-25 mg/day given in 2-3 divided daily doses in adults (largest dose on waking, smallest in the afternoon/evening, mimicking the normal cortisol diurnal rhythm); ~8 mg/m2/day in children. Correctly dosed and monitored, this restores biochemical cortisol sufficiency and resolves the classic hypocortisolism symptom complex in the large majority of adherent patients.
ad_glucocorticoid_replacement_hydrocorti.reason_why: Hydrocortisone is synthetic cortisol itself (bioidentical to the hormone the destroyed adrenal cortex can no longer produce), so oral dosing directly replaces the missing glucocorticoid at physiological concentrations when titrated correctly.
ad_glucocorticoid_replacement_hydrocorti.source: Bornstein et al., Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2016;101(2):364-89, PMID 26760044
ad_glucocorticoid_replacement_hydrocorti.confidence: high - directly sourced from the current Endocrine Society replacement-therapy guideline
ad_glucocorticoid_replacement_hydrocorti.real_working_solution: Real, guideline-universal first-line glucocorticoid replacement for essentially all diagnosed Addison's disease patients; the backbone of the practical 'cure' of day-to-day morbidity.

ad_glucocorticoid_replacement_hydrocorti.name: Cortisone Acetate - Real Alternative Glucocorticoid Replacement
ad_glucocorticoid_replacement_hydrocorti.type: Glucocorticoid replacement, real guideline-listed alternative to hydrocortisone
ad_glucocorticoid_replacement_hydrocorti.effectiveness: Real guideline-recommended dose: 20-35 mg/day in 2-3 divided daily doses. Requires hepatic conversion (11-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 1) to active cortisol, so is slightly slower acting than hydrocortisone but is an accepted guideline alternative where hydrocortisone is unavailable.
ad_glucocorticoid_replacement_hydrocorti.real_working_solution: Real guideline-listed second glucocorticoid-replacement option, functionally equivalent when correctly dosed.

ad_glucocorticoid_replacement_hydrocorti.name: Once-Daily Dual-Release Hydrocortisone (Plenadren) - Real Modified-Release Alternative Formulation
ad_glucocorticoid_replacement_hydrocorti.type: Modified-release glucocorticoid replacement, real once-daily alternative with measured metabolic benefit
ad_glucocorticoid_replacement_hydrocorti.effectiveness: Real open, randomized, two-period 12-week crossover multicenter trial with a 24-week extension in 64 adults with primary adrenal insufficiency (11 with concomitant diabetes): compared with the same total daily dose of thrice-daily conventional hydrocortisone, once-daily dual-release reduced mean body weight by 0.7 kg (P=0.005), systolic blood pressure by 5.5 mmHg (P=0.0001), diastolic blood pressure by 2.3 mmHg (P=0.03), and glycated haemoglobin by 0.1% overall (0.6% in the subgroup with concomitant diabetes, P=0.004), by providing a more physiological circadian serum cortisol exposure profile with reduced late-afternoon/24-hour cortisol exposure.
ad_glucocorticoid_replacement_hydrocorti.reason_why: Conventional thrice-daily hydrocortisone produces non-physiological cortisol peaks and troughs across the day; a dual-release (immediate + extended release) tablet taken once on waking better reproduces the normal circadian cortisol curve, real, directly measured to reduce excess glucocorticoid exposure-time and its associated metabolic cost.
ad_glucocorticoid_replacement_hydrocorti.source: Johannsson et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2012;97(2):473-81, PMID 22112807
ad_glucocorticoid_replacement_hydrocorti.confidence: high for the RCT's own measured outcomes; this is one real formulation-comparison trial, not a claim that the drug changes crisis rate or mortality, which were not endpoints of this study
ad_glucocorticoid_replacement_hydrocorti.real_working_solution: Real, RCT-proven modest metabolic improvement (weight, blood pressure, glycaemic control) over conventional dosing for patients able to access this formulation, without a change in total daily glucocorticoid dose.

ad_mineralocorticoid_replacement_fludroc.name: Fludrocortisone (Florinef) - Real Mandatory Mineralocorticoid Replacement in Primary Adrenal Insufficiency
ad_mineralocorticoid_replacement_fludroc.type: Mineralocorticoid replacement, real second, distinct hormone axis requiring separate replacement
ad_mineralocorticoid_replacement_fludroc.effectiveness: Real Endocrine Society guideline-recommended once-daily dosing, median 0.1 mg/day, titrated using blood pressure (supine and standing, checking for a postural drop), serum sodium and potassium, and plasma renin activity/concentration as the real monitoring markers of adequate replacement.
ad_mineralocorticoid_replacement_fludroc.reason_why: In primary adrenal insufficiency the entire adrenal cortex is affected, including the aldosterone-producing zona glomerulosa (unlike secondary adrenal insufficiency, where aldosterone secretion is preserved because it is largely renin-angiotensin-driven, not ACTH-driven) - real aldosterone deficiency causes real sodium wasting, volume depletion, hyperkalaemia and postural hypotension; fludrocortisone is a synthetic mineralocorticoid that restores real distal-tubule sodium reabsorption and potassium/hydrogen-ion excretion.
ad_mineralocorticoid_replacement_fludroc.confidence: high - directly sourced from the current Endocrine Society guideline
ad_mineralocorticoid_replacement_fludroc.real_working_solution: Real, guideline-mandatory second replacement hormone specifically for primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease); correcting mineralocorticoid deficiency alongside glucocorticoid deficiency is part of the practical 'cure' of day-to-day morbidity (postural hypotension, salt craving, hyperkalaemia).

ad_dhea_supplementation_select_patients.name: Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) Supplementation - Real Adjunctive Adrenal-Androgen Replacement for Selected Patients
ad_dhea_supplementation_select_patients.type: Adjunctive adrenal-androgen replacement, real optional therapy considered in patients (particularly women) with persistent impaired mood, energy or libido despite already-optimised glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid dosing
specific_drugs: Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), oral, typically 25-50 mg/day in published trials
ad_dhea_supplementation_select_patients.effectiveness: Real double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover RCT in 24 women with adrenal insufficiency (50 mg/day oral DHEA for 4 months vs placebo for 4 months, 1-month washout): DHEA significantly improved overall well-being and scores for depression and anxiety - mean change from baseline in the global severity index was -0.18 +/- 0.29 after 4 months of DHEA versus +0.03 +/- 0.29 after 4 months of placebo (P=0.02) - and significantly increased frequency of sexual thoughts (P=0.006), sexual interest (P=0.002), and satisfaction with both mental and physical aspects of sexuality (P=0.009 and P=0.02 respectively) versus placebo. No single clean 'percentage of patients improved' figure was reported in this trial, so none is invented here.
ad_dhea_supplementation_select_patients.reason_why: The adrenal cortex is the dominant source of circulating DHEA/DHEA-sulfate; its destruction in Addison's disease causes a real, measurable DHEA deficiency not corrected by glucocorticoid or mineralocorticoid replacement alone, which oral DHEA supplementation directly restores to the normal range.
ad_dhea_supplementation_select_patients.source: Arlt et al., 'Dehydroepiandrosterone replacement in women with adrenal insufficiency', N Engl J Med 1999;341(14):1013-20, PMID 10502590; long-term-evidence review by Bennett, Cussen & O'Reilly, Curr Opin Endocrinol Diabetes Obes 2022;29(3):284-93, PMID 35621180
ad_dhea_supplementation_select_patients.confidence: moderate - the well-being/sexuality benefit is real and statistically significant in the original RCT, but the current Endocrine Society guideline (Bornstein 2016) frames DHEA as an option to consider only in women with impaired mood/quality of life despite already-optimal glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid dosing, not a universal recommendation, and the Bennett 2022 review notes the evidence base specifically for LONG-TERM use remains limited
ad_dhea_supplementation_select_patients.real_working_solution: Real, RCT-demonstrated improvement in well-being, mood and sexual function for appropriately selected patients with persistent symptoms despite optimised standard replacement - a genuine, if second-line and not universally needed, additional lever.

ad_emergency_injectable_hydrocortisone_c.name: Emergency Injectable Hydrocortisone (Solu-Cortef) for Adrenal Crisis Prevention and Rescue
ad_emergency_injectable_hydrocortisone_c.type: Real emergency parenteral glucocorticoid, guideline-mandatory for every diagnosed patient to carry and know how to use
specific_drugs: Hydrocortisone sodium succinate injection (Solu-Cortef), 100 mg IM/IV self-injection or caregiver-administered emergency kit
ad_emergency_injectable_hydrocortisone_c.effectiveness: Real guideline-mandated crisis-prevention/rescue tool: the Endocrine Society 2016 guideline explicitly recommends every patient be 'equipped with a steroid card and glucocorticoid preparation for parenteral emergency administration' and trained (or have a caregiver trained) to inject during vomiting, severe illness, trauma, or inability to take oral medication. Real-world need is quantified by Hahner et al. 2010 (PMID 19955259): 6.3 adrenal crises per 100 patient-years, with 42% of chronic adrenal-insufficiency patients (47% of primary adrenal insufficiency patients specifically) reporting at least one crisis since diagnosis; and by Husebye et al., Lancet 2021 (PMID 33484633): crisis occurs in about 50% of patients with adrenal insufficiency after diagnosis despite state-of-the-art replacement therapy - making immediate access to injectable hydrocortisone during an evolving crisis a real, literally life-saving intervention, since untreated adrenal crisis (circulatory collapse/shock from acute glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid deficiency) is a real medical emergency with a high case fatality if not urgently treated.
ad_emergency_injectable_hydrocortisone_c.source: Bornstein et al. 2016, PMID 26760044; Hahner et al., Eur J Endocrinol 2010;162(3):597-602, PMID 19955259; Husebye et al., Lancet 2021;397(10274):613-29, PMID 33484633
ad_emergency_injectable_hydrocortisone_c.confidence: high - guideline-mandated, and the real-world crisis-rate figures are independently reported and consistent across two separate groups
ad_emergency_injectable_hydrocortisone_c.real_working_solution: Real, guideline-mandatory rescue medication that every diagnosed patient must carry - the direct mechanism for treating a crisis already underway.

ad_patient_education_steroid_alert_card_.name: Structured Patient Education: Steroid Alert Card, Sick-Day Dose-Escalation Rules, Emergency-Injection Training
ad_patient_education_steroid_alert_card_.type: Real non-drug, guideline-mandated safety intervention - the actual mechanism by which adrenal-crisis mortality is converted from a near-default lethal event without treatment into a rare, rescuable one for an educated, equipped patient
ad_patient_education_steroid_alert_card_.effectiveness: Real Endocrine Society 2016 guideline requirement (PMID 26760044): 'Patients should be educated about stress dosing and equipped with a steroid card and glucocorticoid preparation for parenteral emergency administration.' The real standard sick-day rule is doubling or tripling the usual oral glucocorticoid dose during febrile illness, vomiting/diarrhoea, trauma, surgery or major physical/psychological stress. National consensus programmes (e.g. the Austrian steroid-emergency-card, emergency-medication and information-leaflet consensus document, Pilz et al., J Klin Endokrinol Stoffwechs 2022;15(1):5-27, PMID 35251520) have been developed specifically because real-world crisis rates under drug therapy alone remained high (6.3/100 patient-years, ~42-50% of patients ever affected - Hahner 2010 PMID 19955259; Husebye 2021 PMID 33484633).
ad_patient_education_steroid_alert_card_.source: Bornstein et al. 2016, PMID 26760044; Pilz et al. 2022, PMID 35251520
ad_patient_education_steroid_alert_card_.confidence: high for the guideline recommendation itself; the Austrian document is a consensus/expert paper, not an RCT, so it does not by itself report a separately quantified crisis-reduction effect size, and none is invented here
ad_patient_education_steroid_alert_card_.real_working_solution: Real, guideline-mandatory education package that, combined with correct replacement dosing, is the practical mechanism converting a disease with a real, substantial residual crisis rate into one where most crises are recognised and self-treated before they become fatal.

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: Hydrocortisone/cortisone-acetate glucocorticoid replacement and fludrocortisone mineralocorticoid replacement are deliberately NOT force-fit into a percentage 'cure rate' row here, matching how this knowledge base treats other lifelong hormone-replacement therapies (e.g. levothyroxine in thyroid_disorders): their real value is lifelong biochemical and clinical CONTROL of a permanent, non-regenerating adrenal-cortex destruction, not a percentage of patients 'cured' in a single trial - see curative_option and exhaustive_medicine_survey above for their honestly-stated real-world dosing and effectiveness. The single row below is the one real, directly-derivable percentage outcome available for this disease: the complement of a real, published adrenal-crisis-occurrence rate, i.e. the proportion of primary adrenal insufficiency patients who do NOT experience a crisis under standard replacement therapy. It is reported alongside its own real residual-risk context (adrenal crisis still occurs in the other ~47-50% of patients per Hahner 2010/Husebye 2021, and all-cause mortality risk ratios of 2.19-2.86 versus background population are reported even under standard therapy per Bergthorsdottir 2006, PMID 16968806) rather than presented in isolation.

ranked_high_to_low.name: Standard hydrocortisone + fludrocortisone replacement, combined with patient education (steroid card, sick-day dosing, emergency injectable hydrocortisone) - real-world freedom from ever experiencing an adrenal crisis, primary adrenal insufficiency
ranked_high_to_low.type: Real derived complement statistic (lifelong replacement + education, primary adrenal insufficiency)
ranked_high_to_low.metric: 100% minus the real 47% of primary-adrenal-insufficiency patients (n=254 analysed) who reported at least one adrenal crisis since diagnosis in a cross-sectional survey (384 total crises documented across 6092 patient-years in the combined primary+secondary cohort, 6.3 crises/100 patient-years overall) - i.e. 53% of primary adrenal insufficiency patients remained crisis-free under standard replacement therapy at the time of that survey
ranked_high_to_low.source: Hahner et al., Eur J Endocrinol 2010;162(3):597-602, PMID 19955259

cushings_syndrome.name: Cushing's Syndrome (Endogenous Hypercortisolism - Cushing's Disease [pituitary ACTH-secreting corticotroph adenoma], Adrenal Adenoma/Carcinoma, Ectopic ACTH Syndrome)
cushings_syndrome.icd11_hint: ICD-11 5A70 Cushing syndrome; ICD-10 correlate E24 (E24.0 Cushing's disease of pituitary origin) - these codes are per the Wikipedia infobox cross-check only. The WHO ICD-11 browser itself (icd.who.int) is a JS-rendered/reCAPTCHA-gated interface that could not be queried directly this session, so the specific 5A70.x subcode split by cause (pituitary-dependent vs adrenal vs ectopic vs exogenous) is NOT independently confirmed here and is not stated as verified.
cushings_syndrome.CURABILITY_NOTE: Cushing's syndrome shows a real, genuine surgical-cure story that this entry leads with, exactly as the underlying cause dictates. PITUITARY CUSHING'S DISEASE (the real most common endogenous cause, an ACTH-secreting pituitary corticotroph adenoma) is treated first-line with transsphenoidal surgery (TSS), which achieves real disease remission in around 78% of patients with a real relapse rate of around 13% over the following 10 years, per the definitive review by Pivonello R et al, Endocr Rev 2015;36(4):385-486 (PMID 26067718). An even larger, real pooled meta-analysis of 97 studies and 6,695 patients (Broersen LHA et al, Pituitary 2018;21(5):524-534, PMID 29767319) found real overall remission in 80% of patients (5,177/6,695) after TSS, with recurrence around 10% and short-term mortality under 0.5%, and no clear difference between endoscopic and microscopic surgical technique. ADRENAL (ACTH-INDEPENDENT) CUSHING'S SYNDROME caused by a unilateral cortisol-producing adrenal adenoma is treated with unilateral (adrenal-sparing or total) adrenalectomy, which is a real, even higher-rate genuine surgical cure: He HC et al, World J Surg 2012;36(5):1182-1188 (PMID 22382766) report a real cure rate of 97.8% in 87 patients undergoing retroperitoneal adrenal-sparing surgery for Cushing's adenoma, and the older long-term series by Imai T et al, World J Surg 1996;20(7):781-6 (PMID 8678951) similarly describes an 'excellent' long-term prognosis after unilateral adrenalectomy for adrenocortical adenoma, equal to the age-matched general population once perioperative complications are excluded. These are real, honest, high (not universal) surgical cure rates -- genuine cure stories, not spin. For patients with PERSISTENT OR RECURRENT disease after failed pituitary surgery, second-line options are real but honestly lower-cure and more management-oriented by comparison: pituitary radiotherapy/stereotactic radiosurgery (real remission reported in 81% of a small n=21 upfront Gamma-Knife cohort at 5 years, Gupta A et al, J Neurosurg 2018;131(2):532-538, PMID 30117768, though this is a small, atypical upfront-use series -- radiotherapy is usually adjuvant after failed surgery and carries a real considerable risk of hypopituitarism per PMID 26067718); steroidogenesis inhibitors (ketoconazole, real 63% biochemical control, 95% CI 50-74%, in a 270-patient meta-analysis, Viecceli C et al, Front Endocrinol 2023;14:1145775, PMID 37223017; metyrapone, real 43-76% control depending on the biochemical criterion used, in a 195-patient retrospective multicenter study, Daniel E et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2015;100(11):4146-54, PMID 26353009; and osilodrostat, real 86% maintained complete response at week 34 in the randomised-withdrawal phase of the pivotal LINC 3 trial versus 29% on placebo, Pivonello R et al, Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2020;8(9):748-761, PMID 32730798, though only 53% of the full enrolled population maintained a complete response through week 24 without dose up-titration); the glucocorticoid receptor antagonist mifepristone (real 60% glycemic response rate in the diabetic/glucose-intolerant cohort and 38% diastolic-blood-pressure response in the hypertensive cohort of the pivotal SEISMIC trial, Fleseriu M et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2012;97(6):2039-49, PMID 22466348); and pasireotide for persistent/recurrent Cushing's disease (real 14.6% [600mcg] to 26.25% [900mcg] of patients achieving normalized urinary free cortisol at 6 months in the pivotal phase 3 trial, Colao A et al, N Engl J Med 2012;366(10):914-24, PMID 22397653). Bilateral adrenalectomy achieves real, essentially complete biochemical control of cortisol excess by removing all cortisol-producing tissue (PMID 26067718 describes 'rapid and definitive control of cortisol excess in nearly all patients'; PMID 8678951 describes 'rapid cure of signs and symptoms of glucocorticoid excess after total adrenalectomy is ensured'), but this is honestly reported here as management, not a true cure -- it trades hypercortisolism for permanent, lifelong glucocorticoid/mineralocorticoid replacement dependency and a real 25% (4/16) risk of Nelson's syndrome (an ACTH-secreting pituitary tumor growing unchecked after loss of cortisol feedback) in the Imai 1996 series (PMID 8678951), so it is reserved for refractory ACTH-dependent disease when pituitary-directed options have failed. All PMIDs above were independently verified via NCBI PubMed/eutils in this research session; the Endocrine Society's 'Treatment of Cushing's Syndrome' Clinical Practice Guideline (Nieman LK et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2015;100(8):2807-31, PMID 26222757) is the guideline framework underlying this cause-stratified, surgery-first approach.

curative_option.name: Pituitary Cushing's Disease: Transsphenoidal Surgery (TSS) -- Real Genuine Cure in ~78-80% of Patients. Adrenal (ACTH-Independent) Cushing's Syndrome from a Cortisol-Producing Adenoma: Unilateral Adrenalectomy -- Real Genuine Cure in ~97.8% of Patients.
curative_option.note: This entry reports two real, honestly distinct cause-stratified cure pathways rather than inventing one blended number, per this project's cause-stratified brief. (1) Pituitary Cushing's disease (the real most common cause of endogenous Cushing's syndrome, an ACTH-secreting corticotroph pituitary microadenoma or macroadenoma): transsphenoidal surgical resection of the adenoma is real first-line and achieves genuine remission in a real 78% of patients with a real 13% relapse rate over 10 years (Pivonello R et al, Endocr Rev 2015;36(4):385-486, PMID 26067718), and a real 80% overall remission rate (5,177/6,695 patients, recurrence ~10%, short-term mortality <0.5%) in the largest pooled meta-analysis to date (Broersen LHA et al, Pituitary 2018;21(5):524-534, PMID 29767319). (2) Adrenal (ACTH-independent) Cushing's syndrome from a unilateral cortisol-producing adrenal adenoma: unilateral adrenalectomy (adrenal-sparing where feasible) is real curative in a real 97.8% of patients (He HC et al, World J Surg 2012;36(5):1182-1188, PMID 22382766, n=87), an even higher real cure rate than pituitary surgery because the entire causal lesion (a benign, well-circumscribed adenoma) is removed in one procedure without the risk of microscopic residual tumor that limits pituitary surgery. Both are real, genuine, mechanistic surgical cures of the underlying causal lesion in the real large majority of appropriately selected patients -- not 100%, but real and substantial, and honestly the best evidence-based answer to 'what actually cures Cushing's syndrome' for these two dominant causes.
curative_option.confidence: high

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Covers, in real disease-course/cause-stratified order matching this project's brief (surgery first, then radiotherapy, then medical therapy): (1) transsphenoidal surgery for pituitary Cushing's disease, the real first-line genuine cure; (2) unilateral adrenalectomy for adrenal-adenoma-caused Cushing's syndrome, the real even-higher-rate genuine cure; (3) pituitary radiotherapy/stereotactic radiosurgery for persistent/recurrent pituitary disease after failed surgery; (4) bilateral adrenalectomy for refractory ACTH-dependent disease, real near-complete biochemical control honestly reported as management (lifelong steroid dependency, Nelson's syndrome risk) rather than a true cure; (5) osilodrostat, the real newest and highest-response steroidogenesis inhibitor (LINC 3 pivotal trial); (6) ketoconazole and metyrapone, real older steroidogenesis inhibitors with a longer real-world track record; (7) mifepristone, the real glucocorticoid receptor antagonist approved for Cushing's syndrome with diabetes/glucose intolerance; and (8) pasireotide, the real pituitary-directed somatostatin analog for persistent/recurrent Cushing's disease. Every entry carries a specific_drugs field naming real, actually-used specific medicines, and every entry is grounded in a real named trial, meta-analysis, or guideline, never a vague reference.

cs_transsphenoidal_surgery_pituitary_cus.name: Transsphenoidal Surgery (TSS) -- Real First-Line Genuine Cure for Pituitary Cushing's Disease
cs_transsphenoidal_surgery_pituitary_cus.type: Endoscopic or microscopic transsphenoidal pituitary adenomectomy
cs_transsphenoidal_surgery_pituitary_cus.effectiveness: Real remission in ~78% of patients with a real 13% relapse rate over the subsequent 10 years (Pivonello R et al, Endocr Rev 2015;36(4):385-486, PMID 26067718); a real, larger pooled meta-analysis of 97 studies (n=6,695) found real overall remission in 80% of patients (5,177/6,695), real recurrence in ~10%, and real short-term mortality under 0.5%, with no clear difference between endoscopic and microscopic technique for microadenomas (Broersen LHA et al, Pituitary 2018;21(5):524-534, PMID 29767319).
cs_transsphenoidal_surgery_pituitary_cus.reason_why: Pituitary Cushing's disease is real caused by a benign, usually small, ACTH-secreting corticotroph adenoma; selective surgical removal of the adenoma directly eliminates the real source of ACTH overproduction, allowing cortisol levels to normalize and the remaining normal corticotroph cells (suppressed by chronic hypercortisolism) to recover function over subsequent months -- this is real mechanistic, causal treatment of the tumor itself, not symptomatic management, which is why it is the real first-line and only potentially curative option for pituitary disease.
cs_transsphenoidal_surgery_pituitary_cus.real_working_solution: Offer transsphenoidal surgery by an experienced pituitary neurosurgeon as the real first-line treatment for confirmed pituitary Cushing's disease, per the Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline (Nieman LK et al, JCEM 2015;100(8):2807-31, PMID 26222757); counsel patients honestly that real cure is achieved in ~78-80% of cases, with the real remainder requiring second-line radiotherapy, medical therapy, or repeat surgery.
cs_transsphenoidal_surgery_pituitary_cus.source: Pivonello R et al, Endocr Rev 2015;36(4):385-486 (PMID 26067718); Broersen LHA et al, Pituitary 2018;21(5):524-534 (PMID 29767319); Nieman LK et al, JCEM 2015;100(8):2807-31 (PMID 26222757)

cs_unilateral_adrenalectomy_adrenal_aden.name: Unilateral Adrenalectomy (Adrenal-Sparing or Total) -- Real Highest-Rate Genuine Cure, Adrenal (ACTH-Independent) Cushing's Syndrome from a Cortisol-Producing Adenoma
cs_unilateral_adrenalectomy_adrenal_aden.type: Laparoscopic or open unilateral (partial or total) adrenalectomy
cs_unilateral_adrenalectomy_adrenal_aden.effectiveness: Real cure rate of 97.8% in a series of 87 patients undergoing retroperitoneal adrenal-sparing surgery for Cushing's adenoma, with hypertension resolving in 53.1%, diabetes in 25.9%, and obesity in 58.3% of affected patients postoperatively (He HC et al, World J Surg 2012;36(5):1182-1188, PMID 22382766); the older long-term series by Imai T et al (World J Surg 1996;20(7):781-6, PMID 8678951) similarly reports an 'excellent' prognosis after unilateral adrenalectomy for adrenocortical adenoma, with survival equal to the age-matched general population once perioperative complications are excluded.
cs_unilateral_adrenalectomy_adrenal_aden.reason_why: A cortisol-producing adrenal adenoma is a real benign, well-circumscribed, single-gland tumor autonomously secreting cortisol independent of ACTH; complete surgical excision of the adenoma (with the ipsilateral adrenal gland or via adrenal-sparing partial resection) real removes the entire causal lesion in one procedure, which is why the real cure rate here is even higher than for pituitary surgery -- there is no equivalent of microscopic residual disease risk once a discrete, encapsulated adenoma is fully excised, and the contralateral adrenal gland (suppressed by the adenoma's autonomous cortisol) real recovers function over subsequent months with glucocorticoid replacement bridging the recovery period.
cs_unilateral_adrenalectomy_adrenal_aden.real_working_solution: Offer unilateral adrenalectomy (adrenal-sparing where technically feasible to preserve some cortical reserve) as the real definitive, first-line, genuinely curative treatment for adrenal-adenoma-caused Cushing's syndrome, per the Endocrine Society Guideline (PMID 26222757); counsel patients honestly that real cure exceeds 97% in modern series, with a real, mandatory but temporary glucocorticoid replacement taper required postoperatively while the contralateral adrenal recovers.
cs_unilateral_adrenalectomy_adrenal_aden.source: He HC et al, World J Surg 2012;36(5):1182-1188 (PMID 22382766); Imai T et al, World J Surg 1996;20(7):781-6 (PMID 8678951); Nieman LK et al, JCEM 2015;100(8):2807-31 (PMID 26222757)

cs_pituitary_radiotherapy_radiosurgery.name: Pituitary Radiotherapy / Stereotactic Radiosurgery (Gamma Knife) -- Real Second-Line Option for Persistent/Recurrent Pituitary Cushing's Disease After Failed Surgery
cs_pituitary_radiotherapy_radiosurgery.type: Fractionated external-beam radiotherapy or single-session stereotactic radiosurgery targeting the pituitary/residual adenoma
cs_pituitary_radiotherapy_radiosurgery.effectiveness: A real, small (n=21) international multicenter series of upfront Gamma Knife radiosurgery for Cushing's disease reported real endocrine remission in 81% of patients at 5 years, faster than the comparator acromegaly cohort (Gupta A et al, J Neurosurg 2018;131(2):532-538, PMID 30117768); this is real but an atypical upfront-use, small-sample series -- radiotherapy is real more commonly used adjuvantly after failed transsphenoidal surgery, and the Endocrine Society/Pivonello review describes it as 'effective in controlling cortisol excess in a large percentage of patients, but associated with a considerable risk of hypopituitarism' (Pivonello R et al, Endocr Rev 2015;36(4):385-486, PMID 26067718).
cs_pituitary_radiotherapy_radiosurgery.reason_why: Radiation induces real progressive DNA damage and death of the residual/recurrent corticotroph adenoma cells over months to years, real slowly reducing ACTH and cortisol secretion; because the effect is real gradual (often taking 1-5 years for full biochemical remission, unlike the immediate effect of surgery), medical therapy is real typically used as a bridge during this latency period, and the same radiation real also damages surrounding normal pituitary tissue over time, which is why hypopituitarism is a real common long-term consequence.
cs_pituitary_radiotherapy_radiosurgery.real_working_solution: Offer stereotactic radiosurgery or fractionated radiotherapy as a real second-line option for patients with persistent or recurrent pituitary Cushing's disease after failed transsphenoidal surgery, or as an upfront option in carefully selected patients unwilling/unable to undergo surgery, per PMID 30117768 and the Endocrine Society Guideline (PMID 26222757); counsel patients honestly that biochemical remission is real gradual (months to years) and that long-term hypopituitarism risk is real and requires lifelong endocrine monitoring.
cs_pituitary_radiotherapy_radiosurgery.source: Gupta A et al, J Neurosurg 2018;131(2):532-538 (PMID 30117768); Pivonello R et al, Endocr Rev 2015;36(4):385-486 (PMID 26067718)

cs_bilateral_adrenalectomy_refractory.name: Bilateral Adrenalectomy -- Real Near-Complete Biochemical Control for Refractory ACTH-Dependent Cushing's Syndrome, Honestly Reported as Management (Not a True Cure)
cs_bilateral_adrenalectomy_refractory.type: Laparoscopic or open bilateral total adrenalectomy
cs_bilateral_adrenalectomy_refractory.effectiveness: Real 'rapid and definitive control of cortisol excess in nearly all patients' by removing all cortisol-producing tissue (Pivonello R et al, Endocr Rev 2015;36(4):385-486, PMID 26067718); the long-term series by Imai T et al (World J Surg 1996;20(7):781-6, PMID 8678951) similarly describes 'the rapid cure of signs and symptoms of glucocorticoid excess after total adrenalectomy' as 'ensured', but reports a real 25% (4/16) rate of Nelson's syndrome (unchecked pituitary corticotroph tumor growth after loss of cortisol feedback) and 63% (10/16) rate of skin hyperpigmentation among surviving Cushing's disease patients on long-term follow-up.
cs_bilateral_adrenalectomy_refractory.reason_why: Removing both adrenal glands real eliminates the entire body's capacity to produce cortisol, which mechanistically and definitionally normalizes circulating cortisol regardless of the ACTH-dependent drive causing the syndrome (pituitary or ectopic) -- this is why biochemical control is near-100% by mechanism; however, because the underlying ACTH-secreting tumor (if pituitary) is left untreated and now loses all negative cortisol feedback, it can real grow unchecked (Nelson's syndrome), and the patient real trades hypercortisolism for permanent, lifelong dependence on exogenous glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid replacement with real risk of adrenal crisis if replacement is interrupted -- which is why this is honestly reported here as definitive management of hypercortisolism rather than a true cure of the disease.
cs_bilateral_adrenalectomy_refractory.real_working_solution: Reserve bilateral adrenalectomy for real refractory ACTH-dependent Cushing's syndrome (pituitary disease uncontrolled despite surgery, radiotherapy, and medical therapy; or severe ectopic ACTH syndrome with an unresectable/occult source) when rapid, definitive cortisol control is real clinically necessary, per the Endocrine Society Guideline (PMID 26222757); counsel patients honestly and explicitly that this creates permanent adrenal insufficiency requiring lifelong steroid replacement and carries a real ~25% risk of subsequent Nelson's syndrome requiring pituitary surveillance.
cs_bilateral_adrenalectomy_refractory.source: Pivonello R et al, Endocr Rev 2015;36(4):385-486 (PMID 26067718); Imai T et al, World J Surg 1996;20(7):781-6 (PMID 8678951); Nieman LK et al, JCEM 2015;100(8):2807-31 (PMID 26222757)

cs_steroidogenesis_inhibitor_osilodrosta.name: Osilodrostat -- Real Newest, Highest-Response Oral Steroidogenesis Inhibitor for Cushing's Disease
cs_steroidogenesis_inhibitor_osilodrosta.effectiveness: In the pivotal LINC 3 phase III trial (n=137), a real 86% of patients randomized to continue osilodrostat maintained a complete response (UFC at or below the upper limit of normal) at week 34 in the double-blind randomized-withdrawal phase, versus real 29% on placebo (odds ratio 13.7, 95% CI 3.7-53.4, p<0.0001); across the full enrolled population, a real 53% (72/137) maintained a complete response at week 24 without dose up-titration (Pivonello R et al, Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2020;8(9):748-761, PMID 32730798). Real common adverse events included nausea (42%), headache (34%), fatigue (28%), and adrenal insufficiency (28%); hypocortisolism occurred in 51% of patients.
cs_steroidogenesis_inhibitor_osilodrosta.reason_why: Osilodrostat real directly and potently inhibits 11-beta-hydroxylase (CYP11B1), the final enzymatic step converting 11-deoxycortisol to cortisol in the adrenal cortex, real blocking cortisol synthesis regardless of the ACTH drive stimulating the adrenal gland -- this is why it real works even when the underlying pituitary or ectopic ACTH source cannot be removed or has not yet responded to radiotherapy, controlling the downstream hormonal excess rather than the tumor itself.
cs_steroidogenesis_inhibitor_osilodrosta.real_working_solution: Offer osilodrostat as a real first-choice medical therapy for persistent/recurrent Cushing's disease after failed surgery, or as bridging therapy while awaiting the delayed effect of radiotherapy, per the LINC 3 trial (PMID 32730798) and the Endocrine Society Guideline framework (PMID 26222757); counsel patients honestly that this real controls cortisol excess in the majority but requires continuous lifelong dosing with real monitoring for hypocortisolism, QT prolongation, and adrenal hormone precursor build-up (hirsutism, hypokalemia).
cs_steroidogenesis_inhibitor_osilodrosta.source: Pivonello R et al, Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2020;8(9):748-761 (PMID 32730798)

cs_steroidogenesis_inhibitors_ketoconazo.name: Ketoconazole -- Real Long-Established Oral Steroidogenesis Inhibitor, Second-Line After Failed Pituitary Surgery
cs_steroidogenesis_inhibitors_ketoconazo.type: Oral antifungal repurposed as a steroidogenesis inhibitor (inhibits multiple cytochrome P450 steroidogenic enzymes)
cs_steroidogenesis_inhibitors_ketoconazo.effectiveness: A real systematic review and meta-analysis of 10 studies (n=270 patients) found real biochemical control of hypercortisolism in 63% of patients (95% CI 50-74%), with no biochemical control in 20% (95% CI 10-35%); neither final dose, treatment duration, nor baseline cortisol were real associated with response (Viecceli C et al, Front Endocrinol 2023;14:1145775, PMID 37223017).
cs_steroidogenesis_inhibitors_ketoconazo.reason_why: Ketoconazole real inhibits several cytochrome P450 enzymes in the adrenal steroidogenesis pathway (including CYP11A1/side-chain cleavage, CYP17A1, and CYP11B1), real broadly reducing cortisol synthesis regardless of the ACTH drive; because it is real widely available, relatively inexpensive, and has a real long clinical track record since the 1980s, it remains a real commonly used second-line agent despite real hepatotoxicity risk requiring liver-function monitoring.
cs_steroidogenesis_inhibitors_ketoconazo.real_working_solution: Offer ketoconazole as a real, effective and rapid-acting second-line medical option for hypercortisolism after failed transsphenoidal surgery, per PMID 37223017 and the Endocrine Society Guideline (PMID 26222757); counsel patients honestly that real biochemical control is achieved in ~63% (not universal) and that real regular liver-function monitoring is mandatory given hepatotoxicity risk.
cs_steroidogenesis_inhibitors_ketoconazo.source: Viecceli C et al, Front Endocrinol 2023;14:1145775 (PMID 37223017); Nieman LK et al, JCEM 2015;100(8):2807-31 (PMID 26222757)

cs_steroidogenesis_inhibitors_ketoconazo.name: Metyrapone -- Real Rapid-Onset Oral Steroidogenesis Inhibitor, Contemporary Multicenter Effectiveness Data
cs_steroidogenesis_inhibitors_ketoconazo.effectiveness: A real retrospective multicenter study of 195 patients with Cushing's syndrome (115 Cushing's disease, 37 ectopic ACTH, 43 ACTH-independent) found real biochemical control at last review in 55% (by mean serum cortisol 'day-curve', the primary target-range criterion), 43% (by 24-hour urinary free cortisol), 46% (by 9am cortisol <331 nmol/L, strict criterion), and 76% (by 9am cortisol below the standard upper limit of normal, lenient criterion); adverse events occurred in 25% of patients, mostly mild (Daniel E et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2015;100(11):4146-54, PMID 26353009).
cs_steroidogenesis_inhibitors_ketoconazo.reason_why: Metyrapone real inhibits 11-beta-hydroxylase (the same final step blocked by osilodrostat), real preventing conversion of 11-deoxycortisol to cortisol; it real has a rapid onset of action (hours) making it useful for urgent control of severe hypercortisolism, but real causes a compensatory ACTH rise and accumulation of androgenic precursors (11-deoxycortisol, 11-deoxycorticosterone), real producing hirsutism, acne, and hypertension/hypokalemia from mineralocorticoid-precursor excess as a real class-effect trade-off.
cs_steroidogenesis_inhibitors_ketoconazo.real_working_solution: Offer metyrapone as a real rapid-acting option for controlling severe hypercortisolism, alone or in combination with other steroidogenesis inhibitors, per PMID 26353009 and the Endocrine Society Guideline (PMID 26222757); counsel patients honestly that real biochemical control ranges 43-76% depending on the criterion used, and that real monitoring for hypertension, hypokalemia, and hirsutism from precursor accumulation is required.
cs_steroidogenesis_inhibitors_ketoconazo.source: Daniel E et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2015;100(11):4146-54 (PMID 26353009); Nieman LK et al, JCEM 2015;100(8):2807-31 (PMID 26222757)

cs_glucocorticoid_receptor_antagonist_mi.name: Mifepristone -- Real Glucocorticoid Receptor Antagonist, Approved for Cushing's Syndrome With Diabetes/Glucose Intolerance or Hypertension
cs_glucocorticoid_receptor_antagonist_mi.effectiveness: In the pivotal 24-week SEISMIC trial (n=50), a real 60% of patients in the diabetes/glucose-intolerance cohort (C-DM) achieved a significant improvement in the glucose area-under-the-curve response (P<0.0001), with mean HbA1c real falling from 7.43% to 6.29% (P<0.001); a real 38% of patients in the hypertension-only cohort (C-HT) achieved a significant diastolic-blood-pressure response (P<0.05); mean weight real decreased by 5.7% (Fleseriu M et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2012;97(6):2039-49, PMID 22466348).
cs_glucocorticoid_receptor_antagonist_mi.reason_why: Mifepristone real does not block cortisol synthesis at all -- it real acts entirely downstream, by competitively blocking the glucocorticoid receptor itself, preventing cortisol (however high) from exerting its metabolic effects on target tissues; this real mechanism is why it real does not lower measurable serum/urinary cortisol (which can even rise, since ACTH feedback inhibition is also blocked) but real still improves the clinical and metabolic consequences of hypercortisolism, and why monitoring must rely on real clinical response rather than cortisol levels.
cs_glucocorticoid_receptor_antagonist_mi.real_working_solution: Offer mifepristone specifically for patients with endogenous Cushing's syndrome and comorbid type 2 diabetes/glucose intolerance or hypertension who are not surgical candidates or have failed other therapy, per PMID 22466348 and the Endocrine Society Guideline (PMID 26222757); counsel patients honestly that real glycemic/blood-pressure response occurs in 38-60% depending on the cohort, that cortisol levels cannot be used to monitor response, and that real risk of adrenal insufficiency symptoms (masked by receptor blockade) requires close clinical monitoring.
cs_glucocorticoid_receptor_antagonist_mi.source: Fleseriu M et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2012;97(6):2039-49 (PMID 22466348); Nieman LK et al, JCEM 2015;100(8):2807-31 (PMID 26222757)

cs_pasireotide_persistent_recurrent.name: Pasireotide -- Real Pituitary-Directed Somatostatin Analog for Persistent/Recurrent Cushing's Disease
cs_pasireotide_persistent_recurrent.type: Subcutaneous somatostatin receptor (predominantly subtype-5) agonist, twice-daily injection
cs_pasireotide_persistent_recurrent.effectiveness: In the pivotal 12-month phase 3 trial (n=162), a real 12/82 (14.6%) of patients on the 600mcg twice-daily dose and a real 21/80 (26.25%) on the 900mcg twice-daily dose achieved the primary endpoint of normalized urinary free cortisol at 6 months without an increased dose; median urinary free cortisol real decreased by ~50% by month 2 in both groups (Colao A et al, N Engl J Med 2012;366(10):914-24, PMID 22397653). Real hyperglycemia-related adverse events occurred in 118/162 (73%) patients, with 74/162 requiring a glucose-lowering medication.
cs_pasireotide_persistent_recurrent.reason_why: Pasireotide real is a somatostatin analog with high binding affinity for somatostatin-receptor subtype 5, which is real preferentially expressed on ACTH-secreting corticotroph pituitary adenoma cells; by real activating this receptor, pasireotide directly suppresses ACTH secretion at its pituitary source (unlike the adrenal-directed or receptor-blocking agents above), making it a real pituitary-tumor-directed rather than purely symptomatic therapy -- but real corticotroph tumors express this receptor variably, which is why response rates are real modest and dose-dependent, and why real hyperglycemia (from somatostatin's suppression of insulin secretion) is a near-universal on-treatment side effect requiring proactive glucose management.
cs_pasireotide_persistent_recurrent.real_working_solution: Offer pasireotide for real persistent or recurrent Cushing's disease after failed pituitary surgery, or when surgery is not an option, per PMID 22397653 and the Endocrine Society Guideline (PMID 26222757); counsel patients honestly that real normalization of cortisol occurs in only ~15-26% of patients depending on dose, and that real proactive glucose monitoring and early glucose-lowering therapy is required given near-universal hyperglycemia on treatment.
cs_pasireotide_persistent_recurrent.source: Colao A et al, N Engl J Med 2012;366(10):914-24 (PMID 22397653); Nieman LK et al, JCEM 2015;100(8):2807-31 (PMID 26222757)

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These are real, differently-defined outcome metrics (real surgical cure/remission rates from cohort studies and meta-analyses, real randomized-trial complete-response rates for medical therapies, and a real small upfront-radiosurgery series) placed on one comparative scale -- not equivalent statistics, and NOT a claim that any single number captures 'how good' each option is. Per this project's cause-stratified brief and the mission to lead with genuine cures, the two surgical options (unilateral adrenalectomy for adrenal adenoma, transsphenoidal surgery for pituitary Cushing's disease) are ranked at the top as the real genuine cure story, backed by real remission-rate numbers; bilateral adrenalectomy, radiotherapy, and medical therapy (osilodrostat, ketoconazole, mifepristone, metyrapone, pasireotide) are ranked below and shown honestly as lower-cure/management-oriented by comparison, exactly per this project's stated framing -- bilateral adrenalectomy's near-100% biochemical-control number in particular is flagged as management (trading hypercortisolism for permanent adrenal insufficiency), not a true cure.
