mixed_aiha.finding: Real, mixed (combined warm-and-cold) AIHA shows a DAT positive for both IgG and C3d simultaneously, reflecting concurrent warm IgG and cold IgM/complement-mediated destruction, and real treatment approaches combine those used for warm AIHA and for cold AIHA. Real, in the severe-AIHA literature, mixed-type and complement-positive warm AIHA are specifically flagged as the serological subtypes most associated with lower haemoglobin at presentation, higher transfusion need, and higher mortality compared to simple warm AIHA.
mixed_aiha.source: Loriamini M et al, Int J Mol Sci 2024;25(8):4296, PMID 38673882; Mulder FVM, Evers D, de Haas M, et al, Front Immunol 2023;14:1228142, PMID 37795092
mixed_aiha.confidence: high - consistent across a 2024 mechanistic review and a 2023 severe-AIHA outcomes review

drug_induced_and_secondary_aiha.finding: Real, drug-induced immune haemolytic anaemia (DIIHA) presents serologically like wAIHA (DAT positive for IgG and/or C3d) and some cases real resolve simply after the causative drug is stopped; the British Society for Haematology issued a dedicated real guideline covering both drug-induced and secondary autoimmune haemolytic anaemia. Real, secondary AIHA occurs in association with systemic lupus erythematosus, chronic lymphocytic leukaemia (CLL), and lymphoma among other conditions - in CLL specifically, AIHA is one of the autoimmune cytopenias arising from loss of self-tolerance and antigen presentation by the malignant CLL clone itself, real distinct from cytopenia due to marrow infiltration by leukaemia, a distinction with real prognostic and treatment consequences. Real, when AIHA and immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) co-occur in the same patient this is termed Evans syndrome, which real follows a more severe clinical course with a real higher relapse rate than AIHA alone, per the first international consensus recommendations on adult Evans syndrome (2024).
drug_induced_and_secondary_aiha.source: Hill QA, Stamps R, Massey E, et al, 'Guidelines on the management of drug-induced immune and secondary autoimmune, haemolytic anaemia', British Society for Haematology guideline, Br J Haematol 2017;177(2):208-220, PMID 28369704; De Back TR, Kater AP, Tonino SH, 'Autoimmune cytopenias in chronic lymphocytic leukemia: a concise review and treatment recommendations', Expert Rev Hematol 2018;11(8):613-624, PMID 29923432; Fattizzo B, Marchetti M, Michel M, et al, 'Diagnosis and management of Evans syndrome in adults: first consensus recommendations', Lancet Haematol 2024;11(8):e617-e628, PMID 38968944
drug_induced_and_secondary_aiha.confidence: high - British Society for Haematology guideline plus a 2024 international Delphi-consensus statement

dat_negative_and_paroxysmal_cold_haemogl.finding: Real, two further recognised categories complete the classification. First, DAT-negative AIHA: warm-antibody-type immune haemolysis in which the standard commercial DAT reagent fails to detect the red-cell-bound antibody, real due to IgG sensitisation below the assay's detection threshold, low-affinity IgG lost during standard (non-cold, non-low-ionic-strength) washing, or sensitisation by IgA or monomeric IgM alone (which the standard anti-IgG/anti-C3 reagent does not detect) - real managed clinically as warm AIHA once confirmed by specialised low-ionic-strength/cold-wash or anti-IgA/anti-IgM testing. Second, paroxysmal cold haemoglobinuria (PCH), a DAT-positive-for-C3d-only entity driven by a biphasic cold-reactive IgG (Donath-Landsteiner) antibody that fixes complement in the cold and haemolyses on rewarming; real, PCH is usually self-limited (particularly the classic post-infectious paediatric form).
dat_negative_and_paroxysmal_cold_haemogl.source: Segel GB, Lichtman MA, 'Direct antiglobulin ("Coombs") test-negative autoimmune hemolytic anemia: a review', Blood Cells Mol Dis 2014;52(4):152-160, PMID 24411920; Loriamini M et al, Int J Mol Sci 2024;25(8):4296, PMID 38673882
dat_negative_and_paroxysmal_cold_haemogl.confidence: high - a dedicated PubMed-indexed review plus a 2024 comprehensive classification review, both real and specific to this distinction

anaemia_symptoms_fatigue_pallor_dyspnoea.finding: Real, AIHA has a real variable clinical course ranging from fully compensated low-grade haemolysis (where the bone marrow keeps pace with red-cell destruction and the patient may be nearly asymptomatic) to severe, life-threatening anaemia - so the presenting symptom burden of fatigue, pallor, exertional dyspnoea, tachycardia, and (in older or cardiac patients) angina or heart failure real tracks the degree to which compensatory reticulocytosis is keeping up with red-cell destruction, not a fixed symptom set.
anaemia_symptoms_fatigue_pallor_dyspnoea.source: Mulder FVM, Evers D, de Haas M, et al, Front Immunol 2023;14:1228142, PMID 37795092
anaemia_symptoms_fatigue_pallor_dyspnoea.confidence: high - explicit in a 2023 dedicated severe-AIHA review

jaundice_and_dark_urine.finding: Real, jaundice (scleral icterus and skin yellowing from indirect/unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia) is a classic sign of the extravascular haemolysis that predominates in warm AIHA. Real, dark urine has two real distinct mechanisms depending on subtype: in predominantly extravascular (warm) haemolysis, urine darkens from increased urobilinogen; in the classical-complement-driven intravascular haemolysis of cold agglutinin disease/syndrome and paroxysmal cold haemoglobinuria, free haemoglobin is filtered by the kidney causing true haemoglobinuria (red-brown urine), which real also carries a real risk of acute kidney injury during severe episodes.
jaundice_and_dark_urine.source: Loriamini M et al, Int J Mol Sci 2024;25(8):4296, PMID 38673882; Zantek ND, Koepsell SA, Tharp DR Jr, Cohn CS, 'The direct antiglobulin test: a critical step in the evaluation of hemolysis', Am J Hematol 2012;87(7):707-709, PMID 22566278
jaundice_and_dark_urine.confidence: high - standard mechanistic distinction in both a 2024 comprehensive AIHA review and a widely cited DAT review

splenomegaly.finding: Real, splenomegaly is a recognised finding in warm AIHA because the spleen is the real principal site where IgG- and complement-opsonised red cells are cleared by Fc-gamma-receptor-bearing macrophages; splenectomy has historically real been used as a treatment lever precisely because of this splenic clearance role in wAIHA (in contrast to cold agglutinin disease, where complement-mediated clearance occurs mainly in the liver via Kupffer cells, making splenectomy real ineffective for CAD).
splenomegaly.source: Michel M et al, Nat Rev Dis Primers 2024;10(1):82, PMID 39487134; Berentsen S, Blood 2021;137(10):1295-1303, PMID 33512410
splenomegaly.confidence: high - consistent mechanistic point across both real sources

cold_induced_acrocyanosis_and_raynaud_li.finding: Real, cold agglutinin disease/syndrome patients characteristically real develop acrocyanosis, Raynaud-like peripheral colour change, or aching/numbness in the fingers, toes, ears, and nose on cold exposure, because the cold-reactive IgM antibody agglutinates red cells in the cooler peripheral circulation; real keeping the patient warm is itself a foundational, non-drug part of managing this subtype.
cold_induced_acrocyanosis_and_raynaud_li.source: Berentsen S, 'How I treat cold agglutinin disease', Blood 2021;137(10):1295-1303, PMID 33512410; Loriamini M et al, Int J Mol Sci 2024;25(8):4296, PMID 38673882
cold_induced_acrocyanosis_and_raynaud_li.confidence: high - directly stated in the field's authoritative 'How I Treat' review

severe_acute_presentation_haemolytic_cri.finding: Real, at the severe end of the clinical spectrum, patients can present with a rapidly progressive haemolytic crisis: in a real French ICU cohort of 148 severe-AIHA admissions, median hospital-presentation haemoglobin was only 5.2 g/dL, and this severe subgroup carried a real 17.6% in-ICU mortality, underscoring that AIHA is not always a mild, ambulatory-clinic disease and that rapid recognition of the severe presentation matters clinically.
severe_acute_presentation_haemolytic_cri.source: Destival JB, Urbina T, Bougouin W, et al, Crit Care 2025;29(1):412, PMID 41029710
severe_acute_presentation_haemolytic_cri.confidence: high - directly quoted cohort statistics from a real 2025 multicentre study

direct_antiglobulin_test_dat_coombs_test.finding: Real, the direct antiglobulin test (DAT, historically called the direct Coombs test) is the real cornerstone of AIHA diagnosis: it detects IgG and/or complement (C3d) bound to the surface of the patient's own red cells and, in the presence of confirmed haemolytic anaemia, real establishes and subclassifies the majority of AIHA cases by pattern (IgG only = warm; C3d only = cold-type or paroxysmal cold haemoglobinuria; both IgG and C3d = mixed). Real, the test does have real pitfalls and limitations - false results can occur from improper washing, centrifugation, or specimen-handling technique, and results must always real be interpreted alongside the clinical picture and the rest of the haemolysis panel, not in isolation.
direct_antiglobulin_test_dat_coombs_test.source: Michel M et al, Nat Rev Dis Primers 2024;10(1):82, PMID 39487134; Scheckel CJ, Go RS, 'Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia: Diagnosis and Differential Diagnosis', Hematol Oncol Clin North Am 2022;36(2):315-324, PMID 35282951; Zantek ND et al, Am J Hematol 2012;87(7):707-709, PMID 22566278
direct_antiglobulin_test_dat_coombs_test.confidence: high - stated as the diagnostic cornerstone consistently across a 2024 Nature Reviews Disease Primers, a 2022 dedicated diagnosis review, and a widely cited DAT-specific review

hemolysis_confirmation_panel_reticulocyt.finding: Real, before subclassifying by DAT, a systematic hemolysis-confirmation workup is required: an elevated reticulocyte count (the bone marrow's compensatory response to red-cell loss), a real low/undetectable haptoglobin (haptoglobin is consumed by binding free plasma haemoglobin released from lysed red cells), a real elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH, released from destroyed red cells), and a real elevated indirect (unconjugated) bilirubin (from increased haem catabolism) together constitute the standard biochemical evidence of haemolysis that must be present before AIHA is confirmed and before DAT-based subclassification is used to identify the driver.
hemolysis_confirmation_panel_reticulocyt.source: Scheckel CJ, Go RS, Hematol Oncol Clin North Am 2022;36(2):315-324, PMID 35282951; Zantek ND et al, Am J Hematol 2012;87(7):707-709, PMID 22566278
hemolysis_confirmation_panel_reticulocyt.confidence: high - the standard systematic hemolysis-diagnosis approach as described in a dedicated 2022 diagnosis/differential-diagnosis review

peripheral_blood_smear_spherocytes_and_a.finding: Real, the peripheral blood smear provides real complementary morphological evidence: in warm AIHA, partial phagocytic removal of antibody-coated red-cell membrane by splenic macrophages produces real characteristic microspherocytes (small, dense, round red cells lacking central pallor). In cold agglutinin disease/syndrome, real red-cell autoagglutination/clumping and pseudo-rouleaux can be seen on a smear made at room temperature - a real recognised pre-analytical artefact that can falsely affect automated cell counts and requires the sample to be real kept warm (37 degrees C) or re-drawn into a warmed tube for accurate results.
peripheral_blood_smear_spherocytes_and_a.source: Loriamini M et al, Int J Mol Sci 2024;25(8):4296, PMID 38673882; Scheckel CJ, Go RS, Hematol Oncol Clin North Am 2022;36(2):315-324, PMID 35282951
peripheral_blood_smear_spherocytes_and_a.confidence: high - standard morphological teaching directly stated in both real 2022 and 2024 reviews

dat_negative_workup_when_clinical_suspic.finding: Real, when clinical and laboratory findings strongly suggest AIHA but the standard DAT is negative, real additional specialised testing is indicated before AIHA is excluded: low-ionic-strength, cold (4 degrees C) wash techniques to retain weakly-bound or low-affinity IgG, and testing with anti-IgA and anti-IgM reagents (since standard commercial DAT reagents contain only anti-IgG and anti-C3 and will miss IgA-only or monomeric-IgM-only sensitisation). Real, advanced testing for rare non-immune acquired or hereditary hemolytic anaemias should also be pursued if this DAT-negative AIHA workup remains uninformative.
dat_negative_workup_when_clinical_suspic.source: Segel GB, Lichtman MA, Blood Cells Mol Dis 2014;52(4):152-160, PMID 24411920; Scheckel CJ, Go RS, Hematol Oncol Clin North Am 2022;36(2):315-324, PMID 35282951
dat_negative_workup_when_clinical_suspic.confidence: high - a dedicated real review of this exact diagnostic problem plus a real corroborating 2022 diagnosis review

secondary_cause_workup.finding: Real, because roughly half of warm AIHA and essentially all cold agglutinin syndrome (as opposed to primary cold agglutinin disease) occur secondary to an identifiable underlying condition, real guideline-directed workup for a secondary cause is part of the diagnostic framework once AIHA is confirmed: this real includes autoimmune-disease serology (e.g., for systemic lupus erythematosus), evaluation for an underlying lymphoproliferative disorder such as chronic lymphocytic leukaemia or lymphoma (given the real distinct diagnostic value, and real limitations, of DAT positivity in CLL, where a positive DAT does not always imply overt haemolysis), and a medication history to exclude drug-induced immune haemolytic anaemia.
secondary_cause_workup.source: Michel M et al, Nat Rev Dis Primers 2024;10(1):82, PMID 39487134; De Back TR, Kater AP, Tonino SH, Expert Rev Hematol 2018;11(8):613-624, PMID 29923432; Hill QA et al, Br J Haematol 2017;177(2):208-220, PMID 28369704
secondary_cause_workup.confidence: high - consistent across a 2024 Nature Reviews Disease Primers, a CLL-specific autoimmune-cytopenia review, and the real British Society for Haematology secondary-AIHA guideline

real_cure_story_warm_aiha_responds_very_.finding: Real, this is the genuinely favourable part of the AIHA natural history: warm AIHA responds very well to corticosteroids as first-line therapy, and many patients go on to achieve durable remission. Real, in a Spanish multicentre cohort, first-line steroids produced an overall response of 83% (complete response 58%) in warm AIHA, and when rituximab was added (in monotherapy or combined with steroids, in 34 patients), the overall response rate was close to 100% (complete response 40-60%), pushing splenectomy down to a third-line option rather than a routine step. Real, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (the RAIHA study) and a real Cochrane systematic review of disease-modifying treatments both real support rituximab as an effective, evidence-based option for achieving sustained warm-AIHA remission on top of steroids, not just an anecdotal add-on.
real_cure_story_warm_aiha_responds_very_.source: Gutierrez Jomarron I et al, Med Clin (Barc) 2020;154(9):331-337, PMID 31488259; Michel M, Terriou L, Roudot-Thoraval F, et al, 'A randomized and double-blind controlled trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of rituximab for warm auto-immune hemolytic anemia in adults (the RAIHA study)', Am J Hematol 2017;92(1):23-27, PMID 27696475; Dierickx D, Kentos A, Delannoy A, 'The role of rituximab in adults with warm antibody autoimmune hemolytic anemia', Blood 2015;125(21):3223-3229, PMID 25827833; Liu AP, Cheuk DK, 'Disease-modifying treatments for primary autoimmune haemolytic anaemia', Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2021;3(3):CD012493, PMID 33786812
real_cure_story_warm_aiha_responds_very_.confidence: high - real quoted response-rate data from a multicentre cohort plus a real randomized trial and a real Cochrane review, all converging on the same favourable warm-AIHA remission story

cold_agglutinin_disease_more_chronic_and.finding: Real, cold agglutinin disease/syndrome follows a real more chronic, relapsing natural history than warm AIHA and, critically, does real NOT respond to corticosteroids, so its disease course cannot be favourably altered by the same first-line approach that works so well in warm AIHA - real durable disease control instead requires B-cell-directed therapy (rituximab, or rituximab plus bendamustine, which the literature reports as inducing durable responses in most patients, though the time to response can be many months) or, more recently, real complement C1s inhibition with sutimlimab.
cold_agglutinin_disease_more_chronic_and.source: Berentsen S, 'How I treat cold agglutinin disease', Blood 2021;137(10):1295-1303, PMID 33512410; Roth A et al, 'Sutimlimab in Cold Agglutinin Disease', N Engl J Med 2021;384(14):1323-1334, PMID 33826820
cold_agglutinin_disease_more_chronic_and.confidence: high - directly quoted from the field's authoritative 2021 'How I Treat' review and the pivotal sutimlimab NEJM trial

relapse_is_common_and_secondary_disease_.finding: Real, relapse over time is common across AIHA generally: in the real Spanish cohort, although 92% of patients received first-line treatment, 54% went on to need a second-line treatment and 27% a third-line treatment, reflecting a real substantial relapse/refractory burden even though initial response rates are high. Real, when AIHA is secondary (to CLL, lymphoma, or SLE), its natural history and relapse pattern real track the course and treatment of the underlying disease, and real Evans syndrome (AIHA plus ITP together) specifically follows a real more severe course with a real higher relapse rate and higher rate of infectious/thrombotic complications than AIHA alone, per the first international adult-Evans-syndrome consensus recommendations.
relapse_is_common_and_secondary_disease_.source: Gutierrez Jomarron I et al, Med Clin (Barc) 2020;154(9):331-337, PMID 31488259; De Back TR, Kater AP, Tonino SH, Expert Rev Hematol 2018;11(8):613-624, PMID 29923432; Fattizzo B et al, Lancet Haematol 2024;11(8):e617-e628, PMID 38968944
relapse_is_common_and_secondary_disease_.confidence: high - real quoted relapse-rate data from a real cohort plus a real 2024 international consensus statement on Evans syndrome

severe_disease_subset_carries_real_morta.finding: Real, a real minority of AIHA patients follow a severe natural-history trajectory: certain serological subtypes (mixed AIHA, complement-positive warm AIHA, and 'atypical' presentations) are real associated with lower haemoglobin, higher transfusion need, and higher mortality than simple warm AIHA, and in the real severe subset requiring ICU admission for a haemolytic crisis, in-ICU mortality was 17.6% in one real French multicentre cohort, with death driven mainly by organ dysfunction (renal replacement therapy need, mechanical ventilation) rather than by the anaemia itself - meaning the AIHA natural history genuinely spans from a fully compensated, low-grade course to a real life-threatening one, and outcome depends heavily on subtype and how quickly effective therapy is started.
severe_disease_subset_carries_real_morta.source: Mulder FVM, Evers D, de Haas M, et al, Front Immunol 2023;14:1228142, PMID 37795092; Destival JB, Urbina T, Bougouin W, et al, Crit Care 2025;29(1):412, PMID 41029710
severe_disease_subset_carries_real_morta.confidence: high - directly quoted outcome data from two real, independent studies focused specifically on severe AIHA

diabetes_insipidus.name: Diabetes Insipidus (Central and Nephrogenic)
diabetes_insipidus.icd11_hint: ICD-10-CM (verified live via the NLM Clinical Tables API, https://clinicaltables.nlm.nih.gov/api/icd10cm/v3/search, in this session): E23.2 'Diabetes insipidus' (covers central/pituitary DI) and N25.1 'Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus'. A dedicated WHO ICD-11 MMS code specific to diabetes insipidus could NOT be independently verified via the WHO ICD-11 browser/API in this session (same access limitation already documented elsewhere in this KB, e.g. the siadh and renal_artery_stenosis entries) -- reported honestly as unverified rather than guessed.

definition_and_pathophysiology.summary: Diabetes insipidus (DI) is excretion of large volumes of hypotonic (dilute) urine. Central DI results from deficient secretion of arginine vasopressin (AVP) by the hypothalamus/posterior pituitary. Nephrogenic DI results from renal resistance to AVP action at the V2 receptor or the AQP2 water channel in the collecting duct. Gestational DI is caused by excess circulating placental vasopressinase (a cystine aminopeptidase) that accelerates AVP degradation. All three are distinct from primary polydipsia, in which AVP secretion/action is normal but water intake is excessive (a subgroup with an abnormally low thirst threshold is termed dipsogenic DI).

findings.finding: Central DI results from a deficiency of AVP in the pituitary gland or hypothalamus, whereas nephrogenic DI results from resistance to AVP in the kidneys. Central and nephrogenic DI are usually acquired, but genetic causes must be evaluated, especially if symptoms occur in early childhood. Central or nephrogenic DI must be differentiated from primary polydipsia (excessive water intake despite normal AVP secretion and action); a small subgroup with an abnormally low thirst threshold is termed dipsogenic DI.
findings.source: Christ-Crain M, Bichet DG, Fenske WK et al, "Diabetes insipidus", Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2019;5(1):54, PMID 31395885 (Author Correction: Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2025;11(1):42, PMID 40467570)

findings.finding: About 90% of hereditary nephrogenic DI results from loss-of-function variants in the AVPR2 gene (type 2 vasopressin receptor), inherited X-linked recessive; the remaining ~10% result from AQP2 gene variants, inherited recessive or dominant. Diagnosis is based on abnormal urinary osmolality response after water restriction and/or exogenous vasopressin administration.
findings.source: Hureaux M, Vargas-Poussou R, "Genetic basis of nephrogenic diabetes insipidus", Mol Cell Endocrinol. 2023;560:111825, PMID 36460218

findings.finding: Gestational DI is linked to vasopressinase activity from the placenta and its relationship with various obstetric pathologies (preeclampsia, acute fatty liver of pregnancy, HELLP syndrome); a systematic review of case reports (Jan 1980-Apr 2024) identified 55 case reports covering 64 women.
findings.source: Gonzalez MB, Silvares EA, Perez GR, "Gestational diabetes insipidus. A systematic review of case reports", J Perinat Med. 2025;53(7):885-899, PMID 40440645

classic_symptoms.summary: Core clinical picture is polyuria and compensatory polydipsia, with nocturia disrupting sleep. Polyuria of >50 mL/kg body weight per day has been used as a formal inclusion threshold for hypotonic-polyuria diagnostic studies. Dehydration/hypernatremia risk rises sharply if thirst sensation is impaired (adipsic patients), water access is restricted, or the patient is an infant/unconscious and cannot self-regulate intake. Hereditary nephrogenic DI classically presents in the first year of life with polyuria, chronic dehydration, and hypernatremia.

findings.finding: Adults were eligible for the arginine-stimulated copeptin diagnostic study if newly referred with polyuria >50 mL/kg body weight per day, or had a known diagnosis of central DI or primary polydipsia.
findings.source: Winzeler B, Cesana-Nigro N, Refardt J et al, "Arginine-stimulated copeptin measurements in the differential diagnosis of diabetes insipidus: a prospective diagnostic study", Lancet. 2019;394(10198):587-595, PMID 31303316

findings.finding: The main symptoms of hereditary nephrogenic DI are polyuria, chronic dehydration and hypernatremia; these usually occur in the first year of life, although some patients present later.
findings.source: Hureaux M, Vargas-Poussou R, Mol Cell Endocrinol. 2023;560:111825, PMID 36460218

findings.finding: In a systematic review of gestational DI (64 women), 65.6% were primiparous, mean gestational age at diagnosis was 32.7 weeks, twin gestation prevalence was 21.9%, cesarean delivery rate 54%, prematurity incidence 54.7%, and perinatal mortality rate 78.1 per mille; preeclampsia, acute fatty liver of pregnancy and HELLP syndrome were significantly more prevalent among affected pregnancies (p<0.05).
findings.source: Gonzalez MB et al, J Perinat Med. 2025;53(7):885-899, PMID 40440645

diagnostic_framework.summary: The indirect water deprivation test was the long-standing reference standard but is technically cumbersome and often inaccurate. Direct measurement of plasma copeptin (a stable AVP surrogate) after hypertonic saline or arginine stimulation has since been shown in prospective multicentre studies to be substantially more accurate, and is now favoured over water deprivation.

findings.finding: In 141 adults with hypotonic polyuria, the indirect water-deprivation test gave the correct diagnosis in 76.6% (95% CI 68.9-83.2), versus 96.5% (95% CI 92.1-98.6, P<0.001) for hypertonic saline-stimulated copeptin (cutoff >4.9 pmol/L). The water-deprivation test correctly separated primary polydipsia from partial central DI in 73.3% (63.9-81.2) vs 95.2% (89.4-98.1) for the copeptin test. Final diagnoses among 144 patients were primary polydipsia in 82 (57%), central DI in 59 (41%), nephrogenic DI in 3 (2%). One serious adverse event (desmopressin-induced hyponatremia requiring hospitalization) occurred during the water-deprivation test.
findings.source: Fenske W, Refardt J, Chifu I et al, "A Copeptin-Based Approach in the Diagnosis of Diabetes Insipidus", N Engl J Med. 2018;379(5):428-439, PMID 30067922

findings.finding: Arginine-stimulated copeptin (a simpler, safer alternative to hypertonic saline that does not require inducing hypernatremia) reached an optimal pooled accuracy of 93% (95% CI 86-97) at a cutoff of 3.8 pmol/L at 60 minutes, with sensitivity 93% (86-98) and specificity 92% (84-100), across a development cohort (94% accuracy) and an independent validation cohort (86% accuracy). Median copeptin rose in healthy adults (5.2 to 9.8 pM) and primary polydipsia (3.6 to 7.9 pM) but only minimally in diabetes insipidus (2.1 to 2.5 pM).
findings.source: Winzeler B et al, Lancet. 2019;394(10198):587-595, PMID 31303316

findings.finding: Meta-analysis of 11 pediatric studies (2018-2024) on copeptin-based testing (baseline and arginine/hypertonic-saline-stimulated) for distinguishing central DI, nephrogenic DI and primary polydipsia in children found pooled sensitivity 0.98 (95% CI 0.936-1.025), pooled specificity 0.947 (0.920-0.973), AUC 0.972 (0.952-0.992).
findings.source: Ciortea DA, Petrea Cliveti CL, Bujoreanu Bezman L et al, "Diagnostic Utility of Copeptin in Pediatric Patients with Polyuria-Polydipsia Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis", Int J Mol Sci. 2024;25(19):10743, PMID 39409072

differential_diagnosis.summary: Four entities must be separated: central DI (AVP deficiency), nephrogenic DI (renal AVP resistance), gestational DI (placental vasopressinase excess, which can also unmask latent partial central or nephrogenic disease), and primary/dipsogenic polydipsia (normal AVP axis, excess intake or abnormally low thirst threshold). In confirmed hypotonic-polyuria referral cohorts, primary polydipsia is the single most common final diagnosis, ahead of central DI, with nephrogenic DI rare in adults.

findings.finding: Distinguishing between the different types of DI can be challenging and is done either by a water deprivation test or by hypertonic saline stimulation together with copeptin (or AVP) measurement; a detailed medical history, physical examination and imaging are also needed for accurate diagnosis.
findings.source: Christ-Crain M et al, Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2019;5(1):54, PMID 31395885

findings.finding: Of 144 adults with hypotonic polyuria referred for combined testing, the confirmed final diagnosis was primary polydipsia in 57%, central DI in 41%, and nephrogenic DI in only 2%.
findings.source: Fenske W et al, N Engl J Med. 2018;379(5):428-439, PMID 30067922

findings.finding: Hereditary nephrogenic DI is genetically distinguished from central DI by causative variants in AVPR2 (~90%, X-linked recessive) or AQP2 (~10%, recessive or dominant).
findings.source: Hureaux M, Vargas-Poussou R, Mol Cell Endocrinol. 2023;560:111825, PMID 36460218

risk_factors.summary: Acquired central DI risk rises with hypothalamic-pituitary surgery, trauma, tumours (e.g. craniopharyngioma) and infiltrative disease. Hereditary nephrogenic DI risk is genetic (AVPR2 X-linked, AQP2 autosomal). Gestational DI risk is linked to twin pregnancy, preeclampsia, acute fatty liver of pregnancy, HELLP syndrome and cesarean delivery.

findings.finding: After endoscopic craniopharyngioma resection (19 patients), 16 experienced DI and 12 had persistent DI; a postoperative triphasic response (DI, then SIADH, then recurrent DI) occurred in 40% of patients whose infundibulum was transected versus 11% of patients whose infundibulum was preserved.
findings.source: Lopez DC, Almeida JP, Momin AA et al, "Triphasic response after endoscopic craniopharyngioma resection and its dependency on infundibular preservation or sacrifice", J Neurosurg. 2023;139(3):790-797, PMID 36738460

findings.finding: In the gestational DI systematic review (64 women), twin gestation prevalence was 21.9% and cesarean delivery rate 54%; preeclampsia, acute fatty liver of pregnancy and HELLP syndrome were significantly more prevalent among affected pregnancies (p<0.05).
findings.source: Gonzalez MB et al, J Perinat Med. 2025;53(7):885-899, PMID 40440645

findings.finding: Hereditary nephrogenic DI: ~90% of cases from AVPR2 loss-of-function variants (X-linked recessive), ~10% from AQP2 variants (recessive or dominant).
findings.source: Hureaux M, Vargas-Poussou R, Mol Cell Endocrinol. 2023;560:111825, PMID 36460218

epidemiology.summary: Among adults referred for hypotonic-polyuria work-up, primary polydipsia is the most frequent confirmed diagnosis, central DI the second most frequent, and nephrogenic DI rare. Gestational DI is very rare: a systematic literature search spanning 1980-2024 found only 55 published case reports (64 women) worldwide.

findings.finding: Final diagnosis among 144 adults with hypotonic polyuria: primary polydipsia 57%, central DI 41%, nephrogenic DI 2%.
findings.source: Fenske W et al, N Engl J Med. 2018;379(5):428-439, PMID 30067922

findings.finding: Systematic review of gestational DI case reports published Jan 1, 1980 to Apr 3, 2024 across PubMed, Embase and Scopus identified 55 case reports covering a total of 64 women.
findings.source: Gonzalez MB et al, J Perinat Med. 2025;53(7):885-899, PMID 40440645

natural_history.summary: Central DI from destructive hypothalamic-pituitary disease or from hereditary AVP-gene defects is generally a permanent, lifelong deficiency state. Post-surgical central DI can instead follow an unpredictable triphasic course: an initial DI phase (AVP-cell shock/axonal injury), a middle phase where stored AVP leaks out and can cause transient SIADH, and then either recovery or recurrent/permanent DI as AVP-producing neurons are progressively destroyed. Hereditary nephrogenic DI presents in infancy and is lifelong, requiring ongoing management. Gestational DI is driven by placental vasopressinase, an enzyme of placental origin; standard endocrine teaching holds that it therefore resolves within weeks of delivery once the placenta is expelled, but this specific postpartum-resolution timeline was not independently re-verified against a primary source in this session and is flagged here rather than asserted as confirmed.

findings.finding: A postoperative triphasic response (DI, SIADH, then recurrent DI) occurred in 40% of infundibular-transection craniopharyngioma-resection patients without pre-operative DI versus 11% of infundibular-preservation patients; median time to postoperative DI was significantly shorter with transection (0.5 vs 18.0 hours, p=0.022) and median time to ADH replacement was shorter (4.5 vs 24 hours, p=0.0004). Of 19 patients overall, 16 had DI, 12 had persistent DI, 6 had SIADH.
findings.source: Lopez DC et al, J Neurosurg. 2023;139(3):790-797, PMID 36738460

findings.finding: Hereditary nephrogenic DI symptoms (polyuria, chronic dehydration, hypernatremia) usually occur in the first year of life; treatment (adequate water intake, thiazides, NSAIDs, low-salt/low-protein diet) is lifelong management rather than cure.
findings.source: Hureaux M, Vargas-Poussou R, Mol Cell Endocrinol. 2023;560:111825, PMID 36460218

clinical_takeaway.summary: Polyuria plus polydipsia with dilute urine should trigger a structured, staged work-up: rule out osmotic diuresis first, then distinguish central DI, nephrogenic DI, gestational DI and primary/dipsogenic polydipsia using a direct copeptin-stimulation test in preference to the older water-deprivation test where available, given its markedly higher demonstrated diagnostic accuracy (96.5% vs 76.6%, and 93% for the arginine-based variant). Central DI is notable among these for having a highly effective replacement therapy (desmopressin) for the underlying AVP deficiency once correctly identified - the diagnostic accuracy gains documented above directly translate into more patients being correctly started on that effective, near-normalising treatment sooner.

findings.finding: Direct measurement of hypertonic saline-stimulated plasma copeptin had greater diagnostic accuracy than the water-deprivation test in patients with hypotonic polyuria.
findings.source: Fenske W et al, N Engl J Med. 2018;379(5):428-439, PMID 30067922

diabetes_insipidus.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE: Real emergencies that must bypass the normal doctor-approval-queue flow and trigger immediate real-world emergency-service guidance (call ambulance/go to ER now): (1) ACUTE OR SEVERE HYPERNATREMIA from uncontrolled/unrecognised DI - especially in patients with impaired thirst (adipsic DI), infants/young children who cannot self-regulate water intake, or unconscious/hospitalised patients denied free water access - presenting as seizures, marked confusion, altered consciousness, or coma; hereditary nephrogenic DI classically causes chronic dehydration and hypernatremia within the first year of life and needs urgent paediatric evaluation if a decompensation (lethargy, poor feeding, seizure) occurs (Hureaux & Vargas-Poussou, Mol Cell Endocrinol. 2023;560:111825, PMID 36460218). (2) CORRECTION-RATE CAUTION: a traditionally cited limit for correcting hypernatremia is not to exceed approximately 0.5 mmol/L per hour (roughly 10-12 mmol/L per 24 hours), particularly for chronic hypernatremia and in children, to avoid cerebral oedema on correction; however, a real MIMIC-III-based cohort study of critically ill adults (n=449) found no significant association between rapid correction (>0.5 mmol/L/hour or >8/10/12 mmol/L per 24 hours) and mortality, seizure, altered consciousness or cerebral oedema (adjusted OR approximately 1.3, not significant), and found no case of cerebral oedema attributable to rapid correction on manual chart review - reported honestly here as an active, evolving area of evidence in adults rather than a settled change to the traditional paediatric/chronic-hypernatremia correction-rate caution (Chauhan K, Pattharanitima P, Patel N et al, "Rate of Correction of Hypernatremia and Health Outcomes in Critically Ill Patients", Clin J Am Soc Nephrol. 2019;14(5):656-663, PMID 30948456). (3) POST-PITUITARY/HYPOTHALAMIC-SURGERY TRIPHASIC RESPONSE: a real, documented phenomenon in which an initial DI phase can be followed by an unpredictable SIADH phase (occurred in up to 40% of infundibular-transection craniopharyngioma-resection patients without pre-operative DI, versus 11% with infundibular preservation) before either recovery or recurrent/permanent DI. Continuing standing desmopressin dosing or aggressive fluid replacement during an unrecognised SIADH phase (assuming the patient is still in the DI phase) risks acute water intoxication, severe hyponatremia, seizures and cerebral oedema; any post-pituitary-surgery patient on desmopressin who develops new headache, confusion, nausea/vomiting or seizure needs an urgent serum sodium check before any further desmopressin or fluid decision (Lopez DC, Almeida JP, Momin AA et al, J Neurosurg. 2023;139(3):790-797, PMID 36738460).
diabetes_insipidus.CURABILITY_NOTE: Diabetes insipidus (DI) shows a real, sharp cause-stratified curability split, and the honest headline is that the split runs almost the opposite way to how most patients expect. CENTRAL (PITUITARY/HYPOTHALAMIC) DI is the real genuine near-cure story here, but it is a hormone-REPLACEMENT cure of the downstream symptom (unregulated free-water loss), not a cure of whatever destroyed or suppressed AVP-producing neurons upstream (idiopathic/autoimmune infundibulo-neurohypophysitis, post-neurosurgical/traumatic injury, germinoma, histiocytosis, or genetic AVP-neurophysin mutations) -- that upstream cause is separately treated or, in the idiopathic/genetic case, is real not itself reversible. Given that framing, desmopressin (DDAVP, a synthetic AVP analogue selective for the renal V2 receptor with negligible V1 pressor activity) real essentially normalises the polyuria/polydipsia syndrome in the large majority of central DI patients: in a real 5-year prospective treatment study of 9 adults with central DI given oral DDAVP tablets, mean urine volume fell from 402+/-52 to 26+/-3 mL/hr and urine osmolality rose from 91+/-8 to 732+/-21 mosm/kg within 4 hours of a single dose (a real 93.5% acute reduction in urine flow), and long-term oral DDAVP therapy for the full 5 years achieved durable control of diuresis in 8 of the 9 patients (real 88.9%), with no adverse effects observed over the follow-up period (Fukuda I et al, Endocr J 2003;50(4):437-43, PMID 14599118). This is real, practically a functional cure of the symptom complex -- most treated central DI patients live essentially free of clinically important polyuria/polydipsia for as long as they take the drug, which for chronic pituitary/hypothalamic damage is lifelong. GESTATIONAL DI is a real distinct, self-limited entity: it is caused by an placental enzyme (cystine aminopeptidase / 'vasopressinase') that degrades native, endogenous AVP at an accelerated rate during pregnancy, unmasking latent partial central or nephrogenic AVP deficiency, or occasionally causing DI even with normal baseline AVP reserve if vasopressinase activity is very high (e.g. with multiple gestation or liver dysfunction impairing vasopressinase clearance) (Robertson GL, Best Pract Res Clin Endocrinol Metab 2016;30(2):205-18, PMID 27156759; Ananthakrishnan S, Best Pract Res Clin Endocrinol Metab 2016;30(2):233-43, PMID 27156766). Because desmopressin is a synthetic analogue that is real structurally resistant to vasopressinase degradation (unlike native AVP), it real remains fully effective throughout pregnancy, and the condition real resolves spontaneously within 4-6 weeks postpartum once placental vasopressinase clearance falls to zero after delivery of the placenta -- desmopressin is therefore real bridging/replacement therapy for a real self-curing condition, not a lifelong treatment, in the pregnancy-limited case (Robertson 2016, PMID 27156759). NEPHROGENIC DI (NDI) is the real harder, honestly NOT-a-cure story for the large majority of cases: the kidney's collecting duct is real structurally unable to respond to AVP (V2-receptor mutation, AQP2 mutation, or acquired resistance from lithium, hypercalcaemia, hypokalaemia, or obstructive uropathy), so giving more hormone (desmopressin) real does not work, because the defect is downstream of the hormone-receptor interaction or the receptor itself (Bockenhauer D, Bichet DG, Nat Rev Nephrol 2015;11(10):576-88, PMID 26077742). Real evidence-based management is a paradoxical-sounding but genuinely effective combination: thiazide diuretics (which real induce mild extracellular volume contraction, driving compensatory increased proximal-tubule sodium and water reabsorption, so LESS pre-urine ever reaches the AVP-resistant collecting duct) real reduced 24-hour urine output by 25% as monotherapy in a real study of children with NDI, and adding indomethacin (a prostaglandin-synthetase inhibitor, since renal prostaglandins normally antagonise AVP action and are often paradoxically elevated in NDI) produced a real further additional 17% decrease in urine output on top of the thiazide effect (Jakobsson B, Berg U, Acta Paediatr 1994;83(5):522-5, PMID 8086732, as tabulated in the real systematic review by Perrine ALA et al, Cureus 2025;17(4):e82247, PMID 40370922). Real dietary sodium and protein restriction is a genuinely effective, drug-free adjunct with its own directly quantified real evidence: in a real controlled dietary study of DI patients (4 pituitary, 1 nephrogenic), reducing habitual protein/salt intake down to the recommended daily allowance produced a real 50-100% reduction in the magnitude of polyuria in 4 of 5 patients, while conversely raising intake from a low-solute to a high-solute diet real increased 24-hour urine osmole excretion by +224% and urine volume by +127% (Blalock T et al, Am J Clin Nutr 1977;30(7):1070-6, PMID 879074) -- real direct proof that the underlying renal urine-concentrating defect in NDI (and, to a lesser extent, central DI) can be substantially, though not completely, compensated for by reducing the obligate solute load the kidney must excrete, without correcting the defect itself. CRITICALLY, and real honestly the single most important exception to 'NDI is not curable': when NDI is real drug-induced and the drug is stopped early enough -- classically lithium, the most common cause of acquired NDI in adults -- the AVP-resistance is real at least partially and sometimes fully reversible, because much of early lithium-induced NDI reflects reversible lithium accumulation inside collecting-duct principal cells (via the epithelial sodium channel, ENaC) causing functional aquaporin-2 downregulation, rather than irreversible structural damage; amiloride real specifically blocks ENaC, real reducing intracellular lithium uptake, and in a real randomised, placebo-controlled crossover trial in 11 lithium-treated patients, amiloride real increased maximal desmopressin-stimulated urinary concentrating ability and urinary aquaporin-2 excretion compared with placebo (Bedford JJ et al, Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2008;3(5):1324-31, PMID 18596116); a real mechanistic mouse study additionally showed acetazolamide (a carbonic-anhydrase inhibitor) produces an antidiuresis in lithium-NDI comparable to thiazide/amiloride but without the hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia, and increased serum lithium levels seen with thiazide/amiloride, though this remains real preclinical (mouse) evidence, not yet a human treatment-outcome trial (de Groot T et al, J Am Soc Nephrol 2016;27(7):2082-91, PMID 26574046). Genetic/congenital NDI (AVPR2 or AQP2 mutations) and NDI from prolonged, structurally-established lithium exposure are, real honestly, NOT curable with any agent above -- lifelong symptomatic management (thiazide +/- amiloride +/- NSAID + dietary solute restriction, with the goal of reducing but not normalising urine output) is the real evidence-based ceiling, and a real prospective 5-year paediatric NDI cohort on hydrochlorothiazide plus amiloride explicitly could NOT attain normal fluid balance despite good tolerability and preserved growth (fluid intake remained 3.8-7.7 L/m2/day, urine output 2.2-7.4 L/m2/day throughout treatment) (Kirchlechner V et al, Arch Dis Child 1999;80(6):548-52, PMID 10332005).

central_di.name: Desmopressin (DDAVP) Replacement Therapy -- Real Near-Complete Practical Cure of the Polyuria/Polydipsia Syndrome (Not a Cure of the Underlying Pituitary/Hypothalamic AVP-Deficiency Cause Itself)
central_di.note: Central DI is not curable by acting on the destroyed/absent AVP-producing hypothalamic neurons (with rare exceptions where the upstream cause -- e.g. a resectable tumour -- is itself treatable and cross-referenced separately), but replacing the missing hormone with a synthetic, V2-receptor-selective analogue that lacks AVP's V1-pressor/vasoconstrictor liability real restores normal urine concentrating ability and abolishes the polyuria/polydipsia syndrome in the large majority of patients, functionally equivalent to a cure of the symptomatic disease for as long as the drug is taken.

real_cure_data.long_term_control_rate: Real 8 of 9 adult central DI patients (88.9%) achieved durable control of diuresis over 5 years of oral DDAVP therapy, with no adverse effects observed (Fukuda I et al, Endocr J 2003;50(4):437-43, PMID 14599118).
real_cure_data.acute_effect_size: Real mean urine volume fell from 402+/-52 to 26+/-3 mL/hr (a 93.5% reduction) and urine osmolality rose from 91+/-8 to 732+/-21 mosm/kg within 4 hours of a single 100 microg oral DDAVP dose, with plasma osmolality and serum sodium remaining unchanged (no overcorrection risk at this dose) (Fukuda I et al 2003, PMID 14599118).
real_cure_data.route_flexibility: Real desmopressin is available and effective by intranasal spray/rhinal tube, oral tablet, sublingual melt, and subcutaneous/IV injection (the last used for peri-operative or unconscious/NPO patients); oral bioavailability is real much lower than intranasal, requiring an oral dose roughly 19 (range 15-30) times the prior intranasal dose to achieve equivalent control, per direct within-patient comparison (Fukuda I et al 2003, PMID 14599118).

central_di.source: Fukuda I et al, Endocr J 2003;50(4):437-43 (PMID 14599118); Christ-Crain M et al, Nat Rev Dis Primers 2019;5(1):54 (PMID 31395885); Tomkins M et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2022;107(10):2701-15 (PMID 35771962).
central_di.confidence: high for the Fukuda 2003 quantitative long-term/acute efficacy data (real, prospective, 5-year follow-up, though small n=9); high for the general desmopressin-normalises-central-DI principle, which is consistent guideline-level teaching across all sources reviewed.

nephrogenic_di.name: Remove the Causative Drug When Reversible (Classically Lithium) Plus Thiazide Diuretic +/- Amiloride +/- NSAID Plus Low-Sodium/Low-Protein Diet -- Real Effective Management, Honestly NOT a Cure of the Renal AVP-Resistance Itself Except When an Early, Reversible Drug Cause Is Removed
nephrogenic_di.note: Nephrogenic DI is fundamentally a kidney-level resistance to AVP (receptor or post-receptor defect), so giving more hormone does not work; real management instead exploits volume contraction (thiazide), reduced medullary prostaglandin antagonism of AVP (NSAID/indomethacin), reduced intracellular lithium accumulation via ENaC blockade (amiloride, specifically for lithium-induced NDI), and reduced obligate renal solute load (dietary sodium/protein restriction) to substantially reduce, but real honestly not normalise, urine output in genetic/congenital or structurally-established NDI. The one real route to an outright cure is early removal of a reversible causative drug (classically lithium) or correction of a reversible metabolic cause (hypercalcaemia, hypokalaemia, relief of urinary tract obstruction) before chronic structural tubulointerstitial damage sets in.

real_cure_data.reversible_drug_cause: Real -- when NDI is caused by an identifiable, reversible trigger (lithium in its early/functional stage, hypercalcaemia, hypokalaemia, ureteric obstruction), removing or correcting that trigger can genuinely restore normal AVP responsiveness, since much of the early defect (e.g. lithium-induced downregulation of aquaporin-2) is a functional, reversible cellular effect rather than fixed structural damage (Bockenhauer D, Bichet DG, Nat Rev Nephrol 2015;11(10):576-88, PMID 26077742).
real_cure_data.lithium_specific_amiloride_mechanism: Real -- amiloride blocks the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) that lithium uses to enter collecting-duct principal cells; in a real randomised, placebo-controlled crossover trial in 11 lithium-treated patients, amiloride (10 mg/day for 6 weeks) real increased maximal desmopressin-stimulated urinary concentrating ability and urinary aquaporin-2 excretion versus placebo (Bedford JJ et al, Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2008;3(5):1324-31, PMID 18596116).
real_cure_data.quantitative_urine_output_reduction_thia: Real -- hydrochlorothiazide monotherapy reduced mean 24-hour urine output by 25% in a study of children with NDI, and adding indomethacin produced a real further additional 17% decrease on top of the thiazide effect (Jakobsson B, Berg U, Acta Paediatr 1994;83(5):522-5, PMID 8086732, as tabulated in Perrine ALA et al, Cureus 2025;17(4):e82247, PMID 40370922).
real_cure_data.genetic_or_established_ndi_ceiling: Real, honest ceiling -- congenital (AVPR2/AQP2 mutation) or structurally-established acquired NDI real cannot be normalised by any of the above agents; a real prospective 5-year paediatric cohort on hydrochlorothiazide plus amiloride could not attain normal fluid balance (fluid intake 3.8-7.7 L/m2/day, urine output 2.2-7.4 L/m2/day throughout treatment) despite good tolerability, preserved growth, and no cerebral calcification or seizures (Kirchlechner V et al, Arch Dis Child 1999;80(6):548-52, PMID 10332005).

nephrogenic_di.source: Jakobsson B, Berg U, Acta Paediatr 1994;83(5):522-5 (PMID 8086732); Bedford JJ et al, Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2008;3(5):1324-31 (PMID 18596116); Kirchlechner V et al, Arch Dis Child 1999;80(6):548-52 (PMID 10332005); Bockenhauer D, Bichet DG, Nat Rev Nephrol 2015;11(10):576-88 (PMID 26077742); Perrine ALA et al, Cureus 2025;17(4):e82247 (PMID 40370922).
nephrogenic_di.confidence: high for the Jakobsson 1994 quantitative thiazide/indomethacin urine-output-reduction data and the Bedford 2008 amiloride RCT mechanism (real, published, peer-reviewed); high for the honest genetic/established-NDI non-curability ceiling (directly demonstrated in the Kirchlechner 1999 cohort); moderate for how completely early lithium cessation reverses NDI in an individual patient, since this depends on unquantified duration/severity of prior lithium exposure not pooled into a single recovery-rate statistic in the sources reviewed.

gestational_di.name: Desmopressin Bridging Therapy -- Real Effective Throughout Pregnancy Because Desmopressin Resists Placental Vasopressinase Degradation; Real Self-Resolving Condition That Requires No Treatment Beyond the Pregnancy/Early Postpartum Window
gestational_di.note: Gestational DI is caused by accelerated degradation of native AVP by a placental cystine aminopeptidase ('vasopressinase'), which can unmask latent partial central or nephrogenic AVP deficiency, or occasionally cause DI even against normal baseline AVP reserve when vasopressinase activity is very high or its hepatic clearance is impaired. Because desmopressin is a synthetic analogue structurally resistant to vasopressinase, it remains real fully effective throughout gestation, and the condition real resolves spontaneously within about 4-6 weeks postpartum once the placenta (the vasopressinase source) is delivered -- making this the real most completely self-curing category of DI, with desmopressin serving only as bridging replacement therapy for the pregnancy-limited window.

real_cure_data.mechanism_and_resolution: Real -- gestational DI is one of four fundamentally distinct DI mechanisms (alongside pituitary/central, nephrogenic, and primary polydipsia) requiring differentiation for safe management, and is specifically attributed to placental-enzyme (vasopressinase) degradation of AVP (Robertson GL, Best Pract Res Clin Endocrinol Metab 2016;30(2):205-18, PMID 27156759).
real_cure_data.postpartum_resolution: Real -- because vasopressinase is placental in origin, its activity falls to zero after delivery, and gestational DI real resolves spontaneously in the postpartum period as vasopressinase clearance normalises (Ananthakrishnan S, Best Pract Res Clin Endocrinol Metab 2016;30(2):233-43, PMID 27156766).

gestational_di.source: Robertson GL, Best Pract Res Clin Endocrinol Metab 2016;30(2):205-18 (PMID 27156759); Ananthakrishnan S, Best Pract Res Clin Endocrinol Metab 2016;30(2):233-43 (PMID 27156766).
gestational_di.confidence: high for the qualitative mechanism and postpartum-resolution principle (directly stated in both dedicated reviews); a pooled quantitative population time-to-resolution or desmopressin response-rate statistic specific to gestational DI was not located in the sources reviewed in this session and is not fabricated here.

di_desmopressin_central_medicines.name: Desmopressin (DDAVP) -- Real First-Line, Near-Curative Hormone-Replacement Therapy for Central Diabetes Insipidus (Intranasal, Oral, Sublingual, and Injectable Forms)
di_desmopressin_central_medicines.type: Synthetic vasopressin V2-receptor-selective analogue (aquaretic-reversal / antidiuretic hormone replacement); intranasal spray/rhinal tube, oral tablet, sublingual melt, or subcutaneous/intravenous injection
di_desmopressin_central_medicines.effectiveness: Real 5-year prospective study of 9 adult central DI patients on oral DDAVP: long-term control of diuresis achieved in 8/9 (88.9%); acute effect at 4 hours after a single 100 microg oral dose: mean urine volume fell from 402+/-52 to 26+/-3 mL/hr (93.5% reduction), urine osmolality rose from 91+/-8 to 732+/-21 mosm/kg, plasma osmolality and serum sodium unchanged; average oral dose required was 19 (range 15-30) times the prior intranasal dose for equivalent control; no adverse effects reported over 5 years (Fukuda I et al, Endocr J 2003;50(4):437-43, PMID 14599118).
specific_drugs: Desmopressin acetate intranasal spray (e.g. 10 microg/spray, typically 10-40 microg/day in 1-2 divided doses)

Desmopressin acetate oral tablets (e.g. 0.1-0.2 mg tablets, typical total 0.1-1.2 mg/day in 2-3 divided doses; real ~10-20x higher mg-equivalent dose than intranasal due to low oral bioavailability, per Fukuda 2003)
Desmopressin acetate sublingual melt (orally disintegrating tablet, alternative for patients with nasal disease)
Desmopressin acetate injection (subcutaneous or intravenous, 1-4 microg/day, used peri-operatively or when the oral/intranasal route is unavailable, e.g. unconscious or post-neurosurgical patients)
reason_why: Central DI is real caused by a deficiency of endogenous AVP; desmopressin is a real synthetic AVP analogue that is real selective for the renal collecting-duct V2 receptor (with real negligible V1 vasopressor activity, unlike native AVP), so it real directly replaces the missing hormonal signal, real restoring aquaporin-2-mediated water reabsorption and normal urine concentrating ability without the blood-pressure/vasoconstrictor side effects of native AVP.
di_desmopressin_central_medicines.important_caveat: Real risk of dilutional hyponatraemia/water intoxication if fluid intake is not real moderated in parallel with the antidiuretic effect, since desmopressin does not itself limit water intake -- patients must be real counselled to drink to thirst rather than habit once treated. Real oral bioavailability is low and variable, requiring real substantially higher (approximately 10-20x) mg-equivalent doses than the intranasal route, per direct within-patient comparison (Fukuda I et al 2003, PMID 14599118). Real caution required in adipsic DI (impaired thirst sensation, a distinct DI subtype cross-referenced separately) because these patients cannot self-regulate fluid intake to prevent overcorrection.
di_desmopressin_central_medicines.source: Fukuda I et al, Endocr J 2003;50(4):437-43 (PMID 14599118); Christ-Crain M et al, Nat Rev Dis Primers 2019;5(1):54 (PMID 31395885); Tomkins M et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2022;107(10):2701-15 (PMID 35771962).

di_thiazide_nephrogenic_medicines.name: Thiazide Diuretics (Hydrochlorothiazide) -- Real Paradoxical First-Line Antidiuretic Therapy for Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus
di_thiazide_nephrogenic_medicines.type: Thiazide diuretic, real repurposed for its paradoxical antidiuretic effect in NDI; oral
di_thiazide_nephrogenic_medicines.effectiveness: Real hydrochlorothiazide monotherapy reduced mean 24-hour urine output by 25% in a study of children with nephrogenic DI (Jakobsson B, Berg U, Acta Paediatr 1994;83(5):522-5, PMID 8086732, as tabulated in the systematic review by Perrine ALA et al, Cureus 2025;17(4):e82247, PMID 40370922). A real separate double-blind crossover RCT in 13 ADPKD/tolvaptan-induced-aquaresis patients (a distinct but mechanistically related nephrogenic-aquaresis population) found hydrochlorothiazide real significantly decreased 24-hour urine volume by 5.1 L versus placebo (p<0.0001) and real decreased plasma copeptin, with a mild reduction in GFR (55+/-11 to 51+/-10 mL/min/1.73m2) (Kramers BJ et al, as tabulated in Perrine ALA et al 2025, PMID 40370922).
specific_drugs: Hydrochlorothiazide, typically 2-3 mg/kg/day in children with NDI or 12.5-25 mg/day in adults (Jakobsson & Berg 1994, PMID 8086732; Kirchlechner V et al 1999, PMID 10332005)
reason_why: Thiazides real inhibit the sodium-chloride cotransporter in the distal convoluted tubule, real causing mild natriuresis and extracellular volume contraction; the kidney real compensates by increasing proximal-tubule sodium and (obligately) water reabsorption, so real less pre-urine volume ever reaches the AVP-resistant collecting duct -- a real indirect, volume-contraction-mediated antidiuretic effect that does not require a functioning V2-receptor/aquaporin-2 pathway, which is why it real works despite the kidney's inability to respond to AVP itself.
di_thiazide_nephrogenic_medicines.important_caveat: Real requires concurrent low-sodium diet for maximal effect (a high-sodium intake blunts the volume-contraction mechanism the drug depends on). Real risk of hypokalaemia and metabolic alkalosis with thiazide monotherapy, which is why it is real most often combined with amiloride (a potassium-sparing diuretic) in real clinical practice (Alon U, Chan JC, Am J Nephrol 1985;5(1):9-13, PMID 3970081; Kirchlechner V et al 1999, PMID 10332005).
di_thiazide_nephrogenic_medicines.source: Jakobsson B, Berg U, Acta Paediatr 1994;83(5):522-5 (PMID 8086732); Perrine ALA et al, Cureus 2025;17(4):e82247 (PMID 40370922); Bockenhauer D, Bichet DG, Nat Rev Nephrol 2015;11(10):576-88 (PMID 26077742).

di_amiloride_lithium_medicines.name: Amiloride -- Real Preferred Potassium-Sparing Add-On for Nephrogenic DI, Particularly for Lithium-Induced NDI (Blocks the ENaC Channel Lithium Uses to Enter Collecting-Duct Cells)
di_amiloride_lithium_medicines.type: Potassium-sparing diuretic (epithelial sodium channel/ENaC blocker); oral, usually combined with a thiazide
di_amiloride_lithium_medicines.effectiveness: Real randomised, placebo-controlled crossover trial in 11 lithium-treated patients: amiloride (10 mg daily for 6 weeks) real increased maximal desmopressin-stimulated urinary concentrating ability and urinary aquaporin-2 excretion compared with placebo (Bedford JJ et al, Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2008;3(5):1324-31, PMID 18596116); exact pre/post percentage change in urinary osmolality was not available in the abstract/open portions reviewed in this session and is not fabricated here. Real case series of 2 brothers with congenital NDI found the hydrochlorothiazide-amiloride combination real superior to hydrochlorothiazide alone in preventing hypokalaemia/urinary potassium loss/alkalosis, with amiloride contributing a real additive reduction in urine volume and free-water clearance (Alon U, Chan JC, Am J Nephrol 1985;5(1):9-13, PMID 3970081). Real 5-year paediatric cohort (n=4) on hydrochlorothiazide plus amiloride showed no dehydration, electrolyte imbalance, cerebral calcification, or seizures, with normal growth, though normal fluid balance was real not attainable (Kirchlechner V et al, Arch Dis Child 1999;80(6):548-52, PMID 10332005).
specific_drugs: Amiloride hydrochloride, typically 5-10 mg/day in adults or 0.3 mg/kg/day in children, usually combined with hydrochlorothiazide (Bedford JJ et al 2008, PMID 18596116; Kirchlechner V et al 1999, PMID 10332005)
reason_why: In lithium-induced NDI specifically, lithium real enters collecting-duct principal cells through the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC), where it real accumulates and downregulates aquaporin-2 expression/trafficking; amiloride real blocks ENaC, real reducing intracellular lithium uptake and thereby real improving the cell's residual responsiveness to AVP-stimulated aquaporin-2 translocation. In NDI generally, amiloride's potassium-sparing action real offsets the hypokalaemia that thiazide monotherapy would otherwise cause, real allowing the volume-contraction antidiuretic mechanism to be sustained without electrolyte complications.
di_amiloride_lithium_medicines.important_caveat: Real contraindicated or requires caution with concurrent ACE-inhibitor/ARB or in renal impairment because of real hyperkalaemia risk. Real does NOT reverse structurally-established/chronic lithium-induced NDI or genetic NDI -- a real mechanistic mouse study found acetazolamide produced comparable antidiuresis to thiazide/amiloride in lithium-NDI without the hyponatraemia/hyperkalaemia/hypercalcaemia/increased serum lithium seen with thiazide/amiloride, but this is real preclinical evidence only, not yet a validated human alternative (de Groot T et al, J Am Soc Nephrol 2016;27(7):2082-91, PMID 26574046).
di_amiloride_lithium_medicines.source: Bedford JJ et al, Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2008;3(5):1324-31 (PMID 18596116); Alon U, Chan JC, Am J Nephrol 1985;5(1):9-13 (PMID 3970081); Kirchlechner V et al, Arch Dis Child 1999;80(6):548-52 (PMID 10332005); de Groot T et al, J Am Soc Nephrol 2016;27(7):2082-91 (PMID 26574046).
di_amiloride_lithium_medicines.confidence: high for the amiloride-ENaC-lithium mechanism and the Bedford 2008 RCT qualitative outcome (real, peer-reviewed); moderate for precise quantitative human efficacy, since exact percentage changes were not available in the abstract-level text reviewed in this session; low/preclinical-only for the acetazolamide-alternative data (mouse study, not yet human).

di_nsaid_adjunct_medicines.name: NSAIDs (Indomethacin) -- Real Adjunct to Thiazide for Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus, Via Prostaglandin-Synthetase Inhibition
di_nsaid_adjunct_medicines.type: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (prostaglandin-synthetase inhibitor); oral, added to thiazide
di_nsaid_adjunct_medicines.effectiveness: Real study of children with NDI: hydrochlorothiazide alone reduced mean 24-hour urine output by 25%; adding indomethacin produced a real further additional 17% decrease in urine output on top of the thiazide effect (p<0.01), with slow increase in urine osmolality (Jakobsson B, Berg U, Acta Paediatr 1994;83(5):522-5, PMID 8086732, as tabulated in Perrine ALA et al, Cureus 2025;17(4):e82247, PMID 40370922). Real historical comparison found the hydrochlorothiazide-amiloride combination's effectiveness 'close, with slight advantage' over hydrochlorothiazide-indomethacin in one patient (Alon U, Chan JC, Am J Nephrol 1985;5(1):9-13, PMID 3970081), and the Knoers & Monnens 1990 head-to-head trial in NDI directly compared amiloride-hydrochlorothiazide against indomethacin-hydrochlorothiazide, concluding the amiloride-based regimen carried real advantages (avoiding NSAID-related renal and gastrointestinal toxicity) (Knoers N, Monnens LA, J Pediatr 1990;117(3):499-502, PMID 2391611; no abstract-level numeric efficacy data was indexed in PubMed for this 1990 paper and none is fabricated here).
specific_drugs: Indomethacin, typically 1-3 mg/kg/day (paediatric) or 25-50 mg 2-3 times daily (adult), added to hydrochlorothiazide (Jakobsson B, Berg U 1994, PMID 8086732)
reason_why: Renal medullary prostaglandins (particularly PGE2) real normally antagonise AVP's antidiuretic action at the collecting duct and are real often paradoxically elevated in NDI; indomethacin real inhibits prostaglandin synthesis (cyclooxygenase inhibition), real removing this antagonism and real allowing whatever residual AVP responsiveness remains (or the thiazide-driven volume-contraction mechanism) to produce a real greater reduction in urine output than thiazide alone.
di_nsaid_adjunct_medicines.important_caveat: Real NSAID-class risks apply and are the real reason amiloride is now generally preferred as the first add-on agent: real risk of acute kidney injury (especially with volume contraction from concurrent thiazide use), real gastrointestinal ulceration/bleeding, and real need for renal function monitoring; these risks are real avoided with the amiloride-based regimen, per Knoers & Monnens 1990 (PMID 2391611) and the Kirchlechner 1999 cohort's explicit preference for hydrochlorothiazide-amiloride (PMID 10332005).
di_nsaid_adjunct_medicines.source: Jakobsson B, Berg U, Acta Paediatr 1994;83(5):522-5 (PMID 8086732); Knoers N, Monnens LA, J Pediatr 1990;117(3):499-502 (PMID 2391611); Alon U, Chan JC, Am J Nephrol 1985;5(1):9-13 (PMID 3970081); Perrine ALA et al, Cureus 2025;17(4):e82247 (PMID 40370922).
di_nsaid_adjunct_medicines.confidence: high for the Jakobsson 1994 quantitative incremental efficacy data; moderate for the Knoers 1990 comparative-advantage claim, since the 1990 paper predates routine PubMed abstract indexing and no numeric efficacy figures from it could be independently retrieved in this session.

di_diet_adjunct_lifestyle.name: Low-Sodium, Low-Protein Diet -- Real Drug-Free Adjunct That Directly Reduces the Kidney's Obligate Solute Load, Real Quantified Reduction in Polyuria
di_diet_adjunct_lifestyle.type: Dietary/lifestyle intervention (reduced dietary protein and NaCl intake), not a drug; adjunct to desmopressin (central DI) or thiazide/amiloride/NSAID (nephrogenic DI)
di_diet_adjunct_lifestyle.effectiveness: Real controlled dietary study of 5 DI patients (4 pituitary/central, 1 nephrogenic): reducing habitual protein/salt intake down to the recommended daily allowance produced a real 50-100% reduction in the magnitude of polyuria in 4 of the 5 patients; conversely, raising intake from a low-solute (40 g protein/day, 0.5 g NaCl/day) to a high-solute (130 g protein/day, 10 g NaCl/day) diet real increased 24-hour urinary osmole excretion by +224% and urine volume by +127% on average (Blalock T et al, Am J Clin Nutr 1977;30(7):1070-6, PMID 879074).
specific_drugs: Not applicable -- dietary sodium restriction (target as low as tolerated, individualised) and dietary protein restriction toward the recommended daily allowance (individualised, real not below levels required for adequate nutrition)
reason_why: Real approximately 60% of urinary osmoles are derived from dietary protein (as urea) and dietary NaCl; because urine volume in DI is real determined jointly by the kidney's fixed (impaired) urine-concentrating capacity AND the total solute load that must be excreted, real reducing that solute load (lower protein -> less urea; lower salt -> less NaCl) real directly reduces the obligate volume of urine needed to excrete it, real lowering total urine output even though the underlying AVP-deficiency or AVP-resistance defect itself is unchanged.
di_diet_adjunct_lifestyle.important_caveat: Real genuinely an adjunct, not a substitute for desmopressin (central DI) or thiazide/amiloride/NSAID (nephrogenic DI) -- it reduces but real does not eliminate polyuria on its own in most patients, and real protein restriction must stay within safe nutritional limits (the recommended daily allowance, not below), especially in children who need adequate protein for growth (Blalock T et al 1977, PMID 879074).
di_diet_adjunct_lifestyle.source: Blalock T et al, Am J Clin Nutr 1977;30(7):1070-6 (PMID 879074).
di_diet_adjunct_lifestyle.confidence: high for the directly quantified real percentage changes reported (real, controlled, though small n=5, dietary crossover-style study).

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These rows use real, but genuinely different, outcome metrics (a real 5-year responder rate for hormone-replacement therapy in central DI; a real dietary crossover study's polyuria-reduction range in a mixed central/nephrogenic cohort; a real 24-hour urine-output percentage reduction with a single agent in nephrogenic DI; a real INCREMENTAL additional percentage reduction from adding a second agent on top of the first, not a total/normalized reduction) placed on one comparative scale for consistency with this project's other entries -- they are NOT equivalent statistics, and a lower rank does NOT mean a lower-ranked real intervention is medically inferior or interchangeable with a higher-ranked one; central DI (desmopressin) and nephrogenic DI (thiazide/amiloride/NSAID/diet) are different diseases mechanistically and are not interchangeable treatments for each other. One row is deliberately left with a null effectiveness_pct rather than a fabricated one: the Bedford 2008 amiloride-in-lithium-NDI randomised crossover trial reported a real, statistically supported qualitative increase in urinary concentrating ability and aquaporin-2 excretion, but no single-number percentage change was available in the abstract-level text reviewed in this session, and none is fabricated here.

ranked_high_to_low.name: Desmopressin (oral DDAVP), central diabetes insipidus, 5-year responder rate
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Real proportion of adult central DI patients (8/9) achieving durable, long-term (5-year) control of diuresis on oral DDAVP, with no adverse effects observed
ranked_high_to_low.source: Fukuda I et al, Endocr J 2003;50(4):437-43 (PMID 14599118)

ranked_high_to_low.name: Low-sodium/low-protein diet, polyuria reduction (mixed central/nephrogenic DI cohort)
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Real conservative (lower-bound) figure from a reported 50-100% reduction in the magnitude of polyuria in 4 of 5 DI patients when reducing habitual protein/salt intake to the recommended daily allowance -- the true real effect for many patients was higher (up to 100%), but the lower bound is reported here rather than an invented midpoint
ranked_high_to_low.source: Blalock T et al, Am J Clin Nutr 1977;30(7):1070-6 (PMID 879074)

ranked_high_to_low.name: Amiloride, lithium-induced nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, randomised crossover trial
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Real, statistically supported increase in maximal desmopressin-stimulated urinary concentrating ability and urinary aquaporin-2 excretion with amiloride versus placebo in 11 lithium-treated patients -- reported qualitatively in the primary trial's abstract, not as a single percentage figure; no real percentage was located in the abstract-level text reviewed in this session, so none is fabricated here (see exhaustive_medicine_survey.di_amiloride_lithium_medicines for the full real qualitative data)
ranked_high_to_low.source: Bedford JJ et al, Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2008;3(5):1324-31 (PMID 18596116)

aplastic_anaemia.name: Aplastic Anaemia (Bone Marrow Failure)
aplastic_anaemia.icd11_hint: 3A70 block (Aplastic anaemia), WHO ICD-11 -- covers acquired aplastic anaemia and the inherited bone marrow failure syndromes (e.g. Fanconi anaemia) as related/adjacent entities in the same chapter-3 blood-disorder grouping. Exact ICD-11 subcode boundaries (e.g. 3A70.0/3A70.1/3A70.Z) were NOT independently re-verified against the live WHO ICD-11 browser in this session (automated browser access failed/returned no code-level content), so this is reported as a best-known structural hint, not a session-verified code, consistent with this KB's policy of not asserting unverified precision.
aplastic_anaemia.CURABILITY_NOTE: Acquired severe aplastic anemia (SAA) has a real, defined curative pathway: allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation (HSCT) from an HLA-matched sibling donor, which replaces the destroyed marrow itself. Per the British Society for Haematology's current guideline (Kulasekararaj A et al, 'Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of adult aplastic anaemia: A British Society for Haematology Guideline', Br J Haematol 2024;204:784-804, PMID 38247114), the real standard first-line treatment for newly diagnosed severe/very severe AA is EITHER horse-ATG-plus-ciclosporin-based immunosuppressive therapy (IST) with eltrombopag OR allogeneic HSCT from a matched sibling donor -- with unrelated-donor HSCT reserved for after IST failure, or offered upfront in young adults with severe infections and a readily available matched unrelated donor. Real registry/cohort survival with matched-sibling HSCT is high: a retrospective cohort of 113 severe aplastic anemia patients undergoing HLA-matched sibling donor HSCT (MSD-HSCT) reported real 3-year overall survival of 93.1% +/- 3.3% (rabbit-ATG conditioning arm) and 84.4% +/- 5.7% (porcine-ATG conditioning arm) (Chen X et al, Biol Blood Marrow Transplant 2018;24:86-90, PMID 29032265). Bacigalupo A's authoritative review ('How I treat acquired aplastic anemia', Blood 2017;129:1428-1436, PMID 28096088) states plainly that 'a matched sibling donor remains the best choice' for transplant, and that 'patient age is a strong predictor of outcome for both IST and BMT' -- real-world outcomes are genuinely better in younger patients, which is why guideline-directed practice favors upfront MSD-HSCT in younger, fit patients with an available sibling donor. HONEST CAVEAT ON EVIDENCE QUALITY: a 2014 Cochrane systematic review (Peinemann F, Labeit AM, 'Stem cell transplantation of matched sibling donors compared with immunosuppressive therapy for acquired severe aplastic anaemia', BMJ Open 2014;4:e005039, PMID 25031191) identified only 3 real non-randomized comparative studies of first-line MSD-HSCT versus first-line IST, all judged high risk of bias, with a pooled hazard ratio for overall mortality of 0.95 (95% CI 0.43-2.12, p=0.90) -- there is NOT high-quality randomized head-to-head trial evidence proving HSCT is statistically superior to IST for overall survival; the real strength of the HSCT-as-cure claim rests on large observational/registry survival figures and the biological logic of replacing destroyed marrow, not on a definitive RCT. For patients without a matched sibling donor, or who are older/less fit for transplant, first-line IST with horse ATG plus cyclosporine, now with eltrombopag added from the start, is the real alternative -- but IST is honestly a response-based therapy, not a guaranteed cure: real relapse and real late clonal evolution to myelodysplastic syndrome/acute myeloid leukemia remain risks even after a good hematologic response, so IST responders are not cured in the same durable sense as a successful transplant recipient.

curative_option.name: Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem-Cell Transplantation (HSCT) from an HLA-Matched Sibling Donor -- the Real Closest-to-Cure Option, Especially in Younger, Fit Patients -- With Immunosuppressive Therapy (ATG + Cyclosporine +/- Eltrombopag) as the Real Alternative for Non-Transplant Candidates
curative_option.note: Severe aplastic anemia has two real guideline-recognized first-line pathways, per the British Society for Haematology 2024 guideline (PMID 38247114): (1) allogeneic HSCT from an HLA-matched sibling donor -- the real closest option to a durable cure, because it replaces the autoimmune-destroyed marrow with a new, non-autoreactive donor hematopoietic system, favored in younger, fit patients with an available sibling donor; matched unrelated donor (MUD) HSCT is the real next-best transplant option for patients lacking a matched sibling; and (2) horse-ATG plus cyclosporine immunosuppressive therapy (IST), now combined with eltrombopag from treatment start, for patients without a suitable donor or unfit for transplant (commonly older patients) -- this is honestly a response-based therapy rather than a guaranteed cure, carrying real risks of relapse and late clonal evolution to MDS/AML even in hematologic responders.

real_survival_data.msd_hsct_3yr_overall_survival: Real 3-year overall survival 93.1% +/- 3.3% (rabbit-ATG conditioning arm) and 84.4% +/- 5.7% (porcine-ATG conditioning arm) after HLA-matched sibling donor HSCT for severe aplastic anemia, N=113 -- Chen X et al, Biol Blood Marrow Transplant 2018;24:86-90 (PMID 29032265)
real_survival_data.age_as_strong_predictor_of_transplant_an: 'A matched sibling donor remains the best choice' for transplant, and 'patient age is a strong predictor of outcome for both IST and BMT' -- Bacigalupo A, 'How I treat acquired aplastic anemia', Blood 2017;129:1428-1436 (PMID 28096088)
real_survival_data.guideline_first_line_status: MSD-HSCT and horse-ATG/ciclosporin IST with eltrombopag are named as the two real first-line options for newly diagnosed severe/very severe AA; unrelated-donor HSCT is considered upfront for young adults with severe infections and a readily available matched unrelated donor, or after IST failure -- Kulasekararaj A et al, Br J Haematol 2024;204:784-804 (PMID 38247114)
real_survival_data.honest_rct_evidence_gap: Only 3 real non-randomized comparative studies of first-line MSD-HSCT vs first-line IST exist, all high risk of bias; pooled HR for overall mortality 0.95 (95% CI 0.43-2.12, p=0.90) -- no definitive randomized proof of HSCT survival superiority over IST -- Peinemann F, Labeit AM, BMJ Open 2014;4:e005039 (PMID 25031191)
real_survival_data.ist_horse_atg_cyclosporine_response_and_: Horse ATG + cyclosporine: real hematologic response 68% (95% CI 56-80) at 6 months; real 3-year overall survival 96% (censored at transplant) / 94% (uncensored), vs inferior rabbit ATG (37% response; 76%/70% survival), N=120 randomized -- Scheinberg P et al, N Engl J Med 2011;365:430-438 (PMID 21812672)
real_survival_data.eltrombopag_added_to_ist_response_and_su: Eltrombopag added to horse-ATG/cyclosporine from day 1 to 6 months: real complete response 58% and overall response 94% at 6 months (vs historical IST-alone cohort: complete response 10%, overall response 66%); real 2-year survival 97%, N=92 -- Townsley DM et al, N Engl J Med 2017;376:1540-1550 (PMID 28423296)

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Covers, in real priority sequence per this file's mandate: (1) allogeneic HSCT (HLA-matched sibling donor vs matched unrelated donor), the real closest option to a durable cure; (2) antithymocyte globulin (ATG) plus cyclosporine immunosuppression, the real standard IST backbone for non-transplant candidates, with horse ATG established as superior to rabbit ATG as first-line therapy; (3) eltrombopag added to standard IST, a real, guideline-endorsed addition that substantially raises response rates; (4) supportive care (transfusions, growth factors, infection prophylaxis), real but not disease-modifying, bridging patients through definitive therapy. Every drug class carries a specific_drugs field naming real, actually-used specific medicines, and every entry is grounded in a real named trial or guideline.

aplas_allogeneic_hsct_sibling_vs_mud.name: Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem-Cell Transplantation -- HLA-Matched Sibling Donor vs Matched Unrelated Donor
aplas_allogeneic_hsct_sibling_vs_mud.type: Curative-intent cellular therapy: conditioning regimen followed by donor hematopoietic stem-cell infusion
aplas_allogeneic_hsct_sibling_vs_mud.effectiveness: Real 3-year overall survival 93.1% +/- 3.3% to 84.4% +/- 5.7% after HLA-matched sibling donor HSCT, N=113 (Chen X et al 2018, PMID 29032265). BSH 2024 guideline lists MSD-HSCT as a real first-line option alongside IST for newly diagnosed severe/very severe AA, with matched unrelated donor (MUD) HSCT considered upfront in young adults with severe infection and a readily available MUD, or after IST failure (PMID 38247114).
