systemic_sclerosis.name: Systemic Sclerosis (Scleroderma)
systemic_sclerosis.icd11_hint: 4A42 Systemic sclerosis (4A42.0 Paediatric onset systemic sclerosis, 4A42.1 Diffuse systemic sclerosis, 4A42.2 Limited systemic sclerosis, 4A42.Z unspecified; cross-verified via NLM Clinical Table Search Service ICD-11 API, https://clinicaltables.nlm.nih.gov/api/icd11_codes/v3/search); legacy ICD-10 M34 (Systemic sclerosis)
systemic_sclerosis.CURABILITY_NOTE: Systemic sclerosis (scleroderma) has NO cure: nothing in this survey reverses fibrosis already laid down or restores a normal immune system, and disease-related mortality remains real even with modern therapy. This must be stated plainly. What IS real and dramatic: for patients with severe, early diffuse cutaneous SSc, myeloablative autologous hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation (SCOT trial, Sullivan et al. N Engl J Med 2018, PMID 29298160) achieved 86% overall survival at 72 months vs 51% with standard cyclophosphamide (P=0.02), and 79% per-protocol event-free survival at 54 months vs 50% (P=0.02) -- a genuine, randomized-trial-proven, long-term survival advantage, at the cost of a real early treatment-related mortality risk (3% at 54 months, 6% at 72 months). The independent EBMT/EULAR ASTIS trial (van Laar et al. JAMA 2014, PMID 25058083) confirmed the same long-term event-free survival benefit (hazard ratio 0.34 at 4 years) despite an excess of early deaths in year 1 (8 treatment-related deaths in the transplant arm vs 0 with cyclophosphamide) -- an honest trade-off of real excess early risk for a real long-term survival gain, in carefully selected patients at experienced transplant centers. Separately, for scleroderma renal crisis -- historically often fatal -- ACE inhibitors are a real, life-saving, guideline-mandated emergency treatment: 1-year survival rose from 15% (pre-ACE-inhibitor era) to 76% with ACE inhibitor therapy (P<0.001) (Steen et al. Ann Intern Med 1990, PMID 2382917), and 55% of patients who required dialysis were able to discontinue it while remaining on ACE inhibitors, versus 0% of those not on ACE inhibitors. For the rest of the disease (skin/lung fibrosis, Raynaud's, digital ulcers, pulmonary hypertension), treatment is real but disease-modifying/symptom-controlling rather than curative: cyclophosphamide and mycophenolate mofetil produce modest, real improvements in lung function (2-3 percentage points of FVC), nintedanib slows (does not stop) the rate of interstitial lung disease progression by a calculated ~44%, and calcium-channel blockers, endothelin-receptor antagonists, and PDE5 inhibitors provide real vasodilator relief for Raynaud's phenomenon, digital ulcers, and pulmonary arterial hypertension respectively, without reversing the underlying vasculopathy or fibrosis. Per the EULAR 2023 update (Del Galdo et al., Ann Rheum Dis 2025, PMID 39874231; superseding the 2017 update, Kowal-Bielecka et al., Ann Rheum Dis 2017, PMID 27941129), management remains organ-based and multidisciplinary, and no single therapy is proven to alter overall mortality in unselected SSc -- which is precisely why the HSCT survival data above, in the correctly selected severe-early-diffuse subgroup, represents the single most dramatic real advance in this disease.

curative_option.name: Autologous Hematopoietic Stem-Cell Transplantation for Severe Early Diffuse Cutaneous SSc (Real Long-Term Survival Benefit, Not a Disease Cure) and ACE Inhibitors for Scleroderma Renal Crisis (Real Life-Saving Treatment)
curative_option.note: These are the two genuinely transformative, randomized-trial/large-cohort-proven interventions in SSc. Neither eliminates the underlying autoimmune/fibrotic disease process, but both are real, dramatic, disease-course-altering (HSCT) or life-saving (ACE inhibitors) interventions with hard survival endpoints, not surrogate markers.

autologous_hsct_severe_early_diffuse_cut.mechanism: Myeloablative (SCOT) or non-myeloablative (ASTIS) conditioning followed by reinfusion of CD34+-selected autologous hematopoietic stem cells, eliminating the autoreactive T- and B-cell repertoire and profibrotic cytokine circuits driving SSc, and allowing immune reconstitution from a 'reset' hematopoietic stem-cell pool.

real_outcome_data.astis_early_excess_mortality_year_1: 8 treatment-related deaths in transplant arm vs 0 in cyclophosphamide arm

autologous_hsct_severe_early_diffuse_cut.source: Sullivan KM et al. N Engl J Med. 2018;378(1):35-47. PMID 29298160. van Laar JM et al. JAMA. 2014;311(24):2490-2498. PMID 25058083.

ace_inhibitors_scleroderma_renal_crisis.mechanism: Blockade of angiotensin-converting enzyme interrupts the renin-angiotensin-system-driven malignant hypertension of scleroderma renal crisis (triggered by intrarenal vasospasm/proliferative vasculopathy of interlobular arteries), halting progressive irreversible renal cortical necrosis.

real_outcome_data.dialysis_discontinuation_with_continued_: 55% (11/20) discontinued dialysis after 3-15 months vs 0% (0/15) without ACE inhibitors, P=0.002

ace_inhibitors_scleroderma_renal_crisis.source: Steen VD, Costantino JP, Shapiro AP, Medsger TA Jr. Ann Intern Med. 1990;113(5):352-357. PMID 2382917.

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Full real survey of medicines/cellular therapies used across SSc's organ-based manifestations: severe diffuse skin/organ disease (HSCT), scleroderma renal crisis (ACE inhibitors), skin/lung fibrosis (cyclophosphamide, mycophenolate, nintedanib), Raynaud's phenomenon (calcium channel blockers), and digital ulcers/pulmonary arterial hypertension (endothelin receptor antagonists, PDE5 inhibitors). See curative_option above for the two real disease-course-altering/life-saving interventions.

ss_autologous_hsct_severe_diffuse_cutane.name: Myeloablative CD34+-Selected Autologous HSCT (SCOT Regimen: Total-Body Irradiation + Cyclophosphamide + Equine Anti-Thymocyte Globulin Conditioning)
ss_autologous_hsct_severe_diffuse_cutane.effectiveness: In the NIH-funded SCOT trial (n=75, severe early diffuse cutaneous SSc), per-protocol event-free survival at 54 months was 79% with transplant vs 50% with 12 monthly cyclophosphamide pulses (P=0.02); at 72 months, Kaplan-Meier overall survival was 86% (transplant) vs 51% (cyclophosphamide) (P=0.02) and event-free survival was 74% vs 47% (P=0.03). Only 9% of transplant recipients had started a disease-modifying antirheumatic drug by 54 months vs 44% of the cyclophosphamide group (P=0.001). Treatment-related mortality was 3% at 54 months and 6% at 72 months (vs 0% with cyclophosphamide).
ss_autologous_hsct_severe_diffuse_cutane.reason_why: Myeloablative conditioning eliminates the autoreactive immune repertoire and profibrotic cytokine circuits driving SSc; CD34+ selection removes contaminating lymphocytes from the autograft before reinfusion, allowing immune reconstitution from a 'reset' hematopoietic stem-cell pool.
ss_autologous_hsct_severe_diffuse_cutane.source: Sullivan KM et al. N Engl J Med. 2018;378(1):35-47. PMID 29298160.
ss_autologous_hsct_severe_diffuse_cutane.confidence: high (NIH-funded multicenter phase II/III RCT, real long-term survival endpoint)
ss_autologous_hsct_severe_diffuse_cutane.specific_procedure: Myeloablative autologous HSCT (SCOT protocol): CD34+-selected autograft; conditioning with total-body irradiation, cyclophosphamide, and equine anti-thymocyte globulin

ss_autologous_hsct_severe_diffuse_cutane.name: Autologous HSCT (ASTIS Regimen: Non-Myeloablative Cyclophosphamide + Anti-Thymocyte Globulin Conditioning)
ss_autologous_hsct_severe_diffuse_cutane.effectiveness: In the EBMT/EULAR ASTIS trial (n=156, early diffuse cutaneous SSc), HSCT was associated with excess events in year 1 (16.5% of patients, including 8 treatment-related deaths, vs 10.4% in the cyclophosphamide group with no treatment-related deaths), but a significant long-term event-free survival benefit emerged: time-varying hazard ratio for event-free survival 0.35 (95% CI 0.16-0.74) at 2 years and 0.34 (95% CI 0.16-0.74) at 4 years, with cumulative event rates crossing over by year 4 (19% HSCT vs 26% cyclophosphamide).
ss_autologous_hsct_severe_diffuse_cutane.reason_why: Same immunoablation-and-hematopoietic-reset mechanism as the SCOT regimen, using a non-myeloablative (lower-intensity) conditioning regimen; the real early excess mortality must be weighed against the real long-term survival benefit, which is why patient selection (early diffuse disease, adequate cardiopulmonary reserve, experienced transplant center) is critical.
ss_autologous_hsct_severe_diffuse_cutane.confidence: high (multicenter phase III RCT) with an explicit real early-mortality risk that is not hidden by the long-term benefit
ss_autologous_hsct_severe_diffuse_cutane.specific_procedure: Non-myeloablative autologous HSCT (ASTIS protocol): cyclophosphamide + anti-thymocyte globulin conditioning

ss_ace_inhibitors_renal_crisis.name: ACE Inhibitors (Captopril and Class) for Scleroderma Renal Crisis
ss_ace_inhibitors_renal_crisis.effectiveness: In a 108-patient University of Pittsburgh cohort followed 1972-1987, ACE inhibitor therapy dramatically improved survival of scleroderma renal crisis: 1-year survival was 76% with ACE inhibitors vs 15% without (P<0.001). Among patients who survived more than 3 months on dialysis and continued ACE inhibitor therapy, 55% (11/20) were able to discontinue dialysis after 3-15 months, versus 0% (0/15) of dialysis patients not on ACE inhibitors (P=0.002).
ss_ace_inhibitors_renal_crisis.reason_why: Scleroderma renal crisis is driven by severe renin-angiotensin-system activation following intrarenal vasospasm/proliferative ('onion-skin') vasculopathy of the interlobular arteries; ACE inhibitors block conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II, interrupting the malignant-hypertension feedback loop that would otherwise cause progressive irreversible renal cortical necrosis.
ss_ace_inhibitors_renal_crisis.source: Steen VD, Costantino JP, Shapiro AP, Medsger TA Jr. Ann Intern Med. 1990;113(5):352-357. PMID 2382917.
ss_ace_inhibitors_renal_crisis.confidence: high (real, decades-replicated, guideline-mandated life-saving intervention; scleroderma renal crisis is a medical emergency requiring ACE-inhibitor initiation regardless of degree of renal impairment)
specific_drugs: Captopril (short-acting, preferred for rapid titration in acute crisis)

ss_mycophenolate_cyclophosphamide_skin_l.name: Oral Cyclophosphamide for Skin/Lung Fibrosis (Scleroderma Lung Study I)
ss_mycophenolate_cyclophosphamide_skin_l.effectiveness: In SLS-I (n=158), 1 year of oral cyclophosphamide (<=2 mg/kg/day) produced a mean adjusted 12-month FVC % predicted advantage of 2.53 percentage points over placebo (95% CI 0.28-4.79, P<0.03), with the benefit on lung function, dyspnea, skin thickening and quality of life maintained through 24 months.
ss_mycophenolate_cyclophosphamide_skin_l.reason_why: Alkylates DNA in proliferating lymphocytes, suppressing the autoreactive immune/inflammatory infiltrate (active alveolitis) that drives early SSc-associated interstitial lung disease and dermal fibroblast activation.
ss_mycophenolate_cyclophosphamide_skin_l.source: Tashkin DP et al. N Engl J Med. 2006;354(25):2655-2666. PMID 16790698.
ss_mycophenolate_cyclophosphamide_skin_l.confidence: high (double-blind placebo-controlled RCT), but the effect size is honestly modest, not disease-reversing

ss_mycophenolate_cyclophosphamide_skin_l.name: Mycophenolate Mofetil for Skin/Lung Fibrosis (Scleroderma Lung Study II)
ss_mycophenolate_cyclophosphamide_skin_l.effectiveness: In SLS-II (n=142), 2 years of mycophenolate mofetil produced a within-group adjusted FVC % predicted improvement from baseline of 2.19 percentage points (95% CI 0.53-3.84) at 24 months, statistically indistinguishable from 1 year of cyclophosphamide (2.88 percentage points, 95% CI 1.19-4.58; between-group P=0.24 -- the trial was formally negative for superiority). Mycophenolate had fewer deaths (7% vs 15%), less leucopenia/thrombocytopenia, and fewer withdrawals than cyclophosphamide, which is why it is now generally preferred first-line despite equivalent, not superior, efficacy.
ss_mycophenolate_cyclophosphamide_skin_l.reason_why: Selectively inhibits inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase, blocking de novo purine synthesis in proliferating T and B lymphocytes, suppressing the immune-driven fibrotic cascade in SSc-ILD with a more favorable toxicity profile than an alkylating agent.
ss_mycophenolate_cyclophosphamide_skin_l.source: Tashkin DP et al. Lancet Respir Med. 2016;4(9):708-719. PMID 27469583.
ss_mycophenolate_cyclophosphamide_skin_l.confidence: high (double-blind, double-dummy RCT); real non-inferiority to cyclophosphamide with better tolerability, not proven superiority

ss_nintedanib_ssc_ild.name: Nintedanib for SSc-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease (SENSCIS Trial)
ss_nintedanib_ssc_ild.effectiveness: In SENSCIS (n=576), the adjusted annual rate of decline in FVC was -52.4 mL/year with nintedanib vs -93.3 mL/year with placebo (between-group difference 41.0 mL/year, 95% CI 2.9-79.0, P=0.04) -- a calculated 44% relative reduction in the rate of lung-function decline. There was no significant benefit on skin score (modified Rodnan skin score) or respiratory quality of life (SGRQ).
ss_nintedanib_ssc_ild.reason_why: Inhibits platelet-derived growth factor receptor, fibroblast growth factor receptor, and vascular endothelial growth factor receptor tyrosine kinases implicated in fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition and lung fibrogenesis, slowing (not reversing) the rate of fibrotic lung-function loss -- the same antifibrotic mechanism class first proven in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
ss_nintedanib_ssc_ild.source: Distler O et al. N Engl J Med. 2019;380(26):2518-2528. PMID 31112379.
ss_nintedanib_ssc_ild.confidence: high (double-blind placebo-controlled RCT); this is a rate-of-decline slowing effect, not an improvement or cure -- 75.7% of patients had diarrhea vs 31.6% on placebo

ss_calcium_channel_blockers_raynauds.name: Calcium Channel Blockers (Nifedipine and Class) for Raynaud's Phenomenon in SSc
ss_calcium_channel_blockers_raynauds.effectiveness: Cochrane-methodology meta-analysis of 8 RCTs (n=109 SSc patients) found calcium-channel blockers reduced the frequency of ischemic attacks by a weighted mean difference of 8.3 attacks per 2 weeks (95% CI -15.71 to -0.91) and reduced attack severity by approximately 35% (standardized mean difference -0.69, 95% CI -1.21 to -0.17) versus placebo; nifedipine alone showed the largest effect (WMD -10.21 attacks/2 weeks).
ss_calcium_channel_blockers_raynauds.reason_why: Blocks L-type voltage-gated calcium channels in vascular smooth muscle, reducing intracellular calcium influx and producing peripheral/digital vasodilation, directly counteracting the vasospastic component of SSc-associated Raynaud's phenomenon on top of the fixed structural vasculopathy that CCBs cannot reverse.
ss_calcium_channel_blockers_raynauds.source: Thompson AE, Pope JE. Arthritis Rheum. 2001;44(8):1841-1847. PMID 11508437.
ss_calcium_channel_blockers_raynauds.confidence: moderate (small pooled n=109 across 8 trials, mostly crossover design with possible order effects, per the authors' own caveat) -- described by the authors themselves as 'moderate at best'

ss_endothelin_pde5_pulmonary_hypertensio.name: Bosentan (Dual Endothelin Receptor Antagonist) for Digital Ulcers and Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension in SSc
ss_endothelin_pde5_pulmonary_hypertensio.effectiveness: In RAPIDS-2 (n=188 SSc patients with active digital ulcers), bosentan reduced the number of new digital ulcers over 24 weeks by 30% versus placebo (mean 1.9 vs 2.7 new ulcers, P=0.04); it did not accelerate healing of the existing ('cardinal') ulcer. Bosentan is also an approved therapy for pulmonary arterial hypertension based on the general endothelin-antagonist PAH evidence base, rather than an SSc-PAH-specific pivotal trial verified in this session.
ss_endothelin_pde5_pulmonary_hypertensio.reason_why: Endothelin-1 is markedly overexpressed in SSc vasculopathy and drives both pulmonary and digital vasoconstriction plus vascular smooth-muscle/fibroblast proliferation; blocking both ETA and ETB receptors reduces this vasoconstrictive/proliferative drive, preventing new ischemic digital lesions and pulmonary vascular remodeling.
ss_endothelin_pde5_pulmonary_hypertensio.source: Matucci-Cerinic M et al. Ann Rheum Dis. 2011;70(1):32-38. PMID 20805294.
ss_endothelin_pde5_pulmonary_hypertensio.confidence: high for new-digital-ulcer prevention (RAPIDS-2 RCT); hepatotoxicity (elevated aminotransferases) and peripheral oedema require monitoring

ss_endothelin_pde5_pulmonary_hypertensio.name: Sildenafil (PDE5 Inhibitor) for Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension
ss_endothelin_pde5_pulmonary_hypertensio.effectiveness: In the pivotal SUPER-1 trial (n=278 patients with idiopathic PAH or PAH associated with connective-tissue disease or repaired congenital shunts -- not an SSc-only trial), sildenafil produced a placebo-corrected improvement in 6-minute walk distance of 45-50 m (13.0-14.7%) across the 20-80 mg three-times-daily doses (P<0.001 for all), with improved mean pulmonary artery pressure and WHO functional class.
ss_endothelin_pde5_pulmonary_hypertensio.reason_why: Inhibits phosphodiesterase type 5, preventing breakdown of cyclic GMP downstream of nitric oxide signaling, producing pulmonary vascular smooth-muscle relaxation and antiproliferative effects -- targeting the vasoconstrictive/remodeling arm of PAH pathophysiology that also underlies SSc-associated pulmonary hypertension.
ss_endothelin_pde5_pulmonary_hypertensio.source: Galie N et al. N Engl J Med. 2005;353(20):2148-2157. PMID 16291984.
ss_endothelin_pde5_pulmonary_hypertensio.confidence: moderate-high for the general PAH indication; connective-tissue-disease-associated PAH (including SSc) was a real subgroup within this trial rather than an SSc-exclusive pivotal study, so this effect size should be read as PAH-of-mixed-etiology data, not SSc-specific

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These real percentages come from DIFFERENT trials/cohorts measuring DIFFERENT endpoints (hard survival, event-free survival, dialysis-free survival, lung-function decline, symptom-severity reduction, and walk-distance improvement) in DIFFERENT SSc subpopulations (severe early diffuse disease for HSCT; renal-crisis patients for ACE inhibitors; ILD patients for cyclophosphamide/mycophenolate/nintedanib; Raynaud's/digital-ulcer patients for calcium-channel blockers/bosentan; mixed-etiology PAH, including but not limited to SSc, for sildenafil) -- ranking together is directionally useful, not strict apples-to-apples. Rows 8-9 (cyclophosphamide, mycophenolate) report an absolute percentage-point improvement in FVC % predicted, NOT a percentage of patients responding -- flagged explicitly in each row's metric field so the two number types are not confused.

ranked_high_to_low.name: Autologous HSCT (SCOT trial, severe early diffuse cutaneous SSc)
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Kaplan-Meier overall survival at 72 months (vs 51% with cyclophosphamide), n=75
ranked_high_to_low.source: Sullivan KM et al. N Engl J Med. 2018 (PMID 29298160)

ranked_high_to_low.name: Autologous HSCT (ASTIS trial, early diffuse cutaneous SSc)
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Event-free survival at 4 years (100% minus 19% cumulative event rate), n=156; long-term benefit follows excess early (year-1) transplant-related mortality
ranked_high_to_low.source: van Laar JM et al. JAMA. 2014 (PMID 25058083)

ranked_high_to_low.name: ACE inhibitors for scleroderma renal crisis
ranked_high_to_low.metric: 1-year survival with ACE inhibitors (vs 15% without), n=108, P<0.001
ranked_high_to_low.source: Steen VD et al. Ann Intern Med. 1990 (PMID 2382917)

ranked_high_to_low.name: Nintedanib for SSc-associated interstitial lung disease (SENSCIS)
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Calculated relative reduction in annual rate of FVC decline (-52.4 vs -93.3 mL/year, P=0.04), n=576
ranked_high_to_low.source: Distler O et al. N Engl J Med. 2019 (PMID 31112379)

systemic_sclerosis.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE: Scleroderma renal crisis (SRC) is a real, well-documented, acute life-threatening emergency in systemic sclerosis and must bypass the normal doctor-approval-queue flow to trigger immediate real-world emergency-service guidance (call ambulance/go to ER now, urgent nephrology plus rheumatology referral), not routine queuing. SRC classically presents with abrupt-onset new or rapidly accelerating hypertension (blood pressure that is markedly higher than the patient's own baseline, even if not 'severe' by absolute population thresholds), a rapid rise in serum creatinine, headache, visual disturbance or hypertensive encephalopathy, flash pulmonary oedema, and evidence of microangiopathic haemolysis/thrombotic microangiopathy (schistocytes, low haptoglobin, thrombocytopenia) on labs (Steen VD, 'Kidney involvement in systemic sclerosis', Presse Med 2014;43(10 Pt 2):e305-314, PMID 25174767). Real, actionable risk factors that must raise suspicion: early diffuse cutaneous disease (typically within the first 4 years of skin involvement), rapidly progressive skin thickening, new tendon friction rubs, anti-RNA-polymerase-III antibody positivity (20-year cumulative SRC incidence 28.1% in anti-RNA-polymerase-III-positive patients versus 0.3% in anticentromere-positive limited cutaneous disease -- Nihtyanova SI et al, Arthritis Rheumatol 2020;72:465-476, PMID 31682743, n=1325), and, critically, RECENT HIGH-DOSE CORTICOSTEROID EXPOSURE: a real case-control study (110 SRC cases matched to controls) found antecedent high-dose corticosteroids (>=15 mg/day prednisone-equivalent) in the 6 months before onset in 36% of SRC patients versus 12% of matched controls (McNemar odds ratio 4.37, 95% CI 2.03-9.43, P<0.0001) -- this is a real, modifiable, physician-controllable trigger, and high-dose steroids should be avoided in early diffuse disease at risk of SRC (Steen VD, Medsger TA Jr, Arthritis Rheum 1998;41:1613-1619, PMID 9751093). Outcome depends entirely on speed of recognition and immediate ACE-inhibitor initiation: in a real prospective cohort of 145 SRC patients followed 5-10 years, 61% had a good outcome (55 needed no dialysis, 34 needed only temporary dialysis, of whom just 4% progressed to permanent renal failure) while 39% had a bad outcome (permanent dialysis or early death); more than half of patients who initially required dialysis were able to discontinue it 3-18 months later, so ACE inhibitors must be continued even after dialysis begins (Steen VD, 'Long-term outcomes of scleroderma renal crisis', Ann Intern Med 2000;133:600-603, PMID 11033587). This is a real dial-emergency-services event, not a routine flare. Separately, when systemic sclerosis causes secondary organ-specific emergencies -- pulmonary arterial hypertension decompensating into acute right heart failure, an acute exacerbation of SSc-associated interstitial lung disease, or SSc pericardial effusion progressing to cardiac tamponade -- the same real emergency-recognition criteria already documented in this knowledge base's pulmonary_hypertension, interstitial_lung_disease, and pericardial_disease entries apply in full and must equally bypass routine queuing.

limited_vs_diffuse_cutaneous_subsets.finding: Systemic sclerosis is clinically subdivided by the extent of skin involvement into limited cutaneous SSc (lcSSc) -- skin thickening confined distal to the elbows and knees, which may also involve the face and neck, generally slower-evolving with a longer Raynaud-phenomenon-to-other-organ-involvement interval -- and diffuse cutaneous SSc (dcSSc) -- skin thickening extending proximal to the elbows/knees and onto the trunk, with more rapid progression and a higher early burden of interstitial lung disease, scleroderma renal crisis, and cardiac involvement. This is the foundational LeRoy/Medsger subset system still in clinical use.
limited_vs_diffuse_cutaneous_subsets.source: LeRoy EC, Black C, Fleischmajer R, Jablonska S, Krieg T, Medsger TA Jr, Rowell N, Wollheim F, 'Scleroderma (systemic sclerosis): classification, subsets and pathogenesis', J Rheumatol 1988;15:202-205, PMID 3361530
limited_vs_diffuse_cutaneous_subsets.confidence: high - this is the foundational, universally taught subset classification for SSc, still the working clinical framework layered under the 2013 ACR/EULAR classification criteria

crest_syndrome.finding: CREST syndrome (Calcinosis cutis, Raynaud phenomenon, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia) is the historic descriptive acronym for the clinical constellation seen in most limited cutaneous SSc patients; it is now largely subsumed under the 'limited cutaneous SSc' terminology in modern classification but the CREST features remain the clinically recognised presenting picture of that subset and are individually captured as items in the ACR/EULAR 2013 classification criteria (skin thickening of the fingers, telangiectasia) and in routine clinical description.
crest_syndrome.source: LeRoy EC et al, J Rheumatol 1988;15:202-205, PMID 3361530; van den Hoogen F et al, Arthritis Rheum 2013;65:2737-2747, PMID 24122180
crest_syndrome.confidence: high - CREST is a long-standing, well-recognised descriptive term; modern nomenclature prefers 'limited cutaneous SSc' but the clinical picture it describes is unchanged

raynaud_phenomenon.finding: Raynaud phenomenon -- episodic digital vasospasm with characteristic white-blue-red colour change on cold/stress exposure -- is typically the earliest clinical manifestation of SSc, often preceding skin thickening and other organ involvement by months to years, and is the clinical mirror of the microvascular damage that nailfold videocapillaroscopy detects morphologically. Its presence with abnormal nailfold capillaries and SSc-specific autoantibodies is what allows early differentiation of secondary (SSc-associated) from primary Raynaud phenomenon.
raynaud_phenomenon.source: Cutolo M, Sulli A, Smith V, 'Assessing microvascular changes in systemic sclerosis diagnosis and management', Nat Rev Rheumatol 2010;6:578-587, PMID 20703220
raynaud_phenomenon.confidence: high - Raynaud as the earliest, near-universal presenting feature is foundational and directly stated in this primary review

skin_thickening_and_disease_extent.finding: Progressive skin thickening/fibrosis (sclerodactyly, and in diffuse disease, truncal and proximal-limb thickening) is quantified clinically with the modified Rodnan skin score (mRSS), which is used both as a bedside severity marker and as a real, validated outcome measure in randomized SSc trials (mRSS was one of the five hierarchical components of the primary global rank composite outcome in the SCOT hematopoietic stem-cell-transplant trial).
skin_thickening_and_disease_extent.source: Sullivan KM et al, 'Myeloablative Autologous Stem-Cell Transplantation for Severe Scleroderma', N Engl J Med 2018;378:35-47, PMID 29298160
skin_thickening_and_disease_extent.confidence: high - mRSS as a real, trial-validated skin severity/outcome measure is directly documented in this primary randomized trial

gastrointestinal_involvement.finding: The gastrointestinal tract is the most frequently affected internal organ system in SSc, most commonly via oesophageal smooth-muscle hypomotility producing reflux/GERD (cross-reference this KB's gerd entry for the GERD symptom/emergency framework itself). A less common but real and clinically important SSc-specific GI vascular lesion is gastric antral vascular ectasia (GAVE, 'watermelon stomach'): in a real EUSTAR case-control study of 49 SSc-GAVE patients matched to 93 SSc controls, GAVE prevalence was about 1% of SSc patients, it was associated with anti-RNA-polymerase-III antibodies (odds ratio 4.6, 95% CI 1.2-21.1), it caused anaemia in 82% of cases (45% requiring blood transfusion), and SSc-GAVE patients had significantly more scleroderma renal crisis than matched controls (12% vs 2%, P=0.01) -- i.e. GAVE is a marker of the same vascular/anti-RNA-polymerase-III-driven phenotype that also drives renal crisis risk.
gastrointestinal_involvement.source: Ghrenassia E et al, 'Prevalence, correlates and outcomes of gastric antral vascular ectasia in systemic sclerosis: a EUSTAR case-control study', J Rheumatol 2014;41:99-105, PMID 24293584
gastrointestinal_involvement.confidence: high - specific prevalence, odds ratio, transfusion rate and renal-crisis co-occurrence figures are taken directly from this primary case-control study

pulmonary_involvement.finding: Interstitial lung disease (ILD) and pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) are the two dominant pulmonary manifestations of SSc and, together, are its leading causes of death (cross-reference this KB's interstitial_lung_disease and pulmonary_hypertension entries for the organ-specific symptom/emergency frameworks). Risk is strongly antibody-stratified: in a 1,325-patient cohort, clinically significant pulmonary fibrosis reached 86.1% (limited cutaneous subset) and 84% (diffuse cutaneous subset) by 15 years in anti-Scl-70 (topoisomerase I)-positive patients, versus only 8.5% in anticentromere-positive limited cutaneous patients; pulmonary hypertension incidence at 20 years was highest (33.8%) in the anti-U3-RNP-positive group.
pulmonary_involvement.source: Nihtyanova SI et al, 'Using Autoantibodies and Cutaneous Subset to Develop Outcome-Based Disease Classification in Systemic Sclerosis', Arthritis Rheumatol 2020;72:465-476, PMID 31682743
pulmonary_involvement.confidence: high - antibody-stratified organ-involvement incidence figures are taken directly from this primary cohort study

cardiac_involvement.finding: Primary cardiac involvement in SSc (myocardial fibrosis, conduction disease, pericardial disease -- cross-reference this KB's pericardial_disease entry) is antibody- and subset-dependent: in the same 1,325-patient cohort, 20-year cardiac SSc incidence ranged from as low as 4.9% in anticentromere-positive limited cutaneous disease to 12.9-13.2% in anti-Scl-70-positive diffuse disease and anti-U3-RNP-positive patients respectively.
cardiac_involvement.source: Nihtyanova SI et al, Arthritis Rheumatol 2020;72:465-476, PMID 31682743
cardiac_involvement.confidence: high - figures taken directly from this primary cohort study

renal_involvement_scleroderma_renal_cris.finding: Renal involvement in SSc is dominated by scleroderma renal crisis (SRC) -- once the most severe complication and the leading cause of death in scleroderma before ACE inhibitors, now a very treatable complication if recognised early. It presents with abrupt malignant hypertension, rapidly rising creatinine, and microangiopathic haemolysis, and its incidence is sharply antibody-dependent: 20-year cumulative incidence is 28.1% in anti-RNA-polymerase-III-positive patients versus 0.3% in anticentromere-positive limited cutaneous SSc and 2.7% in limited cutaneous SSc with other/no SSc-specific antibodies (see this entry's top-level EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE for the full acute-recognition and outcome data).
renal_involvement_scleroderma_renal_cris.source: Steen VD, Presse Med 2014;43(10 Pt 2):e305-314, PMID 25174767; Nihtyanova SI et al, Arthritis Rheumatol 2020;72:465-476, PMID 31682743
renal_involvement_scleroderma_renal_cris.confidence: high - both the qualitative clinical picture and the antibody-stratified incidence numbers come from these primary sources

acr_eular_2013_classification_criteria.finding: The 2013 ACR/EULAR classification criteria for SSc were built because the older 1980 ACR criteria lacked sensitivity for early SSc and limited cutaneous disease. Under the new system, skin thickening of the fingers extending proximal to the metacarpophalangeal joints is, by itself, sufficient to classify a patient as having SSc; if that is absent, seven additive weighted items are scored: skin thickening of the fingers (distal only), fingertip lesions (digital tip ulcers or pitting scars), telangiectasia, abnormal nailfold capillaries, interstitial lung disease or pulmonary arterial hypertension, Raynaud's phenomenon, and SSc-related autoantibodies (anticentromere, anti-topoisomerase I/Scl-70, or anti-RNA polymerase III). In the validation cohort, sensitivity/specificity were 0.91/0.92 for the new criteria versus 0.75/0.72 for the 1980 ACR criteria, and every patient classified as SSc under the 1980 criteria was also captured by the new criteria, plus additional true cases.
acr_eular_2013_classification_criteria.source: van den Hoogen F et al, '2013 classification criteria for systemic sclerosis: an American College of Rheumatology/European League against Rheumatism collaborative initiative', Arthritis Rheum 2013;65:2737-2747 (PMID 24122180); simultaneously published in Ann Rheum Dis 2013;72:1747-1755 (PMID 24092682)
acr_eular_2013_classification_criteria.confidence: high - sensitivity/specificity figures and the criteria structure are taken directly from the primary validation abstract

autoantibody_profiles.finding: SSc-specific autoantibodies are both diagnostic (one of the seven ACR/EULAR 2013 criteria items) and strongly prognostic, defining distinct clinical/outcome subsets in a 1,325-patient cohort: (1) anticentromere antibody (ACA)-positive limited cutaneous SSc (n=374) has the best prognosis -- highest 20-year survival (65.3%), lowest pulmonary fibrosis (8.5%), lowest scleroderma renal crisis (0.3%), and lowest cardiac involvement (4.9%); (2) anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I)-positive patients have the highest pulmonary fibrosis risk (86.1% in limited, 84% in diffuse cutaneous disease at 15 years), and anti-Scl-70-positive diffuse cutaneous SSc has the worst 20-year survival of any subgroup (32.4%); (3) anti-RNA-polymerase III-positive patients (n=147) have the highest scleroderma renal crisis incidence (28.1% at 20 years) and are typically associated with rapidly progressive diffuse skin disease; (4) anti-U3-RNP-positive patients (n=56) have the highest pulmonary hypertension (33.8%) and cardiac involvement (13.2%) at 20 years.
autoantibody_profiles.source: Nihtyanova SI et al, Arthritis Rheumatol 2020;72:465-476, PMID 31682743
autoantibody_profiles.confidence: high - all figures taken directly from this primary 1,325-patient cohort study

nailfold_capillaroscopy.finding: Nailfold videocapillaroscopy (NVC) is a real, non-invasive diagnostic tool that images the cutaneous microvasculature and identifies morphological patterns specific to SSc disease stage -- described as 'early', 'active', and 'late' scleroderma patterns -- enabling early differentiation of primary from SSc-associated (secondary) Raynaud phenomenon before other organ involvement appears. Reduced capillary density on NVC is itself a marker of disease severity, associated with higher risk of digital ulcers and pulmonary arterial hypertension. Abnormal nailfold capillaries are one of the seven weighted items in the ACR/EULAR 2013 classification criteria.
nailfold_capillaroscopy.source: Cutolo M, Sulli A, Smith V, Nat Rev Rheumatol 2010;6:578-587, PMID 20703220; van den Hoogen F et al, Arthritis Rheum 2013;65:2737-2747, PMID 24122180
nailfold_capillaroscopy.confidence: high - the NVC pattern nomenclature and its prognostic associations (digital ulcers, PAH) are stated directly in the primary review, and its inclusion in the classification criteria is confirmed in the primary criteria paper

survival_by_autoantibody_and_cutaneous_s.finding: Overall SSc survival is heavily determined by autoantibody profile combined with cutaneous subset rather than by 'SSc' as a single uniform disease. In the largest such cohort (n=1,325), 20-year survival ranged from 65.3% (best: anticentromere-positive limited cutaneous SSc) and 61.8% (anti-Scl-70-positive limited cutaneous SSc) down to 33.6% (diffuse cutaneous SSc with other/no SSc-specific antibodies) and 32.4% (worst: anti-Scl-70-positive diffuse cutaneous SSc) -- a roughly two-fold difference in 20-year survival driven by antibody/subset combination alone, which is the basis for a proposed antibody-plus-subset outcome classification scheme intended to replace subset alone for prognosis and trial design.
survival_by_autoantibody_and_cutaneous_s.source: Nihtyanova SI et al, Arthritis Rheumatol 2020;72:465-476, PMID 31682743
survival_by_autoantibody_and_cutaneous_s.confidence: high - figures taken directly from this primary cohort study

scleroderma_renal_crisis_outcomes_and_a_.finding: SRC outcome is not fixed -- it depends on speed of recognition and treatment. In a real prospective cohort of 145 SRC patients followed 5-10 years, 61% had a good outcome (no dialysis or only temporary dialysis, with just 4% of the temporary-dialysis group progressing to permanent renal failure) while 39% had a bad outcome (permanent dialysis or early death); over half of patients requiring initial dialysis were able to stop it 3-18 months later with continued ACE inhibitor therapy. Separately, a real, modifiable trigger has been identified: antecedent high-dose corticosteroids (>=15 mg/day prednisone-equivalent) in the 6 months before onset were present in 36% of SRC cases versus 12% of matched controls (odds ratio 4.37, P<0.0001) -- meaning a substantial share of SRC risk is iatrogenic and avoidable by not prescribing high-dose steroids in early diffuse disease.
scleroderma_renal_crisis_outcomes_and_a_.source: Steen VD, 'Long-term outcomes of scleroderma renal crisis', Ann Intern Med 2000;133:600-603, PMID 11033587; Steen VD, Medsger TA Jr, Arthritis Rheum 1998;41:1613-1619, PMID 9751093
scleroderma_renal_crisis_outcomes_and_a_.confidence: high - both outcome and risk-factor figures are taken directly from these primary studies

autologous_hsct_real_trial_proven_diseas.finding: SSc has no cure, but real, randomized, published trial data show that early autologous haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation (HSCT) genuinely transforms the natural history of severe early diffuse cutaneous SSc, at the cost of real upfront transplant risk. In the ASTIS trial (156 patients with early diffuse cutaneous SSc, HSCT vs 12 monthly IV cyclophosphamide pulses), HSCT carried a higher first-year event rate driven by 8 treatment-related deaths (13 events, 16.5%, versus 8 events, 10.4%, with zero treatment-related deaths in the cyclophosphamide arm), but this reversed by year 4 (15 cumulative events, 19%, in the HSCT arm versus 20 events, 26%, with cyclophosphamide), giving a time-varying hazard ratio for event-free survival of 0.34 (95% CI 0.16-0.74) favouring HSCT at 4 years. The subsequent SCOT trial (75 patients with severe scleroderma, myeloablative CD34+-selected autologous HSCT vs cyclophosphamide) showed an even larger and more durable effect: at 72 months, event-free survival was 74% with HSCT versus 47% with cyclophosphamide (P=0.03), and overall survival was 86% with HSCT versus 51% with cyclophosphamide (P=0.02); only 9% of HSCT patients had needed to start additional disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs by 54 months, versus 44% of cyclophosphamide patients (P=0.001); treatment-related mortality with HSCT was 3% at 54 months and 6% at 72 months (versus 0% with cyclophosphamide). This is real, dramatic, trial-proven evidence that -- in the right patient (early severe diffuse disease, fit enough for transplant, treated at a specialist transplant centre) -- the disease's otherwise poor natural history can be genuinely altered; it is a disease-course-changing intervention, not a cure, and does not reverse fibrosis or organ damage already present. (Full treatment protocol, patient-selection criteria and dosing are doctor_reference_only and, if present, are covered in this entry's curative_option/treatment content rather than here.)
autologous_hsct_real_trial_proven_diseas.source: van Laar JM et al, 'Autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation vs intravenous pulse cyclophosphamide in diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis: a randomized clinical trial', JAMA 2014;311:2490-2498, PMID 25058083; Sullivan KM et al, 'Myeloablative Autologous Stem-Cell Transplantation for Severe Scleroderma', N Engl J Med 2018;378:35-47, PMID 29298160
autologous_hsct_real_trial_proven_diseas.confidence: high - all event counts, percentages, hazard ratios and P-values are taken directly from these two primary randomized controlled trials

kawasaki_disease.name: Kawasaki Disease
kawasaki_disease.icd11_hint: ICD-10 crosswalk M30.3 (Mucocutaneous lymph node syndrome [Kawasaki]) is the long-established WHO classification for this disease. The exact live WHO ICD-11 foundation/linearization code could NOT be independently machine-verified in this session (same ICD-11 browser/API access limitation noted in the sibling takayasu_arteritis entry in this knowledge base) -- flagged honestly rather than guessed; confirm the exact ICD-11 code against the official WHO ICD-11 coding tool before clinical/billing use.
kawasaki_disease.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE: Two real, distinct Kawasaki-disease-related situations must bypass the normal doctor-approval-queue flow and trigger immediate real-world emergency guidance (call ambulance/go to ER now): (1) Kawasaki disease shock syndrome (KDSS) -- a real, described clinical entity in which a subset of Kawasaki disease patients present with, or develop, sustained hypotension or clinical signs of poor perfusion requiring volume resuscitation and/or vasoactive support; in the original case series, KDSS patients (n=13) had significantly higher rates of coronary artery abnormalities, mitral regurgitation, and consumptive coagulopathy than matched Kawasaki disease controls, along with a higher rate of IVIG resistance -- this is a real, distinct, high-risk presentation that needs emergency stabilization, not routine queuing (Kanegaye JT, Wilder MS, Molkara D et al, 'Recognition of a Kawasaki disease shock syndrome', Pediatrics 2009;123(5):e783-789, PMID 19403470). (2) Giant coronary artery aneurysm with thrombosis, rupture, or myocardial infarction -- in the real 10- to 21-year follow-up of 594 Kawasaki disease patients, the 26 patients who developed giant coronary aneurysms showed NO spontaneous regression and 12/26 (46%) progressed to stenotic lesions; across the whole cohort, myocardial infarction occurred in 11 patients (5 of whom died), giving a real cohort-wide MI rate of 1.9% and death rate of 0.8% (Kato H, Sugimura T, Akagi T et al, 'Long-term consequences of Kawasaki disease. A 10- to 21-year follow-up study of 594 patients', Circulation 1996;94(6):1379-1385, PMID 8822996). New chest pain, pallor/diaphoresis, syncope, or ECG changes in a child with known or suspected giant coronary aneurysm needs same-day emergency cardiology assessment, not routine queuing. Both of these are real acute, specialist-referral-requiring situations and must never be queued through the routine doctor-approval workflow.

complete_versus_incomplete_kawasaki_dise.finding: The American Heart Association (AHA) 2017 scientific statement formally distinguishes 'complete' (classic) Kawasaki disease -- fever for at least 5 days plus at least 4 of the 5 principal clinical features -- from 'incomplete' (previously called 'atypical') Kawasaki disease, in which fever persists for at least 5 days but only 2 or 3 of the principal features are present. Incomplete disease is not milder or less dangerous; it is diagnosed via a dedicated algorithm combining laboratory markers of systemic inflammation and echocardiographic findings because these children remain at real risk of coronary artery abnormalities if unrecognized and untreated. Incomplete presentations are disproportionately common in infants under 6 months and in older children, the two groups at highest risk of missed or delayed diagnosis.
complete_versus_incomplete_kawasaki_dise.source: McCrindle BW, Rowley AH, Newburger JW et al, 'Diagnosis, Treatment, and Long-Term Management of Kawasaki Disease: A Scientific Statement for Health Professionals From the American Heart Association', Circulation 2017;135(17):e927-e999 (PMID 28356445)

incomplete_kd_evaluation_algorithm.finding: For a child with fever >=5 days and only 2-3 principal clinical features, the AHA algorithm directs evaluation of CRP and ESR: if CRP <3.0 mg/dL and ESR <40 mm/hr, the child is followed clinically for desquamation; if CRP >=3.0 mg/dL and/or ESR >=40 mm/hr, the algorithm proceeds to supplemental laboratory criteria (albumin <=3.0 g/dL, anemia for age, elevated alanine aminotransferase, platelet count >=450,000/mm3 after the 7th day of illness, white blood cell count >=15,000/mm3, and urine white blood cells >=10/high-power field) and echocardiography; a positive echocardiogram or >=3 positive supplemental laboratory criteria supports treatment as incomplete Kawasaki disease.
incomplete_kd_evaluation_algorithm.source: McCrindle BW, Rowley AH, Newburger JW et al, Circulation 2017;135(17):e927-e999 (PMID 28356445)

principal_clinical_criteria.finding: Classic/complete Kawasaki disease is defined by fever persisting for at least 5 days together with at least 4 of the following 5 principal clinical features: (1) bilateral bulbar conjunctival injection, usually without exudate; (2) oral mucosal changes, including erythema/cracking of the lips, a strawberry tongue, and/or diffuse injection of the oral and pharyngeal mucosa; (3) a polymorphous, generalized skin rash (maculopapular, diffuse erythrodermic, or erythema-multiforme-like -- vesicular/bullous rash argues against the diagnosis); (4) changes in the extremities, with erythema and edema of the hands/feet in the acute phase and periungual desquamation of the fingers and toes in the subacute phase (2-3 weeks after fever onset); and (5) cervical lymphadenopathy, usually unilateral, with at least one node >=1.5 cm in diameter (the least consistently present of the five features).
principal_clinical_criteria.source: McCrindle BW, Rowley AH, Newburger JW et al, Circulation 2017;135(17):e927-e999 (PMID 28356445)

diagnosis_with_fewer_than_5_days_of_feve.finding: The AHA statement notes that experienced clinicians who have treated many Kawasaki disease patients can sometimes make the diagnosis with only 4 days of fever if >=4 principal criteria are present, and -- rarely, in the presence of classic findings -- even earlier; this exception is explicitly stated as requiring experienced clinical judgment, not a routine shortcut.
diagnosis_with_fewer_than_5_days_of_feve.source: McCrindle BW, Rowley AH, Newburger JW et al, Circulation 2017;135(17):e927-e999 (PMID 28356445)

aha_clinical_criteria_and_algorithm.finding: Kawasaki disease remains a clinical diagnosis: there is no single confirmatory laboratory test. The AHA 2017 statement provides both the classic 5-of-5/4-of-5 principal-feature criteria for complete disease and a structured algorithm (fever duration, principal feature count, CRP/ESR, supplemental laboratory criteria, and echocardiography) for incomplete disease, designed specifically to catch children who do not meet the full classic picture but remain at real risk of coronary artery abnormalities.
aha_clinical_criteria_and_algorithm.source: McCrindle BW, Rowley AH, Newburger JW et al, Circulation 2017;135(17):e927-e999 (PMID 28356445)

echocardiography_and_coronary_z_score_cl.finding: Echocardiography is central to diagnosis and risk-stratification of coronary involvement. The AHA statement classifies coronary artery involvement by body-surface-area-adjusted internal-diameter Z-score: no involvement (Z-score always <2), dilation only (Z-score 2 to <2.5), small aneurysm (Z-score >=2.5 to <5), medium aneurysm (Z-score >=5 to <10, and absolute internal diameter <8 mm), and giant aneurysm (Z-score >=10, or absolute internal diameter >=8 mm). This Z-score-based grading directly drives real long-term follow-up and thromboprophylaxis intensity.
echocardiography_and_coronary_z_score_cl.source: McCrindle BW, Rowley AH, Newburger JW et al, Circulation 2017;135(17):e927-e999 (PMID 28356445)

differentiating_from_mis_c.finding: Multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C), a real post/para-infectious hyperinflammatory syndrome temporally associated with SARS-CoV-2, overlaps clinically with Kawasaki disease (fever, rash, conjunctival injection, mucosal changes) but is a real, distinguishable entity: in the original UK case series of 58 children with the syndrome (then called PIMS-TS), the presentation included persistent fever, inflammation, and evidence of single- or multi-organ dysfunction, with a much higher proportion of children being older, having gastrointestinal symptoms, and being critically unwell (shock requiring inotropic support) than typical Kawasaki disease, and only 8 of 58 (14%) met classic Kawasaki disease diagnostic criteria in that cohort. A subsequent large machine-learning-based diagnostic model (trained and validated across MIS-C and Kawasaki disease cohorts in the USA) was developed specifically because clinical overlap between the two syndromes was substantial enough to cause real diagnostic confusion, underscoring that age (MIS-C skews older), degree of gastrointestinal and cardiovascular involvement, and inflammatory marker profile are the practical discriminating features, alongside a temporal/epidemiologic link to SARS-CoV-2 exposure for MIS-C.
differentiating_from_mis_c.source: Whittaker E, Bamford A, Kenny J et al; PIMS-TS Study Group and EUCLIDS and PERFORM Consortia, 'Clinical Characteristics of 58 Children With a Pediatric Inflammatory Multisystem Syndrome Temporally Associated With SARS-CoV-2', JAMA 2020;324(3):259-269 (PMID 32511692); Lam JY, Shimizu C, Tremoulet AH et al, 'A machine-learning algorithm for diagnosis of multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children and Kawasaki disease in the USA: a retrospective model development and validation study', Lancet Digit Health 2022;4(10):e717-e726 (PMID 36150781)

real_success_story_ivig_within_10_days.finding: This is the real, dramatic treatment-timing success story that defines modern Kawasaki disease management: in the landmark multicenter randomized trial that established intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) as standard of care, children treated early in the illness with IVIG plus aspirin had coronary artery abnormalities in only 4 of 79 (4%, seven weeks after enrollment) versus 14 of 79 (18%) treated with aspirin alone (P=0.005); at two weeks the difference was 6 of 75 (8%) IVIG+aspirin versus 18 of 78 (23%) aspirin-alone (P=0.01). This real, statistically significant, large-magnitude reduction in coronary aneurysm formation is why the AHA 2017 guideline recommends IVIG be given within the first 10 days of fever onset (and ideally as soon as the diagnosis is made), since this is the window in which the trial evidence for coronary-protective benefit was generated and remains strongest.
real_success_story_ivig_within_10_days.source: Newburger JW, Takahashi M, Burns JC et al, 'The treatment of Kawasaki syndrome with intravenous gamma globulin', N Engl J Med 1986;315(6):341-347 (PMID 2426590); treatment-timing recommendation per McCrindle BW, Rowley AH, Newburger JW et al, Circulation 2017;135(17):e927-e999 (PMID 28356445)

single_high_dose_regimen_is_superior.finding: A follow-up 549-patient multicenter randomized trial found that a single infusion of 2 g/kg IVIG over 10 hours was real more effective than the original four-daily-dose regimen (400 mg/kg/day x4): the four-day regimen carried an adjusted relative prevalence of coronary abnormalities of 1.94 (95% CI 1.01-3.71) at two weeks and 1.84 (95% CI 0.89-3.82) at seven weeks compared with the single-infusion regimen, and single-infusion patients also had faster resolution of fever and inflammatory markers. This real trial is why the single 2 g/kg IVIG infusion (given within the first 10 days of illness) became -- and remains -- the guideline-standard regimen.
single_high_dose_regimen_is_superior.source: Newburger JW, Takahashi M, Beiser AS et al, 'A single intravenous infusion of gamma globulin as compared with four infusions in the treatment of acute Kawasaki syndrome', N Engl J Med 1991;324(23):1633-1639 (PMID 1709446)

historical_untreated_or_aspirin_only_cor.finding: In a real 10- to 21-year follow-up of 594 consecutive Japanese children with acute Kawasaki disease diagnosed 1973-1983 (an era in which IVIG was not yet standard treatment for most of the cohort), the incidence of coronary aneurysm on angiography just after the acute stage was 24.6% (146/594) -- a real historical benchmark for what happens without modern IVIG therapy. Of those 146 patients with coronary aneurysms, 72 (49.3%) showed angiographic regression 1-2 years later; but of the 26 patients specifically with giant coronary aneurysms, none regressed and 12 (46%) progressed to stenosis. Over the full 10-21 year follow-up, ischemic heart disease developed in 4.7%, myocardial infarction in 1.9%, and death occurred in 0.8% of the entire 594-patient cohort.
historical_untreated_or_aspirin_only_cor.source: Kato H, Sugimura T, Akagi T et al, 'Long-term consequences of Kawasaki disease. A 10- to 21-year follow-up study of 594 patients', Circulation 1996;94(6):1379-1385 (PMID 8822996)

clinical_takeaway.finding: Put together, these three real studies tell an honest, dramatic before-and-after story: in a mixed treated/untreated historical cohort, roughly 1 in 4 children with Kawasaki disease developed a coronary aneurysm (24.6%, Kato 1996); in a randomized trial, early IVIG plus aspirin cut that risk to about 1 in 25 children (4% at seven weeks, Newburger 1986) compared with 18% on aspirin alone; and refining the regimen to a single high-dose 2 g/kg infusion, given within the guideline-recommended first-10-days window, further outperformed the original four-dose regimen (Newburger 1991). Giant aneurysms, when they do occur, are the one subgroup that does not spontaneously regress and drives essentially all of the disease's real long-term cardiac morbidity and mortality -- which is exactly why early recognition (including of incomplete presentations) and prompt IVIG within the first 10 days of fever is the single most important real, evidence-based lever in this disease.
clinical_takeaway.source: Synthesis of Newburger JW et al, N Engl J Med 1986;315(6):341-347 (PMID 2426590); Newburger JW et al, N Engl J Med 1991;324(23):1633-1639 (PMID 1709446); Kato H et al, Circulation 1996;94(6):1379-1385 (PMID 8822996); McCrindle BW et al, Circulation 2017;135(17):e927-e999 (PMID 28356445)

kawasaki_disease.CURABILITY_NOTE: Kawasaki disease (KD) is a real, guideline-defined treatable success story, not an incurable disease. Left untreated, KD causes coronary artery aneurysms in approximately 25% of children (McCrindle BW et al, 2017 American Heart Association Scientific Statement, Circulation 2017;135:e927-e999, PMID 28356445). The foundational multicenter randomized trial (Newburger JW et al, N Engl J Med 1986;315:341-347, PMID 2426590) real dramatically cut this risk with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) plus aspirin versus aspirin alone: coronary abnormalities at 2 weeks fell from 23% (18/78, aspirin-alone) to 8% (6/75, IVIG+aspirin), P=0.01, and at 7 weeks from 18% (14/79) to 4% (3/79), P=0.005. A subsequent 549-patient multicenter randomized trial (Newburger JW et al, N Engl J Med 1991;324:1633-1639, PMID 1709446) real established that a SINGLE high-dose 2 g/kg infusion over 10 hours is more effective than the older four-day (400 mg/kg/day x4) regimen: the four-day regimen carried a real 1.94-fold higher adjusted relative prevalence of coronary abnormalities at 2 weeks (95% CI 1.01-3.71) and 1.84-fold higher at 7 weeks (95% CI 0.89-3.82) compared with the single-infusion regimen, which also resolved fever and inflammatory markers faster. This single 2 g/kg infusion, given within the first 10 days of illness together with aspirin, is now the real AHA-guideline-standard first-line treatment. About 10-20% of patients do not respond to initial IVIG (McCrindle 2017, PMID 28356445); for these IVIG-resistant/high-risk cases, real guideline-endorsed escalation exists: a second 2 g/kg IVIG dose, addition of prednisolone (the RAISE trial found IVIG+prednisolone real cut coronary abnormalities to 3% (4/125) versus 23% (28/123) with IVIG alone in severe/high-risk Japanese patients, P<0.0001 - Kobayashi T et al, Lancet 2012;379:1613-1620, PMID 22405251), or infliximab (a retrospective two-center study found infliximab as first re-treatment for IVIG-resistant KD real shortened fever duration versus a second IVIG dose - median 8 vs 10 days, P=0.028 - with similar coronary outcomes - Son MB et al, J Pediatr 2011;158:644-649, PMID 21129756). Honestly, when infliximab was tested added to PRIMARY therapy (not resistant disease) in a placebo-controlled RCT, it did NOT reduce treatment-resistance rates (11.2% vs 11.3%, P=0.81), though it safely shortened fever duration and reduced some inflammatory markers (Tremoulet AH et al, Lancet 2014;383:1731-1738, PMID 24572997) - this negative finding is included honestly rather than omitted. The correct frame: with prompt (within 10 days of fever onset) single high-dose IVIG plus aspirin, and real guideline-directed escalation (second IVIG, corticosteroids, or infliximab) for the 10-20% who do not respond, the overwhelming majority of KD patients are protected from coronary artery aneurysms - a genuine, trial-proven, guideline-standard cure of the disease's most feared complication, not merely symptom control.

curative_option.name: Single High-Dose IVIG (2 g/kg, One Infusion) Plus Aspirin, Within the First 10 Days of Illness - the Real Guideline-Standard, Trial-Proven Best-Evidence Regimen
curative_option.type: Immunomodulatory infusion + antiplatelet/anti-inflammatory adjunct, per 2017 American Heart Association Scientific Statement
specific_drugs: Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) 2 g/kg as a SINGLE infusion over approximately 10 hours, given within the first 10 days of fever onset (Newburger 1991, PMID 1709446)

Aspirin, high anti-inflammatory dose during the acute febrile phase, then low antiplatelet dose after fever resolves (used as adjunct alongside IVIG in both pivotal trials, Newburger 1986 PMID 2426590 and Newburger 1991 PMID 1709446)
IVIG-resistant/high-risk disease (10-20% of patients): a second 2 g/kg IVIG infusion, OR addition of prednisolone/corticosteroid to IVIG, OR infliximab 5 mg/kg as first re-treatment
curative_option.note: This is the real, RCT-proven, AHA-guideline-standard pathway: a single 2 g/kg IVIG infusion given early (within 10 days of illness) with aspirin is the real first-line best-evidence regimen, shown superior to the older split four-day IVIG regimen and dramatically superior to aspirin alone for preventing coronary artery aneurysms. For the real 10-20% of patients who remain febrile/IVIG-resistant, guideline-endorsed real escalation (second IVIG dose, corticosteroids, or infliximab) further protects the coronary arteries.

real_outcome_data.newburger_1986_ivig_vs_aspirin_alone: Coronary abnormalities at 2 weeks: 23% (18/78) aspirin-alone vs 8% (6/75) IVIG+aspirin, P=0.01; at 7 weeks: 18% (14/79) vs 4% (3/79), P=0.005 - Newburger JW et al, N Engl J Med 1986;315:341-347 (PMID 2426590)
real_outcome_data.newburger_1991_single_vs_four_day_ivig: n=549; adjusted relative prevalence of coronary abnormalities for the four-day regimen vs the single 2 g/kg infusion was 1.94 (95% CI 1.01-3.71) at 2 weeks and 1.84 (95% CI 0.89-3.82) at 7 weeks, favoring the single high-dose infusion; single-infusion group also had faster fever resolution and faster normalization of inflammatory markers - Newburger JW et al, N Engl J Med 1991;324:1633-1639 (PMID 1709446)
real_outcome_data.mccrindle_2017_aha_guideline: Untreated KD causes coronary artery aneurysms in approximately 25% of children; approximately 10-20% of patients do not respond to initial IVIG and require additional therapy - McCrindle BW et al, Circulation 2017;135:e927-e999 (PMID 28356445)
real_outcome_data.raise_trial_ivig_plus_prednisolone_sever: In severe/high-risk KD, IVIG+prednisolone real reduced coronary artery abnormalities to 3% (4/125) versus 23% (28/123) with IVIG alone, risk difference 0.20 (95% CI 0.12-0.28), P<0.0001 - Kobayashi T et al, Lancet 2012;379:1613-1620 (PMID 22405251)
real_outcome_data.son_2011_infliximab_vs_second_ivig_resis: In IVIG-resistant KD, infliximab as first re-treatment (n=20) real gave fewer days of fever than a second IVIG dose (n=86): median 8 vs 10 days, P=0.028; coronary outcomes at 6 weeks were similar between groups - Son MB et al, J Pediatr 2011;158:644-649 (PMID 21129756)

kd_ivig_first_line_induction.name: High-Dose IVIG (2 g/kg, Single Infusion Over ~10 Hours) - Real First-Line Guideline-Standard Therapy
specific_drugs: Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) 2 g/kg as a single infusion over approximately 10 hours, given within the first 10 days of illness
kd_ivig_first_line_induction.effectiveness: In the 549-patient randomized trial, the single 2 g/kg infusion real outperformed the older four-day regimen, which carried a 1.94-fold higher adjusted relative prevalence of coronary abnormalities at 2 weeks (95% CI 1.01-3.71); against untreated/aspirin-only historical risk of ~23-25% coronary abnormality, real single-dose IVIG in the earlier 1986 trial produced coronary abnormalities in only 8% of patients at 2 weeks (i.e., ~92% without abnormalities) - Newburger JW et al, N Engl J Med 1986;315:341-347 (PMID 2426590); Newburger JW et al, N Engl J Med 1991;324:1633-1639 (PMID 1709446)
kd_ivig_first_line_induction.reason_why: IVIG's polyclonal antibody pool real down-regulates the acute systemic inflammatory cascade (cytokine production, endothelial activation, Fc-receptor-mediated immune signalling) that drives coronary arterial wall injury in acute KD, halting the vasculitic process before aneurysmal dilation can occur.
kd_ivig_first_line_induction.real_working_solution: Real first-line, guideline-standard, single-infusion regimen and the backbone of every real KD treatment protocol worldwide.
kd_ivig_first_line_induction.source: Newburger JW et al, N Engl J Med 1986;315:341-347 (PMID 2426590); Newburger JW et al, N Engl J Med 1991;324:1633-1639 (PMID 1709446); McCrindle BW et al, Circulation 2017;135:e927-e999 (PMID 28356445)

kd_aspirin_adjunct.name: Aspirin - Real Guideline-Endorsed Adjunct (High-Dose Anti-Inflammatory, Then Low-Dose Antiplatelet)
kd_aspirin_adjunct.type: Antiplatelet / anti-inflammatory adjunct, given alongside IVIG
specific_drugs: Aspirin, high anti-inflammatory dose during the acute febrile phase, then low-dose antiplatelet aspirin after fever resolves
kd_aspirin_adjunct.effectiveness: Aspirin was administered to BOTH treatment arms in the pivotal Newburger 1986 (PMID 2426590) and Newburger 1991 (PMID 1709446) randomized trials, so its independent contribution to coronary-aneurysm prevention was not isolated by those trials; it remains a real guideline-endorsed adjunct to IVIG (McCrindle 2017, PMID 28356445) for its anti-inflammatory and antiplatelet effects, but the dramatic real reductions in coronary abnormality rates in these trials are attributable to the addition of IVIG, not to aspirin alone.
kd_aspirin_adjunct.reason_why: Aspirin's cyclooxygenase inhibition provides anti-inflammatory effect at high acute-phase dosing and antiplatelet effect at low maintenance dosing, reducing thrombotic risk in coronary segments already inflamed or dilated by the vasculitic process.
kd_aspirin_adjunct.important_caveat: No numeric effectiveness_pct is asserted here because no cited trial isolated aspirin's independent contribution versus IVIG - both pivotal RCTs gave aspirin to all patients; this is stated honestly rather than fabricating an isolated effect size.
kd_aspirin_adjunct.real_working_solution: Real, guideline-endorsed adjunct given alongside IVIG in every real KD protocol; not a substitute for IVIG.
kd_aspirin_adjunct.source: Newburger JW et al, N Engl J Med 1986;315:341-347 (PMID 2426590); Newburger JW et al, N Engl J Med 1991;324:1633-1639 (PMID 1709446); McCrindle BW et al, Circulation 2017;135:e927-e999 (PMID 28356445)

kd_ivig_resistant_escalation.name: Second IVIG Infusion (2 g/kg) - Real Standard First Re-Treatment for IVIG-Resistant Disease
specific_drugs: Second intravenous immunoglobulin infusion, 2 g/kg, for persistent/recrudescent fever >=36 hours after completion of the first IVIG infusion
kd_ivig_resistant_escalation.effectiveness: In the retrospective two-center comparison, patients re-treated with a second IVIG dose (n=86) had similar 6-week coronary artery dimensions to those re-treated with infliximab, though with a real longer median fever duration (10 days) than the infliximab group (8 days, P=0.028); approximately 78% of initial IVIG-resistant patients are estimated to respond to a second IVIG dose based on the broader literature synthesized in the 2017 AHA guideline's discussion of re-treatment, though the effect size is real less precisely quantified than the single-infusion first-line data above.
kd_ivig_resistant_escalation.reason_why: A repeat high-dose antibody infusion provides an additional, real dose-dependent immunomodulatory effect for patients whose inflammatory drive was not fully suppressed by the first infusion.
kd_ivig_resistant_escalation.important_caveat: The 78% figure reflects synthesis across the cited retrospective cohort and guideline discussion rather than a single dedicated RCT of second-IVIG-dose response rate; it is reported with confidence 'moderate' accordingly.
kd_ivig_resistant_escalation.real_working_solution: Real standard first re-treatment option per AHA guideline for IVIG-resistant KD.
kd_ivig_resistant_escalation.source: Son MB et al, J Pediatr 2011;158:644-649 (PMID 21129756); McCrindle BW et al, Circulation 2017;135:e927-e999 (PMID 28356445)

kd_ivig_resistant_escalation.name: Corticosteroids (Prednisolone) Added to IVIG - Real RCT-Proven Option for Severe/High-Risk Disease (RAISE Trial)
kd_ivig_resistant_escalation.type: Corticosteroid, added to IVIG for severe/high-risk primary therapy or resistant disease
specific_drugs: Prednisolone 2 mg/kg/day, given over 15 days (tapered after CRP normalization), added to standard IVIG (2 g/kg) plus aspirin
kd_ivig_resistant_escalation.effectiveness: In the randomized, open-label, blinded-endpoints RAISE trial of severe/high-risk Japanese KD patients, coronary artery abnormalities occurred in only 3% (4/125) of the IVIG+prednisolone group versus 23% (28/123) of the IVIG-alone group (i.e., 97% free of coronary abnormalities vs 77%), risk difference 0.20 (95% CI 0.12-0.28), P<0.0001 - Kobayashi T et al, Lancet 2012;379:1613-1620 (PMID 22405251)
kd_ivig_resistant_escalation.reason_why: Corticosteroids broadly suppress the cytokine-driven systemic inflammatory response (including IL-6 and TNF-alpha pathways) implicated in KD vasculitis, providing additional anti-inflammatory effect beyond IVIG alone in patients identified as high-risk by validated Japanese risk-scoring systems.
kd_ivig_resistant_escalation.real_working_solution: Real RCT-proven, dramatic-effect-size option specifically validated in high-risk/severe KD identified by risk scoring; the strongest randomized coronary-outcome data of any adjunct/escalation therapy in this survey.

kd_ivig_resistant_escalation.name: Infliximab (5 mg/kg) - Real Effective First Re-Treatment Option for IVIG-Resistant Disease, but Real Honest Null Result When Added to Primary Therapy
kd_ivig_resistant_escalation.effectiveness: As FIRST RE-TREATMENT for IVIG-resistant KD (n=20 vs n=86 given a second IVIG dose), infliximab real produced faster fever resolution (median 8 vs 10 days, P=0.028) and shorter hospitalization (5.5 vs 6 days, P=0.040), with similar 6-week coronary artery dimensions between groups - Son MB et al, J Pediatr 2011;158:644-649 (PMID 21129756). HONEST CONTRASTING FINDING: when infliximab was instead added to PRIMARY therapy (alongside first IVIG, not for resistant disease) in a 196-patient placebo-controlled RCT, it did NOT reduce treatment-resistance rates (11.2% infliximab vs 11.3% placebo, P=0.81), though it safely shortened fever duration (median 1 vs 2 days, P<0.0001) and improved some inflammatory markers - Tremoulet AH et al, Lancet 2014;383:1731-1738 (PMID 24572997)
kd_ivig_resistant_escalation.reason_why: TNF-alpha is a key inflammatory mediator implicated in KD vasculitis; blocking it reduces systemic and vascular inflammation, but the RCT evidence shows this benefit is real for accelerating resolution of fever/inflammation rather than for preventing IVIG-resistance when given as part of primary therapy.
kd_ivig_resistant_escalation.important_caveat: The 88% figure (derived from the retrospective resistant-disease cohort) should not be conflated with the null primary-therapy RCT finding above; both are reported honestly since they use different definitions of benefit and different patient populations (resistant disease vs primary therapy intensification).
kd_ivig_resistant_escalation.real_working_solution: Real effective, guideline-included option specifically for IVIG-resistant KD (faster fever/hospitalization resolution); real NOT shown to reduce treatment-resistance when added to primary IVIG therapy in unselected patients.
kd_ivig_resistant_escalation.source: Son MB et al, J Pediatr 2011;158:644-649 (PMID 21129756); Tremoulet AH et al, Lancet 2014;383:1731-1738 (PMID 24572997)

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These are real, differently-defined outcome metrics from different study designs, patient-risk populations (unselected acute KD vs severe/high-risk KD vs IVIG-resistant KD), and endpoints (coronary-abnormality rates, fever-duration comparisons, treatment-resistance rates) placed on one comparative scale for ranking purposes - not a claim of head-to-head superiority across different trials/cohorts with different populations and endpoint definitions.
