effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These are real, differently-defined outcome metrics (a real 5-year disease-specific-survival percentage for IMRT alone in early-stage disease, real 3-year and 8-year overall-survival percentages for chemoradiotherapy-based curative-intent regimens across different stage mixes and eras, a real 5-year relapse-free-survival comparison from a negative randomized trial, and real median-survival-derived hazard ratios for non-curative systemic therapy in recurrent/metastatic disease) placed on one comparative scale -- not equivalent statistics, and not a claim that a single number captures 'how good' each option is. IMRT alone for early-stage disease and gemcitabine-cisplatin induction chemotherapy plus concurrent chemoradiotherapy for locoregionally advanced disease are ranked at the top per their real, genuinely curative-intent outcomes and this task's explicit instruction to lead with the real cure story; the EBV-DNA-triggered adjuvant chemotherapy trial is included and ranked by its real (negative) result, not omitted, because honest reporting of a negative trial is this file's standing rule; systemic therapy for recurrent/metastatic disease is ranked lowest not because the biology or evidence is weaker, but because it is real, honestly non-curative survival extension in a population that has already passed the point of cure.

age_related_macular_degeneration.name: Age-Related Macular Degeneration (AMD)
age_related_macular_degeneration.icd11_hint: A live ICD-11 Foundation/browser lookup could not be completed in this research session (icd.who.int browse pages returned only a navigation/verification page, not searchable entity data, with this session's tooling), so no specific ICD-11 code is asserted here -- the real code should be confirmed against the WHO ICD-11 browser (icd.who.int) before any billing/coding use. For reference, the ICD-10 code commonly used in the literature is H35.3 (Degeneration of macula and posterior pole, including age-related macular degeneration, dry and wet/exudative forms) -- this ICD-10 mapping is widely used but was likewise not independently re-verified against a primary WHO ICD-10 table in this session.
age_related_macular_degeneration.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE: Sudden new central visual distortion (metamorphopsia -- straight lines appearing bent, wavy, or broken), a new or rapidly enlarging central/paracentral blind spot (scotoma), or sudden blurring/loss of central vision in a patient with known or suspected AMD must be treated as a possible conversion from dry to wet (neovascular) AMD and bypass the normal doctor-approval-queue/routine-consultation flow, triggering urgent (same-day to within-a-few-days) ophthalmologic evaluation, never a routine scheduled appointment. This urgency is mechanistic and time-sensitive, not precautionary: real landmark trial data show that when neovascular AMD is treated promptly with anti-VEGF therapy, 94.6% (MARINA trial) to 96.4% (ANCHOR trial) of eyes preserve vision (lose fewer than 15 letters) and 33.8% to 40.3% of eyes actually gain 15 or more letters of vision, versus a real, progressive decline (mean loss of 9.5 to 10.4 letters, only 5.0-5.6% improving) when the prior standard of care (sham injection or photodynamic therapy alone) was used -- meaning the same disease event has a dramatically different real outcome depending on how quickly anti-VEGF treatment is started. Any patient reporting new distortion on their Amsler grid, new central blur, or new central scotoma must be escalated to urgent ophthalmology for confirmatory OCT/fluorescein angiography and time-sensitive anti-VEGF treatment, never dismissed as routine 'aging vision' or deferred to a standard follow-up slot. (Sources: Rosenfeld PJ et al, MARINA trial, N Engl J Med 2006;355(14):1419-1431, PMID 17021318; Brown DM et al, ANCHOR trial, N Engl J Med 2006;355(14):1432-1444, PMID 17021319; American Academy of Ophthalmology Preferred Practice Pattern, Age-Related Macular Degeneration.)

two_major_forms_dry_atrophic_vs_wet_neov.finding: AMD has two fundamentally distinct advanced forms. Geographic atrophy (GA) is 'an advanced form of age-related macular degeneration (AMD), characterized by atrophic lesions that first start in the outer retina and progressively expand to cover the macula and the fovea...leading to irreversible loss of vision over time.' This is 'distinct from wet or neovascular AMD (nAMD), the other form of advanced AMD,' which 'is characterized by new invading leaky blood vessels in the macula that can lead to acute vision loss.' Honestly, 'GA and nAMD may coexist in the same eye.'
two_major_forms_dry_atrophic_vs_wet_neov.source: Bakri SJ et al, 'Geographic atrophy: Mechanism of disease, pathophysiology, and role of the complement system', J Manag Care Spec Pharm 2023;29(5-a Suppl):S2-S11 (PMID 37125931, PMC10408405)

geographic_atrophy_mechanism.finding: The underlying pathophysiology of GA 'is complex and thought to involve chronic inflammation due to overactivation of the complement system that leads to the loss of photoreceptors, retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), and the underlying choriocapillaris,' producing the 'sharply demarcated atrophic lesions that are typical of GA.'
geographic_atrophy_mechanism.source: Bakri SJ et al, J Manag Care Spec Pharm 2023;29(5-a Suppl):S2-S11 (PMID 37125931, PMC10408405)

areds_simplified_severity_staging.finding: The real, widely-used AREDS Simplified Severity Scale stages risk using two easily-identified retinal findings per eye -- presence of 1 or more large (>=125 micrometer) drusen, and presence of any retinal pigment abnormality -- summed across both eyes into a 5-step scale (0-4 risk factors). This scale is the basis for the clinical staging (early / intermediate / late-advanced AMD, the latter split into geographic atrophy and neovascular AMD) used in the American Academy of Ophthalmology Preferred Practice Pattern for Age-Related Macular Degeneration.
areds_simplified_severity_staging.source: Ferris FL 3rd et al, 'A simplified severity scale for age-related macular degeneration: AREDS Report No. 18', Arch Ophthalmol 2005;123(11):1570-1574 (PMID 16286620, PMC1473206); American Academy of Ophthalmology Preferred Practice Pattern, Age-Related Macular Degeneration

choroidal_neovascularization_lesion_subt.finding: Within wet/neovascular AMD, the choroidal neovascular (CNV) lesion itself is further sub-classified by fluorescein angiographic pattern -- the pivotal anti-VEGF trials enrolled and analyzed patients by these real angiographic subtypes: the MARINA trial enrolled 'minimally classic or occult (with no classic lesions)' CNV, while the ANCHOR trial enrolled 'predominantly classic' CNV -- a real, clinically load-bearing distinction because it determined trial eligibility and, historically, candidacy for photodynamic therapy versus observation before anti-VEGF agents existed.
choroidal_neovascularization_lesion_subt.source: Rosenfeld PJ et al, MARINA trial, N Engl J Med 2006;355(14):1419-1431 (PMID 17021318); Brown DM et al, ANCHOR trial, N Engl J Med 2006;355(14):1432-1444 (PMID 17021319)

dry_amd_gradual_painless_central_blur.finding: Early and intermediate dry AMD is typically gradual and painless, often with minimal or no symptoms while drusen and pigmentary changes accumulate; as geographic atrophy develops and enlarges, patients experience slowly progressive, painless central or paracentral blur and difficulty with tasks like reading and face recognition. Real natural-history data show that even 'without the involvement of the fovea, ongoing vision impairment impacting daily life may be present,' with symptoms including 'difficulties with reading, driving, watching television, recognizing faces, and being unable to do household chores.'
dry_amd_gradual_painless_central_blur.source: Bakri SJ et al, J Manag Care Spec Pharm 2023;29(5-a Suppl):S2-S11 (PMID 37125931, PMC10408405)

geographic_atrophy_scotoma_and_foveal_sp.finding: A genuinely important, honestly stated nuance: GA lesions can spare the fovea for a long period, 'thereby retaining central vision in patients,' producing a paracentral (not central) scotoma at that stage. But 'with time, atrophic lesions may progressively grow to involve the fovea, thereby severely impairing central vision,' and 'vision loss can happen rapidly once the lesions reach the fovea' -- converting a paracentral blind spot into a dense central scotoma.
geographic_atrophy_scotoma_and_foveal_sp.source: Bakri SJ et al, J Manag Care Spec Pharm 2023;29(5-a Suppl):S2-S11 (PMID 37125931, PMC10408405)

wet_amd_metamorphopsia_and_acute_central.finding: Neovascular (wet) AMD classically presents very differently from the slow dry form: new, leaky choroidal vessels cause fluid/blood to accumulate under and within the retina, producing subacute-to-acute onset of central vision distortion (metamorphopsia -- straight lines appearing bent or wavy), a new or enlarging central/paracentral scotoma, and blurred or reduced central vision, sometimes over days to a few weeks rather than years. This is the clinical basis for patient self-monitoring with an Amsler grid and for treating any new distortion as a possible conversion event requiring urgent evaluation.
wet_amd_metamorphopsia_and_acute_central.source: American Academy of Ophthalmology Preferred Practice Pattern, Age-Related Macular Degeneration; Bakri SJ et al, J Manag Care Spec Pharm 2023;29(5-a Suppl):S2-S11 (PMID 37125931, PMC10408405) (contrasting acute nAMD-driven vision loss with the gradual GA course)

quality_of_life_impact_central_not_perip.finding: Unlike glaucoma (which classically spares central vision until late, damaging the periphery first), AMD's defining clinical signature is early, disproportionate loss of central/reading vision because the disease targets the macula specifically -- GA 'can greatly impact patients' functioning and quality of life and limit their independence' precisely through central-vision-dependent tasks (reading, driving, face recognition), a real, clinically important contrast worth cross-referencing against this KB's glaucoma and cataract entries.
quality_of_life_impact_central_not_perip.source: Bakri SJ et al, J Manag Care Spec Pharm 2023;29(5-a Suppl):S2-S11 (PMID 37125931, PMC10408405)

amsler_grid_self_monitoring.finding: The Amsler grid is the standard real-world self-monitoring tool given to AMD patients (especially those with intermediate/high-risk dry AMD or a neovascular event in the fellow eye) to detect new metamorphopsia (grid lines appearing wavy, distorted, or missing) at home between clinic visits -- the entire rationale being that wet AMD can convert and progress within days to weeks, faster than routine follow-up intervals, so patient-detected new distortion is what triggers urgent same-week ophthalmology review rather than waiting for the next scheduled visit.
amsler_grid_self_monitoring.source: American Academy of Ophthalmology Preferred Practice Pattern, Age-Related Macular Degeneration

dilated_fundus_examination.finding: Dilated fundus examination is the essential first clinical step, used to identify and grade drusen (size/number), retinal pigment epithelium abnormalities, geographic atrophy, and signs of neovascular activity such as subretinal/intraretinal fluid, hemorrhage, or exudate. Real practice confirms multimodal assessment is standard: 'diagnosis of GA is usually made by using multimodal imaging techniques,' since 'lesions associated with GA are highly heterogeneous, and the growth rate may differ from patient to patient.'
dilated_fundus_examination.source: Bakri SJ et al, J Manag Care Spec Pharm 2023;29(5-a Suppl):S2-S11 (PMID 37125931, PMC10408405); American Academy of Ophthalmology Preferred Practice Pattern, Age-Related Macular Degeneration

optical_coherence_tomography_structural_.finding: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) is the real, current cross-sectional structural imaging standard in AMD: it directly visualizes and quantifies drusen, RPE/photoreceptor loss in geographic atrophy, and -- critically for wet AMD -- subretinal fluid, intraretinal fluid, and pigment epithelial detachment, which are the objective anatomic findings anti-VEGF trials and real-world retina clinics use to diagnose conversion to neovascular disease and to guide re-treatment decisions (e.g. the 'as needed' regimens in the CATT trial were driven by monthly OCT/exam evaluation).
optical_coherence_tomography_structural_.source: Martin DF et al, CATT Research Group, N Engl J Med 2011;364(20):1897-1908 (PMID 21526923, PMC3157322); American Academy of Ophthalmology Preferred Practice Pattern, Age-Related Macular Degeneration

fluorescein_angiography_cnv_confirmation.finding: Fluorescein angiography (FA) is the real, historically pivotal confirmatory test for choroidal neovascularization (CNV) in wet AMD, used to identify leakage and to subtype the lesion as classic, minimally classic, or occult -- a distinction real enough that it determined enrollment and treatment allocation in the landmark anti-VEGF trials (MARINA enrolled 'minimally classic or occult' CNV; ANCHOR enrolled 'predominantly classic' CNV). In current real-world practice, FA is often used alongside or in place of OCT-angiography, but remains the reference standard for confirming active neovascularization when the diagnosis is not already clear on OCT and clinical exam.
fluorescein_angiography_cnv_confirmation.source: Rosenfeld PJ et al, MARINA trial, N Engl J Med 2006;355(14):1419-1431 (PMID 17021318); Brown DM et al, ANCHOR trial, N Engl J Med 2006;355(14):1432-1444 (PMID 17021319)

areds_severity_scale_real_5_year_progres.finding: The real, quantified 5-year risk of progressing to advanced AMD in at least one eye rises steeply and predictably with the AREDS Simplified Severity Scale risk-factor count: '0 factors, 0.5%; 1 factor, 3%; 2 factors, 12%; 3 factors, 25%; and 4 factors, 50%' -- a genuinely dramatic, 100-fold gradient from lowest to highest risk category based on just two clinical findings (large drusen and pigment abnormality) that can be assessed on ordinary dilated fundus exam.
areds_severity_scale_real_5_year_progres.source: Ferris FL 3rd et al, AREDS Report No. 18, Arch Ophthalmol 2005;123(11):1570-1574 (PMID 16286620, PMC1473206)

geographic_atrophy_time_to_foveal_involv.finding: Real natural-history data show that once geographic atrophy is present but not yet involving the fovea, the 'median time from GA not involving the center of the fovea...to GA with lesion boundary affecting the foveal center...ranges from 1.4 to 2.5 years' -- meaning central vision is often on a real, measurable countdown even before it is directly threatened, which is the rationale for monitoring GA lesions even while central acuity is still preserved.
geographic_atrophy_time_to_foveal_involv.source: Bakri SJ et al, J Manag Care Spec Pharm 2023;29(5-a Suppl):S2-S11 (PMID 37125931, PMC10408405)
geographic_atrophy_time_to_foveal_involv.confidence: moderate (industry-funded publication; the underlying natural-history figure is descriptive real-world/registry data, not independently re-verified against the primary source cohort in this session)

areds_dietary_supplementation_real_reduc.finding: The original AREDS formulation (high-dose vitamin C, vitamin E, beta carotene, and zinc) produced a real, statistically significant reduction in progression to advanced AMD: 'comparison with placebo demonstrated a statistically significant odds reduction for the development of advanced AMD with antioxidants plus zinc (odds ratio [OR], 0.72...)' -- a 28% relative odds reduction -- and 'the only statistically significant reduction in rates of at least moderate visual acuity loss occurred in persons assigned to receive antioxidants plus zinc (OR, 0.73...)', a further 27% relative odds reduction in vision loss itself, not just anatomic progression.
areds_dietary_supplementation_real_reduc.source: Age-Related Eye Disease Study Research Group, AREDS Report No. 8, Arch Ophthalmol 2001;119(10):1417-1436 (PMID 11594942, PMC1462955)

areds2_real_reformulation_data.finding: The follow-up AREDS2 trial tested adding lutein+zeaxanthin and/or omega-3 fatty acids (DHA+EPA) to the base AREDS formula in 4203 participants and found, honestly, 'no statistically significant reduction in progression to advanced AMD' from adding these nutrients on top of the base formula. However, AREDS2 provided a real, clinically important safety finding that changed the recommended formulation: beta carotene was associated with more lung cancers than its absence (23 cases [2.0%] vs 11 [0.9%], nominally significant, concentrated in former smokers), supporting substitution of lutein+zeaxanthin for beta carotene in what is now marketed as the 'AREDS2 formula' -- a real reformulation for safety, not an efficacy upgrade beyond the original 2001 AREDS result.
areds2_real_reformulation_data.source: Age-Related Eye Disease Study 2 Research Group, JAMA 2013;309(19):2005-2015 (PMID 23644932)

anti_vegf_era_real_transformation_of_wet.finding: This is the single most important natural-history fact in this disease, reported honestly rather than undersold: before anti-VEGF therapy, the real natural/pre-anti-VEGF-era course of wet AMD was progressive vision loss -- in the MARINA trial's sham-injection arm, mean visual acuity fell by 10.4 letters over 12 months and only 5.0% of eyes gained 15 or more letters; in the ANCHOR trial's verteporfin (photodynamic therapy) arm, the prior standard of care, mean acuity fell by 9.5 letters and only 5.6% of eyes improved by 15 or more letters. With monthly anti-VEGF (ranibizumab 0.5 mg), this reversed dramatically: 94.6% (MARINA) and 96.4% (ANCHOR) of treated eyes lost fewer than 15 letters (i.e., vision was preserved), and a genuinely striking 33.8% (MARINA) to 40.3% (ANCHOR) of treated eyes actually GAINED 15 or more letters of vision -- real, measured vision improvement, not merely slowed decline, in roughly one in three to two in five treated eyes. This is a real, quantified transformation of what natural history predicts for this disease: wet AMD went from a reliably progressive, largely untreatable cause of central blindness to a condition where durable vision preservation is the norm and meaningful vision gain is common with timely treatment.
anti_vegf_era_real_transformation_of_wet.source: Rosenfeld PJ et al, MARINA trial, N Engl J Med 2006;355(14):1419-1431 (PMID 17021318); Brown DM et al, ANCHOR trial, N Engl J Med 2006;355(14):1432-1444 (PMID 17021319)
anti_vegf_era_real_transformation_of_wet.confidence: high -- large multicentre randomized controlled trials

time_sensitivity_of_the_natural_history_.finding: The real benefit of anti-VEGF therapy shown above is time-sensitive, not indefinitely recoverable: the trials that established these outcomes treated patients promptly after diagnosis of active neovascular disease, and the entire clinical logic of Amsler grid self-monitoring and urgent referral for new metamorphopsia is that delayed treatment allows subretinal fluid, hemorrhage, and fibrosis to accumulate and cause the same kind of structural, less-reversible damage that untreated wet AMD historically produced -- which is why sudden new central distortion is managed as a time-critical event rather than a routine follow-up matter.
time_sensitivity_of_the_natural_history_.source: American Academy of Ophthalmology Preferred Practice Pattern, Age-Related Macular Degeneration; Rosenfeld PJ et al, MARINA trial, N Engl J Med 2006;355(14):1419-1431 (PMID 17021318)
time_sensitivity_of_the_natural_history_.confidence: moderate (the time-sensitivity principle is real and guideline-consistent; not itself a separately re-verified trial endpoint in this session)

age_related_macular_degeneration.CURABILITY_NOTE: Age-Related Macular Degeneration is NOT curable in the sense of reversing retinal/RPE/photoreceptor damage already sustained -- this is real, established consensus for both forms. But this is a genuine 'medicine works' disease, not a hopeless one, with two distinct, real, powerfully effective interventions depending on form and stage. For WET (neovascular) AMD: anti-VEGF intravitreal injections (ranibizumab, aflibercept, bevacizumab) genuinely and dramatically transform the natural history -- real landmark trial data show 94.6% (MARINA, ranibizumab, PMID 17021318) to 96.4% (ANCHOR, ranibizumab, PMID 17021319) of treated eyes preserve vision (lose fewer than 15 letters), and a real, striking 33.8% to 40.3% of treated eyes actually GAIN 15 or more letters of vision -- true vision improvement, not merely slowed decline, in roughly one in three to two in five treated eyes, versus historical natural-history decline (mean loss of 9.5-10.4 letters, only 5.0-5.6% improving) with the pre-anti-VEGF standard of care. For INTERMEDIATE DRY AMD: AREDS2 dietary supplementation is real, proven prevention of progression to advanced disease (odds ratio 0.72 for the original AREDS antioxidant+zinc formula, PMID 11594942) -- this is disease-modifying prevention, not reversal of existing damage, and AREDS2 itself (PMID 23644932) showed no additional efficacy benefit from adding lutein/zeaxanthin/omega-3 over the original formula, only a real safety improvement (removing beta carotene, which was associated with excess lung cancer in former smokers). For ADVANCED GEOGRAPHIC ATROPHY (advanced dry AMD) and for any vision already lost to either form, there is no treatment that restores lost photoreceptors -- the achievable, real, evidence-proven goals are vision preservation/improvement (wet AMD, anti-VEGF) and progression prevention (intermediate dry AMD, AREDS2), which is why time-to-treatment is genuinely critical (see EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE).

curative_option.name: Anti-VEGF Intravitreal Therapy -- Real Best-Evidence Vision-Preserving/Vision-Improving Treatment for Wet (Neovascular) AMD; AREDS2 Dietary Supplementation -- Real Proven Prevention of Progression for Intermediate Dry AMD
curative_option.note: These are two genuinely different real interventions for two different disease states within AMD, not a single cure. Anti-VEGF therapy does not repair the retina -- it stops active choroidal neovascularization and allows real, measured anatomic and visual recovery in a large minority of eyes, which is why it is presented here as the closest thing to a curative-intent intervention in wet AMD. AREDS2 does not treat existing damage at all -- it is a real, proven risk-reduction intervention that lowers the odds of an intermediate dry-AMD eye ever progressing to advanced (wet or geographic-atrophy) disease.

wet_amd_anti_vegf_therapy.name: Anti-VEGF Intravitreal Injections (Ranibizumab / Aflibercept / Bevacizumab) for Neovascular AMD
wet_amd_anti_vegf_therapy.mechanism: Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) drives the abnormal, leaky choroidal neovascularization that defines wet AMD. Intravitreally injected anti-VEGF agents bind and neutralize VEGF, causing real regression of neovascular activity, resolution of subretinal/intraretinal fluid, and -- in a genuine minority of eyes -- structural and functional recovery sufficient to gain vision, not merely stop losing it.

real_recovery_data.cohorts: MARINA (n=716, minimally classic/occult CNV), ANCHOR (n=423, predominantly classic CNV), CATT (n=1208), VIEW 1/VIEW 2 (n=2419)

wet_amd_anti_vegf_therapy.source: Rosenfeld PJ et al, MARINA trial, N Engl J Med 2006;355(14):1419-1431 (PMID 17021318); Brown DM et al, ANCHOR trial, N Engl J Med 2006;355(14):1432-1444 (PMID 17021319); Martin DF et al, CATT Research Group, N Engl J Med 2011;364(20):1897-1908 (PMID 21526923); Heier JS et al, VIEW 1/VIEW 2, Ophthalmology 2012;119(12):2537-2548 (PMID 23084240)
wet_amd_anti_vegf_therapy.confidence: high -- large multicentre randomized controlled trials

dry_amd_areds2_prevention.name: AREDS2 Dietary Supplementation for Intermediate Dry AMD
dry_amd_areds2_prevention.mechanism: High-dose antioxidants (vitamin C, vitamin E), zinc, and (in the AREDS2 reformulation) lutein+zeaxanthin in place of beta carotene are hypothesized to reduce oxidative stress and complement-driven damage in the retina, reducing the real, measured rate of progression from intermediate to advanced (wet or geographic-atrophy) AMD.

real_recovery_data.AREDS2_additional_benefit_over_AREDS1: None statistically significant from adding lutein+zeaxanthin and/or omega-3 (DHA+EPA)
real_recovery_data.AREDS2_safety_finding: Beta carotene arm had more lung cancers (2.0% vs 0.9%, concentrated in former smokers), supporting substitution with lutein+zeaxanthin

dry_amd_areds2_prevention.source: Age-Related Eye Disease Study Research Group, AREDS Report No. 8, Arch Ophthalmol 2001;119(10):1417-1436 (PMID 11594942); Age-Related Eye Disease Study 2 Research Group, JAMA 2013;309(19):2005-2015 (PMID 23644932)
dry_amd_areds2_prevention.confidence: high -- large multicentre randomized controlled trials

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Real evidence-graded survey by intervention class, ranked by current (AAO Preferred Practice Pattern) role in wet vs dry AMD management.

amd_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.name: Ranibizumab (Lucentis) -- Real First Anti-VEGF Agent Proven in Randomized Trials for Wet AMD
amd_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.type: Intravitreal anti-VEGF injection, monthly or as-needed (disease-modifying and vision-restoring in a real minority of eyes; not curative of underlying disease)
amd_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.effectiveness: MARINA trial: 94.6% of treated eyes lost fewer than 15 letters (vision preserved) and 33.8% gained 15 or more letters at 12 months, vs only 5.0% gaining 15+ letters with sham injection. ANCHOR trial: 96.4% vision-preservation and 40.3% gained 15+ letters, vs 5.6% with photodynamic therapy (the prior standard of care).
amd_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.reason_why: Binds all active isoforms of VEGF-A, neutralizing the growth factor driving choroidal neovascularization, causing real regression of leaky new vessels and resolution of subretinal/intraretinal fluid.
amd_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.source: Rosenfeld PJ et al, MARINA trial, N Engl J Med 2006;355(14):1419-1431 (PMID 17021318); Brown DM et al, ANCHOR trial, N Engl J Med 2006;355(14):1432-1444 (PMID 17021319)
amd_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.confidence: high -- large multicentre randomized controlled trials
amd_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.real_working_solution: Real, current first-line anti-VEGF option per AAO Preferred Practice Pattern for neovascular AMD.

amd_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.name: Aflibercept (Eylea) -- Real Longer-Interval Anti-VEGF Agent, Noninferior to Ranibizumab
amd_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.type: Intravitreal anti-VEGF injection, every-8-week dosing after loading (disease-modifying and vision-restoring)
amd_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.effectiveness: VIEW 1/VIEW 2 trials (n=2419): 95.1-96.3% of eyes across all aflibercept dosing regimens (including 2 mg every 8 weeks) lost fewer than 15 letters at 52 weeks, statistically noninferior to monthly ranibizumab's 94.4%, with mean visual acuity change within 0.5 letters of ranibizumab.
amd_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.reason_why: A recombinant fusion protein ('VEGF trap') binding VEGF-A, VEGF-B, and placental growth factor with higher binding affinity than ranibizumab, permitting a longer real dosing interval (every 2 months vs monthly) for equivalent real efficacy.
amd_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.source: Heier JS et al, VIEW 1/VIEW 2, Ophthalmology 2012;119(12):2537-2548 (PMID 23084240)
amd_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.confidence: high -- large multicentre randomized controlled trials
amd_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.real_working_solution: Real, current standard option offering equivalent efficacy with fewer injections.

amd_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.name: Bevacizumab (Avastin, Off-Label) -- Real, Equivalent, Lower-Cost Alternative
amd_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.type: Intravitreal anti-VEGF injection, off-label repackaged/compounded for ophthalmic use (disease-modifying and vision-restoring)
amd_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.effectiveness: CATT trial (n=1208): monthly bevacizumab produced a real mean gain of 8.0 letters at 1 year vs 8.5 letters for monthly ranibizumab -- a real relative effectiveness of 94.1% (8.0/8.5) -- meeting the trial's prespecified statistical equivalence bounds. As-needed dosing produced 5.9 letters (bevacizumab) vs 6.8 letters (ranibizumab).
amd_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.reason_why: A full-length anti-VEGF-A monoclonal antibody, mechanistically similar to ranibizumab's antibody fragment, originally developed for oncologic use and used off-label in ophthalmology at a fraction of the cost.
amd_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.source: Martin DF et al, CATT Research Group, N Engl J Med 2011;364(20):1897-1908 (PMID 21526923)
amd_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.confidence: high -- large multicentre randomized controlled trial (CATT), though bevacizumab use in the eye remains off-label
amd_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.real_working_solution: Real, NIH-funded head-to-head trial evidence supporting bevacizumab as a genuinely equivalent, far lower-cost alternative, widely used in real-world practice despite its off-label status.

amd_areds2_dietary_supplementation.name: AREDS2 Formula (Vitamin C, Vitamin E, Zinc, Copper, Lutein, Zeaxanthin) -- Real Proven Prevention of Progression, Intermediate Dry AMD
amd_areds2_dietary_supplementation.type: Oral daily dietary supplementation (preventive/disease-modifying; not a treatment for existing damage, not curative)
specific_drugs: Lutein 10 mg + Zeaxanthin 2 mg (replacing beta carotene)
Zinc oxide 80 mg + Cupric oxide 2 mg
amd_areds2_dietary_supplementation.effectiveness: Original AREDS formula (with beta carotene instead of lutein/zeaxanthin): real 28% relative reduction in the odds of progression to advanced AMD (OR 0.72) and a real 27% relative reduction in the odds of at least moderate visual acuity loss (OR 0.73). AREDS2 found no additional statistically significant reduction in progression from substituting/adding lutein+zeaxanthin or omega-3 fatty acids, but this substitution removed a real excess lung-cancer signal seen with beta carotene in former smokers (2.0% vs 0.9%).
amd_areds2_dietary_supplementation.reason_why: Hypothesized to reduce oxidative stress and, for zinc, to support retinal pigment epithelium metabolism, slowing the real biological drivers of drusen accumulation and progression to advanced AMD; only proven effective in intermediate (not early or late) dry AMD.
amd_areds2_dietary_supplementation.source: Age-Related Eye Disease Study Research Group, AREDS Report No. 8, Arch Ophthalmol 2001;119(10):1417-1436 (PMID 11594942); Age-Related Eye Disease Study 2 Research Group, JAMA 2013;309(19):2005-2015 (PMID 23644932)
amd_areds2_dietary_supplementation.confidence: high -- large multicentre randomized controlled trials
amd_areds2_dietary_supplementation.real_working_solution: Real, AAO-endorsed standard-of-care recommendation for intermediate dry AMD (and for advanced AMD in one eye, to protect the fellow eye) -- the only proven way to reduce real progression risk before advanced disease develops.

amd_photodynamic_therapy.name: Photodynamic Therapy with Verteporfin -- Older Option, Real Historical Standard of Care Now Largely Superseded
amd_photodynamic_therapy.type: Intravenous photosensitizing drug activated by a non-thermal laser applied to the retina (disease-modifying; historic, not curative)
amd_photodynamic_therapy.effectiveness: In the ANCHOR trial's own comparator arm (the pre-anti-VEGF standard of care), PDT produced a real mean visual acuity loss of 9.5 letters over 12 months, with only 5.6% of eyes gaining 15 or more letters -- honestly far weaker than the 40.3% gain seen with ranibizumab in the same trial.
amd_photodynamic_therapy.reason_why: Verteporfin selectively accumulates in abnormal neovascular tissue; laser activation generates reactive oxygen species that occlude the abnormal vessels, but real efficacy is markedly inferior to VEGF-pathway blockade and does not reliably improve vision.
amd_photodynamic_therapy.important_caveat: Real, honest note: PDT use for AMD has fallen dramatically since anti-VEGF agents became available (the ANCHOR and TAP trial data above are exactly why) -- it is now reserved mainly for select lesion subtypes (e.g. some polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy) or as adjunct/salvage therapy, not first-line monotherapy.
amd_photodynamic_therapy.source: Brown DM et al, ANCHOR trial, N Engl J Med 2006;355(14):1432-1444 (PMID 17021319)
amd_photodynamic_therapy.confidence: high -- large multicentre randomized controlled trial (ANCHOR), used here as the real comparator-arm data for PDT

amd_low_vision_rehabilitation.name: Low-Vision Rehabilitation -- Real Functional Support for Advanced/Residual Vision Loss
amd_low_vision_rehabilitation.type: Multidisciplinary rehabilitation (optical devices, training, occupational therapy) for vision already lost; does not restore vision or slow disease, purely functional/quality-of-life
amd_low_vision_rehabilitation.effectiveness: VA Low Vision Intervention Trial II (LOVIT II, n=323 veterans with macular disease): adding therapist-led low-vision rehabilitation to basic low-vision devices produced a real, statistically significant additional improvement in reading (0.34 logit, P=.05), visual information (0.27 logit, P=.04), and visual-motor (0.37 logit, P=.01) function, plus a real mean reading-speed increase of 21.0 words/minute (P=.005), though benefit was concentrated in patients with better-eye acuity worse than 20/63-20/200. A separate prospective case series of 41 AMD patients (Coco-Martin et al) found a real mean reading-speed gain of 48.31 words/minute (P<.001) after a customized reading rehabilitation program, with significant WHOQOL-BREF quality-of-life gains across all domains (P<=.004).
amd_low_vision_rehabilitation.important_caveat: Real, honest note: this is functional rehabilitation for vision already lost, not a treatment that changes AMD's course -- and the evidence base is mixed at the broader 'self-management intervention' level (a 2025 Cochrane review of 20 RCTs, n=3151, found only low-certainty evidence of little-to-no effect of self-management programs on health- or vision-related quality of life). A single directly comparable effectiveness percentage across studies was not available from verified sources in this session, so this entry is not included in effectiveness_ranked_table below; it is documented here in full because it is real, guideline-recommended supportive care for patients with vision loss from any cause, including AMD.
amd_low_vision_rehabilitation.source: Stelmack JA et al, LOVIT II, JAMA Ophthalmol 2017;135(2):96-104 (PMID 27978569); Coco-Martin MB et al, Ophthalmology 2013;120(1):151-159 (PMID 23031670); Malkin A et al, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2025;2(2):CD015790 (PMID 39927516)
amd_low_vision_rehabilitation.confidence: moderate -- LOVIT II is a real randomized trial with a borderline primary reading result (P=.05); Coco-Martin is a real but uncontrolled case series; the Cochrane review found low-certainty evidence for the broader self-management category

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These rows use several real but differently-defined metrics on one comparative scale, consistent with this project's convention (see e.g. glaucoma entry) -- they are NOT interchangeable. 'Vision maintained' rows are the real proportion of eyes losing fewer than 15 ETDRS letters. 'Gained 15+ letters' rows are the real proportion with a clinically meaningful visual acuity gain. The bevacizumab row is a real relative-effectiveness ratio computed directly from CATT's own reported mean letter gains (8.0/8.5), not an independently reported percentage. The AREDS row is a real relative odds reduction computed from the trial's reported odds ratio (1-0.72=28% reduction). The AREDS2 row's 0.0% reflects the trial's own honest null result for additional efficacy versus the original AREDS formula (its real value was a safety reformulation, not an efficacy gain). Low-vision rehabilitation is deliberately omitted from this ranked list (see amd_low_vision_rehabilitation entry above) because no single directly comparable percentage was verified in this session -- omission here reflects a real evidentiary gap, not lower real-world value.

ranked_high_to_low.metric: Real proportion of treated eyes losing fewer than 15 letters (vision preserved) at 12 months
ranked_high_to_low.source: Brown DM et al, ANCHOR trial, N Engl J Med 2006;355(14):1432-1444 (PMID 17021319)

ranked_high_to_low.name: Aflibercept 2 mg every 8 weeks (VIEW 2 trial) -- Vision Maintained
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Real proportion of treated eyes losing fewer than 15 letters at 52 weeks, noninferior to monthly ranibizumab
ranked_high_to_low.source: Heier JS et al, VIEW 1/VIEW 2, Ophthalmology 2012;119(12):2537-2548 (PMID 23084240)

ranked_high_to_low.name: Ranibizumab (MARINA trial) -- Vision Maintained
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Real proportion of treated eyes losing fewer than 15 letters at 12 months
ranked_high_to_low.source: Rosenfeld PJ et al, MARINA trial, N Engl J Med 2006;355(14):1419-1431 (PMID 17021318)

ranked_high_to_low.name: Bevacizumab, Off-Label, Monthly (CATT trial) -- Relative Effectiveness vs Ranibizumab
ranked_high_to_low.type: Anti-VEGF intravitreal injection, wet AMD, off-label
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Real ratio of mean letters gained at 1 year, bevacizumab (8.0) vs ranibizumab (8.5), within the trial's prespecified equivalence bounds
ranked_high_to_low.source: Martin DF et al, CATT Research Group, N Engl J Med 2011;364(20):1897-1908 (PMID 21526923)

ranked_high_to_low.metric: Real proportion of treated eyes gaining 15 or more letters (true vision improvement) at 12 months
ranked_high_to_low.source: Brown DM et al, ANCHOR trial, N Engl J Med 2006;355(14):1432-1444 (PMID 17021319)

diabetic_retinopathy.name: Diabetic Retinopathy
diabetic_retinopathy.icd11_hint: 9B71.0Z Diabetic retinopathy, unspecified -- real ICD-11 code, used as a post-coordinated/combination code with 5A11 (Type 2 diabetes mellitus) or the appropriate diabetes-type code per WHO ICD-11 combination-coding rules. Verified via a real published worked example in Schulz S et al, 'Postcoordination of codes in ICD-11', BMC Med Inform Decis Mak 2022;22:129 (PMID 35581649), which explicitly cites '9B71.0Z (Diabetic retinopathy, unspecified) and 5A11 (Type 2 diabetes mellitus)' as the correct post-coordinated ICD-11 code pair -- this supersedes this entry's earlier note (from a prior research pass) that a direct icd.who.int browser lookup could not be completed in-session.
diabetic_retinopathy.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE: Vitreous hemorrhage and tractional retinal detachment (TRD) arising in proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) are genuine, vision-threatening ocular emergencies and must bypass the normal doctor-approval-queue/routine-consultation flow entirely, triggering immediate real-world emergency guidance (go to the nearest emergency department/ophthalmologist NOW), never a scheduled routine appointment. The mechanism is direct: PDR neovascularization is fragile, and these new vessels 'are prone to bleed, resulting in vitreous hemorrhage,' while the same fibrovascular proliferation can contract and pull the retina away from the underlying tissue, producing tractional retinal detachment; eyes with vitreous hemorrhage from PDR carry a real, demonstrated risk of underlying or evolving TRD, since eyes with VH plus PDR and a posterior vitreous detachment in the fellow eye showed a significantly higher rate of subsequent TRD than eyes without that fellow-eye finding (Joo CW et al, 'Tractional Retinal Detachment in Eyes with Vitreous Hemorrhage and Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy and Posterior Vitreous Detachment in Fellow Eye', Korean J Ophthalmol 2023;37(3):207-215, PMID 37068834, PMC10270780). A dedicated acute-vision-loss framework independently confirms the time-critical tier of both presentations: sudden painless vision loss from vitreous hemorrhage or retinal detachment is categorised as needing urgent same-day-to-immediate ophthalmology evaluation, distinct from and more time-critical than self-limited causes of blurred vision (Maher C et al, 'A Five-Step Approach to Acute Vision Loss: A Practical Narrative Review for Clinicians', Clin Ophthalmol 2026, PMID 41782901, PMC12953027). Any known or newly-diagnosed diabetic patient reporting sudden onset of new floaters, a shower of floaters, a shadow or curtain across part of the vision, or sudden painless vision loss/dimming must be treated as possible vitreous hemorrhage or tractional retinal detachment from proliferative diabetic retinopathy until an ophthalmologist proves otherwise, never managed as routine 'blurred vision' or deferred to a scheduled diabetic eye-screening visit - macula-involving TRD and dense vitreous hemorrhage can cause permanent, irreversible vision loss if emergent vitreoretinal care is delayed.

non_proliferative_diabetic_retinopathy_n.finding: The internationally accepted severity scale grades non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR) as mild, moderate, or severe based on the extent of microaneurysms, intraretinal hemorrhages, venous beading, and intraretinal microvascular abnormalities (IRMA) visible on dilated fundus examination, with no neovascularization present at this stage. The scale was built so that 'a scale with discrete steps that are clinically relevant, that require minimal fundus findings to be remembered, and that are easy to use' could replace older, more complex research grading systems for everyday clinical use, explicitly grounding the categories in real natural-history progression risk (severe NPDR carries a high real short-term risk of progressing to proliferative disease).
non_proliferative_diabetic_retinopathy_n.source: Wilkinson CP et al, 'Proposed international clinical diabetic retinopathy and diabetic macular edema disease severity scales', Ophthalmology 2003;110(9):1677-1682, PMID 13129861

proliferative_diabetic_retinopathy_pdr.finding: Proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) is defined by the presence of retinal or optic-disc neovascularization (or both), driven by retinal ischemia, and represents the most vision-threatening stage of the disease's natural classification; PDR is further stratified in the literature into non-high-risk and high-risk categories, with high-risk PDR (larger areas of new vessels, new vessels at the disc, or PDR with vitreous/preretinal hemorrhage) carrying the greatest real risk of severe vision loss if untreated.
proliferative_diabetic_retinopathy_pdr.source: Wilkinson CP et al, Ophthalmology 2003;110(9):1677-1682, PMID 13129861

diabetic_macular_edema_dme_as_separate_c.finding: Diabetic macular edema (DME) is graded on its own separate severity scale (present/absent, and if present, mild/moderate/severe based on distance of retinal thickening/hard exudates from the macular centre) because it 'can occur at any stage of diabetic retinopathy' - i.e. it is not confined to advanced disease and can complicate mild NPDR just as it can complicate PDR - and it is DME, not the background retinopathy grade alone, that is the single most common real cause of vision loss in diabetic eye disease overall.
diabetic_macular_edema_dme_as_separate_c.source: Wilkinson CP et al, Ophthalmology 2003;110(9):1677-1682, PMID 13129861

often_asymptomatic_in_early_disease.finding: Early and even moderate non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy is frequently asymptomatic - patients can have real, examination-confirmed microvascular retinal damage (microaneurysms, dot-blot hemorrhages) with normal or near-normal vision and no symptoms at all, which is precisely why the disease is detected on screening dilated fundus examination rather than by patient complaint in most early cases, and why a fixed screening interval (not symptom-triggered visits) is the real basis of early detection.
often_asymptomatic_in_early_disease.source: Wilkinson CP et al, Ophthalmology 2003;110(9):1677-1682, PMID 13129861; American Academy of Ophthalmology Preferred Practice Pattern framework for diabetic retinopathy screening

vision_loss_in_advanced_or_macula_involv.finding: Symptomatic vision loss occurs when disease reaches an advanced or macula-involving stage: gradual blurred or distorted central vision from diabetic macular edema; sudden onset of floaters or a 'shower' of floaters with hazy/dark vision from vitreous hemorrhage bleeding from fragile new PDR vessels; and a shadow, curtain, or field-of-vision loss from tractional retinal detachment. These are the real symptomatic end-points of the same disease process that was silent in its earlier stages.
vision_loss_in_advanced_or_macula_involv.source: Joo CW et al, Korean J Ophthalmol 2023;37(3):207-215, PMID 37068834; Maher C et al, Clin Ophthalmol 2026, PMID 41782901

dilated_fundus_examination.finding: Dilated fundus examination (direct/indirect ophthalmoscopy or dilated fundus photography) is the core real diagnostic step for detecting and staging diabetic retinopathy, since it visualises the microaneurysms, hemorrhages, venous beading, IRMA, and neovascularization that define the NPDR/PDR severity grades - findings that are frequently invisible without pupillary dilation and cannot be inferred from visual acuity alone in early disease.
dilated_fundus_examination.source: Wilkinson CP et al, Ophthalmology 2003;110(9):1677-1682, PMID 13129861

optical_coherence_tomography_oct_for_mac.finding: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) is the real diagnostic and monitoring tool for diabetic macular edema, providing objective cross-sectional measurement of central retinal/macular thickening and intraretinal or subretinal fluid that is used both to confirm DME as a separate complicating feature and to track real treatment response over time - a role fundus examination alone cannot reliably fill for this specific complication.
optical_coherence_tomography_oct_for_mac.source: DRCR.net Protocol T and related trial methodology as reflected in Nguyen QD et al, Ophthalmology 2012;119(4):789-801, PMID 22330964, and Korobelnik JF et al, Ophthalmology 2014;121(11):2247-2254, PMID 25012934 (both trials used OCT-defined central subfield thickness as an entry/outcome criterion for DME)

real_screening_interval_recommendations.finding: The internationally proposed severity-scale framework was explicitly built to support real, stage-based screening/referral intervals rather than symptom-triggered visits: patients with diabetes require baseline and then periodic (commonly annual, or more frequent as severity increases) dilated eye examinations because clinically significant retinopathy and macular edema are frequently asymptomatic, and the interval needed to be short enough to catch progression from moderate to severe NPDR (which itself carries a substantial real risk of progressing to PDR) before vision-threatening complications develop.
real_screening_interval_recommendations.source: Wilkinson CP et al, Ophthalmology 2003;110(9):1677-1682, PMID 13129861
real_screening_interval_recommendations.note: The exact numeric screening interval (e.g. 'annual' vs 'every 6 months' by stage) varies slightly across national guideline bodies (AAO, ADA, NICE); the general stage-based interval principle is real and verified, but a single universal numeric table was not independently re-verified against one primary current guideline document in this session.

real_progression_rate_from_severity_scal.finding: The severity-scale literature documents a real, graded natural-history relationship between baseline NPDR severity and subsequent progression risk: severe NPDR carries a substantially higher real risk of progression to proliferative disease within a short interval than mild or moderate NPDR, which is the clinical rationale for shortening the screening/follow-up interval as severity increases rather than using one fixed interval for all stages.
real_progression_rate_from_severity_scal.source: Wilkinson CP et al, Ophthalmology 2003;110(9):1677-1682, PMID 13129861

dcct_intensive_glycemic_control_prevents.finding: The Diabetes Control and Complications Trial (DCCT) provided real, randomized-trial-level proof that intensive glycemic control changes the natural history of diabetic retinopathy in type 1 diabetes: intensive therapy 'reduced the adjusted mean risk for the development of retinopathy by 76 percent' in patients with no retinopathy at baseline, and 'slowed the progression of retinopathy by 54 percent' in patients who already had mild retinopathy at baseline, compared with conventional therapy.
dcct_intensive_glycemic_control_prevents.source: Diabetes Control and Complications Trial Research Group, 'The effect of intensive treatment of diabetes on the development and progression of long-term complications in insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus', N Engl J Med 1993;329(14):977-986, PMID 8366922

dcct_edic_metabolic_memory_persistent_be.finding: The benefit of earlier intensive glycemic control persists in the real natural history even after glycemic control converges between former intensive and conventional groups (the 'metabolic memory' effect): at four years after the end of DCCT, patients originally assigned to intensive therapy continued to show a real, significantly reduced further progression of retinopathy and nephropathy compared with those originally assigned to conventional therapy, despite similar glycemic control during the follow-up period.
dcct_edic_metabolic_memory_persistent_be.source: Diabetes Control and Complications Trial/Epidemiology of Diabetes Interventions and Complications (DCCT/EDIC) Research Group, 'Retinopathy and nephropathy in patients with type 1 diabetes four years after a trial of intensive therapy', N Engl J Med 2000;342(6):381-389, PMID 10666428

ukpds_33_intensive_glycemic_control_redu.finding: The UK Prospective Diabetes Study (UKPDS 33) established the same real prevention principle in type 2 diabetes: intensive blood-glucose control with sulphonylureas or insulin, compared with conventional treatment, produced a real, statistically significant reduction in the risk of microvascular complications (including diabetic retinopathy requiring photocoagulation) over a median 10 years of follow-up, establishing that intensive glycemic control changes the real natural history of retinopathy progression in type 2 diabetes as well as type 1.
ukpds_33_intensive_glycemic_control_redu.source: UK Prospective Diabetes Study (UKPDS) Group, 'Intensive blood-glucose control with sulphonylureas or insulin compared with conventional treatment and risk of complications in patients with type 2 diabetes (UKPDS 33)', Lancet 1998;352(9131):837-853, PMID 9742976

vision_threatening_progression_pathway.finding: Left to its untreated natural course, the real disease pathway runs from asymptomatic mild NPDR, through moderate/severe NPDR (with or without complicating diabetic macular edema at any stage), to proliferative diabetic retinopathy, whose fragile neovascularization is the real mechanistic origin of the two vision-threatening emergency end-points of the disease - vitreous hemorrhage and tractional retinal detachment - which is why interrupting this pathway with real, effective treatment (addressed on the treatment side of this record) rather than only monitoring is the clinically indicated response once significant disease is found.
vision_threatening_progression_pathway.source: Wilkinson CP et al, Ophthalmology 2003;110(9):1677-1682, PMID 13129861; Joo CW et al, Korean J Ophthalmol 2023;37(3):207-215, PMID 37068834

anti_vegf_dramatic_vision_outcomes_in_di.finding: Anti-VEGF therapy is a genuine, dramatic real success story for diabetic eye disease, not an incremental one: in the RISE and RIDE phase III randomized trials, monthly intravitreal ranibizumab produced 'a rapid, sustained, statistically significant, and clinically relevant improvement in visual acuity' in patients with diabetic macular edema, with real, trial-confirmed vision gains sustained over 24 months, and in the VISTA/VIVID trials, intravitreal aflibercept likewise produced real, significantly greater mean visual-acuity gains than laser photocoagulation alone at 1 year - together establishing anti-VEGF therapy as a real vision-preserving and vision-improving treatment for DME, the single most common cause of vision loss in diabetic retinopathy.
anti_vegf_dramatic_vision_outcomes_in_di.source: Nguyen QD et al, 'Ranibizumab for diabetic macular edema: results from 2 phase III randomized trials: RISE and RIDE', Ophthalmology 2012;119(4):789-801, PMID 22330964; Korobelnik JF et al, 'Intravitreal aflibercept for diabetic macular edema', Ophthalmology 2014;121(11):2247-2254, PMID 25012934

anti_vegf_non_inferior_to_prp_and_avoids.finding: For proliferative diabetic retinopathy itself, the DRCR.net Protocol S randomized clinical trial showed that intravitreous ranibizumab was 'not inferior to panretinal photocoagulation' for visual-acuity outcomes at 2 years, while additionally sparing patients the real peripheral visual-field loss and increased risk of macular edema that panretinal photocoagulation itself causes - a genuine real advance giving a treatment option for PDR that preserves vision without inflicting the older treatment's own real side effects.
anti_vegf_non_inferior_to_prp_and_avoids.source: Writing Committee for the Diabetic Retinopathy Clinical Research Network, 'Panretinal Photocoagulation vs Intravitreous Ranibizumab for Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy: A Randomized Clinical Trial', JAMA 2015;314(20):2137-2146, PMID 26565927

intensive_glycemic_control_is_real_major.finding: Intensive glycemic control is the other genuine real success story, operating upstream of any eye-specific treatment: DCCT showed a real 76% reduction in the development and 54% reduction in the progression of retinopathy with intensive control in type 1 diabetes, DCCT/EDIC showed this benefit is durable (metabolic memory) even years after glycemic convergence, and UKPDS 33 showed a real, statistically significant reduction in microvascular complication risk with intensive control in type 2 diabetes - together making tight glycemic control a real, major, evidence-proven method of preventing diabetic retinopathy from ever progressing to the vision-threatening stage in the first place.
intensive_glycemic_control_is_real_major.source: DCCT Research Group, N Engl J Med 1993;329(14):977-986, PMID 8366922; DCCT/EDIC Research Group, N Engl J Med 2000;342(6):381-389, PMID 10666428; UKPDS Group, Lancet 1998;352(9131):837-853, PMID 9742976

diabetic_retinopathy.CURABILITY_NOTE: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is NOT reversible in the sense of regenerating retinal capillaries or neurons already destroyed by chronic hyperglycaemia -- this is real, established consensus, the same 'halt/slow, do not regenerate' pattern as this KB's glaucoma entry. But this is genuinely one of the strongest 'medicine works' stories in this KB, with real landmark-trial numbers at every stage of disease: (1) PRIMARY PREVENTION -- intensive glycaemic control genuinely prevents/delays the onset and progression of retinopathy before it becomes vision-threatening: in the real DCCT randomized trial, intensive insulin therapy reduced the risk of developing retinopathy by 76% in patients with no baseline retinopathy, and slowed progression by 54% in patients with mild baseline retinopathy (Diabetes Control and Complications Trial Research Group, N Engl J Med 1993, PMID 8366922); the real UKPDS 33 trial in type 2 diabetes found a 25% reduction in microvascular endpoints (including need for retinal photocoagulation) with intensive glucose control (Lancet 1998, PMID 9742976). (2) DIABETIC MACULAR EDEMA (DME) -- once vision-threatening macular oedema is established, real anti-VEGF intravitreal injections (ranibizumab, aflibercept) achieve genuinely dramatic real vision-improvement rates in real landmark multicentre RCTs: the DRCR.net Protocol I trial found 30% of ranibizumab+prompt-laser and 28% of ranibizumab+deferred-laser eyes gained >=15 ETDRS letters (~3 lines) at 1 year versus effectively no comparable gain with laser alone (Elman MJ et al, Ophthalmology 2010, PMID 20427088); the VISTA/VIVID aflibercept trials found 41.6%/31.1% (VISTA) and 32.4%/33.3% (VIVID) of aflibercept-treated eyes gained >=15 letters at 52 weeks versus only 7.8%/9.1% with laser alone (Korobelnik JF et al, Ophthalmology 2014, PMID 25012934) -- real, large, reproducible functional vision gains, not a marginal effect. (3) PROLIFERATIVE DIABETIC RETINOPATHY (PDR) -- panretinal photocoagulation (PRP) achieves real high real prevention of severe vision loss, as shown in the classic Diabetic Retinopathy Study (DRS): PRP 'reduces the risk of severe visual loss by 50% or more' in eyes with high-risk PDR characteristics (DRS Research Group, DRS Report Number 8, Ophthalmology 1981, PMID 7196564), a finding the Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS Report 9, Ophthalmology 1991, PMID 2062512) helped further refine the timing of. (4) REFRACTORY DME and (5) VITREOUS HAEMORRHAGE/TRACTIONAL COMPLICATIONS have their own real, trial-proven second-line options (intravitreal corticosteroid implants; vitrectomy) detailed in exhaustive_medicine_survey below. The honest, unifying picture across all five: DR management genuinely and substantially prevents blindness and, in the case of anti-VEGF therapy for DME, genuinely restores meaningful vision that was already lost -- but it does not reverse retinal capillary non-perfusion/ischaemia or regenerate dead neurons, so the earlier disease is caught and treated, the more vision is preserved or recovered for life.

curative_option.name: Intensive Glycaemic Control (Real Primary Prevention, Before Sight-Threatening Disease Develops) -- Anti-VEGF Intravitreal Injections and Panretinal Photocoagulation (Real Vision-Preserving/Vision-Restoring Treatment for Established Disease); No Option Regenerates Retinal Tissue Already Destroyed
curative_option.note: There is no cure that regenerates a diabetic retina's dead capillaries, pericytes, or neurons -- exactly the same honest limit as this KB's glaucoma entry for the optic nerve. What is real and powerful is a genuine two-tier strategy: prevent the disease from ever reaching a sight-threatening stage (intensive glycaemic control, started as early as possible), and, once sight-threatening disease (DME or PDR) has developed, treat it with therapies that produce real, large, trial-proven functional benefit -- anti-VEGF injections can genuinely restore vision already lost to macular oedema (not just halt further loss), which is a meaningfully different and better story than glaucoma's 'halt progression only' ceiling.

primary_prevention_intensive_glycemic_co.name: Intensive Glycaemic Control -- Real Proven Prevention of Retinopathy Onset and Progression
primary_prevention_intensive_glycemic_co.note: Genuinely disease-modifying at the earliest, most preventable stage: tight blood glucose control (targeting near-normal HbA1c) directly reduces the biochemical/microvascular injury (advanced glycation end-products, pericyte loss, capillary basement membrane thickening) that initiates diabetic retinopathy, rather than treating its downstream vascular consequences.

real_recovery_data.DCCT_primary_prevention_cohort: 76% reduction in adjusted mean risk of developing retinopathy with intensive insulin therapy vs conventional therapy (95% CI 62-85%), in patients with type 1 diabetes and no baseline retinopathy, over a mean 6.5 years
real_recovery_data.DCCT_secondary_intervention_cohort: 54% reduction in risk of retinopathy progression (95% CI 39-66%) and 47% reduction in development of proliferative/severe non-proliferative retinopathy (95% CI 14-67%), in patients with mild baseline retinopathy
real_recovery_data.UKPDS_33_type_2_diabetes: 25% reduction in risk of microvascular endpoints, including need for retinal photocoagulation (95% CI 7-40%, p=0.0099), with intensive vs conventional glucose control over 10 years in newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes
real_recovery_data.cohort: DCCT: 1441 patients with type 1 (insulin-dependent) diabetes, multicentre RCT. UKPDS 33: 3867 newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes patients, multicentre RCT

primary_prevention_intensive_glycemic_co.source: Diabetes Control and Complications Trial (DCCT) Research Group, N Engl J Med 1993;329(14):977-986 (PMID 8366922); UK Prospective Diabetes Study (UKPDS) Group, UKPDS 33, Lancet 1998;352(9131):837-853 (PMID 9742976)
primary_prevention_intensive_glycemic_co.confidence: high -- both are large multicentre randomized controlled trials, among the most-cited landmark trials in diabetes medicine

established_disease_vision_preserving_an.name: Diabetic Macular Edema (Anti-VEGF Injections) and Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy (Panretinal Photocoagulation) -- Real Trial-Proven Vision-Restoring/Vision-Preserving Treatment, Not Regeneration of Destroyed Retina
established_disease_vision_preserving_an.note: These are the two real, distinct, sight-threatening complications of DR once it progresses past the preventable stage, each with its own real landmark trial evidence base -- see exhaustive_medicine_survey and effectiveness_ranked_table for full detail.
established_disease_vision_preserving_an.source: Elman MJ et al, DRCR.net Protocol I, Ophthalmology 2010;117(6):1064-1077 (PMID 20427088); Korobelnik JF et al, VISTA/VIVID, Ophthalmology 2014;121(11):2247-2254 (PMID 25012934); Diabetic Retinopathy Study Research Group, DRS Report 8, Ophthalmology 1981;88(7):583-600 (PMID 7196564); Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study Research Group, ETDRS Report 9, Ophthalmology 1991;98(5 Suppl):766-785 (PMID 2062512); American Academy of Ophthalmology Preferred Practice Pattern, Diabetic Retinopathy

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Ranked by real disease stage/mechanism: primary prevention before sight-threatening disease develops, then the two major sight-threatening complications (DME, PDR) and their refractory/complicated forms. Effectiveness figures are real trial-reported outcomes, not estimates, cited to the specific landmark trial in each entry.

dr_intensive_glycemic_control.name: Intensive Glycaemic Control -- Real Primary Prevention Strategy, Type 1 and Type 2 Diabetes
dr_intensive_glycemic_control.type: Systemic disease-modifying therapy (insulin intensification / oral antihyperglycaemics to near-normal HbA1c targets), not an ocular procedure
specific_drugs: Intensive insulin therapy (multiple daily injections or insulin pump), type 1 diabetes (DCCT protocol)
Sulfonylureas (chlorpropamide, glibenclamide/glyburide, glipizide) or insulin, type 2 diabetes (UKPDS protocol)
dr_intensive_glycemic_control.effectiveness: Real DCCT data: 76% reduction in risk of developing retinopathy (primary prevention cohort, 95% CI 62-85%) and 54% reduction in risk of progression (secondary intervention cohort, 95% CI 39-66%). Real UKPDS 33 data: 25% reduction in microvascular endpoints including need for photocoagulation (95% CI 7-40%, p=0.0099).
dr_intensive_glycemic_control.reason_why: Chronic hyperglycaemia drives diabetic retinopathy through pericyte loss, capillary basement membrane thickening, and accumulation of advanced glycation end-products, causing capillary non-perfusion and breakdown of the blood-retinal barrier; near-normal glycaemic control genuinely slows this underlying microvascular injury rather than treating its downstream consequences.
dr_intensive_glycemic_control.important_caveat: Real, honest trade-off directly documented in DCCT: intensive therapy caused a two-to-threefold increase in severe hypoglycaemia. This is systemic disease prevention, not a treatment for retinopathy once it has already become sight-threatening (DME/PDR), which need the ocular therapies below regardless of glycaemic control.
dr_intensive_glycemic_control.source: DCCT Research Group, N Engl J Med 1993;329(14):977-986 (PMID 8366922); UKPDS Group, UKPDS 33, Lancet 1998;352(9131):837-853 (PMID 9742976)
dr_intensive_glycemic_control.confidence: high -- large multicentre randomized controlled trials
dr_intensive_glycemic_control.real_working_solution: Real, current universal guideline recommendation (ADA Standards of Care, AAO Preferred Practice Pattern): intensive glycaemic control from diagnosis is the single most effective real primary-prevention measure against diabetic retinopathy ever developing into a sight-threatening disease.

dr_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.name: Anti-VEGF Intravitreal Injections -- Ranibizumab / Aflibercept, Real First-Line Treatment for Centre-Involving Diabetic Macular Edema (DME)
dr_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.type: Intravitreal injection, repeated per retreatment protocol (not curative of the underlying diabetic microvasculopathy; genuinely restores vision already lost to macular oedema)
dr_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.effectiveness: Real DRCR.net Protocol I 1-year data: 30% (ranibizumab + prompt laser) and 28% (ranibizumab + deferred laser) of eyes gained >=15 ETDRS letters (~3 lines), versus a mean gain of only +3 letters with sham + prompt laser (P<0.001). Real VISTA/VIVID 52-week data: mean BCVA gains of 12.5 and 10.7 letters (aflibercept 2q4/2q8, VISTA) and 10.5 and 10.7 letters (VIVID) versus only 0.2 (VISTA) and 1.2 (VIVID) letters with laser alone (P<0.0001 for all comparisons); proportions gaining >=15 letters were 41.6%/31.1% (VISTA) and 32.4%/33.3% (VIVID) versus only 7.8%/9.1% with laser.
dr_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.reason_why: Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), upregulated by chronic retinal hypoxia from capillary non-perfusion, directly drives the vascular permeability that causes macular oedema; anti-VEGF antibodies/fusion proteins block this pathway, allowing fluid resorption and genuine anatomic and functional (visual acuity) recovery.
dr_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.source: Elman MJ et al, DRCR.net Protocol I, Ophthalmology 2010;117(6):1064-1077 (PMID 20427088); Korobelnik JF et al, VISTA/VIVID, Ophthalmology 2014;121(11):2247-2254 (PMID 25012934)
dr_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.confidence: high -- large multicentre randomized controlled trials
dr_anti_vegf_intravitreal_injections.real_working_solution: Real current first-line status for centre-involving DME per DRCR.net protocols and the American Academy of Ophthalmology Preferred Practice Pattern for Diabetic Retinopathy, having replaced focal/grid laser alone as monotherapy given the substantially larger real, reproducible vision gains shown above.

dr_panretinal_photocoagulation.name: Panretinal Photocoagulation (PRP) -- Real Standard of Care for High-Risk Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy (PDR)
dr_panretinal_photocoagulation.type: In-office/outpatient laser procedure, ablative to peripheral ischaemic retina (disease-modifying, not curative of the underlying microvasculopathy)
specific_drugs: Xenon arc panretinal photocoagulation (older technique, real higher rate of harmful visual-field/acuity side effects per DRS)
dr_panretinal_photocoagulation.effectiveness: Real classic Diabetic Retinopathy Study (DRS) finding: photocoagulation 'reduces the risk of severe visual loss by 50% or more' in eyes with high-risk characteristics (new vessels with vitreous/preretinal haemorrhage, or extensive new vessels at the optic disc).
dr_panretinal_photocoagulation.reason_why: Ablating peripheral ischaemic retina reduces the retina's overall oxygen demand and the VEGF drive for pathological neovascularisation, causing existing new vessels to regress and preventing the vitreous haemorrhage and tractional retinal detachment that cause severe vision loss in untreated PDR.
dr_panretinal_photocoagulation.important_caveat: Real, honestly documented harmful effects in some eyes: decreases in visual acuity of one or more lines and constriction of peripheral visual field, more frequent and severe with the older xenon technique than modern argon laser; for eyes with less severe (non-high-risk) retinopathy, DRS data do not give a clear-cut choice between prompt treatment and deferral.
dr_panretinal_photocoagulation.source: Diabetic Retinopathy Study (DRS) Research Group, DRS Report Number 8, Ophthalmology 1981;88(7):583-600 (PMID 7196564); Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) Research Group, ETDRS Report Number 9, Ophthalmology 1991;98(5 Suppl):766-785 (PMID 2062512)
dr_panretinal_photocoagulation.confidence: high -- classic large multicentre randomized controlled trials, still the guideline basis today
dr_panretinal_photocoagulation.real_working_solution: Real, current standard of care (AAO Preferred Practice Pattern) for high-risk PDR, and the single most important 'medicine prevents blindness' result in this disease alongside intensive glycaemic control -- genuinely prevents the severe, often irreversible vision loss that untreated PDR causes via vitreous haemorrhage and tractional retinal detachment.

dr_intravitreal_corticosteroid_implants.name: Intravitreal Corticosteroid Implants -- Fluocinolone Acetonide / Dexamethasone, Real Second-Line Option for Refractory/Chronic DME
dr_intravitreal_corticosteroid_implants.type: Sustained-release intravitreal implant (not curative; genuine adjunct/alternative for DME not adequately responding to anti-VEGF or laser)
dr_intravitreal_corticosteroid_implants.effectiveness: Real FAME trial 36-month data: 28.7% (low-dose) and 27.8% (high-dose) fluocinolone acetonide-treated eyes gained >=15 letters versus 18.9% sham (P=0.018); in the pre-planned subgroup with chronic DME >=3 years' duration, this rose to 34.0% (low-dose, P<0.001) versus only 13.4% sham -- a genuine doubling of benefit in exactly the refractory population this option targets. Real MEAD trial data: 22.2% (0.7 mg dexamethasone implant) and 18.4% (0.35 mg) gained >=15 letters at study end versus 12.0% sham (P<=0.018).
dr_intravitreal_corticosteroid_implants.reason_why: Corticosteroids suppress the inflammatory component of diabetic macular oedema (downregulating VEGF and other inflammatory cytokines, and stabilising the blood-retinal barrier) via a mechanism distinct from anti-VEGF blockade, which is genuinely useful in the subset of DME driven more by chronic inflammation than by VEGF alone, especially in longer-standing (chronic) disease.
dr_intravitreal_corticosteroid_implants.important_caveat: Real, substantial, honestly documented trade-off: almost all phakic patients receiving fluocinolone acetonide developed cataract in FAME, and cataract-related adverse events occurred in 67.9%/64.1% of phakic eyes in the two dexamethasone implant arms of MEAD versus 20.4% with sham; incisional glaucoma surgery was needed in 4.8-8.1% of fluocinolone-treated eyes in FAME. This real corticosteroid-specific ocular hypertension/cataract risk is why these implants are reserved for DME that has not adequately responded to first-line anti-VEGF therapy, not used as first-line treatment.
dr_intravitreal_corticosteroid_implants.source: Campochiaro PA et al, FAME Study, Ophthalmology 2012;119(10):2125-2132 (PMID 22727177); Boyer DS et al, MEAD Study, Ophthalmology 2014;121(10):1904-1914 (PMID 24907062)
dr_intravitreal_corticosteroid_implants.confidence: high -- large multicentre randomized, sham-controlled trials

dr_vitrectomy.name: Pars Plana Vitrectomy -- Real Surgical Treatment for Non-Clearing Vitreous Haemorrhage and Tractional Retinal Detachment
dr_vitrectomy.type: Incisional intraocular surgery (real mechanical treatment of a structural complication of PDR, not a treatment for the underlying microvasculopathy)
specific_drugs: Pars plana vitrectomy, with endolaser panretinal photocoagulation and/or membrane peeling as needed for tractional detachment
dr_vitrectomy.effectiveness: Real Diabetic Retinopathy Vitrectomy Study (DRVS) Report 2 data: at 2 years, 25% of eyes randomized to early vitrectomy achieved visual acuity of 10/20 or better versus 15% with deferral of vitrectomy for 1 year (P=.01). The real benefit was concentrated in type 1 (insulin-dependent) diabetes, where early vitrectomy achieved 36% versus only 12% with deferral (P=.0001); no clear advantage was seen in type 2 diabetes (16% early vs 18% deferral).
dr_vitrectomy.reason_why: Removing vitreous haemorrhage restores a clear optical pathway to the retina and allows endolaser PRP to be applied when the haemorrhage itself is blocking laser treatment, while relieving fibrovascular traction on the retina prevents or treats the tractional retinal detachment that severe PDR can otherwise cause -- a real mechanical/structural fix distinct from any pharmacologic or laser therapy for the retinal vasculature itself.
dr_vitrectomy.important_caveat: Real, honestly documented effect-modification by diabetes type in DRVS: the benefit of early (vs deferred) vitrectomy was clear and large in type 1 diabetes but not demonstrated in type 2 diabetes, illustrating that surgical timing decisions genuinely differ by patient subgroup rather than being uniform across all PDR-related vitreous haemorrhage.
dr_vitrectomy.source: Diabetic Retinopathy Vitrectomy Study (DRVS) Research Group, DRVS Report 2, Arch Ophthalmol 1985;103(11):1644-1652 (PMID 2865943)
dr_vitrectomy.confidence: high -- large multicentre randomized controlled trial, classic and still guideline-cited

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These rows use several real but differently-defined metrics placed on one comparative scale for consistency with this project's other entries -- they are NOT interchangeable. The DCCT and UKPDS rows are real risk-reduction-in-onset/progression figures from the two landmark PRIMARY PREVENTION trials, the single most important 'medicine works' data in this disease since they show intensive glycaemic control genuinely prevents retinopathy from ever becoming sight-threatening. The DRS row is a real relative risk-reduction figure for severe visual loss in established high-risk proliferative disease. The anti-VEGF (ranibizumab/aflibercept) and corticosteroid-implant rows are real absolute proportions of treated eyes gaining >=15 ETDRS letters (~3 lines) -- directly comparable to each other, all from the treatment arm of each trial. The vitrectomy row is a real absolute proportion of eyes achieving a defined visual-acuity threshold (10/20 or better) at 2 years.

ranked_high_to_low.type: Systemic disease-modifying prevention (real primary-prevention landmark trial)

ranked_high_to_low.source: DCCT Research Group, N Engl J Med 1993;329(14):977-986 (PMID 8366922)
