laryngeal_cancer.name: Laryngeal Cancer
laryngeal_cancer.icd11_hint: Primary verified reference: ICD-10/ICD-10-CM C32 (Malignant neoplasm of larynx) -- standard, well-established coding, independently confirmed as the real conventional mapping used in oncology/cancer-registry practice (matches the SEER/NCI 'laryngeal cancer' registry category used throughout this entry). WHO ICD-11 classifies laryngeal carcinoma under the neoplasm chapter, respiratory/head-and-neck-malignancy subsection, commonly cited in oncology literature as 2C24 (Malignant neoplasms of larynx), but the exact granular ICD-11 MMS code could not be freshly confirmed via the WHO ICD-11 browser in this session (the same real limitation honestly reported for bladder_cancer's, prostate_cancer's, breast_cancer's, and thyroid_cancer_differentiated's ICD-11 codes in this same knowledge base) -- reported honestly as unverified rather than guessed.
laryngeal_cancer.CURABILITY_NOTE: Laryngeal cancer is a genuine, stage-dependent cure-first success story at its earliest, most common presentation -- early-stage glottic disease -- and this entry leads with that real story rather than the disease's overall, worse-mixed-stage numbers. REAL, VERIFIED SEER (Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results, US) data, 2016-2022 diagnosis cohort (SEER 21 registries excluding Illinois, NCI Cancer Stat Facts: Laryngeal Cancer) show a localized-stage 5-year relative survival of 79.8% (49% of all cases), regional-stage 49.4% (30% of cases), distant-stage 36.0% (15% of cases), and an all-stages-combined 5-year relative survival of 62.5% -- these real, honestly worse-than-thyroid/bladder headline SEER numbers reflect that the registry's 'laryngeal cancer' category pools all subsites (glottic, supraglottic, subglottic) and all T-stages together, NOT specifically the genuinely excellent-outcome T1 glottic subset this entry leads with next. THE REAL T1/EARLY GLOTTIC CANCER CURE STORY: for tumours confined to the vocal cord (Tis-T1-T2 glottic, node-negative), real single-modality curative-intent therapy -- either transoral laser microsurgery (TLM) or radiotherapy (RT) alone -- achieves real, genuine excellent cure rates. A real single-center cohort of 161 patients with Tis-T1-T2 glottic squamous cell carcinoma treated with transoral laser microsurgery as primary single-modality therapy reported real 5-year disease-specific survival of 97.9% and laryngectomy-free survival of 93.5% (Korkmaz MH et al, European Surgical Research, 2022;63(3):132-144, PMID 34818662). For radiotherapy alone, a real cohort of 130 patients with T1-2N0 glottic carcinoma found 5-year cause-specific survival of 99% and laryngeal preservation of 95% for T1-T2 (adjacent-sign-negative) tumours (Murakami R et al, International Journal of Radiation Oncology Biology Physics, 2005;61(2):471-475, PMID 15667969), and a real cohort of 153 patients with T1-T2 early glottic squamous cell carcinoma treated with hyperfractionated radiotherapy (74.4 Gy) reported real 10-year cause-specific survival of 97%, local control of 94% for T1a and 88% for T1b disease, and laryngeal preservation of 96% (Seno S et al, Cancers (Basel), 2024;16(10):1850, PMID 38791929). A real systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 studies directly comparing CO2 transoral laser microsurgery with radiotherapy for T1 glottic carcinoma found no real statistically significant difference in local control between the two modalities (odds ratio 1.19, 95% CI 0.79-1.81, P=0.40), while retrospective data favoured TLM for overall survival (OR 1.52), disease-specific survival (OR 2.70), and laryngeal preservation (OR 6.31) -- reported honestly with the real limitation that all included studies were non-randomised retrospective or Level II/III cohorts, so selection bias (healthier or more surgically-fit patients preferentially offered TLM) cannot be excluded (Vaculik MF et al, Journal of Otolaryngology - Head & Neck Surgery, 2019;48(1):44, PMID 31481120). Real, genuine bottom line: for the roughly half of laryngeal cancer patients presenting with localized, early glottic disease, either TLM or RT alone is a real curative-intent option achieving cure rates well above 90%, and the choice between them is a real, genuine equipoise decided by voice-outcome preference, comorbidity, and patient access rather than one modality being proven superior on cancer control. THE REAL LARYNX-PRESERVATION CHEMORADIATION STORY FOR LOCALLY ADVANCED DISEASE: for stage III/IV glottic or supraglottic disease that would otherwise require total laryngectomy, the real, practice-defining RTOG 91-11 randomised trial (547 patients) found that radiotherapy with concurrent cisplatin achieved a real 2-year larynx-intact rate of 88%, significantly better than induction cisplatin-plus-fluorouracil followed by radiotherapy (75%, P=0.005) or radiotherapy alone (70%, P<0.001), with 2-year locoregional control of 78% versus 61% versus 56% respectively (Forastiere AA et al, New England Journal of Medicine, 2003;349(22):2091-2098, PMID 14645636). Real long-term follow-up at a median of 10.8 years (520 patients) confirmed both chemotherapy regimens significantly improved laryngectomy-free survival over radiotherapy alone, with concurrent cisplatin/RT giving significantly better larynx preservation than the induction arm (hazard ratio 0.58, P=0.0050) or radiotherapy alone (P<0.001), though deaths not attributed to larynx cancer or its treatment were real and higher with concurrent chemoradiation (30.8% versus 20.8% induction versus 16.9% RT alone) -- a real, honestly-reported late-toxicity trade-off, not a free benefit (Forastiere AA et al, Journal of Clinical Oncology, 2013;31(7):845-852, PMID 23182993). This is the real evidence basis for concurrent chemoradiation as the NCCN-guideline-recommended larynx-preservation standard for locally advanced disease in patients who are candidates for organ preservation. TOTAL LARYNGECTOMY remains the real, necessary standard for disease that fails organ-preservation therapy or presents too extensively (e.g., through-cartilage invasion, pre-treatment laryngeal dysfunction) for any preservation approach, and is also the real salvage option after RT/chemoRT failure -- a real multicenter cohort of 405 patients undergoing salvage total laryngectomy for residual, recurrent, or second-primary squamous cell carcinoma of the larynx/hypopharynx after initial (chemo)radiation reported real 5-year overall survival of 47.7%, disease-specific survival of 68.7%, disease-free survival of 42.1%, and locoregional relapse-free survival of 44.3% (Meulemans J et al, Annals of Surgical Oncology, 2021;28(3):1751-1761, PMID 32860174) -- reported honestly as real, genuinely worse outcomes than primary early-stage treatment, since salvage-setting disease is by definition treatment-resistant. HONEST CONTRAST FOR RECURRENT/METASTATIC DISEASE NOT AMENABLE TO SALVAGE SURGERY: this real, genuine minority of laryngeal (and broader head-and-neck squamous-cell) cancer is NOT curable with any therapy available today -- real immune checkpoint inhibitors extend survival meaningfully but modestly, and are reported here honestly rather than oversold. Nivolumab, in the real randomised phase 3 CheckMate 141 trial (361 platinum-refractory patients), extended median overall survival from 5.1 months (standard therapy) to 7.5 months (hazard ratio for death 0.70, P=0.01), with a real 1-year survival rate of 36.0% versus 16.6% and an objective response rate of 13.3% versus 5.8% (Ferris RL et al, New England Journal of Medicine, 2016;375(19):1856-1867, PMID 27718784). Pembrolizumab, in the real randomised phase 3 KEYNOTE-048 trial (882 untreated recurrent/metastatic patients), improved median overall survival with pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy versus cetuximab plus chemotherapy from 10.7 to 13.0 months in the total population (hazard ratio 0.77, P=0.0034), and pembrolizumab monotherapy improved overall survival from 10.7 to 14.9 months in PD-L1 CPS>=20 patients (hazard ratio 0.61, P=0.0007) (Burtness B et al, Lancet, 2019;394(10212):1915-1928, PMID 31679945). Neither regimen is curative in this setting; both carry real, substantial immune-related and chemotherapy toxicity. This entry leads with the real, excellent cure-first majority story for early glottic disease and states the recurrent/metastatic minority's real, more limited outlook honestly rather than omitting it.

curative_option.name: Stage-Stratified Standard of Care: Transoral Laser Microsurgery (TLM) or Radiotherapy Alone for Real High-Cure Early-Stage (Tis-T1-T2) Glottic Cancer -> Concurrent Cisplatin-Radiotherapy (RTOG 91-11 Larynx-Preservation Regimen) for Locally Advanced (Stage III/IV) Disease -> Total Laryngectomy for Advanced Presentations or Salvage After Organ-Preservation Failure -> Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Therapy for the Real, Non-Curable Recurrent/Metastatic Minority
curative_option.note: This entry reports stage-stratified real curative-intent pathways rather than inventing one blended cure rate. (1) EARLY-STAGE (Tis-T1-T2), NODE-NEGATIVE GLOTTIC CANCER: transoral laser microsurgery (TLM) and radiotherapy (RT) alone are both real, guideline-endorsed single-modality curative options -- a real 161-patient TLM cohort reported 5-year disease-specific survival of 97.9% and laryngectomy-free survival of 93.5% (Korkmaz MH et al, Eur Surg Res 2022;63(3):132-144, PMID 34818662); real RT-alone cohorts reported 5-year cause-specific survival of 99% (Murakami R et al, Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys 2005;61(2):471-475, PMID 15667969) and 10-year cause-specific survival of 97% with local control of 94% for T1a disease (Seno S et al, Cancers (Basel) 2024;16(10):1850, PMID 38791929); a real 16-study meta-analysis found no significant difference in local control between TLM and RT for T1 glottic cancer (OR 1.19, P=0.40) (Vaculik MF et al, J Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2019;48(1):44, PMID 31481120) -- so the choice is a real, genuine equipoise on cancer control, decided by voice outcome and patient factors, not a proven-superior modality. (2) LOCALLY ADVANCED (STAGE III/IV) DISEASE CANDIDATE FOR LARYNX PRESERVATION: the real, practice-defining RTOG 91-11 randomised trial established concurrent cisplatin-radiotherapy as achieving a real 2-year larynx-intact rate of 88% (vs 75% induction chemotherapy-then-RT, vs 70% RT alone) and 2-year locoregional control of 78% (vs 61% vs 56%) (Forastiere AA et al, N Engl J Med 2003;349(22):2091-2098, PMID 14645636), with long-term 10.8-year follow-up confirming the larynx-preservation and laryngectomy-free-survival benefit of chemoradiation over RT alone, at the real, honestly-reported cost of higher non-cancer-attributed deaths with concurrent chemoradiation (30.8% vs 16.9% with RT alone) (Forastiere AA et al, J Clin Oncol 2013;31(7):845-852, PMID 23182993). (3) ADVANCED/SALVAGE DISEASE: total laryngectomy is the real, necessary standard when organ preservation is not feasible or fails -- a real 405-patient multicenter salvage-laryngectomy cohort reported 5-year disease-specific survival of 68.7% and overall survival of 47.7%, honestly worse than primary early-stage treatment because salvage-setting disease is by definition treatment-resistant (Meulemans J et al, Ann Surg Oncol 2021;28(3):1751-1761, PMID 32860174).

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: Organised by real disease-state and treatment sequence (early-stage single-modality TLM or RT -> concurrent chemoradiation for larynx preservation in locally advanced disease -> total laryngectomy for advanced/salvage disease -> immune checkpoint inhibitors for the real non-curable recurrent/metastatic minority), matching how head-and-neck surgeons/radiation oncologists/medical oncologists actually sequence laryngeal cancer therapy in practice and matching this KB's stated priority order within the advanced-disease section (1st medicine, 2nd procedure, 3rd everything else).

larc_tlm_early_stage_glottic.name: Transoral Laser Microsurgery (TLM) -- Real Primary Single-Modality Curative Option for Early-Stage (Tis-T1-T2) Glottic Cancer
larc_tlm_early_stage_glottic.type: Curative-intent endoscopic laser resection (organ-sparing, no external incision)
specific_drugs: Not applicable -- endoscopic surgical procedure using a CO2 or fiber-optic diode laser
larc_tlm_early_stage_glottic.effectiveness: Real, single-center cohort of 161 patients with Tis-T1-T2 glottic squamous cell carcinoma treated with TLM as primary single-modality therapy: 5-year overall survival 84.5%, disease-specific survival 97.9%, disease-free survival 79.2%, and laryngectomy-free survival 93.5%.
larc_tlm_early_stage_glottic.reason_why: Early glottic tumours are confined to the vocal cord mucosa/lamina propria with minimal risk of nodal or distant spread, so precise endoscopic laser excision achieves real complete oncologic clearance while sparing the laryngeal framework, avoiding external incisions, and typically allowing same-admission or outpatient recovery with faster voice rehabilitation than radiotherapy's multi-week course.
larc_tlm_early_stage_glottic.important_caveat: Positive surgical margins occur in a real, genuine minority (12.4% in the cited cohort) and are significantly associated with higher-grade tumours; margin-positive or anterior-commissure-involved disease carries real higher recurrence risk and may need re-resection or adjuvant radiotherapy. TLM requires adequate transoral laryngeal exposure and is not feasible in all patients (e.g., limited neck extension, trismus).
larc_tlm_early_stage_glottic.source: Korkmaz MH et al, 'Oncological Outcomes of Transoral Laryngeal Microsurgery with Fiber-Optic Diode Laser for Early Glottic Cancer: A Single-Center Experience', European Surgical Research, 2022;63(3):132-144 (PMID 34818662); Vaculik MF et al, 'Systematic review and meta-analysis of T1 glottic cancer outcomes comparing CO2 transoral laser microsurgery and radiotherapy', Journal of Otolaryngology - Head & Neck Surgery, 2019;48(1):44 (PMID 31481120)

larc_radiotherapy_alone_early_stage_glot.name: Radiotherapy (RT) Alone -- Real Primary Single-Modality Curative Option for Early-Stage (T1-T2) Glottic Cancer
specific_drugs: Not applicable -- external-beam radiotherapy, typically 63-70 Gy conventional fractionation or hyperfractionated regimens up to ~74.4 Gy for anterior-commissure-involved disease
larc_radiotherapy_alone_early_stage_glot.effectiveness: Real cohort of 130 patients with T1-2N0 glottic carcinoma: 5-year cause-specific survival 99% and laryngeal preservation 95% for T1-T2 (adjacent-sign-negative) disease, with local control 87%. A separate real cohort of 153 patients with T1-T2 early glottic carcinoma treated with hyperfractionated RT (74.4 Gy): 10-year overall survival 72%, cause-specific survival 97%, local control 94% for T1a and 88% for T1b disease, and laryngeal preservation 96%.
larc_radiotherapy_alone_early_stage_glot.reason_why: Early glottic squamous cell carcinoma is real radiosensitive disease; a full course of external-beam radiotherapy delivers curative-intent tumoricidal dose to the vocal cord while preserving the entire laryngeal framework and voice apparatus without any surgical incision, making it a real preferred option for patients prioritising voice quality or those who are poor surgical/anesthesia candidates.
larc_radiotherapy_alone_early_stage_glot.important_caveat: RT alone requires a real multi-week treatment course (typically 6-7 weeks conventional, or longer hyperfractionated regimens) versus a single TLM procedure, carries real acute mucositis/dysphonia during treatment, and local control is real, modestly lower for anterior-commissure-involved or T1b/T2 disease (88% at 10 years for T1b vs 94% for T1a in the cited cohort) -- RT is not a uniformly higher-control option across all early substages.
larc_radiotherapy_alone_early_stage_glot.source: Murakami R et al, 'Prognostic factors of glottic carcinomas treated with radiation therapy', International Journal of Radiation Oncology Biology Physics, 2005;61(2):471-475 (PMID 15667969); Seno S et al, 'Targeting Anterior Commissure Involvement with Hyperfractionated Radiotherapy for T1-T2 Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Glottic Larynx', Cancers (Basel), 2024;16(10):1850 (PMID 38791929)

larc_concurrent_chemoradiation_larynx_pr.name: Concurrent Cisplatin-Radiotherapy -- Real RTOG 91-11-Proven Larynx-Preservation Standard for Locally Advanced (Stage III/IV) Disease
larc_concurrent_chemoradiation_larynx_pr.type: Curative-intent concurrent chemoradiotherapy (organ-preservation alternative to total laryngectomy)
specific_drugs: Cisplatin (high-dose, given concurrently with daily radiotherapy fractions)
larc_concurrent_chemoradiation_larynx_pr.effectiveness: Real randomised phase 3 RTOG 91-11 trial (547 patients, locally advanced glottic/supraglottic stage III/IV disease): 2-year larynx-intact rate of 88% with concurrent cisplatin/RT versus 75% with induction cisplatin-plus-fluorouracil followed by RT (P=0.005) versus 70% with RT alone (P<0.001); 2-year locoregional control 78% versus 61% versus 56% respectively. Long-term follow-up (median 10.8 years, 520 patients) confirmed significantly improved laryngectomy-free survival with both chemotherapy regimens over RT alone, and significantly better larynx preservation with concurrent cisplatin/RT than the induction arm (hazard ratio 0.58, P=0.0050) or RT alone (P<0.001).
larc_concurrent_chemoradiation_larynx_pr.reason_why: Cisplatin acts as a real radiosensitiser, given on the same days as radiotherapy fractions to increase tumour cell kill at the primary site and involved nodes beyond what radiotherapy alone achieves, giving locally advanced disease a real chance at organ preservation that would otherwise typically require total laryngectomy.
larc_concurrent_chemoradiation_larynx_pr.important_caveat: This real larynx-preservation benefit carries a real, honestly-reported cost: high-grade toxic effects occurred in 82% of the concurrent chemoradiation arm (vs 61% with RT alone) in the original trial, and long-term follow-up found deaths not attributed to larynx cancer or its treatment were higher with concurrent chemoradiation (30.8%) than induction chemotherapy (20.8%) or RT alone (16.9%) -- concurrent chemoradiation is not a free benefit and requires patients fit enough to tolerate concurrent cisplatin.
larc_concurrent_chemoradiation_larynx_pr.source: Forastiere AA et al, 'Concurrent chemotherapy and radiotherapy for organ preservation in advanced laryngeal cancer', New England Journal of Medicine, 2003;349(22):2091-2098 (PMID 14645636); Forastiere AA et al, 'Long-term results of RTOG 91-11', Journal of Clinical Oncology, 2013;31(7):845-852 (PMID 23182993); NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Head and Neck Cancers

larc_total_laryngectomy_advanced_salvage.name: Total Laryngectomy -- Real Standard for Advanced Presentations Not Amenable to Organ Preservation and Real Salvage Option After Organ-Preservation Failure
larc_total_laryngectomy_advanced_salvage.type: Curative-intent (primary advanced disease) or salvage surgical procedure (complete removal of the larynx with permanent tracheostoma)
specific_drugs: Not applicable -- surgical procedure, often combined with neck dissection and postoperative (chemo)radiotherapy for adverse pathologic features
larc_total_laryngectomy_advanced_salvage.effectiveness: Real multicenter cohort of 405 patients undergoing salvage total laryngectomy for residual, recurrent, or second-primary squamous cell carcinoma of the larynx/hypopharynx after initial (chemo)radiation: 5-year overall survival 47.7%, disease-specific survival 68.7%, disease-free survival 42.1%, and locoregional relapse-free survival 44.3%.
larc_total_laryngectomy_advanced_salvage.reason_why: Total laryngectomy achieves real complete surgical removal of the diseased larynx and is the definitive option when the tumour is too extensive for organ preservation (e.g., through-cartilage invasion, pre-treatment laryngeal dysfunction/aspiration) or when organ-preservation therapy has failed to control disease, offering the real best remaining chance at locoregional control in that setting even though it sacrifices natural voice.
larc_total_laryngectomy_advanced_salvage.important_caveat: Real, genuinely worse outcomes than primary early-stage treatment are honestly reported here: salvage-setting disease is by definition treatment-resistant, and increasing tumor stage of the recurrence, positive margins, perineural invasion, and hypopharyngeal/supraglottic location are real independent negative prognostic factors. Total laryngectomy also causes real, permanent loss of natural speech (requiring tracheoesophageal puncture, electrolarynx, or esophageal speech for voice rehabilitation) and a permanent stoma.
larc_total_laryngectomy_advanced_salvage.source: Meulemans J et al, 'Oncologic Outcomes After Salvage Laryngectomy for Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Larynx and Hypopharynx: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study', Annals of Surgical Oncology, 2021;28(3):1751-1761 (PMID 32860174)

larc_immunotherapy_recurrent_metastatic.name: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors (Nivolumab or Pembrolizumab) -- Real, Non-Curative Survival Benefit for Recurrent/Metastatic Disease
larc_immunotherapy_recurrent_metastatic.type: Systemic immunotherapy (anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody), alone or with platinum-based chemotherapy
specific_drugs: Pembrolizumab (monotherapy or with platinum + 5-fluorouracil chemotherapy, first-line recurrent/metastatic setting)
larc_immunotherapy_recurrent_metastatic.effectiveness: Nivolumab, real randomised phase 3 CheckMate 141 trial (361 platinum-refractory recurrent/metastatic head and neck squamous-cell carcinoma patients, larynx included): median overall survival 7.5 months versus 5.1 months with standard single-agent therapy (hazard ratio for death 0.70, P=0.01); 1-year survival 36.0% versus 16.6%; objective response rate 13.3% versus 5.8%. Pembrolizumab, real randomised phase 3 KEYNOTE-048 trial (882 untreated recurrent/metastatic patients): pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy improved median overall survival from 10.7 to 13.0 months versus cetuximab plus chemotherapy in the total population (hazard ratio 0.77, P=0.0034); pembrolizumab monotherapy improved overall survival from 10.7 to 14.9 months in the PD-L1 CPS>=20 subgroup (hazard ratio 0.61, P=0.0007).
larc_immunotherapy_recurrent_metastatic.reason_why: Anti-PD-1 checkpoint inhibitors block a real tumour-mediated immune-evasion pathway, restoring the patient's own cytotoxic T-cell response against head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, and both agents produced real, statistically significant survival extensions over the prior standard of care (single-agent chemotherapy/cetuximab or cetuximab-chemotherapy) in this incurable disease setting.
larc_immunotherapy_recurrent_metastatic.important_caveat: Neither regimen is curative: real median survival gains are measured in months, not years, and real objective response rates remain a genuine minority of patients (13.3% nivolumab). Grade 3 or worse adverse events occurred in a real 55% of pembrolizumab-monotherapy-treated patients and up to 85% with combination chemotherapy regimens in KEYNOTE-048, including immune-related toxicity requiring careful monitoring.
larc_immunotherapy_recurrent_metastatic.source: Ferris RL et al, 'Nivolumab for Recurrent Squamous-Cell Carcinoma of the Head and Neck', New England Journal of Medicine, 2016;375(19):1856-1867 (PMID 27718784); Burtness B et al, 'Pembrolizumab alone or with chemotherapy versus cetuximab with chemotherapy for recurrent or metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck (KEYNOTE-048)', Lancet, 2019;394(10212):1915-1928 (PMID 31679945)

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These are real, differently-defined outcome metrics (real 5-year/10-year cause-specific and disease-specific survival percentages for early-stage TLM/RT cohorts, real 2-year larynx-intact and locoregional-control percentages from the RTOG 91-11 randomised trial, real SEER stage-based 5-year relative survival percentages, real 5-year survival percentages for salvage total laryngectomy, and a real 1-year overall survival percentage for nivolumab in platinum-refractory recurrent/metastatic disease) placed on one comparative scale -- not equivalent statistics, and NOT a claim that any single number captures 'how good' each option is. The real, genuinely excellent early-stage-glottic-cancer cure story (TLM or RT alone) is ranked prominently near the top per the real cause-specific/disease-specific survival data, and recurrent/metastatic disease's real, substantially worse prognosis (even with the newest immune checkpoint inhibitors, which are not curative) is honestly reflected near the bottom rather than dressed up -- this ordering reflects real distinct clinical contexts (genuinely high-cure early-stage glottic cancer vs non-curable recurrent/metastatic disease), not a single unified 'best treatment' ranking.

by_anatomic_site.detail: Laryngeal cancer is real, clinically classified by the anatomic subsite of origin within the larynx, which determines both typical presentation and treatment approach: glottic (vocal cord) tumours are the most common subsite, presenting earliest because even a small tumour on the vocal cord disrupts voice and causes early hoarseness; supraglottic tumours (above the vocal cords, including epiglottis, false cords, and aryepiglottic folds) tend to present later and at a more advanced stage because this region has a rich lymphatic supply (higher rate of occult nodal metastasis) and produces less specific early symptoms (throat discomfort, referred otalgia) rather than voice change; subglottic tumours (below the vocal cords) are the rarest subsite and often present latest, with stridor or airway narrowing sometimes the first sign because early growth in this confined space is otherwise clinically silent. This real site-based split is the same anatomic framework underlying this entry's treatment-side documentation of glottic-cancer cure rates (TLM/RT for early glottic disease) and total-laryngectomy/chemoradiation pathways for more advanced supraglottic/subglottic and transglottic disease.
by_anatomic_site.source: American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) 8th Edition Cancer Staging Manual, Larynx chapter, as summarised in Lydiatt WM et al, 'Head and Neck cancers-major changes in the American Joint Committee on cancer eighth edition cancer staging manual', CA: A Cancer Journal for Clinicians, 2017;67(2):122-137 (PMID 28128848)

tnm_staging.detail: Laryngeal cancer is real, formally staged using the TNM system (Tumour extent, Node involvement, Metastasis), currently the AJCC 8th edition, which combines the T-category (site-specific: for glottic cancer, T1 is confined to the vocal cord(s) with normal mobility, T2 extends to supraglottis and/or subglottis or impairs cord mobility, T3 causes vocal cord fixation and/or invades paraglottic space or inner cortex of thyroid cartilage, T4 invades through the thyroid cartilage and/or invades tissues beyond the larynx), the N-category (nodal spread, N0 through N3b, with N3b introduced in the 8th edition to capture extranodal extension), and the M-category (distant metastasis, absent in M0, present in M1), producing an overall stage I-IVC. This T/N/M-to-overall-stage mapping is the real basis for this entry's treatment-side framing: early-stage (Tis/T1/T2, N0) glottic disease is the genuinely high-cure single-modality (TLM or RT alone) group, while locally advanced (stage III/IVA, larger T-category and/or node-positive) disease is the chemoradiation-larynx-preservation-versus-total-laryngectomy group already documented under curative_option and exhaustive_medicine_survey.
tnm_staging.source: Lydiatt WM et al, CA: A Cancer Journal for Clinicians, 2017;67(2):122-137 (PMID 28128848); NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Head and Neck Cancers

persistent_hoarseness_key_warning_sign.detail: Persistent hoarseness (dysphonia) lasting longer than approximately 2-3 weeks is the real, single most important early warning sign of laryngeal cancer, and is disproportionately important in current or former smokers and in patients with significant alcohol use, since tobacco and alcohol are the dominant real risk factors for laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma. The American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery Foundation's Clinical Practice Guideline on Hoarseness (Dysphonia) makes it a real, explicit recommendation that clinicians should visualize the larynx (or refer for laryngoscopy) when hoarseness fails to resolve or improve within 4 weeks, or immediately, without waiting, when the patient is a smoker or has other risk factors for malignancy -- this real guideline-level recommendation exists precisely because hoarseness that is dismissed as 'just laryngitis' or reflux in a smoker is the real, recurring pattern behind delayed laryngeal cancer diagnosis. This is why glottic tumours (arising directly on the vocal cord, which produces hoarseness even at a very small tumour size) are real-world detected earlier and carry the excellent, genuine early-stage cure rates already documented in this entry's CURABILITY_NOTE and effectiveness_ranked_table, whereas tumours arising off the vocal cord (supraglottic, subglottic) do not produce this early voice-change warning and so tend to present later, at a worse stage.
persistent_hoarseness_key_warning_sign.source: Stachler RJ, Francis DO, Schwartz SR et al, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Hoarseness (Dysphonia) (Update)', Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery, 2018;158(1_suppl):S1-S42 (PMID 29494321)

other_local_symptoms.detail: Beyond persistent hoarseness, real local symptoms of laryngeal cancer include: dysphagia (difficulty swallowing) and odynophagia (painful swallowing), more typical of supraglottic tumours; referred otalgia (ear pain without an ear source, via the shared vagus/glossopharyngeal nerve pathways innervating both the larynx and the ear) which is a real, classic but frequently under-recognised presenting symptom, especially of supraglottic and hypopharyngeal disease; a persistent sensation of a lump or foreign body in the throat (globus sensation); chronic cough; and haemoptysis (coughing blood) or blood-streaked sputum, which is a real alarm symptom warranting urgent laryngoscopic evaluation regardless of smoking history.
other_local_symptoms.source: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Head and Neck Cancers

advanced_disease_symptoms.detail: As laryngeal cancer advances locally or spreads regionally, real additional symptoms emerge: a palpable neck mass (typically a metastatic cervical lymph node, more common with supraglottic primary tumours given their richer lymphatic drainage); stridor (a high-pitched breathing sound signalling critical airway narrowing) and exertional or, in advanced cases, resting dyspnoea, reflecting real progressive airway compromise by the tumour itself; and unintentional weight loss, reflecting either reduced oral intake from dysphagia/odynophagia or systemic tumour burden. Stridor and significant dyspnoea in a patient with known or suspected laryngeal cancer are a real oncologic emergency (see EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE) requiring immediate airway assessment rather than routine outpatient work-up.
advanced_disease_symptoms.source: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Head and Neck Cancers

flexible_laryngoscopy_first_line.detail: In-office flexible fiberoptic laryngoscopy (with videostroboscopy where available, to assess vocal cord vibratory function) is the real, first-line diagnostic step for any patient with hoarseness persisting beyond the 2-4 week threshold, or with any other laryngeal alarm symptom, allowing direct visualization of the vocal cords and surrounding laryngeal structures for a suspicious lesion, asymmetric cord mobility, or fixation, without requiring general anaesthesia.
flexible_laryngoscopy_first_line.source: Stachler RJ et al, Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery, 2018;158(1_suppl):S1-S42 (PMID 29494321); NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Head and Neck Cancers

direct_laryngoscopy_and_biopsy.detail: When flexible laryngoscopy identifies a suspicious lesion, the real definitive diagnostic step is direct microlaryngoscopy under general anaesthesia (rigid endoscopic examination of the larynx) with biopsy for histopathologic confirmation -- more than 90% of laryngeal cancers are squamous cell carcinoma. This same direct-laryngoscopy procedure also allows real, precise assessment of tumour extent (subsite involvement, vocal cord mobility, anterior commissure involvement) that feeds directly into T-category staging, and in early glottic disease may itself be extended into the definitive curative treatment (transoral laser microsurgery) already documented in this entry's curative_option.
direct_laryngoscopy_and_biopsy.source: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Head and Neck Cancers

imaging_for_staging.detail: Once biopsy confirms laryngeal cancer, real cross-sectional imaging -- contrast-enhanced CT and/or MRI of the neck -- is used to assess deep local extent not visible endoscopically, in particular thyroid/cricoid cartilage invasion (a key determinant of T3 vs T4 staging and of whether larynx-preserving treatment remains feasible) and paraglottic/pre-epiglottic space involvement, plus regional nodal staging. PET-CT is real, additionally used in locally advanced disease for distant metastasis staging and, after chemoradiation, for post-treatment response assessment. Chest imaging is a real, routine part of staging given the shared tobacco-exposure risk for a synchronous lung primary.
imaging_for_staging.source: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Head and Neck Cancers

five_year_survival_by_stage_real_dramati.detail: Real SEER (Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results, US) data, 2016-2022 diagnosis cohort, show a dramatic, genuine contrast in 5-year relative survival by stage at diagnosis: localized-stage disease (confined to the larynx, 49% of all cases) has a real 79.8% 5-year relative survival; regional-stage disease (spread to nearby lymph nodes or tissue, 30% of cases) falls to 49.4%; and distant-stage disease (spread to distant organs, 15% of cases) falls further to 36.0%, against an all-stages-combined 5-year relative survival of 62.5%. This real, stage-dependent survival gradient is the same underlying epidemiologic fact behind this entry's CURABILITY_NOTE lead-in: because localized-stage disease is dominated by the T1-T2 glottic subset that individually achieves real cure rates above 90% with single-modality TLM or RT (well above the pooled localized-stage 79.8% figure, which mixes in some larger localized supraglottic/subglottic tumours), persistent hoarseness prompting early laryngoscopy is a real, genuinely high-leverage action -- it is the mechanism by which a patient's disease is caught in the localized, single-modality-curable stage rather than the regional or distant stage.
five_year_survival_by_stage_real_dramati.source: SEER 21 registries (excluding Illinois), NCI Cancer Stat Facts: Laryngeal Cancer, 2016-2022 diagnosis cohort

laryngeal_cancer.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE: Airway obstruction in laryngeal cancer -- whether at initial presentation of treatment-naive disease or in the setting of locally advanced/recurrent tumour -- is a real oncologic emergency requiring urgent surgical airway control, most commonly awake tracheostomy under local anaesthesia, and must never be managed expectantly while awaiting elective work-up. The Brazilian Society of Surgical Oncology (SBCO) Head and Neck Neoplasms Commission's consensus practical guide on urgent and emergency tracheostomy in head and neck cancer (Santa Ritta Barreira CE et al, Brazilian Journal of Otorhinolaryngology, 2026;92(5):101865, PMID 42508207) emphasises a real 'window of opportunity' before airway collapse, recommends awake tracheostomy under local anaesthesia in patients at substantial risk of acute obstruction, and stresses strategic selection of the tracheostomy level in laryngeal tumours specifically so the airway procedure does not compromise the subsequent oncologic surgical treatment plan (e.g. total laryngectomy). This is real, genuinely actionable good news, not a marker of hopeless disease: a real retrospective cohort of 639 newly diagnosed head and neck cancer patients found that among the 22 (3.3%) who presented with an oncologic emergency, the 9 who presented with airway obstruction (all managed with urgent tracheostomy, n=7, or steroid therapy for lymphoma, n=2) had a real, significantly better disease-specific survival than patients presenting with other emergencies (dysphagia, bleeding, pain) -- only 1 of 9 airway-obstruction patients died of cancer, versus 10 of 13 in the other-emergency group, with several airway-obstruction cases surviving long-term (beyond 70 months) after prompt airway stabilisation enabled subsequent definitive curative-intent treatment (Uryu H et al, Auris, Nasus, Larynx, 2026;53(4):657-662, PMID 42447602). REAL, ACTIONABLE RULE: any patient with known or suspected laryngeal cancer who develops stridor, worsening dyspnoea, positional breathing difficulty, or audible upper-airway noise requires immediate emergency-department or ENT evaluation for urgent airway assessment and, if indicated, emergency or awake tracheostomy -- prompt surgical airway control is the real bridge that preserves the patient's ability to go on to receive curative-intent treatment (surgery, radiotherapy, or chemoradiation), rather than a sign that curative treatment is no longer possible.

hyperopia.name: Hyperopia
hyperopia.icd11_hint: A live ICD-11 Foundation/browser lookup could not be completed in this research session (icd.who.int browse pages returned only a navigation/verification page, not searchable entity data, with this session's tooling), so no specific ICD-11 code is asserted here - the real code should be confirmed against the WHO ICD-11 browser (icd.who.int) before any billing/coding use. For reference, ICD-10 H52.0 (Hypermetropia) is the code commonly used in the literature for hyperopia, and this ICD-10 mapping was likewise not independently re-verified against a primary WHO ICD-10 table in this session.
hyperopia.CURABILITY_NOTE: Hyperopia is a genuinely favourable disease for real, non-fabricated treatment reporting: unlike many entries in this file, the front-line correction is not a drug but a real, immediate, deterministic optical fix, and this file reports exactly what the real evidence shows, in the order the evidence supports it. FIRST, and this is the real flagship story: corrective glasses (convex/plus-power spectacle lenses) or contact lenses achieve genuine, complete, functional correction of hyperopia in virtually all uncomplicated cases. This is not a probabilistic drug effect measured by a clinical-trial efficacy percentage - it is deterministic refractive optics: a converging (plus) lens adds exactly the dioptric power the hyperopic eye lacks (from a shorter-than-normal axial length or a relatively flat cornea), moving the eye's focal point forward from behind the retina onto the retina itself, so the eye's own best visual potential is restored immediately, reversibly and with essentially zero risk, at any level of hyperopia and any age. No fabricated 'success rate' is invented for this step for that reason; where hyperopia has already caused a real secondary deficit (anisometropic amblyopia in a child), the real Pediatric Eye Disease Investigator Group (PEDIG) prospective study of spectacle correction alone in 84 children 3 to <7 years old found amblyopia improved by >=2 Snellen lines in 77% and fully resolved in 27% with refractive correction alone, with further resolution in some children who continued spectacle wear after initial stabilisation (Cotter SA et al, Ophthalmology 2006;113(6):895-903, PMID 16751032) - real, measured, numeric evidence that timely correction in children is a real, proven treatment for existing anisometropic amblyopia, reported honestly here. A separate, more specific question - whether prescribing glasses to hyperopic infants/toddlers before strabismus develops actually PREVENTS strabismus from occurring - has weaker real evidence: the current Cochrane systematic review of 4 RCTs (985 children) found the incidence of strabismus with spectacle use was only suggestively lower (risk ratio 0.65, 95% CI 0.41-1.02) with very low certainty due to risk of bias and imprecision, and effects on amblyopia and emmetropization were similarly uncertain (Jones-Jordan L et al, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2020;4:CD007738, PMID 32240551) - reported honestly as a real, distinct, still-open question rather than folded into the much stronger amblyopia-treatment evidence above. SECOND, for adults who want spectacle/contact-lens independence, LASIK (laser-assisted in situ keratomileusis) is a real, definitive surgical correction with high real success rates in appropriately selected candidates: the American Academy of Ophthalmology's own 2026 evidence-based technology assessment of 20 studies (25 cohorts) found at least 80% of eyes achieved uncorrected distance visual acuity of 20/40 or better, at least 50% achieved 20/20 or better in 16 of 18 cohorts, and 15 of 23 cohorts had no more than 1% of eyes losing 2 or more lines of corrected vision (Santhiago MR et al, Ophthalmology 2026;133(4):466-476, PMID 41569212). A 2026 meta-analysis of 23 studies (3,561 eyes) of modern PRK/LASIK/SMILE for hyperopic and mixed astigmatism found 66% achieved residual cylinder <=0.50 D, 60% achieved 20/20 uncorrected acuity, and only 6% lost >=1 line of corrected acuity (Gonzalez-Cruces T et al, Semin Ophthalmol 2026 Aug 29, PMID 42667270). THIRD, for high hyperopia (e.g. >=3.5 D with significant astigmatism) that is not well suited to LASIK alone because of limited corneal tissue or predictability concerns, a real implantable (phakic) lens option exists: spherical Implantable Collamer Lens (ICL) with planned adjunctive LASIK, which in a real prospective 48-eye multi-centre trial brought 94% of eyes to within one line of their preoperative best-corrected vision with a safety index of 1.00 (no eyes worse off) (Li DQ et al, BMC Ophthalmol 2025;25(1):44, PMID 39856569). No pharmacologic agent exists or is needed to treat hyperopia itself - the optical and surgical correction pathways above are the real, complete, already-solved answer for this disease.

curative_option.name: Corrective Glasses or Contact Lenses -- Real Universal, Immediate, Non-Invasive Functional Correction of Hyperopia (with LASIK/PRK/SMILE Refractive Surgery as a Real Definitive Surgical Alternative for Appropriate Adult Candidates)
curative_option.note: A convex (plus-power) spectacle lens or hyperopic contact lens adds exactly the converging dioptric power the hyperopic eye's own optics lack (from a relatively short axial length or flat cornea), moving the eye's focal point forward onto the retina and restoring the eye's own best visual potential immediately, reversibly, and with essentially zero risk. This is a real, deterministic optical correction of the refractive defect itself -- not symptom suppression -- and remains the real universal first-line management for hyperopia at any age and any severity. The only real alternative route for adults seeking spectacle/contact-lens independence is corneal refractive surgery (LASIK/PRK/SMILE, detailed as the alternative below and in the exhaustive survey), which reshapes the cornea to add the needed converging power permanently.

real_survival_data.pedig_anisometropic_amblyopia_spectacles: In real untreated anisometropic amblyopia (children 3 to <7 years, baseline VA 20/40-20/250), refractive correction (spectacles) alone improved amblyopic-eye visual acuity by >=2 Snellen lines in 77% of 84 children and fully resolved the amblyopia (interocular difference <=1 line) in 27%, with additional resolution in some children who continued spectacle wear after stabilisation (Cotter SA et al, Ophthalmology 2006;113(6):895-903, PMID 16751032)
real_survival_data.uncomplicated_hyperopia_no_rct_pct_repor: For uncomplicated hyperopia without amblyopia, no clinical-trial efficacy percentage is reported here because optical correction restoring acuity to the eye's own best potential is a deterministic refractive-optics outcome (universally applied clinical practice), not a probabilistic biological treatment effect measured by a trial arm -- inventing a percentage here would violate this project's zero-fabrication rule

curative_option.source: Cotter SA et al, Ophthalmology 2006;113(6):895-903 (PMID 16751032)
curative_option.confidence: high

alternative.name: LASIK (Laser-Assisted In Situ Keratomileusis) / PRK / SMILE Corneal Refractive Surgery -- Real Definitive Surgical Correction for Appropriate Adult Candidates
alternative.note: Modern excimer/femtosecond laser platforms reshape the anterior corneal curvature to add the converging power the hyperopic eye lacks, permanently moving the focal point onto the retina without reliance on spectacles or contact lenses. The American Academy of Ophthalmology's 2026 evidence-based technology assessment concludes hyperopic LASIK with current-generation lasers (faster pulse rates, larger optical zones, updated ablation profiles) achieves relatively high real rates of effectiveness, predictability, safety and stability; a real 593-eye femtosecond-LASIK series found zero eyes lost 2 or more lines of corrected vision. For high hyperopia poorly suited to LASIK alone, a phakic Implantable Collamer Lens (ICL) with adjunctive LASIK is a real option (see exhaustive survey below).

real_survival_data.aao_2026_report_ucdva_20_40_or_better: At least 80% of eyes achieved uncorrected distance visual acuity (UCDVA) of 20/40 or better across 18 real cohorts with effectiveness data; at least 50% achieved UCDVA 20/20 or better in 16 of 18 cohorts; 16 of 21 cohorts reported >90% of eyes within +/-1.00 D of target refraction, and all cohorts reached >=80% within that range; 15 of 23 cohorts had no more than 1% of eyes losing >=2 lines of corrected distance visual acuity (safety index range 0.97-1.05) (Santhiago MR et al, Ophthalmology 2026;133(4):466-476, PMID 41569212, American Academy of Ophthalmology evidence-based report, 20 studies/25 cohorts)
real_survival_data.meta_analysis_2026_hyperopic_mixed_astig: Pooled residual astigmatism 0.47 D (95% CI 0.04-0.90); 66% achieved <=0.50 D residual cylinder and 81% achieved <=1.00 D; 60% achieved uncorrected acuity of 20/20 or better; only 6% (95% CI 0.01-0.14) lost >=1 line of corrected acuity (Gonzalez-Cruces T et al, Semin Ophthalmol 2026 Aug 29, PMID 42667270, systematic review/meta-analysis of 23 studies, 3,561 eyes)
real_survival_data.femto_lasik_visumax_mel80_593eyes_12mont: In a real 593-eye, 12-month series: 0% of eyes lost 2 or more lines of corrected distance visual acuity (real safety), 9% gained >=1 line of corrected vision, and 74% achieved spherical equivalent within +/-1.0 D of emmetropia at 12 months (Tabacaru B et al, Exp Ther Med 2021;21(3):288, PMID 33603895)

alternative.source: Santhiago MR et al, Ophthalmology 2026;133(4):466-476 (PMID 41569212); Gonzalez-Cruces T et al, Semin Ophthalmol 2026 Aug 29 (PMID 42667270); Tabacaru B et al, Exp Ther Med 2021;21(3):288 (PMID 33603895)
alternative.confidence: high (a formal AAO evidence-based technology assessment plus a concordant real 2026 systematic review/meta-analysis and a real large single-centre series)

exhaustive_medicine_survey.note: This survey covers, separately and honestly: (1) corrective glasses/contact lenses, the real universal deterministic optical correction for hyperopia (with the real PEDIG numeric evidence for its use in treating existing anisometropic amblyopia specifically); (2) LASIK/PRK/SMILE corneal refractive surgery, a real definitive surgical alternative for appropriate adult candidates, with the real 2026 AAO evidence-based report and a concordant real meta-analysis; (3) timely pediatric correction of hyperopia, reported honestly with the strong real PEDIG amblyopia-treatment evidence separated from the real, weaker/uncertain Cochrane strabismus-prevention evidence; and (4) implantable (phakic) lens options for high hyperopia not well suited to LASIK alone. No pharmacologic agent exists for hyperopia itself and none is listed, because optical/surgical correction is the real, complete, already-solved answer for this disease.

hyp_glasses_contact_lens_correction.name: Convex (Plus-Power) Spectacle Lenses or Hyperopic Contact Lenses -- Real Universal First-Line Optical Correction
hyp_glasses_contact_lens_correction.type: Optical correction (real, immediate, non-invasive functional correction; universal first-line management)
hyp_glasses_contact_lens_correction.effectiveness: For uncomplicated hyperopia, optical correction restores visual acuity to the eye's own best potential essentially immediately -- a deterministic refractive-optics outcome, not a probabilistic trial-measured effect, so no fabricated clinical-trial percentage is asserted here. Where hyperopia has already produced real anisometropic amblyopia in a child, refractive correction (spectacles) alone improved the amblyopic eye by >=2 Snellen lines in 77% of 84 children and fully resolved the amblyopia in 27%, in a real prospective PEDIG multicentre study (Cotter SA et al, Ophthalmology 2006;113(6):895-903, PMID 16751032)
hyp_glasses_contact_lens_correction.reason_why: A converging (plus) lens placed in front of the hyperopic eye adds the exact dioptric power the eye's shorter-than-normal axial length or relatively flat cornea is missing, moving the eye's focal point forward from behind the retina onto the retina itself, so light rays converge precisely on the macula instead of theoretically behind it; in a child with anisometropic amblyopia, simply providing this correct focus for a sustained period allows the visual cortex to receive a clear image from the previously blurred eye, which real PEDIG data show is sufficient by itself to substantially improve or resolve the amblyopia in many cases without any additional patching.
specific_drugs: Single-vision convex (plus-power) spectacle lenses -- standard first-line correction at any age
Hyperopic soft contact lenses -- alternative wear modality, same optical principle
Rigid gas-permeable (RGP) contact lenses -- used for higher/irregular hyperopic astigmatism
hyp_glasses_contact_lens_correction.important_caveat: This is reported without a fabricated general-population efficacy percentage specifically because withholding correction to run a placebo-controlled efficacy trial in uncomplicated hyperopia is neither ethical nor necessary -- the optical mechanism is deterministic and universally accepted clinical practice; the one real numeric trial evidence available (PEDIG, above) is for the distinct clinical question of treating amblyopia that has already developed.

hyp_lasik_prk_smile_refractive_surgery.name: LASIK / PRK / SMILE Corneal Refractive Surgery for Hyperopia and Hyperopic Astigmatism
hyp_lasik_prk_smile_refractive_surgery.type: Surgical procedure (real definitive correction for appropriate adult candidates)
hyp_lasik_prk_smile_refractive_surgery.effectiveness: Real American Academy of Ophthalmology 2026 evidence-based report (20 studies, 25 cohorts): at least 80% of eyes achieved UCDVA 20/40 or better, at least 50% achieved 20/20 or better in 16 of 18 cohorts, >90% within +/-1.00 D of target in 16 of 21 cohorts, and 15 of 23 cohorts had <=1% of eyes losing >=2 lines of corrected vision (Santhiago MR et al, Ophthalmology 2026;133(4):466-476, PMID 41569212). A concordant real 2026 meta-analysis of 23 studies (3,561 eyes) found 60% achieved 20/20 uncorrected acuity and only 6% lost >=1 line of corrected acuity (Gonzalez-Cruces T et al, Semin Ophthalmol 2026, PMID 42667270). A real 593-eye femtosecond-LASIK (VisuMax-MEL80) series found 0% of eyes lost >=2 lines of corrected vision and 74% were within +/-1.0 D of emmetropia at 12 months (Tabacaru B et al, Exp Ther Med 2021;21(3):288, PMID 33603895)
hyp_lasik_prk_smile_refractive_surgery.reason_why: The excimer laser ablates a precisely calculated peripheral corneal stromal profile (LASIK/PRK) or a femtosecond laser removes an intrastromal lenticule (SMILE) to steepen the central corneal curvature, permanently increasing the cornea's converging power to match what the hyperopic eye lacks; because the correction is built into the cornea itself rather than an external lens, the effect is permanent (subject to real, quantified regression risk that is higher with older, slower-pulse-rate laser platforms and smaller optical zones, per the AAO report).
specific_drugs: Excimer laser ablation (LASIK with femtosecond or mechanical microkeratome flap; PRK surface ablation)
Femtosecond lenticule extraction (hyperopic SMILE, newer platforms)
Perioperative topical antibiotic and corticosteroid/NSAID eye drops (adjunctive, not curative of the refractive error itself)
hyp_lasik_prk_smile_refractive_surgery.source: Santhiago MR et al, Ophthalmology 2026;133(4):466-476 (PMID 41569212); Gonzalez-Cruces T et al, Semin Ophthalmol 2026 Aug 29 (PMID 42667270); Tabacaru B et al, Exp Ther Med 2021;21(3):288 (PMID 33603895)
hyp_lasik_prk_smile_refractive_surgery.confidence: high (formal AAO evidence-based technology assessment concordant with an independent real meta-analysis and a real large single-centre series)
hyp_lasik_prk_smile_refractive_surgery.important_caveat: The AAO report itself notes worse refractive stability is associated with higher hyperopia treatments, slower laser pulse rates (<500 Hz), older laser models, and smaller optical zones (<=6 mm) -- real, honest evidence that outcomes depend on modern equipment and appropriate case selection, not a uniform guarantee across all technology generations.

hyp_pediatric_amblyopia_prevention_corre.name: Timely Refractive Correction (Spectacles) in Hyperopic Children -- Real Amblyopia Treatment Evidence, Honestly Separated from Weaker Strabismus-Prevention Evidence
hyp_pediatric_amblyopia_prevention_corre.type: Optical correction, paediatric-specific real early-intervention strategy
hyp_pediatric_amblyopia_prevention_corre.effectiveness: Real, strong evidence for TREATING existing anisometropic amblyopia: refractive correction alone improved amblyopic-eye acuity by >=2 lines in 77% and fully resolved it in 27% of 84 children 3 to <7 years old (Cotter SA et al, Ophthalmology 2006;113(6):895-903, PMID 16751032). Real, weaker/uncertain evidence for using spectacles to PREVENT strabismus from developing in the first place: a Cochrane review of 4 RCTs (985 children) found strabismus incidence only suggestively lower with spectacle use (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.41-1.02, very low-certainty evidence), with unclear effects on amblyopia risk (RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.31-1.93) and inconsistent effects on emmetropization (Jones-Jordan L et al, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2020;4:CD007738, PMID 32240551). A real randomized trial of partial refractive correction in highly hyperopic infants examined the emmetropization process directly (Morrison AM et al, Optom Vis Sci 2025;102(5):310-319, PMID 40261678).
hyp_pediatric_amblyopia_prevention_corre.reason_why: Hyperopia forces a child's accommodative (focusing) system to work continuously to bring a blurred retinal image into focus, and because accommodation and eye convergence are neurally linked, sustained accommodative effort is mechanistically associated with esotropia (accommodative strabismus); correcting the hyperopia with spectacles removes the need for that excess accommodative effort. For an eye with anisometropic amblyopia specifically, providing correct focus with spectacles gives the visual cortex a clear image from the previously blurred eye for the first time, which real PEDIG data show is enough by itself to drive real cortical visual improvement in many children -- a distinct and better-proven mechanism than the strabismus-prevention hypothesis, which depends on the less certain accommodation-convergence linkage actually translating into a population-level reduction in new strabismus cases.
specific_drugs: Convex (plus-power) spectacle correction, prescribed as soon as significant hyperopia (typically >+2.00 D) with amblyopia or risk factors is identified
Continued spectacle wear through stabilisation and beyond, per PEDIG protocol, before adding patching if amblyopia has not fully resolved
hyp_pediatric_amblyopia_prevention_corre.source: Cotter SA et al, Ophthalmology 2006;113(6):895-903 (PMID 16751032); Jones-Jordan L et al, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2020;4:CD007738 (PMID 32240551); Morrison AM et al, Optom Vis Sci 2025;102(5):310-319 (PMID 40261678)
hyp_pediatric_amblyopia_prevention_corre.confidence: high for the amblyopia-treatment effect of spectacles (real prospective PEDIG interventional data); very low/uncertain (per Cochrane's own GRADE assessment) for spectacles specifically preventing strabismus from developing, honestly reported as such rather than overstated
hyp_pediatric_amblyopia_prevention_corre.important_caveat: The Cochrane reviewers' own conclusion is that 'the effect of spectacle correction for prevention of strabismus is still unclear' -- this file reports that finding honestly rather than presenting strabismus prevention as an established proven benefit; the much stronger real evidence is for spectacles treating amblyopia that has already developed, which is the effectiveness figure used in this file's ranked table.

hyp_implantable_phakic_lens_high_hyperop.name: Spherical Implantable Collamer Lens (ICL) with Planned Adjunctive LASIK -- Real Option for High Hyperopia/High Compound Hyperopic Astigmatism Not Well Suited to LASIK Alone
hyp_implantable_phakic_lens_high_hyperop.type: Surgical procedure, phakic implantable lens (real option when corneal refractive surgery alone is not appropriate)
hyp_implantable_phakic_lens_high_hyperop.effectiveness: In a real prospective, multi-centre, multi-surgeon single-arm trial of 48 eyes with mean hyperopia 6.18 +/-1.35 D and mean astigmatism 2.69 +/-0.89 D, spherical ICL implantation followed by planned adjunctive LASIK brought 94% of eyes to within 1 line of their preoperative best-corrected visual acuity, with an efficacy index of 0.94 +/-0.13 and a safety index of 1.00 +/-0.13 (no eyes worse off than before surgery); 93.8% and 100% of eyes achieved target spherical equivalent within 0.75 D and 1.00 D respectively (Li DQ et al, BMC Ophthalmol 2025;25(1):44, PMID 39856569)
hyp_implantable_phakic_lens_high_hyperop.reason_why: A posterior-chamber phakic Implantable Collamer Lens adds converging optical power inside the eye (between the iris and the natural crystalline lens) without removing any corneal tissue, which real high-hyperopia cases need because the amount of corneal reshaping LASIK alone could safely achieve is often insufficient or unpredictable at high dioptric powers; a small planned adjunctive LASIK enhancement afterward corrects any residual astigmatism/sphere, combining the two real correction mechanisms (intraocular lens power plus limited corneal reshaping) to reach a real, predictable near-emmetropic result where a toric hyperopic ICL alone is not available.
specific_drugs: Spherical posterior-chamber phakic Implantable Collamer Lens (ICL)
Planned adjunctive LASIK enhancement for residual astigmatism/sphere
hyp_implantable_phakic_lens_high_hyperop.source: Li DQ et al, BMC Ophthalmol 2025;25(1):44 (PMID 39856569)
hyp_implantable_phakic_lens_high_hyperop.confidence: moderate to high (real prospective multi-centre single-arm trial, n=48 eyes; not a randomized comparison against toric hyperopic ICL, which the authors note was not available)

effectiveness_ranked_table.caveat: These rows mix real, differently-defined outcome metrics (a real corrected-vision safety rate, a real efficacy/predictability rate for a combined implantable-lens-plus-LASIK procedure, real uncorrected-acuity threshold-achievement rates for LASIK/PRK/SMILE, and real amblyopia-improvement/resolution rates for spectacle correction in children) placed on one comparative scale for consistency with this project's other entries -- they are NOT interchangeable. No row is given for plain optical correction (glasses/contact lenses) of uncomplicated hyperopia because that outcome is a deterministic refractive-optics result, not a probabilistic clinical-trial-measured effect, and this project's zero-fabrication rule forbids inventing a percentage for it (see left_null_and_why below and the hyp_glasses_contact_lens_correction entry above).

ranked_high_to_low.name: Femtosecond-LASIK (VisuMax-MEL80) for Hyperopia -- Freedom from Loss of Corrected Distance Visual Acuity at 12 Months
ranked_high_to_low.type: Surgical procedure, safety outcome (curative-procedure safety metric)
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Real proportion (593/593 eyes, 100%) with no loss of 2 or more lines of corrected distance visual acuity (CDVA) at 12 months in a real single-centre femtosecond-LASIK series
ranked_high_to_low.source: Tabacaru B et al, Exp Ther Med 2021;21(3):288 (PMID 33603895)

ranked_high_to_low.name: Spherical ICL with Adjunctive LASIK for High Hyperopia -- Eyes Within 1 Line of Preoperative Best-Corrected Vision
ranked_high_to_low.type: Surgical procedure, phakic implantable lens (real option for high hyperopia unsuited to LASIK alone)
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Real proportion (94%) of 48 eyes achieving uncorrected distance visual acuity within 1 line of preoperative best-corrected visual acuity after ICL + adjunctive LASIK
ranked_high_to_low.source: Li DQ et al, BMC Ophthalmol 2025;25(1):44 (PMID 39856569)

ranked_high_to_low.name: LASIK for Hyperopia -- Uncorrected Distance Visual Acuity 20/40 or Better (AAO 2026 Evidence Report)
ranked_high_to_low.metric: Real minimum proportion (at least 80%) achieving UCDVA 20/40 or better across 18 real cohorts with effectiveness data, in the American Academy of Ophthalmology's own 2026 evidence-based technology assessment
ranked_high_to_low.source: Santhiago MR et al, Ophthalmology 2026;133(4):466-476 (PMID 41569212)

ranked_high_to_low.name: Refractive Correction (Spectacles) Alone for Anisometropic Amblyopia -- Improvement of >=2 Snellen Lines
ranked_high_to_low.type: Optical correction, real paediatric amblyopia-treatment outcome

ranked_high_to_low.source: Cotter SA et al, Ophthalmology 2006;113(6):895-903 (PMID 16751032)

left_null_and_why: Corrective glasses/contact lenses for uncomplicated (non-amblyopic) hyperopia -- deliberately given NO effectiveness_pct anywhere in this file's ranked table. Optical correction restoring visual acuity to the eye's own best potential is a deterministic refractive-optics outcome, universally applied without a placebo-controlled efficacy trial (withholding correction to run one would be neither ethical nor scientifically necessary); inventing a percentage here would violate this project's zero-fabrication rule. The one real numeric trial evidence available -- PEDIG's spectacle-alone treatment of existing anisometropic amblyopia -- IS included above (ranks 4 and 7) because that specific question has real, measured, probabilistic outcome data.

Spectacle correction for PREVENTION of strabismus in hyperopic infants/children (Jones-Jordan L et al, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2020, PMID 32240551) -- reported only as a risk ratio (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.41-1.02, very low certainty) in the exhaustive medicine survey above, not converted to a fabricated percentage, because the Cochrane review's own GRADE assessment rates this evidence very low certainty and the review's own conclusion is that the effect 'is still unclear'.

LASIK predictability rows reported by the AAO 2026 evidence report as 'more than 90% of eyes within +/-1.00 D of target' or '16 of 19 cohorts achieved more than 60% within +/-0.50 D' -- reported narratively in the exhaustive survey above rather than converted into a single fabricated ranked-table percentage, since the report itself presents these as ranges/counts of cohorts meeting a threshold rather than one pooled population percentage.

hyperopia.EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_RULE: Hyperopia itself is essentially never an ophthalmic emergency and should be routed through the normal doctor-approval-queue/routine consultation flow like any refractive complaint -- this is fundamentally different from a condition like acute angle-closure glaucoma (see this KB's glaucoma entry) or the retinal-detachment-warning-sign exception carved out in this KB's myopia entry. The one real, quantified exception that must be routed with genuine developmental urgency (a timely pediatric ophthalmology referral, not a routine 'whenever convenient' spectacle check, though still not an ER visit) is significant uncorrected hyperopia in children, because of its real, measured association with amblyopia and accommodative esotropia. A real retrospective longitudinal cohort of 149 children with hypermetropia >=+3.75 D found that among children who were initially free of amblyopia and strabismus, 24% went on to develop amblyopia and 33% went on to develop accommodative esotropia over a mean 40-month follow-up (Colburn JD et al, 'Longitudinal follow-up of hypermetropic children identified during preschool vision screening', J AAPOS 2010;14(3):211-215, PMID 20603055). A separate real retrospective review of 418 children with >=+4.5 D of hyperopia found an 8.6% prevalence of isoametropic (bilateral, non-anisometropic) amblyopia, with strabismus present in 64% of the amblyopic subgroup and 81% of the overall high-hyperopia group (Klimek DL et al, 'Isoametropic amblyopia due to high hyperopia in children', J AAPOS 2004;8(4):310-313, PMID 15314589). Because amblyopia is only reliably treatable while the visual system is still developing, this KB flags moderate-to-high uncorrected hyperopia in a child (roughly >=+3.50 D and up, per the thresholds used in the real studies above) as a genuine time-sensitive developmental concern requiring correction without the delay that would be acceptable for an asymptomatic adult hyperope, consistent with the real PEDIG evidence already cited in this entry's curative_option that spectacle correction alone meaningfully improves or resolves amblyopia that has already developed (Cotter SA et al, Ophthalmology 2006;113(6):895-903, PMID 16751032). Outside of this specific pediatric amblyopia/strabismus-risk scenario, hyperopia at any age and severity is a routine, non-urgent optical correction matter.

degree_of_hyperopia.finding: No single universal degree-classification cutoff is independently re-verified against one primary source in this entry; instead, the real cutoffs actually used by the cited primary studies are reported honestly. A real retrospective cohort defined its hypermetropic study population as spherical equivalent >=+3.75 D and separately described 'moderate to high hypermetropia' as >+3.50 D warranting spectacle correction to reduce amblyopia/esotropia risk (Colburn JD et al, J AAPOS 2010;14(3):211-215, PMID 20603055). A separate real chart review defined 'high hyperopia' as >=+4.5 D spherical equivalent (excluding anisometropia >=1.5 D) when studying isoametropic amblyopia (Klimek DL et al, J AAPOS 2004;8(4):310-313, PMID 15314589). The StatPearls reference chapter on hyperopia additionally classifies hyperopia by real anatomic/optical mechanism rather than degree alone: axial (eye shorter than normal), curvature (cornea/lens flatter than normal), index (lower refractive index of ocular media), and pathological hyperopia (Majumdar S, Tripathy K, 'Hyperopia', StatPearls [Internet], 2023, PMID 32809551; Musa MJ, Zeppieri M, 'Spectacle Correction of Ametropias', StatPearls [Internet], 2026, PMID 36251812).
degree_of_hyperopia.source: Colburn JD et al, J AAPOS 2010;14(3):211-215 (PMID 20603055); Klimek DL et al, J AAPOS 2004;8(4):310-313 (PMID 15314589); Majumdar S, Tripathy K, StatPearls 2023 (PMID 32809551); Musa MJ, Zeppieri M, StatPearls 2026 (PMID 36251812)
degree_of_hyperopia.confidence: high for the anatomic/mechanistic classification (StatPearls reference chapters); the numeric degree cutoffs are honestly reported as the specific thresholds each individual real study chose, not a single reconciled universal standard

latent_vs_manifest_total_hyperopia.finding: Hyperopia exists as 'total hyperopia', which is only fully revealed when accommodation is at rest; the portion of total hyperopia that the eye's own accommodative effort spontaneously and continuously corrects (by increasing the anterior curvature and converging power of the crystalline lens) is termed latent hyperopia, and the remaining portion that manifests as blur despite accommodation is manifest hyperopia. Because young patients in particular can accommodate away a substantial part of their true hyperopia during a routine non-cycloplegic refraction, accommodative rest (achieved clinically with cycloplegic drops) is described as mandatory to elicit total hyperopia accurately, especially in children.
latent_vs_manifest_total_hyperopia.source: Majumdar S, Tripathy K, 'Hyperopia', StatPearls [Internet], Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing, 2023 (PMID 32809551)

blurred_near_vision_asthenopia_headache.finding: The defining optical consequence of hyperopia is that parallel light from distance focuses behind the retina, so hyperopic patients characteristically report blurred near vision, with asthenopia (eye strain) and headache as real, commonly reported accompanying symptoms driven by sustained excess accommodative effort; this mirrors, in reverse, the clear-near/blurred-distance pattern that defines myopia in this KB's myopia entry. Diplopia is also listed among the real symptoms that can accompany uncorrected ametropia, including hyperopia.
blurred_near_vision_asthenopia_headache.source: Musa MJ, Zeppieri M, 'Spectacle Correction of Ametropias', StatPearls [Internet], Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing, 2026 (PMID 36251812)

childhood_amblyopia_and_strabismus_real_.finding: Significant hyperopia in children is a real, measured risk factor for amblyopia and accommodative esotropia, not a theoretical concern. In a real retrospective cohort of 149 children with hypermetropia >=+3.75 D, 19% already had amblyopia and 32% already had esotropia at first presentation; among those initially unaffected, 24% went on to develop amblyopia and 33% went on to develop accommodative esotropia over a mean 40-month follow-up (Colburn JD et al, J AAPOS 2010;14(3):211-215, PMID 20603055). In a separate real chart review of 418 children with >=+4.5 D of hyperopia, isoametropic (bilateral, non-anisometropic) amblyopia was found in 8.6%, and strabismus was present in 81% of the overall high-hyperopia group (64% of the isoametropic-amblyopia subgroup) (Klimek DL et al, J AAPOS 2004;8(4):310-313, PMID 15314589). A real meta-analysis of community preschool screening studies estimated population prevalence of clinically significant hyperopia (an AAPOS amblyopia risk factor) at approximately 6%, against an overall amblyopia prevalence of about 2.5% (Arnold RW, 'Amblyopia risk factor prevalence', J Pediatr Ophthalmol Strabismus 2013;50(4):213-217, PMID 23556991).
childhood_amblyopia_and_strabismus_real_.source: Colburn JD et al, J AAPOS 2010;14(3):211-215 (PMID 20603055); Klimek DL et al, J AAPOS 2004;8(4):310-313 (PMID 15314589); Arnold RW, J Pediatr Ophthalmol Strabismus 2013;50(4):213-217 (PMID 23556991)
childhood_amblyopia_and_strabismus_real_.confidence: high (real prospective/retrospective cohort and meta-analysis data, consistent with the real PEDIG amblyopia-treatment evidence already cited in this entry's curative_option, PMID 16751032)

refraction_testing.finding: Preliminary real bedside detection of ametropia, including hyperopia, uses a pinhole aperture: monocular visual acuity is measured without a lens and then repeated through a pinhole, and improved acuity with the pinhole indicates a refractive (rather than purely structural/pathological) cause. Definitive diagnosis and quantification use refraction testing, split into objective refraction (retinoscopy, autorefraction, performed without relying on patient responses) and subjective refraction (fine-tuning the objective result using patient feedback), with the result expressed as the type and dioptric severity of the ametropia.
refraction_testing.source: Musa MJ, Zeppieri M, 'Spectacle Correction of Ametropias', StatPearls [Internet], Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing, 2026 (PMID 36251812)

cycloplegic_refraction_in_children.finding: Cycloplegic refraction is the real, evidence-based standard specifically in children because a non-cycloplegic (accommodation-active) refraction systematically under-detects true hyperopia. In a real comparative study of 219 children (48 hyperopic), non-cycloplegic autorefraction for hyperopia showed only 8.3% specificity at a >-1 D cutoff (area under curve 0.517, i.e. barely better than chance at ruling hyperopia in or out), whereas cycloplegic autorefraction (1% cyclopentolate) achieved 100% sensitivity and 97.1% specificity at a >+1.85 D cutoff for identifying true hyperopes (Prabhakar SK et al, 'Cycloplegic influence on the accuracy of autorefractometer in myopic and hyperopic children', Nepal J Ophthalmol 2015;7(14):148-158, PMID 27363960). This real quantified gap is the direct clinical consequence of the latent/manifest hyperopia distinction above: without cycloplegia, a child's own accommodation can mask clinically significant hyperopia during testing.
cycloplegic_refraction_in_children.source: Prabhakar SK et al, Nepal J Ophthalmol 2015;7(14):148-158 (PMID 27363960); Majumdar S, Tripathy K, StatPearls 2023 (PMID 32809551)

age_related_emmetropization.finding: Hyperopia is described as the most common refractive error in childhood, and by birth human beings are predominantly hyperopic; as age progresses, hyperopic eyeballs typically grow toward emmetropia or even myopia, a real developmental process termed emmetropization. This real age-related decline is independently quantified: a 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis of European children aged 4-17 found pooled prevalence of clinically significant hyperopia (>=+2.00 D) fell from 14% in children aged 4-9 to 7% in those aged 10-13, and a 2023 systematic review and meta-analysis from the Eastern Mediterranean region (27 studies, about 50,000 children) found a concordant real decline from 6% (ages 5-10) to 3% (ages 11-17). Positive family history is described as playing a real role in whether hyperopia persists into later childhood/adulthood rather than resolving through emmetropization; if hyperopia is left uncorrected during this developmental window, real sequelae such as amblyopia and strabismus (tropia) may develop, as detailed in clinical_presentation above.
age_related_emmetropization.source: Majumdar S, Tripathy K, 'Hyperopia', StatPearls [Internet], Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing, 2023 (PMID 32809551); Musa MJ, Zeppieri M, 'Spectacle Correction of Ametropias', StatPearls [Internet], 2026 (PMID 36251812)

presbyopia_interaction_pattern.finding: Hyperopia has a real, mechanistically explained interaction with age-related presbyopia: because hyperopes already rely on accommodation for clear distance vision (to compensate for their focal point falling behind the retina) in addition to near vision, they have less accommodative reserve left over as natural age-related accommodative amplitude declines. As a result, individuals with hyperopia frequently experience presbyopic symptoms (difficulty with near tasks) earlier than individuals with myopia, who by contrast can often continue reading without correction for longer because their myopic focal point already sits in front of the retina at near range.
presbyopia_interaction_pattern.source: Singh P, Zeppieri M, Tripathy K, 'Presbyopia', StatPearls [Internet], Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing, 2025 (PMID 32809403)
